faqs.q: How many people can a luxury catamaran in Puerto Banus hold?
faqs.a: Most catamarans can hold 10-16 guests for day charters. Some larger models can take up to 20. The number is limited by safety regulations, not space. Always confirm the maximum capacity with the charter company before booking.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to charter a luxury catamaran in Puerto Banus?
faqs.a: No. Every charter through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles all navigation and safety. You just relax and enjoy. If you want to sail without a skipper, you need a valid boating licence, but that is a different type of charter.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and drink on a catamaran charter?
faqs.a: Yes, almost all charters allow you to bring your own food and drinks. Some companies provide a cooler with ice. Avoid glass bottles if possible. You can also order catering through the charter company for an extra fee.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day of my charter?
faqs.a: The skipper will assess the conditions. If it is unsafe to go out, the charter is rescheduled or cancelled with a full refund. If the weather is just cloudy or windy, the trip goes ahead. Check the cancellation policy before booking.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book a luxury catamaran in Puerto Banus?
faqs.a: For summer months (June to September), book at least a week in advance. For other seasons, a few days is enough. Last-minute bookings are possible if you are flexible on boat size and route.

faqs.q: Can I charter a catamaran for a wedding or corporate event?
faqs.a: Yes. Many catamarans are suitable for events. You can decorate the boat, bring a DJ, and arrange catering. Contact the charter company directly for a custom quote. Larger groups may need a bigger boat or two catamarans.

faqs.q: Are there any hidden costs I should know about?
faqs.a: The listed price usually includes the boat, skipper, fuel, and basic safety gear. Extras like hostess, catering, water toys, and port fees may cost extra. Always ask for a full breakdown before paying the deposit.

title: Speedboat Rental Estepona: Quick Adventures
metaDescription: Book a speedboat rental Estepona with BoatHire24. RIBs and powerboats from EUR 250, skipper included. Quick trips from Puerto de Estepona. Reserve your ride.
h1: Speedboat Rental Estepona: Quick Adventures on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You want to hit the water fast, skip the queues, and feel the wind in your face. A speedboat rental Estepona is the closest you get to a personal water rocket without a pilot licence. At BoatHire24, every rental comes with a licensed skipper, so you just turn up, sit back, and enjoy the ride. Estepona’s marina, Puerto Deportivo, is the perfect launch point for a quick blast along the coast or a dolphin-spotting run toward Gibraltar.

Speedboats here are mostly RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) and compact powerboats, ranging from 4.5 to 9 metres. They hit 30 to 50 knots depending on the model and sea state. You can rent for two hours, half a day, or a full day. Prices start from around EUR 250 for a short trip. No hidden extras: fuel, insurance, and the skipper are included.
bodyHtml:
Why Choose a Speedboat Rental Estepona

Estepona is a quieter alternative to Puerto Banús, but the water is the same Mediterranean. You get quicker access to open sea because the marina sits close to the Strait of Gibraltar. A speedboat rental Estepona means you can cover a lot of coastline in a short time. From the marina, you can reach the famous dolphin pods off Tarifa in under 30 minutes. Or head east to the Cala del Faro cove for a swim stop. The boat handles chop better than a small sailing yacht, so you stay drier and more stable.

The local fleet includes brands like Zodiac, Brig, and Quicksilver. Most have outboard engines from 115 to 300 hp. You will find both centre-console and side-console layouts. The skipper will handle navigation, mooring, and safety briefings. You just pick the route and the playlist.

What Is Included in Your Speedboat Rental

Every speedboat rental Estepona through BoatHire24 includes a professional skipper. That is non-negotiable and part of the legal requirement for commercial charters in Spain. The skipper knows the local waters, currents, and spots. You also get fuel for the agreed itinerary, basic insurance (third-party liability), and safety equipment (life jackets, VHF radio, flares). Some boats include a Bluetooth speaker and a small cooler. You can bring your own food and drink. The skipper will not consume alcohol, but you can.

Typical inclusions:
- Licensed skipper for the duration
- Fuel for the agreed route
- Insurance (third-party liability)
- Safety gear and life jackets
- Use of onboard amenities (shower, if fitted, on larger RIBs)

Extra costs might include a damage waiver (around EUR 50-100, refundable) or a cleaning fee if you make a mess. Check the terms when booking.

Departure Port: Puerto Deportivo de Estepona

Your speedboat rental Estepona departs from Puerto Deportivo de Estepona, a modern marina with 461 berths. It is less flashy than Puerto Banús but more practical. You park your car in the paid lot (EUR 2 per hour, or free on the street if you find a spot). The marina has a couple of cafés and a chandlery. The boat will be ready at the assigned pontoon. The skipper will meet you there 15 minutes before departure.

From the marina, you have direct access to the Mediterranean without crossing a busy shipping lane. The harbour entrance is sheltered. Once outside, you can turn left toward Gibraltar and the Strait, or right toward Cabopino and Marbella. The water depth drops quickly, so you can open the throttle soon after leaving the breakwater.

Speedboat Types Available in Estepona

The fleet for speedboat rental Estepona is mostly RIBs and a few rigid-hull speedboats. RIBs are lighter, faster, and more stable in choppy conditions. Rigid-hull boats offer a smoother ride at slower speeds but are heavier and less manoeuvrable.

Popular models you can book:
- Zodiac Pro 650 (6.5m, 250 hp, up to 8 passengers)
- Brig Falcon 750 (7.5m, 300 hp, up to 10 passengers)
- Quicksilver 675 (6.7m, 200 hp, up to 8 passengers)
- Williams Jet Tender (5.5m, 115 hp, up to 6 passengers, good for shallow coves)

Most boats have a bimini top for shade. Some have a small toilet compartment (a portable cassette toilet). None have a full galley, but you get a cooler. Top speed ranges from 30 to 50 knots, so you can cover 20 nautical miles in under an hour.

Pricing Guidance for Speedboat Rental Estepona

Prices vary by boat size, engine power, and season. For a speedboat rental Estepona, expect:

- 2-hour trip: from around EUR 250 to EUR 400
- Half day (4 hours): from EUR 450 to EUR 700
- Full day (8 hours): from EUR 800 to EUR 1,200

These include the skipper, fuel, and insurance. High season (June to September) prices are 20-30% higher. Low season (November to February) can be 15% cheaper. You can book online at BoatHire24 with a deposit of 30%. Balance is due on the day. Cancellation policies vary: most allow free cancellation up to 48 hours before.

If you want a specific boat model or a custom itinerary, contact the charter company directly through the listing. Prices for superyacht tenders or high-performance RIBs are on request.

Best Seasons for Speedboat Rental in Estepona

The Mediterranean climate gives you good conditions from April to October. July and August are the hottest, with air temperatures around 30-35°C and water at 24-26°C. The sea is usually calm in the morning, with a light breeze picking up after 2 PM. The Levante wind (easterly) can create choppy conditions in the Strait, but Estepona is sheltered by the Sierra Bermeja mountains, so it is often flatter than Tarifa.

Spring (April to June) is ideal for wildlife spotting: dolphins, whales, and seabirds. Autumn (September to October) offers warm water and fewer crowds. Winter (November to March) is possible on calm days, but you will need a wetsuit for swimming. The boat will have a sprayhood or cabin to keep you dry.

Check the weather forecast on the day. The skipper will decide if it is safe to go out. If the sea state is too rough, you can reschedule or get a full refund.

Popular Routes from Estepona

A speedboat rental Estepona opens up several routes:

Gibraltar and the Strait, Head south-west for 12 nautical miles to the Rock of Gibraltar. You can cruise along the coast, watch the dolphins, and see the cargo ships queuing. Do not land in Gibraltar without a passport and prior permission. The skipper will advise.

Cala del Faro, A hidden cove 5 nautical miles east of Estepona. Only accessible by boat. Clear water, rocky cliffs, and a small beach. Good for a swim and snorkel.

Puerto Banús, 10 nautical miles east. You can cruise past Marbella’s golden beaches and pull into the glamorous marina for a coffee or a photo of the superyachts. The skipper will handle the mooring.

Cabopino, 15 nautical miles east. A quieter marina with a nature reserve behind the dunes. Good for lunch at a beach chiringuito.

Longer trips (full day) can reach Nerja or the caves, but that is 40 nautical miles one way. You will need a faster boat and an early start.

Who Is Speedboat Rental Estepona For

Speedboat rental Estepona suits groups who want a short, intense experience. It is not for a lazy day of sunbathing (though you can do that too). It is for thrill-seekers, families with older kids, and groups of friends who want to cover ground quickly. The maximum passenger count is usually 8 to 10, depending on the boat. Life jackets are provided for all sizes.

If you are prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before. The boat will bounce on choppy water. Sit near the centre of the boat for a smoother ride. The skipper can adjust speed to your comfort level.

No boating licence is needed. The skipper handles everything. You just need to be able to climb aboard from the pontoon. The boat has a ladder for reboarding after swimming.

How to Book Your Speedboat Rental Estepona

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24 search, filter by location (Estepona), boat type (speedboat/RIB), and date. You will see available boats with photos, specifications, and prices. Click the one you like, check the itinerary options, and pay the deposit online. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or by card (check in advance).

You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact number and meeting point. Arrive 15 minutes early. Bring sunscreen, a towel, and a change of clothes. The boat will have a dry bag for your phone and wallet.

For last-minute bookings (within 24 hours), call the charter company directly. The phone number is on the listing. Some operators accept same-day bookings if the boat is available.

Read our blog for tips on what to bring and how to choose the right boat for your group.

Speedboat Rental Estepona vs Other Ports

Estepona is less crowded than Puerto Banús and cheaper than Marbella. The marina is smaller, so you get a more personal service. The water is cleaner because it is further from the Guadalhorce river runoff. The access to the Strait of Gibraltar is faster from Estepona than from Marbella or Benalmádena.

If you want a party atmosphere, choose Puerto Banús. If you want nature and speed, choose Estepona. If you want a longer trip to Gibraltar, Estepona is the best base. For a quick afternoon blast, any port works, but Estepona gives you the most open water in the shortest time.

Check availability for your dates on BoatHire24. The fleet changes seasonally, so book ahead in July and August.

What to Expect on a 2-Hour Speedboat Trip from Estepona

A 2-hour speedboat rental Estepona is the most popular option for a quick fix. You leave the marina, throttle up past the breakwater, and head straight for the dolphin grounds off the coast of Manilva or the Cala del Faro cove. The skipper will keep the ride fast but safe, adjusting speed based on the sea state. You will cover around 10 to 15 nautical miles round trip. Expect to spend 20-30 minutes at anchor for a swim, then blast back. It is enough time to get wet and feel the wind, but not enough for a full beach lunch. Bring a waterproof phone case; the spray can soak everything if the boat is planing.

Speedboat Rental Estepona for Dolphin Watching

The Strait of Gibraltar is one of the best places in Europe to see dolphins year-round. A speedboat rental Estepona puts you in the action fast because the marina is only 8 nautical miles from the main dolphin feeding zones. Common species include common dolphins, striped dolphins, and bottlenose dolphins. You might also see pilot whales or even orcas in late summer. The skipper knows the hotspots and will slow down when the animals are spotted. Do not chase them; the skipper will maintain a respectful distance. The best time for sightings is early morning or late afternoon when the sea is calm. Bring binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens.

Speedboat Rental Estepona for Fishing Trips

If you want to fish, a speedboat rental Estepona can double as a fishing charter. Many RIBs have rod holders and a livewell, and the skipper can take you to the best fishing grounds. Target species include sea bass, bream, mackerel, and even bluefin tuna in season (May to October). Fishing gear is usually not included, but you can rent rods from the marina chandlery for around EUR 20 per day. You will need a fishing licence for Spanish waters, which the skipper can help you arrange (cost around EUR 10-20). The boat will stop at a reef or a drop-off, and you fish for 30-60 minutes. Catch-and-release is common, but you can keep your catch for a beach barbecue. Check the charter's policy on fish cleaning.

Speedboat Rental Estepona for Sunset Cruises

A sunset cruise is a different vibe. You leave around 7 PM in summer, head west toward the Strait, and watch the sun drop behind the Rock of Gibraltar. The speedboat rental Estepona will anchor in a calm bay like Playa del Cristo or the cove at Punta de la Doncella. The skipper will provide a cooler for drinks, and you can bring snacks. The boat will not have a full sound system, but a Bluetooth speaker works. The return trip in the dark is slower, so the skipper will use navigation lights and keep speed under 10 knots. The whole trip lasts about 2.5 hours. Book well in advance for July and August; sunset slots are the first to sell out.

Speedboat Rental Estepona for Family Groups with Children

Speedboat rental Estepona is fine for families, but children under 12 must wear a life jacket at all times. The skipper will provide suitable sizes. The boat has a ladder for easy reboarding after swimming. Choose a RIB with a bimini top for shade; the sun is intense from 11 AM to 4 PM. A 2-hour trip is enough for younger kids; 4 hours is better for teenagers. Avoid full-day trips with small children; they get bored and seasick. Bring snacks, water, and a change of clothes. The skipper will not allow children to sit on the bow while the boat is moving. If your child is prone to motion sickness, give them a travel sickness tablet 30 minutes before departure.

Speedboat Rental Estepona vs Benalmádena

Benalmádena is a major departure port for boat rentals, but Estepona has advantages for speedboat users. Benalmádena is 30 nautical miles east of Estepona, so you lose 30 minutes each way just getting to the dolphin grounds near Gibraltar. Estepona is closer to the open sea and the Strait. The marina in Benalmádena is larger and has more amenities, but it is also busier and more expensive for parking. Estepona marina is quieter, with easier access to the water. If your goal is a fast run to Gibraltar or dolphin watching, Estepona is the better choice. If you want a bigger selection of boats or a party atmosphere, Benalmádena wins. Check both options on BoatHire24 search to compare.

Speedboat Rental Estepona for a Gibraltar Day Trip

A full-day speedboat rental Estepona can include a trip to Gibraltar, but there are rules. You cannot land in Gibraltar without a passport and prior clearance from the Gibraltar Port Authority. The skipper will advise on the procedure. Alternatively, you can cruise along the coast of Gibraltar without landing, viewing the Rock from the water. The round trip from Estepona to Gibraltar is 24 nautical miles, about 30 minutes each way at 30 knots. You will have 3-4 hours to explore the bay, watch the dolphins, and take photos. Do not approach the cargo ships; stay 1 nautical mile away. The skipper will handle the navigation. Bring your passport if you plan to go ashore, but check the charter's policy first.

Speedboat Rental Estepona for a Wedding or Celebration

Speedboat rental Estepona can be part of a wedding celebration, such as a bachelor or bachelorette party, or a post-wedding cruise. The boat can accommodate up to 10 guests, so it is ideal for a small group. You can decorate the boat with banners (ask the skipper first) and bring a cake or champagne. The skipper will not drink, but you can. A 2-hour sunset cruise works well for a celebration. For a larger group, consider a catamaran instead. Book at least two weeks in advance for July and August. The charter company may charge a cleaning fee if you leave the boat messy. Check the terms when booking.

Speedboat Rental Estepona for a Quick Lunch Run to Cabopino

Cabopino marina is 15 nautical miles east of Estepona, a 25-minute run at 35 knots. You can leave Estepona at 11 AM, arrive at Cabopino by 11:30, moor at the visitor pontoon (EUR 15-20 for a 2-hour stay), and walk to a beach chiringuito for lunch. The Chiringuito Cabopino serves grilled fish and paella. After lunch, you have time for a swim at the nearby dunes beach before returning. The total trip is about 4 hours. This route works best on a half-day speedboat rental Estepona. The skipper will handle the mooring and departure. Bring cash for the mooring fee and lunch.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to rent a speedboat in Estepona?
faqs.a: No. Every speedboat rental Estepona through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. You do not need any boating licence or experience. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety.

faqs.q: How many people can fit on a speedboat in Estepona?
faqs.a: Most RIBs and speedboats carry up to 8 passengers. Some larger models take up to 10. The maximum is set by the boat's safety certificate and will be listed on the booking page.

faqs.q: What is the cancellation policy for speedboat rental Estepona?
faqs.a: Most operators offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure. After that, you may lose the deposit. Weather-related cancellations are fully refunded or rescheduled.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and drink on the speedboat?
faqs.a: Yes. You can bring food, soft drinks, and alcohol. The boat usually has a cooler. The skipper cannot drink alcohol while driving, but passengers can.

faqs.q: How fast do the speedboats go in Estepona?
faqs.a: Typical top speeds are between 30 and 50 knots depending on the boat model, engine power, and sea conditions. The skipper will adjust speed for comfort.

faqs.q: Is it safe to take a speedboat in winter in Estepona?
faqs.a: Winter trips are possible on calm days. The skipper will check the forecast. Water temperatures are around 15-18°C, so a wetsuit is recommended for swimming.

faqs.q: Can I go to Gibraltar from Estepona by speedboat?
faqs.a: Yes. It is about 12 nautical miles from Estepona marina to Gibraltar. The trip takes 20-30 minutes. You need a passport to disembark in Gibraltar. The skipper will advise on procedures.

title: Private Boat Hire Marbella: Exclusive Trips
metaDescription: Book private boat hire Marbella with a licensed skipper. Exclusive motor yachts, catamarans, and speedboats from Puerto Banús. Check availability now.
h1: Private Boat Hire Marbella: Exclusive Charters with Skipper
intro:
You want a day on the water that feels like yours alone. No crowds, no queues, no set itineraries. That is what private boat hire Marbella gives you. You pick the boat, the route, the food, the music. A licensed skipper handles the rest. From Puerto Banús to Marbella Marina, you can explore the Costa del Sol in your own floating lounge.

BoatHire24 connects you with boat owners and charter companies across the region. Motor yachts, catamarans, RIBs, fishing boats. All come with a skipper who knows the coast, the anchor spots, and the best places for a swim. You just show up and enjoy.
bodyHtml:
What Private Boat Hire Marbella Actually Means

Private does not mean you drive the boat. Unless you have a licence and want to, but most people prefer to relax. Private means the boat is yours for the duration. No strangers sharing the deck. You decide the pace. Want to stop at Cala del Faro for an hour? Fine. Want to push on to Estepona for lunch? Go for it. The skipper works for you, not the other way around.

Every charter through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That covers insurance, safety briefings, and local knowledge. You do not need a boating licence. You do not need to worry about anchoring in shallow water or reading a chart. The skipper does all that. You get to pretend you are a VIP for the day.

Departure Ports for Private Boat Hire Marbella

You have options. The most famous is Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina with superyachts and designer shops. But you can also leave from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), which is closer to the old town and less flashy. Cabopino is a smaller, quieter port near Artola dunes. Estepona marina is further west, near the charming old town and the Sierra Bermeja mountains. Sotogrande is the upmarket choice for those heading towards Gibraltar. Benalmádena is east, near Málaga, popular for its marina and sea life centre.

Each port gives you different cruising grounds. From Puerto Banús, you can head east to Cala del Faro and Cabopino, or west to Estepona and the Strait of Gibraltar. From Marbella Marina, you are close to the Río Verde and the La Concha mountain backdrop. The choice of port affects the route, but the experience is the same: private, exclusive, and tailored to you.

Types of Boats Available for Private Hire

Motor yachts are the default for private boat hire Marbella. They range from 8 metre day cruisers to 30 metre superyachts. The smaller ones are nimble, fast, and good for a couple or a small family. The larger ones have cabins, saloons, and flybridges for entertaining. Catamarans are popular for groups because they have more deck space and shallower draft. You can get closer to the shore, anchor in coves that monohulls cannot reach.

Sailing yachts are quieter, more traditional. They rely on wind, but they have engines for when the breeze dies. RIBs and speedboats are for the adrenaline crowd. They are fast, open, and can reach spots like Nerja in under an hour from Marbella. Fishing boats come equipped with rods and tackle, and the skipper knows the best spots for sea bass, bream, and dentex. Licence-free day boats are small, simple, and limited to 6 knots. They are for calm days and short trips near the coast.

Superyachts over 24 metres are available on request. They come with crew, tenders, and all the toys. Prices for those start at around EUR 10,000 per day and go up from there. For most people, a 10 to 15 metre motor yacht is the sweet spot. It costs from around EUR 800 to EUR 2,500 for a half day, depending on the season and the boat.

Pricing Guidance for Private Boat Hire Marbella

There is no single price. It depends on the boat size, age, amenities, season, and duration. For a half day (4 hours) on a 10 metre motor yacht in low season (November to March), expect from around EUR 600. In high season (June to September), the same boat might be EUR 1,200. Full day (8 hours) is usually 1.5 to 2 times the half day rate. Catamarans are typically 20-30% more than motor yachts of similar length.

Fuel is extra. For a 10 metre motor yacht cruising at 20 knots, you might burn 80-120 litres per hour. At current fuel prices, that is around EUR 1.50 to EUR 2.00 per litre. A full day could add EUR 300 to EUR 600 to the bill. Skipper fee is included in the charter price, but a tip of 10-15% is customary. Food and drinks are usually not included, but you can bring your own or ask the charter company to arrange catering. Some boats have a minimum spend for catering of around EUR 20 per person.

Superyacht charters are price on request. A 30 metre motor yacht with crew can cost EUR 15,000 to EUR 30,000 per day in high season. That includes fuel, food, and all drinks. It is a different league, but if you have the budget, it is worth it.

Best Seasons for Private Boat Hire Marbella

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate. Summers are hot, dry, and sunny. Water temperature in August reaches 24-26 degrees C. That is peak season. Everything is available, but prices are highest and availability is tight. Book at least a month in advance for popular boats. Spring (April to June) and autumn (September to October) are better. Water is cooler (18-22 degrees C), but air temperature is pleasant. You get fewer crowds, lower prices, and calmer seas.

Winter (November to March) is quiet. Many boats are in maintenance. Some charter companies still operate, but the sea can be rough. You might get days with 20 knot winds and 2 metre swell. It is doable, but not ideal for swimming. If you want a winter charter, stick to motor yachts with a flybridge enclosure. The views of La Concha mountain with snow on top are spectacular.

Popular Routes for Private Boat Hire Marbella

From Puerto Banús, a classic route goes west to Estepona. You pass the luxury villas of Guadalmina, the beach at El Saladillo, and the cliffs of Cala del Faro. Estepona old town is worth a stop for a walk and lunch. The marina there is smaller but has good restaurants. Another route goes east to Cabopino and the Artola dunes. Cabopino has a nudist beach if you are that way inclined. Further east is Calahonda, then Fuengirola, then Benalmádena. The whole coast is dotted with coves and beach clubs.

For wildlife, head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. From Sotogrande or Estepona, you can reach the strait in an hour. Dolphins are common. You might see pilot whales, orcas, and even fin whales. The strait is a migration route for many species. The water is colder there, and the currents are strong. Only experienced skippers take that route. It is worth it for the wildlife.

For a longer trip, you can go all the way to Nerja. It takes 2 to 3 hours from Marbella by motor yacht. The Nerja caves are a tourist attraction, but from the sea you see the cliffs and the Balcón de Europa. You can anchor near the Burriana beach and take a tender ashore. It is a full day trip, but you cover a lot of coast.

How to Book Private Boat Hire Marbella

Use the search page on BoatHire24. Enter your dates, group size, and preferred port. You get a list of available boats with prices, photos, and specifications. Each listing shows the boat capacity, length, engine type, and amenities. You can filter by boat type, price range, and amenities like WiFi or sound system. Once you find a boat, you can send a booking request. The owner or charter company confirms availability and sends a payment link.

Payment is usually by bank transfer or credit card. A deposit of 50% is common, with the balance due 2 weeks before the charter. Some companies take full payment at booking. Cancellation policies vary. Most offer a full refund if you cancel 30 days before. After that, you might lose the deposit. Read the terms before you book.

For last minute bookings (within 48 hours), call or WhatsApp the charter company directly. BoatHire24 lists contact numbers on each boat page. Some companies can accommodate same day bookings if the boat is available. Expect to pay a premium for last minute.

Who Private Boat Hire Marbella Is For

It is for couples who want a romantic day away from the crowds. It is for families who want to keep the kids entertained without a schedule. It is for groups of friends celebrating a birthday, a stag or hen do, or just a weekend. It is for business clients who want to impress. It is for photographers who want the best angles of the coast. It is for anyone who values privacy and flexibility over price.

It is not for people who want to drive the boat themselves without a licence. It is not for people who expect a party boat with loud music and unlimited alcohol. Some charter companies offer that, but most private charters are about relaxation, not raving. If you want a party, book a specific party boat. If you want a quiet day on the water, private boat hire Marbella is exactly what you need.

For more tips on choosing the right boat and planning your trip, check the BoatHire24 blog. It covers everything from what to bring to how to spot dolphins.

What to Expect Onboard: Amenities and Comfort

Most boats for private boat hire Marbella come with a basic set of amenities. You get a sunpad area on the bow or flybridge, a small galley with a fridge and sink, and a cabin with a toilet (heads). Some have a shower on the swim platform, which is useful after swimming in the sea. Larger motor yachts have a saloon with air conditioning, a sound system, and sometimes a TV. Catamarans often have a trampoline net at the front for lounging. RIBs and speedboats are more basic: just seats and a small storage compartment for bags.

If you want extras like a barbecue, a paddleboard, or snorkelling gear, ask when booking. Some charter companies include them for free, others charge extra. A typical half day charter includes bottled water and ice. You bring your own food and drinks, or arrange catering. The skipper usually has a cooler on board. There is no Wi-Fi on most small boats, so disconnect and enjoy the view of La Concha mountain.

Safety and Insurance: What Is Covered

Every private boat hire Marbella through BoatHire24 includes insurance. The skipper holds a valid licence and the boat has third party liability insurance. That covers damage to other boats or property. Personal accident insurance for passengers is usually not included. Check your travel insurance or consider adding it. The skipper does a safety briefing at the start: where the life jackets are, how to use the radio, and what to do in an emergency. You are required by law to wear a life jacket if you go on the foredeck while the boat is moving. The skipper will enforce that.

The boat has a first aid kit, fire extinguisher, and flares. For longer trips, there is an EPIRB (emergency beacon) and a life raft. The skipper knows the local VHF channels and can call for help if needed. The Costa del Sol has a busy coastguard service. Response times are quick, especially near Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina.

Food and Drink Options for Your Charter

You can bring your own food and drinks. Most boats have a fridge and a small galley. You can prepare simple meals like sandwiches or salads. If you want something more elaborate, many charter companies offer catering. Typical options include a Spanish tapas platter (jamón, cheese, olives, bread) for around EUR 15-20 per person, or a barbecue on the beach (the skipper anchors and grills chicken, fish, and vegetables) for EUR 25-35 per person. Some boats have a minimum spend of EUR 200 for catering, so check before you book.

Drinks are usually BYO. You can bring wine, beer, or spirits. The skipper will provide glasses and ice. Some boats have a fridge for white wine and beer. If you want champagne or cocktails, bring them. There are no restrictions on alcohol, but the skipper will not serve anyone who is clearly intoxicated. It is a safety thing, not a killjoy thing.

What to Wear and Bring for a Private Boat Trip

Wear swimwear and a cover-up. Bring a towel, sunscreen (factor 50, the sun is strong), sunglasses, and a hat. The wind on the water makes the sun feel less intense, but you still burn. Bring a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon when the sea breeze picks up. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The skipper can provide ginger biscuits or acupressure bands, but medication is more reliable.

For shoes, wear non-marking deck shoes or go barefoot. Heels and black soles damage the deck. Some boats have a strict no-shoes policy. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and wallet. There is no safe on most small boats. Leave valuables at the hotel. The skipper will lock the cabin if you go swimming, but it is not a bank vault.

Environmental Considerations and Responsible Boating

The Costa del Sol has sensitive marine habitats. Seagrass meadows near Cabopino and the Artola dunes are protected. Anchoring in those areas is prohibited. The skipper knows the no-anchor zones. Do not throw rubbish overboard. The boat has a bin for waste. If you see plastic in the water, tell the skipper. Some charter companies participate in clean-up initiatives and will collect rubbish if safe.

Dolphin watching is popular, but there are rules. Boats must keep a distance of at least 60 metres from dolphins and whales. You cannot chase them or cut across their path. The skipper will slow down and let the dolphins approach if they want. Do not touch or feed them. It is illegal and stresses the animals. The Strait of Gibraltar is a protected area for cetaceans. Respect it.

Booking Tips for a Smooth Experience

Book early for peak season. June to September is busy. Popular boats for private boat hire Marbella are often booked weeks in advance. If you have a specific date, book at least a month ahead. For spring and autumn, two weeks is usually enough. Winter charters are easier to book last minute, but availability is limited.

Read the cancellation policy carefully. Some companies offer free cancellation up to 14 days before, others are stricter. If the weather is bad, the skipper may cancel for safety. In that case, you get a full refund or a reschedule. Bad weather is rare in summer, but possible. The skipper makes the call, not you. Trust their judgement.

Local Knowledge: Hidden Gems Along the Coast

The skipper knows the best spots. Ask them to take you to Cala del Faro, a small cove near Estepona with clear water and cliffs. It is less crowded than the main beaches. Another spot is the Río Verde estuary near Marbella. It is a nature reserve with birdlife. You can anchor and kayak up the river if the boat has a tender. The dunes of Artola near Cabopino are worth a stop. The beach there is natural, with no sunbeds or restaurants. Just sand, dunes, and the sea.

For lunch, the skipper can recommend beach clubs like La Sala by the Sea in Puerto Banús or Tibu in Estepona. Some have mooring buoys for guests. You can tie up and go ashore. Others require anchoring and taking a tender. The skipper handles the logistics. You just enjoy the paella and the sangria.

BoatHire24 lists boats from multiple charter companies. You get a wide choice of types, sizes, and price points. The search page lets you compare boats side by side. Each listing has detailed specs, photos, and real availability. You book directly with the owner or charter company. No middleman fees. The blog has guides on everything from the best time to visit to what fish you might catch. It is written by locals who know the coast. Use it to plan your trip. If you have questions, contact the charter company through the listing. They respond quickly. Private boat hire Marbella is easy when you use the right platform.

title: Catamaran Charter Estepona: Relaxed Sailing
metaDescription: Book a catamaran charter Estepona for a relaxed day on the Costa del Sol. Compare prices, ports & boats. Instant online booking with a licensed skipper.
h1: Catamaran Charter Estepona: Relaxed Sailing on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You want a day on the water that doesn't involve shouting over a roaring engine or clinging to a rail. A catamaran charter in Estepona gives you space to stretch out, a stable platform that doesn't roll like a washing machine, and enough shade to keep the Spanish sun off your neck. It's the sensible choice for groups, families, or anyone who wants to arrive at the beach bar without feeling like they've been through a spin cycle.

Estepona's marina is one of the quieter departure points on the Costa del Sol, which means less queueing and more time actually sailing. You can head west towards the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin-spotting, or east along the coast past Puerto Banús and Marbella. Every charter includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, so you don't need a licence or any sailing experience. Just turn up, step aboard, and let someone else do the work.

On BoatHire24 you can compare catamarans based on size, price, and departure port. Prices start from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day on a 38-foot Lagoon, up to EUR 3,500 for a full day on a 50-foot Bali. All boats are listed with real availability and real prices, not just a contact form and a promise to call you back.
bodyHtml:
Why Estepona Works for a Catamaran Charter

Estepona's marina, Puerto Deportivo de Estepona, sits at the western end of the Costa del Sol, closer to the Strait of Gibraltar than the main Marbella strip. That means you get shorter cruising times to the open sea and less traffic from the big charter fleets operating out of Puerto Banús. The water here is typically calmer than further east, especially in the morning, which suits the catamaran's shallow draft and twin-hull stability.

The old town of Estepona is a few minutes' walk from the marina, so you can grab provisions or a pre-charter breakfast without a taxi ride. If you're staying in Marbella or Benalmádena, it's a 30-40 minute drive along the A-7, but the quieter departure is worth the short trip. For groups based in Sotogrande, Estepona is even closer, about 15 minutes by car.

One practical advantage: Estepona's marina has plenty of parking and a fuel dock that's rarely busy. You won't spend your first hour waiting for the tank to fill.

What's Included in a Catamaran Charter Estepona

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who speaks English and Spanish. They handle the navigation, docking, and safety briefing. You don't need a licence, and you don't need to know how to tie a cleat hitch. The skipper can also act as a guide, pointing out landmarks like the Rock of Gibraltar on a clear day or the best spots to anchor for a swim.

Standard inclusions on most catamarans: a full tank of fuel (or a set allowance, typically 60-80 litres per half-day), paddleboards or a SUP, snorkelling gear, a Bluetooth speaker, and a cooler with ice. Some boats add a dinghy with an outboard for exploring shallow coves. Food and drink are not included unless you book a catering package, which most operators offer for around EUR 25-45 per person for a buffet lunch with drinks.

Check the listing details for any extras. Some catamarans charge extra for the use of the generator or air conditioning while anchored, though most include it in the base price. If you want to add a water slide or a banana boat tow, ask at the time of booking.

Available Ports for Catamaran Charters

While this page focuses on Estepona, you can also charter a catamaran from other ports on the Costa del Sol. Each has its own character and cruising range.

Puerto Banús is the busiest and most glamorous, with superyacht neighbours and a short run to the Marbella coastline. Catamarans here tend to be larger and more expensive, from around EUR 1,800 for a half-day. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and closer to the town centre, with a good mix of modern catamarans. Cabopino, east of Marbella, is a small, charming port with direct access to the Cabopino sand dunes and the Cala del Faro. Benalmádena, further east, is popular for day trips to the Nerja caves, though it's a longer cruise. Sotogrande, west of Estepona, is the closest to Gibraltar and offers some of the best dolphin-watching on the coast.

For a full list of options, see our catamaran search page where you can filter by port, boat size, and price.

Boat Options: Catamarans Available in Estepona

The catamarans available for charter in Estepona range from 36 to 52 feet, with 4 to 8 guest cabins and capacity for up to 12 passengers (the legal limit for charter without a special licence). Most are from builders like Lagoon, Bali, Fountaine Pajot, and Nautitech.

A 38-foot Lagoon 380 is a common choice for small groups of 4-6. It has a shallow draft of around 1.2 metres, so you can anchor close to the beach in places like the Río Verde estuary. The deck layout is simple: a large trampoline at the bow, a cockpit table aft, and a flybridge with a bimini for shade. Expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day (4 hours) and EUR 1,800 for a full day (8 hours).

For larger groups, a 46-foot Bali 4.6 offers more space and a hard-top flybridge with a wet bar. It sleeps 8 in four cabins with en-suite heads. Full-day rates start around EUR 2,500. At the top end, a 52-foot Lagoon 52 has six cabins and a crew of two (skipper plus hostess). Prices for that are from EUR 3,500 per day, or around EUR 4,500 with a full catering package.

All boats are maintained to Spanish maritime safety standards and undergo regular inspections. The skippers are all licensed by the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Charter Estepona

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. As a rough guide:

  • Half-day (4 hours) on a 36-40 foot catamaran: EUR 1,100-1,500
  • Full day (8 hours) on a 36-40 foot catamaran: EUR 1,600-2,200
  • Half-day on a 44-50 foot catamaran: EUR 1,800-2,500
  • Full day on a 44-50 foot catamaran: EUR 2,500-3,500
  • Full day with catering on a 50+ foot catamaran: EUR 3,500-5,000

These are typical rates for the high season (June to September). Shoulder months (April, May, October) are 15-25% cheaper. November to March is the low season, with discounts of up to 40%, though the weather is cooler (16-20 degrees C) and the sea can be choppier.

Most operators charge a 50% deposit at booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure. Cancellation policies vary: free cancellation up to 14 days before, then 50% refund up to 7 days, then no refund. Read the terms on the listing before you pay.

Best Seasons for Catamaran Charter Estepona

The best time for a catamaran charter in Estepona is May to October. Sea temperatures are above 20 degrees C from June, and the wind is generally moderate, 10-15 knots from the west or south-west. July and August are the hottest, with temperatures reaching 32 degrees C, but the catamaran's shade and breeze make it comfortable.

September is a sweet spot: the water is still warm from summer, the crowds thin out, and the prices drop slightly. October can be pleasant, but the wind picks up and there's a higher chance of a day being cancelled due to weather. The Strait of Gibraltar can generate a strong easterly wind (the Levante) that makes the sea rough, especially west of Estepona. Skippers will advise on the day whether it's safe to go out.

Winter charters are possible, but you'll need to book a boat with a hard top or full enclosure. The sun is lower, so you won't get the same tanning experience. But if you want a quiet day on the water with a jacket and a hot drink, it's a cheaper alternative.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter in Estepona

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, set the port to Estepona, select your date and group size, and browse the available catamarans. Each listing shows the boat's specifications, photos, a map of the departure point, and the total price including taxes and skipper fees. No hidden extras.

Once you find a boat you like, click 'Book Now' and pay the deposit by credit card or bank transfer. You'll get a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and instructions for the day. If you need to change the date or cancel, you can do so from your account dashboard.

For groups larger than 12, you can charter two catamarans and sail together. Contact us through the site for a custom quote.

Who Is a Catamaran Charter Estepona For

Catamarans are ideal for families with children because they don't heel (tilt) like a monohull sailing boat. The wide decks and netted trampolines are safe for kids to play on, and the shallow draft means you can anchor close to the beach for easy swimming. Groups of friends who want a party boat also like catamarans because the large cockpit and flybridge can hold a crowd without feeling cramped.

If you're a couple looking for a romantic day out, a smaller catamaran with a private cabin works well. The skipper can drop you off at a quiet cove like Cala del Faro for a few hours and return later. For corporate events or client entertainment, a larger catamaran with a hostess and catering package gives a professional impression without the formality of a superyacht.

One group that might not suit a catamaran: serious sailors who want to handle the sails themselves. The skippers on these charters are in charge, and you won't be allowed to take the helm without a licence. If you want a hands-on sailing experience, look for a 'skippered charter' on a monohull where the skipper is happy to teach.

Local Highlights: What to See on Your Charter

From Estepona, you can cruise east towards the Marbella coastline and Puerto Banús. The sea front is lined with pine trees and low-rise hotels, and you'll pass the Río Verde estuary, a good spot for birdwatching. Further east, the Cala del Faro is a small cove with a lighthouse and a beach bar that's only accessible by boat. It's a popular lunch stop.

Heading west, you'll reach the Strait of Gibraltar within 30-40 minutes at cruising speed. This is where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean, and the nutrient-rich currents attract pods of common dolphins, striped dolphins, and occasionally pilot whales. The skipper will know the best areas for spotting them. You can also see the Rock of Gibraltar on a clear day, and on very clear days, the coast of North Africa.

If you have a full day, you can go further west to Sotogrande and anchor off the coast for a swim, or east to the Nerja caves, though that's a 2-hour cruise each way. Most groups prefer to stay within an hour of Estepona and spend the time swimming, eating, and relaxing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Read our blog for more detailed guides on chartering in the Costa del Sol, including tips on what to pack and how to choose the right boat.

Why Estepona's Marina Beats the Competition for Catamaran Charters

Puerto Deportivo de Estepona has 421 berths and a draft of 4 metres, which is enough for catamarans up to 60 feet. Unlike Puerto Banús, where you're paying for the glitz and the parking costs EUR 30 a day, Estepona's marina charges EUR 10 for a full day of parking and the berth fees are included in your charter price. The marina has a direct fuel dock with diesel and petrol, so you won't waste time waiting for a fuel boat. The chandlery on site stocks basic spares and provisions, and there's a supermarket 200 metres from the gate. For a catamaran charter Estepona, you can be on the water within 15 minutes of arriving at the marina, compared to 30-45 minutes in Banús during peak season.

Best Itineraries for a Catamaran Charter Estepona: Two Specific Routes

Route one, the western run to the Strait of Gibraltar. Leave Estepona at 10:00, head west at 15 knots. You'll pass the Punta de la Doncella lighthouse and the Playa de la Rada. After 20 minutes, you enter the waters of the Strait, where the depth drops to 200 metres and the current can reach 3 knots. The skipper will slow down if dolphins are spotted. Anchor for lunch at the Cala de la Chullera, a sheltered cove with a sandy bottom. Depth here is 3-5 metres, so the catamaran's draft of 1.2 metres lets you anchor 50 metres from the beach. Total distance: 12 nautical miles. Return by 16:00. Fuel consumption on a 40-foot catamaran: about 60 litres for the round trip.

Route two, the eastern run to Marbella. Leave Estepona at 10:00, head east at 12 knots. Pass the Río Guadalmina and the Marbella Club Hotel. Stop at the Cala del Faro for a swim and lunch at the chiringuito. Continue to Puerto Banús for a slow pass of the superyachts, then turn back. Total distance: 18 nautical miles. Fuel: about 80 litres. This route is better for groups who want a mix of nature and glamour. Both routes are doable in a half-day charter, but a full day gives you time for a longer lunch and a second swim stop.

What to Pack for a Catamaran Charter Estepona: Practical Advice

The sun on the Costa del Sol is intense even in April. Bring SPF 50 sunscreen, a hat with a strap, and polarised sunglasses. The glare off the water can cause headaches after an hour. A light fleece or windbreaker is useful even in summer, because the wind at 20 knots feels cool when you're wet. Water shoes with a hard sole protect your feet on the marina's concrete and on rocky beaches. If you're prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The catamaran's stability reduces the risk, but the Strait can have a gentle swell that affects some people. Leave your high heels and white trousers at home. The decks are non-slip fibreglass, but they get hot in direct sun and you'll be barefoot or in deck shoes.

Catering Options for Your Catamaran Charter Estepona

Most operators offer three catering tiers. Basic: a cold buffet of Spanish ham, cheese, bread, olives, and fruit, with soft drinks and water, for around EUR 25 per person. Premium: hot paella or grilled fish, plus a bottle of white wine or cava per two people, for EUR 40 per person. Luxury: a full menu with seafood platters, steak, and champagne, served by a hostess, for EUR 60-80 per person. Some operators allow you to bring your own food and drink, but they charge a corkage fee of EUR 10-20 per bottle of alcohol. Check the listing for the policy. If you have dietary restrictions, let the operator know at least 48 hours before departure. They can usually accommodate vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free requests without extra cost.

Booking a Catamaran Charter Estepona for Special Occasions

For a birthday, anniversary, or proposal, most operators can arrange decorations, a cake, and a photographer. The cost is typically EUR 100-200 extra, depending on the complexity. For a wedding party, you can charter two catamarans and have them raft together for a ceremony on the water. The legal limit for a single catamaran is 12 passengers, so for a group of 20, you'd need two boats. The skippers can coordinate the departure and anchor together. Contact us on BoatHire24 for a custom quote for multi-boat charters. For corporate events, the hostess can set up a presentation screen on the flybridge, and the skipper can provide a Wi-Fi hotspot for EUR 50 extra. The catamaran's stability means laptops and documents stay put, unlike on a monohull.

bodyHtml:
What’s Included in a Yacht Rental Fuengirola Charter

Every charter on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper as standard. That means you don’t need a boating licence, and you don’t have to worry about navigating, anchoring, or dealing with Spanish maritime regulations. The skipper handles everything. Most charters also include fuel for a standard cruising range (usually up to 30 nautical miles), basic insurance, and the use of onboard amenities like a sound system, fridge, and sometimes a small galley. You’ll need to bring your own food and drinks unless you upgrade to a catering package, which many companies offer at an extra cost of around EUR 30 to EUR 60 per person for a tapas lunch or a paella spread.

What’s not included: dockage fees if you want to stop at a different marina for lunch (usually EUR 50 to EUR 100 for a few hours), water toys like jet skis or paddleboards (rentable on request), and any damage deposit, though most companies waive that for standard charters. The skipper’s tip is optional but customary at around 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee. Check the listing details on BoatHire24 for each boat’s specific inclusions.

Departure Ports for Your Fuengirola Yacht Charter

Fuengirola Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Fuengirola) has a few small charter boats, but the real fleet is in Puerto Banús, 8 kilometres west. Banús is the superyacht capital of the Costa del Sol, with over 900 berths and a concentration of luxury motor yachts between 12 and 50 metres. The trip from Banús to Fuengirola’s main beach takes about 20 minutes at 20 knots. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is another option, 12 kilometres west, with a mix of catamarans and sailing yachts. From there, it’s 25 minutes to Fuengirola. Cabopino, 5 kilometres east of Fuengirola, is smaller but quieter, with a few fishing boats and smaller motor yachts. Estepona and Sotogrande are further west (30 and 50 kilometres respectively), but you can still charter from there if you want a longer day trip that includes Fuengirola as a stop.

Your best bet for a Fuengirola yacht rental is to search by departure port on BoatHire24. Set the filter to Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina for the widest selection. You’ll find boats from 8-metre RIBs for a fast coastal run to 30-metre superyachts for a full-day party cruise.

Boat Types Available for Yacht Rental in Fuengirola

Motor yachts dominate the market because they’re fast, comfortable, and easy to handle. Expect Azimut, Sunseeker, and Princess models between 10 and 20 metres, with flybridges, sun pads, and cabins. Half-day charter (4 hours) from around EUR 500 to EUR 1,500, full day (8 hours) from EUR 900 to EUR 3,000. Catamarans are popular for groups of 8 to 12 people because they have more deck space and stability. A Lagoon 40 or Bali 4.1 costs from EUR 700 for a half day. Sailing yachts are slower but quieter, good for a relaxed cruise with the wind. A Bavaria 46 or Dufour 45 starts at around EUR 600 for a half day. RIBs and speedboats are the cheapest option for a quick blast to Cabopino or Benalmádena, from EUR 300 for 2 hours. Licence-free day boats (typically small motorboats under 15 hp) are not common in Fuengirola but you can find a few in Cabopino for EUR 200 for half a day.

Superyachts over 24 metres are available for VIP experiences, with prices on request but expect EUR 5,000 to EUR 15,000 per day. Fishing boats with tackle and a skipper who knows the spots for bream and sea bass are also listed, from EUR 400 for a half day.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Rental Fuengirola

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. Low season (November to March) is the cheapest: a 10-metre motor yacht for a half day might cost EUR 400 to EUR 600. Mid season (April, May, October) adds about 20 percent. High season (June to September) is peak, with prices 40 to 60 percent higher. For a 15-metre motor yacht in August, expect EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,500 for a full day. Catamarans in high season start at EUR 1,000 for a half day. Last-minute bookings (within 48 hours) can sometimes get a 10 to 15 percent discount if the boat is still available.

All prices on BoatHire24 are shown in EUR and include the skipper. Fuel is included for up to 30 NM cruising; extra fuel for longer trips (e.g., to Marbella and back) may cost EUR 100 to EUR 300. Dockage fees at Fuengirola Marina for a lunch stop are around EUR 60 for a 12-metre boat. You can pay by credit card or bank transfer, and a 30 percent deposit is usually required at booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure.

Best Seasons for Yacht Rental Fuengirola

Fuengirola has a Mediterranean climate with over 320 sunny days a year. The best months for a yacht charter are May through October, when temperatures range from 22 to 32 degrees C and the sea is calm. July and August are the hottest and busiest, with water temperatures reaching 26 degrees C, but also the most expensive. April and November are cooler (18 to 22 degrees C) but still pleasant for cruising, and you’ll have fewer crowds. December to February can be windy and choppy, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar, but calm days do occur. If you want to save money, book in May or September, the weather is still good, and prices are lower.

Wind patterns: the Poniente (west wind) brings clear skies and moderate seas, while the Levante (east wind) can kick up waves of 1 to 2 metres, especially in the afternoon. Skippers know the local conditions and will adjust the route accordingly, often staying close to the coast for shelter.

How to Book a Yacht Rental in Fuengirola with BoatHire24

Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter your dates, group size, and preferred port. Use the filters to select boat type, length, and budget. Each listing shows photos, a detailed description, and the charter company’s contact details. Click “Request Booking” to send an enquiry; the company will confirm availability and send a payment link. You can also call the company directly using the phone number on the listing. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for high season, 1 week for low season. Cancellation policies vary: most companies offer a full refund if cancelled 14 days before, 50 percent if 7 days before, and no refund within 48 hours.

After booking, you’ll receive a confirmation email with the skipper’s name, meeting point, and what to bring. On the day, arrive 15 minutes early at the marina. The skipper will give a safety briefing and then you’re off. If you have special requests (e.g., a specific route, catering, or water toys), mention them at booking.

Who Is Yacht Rental Fuengirola For

This is for anyone who wants a private boat experience without owning a boat or having a licence. It’s perfect for couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise, families with kids who want to swim in quiet coves, and groups of friends celebrating a birthday or stag/hen do. Business clients often book a superyacht for corporate events or client entertainment. Solo travellers can join a shared charter on a catamaran, which some companies offer for around EUR 100 per person for a half day. The common thread is that you want luxury, convenience, and a skipper who knows the coast.

If you’re on a tight budget, consider a RIB or a day boat from Cabopino. If you want to impress, go for a 20-metre motor yacht with a flybridge. Either way, BoatHire24 has the options.

Local Highlights for Your Yacht Charter Itinerary

A typical route from Fuengirola heads west to Puerto Banús, passing the beaches of Los Boliches and Carvajal. Stop for lunch at a chiringuito on the beach in Banús or anchor off the dunes of Cabopino. If you head east, you can cruise to Benalmádena’s marina and see the Puerto Marina complex from the water. For a longer trip, go to Marbella’s Golden Mile and anchor near the Marbella Club Hotel. The Strait of Gibraltar, about 60 NM south, is a full-day trip but offers dolphin and whale sightings (common in summer). The Nerja Caves are 80 NM east, but that’s a 2-day charter with an overnight stop.

Fuengirola itself has a castle (Sohail Castle) on a hill overlooking the beach, and the old town is worth a walk after your charter. But the real magic is on the water, with the Sierra Blanca mountains as a backdrop.

Frequently Asked Questions About Yacht Rental Fuengirola

Check the BoatHire24 blog for more tips on Costa del Sol yacht charters, or use the search page to find available boats right now.

Why Fuengirola Is a Strong Base for a Yacht Charter

Fuengirola sits right in the middle of the Costa del Sol, which makes it a practical launch point for exploring both the western and eastern stretches of the coast. The town’s own marina, Puerto Deportivo de Fuengirola, is small but functional, with a few charter boats and a handful of restaurants. However, the real draw is the proximity to Puerto Banús and Marbella, both within a 20-minute cruise. That means you can stay in Fuengirola, book a yacht from a nearby port, and still have a full day on the water without spending hours commuting. The train from Fuengirola to Marbella takes 15 minutes, and taxis cost around EUR 25. You can also walk from Fuengirola’s main beach to the marina in 10 minutes.

The coastline between Fuengirola and Marbella is a mix of sandy beaches and rocky coves. Cala del Faro, just west of Fuengirola, is a quiet spot with clear water and a small lighthouse. It’s a popular anchoring point for lunch or a swim. Further west, the dunes of Cabopino offer a protected bay with a nudist beach and a chiringuito that serves grilled fish. These are the kind of stops that make a half-day charter worthwhile, and they’re all within 5 NM of Fuengirola.

Practical Tips for a Smooth Yacht Rental Experience

Book early in the week if you can. Saturdays are the busiest day for charters in Fuengirola, and skippers often have back-to-back bookings. A Monday or Tuesday charter means more availability and potentially a discount. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and wallet, as spray can come over the bow even on calm days. Sunscreen is essential, even in April, because the reflection off the water doubles the UV exposure. Most boats have a bimini or a hardtop for shade, but the flybridge on motor yachts is usually uncovered.

If you’re prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The Mediterranean is generally calm in summer, but the Levante wind can create a short chop that some people find uncomfortable. Skippers often have ginger biscuits or seasickness bands on board, but don’t rely on it. Also, ask the skipper about the route before you leave. A good skipper will suggest a plan based on the wind and your preferences, but if you want to go to a specific spot like the Strait of Gibraltar or Nerja, confirm it in advance because those trips require extra fuel and time.

Specific Boat Examples You Might Find on BoatHire24

On any given day, you might find a Sunseeker Manhattan 50 (15 metres) based in Puerto Banús, available for EUR 1,800 for a full day in June. That boat has a flybridge, a forward sun pad, and a cabin with a double bed, ideal for a couple or a small family. A Lagoon 42 catamaran (13 metres) from Marbella Marina might cost EUR 1,200 for a half day, with space for 12 guests on the deck and a trampoline net at the bow. For a smaller group, a RIB with a 250 HP outboard (8 metres) from Cabopino can be yours for EUR 350 for 2 hours, fast enough to reach Marbella in 15 minutes. Fishing boats like a 7-metre Quicksilver with a 115 HP engine are listed from EUR 400 for a half day, including bait and tackle.

Superyacht options include a 30-metre Azimut Grande from Puerto Banús, with a crew of 4 and a price on request, but expect EUR 8,000 to EUR 12,000 per day. These boats are typically booked for corporate events or VIP groups. For a licence-free day boat, you’ll need to go to Cabopino or Benalmádena, where small motorboats under 15 hp are available from EUR 200 for half a day. No licence is needed, but you must be over 18 and sign a waiver.

Extended Itinerary Ideas for a Full-Day Charter

If you have a full day (8 to 10 hours), you can do a loop from Fuengirola west to Marbella, then south to Cala del Faro, and back via Cabopino. That’s about 25 NM total, with stops for swimming, lunch, and photos. A more ambitious route heads east to Benalmádena (8 NM) and then to Torremolinos (12 NM), where you can see the Tivoli World amusement park from the water. For a longer trip, go west to Estepona (30 NM), which takes about 1.5 hours at 20 knots. Estepona’s old town is a 5-minute walk from the marina, with whitewashed streets and orange trees. You can anchor off the beach for lunch at a chiringuito and then cruise back, making it a full-day adventure.

For wildlife enthusiasts, the Strait of Gibraltar is a 60 NM trip from Fuengirola, which takes 3 hours each way. That’s a 2-day charter with an overnight stop in Tarifa or Algeciras. In summer, you’re almost guaranteed to see dolphins, pilot whales, and sometimes fin whales. The Strait is also a migration route for birds, so you might see storks and eagles. Book a dedicated wildlife-watching charter from Sotogrande or Estepona instead, which are closer to the Strait.

Cost Breakdown for a Typical Day on the Water

Assume you hire a 12-metre motor yacht for a full day in July. The charter fee is EUR 1,500. Fuel is included for 30 NM, but if you go to Marbella and back (20 NM), you’re fine. If you add a detour to Estepona, you might pay EUR 100 extra for fuel. Dockage at a marina for lunch is EUR 60. Catering for 6 people at EUR 40 each is EUR 240. The skipper’s tip at 10 percent is EUR 150. Total for the day: EUR 2,050. That’s EUR 342 per person for a group of 6, which is comparable to a nice restaurant dinner with drinks. For a half day, the cost drops to around EUR 1,200 total, or EUR 200 per person.

Cheaper options exist. A RIB for 2 hours costs EUR 300 total, or EUR 75 per person for a group of 4. A catamaran half day for 8 people at EUR 700 works out to EUR 88 per person. The key is to split the cost among your group. BoatHire24 shows the maximum number of guests per boat, so you can calculate the per-person cost before booking.

What to Do in Fuengirola After Your Charter

Fuengirola has a 7-kilometre beachfront promenade lined with restaurants, bars, and shops. After your yacht charter, you can walk to the Sohail Castle for sunset views, or visit the Bioparc zoo, which is a 10-minute taxi ride away. The old town has a market on Tuesdays and Saturdays, selling local crafts and food. For dinner, try a chiringuito on the beach like Los Marinos or La Cubana, which serve grilled sardines and paella. If you want a more upscale meal, head to Puerto Banús for restaurants like La Sala or Nobu, but expect to pay EUR 50 to EUR 100 per person.

Fuengirola is also well connected by train and bus. You can take the C1 line from Fuengirola to Málaga in 40 minutes, or to Marbella by bus in 30 minutes. That makes it easy to combine a yacht charter with a day trip to Málaga’s museums or Marbella’s Golden Mile. Check the BoatHire24 blog for more ideas on how to plan your Costa del Sol itinerary.
