All prices include skipper, fuel, lunch, water, and soft drinks. Extras like jet ski, photographer, or premium catering are additional. You pay a 50% deposit at booking and the balance 7 days before departure. Cancellations up to 14 days before are fully refundable, minus a 5% processing fee.

For a full breakdown of costs and what's included, read the BoatHire24 blog guide on charter pricing.

Best Season for a Motor Yacht Charter in Estepona

The best months for a motor yacht charter Estepona day are May through October. Sea temperatures range from 18°C in May to 26°C in August. Air temperatures hover around 25°C to 32°C, with light winds from the east (levante) or west (poniente). July and August are the busiest, so book at least 2 to 3 weeks in advance.

Spring (April to May) and autumn (September to October) offer quieter conditions, fewer boats on the water, and lower prices by about 15 to 20 percent. The water is cooler in April (around 16°C), but the sun is still warm. If you want to avoid crowds and don't mind a wetsuit for swimming, these shoulder months are a good choice.

Winter charters are possible but less common. The sea can be choppy, and the wind is stronger. Most motor yachts remain in the water, but the skipper may limit the route to sheltered areas. Prices drop by 30 to 40 percent from November to March.

How to Book a Motor Yacht Charter Estepona Day

Booking a motor yacht charter Estepona day on BoatHire24 takes about five minutes. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage, select Estepona as the departure port, choose the date, and filter by boat type (motor yacht). You will see a list of available yachts with photos, specifications, and the total price.

Click on a listing to see the full itinerary, included amenities, and any optional extras. You can send a direct message to the owner to ask about specific requirements, such as dietary restrictions or a custom route. Once you confirm, you pay a 50% deposit via credit card or bank transfer. The owner sends a confirmation email with the meeting point and the skipper's contact details.

On the day, arrive at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The skipper will greet you at the pontoon, show you the safety equipment, and answer any last-minute questions. Then you cast off and enjoy the cruise.

Who Is This Charter For

A motor yacht charter Estepona day works for couples, families with older children, or groups of friends. It is not ideal for toddlers or infants because the deck has no railings and the boat moves at speed. Most yachts accept children aged 5 and above, but check with the owner if you have younger kids.

If you are a solo traveller, you can book a private charter, but you pay the full boat price. There are no shared or group charters on BoatHire24. For a smaller group or a tighter budget, consider a RIB speedboat or a licence-free day boat, which cost around EUR 400 to EUR 800 per day.

If you want a party atmosphere, choose a larger yacht with a flybridge and a powerful sound system. If you prefer a quiet, relaxing day, go for a smaller, more intimate boat. The skipper will match the vibe to your group.

Local Highlights Near Estepona

Estepona old town is worth a visit before or after your charter. It has narrow cobbled streets, whitewashed buildings, and flower-filled balconies. The Plaza de las Flores market sells local produce and crafts. If you have time, walk up to the Castillo de San Luis castle ruins for a view of the coast.

For a pre-charter breakfast, try a churro stand at the marina or a café on the Avenida de España. For a post-charter dinner, the harbour area has several seafood restaurants serving grilled sardines and fried anchovies. Book a table in advance during summer.

If you want to extend your stay, the area around Estepona has several golf courses, including the Finca Cortesín and the Estepona Golf Club. The beaches are clean and have Blue Flag status, but they get crowded in August. The charter gives you a private spot on the water away from the crowds.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why Estepona Beats Puerto Banús for a Day Charter

Puerto Banús gets all the attention, but for a motor yacht charter Estepona day, you get a better deal. Banús is a show-off harbour with superyachts and paparazzi. Estepona is a working marina with real fishermen, lower berth fees, and less ego. The skipper can leave the harbour without queuing behind a 50-metre Lürssen. The water is cleaner too, because you are further from the Guadalmina river runoff. If you want to see the Banús glamour, the skipper can cruise past it on the way to Marbella. You get the views without the parking hassle.

The marina staff in Estepona are more relaxed about boarding times. If you arrive 30 minutes early, you can sit at the beach bar with a coffee and watch the boats come in. In Banús, you pay EUR 5 for the same coffee and get a side of attitude. For a family or a group of friends who want a stress-free start, Estepona wins every time.

Fuel Costs and Range: What You Actually Burn

Fuel is included in the price of a motor yacht charter Estepona day, but it helps to understand what that covers. A 40-foot motor yacht with twin diesel engines burns about 80 to 120 litres per hour at cruising speed (20 to 25 knots). At EUR 1.50 per litre, that is EUR 120 to EUR 180 per hour. Over 8 hours, the fuel bill alone is EUR 960 to EUR 1,440. The charter price absorbs that, so you are not watching the gauge all day.

If you ask the skipper to open the throttles to 30 knots for a thrill run, fuel consumption jumps to 200 litres per hour. Most skippers will do this for 10 or 15 minutes, then drop back to a comfortable cruise. The range at cruising speed is about 150 to 200 NM, which is enough to reach Gibraltar and back with a margin. If you want to go to the Nerja caves or the Moroccan coast, you need a yacht with larger fuel tanks, which costs more. For a standard day, the included fuel is more than enough.

Weather Windows and the Levante Wind

The Costa del Sol has two main winds. The levante comes from the east, blowing warm and dry air from the Sahara. It can kick up a chop in the afternoon, especially between Marbella and Estepona. The poniente comes from the west, bringing cooler, more humid air and flatter seas. For a motor yacht charter Estepona day, the skipper checks the forecast 24 hours before departure. If the levante is forecast above 20 knots, the skipper will suggest a route that stays close to the coast, where the sea is calmer.

In July and August, the thermal wind builds around 2pm and dies by sunset. That means the morning is glassy, the afternoon is bumpy, and the evening is calm again. If your group gets seasick, ask for a 10am to 6pm charter instead of noon to 8pm. You get the flat water in the morning for the swim stop, and the wind picks up just as you head back to port. The skipper will adjust the speed to keep the ride comfortable.

What to Bring on a Day Charter

Pack light for a motor yacht charter Estepona day. You need a swimsuit, a towel, sunscreen (factor 50, not the cheap stuff), sunglasses with a strap, and a light jacket or windbreaker. The sun reflects off the water and burns faster than on land. A hat is essential unless you want a red scalp. Leave the high heels at home; the deck gets slippery, and the crew will ask you to take them off anyway.

Bring a waterproof phone case or a dry bag for your valuables. The yacht has a small safe in the cabin, but it is not big enough for a laptop. If you want to take photos, a GoPro on a stick is better than a DSLR because of the spray. The skipper has a first aid kit and a fire extinguisher, but if you need specific medication, bring it yourself. The nearest pharmacy is at the marina, but it closes for siesta from 2pm to 5pm.

How to Tip the Crew on a Day Charter

Tipping is not mandatory on a motor yacht charter Estepona day, but it is appreciated. The crew works a 10-hour day including cleaning before and after the charter. A typical tip is 10 to 15 percent of the charter price, split between the skipper and the deckhand. For a EUR 3,000 charter, that is EUR 300 to EUR 450. If the service was average, EUR 100 is fine. If the skipper went out of the way to find dolphins or let you steer the boat, tip on the higher end.

Cash in euros is easiest. The crew does not carry a card machine. Some guests tip via bank transfer after the charter, but cash is more direct. Do not tip in dollars or pounds; the crew has to exchange it and loses on the rate. If you are unsure, ask the owner during booking what the crew expects. Most owners will say "not required but welcome", which means yes.

Alternative Departure Ports Near Estepona

If Estepona Marina is fully booked or you want a different starting point, you can book a motor yacht charter Estepona day from Sotogrande, about 15 minutes west by road. Sotogrande is a private marina with a polo club and gated communities. The boats there are generally larger and more expensive, starting at EUR 3,000 per day. The advantage is that you are closer to the Strait of Gibraltar, so dolphin sightings are almost guaranteed.

To the east, Cabopino Marina is a small, quiet harbour near the Artola sand dunes. It has a relaxed vibe and a good beach bar. The boats there are mostly 30 to 40 feet, costing from EUR 1,000 per day. Cabopino is closer to Marbella, so you can cruise to Puerto Banús in 20 minutes. Benalmádena is further east, about 40 minutes from Estepona by car, and has a large selection of motor yachts. All these ports are listed on the search page with filters for departure location and boat size.

What Happens in Bad Weather

If the weather turns bad on the day of your motor yacht charter Estepona day, the skipper has the final say on whether to sail. The decision is based on wind speed, wave height, and visibility. If the skipper cancels, you get a full refund or a free reschedule. If you decide to cancel because of a light drizzle, you lose the deposit. The definition of "bad weather" is subjective, but the skipper will not go out if the waves are over 1.5 metres or the wind is above 25 knots.

In practice, cancellations are rare on the Costa del Sol. The region gets over 300 days of sunshine per year. If a storm is forecast, the owner will contact you 48 hours before to discuss options. You can move the charter to the next day or switch to a different port where the weather is better. The crew would rather lose a day of income than risk the boat and the guests.

Combining the Charter with a Land Excursion

A motor yacht charter Estepona day usually runs from 10am to 6pm. That leaves the evening free for a land activity. Estepona old town is a 10-minute walk from the marina. The streets are quiet after 8pm when the shops close. The Plaza de las Flores has a few tapas bars where you can eat for EUR 15 to EUR 20 per person. For a fancier meal, try the Restaurante El Puerto on the marina front, which serves grilled sea bass and lobster.

If you have a car, drive 20 minutes to the village of Casares, a whitewashed hill town with a Moorish castle. The views from the top stretch to Gibraltar on a clear day. Alternatively, the Cueva del Gato (Cat's Cave) is a natural swimming hole about 30 minutes inland. The water is cold but crystal clear. These trips work well the day before or after the charter, not on the same day, because you will be tired from the sun and the sea.

title: Speedboat Rental Puerto Banus Hourly: Flexible Rates
metaDescription: Book a speedboat rental Puerto Banus hourly with flexible rates. No licence needed. Depart from Puerto Banús or Marbella. Compare prices and book online.
h1: Speedboat Rental Puerto Banus Hourly: Flexible Rates
intro:
You want to zip across the Costa del Sol without committing to a full day on the water. A speedboat rental Puerto Banus hourly gives you the freedom to escape the marina crowds for an hour or two, explore hidden coves like Cala del Faro, and be back for a late lunch. No licence required, no long-term commitment, just a fast, fun ride with a licensed skipper who knows the coast.

BoatHire24 connects you with local operators who offer hourly speedboat charters from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and Cabopino. Rates start from around EUR 200 per hour for a 4-metre RIB, up to EUR 600 per hour for a high-performance 8-metre speedboat. All include fuel, skipper, and safety gear. You decide the duration, route, and pace.
bodyHtml:
Why Choose an Hourly Speedboat Rental in Puerto Banus

Hourly rentals make sense when you want a quick burst of adrenaline, a short sightseeing tour, or a flexible schedule. You don't pay for dock time you won't use. You can book 1, 2, or 3 hours and tailor the route to your mood. Want to see the superyachts in Puerto Banús, then race to Cabopino for a swim? That's a 2-hour trip. Prefer to cruise the Marbella coastline and stop at a beach club for a drink? A 1-hour rental covers that.

The key advantage is flexibility. You can book last-minute, change your itinerary on the fly, and avoid the fixed departure times of longer charters. The skipper handles navigation, so you just sit back and enjoy the speed.

What's Included in an Hourly Speedboat Charter

Every speedboat rental Puerto Banus hourly through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, fuel, life jackets, and basic insurance. The boat is cleaned and fuelled before your departure. You bring sunscreen, towels, and snacks if you want them. Some operators offer optional extras: snorkel gear, soft drinks, or a cooler for your own drinks.

The skipper speaks English and Spanish, knows the local waters, and can point out landmarks like La Concha mountain, the Río Verde estuary, and the exclusive villas of the Golden Mile. You don't need a boating licence. The skipper is in charge of the boat, but you can steer if you want to try.

Departure Ports for Your Hourly Speedboat Trip

Your hourly speedboat can depart from several ports along the Costa del Sol. The most popular is Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina in Marbella with its designer shops and superyachts. From there, you can head east to Marbella's beaches or west to the quieter coves near Estepona.

Other departure options include Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino with its dune-backed beach, Estepona port near the old town, Sotogrande for the upscale crowd, and Benalmádena with its marina and nearby dolphin-watching spots. Each port offers different cruising ranges within a 1-3 hour window. A 1-hour trip from Puerto Banús covers about 5-7 nautical miles at cruising speed, enough to reach Cala del Faro or the Cabopino sand dunes.

Types of Speedboats Available for Hourly Rental

The hourly rental fleet includes RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) from 4 to 7 metres, and hard-hulled speedboats up to 9 metres. RIBs are lighter, faster, and more manoeuvrable, great for a thrill ride. Hard-hulled boats offer more comfort and shade, better for a relaxed cruise with a few friends.

Typical models include the Zodiac Pro 650, Brig Falcon 750, and Axopar 28. These boats have outboard engines from 150 to 300 hp, reaching speeds of 30-45 knots depending on load and sea conditions. For a 2-hour rental, you can cover 15-20 nautical miles, enough to reach the Strait of Gibraltar area for dolphin sightings if conditions allow.

Pricing Guidance for Hourly Speedboat Rentals

Rates vary by boat size, engine power, and operator. As a rough guide, expect to pay from around EUR 200 per hour for a 4-metre RIB, EUR 350 per hour for a 6-metre RIB, and EUR 500-600 per hour for a luxury 8-metre speedboat with a cabin. Prices are for the boat, not per person. Most operators charge a minimum of 1 hour, but 2-hour bookings are the sweet spot for value.

Fuel is included in the hourly rate, so you don't need to worry about topping up. Some operators offer discounted rates for 3+ hour bookings. Compare prices on BoatHire24's search page to find the best deal for your dates.

Best Seasons for Hourly Speedboat Trips in Marbella

The Costa del Sol has a long boating season, from April to October. June, July, and August are the busiest and warmest months, with sea temperatures around 22-26 degrees C. Book ahead in peak season, as hourly slots fill up quickly. May and September offer pleasant conditions with fewer crowds, making them ideal for a spontaneous 1-hour rental.

Winter months (November to March) are cooler, with sea temps around 15-18 degrees C. Some operators run hourly charters year-round, but you'll want a wetsuit for swimming. The advantage of winter is lower demand and more flexible pricing.

How to Book an Hourly Speedboat Rental

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Use the search filters to select your preferred port, date, and duration. You'll see available boats and their hourly rates. Choose your boat, add any extras like snorkel gear or drinks, and pay a deposit online. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day.

You'll receive a confirmation with meeting instructions, the skipper's contact details, and what to bring. On the day, arrive 15 minutes early at the designated marina berth. The skipper will give a safety briefing, then you're off.

Who Is an Hourly Speedboat Rental For

Hourly speedboat rentals are perfect for couples wanting a romantic sunset cruise, small groups of friends looking for a quick adventure, or families with older children who want a taste of speed. They also suit photographers who want to capture the coastline from the water, or business visitors with a tight schedule who want to see Marbella from the sea in a short time.

If you're planning a full day of exploration, a half-day or full-day charter might be better value. But for a flexible, no-fuss outing, hourly rental is hard to beat. For more tips on planning your trip, check out the BoatHire24 blog for guides on local routes and weather conditions.

Popular Routes for an Hourly Speedboat Trip

From Puerto Banús, a classic 1-hour route heads east past the Marbella Club Hotel and Puente Romano beach, then back. A 2-hour route goes west to Cabopino, where you can anchor off the sand dunes for a swim, then return via the Marbella coastline. From Estepona, a 1-hour trip takes you past the old town's beachfront and the marina, while a 2-hour route can reach the dolphin-rich waters near the Gibraltar Strait.

From Benalmádena, a 1-hour run goes to the Torre Bermeja lighthouse and back, with good dolphin chances. From Sotogrande, you can cruise the Guadiaro river mouth and the upscale marina in 1-2 hours.

What to Bring and Expect on the Day

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful even in summer, as the wind at speed can feel cool. The skipper will have a VHF radio and first aid kit. You can bring your own drinks and snacks, but glass bottles are not allowed on most boats.

The boat has a small cabin or storage compartment for your bags. Expect a safety briefing covering life jacket locations, emergency procedures, and basic boat etiquette. The skipper will ask about your preferred pace and route. If you want to stop for a swim, just say the word.

Safety and Licensing Requirements

No boating licence is needed for hourly speedboat rentals because a licensed skipper is always on board. The skipper holds a Spanish Patrón de Navegación Básica or higher qualification, and the boat is insured for commercial charter. Life jackets are provided for all passengers, and children must wear them at all times.

The skipper monitors weather and sea conditions. If the forecast is rough, they may cancel or suggest a different route. Your safety is the priority. For more details on regulations, read the BoatHire24 blog on Spanish boating rules.

Comparing RIBs vs Hard-Hulled Speedboats for Hourly Rentals

RIB and hard-hulled speedboats handle differently, and your choice affects the experience. RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) have a fibreglass hull with inflatable tubes around the edge. They are lighter, so they accelerate faster and plane at lower speeds. A 6-metre RIB with a 200 hp engine hits 40 knots in calm water. The tubes absorb some wave impact, making the ride softer at speed. But they offer less shelter, and the open deck can get wet in choppy conditions. Hard-hulled boats, like the Axopar 28 or the Jeanneau Merry Fisher, have a deep-V fibreglass hull and a small cabin or windscreen. They are heavier and slightly slower, but they provide more comfort on longer trips. For a 1-hour rental, a RIB gives you more excitement. For a 2-hour trip with a swim stop, a hard-hulled boat adds shade and a place to change out of wet clothes.

How Sea Conditions Affect Hourly Speedboat Rentals

The Mediterranean is generally calm, but the Costa del Sol has local quirks. The Levante wind blows from the east and can create short, steep waves of 1-2 metres, especially near the Gibraltar Strait. Poniente wind from the west is lighter and produces flatter seas. In summer, the sea is usually calm in the morning, with a light breeze picking up after 2 PM. Hourly rentals work best in the morning or late afternoon. If the forecast shows waves above 1.5 metres, the skipper may limit speed or suggest a different route. For example, a 1-hour trip from Puerto Banús to Cabopino is safe in moderate conditions, but heading west past Estepona towards Gibraltar is riskier when the Levante blows. Check the BoatHire24 blog for weekly sea condition updates.

Cost Comparison: Hourly vs Half-Day vs Full-Day Rentals

Hourly rentals cost more per hour than longer charters because the operator covers the same fixed costs (skipper, fuel, cleaning) for a shorter booking. As a rough guide, a 1-hour RIB rental might cost EUR 200, while a 4-hour half-day on the same boat might cost EUR 500-600. That works out to EUR 125-150 per hour for the longer booking. For a 2-hour trip, you pay around EUR 400, which is EUR 200 per hour, still higher than a half-day rate. But you are not paying for time you do not use. If you only want a quick spin, hourly is cheaper overall. If you plan to spend 3-4 hours on the water, book a half-day charter. For a full day (6-8 hours), expect EUR 800-1200 for a RIB and EUR 1200-2000 for a luxury speedboat. Use the BoatHire24 search page to compare rates for different durations.

Best Hourly Routes from Estepona and Sotogrande

Estepona port is a good base for hourly speedboat trips because the marina is close to the old town and the beaches are quieter than Marbella. A 1-hour route from Estepona goes west past the Costa Galera beach and the Punta de la Doncella lighthouse, then returns. You see the Sierra Bermeja mountains in the background and the whitewashed buildings of the old town from the water. A 2-hour route goes further west past the Guadalmansa River mouth to the Cabo de Estepona area, where you might spot dolphins. From Sotogrande, a 1-hour trip goes south to the Guadiaro River mouth and the Sotogrande beach, then loops back past the marina's superyacht berths. A 2-hour route heads towards Gibraltar, but you need calm seas to get close to the Rock. The skipper can adjust the route based on the weather and your preferences.

What Happens if the Weather Cancels Your Hourly Booking

Weather cancellations are rare in summer, but they happen when the Levante wind kicks up. If the skipper cancels for safety reasons, you get a full refund or the option to reschedule. The decision is made on the morning of your booking, based on the latest forecast and local observations. You are not charged for cancellations due to weather. If you cancel voluntarily, the deposit is usually non-refundable unless you cancel more than 48 hours in advance. Check the operator's policy on the BoatHire24 listing before booking. Some operators offer a free reschedule if you cancel 24 hours ahead, but that varies. For peace of mind, book a flexible rate if available.

Tips for First-Time Speedboat Passengers

If you have never been on a speedboat before, a few things help. Sit towards the rear of the boat for a smoother ride, as the bow lifts and bounces more at speed. Hold onto the grab rails when the boat is planing. Wear a hat with a strap, because the wind will take a loose hat. Keep your phone in a waterproof case or leave it in the storage compartment. Do not stand up while the boat is moving, even at slow speed, as a sudden turn can throw you off balance. The skipper will slow down for turns and when approaching the marina. If you feel seasick, look at the horizon and avoid reading your phone. Most people adjust after a few minutes. The skipper can also reduce speed if you feel uncomfortable.

How to Combine an Hourly Speedboat Rental with Other Activities

An hourly speedboat trip works well as part of a larger day out. For example, book a 2-hour rental from Puerto Banús in the morning, then have lunch at a beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club. Or take a 1-hour sunset cruise from Marbella Marina, then walk to the old town for dinner. From Benalmádena, a 1-hour trip to the Torre Bermeja lighthouse fits before a visit to the Puerto Marina shopping area. From Cabopino, a 2-hour rental includes a swim stop at the sand dunes, then you can walk to the chiringuito beach bar for seafood. The flexibility of hourly rentals means you can slot the boat trip into your schedule without committing to a full day. For more ideas, read the BoatHire24 blog on combining boat rentals with Marbella activities.

What to Expect from the Skipper on an Hourly Rental

The skipper is a professional with local knowledge and a commercial licence. They handle the boat, navigation, and safety. They also act as a guide, pointing out landmarks like the Rio Verde estuary where flamingos sometimes feed, or the luxury villas of the Golden Mile. You can ask them to speed up or slow down, take a detour to see a particular beach, or stop for a swim. They will not push you to do anything you do not want to do. The skipper speaks English, so communication is easy. If you want to steer the boat, they will let you try in open water, but they stay in control for docking and tricky manoeuvres. The skipper expects you to follow basic safety rules, like staying seated when the boat is moving and wearing a life jacket if you cannot swim.

Hidden Costs and What to Watch Out For

Most hourly speedboat rentals include fuel, skipper, and insurance in the quoted rate. But some operators add extras. Check if the price includes VAT (IVA in Spain), which is 21 per cent. Some listings show prices excluding tax, so the final cost is higher. Also confirm if the price covers the full boat or per person. In Spain, hourly rentals are almost always per boat, not per person, but some resellers list per-person rates. Deposit policies vary, with some operators charging 50 per cent upfront and others only 25 per cent. Read the terms on the BoatHire24 listing carefully. Ask about cancellation fees, weather refunds, and whether the skipper expects a tip. Tipping is not mandatory, but 10-15 per cent of the rental cost is appreciated if the service is good.

Last-Minute Bookings and Same-Day Availability

Hourly speedboat rentals are often available for same-day or next-day booking, especially outside peak season. In July and August, book at least 2-3 days ahead for the best selection. Some operators hold back a few slots for last-minute bookings, but you pay a premium. Use the BoatHire24 search page to filter by availability today or tomorrow. If you see no slots, try a different port or a different boat type. RIBs are more likely to have last-minute availability than luxury speedboats. For a spontaneous trip, call the operator directly through the contact details on the listing to check availability. Same-day bookings usually require payment in full online, as the skipper needs to prepare the boat and schedule the slot.

h1: Luxury Catamaran Charter Puerto Banus Group: Party Packages
keyword: luxury catamaran charter Puerto Banus group
intro:
You want to throw a proper party on the water in Puerto Banus, and you need a boat that can handle a crowd without feeling cramped. That is where a luxury catamaran charter comes in. These wide, stable vessels give you space to dance, lounge, and eat while a licensed skipper handles the navigation. No seasickness, no crowding, just a floating terrace with a bar and a sound system.

BoatHire24 lists dozens of catamarans based in Puerto Banus, from sleek 40-footers to 80-foot beasts that can take 50 guests plus crew. Every booking includes a skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. You choose the route, the catering, and the playlist. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a mid-sized cat, going up to EUR 8,000 for a full-day blowout on a 70-footer with a tender and water toys.

This page covers everything you need to know about organising a luxury catamaran party in Puerto Banus for your group: what is included, which ports to use, how many people you can bring, and how to book without getting ripped off.
bodyHtml:
What a Luxury Catamaran Charter in Puerto Banus Includes

When you book a catamaran through BoatHire24, the base package always includes a professional skipper, fuel for the agreed itinerary, and third-party liability insurance. The skipper is your host and safety officer, not a waiter, so you still need to organise food and drink separately unless you add a crew package. Most catamarans come with a basic sound system (Bluetooth or aux), a flybridge with sun loungers, a shaded saloon, and a forward trampoline net where people can lie down and watch the sea. Some larger models also have a small kitchen, a grill, and a freshwater deck shower.

For a party group, the key numbers are the maximum passenger capacity, which ranges from 12 to 50 depending on the boat's licence. Spanish maritime law caps the number of guests per vessel, and the skipper will enforce it. Do not try to sneak extra people on board, because the skipper can refuse to sail and you will still pay the full charter fee. Stick to the limit and everyone gets a seat, a life jacket, and a good time.

Puerto Banus: The Departure Port for Your Party

Puerto Banus is the obvious starting point for a luxury catamaran charter with a group. The marina is a 15-minute drive from Marbella town and has direct access to the open Mediterranean without any locks or bridges. Your charter will usually depart from one of the main quays near the casino or the commercial pier. The skipper will meet you at the boat 15 minutes before departure, give a safety briefing, and then you are off.

From Puerto Banus you can head east towards Marbella's beaches, west towards Estepona, or south towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The most popular party route is a two-hour cruise along the coast to a quiet anchorage like Cala del Faro or the area off the Rio Verde, where the water is calm and you can anchor, swim, and eat. If you want to see dolphins, the skipper can take you towards the Strait, where pods of common and striped dolphins often appear. That trip takes longer, so factor in at least five hours for a dolphin-watching party.

Boat Options for a Group Party Catamaran Charter

Not all catamarans are the same, and the one you choose depends on your group size and budget. For 12-20 people, a Lagoon 42 or a Bali 4.5 works well. These boats have a large cockpit, a flybridge with seating, and a trampoline at the front. Prices for these start around EUR 1,500 for a half-day (4 hours) and EUR 2,500 for a full day (8 hours).

For 20-30 people, you need a bigger cat like a Lagoon 52 or a Fountaine Pajot 67. These have a fully enclosed saloon, a flybridge with a bar, and often a small swim platform at the back. Half-day prices go from EUR 3,000 to EUR 5,000. For 30-50 people, look at a Lagoon 77 or a Sunreef 80. These are proper party platforms with multiple decks, a DJ booth option, and a tender for water sports. Prices are on request, but expect EUR 6,000 to EUR 10,000 for a full day.

If your group is smaller than 12, you might be better off with a motor yacht or a sailing yacht, but catamarans offer the most deck space per person. Check our search page to filter by passenger capacity and price.

Pricing Guidance for a Luxury Catamaran Party in Puerto Banus

Prices vary by season, boat size, duration, and extras. High season runs from June to September, when demand peaks and prices are 30-50 percent higher than in spring or autumn. Low season (November to March) sees the lowest rates, but the weather is cooler and you risk rain or choppy seas. The sweet spot is May or October, when the water is warm enough for swimming and the marinas are less crowded.

Here is a rough breakdown of costs for a luxury catamaran charter in Puerto Banus for a group party:

  • Half-day (4 hours): EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,500 for a 40-50 foot catamaran
  • Full day (8 hours): EUR 2,500 to EUR 6,000 for a 40-50 foot catamaran
  • Full day on a 60-80 foot catamaran: EUR 5,000 to EUR 10,000
  • Extras: catering (EUR 30-60 per person), open bar (EUR 20-40 per person), water toys (EUR 200-500 per item), crew gratuity (10-15 percent of charter fee)

These are guide prices. Always ask for a detailed quote before booking, and confirm what is included. Some operators charge extra for fuel if you go beyond a certain distance, so agree on the itinerary in advance.

Best Season for a Catamaran Party in Puerto Banus

The Mediterranean climate in this part of Spain gives you about eight months of reliable good weather. From April to October, average daytime temperatures range from 20 to 30 degrees C, and the sea temperature is comfortable for swimming from June to September. July and August are the hottest and busiest months, with marinas full and prices at their peak. If you want a party atmosphere with other boats around, summer is your time. If you prefer quieter waters and lower prices, May or September work well.

Wind is a factor. The Levante wind can pick up in the afternoon, especially in summer, creating choppy conditions on the east side of the coast. Catamarans handle chop better than monohulls, but if the wind hits 25 knots, the skipper may cancel or alter the route. For a party, you want calm seas so people can move around safely and the catering stays on the table. Morning departures are usually calmer than afternoon ones.

For the best balance of weather, availability, and price, book a luxury catamaran charter in Puerto Banus for your group in May, June, or September. July and August are fine if you book three months in advance and accept the higher cost.

How to Book a Luxury Catamaran Charter for a Group Party

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, select Puerto Banus as the departure port, choose catamaran as the boat type, and set the passenger count to match your group size. The system shows available boats with prices, photos, and specifications. Click on a listing to see the full details, including the cancellation policy and what is included.

Once you pick a boat, you can request a booking for a specific date. The platform sends your request to the boat owner or charter company, who confirms availability within 24 hours. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50 percent) to secure the date, and the balance is due a few days before departure. Payment is via bank transfer or credit card. The company will send you a contract with the terms, including the maximum number of guests, the itinerary, and the cancellation policy.

For large groups, especially those over 20 people, it is wise to book at least two weeks in advance. In peak season, book a month ahead. If you need catering, a DJ, or water toys, arrange those at the time of booking. Many charter companies offer add-on packages, but you can also bring your own food and drink as long as the skipper approves.

If you are unsure which boat suits your group, contact the BoatHire24 team via the website. They know the local fleet and can recommend a catamaran based on your budget and party style. Read our blog for tips on planning a boat party in Marbella.

Who Should Book a Luxury Catamaran Party in Puerto Banus

This type of charter is ideal for groups celebrating a birthday, a stag or hen do, a corporate event, or just a weekend blowout with friends. The catamaran's stability and space make it suitable for all ages, from 20-something party crowds to family reunions with kids and grandparents. The skipper keeps things safe, so you can drink, dance, and swim without worrying about navigation.

If your group is mostly adults who want to party hard, choose a catamaran with a powerful sound system and a flybridge bar. If you have children or older guests, pick a boat with a shaded saloon and a swim platform for easy water access. Either way, the experience is about relaxing on the sea with your people, not about the sailing itself.

One thing to note: catamarans are not fast. They cruise at around 8-10 knots, so you will not cover huge distances in a half-day charter. For a party, that is fine because you want time to anchor, swim, and eat. If your group wants to go fast and visit multiple beaches, a motor yacht or a RIB might be a better fit. But for pure party space, a catamaran wins every time.

Other Departure Ports for a Catamaran Party on the Costa del Sol

While Puerto Banus is the party capital, you can also charter a catamaran from other ports along the coast. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a short walk from the old town and offers a slightly quieter departure point. Cabopino, near the dunes of Artola, is good for groups who want a nature-focused trip with less crowd. Estepona port has a charming old town and is closer to the dolphin zones in the Strait. Sotogrande is a luxury resort port with high-end catamarans, ideal for corporate groups. Benalmadena, east of Marbella, is another option with a lively marina and easy access to the coast.

Each port has its own character, but the experience is similar: a licensed skipper, a clean boat, and the same Mediterranean sea. If you are staying in Marbella, Puerto Banus is the most convenient. If you are based in Estepona or Sotogrande, chartering from there saves you travel time and may give you more boat options for the same price.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind on a Catamaran Party

Pack light. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe if possible), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the evening. If you want to take photos, a waterproof phone case or a GoPro is useful. Leave high heels on the dock, because they damage the teak deck and the skipper will ask you to remove them. Barefoot or flat shoes only.

For food and drink, most groups bring a cooler with beer, wine, soft drinks, and snacks. Some catamarans have a fridge and an ice maker, but confirm in advance. If you order catering, the company will provide platters, cutlery, and plates. Do not bring glass bottles to the beach or swimming area, because broken glass is a hazard. Use plastic or metal cups instead.

If you plan to swim, bring a float or a noodle. Some catamarans have a SUP or a kayak included in the charter, but ask before you assume. Water toys like a jet ski or a donut can be added for an extra fee, but they require a separate operator and insurance.

Common Mistakes to Avoid When Booking a Catamaran Party

The biggest mistake is underestimating the passenger limit. Spanish regulations are strict, and the skipper will count heads before departure. If you have 25 guests, do not book a boat rated for 20. You will either have to leave five people behind or upgrade to a larger boat at the last minute, which costs more. Always book for the exact number of guests, plus a buffer if you expect last-minute additions.

Another mistake is assuming the price includes everything. Read the contract carefully. Some charters charge extra for fuel beyond a 20 NM radius, for cleaning if the boat is left messy, or for port fees if you stop at a marina. Ask for a full breakdown before you pay the deposit.

Finally, do not book a catamaran party during a forecasted storm. The skipper has the final say on whether to sail, and if the weather is bad, you will either get a refund or a reschedule. Check the forecast a few days before and have a backup date in mind. In summer, storms are rare, but they do happen.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Luxury Catamaran Charter in Puerto Banus

BoatHire24 is a local marketplace that lists only verified charter boats with licensed skippers. We do not sell tickets for shared trips, so every booking is a private charter for your group. The platform shows real availability and real prices, not bait-and-switch offers. You can compare multiple boats side by side, read the boat specifications, and see photos taken by the owners.

We also provide a dedicated support team who speak English and Spanish. If you have questions about a specific boat or need help arranging catering, we can connect you with the charter company directly. Our blog has guides on the best anchorages, what to wear, and how to negotiate a good deal. And if something goes wrong, we mediate disputes between guests and operators.

For a luxury catamaran charter in Puerto Banus for your group party, start your search on BoatHire24. Find the boat, book it, and let the skipper take care of the rest.

title: Private Yacht Hire Marbella Wedding: Elegant Venue
metaDescription: Private yacht hire Marbella wedding: elegant floating venue for your ceremony and reception. Expert skippers, Puerto Banús departures. Book your dream day.
h1: Private Yacht Hire Marbella Wedding: Your Elegant Floating Venue
intro:
If you are planning a wedding on the Costa del Sol, the idea of a private yacht hire Marbella wedding might sound like a logistical nightmare. It is not. You get a fully licensed skipper, a dedicated crew, and a venue that moves with the Mediterranean light. No dodgy marquee on a damp lawn. No fighting for parking in Puerto Banús. Just you, your guests, and the sea.

We are BoatHire24, a marketplace for boat and yacht charters along the Costa del Sol. We do not own the boats, but we know which ones work for weddings, which ports suit different party sizes, and what the real costs look like. This page is the straight-talking guide to hiring a private yacht for your Marbella wedding, with concrete numbers, honest advice, and no marketing fluff.
bodyHtml:
What a Private Yacht Wedding Actually Includes

When you book a private yacht hire Marbella wedding through BoatHire24, the package typically includes the vessel, a licensed skipper, and basic crew for the duration of the charter. Most boats allow up to 12 guests for a wedding ceremony, but larger superyachts can host up to 50 or more for a reception. The standard charter is 4 hours, but you can extend to 6 or 8 hours for a full ceremony plus party. Catering is usually arranged separately, either through the charter company or an external caterer approved by the port authority. Some boats have a small galley for heating food, but most rely on pre-prepared catering brought onboard. You will also need a wedding officiant if you want a legal ceremony; the yacht itself does not provide that. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring in scenic spots like Cala del Faro or off Puerto Banús, and ensuring everyone stays safe. No one is going to ask you to help tie a fender.

Departure Ports for Your Wedding Charter

The main departure ports for a private yacht hire Marbella wedding are Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, and Benalmádena. Puerto Banús is the most glamorous option, with direct access to the Golden Mile and the best photo opportunities with superyachts in the background. Marbella Marina is quieter and closer to the old town, good for a more intimate ceremony. Cabopino has a small, relaxed harbour near the Artola dunes, ideal for a bohemian vibe. Estepona offers a charming old town backdrop and slightly lower mooring fees. Benalmádena is further east but has a large marina with plenty of parking. Sotogrande is an option for very high-end weddings, but it is 30 minutes from Marbella. The choice of port affects the cruising route: from Puerto Banús you can head west to the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin sightings, or east to the Cala del Faro cove. From Marbella Marina, you can anchor off La Concha mountain for a dramatic backdrop. Your skipper will advise on the best route based on wind and swell on the day.

Boat Types Suitable for a Wedding

Not every boat on BoatHire24 is suitable for a wedding. The best options are motor yachts and catamarans. Motor yachts from 15 to 25 metres offer a sleek profile, a spacious flybridge for the ceremony, and an enclosed saloon for the reception. Catamarans, typically 12 to 18 metres, provide more deck space and stability, which matters if you have guests prone to seasickness. Sailing yachts can work for a small, rustic wedding, but the mast and rigging limit the usable deck area. RIBs and speedboats are too small. Fishing boats are not appropriate. Superyachts over 30 metres are available for larger parties but require a budget of EUR 10,000 or more for a half-day charter. Licence-free day boats are not allowed to carry more than 12 people and are not suitable for weddings. For a typical wedding party of 10 to 20 guests, a 16-metre motor yacht or a 14-metre catamaran is the sweet spot. You can browse our full search to filter by size and type.

Pricing Guidance for a Private Yacht Wedding

Let us talk money. A private yacht hire Marbella wedding for 12 guests on a 15-metre motor yacht starts from around EUR 2,500 for a 4-hour charter including skipper and basic crew. That is the base price. Add catering at EUR 50 to 100 per person for canapés and drinks. Add a wedding officiant at EUR 300 to 500. Add flowers and decorations, which the charter company can arrange for an extra EUR 500 to 1,500. Add a photographer for EUR 500 to 1,000. If you want a larger catamaran for 20 guests, expect from around EUR 3,500 for 4 hours. Superyacht charters for 30-plus guests start at EUR 8,000 and go up to EUR 25,000 for a full day. Fuel is usually included in the charter fee for local cruising, but if you want to go to Nerja or the Strait of Gibraltar, there may be a surcharge. Port fees are typically included for departures from the home port. The total cost for a wedding with 12 guests, decent catering, and basic decorations is realistically EUR 4,000 to 6,000. That is competitive with a hotel ballroom or a marquee on a golf course, and you get a view that moves.

Best Seasons for a Marbella Yacht Wedding

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate, but the sea is not always calm. The best months for a private yacht hire Marbella wedding are May, June, September, and October. In these months, the air temperature is 22 to 28 degrees C, the water is warm enough for a swim (18 to 24 degrees C), and the wind is moderate. July and August are hot, 30 to 35 degrees C, and the marinas are crowded. The sea is flat, but the sun is brutal. You will need shade on the flybridge and plenty of water. November to March is risky: temperatures drop to 15 to 20 degrees C, and the wind can pick up, especially in the afternoon. April is unpredictable, with some calm days and some windy ones. If you book in winter, choose a motor yacht with a heated saloon. The skipper will cancel if the wind exceeds 25 knots, so have a backup plan. The best time of day for a wedding ceremony is late afternoon, 16:00 to 18:00, when the light is golden for photos and the sea breeze is gentle. Sunset around 20:00 in summer is spectacular from the water.

How to Book Your Wedding Yacht

Booking a private yacht hire Marbella wedding through BoatHire24 is straightforward, but you need to plan ahead. Start by checking availability on our BoatHire24 homepage or the search page. Filter by boat type, guest capacity, and port. Contact the charter company directly through the listing to discuss your wedding requirements. They will ask for the date, number of guests, duration, and any special requests like catering or decorations. You will need to pay a deposit, typically 30 to 50 percent, to secure the date. The balance is due 2 to 4 weeks before the charter. Make sure you have a contract that specifies the cancellation policy, weather contingency, and what happens if the boat breaks down. Most charter companies have a backup vessel. We recommend booking at least 3 months in advance for summer weddings, and 6 months for a superyacht. For a last-minute wedding, you might find availability in spring or autumn, but do not count on it.

Who Is a Private Yacht Wedding For

A private yacht hire Marbella wedding is not for everyone. It is ideal for couples who want an intimate ceremony with 12 to 20 guests, a unique backdrop, and a built-in party venue. It works well for destination weddings, where guests are already on holiday and want a memorable experience. It is less suitable for large weddings with 50-plus guests, elderly relatives with mobility issues, or anyone who gets seasick easily. The boat moves, even in calm conditions. If your grandmother uses a walker, a yacht is not a good idea. The ceremony area is usually on the flybridge or aft deck, both accessed by stairs. There is no wheelchair access on most boats. If you want a legal wedding in Spain, you need a civil officiant who can board the vessel, which is possible but requires paperwork. Many couples opt for a symbolic ceremony on the yacht and do the legal part at the registry office beforehand. That is simpler and avoids the risk of the officiant being late because of traffic in Puerto Banús.

Local Colour and Photo Opportunities

One of the best reasons to choose a private yacht hire Marbella wedding is the photo opportunities. From the water, you get angles you cannot get from land. The silhouette of La Concha mountain behind the boat at sunset, the colourful buildings of Puerto Banús fading into the distance, the cliffs of Cala del Faro, and the chance to see dolphins off the coast of Estepona. If you charter for a full day, you can anchor near the Strait of Gibraltar and watch the cargo ships pass. For a more adventurous route, head east towards Nerja and anchor near the caves. The water there is turquoise, and the cliffs are dramatic. Your skipper will know the best spots for a swim stop after the ceremony. Just remember that the sea is not a swimming pool; you need to be comfortable with a ladder and a current.

What to Wear and What to Bring

For a private yacht hire Marbella wedding, dress code is smart casual to formal, depending on your preference. Heels are a bad idea on a boat deck; they get stuck in the teak grills and can damage the surface. Flat shoes or wedges are better. Bring a light jacket or pashmina for the evening breeze, even in summer. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat are essential. If you plan to swim, bring a change of clothes. The boat will have a cooler for drinks, but you can bring your own if the charter company allows it. Most provide ice and water. Do not bring glass bottles; they break and are dangerous on deck. Use plastic or cans. The skipper will have a first aid kit and life jackets, but if anyone needs medication, bring it. Seasickness tablets are a good idea for guests who are not sure. Take them an hour before departure.

Legal and Safety Considerations

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who is responsible for the safety of the vessel and everyone onboard. The skipper has the authority to cancel or shorten the charter if the weather is unsafe. That is rare in summer, but it happens. You will not get a refund for bad weather unless the charter company offers a flexible policy. Read the terms carefully. The boat is insured, but your personal belongings are not. Do not bring valuables you cannot afford to lose. If you want a legal wedding on the yacht, you need to arrange a civil officiant who is registered in Spain. The officiant will need to board the vessel and perform the ceremony in Spanish or with a translator. That adds complexity and cost. Most couples do a symbolic ceremony on the yacht and sign the legal papers at the registry office later. That is simpler and avoids the risk of the officiant not showing up because of traffic or a scheduling conflict.

Alternatives to a Full Wedding Charter

If a full private yacht hire Marbella wedding is out of budget, you can consider a smaller option. Hire a 10-metre motor yacht for just the ceremony and photos, then move the reception to a restaurant on the Puerto Banús waterfront. That costs from around EUR 800 for 2 hours. Or book a catamaran for a sunset cruise with canapés and drinks for 20 guests, starting at EUR 1,500 for 2 hours. You can also hire a RIB for a quick photo shoot on the water, from EUR 300 for 1 hour. These alternatives give you the yacht wedding vibe without the full cost. For more ideas, read our blog on budget-friendly yacht charters on the Costa del Sol.

intro:

bodyHtml:
What a Fuengirola sunset catamaran cruise includes

Every catamaran charter from BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. You do not need a boating licence, and you do not need to help with the sailing unless you want to. The standard sunset package includes a welcome drink (cava or soft drink), sometimes a small tapas platter, and a route that keeps you on the water for the best light. Most trips last 2 to 3 hours, departing around 7.30 pm in summer and earlier in spring and autumn.

Shared cruises often take up to 12 passengers. Private charters let you bring your own playlist, your own food, and your own crowd. Both options include life jackets, basic insurance, and the skipper's commentary in English and Spanish. If you book through BoatHire24, you get the price upfront and a confirmation within a few hours.

Which port to depart from for a Fuengirola sunset

You have two practical departure points for a Fuengirola sunset catamaran trip. The first is Cabopino, a small marina on the eastern edge of Fuengirola. It is quieter than Puerto Banús, parking is easier, and the channel out to sea takes you straight past the Fuengirola waterfront. Cabopino catamarans are usually 12 to 15 metres long, built for stability rather than speed, which matters when you are sipping cava at anchor.

The second option is Benalmádena Marina, a larger port with more boat choices. From Benalmádena the catamaran will cruise west along the coast, passing Fuengirola's beachfront and the Sohail Castle. Benalmádena has more bars and restaurants for a pre- or post-cruise drink, but it also has more foot traffic. Both ports are about the same distance from Fuengirola town centre, so the choice comes down to boat availability and your tolerance for crowds.

Types of catamaran available for sunset hire

Catamarans on the Costa del Sol fall into two broad categories. The first is the luxury cruising cat, 40 to 50 feet, with a flybridge, a forward sunbathing area, and a saloon that opens onto the back deck. These are the boats you see anchored off Cala del Faro, with a table laid out for dinner. They are stable, quiet, and designed for groups of 6 to 12 people. They cost from around EUR 120 per person on a shared sunset cruise or EUR 600 to EUR 900 for a private 3-hour charter.

The second category is the smaller performance cat, usually 35 to 40 feet, with less deck space but a faster hull. These are less common for sunset cruises because the focus is on lounging, not sailing. Still, if you want a bit of speed and a more intimate group (4 to 6 people), a smaller cat works. You can see the full range on the BoatHire24 search page, filtered by port and boat type.

Pricing for catamaran hire Fuengirola sunset cruises

Shared sunset cruises from Cabopino or Benalmádena start at around EUR 80 per person. That includes the skipper, drinks, and about 2.5 hours on the water. Private catamaran charters for a sunset trip cost between EUR 600 and EUR 1,200 depending on the boat size, the duration, and whether you add catering. A 3-hour private charter on a 45-foot cat for up to 10 people typically comes in around EUR 800. If you want a full evening with dinner and an open bar, expect to pay EUR 150 to EUR 200 per person.

Peak season (July and August) prices are about 20% higher. June and September offer the same sunset quality for less. The prices on BoatHire24 are shown in EUR and include VAT. You pay a deposit online and the balance to the skipper on the day. No hidden fees, no booking charges.

Best time of year for a Fuengirola sunset cruise

The sunset season runs from April to October, with the best light in May, June, and September. In midsummer the sun sets around 9.30 pm, which means you depart at 7.30 pm and watch the whole transition from bright blue to orange to purple. In April and October the sun sets earlier, around 8 pm, and the air temperature drops to about 18 degrees C, so you want a jacket. The water is warm enough for a swim from June to September.

Wind conditions matter. The afternoon Levante wind can kick up a chop in the Strait of Gibraltar area, but Fuengirola's coastline is sheltered by the Mijas mountains and the bay shape. Most sunset cruises anchor in a calm spot rather than sail, so you get a stable platform even if the breeze picks up. If you are prone to seasickness, a catamaran is the best option because it does not heel like a monohull.

How to book a catamaran sunset cruise from Fuengirola

Booking through BoatHire24 takes about five minutes. You select the date, the port (Cabopino or Benalmádena), the boat type (catamaran), and the number of guests. The system shows available boats with photos, specs, and the exact price. You can filter by shared or private. Once you book, you get a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and the meeting point at the marina.

If you are unsure which boat suits you, use the live chat or WhatsApp number on the site. The team speaks English and Spanish and can recommend a catamaran based on your group size and budget. Last-minute bookings are possible if the boat is available, but sunset slots go fast in July and August, so booking a week ahead is sensible. For more tips on planning, check the BoatHire24 blog.

Who the Fuengirola sunset catamaran cruise is for

Couples, small groups of friends, families with older children, and solo travellers who want a sociable evening. The shared cruises are popular with tourists staying in Fuengirola, Mijas Costa, and La Cala de Mijas. Private charters are used for birthday celebrations, proposals, and corporate events. The boat is not suitable for very young children because of the low railings and the lack of a dedicated play area, but children over 6 are fine with adult supervision.

If you are a solo traveller looking to meet people, a shared sunset cruise is a good bet. The group size is small enough that you end up talking, and the drinks help. If you want complete privacy, a private charter costs more but gives you the whole boat to yourself. Either way, you get the same sunset over the same sea.

What to bring on a catamaran sunset cruise

Sunscreen, even for a sunset trip, because the UV reflection off the water is strong until the sun dips below the horizon. A light jacket or jumper for the return leg when the wind picks up. Sunglasses. A camera or phone with enough battery. If you booked a private charter, bring your own food and drink unless you arranged catering. The boat has a fridge, a sound system, and usually a Bluetooth speaker. Avoid glass bottles on some boats, so check with the skipper first.

If you plan to swim, bring a towel and a change of clothes. The skipper will anchor in a calm bay if the conditions allow, typically off Cala del Faro or near the Fuengirola castle. The water temperature in summer is around 24 degrees C, so a quick dip is refreshing before the sun goes down.

Things to do in Fuengirola before or after the cruise

Fuengirola has a long promenade, a castle (Sohail Castle) that hosts concerts in summer, and a Bioparc that is actually worth visiting. For food, the port area has seafood restaurants with terrace seating overlooking the water. If you depart from Cabopino, you are next to the Artola dunes and a naturist beach that is quiet in the evening. If you depart from Benalmádena, you have the marina restaurants and the cable car up to Mount Calamorro.

The sunset cruise itself ends around 10 pm in summer, so you have time for a late dinner at one of the chiringuitos on the beach. The crew will usually recommend a place nearby. If you are staying in Fuengirola, a taxi from Cabopino or Benalmádena back to your hotel costs about EUR 10 to EUR 15.

Why book through BoatHire24 rather than direct

BoatHire24 aggregates catamarans from multiple operators, so you see the options side by side. You avoid the language barrier, the unclear pricing, and the risk of a boat being cancelled because the operator overbooked. The site shows real availability, real photos, and real prices in EUR. You pay a deposit by card, and the balance is paid to the skipper on the day, so you are not out the full amount if something goes wrong.

BoatHire24 also covers the whole Costa del Sol, not just Fuengirola. If you decide you want a sunset cruise from Puerto Banús or Estepona instead, you can find it on the same site with the same booking process. The customer service team is based in Marbella and knows the local operators personally. That means fewer surprises and more time watching the sun go down.

What the sunset route looks like from Fuengirola

The standard sunset route from Cabopino takes you west along the coast past the Fuengirola beachfront. You pass the Sohail Castle on the hill, then the marina, then the long stretch of sand that runs all the way to the Mijas Costa. The skipper will anchor about 500 metres offshore, facing the coast, so you watch the sun drop behind the Mijas mountains. From Benalmádena the route goes east first, past the marina and the Torre Bermeja lighthouse, then turns west towards Fuengirola. The total distance covered is about 5 to 8 nautical miles, depending on how much the skipper motors versus sails. The boat moves slowly, around 4 to 6 knots, which is exactly what you want for a sunset trip.

How the light changes during a Fuengirola sunset

The golden hour starts about 60 minutes before the sun hits the horizon. The light turns warm, the sea goes glassy, and the white hull of the catamaran picks up a pink tint. In the final 15 minutes the sky goes through a sequence that locals call the Costa del Sol palette: orange, magenta, deep purple, then a dark blue that lasts another 20 minutes after the sun is gone. The best spot on the boat is the forward trampoline net, where you lie flat and watch the whole thing without any rigging in the way. If you are on a flybridge catamaran, the upper deck gives you a 360-degree view that includes the lights coming on in Fuengirola and the mountains behind.

Why a catamaran is better than a motor yacht for sunset

A catamaran has two hulls and a wide beam, which means it does not roll when anchored. A motor yacht of the same length will rock side to side in any swell, which can make the drinks slide and the less stable passengers queasy. The catamaran's deck space is also bigger. A 40-foot cat has about the same usable deck area as a 55-foot motor yacht, so you are not cramped even with a full group. The low freeboard on a catamaran means you are closer to the water, which makes the sunset feel more immersive. The only downside is speed: a catamaran motors at 6 to 8 knots, while a RIB or speedboat can get you out to the sunset spot in 10 minutes. But speed is not the point of a sunset cruise.

What the drinks and food actually look like

On shared sunset cruises the welcome drink is usually a glass of cava or a soft drink. Some operators include a small platter of olives, almonds, and manchego cheese. Private charters let you bring your own catering, and the skipper will usually have a cooler with ice. If you want a full dinner on board, you can arrange it through BoatHire24 for an extra EUR 25 to EUR 40 per person. The catering comes from local restaurants in Cabopino or Benalmádena and includes things like grilled prawns, jamón ibérico, and paella. The boat has a small galley with a fridge and a sink, but no oven, so the food is cold or pre-cooked. For a proper hot meal, book a charter that includes a stop at a beach chiringuito, but that adds an hour to the trip.

What happens if the weather is bad

The skipper makes the call on the day. If the wind is above 20 knots or there is a thunderstorm forecast, the cruise gets cancelled or rescheduled. You get a full refund or a free date change. The Costa del Sol has about 320 sunny days a year, so cancellations are rare. The most common issue is the Levante wind in July and August, which can create a chop in the afternoon but usually drops by sunset. The skipper will check the wind forecast and the swell report before departure. If the conditions are marginal, the cruise goes ahead but stays closer to the coast, where the water is flat. You can check the weather on the day by calling the BoatHire24 team, who will have spoken to the skipper.

How to get to Cabopino and Benalmádena from Fuengirola

Cabopino marina is a 10-minute drive from Fuengirola town centre. You take the A-7 motorway east, exit at Cala de Mijas, and follow the signs to the port. Parking at Cabopino is free in the dirt lot outside the marina, or EUR 5 for the covered car park. Benalmádena Marina is a 15-minute drive west on the A-7, exit at Arroyo de la Miel. Parking at Benalmádena costs EUR 2 per hour and gets busy on summer weekends. If you are staying in Fuengirola without a car, a taxi from the town centre to Cabopino costs about EUR 8 to EUR 12, and to Benalmádena about EUR 12 to EUR 15. The bus line M-120 runs between Fuengirola and Benalmádena every 20 minutes and costs EUR 1.80.

What to do if you miss the sunset cruise

If you arrive late at the marina, call the skipper directly using the number on your confirmation. Most skippers will wait 10 to 15 minutes, but they will not delay the whole group. If you miss the departure, you lose the deposit. BoatHire24 will try to rebook you on another cruise the same week if one is available, but there is no guarantee. To avoid this, aim to arrive at the marina 20 minutes before the scheduled departure. That gives you time to find the boat, use the toilet, and settle in. The meeting point is usually the fuel dock or the main pier, and the skipper will be wearing a BoatHire24 polo shirt or holding a sign.
