faqs.a: No. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you do not need any licence. You can also hire a licence-free day boat (up to 15 hp) from some ports, but those are rare and smaller.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest boat hire option?
faqs.a: The cheapest option is a half-day RIB or speedboat hire, starting from around EUR 400. Licence-free day boats start from around EUR 200 for a half day. Prices vary by season and port.

faqs.q: How many people can a boat hold?
faqs.a: It depends on the boat. RIBs typically hold 6-8 people, motor yachts 8-12, catamarans 10-20, and superyachts up to 30 or more. Check the boat profile for maximum capacity.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and drink?
faqs.a: Yes, you can bring your own. Most boats have a fridge, ice box, and sometimes a barbecue. You can also order a catering package when you book. The skipper will not serve it unless you pay for crew.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.a: The skipper will assess the conditions on the day. If it is unsafe, the charter will be rescheduled or cancelled with a full refund. You are not charged for weather cancellations.

faqs.q: Is the Costa del Sol as good as Santorini for a boat trip?
faqs.a: It is different but equally good. You get more space, fewer crowds, lower prices, and a longer coastline to explore. The water is warm, the scenery is beautiful, and the sunsets are impressive. It is a solid alternative.

title: Boat Hire In Cannes
metaDescription: Book boat hire in Cannes with a licensed skipper. Motor yachts, catamarans, RIBs from EUR 450. Departure ports: Cannes, Antibes, Nice. Instant online booking.
h1: Boat Hire in Cannes: Yacht & Catamaran Charters with Skipper
intro:
You want boat hire in Cannes, but the options are a blur of glossy brochures and hidden fees. We get it. Cannes is the French Riviera’s show-off sibling: the red-carpet crowd, the superyachts, the EUR 20 cocktails. But hiring a boat here doesn’t have to be a money pit. At BoatHire24, we connect you with skippered boats from Cannes, Antibes, and Nice for a day on the water that actually makes sense. No skipper license needed, no surprises, just a boat that fits your crew and your wallet.

Whether you want a RIB for a quick blast to the Lérins Islands, a motor yacht for a glamorous cruise past the Palais des Festivals, or a catamaran for a lazy afternoon with drinks, we’ve got the lot. Prices start from around EUR 450 for a half-day on a 6-metre RIB, and go up to price on request for a 30-metre superyacht. All boats include a licensed skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. You just turn up, step aboard, and let someone else do the steering.
bodyHtml:
What’s Included in a Cannes Boat Hire

Every boat hire through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters. That means no paperwork, no stress about anchoring, and no worrying about weather forecasts. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety briefings. Fuel is included in the price for standard cruising distances (usually up to 30 nautical miles per day). Insurance is also covered, so you’re not liable for damage beyond a standard deposit (typically EUR 500 to EUR 2,000, refundable). Onboard you’ll find life jackets, a first aid kit, and basic safety equipment required by French maritime law. Some boats also include snorkelling gear, a cooler, or a Bluetooth speaker. Check the individual listing for specifics.

Departure Ports for Cannes Boat Hire

You can depart from several ports along the Côte d’Azur. The most popular is Port Pierre Canto in Cannes itself, right next to the Palais des Festivals and the Croisette. It’s a large marina with plenty of parking (paid) and easy access to the bay. Port de Cannes (Vieux Port) is smaller but closer to the old town and the Marché Forville. From Antibes, about 20 minutes east, you have Port Vauban, one of the largest marinas in Europe. It’s a good choice if you want to explore the Cap d’Antibes or head towards Nice. Port de Nice is further east, about 40 minutes by road from Cannes, and offers direct access to Villefranche-sur-Mer and the Baie des Anges. Each port has its own vibe and proximity to different cruising grounds. We recommend choosing based on where you’re staying and what you want to see.

Types of Boats Available for Hire in Cannes

The range is broad. Motor yachts from 8 to 20 metres are the classic choice: fast, stable, and with plenty of deck space for sunbathing. A 12-metre motor yacht can seat 8 to 10 people and costs from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day. Catamarans are wider and more stable, ideal for groups who want to move around without feeling seasick. A 14-metre catamaran fits 12 guests and starts at EUR 1,800 for a full day. Sailing yachts are quieter and more eco-friendly, but slower. A 12-metre sailing yacht with a skipper costs from EUR 900 for a half-day. RIBs and speedboats are the budget option: 6 to 8 metres, seating 6 to 8 people, from EUR 450 for a half-day. They’re perfect for a quick trip to the islands or a water sports session. Fishing boats are available too, usually 7 to 9 metres with basic fishing gear. Prices start at EUR 600 for a half-day. Superyachts over 24 metres are available on request, with prices starting at EUR 8,000 per day. For a full list, see our boat search page.

Popular Itineraries from Cannes

A typical half-day trip (4 hours) from Cannes heads to the Lérins Islands: Île Sainte-Marguerite and Île Saint-Honorat. Sainte-Marguerite has a small beach, a fort, and pine forests. Saint-Honorat is quieter, with a monastery and vineyards. The crossing takes about 20 minutes from Cannes. For a full day (8 hours), you can go east to the Cap d’Antibes, stop for lunch at a beach restaurant in Juan-les-Pins, then cruise past the Billionaire’s Quay in Antibes. Alternatively, head west to Théoule-sur-Mer and the red rocks of the Esterel Massif, where the water is clear and the cliffs are dramatic. If you want a longer trip, you can go to Saint-Tropez (about 2.5 hours from Cannes by fast boat) or Monaco (1.5 hours). These require a full-day booking and extra fuel costs may apply. Dolphins are occasionally spotted near the Lérins Islands, especially in spring and autumn.

Pricing and What Affects the Cost

Prices vary by boat size, type, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 6-metre RIB costs from EUR 450. A half-day on a 10-metre motor yacht starts at EUR 900. Full-day rates are roughly double the half-day rate. Superyachts are price on request. Peak season is July and August, when prices can be 20% to 30% higher. June and September are shoulder months with lower rates and still good weather (25°C to 28°C water temperature). May and October are cheaper but cooler (20°C to 23°C). Weekends are more expensive than weekdays. Some operators charge extra for fuel beyond 30 nautical miles, or for additional crew like a hostess or chef. Always check the cancellation policy: most require 48 hours’ notice for a full refund. Deposits are usually refunded within 7 days after the charter, minus any damage.

Who Is Cannes Boat Hire For?

Cannes boat hire works for couples, families, groups of friends, and corporate events. Couples often choose a small motor yacht or a sailing yacht for a romantic sunset cruise. Families with kids prefer catamarans or RIBs because of the stability and space. Groups of 8 to 12 people usually go for a motor yacht or catamaran with a water slide or paddleboard. Corporate groups book superyachts for client entertainment or team-building. Solo travellers can join a shared charter if available, but most boats are private. If you’re planning a wedding proposal, a birthday party, or a networking event, many operators can arrange catering, decorations, or a photographer. Just mention it when you book.

How to Book Boat Hire in Cannes

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter Cannes as the departure port, select your date and group size, and browse available boats. Each listing shows photos, specifications, price, and cancellation policy. You can request a quote or book directly online. Payment is by credit card or bank transfer. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance during summer, and 1 week in shoulder seasons. Last-minute bookings (within 48 hours) are possible but limited. After booking, you’ll receive a confirmation with the skipper’s contact details and meeting point. On the day, arrive 15 minutes early at the port. The skipper will greet you, do a safety briefing, and you’re off. For more tips, read our blog on what to bring and what to expect.

Weather and Best Time for a Boat Trip

The best months for boat hire in Cannes are June to September, when the weather is warm (25°C to 30°C air temperature) and the sea is calm. July and August are the hottest and busiest, with sea temperatures around 26°C. May and October are cooler but still pleasant, with fewer crowds and lower prices. The Mistral wind can blow in spring and autumn, causing choppy seas, but skippers will advise if it’s safe to go out. In winter (November to March), most boats are not available for hire, and the water is too cold for swimming (below 18°C). If you’re flexible, aim for June or September for the best balance of weather and price.

Local Tips for Your Cannes Boat Hire

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses. The sun on the water is intense even in spring. Pack a swimsuit and a towel if you plan to swim. Most boats have a small fridge, so you can bring your own drinks and snacks, but many operators offer catering options (EUR 20 to EUR 50 per person for a lunch platter). If you’re prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure. The skipper can suggest anchor spots away from the crowds, like the Calanque d’Anthéor or the Baie de la Figueirette. For a truly memorable experience, book a sunset cruise from 6pm to 9pm. The light on the Esterel cliffs is stunning, and you’ll see Cannes lit up from the water.

Why Choose Cannes for Your Boat Hire

Cannes sits right in the middle of the French Riviera, which gives you access to some of the best cruising grounds in the Mediterranean. The bay is sheltered by the Lérins Islands, so the sea is usually calm even when other parts of the coast get choppy. You can leave from Port Pierre Canto and be at the islands in 15 minutes, or head east to Antibes in 30. The water is clear enough to see the seabed at 10 metres depth, especially near the Esterel Massif. If you want a day trip that feels like a proper escape, Cannes is hard to beat. The marina facilities are modern, with fuel docks, water, and electricity at every berth. Parking at Port Pierre Canto costs around EUR 25 for a full day, but there’s a public car park under the Palais des Festivals for EUR 15.

Specific Boats You Can Hire in Cannes

To give you a concrete idea, here are some real examples from the BoatHire24 fleet. A Jeanneau 8-metre motor yacht seats 6 people, has a small cabin, and costs from EUR 700 for a half-day. A Beneteau 12-metre sailing yacht seats 8, has a galley and two cabins, and costs from EUR 950 for a half-day. A Lagoon 14-metre catamaran seats 12, has a flybridge and a trampoline net at the bow, and costs from EUR 1,900 for a full day. A Zodiac 7-metre RIB with a 250 hp engine seats 8, hits 40 knots, and costs from EUR 500 for a half-day. A Fishing boat like the Quicksilver 7.5-metre seats 6, includes basic rods and tackle, and costs from EUR 650 for a half-day. For a superyacht, the 30-metre Lady Lola sleeps 10 guests in 5 cabins, has a jacuzzi and a beach club, and costs from EUR 15,000 per day. Prices vary by date and operator, so check the listing for exact rates.

What to Do During Your Cannes Boat Trip

Most people use the boat as a base for swimming, sunbathing, and eating. The Lérins Islands have several anchorages where you can drop the hook and jump in. The water is usually 5 to 10 metres deep, clear, and calm. If you want a beach, head to Plage de la Figueirette near Théoule-sur-Mer, a small sandy cove surrounded by red cliffs. For lunch, you can moor at a restaurant with a buoy, like La Plage du Château on Île Sainte-Marguerite (booking required, around EUR 50 per person for a fixed menu). Alternatively, bring a picnic and anchor off the Cap d’Antibes. If you want to explore on foot, the skipper can drop you at the port of Saint-Honorat, where you can visit the monastery and buy wine from the monks. For a longer trip, you can go to the Gorges du Verdon by boat, but that’s a 4-hour cruise from Cannes, so you’d need a full-day booking and a fast boat.

Cost Breakdown for a Typical Cannes Boat Hire

Here’s a realistic budget for a half-day charter for 6 people on a 10-metre motor yacht. The base price is EUR 1,000. Fuel for 30 nautical miles costs around EUR 150, but it’s included in the price for standard cruising. Catering for lunch adds EUR 30 per person, so EUR 180 total. A deposit of EUR 1,000 is refundable. Tips for the skipper are optional but customary at 10% to 15% of the charter fee. So the total outlay is EUR 1,180 plus a refundable deposit. Split six ways, that’s EUR 197 per person. For a full-day trip to Saint-Tropez, add EUR 300 for extra fuel and EUR 50 per person for a restaurant lunch. The extra crew for a hostess costs EUR 200 per day. Always confirm what’s included in the price before booking, as some operators charge extra for fuel beyond 30 NM.

When to Book Your Cannes Boat Hire

June and September are the sweet spots. The weather is warm, the sea is calm, and the crowds are thinner than in July and August. In June, the water temperature is around 22°C, rising to 26°C in August. September is still pleasant, with air temperatures of 25°C and water at 24°C. July and August are peak season, so prices are higher and availability is lower. Book at least 3 weeks in advance for those months. May and October are cheaper but riskier: the Mistral wind can blow, and the water is cooler (18°C to 20°C). If you’re flexible on dates, aim for a weekday in June or September. Weekends in July can be 30% more expensive than weekdays in June. For a sunset cruise, book for 6pm to 9pm in summer, when the sun sets around 9pm.

How to Get to the Departure Ports

If you’re flying in, Nice Côte d’Azur Airport is the closest, about 30 minutes by taxi (EUR 60 to EUR 80) or 45 minutes by train (EUR 10 from Nice to Cannes station). From Cannes station, it’s a 10-minute walk to Port Pierre Canto or a 5-minute taxi (EUR 10). If you’re driving, the A8 motorway has exits for Cannes and Antibes. Parking at Port Pierre Canto costs EUR 25 for a full day, but there’s free street parking 10 minutes away near the Palm Beach area. For Port Vauban in Antibes, parking costs EUR 20 per day. For Port de Nice, parking is EUR 30 per day. If you’re staying in Cannes, most hotels are within walking distance of the port. We recommend arriving 15 minutes before departure to meet the skipper and stow your bags.

What to Bring on Your Cannes Boat Hire

Pack light. A small backpack with sunscreen (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses, and a swimsuit. A towel that dries quickly. A light jacket or windbreaker, even in summer, because the wind can be cool at 25 knots. Waterproof phone case if you want to take photos from the water. Snorkelling mask if you have one (some boats provide them). Drinks and snacks if you’re not ordering catering. A cooler bag with ice packs. Cash for tips and any extras (most places accept cards, but some beach restaurants prefer cash). Seasickness tablets if you’re prone to motion sickness. A book or a speaker for music (the skipper will have a Bluetooth connection). Leave valuables at the hotel; there’s limited storage on smaller boats.

Safety and Skipper Qualifications

Every skipper on BoatHire24 holds a valid French licence (either a permis plaisance or an equivalent international certificate). They have at least 2 years of experience in the local waters. They will do a safety briefing at the start of the trip, covering life jacket locations, emergency procedures, and the route. The boat has a VHF radio, flares, and a first aid kit. In case of bad weather, the skipper has the authority to cancel or shorten the trip. If the sea state exceeds 2 metres waves, most skippers will recommend staying in port. You are not liable for damage beyond the deposit, and the boat is insured for third-party liability. If you have any medical conditions, inform the skipper before departure. Children must wear life jackets at all times on deck, and the skipper will provide appropriate sizes.

title: Luxury Motor Yacht Charter
metaDescription: Book a luxury motor yacht charter in Marbella and Costa del Sol. Skipper included, premium yachts from Puerto Banús. Compare prices and book online with BoatHire24.
h1: Luxury Motor Yacht Charter on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You want a luxury motor yacht charter on the Costa del Sol. You want to skip the crowds, the queues, and the hassle. BoatHire24 connects you directly with licensed skippers and owners of premium motor yachts in Marbella, Puerto Banús, and beyond. Every charter includes a professional skipper, so you just turn up, relax, and enjoy.

Think crystal-clear coves, champagne at sunset, and the Mediterranean stretching out in front of you. Whether it's a 40-foot Sunseeker for a day trip or a 100-foot superyacht for a week, we've got the options. No hidden fees, no fluff. Just a straight-up booking process and a boat that delivers.
bodyHtml:
What a Luxury Motor Yacht Charter Actually Includes

When you book a luxury motor yacht charter through BoatHire24, you get more than just a boat. You get a full package designed for zero stress. Here's what's standard:

  • Skipper included: Every charter comes with a licensed, experienced skipper. They know the coast, the weather, and the best spots. You don't need a licence or any experience.
  • Fuel and port fees: Most charters include fuel for a standard day's cruising (typically 6-8 hours) and marina fees. Check the listing for specifics, but it's usually covered.
  • Insurance: Fully insured for passengers and the vessel. You're covered.
  • Snorkelling gear, paddleboards, toys: Many yachts come with inflatable toys, snorkel masks, even jet skis (extra cost). Ask when booking.
  • Crew (optional): For larger yachts, you can add a stewardess or chef. Prices vary, but expect from around EUR 200 per day extra.

What's not included? Food and drink (you can bring your own or pre-order catering), and tips for the crew (customary 10-15 percent of the charter fee). Some charters also charge extra for overnight stays or extended cruising beyond the standard area.

Departure Ports: Where Your Charter Begins

The Costa del Sol has several key marinas for luxury motor yacht charters. Your choice of departure port affects the cruising grounds and the vibe. Here are the main ones:

  • Puerto Banús, The glitziest option. Superyacht central, with designer shops and flashy restaurants. From here, you're minutes from Cala del Faro and the Marbella coastline.
  • Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), More laid-back than Banús, but still upscale. Good for accessing the eastern coast towards Cabopino and Calahonda.
  • Cabopino, Smaller, quieter marina near the Artola dunes. Ideal if you want to avoid the crowds and head straight to the coves like Cala del Moral.
  • Estepona, A charming Andalusian town with a well-equipped marina. Great for trips towards the Strait of Gibraltar and dolphin spotting.
  • Sotogrande, Exclusive, residential marina near the border with Gibraltar. Polo fields, golf courses, and access to the open sea quickly.
  • Benalmádena, Larger marina with plenty of boat options. Close to Málaga airport and the Nerja caves (a longer cruise, but doable).

Each port has its own character. If you want the full VIP experience, start from Puerto Banús. If you prefer something more understated, try Cabopino or Estepona. Your skipper will advise on the best route based on weather and your preferences.

Boat Options: What You Can Charter

Luxury motor yachts come in various sizes and styles. Here's a quick guide to what's available on BoatHire24:

  • Motor yachts (40-60 feet): The sweet spot for day charters. Brands like Sunseeker, Princess, and Azimut. Expect flybridge, sun pads, a saloon with AC, and a decent head (toilet). Prices from around EUR 2,500 to EUR 5,000 per day.
  • Catamarans (motor versions): More stable, more space. Often have a flybridge and multiple cabins. Good for groups up to 12. Prices from EUR 3,000 per day.
  • Sailing yachts (with motor assist): If you want the sailing experience but with luxury, some large sailing yachts have powerful engines. Less common for pure luxury charters, but available.
  • RIBs and speedboats: Not strictly luxury, but some high-end RIBs (like Ribeye or Zodiac) with powerful outboards offer a sporty luxury experience. Prices from EUR 800 per day.
  • Superyachts (80+ feet): The top tier. Full crew, jacuzzi, helipad, the works. Price on request, but start from EUR 15,000 per day.

All boats are maintained to commercial standards and inspected regularly. You can filter by length, price, and amenities on our search page.

Pricing Guidance: What to Expect

Pricing for a luxury motor yacht charter varies hugely based on boat size, age, season, and duration. Here's a rough guide to avoid sticker shock:

  • Day charter (6-8 hours): EUR 2,500 to EUR 10,000 for a standard motor yacht. Superyachts can be EUR 20,000+.
  • Half-day (4 hours): Usually 60-70 percent of the full-day rate.
  • Overnight or multi-day: Expect a daily rate plus overnight fees (mooring, crew overtime). Often 20-30 percent discount on the daily rate for longer bookings.
  • Seasonal variation: July and August are peak, prices can be 30-50 percent higher than May or September. June and September offer good weather and lower prices.
  • Extras: Catering (from EUR 50 per person for a lunch spread), jet ski rental (EUR 300-500 per day), port taxes for certain marinas (e.g., Gibraltar).

Always confirm what's included before booking. BoatHire24 shows the base price and any mandatory extras clearly. If you see a price that seems too good to be true, it probably is, check the fine print.

Best Time of Year for a Luxury Motor Yacht Charter

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 days of sunshine a year. But the sea conditions vary. Here's the breakdown:

  • May-June: Air temps 22-28 degrees C, sea temps 18-22 degrees C. Less wind, calm seas. Ideal for cruising. Prices moderate.
  • July-August: Peak heat (30-35 degrees C). Sea temps 24-26 degrees C. Busy ports, but perfect for swimming. Higher prices, book well in advance.
  • September-October: Air temps 25-30 degrees C, sea still warm (22-24 degrees C). Fewer crowds, lower prices. Still great for swimming.
  • November-April: Cooler (15-20 degrees C), windier. Some days are fine for cruising, but swimming is limited. Prices drop significantly. Many boats are in for maintenance.

For a luxury motor yacht charter, the sweet spot is late May to early June or September to early October. You get good weather, fewer boats on the water, and better availability. If you want the party vibe, July and August are your months, just expect to pay more and book months ahead.

How to Book Your Luxury Motor Yacht Charter on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Here's the process:

  1. Browse or search: Use our search page to filter by port, boat type, size, and price. You can also browse by category.
  2. Check availability: Each listing shows a calendar. Pick your date and duration. Most boats require at least 48 hours notice.
  3. Send an enquiry: You don't pay upfront. Send a message with your preferred date, group size, and any special requests. The owner or skipper responds within a few hours.
  4. Confirm and pay deposit: Once you agree on the price and itinerary, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50 percent) to secure the booking. The balance is due on the day.
  5. Enjoy: On the day, you meet at the port, meet the skipper, and head out. Bring sunscreen, swimwear, and your camera.

We recommend booking at least 2-3 weeks in advance for summer dates. For superyachts, a month or more is standard. If you need help choosing, our team can advise, just use the contact form.

Who Is a Luxury Motor Yacht Charter For

This isn't for everyone. But if you fit any of these profiles, it's worth it:

  • Celebrations: Birthdays, anniversaries, proposals. The skipper can help with a special moment, just let them know.
  • Corporate events: Client entertainment, team building, product launches. Many yachts have Wi-Fi and AV systems.
  • Families: A private charter means no crowds, safe swimming, and space for kids. Many boats have child-friendly features.
  • Couples: Romantic sunset cruises, private dinners on deck. Some yachts offer overnight stays for two.
  • Groups of friends: Day trips with music, swimming, and good food. Maximum passenger numbers vary by boat (usually 10-12 for motor yachts).

If you're looking for a party boat with loud music and unlimited drinks, a luxury motor yacht might feel too formal. Consider a RIB or a smaller speedboat instead. But if you want comfort, style, and a professional crew, this is the way to go.

Local Highlights: What to See on Your Charter

The Costa del Sol coastline is packed with spots worth visiting. Your skipper will have suggestions, but here are some favourites:

  • Puerto Banús and the Marbella coast: Cruise past the mega yachts and celebrity villas. Stop at Cala del Faro for a swim.
  • Río Verde: A small river mouth near Marbella where you can anchor and swim. Calm waters, good for lunch.
  • Estepona old town: From the sea, you get a view of the whitewashed houses. You can dock at the marina and explore.
  • Strait of Gibraltar: A longer trip (2-3 hours from Estepona or Sotogrande). Dolphin and whale watching is almost guaranteed. The currents can be strong, so only with an experienced skipper.
  • Nerja caves: A full-day trip from Benalmádena or Marbella. Combine a cruise with a visit to the caves (accessible from the shore).
  • La Concha mountain backdrop: The iconic peak behind Marbella. From the sea, it's a stunning photo op.

Your skipper will tailor the route to your preferences and the day's conditions. If you want to maximise swimming time, choose a route with multiple coves and calm anchorages.

Why Book Through BoatHire24

We're a marketplace, not a broker. That means you see real boats, real prices, and real availability. No middleman markup. Our skippers are licensed, insured, and vetted. We don't take your money until you confirm the booking, and we're here to help if anything goes wrong.

We also have a blog with guides on the best coves, weather tips, and boat etiquette. Read it before you go to get the most out of your day.

If you're ready to book, start by browsing our listings. If you have questions, BoatHire24 is your first stop for luxury motor yacht charters in Marbella and the Costa del Sol.

What to Expect on Board a 50-Foot Motor Yacht

Take a typical 50-foot Sunseeker or Princess from Puerto Banús. You step onto the aft deck, a teak-floored area with a U-shaped sofa and a table for lunch. Inside, the saloon has leather seating, a galley with a fridge and ice maker, and air conditioning that works even in August. Up on the flybridge, there's a second helm station, more sun pads, and a bimini for shade. Below deck, you find two or three cabins with en-suite heads, though for a day charter you probably won't use them. The bow has a large sun pad where you can stretch out while the skipper navigates past La Concha mountain. Top speed is around 28-32 knots, but cruising speed is a comfortable 18-22 knots, which means you can cover 30 nautical miles in under two hours. That's enough to reach the coves near Cala del Faro or head west towards Estepona.

How the Skipper Shapes Your Day

Your skipper isn't just a driver. They know the local conditions, like the Poniente and Levante winds that can pick up in the afternoon. On a typical day from Marbella Marina, the skipper will check the forecast, decide which side of the coast is calmer, and adjust the route accordingly. If the wind is light, you might head east towards Cabopino and the Artola dunes. If it's stronger, west towards Estepona and the shelter of the harbour. Skippers also know the best spots for lunch. Many will recommend anchoring near the Río Verde, where the water is flat and there's a beach club that delivers food to your boat. They'll also handle the paperwork, port entry, and any radio communication. You just sit back and decide where to swim next.

Cost Comparison: Day Charter Versus Overnight Charter

A day charter from around EUR 2,500 might feel steep, but compare it to an overnight charter. Suppose you want to cruise from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande, spend the night, and return the next day. The daily rate for a 55-foot motor yacht might be EUR 3,500. For two days, that's EUR 7,000, plus overnight fees of around EUR 200-400 for marina berthing, plus crew overtime of EUR 150-200 per night. Total around EUR 7,800 to EUR 8,000. That gives you two full days on the water, dinner at a marina restaurant, and a morning swim before heading back. If you split that between six people, it's about EUR 1,300 each. For a day charter with the same group, it's around EUR 600 each. The overnight version offers more value if you want a proper mini-holiday rather than a single-day trip.

What to Pack for a Luxury Motor Yacht Charter

Bring soft bags, not hard suitcases, because storage on a yacht is limited. Pack swimwear, a towel (though some yachts provide them), sunscreen with at least SPF 50, a hat, and sunglasses. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful, even in summer, because the wind at 20 knots can feel cool. Non-slip shoes are recommended for the deck, but many people go barefoot. If you plan to eat on board, bring your own food and drink, or pre-order catering. Most skippers have a cooler with ice. A waterproof phone case is handy for photos near the water. And if you're prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure, even if the sea looks flat, the swell can be deceptive.

The Best Coves for Swimming and Lunch Stops

The Costa del Sol has several coves that are perfect for a luxury motor yacht charter. Cala del Faro, just west of Puerto Banús, is a small cove with clear water and a backdrop of cliffs. It's sheltered from the east wind, so it's often calm. Cala del Moral, near Cabopino, is another option with sandy patches and rocky outcrops. For a longer stop, head to the area off Estepona, where the water is deeper and cleaner, and you can see the old town from the sea. If you want a beach club experience, anchor near the Nikki Beach or Ocean Club in Marbella, where you can take a tender to the shore. Your skipper will know which spots are busy and which are quiet, and can adjust based on your preference for solitude or socialising.

How to Choose Between a Motor Yacht and a Catamaran

Motor yachts are faster and more luxurious in a traditional sense, with sleek lines and plush interiors. Catamarans, even motor catamarans, offer more deck space and stability. On a 45-foot catamaran, you have a wide aft deck, a flybridge with seating for 12, and a saloon that opens onto the back. The motion at anchor is less, so if anyone in your group gets queasy, a catamaran is better. Speed is lower, around 15-20 knots, but you don't need speed for a relaxing day. Prices for a motor catamaran start around EUR 3,000 per day, similar to a motor yacht of the same length. The trade-off is style versus space. If you want to impress clients with a sleek profile, go motor yacht. If you want to spread out with friends, go catamaran.

What Happens if the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is generally stable, but the Levante wind can blow from the east at 20-30 knots, creating choppy seas. If the forecast shows strong winds, your skipper will suggest a sheltered route, such as staying close to the coast or heading into a marina early. Most charters include a weather clause. If the skipper deems it unsafe, you can reschedule without penalty, or in some cases, cancel with a full refund. If the weather is marginal, you might still go out but stick to the lee of the coast. Always check the forecast before your booking and stay flexible. In July and August, the risk is low, but in spring and autumn, afternoon storms can develop. Your skipper will monitor conditions and keep you informed.

Why You Should Book a Luxury Motor Yacht Charter for a Proposal

Proposing on a yacht is a cliche for a reason, it works. The setting is private, the backdrop is the Mediterranean, and the skipper can help with timing. Many skippers are happy to anchor at a scenic spot, like Cala del Faro at sunset, and give you a moment alone on the bow. Some yachts have a sound system for music, and you can arrange for champagne and flowers. The cost is the same as a regular charter, but you might want to add a photographer or videographer, which costs from around EUR 300 extra. Book at least three weeks ahead and tell the skipper your plan. They'll keep the crew discreet and make sure everything runs smoothly. Just don't propose during a rough crossing, save it for when the engine is off and the anchor is down.

h1: Yacht Rental Marina del Rey: Your Costa del Sol Escape
intro:
If you typed 'yacht rental Marina del Rey' into Google, you were probably thinking of the famous marina in Los Angeles. Fair enough, it has its charms. But here on the Costa del Sol, we have our own Marina del Rey moment waiting for you, and it comes with better weather, fewer queues, and a cold beer for less than a tenner. We are BoatHire24, and we connect you with private yachts, catamarans, and speedboats that depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. Every single charter includes a licensed skipper, so you can sit back and enjoy the Mediterranean without worrying about docking or navigation.

Whether you want a half-day cruise along the coast, a sunset party for ten, or a week-long exploration of the Strait of Gibraltar, we have the boat and the local knowledge. Our fleet ranges from 8-metre RIBs to 30-metre superyachts. Prices start from around EUR 500 for a half-day on a small motor yacht, and go up to EUR 15,000 for a full-day superyacht charter with a crew. You do not need a boating licence for any of our rentals. We handle the paperwork, you handle the sunscreen.
bodyHtml:
Why Search for Yacht Rental Marina del Rey? Here Is the Better Option

You searched for 'yacht rental Marina del Rey' because you want a luxurious, hassle-free day on the water. The original Marina del Rey in California is a fine place, but the Costa del Sol offers a similar vibe with a fraction of the cost and a lot more sunshine. Our marinas are packed with sleek motor yachts and catamarans, and the water temperature hits 24 degrees Celsius in summer. You can anchor off Cala del Faro, swim in clear coves, and watch the sun set behind La Concha mountain. The best part: you do not need a licence. Every charter includes a local skipper who knows the best spots for dolphin watching and where to find the quietest anchorage.

What Is Included in Every Yacht Rental

When you book through BoatHire24, the price covers the boat, the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and basic insurance. Some charters also include a hostess, paddleboards, snorkelling gear, and a welcome bottle of cava. You can add catering, a DJ, or a photographer at extra cost. The skipper speaks English and Spanish, and they handle all docking and safety briefings. You are responsible for your own food and drinks unless you order a catering package. Most boats have a fridge, a sound system, and a shaded cockpit. For larger groups, catamarans offer more deck space and a trampoline at the bow for lounging.

Departure Ports: Where Your Yacht Rental Starts

We operate from six ports along the Costa del Sol. Puerto Banús is the most glamorous, with superyachts and designer boutiques. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a short walk from the old town and offers a mix of sporty and luxury boats. Cabopino is quieter, ideal for families who want a relaxed start. Estepona Marina is close to the charming old town and the port for fishing trips. Sotogrande is an exclusive estate with a world-class marina, perfect for longer charters. Benalmádena is a lively port with plenty of restaurants and a dolphinarium nearby. Each port has free parking for charter guests, and we can arrange transfers from your hotel.

Types of Boats Available for Your Yacht Rental

Our inventory covers five main categories. Motor yachts from 10 to 20 metres are the most popular, offering speed and comfort. Catamarans are wider and more stable, great for families or groups who want to avoid seasickness. Sailing yachts appeal to those who want a quieter, wind-powered experience. RIBs and speedboats are fast and nimble, ideal for water sports and short trips. Fishing boats are equipped with rods and fish finders for serious anglers. Licence-free day boats are small motorboats you can drive yourself if you have a basic certificate, but we still recommend the skipper option for safety. Superyachts over 24 metres come with a full crew including a chef and stewardess.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Rental Marina del Rey

Prices vary by boat size, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht costs from around EUR 500 in low season. A full day (8 hours) on a 15-metre catamaran is from EUR 1,200. A superyacht over 24 metres starts at EUR 8,000 per day and goes up to EUR 20,000 for the largest models. All prices include VAT and the skipper. Fuel for a standard itinerary is included, but extra cruising outside the usual area costs extra. You can pay by bank transfer or credit card, and we require a 50% deposit at booking. Cancellations up to 14 days before the charter are fully refundable.

Best Seasons for Yacht Rental on the Costa del Sol

The peak season is June to September, when the weather is hot and the sea is calm. Air temperatures reach 30 degrees Celsius, and water temperatures are 22-25 degrees. July and August are the busiest, so book at least two weeks ahead. May and October are shoulder months with pleasant conditions and lower prices. April and November can be windy, but you can still get good days for sailing or a short motor. Winter charters (December to March) are possible on larger yachts with enclosed cabins, but the sea can be rough. For dolphin watching in the Strait of Gibraltar, the best months are April to October.

How to Book Your Yacht Rental with BoatHire24

You can browse our fleet on the BoatHire24 homepage and use the search page to filter by port, boat type, price, and capacity. Once you find a boat you like, click 'Request a Quote' and fill in your preferred date, duration, and any special requests. We will respond within 24 hours with a confirmed price and availability. You can also call or WhatsApp us for instant help. After you pay the deposit, we send you a booking confirmation with the skipper's details, meeting point, and a checklist of what to bring. Payment is secure and we use encrypted connections.

Who Should Book a Yacht Rental on the Costa del Sol

This is for anyone who wants a private, flexible day on the water without the crowds of a tour boat. Couples celebrate anniversaries or proposals. Families with kids enjoy swimming stops and beach picnics. Groups of friends book for birthdays, bachelor parties, or just a lazy Sunday. Business clients use charters for corporate events or client entertaining. Solo travellers can join a shared charter if they do not want to rent the whole boat. We do not allow stag or hen parties that involve excessive drinking or rowdy behaviour, but a well-behaved group is welcome.

Local Highlights You Will Experience on Your Charter

From Puerto Banús, you can cruise past the famous yachts and head to Cala del Faro, a secluded cove with a small beach. From Marbella, you see the old town from the sea and the La Concha mountain backdrop. From Estepona, you can sail to the Strait of Gibraltar and spot dolphins, whales, and sometimes orcas. From Sotogrande, you can explore the Guadiaro river estuary. From Benalmádena, you have views of the Fuengirola coastline and the Mijas mountains. For a longer trip, you can charter a superyacht to the Nerja caves, which are visible from the sea, or across to North Africa. The Strait is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a prime spot for marine life.

Read More on Our Blog

For tips on choosing the right boat, packing for a day on the water, and the best anchorages along the coast, visit our blog. We post regularly about local events, weather patterns, and hidden coves. You can also find guides on what to expect from a skipper-led charter and how to save money on your rental.

Why Marina del Rey vs Costa del Sol: A Cost Comparison

You might be wondering what you actually save by choosing the Costa del Sol over Marina del Rey. A half-day charter on a similar-sized motor yacht in California typically costs from EUR 800 to EUR 1,200, not including fuel or gratuity. Here, you pay from around EUR 500 for the same duration, and fuel is included. A full-day catamaran charter in Marina del Rey can hit EUR 2,500 or more. On the Costa del Sol, you get the same for around EUR 1,200. The exchange rate also works in your favour if you are paying in euros. Plus, the skipper is mandatory and included, so you do not need to worry about licensing or insurance. The weather is more predictable too. Marina del Rey gets a marine layer in June that can block the sun until midday. The Costa del Sol averages 320 sunny days per year.

Specific Boat Models You Can Expect to Find

Our fleet includes some well-known models that you might recognise from Mediterranean charter hubs. The Azimut 50 is a popular motor yacht with three cabins and a flybridge, perfect for a group of six. The Lagoon 42 is a catamaran that sleeps eight and has a spacious saloon and a forward trampoline. For speed lovers, the Ribcraft 7.8 with twin 250hp outboards can hit 40 knots and is ideal for a fast trip to the Strait of Gibraltar. The Beneteau Oceanis 46 is a sailing yacht with a shallow draft, letting you anchor close to the beach. Smaller options include the Quicksilver 755 for licence-free day trips with a skipper. Each boat is maintained to RINA or CE standards, and you can request a pre-charter inspection if you want.

Puerto Banús: The Superyacht Hub

If you want the closest experience to Marina del Rey's glamour, Puerto Banús is your port. The marina holds over 900 berths and regularly hosts superyachts over 50 metres. You can start your charter from here and cruise past the Marbella Club Hotel and the Golden Mile. The water depth at the marina entrance is 5 metres, so even large yachts can dock easily. The port has a helipad if you want to arrive by helicopter. The nearby restaurants include a Michelin-starred option for a pre-charter lunch. From Puerto Banús, you can reach Cala del Faro in 20 minutes at cruising speed. The cove has a small sandy beach and clear water ideal for swimming. The skipper will anchor and you can use the paddleboard or snorkel gear if your charter includes it.

Estepona: The Quiet Alternative for Fishing and Dolphin Watching

Estepona Marina is less crowded than Puerto Banús but offers excellent access to the Strait of Gibraltar. The marina has 419 berths and is a 10-minute walk from the old town with its flower-filled streets and tapas bars. Fishing charters depart from here regularly, targeting sea bass, bream, and tuna. The water depth in the marina is 3.5 metres, and the entrance is protected by a breakwater. For dolphin watching, you motor 8 nautical miles south to the Strait. The common species are striped dolphins, common dolphins, and bottlenose dolphins. You might also see pilot whales and, from June to August, orcas hunting tuna. The skipper knows the best spots based on the day's conditions. A half-day fishing charter with all gear included costs from around EUR 600.

Cabopino: The Family-Friendly Port with a Sandy Beach

Cabopino is a small marina with 250 berths and a direct connection to the Artola sand dunes, a protected natural area. The beach is 500 metres from the marina and is less crowded than Marbella's main beaches. The water depth at the marina is 2.5 metres, so it is suitable for smaller yachts and catamarans. From Cabopino, you can cruise east to Cala del Moral or west to the Dunas de Artola. The area is popular for families because the sea is calmer here than near the Strait. You can book a half-day charter from around EUR 400 on a licence-free day boat with a skipper. The marina has a playground and a few casual restaurants. Parking is free and usually available even in August.

Sotogrande: The Exclusive Estate for Longer Charters

Sotogrande is a gated community with a 900-berth marina and a polo club. The atmosphere is more subdued than Puerto Banús, but the facilities are top-tier. The marina has a fuel dock, a chandlery, and a restaurant with a terrace overlooking the water. From Sotogrande, you can sail to the Guadiaro river estuary, a nature reserve with birdwatching opportunities. The river is navigable for about 2 nautical miles at high tide. For longer charters, you can head to Gibraltar, 10 nautical miles south, or across the Strait to Morocco. A full-day charter on a 15-metre motor yacht from Sotogrande starts at around EUR 1,500. The area is less busy than Marbella, so you get more privacy. The marina has a 24-hour security gate, and you can arrange a driver to take you to the nearby Valderrama golf course.

Benalmádena: The Lively Port with Nightlife Options

Benalmádena Marina has 900 berths and is known for its nightlife and entertainment. The marina has a casino, a dolphinarium, and a cable car that goes up to the Calamorro mountain. The water depth at the entrance is 4 metres, and the marina is protected by a breakwater. From Benalmádena, you can cruise to the Fuengirola coastline, where you can anchor off the beach and swim. The port is also close to the Mijas mountains, which you can see from the sea. A half-day charter from Benalmádena costs from around EUR 450 on a 10-metre motor yacht. The marina has plenty of restaurants and bars for an après-charter drink. If you want a party boat, some larger catamarans offer a DJ and a sound system for an extra fee.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group Size

For a couple, a 10-metre motor yacht with a cabin and a small galley is enough. For a family of four, a catamaran over 12 metres gives you more deck space and separate cabins. For a group of eight to ten, a 15-metre catamaran or a 17-metre motor yacht works well. For twelve or more, you need a superyacht or a large catamaran over 20 metres. The skipper can advise on the best layout based on your plans. If you want to do water sports, choose a boat with a swim platform and a tender. If you want to dine on board, a catamaran with a large cockpit table is better. The search page on our site allows you to filter by capacity, so you can see only boats that fit your group.

Packing List for Your Yacht Charter

Bring sunscreen with SPF 50, a hat, and sunglasses. The reflection off the water intensifies the sun. Pack a light jacket or a windbreaker because the sea breeze can feel cool at 20 knots. Swimwear and a towel are essential for swimming stops. Non-slip shoes are useful for walking on the deck. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure. The skipper can provide ginger candies or wristbands. Bring your own food and drinks unless you order catering. Most boats have a fridge and a cooler. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper will limit consumption if it affects safety. Do not bring glass bottles on board because broken glass is a hazard. Use plastic or cans instead.

What Happens in Bad Weather

The skipper monitors the weather forecast and will cancel the charter if conditions are unsafe. The Mediterranean can get strong winds in the afternoon, especially in July and August when the Poniente wind blows. If the wind exceeds 25 knots, the skipper may postpone or reroute the trip. You get a full refund if the charter is cancelled due to weather. If the weather is marginal, the skipper can adjust the itinerary to stay in sheltered areas like the Guadiaro river or the lee of the coast. Morning charters are usually calmer than afternoon ones. The best months for calm seas are June and September. July and August can have afternoon winds but they are usually manageable.

How to Save Money on Your Yacht Rental

Book in May or October for lower rates and fewer crowds. Choose a half-day instead of a full day if you just want a quick trip. Smaller boats cost less, and RIBs are the cheapest option for a group of four. Share the cost with friends by booking a catamaran that fits everyone. Avoid the peak weeks of August when prices are highest. Look for last-minute deals on our site if you are flexible with dates. Some boats offer a discount for bookings made more than 30 days in advance. Do not add extras like a hostess or a DJ unless you really need them. You can bring your own food and drinks to save on catering costs. The skipper is included, so you do not need to tip separately, but a small gratuity for good service is appreciated.

intro:
You might be searching for havasu boat rentals expecting Lake Havasu in Arizona, but we are BoatHire24, based in Marbella, Spain. bodyHtml:
Why You Might Be Looking at Havasu Boat Rentals

Lake Havasu is famous for its man-made lake, spring break crowds and the London Bridge. It is a party spot on a boat. If that is what you want, you might be disappointed that we are not there. But if you want the same elements, sun, warm water, a private boat with a skipper, the Costa del Sol delivers. The water temperature hits 24 degrees C in summer, the sun shines 320 days a year and the beaches are dotted with chiringuitos. The main difference is that you are on the Mediterranean Sea, not a lake, so you can cruise along the coast, anchor in coves and spot wildlife.

What a Havasu Boat Rental Includes on the Costa del Sol

Every boat rental through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. You do not need a boating licence. The skipper handles navigation, safety and mooring. You just relax. The typical rental includes fuel for a standard day trip, insurance and a basic safety briefing. Some boats offer a host or hostess for an extra fee. You can bring your own food and drink, or arrange catering through the charter company. Most boats have a sound system, a sun deck and a small kitchen or galley. For a full day, expect to depart around 10am and return by 6pm. Half-day trips are also common.

Ports Where You Can Start Your Rental

You have several departure points along the coast. BoatHire24 lists boats from Puerto Banús (the glitzy marina with designer shops), Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo, central location), Cabopino (smaller, quieter, near the dunes), Estepona (old town charm, good for fishing trips), Sotogrande (upmarket, near Gibraltar) and Benalmádena (family-friendly, with a marina full of restaurants). Each port offers different cruising grounds. From Puerto Banús you can head west to Cala del Faro or east towards Cabopino. From Estepona you can cross the bay to Gibraltar and spot dolphins. From Benalmádena you can visit the Nerja caves by boat, though that is a longer trip.

Boat Options: From RIBs to Superyachts

If you want speed and adrenaline, a RIB or speedboat is your best bet. These are 6 to 10 metres long, with outboard engines that push you to 40 knots. They are ideal for a quick blast to a beach club or a water sports session. For a relaxed day with friends, a motor yacht from 10 to 20 metres gives you a cabin, a flybridge and a sundeck. Catamarans are stable and spacious, good for families or groups who want to avoid seasickness. Sailing yachts offer a quieter, more traditional experience. Fishing boats are equipped with rods and fish finders. Licence-free day boats (under 6 metres and limited power) are available from some ports for those who want to drive themselves, but they are rare on the Costa del Sol. Superyachts over 24 metres are available for VIP events, with prices on request.

Pricing Guidance for Your Trip

Prices vary by boat type, size, season and duration. For a half-day on a RIB, expect from around EUR 250. A full day on a 10-metre motor yacht starts from around EUR 600. Catamarans for a full day start from around EUR 800. Sailing yachts are similar. Fishing boats start from around EUR 400 for a half-day. Superyachts are price on request, but you can expect EUR 2,000 to EUR 10,000 per day. These prices include the skipper and fuel for a standard itinerary. Extra costs may include a host, food and drinks, mooring fees at beach clubs or a longer cruising range. Always confirm what is included before booking. You can browse current listings on our search page.

Best Time of Year for a Boat Rental

The Costa del Sol has a long season. From May to October, the weather is warm, the sea is calm and the water is swimmable. July and August are peak months, with higher prices and more crowds. September and October offer the same conditions with fewer people. April and November can be pleasant, but the water is cooler (around 18 degrees C) and you might get a breeze. December to March is low season; many boats are in maintenance, but some operators still run trips on good days. If you want to guarantee a rental, book between May and September. For a quieter experience, try late September or early October.

How to Book a Havasu-Style Boat Rental

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24, select your port and date, and browse available boats. Each listing shows photos, specifications, capacity and price. You can send an enquiry or book directly through the platform. The charter company will confirm availability and send you a contract. Payment is usually by bank transfer or card. You will need to provide a deposit, typically 30 to 50 percent. The balance is due on the day. Cancellation policies vary, so read the terms. For last-minute bookings, some operators accept bookings up to 24 hours in advance, but availability is limited. If you have a specific boat in mind, book at least two weeks ahead in summer.

Who Is This For?

This is for anyone who wants a private boat day without the hassle of a licence. It works for couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise, families with children who want a safe, stable catamaran, groups of friends wanting a party boat, corporate teams for a team-building day, fishermen after a catch, and photographers wanting coastal views. It is also for people who have been to Lake Havasu and want a similar experience but in Europe. The Costa del Sol offers the same sun, water and social atmosphere, but with a Spanish twist: tapas, sangria and the scent of pine trees from the mountains.

Local Colour and Landmarks

Puerto Banús is the centre of the action. You can see the La Concha mountain from the marina. The Río Verde flows into the sea near Marbella. Cala del Faro is a quiet cove west of Puerto Banús, perfect for anchoring. Estepona old town has whitewashed houses and flower pots. The Strait of Gibraltar is a dolphin hotspot; you often see pods of common dolphins and pilot whales. If you head east from Benalmádena, you can reach the Nerja caves, though you need a full day. The coast is dotted with beach clubs like Nikki Beach, Ocean Club and La Sala, where you can moor up and have lunch.

What About the Weather and Sea Conditions

The Costa del Sol is known for its microclimate. Summer temperatures average 30 degrees C, with sea breezes. The sea is usually calm in the morning, with a light chop in the afternoon from the Poniente wind. The Levante wind from the east can bring stronger waves, especially near Gibraltar. Skippers monitor conditions and will cancel if it is unsafe. In winter, the sea can be rougher, but many days are still fine for a sheltered cruise. If you are prone to seasickness, choose a catamaran or a calm day. The water is clear, with visibility up to 15 metres in summer.

What to Bring on Your Rental

Bring sunscreen (factor 50), a hat, sunglasses, swimwear, a towel and a light jacket for the evening. Most boats have a fridge and a sound system, so bring your own music and drinks. If you want to eat at a beach club, bring cash or a card. Some beach clubs accept mooring fees of EUR 20 to EUR 50 for a few hours. Do not bring glass bottles on some boats; check with the skipper. If you are fishing, the boat may provide gear, but confirm. For a sunset trip, bring a camera. The views of the coast from the water are stunning.

Why Choose BoatHire24 Over Other Platforms

BoatHire24 focuses exclusively on the Costa del Sol. We know the local operators, the ports and the conditions. Our listings are verified, and we offer direct communication with the charter companies. You are not booking through a faceless aggregator. We also have a blog with tips on the best coves, restaurants and itineraries. If you have questions, you can contact us. We do not charge hidden fees. The price you see is the price you pay, minus any extras you add. We are not Lake Havasu, but we are the next best thing in Europe.

Comparing Lake Havasu to the Costa del Sol: What Changes

Lake Havasu is a freshwater lake with a controlled environment. The Costa del Sol is open sea. That means you get waves, currents and tides. But it also means you can cruise to different towns, anchor in secluded coves and see marine life. The London Bridge is a novelty. The Costa del Sol has Roman ruins, Moorish castles and white villages. If you want a party, Puerto Banús has the same vibe as the Havasu strip, but with yachts instead of houseboats. The water is saltier, so you float more easily. The sun is stronger, so bring more sunscreen. The main difference is that you are not confined to a lake. You can go anywhere along 150 kilometres of coastline.

Specific Itineraries for a Day Trip

From Puerto Banús, a common itinerary is west to Cala del Faro, then to the beach club at La Sala by the Sea in Estepona. That is about 10 nautical miles each way. You can anchor, swim, have lunch and return by late afternoon. From Marbella Marina, head east to Cabopino, a natural dune area with a beach club. That is 8 nautical miles. From Estepona, cross the bay to Gibraltar. That is 15 nautical miles. You can see the Rock, spot dolphins and have lunch in the marina. From Benalmádena, go east to the Nerja caves. That is 25 nautical miles, a full day trip. From Sotogrande, head to the Strait of Gibraltar for whale watching. That is 20 nautical miles. Each itinerary offers different scenery, from rocky cliffs to sandy beaches to bustling marinas.

Fuel Costs and Range

Fuel is included in the standard rental for a typical day trip. But if you want to go further, you may pay extra. A RIB uses about 30 to 50 litres per hour at cruising speed. A motor yacht uses 50 to 150 litres per hour. Diesel is around EUR 1.30 per litre. A typical day trip of 6 hours might use EUR 200 to EUR 600 in fuel, depending on the boat. Catamarans and sailing yachts use much less. If you are on a budget, choose a sailing yacht or a catamaran. The skipper will manage the fuel and advise on range. Most boats have a range of 50 to 100 nautical miles on a full tank, more than enough for a day trip.

Licence-Free Day Boats: A Rare Option

On Lake Havasu, you can rent a houseboat without a licence. On the Costa del Sol, licence-free boats are rare. Spanish law requires a licence for boats over 6 metres or with engines over 15 horsepower. Some operators offer small boats under 6 metres with limited power that you can drive without a licence. These are usually RIBs or small motorboats. They are not common. Most rentals through BoatHire24 include a skipper. If you want to drive yourself, you need an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or a Spanish licence. Check with the operator. For most visitors, the skipper is a bonus: you get a local guide who knows the best spots.

Beach Clubs and Mooring Fees

Many beach clubs along the Costa del Sol allow you to moor your boat for a few hours. You pay a mooring fee, usually EUR 20 to EUR 50, depending on the club and the boat size. Popular clubs include Nikki Beach in Marbella, Ocean Club in Puerto Banús, La Sala in Estepona and Cala del Faro. You can have lunch, swim and use the facilities. Some clubs require a minimum spend on food and drink. Others allow you to just anchor offshore and swim to the beach. The skipper will handle the mooring. You can also anchor in a cove for free. The water is clear and you can jump off the boat. Bring a mask and snorkel.

Wildlife You Might See

The Costa del Sol is rich in marine life. In the Strait of Gibraltar, you can see common dolphins, striped dolphins, pilot whales and even orcas in summer. From Estepona and Sotogrande, dolphin sightings are almost guaranteed. From Benalmádena, you might see sea turtles and rays. In the coves, you can see fish like bream, sea bass and mullet. Birdlife includes gulls, cormorants and sometimes ospreys. The water is clear, so you can see the seabed in shallow areas. If you are lucky, you might see a sunfish or a whale shark, though they are rare. The skipper will know where to go for the best wildlife viewing.

What About Insurance and Safety

Every boat on BoatHire24 is insured. The insurance covers third-party liability and damage to the boat. You are not liable for damage caused by the skipper. You are responsible for your own belongings and for following safety instructions. The skipper will give a safety briefing before departure. Life jackets are provided. The boat has a VHF radio, flares and a first aid kit. In case of bad weather, the skipper will cancel or shorten the trip. You are not charged if the trip is cancelled due to weather. The platform requires operators to have valid insurance and licences. You can ask for proof if you want.

How to Get to the Ports

Puerto Banús is 10 minutes from Marbella town by car. Marbella Marina is in the centre of Marbella. Cabopino is 15 minutes east of Marbella. Estepona is 20 minutes west of Marbella. Sotogrande is 30 minutes west of Estepona. Benalmádena is 15 minutes east of Marbella, near Fuengirola. All ports are accessible by car or taxi. Malaga Airport is 30 minutes from Benalmádena and 45 minutes from Marbella. Gibraltar Airport is 30 minutes from Sotogrande. Most charter companies offer a pick-up service from your hotel or airport for an extra fee. If you are staying in Marbella, you can walk to the marina. Parking is available at all ports, but it can be expensive in summer.

Special Occasions and Events

Boat rentals are popular for birthdays, anniversaries, proposals and corporate events. You can arrange a private chef, a DJ, flowers or a photographer. Some boats have a flybridge for dancing. Catamarans are good for parties because they are stable and have a large deck. Superyachts can host up to 50 guests. For a proposal, the skipper can take you to a quiet cove at sunset. For a corporate event, you can combine a boat trip with a lunch at a beach club. Prices for special events are higher, but you can negotiate. Contact the charter company directly through BoatHire24 for a custom quote.

Environmental Considerations

The Costa del Sol is a protected area. You cannot throw rubbish overboard. The skipper will collect waste and dispose of it at the marina. Some boats have a holding tank for sewage. You should not use single-use plastics. Bring a reusable water bottle. The boat may have a water dispenser. Anchoring is allowed in most coves, but not in protected areas like Cabopino dunes. The skipper will know the rules. If you see marine life, keep a safe distance. Do not feed the dolphins. The Costa del Sol is a popular destination, so the sea can be busy in summer. Respect other boats and swimmers. A clean sea is a better sea for everyone.
