h1: Yacht Rental Dubai: Your Guide to Marbella Alternatives
intro:
You are searching for yacht rental Dubai, but here is the thing: Dubai is a long way from the Costa del Sol, and if you are already in Europe or planning a Spanish holiday, you do not need to fly to the UAE to get a world-class yacht charter. BoatHire24 operates from Marbella, Puerto Banús, and six other ports along the Costa del Sol, offering the same level of luxury, service, and skippered experiences you would expect from Dubai. Think private motor yachts, spacious catamarans, and even superyachts, all with a licensed skipper included. No hidden fees, no unfamiliar regulations. Just the Mediterranean sun, the Rock of Gibraltar, and a cold drink in your hand.

Why consider Marbella over Dubai? For one, the proximity. If you are in the UK, a three-hour flight gets you to Málaga. For another, the variety. You can rent a RIB for a day trip to Cala del Faro, a sailing yacht for a week cruising the coast, or a superyacht for a party off Puerto Banús. And every charter includes a skipper, so you do not need a licence or experience. This page is your practical guide to booking a yacht rental on the Costa del Sol, with all the details you need to make a decision.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Yacht Rental on the Costa del Sol

When you book a yacht rental through BoatHire24, you get a few things that make life easy. First, every charter includes a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a boating licence, you do not need to know how to dock, and you do not need to worry about navigation. The skipper handles everything from mooring to safety briefings. Second, the price typically includes fuel for a standard day trip (usually up to 8 hours and a certain number of nautical miles, depending on the boat). Some charters also include a basic catering package, like water, soft drinks, and ice. Third, you get insurance, life jackets, and all safety equipment. What is not included? Food and premium drinks (though you can order catering), dockage fees if you stop at a marina for lunch, and any extra hours beyond the agreed charter time. Always confirm the inclusions with the boat owner before booking.

Ports of Departure for Your Yacht Rental

BoatHire24 covers six ports along the Costa del Sol, each with its own character. Puerto Banús is the glitzy one: think superyachts, designer shops, and a lively atmosphere. It is the closest you will get to a Dubai-style marina in Europe. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more relaxed, with a mix of fishing boats and leisure craft, and it is a short walk from Marbella old town. Cabopino is a small, charming port near the dunes of Artola, ideal for a quiet day out. Estepona offers a modern marina with easy access to the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can spot dolphins. Sotogrande is an exclusive residential area with a large marina, popular for longer charters. Benalmádena is a family-friendly port with a big marina and plenty of restaurants. Your choice of port affects the scenery, the distance to open water, and the type of boats available. For a luxury yacht rental, Puerto Banús is the obvious pick. For a fishing trip, Estepona or Cabopino might be better.

Types of Boats Available for Rent

The fleet on BoatHire24 is diverse. You can choose from motor yachts (from 8 m to 30 m plus), which are the most common for day charters and parties. They are fast, comfortable, and often come with a flybridge for sunbathing. Catamarans are stable and spacious, perfect for families or groups who want to avoid seasickness. They have a shallow draft, so you can anchor close to beaches. Sailing yachts are for those who want a quieter, more traditional experience. They are slower, but the silence under sail is unbeatable. RIBs and speedboats are small, fast, and great for thrill-seekers or short trips to nearby coves. Fishing boats are equipped with rods, reels, and fish finders, and the skipper often knows the best spots. Licence-free day boats are small motorboats (typically under 6 m) that you can drive yourself without a licence, but they are limited to certain areas. Superyachts are the top tier: over 24 m, with crew, jacuzzis, and all the trimmings. Prices for these are on request, but expect to pay from around EUR 5,000 per day in high season.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Rental in Marbella

Let us talk money. Prices vary wildly based on boat size, type, season, and duration. As a rough guide, a 7 m to 9 m motor boat for a half-day (4 hours) starts from around EUR 300 to EUR 500. A 10 m to 12 m motor yacht for a full day (8 hours) ranges from EUR 800 to EUR 1,500. A 15 m to 20 m luxury motor yacht can be EUR 2,000 to EUR 4,000 per day. Catamarans in the 12 m to 15 m range are similar, often EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 per day. Superyachts over 24 m are price on request, but budget EUR 5,000 to EUR 15,000 per day. These prices usually include the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary (e.g., 30-50 NM), and basic insurance. VAT (10% in Spain) is usually extra. High season (June to September) commands a premium of 20-30% over low season (November to March). Easter and the August peak are the most expensive. For the best value, book in May or October, when the weather is still good but prices are lower. You can compare options on the search page and filter by price, boat type, and port.

Best Seasons for a Yacht Rental on the Costa del Sol

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days a year. The yacht rental season runs from April to October, with the peak in July and August. Summer temperatures average 28-32 degrees C, and the sea water is warm (22-26 degrees C). This is the best time for swimming, sunbathing, and water sports. However, it is also the busiest and most expensive. Spring (April to June) and autumn (September to October) offer pleasant temperatures (20-28 degrees C) and fewer crowds. You might get some wind in spring, which is great for sailing but can make the sea choppy for small boats. Winter (November to March) is quieter, with temperatures around 15-20 degrees C. Some boats are still available, but the sea can be rough, and many restaurants and services are closed. For a reliable, comfortable yacht rental, aim for May, June, or September. If you want to see dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar, the best months are April to October, with peak sightings in summer.

How to Book a Yacht Rental with BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the homepage and use the search bar to enter your dates, preferred port, and boat type. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Each listing includes the boat's size, capacity, amenities, and the skipper's experience. You can send an enquiry directly through the platform. The owner or charter manager will confirm availability and send you a quote. You do not pay anything until you agree on the details. Once you confirm, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) via bank transfer or card, and the balance is due on the day of the charter. Some owners accept PayPal or cash on the day. Make sure you read the cancellation policy: most offer full refund if cancelled 30 days before, 50% if 14 days before, and no refund within 7 days. For last-minute bookings, you can try calling the owner directly (the number is on the listing). Always check the boat's licence and insurance documents before boarding. BoatHire24 verifies all listings, but it is your right to ask.

Who Is a Yacht Rental Suitable For

A yacht rental is not just for millionaires. It works for couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise, families with kids who want a safe day on the water, groups of friends celebrating a birthday or bachelor party, and corporate clients hosting a team event or client meeting. The skipper takes care of the navigation, so you can relax. For families, catamarans are ideal because they are stable and have plenty of space. For parties, motor yachts with a sound system and flybridge are popular. For fishing enthusiasts, there are dedicated fishing boats with gear and a knowledgeable skipper. Even if you have never been on a boat before, you can rent one. The skipper will give a safety briefing and can tailor the itinerary to your interests. Just tell them what you want to do: swim, snorkel, visit a beach, eat at a chiringuito, or just cruise along the coast. It is your day.

Local Highlights You Can Visit on a Yacht Rental

The Costa del Sol coast is packed with interesting spots. From Puerto Banús, you can head west to the Strait of Gibraltar (about 20 NM) to see dolphins and, if you are lucky, whales. From Estepona, you can anchor off the Estepona old town and take a tender to shore for lunch. From Cabopino, you can visit the dunes of Artola and the nudist beach. From Marbella, you can cruise past the La Concha mountain backdrop and stop at Cala del Faro, a quiet cove with a lighthouse. From Sotogrande, you can head to Gibraltar (if you have a passport) or the Río Verde estuary. From Benalmádena, you can go east to Nerja and the famous caves, though that is a longer trip (about 30 NM). Most day charters stay within 10-15 NM of the departure port, so you can combine a few stops. The skipper will have suggestions based on the weather and your preferences. For more ideas, read our blog posts on the best coves and anchorages.

What to Bring and What to Wear on a Yacht Rental

Pack light. Essentials include sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a light jacket or windbreaker (even in summer, the breeze can be cool). Swimwear is a must if you plan to swim. Non-slip shoes are recommended for walking on deck, but many people go barefoot. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The skipper will have a first aid kit, but bring any personal medication. For food and drink, you can bring your own or order a catering package from the charter company. Most boats have a cooler with ice. Alcohol is allowed, but do not overdo it: the skipper is responsible for your safety, and being drunk on a boat is not fun. Also, remember that the sun is stronger on the water, so reapply sunscreen regularly. And bring a camera: the views of the coastline and the mountains are stunning.

Safety and Legal Requirements for Yacht Rental in Spain

In Spain, any boat rented for leisure must comply with the Real Decreto 876/2014. The key requirement is that if the boat is over 6 m in length or has an engine over 15 HP, you need a licence to drive it yourself. However, all charters on BoatHire24 include a licensed skipper, so you are covered. The skipper holds a Professional Skipper licence (Patrón Profesional de Embarcaciones de Recreo) and is responsible for the boat and passengers. They will conduct a safety briefing at the start of the charter. The boat must have life jackets for all passengers, a life raft, flares, and a VHF radio. Insurance is mandatory, covering third-party liability and damage to the boat. You are advised to take out travel insurance that covers water activities. For day charters, no passport is needed if you stay within Spanish waters, but if you want to cross to Gibraltar or Morocco, you need a valid passport and the boat must have a clearance from the marina. Most charters stay within Spanish waters, so it is not an issue.

Comparing Yacht Rental Costa del Sol vs Dubai

You might be wondering how a yacht rental in Marbella compares to Dubai. Both offer luxury, but the experience is different. Dubai has man-made islands, skyline views, and a more commercial, high-tech feel. The water is warm year-round, but the summer heat (45-50 degrees C) is brutal. The Costa del Sol has natural beauty, historic towns, and a more relaxed vibe. The climate is milder, with pleasant temperatures even in summer. The cost is generally lower: a similar-sized motor yacht in Marbella might be 20-30% cheaper than in Dubai. The regulations are simpler: in Spain, you need a skipper for most boats, but in Dubai, you can rent a boat without a skipper if you have a licence. However, the service level is comparable. Both destinations have a wide range of boats, from RIBs to superyachts. If you are already in Europe, Marbella is a no-brainer. If you are in Asia or the Middle East, Dubai might be more convenient. But for a European holiday, the Costa del Sol is hard to beat.

Frequently Asked Questions About Yacht Rental

You probably have questions. Below are the most common ones we get from clients. If you do not see your question, contact us through the website and we will answer within 24 hours.

h1: Boat Rental Lake Como, Skippered Charters on Italy’s Finest Lake
intro:
You want to see Lake Como from the water, not from a crowded ferry. A boat rental Lake Como gives you the freedom to explore the villas, the mountain backdrop, and the hidden coves at your own pace. With BoatHire24, every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you don’t need a licence or any boating experience. Just turn up, step aboard, and let someone else handle the navigation while you enjoy the prosecco.

We operate from multiple ports around the lake, Como town, Bellagio, Menaggio, Varenna, and Lecco, and offer motor yachts, classic wooden boats, RIBs, catamarans, and sailing yachts. Prices start from around EUR 350 for a half-day on a small RIB, and go up to EUR 5,000+ for a full-day luxury yacht charter. This page covers everything you need to know: what’s included, which boat type suits you, how the seasons work, and how to book without the hassle.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Boat Rental Lake Como

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who knows the lake inside out. You don’t pay extra for fuel, insurance, or cleaning fees, those are built into the price you see. Most boats also include a cooler with ice, a Bluetooth speaker, and a sun deck with cushions. Some of the larger yachts come with a full crew (hostess, chef) and water toys like paddleboards or a Seabob.

What is not included: food and drink (unless you book a catered package), dockage fees at private villas or restaurants, and any damage caused by negligence. You can bring your own food and drink on board, or arrange a catering package through the operator. The skipper will help you plan a route and suggest stops, but the final itinerary is yours to decide.

Lake Como Ports and Departure Points

Lake Como is shaped like an inverted Y, with three main branches. The most popular departure ports are Como town at the southwest tip, Bellagio at the central junction, Menaggio on the west shore, Varenna on the east shore, and Lecco at the southeast tip. Each port has its own character and gives you access to different parts of the lake.

From Como, you can head north past the Villa Olmo and the first set of mountains. From Bellagio, you are in the centre, with quick access to both branches. Menaggio and Varenna are quieter, with smaller marinas and fewer crowds. Lecco is less touristy and offers a more rugged landscape with the Grigna mountains rising straight from the water. We also offer pickups from private jetties at hotels or villas along the shore, subject to a small surcharge.

Boat Types Available for Lake Como Charters

The classic choice is a wooden Riva or similar vintage motorboat. These boats are 6 to 10 metres long, with a teak deck, leather seats, and a top speed of around 30 knots. They seat 6 to 10 people and cost from EUR 450 for a half-day. If you want something faster, a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) is more practical, 5 to 8 metres, seats 6 to 8, top speed 40+ knots, price from EUR 350 for a half-day.

For larger groups, motor yachts from 10 to 18 metres are available. These have a cabin, a proper galley, a sun deck, and sometimes a bow thruster for easy docking. Prices range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 3,500 for a full day, depending on size and season. Catamarans are rarer on Lake Como but you can find a few, usually around 12 to 15 metres, with a shallow draft and stable platform, good for families. Sailing yachts are also available, from 8 to 14 metres, with a skipper who handles the sails. A half-day sail costs from EUR 600.

Licence-free day boats (no skipper required) are not common on Lake Como because the lake is narrow and busy, but some operators offer small electric boats that you can drive yourself without a licence. These are typically 4 to 5 metres, seat 4 to 6 people, and cost from EUR 200 for two hours. They are limited to the area near Como or Bellagio and have a restricted range.

Pricing Guidance for Lake Como Boat Rentals

Prices vary by boat type, duration, season, and departure port. As a rough guide, a half-day (4 hours) on a small RIB costs from EUR 350. A half-day on a classic wooden motorboat costs from EUR 450. A full day (8 hours) on a 12-metre motor yacht costs from EUR 1,500. A full day on a sailing yacht costs from EUR 800. Superyachts over 20 metres are available on request, with prices starting around EUR 5,000 for a full day.

High season (July and August) sees prices increase by 20 to 30 percent. Shoulder seasons (May, June, September) are cheaper and still have good weather. Low season (October to April) is the cheapest, but many boats are laid up for winter, and the weather can be cold, daytime temperatures in April are around 15 degrees C, and the lake water is too cold for swimming. All prices on BoatHire24 include VAT (22 percent in Italy) and the skipper’s fee. There are no hidden charges.

Best Times of Year for a Lake Como Charter

The best time for a boat rental Lake Como is from May to September. In May and June, the weather is warm (20 to 28 degrees C), the water is calm, and the crowds are manageable. July and August are the peak months, hot (30 to 35 degrees C), busy on the water, and expensive. If you want to swim, the lake water is warmest in August, around 24 degrees C. September is often the best month: warm, less crowded, and lower prices.

April and October are marginal. You might get a sunny day with 18 degrees C, but the wind can pick up, and the chance of rain is higher. Some operators close for the season in November and reopen in March. If you book in the off-season, confirm with the operator that the boat is available and that the skipper is willing to go out. The lake can get rough in winter, with waves up to 1 metre, so smaller boats are not recommended.

How to Book a Boat Rental Lake Como on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24 and enter Lake Como as your destination. Select your preferred port, date, and group size. The search results show all available boats with photos, specs, and prices. You can filter by boat type, price range, and capacity. Once you find a boat you like, click to see the full details, including the cancellation policy and what’s included.

To confirm, you pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) via credit card or bank transfer. The balance is due on the day of the charter, paid directly to the skipper in cash or by card. We send you a confirmation email with the skipper’s contact details and meeting point instructions. If you need to cancel, most operators offer a full refund if you cancel at least 7 days before the charter. For last-minute cancellations, the deposit is non-refundable.

You can also browse our blog for route ideas, restaurant recommendations on the lake, and tips on what to bring. For example, we have a post on the best villas to see from the water, Villa del Balbianello, Villa Carlotta, and Villa Melzi, and where to moor for a swim or a lunch stop.

Who Is a Skippered Lake Como Charter For

A skippered charter is for anyone who wants to enjoy the lake without the stress of driving a boat. It is ideal for couples, families with children, groups of friends, and corporate events. You do not need a boating licence, and you do not need to know how to anchor, dock, or read a chart. The skipper handles all of that, and they also know the best spots for swimming, the quietest coves, and the restaurants that are only accessible by boat.

If you are a confident boat driver with an International Certificate of Competence (ICC), you can rent a boat without a skipper. However, Lake Como has strict speed limits (10 knots within 100 metres of the shore) and busy traffic around the main towns. Most operators recommend a skipper for first-time visitors. The price difference is not huge, a bareboat charter of a small motorboat might save you EUR 100 to EUR 200 compared to a skippered charter, but you lose the local knowledge and the ability to relax completely.

What to Expect on the Day of Your Charter

Arrive at the departure port 15 minutes before the start time. The skipper will meet you at the dock, give you a safety briefing, and show you the boat. You can bring your own food and drink, or arrange a catering package in advance. The skipper will ask about your preferred route and any stops you want to make. Typical routes include a cruise past the villas of the central lake, a stop at the Isola Comacina for lunch, or a trip up to the northern town of Colico for a swim in the clearer water.

The skipper will handle the mooring at any restaurant or beach you choose. They are also happy to take photos of your group, point out landmarks, and give you space if you want privacy. At the end of the charter, you return to the departure port, settle any extras (like catering or extra hours), and tip the skipper if you wish, 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee is standard.

Combining Lake Como with Other Destinations

If you are visiting the Costa del Sol or Marbella, you can also book a boat rental there through BoatHire24. We operate in multiple locations, so you can charter a yacht in Puerto Banús one week and a RIB on Lake Como the next. Check our search page to see all available destinations. Lake Como is a 2-hour flight from Málaga, or a 12-hour drive through France and Switzerland. Many visitors combine a week on the coast with a few days on the lake.

The lake itself is a good base for day trips to Milan (1 hour by train), the Swiss border (30 minutes by car), or the Bergamo Alps. But the best part of a Lake Como holiday is the water, and a private boat charter is the only way to experience it properly. No queues, no timetables, no crowds. Just you, the lake, and the mountains.

Specific Lake Como Routes and Highlights

One of the best routes from Como town takes you north past the Villa Olmo, then across to the western shore near Cernobbio. You can stop at the village of Moltrasio for a swim off the rocks, then continue to Laglio, where George Clooney used to moor his boat. The water here is deep, up to 80 metres in places, so it stays cool even in August. From Bellagio, a popular route is to head east toward Varenna, passing the Villa Melzi gardens, then cross to Menaggio for lunch. The distance between Bellagio and Varenna is only 2 nautical miles, so you can make multiple stops in a half-day charter.

If you start from Menaggio, you can cruise north to the mouth of the River Adda near Colico, where the water turns a milky green from glacial silt. This area is less developed and has a wilder feel, with the Alps rising directly from the shore. From Varenna, a good route is south toward the Lierna area, where the cliffs drop straight into the lake and there are a few hidden caves you can swim into. The skipper will know which caves are accessible and which are blocked by rocks. For a full-day charter, you can circumnavigate the entire central basin, covering about 20 nautical miles, with stops for lunch, swimming, and photos.

Lake Como Weather and Wind Patterns

The lake has its own microclimate, with two main winds. The tivano is a light north wind that blows in the morning, usually from 6 am to noon, with speeds of 5 to 10 knots. The breva is a stronger south wind that picks up around 1 pm and can reach 15 to 20 knots in the afternoon, especially in the central basin. This makes the afternoon choppy on the open water, with waves up to 0.5 metres. Smaller boats like RIBs handle this fine, but wooden motorboats with a low freeboard can get wet. If you want a smooth ride, book a morning charter or choose a sheltered route along the shore.

In summer, thunderstorms can build quickly over the mountains in the late afternoon, especially in July and August. The skipper will watch the radar and bring you back to port if a storm is coming. The lake is safe in a storm if you stay close to the shore and avoid open water. Lightning strikes on the lake are rare but not unheard of, so the skipper will take precautions. In spring and autumn, the wind is more unpredictable, with gusts from the west that can catch you off guard. A skippered charter is safer in these conditions because the skipper knows how to read the weather.

Dining Options on Lake Como Charters

You can bring your own picnic, but many operators offer a catering package with local specialities. A typical lunch spread includes prosciutto, salami, cheeses like taleggio and gorgonzola, bread, olives, and a bottle of Franciacorta or a local red like Valtellina Superiore. Prices for catering range from EUR 25 to EUR 50 per person, depending on the menu. Some operators also offer a full sit-down meal at a restaurant that you reach by boat, such as the Locanda dell’Isola Comacina, which is the only restaurant on the small island. They serve a fixed menu of lake fish, risotto, and dessert for about EUR 60 per person, not including wine.

Another option is to moor at a lakeside restaurant like the Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni in Bellagio, which has a private dock and a Michelin-starred restaurant. The skipper will call ahead to reserve a table and arrange the mooring. You pay for the meal separately, and the skipper waits at the boat or joins you if you invite them. For a more casual stop, the bar at the Hotel du Lac in Varenna has a dock and serves simple pasta and pizza for around EUR 15 to EUR 20 per person. The skipper will recommend places based on your budget and preferences.

Special Occasions and Events on Lake Como

A private boat charter is a popular choice for proposals, weddings, and birthday celebrations. The classic proposal spot is in front of Villa del Balbianello at sunset, with the lake and mountains as a backdrop. The skipper can coordinate with the villa to arrange a private tour of the gardens before the proposal. Prices for a proposal package start from EUR 800 for a half-day charter with champagne and flowers. For a wedding, you can charter a larger yacht and have a civil ceremony on board, but you need to arrange the paperwork with the local municipality, which takes about 30 days. The operator can help with the logistics.

Birthday parties are easier. You can book a yacht with a sound system, bring your own playlist, and have a floating party on the lake. Some operators allow a maximum of 12 guests on a motor yacht, but you can charter a catamaran for up to 20 people. Noise restrictions apply after 10 pm in most ports, so the skipper will anchor away from residential areas. Fireworks are not allowed on the lake without a permit, but sparklers are fine. The operator will advise on what is permitted and help you plan the day.

Practical Tips for Your Lake Como Charter

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses even on cloudy days, because the sun reflects off the water and you will burn faster than on land. The UV index in summer is often 8 or 9. Wear non-slip shoes on wooden boats, as the teak deck gets slippery when wet. Swimwear is fine, but bring a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. If you are prone to seasickness, take a pill an hour before departure, the lake is generally calm in the morning but can get choppy in the afternoon. Mobile phone reception is good across the lake, but some remote coves have weak signal, so download maps or directions beforehand.

Cash is useful for tips and any extras like catering or extra hours. Most skippers accept card payments for the balance, but not all, so ask in advance. The charter time is strict, if you return late, you may be charged overtime at a rate of around EUR 100 to EUR 200 per hour, depending on the boat. Plan your route to allow time for unexpected delays. If you are staying at a hotel with a private jetty, confirm the pickup point with the operator a day before, and be ready 10 minutes early. The skipper will text or call you on the day to confirm the meeting.

For bareboat rentals, you need an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or an Italian equivalent. Some small electric boats can be driven without a licence, but they are limited to calm areas near the main towns.

Superyachts cost EUR 5,000 or more per day. All prices include VAT and the skipper. High season (July, August) adds 20 to 30 percent.

faqs.a: Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, a swimsuit, a towel, and a light jacket or windbreaker (it can be cooler on the water even in summer). faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day of my charter?

h1: Boat Rental Mallorca, Book a Skippered Charter Today
intro:
Mallorca is the biggest of the Balearic Islands, and getting on the water is the only way to see it properly. You can rent a boat here without a licence, as long as it comes with a skipper, and every charter we list includes one. That means you turn up, step aboard, and let someone else handle the navigation while you decide where to drop anchor for lunch.

The island has more than 550 kilometres of coastline, with hidden coves, sea caves and beach clubs that are only reachable from the sea. A day charter from Palma, Pollensa or Alcudia gives you access to places like Cala Mondragó, Es Trenc and the rugged coastline of the Serra de Tramuntana. You can book a motor yacht, a catamaran, a sailing yacht or a RIB, and the price includes fuel, the skipper and usually a cooler with ice.

We are BoatHire24, a marketplace that lists boats from local rental companies in Mallorca. You compare the options, check availability and book online. No phone calls, no back-and-forth emails.
bodyHtml:
What You Get With a Skippered Boat Rental in Mallorca

Every boat we list comes with a licensed skipper. That is not an optional extra, it is included in the price. The skipper handles the mooring, the anchoring and the navigation, and they know the local waters. They will take you to the best spots for swimming, snorkelling or just floating around with a cold drink.

You do not need a boating licence. You do not need to have any experience. You just need to decide where you want to go and what you want to eat or drink. The skipper can also arrange a lunch stop at a chiringuito or a beach club, or you can bring your own food and drinks on board.

The typical day charter runs from 10:00 to 18:00, though you can also book half-day trips (4 hours) or sunset cruises (2-3 hours). Most boats have a maximum capacity between 8 and 12 passengers, so you can split the cost with friends or family.

Departure Ports for Mallorca Boat Rentals

Mallorca has several marinas and ports where you can start your charter. The most popular departure points are:

  • Palma, the main hub. You leave from Portixol or the Real Club Náutico. Easy to reach from the airport (15 minutes by taxi). Good for heading south to Es Trenc or north to the Bay of Palma.
  • Port d'Alcudia, on the north coast. Close to the beaches of Muro and the Albufera nature reserve. Popular for trips to Formentor and the Cap de Formentor lighthouse.
  • Port de Pollença, a quieter alternative to Alcudia. The marina is right next to the old town. Great for exploring the northern coves like Cala Bóquer and Cala Castell.
  • Port de Sóller, in the northwest, inside the Tramuntana mountains. The tram from Palma goes straight here. Best for trips to Sa Calobra and the Torrent de Pareis gorge.
  • Colònia de Sant Jordi, in the south. The closest port to Es Trenc beach and the Cabrera archipelago. Ideal if you are staying in the Campos or Ses Salines area.
  • Cala d'Or, in the southeast. A small marina surrounded by pine trees. Good for the calas of the southeast coast, including Cala Llombards and Cala S'Almunia.

If you are not sure which port to use, check our search page to filter by location and see which boats are available near you.

Types of Boats Available

You can rent almost any type of boat in Mallorca. The most common categories are:

Motor yachts, from 30 to 60 feet. Fast, comfortable, with a cabin, a bathroom and a sun deck. Prices start from around EUR 900 for a full day. Good for groups who want to cover distance and visit several coves in one day.

Catamarans, 35 to 50 feet. Stable, with a large trampoline net at the front and plenty of deck space. Prices from around EUR 1,200 for a full day. Best for families or anyone prone to seasickness, catamarans barely roll.

Sailing yachts, 35 to 50 feet. Quieter, more traditional, and you can help the skipper if you want. Prices from around EUR 700 for a full day. Good for couples or small groups who want a more relaxed pace.

RIBs and speedboats, 25 to 35 feet. Open boats with outboard engines. Fast and nimble. Prices from around EUR 500 for a half day. Best for adrenaline seekers or small groups who want to reach remote coves quickly.

Licence-free day boats, small motorboats up to 15 feet. No skipper required, but you do need to be over 18 and have a basic understanding of navigation. Prices from around EUR 200 for a half day. These are not listed on our site because we focus on skippered charters, but you can find them locally.

Pricing Guidance for Mallorca Boat Rentals

Prices vary depending on the boat size, the season and the duration. Here are rough ranges to help you budget:

  • Half-day (4 hours): EUR 400 to EUR 1,000
  • Full day (8 hours): EUR 700 to EUR 2,500
  • Sunset cruise (2-3 hours): EUR 300 to EUR 600
  • Multi-day charter: price on request, usually from EUR 2,000 per day for a 50-foot yacht

Most listings include fuel, the skipper, insurance and a cooler with ice. Some include soft drinks, water and snorkelling gear. You should confirm what is included before booking, but the listing description on our site will tell you.

Peak season is July and August, when prices are highest and availability is tight. June and September are still warm (water around 24-26 degrees C) and cheaper. May and October are cooler but less crowded.

Best Times to Rent a Boat in Mallorca

The boating season runs from April to October. July and August are the hottest months, with air temperatures hitting 35 degrees C and sea temperatures around 27 degrees C. The trade-off is that the marinas and popular coves get busy.

June and September are the sweet spots. The weather is still excellent, the water is warm enough for swimming, and the anchorages are less crowded. Prices are about 20-30% lower than in August.

May and October are quieter. You might get some wind and cooler evenings, but you will often have coves to yourselves. The sea temperature in May is around 18-20 degrees C, so a wetsuit is useful for snorkelling.

Winter charters (November to March) are possible but less common. The weather can be unpredictable, and many boats are laid up for maintenance. If you want to go in winter, contact us and we will check what is available.

Popular Routes and Destinations

Here are some of the most popular itineraries for a day charter in Mallorca:

From Palma to Es Trenc, head south along the coast. Stop at Cala Blava, Cala Pi and the Cabrera National Park (if you have time). Es Trenc is a long white sand beach with crystal clear water. The trip is about 1.5 hours each way from Palma.

From Alcudia to Formentor, go north along the bay. Stop at the beaches of Muro and the Cap de Formentor lighthouse. The water is turquoise and the cliffs are dramatic. The trip is about 45 minutes each way from Alcudia.

From Sóller to Sa Calobra, go east along the Tramuntana coast. The coastline is steep and rocky, with hidden coves like Cala Tuent. Sa Calobra is a pebble beach at the mouth of a canyon. The trip is about 1 hour each way from Sóller.

From Cala d'Or to the southeast calas, explore the coves of the southeast coast, including Cala Llombards, Cala S'Almunia and Cala Mondragó. The water is clear and the beaches are small and sheltered. The trip is short, so you can visit several in one day.

For more ideas, read our blog on the best anchorages in the Balearics.

How to Book a Boat Rental in Mallorca

Booking through our site takes about five minutes. Here is the process:

  1. Go to the search page and enter your dates and the number of guests.
  2. Browse the available boats. Filter by type, price, capacity and departure port.
  3. Click on a boat to see the full description, photos, included items and cancellation policy.
  4. Select a time slot (usually 10:00-18:00 for full day, or 10:00-14:00 / 15:00-19:00 for half day).
  5. Pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) online. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day.
  6. Receive a confirmation email with the meeting point and the skipper's contact details.

You can cancel up to 48 hours before the charter for a full refund, unless the listing says otherwise. Weather cancellations are handled by the skipper, if the sea is too rough, you get a full refund or a reschedule.

Who Is This For

Boat rental in Mallorca works for almost anyone. It is popular with:

  • Families, catamarans are stable and have plenty of space for kids. The skipper can take you to shallow coves where children can swim safely.
  • Groups of friends, split the cost of a motor yacht and spend the day jumping off the bow, drinking and listening to music.
  • Couples, a sailing yacht or a small motorboat for two. Sunset cruises are particularly popular for proposals.
  • Corporate groups, team-building days or client entertainment. Most boats can be catered with food and drink.
  • Solo travellers, you can join a shared charter if you are on your own. Some operators run regular group trips.

If you are unsure which boat type suits your group, contact us and we will recommend something based on your numbers and preferences.

What to Expect from a Skippered Charter in Mallorca

When you book through BoatHire24, every rental includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters inside out. They handle all the navigation, mooring and safety, so you can focus on enjoying the day. The skipper will also suggest the best spots based on the weather and your preferences, whether that is a secluded cove for swimming or a lively beach club for lunch. You do not need a boating licence or any prior experience, the skipper does everything. The only thing you need to decide is the itinerary and what to bring for food and drinks. Most charters run from 10:00 to 18:00, but half-day options (4 hours) and sunset trips (2-3 hours) are also common. Boat capacities typically range from 8 to 12 passengers, making it easy to split the cost among a group.

Detailed Pricing by Boat Type and Season

Prices for boat rental in Mallorca vary significantly depending on the boat type, size and season. For a 40-foot motor yacht in June, expect to pay around EUR 1,200 for a full day, while the same boat in August might cost EUR 1,800. Catamarans of similar size start at EUR 1,400 in June and go up to EUR 2,000 in August. Sailing yachts are generally cheaper, with 40-foot models costing around EUR 800 in June and EUR 1,200 in August. RIBs and speedboats are the most affordable, with half-day rates from EUR 400 in June and EUR 600 in August. For luxury superyachts over 60 feet, prices start at EUR 3,000 per day and can exceed EUR 10,000, especially during peak weeks like the first week of August or the Mallorca Boat Show in late April.

Discounts are often available for multi-day bookings. A two-day charter might reduce the daily rate by 10-15%, and a full week could save you 20-25%. Always check the listing for any special offers or last-minute deals, particularly in May and September when demand is lower.

Local Tips for a Smooth Charter Experience

Book at least two weeks in advance during July and August, as popular boats are often reserved months ahead. For June and September, one week is usually enough. Always confirm the meeting point with the skipper the day before, some marinas have multiple docks and it is easy to get confused. Bring sunscreen, a hat and a windbreaker, even in summer the wind can be strong on the water. Most boats have a cooler with ice, but you should bring your own food and drinks unless catering is included. If you want a lunch stop at a chiringuito, let the skipper know in advance so they can reserve a table. Tipping the skipper is not mandatory but appreciated, around 10-15% of the charter cost is standard for good service.

Weather cancellations are handled by the skipper. If the sea is too rough or there is a storm warning, you get a full refund or the option to reschedule. Check the forecast a day before and communicate with the skipper if you have concerns.

Hidden Gems and Less Crowded Coves

While the popular spots like Es Trenc and Formentor are beautiful, they can get crowded in peak season. For a quieter experience, ask your skipper to take you to Cala Varques on the east coast, a pristine cove accessible only by boat or a long hike. Cala Bóquer near Port de Pollença is another hidden gem, a small pebble beach surrounded by cliffs. In the northwest, Cala Tuent near Sa Calobra is less frequented than its famous neighbour and offers excellent snorkelling. For a truly remote spot, head to the Cabrera National Park, a protected archipelago south of Mallorca. You need a permit to land on the main island, but your skipper can arrange this in advance. The waters around Cabrera are crystal clear and teeming with marine life.

For sunset cruises, the area around Cap de Formentor is spectacular, but so is the view from the Bay of Palma with the cathedral lit up in the background. Ask your skipper for their favourite sunset spot, they often know a quiet anchorage away from the crowds.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind

Pack light but smart. Essentials include swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (biodegradable is better for the environment), sunglasses and a hat. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful even in summer, as the wind can pick up in the afternoon. If you plan to snorkel, most boats provide masks and fins, but bring your own if you have them. Leave behind high heels or black-soled shoes, they can damage the deck. Most boats have a no-shoes policy or require soft-soled footwear. Glass bottles are often banned on boats for safety reasons, so bring drinks in cans or plastic containers. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure, catamarans are more stable than monohulls if you are worried.

For food, pack a picnic or arrange catering through the skipper. Many boats have a barbecue on board, and the skipper can grill fresh fish or meat for an extra fee. Check with the skipper beforehand if you have dietary restrictions.

Booking Flexibility and Cancellation Policies

Most listings on our site offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before the charter. Some premium boats or superyachts may have a 72-hour policy. Always read the cancellation terms on the listing page before booking. If you need to change the date, contact the skipper directly, many are flexible and will accommodate you if they have availability. Weather-related cancellations are always free, and you receive a full refund or a reschedule. For last-minute bookings (within 48 hours), we recommend calling the skipper directly through the contact details provided after booking, as online availability may not update in real time.

Payment is split into a deposit (usually 30-50%) paid online at the time of booking, and the balance paid in cash or by card to the skipper on the day of the charter. Some skippers accept bank transfers for the balance, but cash is the most common method. Always confirm the payment method with the skipper in advance.

title: Jet Ski Rental Marbella
metaDescription: Book jet ski rental Marbella with BoatHire24. Ride the Costa del Sol coast from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina. Licensed skippers and top gear included. Book now.
h1: Jet Ski Rental Marbella
intro:
If you want to rent a jet ski in Marbella, you are probably after speed, salt spray, and a bit of showing off. That is fair enough. The Costa del Sol coast offers a decent stretch of water from Puerto Banús to Cabopino, with the Sierra Blanca mountains as a backdrop and the occasional dolphin pod to make you feel like a wildlife presenter. At BoatHire24, we connect you with operators who provide jet skis as part of a full charter experience, always with a licensed skipper onboard. No need to worry about licences or insurance. You just turn up and ride.

This page covers everything you need to know about jet ski rental in Marbella. We talk about where you can ride, what it costs, what the weather is like, and how to book without getting ripped off. We also include a few practical details that most guides skip, like fuel policies and deposit requirements. If you are in a hurry, head straight to our search page to see current availability.
bodyHtml:
What a Jet Ski Rental in Marbella Includes

When you book a jet ski through BoatHire24, the package usually includes the machine itself, a full tank of fuel (or enough for your session), life jackets, and a safety briefing. Most rentals run for 30 minutes, 60 minutes, or 90 minutes. Some operators offer half-day or full-day options, but those are less common because jet skis are thirsty and the sea can get choppy by midday. The skipper stays with you for the whole session, either on a separate chase boat or on the jet ski if it is a two-seater. They know the local spots: the best coves, the areas with less traffic, and where the sea is calm enough for a bit of speed. You do not need a licence. The skipper takes responsibility for the vessel, which means you can just enjoy the ride.

The jet skis themselves are typically Yamaha or Sea-Doo models, between 100 and 180 horsepower. They seat two or three people. If you want a single-seater, you might need to ask in advance. Most operators have a maximum weight limit of around 150 kg per person, and a combined limit of 200 kg for two riders. Check with the operator when you book. Helmets are not standard, but you can request one if you prefer. Some operators also provide waterproof phone pouches, but bring your own to be safe.

Where You Can Ride a Jet Ski in Marbella

The main departure points for jet ski rental in Marbella are Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo). From Puerto Banús, you head west towards the Cala del Faro and the cliffs of the Sierra Bermeja, or east towards the Marbella coastline and the Cabopino dunes. From Marbella Marina, you have the same options but you start closer to the town centre. Some operators also offer pick-ups from Cabopino and Estepona, but those are less frequent. The riding zone is usually marked by buoys and restricted to a few kilometres from the coast. You cannot cross the Strait of Gibraltar on a jet ski, no matter how tempting that sounds. The commercial shipping lanes are busy, and the Guardia Civil take a dim view of joyriders in the Algeciras traffic separation scheme.

The best spots for jet skiing include the stretch between Puerto Banús and the Río Verde estuary, where the water is relatively flat in the morning. The area around the Cabopino dunes is also popular, with fewer boats and a nice view of the sand. If you want to see the Marbella skyline from the water, head east from the marina towards the La Concha mountain. The mountain acts as a landmark, and on a clear day you can see the snow on top in winter. For a longer ride, some operators offer a trip to the Nerja caves, but that is a 50 km journey each way, so expect a premium price and a full-day commitment.

Boat Types and Alternatives to Jet Skis

Jet skis are not the only way to get your adrenaline fix on the Costa del Sol. If you are travelling with a group, a RIB or speedboat might be a better option. RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) are essentially the same concept as a jet ski but with more seats and a bit more stability. They can carry up to eight people and still hit 40 knots. You can find RIB rentals in Marbella through our BoatHire24 homepage. For a more relaxed day, consider a motor yacht or a catamaran. They are slower, but you can anchor in a cove, swim, and eat lunch. Jet skis are for the short, fast blast. Boats are for the full day out.

If you are set on a jet ski but want to combine it with other water sports, some operators offer packages that include a jet ski session plus a banana boat ride or paddleboarding. That is more common in Puerto Banús, where the water sports centres are clustered around the harbour entrance. You can also rent a jet ski as part of a larger charter. For example, you could book a motor yacht for the day and have a jet ski towed behind for use when you anchor. That is a luxury option, but it exists. Ask your operator when you book.

Pricing Guidance for Jet Ski Rental Marbella

Prices for jet ski rental in Marbella vary depending on the season, the duration, and the operator. As a rough guide, expect to pay from around EUR 80 for a 30-minute session, EUR 130 for 60 minutes, and EUR 180 for 90 minutes. These are per jet ski, not per person. If you want a two-seater and you are sharing, the price is the same. Some operators charge a premium for weekends and public holidays. High season (July and August) can add 20 to 30 percent to the base rate. Low season (November to February) often has discounts, but the weather is cooler and the sea can be rougher.

Fuel is usually included in the price, but not always. Ask the operator before you book. Some charge a separate fuel fee based on the time you use, typically around EUR 20 to EUR 40 for a 30-minute session. Deposits are common. You may be asked to leave a credit card imprint or a cash deposit of EUR 200 to EUR 500 as security against damage. If you return the jet ski in the same condition, you get the deposit back. If you crash it, you pay for repairs. Insurance is usually included in the rental price, but it often comes with a deductible of EUR 500 to EUR 1,000. Read the terms carefully.

Best Seasons for Jet Ski Rental Marbella

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate, which means hot summers and mild winters. The best time for jet skiing is from May to October, when the water temperature is above 18 degrees Celsius and the sea is calm. July and August are the peak months. The water temperature hits 24 degrees, the air is 30 degrees plus, and the sea is flat in the mornings. The downside is the crowds. Puerto Banús gets busy, and the jet ski zones can feel like a motorway. If you want quieter conditions, aim for early morning (9 am to 11 am) or late afternoon (5 pm to 7 pm). The wind picks up around midday, making the water choppy.

Winter jet skiing is possible but less comfortable. From November to April, the water temperature drops to around 15 degrees, and the air can be 12 to 18 degrees. You will need a wetsuit. The sea is rougher, and the wind is stronger. Some operators close for the winter months. If you want to ride in winter, call ahead to check availability. The advantage is lower prices and empty beaches. You might have the whole stretch of coast to yourself.

How to Book a Jet Ski in Marbella

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You go to our search page, select the date, the number of participants, and the port. The system shows you available operators and their packages. You choose one, pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent), and the rest on the day. You receive a booking confirmation by email with the meeting point and the operator's contact details. On the day, you arrive at the port, meet the skipper, sign a waiver, and go. The whole process takes about 15 minutes from arrival to getting on the water.

If you prefer to book directly, you can call or email the operator. But we recommend using our platform because it gives you a comparison of prices and availability. It also provides a layer of protection: if the operator cancels, we help you find an alternative or refund your deposit. We do not charge you a booking fee. The price you see is the price you pay.

Who Jet Ski Rental Marbella Is For

Jet ski rental in Marbella is suitable for most people aged 16 and over. Some operators allow children from 12 years old if they are accompanied by an adult on the same machine. You do not need any previous experience. The skipper gives a brief lesson before you start. If you have a disability or a medical condition, check with the operator in advance. Jet skis are physically demanding: you need to hold on, steer, and absorb the impact of waves. Pregnant women and people with back problems should avoid it.

Groups of friends and stag/hen parties are common customers. The operators are used to rowdy groups, but they will cut the session short if you behave dangerously. The Guardia Civil patrol the coast and can fine you for reckless riding. The speed limit in the port area is 3 knots. Outside the port, there is no formal speed limit, but the skipper will keep you to a safe speed based on conditions. If you want to show off, keep it within the designated area and away from swimmers and other boats.

Safety and Legal Requirements

You do not need a licence to rent a jet ski in Marbella, because the skipper holds the licence and is responsible for the vessel. However, you must be at least 16 years old to drive. Some operators require you to show a form of ID (passport or national ID card). You also sign a liability waiver that releases the operator from responsibility for injury or damage caused by your actions. Read it before you sign. If you are under the influence of alcohol or drugs, the operator will refuse to let you ride. The blood alcohol limit for skippers in Spain is 0.3 grams per litre, but for passengers it is usually zero tolerance. Do not drink and ride.

Life jackets are mandatory. You must wear them at all times while on the jet ski. The operator provides them. If you do not want to wear one, you cannot ride. The jet ski is equipped with a kill switch lanyard that stops the engine if you fall off. Attach it to your wrist or life jacket. Do not remove it. The skipper will check this before you start.

Local Attractions and Things to Do After Your Ride

After your jet ski session, you are in Marbella. You can head to Puerto Banús for lunch at one of the beach clubs or seafood restaurants. The port is full of superyachts, designer shops, and people watching. If you prefer something quieter, go to Estepona old town, about 15 minutes drive west. The streets are whitewashed and lined with flower pots. There is a market on Sundays. For a more active afternoon, hike up La Concha mountain. The trail starts near the Marbella Marina and takes about three hours round trip. The view from the top is worth it.

If you are staying in the area for a few days, consider a day trip to the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins. The strait is a migration route for pilot whales, common dolphins, and striped dolphins. Several operators offer boat trips from Tarifa, about an hour's drive west of Marbella. Alternatively, visit the Nerja caves, about 40 minutes east. The caves are huge, with stalactites and stalagmites, and the Balcony of Europe viewpoint in Nerja town offers a great photo opportunity.

Common Questions About Jet Ski Rental Marbella

We hear the same questions from customers. Here are the answers. Can you rent a jet ski without a skipper in Marbella? No. Spanish law requires a licensed skipper on board for any powered vessel rented to the public. The skipper is included in the price. How many people can ride a jet ski? Most jet skis seat two or three people. The driver must be 16 or over. Passengers can be younger. Do you need to know how to swim? It is recommended, but not mandatory. The life jacket keeps you afloat. If you cannot swim, tell the skipper. They will keep you close to the shore. What happens if the weather is bad? The operator cancels and you get a full refund or a reschedule. We do not charge cancellation fees for weather-related cancellations. Can you take a jet ski to another port? No. The rental is for a specific area around the departure port. You cannot take the jet ski to another marina. If you want to explore different ports, book separate rentals at each location.

For more details on boat rental options in the region, check our blog for guides on Marbella's coastline and the best spots for water sports.

h1: Jet Ski Marbella: Rent a Jet Ski on the Costa del Sol
intro:
If you want to blast across the Mediterranean at 50 knots, a jet ski hire in Marbella is your cheapest thrill. You don't need a licence, you don't need experience, and you don't need to share the water with 50 other tourists if you go early. BoatHire24 lists jet skis for rent at Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and other Costa del Sol ports. Prices start from around EUR 90 for 30 minutes, but you can book longer sessions for a proper ride along the coast.

Most rentals include a quick safety briefing, a life jacket, and a limited fuel allowance. You can go solo or take a passenger on a two-seater model. The typical route takes you past the golden beaches of Marbella, the rock of Gibraltar in the distance, and if you're lucky, you'll spot dolphins near the Strait. Just remember: these things drink fuel, so keep an eye on the gauge unless you fancy a tow back.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Jet Ski Rental in Marbella

A standard jet ski hire includes the watercraft, a life jacket, a safety briefing, and a set amount of fuel (usually enough for 30, 60 minutes of riding). Most operators use Yamaha or Sea-Doo models that hit 50, 60 km/h. You don't need a boating licence, but you must be at least 18 to drive (or 16 with parental consent). Some places let you take a passenger, but that cuts your top speed and handling. Expect to pay a deposit of around EUR 200, 500, refundable if you don't crash it.

You can book a 30-minute session for around EUR 90, 120, a 1-hour session for EUR 150, 200, or a 2-hour tour for EUR 250, 350. Longer rides often include a guided tour of the coastline, with stops for photos or a swim. Fuel is usually included in the price, but if you run out, you'll pay extra for the rescue. Check the terms before you go.

For a more relaxed day on the water, consider a boat rental with a skipper instead. But if you want speed and adrenaline, jet skis are the way to go.

Best Ports for Jet Ski Hire in Marbella

You can rent a jet ski from several ports along the Costa del Sol, each with its own vibe. Here are the main ones listed on BoatHire24:

Puerto Banús is the flashiest option. You'll launch from the same marina where superyachts dock, and you can ride past the luxury boutiques and beach clubs. The water is calm inside the bay, but once you exit the breakwater, you get open sea. Expect higher prices here (from around EUR 120 for 30 minutes) because of the location.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more laid-back and cheaper. Prices start from around EUR 90 for 30 minutes. You'll ride along the Marbella promenade, past the old town and the La Concha mountain backdrop. It's a good choice if you want a longer session without the Banús markup.

Cabopino is a small, quieter marina near the Artola dunes. It's less crowded, so you can get a better deal (from around EUR 80 for 30 minutes). The coastline here is more natural, with fewer buildings.

Estepona offers a longer ride south towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You can cover more distance and see the dolphin pods that gather near the shipping lanes. Prices are similar to Cabopino.

Benalmádena is further east, near Torremolinos. It's a busy port with lots of jet ski operators. You can ride past the marina and the Tivoli World park. Good for a quick session if you're staying in that area.

Sotogrande is more exclusive and quieter. Jet ski hire here is less common, but you can find it if you look. The water is usually flat, and you can ride towards Gibraltar.

All these ports are within a 30-minute drive of Marbella town. Use the BoatHire24 search to check availability at your preferred location.

Types of Jet Skis Available for Rent

Most operators offer two main types: the standard 1, 2 seater and the larger 3-seater. The 1, 2 seater is lighter, faster, and more manoeuvrable. The 3-seater is bulkier but more stable, and it can carry two passengers. If you're a beginner, stick with the 2-seater. If you want to take a friend, go for the 3-seater but expect a slower ride.

Engine sizes range from 900cc to 1,800cc. The smaller engines are fine for cruising, but the big ones will throw you off if you're not careful. Most rentals cap the speed at 50, 60 km/h for safety, but you can ask for a faster model if you have experience.

Some operators also offer stand-up jet skis (like the Yamaha SuperJet) for experienced riders. These are harder to ride but more fun for tricks. They're rare on the Costa del Sol, so you'll need to ask specifically.

If you want something different, check out BoatHire24 for other options like RIBs or speedboats that go just as fast but seat more people.

Jet Ski Prices in Marbella: What to Expect

Prices vary by season, port, and operator. Here's a rough guide based on current listings on BoatHire24:

Low season (November, February): EUR 70, 100 for 30 minutes, EUR 120, 150 for 1 hour. You can often negotiate because demand is low.

Mid season (March, May, October): EUR 90, 120 for 30 minutes, EUR 150, 200 for 1 hour. Book in advance to get the best price.

High season (June, September): EUR 120, 180 for 30 minutes, EUR 200, 300 for 1 hour. Prices peak in August. You'll need to book weeks ahead.

Longer sessions (2 hours) cost EUR 250, 450 depending on the season. Some operators offer a guided tour that includes a stop at a beach club or a cove like Cala del Faro. Fuel is usually included, but check if there's a fuel surcharge for extra distance.

Deposits are typically EUR 200, 500, refundable if you return the jet ski undamaged. You can pay by credit card or cash. Some operators require a damage waiver fee of EUR 20, 50 instead of a deposit.

For a full breakdown of costs, see our blog on boat rental prices in Marbella.

When to Go Jet Skiing in Marbella

The best time for jet skiing is from May to October, when the sea temperature is above 18°C and the wind is light. July and August are the hottest months, with air temperatures hitting 30°C and water at 24°C. But the sea can be choppy in the afternoon due to the thermal wind (levante). Go early in the morning (9, 11 AM) for flat water and fewer boats.

Spring (March, April) and autumn (October, November) are also good, but the water is cooler (15, 18°C). You'll need a wetsuit if you plan to fall off. Winter (December, February) is too cold for most people, but the sea is often calm. Some operators close for the season.

Check the weather forecast before you book. If the wind is above 15 knots, the sea will be rough and the ride will be less enjoyable. Most operators will cancel or reschedule if conditions are dangerous.

How to Book a Jet Ski in Marbella

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, select 'jet ski' as the boat type, choose your port and date, and see available options. You can filter by price, duration, and passenger capacity. Each listing shows the operator's details, the exact model, and the cancellation policy.

You can book online with a credit card or PayPal. Most operators require a deposit of 50% at booking and the rest on arrival. Some offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before. Read the fine print.

If you prefer to book by phone or WhatsApp, contact the operator directly through the listing. They speak English, Spanish, and often German or French.

For last-minute bookings, call the operator to check availability. In high season, you'll struggle to find a same-day slot.

Who Should Rent a Jet Ski in Marbella

Jet skis are for anyone who wants a quick adrenaline hit without a big time commitment. They're popular with groups of friends, couples, and stag or hen parties. If you're a family with kids under 16, you're better off with a BoatHire24 boat rental that includes a skipper and more space.

If you're a first-timer, the operator will give you a 5-minute briefing. You'll be slow at first, but you'll get the hang of it quickly. Don't try to show off; the sea can be unpredictable. Stick to the designated area and watch for other boats.

Experienced riders can ask for a faster model or a longer tour. Some operators offer a 'performance' package that removes the speed limiter. That's for experts only.

If you're not sure, try a 30-minute session first. You can always book a longer one later.

Safety Tips for Jet Skiing in Marbella

Always wear the life jacket provided. It's not optional. Keep a safe distance from other boats, swimmers, and anchored vessels. The speed limit inside the marina is 3 knots, so slow down when you're near the dock. Outside, you can go faster, but watch for buoys and fishing lines.

Don't drink alcohol before or during the ride. The operator will refuse to let you drive if you're intoxicated. And don't try to jump the wake of a big boat; it's dangerous and can damage the jet ski.

If you fall off, stay with the jet ski. It floats, and the engine will cut out automatically if the lanyard detaches. Wave for help if you're far from shore. Most operators have a chase boat that follows the group.

Check the fuel level before you leave. A full tank lasts about 1 hour of hard riding. If you run out, you'll be stranded until the operator comes to rescue you, which costs extra.

What to Bring on a Jet Ski Rental

Bring a swimsuit, sunscreen (waterproof, SPF 50+), a towel, and a change of clothes. You'll get wet. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos, but don't rely on it. Leave valuables in a locker at the marina or in your car. Most operators provide a small dry bag for keys and phones.

If you wear glasses, use a strap or wear contact lenses with goggles. The wind will rip them off. A rash guard or wetsuit top is a good idea if you're prone to sunburn.

Don't bring a big bag or anything that can't get wet. You'll be on the water for 30 minutes to 2 hours, so keep it minimal.

Other Water Activities Near Marbella

If jet skis aren't your thing, you can try parasailing, flyboarding, or a banana boat ride. Or rent a RIB speedboat that seats 4, 6 people and hits 40 knots. For a more relaxed day, charter a catamaran or a sailing yacht with a skipper. You can anchor at Cala del Faro or go dolphin watching near the Strait of Gibraltar.

BoatHire24 lists all these options on the homepage. You can compare prices, read descriptions, and book directly.

If you're interested in the local history, take a day trip to the Nerja caves or Estepona old town. But that's a different kind of adventure.

Frequently Asked Questions About Jet Ski Marbella

How Jet Skiing Differs Between Marbella and Puerto Banús

The experience changes depending on where you launch. In Marbella Marina, you ride along a 3 km stretch of coastline with the old town on one side and the sea on the other. The water is usually calm in the morning, with a slight chop by midday. You'll see the La Concha mountain behind you and the beach clubs like La Sala and Bono Beach ahead. The ride is scenic but not extreme. In Puerto Banús, you start inside the marina, weaving between superyachts and dinghies. Once you exit the breakwater, you hit open water immediately. The swell is bigger, and the wind picks up faster. You can ride south towards the Rio Verde or north towards the Cabopino dunes. The adrenaline is higher because the sea is less predictable. Prices reflect that: Banús is about 20% more expensive for the same duration.

Best Time of Day for Jet Skiing in Marbella

The morning slot between 9 AM and 11 AM is the best. The sea is flat, the wind is light (under 5 knots), and the sun is not yet scorching. You'll have the water mostly to yourself because the big charter boats leave later. The afternoon from 2 PM to 5 PM is busier and choppier. The levante wind picks up, creating waves of 0.5 to 1 metre. That makes the ride bumpy and less enjoyable for beginners. The sunset slot around 7 PM to 8 PM in summer is popular for couples. The light is golden, and the sea often calms down again. But you need to be back before the marina closes, usually at 8 PM. Some operators offer a sunset tour that includes a stop for photos. That costs around EUR 200 for 1 hour.

What Happens If You Damage the Jet Ski

You are liable for any damage you cause. The deposit of EUR 200 to EUR 500 covers minor scratches and dings. If you crack the hull, snap the steering, or sink the thing, you pay the full repair cost. That can be EUR 1,000 to EUR 5,000 depending on the damage. Some operators offer a damage waiver for EUR 30 to EUR 50 that caps your liability at the deposit amount. Read the contract before you sign. Do not take the jet ski out of the designated area. If you hit a rock or a buoy, that's on you. If you crash into another boat, you pay for both repairs. The operator will take photos of the jet ski before you leave. Inspect it yourself and note any existing scratches. That saves arguments later.

Jet Ski Tours vs Self-Guided Rides

A self-guided ride lets you go where you want within a set area, usually a 3 to 5 km stretch of coast. You get a map and a radio, and you're on your own. That's fine if you know the area. A guided tour costs about 20% more but includes a lead jet ski that takes you to specific spots. For example, a 2-hour guided tour from Puerto Banús might go south to the Cala del Faro cove, stop for a swim, then head to the Rio Verde estuary to see the birdlife. From Estepona, a guided tour can go towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you might see dolphins. The guide knows the safe routes and the best photo spots. If you're a first-timer, a guided tour is worth the extra money. You won't get lost, and you'll see more.

Jet Skiing for Non-Swimmers and Beginners

You do not need to be a strong swimmer to ride a jet ski. The life jacket keeps you afloat. But you should be comfortable in the water. If you fall off, you need to stay calm and wait for the operator to pick you up. The jet ski floats, so you can hold onto it. Beginners should start with a 30-minute session in calm conditions. Do not go out in rough sea. The operator will give you a 5-minute briefing covering the controls, the throttle, and the kill switch. You will start slow and build up speed. Do not try to turn sharply at high speed; you will flip. Keep your weight back and your knees bent. Most people get the hang of it within 10 minutes. If you are nervous, ask for a 2-seater so you can ride as a passenger first.

Group Jet Ski Rentals in Marbella

You can rent multiple jet skis for a group. Most operators have 4 to 8 units available. For a stag or hen party, you can book a block of 30-minute or 1-hour slots. The group goes out together, with a chase boat following. The price per person is the same as for a single rental, but some operators offer a 10% discount for groups of 4 or more. You need to book in advance, especially in July and August. The group must stay together and follow the guide. If someone in the group is reckless, the whole group gets called back. For large groups of 10 or more, consider a BoatHire24 catamaran charter instead. It's more social and includes drinks and food.

Jet Ski vs RIB Speedboat: Which Is Better

A jet ski is for 1 or 2 people. A RIB speedboat seats 4 to 6 and hits similar speeds (40 to 50 knots). The RIB is more stable, has more storage, and you can sit down properly. It's better for families or groups who want speed without the physical effort of balancing on a jet ski. The cost is higher: a 1-hour RIB rental is around EUR 300 to EUR 500, compared to EUR 150 to EUR 200 for a jet ski. But you share the cost among passengers. If you are 4 people, a RIB works out cheaper per person. If you are alone or with one other, a jet ski is more fun. Both are listed on the BoatHire24 search under 'speedboats' and 'jet skis'.
