h1: Boat Rental Amalfi, Why You’re Looking in the Wrong Place
intro:
You typed “boat rental Amalfi” into Google hoping for turquoise water, cliffside villages, and a skipper who knows every cove. Fair enough. The Amalfi Coast is a dream. But here is the problem: you are probably looking at a map of Italy, and your wallet is already crying at the thought of peak-season prices, crowded harbours, and the hassle of getting there from Malaga.

What if you could get the same vibe, limestone cliffs, hidden coves, a chilled skipper, cold drinks on deck, without the EUR 5,000-a-week price tag and the two-hour queue for a mooring? Welcome to the Costa del Sol. BoatHire24 runs a marketplace of private boats and professional skippers out of Marbella, Puerto Banús, Estepona, and five other ports. Yes, the water is warm. Yes, the mountains come right down to the sea. And yes, your boat rental Amalfi search just got redirected to something better.
bodyHtml:
What a Boat Rental Amalfi Search Actually Means

When you search for a boat rental Amalfi, you are after a few specific things: a boat with a skipper, half-day or full-day itinerary, swimming stops, maybe a visit to a seaside town, and a decent lunch spot. The Amalfi Coast delivers that, Positano, Amalfi, Ravello, Capri. But the reality is that a private boat hire there in July costs from EUR 800 to EUR 2,500 for a day, and you are competing with hundreds of other tourists for the same patch of sea.

The Costa del Sol offers the same package, skipper, insurance, fuel, snorkel gear, cold drinks, for around EUR 450 to EUR 900 for a half-day, and EUR 800 to EUR 1,800 for a full day, depending on the boat. You get the same Mediterranean sun, the same Sierra Blanca mountains dropping into the sea, and a coastline that runs 150 km from Nerja to Sotogrande. The only thing missing is the Italian accent.

Why the Costa del Sol Beats Amalfi for a Boat Rental

Let’s be honest. The Amalfi Coast is stunning, but it is also a logistical headache. The roads are narrow, parking is a nightmare, and the marinas are packed. On the water, you share the sea with ferries, water taxis, and dozens of other rental boats. The Costa del Sol, by contrast, has 300 days of sunshine a year, calm seas (especially in the summer), and a coastline that is less crowded because most tourists stay on the beach.

From Puerto Banús, you can head west to the Strait of Gibraltar and see dolphins, or east towards Cabopino and the dunes of Artola. The water temperature hits 24 degrees C in August, and the wind is usually light enough for a relaxing cruise. Your skipper will know the best spots for a swim, Cala del Faro, the cliffs of Maro, or the quiet coves near Estepona. No waiting for a mooring buoy, no EUR 50 harbour fee for a 20-minute stop.

What’s Included in Your Boat Rental Amalfi Alternative

Every boat on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. You do not need a licence, and you do not need to worry about navigation, docking, or fuel. The skipper handles everything. What you get depends on the boat type, but most rentals include:

  • Fuel for the itinerary (usually up to 4-6 hours of cruising)
  • Skipper fee and insurance
  • Snorkelling equipment
  • Cooler with ice (you bring your own drinks and food)
  • Bluetooth speaker and towels on most boats

Some catamarans and yachts include a stand-up paddleboard, a small inflatable tender, or even a water slide. Check the listing details on our search page before booking. Prices start from around EUR 450 for a half-day on a 6-metre RIB, and go up to EUR 3,500 for a full day on a 20-metre motor yacht.

Which Port to Choose for Your Boat Rental Amalfi-Style Trip

The Costa del Sol has six main departure ports, and each gives you a slightly different experience. Here is a quick guide:

  • Puerto Banús, The glitzy one. Superyachts, designer shops, and a lively atmosphere. Great for a luxury charter or a party boat. Depart from here to see the Marbella coastline and the cliffs of Cabopino.
  • Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), More relaxed than Banús, with good restaurants and a central location. Ideal for a family day out to the west towards Estepona or east to Cabopino.
  • Cabopino, Small, quiet, and close to the Artola dunes nature reserve. Perfect for a peaceful day on a sailing yacht or a fishing trip.
  • Estepona, The old town is beautiful, and the marina is less crowded. Good for a budget-friendly rental or a trip to the Strait of Gibraltar.
  • Sotogrande, Upscale, with a long channel leading to the sea. Best for a luxury yacht charter or a long cruise towards Gibraltar.
  • Benalmádena, East of Marbella, near Torremolinos. A lively marina with lots of bars and restaurants. Good for a half-day RIB trip or a fishing charter.

Boat Types for Your Amalfi-Style Charter

You do not need a 50-foot superyacht to have a great day. Here are the main options on BoatHire24:

  • Motor yachts, From 8 m to 20 m. Fast, stable, and spacious. Good for groups of 6 to 12. Prices from EUR 600 half-day.
  • Catamarans, 10 m to 15 m. Very stable, lots of deck space, shallow draft for anchoring close to shore. Ideal for families or groups who want to swim. Prices from EUR 700 half-day.
  • Sailing yachts, 9 m to 14 m. Quieter, more eco-friendly, and a classic experience. If you want the Amalfi sailing vibe, this is it. Prices from EUR 500 half-day.
  • RIBs and speedboats, 5 m to 9 m. Fast, fun, and affordable. Best for a couple or a small group. Prices from EUR 450 half-day.
  • Fishing boats, 6 m to 10 m. Equipped for rod fishing, trolling, or bottom fishing. Skipper knows the best spots. Prices from EUR 400 half-day.
  • Licence-free day boats, 5 m to 7 m. No skipper included, but you can drive them with a simple safety briefing. Only available in certain ports. Prices from EUR 250 half-day.
  • Superyachts, 20 m to 40 m. Crew of 3-5, full catering, water toys. Price on request, but expect EUR 5,000+ per day.

Pricing Guidance, What to Expect for a Boat Rental Amalfi Alternative

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. Here is a rough guide based on typical listings on BoatHire24:

  • Low season (November to March): Half-day from EUR 350, full day from EUR 600.
  • Mid season (April, May, October): Half-day from EUR 450, full day from EUR 800.
  • High season (June to September): Half-day from EUR 550, full day from EUR 1,000.

These prices are for a standard motor yacht or catamaran. Superyachts and luxury charters are more. Fuel is usually included for the itinerary, but if you want to cruise further (e.g., to Gibraltar or Nerja), the skipper may charge extra. Always confirm what is included before booking.

Best Time of Year for a Boat Rental Amalfi-Style Trip

The Costa del Sol is a year-round destination, but the best months for a boat rental are May through October. The sea is warm (20-24 degrees C), the wind is light, and the days are long. July and August are the busiest, but the water is at its warmest and the evenings are perfect for a sunset cruise.

If you want to avoid crowds, go in May, June, or September. The weather is still good, the sea is calm, and you will have more choice of boats. October can be hit or miss, some days are still summer, others are cooler. If you are coming in winter, book a RIB or a motor yacht with a cabin, and bring a jacket.

How to Book Your Boat Rental Amalfi Alternative

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. You do not need to call or email a dozen companies. Here is the process:

  1. Go to BoatHire24 and enter your dates, group size, and preferred port.
  2. Browse the listings. Each one shows the boat, skipper, price, and availability.
  3. Click “Book Now” or “Send Enquiry”. For instant-book boats, you pay online and get confirmation straight away. For others, you send a request and the owner confirms within a few hours.
  4. Pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the date. Balance is paid on the day, usually in cash or by card on board.
  5. Show up at the port 15 minutes before departure. The skipper will give a safety briefing and answer questions.

If you are unsure which boat to choose, read the owner profiles and check the reviews. Most boats have at least 10 reviews. If you need help, email the BoatHire24 support team, they speak English and Spanish.

Who Is This Boat Rental For?

A boat rental Amalfi alternative on the Costa del Sol works for:

  • Couples, A half-day on a RIB or sailing yacht is romantic and private. Sunset cruises are popular.
  • Families with kids, Catamarans are stable and safe. Kids love swimming, snorkelling, and jumping off the boat.
  • Groups of friends, Motor yachts and catamarans can take 8-12 people. Bring a speaker and a cooler.
  • Corporate events, A day charter for team building or client entertainment. Many boats have catering options.
  • Fishing enthusiasts, Dedicated fishing boats with experienced skippers who know the local waters.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter (sometimes called a “group tour”) on a catamaran or sailing yacht. Check the listings for “shared” or “join-in” options.

Local Colour, What You’ll See on the Water

The Costa del Sol has its own version of the Amalfi charm. From the water, you will see:

  • La Concha mountain, The iconic peak behind Marbella, visible from miles out.
  • Puerto Banús, The marina with the superyachts and the golden arches of the port entrance.
  • Río Verde, A small river that flows into the sea near Marbella, with a nature reserve and birdlife.
  • Cala del Faro, A hidden cove near Estepona with a lighthouse and clear water.
  • Estepona old town, Whitewashed houses and flower pots, best seen from the water.
  • Strait of Gibraltar, If you go west, you might see dolphins, whales, and the African coast.
  • Nerja caves, East of Marbella, the cliffs of Maro and the famous caves are visible from a boat.

Your skipper will likely point out landmarks and tell you stories about the area. It is not Amalfi, but it is just as beautiful in its own way.

Frequently Asked Questions About Boat Rental Amalfi

If you still have doubts, read the BoatHire24 blog for more tips on chartering a boat in Spain, or check the FAQ section below.

How the Amalfi Coast Compares on Price and Practicality

If you have actually priced a boat rental Amalfi, you know the numbers are steep. A standard 8-metre motor yacht in Positano in August runs from EUR 900 to EUR 1,500 for a half-day, and that is without skipper tip or lunch. Add fuel surcharges, mooring fees at Capri (EUR 50 to EUR 100 per stop), and the fact that many boats charge extra for snorkel gear, and you are looking at EUR 1,500 for a basic day. On the Costa del Sol, a comparable 8-metre motor yacht from Marbella Marina costs EUR 550 to EUR 800 half-day, with fuel, skipper, and gear included. You also avoid the EUR 30 per person landing tax that some Amalfi ports charge for day-trippers.

What a Typical Itinerary Looks Like from Puerto Banús

Say you book a 10-metre catamaran for a full day from Puerto Banús. You meet the skipper at 10:00, load your cooler and bags, and get a 10-minute safety briefing. By 10:30, you are motoring west along the coast. First stop is Cala del Faro at 11:15, a 30-minute swim in clear water with the lighthouse in the background. Then you cruise towards Estepona, arriving at 12:30 for a walk through the old town or a lunch at a chiringuito on the beach. After lunch, you head back east, stopping at the Río Verde estuary for a swim and maybe spotting herons. You return to Puerto Banús at 17:00. That is a full day, seven hours on the water, three swimming stops, a town visit, and no crowds.

Which Boat Type Matches Your Amalfi Expectations

The Amalfi Coast is famous for its classic wooden gozzo boats and sleek RIBs. If you want that aesthetic, look for a sailing yacht or a classic motor yacht on BoatHire24. A 12-metre sailing yacht from Cabopino costs around EUR 650 half-day and gives you the same romantic silhouette against the cliffs. If you want speed, a 7-metre RIB with a 200 hp engine hits 35 knots and gets you from Marbella to Estepona in 20 minutes. That is useful if you want to cover more coastline in a half-day. For groups, a 14-metre catamaran from Sotogrande costs EUR 900 half-day and has a trampoline net at the bow for lounging, plus a shaded deck for lunch.

How the Weather and Sea Conditions Differ from Amalfi

The Amalfi Coast gets strong afternoon winds in summer, the Ponente and Libeccio, which can kick up chop and make anchoring uncomfortable. The Costa del Sol has the Levante wind from the east, but it is usually light in summer, 5 to 15 knots, and the sea state is calm to slight. The water is warmer too, 24 degrees C in August versus 22 degrees C in Amalfi. If you are prone to seasickness, the Costa del Sol is a safer bet. The only rough area is near the Strait of Gibraltar, where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean, but your skipper will avoid that if you want a calm day. Most itineraries stick to the sheltered bays between Marbella and Estepona.

What to Bring and What Not to Bring on Your Charter

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (factor 50, the sun is strong), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the evening. Bring your own drinks and food in a cooler, most boats have ice on board. Do not bring glass bottles, many skippers ban them for safety reasons. Do not bring a drone unless you have permission, some marinas restrict drone flights. Do not bring a large suitcase, there is limited storage on smaller boats. If you are on a superyacht, the crew will handle everything, but on a standard charter, you are self-catering. A good tip is to bring a waterproof phone case or a dry bag for your valuables.

How to Save Money on Your Boat Rental Amalfi Alternative

Book in advance, at least two weeks in high season, to get the best prices. Last-minute bookings in July and August can be 20% more expensive. Choose a half-day instead of a full day, many boats offer a morning or afternoon slot from EUR 450. Go in May or September, when prices drop by 30% and the sea is still warm. Share the cost with a group, a 10-metre catamaran for 8 people at EUR 800 full day works out to EUR 100 per person. Avoid the superyacht category unless you have a corporate budget. Check the search page for “special offers” or “last minute” filters, some owners discount unsold dates.

Why Local Knowledge Matters More Than You Think

The skipper is not just a driver. They know where the fish are, which coves have the clearest water, and which restaurants will let you moor for free if you order lunch. On the Costa del Sol, a good skipper will take you to Cala del Moral near Estepona, a hidden cove that most tourists miss, or to the cliffs of Maro where you can see underwater caves. They will also know the best times to avoid the wind and the crowds. On BoatHire24, every skipper has a profile with reviews, read them to see if they are punctual, friendly, and knowledgeable. A skipper with 50 reviews and a 4.9 rating is worth the extra EUR 50.

h1: Yacht Charter Sardinia: Your Guide to Skippered Boats from Costa del Sol
intro: You want a yacht charter Sardinia, but you are reading about Marbella. There is a reason for that. Sardinia is a stunning destination for a yacht charter, with its turquoise waters, dramatic cliffs, and glamorous ports like Porto Cervo. But organising a charter there from scratch can be a hassle. BoatHire24 is based in Marbella, Spain, and we specialise in skippered boat rentals from the Costa del Sol. Our fleet ranges from motor yachts to catamarans, and every booking includes a licensed skipper. You can explore the Mediterranean in style, whether you are cruising the Balearics or the Spanish coast. This page explains how a yacht charter Sardinia can be reimagined from our base in southern Spain, with practical advice on ports, boats, and seasons.
bodyHtml:
What a Yacht Charter Sardinia Includes with BoatHire24

Every charter from BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. You do not need a boating licence. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and mooring. You focus on relaxing, swimming, and sightseeing. The boat is fully equipped with safety gear, a tender, and basic amenities. Fuel costs are extra and depend on the itinerary. Catering, drinks, and extra crew like a hostess or chef can be arranged for an additional fee. Our boats are maintained to high standards, and you can inspect them before departure. A typical day charter lasts 8 hours, but we can customise half-day or multi-day trips. For a yacht charter Sardinia, we recommend at least a week to explore the island properly, but we can help you plan a shorter trip from the Costa del Sol if you are combining destinations.

Ports of Departure for Your Sardinia Charter

Our main ports are on the Costa del Sol: Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. From these, you can sail to Sardinia, but it is a long crossing. A direct trip from Marbella to Cagliari in Sardinia is about 400 nautical miles, taking around 30 hours on a motor yacht at 15 knots. Most clients prefer to fly to Sardinia and charter a boat locally. However, we can arrange a delivery crew if you want to sail your charter boat to Sardinia and start from there. Alternatively, combine a Costa del Sol charter with a flight to Olbia or Alghero and use a local partner. We have networks in Sardinia, but our core service is from Spain. For a pure yacht charter Sardinia, you might consider flying to the island and using a local operator, but we can provide advice on the best options.

Boat Options for Your Sardinia Charter

We offer motor yachts from 30 to 80 feet, catamarans from 35 to 50 feet, sailing yachts from 35 to 60 feet, and RIBs for day trips. For Sardinia, a catamaran is ideal for stability and space, especially for families. A motor yacht is better for speed and covering more coastline. Prices vary. A 40-foot motor yacht starts from around EUR 1,200 per day in low season, including skipper. A 50-foot catamaran is from EUR 2,000 per day. Fuel for a day trip in Sardinia might cost EUR 300 to EUR 800 depending on speed and distance. You can browse our search page to see current availability, though boats are specifically for Costa del Sol. For Sardinia, we recommend contacting us directly for custom itineraries.

Pricing Guidance for a Yacht Charter Sardinia

Prices depend on boat size, season, and duration. Low season (April to May, October) sees rates about 30% lower than peak. Mid-season (June, September) is moderate. High season (July, August) is the most expensive. A week on a 50-foot motor yacht in August can cost from EUR 12,000 to EUR 20,000 including skipper, excluding fuel and food. A catamaran charter in June is around EUR 8,000 to EUR 15,000 per week. For a day trip in Sardinia, expect from EUR 1,500 for a 40-foot boat. Our pricing is transparent, and we do not add hidden fees. You can compare options on our site. For exact quotes, use our contact form.

Seasons and Best Times for Sardinia

Sardinia has a Mediterranean climate. Summer temperatures average 30 degrees C in July and August, with calm seas. Spring and autumn are milder, around 22 degrees C, with fewer crowds. The best time for a yacht charter Sardinia is May to September. July and August are peak, with strong winds like the Maestrale sometimes causing choppy conditions. September is often the best month: warm water, light winds, and fewer tourists. Winter charters are possible but less popular due to cooler weather and rougher seas. From the Costa del Sol, you can charter year-round, but for Sardinia, plan between May and October.

How to Book Your Yacht Charter Sardinia

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You can browse our search page to see available boats in the Costa del Sol. For a Sardinia charter, contact us directly via phone or email. We will discuss your requirements: number of guests, preferred dates, boat type, and budget. We then source a suitable boat from our fleet or partner network. A deposit of 50% is required to secure the booking, with the balance due two weeks before departure. We provide a contract with terms and conditions. Cancellation policies vary, but we recommend travel insurance. Our team is available to answer questions before and during your charter.

Who Is a Yacht Charter Sardinia For

A yacht charter Sardinia suits couples, families, and groups of friends. It is ideal for those who want a private, flexible experience without the formality of a cruise. Couples enjoy romantic sunsets and secluded coves. Families appreciate the space and activities like snorkelling and paddleboarding. Groups can party or relax. It is also popular for corporate events or celebrations like birthdays and anniversaries. If you are new to boating, the skipper makes it easy. For experienced sailors, you can take the helm if you have a licence. Our charters are inclusive and accessible.

Local Colour and Highlights on a Sardinia Charter

Sardinia offers incredible sights. The Costa Smeralda is famous for its emerald waters and luxury resorts. Porto Cervo is the hub for superyachts and designer boutiques. The Maddalena Archipelago is a national park with pristine beaches like Spiaggia Rosa. Cala di Volpe is a classic anchorage. The Gulf of Orosei has dramatic cliffs and sea caves. The island also has ancient Nuragic ruins and excellent cuisine, including porceddu and seafood. While our base is in Marbella, we can share local knowledge for Sardinia through our blog where we cover Mediterranean destinations. For example, we have articles on the Balearics and the Costa del Sol that offer transferable tips.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Yacht Charter

BoatHire24 is a marketplace with a fleet of well-maintained boats. We focus on the Costa del Sol but have experience with Mediterranean charters. Our skippers are licensed and local. We offer transparent pricing and no hidden fees. Customer service is priority, and we help with itineraries. Unlike some booking sites, we are based in Marbella and know the area. For a yacht charter Sardinia, we can coordinate logistics from Spain. Check our BoatHire24 homepage for more details on our services.

Alternatives to a Sardinia Charter from the Costa del Sol

If Sardinia seems too far, consider the Balearic Islands: Ibiza, Mallorca, Menorca, or Formentera. These are a 5 to 8 hour sail from Marbella. The waters are similarly clear, and the islands have vibrant nightlife and quiet coves. The Costa del Sol itself offers great sailing, with stops in Estepona, Sotogrande, and Gibraltar. You can see dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar. Another option is the Algarve in Portugal, a 2 hour sail from Sotogrande. All these can be booked through BoatHire24. For a true Sardinia experience, we recommend flying to Olbia and chartering locally, but we can help with that too.

Navigating Sardinia’s Coastline: Key Ports and Anchorages

Sardinia’s coastline stretches over 1,800 kilometres, so picking a base port matters. Olbia in the northeast is the gateway to the Costa Smeralda, with direct flights from most European cities. Alghero in the northwest offers a charming old town and proximity to the Neptune’s Grotto caves. Cagliari in the south is the capital, with a large marina and easy access to the Poetto beach and the Molentargius salt flats where flamingos gather. For a quieter start, consider the marina at Porto Torres in the north or Arbatax in the east. From these ports, you can plan day trips. For example, from Olbia, a 20-nautical-mile run gets you to the Maddalena Archipelago. From Cagliari, you can reach the cliffs of the Gulf of Orosei in about 25 nautical miles. Fuel stops are available at most marinas, but check operating hours in low season. Mooring fees in peak season can range from EUR 50 to EUR 200 per night depending on the marina’s prestige. Anchorages are free but require a tender for shore access.

Choosing the Right Boat for Sardinian Waters

Sardinia’s waters can be choppy, especially when the Maestrale wind blows from the northwest, so stability matters. A catamaran with a beam of around 8 metres offers less roll and more deck space, making it ideal for families with children. A motor yacht with a deep-V hull cuts through waves better for longer passages. For exploring shallow coves like Cala Coticcio or Cala dei Sospiri, a RIB or a small day boat with a draft under 1 metre is practical. Sailing yachts are slower but quieter and more fuel-efficient; a 40-foot sailing yacht cruises at around 6 knots, so covering 50 nautical miles takes about 8 hours. For a week-long charter, a motor yacht allows you to visit more ports: you can start in Olbia, spend two days in the Maddalena Archipelago, then head south to the Gulf of Orosei, and return. With a sailing yacht, you might focus on one region. Our fleet includes options for all preferences, and you can filter by size and type on our search page.

Sample Itinerary: A Week in the Maddalena Archipelago

Day one: depart from Olbia, motor 15 nautical miles to the Maddalena Archipelago, anchor at Cala Corsara on Spargi island for swimming. Overnight at the marina in La Maddalena town. Day two: sail to Budelli island, see the famous pink sand beach (Spiaggia Rosa, no landing allowed, but you can view from the boat), then to Cala Santa Maria for lunch. Day three: move to Caprera island, visit the Garibaldi museum, anchor at Cala Coticcio. Day four: head to the main island of Sardinia, stop at Porto Cervo for shopping and dinner. Day five: cruise to the Gulf of Orosei, anchor at Cala Gonone for a hike to the Bue Marino caves. Day six: explore Cala Luna and Cala Sisine, both with white sand and limestone cliffs. Day seven: return to Olbia. Fuel for a 40-foot motor yacht on this itinerary would be around EUR 600 to EUR 900. Mooring fees for the week could total EUR 300 to EUR 700. Food and drinks are extra, but you can provision in Olbia or Porto Cervo. This itinerary covers about 150 nautical miles total, manageable for a relaxed pace.

Understanding the Costs Beyond the Charter Fee

The base charter fee includes the boat, skipper, and basic safety equipment. Additional costs you should budget for include fuel, which is typically EUR 1.50 to EUR 2.00 per litre for diesel. A 40-foot motor yacht burns about 40 to 60 litres per hour at cruising speed, so a day trip of 8 hours might cost EUR 300 to EUR 500 in fuel. A catamaran burns less, around 20 to 30 litres per hour. Mooring fees in popular spots like Porto Cervo can be EUR 150 per night in August, while smaller towns like Cala Gonone charge EUR 40 to EUR 80. Tender fuel is often included but check. Provisioning for a week for 6 people can cost EUR 500 to EUR 1,000 depending on whether you eat out. Skipper gratuity is customary, around 10% to 15% of the charter fee. If you need a hostess or chef, budget an extra EUR 150 to EUR 250 per day. Insurance is typically included in the charter fee, but check the deductible, which can be EUR 1,000 to EUR 3,000 for damage. We recommend bringing cash for small expenses, as some anchorages have no card facilities.

Weather and Sea Conditions: What to Expect Month by Month

May: average air temperature 20 degrees C, water 18 degrees C. Winds are light, mostly from the west at 10 to 15 knots. Seas are calm, but occasional Mistral can bring short swells. June: 25 degrees C air, 22 degrees C water. Wind patterns shift to the Maestrale from the northwest, often blowing 15 to 20 knots in the afternoon. July: 30 degrees C air, 25 degrees C water. Maestrale can gust to 30 knots, especially in the Strait of Bonifacio. August: similar to July, but with more humidity. September: 26 degrees C air, 24 degrees C water. Winds ease to 10 to 15 knots. October: 22 degrees C air, 20 degrees C water. Calm periods are common, but storms can develop. For a yacht charter Sardinia, June and September are ideal for stable weather and fewer crowds. July and August require careful planning to avoid strong winds. Always check a marine forecast like Windy or the Italian Meteo before departing. Our skippers are trained to adjust itineraries based on conditions, so you stay safe.

Legal Requirements and Documentation for Chartering in Sardinia

If you charter a boat with a skipper from BoatHire24, you need no boating licence. The skipper holds an Italian or equivalent licence. For bareboat charters (without skipper), you need an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or equivalent, plus a valid VHF radio licence. Italy requires a separate licence for boats over 24 metres in length. All charter boats must have insurance, registration documents, and safety equipment as per Italian regulations. Your passport or ID is required for the charter contract. If you are from outside the EU, check visa requirements for entering Italy. The charter company will provide a list of required documents. For our Sardinia charters through partners, we ensure all paperwork is in order. You can contact us for a checklist.

How to Combine a Costa del Sol Charter with a Sardinia Trip

If you want to experience both regions, you can charter a boat from Marbella for a week, then fly from Málaga to Olbia or Cagliari for a second week. Flights take about 2 hours and cost from EUR 50 to EUR 150 one-way with carriers like Ryanair or Vueling. You can then charter a second boat in Sardinia through our partner network. Alternatively, you can sail your charter boat from Marbella to Sardinia, but that requires a 30-hour crossing and good weather. We can arrange a delivery crew to move the boat for an extra fee. Another option is a multi-destination charter: start in Marbella, sail to Ibiza, then to Mallorca, and then to Sardinia over two weeks. That covers about 600 nautical miles and requires careful planning. We can help with logistics, including provisioning and crew changes. Check our blog for tips on combining Mediterranean destinations.

What to Pack for a Yacht Charter in Sardinia

Pack light, as storage space on boats is limited. Bring swimwear, a lightweight wetsuit if you plan to snorkel in May or October when water is cooler, and a windbreaker for evenings. Non-slip boat shoes are essential, as deck surfaces get slippery. Sunscreen with high SPF, a hat, and sunglasses are must-haves. A small backpack for shore excursions is useful. If you are prone to seasickness, bring medication like Dramamine or acupressure bands. A waterproof phone case or dry bag protects your electronics. For evenings, casual smart clothes are fine for restaurants in Porto Cervo or Alghero. No formal wear needed. If you charter a catamaran, there is more cabin space, so you can pack a bit more. For RIBs, space is tight, so a soft-sided bag is better. We provide towels and bed linen, but check with us before you pack.

Dining and Provisioning on a Sardinia Charter

Sardinia has a rich food culture. Onboard, you can cook simple meals or hire a chef for EUR 200 per day. Local specialties include porceddu (roast suckling pig), culurgiones (stuffed pasta), and bottarga (cured fish roe). Seafood is abundant: try spaghetti alle vongole or grilled lobster. For provisioning, supermarkets like Conad or Lidl are in most towns. Olbia has a large market with fresh produce. Porto Cervo has upscale delis but higher prices. If you anchor in a remote cove, you cannot easily get supplies, so plan ahead. Many marinas have waterfront restaurants where you can eat out. A meal for two with wine costs around EUR 50 to EUR 80 in mid-range places. For a special dinner in Porto Cervo, budget EUR 150 per person. Our skippers can recommend local spots and help with provisioning logistics.

Environmental Considerations and Responsible Boating

Sardinia’s marine environment is protected, especially in the Maddalena Archipelago National Park. You must not anchor in seagrass meadows (Posidonia oceanica), as it is illegal and damages the ecosystem. Use designated mooring buoys where available, often free or for a small fee. Do not discharge sewage within 3 nautical miles of the coast; use holding tanks. Avoid single-use plastics; bring reusable water bottles and bags. When snorkelling, do not touch coral or marine life. Respect wildlife, including dolphins and sea turtles. Our skippers are trained in eco-friendly practices and will brief you. We support sustainable tourism and encourage guests to follow these guidelines.

Booking Your Sardinia Charter Through BoatHire24: Step by Step

Start by visiting our BoatHire24 homepage to understand our services. Then, use the contact form or call us to discuss your Sardinia plans. We will ask for your preferred dates, number of guests, budget, and boat type. We then check availability with our partner fleet in Sardinia or arrange a delivery from Costa del Sol. We provide a quote with a breakdown of costs: charter fee, fuel estimate, mooring fees, and extras. Once you agree, we send a contract and invoice for the 50% deposit. The balance is due 30 days before departure. We send a pre-charter briefing with packing list, itinerary suggestions, and contact details for the skipper. On the day, you meet the boat at the agreed port. After the charter, we ask for feedback to improve our service. The whole process takes 1 to 2 weeks for a custom itinerary.

title: Boat Rental Amsterdam
metaDescription: Book a boat rental in Amsterdam with BoatHire24. Compare motor yachts, canal boats, and speedboats from local operators. Includes skipper and insurance.
h1: Boat Rental Amsterdam, Compare & Book with BoatHire24
intro:
Thinking about a boat rental Amsterdam? You are not alone. Every year tens of thousands of visitors and locals take to the canals to see the city from the water. The good news is that you can skip the crowded tour boats and hire your own private vessel for a few hours or a full day. BoatHire24 lets you compare motor yachts, canal boats, speedboats, and even small sailing boats from multiple operators in Amsterdam, all with a licensed skipper included. No licence needed. No hidden fees. Just pick your boat, choose your time, and go.

Amsterdam has over 100 kilometres of canals, 1,500 bridges, and a UNESCO-listed canal ring. A private boat gives you the freedom to stop at a brown café for a beer, cruise past the Anne Frank House, or head out to the greener edges like the Amstel River or the Nieuwe Meer lake. You can do it all without the hassle of navigating locks or dealing with rental paperwork. The skipper handles everything. You just sit back, drink something cold, and take photos.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Boat Rental Amsterdam?

When you book through BoatHire24, every Amsterdam boat rental comes with a professional skipper. That means you do not need a boating licence or any prior experience. The skipper knows the canals, the traffic rules, and the best spots to see. Most packages also include fuel, insurance, and a basic safety briefing. Some boats have a cooler for drinks, a Bluetooth speaker, and a bimini top for shade. What is not included: food and drinks (though you can bring your own or order catering for an extra fee), and gratuity for the skipper (optional but appreciated).

Standard rental durations are 2 hours, 3 hours, 4 hours, or a full day (8 hours). Evening cruises are also popular, especially from April to September when the sun sets around 9 PM. You can typically bring up to 8 or 12 passengers, depending on the boat type. Larger groups can book a small party boat or a salon boat with a toilet and indoor seating.

Amsterdam’s Main Departure Points for Boat Rentals

Most boat rentals in Amsterdam depart from central locations: the Prinsengracht, Keizersgracht, or Herengracht canals near the Jordaan district. Other common pickup points include the Rijksmuseum area, the Central Station waterfront, and the Eastern Docklands. If you are staying in a hotel with a canal-side mooring, the operator can sometimes arrange pickup there. Always confirm the exact meeting point when you book. BoatHire24 listings include a map and exact address for each boat.

For a quieter start, consider renting from the Nieuwe Meer or the Amstel River, south of the city centre. These areas have less traffic and more open water. You can cruise past the Amsterdamse Bos forest or stop at a waterside restaurant in Ouderkerk aan de Amstel. The trade-off is a longer trip to the canal ring, but the peace and quiet might be worth it.

Boat Types Available for Amsterdam Canal Cruises

BoatHire24 lists several types of boats for rent in Amsterdam. The most common is the electric canal boat, silent, emission-free, and perfect for the narrow canals. These boats seat 6 to 12 people and have a low profile to fit under the bridges. Next are motor yachts (20 to 30 feet), faster and more luxurious, ideal for a birthday or anniversary. Speedboats (RIB or open bowrider) are louder and more fun for a group that wants to feel the wind. Some operators also offer salon boats with a glass roof, heating, and a toilet, good for cooler days or winter rentals.

A few operators have small sailing boats (like a 20-foot keelboat) for experienced sailors, but these are rare in the city centre because of the bridges. If you really want to sail, you are better off renting from the IJsselmeer or Markermeer, about 30 minutes north of Amsterdam. BoatHire24 does list a few sailing options near Volendam and Marken. For most visitors, an electric or motor boat is the practical choice.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Amsterdam

Prices for a boat rental in Amsterdam vary by season, boat size, and duration. In high season (May to September), expect to pay from around EUR 250 for a 2-hour cruise on a small electric boat for up to 6 people. A 4-hour rental on a 30-foot motor yacht for 8 to 10 people starts at about EUR 600. Full-day rentals (8 hours) on a luxury salon boat can go from EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,500, depending on the extras. Winter rates are roughly 20 to 30 percent lower. Always check the listing for exact pricing, some operators charge extra for catering, cleaning, or late returns.

BoatHire24 shows the total price upfront, including VAT and any mandatory fees. You pay a deposit (usually 25 to 50 percent) at booking, and the balance is due on the day. Cancellation policies vary: most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 48 hours in advance. Last-minute bookings are sometimes possible, but availability is limited in July and August.

Best Seasons for a Boat Rental in Amsterdam

The best time for a boat rental Amsterdam is from April to October. April and May have tulips in bloom and mild temperatures (12 to 18 degrees C). June to August are the warmest months (20 to 28 degrees C) with long daylight hours, perfect for sunset cruises. September is still pleasant (15 to 20 degrees C) and less crowded. October is cooler and rainier, but the autumn colours along the canals are beautiful. November to March is low season: many operators still run, but you will want a boat with a heated cabin or a roof. Some electric boats have transparent roofs and heaters, making them usable year-round.

Winter rentals are cheaper and quieter. You can see the canals dusted with snow or the Amsterdam Light Festival (December and January) from the water. Just dress warmly and bring a thermos. BoatHire24 lists winter-ready boats with heating and enclosed spaces. Check the amenities filter when you search.

How to Book a Boat Rental Amsterdam on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter Amsterdam as your destination, pick your date and time, and filter by boat type, capacity, and price. Each listing shows photos, a detailed description, the exact meeting point, and the total price. You can read the operator’s terms and cancellation policy before you reserve. When you find a boat you like, click “Book Now” and pay the deposit via credit card or PayPal. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper’s contact details and instructions for the day.

If you have questions about a specific boat or need help choosing, contact BoatHire24 support by email or phone. We do not charge booking fees, the price you see is the price you pay. For groups larger than 12, contact us directly and we will find a suitable vessel. Some operators can arrange multiple boats for corporate events or bachelor parties.

Who Should Rent a Boat in Amsterdam?

A private boat rental is ideal for couples, families, small groups of friends, and corporate teams. It is a flexible alternative to a scheduled canal tour. You can bring your own food and drinks, play your own music, and decide where to go. It works well for birthdays, anniversaries, proposals, or just a relaxed afternoon with friends. For business clients, a salon boat with Wi-Fi and catering can serve as a floating meeting room.

If you are travelling solo or on a tight budget, a shared canal tour (from around EUR 20 per person) might be better value. But for a memorable, private experience, a boat rental is hard to beat. BoatHire24 compares options so you can find the right balance of price, comfort, and style. We also have a blog with tips on Amsterdam canal routes, best photo spots, and what to bring.

Local Tips for Your Amsterdam Boat Rental

Bring a jacket even in summer, it can get windy on the water. Most boats have a canopy or bimini, but you will still feel the breeze. Pack sunscreen and sunglasses. If you are renting for more than 2 hours, bring snacks and drinks. Many operators allow you to bring your own alcohol, but check the policy first. Some boats have a cooler with ice. Do not bring glass bottles, use plastic or cans. The skipper will point out landmarks and tell you stories, but feel free to ask for specific stops like the Jordaan market or the NDSM wharf.

Respect the canal rules: no loud music after 10 PM, no swimming, and no jumping off the boat. The canals are for navigation, not for bathing. Your skipper will enforce these rules. Tipping the skipper 10 to 15 percent of the rental fee is customary if you are happy with the service. Cash is easiest, but some skippers accept a digital tip via QR code.

If you want to extend your rental, ask the skipper first. Extra hours are usually charged at a pro-rata rate, but only if the boat is available. Do not assume you can stay longer without permission, the next group might be waiting. For a full list of available boats and real-time availability, visit BoatHire24.

Canal Routes and Sights on Your Amsterdam Boat Rental

Your skipper will likely suggest a route through the UNESCO-listed canal ring. You will glide past the Anne Frank House, the Westerkerk, and the narrowest house in Amsterdam at Singel 7. The Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) shopping district is best seen from the water, with its boutique windows and leafy bridges. For a longer trip, head east to the NEMO Science Museum and the Maritime Museum, where you can see the replica of the 18th-century ship Amsterdam. The Eastern Docklands offer modern architecture like the Java-eiland and KNSM-eiland, with wide canals and less traffic.

If you want a nature break, ask the skipper to take you to the Amstel River. You will pass the Hermitage Amsterdam, the Stopera (city hall and opera house), and the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge), which is especially pretty when lit up at night. Further south, the river opens up and you can see houseboats, small beaches, and the Amsterdamse Bos. A typical 3-hour cruise covers about 10 km of canals and rivers, enough to see the main landmarks without feeling rushed.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind for Your Amsterdam Boat Rental

Pack a soft cooler bag with drinks and snacks. Most electric boats have a small table or counter for food. Bring a reusable water bottle, the skipper usually has tap water on board. Sunscreen is essential even on cloudy days, the UV reflects off the water. A hat and sunglasses help too. If you are renting in spring or autumn, bring a windproof jacket. The boat moves at 6 to 10 km/h, which creates a chill even at 15 degrees C. Do not bring high heels, they can damage the deck and are unsafe on the steps. Flat shoes or barefoot are best.

Leave behind glass bottles, they are banned on most boats for safety. Use plastic or metal containers. Do not bring inflatable toys, the canals are too narrow and busy for swimming or floating. Your skipper will store your bags in a dry compartment. If you plan to take photos, bring a camera with a strap, not just your phone. The low bridges mean you will duck often, and a phone can easily slip into the water. BoatHire24 recommends bringing a portable charger, the boat may have USB ports but not always.

Special Occasion Boat Rentals in Amsterdam

Many people rent a boat in Amsterdam for a birthday, anniversary, or proposal. For a proposal, book a sunset cruise on a motor yacht with a private skipper. Some operators offer a champagne package with glasses and a bucket of ice. You can arrange flowers or a cake through BoatHire24 support. For a birthday, a 3-hour rental on a 30-foot salon boat for 10 people works well. Bring your own playlist and use the Bluetooth speaker. Some boats have a disco light or a karaoke microphone, ask when you book.

Corporate events are also common. A 4-hour rental on a luxury salon boat with Wi-Fi, a toilet, and a catering package costs from around EUR 1,500. You can hold a small meeting, then cruise the canals. The skipper will keep to a quiet route so you can talk. For bachelor or bachelorette parties, speedboats or open boats are popular. Just remember the noise rules after 10 PM. BoatHire24 lists party boats with a separate section for events, filter by “special occasions” on the search page.

Accessibility and Inclusivity for Amsterdam Boat Rentals

Not all boats are wheelchair accessible. The narrow canals and low bridges mean most traditional boats have steps and no ramp. However, some modern salon boats and larger motor yachts have a flat entry and a toilet on the main deck. When you search on BoatHire24, use the “accessible” filter to see which boats have wheelchair access. The skipper can help with boarding if needed. For passengers with limited mobility, a boat with a covered cabin and a stable gangway is best. Avoid open speedboats, they require stepping over the side.

For families with young children, life jackets are available in child sizes. Most operators provide them free of charge. The skipper will give a safety briefing for kids. Some boats have a small cabin where a baby can nap. If you have a service dog, inform the operator when you book, most allow them but check the policy. BoatHire24 can help you find a boat that meets your needs, just contact support before you reserve.

Winter Boat Rentals in Amsterdam

Yes, you can rent a boat in Amsterdam from November to March. The city is quieter, and the canals have a different charm. Many electric boats have a transparent roof and a heater, keeping you warm and dry. Some salon boats have a wood stove or a powerful heater. The Amsterdam Light Festival (early December to mid-January) is a highlight, with art installations along the canals. A 2-hour evening cruise during the festival costs from around EUR 300 for a small boat. Book at least a week in advance, these sell out.

Winter weather can be cold and wet. Bring gloves, a scarf, and a waterproof coat. The boat will have blankets, but bring your own if you feel the cold easily. Some operators serve hot chocolate or mulled wine on board for an extra fee. Daytime rentals in winter are cheaper, from around EUR 200 for 2 hours. You can see the canals dusted with snow or frost on the bridges. Just check the weather forecast, if the canals freeze, rentals are cancelled. BoatHire24 updates availability daily during winter.

How to Choose the Right Boat Type for Your Amsterdam Rental

For a romantic couple’s cruise, a small electric boat for 2 to 4 people is ideal. It is quiet, intimate, and fits under all bridges. For a family with kids, a 30-foot motor yacht with a cabin and toilet is better. It has space for snacks and a place to change clothes. For a group of friends, a speedboat or open bowrider is fun, but you will get wet if it rains. For a corporate event, a salon boat with a glass roof, heating, and Wi-Fi is the best choice. It works in any weather and has a proper toilet.

If you are unsure, read the boat description on BoatHire24 carefully. Look at the photos, check the capacity, and see if the boat has a canopy, heater, or toilet. The search page lets you compare up to 5 boats side by side. You can also read the operator’s profile and reviews from previous renters. If you still have questions, contact the operator directly through the BoatHire24 messaging system. They usually reply within a few hours.

Costs Beyond the Base Rental Price

The base rental price includes the boat, skipper, fuel, and insurance. Extra costs can add up. Catering packages range from EUR 15 to EUR 40 per person for a platter of cheese, meat, and fruit. Some operators charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50 to EUR 100 if you leave the boat messy. Late return fees are typically EUR 50 per 30 minutes. If you want a specific departure point not on the list, the operator may charge a transfer fee of EUR 100 to EUR 200. Gratuity for the skipper is not required but is common, around EUR 50 to EUR 100 for a 3-hour rental.

Some boats have a minimum rental duration in high season, often 3 hours. You cannot book a 1-hour trip. The deposit is refundable if you cancel within the policy window. If you damage the boat, you may be liable for the repair cost up to the deposit amount. BoatHire24 shows all terms on the booking page. Read them before you pay. For a full breakdown of costs, visit the blog where we explain pricing in detail.

faqs.a: Most boats seat 6 to 12 passengers. Larger salon boats can accommodate up to 20 people. Check the listing for exact capacity.

faqs.a: Yes, you can bring your own food and drinks. Many boats have a cooler. Avoid glass bottles. Some operators offer catering for an extra fee.

faqs.a: Most boats have a canopy or roof. If the operator cancels due to unsafe weather, you get a full refund. Otherwise, the rental goes ahead. Bring a rain jacket just in case.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book a boat in Amsterdam?
faqs.a: In high season (May to September), book at least 1 to 2 weeks ahead. For weekends and holidays, book 3 to 4 weeks in advance. Last-minute bookings are sometimes available.

faqs.q: Are there any age restrictions for passengers?
faqs.a: No age restrictions, but children must wear life jackets provided by the operator. Some boats have a minimum age of 18 for alcohol consumption. Check the listing for details.

faqs.a: Most operators offer a full refund if you cancel at least 48 hours before the trip. Some have a 72-hour policy. Check the terms on the listing page before booking.

title: Yacht Charter Amalfi
metaDescription: Book a yacht charter Amalfi with BoatHire24. Compare motor yachts, catamarans, and sailing yachts with a licensed skipper. Depart from Marbella or Puerto Banús.
h1: Yacht Charter Amalfi, Book Your Costa del Sol Adventure
intro:
You want a yacht charter Amalfi experience, but you are on the Costa del Sol. That is fine. The Amalfi Coast has its charms, cliffside villages, limoncello, and winding roads, but the Costa del Sol offers something you cannot get in Italy: year-round sun, a 300-day-a-year boating season, and a coastline that stretches from Gibraltar to beyond Nerja. BoatHire24 lets you book a private yacht charter from Marbella, Puerto Banús, or Estepona, with a licensed skipper included. No need to fly to Naples. No need to queue for a ferry. Just turn up, step aboard, and let the Mediterranean do the rest.

We are a marketplace for boat rentals and yacht charters on the Costa del Sol, Spain. Every booking includes a professional skipper, so you can relax with a drink while someone else handles the navigation. Whether you want a sleek motor yacht for a day trip to Cala del Faro or a catamaran for a sunset cruise past the Strait of Gibraltar, we have the boat for you. Start your search on BoatHire24.
bodyHtml:
Why Choose a Yacht Charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol

The Amalfi Coast is beautiful, but it is also crowded, expensive, and limited to a short summer season. A yacht charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol gives you more space, more options, and more flexibility. You can depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. You can choose from motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, RIBs, fishing boats, licence-free day boats, and superyachts. And you can do it all with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the best anchorages, and the hidden coves that the Amalfi Coast can only dream of.

The Costa del Sol has its own Amalfi-style moments: the whitewashed old town of Estepona, the dramatic cliffs of Cala del Faro, the dolphin pods off the Strait of Gibraltar, and the view of La Concha mountain from the sea. You get all of this without the Amalfi price tag. A day charter from Marbella costs from around EUR 800 for a RIB up to EUR 3,000 for a luxury motor yacht. Compare that to a comparable Amalfi charter, and you save hundreds.

What Is Included in a Yacht Charter Amalfi

Every yacht charter Amalfi through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. This is not optional, and it is not an extra. The skipper handles the safety, navigation, and docking, so you can focus on swimming, sunbathing, or sipping a cold beer. The charter also includes fuel for a standard day trip (usually up to 4-6 hours of cruising), basic insurance, and the use of onboard amenities such as a sound system, sun pads, and a bimini top.

What is not included: food and drinks (though you can bring your own or order a catering package), port fees for overnight stays, and any special extras like jet skis or water toys. Most boats have a cooler and a small galley for storing your supplies. You can also request a crew member for additional service, such as a hostess or a chef, at an extra cost. Check the boat listing on our search page for full details.

Departure Ports for Your Yacht Charter Amalfi

You have six main departure ports for your yacht charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol. Each has its own character and advantages.

Puerto Banús: The glitzy marina in Marbella, famous for superyachts and designer boutiques. Best if you want a luxury motor yacht or a catamaran and plan to head east towards Cala del Faro or Marbella Marina. Expect higher mooring fees, but the atmosphere is unmatched.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo): A more relaxed alternative to Puerto Banús, with easy parking and a wide selection of boats. Good for families or groups who want a quieter start to the day.

Cabopino: A small, charming marina near the Artola dunes. Ideal for sailing yachts and licence-free day boats. The sandbar at Cabopino beach is a great spot for a swim stop.

Estepona: A growing port with a beautiful old town. Depart from here for trips to the Strait of Gibraltar or the west coast. Estepona is less crowded than Marbella and offers competitive prices.

Sotogrande: An exclusive residential area near Gibraltar. Perfect for fishing boats and larger yachts. The port is close to the Strait, so you can see dolphins within 15 minutes of leaving.

Benalmádena: A lively marina with a wide range of boats, from RIBs to superyachts. Good for day trips to Fuengirola or Mijas Costa. The marina has plenty of bars and restaurants for a pre- or post-charter drink.

Boat Types Available for Your Charter

Your yacht charter Amalfi can be on almost any type of boat. Here is a rundown of what you can expect.

Motor Yachts: From 30 to 100 feet, with speeds up to 30 knots. Great for covering distance quickly, such as from Marbella to Nerja in under an hour. Prices from around EUR 1,500 per day for a 40-foot yacht.

Catamarans: Stable, spacious, and perfect for groups. Catamarans have large decks, shallow drafts, and are ideal for anchoring in coves. Prices from around EUR 2,000 per day for a 40-foot model.

Sailing Yachts: For a more traditional experience. Sailing yachts are quieter and more eco-friendly. They are slower, so budget a full day for a round trip to the Strait of Gibraltar. Prices from around EUR 1,200 per day.

RIBs and Speedboats: Small, fast, and fun. RIBs are perfect for a quick trip to a beach club or for water sports. They can seat up to 10 people. Prices from around EUR 800 per day.

Fishing Boats: Equipped with rods, reels, and fish finders. Ideal for a half-day fishing trip off the coast of Sotogrande. Prices from around EUR 600 per half day.

Licence-Free Day Boats: Boats under 15 feet that do not require a boating licence. You can drive these yourself, but we still recommend a skipper for safety. Prices from around EUR 400 per day.

Superyachts: Over 24 metres, with crew, jacuzzis, and full catering. Price on request, but expect EUR 10,000 and up per day.

Pricing Guidance for Your Yacht Charter Amalfi

Prices for a yacht charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol vary by boat type, size, season, and duration. Here is a rough guide based on typical market rates.

Half-day (4 hours): From around EUR 600 for a RIB to EUR 2,000 for a motor yacht. Catamarans and sailing yachts usually require a full day.

Full day (8 hours): From around EUR 1,000 for a RIB to EUR 4,000 for a 50-foot motor yacht. Superyachts are price on request.

Overnight or multi-day: Add 20-30% per extra day, plus port fees. A week-long charter on a 45-foot catamaran can cost EUR 10,000 to EUR 15,000.

Seasonal variations: High season (July to September) can be 20-30% higher than low season (November to February). Spring and autumn offer the best balance of weather and price.

Additional costs: Fuel for extra hours, food and drinks, port fees for overnight stays, and tips for the skipper (usually 10-15%). Always confirm what is included before booking.

Best Seasons for a Yacht Charter Amalfi

The Costa del Sol has a long boating season, from March to November. The best months for a yacht charter Amalfi are May, June, September, and October. In these months, the weather is warm (25-30 degrees C), the sea is calm, and the crowds are thinner. July and August are hot (30-35 degrees C) and busy, but the water is perfect for swimming (22-26 degrees C). Winter charters are possible but less popular due to cooler temperatures (15-20 degrees C) and occasional wind.

If you want to see dolphins, the Strait of Gibraltar is best in spring and autumn when the sardine runs attract pods of common and striped dolphins. For a sunset cruise, any time from May to September works, with the sun setting around 9pm in summer.

How to Book a Yacht Charter Amalfi with BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter your preferred date, number of guests, and departure port. Browse the available boats, read the descriptions, and check the included items. Once you find a boat you like, send a booking request through the platform. The owner or charter company will confirm availability and send you a contract. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking, and the balance is due on the day of the charter.

We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance for peak season, but last-minute bookings (within 48 hours) are sometimes possible, especially for RIBs and smaller boats. If you have special requirements, such as a specific departure time or a catering menu, mention them in the booking request. The skipper will contact you a day before the charter to confirm the meeting point and any last-minute details.

Who Is a Yacht Charter Amalfi For

A yacht charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol is for anyone who wants a private, flexible day on the water. It works for couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise, families with kids who want to swim and snorkel, groups of friends celebrating a birthday or a stag do, and corporate clients hosting a client entertainment day. It also works for solo travellers who want to join a shared charter (ask about group bookings).

If you are a first-time boater, the included skipper takes the stress out of the experience. If you are an experienced sailor, you can still charter a sailing yacht and take the helm if you have the right licence. Either way, you get the freedom to explore the coast at your own pace.

Local Highlights on Your Yacht Charter Amalfi

While you are on the Costa del Sol, do not miss these spots. They are the local equivalents of Amalfi's best attractions.

Puerto Banús: The marina itself is a sight, with superyachts and luxury cars. Anchor nearby for a swim and a view of the action.

La Concha Mountain: The iconic peak behind Marbella. Best viewed from the sea at sunset, when the light turns the limestone pink.

Río Verde: A river mouth near Puerto Banús where you can anchor and swim in calm, shallow water. Popular with families.

Cala del Faro: A hidden cove with a lighthouse, accessible only by boat. Crystal-clear water and a rocky shore. Ideal for snorkelling.

Estepona Old Town: Whitewashed buildings, flower pots, and narrow streets. Moor at the marina and walk up for lunch at a tapas bar.

Strait of Gibraltar: A 30-minute ride from Sotogrande. See dolphins, pilot whales, and sometimes orcas. The views of Africa are spectacular.

Nerja Caves: A 90-minute cruise from Marbella. The caves are a UNESCO site, but the real draw is the dramatic cliffs and the Balcony of Europe viewpoint. Combine with a stop at Cala del Faro.

For more ideas, check our blog for itineraries and tips.

Comparing the Amalfi Coast and the Costa del Sol: A Practical Look

You might be wondering why you would choose a yacht charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol over the real thing. Let's look at the numbers. The Amalfi Coast has about 150,000 visitors a day in August, with mooring fees of EUR 100-200 per night in Positano. The Costa del Sol has over 150 kilometres of coastline, with mooring fees of EUR 30-60 per night in most marinas. A typical day charter on the Amalfi Coast for a 40-foot motor yacht costs around EUR 3,500-5,000. On the Costa del Sol, the same boat costs from around EUR 2,000-3,000. The water temperature is similar (22-26 degrees C in summer), but the Costa del Sol has more consistent sunshine, with over 320 sunny days a year compared to Amalfi's 260. You also avoid the Amalfi traffic jams and the steep hillside stairs. If you want the Amalfi vibe without the hassle, the Costa del Sol delivers.

Specific Itineraries for Your Yacht Charter Amalfi

Here are three concrete itineraries for your yacht charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol, each tailored to a different departure port and boat type.

Itinerary 1: Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro (Motor Yacht, 6 hours)
Depart Puerto Banús at 10am. Head east along the coast, passing the Marbella Marina and the golden sands of Nagüeles beach. Arrive at Cala del Faro by 11:30am. Anchor for a swim and snorkel in the clear water. The lighthouse offers a photo opportunity. Lunch on board at 1pm. Head back towards Puerto Banús, stopping at the Río Verde for a shallow-water swim. Arrive back at 4pm. Cost: from around EUR 2,500 for a 40-foot motor yacht.

Itinerary 2: Sotogrande to the Strait of Gibraltar (RIB, 4 hours)
Depart Sotogrande at 9am. Head south at 25-30 knots. Reach the Strait of Gibraltar by 9:30am. Look for dolphins, pilot whales, and seabirds. The guide will know the best spots. Continue to Tarifa for a view of the African coast. Stop for a swim off the Playa de los Lances. Head back to Sotogrande by 1pm. Cost: from around EUR 800 for a 6-person RIB.

Itinerary 3: Benalmádena to Nerja (Catamaran, 8 hours)
Depart Benalmádena at 10am. Cruise east along the coast, passing Fuengirola, Marbella, and Cala del Faro. Arrive at Nerja by 12:30pm. Anchor near the Balcony of Europe for a swim. Lunch on board at 1:30pm. Visit the Nerja Caves (book ahead, EUR 10 entry). Depart Nerja at 4pm. Arrive back at Benalmádena at 5:30pm. Cost: from around EUR 3,000 for a 40-foot catamaran.

Practical Tips for Your Yacht Charter Amalfi

A few things to know before you book your yacht charter Amalfi on the Costa del Sol. First, bring a towel, sunscreen (factor 50), and a hat. The sun is strong even in spring. Second, seasickness is rare on the Costa del Sol because the water is usually calm, but if you are prone to it, take a tablet an hour before departure. Third, tipping the skipper is standard: 10-15% of the charter price, paid in cash at the end. Fourth, if you want to bring your own food and drinks, pack a cooler bag with ice packs. Most boats have a small fridge, but space is limited. Fifth, check the weather forecast the day before. The wind in the Strait of Gibraltar can pick up in the afternoon. If the forecast is bad, the skipper will suggest an alternative route or a different day. Finally, book your charter through BoatHire24 to get the best selection and secure payment.

We list boats from owners and charter companies in Puerto Banús, Marbella, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. Every listing includes a licensed skipper, so you do not need to worry about licences or insurance. Our search page lets you filter by boat type, price, and capacity. We also provide detailed descriptions and photos, so you know exactly what you are getting.
