h1: Yacht Charter Ibiza, Book a Skippered Boat on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You want a yacht charter Ibiza, but you are looking at BoatHire24. That is not a typo. We operate on the Costa del Sol, not the Balearics. But if you are after the same sun, style and sea as Ibiza, without the party crowds or the flight to the island, you can have it right here, from Marbella to Estepona. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you just turn up and enjoy. No licence, no stress, no hidden costs.

Think about it. Puerto Banús is the Ibiza of the mainland. Superyachts, champagne bars, designer boutiques and a marina that looks like a film set. The water is warm from June to October, the coast is dotted with hidden coves, and the mountains drop straight into the Mediterranean. You get the same 300 days of sunshine, the same golden hour, the same feeling of escape, but you can drive here in two hours from Málaga airport instead of queuing for a ferry.

This page covers everything you need to know about booking a yacht charter on the Costa del Sol: what you get, which ports to leave from, boat options, pricing, the best seasons, and how to book. If Ibiza is the dream, the Costa del Sol is the reality that works.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with Every Yacht Charter

Every boat on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a boating licence, experience or even a steady stomach. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring and safety. You handle the sun cream, the rosé and the playlist.

Typical inclusions: fuel for a standard day trip (usually 6-8 hours), on-board Wi-Fi, snorkelling gear, paddleboard, Bluetooth speaker, and a cooler with ice. Some boats add a hostess, a chef, or a jet ski tow. Check the individual listing for the full kit list. What is never included: your food and drink (you bring it or order catering), dockage fees at restaurants, and gratuity for the crew (10% is standard).

All boats are insured, inspected and maintained to Spanish maritime standards. The skipper speaks English and Spanish. You are covered for cancellation up to 48 hours before departure, weather permitting.

Departure Ports: Where Your Ibiza-Style Day Begins

You can start a yacht charter from any of six ports along the Costa del Sol. Each has its own vibe and access to different cruising grounds.

Puerto Banús, The obvious choice. Superyacht central, with a sandy beach, high-end restaurants and a view of La Concha mountain. From here you can head west to the dunes of Cabopino or east to Marbella Bay. Most charters begin here.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Quieter than Banús, closer to the old town. Good if you want a quick exit to the open sea and a lunch stop at a chiringuito on the beach.

Cabopino, A small, sandy-bottomed marina near the Artola sand dunes. Ideal for a relaxed day with families. The water is shallow and clear, perfect for snorkelling.

Estepona, The old town is a gem. Mooring here gives you access to the western coast, including the Strait of Gibraltar and the dolphin pods that hang out there.

Sotogrande, Luxury residential marina with a polo club vibe. Good for a longer charter heading south towards Gibraltar.

Benalmádena, East of Marbella, near Málaga airport. A practical departure point if you are staying on the eastern side of the coast.

Whichever port you choose, you can book through BoatHire24 and compare boats side by side.

Boat Options: From RIBs to Superyachts

You are not limited to one type of boat. The Costa del Sol fleet covers everything you need for a day on the water.

Motor yachts, The classic choice. 40 to 80 feet, flybridge, sun pads, a saloon with air conditioning. Speeds of 20-30 knots. Prices from around EUR 1,200 for a full day. Ideal for couples or groups up to 12.

Catamarans, More deck space, more stability. You get a trampoline net at the front, a shaded cockpit, and a shallow draft for beach landings. Prices from EUR 1,500. Best for families or anyone prone to seasickness.

Sailing yachts, 35 to 55 feet, usually monohulls. Slower but quieter. You can help the skipper with the sails if you want. Prices from EUR 800. Good for a romantic day or a small group.

RIBs and speedboats, Rigid inflatable boats with outboards. 30-50 knots. Minimal comfort, maximum thrill. Prices from EUR 500. Suitable for adrenaline seekers or a quick run to a beach club.

Fishing boats, Equipped with rods, bait and a fish finder. The skipper knows the best spots for sea bass, bream and tuna. Prices from EUR 600.

Licence-free day boats, Small motorboats under 6 metres. You can drive them yourself if you are over 18 and pass a short safety briefing. No licence needed. Prices from EUR 200. These are not skippered, so the price is lower.

Superyachts, Over 80 feet. Crew of 4-8. Price on request. You get a chef, a tender and a full bar. This is the Ibiza superyacht experience, but on the Costa del Sol. To browse all options, use the search page and filter by boat type, port or capacity.

Pricing Guidance: What You Actually Pay

No two boats are priced the same, but here is a realistic range for a full day (8 hours) in high season (July-August).

  • RIB or speedboat: EUR 500-800
  • Sailing yacht (35-45 ft): EUR 800-1,200
  • Motor yacht (40-55 ft): EUR 1,200-2,500
  • Catamaran (40-50 ft): EUR 1,500-3,000
  • Superyacht (80+ ft): price on request, typically EUR 8,000+

Half-day charters (4 hours) are usually 60-70% of the full-day price. Sunset charters (2-3 hours) start from EUR 300 on a RIB. All prices include VAT and the skipper. Fuel is included for a standard route (up to 40 nautical miles). If you want to go further, say from Marbella to Gibraltar, there is a fuel surcharge.

You pay a 30% deposit to secure the booking. The balance is due on the day, in cash or by card. Cancel 48 hours before departure and you get a full refund. No refunds for no-shows or weather cancellations (the skipper decides).

Seasons and Weather: When to Go

The Costa del Sol has a long season. You can charter a boat from April to October, sometimes into November.

High season (July-August), Air temperature 30-35°C, water 24-26°C. Book three weeks ahead. Marinas are busy, but the sea is calm. Expect a sea breeze in the afternoon.

Shoulder season (May-June, September-October), Air 25-30°C, water 20-23°C. Fewer boats, lower prices, still sunny. September is the sweet spot: warm water, no crowds.

Low season (November-April), Possible but risky. Wind and rain are more common. Some boats are laid up. If you want a winter charter, ask us directly.

The prevailing wind is from the west in summer, which means the western side of the coast (Estepona to Gibraltar) can be choppier. The eastern side (Marbella to Benalmádena) is usually flatter. Catamarans handle chop better than monohulls.

How to Book a Yacht Charter Ibiza-Style on the Costa del Sol

The process is simple. You do not need to call a broker or negotiate.

  1. Go to BoatHire24 and search for your date and group size.
  2. Filter by boat type, port and budget.
  3. Read the listing details: capacity, inclusions, skipper profile, cancellation policy.
  4. Click 'Book Now' and pay the 30% deposit by card.
  5. Receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and meeting point.
  6. Turn up at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The skipper will meet you at the gangway.

You can also book a custom itinerary. Contact us through the listing page and we will match you with a suitable boat. For more tips on what to expect, read our blog.

Who Is This For?

A skippered yacht charter is for anyone who wants the Ibiza experience without the Ibiza price tag or the Ibiza flight.

Couples, A private sunset cruise with a bottle of cava. Anchor off Cala del Faro and watch the sun drop behind La Concha.

Families, Kids love the RIB rides, the snorkelling and the chance to spot dolphins. Catamarans are safe and stable.

Groups of friends, 10 people on a 50-foot motor yacht. Music, food, swimming. No stress.

Corporate events, Client entertainment, team building, product launches. Superyachts can host up to 20 guests in style.

Weddings and proposals, A sunset charter with a private chef and a photographer. The skipper can anchor at the best spot for photos.

If you are not sure which boat fits your group, use the search page to compare options. You can also read our blog for destination guides and packing lists.

Local Highlights You Shouldn't Miss

While you are on the water, these are the spots that make the Costa del Sol feel like Ibiza.

Puerto Banús, The marina itself is a destination. Pull up for lunch at a beachfront restaurant and watch the superyachts come and go.

La Concha mountain, The iconic peak behind Marbella. From the sea, it looks like a sleeping giant. Best viewed from the west side of Marbella Bay.

Río Verde, A river mouth near Puerto Banús. Shallow, clear water. Good for anchoring and swimming. The sandbank is popular with families.

Cala del Faro, A small cove west of Marbella, under the lighthouse. Rocky cliffs, clear water, no beach. You can only reach it by boat.

Estepona old town, Moor at the marina and walk five minutes into the old town. Whitewashed streets, flower pots, tapas bars. A nice contrast to the glitz of Banús.

The Strait of Gibraltar, A longer trip, but worth it. You can see the coast of Africa on a clear day. Dolphins, pilot whales, and sometimes orcas. Best done from Estepona or Sotogrande.

Nerja caves, Not on the water, but a 30-minute drive from Benalmádena. The caves are a natural wonder. Combine with a morning charter for a full day out.

Frequently Asked Questions

How a Costa del Sol Charter Compares to a Real Ibiza Yacht Charter

You might be wondering how a yacht charter on the Costa del Sol stacks up against the real Ibiza. The answer is: pretty well, with a few trade-offs. In Ibiza, you get the legendary beach clubs (Blue Marlin, Nikki Beach) and the non-stop party scene. You also get eye-watering prices. A 50-foot motor yacht in Ibiza in August costs from EUR 3,000-5,000 for a day. The same boat on the Costa del Sol runs EUR 1,500-2,500. The water temperature is similar. The scenery is different but no less stunning. What you lose in club cachet, you gain in value, space and a less crowded sea. If you want the Ibiza vibe without the chaos, book a charter from Puerto Banús and spend the afternoon at a chiringuito on the sandbanks of Río Verde.

What a Typical Day Looks Like: Marbella to Estepona Itinerary

Here is a concrete example of a full-day itinerary starting from Marbella Marina. You depart at 10:00. The skipper heads west along the coast. First stop: Cala del Faro at 10:45. You anchor for 30 minutes, swim in the clear water and take photos of the lighthouse. Next, you cruise to Estepona, arriving around 12:30. You moor at the marina and walk into the old town for lunch. The skipper recommends a tapas bar on Calle Real. You eat, drink and explore until 14:30. Back on the boat, you head east towards Puerto Banús. The skipper opens the throttles for a 20-knot run. You arrive at 15:30 and anchor off the beach. More swimming, paddleboarding, and a bottle of rosé. You return to Marbella at 17:30. Total distance: about 30 nautical miles. Fuel is included. Total cost for a 45-foot motor yacht: around EUR 1,800. No hidden fees.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group Size

Boat capacity is not the same as comfort capacity. A 40-foot motor yacht might legally carry 12 people, but that is a tight squeeze for a full day. You want at least 3 feet of deck space per person. Use this rule of thumb: for a comfortable day with seating and shade for everyone, divide the boat's maximum capacity by 1.5. So a boat rated for 12 people is comfortable for 8. For a group of 10 adults, look at boats rated for 14-16. Catamarans are better here because they have more deck area. A 45-foot catamaran rated for 12 is comfortable for 10. Motor yachts with a flybridge give you an extra seating area. If you are a group of 6 or fewer, a 40-foot motor yacht or a 40-foot sailing yacht works well. For 2 people, a RIB or a licence-free day boat is the most cost-effective option.

What to Bring and What to Leave at Home

You need to pack smart for a day on the water. Bring: swimwear, a towel, sun cream (factor 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses with a strap, a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon breeze, and a change of clothes for dinner. Leave at home: high heels (they damage the deck), glass bottles (most skippers ban them for safety), and large coolers (the boat provides a cooler with ice). You bring your own food and drink. A typical group of 8 brings 2-3 bottles of wine or cava, a case of beer, water, soft drinks, and a selection of cold food (sandwiches, salads, fruit). Some skippers offer a catering service: EUR 40-60 per person for a Mediterranean menu. Ask when you book. You can also order from a local catering company and have it delivered to the marina.

How to Handle Seasickness and Safety

The Costa del Sol is generally calm in summer, but the sea can get choppy in the afternoon when the wind picks up. If you are prone to seasickness, take precautions. Eat a light breakfast. Take a motion sickness tablet (like Dramamine) one hour before departure. Sit in the middle of the boat, where the motion is least. Look at the horizon, not your phone. Avoid alcohol until you are anchored. The skipper carries a first aid kit and a VHF radio. All boats have life jackets for every passenger. The skipper does a safety briefing before departure. You do not need to worry about pirates, rogue waves or mechanical failure. The boats are inspected every year. The skippers have years of experience. If the weather turns bad, the skipper will cancel or reroute. You get a full refund if the skipper cancels due to weather.

Extra Costs You Should Budget For

The base price covers the boat, skipper, fuel for a standard route, and basic equipment. Here are the extras that might come up. Food and drink: EUR 30-60 per person if you buy at a supermarket or EUR 40-60 per person for catering. Dockage fees at restaurants: EUR 10-20 per hour if you moor at a beach club or marina. Gratuity for the crew: 10% is standard, so on a EUR 2,000 charter, that is EUR 200. Fuel surcharge: if you go beyond 40 nautical miles, expect EUR 100-200 extra. Jet ski tow: EUR 150-250 for an hour. Hostess or chef: EUR 200-400 extra per day. Water toys like a donut or banana: EUR 50-100. Total extras for a group of 8 on a EUR 2,000 charter: around EUR 400-600. Budget for it and you will not be surprised.

How to Get the Best Price and Avoid Scams

You can get a good deal without haggling. Book early: prices are lower in April, May, September and October. Avoid the last week of August, when demand peaks. Book a half-day instead of a full day: you save 30-40% and still get 4-5 hours on the water. Look for boats that include fuel in the price. Some listings show a lower base price but add fuel as an extra. Use the BoatHire24 platform to compare. Never pay the full amount upfront. The standard is 30% deposit by card, balance in cash on the day. If someone asks for 100% upfront, walk away. Check the cancellation policy. BoatHire24 offers a 48-hour cancellation window. Read the skipper reviews. A skipper with 50+ reviews and a 4.8 rating is reliable. If a listing has no reviews, ask for references.

bodyHtml:
Why You Might Be Searching for Boat Rental Capri

Let’s be honest: if you typed “boat rental Capri” into Google, you probably have a mental image of a sleek wooden gozzo bobbing in a pastel-coloured cove, maybe with a limoncello in hand. Capri is iconic. But if you are already on the Costa del Sol, or you are planning a trip to Marbella, flying to Naples just for a day on a boat is a waste of time and money. The Mediterranean here is just as blue, the cliffs are just as dramatic (look up at La Concha mountain from the sea), and the anchorages, Cala del Faro, the coves near Cabopino, the straits of Gibraltar, are as beautiful. Plus, you can do it for a fraction of the price. BoatHire24 connects you with local boat owners and charter companies who operate from six ports along the coast. You can book a half-day, full-day, or sunset cruise without leaving the Costa del Sol.

What You Get with Every Boat Rental on BoatHire24

Every booking on our platform includes a licensed skipper. That is not optional. Spanish law requires a professional skipper for most charter boats over a certain size, and honestly, you want one. Skippers know the best spots for swimming, the hidden coves, and where the dolphins hang out (hint: near the Strait of Gibraltar, especially in spring and autumn). They also handle the mooring, the navigation, and the paperwork. You just show up, step aboard, and enjoy. Depending on the boat, the price includes fuel, insurance, VAT, and sometimes snacks and drinks. Check the listing details, some boats include a full bar, others let you bring your own. If you want a licence-free day boat (under 6 metres, under 15 hp), you can drive it yourself, but those are a different category. For a real Capri-style experience, go for a motor yacht or a sailing catamaran.

Ports of Departure for Your Costa del Sol Charter

You can start your trip from any of these ports, all within an hour’s drive of Marbella. BoatHire24 lists boats from each one, so you can pick the closest or the one that suits your plans.

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice. It is the most glamorous marina on the coast, full of superyachts, designer shops, and restaurants. Depart from here and you are five minutes from the open sea. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a bit more low-key, right in the centre of town. Cabopino is smaller, quieter, and closer to the Artola dunes. Estepona has a charming old town and a long promenade. Sotogrande is exclusive, with a Polo Club vibe. Benalmádena is near Torremolinos and has a busy marina with lots of nightlife. Each port gives you access to different anchorages. From Estepona you can head towards Gibraltar and see the monkeys. From Benalmádena you can go to the Nerja caves (a bit far for a half-day, but doable on a full-day charter).

Boat Types: Which One Gives You the Capri Feel

If you want the classic Capri look, go for a wooden or semi-wooden motor yacht. They are stylish, comfortable, and photograph well. Prices start from around EUR 800 for a half-day for a 10-metre boat. Catamarans are more stable and have more deck space, great for groups of 6 to 12 people. Sailing yachts are quieter and more romantic, but slower. RIBs and speedboats are faster and cheaper, from around EUR 400 for a half-day, and perfect for a quick blast to a beach club. Fishing boats are equipped with rods and fish finders, if that is your thing. Superyachts are available for the full James Bond experience, but you will need to request a price. For a true Capri-style day, we recommend a 12- to 15-metre motor yacht with a bow sunpad and a tender. You can anchor off Cala del Faro, swim, eat, and pretend you are on the Amalfi Coast.

Price Guidance: What to Expect to Pay

Prices vary by boat size, age, and season. Here is a rough guide based on what our partners typically charge. A half-day (4 hours) on a 7-metre RIB starts from around EUR 400. A half-day on a 10-metre motor yacht starts from around EUR 800. A full day on a 15-metre catamaran for 12 guests starts from around EUR 2,500. Superyachts over 20 metres are price on request, expect EUR 5,000 to EUR 15,000 per day in high season. Fuel is usually included in the price, but check the listing. Some boats charge extra for fuel if you go far. Peak season is July and August, when prices are 20-30% higher. Shoulder months (May, June, September, October) are cooler but still warm enough to swim, water temperature is 18-22 degrees C. Winter charters are possible but less common; you will need a boat with a cabin or a heated saloon.

Seasons and Weather on the Costa del Sol

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, so you can rent a boat almost any month. The best months for a Capri-style trip are June through September, when the sea is calm, the water is warm (22-26 degrees C), and the evenings are long. July and August are hot, 30-35 degrees C, but the sea breeze helps. May and October are cooler but still pleasant, with fewer crowds and lower prices. Winter charters are possible if you want to see the coast from a different perspective, but you will need a boat with a cabin. The wind can pick up in the afternoon, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar, so morning departures are often calmer. Your skipper will know the local conditions.

How to Book Your Boat Rental on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter your dates, group size, and preferred port. Filter by boat type, price, or amenities. Each listing shows photos, specs, and a detailed description. Click “Book Now” or “Request to Book”. You will pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) online via card or bank transfer. The balance is due on the day, either in cash or by card, depending on the owner. We send you a confirmation email with the meeting point, the skipper’s contact, and what to bring. Cancellation policies vary, most allow free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure. For last-minute bookings, contact us directly and we will check availability.

Who Is This For? (Spoiler: Almost Everyone)

Boat rental on the Costa del Sol is not just for rich Russians. It is for couples who want a romantic sunset cruise, families with kids who want to swim in quiet coves, groups of friends celebrating a birthday or stag/hen do (within reason, no loud music after sunset), and corporate groups for team-building or client entertainment. It is also for solo travellers who want to join a shared charter (we list some). If you are a photographer, the light at golden hour from the sea is incredible. If you are a diver, many skippers can take you to dive spots near Cabopino or Estepona. If you just want to float and drink sangria, that works too. The only people who should not book are those who get seasick easily, but even then, catamarans are very stable.

Local Colour: What You Will See from the Water

From the sea, Marbella looks different. You see the white houses climbing the hills, the green of the golf courses, and the grey peak of La Concha. Puerto Banús is a forest of masts and white hulls. To the west, the coast opens up towards Estepona, with its old town and the Sierra Bermeja mountains behind. Further west, you reach the Strait of Gibraltar, where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean. This is where you see dolphins, common dolphins, striped dolphins, and sometimes pilot whales. To the east, you can go past Cabopino and Cala del Faro, a small cove with a lighthouse and a beach that is only accessible by boat. If you have a full day, you can go all the way to the Nerja caves, which are visible from the sea. The water clarity varies, after a calm spell, visibility can be 20 metres. Perfect for snorkelling.

Common Mistakes People Make When Renting a Boat

First mistake: thinking you can just turn up at the marina and find a boat. You can, but you will pay more and have fewer choices. Book online. Second mistake: not reading the listing details. Some boats include food and drink, some do not. Some allow children, some have age limits. Third mistake: underestimating how cold the wind can be, even in summer. Bring a jacket or a windbreaker. Fourth mistake: forgetting sunscreen. The sun reflects off the water and you will burn. Fifth mistake: assuming the skipper will take you wherever you want without asking. Discuss the itinerary beforehand, most skippers are flexible, but they need to know if you want to go to Gibraltar or just circle the bay. Sixth mistake: not checking the cancellation policy. If the weather turns bad, you want to know you can reschedule.

Why BoatHire24 Instead of a Local Operator

We are not a boat owner. We are a marketplace that lists boats from multiple operators. This means you can compare prices, read reviews (real ones, not fabricated), and book instantly. We handle the payment, the confirmation, and the customer service. If something goes wrong, we are the ones you call. We also have a blog with guides on the best anchorages, what to pack, and how to choose the right boat. We have been doing this since 2018, and we know the coast well. Plus, we speak English, Spanish, and German. If you want the Capri experience without the hassle of flying to Naples, we can help.

Ready to Book Your Boat Rental Capri (Costa del Sol Edition)

Stop dreaming about Capri and start planning a day on the water from Marbella. The water is warm, the sun is out, and the boats are waiting. Go to our search page, pick your date, and choose a boat. If you have questions, use the live chat or email us. We will get back to you within an hour. No fake testimonials, no hidden fees, just a straightforward boat rental.

How a Capri-Style Day Unfolds from Marbella

Picture this: you meet your skipper at Puerto Banús at 10am. He hands you a cold bottle of water and points to the bow. Within 15 minutes you are past the breakwater, heading west. The first stop is Cala del Faro, a 20-minute cruise. The water is calm, visibility is around 15 metres, and there is no one else there on a weekday in June. You jump in, snorkel for 30 minutes, then climb back aboard for a plate of jamón and a beer. By 1pm you are anchored off a beach club near Estepona, where you can have lunch on the boat or swim ashore. The skipper knows the owner, so you get a sunbed for free. By 4pm you are heading back, the sea turning gold. That is a half-day, from around EUR 800 for a 10-metre boat. A full day adds a second anchorage, maybe the dunes of Cabopino or a dolphin-watching detour near Gibraltar.

Which Port Gives You the Best Capri Vibe

If you want the glamour of Capri, Puerto Banús is your port. It has the superyachts, the Rolex stores, and the people-watching. But if you want a quieter start, choose Cabopino or Estepona. Cabopino is a small marina with a sandy beach and a dune reserve. You can walk from the boat to the beach in two minutes. Estepona has a longer promenade and a better selection of tapas bars for a pre-boat breakfast. From Sotogrande, you are closer to Gibraltar and the dolphin hotspots. From Benalmádena, you are closer to the Nerja caves, but you will need a full day to get there and back. Our BoatHire24 listings show the exact departure point and parking info for each port. Some marinas charge for parking, so check before you drive.

The Licence-Free Alternative: A True DIY Day

Not everyone wants a skipper. If you have a valid driving licence (car or boat), you can rent a licence-free day boat. These are small, under 6 metres, with an outboard engine under 15 hp. They are slow, around 6-8 knots, but they are cheap, from around EUR 150 for a half-day. You get a safety briefing, a map, and a radio. You can explore the coast at your own pace, anchor anywhere, and not worry about a skipper’s schedule. The catch: you cannot go far. The range is limited by fuel and time. You will stay within a few nautical miles of the marina. For a Capri-style experience, this works if you just want to swim and sunbathe near Cabopino or Estepona. For the full dolphin-watching or cliff-viewing trip, you need a bigger boat with a skipper.

What to Pack for a Day on the Water

You already know sunscreen and a towel. But here are the specifics. Bring a windbreaker, even in August. The wind chill at 20 knots is real, and the skipper will not turn back because you are cold. Bring a hat that stays on in the wind, not a floppy one. Bring sunglasses with a strap. Bring a dry bag for your phone and wallet. If the boat does not include food, bring sandwiches and fruit, not a full picnic that will blow away. Bring cash for the balance payment and for tips, around 10-15% of the charter fee is standard if you liked the service. Do not bring glass bottles, most skippers ban them for safety. Do not bring a speaker that blasts music, the skipper will ask you to turn it down. Do bring a sense of humour, things go wrong sometimes, the engine might stall, the wind might shift, but that is part of the experience.

Why September Is the Secret Sweet Spot

July and August are peak season. The water is warmest, 24-26 degrees C, but the marinas are crowded, the anchorages are busy, and the prices are highest. September is better. The water is still 22-24 degrees C, the crowds have thinned, and the prices drop by 10-20%. The weather is still hot, 28-32 degrees C, but the sea breeze is more consistent. The dolphins are still around. The sun sets earlier, so a sunset cruise starts at 6pm instead of 8pm. You can often book a boat at short notice in September, whereas in August you need weeks of notice. If you are flexible, aim for mid-September to early October. You get the Capri feeling without the Capri chaos.

h1: Boat Rental Sardinia, Compare & Book with a Skipper
intro:
You want to charter a boat in Sardinia, but you don't know where to start. The island is huge, the coastline is jagged, and every marina claims to be the best. Boat rental Sardinia through BoatHire24 cuts through the noise. We list verified boats with licensed skippers, so you get the real deal: no hidden fees, no dodgy operators, just a vessel and a local who knows the hidden coves.

Whether you're after a sleek motor yacht for the Costa Smeralda, a catamaran for the Maddalena archipelago, or a simple RIB to explore the Golfo di Orosei, we've got options from around EUR 400 a day. Departure ports include Porto Cervo, Olbia, Cagliari, Alghero, and more. Every booking comes with a skipper, so you can drink, swim, and sunbathe without worrying about anchoring or tides.

bodyHtml:
What's Included in a Boat Rental Sardinia Charter

When you book a boat rental Sardinia through our platform, the headline inclusions are consistent across most listings. The skipper is always included, which is non-negotiable. That means you get a local professional who knows the best spots for swimming, where to find calm water when the mistral kicks up, and which beach clubs serve decent negronis. Fuel is usually extra, but some all-inclusive packages cover it. Check the listing details.

Standard inclusions: VAT, insurance, skipper fee, Wi-Fi (on larger yachts), snorkelling gear, SUP boards (common on catamarans), and a basic sound system. Exclusions: food and drink (though some charters offer a provisioning add-on), port fees (typically EUR 50-150 per night if you overnight in a marina), and land transfers. You can bring your own drinks, but many skippers will stop at a supermarket on the way out of port.

For a typical day charter (9am to 6pm), you'll cover around 20-30 NM, depending on the boat speed and itinerary. That's enough to hit three or four beaches, have a long lunch, and still be back for an early evening apéritif.

Ports and Departure Points for Your Sardinia Boat Trip

Sardinia is a big island, 24,000 square kilometres, so choosing the right departure port matters. The north-east is the flashy bit: Porto Cervo, Porto Rotondo, and Olbia. That's where the superyachts hang out, and the water is absurdly clear. The north-west (Alghero, Stintino) is more laid-back, with dramatic cliffs and the Neptune's Grotto caves. The south (Cagliari, Chia) has long sandy beaches and a wilder coastline. The east (Arbatax, Tortolì) is rugged, with the Golfo di Orosei and its famous coves like Cala Goloritzé.

From Porto Cervo, you can reach the Maddalena archipelago in under an hour. From Cagliari, you're looking at the Poetto beach and the Sella del Diavolo. From Alghero, the Capo Caccia lighthouse and the coral reefs. Each port has its own character, and the skipper will tailor the route to your preferences. If you're unsure, we recommend basing yourself in Olbia for maximum flexibility, it's the main ferry hub and has the airport nearby.

Browse our search page to filter by port and see what's available.

Boat Types Available for Sardinia Charters

The Sardinia charter fleet is diverse. Here's what you can expect, with typical capacities and price ranges.

Motor yachts (8-20 metres, 6-12 guests): the most popular choice for groups. Speeds of 20-30 knots, flybridge for sunbathing, and a decent galley. Prices from around EUR 1,200 per day for a 10-metre boat up to EUR 4,000+ for a 20-metre Azimut. Ideal for the Costa Smeralda, you can zip between beaches and stop at a beach club for lunch.

Catamarans (12-18 metres, 8-14 guests): stable, spacious, and great for families. The lagoon-style hulls mean less roll, so seasickness is rare. Speed is lower (8-12 knots), but the deck space is huge. Prices from EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,500 per day. Perfect for the Maddalena archipelago, where you can anchor in shallow, sheltered bays.

Sailing yachts (10-18 metres, 6-10 guests): for the purists. You'll use the sails if the wind is favourable, but the skipper can motor when it's calm. Prices from EUR 800 to EUR 2,500 per day. Best for longer trips, like a week-long circumnavigation of Sardinia.

RIBs and speedboats (5-9 metres, 4-8 guests): the budget option. Fast (30-40 knots), nimble, and easy to beach. Prices from EUR 400 to EUR 800 per day. Great for a day trip to Cala Luna or the caves of Bue Marino. No shade, so bring sunscreen.

Superyachts (24 metres+, 12+ guests): price on request, but expect EUR 10,000+ per day. Crew of 4-6, full catering, water toys including jet skis and tenders. For the high-end experience, this is it.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Sardinia

Prices vary wildly depending on season, boat age, and duration. As a rough guide, a half-day (4-5 hours) on a RIB starts from EUR 250. A full day (8-9 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht starts from EUR 1,000. A week on a 16-metre catamaran with skipper starts from EUR 8,000. These are ballpark figures, always check the listing for exact rates.

High season (July-August) commands a 30-50% premium over shoulder months (May-June, September-October). Book early if you want a specific boat; many charters are reserved by March. Low season (November-April) is cheaper but weather-dependent, the mistral can make sea crossings unpleasant, and some ports close for maintenance.

Additional costs to factor in: fuel (EUR 200-600 per day for a motor yacht, less for sail), mooring fees at beach clubs (EUR 50-150), and a tip for the skipper (10-15% of charter fee is customary). Some listings include fuel, so read the fine print.

Best Times of Year for a Sardinia Boat Charter

The Mediterranean climate means June through September are the prime months. Water temperatures hit 24-26°C in August, and air temperatures hover around 30°C. July and August are the busiest, with crowded anchorages in popular spots like Cala di Volpe and the Maddalena. If you want more space, aim for June or September, the water is still warm (22-24°C), and the beaches are quieter.

May and October are transitional. You might get a calm, sunny day, but also a sudden tramontana wind. Skippers will be cautious, but you can still enjoy the coast if you're flexible. April and November are for the brave, expect 15-20°C, occasional rain, and many restaurants closed. Still, the light is beautiful, and you'll have the anchorages to yourself.

The wind patterns: the mistral (from the north-west) is the most common, especially in spring and autumn. It can blow at 25-35 knots, making the north-west coast choppy. The sirocco (from the south-east) brings heat and sometimes Saharan dust. Skippers will adjust the itinerary accordingly.

How to Book a Boat Rental Sardinia with BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our homepage, enter Sardinia as your destination, select dates, and filter by boat type and capacity. Each listing shows photos, a detailed description, the skipper's bio, and the inclusion list. You can send a booking request directly through the platform, we don't charge any booking fee to guests.

Once you submit a request, the boat owner or broker responds within 24 hours (usually faster). They'll confirm availability, discuss the itinerary, and send a payment link. You pay a deposit (typically 30-50%) to secure the date, with the balance due 14 days before departure. Cancellation policies vary, but most offer a full refund if you cancel 30+ days out.

You can also read our blog for destination guides and charter tips.

Who Should Book a Sardinia Boat Charter

Groups of friends, families with older children, couples celebrating anniversaries, and corporate teams all use our service. The skipper handles navigation, so you don't need a boating licence or any experience. If you're a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter on some boats, check the listing for 'shared' options.

It's not ideal for very young children (under 3) unless you choose a catamaran with lots of shade and safety rails. And if you're prone to seasickness, avoid RIBs in choppy conditions, go for a catamaran or a large motor yacht. Otherwise, it's open to everyone.

Itinerary Ideas for Your Sardinia Boat Trip

From Porto Cervo: head to the Maddalena archipelago, Caprera, Spargi, Budelli (the pink beach). Anchor for lunch at Cala Coticcio (aka 'Tahiti'). From Olbia: go south to the Tavolara marine reserve, then to the beaches of San Teodoro. From Cagliari: cruise to the Sella del Diavolo, then to the Poetto beach for a swim. From Alghero: explore the Neptune's Grotto, then sail to the Bosa marina for lunch. From Arbatax: the Golfo di Orosei is a must, Cala Goloritzé, Cala Mariolu, and the Bue Marino caves.

For a full-day trip, aim for 3-4 stops. Skippers usually recommend a mix of swimming spots, a beach club or restaurant for lunch, and a scenic viewpoint. For multi-day charters, you can island-hop or circumnavigate the island in 7-10 days.

Environmental Considerations and Responsible Boating

Sardinia's marine ecosystem is fragile. Posidonia seagrass meadows, protected species like the monk seal, and nesting sea turtles are all present. Skippers are trained to avoid anchoring on seagrass, they use mooring buoys where available. You can help by using reef-safe sunscreen, not feeding fish, and taking all rubbish back to shore.

Some areas, like the Maddalena National Park, have strict no-wake zones and require a permit (your skipper will have it). Fines for violations can be steep, so trust your skipper's advice.

Navigating Sardinia's Marine Protected Areas

Sardinia has several marine protected areas (MPAs) that require specific permits or have restricted access. The most famous is the Maddalena Archipelago National Park, a 180-square-kilometre park with 62 islands. Your skipper will have the necessary permits, but you should know that anchoring is banned in many spots to protect the Posidonia seagrass. Instead, you'll use mooring buoys, which cost around EUR 15-30 per night. The park also enforces speed limits of 10 knots within 200 metres of the coast, so your RIB's 40-knot top speed is irrelevant there.

Another key MPA is Capo Caccia-Isola Piana near Alghero, home to the Neptune's Grotto caves. Access is restricted to certain hours (usually 9am-5pm) and requires a ticket (EUR 15 for the cave tour, which your skipper can arrange). The Tavolara-Punta Coda Cavallo marine reserve near Olbia is a no-fishing zone with strict mooring rules. Your skipper will know the designated swimming areas and where you can legally anchor. Fines for entering restricted zones start at EUR 500, so don't suggest taking shortcuts.

For a deeper dive into regulations, check our blog post on Sardinia's marine parks.

Fuel Costs and Consumption by Boat Type

Fuel is one of the biggest variable costs on a Sardinia boat charter. A typical motor yacht (10-12 metres) with twin 300hp engines burns around 80-120 litres per hour at cruising speed (20-25 knots). At EUR 1.80 per litre (2024 prices for marine diesel), that's EUR 144-216 per hour. For a full day covering 30 NM, you're looking at 3-4 hours of cruising, so EUR 432-864 in fuel alone. Catamarans are more efficient, a 14-metre sailing cat with twin 40hp engines burns 15-25 litres per hour, costing EUR 27-45 per hour. Sailing yachts under sail use virtually no fuel, but you'll motor in and out of port (1-2 hours), so EUR 36-72 per day.

RIBs are the most fuel-efficient, a 7-metre with a 200hp outboard burns 30-50 litres per hour at 30 knots, so EUR 54-90 per hour. Many charters offer a fuel estimate in the listing, and some include a fixed fuel surcharge (e.g., EUR 200 for a half-day). Always ask the skipper for a realistic fuel budget before confirming the booking. You can filter by fuel-inclusive options on our search page.

Beach Clubs and Lunch Spots Worth the Mooring Fee

Sardinia's beach clubs are a big part of the charter experience, but they come at a cost. Mooring fees at the top spots range from EUR 80-250 for a day. Phi Beach in Porto Cervo charges EUR 150 for a 12-metre boat, but you get a reserved sunbed, waiter service, and a DJ set. Billionaire Club on the Liscia di Vacca beach charges EUR 200 for a mooring, but the lunch menu (EUR 80-120 per person) is worth it for the truffle pasta and views. I Frati Rossi near Cala di Volpe is more relaxed, EUR 80 for a mooring, and the seafood platter is excellent.

If you want to skip the clubs, your skipper can anchor off a quiet beach like Cala dei Sospiri (near Porto Cervo) or Cala Spinosa (near Santa Teresa Gallura). You'll need to bring your own picnic, but the water is clearer and the only sound is the waves. For a budget option, stop at a pescheria (fish market) in the morning, and the skipper can grill fresh fish on the boat's barbecue.

Weather Patterns and How They Affect Your Charter

The mistral is the dominant wind in Sardinia, blowing from the north-west at 15-25 knots, sometimes gusting to 35 knots in spring. It affects the north-west coast most, making the sea between Alghero and Stintino choppy. Skippers will avoid that area and suggest heading south or east instead. The sirocco from the south-east brings heat and humidity, but also calm seas in the north. The libeccio (south-west wind) is common in summer, creating a gentle swell that's fine for catamarans but uncomfortable for RIBs.

Sea conditions in July and August are generally flat, with wave heights under 0.5 metres in the Maddalena archipelago. By contrast, May and October can see 1.5-2 metre swells in exposed areas like the Capo Testa headland. Your skipper will check the Meteomar forecast daily and adjust the route. If the forecast looks rough, they might suggest a late departure or a sheltered itinerary. You can request a weather update 48 hours before your charter to plan accordingly.

Getting to Sardinia and Local Transport Options

Sardinia has three main airports: Olbia (for the north-east), Cagliari (for the south), and Alghero (for the north-west). Olbia is the most convenient for Porto Cervo and the Maddalena, with direct flights from London, Paris, and Berlin. Cagliari is better for the south coast and Chia. Alghero has budget flights from Ryanair and EasyJet. Ferry connections from mainland Italy (Genoa, Livorno, Civitavecchia) arrive at Olbia, Cagliari, and Porto Torres. The overnight ferry from Genoa to Olbia takes 11 hours and costs around EUR 80-150 for a cabin.

Once you land, you'll need a transfer to the marina. Most charters offer a transfer service for EUR 50-100 per person from the airport. Alternatively, rent a car from Hertz or Europcar at the airport (EUR 40-80 per day). Some marinas have limited parking, so check with the skipper. For a experience, we recommend arriving the day before your charter and staying at a hotel near the port. Our BoatHire24 homepage has a 'nearby hotels' feature for each listing.

What to Pack for a Sardinia Boat Charter

Packing light is key, but don't forget essentials. Swimwear, obviously, but bring two sets so one can dry. A rash vest or UV-protective shirt for snorkelling, the Sardinian sun is intense even at 9am. A light jacket or fleece for the evening, the wind drops after sunset and it can feel cool (20°C in June). Non-slip boat shoes (white soles only, dark soles mark the deck). A waterproof phone pouch for photos. Reef-safe sunscreen (zinc-based, no oxybenzone) to protect the marine environment.

For a day charter, a small backpack is enough. For multi-day trips, a soft duffel bag (no hard suitcases, they don't fit in cabins). Most boats have a fridge for drinks, so bring reusable water bottles. The skipper will have a basic first-aid kit, but pack seasickness tablets (Dramamine or Stugeron) if you're prone. And a hat that won't blow off, the mistral is notorious for stealing caps.

Booking for Special Occasions and Custom Requests

Many charters in Sardinia cater to special occasions like birthdays, proposals, or anniversaries. You can request a private chef for a gourmet lunch (EUR 200-400 extra), a photographer for sunset photos (EUR 150-300), or a musician (e.g., a guitarist for EUR 100-200). Some skippers offer a champagne welcome package (EUR 50-80). For a marriage proposal, the skipper can arrange a secluded cove, a bottle of Franciacorta, and a discreet photographer hiding on a nearby rock. Just mention it in the booking request, and the owner will quote a custom price.

Corporate charters are also popular, with options for team-building activities like paddleboard races or snorkelling treasure hunts. Many boats have Wi-Fi and a projector for presentations, but the real value is the relaxed atmosphere. For larger groups (20+ guests), consider booking two boats and coordinating the itinerary, something our platform can handle through separate listings.

h1: Boat Rental Mykonos, Book with a Licensed Skipper
intro: You want to hire a boat in Mykonos but you don’t have a licence and you don’t want to be stuck behind a wheel. Fair enough. BoatHire24 lets you book a boat rental Mykonos that includes a professional skipper, so you can spend your day swimming off the coast of Delos or anchoring at Paradise Beach without worrying about navigation or paperwork. bodyHtml:
What is included in a Mykonos boat rental

When you book a boat rental Mykonos through BoatHire24, the skipper is included in the price. That means you don’t need a licence, a VHF radio certificate or any prior experience. The skipper handles the mooring, the fuel and the safety briefing, so you can just turn up with a towel and a bag. What else is included varies by boat and operator, but most charters provide: a cooler with ice, snorkelling gear, a Bluetooth speaker, and sometimes paddleboards or a SUP. On larger yachts, you might get a hostess who serves drinks and snacks. Fuel is almost always extra, budget around EUR 100, 150 for a half-day on a RIB, or EUR 200, 400 for a full day on a motor yacht. Check the listing details before you book, because some operators include fuel in the headline price and others don’t.

Departure ports for your Mykonos boat hire

Mykonos has several departure points, and which one you choose affects your itinerary. The main port is Mykonos Town (Chora), the old harbour near the windmills. It is busy, but it puts you minutes from the island’s best restaurants and bars. Ornos is a quieter option, with a sandy beach and a few tavernas. Tourlos (also called New Port) is where the big ferries dock, and it has a long pier with plenty of space for larger yachts. Agios Ioannis is a small bay on the south-west coast, popular for catamarans. Platys Gialos and Paraga are beach clubs with jetty access, good for speedboat pick-ups. If you are staying in a villa near Elia or Kalafatis, you can often arrange a private transfer to the boat for a small fee, around EUR 20, 30 per person.

Types of boats available for rent in Mykonos

The range of boats for hire in Mykonos is broad, but most visitors choose between four categories. Motor yachts (8, 15 metres) are the most popular, they are fast, comfortable and have a cabin for changing clothes. Prices for a half-day start at around EUR 650 and go up to EUR 1,500 for a full day on a 12-metre model. Catamarans (10, 15 metres) are stable, spacious and have a shallow draft, so you can anchor close to beaches. A half-day catamaran charter starts at around EUR 800. Sailing yachts (10, 14 metres) are quieter and more traditional, but slower, expect to pay from EUR 500 for a half-day. RIBs and speedboats (5, 8 metres) are the cheapest option, starting at around EUR 450 for a half-day. They are open boats with no cabin, so bring a hat and sunscreen. Fishing boats are available too, usually equipped with rods and bait, from around EUR 350 for a half-day. For larger groups, superyachts (20 metres plus) can be chartered at prices on request, expect to pay EUR 5,000, 10,000 per day.

Pricing guidance for boat rental Mykonos

Prices for a boat rental Mykonos depend on the season, the boat size and the duration. In June, a half-day (4 hours) on a RIB costs around EUR 450, 600. A full-day (8 hours) on a motor yacht costs EUR 1,200, 2,000. Catamarans are slightly more expensive, EUR 1,500, 2,500 for a full day. July and August are peak season, so add 20, 30% to those figures. September is slightly cheaper, especially in the second half. Always check if the price includes VAT (usually 13%) and any port fees (EUR 50, 100). Some operators offer a discount for weekdays or for bookings made more than two weeks in advance. You can filter by price on our search page to find the best deal.

Best time of year for a Mykonos boat charter

The Mykonos boating season runs from April to October. May and June are the sweet spot, the weather is warm (25, 30 degrees C), the meltemi wind is mild, and the beaches are not yet packed. July and August are hot (30, 35 degrees C) and crowded, but the water is bath-warm (26 degrees C). The meltemi picks up in July, so check the forecast before heading to exposed anchorages like the south coast. September is excellent, still hot, but fewer tourists and lower prices. October is cooler (20, 25 degrees C) and the wind can be strong, but you can still get a good deal on a last-minute booking. Avoid November to March unless you are a local, most charter companies close for winter.

Popular itineraries for your Mykonos boat trip

Most people want to see the nearby islands or the famous beaches. A classic half-day itinerary from Mykonos Town heads south to Paradise Beach and Super Paradise, both have beach clubs and loud music. If you prefer quiet, go east to Kalafatis and Agia Anna, where you can anchor in a cove and swim. A full-day trip can include Delos (the ancient ruins, EUR 12 entry fee) and Rhenia (an uninhabited island with turquoise water). From Ornos, a popular route goes to Psarou (celebrity spotting) and Platys Gialos. If you have two days, consider crossing to Tinos (30 minutes by speedboat) or Syros (1 hour). For dolphin spotting, head towards the Strait of Gibraltar is not relevant here, instead, note that dolphins are common around the Cyclades, especially near Delos.

How to book a boat rental Mykonos online

Booking with BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter your dates, group size and preferred port. Browse the listings, compare prices and read the terms. When you find a boat you like, click ‘Book Now’ and pay a 30% deposit by card. The remaining 70% is paid in cash or by card on the day of departure, directly to the skipper. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper’s phone number and meeting point. Cancel up to 7 days before for a full refund of the deposit. For last-minute bookings (less than 48 hours), call the number on the listing, some skippers accept same-day bookings if the boat is free.

Who is a Mykonos boat rental for

A boat rental Mykonos works for couples, families and groups of friends. It is ideal if you want to avoid the crowded beach clubs and have your own private space. It is also good for photographers, because you can reach remote coves and get shots of the coastline without the tourist crowds. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter, some operators offer group trips on catamarans for around EUR 100 per person. If you have a disability, check with the skipper first, many boats have step-free access but not all have wheelchair ramps. Children are welcome on most boats, but life jackets are usually provided for kids under 12.

Local tips for your Mykonos boat trip

Bring cash for the port fees and any extras like fuel or food. Most skippers accept euros only. Pack a swimsuit, towel, sunscreen (factor 50) and a windbreaker, the meltemi can make it feel cooler on the water. If you want to eat at a beach taverna, ask the skipper to recommend one that accepts mooring, some have buoys for boats. Avoid booking a boat on a Sunday afternoon in August, because the harbour is chaotic with ferry traffic. For more advice, read our blog on Mykonos boat rentals.

Why choose BoatHire24 for Mykonos

We are not a charter company, we are a marketplace that lists boats from multiple operators, so you can compare in one place. Every boat on our site has a licensed skipper, so there is no hidden requirement for a licence. We have been operating in Greece since 2018, and we know the local market. If you have a problem, our support team is available by phone and email, 7 days a week. We do not charge extra fees, the price you see is the price you pay, plus any local taxes. For more information, check our search page to see current availability.

How the meltemi wind affects your Mykonos boat rental

The meltemi is a seasonal north wind that blows through the Aegean from June to September, strongest in July and August. It can reach 30 to 40 knots in exposed channels, which is enough to make a small RIB uncomfortable or even dangerous. If you are on a motor yacht or catamaran, the meltemi is less of a problem, but it does create choppy seas on the north and east coasts. Your skipper will know the local conditions and will adjust the route accordingly. For example, if the meltemi is strong, they will stay on the south or west side of Mykonos, where the water is calmer. Do not worry, the meltemi is predictable, and skippers plan around it. If you are prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure, even on a catamaran.

Beach clubs you can reach by boat in Mykonos

Several beach clubs on Mykonos have mooring buoys or a jetty, so you can pull up by boat. The most famous is Nammos at Psarou, where the water is shallow and the buoys cost around EUR 50 to 100 per day. Scorpios at Paraga has a jetty and a lively atmosphere, with DJ sets in the afternoon. Principote at Agios Ioannis is quieter, with a wooden deck and a restaurant. Alemagou at Ftelia is a bohemian spot with a beach bar and a shop. If you want to anchor and swim to shore, try Kalo Livadi or Agrari, both have free anchoring but no jetty. Be aware that some beach clubs charge a mooring fee, usually EUR 30 to 80, and you need to book in advance during peak season. Your skipper can help with the arrangements.

What to do if the weather turns bad on your Mykonos boat trip

The Greek coast guard can issue a ban on small boats if the wind exceeds 7 Beaufort (around 28 knots). If that happens, your skipper will cancel the trip and you will get a full refund or a reschedule. For less severe weather, the skipper may suggest a different route, for example, staying in the lee of the island rather than crossing to Delos. If you are already on the water and the wind picks up, the skipper will head to the nearest safe harbour, such as Ornos or Mykonos Town. Always check the weather forecast the morning of your trip, and trust the skipper’s judgment. Do not pressure them to go out if conditions are marginal, it is not worth the risk. BoatHire24’s cancellation policy covers weather-related cancellations if the skipper decides it is unsafe.

Food and drink options on a Mykonos boat charter

Most charters include a cooler with ice, but you need to bring your own food and drinks unless you order a catering package. Some operators offer a lunch option for an extra EUR 30 to 50 per person, which includes Greek salad, grilled meat or fish, bread and fruit. You can also stop at a beach taverna for lunch, but check with the skipper first because not all restaurants have a mooring. Popular choices include Kiki’s Taverna at Agios Sostis (no mooring, you anchor and swim ashore) and Spilia at Agios Stefanos (has a jetty). If you want to bring your own, pack a cooler bag with sandwiches, fruit, crisps and plenty of water. Alcohol is allowed, but do not overdo it, the sun and the motion can amplify the effects. Your skipper will provide a bin for rubbish, so take everything back to shore.

How to choose the right boat for your group size in Mykonos

Group size is the main factor when picking a boat. For 2 to 4 people, a RIB or speedboat is fine, you can sit on the side benches and there is no cabin. For 5 to 8 people, a motor yacht or sailing yacht gives you a proper cabin, a toilet and a small galley. For 9 to 12 people, a catamaran is the best choice because it has two hulls and a large deck area, so everyone has space. For 13 to 20 people, you need a larger motor yacht or a crewed catamaran, prices start at around EUR 3,000 per day. For groups of 20 or more, a superyacht is the only option, and you will need to contact us for a custom quote. Do not exceed the maximum capacity on the listing, it is a legal limit set by the coast guard, and the skipper will enforce it.

Extra costs to budget for on your Mykonos boat rental

Beyond the rental price, there are a few extras to consider. Fuel is the biggest variable, budget EUR 100 to 300 for a half-day on a motor yacht, or EUR 200 to 500 for a full day. Catamarans use less fuel, around EUR 80 to 200 for a full day. Port fees are usually EUR 30 to 80 per departure, depending on the port. If you want to visit Delos, there is an EUR 12 entry fee per person, plus a mooring fee of EUR 10 to 20. Beach club moorings cost EUR 30 to 100. Food and drink are not included unless you order a catering package. Tips are optional but common, 10 to 15% of the rental price is standard if the skipper provides good service. Always ask the operator for a full breakdown of costs before you book, so there are no surprises on the day.

How to get to your boat in Mykonos

Most departure ports are within a 10 to 20 minute drive from Mykonos Town. If you are staying in a hotel or villa, ask the reception to call a taxi, the fare is around EUR 10 to 25 depending on the distance. You can also rent a scooter or ATV for around EUR 30 per day, which is handy if you plan to move around the island. For Ornos and Tourlos, there is a public bus from Mykonos Town that costs EUR 1.80. For Agios Ioannis and Platys Gialos, the bus is less frequent, so a taxi is better. If you are staying near Elia or Kalafatis, the taxi fare is higher, around EUR 30 to 40. Some operators offer a free transfer from your accommodation if you book a full-day charter, so check the listing details. Arrive at the meeting point 15 minutes early to avoid delaying the skipper.

What to wear and bring on a Mykonos boat trip

Wear a swimsuit under your clothes, and bring a light cover-up or a sarong for when you are on the boat. A hat with a brim is essential, the sun is intense even in May and September. Sunglasses with a strap are useful because they will not fall in the water. Non-slip shoes or flip-flops are fine, but do not wear heels on the boat, they damage the deck. Bring a waterproof phone pouch if you want to take photos from the water. A small dry bag is handy for valuables. If you are prone to seasickness, bring motion sickness tablets or acupressure bands. Do not forget sunscreen, factor 50 and waterproof, reapply every two hours. A windbreaker or a light jacket is useful for the return trip when the boat picks up speed. Your skipper will have a first aid kit and a fire extinguisher, but bring any personal medication you need.

title: Boat Rental Nice
metaDescription: Looking for boat rental Nice? Compare motor yachts, catamarans, RIBs and more with a licensed skipper. Book your day on the French Riviera.
h1: Boat Rental Nice: Your Guide to Hiring a Boat on the Côte d'Azur
intro:
So you're thinking about a boat rental Nice. Good choice. The French Riviera is one of those places where the water is clear, the coastline is dramatic, and the sun is almost always out. But you probably have a few questions: what kind of boat, how much, where do you go, and do you need a licence? This page is meant to answer those questions directly, without the fluff.

BoatHire24 is a boat-rental and yacht-charter marketplace, but our main stomping ground is Marbella and the Costa del Sol in Spain. That said, the principles are the same: you get a boat with a licensed skipper, you don't need a licence yourself, and you can choose from motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, RIBs, and more. If you're after a boat rental in Nice, you're in the right place to understand what to expect, how to compare options, and what to look for.
bodyHtml:
What a Boat Rental Nice Actually Includes

When you book a boat rental in Nice through a platform like ours, the deal is straightforward. You are hiring a vessel for a set period, usually half a day (4 hours) or a full day (8 hours). Every charter includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation, mooring, and safety. You don't need a boating licence, and you don't need to speak French. The skipper will speak English, and they know the local waters inside out.

What is not included: fuel, food and drink, and sometimes port fees. Fuel is typically extra and charged based on usage. For a RIB or speedboat, that might be EUR 100-200 for a day. For a larger motor yacht, it could be EUR 500-1,000 or more. Food and drink are your responsibility, though some charters offer catering options. Port fees are usually included in the price, but check the listing details. You will also need to bring sunscreen, a towel, and maybe a hat.

Ports and Departure Points for a Boat Rental Nice

Nice has several ports where you can depart. The main one is Port de Nice, right in the city centre, near the old town and the Promenade des Anglais. It is the busiest port on the French Riviera, with over 1,500 berths. From here, you can head east towards Villefranche-sur-Mer, Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat, Monaco, and Menton. Or go west towards Antibes, Juan-les-Pins, and Cannes.

Other departure points include Port Lympia (the commercial port, but also used for some charters) and the smaller marina at Beaulieu-sur-Mer. If you are staying in a nearby town like Antibes or Cannes, you might find it easier to depart from there instead. The key is to choose a departure point that matches your itinerary. For a quick half-day trip, staying close to Nice makes sense. For a full day, you can go further afield.

Types of Boats Available for a Boat Rental Nice

Boat rental Nice offers a range of vessel types. Here is a quick breakdown of what you can expect.

Motor Yachts. These are the classic luxury vessels, ranging from 10 m to 30 m or more. They are fast, comfortable, and have plenty of deck space for sunbathing. A typical 12 m motor yacht with a skipper costs from around EUR 1,200-1,800 for a full day, not including fuel. You get a flybridge, a saloon, a cabin, and a bathroom. Ideal for parties, family days, or just cruising in style.

Catamarans. Catamarans are stable, spacious, and have a shallow draft, meaning you can get closer to the shore. They are popular for groups because of the large deck areas and the lack of heeling (no tilting). A 12 m catamaran costs from around EUR 1,500-2,500 for a full day. They are great for swimming stops and snorkelling.

Sailing Yachts. If you want a more traditional experience, a sailing yacht gives you the feel of the wind and the sea. They are slower than motor yachts, so you cover less distance, but the experience is more relaxed. A 12 m sailing yacht with a skipper costs from around EUR 800-1,200 for a full day. Perfect for couples or small groups who want a peaceful day.

RIBs and Speedboats. Rigid inflatable boats (RIBs) are fast, nimble, and fun. They are open boats, so you get wind in your hair and spray in your face. A 6-8 m RIB with a skipper costs from around EUR 400-700 for a half day. They are ideal for adrenaline seekers or for reaching remote coves quickly. You can also drive them yourself if you have a licence, but our charters always include a skipper.

Fishing Boats. Some charters specialise in fishing trips. These boats are equipped with rods, reels, and fish finders. A half-day fishing trip costs from around EUR 500-800. You can target species like sea bass, bream, and sometimes tuna. The skipper will know the best spots.

Licence-Free Day Boats. In France, you can drive a boat up to 6 m with a 15 HP engine without a licence. Some operators offer these for self-drive. But if you are not confident, just book a skipper. It is easier and safer.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Nice

Prices vary wildly depending on the boat, the season, and the duration. Here are rough ranges based on typical listings. These are not exact prices for specific boats, just a guide.

Half Day (4 hours): RIBs from EUR 400-700. Motor yachts from EUR 800-1,500. Catamarans from EUR 1,000-2,000. Sailing yachts from EUR 500-1,000.

Full Day (8 hours): RIBs from EUR 700-1,200. Motor yachts from EUR 1,200-3,000. Catamarans from EUR 1,500-3,500. Sailing yachts from EUR 800-1,500.

Fuel: Add 20-30% of the charter price for fuel, sometimes more for large motor yachts. Ask the operator for an estimate.

Crew Gratuity: Not mandatory but customary. 10-15% of the charter fee is standard if the service is good.

Remember, these are starting points. A superyacht over 30 m will be price on request, usually EUR 10,000+ per day. For a budget option, a small RIB for a half day is your best bet.

Best Time of Year for a Boat Rental Nice

The season runs from May to October, with July and August being the peak. Water temperature in summer is around 22-26 degrees C. Air temperature can hit 30-35 degrees C. June and September are the sweet spots: warm, less crowded, and slightly lower prices. May and October are cooler (air 18-22 degrees C, water 16-20 degrees C) but still pleasant if you get a sunny day.

Winter charters are possible but rare. The weather is more unpredictable, and many operators close. If you are visiting in November to March, you might find only a few boats available. Stick to the summer months for the best experience.

How to Book a Boat Rental Nice

Booking is straightforward. You can use a marketplace like BoatHire24 to compare options, or contact local operators directly. Here is the process.

1. Choose your date and duration. Half day is good for a quick trip to Villefranche-sur-Mer or Cap d'Antibes. Full day lets you reach Monaco or the Lerins Islands.

2. Decide on boat type. Motor yacht for comfort, catamaran for space, RIB for speed, sailing yacht for tradition.

3. Check the skipper is included. All our listings include a licensed skipper. You do not need a licence.

4. Confirm the price, including fuel and any extras. Ask about cancellation policy.

5. Book and pay a deposit (usually 30-50%). The balance is paid on the day.

6. On the day, arrive at the port 15 minutes early. Meet the skipper, do a safety briefing, and off you go.

You can also browse our search page to filter by boat type, price, and departure port. For more tips, check our blog.

Who Is a Boat Rental Nice For?

A boat rental in Nice is for anyone who wants to see the French Riviera from the water. It works for couples looking for a romantic day, families with kids who want to swim and snorkel, groups of friends wanting a party, or corporate clients for a team-building event. The skipper handles everything, so you just relax.

It is not for people who want to drive the boat themselves without a licence. Some operators offer self-drive for small boats, but the majority require a licence or a skipper. If you want to be at the helm, you need a boat licence recognised in France (ICC or equivalent). Otherwise, let the skipper do the work.

It is also not for people on a tight budget. A boat rental is a luxury. A half-day RIB trip for four people might cost EUR 100-150 per person, which is reasonable. A full-day motor yacht for 12 people might be EUR 200-300 per person. But it is more expensive than a beach day.

What to Expect on the Day of Your Boat Rental Nice

On the day, you meet the skipper at the port. They will give a safety briefing, show you the boat, and explain the itinerary. You can discuss where you want to go. Popular destinations from Nice include:

Villefranche-sur-Mer. A beautiful bay with calm water, just east of Nice. You can anchor, swim, and have lunch at a beach restaurant.

Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat. A peninsula with luxury villas and hidden coves. Stop at Paloma Beach or Plage de la Plage.

Monaco. About 30-40 minutes by boat from Nice. You can see the harbour, the casino, and the Formula 1 circuit from the water. You can also dock and explore the town.

Menton. Further east, near the Italian border. Known for its gardens and pastel-coloured buildings. A full-day trip from Nice.

Antibes and Juan-les-Pins. West of Nice. Antibes has a historic old town and a large marina. Juan-les-Pins has sandy beaches and a lively atmosphere.

The Lerins Islands. Off Cannes. Sainte-Marguerite and Saint-Honorat. You can anchor, swim, and visit the monastery on Saint-Honorat. A full-day trip from Nice.

The skipper will adjust the itinerary based on weather and your preferences. You can stop for swimming, snorkelling, lunch at a beachside restaurant, or just cruising. Bring your own food and drink, or ask the operator if they provide catering.

Safety and Legal Considerations for a Boat Rental Nice

Safety is the skipper's responsibility. They will have a VHF radio, life jackets, a first aid kit, and a fire extinguisher. They will also monitor the weather. If conditions are bad, the trip may be cancelled or rerouted.

Legally, you need to be at least 18 to book. Some operators require a minimum age for passengers, usually 2-3 years old. Check the listing. Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper cannot drink. They are responsible for your safety.

Insurance is usually covered by the operator. But ask for confirmation. If you damage the boat, you might be liable for the excess on the insurance policy, typically EUR 500-2,000. Treat the boat with respect.

Alternatives to a Boat Rental Nice

If Nice does not suit you, consider other departure points on the Côte d'Azur. Cannes, Antibes, Monaco, and Saint-Tropez all have boat rentals. Each has a different vibe. Cannes is glitzy, Antibes is historic, Monaco is exclusive, Saint-Tropez is party central.

Or consider a different region altogether. Our main marketplace is for Marbella and the Costa del Sol in Spain. The water is warmer, the prices are generally lower, and the coastline is just as beautiful. You can depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. The boat types are the same: motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, RIBs, fishing boats, licence-free day boats, and superyachts. The local attractions include Puerto Banús, La Concha mountain, Río Verde, Cala del Faro, Estepona old town, the Strait of Gibraltar (for dolphin watching), and Nerja caves. If you are flexible, it is worth comparing.

Final Advice for a Boat Rental Nice

Book early, especially for July and August. The best boats go fast. Check the cancellation policy. Most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 7-14 days in advance. Bring cash for fuel and gratuity. And remember, the skipper is there to help. Ask them for recommendations on restaurants, beaches, and things to do. They know the area.

For more information, browse our search page to see what is available. Or read our blog for tips on planning your trip. If you have specific questions, contact us and we will point you in the right direction.
