h1: Yacht Rental Monaco, Book Your Costa del Sol Charter
intro:
You are looking for a yacht rental Monaco, but the prices in the Principality are eye-watering and the marinas are packed. We get it. The good news is that you can get the same Med luxury, the same sun, the same champagne lifestyle, for a fraction of the cost by chartering from Marbella. BoatHire24 connects you with skippered motor yachts, catamarans and sailing yachts based in Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande and Benalmádena. Every booking includes a licensed skipper, so you can relax and let someone else steer.

Monaco is famous for its superyacht scene, but the Costa del Sol gives you more space, more coastline and more value. You can cruise the Strait of Gibraltar, anchor off Cala del Faro, or take in the view of La Concha mountain while sipping a cold drink. This page tells you everything you need to know about renting a yacht from this side of the Med, including boat types, ports, seasons and how to book without the Monaco markup.
bodyHtml:
Why Choose a Yacht Rental on the Costa del Sol Instead of Monaco

Monaco is a status symbol, no question. But a yacht rental Monaco costs you a premium for the name alone. On the Costa del Sol, you get the same Mediterranean climate, the same blue water, and often better service for around half the price. Puerto Banús is the superyacht capital of southern Spain, with berths for vessels up to 80 metres. Marbella Marina offers a more relaxed vibe, while Estepona gives you a charming old town backdrop. The water temperature hits 24 degrees C in summer, and you have 150 kilometres of coastline to explore.

You also get more flexibility. In Monaco, you are confined to a small stretch of coast. From Marbella, you can head south to the Strait of Gibraltar to spot dolphins, east to Cabopino’s sand dunes, or west to Sotogrande’s exclusive marinas. The choice is yours, and the cost is lower.

What Is Included in Every Yacht Rental

Every charter booked through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a boating licence, and you do not have to navigate or dock. The skipper knows the local waters, the best anchorages and the weather patterns. Fuel is usually extra, as is food and drink, but you can arrange catering through the charter company. Most boats come with safety equipment, insurance, and a standard itinerary. You can customise the route, but expect to pay for extended cruising hours or overnight stays.

Typical inclusions: skipper, insurance, VAT, Wi-Fi on larger yachts, snorkelling gear, paddleboards on catamarans. Exclusions: fuel, port fees for overnight stops, food, drinks, crew tip (10% is standard). Always confirm the exact list with the charter company before you book.

Boat Types Available for Your Yacht Rental

You have several options when you search for a yacht rental Monaco alternative on the Costa del Sol. Motor yachts are the most popular, ranging from 30 feet to 80 feet plus. They offer speed, comfort and air-conditioned cabins. Catamarans are stable and spacious, ideal for families or groups who want deck space. Sailing yachts give you a quieter, more traditional experience, often at a lower price point.

RIBs and speedboats are perfect for day trips to Cala del Faro or the Strait of Gibraltar. They are fast (30-50 knots) and fun, but less comfortable for lounging. Fishing boats are equipped for deep-sea angling, with rods and tackle included. Licence-free day boats are a cheap option for two to four people, but they are limited to inshore waters. Superyachts (20 metres plus) are available on request, with prices starting from around EUR 8,000 per day.

Departure Ports for Your Charter

Your yacht rental starts from one of six main ports. Puerto Banús is the most glamorous, with designer boutiques and flashy cars lining the quay. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter, closer to the old town. Cabopino is a small, sandy port near the Artola dunes, ideal for a relaxed start. Estepona has a modern marina next to the colourful old town. Sotogrande is upmarket, with a golf course and polo club. Benalmádena is a lively port with restaurants and bars, popular with families.

Each port has its own character. If you want nightlife, choose Puerto Banús. For a peaceful day, pick Cabopino. For a mix of culture and beach, go with Estepona. The distance between ports is short: Marbella to Estepona is 15 nautical miles, about 30 minutes by motor yacht.

Popular Routes and Destinations

A typical day charter from Marbella might include a stop at Cala del Faro, a secluded cove with crystal water, then lunch at a chiringuito on the beach. If you head south, you reach the Strait of Gibraltar in about two hours. Here you can see dolphins and sometimes whales. The current is strong, so your skipper will handle the navigation.

Eastbound, you can cruise to Nerja and see the famous caves from the sea. The cliffs are dramatic, and the water is deep blue. Westbound, you reach the mouth of the Río Verde, where you can anchor and swim. For a longer trip, you can go to Gibraltar itself, but you need to clear customs. Most charters stick to the Spanish coast.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Rental

Prices vary by boat type, size, season and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 30-foot motor yacht starts from around EUR 800. A full day (8 hours) on a 40-foot catamaran costs from EUR 1,500. Superyachts of 60 feet plus start from EUR 4,000 per day. Fuel adds EUR 200-600 depending on distance and speed. Overnight charters include accommodation and breakfast, starting from EUR 2,500.

High season (June to September) is more expensive, with prices up to 30% higher. Low season (November to March) offers discounts, but weather is less reliable. Always ask for a detailed quote, including all taxes and fees. No two boats are priced the same, so compare options on our search page.

Best Time of Year for a Yacht Rental

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, so you can charter almost any month. July and August are peak: hot (30-35 degrees C), crowded, and expensive. May, June and September offer warm weather (25-30 degrees C) with fewer crowds. October is still pleasant, though evenings cool down. April and November are borderline: you might get rain, but prices are low.

Wind conditions matter. The Levante wind blows from the east in summer, creating choppy seas on the eastern coast. The Poniente from the west is lighter. Your skipper will know the forecast and adjust the route. For calm waters, book a morning charter before the afternoon breeze picks up.

How to Book Your Yacht Rental

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You browse available boats, choose your date and duration, and submit a request. The charter company responds within 24 hours with availability and price. You pay a deposit (usually 50%) to confirm, and the balance on the day. Cancellation policies vary: most allow free cancellation up to 7 days before, then a 50% charge.

You need to provide the number of guests, any special requests (catering, music, decorations), and your preferred departure port. The skipper will contact you a day before to confirm the meeting point and time. No hidden extras, but read the terms carefully. For more tips, check our blog on charter etiquette.

Who Is This Yacht Rental For

This is for anyone who wants a luxury day on the water without the Monaco price tag. Couples celebrate anniversaries, families take kids for a swim, groups of friends party on a catamaran. Business clients use charters for corporate events or client entertainment. Fishing enthusiasts book specialised boats for a day of angling. Even solo travellers can join a shared charter on some boats.

The common thread is that you want to relax, explore the coast, and let someone else handle the logistics. You do not need boating experience, and you do not need to speak Spanish (most skippers speak English). If you have a specific request, just ask. The charter companies are flexible within reason.

Local Colour and Attractions

Puerto Banús is worth a visit even if you do not charter. The marina is lined with luxury shops and restaurants. La Concha mountain looms over Marbella, its peak often dusted with snow in winter. Río Verde is a river mouth where you can anchor and walk to a beach bar. Cala del Faro is a small cove with a lighthouse, popular for swimming. Estepona old town has cobbled streets and flower pots. The Strait of Gibraltar is a wildlife corridor: dolphins, tuna, and occasionally orcas. Nerja caves are a UNESCO site, accessible by boat from the coast.

These are the places that make a yacht rental from Marbella special. You are not just renting a boat; you are buying access to a coastline that rivals anything Monaco offers.

Comparing Yacht Rental Costs: Monaco vs Costa del Sol

To give you a concrete sense of the savings, a 20-metre motor yacht in Monaco during August costs from around EUR 12,000 per day, excluding fuel and VAT. On the Costa del Sol, the same size vessel starts from EUR 4,500 per day, with fuel and VAT often included in the base price. For a 15-metre catamaran, Monaco charges EUR 6,000-8,000 daily; here you pay EUR 2,500-3,500. The difference is not just in the sticker price. Port fees in Monaco can add EUR 500-1,000 per night, while Puerto Banús charges around EUR 200-400. Crew tips are standard at 10% everywhere, but the lower base means your total outlay is significantly less. You also avoid the EUR 50 per person docking fee for tenders in Monaco’s harbour. For a group of eight, the savings on a week-long charter can exceed EUR 40,000. That is a real number, not a marketing line.

What You Actually Get for Your Money in Marbella

When you book a yacht rental through BoatHire24, the skipper is not just a driver. He knows where to find the clearest water for swimming, which chiringuitos serve the best grilled fish, and how to avoid the afternoon chop. On a typical 40-foot motor yacht, you get a flybridge with sun loungers, a saloon with air conditioning, a galley with fridge and hob, and two or three cabins for overnight trips. The sound system is Bluetooth-enabled, and most boats have a shower on the swim platform. For a full-day charter, the skipper will anchor at Cala del Faro for a two-hour swim stop, then take you to a beachfront restaurant for lunch. You can eat on board if you prefer; the charter company can arrange a catered menu from around EUR 35 per person. The boat will have a dinghy with an outboard motor, so you can explore shallow coves. The only thing you need to bring is sunscreen and a towel.

Which Boat Type Suits Your Group Size

For two to four people, a 30-foot motor yacht or a RIB is ideal. The RIB is faster (35-45 knots) and cheaper (from EUR 600 for a half-day), but you get wet and have minimal shade. For five to eight people, a 40-foot catamaran is the best option. It has a wide deck, a trampoline at the bow, and stable motion. For nine to twelve people, you need a 50-foot motor yacht or a sailing catamaran. For larger groups, superyachts of 60 feet plus are available, but you need to book weeks in advance in high season. A common mistake is booking a boat that is too small. The rule of thumb: allow 1 metre of boat length per person for comfort, excluding the skipper. So eight guests need a 40-foot boat minimum. If you want to party with music and dancing, add another 10 feet for space.

How Weather Affects Your Charter Day

The Costa del Sol has a microclimate that is generally stable, but wind patterns matter. The Levante wind blows from the east, funnelling through the Strait of Gibraltar. It creates short, choppy waves on the eastern coast, especially around Nerja. The Poniente wind from the west is lighter and brings calmer seas. In July and August, the thermal breeze picks up around 2pm, so morning charters are smoother. Your skipper will check the forecast and may suggest a route change. For example, if the Levante is strong, he will stay in the western bays near Estepona, where the water is flatter. If the wind is light, you can cross to the African coast in about three hours. The water temperature is 24 degrees C in August, dropping to 16 degrees C in February. For swimming, June to October is best. If you charter in April or November, bring a wetsuit for snorkelling.

Port-Specific Tips for Your Departure

Puerto Banús is the most convenient for first-time visitors. It has a taxi rank, a supermarket, and multiple restaurants. If you drive, parking costs EUR 30-50 per day in the underground car park. Marbella Marina is quieter and closer to the old town, with free street parking nearby. Cabopino is small and sandy, with a beach bar and a naturist section at the eastern end. Estepona marina has a fuel dock and a chandlery, useful if you need last-minute supplies. Sotogrande is exclusive but remote; you need a car to reach it. Benalmádena is family-friendly, with a sealife centre and a cable car up to the mountain. Each port has a different vibe. If you want to combine a charter with a night out, start from Puerto Banús. If you want a relaxed day with no crowds, choose Cabopino. The skipper will meet you at the pontoon 15 minutes before departure, so arrive early to find the berth.

Hidden Costs and How to Avoid Them

The quoted price for a yacht rental rarely includes everything. Fuel is the biggest variable. A 40-foot motor yacht burns about 80 litres per hour at cruising speed. For a full day covering 60 nautical miles, you use around 200 litres, costing EUR 300-400 at current diesel prices. Catamarans are more efficient, using 30-40 litres per hour. RIBs are thirstier, burning 100 litres per hour at speed. Port fees for overnight stops add EUR 100-300 per night, depending on the marina. Food and drink are extra; a basic catering package for eight people costs EUR 200-400. Crew tip is not included; budget 10% of the total charter price. Some companies charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50-100 if you leave the boat messy. To avoid surprises, ask for a written breakdown before you pay the deposit. Most reputable companies will provide a full quotation within 24 hours. If they hesitate, find another operator.

What to Do If the Weather Turns Bad

Even in summer, the Mediterranean can throw a surprise. If the forecast shows strong winds or thunderstorms, your skipper may recommend postponing or rerouting. Most charter companies allow you to reschedule for free up to 48 hours before departure. If you are already on the water and conditions deteriorate, the skipper will head to the nearest port. You do not get a refund for a shortened trip, but you can negotiate a credit for a future charter. In practice, bad weather is rare from June to September. The Costa del Sol averages only 3-4 rainy days per month in summer. If you are unlucky, accept it and spend the day exploring the port instead. The local restaurants and shops are worth a visit, and you can rebook for the next day. Flexibility is part of the deal when you charter a boat.

h1: Yacht Charter Mallorca, Book Your Boat Rental with Skipper
intro:
You want a yacht charter Mallorca, but you are based on the Costa del Sol or visiting Marbella. That is fine. BoatHire24 lists hundreds of boats in Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande and Benalmádena. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you do not need a licence. You can book a motor yacht, catamaran, sailing yacht or RIB for a day trip, a week or longer. Mallorca is a 12-hour sail away, but you can also fly there from Málaga in 50 minutes. We do not have boats based in Mallorca itself, but we can arrange a transfer or help you plan a multi-day itinerary from the mainland.

Why would you charter a yacht from the Costa del Sol when you want Mallorca? Because the boats here are newer, the prices are competitive, and you can combine a trip to the Balearics with a stop in Gibraltar or along the coast of Granada. The skipper knows the best anchorages, from Cala del Faro to the waters off Estepona old town. If you insist on a Mallorca-based charter, we can point you to partners, but our fleet is concentrated on the Costa del Sol. Read on to see how a yacht charter Mallorca can start from Marbella.
bodyHtml:
What a Yacht Charter Mallorca Includes

A yacht charter Mallorca from BoatHire24 is not the same as renting a bareboat in Palma. Every booking comes with a professional skipper, fuel for a standard day (usually 8 hours), VAT and insurance. You do not pay extra for the captain. The boat is cleaned before you board, and you get a safety briefing. Some charters include snacks, soft drinks or a welcome cava. You can add a hostess, a chef, water toys (jet skis, paddleboards) or a photographer for an extra fee. The price you see on the listing is the starting price for the boat and skipper. Check the description for what is included because each owner sets their own terms.

You can book a half-day (4 hours), a full day (8 hours), a sunset cruise (2-3 hours) or a multi-day trip. For a yacht charter Mallorca, you would typically need a minimum of 3-5 days to sail from Marbella to Mallorca, enjoy the island and return. The skipper works 8-10 hours per day, and overnight passages require rest breaks. You pay for marina fees and any dockage in Mallorca separately. Food and drinks are your own cost unless you opt for a catering package.

Departure Ports for Your Yacht Charter Mallorca

All our boats depart from the Costa del Sol. The main ports are:

  • Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina in Marbella, with superyachts and designer shops. Most of our motor yachts and catamarans are based here.
  • Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), a quieter option near the old town. Good for sailing yachts and licence-free day boats.
  • Cabopino, a small marina near Artola dunes. Ideal for fishing boats and RIBs.
  • Estepona, the port near Estepona old town. Catamarans and motor yachts available.
  • Sotogrande, a luxury residential port. Some larger yachts and superyachts.
  • Benalmádena, a busy marina with a range of boats, good for day trips.

From any of these ports, a yacht charter Mallorca means a 250-300 nautical mile crossing. You can sail overnight or break the journey in Almería or Cabo de Gata. The skipper will plan the route based on weather and your preferences.

Boat Types for a Yacht Charter Mallorca

You have choices. Here is what works best for a Mallorca trip:

Motor yachts, from 30 to 70 feet. Speeds of 20-30 knots. A 50-foot motor yacht can reach Mallorca in 10-12 hours from Marbella. Prices from around EUR 2,500 per day for a 40-foot model. Larger ones cost EUR 5,000-10,000 per day.

Catamarans, stable and spacious. 40-50 feet. Slower (8-12 knots), so the crossing takes 24-30 hours. Better for a relaxed multi-day trip. Prices from EUR 1,500 per day for a 40-foot catamaran.

Sailing yachts, classic option. 35-55 feet. Speed 6-8 knots. The crossing takes 36-48 hours. Prices from EUR 1,200 per day for a 40-foot sailboat.

RIBs and speedboats, small and fast (30-50 knots). Only for day trips along the coast, not for Mallorca. Max range 100 NM.

Fishing boats, equipped for sport fishing. Can be used for Mallorca if you want to fish en route. Prices from EUR 800 per day.

Licence-free day boats, up to 15 meters, no licence needed. Only for coastal use. Not suitable for Mallorca crossing.

Superyachts, 80 feet and above. Full crew, luxury. Prices on request. A superyacht charter Mallorca from Marbella is common for high-end clients.

Pricing Guidance for a Yacht Charter Mallorca

Prices vary by boat size, age, season and extras. Here are rough daily rates (8 hours) for a boat based in Marbella, including skipper and fuel:

  • Motor yacht 40-50 ft: EUR 2,500-4,500
  • Catamaran 40-50 ft: EUR 1,500-3,000
  • Sailing yacht 40-50 ft: EUR 1,200-2,500
  • RIB 30-40 ft: EUR 800-1,500
  • Superyacht 80+ ft: from EUR 10,000

For a multi-day yacht charter Mallorca, you pay the daily rate plus overnight fees. Some owners offer a discount for 3+ days. The total for a 5-day trip on a 50-foot motor yacht could be EUR 12,000-20,000. Add fuel for the crossing (EUR 500-1,500 depending on speed), marina fees in Mallorca (EUR 100-300 per night) and crew meals. A 10% service charge is sometimes added.

Best Seasons for a Yacht Charter Mallorca

Summer (June-September), peak season. Water temperature 24-28 degrees C. Air temperature 28-35 degrees C. Calm seas, but afternoon winds in the Alboran Sea. Crowded marinas. Book 3-6 months ahead. Prices are 20-40% higher.

Spring (April-May), good weather, fewer crowds. Water 18-22 degrees C. Ideal for sailing. Prices lower.

Autumn (October-November), warm air, cooler water. Risk of storms in November. Still bookable. Good for motor yachts.

Winter (December-March), cold and windy. Not recommended for a crossing. Some boats operate for day trips in sheltered waters.

For a yacht charter Mallorca, aim for May-September for the best experience.

How to Book a Yacht Charter Mallorca on BoatHire24

Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters. Select your preferred port (Puerto Banús, Marbella, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande or Benalmádena). Choose the boat type (motor yacht, catamaran, sailing yacht, or superyacht). Set the date and duration. Browse listings with photos, specs and prices. Click on a boat to see the full description, what is included, and the skipper's profile. Send an enquiry with your preferred dates and any special requests. The owner or booking manager will confirm availability and send a quote. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is due 2-4 weeks before departure. If you need help, contact our team via the search page.

We recommend checking the blog for tips on planning a multi-day itinerary, packing lists and weather advice. We have articles on the best anchorages in Mallorca, like Cala d'Or, Port de Sóller and Es Trenc.

Who is a Yacht Charter Mallorca For

This is for groups of 6-12 people who want a private, luxury experience. Families, friends, corporate groups or celebrations. You do not need any sailing experience. The skipper handles everything. You just relax, swim, eat and explore. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter, but we do not list those on our site. You would need to ask the owner.

Business clients often charter a superyacht for client entertainment. The departure from Puerto Banús adds prestige. For a wedding or anniversary, a sunset cruise around Marbella Bay is popular. For a Mallorca trip, you get the added adventure of a sea crossing.

Local Colour on the Costa del Sol and Mallorca

On the Costa del Sol, you see La Concha mountain behind Marbella, the Río Verde estuary, and the cliffs at Cala del Faro. In Estepona, the old town has flower-filled streets. Near Gibraltar, you often spot dolphins and whales. On the crossing to Mallorca, you pass Cabo de Gata in Almería, then the Cabrera Archipelago. Mallorca offers the Tramuntana mountains, the caves at Drach and the coves of Cala Llombards. The Strait of Gibraltar is a detour south, but worth it for the marine life.

Our skippers know these waters. They can recommend stops for lunch, swimming or snorkelling. Some boats have a barbecue on the back deck.

What to Expect on Board

Each boat has a flybridge or sundeck, a saloon with air conditioning, cabins with en-suite bathrooms, a galley kitchen, and a sound system. Larger yachts have a jacuzzi, stabilisers and Wi-Fi. You bring your own food and drink unless you order catering. The skipper will help with mooring and safety. You can swim off the boat in calm bays. Some boats have a tender for shore trips.

For a yacht charter Mallorca, pack light: swimwear, sunscreen, a hat, a light jacket for evenings, and non-slip shoes. The skipper will have a first aid kit and life jackets.

Alternatives to a Yacht Charter Mallorca

If the crossing seems too long, consider a charter along the Costa del Sol. You can explore Marbella, Puerto Banús, Estepona and Sotogrande in a day. Or head to Gibraltar for lunch. The water is warm, the views are good, and it costs less. A day charter from Marbella starts at EUR 800 for a RIB or EUR 1,500 for a motor yacht. You can also charter a catamaran for a sunset cruise with drinks.

If you really want Mallorca, you can fly from Málaga to Palma and charter a boat there. We do not list those, but you can use local companies. Our advantage is the integrated skipper and the ability to combine a mainland trip with the islands.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for a Yacht Charter Mallorca

We are a marketplace, not a rental company. We list boats from private owners and charter companies. You get direct contact with the skipper. Prices are transparent. No hidden fees. We cover the Costa del Sol, not Mallorca, but we can help plan the logistics. Our team speaks English, Spanish and German. We have been operating since 2018 and have hundreds of verified boats.

For a yacht charter Mallorca, start your search on BoatHire24. Use the filters to narrow down by port, boat type and budget. Send an enquiry for a custom quote. We will confirm within 24 hours.

Planning the Crossing: Marbella to Mallorca

The direct route from Puerto Banús to Palma de Mallorca is about 260 nautical miles. At 20 knots on a motor yacht, you are looking at 13 hours of sea time. That is doable in a single long day if you leave at 6am and arrive by 7pm. With a catamaran at 10 knots, it is 26 hours, so you need an overnight passage or a stop. The skipper will split the journey into two legs: Marbella to Cabo de Gata (100 NM, 5 hours), then Cabo de Gata to Mallorca (160 NM, 8 hours by motor yacht or 16 hours by catamaran). Some skippers prefer to stop at Almería port for fuel and rest. You can also anchor at Cala de los Genoveses near Cabo de Gata for a swim. The cost of marina fees in Almería is around EUR 50-80 for a 40-foot boat overnight.

Fuel Costs for the Crossing

Fuel is the biggest variable. A 40-foot motor yacht burns about 100 litres per hour at 20 knots. For 13 hours, that is 1,300 litres. At EUR 1.50 per litre (marine diesel in Spain, 2025 prices), that is EUR 1,950. A 50-foot motor yacht might burn 150 litres per hour, so 1,950 litres, costing EUR 2,925. A catamaran uses much less: 20 litres per hour at 8 knots, so 520 litres for 26 hours, costing EUR 780. Sailing yachts use little fuel under sail, but you need the engine for manoeuvring and calm conditions. Expect EUR 200-400 for a sailing yacht crossing. These costs are usually not included in the daily charter rate. Always ask the owner if fuel for the crossing is separate. Most listings include fuel for a standard day (8 hours) within 50 NM of port. Anything beyond that is extra.

Marina Options in Mallorca

When you arrive in Mallorca, you have several marina options. Palma Marina (Port de Palma) is the main hub, with berths for yachts up to 100 feet. Rates are EUR 150-300 per night for a 50-foot boat. Port de Sóller is a scenic natural harbour in the Tramuntana mountains, EUR 100-150 per night. Port d'Andratx is quieter, EUR 120-200. Cala d'Or has a small marina, EUR 80-120. If you want to anchor for free, try Cala Llombards or Cala Figuera, but check for protected areas. In peak summer, book a berth weeks ahead. The skipper will handle the booking, but you pay the fee. Some marinas offer discounts for multi-night stays.

Best Anchorages in Mallorca for a Yacht Charter

For a day at anchor, head to Cala Mondragó, a protected cove with turquoise water. Cala Santanyí is another good option, with a sandy beach. Cala Deià is dramatic, under cliffs, but can be crowded. Cala Bóquer is remote, only accessible by boat or hike. Cala Torta is wild and windy. For snorkelling, Cala Varques has caves. For lunch, you can dock at Port de Sóller and walk to the town for paella. The skipper will recommend spots based on wind direction. In the afternoon, the prevailing wind is from the southwest, so choose a north-facing cove for shelter.

What to Eat and Drink on Board

You bring your own provisions. In Marbella, stock up at Supercor in Puerto Banús or Mercadona in town. For a 5-day trip for 8 people, budget EUR 300-500 for food and drinks. Many boats have a fridge, freezer and hob. Some have a barbecue on the aft deck. You can order a catering package from the owner: a hostess costs EUR 200-300 per day, a chef EUR 400-600 per day, plus food cost. Typical menus include grilled fish, paella, salads and tapas. For drinks, buy cava, wine, beer and mixers. The skipper does not drink while operating the boat. You can bring your own alcohol, but glass bottles are safer in plastic containers. Some boats have a policy against red wine on deck because of stains.

Weather and Sea Conditions

The crossing from Marbella to Mallorca crosses the Alboran Sea and the Balearic Sea. In summer, the wind is usually light to moderate (force 2-4). Afternoon thermal winds can build to force 5 in the Alboran Sea, causing choppy seas. The skipper checks the forecast 48 hours before departure. If the wind is too strong, they may delay or reroute. Sea sickness is common on the crossing. Bring motion sickness tablets or patches. The boat has a stabiliser system on larger yachts, which reduces roll. Catamarans are more stable than monohulls. If you are prone to seasickness, choose a catamaran or a large motor yacht with stabilisers. The water temperature in summer is 24-26 degrees C, so swimming is pleasant. In spring and autumn, it is 18-22 degrees C, still swimmable with a wetsuit.

Insurance and Safety

All boats on BoatHire24 have third-party liability insurance and passenger insurance. The skipper holds a valid Spanish licence (PER or Patrón de Yate). The boat has life jackets for all passengers, a first aid kit, fire extinguishers and an EPIRB (emergency beacon). For the Mallorca crossing, the boat must have a VHF radio, radar and GPS. Some older boats may lack radar; check the listing. The skipper will give a safety briefing before departure. You sign a charter agreement that outlines your responsibilities. If the weather is dangerous, the skipper has the final say on cancelling. You get a full refund or reschedule. Our team can help with insurance questions via the contact form on the site.

What to Do in Mallorca on a Yacht Charter

Once docked, you can explore the island. Rent a car or hire a driver for a day trip to the Serra de Tramuntana, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Visit the village of Valldemossa, where Chopin spent a winter. Go to the Caves of Drach in Porto Cristo, a 25-minute walk from the marina. The caves have an underground lake and a classical music concert. For nightlife, Palma has clubs like Tito's and Pacha. Port de Sóller has quieter bars. For shopping, the Passeig del Born in Palma has luxury brands. For a beach day, take the tender to Cala Mesquida or Cala Agulla. The skipper can drop you off and pick you up later. Some boats have a jet ski for EUR 300-500 per day extra. You can also book a fishing trip in Mallorca waters for dorado and tuna.

title: Boat Rental Split

h1: Boat Rental Split, What You Need to Know
intro:
You’re probably here because you typed “boat rental Split” into Google, expecting to find options in Croatia. We get it. Split is a stunning Adriatic port, and the yacht charter scene there is legendary. But here’s the thing: we operate on the Costa del Sol, Spain, and we don’t have boats in Split. What we do have is a fleet of skippered motor yachts, catamarans, and sailing boats based in Marbella, Puerto Banús, Estepona, and Benalmádena. If you’re open to swapping the Dalmatian coast for the Andalusian one, you might find this page useful.

This page is for anyone who searched for boat rental Split but is flexible enough to consider a different destination. Maybe you’re planning a trip to southern Spain anyway, or perhaps you’re comparing Mediterranean options. Either way, we’ll give you a clear picture of what a boat charter on the Costa del Sol looks like, how it compares to Split, and how to book one. And if you’re dead set on Croatia, we’ll even point you to some resources to help you there.
bodyHtml:
Why You Might Have Searched for Boat Rental Split

Split is one of Europe’s most popular yachting hubs, especially for bareboat charters (where you sail yourself) and flotilla holidays. The city sits on a peninsula with a historic Diocletian’s Palace, and it’s the gateway to islands like Hvar, Brač, and Vis. Typical boat rental Split options include sailing yachts from 10 m to 15 m, catamarans, and motorboats. Prices can range from EUR 800 per week for a small sailing yacht in low season to EUR 5,000 or more for a luxury catamaran in August. Many operators require a sailing licence or a skipper, but there are also licence-free options for smaller boats.

If you’re comparing Split to the Costa del Sol, the main differences are sea conditions (the Adriatic is calmer), distances (islands are closer), and the vibe (more historical, less glitzy). But if you’re after guaranteed sunshine, warm water from May to October, and a party atmosphere in places like Puerto Banús, then Marbella might be a better fit. And we’re here to help with that.

What We Offer Instead: Skippered Boat Charters on the Costa del Sol

On BoatHire24, every charter includes a licensed skipper. You don’t need a sailing licence or any experience. You just show up, relax, and let the skipper handle the navigation, mooring, and safety. This is different from many boat rental Split companies, where you often sail yourself or hire a skipper separately. Our model is all-inclusive: the skipper’s fee is built into the price, and they’ll also act as a guide, pointing out landmarks like La Concha mountain or the Cabo de Gata cliffs.

We operate from five ports along the Costa del Sol: Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, and Benalmádena. Each port has its own character. Puerto Banús is the flashiest, with superyachts and designer boutiques. Marbella Marina is more laid-back, near the old town. Estepona is quieter, with a charming old quarter. Benalmádena is family-friendly, with a marina that feels like a mini theme park. You can choose your departure point based on your accommodation or itinerary.

Boat Types Available for Your Charter

We have a range of boats, from small RIBs to superyachts. Here’s a breakdown of what you can expect, with rough price ranges (prices vary by season and boat age).

Motor yachts: These are the most popular for day charters. Typically 10 m to 18 m, with a sun deck, cabin, and bathroom. Prices from around EUR 800 for a half-day to EUR 2,500 for a full day in high season. Examples: Azimut, Sunseeker, Jeanneau.

Catamarans: Stable and spacious, ideal for groups and families. Usually 12 m to 15 m, with multiple cabins and a large trampoline net at the bow. Half-day from around EUR 1,200, full day from EUR 1,800. Lagoon and Fountaine Pajot are common brands.

Sailing yachts: If you prefer the experience of sailing, we have 10 m to 14 m yachts. They’re slower but quieter and more eco-friendly. Prices similar to motor yachts, from EUR 700 half-day.

RIBs and speedboats: For adrenaline seekers, 6 m to 9 m rigid inflatable boats with powerful outboards. Great for water sports like wakeboarding or tubing. From around EUR 400 for 2 hours.

Fishing boats: Specialised boats for deep-sea fishing, equipped with rods and fish finders. Half-day from EUR 600.

Licence-free day boats: Small motorboats (up to 6 m) that you can drive without a licence. Perfect for a couple or small family to explore the coast at their own pace. From around EUR 250 for 4 hours.

Superyachts: For the ultimate luxury, we can arrange charters on yachts over 20 m with crew, jet skis, and gourmet catering. Price on request, but expect EUR 10,000+ per day.

Pricing Guidance and What’s Included

Unlike some boat rental Split operators that quote per week, we mostly do half-day (4 hours) and full-day (8 hours) charters. This is because the Costa del Sol is a day-charter destination: you cruise along the coast, stop for lunch at a chiringuito, swim in a cove, and return to port by evening. Overnight charters are possible but less common.

Prices vary by boat, season, and duration. As a rough guide:

  • Low season (November to March): 20-30% less than high season.
  • Mid season (April, May, October): standard rates.
  • High season (June to September): peak rates, especially August.

Most charters include the skipper, fuel for up to 4 hours of cruising, VAT, and basic insurance. Extras like food, drinks, water toys, or extra fuel for longer distances are charged separately. Always confirm what’s included when you search for a boat on our site.

For example, a 12 m motor yacht for a full day in July might cost around EUR 1,800, including skipper and fuel. A similar boat in Split for a bareboat week might be EUR 2,500, but you’d need to add fuel, a skipper if you want one, and provisioning. So the total cost can be comparable, but the experience is different.

Best Time for a Boat Charter on the Costa del Sol

The season runs from April to October, with the best weather from June to September. Sea temperatures reach 24-26 degrees C in August. Winds are generally light, with occasional afternoon sea breezes (the Poniente and Levante). The Levante can bring choppy conditions, but skippers know how to handle it and will adjust the route.

If you’re comparing to Split, note that the Adriatic sea is usually calmer and warmer in summer, but the Costa del Sol has more consistent sunshine. Split can have thunderstorms in July, while Marbella is typically dry.

For a quieter experience, consider May or September. The water is still warm enough for swimming, and the crowds are thinner. July and August are peak, with Puerto Banús buzzing with nightlife.

Popular Routes and Destinations

From Marbella or Puerto Banús, common day trips include:

  • Puerto Banús to Marbella: 15 minutes by boat. You can stop at the Marbella Club Hotel beach club or anchor off the old town.
  • Marbella to Cabopino: 30 minutes east. Cabopino has a small marina and the Artola dunes, a protected natural area.
  • Puerto Banús to Estepona: 45 minutes west. Estepona’s old town is worth a visit, and the port has a nice promenade.
  • Estepona to Gibraltar: 1.5 hours. You can see the Rock and often spot dolphins in the Strait. Note: you need a passport for Gibraltar, and the skipper will advise.
  • Benalmádena to Nerja: 2 hours east. Nerja has the famous caves, but you’ll need to moor at the nearby marina or anchor and go ashore by tender.

Most charters include a stop for swimming in a cove like Cala del Faro (near Cabopino) or Cala de la Leche (near Estepona). The skipper will know the best spots for the day’s conditions.

How to Book a Charter on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter your preferred port, date, and group size. You’ll see available boats with prices, photos, and specifications. Once you select a boat, you can request a booking. We’ll confirm availability and send you a payment link. Payment is by card or bank transfer. The skipper will contact you a few days before to discuss the itinerary.

We recommend booking at least a week in advance for high season, but last-minute bookings are sometimes possible. Cancellation policy varies by boat, but typically you can cancel up to 7 days before for a full refund.

If you’re unsure which boat or port suits you, you can call or email us. We’re based in Marbella and know the local scene well.

Who Is This For? (And Who Should Look Elsewhere)

Our charters are ideal for:

  • Groups of friends or families who want a private, relaxing day on the water without the hassle of sailing.
  • Corporate events or celebrations (birthdays, anniversaries), we can arrange catering and drinks.
  • Tourists staying in Marbella, Puerto Banús, or nearby resorts who want a unique experience.
  • People who prefer a skipper to handle navigation and safety.

If you’re a seasoned sailor who wants to sail yourself, our model might not suit you. In that case, you might be better off with a bareboat charter in Split or elsewhere. Similarly, if you’re on a tight budget, a half-day RIB trip might be affordable, but full-day luxury charters are expensive.

We also don’t offer flotilla holidays or multi-day sailing trips. Our focus is on day charters from the Costa del Sol.

Comparing Boat Rental Split vs. Costa del Sol: Which Is Right for You?

Let’s break it down.

Split (Croatia): Best for experienced sailors who want to island-hop. You can rent a bareboat sailing yacht and explore the Adriatic at your own pace. The scenery is dramatic, with limestone cliffs and hidden coves. The water is crystal clear. But you need a licence or a skipper, and the season is shorter (May to October). Prices can be high in August, but off-peak deals exist.

Costa del Sol (Spain): Best for a relaxed day charter with a skipper. You don’t need a licence. The coast is more developed, with beach clubs and restaurants. The weather is warmer and more stable. You’ll see the Rock of Gibraltar, the Sierra Nevada mountains, and maybe dolphins. It’s also easier to combine with a city break in Marbella or a visit to the Alhambra in Granada.

If you’re still set on Split, we recommend checking out specialist Croatia charter websites. But if you’re open to a different kind of Mediterranean experience, give the Costa del Sol a try. You might find it more convenient and less crowded.

For more reading, check out our blog, where we cover topics like “Best Beaches on the Costa del Sol” and “What to Expect on a Skippered Charter”.

Final Thoughts on Boat Rental Split and Alternatives

We know this page isn’t what you expected when you searched “boat rental Split”. But we hope it’s given you a clear picture of what we offer and how it compares. If you’re flexible, you might discover a fantastic option on the Costa del Sol. If not, no hard feelings, the Adriatic is beautiful.

Either way, we’re here to answer any questions. Contact us via the website or give us a call. Happy sailing, wherever you end up.

Why the Costa del Sol Works Better for a Group of Mixed Abilities

If your group includes people who aren't confident on the water, or if you have children or elderly members, a skippered charter on the Costa del Sol is a safer bet than a bareboat in Split. In Split, you'd either need everyone to be a capable sailor or you'd have to hire a skipper separately, which adds cost and complexity. On our boats, the skipper handles everything. You can have a grandparent who just wants to sunbathe on the bow, a teenager who wants to jump off the boat into the sea, and a parent who wants to steer for a bit under supervision. It works for all ages and fitness levels. The boats are also more stable: catamarans barely roll, and motor yachts have stabilisers. Split's sailing yachts can heel over, which makes some people seasick.

Specific Ports and Their Advantages for Your Charter

Each of our ports offers a different starting point. If you're staying in the heart of Marbella, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is the most convenient. It's a 10-minute walk from the old town and the beach. The marina itself is quieter than Puerto Banús, so boarding is less chaotic. If you want the full glamour, Puerto Banús is where you'll find the biggest yachts and the most people-watching. The downside is that parking is expensive and the marina can be crowded on weekends. Cabopino is the smallest and most charming; it's near the Artola dunes and has a lovely sandy beach. It's ideal if you're staying in the quieter east side of Marbella. Estepona is the best choice if you want to head west towards Gibraltar and the Strait. The marina is modern and has good restaurants. Benalmádena is further east, closer to Málaga airport, so it's convenient if you're flying in and want to start your charter quickly.

Cost Breakdown: What You Actually Pay vs. a Split Charter

Let's be specific about money. A half-day (4-hour) charter on a 10 m motor yacht from Puerto Banús in June costs around EUR 800 to EUR 1,000. That includes the skipper, fuel for the first 4 hours of cruising, VAT, and basic insurance. If you want to go further, extra fuel is charged at roughly EUR 100 per hour of cruising. Drinks and food are not included; you can bring your own or ask the skipper to stop at a beach club where you pay separately. Compare that to Split: a bareboat 10 m sailing yacht for a week in June starts at around EUR 1,500, but you'll need to add EUR 200-300 for fuel, EUR 100 for marina fees, and EUR 500-700 for a skipper if you want one. That works out to around EUR 2,300 to EUR 2,600 for a week, but you're sailing yourself and you have to plan the route. For a single day, our charter is more expensive per hour, but you get the convenience of a skipper and a fixed itinerary. For a week-long holiday, Split might be cheaper per day, but you're doing all the work.

Weather and Sea Conditions: When to Choose the Costa del Sol Over Split

The Costa del Sol has a microclimate that gives it more sunny days than almost anywhere else in Europe. From May to October, you can expect 300 days of sunshine. The water temperature in August hits 26 degrees C, which is warm enough for swimming without a wetsuit. The winds are usually light in the morning, building to a gentle sea breeze in the afternoon. The Levante wind can bring choppy seas, but it's rare in summer. In Split, the Adriatic is known for the Bora wind, which can be strong and gusty, especially in spring and autumn. The sea is calmer in July and August, but thunderstorms can appear suddenly. If you want guaranteed stable weather for your charter day, the Costa del Sol is more reliable. If you're a sailor who enjoys a bit of wind, Split might be more exciting.

Practical Tips for Booking Your Charter on BoatHire24

When you search for a boat, pay attention to the "maximum guests" number. This is the legal limit including the skipper. If you have 8 people, you need a boat that says "max 9 guests" or more. Also check the "included fuel" hours. Most charters include 4 hours of cruising fuel for a half-day or 8 hours for a full day. If you plan to motor for longer, ask about extra fuel costs. For a full-day charter, plan to leave the port around 10:00, cruise for an hour, anchor for swimming and lunch for 2-3 hours, then cruise back. The skipper will suggest a route based on the weather. If you want to visit a specific beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club, let the skipper know in advance so they can arrange mooring.

intro:

What we do offer is a better alternative: a huge selection of boats from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. bodyHtml:
Why Choose Boat Rental on the Costa del Sol Instead of Barcelona?

Barcelona has its charms: Gaudí, the Ramblas, and a bustling port. But boat rental Barcelona can be expensive, especially in summer. The Costa del Sol offers a similar Mediterranean experience with warmer water (averaging 24 degrees C in August), more sunshine (over 320 days a year), and fewer tourists on the water. Puerto Banús alone has over 900 berths and a concentration of luxury yachts that rivals anywhere. You can sail from Marbella to Estepona in 30 minutes, anchor at a secluded cove like Cala del Faro, and have the water almost to yourself. Plus, the cost of chartering a boat here is often 20-30% lower than in Barcelona, because there’s more competition and lower port fees. So unless you absolutely need to be in Barcelona, consider the Costa del Sol.

What’s Included in Every Boat Rental

Every boat rental through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That’s not optional: it’s the law in Spain for most charter boats over a certain size, and it’s included in the price. You don’t need a boating licence, and you don’t need to worry about navigation, anchoring, or safety. The skipper handles everything. Fuel is sometimes included, sometimes extra: check the listing details. Most rentals also include basic insurance, life jackets, and a first-aid kit. Some include snorkelling gear, paddleboards, or a welcome drink. You can also add extras like a catered lunch, a photographer, or water toys. Read the fine print before booking, but generally, what you see is what you get.

Available Boat Types for Your Rental

We categorise boats into six types, so you can filter by what suits your group and budget. First, motor yachts: from 8-metre day cruisers to 30-metre flybridges. They’re fast (20-30 knots), stable, and great for cruising along the coast. Second, catamarans: these are wide, stable, and have huge deck space. Ideal for groups of 10-20 people who want to sunbathe and party. Third, sailing yachts: from 10-metre classics to 20-metre performance cruisers. Slower but quieter, and you can help hoist the sails if you want. Fourth, RIBs and speedboats: small, fast, and fun. Great for a couple or a small family. Fifth, fishing boats: equipped with rods, bait, and a skipper who knows the best spots. Sixth, licence-free day boats: boats under 6 metres that you can drive yourself without a licence. These are popular for a few hours of exploring the coastline. And finally, superyachts: over 24 metres, with crew, jacuzzis, and all the luxury you can imagine. Price on request for those.

Departure Ports on the Costa del Sol

You can start your trip from any of our six departure ports. Puerto Banús is the most famous: a glamorous marina with designer shops and restaurants. It’s the default for luxury charters. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a bit more laid-back and closer to the old town. Cabopino is smaller and quieter, near the Artola dunes. Estepona has a charming old town and a long promenade. Sotogrande is an exclusive residential area with a top-class marina. Benalmádena is near Málaga airport and has a large marina with many boat options. Each port has its own character, and the distances between them are short: 20-30 minutes by boat. So you can depart from one and visit another for lunch. For example, depart from Puerto Banús, cruise to Estepona for a paella, and return in the afternoon.

Pricing Guidance, What to Expect

Prices vary by boat size, type, season, and duration. Here’s a rough guide based on real listings. A half-day (4 hours) on a small RIB or licence-free boat: from around EUR 300. A full day (8 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht: from around EUR 800. A catamaran for 12 people, full day: from around EUR 1,500. A 20-metre luxury motor yacht: from around EUR 3,000. A superyacht over 30 metres: price on request, typically EUR 10,000+. These are starting prices; peak season (July-August) can be 20-50% higher. Off-season (October-May) you can negotiate. Always check the listing for what’s included: some include fuel, food, and drinks; others don’t. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for summer, and 1 week for other seasons.

Best Seasons for Boat Rental on the Costa del Sol

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and hot summers. The best time for boating is May to October. In May and June, the water is around 18-22 degrees C, the air is warm (25-30 degrees C), and there are fewer tourists. July and August are peak season: water temperature reaches 24-26 degrees C, air can hit 35 degrees C, and marinas are busy. September and October are still warm, with water around 22 degrees C, and prices drop. November to April is possible but cooler: water around 16-18 degrees C, air 15-20 degrees C, and more chance of wind. Some boats still operate, especially for fishing or whale watching. But for a comfortable day of swimming and sunbathing, aim for June or September.

How to Book Your Boat Rental Online

Booking is straightforward. Go to our BoatHire24 homepage, enter your preferred date, group size, and port. Browse the results, filter by boat type, price, or amenities. Click on a listing to see full details: photos, specifications, included extras, and the skipper’s profile. Most listings have a “Book Now” button that takes you to a secure payment page. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to confirm, and the balance is due on the day, usually in cash or by card to the skipper. We recommend reading the cancellation policy: most are flexible up to 7 days before. If you have questions, use the contact form on each listing to message the owner directly. For complex requests (like a multi-day charter or a superyacht), use our search page to refine your criteria, or contact us and we’ll help.

Who Is Boat Rental on the Costa del Sol For?

It’s for anyone who wants to spend a day on the water without the hassle of owning a boat. Families with kids: the skipper handles safety, and you can anchor at a calm beach for swimming. Groups of friends: catamarans and motor yachts are perfect for parties, with music, drinks, and a BBQ. Couples: a private sailing yacht or a RIB for a romantic sunset cruise. Corporate groups: team-building or client entertainment on a luxury motor yacht. Fishing enthusiasts: specialised fishing boats with all gear included. And if you’re a first-timer, don’t worry. The skipper will show you around, and you can even try steering if you want. It’s all about relaxing and enjoying the coast.

Local Highlights You Can See on Your Trip

The Costa del Sol has plenty of sights from the water. From Puerto Banús, you see the famous marina and the luxury cars on the promenade. From Marbella, you get a view of La Concha mountain, which looks like a giant shell. Along the coast, you can stop at Cala del Faro, a secluded cove near Marbella with crystal-clear water. Further west, near Estepona, the old town’s whitewashed buildings are visible from the sea. If you go south towards Gibraltar, you might spot dolphins and even whales in the Strait of Gibraltar. For a longer trip, you can sail east to Nerja and see the famous caves from the water (though you’ll need to dock and walk up). The coastline is varied: cliffs, sandy beaches, and small coves. Your skipper will know the best spots for swimming, snorkelling, and lunch.

Boat Rental Barcelona, A Note on Search Intent

If you searched for “boat rental Barcelona”, you might be planning a trip to Catalonia. We don’t have boats there. But before you leave, consider this: the Costa del Sol is a 90-minute flight from Barcelona, and many people fly down for a weekend charter. Alternatively, if you’re already in Barcelona, you might want to check local operators. But if you’re flexible, the Costa del Sol offers better value, more boat options, and a longer season. Our blog has more articles on the best spots for boating in southern Spain. And if you decide to come here, we’ll help you find the perfect boat. Otherwise, good luck with your search in Barcelona.

How Boat Rental Barcelona Compares to Costa del Sol on Price

Let’s be honest: you came here searching for boat rental Barcelona, and we’re telling you to look at Marbella instead. So here’s the financial breakdown. In Barcelona, a half-day on a 10-metre motor yacht starts at around EUR 800-1,000 in summer. On the Costa del Sol, the same boat from Puerto Banús starts at around EUR 600-700. A catamaran for 12 people in Barcelona? Expect EUR 2,000-2,500 for a full day. Here, you’re looking at EUR 1,500-1,800. The reasons are simple: lower port fees in Marbella, more competition among charter companies, and a longer season that spreads demand. You also avoid the congestion of Barcelona’s port, where you spend 30 minutes just getting out of the marina. In Puerto Banús, you’re on open water in 10 minutes. So if your budget is tight, the Costa del Sol wins by a clear margin.

Specific Itineraries for a Day on the Water

Your skipper will suggest routes, but here are three concrete options. First, the Marbella to Estepona run: depart Puerto Banús at 10am, cruise west at 20 knots, arrive at Estepona marina by 10.30am. Anchor off the beach for swimming and snorkelling (water clarity is best here). Lunch at a chiringuito on the beach, then return via the coast, stopping at Cala del Faro for a final dip. Total distance: 15 nautical miles. Second, the Gibraltar dolphin trip: depart from Sotogrande or Estepona, head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You’ll reach the dolphin zone in about 40 minutes. Common species: common dolphins, striped dolphins, and occasionally pilot whales. Bring binoculars. The water is deeper here (up to 900 metres), so the wildlife is abundant. Third, the Benalmádena to Cabopino loop: depart Benalmádena, head east past the marina, stop at the Artola dunes for a walk, then anchor at Cabopino’s sandy beach. This is a shorter trip, about 10 nautical miles, ideal for a half-day with kids.

Fuel Costs and What to Budget Extra

Fuel is a significant cost that many first-time renters overlook. A 10-metre motor yacht burns about 60-80 litres per hour at cruising speed. At EUR 1.50 per litre (current diesel price in Marbella), that’s EUR 90-120 per hour. For a full day (8 hours), that’s EUR 720-960. Some charters include fuel in the price, but many don’t. Always check the listing. Catamarans are more fuel-efficient: a 12-metre cat uses about 40-50 litres per hour, so EUR 60-75 per hour. Sailing yachts use almost no fuel if you sail, but you’ll still need the engine for manoeuvring in port. RIBs are the cheapest: a 6-metre RIB with a 200hp outboard uses about 30 litres per hour. Budget an extra EUR 300-500 for a day on a motor yacht if fuel is not included. And don’t forget the skipper’s tip: 10-15% of the charter price is customary if the service is good.

Weather Windows and Sea Conditions

The Costa del Sol has a reputation for calm seas, but it’s not guaranteed. The best conditions are from June to September, when the wind is light (typically Force 2-3 on the Beaufort scale) and the swell is under 0.5 metres. In May and October, you might get a Levante wind from the east, which can kick up a short, choppy sea, especially near Gibraltar. If the wind is over Force 5 (about 20 knots), most charters will cancel or reroute to sheltered areas like the Marbella bay. Your skipper monitors the forecast and will make the call. In winter (November to March), the sea is rougher, with swells of 1-2 metres common. Fishing charters still operate because the fish are more active, but swimming trips are less comfortable. Always check the 7-day forecast before booking, and ask the owner about their cancellation policy for bad weather.

What to Bring and What Not to Bring

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses with a strap, a towel, swimwear, and a light jacket or windbreaker (even in summer, the breeze can be cool at 20 knots). Bring a waterproof phone case or a dry bag. Bring your own snacks and drinks if they’re not included; most boats have a cooler and ice. What not to bring: high heels (they damage the deck), glass bottles (they break and are dangerous), large coolers (the boat has limited space), or anything that can blow away. Leave your passport and valuables in a safe place onshore. If you’re prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure. The skipper will have a first-aid kit, but bring your own if you have specific needs. And don’t forget a camera: the views of La Concha mountain from the sea are stunning.

Booking for Large Groups and Events

If you’re planning a group of 15-30 people, a catamaran is your best bet. We have catamarans up to 20 metres that can carry 30 passengers. For example, a 15-metre Lagoon catamaran from Puerto Banús costs from around EUR 2,500 for a full day with skipper and fuel. That’s about EUR 83 per person for a group of 30. For a party, you can add a DJ, a BBQ, and an open bar. For corporate events, many boats offer AV equipment and catering. For a wedding proposal, the skipper can arrange a sunset cruise with champagne and a photographer. The key is to book early: large groups need at least 2-3 weeks’ notice in summer. Use our search page to filter by passenger capacity and amenities. And if you need a superyacht for a VIP event, contact us directly for a quote.

h1: Jet Ski Miami: Rent and Ride on the Atlantic
intro:
You want to ride a jet ski in Miami. The sun, the sea, the skyline. We get it. BoatHire24 connects you with local operators who rent jet skis by the hour or half-day. No licence required for most rentals. You just turn up, get a safety briefing, and hit the water. We list prices, locations, and availability so you can book directly online.

This page covers everything you need to know about jet ski hire in Miami: where to launch, what it costs, what to expect, and how to make the most of your time on the water. We keep it honest and straightforward. No fluff.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Jet Ski Rental in Miami

A typical jet ski rental in Miami includes the machine, a life jacket, a fuel tank, and a safety briefing. Most operators let you ride for 30 minutes, one hour, or two hours. Some offer half-day deals. You do not need a boating licence for a jet ski in Florida if you are over 14 and have completed a short online safety course, but many rental companies handle that for you on the spot.

You get a modern jet ski, usually a Yamaha, Sea-Doo, or Kawasaki, with enough power to reach 40-50 knots. The rental includes a designated riding area, often around Biscayne Bay or the Atlantic Ocean near South Beach. Some operators let you explore further, but they will give you a map and a radio. You must stay within the boundaries. The water can get busy, especially near the shore, so expect a few rules about speed and distance from swimmers.

Fuel is usually included in the price, but check the small print. Some companies charge extra for a full tank. Insurance is often included, but you might pay a deductible if you crash. Ask before you sign. We list all the details on the search page so you can compare.

Where to Ride a Jet Ski in Miami

Miami offers several launch points for jet skis. The most popular is Biscayne Bay, a large protected body of water between Miami Beach and the mainland. You get views of the skyline, the Port of Miami, and the Venetian Islands. The water is calm most of the year, making it ideal for beginners. You can ride past the Miami Marine Stadium, the old stilt houses, and even spot manatees if you are lucky.

Another option is Key Biscayne, which gives you access to the Atlantic side. You can ride along the coast, past Cape Florida Lighthouse, and into the open ocean. The waves can be bigger here, so it suits more experienced riders. Some tours go as far as Stiltsville, a cluster of historic houses on stilts in the bay. You can also launch from Virginia Key or Watson Island, both near downtown.

If you want a longer ride, some operators offer guided tours that take you to Sand Key or Elliott Key, part of the Biscayne National Park. Those trips last 2-3 hours and cost more, but you get to see wilder parts of the coast. We cover the best launch spots and routes on our blog.

Boat Types and Alternatives

Jet skis are not the only option for getting on the water in Miami. You can also rent a small speedboat or a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) if you want more space or a smoother ride. Speedboats go faster and handle rougher water better, but they need a licence in some cases. RIBs are stable and easy to drive, but they are slower than jet skis.

For groups, a pontoon boat or deck boat works well for cruising around the bay. You can anchor, swim, and have lunch. Those do not need a licence either. If you want to fish, consider a fishing boat with a guide. Jet skis are for speed and fun, not comfort or long trips.

BoatHire24 lists all these options for Miami. You can filter by type, price, and capacity. Just go to the homepage and enter your dates.

Pricing: How Much Does a Jet Ski Cost in Miami?

Prices for jet ski rentals in Miami vary by season, duration, and location. Expect to pay from around EUR 80 to EUR 150 per hour for a single jet ski. Half-day rentals (four hours) range from EUR 250 to EUR 400. Guided tours cost more, typically EUR 150 to EUR 250 per person for a two-hour trip with a guide.

You can sometimes get a discount for booking online or renting two jet skis. The price includes the machine, fuel, life jacket, and basic insurance. Some operators add a cleaning fee or a deposit (EUR 100-300) which you get back if you return the ski undamaged. Check the cancellation policy before you pay. Most companies offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

Prices are higher in peak season (December to April) and during holidays like Spring Break or New Year. In summer, rates drop by 20-30%. Booking early usually gets you a better deal. We show live prices on the search page so you can compare without calling around.

Best Seasons for Jet Skiing in Miami

Miami has a subtropical climate. You can ride a jet ski year-round, but the best months are November to April. That is the dry season. Temperatures range from 20 to 28 degrees C. The water is warm (22-26 degrees C). The wind is lighter, and the sea is calm. You get clear skies and low humidity. This is also the busy season, so book early.

From May to October, it is hotter and more humid. Temperatures hit 30-35 degrees C. Afternoon thunderstorms are common, especially in August and September. The water gets warmer (28-30 degrees C). Hurricane season runs from June to November, so check the forecast. If a storm is coming, operators cancel rentals and refund you. The upside is lower prices and fewer crowds.

Winter mornings can be cool (15 degrees C), but by 10am it warms up. Bring a wetsuit if you are sensitive to cold. Summer afternoons are best avoided for riding because of the storms. Go early in the morning or late afternoon.

How to Book a Jet Ski in Miami

Booking a jet ski through BoatHire24 is simple. Go to the search page, enter your dates, and filter by jet ski. You will see a list of available rentals with prices, durations, and operator details. Click on one to see the full description, photos, and reviews. Then book online with a credit card or PayPal. You get a confirmation email with the operator's contact details and meeting point.

You need to be at least 18 to rent a jet ski. Some operators allow 16-year-olds with parental consent. You must show a valid ID (passport or driving licence). The rental company will give you a safety briefing and a quick test drive in the dock area. Then you are free to go.

If you have never been on a jet ski before, ask for a short training session. Most operators offer it for free. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses. Bring a waterproof phone case or leave your phone onshore. Do not drink alcohol before riding. The police patrol the water and check for intoxication.

We recommend booking at least a week in advance during peak season. In summer, you can often book the day before. If you need help, contact us through the website. We do not charge booking fees.

Who Should Rent a Jet Ski in Miami?

Jet skis are for people who want speed, thrills, and a quick hit of adrenaline. They are not for relaxing cruises or long-distance trips. If you want to explore the coast for hours, get a boat. If you want to jump waves, spin, and feel the wind in your face, get a jet ski.

They work well for couples, friends, or solo riders. Groups of 2-4 people can rent two jet skis and ride together. Some operators offer double-seat jet skis for a passenger. The passenger just holds on. It is fun but less stable for sharp turns.

You do not need any experience. The controls are simple: throttle, brake, and steering. The hardest part is getting used to the weight and balance. Most people pick it up in 10 minutes. If you are nervous, take a guided tour. The guide leads the group and keeps an eye on everyone.

If you have a disability, check with the operator. Some jet skis have adaptive controls. Miami has a few companies that cater to riders with limited mobility. Ask before you book.

Safety Tips for Jet Skiing in Miami

Jet skis are safe if you follow the rules. The main risks are collisions, falls, and dehydration. To avoid collisions, keep a safe distance from other boats, swimmers, and jet skis. Miami waters are busy, especially near the beaches. Stay in the designated riding area. Do not go into the swimming zones marked by buoys.

Falls happen when you turn too sharply or hit a wave at speed. Always keep both hands on the handlebars. Sit down when accelerating. Do not stand up unless the water is flat. If you fall, stay calm. The jet ski will float and circle back if it has a lanyard cut-off switch. Wait for it to stop, then climb back on from the rear. Do not try to mount from the side.

Dehydration is a real issue. The sun and wind dry you out fast. Drink water before and during the ride. Wear a life jacket at all times. The rental company provides one. Do not remove it. If you get into trouble, use the radio or wave for help. Most operators have a support boat nearby.

Check the weather before you go. If the forecast shows storms or high winds, reschedule. Do not ride alone if you are a beginner. Always tell someone onshore where you are going and when you expect to return.

Local Attractions and Sights from a Jet Ski

From a jet ski in Miami, you can see some iconic landmarks. The Miami skyline is best viewed from the bay, especially at sunset. The Port of Miami is a busy container port with huge ships. You can ride past the Venetian Islands, a chain of man-made islands with luxury homes. The Miami Beach coastline stretches for miles, with hotels and condos lining the shore.

If you go south towards Key Biscayne, you will see the Cape Florida Lighthouse, built in 1825. The area around it is a state park with mangroves and wildlife. You might spot dolphins, pelicans, and sea turtles. Further out, Stiltsville is a group of historic houses on stilts, built in the 1930s. They are now part of a national park and can only be seen from the water.

For a longer ride, head to Biscayne National Park. It is about 30 minutes by jet ski from downtown. The park has coral reefs, shipwrecks, and islands. You can stop at Boca Chita Key or Elliott Key for a break. These are protected areas, so do not disturb the wildlife or take anything.

We have a full guide to Miami jet ski routes on our blog.

Frequently Asked Questions

Jet Ski Rental Requirements in Miami

To rent a jet ski in Miami, you must be at least 18 years old with a valid credit card and photo ID. Some operators accept 16-year-olds with a parent present. Florida law requires anyone born after 1988 to have a Boating Safety Education ID card, but most rental companies offer a temporary certificate as part of the booking. The process takes about 30 minutes online. You do not need a physical licence. The rental includes a 10-15 minute orientation on the dock where you learn the controls, hand signals, and local navigation rules. Bring a towel and a change of clothes because you will get wet. Leave valuables in a locker or your car. Most operators have secure storage on site.

Fuel Policies and Hidden Costs

Fuel is almost always included in the advertised price for jet ski rentals in Miami. The machine comes with a full tank, and you return it empty. Some operators charge a fuel surcharge if you use more than the allocated amount, usually around EUR 20-30 for a one-hour ride. Check the terms before you book. Other potential extra costs include a security deposit of EUR 100-300, which is refunded if the jet ski is returned undamaged. Damage waivers cost around EUR 15-30 and reduce your liability. Late return fees are steep, often EUR 50-100 per hour. Cleaning fees are rare but can appear if you leave the machine covered in sand or fish guts. We show all fees clearly on the search page so you know the total upfront.

Best Launch Points for Jet Ski Rentals in Miami

The main launch points for jet ski rentals in Miami are along the MacArthur Causeway, near Watson Island, and at the Miami Beach Marina on Alton Road. Watson Island is the most convenient for tourists staying in downtown or South Beach. It has free parking and direct access to Biscayne Bay. The Miami Beach Marina offers rentals that launch into the Atlantic Ocean, ideal for riders who want bigger waves and longer trips. Key Biscayne has a few operators near the Rickenbacker Causeway, with easy access to both the bay and the ocean. Virginia Key is quieter and less crowded, good for beginners. Each location has different riding zones and speed limits. Ask the operator for a map of the permitted area before you set off.

Group Rentals and Double Jet Skis

If you are renting with friends or family, consider a double-seat jet ski. These models have a seat for a passenger behind the driver. The passenger does not need a licence or safety certificate. Double jet skis cost around EUR 100-180 per hour, about 20% more than a single. They are less agile and slower to turn, but they let two people share the experience. For groups of 3-6 people, renting two or three single jet skis is often cheaper and more fun because everyone gets to drive. Some operators offer a group discount for booking multiple machines. You can ride together in a loose formation. The lead rider sets the pace. We list group-friendly operators on the BoatHire24 homepage.

Weather and Water Conditions for Jet Skiing in Miami

Miami waters are generally calm in the morning, with winds below 10 knots and wave heights under 0.5 metres. By midday, the sea breeze picks up, especially in summer, creating chop of 0.5-1 metre. Biscayne Bay stays flatter than the Atlantic side. The best riding conditions are from November to April when cold fronts pass every 5-7 days, bringing clear skies and light winds. Summer afternoons often see thunderstorms that develop quickly. If you hear thunder or see lightning, head back immediately. Operators monitor the weather and will call you in if conditions turn dangerous. Water temperature ranges from 22 degrees C in January to 30 degrees C in August. A wetsuit is optional in winter but not necessary. Sunscreen with SPF 50 is essential year-round.

Jet Ski Tours and Guided Experiences

Guided jet ski tours in Miami offer a structured way to explore the coastline. A typical tour lasts 1.5 to 3 hours and covers 15-25 nautical miles. The guide leads a group of 4-10 riders, stopping at points of interest like Stiltsville, the Miami Marine Stadium, or the Venetian Islands. Tours cost EUR 120-200 per person, including the jet ski, fuel, guide, and insurance. Some tours include a stop at a sandbar or a small island for a swim break. Others focus on sightseeing or wildlife spotting. You can book a private tour for your group only, which costs more but gives you flexibility on route and pace. Guided tours are ideal if you are unfamiliar with the area or want to see more than you could on your own. We have a selection of tours listed on our blog.

Environmental Rules and Responsible Riding

Miami has strict environmental rules for jet ski riders. You must stay at least 100 feet from manatees, dolphins, and sea turtles. Do not chase or feed wildlife. Slow down in seagrass beds and shallow areas. Idle speed zones are marked with signs or buoys. Fines for violating these rules start at EUR 500. You cannot ride within 200 feet of a swimmer or a diver-down flag. No wake zones exist near marinas, bridges, and the shoreline. Jet skis are not allowed in certain areas of Biscayne National Park without a permit. Most rental operators give you a briefing on the local rules and a map of restricted zones. Follow them to avoid fines and protect the ecosystem. If you see a manatee, cut your engine and let it pass. Do not touch it.
