h1: Boat Rental Phuket: Your Guide to Chartering in Paradise
intro:
You want a boat rental in Phuket, but you are probably drowning in options. Phuket has hundreds of boats, dozens of operators, and more hidden coves than you can shake a snorkel at. The problem is sorting the floating palaces from the rust buckets, and the genuine operators from the guys who will take your money and leave you stranded on a sandbank.

Here is the truth. A proper Phuket boat rental includes a licensed skipper, safety gear, and a boat that actually runs. Anything less is a floating liability. At BoatHire24, we list only verified charters with experienced skippers. No surprises. No sunken dreams. Just you, the Andaman Sea, and a cold Singha in your hand.
bodyHtml:
What a Phuket Boat Rental Actually Includes

Most people assume a boat rental in Phuket is just the hull and an engine. It is not. A proper charter includes a skipper who knows the local waters, fuel for the day, safety equipment (life jackets, flares, first aid), and basic insurance. Some include snorkeling gear, fishing rods, or a cooler with ice. Check the listing details because the extras vary.

You do not need a licence for any boat rental on BoatHire24. Every vessel comes with a skipper. That means you can drink, relax, and let someone else navigate the tidal currents around Phi Phi. The skipper also knows the best spots to anchor, the quietest beaches, and where the sea gypsies sell fresh grilled fish.

Typical inclusions for a day charter: soft drinks and water, snorkel masks and fins, towels, and sometimes a basic lunch. Premium charters add champagne, gourmet catering, jet skis, or paddleboards. Read the fine print. If a listing says "fuel excluded," budget an extra EUR 100-300 depending on the boat and distance.

Phuket Departure Ports and Their Vibe

Phuket has three main departure points for boat rentals. Each has a different feel and accessibility.

Chalong Bay is the busiest port for day trips to Coral Island, Racha Island, and Phi Phi. It is functional, with plenty of parking and a few cafes. Most speedboats and RIBs depart from here. If you want a quick exit to the southern islands, Chalong is your spot.

Phuket Marina (Ao Po Grand Marina) is north of the island, near the airport. It is where the big yachts live. If you are chartering a 20-metre motor yacht or a catamaran for a full-day cruise around Phang Nga Bay, you will probably leave from here. The marina has a restaurant, showers, and a small shop for last-minute sunscreen.

Royal Phuket Marina is in the east, close to Phuket Town. It is a luxury marina with high-end yachts and catamarans. If you want a superyacht or a sailing catamaran, this is the departure point. The marina itself is worth a wander, with boutiques and a decent deli for pre-charter supplies.

Less common departure points include Bang Rong Pier (for Koh Yao Noi) and the beach launches at Kata and Karon for small RIBs. Your skipper will tell you the exact meeting point when you book.

Boat Options for Your Phuket Rental

Phuket boat rentals range from small speedboats to superyachts. Here is what you can expect.

Speedboats and RIBs (4-8 passengers) are the most common for day trips. They are fast, nimble, and can reach Phi Phi in under an hour. Expect to pay from around EUR 400 for a full day. They are basic but reliable. Great for groups who want to island-hop and snorkel.

Catamarans (8-20 passengers) offer stability and space. They are the best choice if you get seasick or want to lounge on netting over the water. A day charter on a 40-foot catamaran starts around EUR 800. They are slower than speedboats but more comfortable for long cruises around Phang Nga Bay.

Motor yachts (6-12 passengers) are the luxury option. Think leather seating, a flybridge, and a crew that refills your drink before you finish it. Prices start around EUR 1,500 for a day. These are for anniversaries, proposals, or impressing clients.

Sailing yachts (4-8 passengers) are less common but available. They are slower and more romantic. A day on a 40-foot monohull starts around EUR 600. You can help with the sails or just lie on deck and watch the sun.

Superyachts (10+ passengers, 25+ metres) are price-on-request territory. If you have to ask, you probably cannot afford it. But if you can, they come with full crews, gourmet chefs, and water toys.

Browse all options on our boat rental search page.

Pricing Guidance for Phuket Boat Rentals

Prices vary wildly based on boat size, season, and itinerary. Here are rough ranges so you do not get ripped off.

A half-day speedboat trip (4 hours) to Coral Island: EUR 250-400. Full day to Phi Phi: EUR 500-800. Catamaran day trip to Phang Nga Bay: EUR 800-1,200. Motor yacht day charter: EUR 1,500-3,000. Superyacht: from EUR 5,000 upwards.

These prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. They do not include national park fees (EUR 10-20 per person for Phi Phi or Similan Islands), lunch (sometimes included, sometimes not), or gratuities for the crew (10% is standard).

High season (November to April) commands a premium of 20-30%. Low season (May to October) offers discounts but also rain and rougher seas. Book early for Chinese New Year or Christmas, because prices triple and availability vanishes.

Always confirm the total cost before booking. Some operators try to add fuel surcharges or extra cleaning fees. We vet our listings to avoid these tricks, but ask directly if you are unsure.

Best Seasons for a Phuket Boat Rental

The Andaman Sea has two main seasons. The dry season runs from November to April. This is the best time for a boat rental in Phuket. Calm seas, blue skies, and visibility of 20-30 metres for snorkeling. Water temperature sits around 28-30 degrees C. Perfect for swimming.

The wet season is May to October. The southwest monsoon brings rain, big waves, and occasional storms. Many operators still run trips, but the sea can be rough, especially on the west coast. Phang Nga Bay is more sheltered and remains navigable. Prices drop by up to 40% though, so if you are on a budget and flexible with plans, it is an option.

For dolphin spotting, the best months are December to March. The waters around the Similan Islands and the Hin Daeng/Hin Muang dive sites are clearest in February and March.

If you want to avoid crowds, book a boat rental in Phuket during late April or early May. The weather is still good, the tourists have gone home, and the marine life is active.

How to Book Your Phuket Boat Rental

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Pick your date, number of guests, and preferred boat type. We show you available charters with real-time calendars. No back-and-forth emails with some guy called "Captain Ron" who never replies.

Once you select a boat, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or by card. We hold your deposit in escrow until the trip is completed, so if the boat breaks down or the operator cancels, you get your money back.

You will receive a confirmation with the skipper's contact details, meeting point, and a packing list (sunscreen, hat, camera, swimwear, and a light jacket for the breeze).

Cancel at least 48 hours before departure for a full refund. Within 48 hours, you lose the deposit unless the weather is dangerous, in which case the operator cancels and you get everything back.

For more tips, read our blog on how to choose a boat charter.

Who Should Rent a Boat in Phuket

Boat rental in Phuket is not just for rich tourists. It works for couples wanting a private sunset cruise, families with kids who need space to run around, groups of friends celebrating a birthday or bachelor party, and even solo travellers who join a shared charter.

If you are a photographer, a private boat gets you to the viewpoints of Phi Phi before the crowds. If you are a fisherman, there are charters targeting marlin, sailfish, and tuna. If you just want to float in the Andaman Sea with a beer, that works too.

Do not rent a boat in Phuket if you are on a shoestring budget (stay on land and take a ferry), if you get severely seasick (choose a catamaran or stay in the bay), or if you expect five-star service for a speedboat price (you get what you pay for).

For most people, a day on the water is the highlight of a Phuket trip. The islands, the limestone karsts, the hidden lagoons. It beats lying by a pool.

Local Knowledge: Hidden Gems and Practical Tips

Every skipper has a secret spot. Ask yours to take you to Koh Yao Noi for a quiet lunch on the beach, or Koh Phanak for the hidden lagoon that appears only at low tide. The Similan Islands are a two-hour speedboat ride north, but the snorkeling is world-class. The Phi Phi Leh lagoon (Maya Bay) is iconic but crowded. Go early or late.

Bring cash for national park fees and tips. Most operators accept credit cards for the balance, but smaller boats prefer cash. The local currency is Thai Baht. ATMs are everywhere but charge a fee.

Do not feed the monkeys on Phi Phi. They bite, and they have no fear. Do not leave valuables on the beach while you swim. Do not forget reef-safe sunscreen, because the coral is already stressed.

If you want a sunset cruise, book a catamaran from Royal Phuket Marina. The views over Phang Nga Bay at golden hour are worth the extra cost.

For a full list of available boats, check our Phuket boat rental search.

How to Choose the Right Boat Size for Your Group

A speedboat for 4 people works fine for a quick dash to Coral Island. But if you have 8 guests, you need a catamaran or a motor yacht. The rule is simple: one person per metre of boat length for comfort. A 10-metre speedboat feels cramped with 10 people. A 12-metre catamaran handles 12 guests without anyone elbowing for space.

For families with children under 10, a catamaran is safer. The deck is flat, no steep stairs, and the netting keeps kids from falling overboard. For a bachelor party, a motor yacht with a flybridge gives everyone room to dance. For a romantic couple, a 30-foot sailing yacht is intimate without being claustrophobic.

Check the maximum capacity on the listing. Do not exceed it. Thai maritime police do random checks, and if you are over capacity, the skipper cancels the trip and you lose your deposit.

Phuket Boat Rental for Specific Activities

Different boats suit different activities. If you want to snorkel at Koh Racha Yai, a speedboat gets you there in 30 minutes from Chalong Bay. The water is clear, and the coral is healthy. Bring your own mask if you have one, because the rental ones fog up.

For fishing, book a dedicated fishing boat from Bang Rong Pier. These are slower, with outriggers and a fighting chair. The season for marlin is November to March. For tuna, try the waters off the Similan Islands. Expect to pay from around EUR 600 for a full day with tackle and bait included.

For sunset photography, a catamaran from Royal Phuket Marina gives you a stable platform. The light over Phang Nga Bay at 5:30 PM is orange and pink. Your skipper will anchor near Koh Phing Kan (James Bond Island) for the classic shot.

For a party, book a motor yacht with a sound system. Some have Bluetooth speakers. Others have full DJ setups. Check the listing for "party package." Prices start around EUR 2,000 for a full day with a crew of three.

The Hidden Costs of a Phuket Boat Rental

National park fees are the biggest surprise. Phi Phi Islands cost THB 400 per adult (about EUR 10). Similan Islands cost THB 500 per adult. Coral Island is free. Phang Nga Bay has a THB 300 fee per person. These are cash only, paid at the park entrance or collected by the skipper.

Lunch is not always included. Some charters offer a basic buffet of fried rice, chicken, and fruit. Others expect you to bring your own. Premium charters include a Thai feast with prawns, squid, and green curry. Confirm before you book.

Gratuities are expected. The standard is 10% of the charter price, split between the skipper and the deckhand. If the crew goes out of their way, 15% is generous. Hand it to the skipper in cash .

Fuel surcharges can appear if you change the itinerary mid-trip. If you decide to go to Similan Islands instead of Phi Phi, the extra fuel costs THB 3,000-5,000. Stick to the agreed route.

Phuket Boat Rental for Non-Swimmers and Nervous Guests

You do not need to swim to enjoy a boat rental. Many charters stop at beaches where you can wade in waist-deep water. Koh Yao Noi has shallow sandbanks. Phang Nga Bay has floating villages you can explore on foot.

Life jackets are mandatory on all boats. The skipper will give you one before departure. Wear it even if you are a strong swimmer. The currents around Phuket can be strong, especially near the southern tips of islands.

If you are nervous, book a catamaran. They are stable and rarely tip. Avoid speedboats and RIBs, which bounce on choppy water. Tell the skipper you are anxious. They will avoid rough passages and keep the speed down.

Most boats have a toilet on board. Speedboats have a basic marine head. Catamarans have a proper bathroom with a shower. Motor yachts have luxury facilities. Ask if you need to know.

How Weather Affects Your Phuket Boat Rental

The Andaman Sea can change in an hour. A sunny morning can turn into a monsoon by noon. The skipper monitors the radar and will adjust the route. If the sea is too rough for Phi Phi, they will suggest Phang Nga Bay, which is sheltered by limestone islands.

In the wet season (May to October), the west coast gets big waves. Chalong Bay is calmer, but the rain reduces visibility for snorkeling. Phang Nga Bay is the safest bet. The water is flat, and the rain often passes in 20 minutes.

If the weather is dangerous, the operator cancels and you get a full refund. This is rare. Most days have some sun, even in the wet season. Check the forecast on Windy or the Thai Meteorological Department app before you go.

Do not book a boat rental in Phuket during a typhoon warning. These happen once or twice a year, usually in October. The ports close, and no boats go out.

Phuket Boat Rental for Long-Term Charters

If you want to live on the water for a week, you can charter a catamaran or motor yacht for multiple days. Prices drop per day for longer bookings. A 7-day catamaran charter starts around EUR 4,000, including a skipper and basic provisions.

You can island-hop from Phuket to Koh Lanta, Koh Muk, and Koh Kradan. The itinerary is flexible. Your skipper will plan the route based on weather and your preferences. You sleep on the boat, eat on board or at beach restaurants, and snorkel every morning.

Long-term charters require a larger deposit (50-70%). You also need to budget for food, drinks, and mooring fees (EUR 10-30 per night). National park fees apply for each island you visit.

For a superyacht week, expect to pay from EUR 20,000. This includes a full crew, gourmet meals, and water toys like jet skis and seabobs. Contact us directly for these bookings.

metaDescription: Looking for boat rental Corfu? Compare motor yachts, catamarans and RIBs with a skipper. Prices from around EUR 400. Book online with BoatHire24.
h1: Boat Rental Corfu, Book a Skippered Charter
intro:
You want to rent a boat in Corfu, but you don't have a licence and you don't want to deal with the hassle of navigating unfamiliar waters. Fair enough. The solution is a skippered charter, which is exactly what BoatHire24 offers across the Costa del Sol and beyond. While our home ports are in Marbella, Puerto Banús and Estepona, we can arrange a boat rental Corfu experience through our network of trusted partners. Every booking includes a licensed skipper who knows the coast, so you can focus on swimming, sunbathing and exploring the island's coves.

Corfu has a lot going for it: turquoise water, Venetian architecture and a coastline that begs to be seen from the sea. A day charter from Corfu town, Gouvia or Kassiopi gets you to spots like Paleokastritsa, the Blue Lagoon and the tiny island of Vido. Prices vary by boat size and season, but you can expect to pay from around EUR 400 for a half-day on a motorboat up to several thousand for a full-day luxury catamaran. The skipper handles the navigation, mooring and any local regulations, so all you have to do is show up with your swimsuit and sunglasses.
bodyHtml:
What a Skippered Boat Rental Corfu Includes

When you book a boat rental Corfu through BoatHire24, you are getting a complete package. The skipper is a licensed professional who knows the local waters, weather patterns and best anchorages. They also handle fuel costs, insurance and any port fees that apply during the charter. Most boats come with a cooler, ice, snorkelling gear and a Bluetooth speaker. Some include SUP boards, inflatable slides or fishing rods. You do not need a boating licence, and you do not need to speak Greek, the skippers speak English.

The typical half-day charter lasts 4 hours, a full day is 8 hours. You can customise the route with the skipper on the morning of departure. Want to stop at a secluded beach for lunch? No problem. Fancy a swim in the middle of the channel? The skipper will find a safe spot. The boat is yours for the duration, but the skipper stays in charge of the vessel at all times.

Corfu Ports and Departure Points

Most boat rental Corfu charters depart from Corfu town's old port or the new marina in Gouvia. Gouvia marina is the largest on the island and has plenty of parking, restaurants and a chandlery. If you are staying in the north, Kassiopi and Sidari have smaller harbours that work for speedboats and RIBs. The south of the island has a marina in Lefkimmi, but that is less common for day charters. When you book on BoatHire24, you can filter by departure port to find the most convenient option for your villa or hotel.

For a full-day trip, many skippers head north to the channel between Corfu and Albania, where the water is incredibly clear. Alternatively, you can go south towards the island of Paxos, though that is a longer journey, more of a full-day or overnight trip. The most popular routes include the north-east coast with its olive groves and small pebble beaches, and the west coast near Paleokastritsa, famous for its underwater caves.

Types of Boats Available for Corfu Charters

BoatHire24 lists a range of vessels for boat rental Corfu, from simple motorboats to luxury catamarans and sailing yachts. Motor yachts are the most common: they are fast, stable and have plenty of deck space for sunbathing. A typical 8-metre motorboat with a 150hp engine can carry up to 8 passengers and costs from around EUR 400 for a half-day. Catamarans are wider and more stable, ideal for groups who want to move around without feeling seasick. A 12-metre catamaran with a skipper might cost EUR 1,200 for a full day, including fuel.

RIB boats (rigid inflatable boats) are a good option for smaller groups or those on a tighter budget. They are fast and nimble, perfect for reaching remote beaches quickly. Sailing yachts are available but less common for day charters, they are better for week-long flotillas or overnight trips. If you want something special, there are a few luxury motor yachts over 20 metres that can be chartered with crew, but those are price on request and usually require advance booking.

Pricing and What Affects the Cost

Pricing for boat rental Corfu depends on boat size, engine type, season and duration. High season (July and August) is the most expensive, with rates roughly 30-50% higher than in May or October. A half-day on a basic motorboat starts around EUR 400, while a full-day on a 10-metre catamaran with a skipper can be EUR 1,500. Fuel is usually included in the price, but check the listing details, some operators charge extra for fuel or for long distances. Port fees are typically covered by the skipper, but if you want to stop at a private beach club that charges mooring fees, that is on you.

BoatHire24 does not set the prices, the skippers and boat owners do. We simply list them and take a small commission. You can compare multiple options on the search page and filter by price, boat type and passenger capacity. Always read the terms carefully: some boats have a maximum passenger limit that includes the skipper, so a 10-person boat means 9 guests plus the skipper.

Best Time for a Boat Rental Corfu

The Corfu charter season runs from April to October. May and June are fantastic: the weather is warm (25-30 degrees C), the water is clean, and the beaches are less crowded. July and August are peak season, hot and busy, but the sea is calm and the evenings are long. September is the sweet spot: the water is still warm from summer, the crowds thin out, and the prices drop slightly. October can be hit or miss, some days are perfect, others bring wind and rain. For the best balance of weather and value, aim for late May or early September.

Wind is a factor in the Ionian Sea. The meltemi wind can blow in July and August, but Corfu is partly sheltered by the mainland and the mountains. Most skippers will check the forecast and adjust the route accordingly. If the wind is strong on the west coast, they will stay on the calmer east side. You can trust the skipper to make the right call.

How to Book a Boat Rental Corfu Online

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage, enter your destination (Corfu), dates and passenger count. The system shows available boats with photos, specs and skipper profiles. You can read a brief bio of the skipper, see the boat's amenities and check the cancellation policy. Once you choose a boat, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) online. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day of the charter, either in cash or by card, depending on the operator.

We recommend booking at least a week in advance during high season. Last-minute bookings are sometimes possible, but the best boats go fast. If you have a specific request, a birthday cake, a photographer, a water sports instructor, mention it in the booking notes. The skipper will do their best to arrange it (extra costs may apply).

Who Is a Skippered Boat Rental Corfu For?

This service is for anyone who wants to enjoy the sea without the stress of driving a boat. Couples, families with children, groups of friends, corporate events, all work. The skipper is there to ensure safety and to show you the best spots. If you are a confident sailor with a licence, you might prefer a bareboat charter, but that is a different product. For the majority of tourists, a skippered boat rental Corfu is the easiest and safest way to explore the coast.

Children are welcome on most boats, but check the age restrictions, some skippers require life jackets for kids under 12. If you are planning a party with alcohol, keep it reasonable. The skipper is responsible for the safety of everyone on board, and excessive drinking can cut the trip short. Most skippers are happy to stop at a taverna for lunch where you can have wine or beer, but they will not allow open bottles on the boat if it creates a risk.

Local Highlights You Can See on a Corfu Charter

Corfu's coastline is packed with natural and historical sights. The Blue Lagoon near the north-east tip is a shallow bay with electric blue water, perfect for swimming and snorkelling. Paleokastritsa has several small beaches and a monastery on the hill. The channel between Corfu and the mainland offers views of the Albanian mountains and the abandoned fort at Butrint. On the west coast, the cliffs near Agios Georgios are dramatic, and there are sea caves you can swim into when the water is calm.

Many skippers will also take you to the tiny island of Vido, just 10 minutes from Corfu town. It has a small beach, a café and walking trails. Further south, the islet of Othonoi is a popular lunch stop with a fish taverna. If you are interested in history, ask the skipper to pass by the Old Fortress or the Mon Repos estate, both are visible from the water. For more ideas, check the BoatHire24 blog for route suggestions and local tips.

What to Bring on Your Boat Rental Corfu

Pack light. Swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (biodegradable is best), a hat and sunglasses are essential. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful if you are out in the afternoon when the breeze picks up. Most boats have a small cabin or a shaded area, but it is not guaranteed. Bring your own drinks and snacks, unless the operator provides catering. Some premium charters include a lunch of grilled fish and salad, check the listing details. A waterproof phone case is a good idea for photos without the risk of dropping your phone in the sea.

Do not bring glass bottles on board, they are a hazard if they break, and many skippers prohibit them. Use plastic or metal containers instead. If you plan to fish, bring your own gear or ask if the boat has rods. Some boats have a fishing licence included, but not all. Finally, bring cash for the balance payment, tips for the skipper (10-15% is standard) and any extras like mooring fees at beach clubs.

Frequently Asked Questions About Boat Rental Corfu

How to Choose the Right Boat Size for Your Group

Getting the boat size right matters more than you think. A 6-metre RIB can feel cramped with 6 adults for a full day. For a group of 4 to 6 people, an 8-metre motor yacht gives you enough deck space to move around and a small cabin for changing. For 8 to 10 people, go for a 10-metre catamaran or a 12-metre motor yacht. The general rule is one metre of boat length per person for comfort. If you have children, add a bit more space so they can play without tripping over adults. The search page lets you filter by passenger capacity including the skipper, so you can see exactly how many guests fit.

What to Expect from Different Skipper Styles

Not all skippers run the same kind of trip. Some are relaxed and let you do your own thing, they will anchor and leave you to swim while they stay on the boat. Others are more interactive, pointing out landmarks, telling you about the history of the coast, and suggesting the best spots for photos. A few are very professional and keep conversation to a minimum, focusing purely on navigation and safety. On BoatHire24, each skipper has a short profile that gives you a sense of their style. If you want a social skipper who will join your group for lunch, look for one who mentions local knowledge and hospitality. If you prefer privacy, choose a skipper who emphasises discretion and professionalism.

Hidden Costs to Watch Out For

The listed price on BoatHire24 usually includes the boat, skipper, fuel and basic insurance. But there are extras that can add up. Some operators charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50 to EUR 100 if you leave the boat messy. If you want to dock at a beach club in Kassiopi or a taverna in Paleokastritsa, the mooring fee is typically EUR 10 to EUR 30. Water toys like a wakeboard or a sea scooter cost extra, around EUR 50 to EUR 100 per item per day. If you want the skipper to provide a lunch of grilled fish and local wine, that can be EUR 25 to EUR 40 per person. Always ask for a full breakdown before you confirm the booking. The skipper should tell you about any potential extras when you discuss the route on the morning of the charter.

Best Routes for Half-Day and Full-Day Charters

For a half-day boat rental Corfu, the most efficient route is north from Corfu town to the Blue Lagoon and back. That gives you about 90 minutes of cruising each way and two hours to swim and snorkel. Another good half-day option is the south route to the island of Vido and the nearby beach of Agios Gordios. For a full day, head north to the channel between Corfu and Albania, stop at the Blue Lagoon, then continue to the small port of Kassiopi for lunch. After lunch, cross to the west coast and explore the caves near Paleokastritsa before returning. That route covers about 50 nautical miles and takes 8 hours with stops. If you want something different, ask the skipper to take you south to the islet of Othonoi, which is about 20 nautical miles from Corfu town, a longer journey but with excellent fish tavernas and fewer boats.

How Weather Affects Your Charter in Corfu

The Ionian Sea is generally calm in summer, but weather can still disrupt plans. The meltemi wind, which comes from the north, can pick up in July and August, creating choppy conditions on the west coast. The east coast, sheltered by the mainland, stays calm in most conditions. If the forecast shows strong winds, the skipper will suggest an alternative route on the east side. In May and June, the sea is usually flat, but afternoon thunderstorms can blow in from the mountains. These pass quickly, usually within 30 minutes. In September and October, the risk of longer storms increases, but the weather is still good enough for charters on most days. The skipper will check the forecast the night before and decide if it is safe to go out. If the weather is dangerous, you can reschedule or cancel according to the operator's policy.

Tips for First-Time Charterers in Corfu

If you have never been on a private boat charter before, here are a few things to know. Arrive at the port 15 minutes early so the skipper can do a safety briefing and show you the facilities. Bring seasickness tablets if you are prone to motion sickness, the boat can rock at anchor. Let the skipper know if anyone in your group cannot swim, they will provide life jackets and stay near shallow areas. Do not expect Wi-Fi on board, most boats do not have it. The skipper will have a phone for emergencies. If you want music, bring your own playlist on a phone and a Bluetooth speaker if the boat does not have one. Finally, tip the skipper in cash at the end of the trip, 10-15% of the charter price is standard in Greece.

title: Rent A Speedboat San Diego
metaDescription: Rent a speedboat San Diego with BoatHire24. Compare boats, prices, and ports on the Costa del Sol. Book your high-speed day on the water now.
h1: Rent a Speedboat San Diego, High-Speed Fun on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You want to rent a speedboat in San Diego. Fair enough, San Diego has great weather, a long coastline, and a lively boating scene. But here's the thing: BoatHire24 operates on the Costa del Sol, Spain, not California. So if you're actually looking for a speedboat rental in Marbella, Puerto Banús, or Estepona, you're in the right place. If you typed 'San Diego' by accident, stick around, you might find a better deal on a RIB or speedboat in the Mediterranean, where the water is warmer and the fuel is cheaper.

On the Costa del Sol, renting a speedboat means you get a powerful RIB or a sleek motorboat, typically with a 150-300 HP outboard, capable of 30-50 knots. Every rental includes a licensed skipper, so you don't need a licence. You just sit back, hold on, and enjoy the ride along the coast from Marbella to Estepona, past the Strait of Gibraltar. Prices start from around EUR 350 for a half-day. This page covers everything you need to know: ports, boat types, pricing, seasons, and how to book.
bodyHtml:
What You Get When You Rent a Speedboat on the Costa del Sol

When you book through BoatHire24, every speedboat rental includes a professional skipper. This is not optional, it's Spanish law for commercial charters. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and docking. You get the thrill of high-speed cruising without the paperwork. Most speedboats are RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) or centre-console motorboats, 6-10 metres long, with seating for 6-12 passengers. You'll find Yamaha, Zodiac, and Brig models, often with bimini tops for shade, Bluetooth speakers, and a cooler for drinks. The skipper will show you the best spots: the cliffs at Cala del Faro, the exclusive beaches near Puerto Banús, and the dolphin-watching zones off Estepona. You can also request a fishing rod or snorkelling gear for a stop.

Departure Ports for Your Speedboat Rental

You can rent a speedboat from five main ports on the Costa del Sol. Each has its own character and advantages.

Puerto Banús is the most famous. It's a glamorous marina with superyachts, designer shops, and beach clubs. Departing from here puts you right in the centre of Marbella's action. You can zip over to the Marbella coastline or head south to the Cabopino dunes. Search for speedboats in Puerto Banús to see available options.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and more local. It's next to the old town, so you can combine a speedboat ride with tapas and a walk through the orange-tree-lined streets. The marina has good parking and easy access to the main beaches.

Cabopino is a small, charming port near the Artola dunes. It's less crowded, ideal for a relaxed start. The nearby Cabopino beach is a naturist-friendly spot, and the speedboat can take you to the coves east of Marbella.

Estepona offers a longer run south towards Gibraltar. The port is modern, with plenty of restaurants. From here, you can explore the coast to the Punta de la Doncella or head out to the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin sightings. The old town of Estepona is worth a visit after your trip.

Benalmádena is north of Marbella, close to Torremolinos and Fuengirola. The marina is large and tourist-friendly. Speedboat rentals here often include trips past the Benalmádena cable car or out to the open sea for a faster ride.

Types of Speedboats Available for Rent

Not all speedboats are the same. Here's what you can expect on the Costa del Sol.

RIBs (Rigid Inflatable Boats) are the most common. They have a fibreglass hull and inflatable tubes, making them stable and fast. Typical models are the Zodiac Pro 650 or Brig 750, with 200-300 HP engines. They seat 8-10 people and hit 35-45 knots. Perfect for a thrill ride or a quick hop between beaches.

Centre-console motorboats are more traditional. They have a single deck with the helm in the middle, offering 360-degree views. Examples include the Boston Whaler 270 or Grady-White 250. They are slightly slower (25-35 knots) but more comfortable for families, with a small cabin and a toilet.

Licence-free day boats are a special category. These are small motorboats (under 15 HP) that you can drive without a licence. They are not speedboats, top speed is around 6 knots, but they are a cheap option for a lazy day on the water. Prices start from EUR 150 for a half-day. Not what you want if you're after speed, but worth knowing.

For a true speed experience, stick with RIBs. Most operators have boats that can reach 50 knots, but the skipper will adjust the speed to your comfort level. You can ask for a full-throttle run across the bay if you want.

Pricing Guidance for Speedboat Rentals

Prices vary by boat size, engine power, duration, and season. Here are typical ranges. Always check the exact price on the booking page, as deals change.

  • Half-day (4 hours): from around EUR 350 for a 6-metre RIB, up to EUR 700 for a 9-metre boat.
  • Full day (8 hours): from EUR 600 to EUR 1,200.
  • Sunset cruise (2-3 hours): from EUR 250 to EUR 500.
  • Fuel is usually extra, around EUR 50-100 per hour depending on speed. Some operators include a fuel allowance.
  • Skipper fee is included in the charter price. Gratuity (10-15%) is customary if you're happy.

Prices are higher in July and August, when demand peaks. May, June, and September offer better value and still great weather (25-30 degrees C).

You can also rent a superyacht or a large catamaran if you want luxury, but that's a different budget, from EUR 2,000 per day. For pure speed, a RIB is the best value.

Best Seasons for Speedboat Rentals

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate, with over 300 sunny days a year. You can rent a speedboat from March to November, but the best time is May to October.

May and June are ideal. The water temperature is around 20-22 degrees C, the air is 25-28 degrees C, and the sea is calm. Tourist crowds are smaller, and prices are lower than peak summer.

July and August are the busiest. Expect full marinas, higher prices, and strong afternoon winds (the Poniente or Levante). The water is warm (24-26 degrees C), but the sea can get choppy in the afternoon. Book early morning for smoother conditions.

September and October are still warm, with water temperatures around 22 degrees C. The winds are lighter, and the sun is less intense. This is a good time for a sunset cruise.

November to February are cooler (15-20 degrees C) and windier. Some operators run speedboats on calm days, but it's not the peak season. You'll find lower prices, but you might need a wetsuit.

How to Book Your Speedboat Rental

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You can browse speedboat rentals on the search page, filter by port, boat type, and price, and see real-time availability. Each listing includes photos, specifications, and the skipper's profile. You pay a deposit online (usually 30-50%), and the balance on the day of the charter. Cancellation policies vary, but most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 48 hours in advance.

On the day, you meet the skipper at the marina. They will brief you on safety, the route, and the boat's features. You can bring food and drink (no glass on most boats). The skipper will take photos of your group if you ask. At the end, you return to the same port unless you arrange a different drop-off.

Who Should Rent a Speedboat on the Costa del Sol

Speedboat rentals are not for everyone. They are best for groups of friends, couples, or small families who want a high-energy day on the water. If you want a quiet, relaxed cruise, a catamaran or sailing yacht is a better choice. Speedboats are loud, bumpy at high speed, and limited in shade, you will get wet and sunburned if you're not careful. But if you want to feel the wind in your hair, jump off the boat into clear water, and cover a lot of coastline in a few hours, a speedboat is perfect.

You can also use a speedboat for watersports: towing a ringo or a wakeboard. Some operators have equipment available. Ask when booking.

Local Highlights You'll See on a Speedboat Trip

The Costa del Sol coastline is varied. From the speedboat, you'll see the whitewashed houses of Marbella's old town, the golden sands of Cabopino, and the pine-clad hills behind Estepona. The landmark is La Concha mountain, which looms over Marbella. If you head south from Estepona, you enter the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can spot dolphins, pilot whales, and even orcas in summer. The water is deeper and the current is strong, so the skipper will be careful.

Further east, the coast becomes more rugged, with cliffs and hidden coves like Cala del Faro. You can also take a longer trip to the Nerja caves, but that's a 90-minute run from Marbella, best done as a full-day charter.

For more tips on what to see, read our blog on Costa del Sol boating itineraries.

Frequently Asked Questions

What to Bring on Your Speedboat Charter

Packing smart makes the difference between a good day and a great one. Bring sunscreen (SPF 50, waterproof), a hat, and polarised sunglasses. The reflection off the water is brutal, even on cloudy days. A towel and a change of clothes are essential because you will get wet. Most RIBs have a small storage compartment, but space is tight, so pack light. A soft cooler with drinks and snacks is fine, most skippers provide ice. Avoid glass bottles, they are banned on nearly all charter boats. If you're prone to seasickness, take a pill an hour before departure, the Mediterranean can get choppy in the afternoon. A waterproof phone case or a GoPro is useful for photos, the skipper will point out the best photo spots.

Speedboat vs Other Boat Types: Which Is Right for You

Speedboats are not the only option on the Costa del Sol, and they are not the best choice for everyone. If your priority is speed, adrenaline, and covering distance, a RIB or centre-console is your boat. But if you want a stable platform for swimming, sunbathing, and eating, a catamaran is better. Catamarans are wider, have more deck space, and don't heel. They are slower, around 8-12 knots, but you can anchor in a cove and relax for hours. Sailing yachts offer a quieter, more traditional experience, with the option to help the skipper if you know the ropes. For a party, a motor yacht with a flybridge and a sound system is the way to go. Speedboats are the cheapest powered option, but they are also the least comfortable for long periods. If you're unsure, browse all boat types on the search page and compare.

Speedboat Rentals for Watersports Enthusiasts

Speedboats are the ideal platform for watersports. Many operators on the Costa del Sol offer towable toys, rings (also called donuts or bananas), wakeboards, and waterskis. The boat’s power and speed are perfect for pulling a rider. You'll need at least a half-day charter to get proper use, as setup and safety briefings take time. The best areas for watersports are the open water off Benalmádena and the calm bays near Cabopino. The skipper will handle the driving while you focus on staying upright. Some boats have a dedicated tow pylon, which makes the pull smoother. Ask at the time of booking if watersports equipment is included or available for an extra fee, typically EUR 50-100 per session. Not all speedboat rentals allow towing, so confirm before you pay.

Speedboat Rentals for Fishing Trips

You can also use a speedboat for a fishing charter, but with a few caveats. Speedboats are not purpose-built fishing boats, they lack rod holders, live wells, and fish-finding electronics. However, a RIB with a centre console can work for light tackle fishing. The skipper will take you to known spots near Estepona or the Cabopino reef, where you can catch sea bass, bream, or mackerel. Trolling at low speed is possible, but you won't get the same experience as a dedicated fishing boat. If fishing is your main goal, consider a purpose-built fishing boat from our fleet, which includes outriggers, bait tanks, and a skipper who knows the local grounds. Speedboat fishing is best as a casual add-on, a way to pass an hour while anchored in a cove. Bring your own rod if you have one, or ask the skipper if they have gear to lend.

Speedboat Rentals for Special Occasions

A speedboat charter works well for birthdays, bachelor or bachelorette parties, and small celebrations. The thrill of the ride and the photo opportunities make it memorable. For a birthday, you can bring a cake (no candles, fire risk on a boat) and the skipper will help you find a quiet cove for a swim and a toast. For a stag or hen do, a speedboat is a good warm-up before a night out in Puerto Banús. Keep the group to 8-10 people maximum, larger parties are better on a catamaran or motor yacht. Some operators allow you to decorate the boat with banners or balloons, but check first. Champagne and beer are fine, but no glass. The skipper will play your playlist through the Bluetooth speakers. For a proposal, a sunset speedboat cruise is hard to beat, the skipper can help arrange flowers or a photographer on the beach.

Speedboat Rentals from Puerto Banús: What to Expect

Puerto Banús is the most popular departure point for speedboat rentals on the Costa del Sol. The marina is a spectacle in itself, with superyachts, Ferraris, and designer boutiques. Your skipper will meet you at a designated spot near the main entrance. The port can be chaotic in summer, so arrive 15 minutes early to find parking (expensive, around EUR 3-5 per hour) or take a taxi. Once you're out of the harbour, you'll pass the golden beach of Puerto Banús and head towards the Marbella coastline. The water is clear and blue, and you'll see the La Concha mountain behind you. The skipper will likely head east towards the Cabopino dunes or west towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro. The run from Puerto Banús to Cabopino takes about 15 minutes at full speed. You can also stop at the exclusive beach clubs like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club, but you'll need to anchor and swim in, there is no dock. Puerto Banús speedboat rentals are popular, so book at least a week in advance for July and August.

Speedboat Rentals from Estepona: A Different Vibe

Estepona offers a more relaxed start compared to Puerto Banús. The marina is modern but less flashy, with good restaurants and a promenade. Speedboat rentals from Estepona are ideal if you want to explore the coast towards Gibraltar. The run south takes you past the Punta de la Doncella lighthouse and the beaches of El Cristo and Bahía Dorada. The water gets deeper and darker as you approach the Strait of Gibraltar. This is where you have the best chance of seeing dolphins, common and striped, often in pods of 50 or more. The skipper will slow down and approach respectfully. The current in the Strait is strong, so the skipper will keep a safe distance. You can also head north towards Marbella, but that's a 30-minute run each way. Estepona is a good choice if you want a quieter day with a focus on wildlife and scenery. Prices are slightly lower than Puerto Banús, with half-day RIB rentals from around EUR 300.

Speedboat Rentals for Licence-Free Boats: A Budget Alternative

If you don't have a boating licence and want to drive yourself, licence-free day boats are an option. These are small motorboats with engines under 15 HP, limited to 6 knots. They are not speedboats by any definition, but they let you explore the coastline at your own pace. You can rent them from Cabopino, Marbella, or Benalmádena. The rental includes a brief safety instruction and a map of the area. You can take the boat to a nearby cove, anchor, and swim. It's a cheap and cheerful option for a family day out. Prices start from around EUR 150 for a half-day. The downside is the limited range, you won't get far from the port. And you are at the mercy of the wind and current, so check the weather forecast. If you want speed, stick with a skippered RIB. But if you want independence and a low budget, a licence-free boat is worth considering.

bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Boat Rental Dubai Booking

Every boat rental Dubai booking through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the coastguard regulations, and the best spots for swimming or sightseeing. The skipper handles all navigation, docking, and safety briefings, so you don't need a boating licence or any previous experience. Fuel is included in the price for the agreed duration, and the boat comes with basic safety equipment such as life jackets, fire extinguishers, and a first-aid kit. Some operators also provide snorkelling gear, fishing rods, or a cooler with ice, but you should check the listing details before booking. What is not included: food and drinks (unless specified), gratuities for the crew, and any extra hours beyond the booked time. If you want to extend your trip, you can request it through the onboard skipper, and the cost will be calculated at the hourly rate shown on the listing.

Departure Ports for Boat Rental Dubai

Dubai has several marinas and harbours where you can start your boat rental Dubai trip. The most popular departure point is Dubai Marina, a man-made canal city with dozens of restaurants, shops, and residential towers. From here, you can cruise past the Ain Dubai observation wheel and head towards Palm Jumeirah or the Atlantis hotel. Palm Jumeirah itself has its own marina, the Palm Jumeirah Marina, which offers direct access to the crescent and the open sea. Jumeirah Beach Residence (JBR) has a smaller dock used by RIBs and speedboats for short tours along the coast. Port Rashid is the main cruise ship terminal and also a base for larger superyachts and fishing charters. Dubai Creek, the historic heart of the city, is where you will find traditional wooden abras and dhow cruises, but it can also be used for smaller motorboats. Each port has parking, taxi access, and nearby hotels, so you can choose the one that is most convenient for your schedule.

Types of Boats Available for Rental in Dubai

The boat rental Dubai fleet on BoatHire24 covers a wide range of vessels, from compact speedboats to full-sized superyachts. Motor yachts are the most common choice: they range from 30 to 80 feet, can carry 10 to 30 passengers, and offer a mix of indoor saloons, outdoor sun decks, and a flybridge. Catamarans are popular for their stability and space, especially for larger groups or parties. Sailing yachts are available but less common in Dubai because the wind conditions can be inconsistent. RIBs and speedboats are the go-to for adrenaline seekers: they are fast, nimble, and perfect for a two-hour tour of the coastline, the Palm, or the World Islands. Fishing boats are equipped with rods, bait, and a fishfinder, and the skipper will take you to known hotspots like the Dubai Fishing Harbour or the deep waters off the coast. Licence-free day boats are a new category: these are small, easy-to-drive vessels that you can operate yourself without a licence, though a safety briefing is always provided. Superyachts, 80 feet and above, are available for luxury charters with a full crew including a captain, stewardess, and chef.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Dubai

Prices for boat rental Dubai vary depending on the boat size, duration, season, and included extras. As a rough guide, a two-hour RIB tour costs from around EUR 250 for up to 6 passengers. A half-day (4-hour) motor yacht charter for 10 to 12 people starts at approximately EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. Full-day (8-hour) charters on a 50-foot motor yacht can range from EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. Superyachts, 80 feet and above, are priced on request and typically start from EUR 8,000 to EUR 15,000 per day. Catamarans tend to be slightly more expensive than equivalent-sized motor yachts because of their stability and deck space. Fishing charters are usually priced per boat, not per person, and start from around EUR 400 for a four-hour trip. All prices include the skipper and fuel, but you should confirm whether VAT is included or added at checkout. During peak season (November to April), prices can increase by 20 to 30 percent, and availability is lower, so early booking is recommended.

Best Time of Year for Boat Rental Dubai

The climate in Dubai means you can enjoy boat rental Dubai almost year-round, but the most comfortable months are from November to April. During this period, daytime temperatures range from 25 to 30 degrees Celsius, the humidity is lower, and the sea is calm. This is also the peak tourist season, so marinas are busier and prices are higher. From May to October, temperatures often exceed 40 degrees Celsius, and the humidity can be oppressive. However, many boats have air-conditioned cabins and shaded decks, and the water temperature is warm enough for swimming. Early morning or late afternoon charters are best in summer to avoid the midday heat. The sea conditions are generally good throughout the year, though occasional wind events can cause choppy water, especially in January and February. If you are planning a fishing trip, the best catches are usually from October to March when the water is cooler and fish are more active.

Popular Activities on a Boat Rental Dubai Trip

Once you have booked your boat rental Dubai, you can decide how to spend your time on the water. Many people choose a sightseeing cruise that passes the Burj Al Arab, the Atlantis hotel, Palm Jumeirah, and the Dubai skyline from the sea. Swimming and snorkelling are common at spots like the Palm Jumeirah crescent or near the World Islands, where the water is clearer. Fishing charters focus on species such as kingfish, barracuda, and grouper, and the skipper will clean and pack your catch at the end of the trip. For a more relaxed experience, you can anchor off a quiet beach, have lunch on board, and enjoy the sun deck. Some operators offer add-ons like jet skis, paddleboards, or inflatable water toys. Evening charters are popular for sunset views and dinner cruises, especially along the Dubai Marina coastline. Corporate events and parties are also common, with boats equipped with sound systems, LED lighting, and catering options.

How to Book a Boat Rental Dubai on BoatHire24

Booking a boat rental Dubai through BoatHire24 is a straightforward process. Start by visiting the BoatHire24 homepage and entering your preferred date, duration, and number of guests. Use the search filters to narrow down by boat type, price range, and departure port. Browse the listings, read the descriptions, and check the photos and included amenities. When you find a boat you like, click the booking button and follow the prompts to complete the payment. You can pay by credit card, debit card, or bank transfer, depending on the operator. After booking, you will receive a confirmation email with the skipper’s contact details, the exact meeting point at the marina, and any last-minute instructions. If you need to cancel or modify your booking, check the cancellation policy on the listing page, as terms vary by operator. For any questions, you can contact the BoatHire24 support team via the website chat or by email. We recommend booking at least 48 hours in advance, especially during peak season, to secure your preferred boat and time slot.

Who Is Boat Rental Dubai For

Boat rental Dubai suits a wide range of visitors and residents. Families with children can choose a stable catamaran or a motor yacht with a shaded deck and a skipper who can adjust the route to include calm swimming spots. Groups of friends celebrating a birthday, bachelor party, or anniversary often book a half-day or full-day charter with catering and a sound system. Corporate groups use boat rentals for team-building events, client entertainment, or product launches, and superyachts provide a high-end venue for such occasions. Solo travellers or couples can join a shared tour on a RIB or a small motorboat, which is more affordable and social. Fishing enthusiasts will find dedicated charters with experienced skippers who know the local waters. Even if you have never been on a boat before, the included skipper ensures a safe and enjoyable experience. If you are unsure which boat type is best for your group, you can use the search page to compare options side by side or read our blog for destination guides and tips.

Local Regulations and Safety for Boat Rental Dubai

Dubai has strict maritime regulations to ensure safety on the water. All commercial boats must be registered with the Dubai Maritime Authority and undergo regular inspections. Skippers are required to hold a valid licence issued by the UAE, and they are responsible for enforcing safety rules on board. Life jackets must be available for all passengers, and children under 12 must wear them at all times while on deck. Alcohol consumption is allowed on board only if the operator has a valid liquor licence, and the skipper reserves the right to refuse service to anyone who appears intoxicated. Open flames, such as barbecues, are prohibited on most boats unless specifically permitted by the operator. Swimming is allowed only in designated areas away from boat traffic and with the skipper’s approval. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication before boarding, as the waters off Dubai can be choppy, especially in winter. For more information on safety and regulations, you can check the Dubai Maritime Authority website or consult your skipper on the day.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Boat Rental Dubai

BoatHire24 is a marketplace that aggregates boat rental Dubai listings from multiple operators, giving you transparent pricing, real-time availability, and verified photos. Unlike booking directly with a charter company, you can compare different boats side by side without having to call or email each one. Every listing includes a detailed description, a list of included and excluded items, and the cancellation policy. We do not display fake reviews or testimonials; instead, we provide clear information so you can make your own decision. The booking process is secure and your payment is processed through a trusted third-party gateway. If any issue arises with your booking, our support team acts as a mediator between you and the operator. We also update our inventory regularly, so you can find new boats and special offers as they become available. Whether you are a first-time renter or a seasoned charterer, BoatHire24 simplifies the process of finding and booking the right boat for your needs.

Frequently Asked Questions About Boat Rental Dubai

Choosing the Right Departure Port for Your Trip

Your choice of departure port can change the entire feel of your boat rental Dubai experience. If you want a quick blast past the skyscrapers and the Burj Al Arab, start from Dubai Marina or JBR. From there, you can reach the Palm Jumeirah in 15 minutes and the Burj Al Arab in 20. If you are heading to the World Islands or the deeper fishing grounds, Port Rashid cuts your travel time by 10 to 15 minutes compared to the Marina. For a traditional vibe, Dubai Creek puts you near the Gold Souk and the Spice Souk, but the water is shallower and the boat options are limited to smaller vessels. If you are staying in a hotel on the Palm, the Palm Jumeirah Marina is the most convenient. Each port has its own parking rates, which range from free to around EUR 15 for a full day, and taxi fares from central Dubai to the Marina are about EUR 10 to EUR 15.

How Group Size Affects Your Boat Selection

The number of people in your group directly determines which boat you should book for your boat rental Dubai trip. A RIB or speedboat typically holds 6 to 8 passengers, and anything beyond that means you are cramped and uncomfortable. For groups of 10 to 15, a 40-foot motor yacht or a catamaran is the minimum. Groups of 15 to 25 need a 50 to 60-foot vessel, and anything above 25 people requires a superyacht or a large catamaran. Keep in mind that the passenger capacity listed on BoatHire24 includes everyone on board, including children and infants. If you have a mix of adults and kids, a catamaran gives you more deck space and a lower risk of seasickness. If your group includes elderly guests or people with mobility issues, a motor yacht with a main-deck saloon and a wide stern platform is easier to board than a sailing yacht with narrow steps.

What to Expect from the Skipper and Crew

The skipper included with your boat rental Dubai booking is not just a driver. They are a licensed professional who knows the local waters, the tide patterns, and the best anchorages for swimming or lunch stops. Most skippers speak English, and many speak Arabic, Hindi, or Russian as well. They will give a short safety briefing at the start of the trip and show you where the life jackets and toilets are. You can ask them to adjust the route if you want to see a specific landmark or avoid a crowded area. Some skippers also act as informal guides, pointing out the history of the Palm or the architecture of the Burj Al Arab. If you book a superyacht, you get a full crew: a captain, a stewardess who serves food and drinks, and sometimes a chef. Tips are not mandatory, but if you are happy with the service, 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee is standard.

Hidden Costs and Extra Charges to Watch For

While the base price of your boat rental Dubai includes the skipper and fuel, there are a few extra costs you should plan for. Food and drinks are almost never included, so you need to bring your own or order catering through the operator at an additional cost, typically EUR 20 to EUR 50 per person. Some marinas charge a docking fee that the operator passes on to you, usually EUR 30 to EUR 100 depending on the port and the boat size. If you want to use water toys like jet skis or paddleboards, expect to pay EUR 50 to EUR 150 per item per hour. Gratuities for the crew are not included, and most guests leave EUR 50 to EUR 200 at the end of a half-day charter. If you exceed the booked time, the skipper will charge you at the hourly rate listed on the listing, which is usually 20 to 30 percent higher than the hourly equivalent of the full booking. Always confirm the total price, including any VAT, before you pay.

Departure Ports for Athens Boat Charters

The main departure points for a boat rental Athens are clustered along the southern coast. The most popular is Alimos Marina, about 20 minutes from the city centre by taxi. It has 24-hour security, parking, and a few decent cafes for a pre-sail coffee. Kalamaki Marina is next door, smaller but quieter. Both are within a short drive from the airport.

Further south, Vouliagmeni Marina is the most upmarket option. It is surrounded by pine trees and expensive villas, and the water is noticeably clearer than in the city ports. If you are staying at the Four Seasons or the Astir Palace, this is your best bet. There is also Flisvos Marina in Paleo Faliro, which is closer to the centre but can be busy on weekends.

For a longer trip, you can depart from Piraeus, the main port. That makes sense if you want to head straight for the Cyclades or the Argolic Gulf. But for a day trip, the southern marinas are much more convenient. Check our boat search to filter by departure port and see what is available.

Types of Boats Available in Athens

Catamarans are the most popular choice for groups. They are stable, spacious, and have a shallow draft, meaning you can anchor close to beaches. A 40-foot Lagoon or Fountaine Pajot sleeps six to eight people and costs from around EUR 800 for a full day. The skipper usually stays in a separate cabin or sleeps on deck.

Motor yachts are faster and more luxurious. A 50-foot Sunseeker or Azimut can hit 25 knots, so you can cover more ground. Expect to pay from EUR 1,200 for a day charter, depending on the model and season. These boats have a flybridge, a sun pad at the bow, and a cabin for the skipper if you want to stay overnight.

Sailing yachts are cheaper and more authentic. A 40-foot Bavaria or Jeanneau costs from EUR 500 for a day with a skipper. The pace is slower, but you get the full sailing experience. RIBs and speedboats are available for small groups who want to go fast. A 6-metre RIB with a 200hp engine starts at around EUR 350 for a half-day. Fishing boats are also an option, with basic tackle included.

For something completely different, try a licence-free day boat. These are small motorboats that you can drive yourself without any paperwork. They are limited to 30hp and a 2-nautical-mile radius, but they cost only EUR 200 for a half-day. Perfect for a couple or a small family who just want to putter around a quiet bay.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Athens

Prices for a boat rental Athens vary by boat type, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a small RIB starts from around EUR 250. A full day (8 hours) on a 40-foot catamaran in high season is roughly EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. A luxury motor yacht can easily hit EUR 2,500 or more. Superyachts are price on request, but you can expect EUR 5,000 and up.

The low season (April, May, October) is cheaper by about 20-30%. June and September are shoulder months. July and August are peak, especially around the Assumption holiday on 15 August. Book at least two weeks ahead in summer. You can also negotiate a discount for multiple days or last-minute bookings in shoulder season.

Fuel is included in the price for standard itineraries. If you ask the skipper to go further, like to Hydra or Spetses, you may pay a fuel surcharge. Port fees for overnight stops are extra, usually EUR 20-50 per night depending on the marina. The skipper's tip is separate, as mentioned.

For a precise quote, use our BoatHire24 homepage to compare boats side by side. We show you the total price including all fees, so there are no surprises.

Best Time for a Boat Rental Athens

The sailing season in Athens runs from April to October. The best months are May, June, and September. The water temperature is 22-25 degrees C, the air temperature is a comfortable 28-32 degrees C, and the meltemi wind is moderate. July and August are hotter (35 degrees C plus) and busier, but the sea is calm in the mornings and the evenings are long.

April and October are cooler, around 20 degrees C air temperature. The water is still swimmable for most people. You will have the anchorages mostly to yourself, and prices are lower. Just bring a windbreaker for the afternoon breeze.

Winter charters are possible but rare. Most boats are hauled out for maintenance from November to March. If you really want to go out in December, you can find a few hardy operators, but the weather is unpredictable.

How to Book a Boat Rental Athens

Booking with BoatHire24 is done entirely online. Go to the search page, select your dates, group size, and preferred boat type. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on one to see the full description, cancellation policy, and skipper details. Then you can request a booking.

We will confirm within 24 hours. You pay a deposit of 30% to secure the booking, and the balance is due 7 days before departure. Payment is by credit card or bank transfer. If you need to cancel, you get a full refund up to 14 days before the charter. After that, it is 50% refundable.

On the day, you meet the skipper at the marina. They will give you a safety briefing and explain the boat. Then you cast off. Most charters start at 10:00 and return by 18:00, but you can customise the schedule. The skipper will suggest an itinerary based on the weather and your preferences.

Who Is a Boat Rental Athens For

A boat rental Athens is for anyone who wants to see the city from the sea without the hassle of owning a boat. It works for couples, families with children, groups of friends, and corporate events. The skipper handles the navigation, so you can relax. You do not need any boating experience, and the minimum age is usually 18 to book, though children are welcome on board.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter on some boats. That is cheaper, but you will be with strangers. Check the listing details for shared options. If you have a special request, like a wedding proposal or a birthday party, let us know in the booking notes. The skipper can arrange decorations, catering, or a photographer at an extra cost.

For more tips on what to expect, read our blog about day trips from Athens and the best swimming spots in the Saronic Gulf.

Saronic Gulf Itineraries from Athens

The Saronic Gulf is the default playground for any boat rental Athens. Within 30 minutes of departure, you can be swimming in water that looks nothing like the city beaches. The standard day trip heads east towards the island of Aegina. The skipper will anchor at Perdika, a fishing village on the south coast, where you can swim off the boat and eat grilled octopus at a taverna on the sand. The return leg usually passes the Temple of Aphaia, visible from the water.

If you have a faster boat, you can push further to Hydra. That is about 2.5 hours from Alimos at 20 knots. Hydra has no cars, just donkeys and stone streets. You dock at the harbour, have lunch, and swim at a cove called Vlychos on the way back. The fuel surcharge for Hydra is typically EUR 50-80 extra, depending on the boat. For a shorter trip, the island of Agistri is only 45 minutes from Piraeus. The water at Skala beach is absurdly clear, and the pine forest comes right down to the shore.

Another popular route is the Athenian Riviera heading south. You cruise past Vouliagmeni, the Cape Sounion road, and stop at the Temple of Poseidon. That is a 6-hour round trip from Alimos, including a swim stop at a beach called Legrena. The temple looks best in the late afternoon light, so aim for a 14:00 departure if you want sunset photos.

Vouliagmeni Marina Specifics

Vouliagmeni Marina is worth a separate mention because it is the most scenic departure point for a boat rental Athens. It sits inside a natural bay, protected from the meltemi wind. The water inside the marina is clean enough to swim in, which is rare for a working port. The marina has a fuel dock, a chandlery, and a restaurant that does a decent club sandwich. Parking is EUR 10 per day, and taxis are easy to find.

Boats based here tend to be newer and better maintained than those in Alimos. The owners are often private individuals who charter out their weekend toy, so the interior is usually spotless. Expect a higher price point, maybe 10-15% more than Alimos for the same boat. But the convenience is real: you are 5 minutes from the Astir Palace beach, and the first swimming spot is 10 minutes from the marina exit.

From Vouliagmeni, a good half-day itinerary is to head to the islet of Fleves, a rocky outcrop with a small beach and a cave. Then cross to the coast of Anavyssos for a second swim. The total distance is about 6 nautical miles, so even a slow boat can do it in 4 hours. The water depth here drops quickly, so you can anchor in 10 metres and jump off the bow.

Athens Boat Rental for Fishing

Fishing from a boat rental Athens is a specific niche, but it is well served. The Saronic Gulf has decent fishing for bream, sea bass, and the occasional amberjack. Most fishing boats come with basic tackle: rods, reels, and lures. The skipper will know the reefs and drop-offs where the fish hold. A half-day fishing charter starts at around EUR 300 for up to 4 people. You keep what you catch, and the skipper can clean it for you.

The best fishing grounds are off the coast of Salamina island, about 30 minutes from Piraeus. The water is deeper there, up to 50 metres, and the currents bring in baitfish. Another spot is the area around the islet of Patroklos, east of Sounion. That is a longer trip, so you need a full day. If you want to try trolling for larger fish, you need a motor yacht with a bit of speed. A 30-foot RIB with twin 250hp engines can troll at 6 knots and still have enough power to chase a school.

Fishing charters are less popular in July and August because the water is warm and the fish go deep. Spring and autumn are better. Also, note that you need a fishing licence in Greece if you are fishing from a private boat without a skipper. But since you have a skipper, they handle the paperwork. Just ask when you book.

Overnight Charters from Athens

An overnight boat rental Athens is a different experience. You leave in the afternoon, anchor in a quiet bay for the night, and return the next day. Most catamarans and motor yachts have cabins for 4-8 guests. The skipper sleeps in a separate cabin or on deck. Overnight charters cost roughly 1.5 times the daily rate, plus port fees if you dock at a marina.

The best overnight anchorages are on the east coast of Aegina, near the town of Souvala. The water is calm, and there are a few tavernas that will send a boat to pick you up. Another option is the bay of Vathi on the island of Agistri. It is a narrow inlet with a beach at the end, surrounded by trees. No restaurants, so you need to bring your own food. But the stars are incredible because there is no light pollution.

For a two-night trip, you can go to Poros or Spetses. Poros is a small island with a lively waterfront. Spetses is more upmarket, with old mansions and a car-free centre. The distance from Alimos to Spetses is about 40 nautical miles, so a motor yacht can do it in 2 hours. A catamaran takes 3-4 hours. The fuel cost for the round trip is usually EUR 100-150 extra for a motor yacht, less for a catamaran.

Weather and Wind Considerations

The meltemi wind is the main factor in any boat rental Athens. It blows from the north in July and August, often reaching 25-30 knots in the afternoon. That can make the Saronic Gulf choppy, especially in the open channels. Experienced skippers will plan the itinerary to stay in the lee of the coast. For example, if the meltemi is strong, they will keep to the west side of Aegina, where the water is flat.

In spring and autumn, the wind is lighter, usually 10-15 knots from the south. That is perfect for sailing yachts. The sea state is calm in the morning, and the afternoon breeze is just enough to keep you cool. If you are prone to seasickness, take a pill before you leave. The Saronic Gulf is not rough by Mediterranean standards, but a 30-knot meltemi can be uncomfortable on a small boat.

Check the weather forecast on Windy or Poseidon before you go. The skipper will do the same, but it helps to know what to expect. If the forecast is bad, you can reschedule for free up to 48 hours before departure on most boats. BoatHire24 has a flexible cancellation policy for weather-related changes.

What to Bring on an Athens Boat Charter

Packing for a boat rental Athens is simple but specific. Sunscreen is essential, and it should be reef-safe to avoid damaging the marine life. A hat, sunglasses, and a rash guard or light long-sleeve shirt will save you from burning. Towels are usually not provided, so bring your own. A dry bag for your phone and wallet is a good idea, because splashes happen.

Food and drink are not included, so bring whatever you want to eat and drink. Most boats have a fridge and a cooler. The skipper will usually have bottled water on board, but confirm that. If you want to eat at a taverna on shore, bring cash. Many of the smaller island tavernas do not take cards. Also bring a swimsuit, a change of clothes, and a light jacket for the evening breeze.

If you are prone to seasickness, bring medication. The skipper will have some on board, but it is better to have your own. A small first-aid kit is also useful, though the boat will have a basic one. Finally, bring a sense of humour. Things go wrong sometimes: a late start, a sudden wind shift, a broken fridge. The skipper will handle it, but a flexible attitude makes the trip better for everyone.
