bodyHtml:
What a Yacht Charter Athens (on the Costa del Sol) Includes

Every charter with BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. You do not need a boating licence. The skipper knows the coast, the weather, and the best spots for swimming, lunch, or photos. The boat is yours for the day, half-day, or multiple days. Fuel is usually included in the price for local trips, but check with the operator for longer passages. You bring your own food and drink, or arrange catering through the charter company. Most boats have a sound system, a shaded deck, and a bathroom. Some have a kitchen, a grill, or water toys like paddleboards and snorkel gear.

Departure ports are all within a 30-minute drive of Marbella. Puerto Banús is the most famous, with its superyachts and designer shops. Marbella Marina is quieter and closer to the old town. Cabopino is a small, sandy port near the dunes of Artola. Estepona has a charming marina with a promenade. Sotogrande is upmarket and close to Gibraltar. Benalmádena is a busy port with plenty of restaurants. You choose the port, and we arrange the boat there.

Typical itineraries include a cruise along the coast, a stop for swimming at a secluded cove like Cala del Faro, lunch at a beach club or on board, and a return before sunset. For longer charters, you can go to Gibraltar, Tarifa, or even cross to Morocco. The Strait of Gibraltar is famous for dolphins and whales. You can also visit the Nerja caves from the sea, though you need to dock and walk up.

Why You Might Be Searching for Yacht Charter Athens

Athens is a historic city with a long coastline. It is a popular destination for yacht charters, especially in the Saronic Gulf and the Cyclades. But Athens is far from Marbella. If you are based in Europe, the Costa del Sol is easier to reach. Flights to Málaga are frequent and cheap from most UK and European airports. The weather is similar: 300 days of sunshine a year, sea temperatures of 20-26 degrees C in summer, and calm winds in the morning. The water is clear and clean. The food is Spanish, not Greek, but equally good: fresh seafood, paella, jamón, and local wine.

If you are planning a trip to Greece, we cannot help you. But if you want the same experience on the Spanish coast, we can. You get a private boat with a skipper, a flexible itinerary, and a day on the water without the crowds of Santorini or Mykonos. The Costa del Sol is less hyped, but just as beautiful. And it is cheaper. A half-day charter on a 40-foot motor yacht costs from around EUR 800, while a similar boat in Greece might be EUR 1,200 or more. You save money and travel time.

Boat Types Available for Your Charter

We offer five main types of boats for charter. Motor yachts are the most popular. They are fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space. Sizes range from 30 feet to over 100 feet. A 40-foot motor yacht sleeps 4-6 people and cruises at 20 knots. Catamarans are wider and more stable. They have a large trampoline at the front and a flybridge. They are great for families or groups who want space. A 40-foot catamaran can carry 12 guests comfortably. Sailing yachts are for those who want the experience of sailing. They are slower but quieter. A 45-foot sailing yacht takes 8-10 guests. RIBs and speedboats are smaller, faster, and cheaper. They are good for a day trip to a beach club or for water sports. A 26-foot RIB costs from around EUR 350 for a half-day. Fishing boats are equipped for deep-sea fishing. You can catch tuna, dorado, or swordfish. Licence-free day boats are available for up to 8 people with no skipper required, but you need a basic licence for some of them. Superyachts are for the ultimate luxury. Prices are on request.

All boats are maintained to high standards. We check them before every charter. The skippers are experienced and speak English. You do not need to worry about navigation, anchoring, or safety. Just relax and enjoy.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Charter Athens (Costa del Sol)

Prices vary by boat size, type, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 30-foot motor yacht starts from around EUR 600. A full day (8 hours) on the same boat is EUR 900-1,200. A 50-foot motor yacht for a full day is EUR 1,500-2,500. Catamarans are similar. A 40-foot catamaran for a full day is EUR 1,200-1,800. Sailing yachts are slightly cheaper. A 45-foot sailing yacht for a full day is EUR 1,000-1,500. RIBs and speedboats are the most affordable. A 26-foot RIB for a half-day is EUR 350-500. Fishing boats cost EUR 600-1,000 for a full day, including gear and bait. Superyachts are price on request. Expect EUR 5,000-15,000 per day for a 80-foot yacht, and more for larger vessels.

Peak season is June to September. Prices are 20-30% higher. Off-peak (April, May, October) is cheaper and less crowded. November to March is low season. Some boats are available, but weather is less predictable. You can book for a sunset cruise in winter for around EUR 400 on a small boat. Always ask about extras: fuel for longer trips, port fees, food, drinks, and water toys. We list everything upfront on the search page.

Best Seasons for a Yacht Charter on the Costa del Sol

The best time for a yacht charter is May to October. The sea is warm, the sun is strong, and the wind is light. July and August are the hottest, with temperatures of 30-35 degrees C. The water is 24-26 degrees C. This is peak season, so book early. September and June are also excellent. The crowds are smaller, and the weather is still hot. April and October are shoulder months. You might get some rain, but most days are sunny. The water is cooler, around 18-20 degrees C, but still swimmable. Winter charters are possible on calm days. The sun sets early, and the sea is rougher. But if you want a winter escape, you can still find a boat.

Wind is important. The Levante wind comes from the east and can be strong in summer. It creates choppy seas on the eastern side of the coast. The Poniente wind from the west is lighter and brings clear skies. Our skippers know the conditions and adjust the itinerary. They avoid exposed areas in high wind and find sheltered coves. You will not be stuck on a boat in bad weather. We monitor forecasts and cancel or reschedule if needed.

How to Book a Yacht Charter with BoatHire24

Booking is simple. Go to our search page, enter your dates, number of guests, and preferred port. We show you available boats with prices and photos. You can filter by boat type, size, and price. Once you find a boat, click to see details. You can message the operator directly through our platform. We do not charge booking fees. You pay a deposit to secure the date, and the rest on the day. We hold the deposit in escrow until after the charter. If the operator cancels, you get a full refund. If you cancel, you get a partial refund depending on the notice period. Read the terms on each listing.

You can also call or email us. We help you choose the right boat and itinerary. We have recommendations for lunch spots, swimming areas, and activities. We can arrange catering, transport to the port, or additional services like a photographer or a DJ. Just ask. We have been doing this for years, and we know the coast.

For a superyacht, contact us directly. We have a network of owners and brokers. We can find a boat that is not listed on the site. Prices are on request, but we give you a range upfront. No hard sell.

Who Is a Yacht Charter For

A yacht charter is for anyone who wants a private day on the water. It is not a party boat with strangers. You and your group have the whole boat. It is for couples, families, friends, or business groups. You can celebrate a birthday, anniversary, or corporate event. You can propose. You can just relax. No experience needed. The skipper handles everything. You can help sail if you want, but you do not have to. Children are welcome. Most boats have safety equipment for kids. Some have nets on the sides. Ask when booking. Pets are allowed on some boats. Check the listing.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter. We sometimes have group trips on catamarans. Check the search page for shared options. Otherwise, you need to book the whole boat. It is worth it for the privacy.

If you are a boat owner, you can list your boat with us. We have a simple process. You set the price, dates, and rules. We handle the bookings and payments. You get paid after each charter. We take a small commission. More details on our blog.

Local Highlights and Activities on Your Charter

The Costa del Sol has a lot to offer. From the sea, you see the mountains behind the coast. La Concha mountain looms over Marbella. The coastline is a mix of sandy beaches, rocky coves, and cliffs. Puerto Banús is a spectacle of luxury yachts and cars. You can anchor near the port and watch the people. Cala del Faro is a quiet cove with a lighthouse. It is good for swimming and snorkeling. The water is clear. You might see fish and octopus. Rio Verde is a river that flows into the sea near Marbella. You can take a small boat up the river for a different view. Estepona old town is a short walk from the marina. It has whitewashed houses and flower pots. You can have lunch there. The Strait of Gibraltar is a 45-minute cruise from Sotogrande. Dolphins are common. You can see them from the boat. Sometimes whales pass through. The Nerja caves are a 2-hour cruise from Marbella. You can dock at Nerja and walk to the caves. They are impressive, with huge stalactites and an underground lake.

You can also go to Gibraltar. You need a passport. The Rock is visible from the sea. You can see the monkeys and the tunnels. Or you can stay on the boat and enjoy the view. Tarifa is a windsurfing and kitesurfing hotspot. The wind is strong there. You can watch the surfers from the boat. For a longer trip, you can cross to Morocco. Tangier is 2 hours from Tarifa by fast boat. You need a visa and a passport. We can arrange the paperwork.

Food is a big part of the experience. You can order from a beach club or a restaurant and have it delivered to the boat. Or you can bring your own. Paella is a good choice. Seafood is fresh. Try the grilled sardines or the fried fish. For drinks, local wine from Ronda or sherry from Jerez. Or just beer and sangria. The skipper will not drink. You can drink as much as you want.

Safety and Skipper Details

Every skipper is licensed by the Spanish authorities. They have years of experience on this coast. They know the hazards: rocks, shallow water, currents. They have a VHF radio, life jackets, a first aid kit, and a fire extinguisher. The boat is insured. You are covered for liability. You do not need extra insurance, but check your travel insurance for cancellation or medical cover. The skipper gives a safety briefing at the start. They show you where the life jackets are and how to use the radio. They do not let you do anything dangerous. If you want to swim, they check for boats and currents. If you want to jump off the boat, they make sure the water is deep enough. They are professional and friendly. They speak English and Spanish. Some speak French, German, or Italian.

If you have a medical condition, tell us. We can accommodate most needs. The boat has a toilet and a small cabin for resting. If you get seasick, take medication before boarding. The water is usually calm in the morning. Afternoon wind can create waves. The skipper adjusts the speed and route to keep you comfortable.

bodyHtml:
What a Yacht Charter Cannes Actually Means on the Costa del Sol

Let us be clear. When you search for a yacht charter Cannes, you are probably imagining a sleek motor yacht, a professional crew, and a day exploring the French Riviera. But Cannes is expensive, crowded in summer, and the anchorages are packed. The Costa del Sol offers the same experience, better weather, lower prices, and fewer tourists. A yacht charter here means a private boat with a licensed skipper, fuel included, and the freedom to choose your own itinerary. You can cruise from Puerto Banús to Marbella Marina, stop for lunch at a beach club in Cabopino, or head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar to see the dolphins. The boats range from 8-metre RIBs for a fast, wet ride to 30-metre superyachts with a crew of four. Every charter includes a skipper who knows the coast, the anchorages, and the best spots for a swim.

Ports of Departure for Your Yacht Charter Cannes Alternative

You have six main departure ports on the Costa del Sol, each with its own character. Puerto Banús is the obvious choice, it is the most glamorous marina in Spain, with designer shops, flashy cars, and a constant buzz. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more relaxed, closer to the old town, and easier to park. Cabopino is a small, sandy marina near the dunes of Artola, perfect for a quiet start. Estepona has a renovated port with good restaurants and quick access to the western coast. Sotogrande is the luxury enclave near Gibraltar, with long, straight channels and a more exclusive feel. Benalmádena is further east, near Málaga, and offers a mix of family-friendly boats and fishing charters. For a yacht charter Cannes substitute, you want Puerto Banús or Sotogrande, they have the largest selection of motor yachts and catamarans. Use our search to filter by port and boat type.

Boat Types Available for Your Yacht Charter Cannes

The Costa del Sol fleet is diverse. Motor yachts from 10 to 20 metres are the most popular for a yacht charter Cannes style day, think Azimut, Princess, or Sunseeker. They cruise at 20-25 knots, have a sun pad on the bow, a shaded cockpit, and a cabin for changing. Catamarans are better for stability and space: a 12-metre Lagoon or Fountaine Pajot gives you two hulls, a trampoline net, and room for 12 guests. Sailing yachts are slower but more authentic, you can help with the sails or just lie on the deck and listen to the water. RIBs and speedboats are for the adrenaline crowd: 8-10 metres, 40+ knots, and a very wet ride. Fishing boats are fully equipped with rods and a skipper who knows the marks. Licence-free day boats are available for the brave, no licence needed, but you still get a skipper who can teach you the basics. Superyachts over 24 metres are bookable on request, with prices from around EUR 5,000 per day. All boats include a licensed skipper, insurance, and basic safety equipment.

Pricing Guidance for a Yacht Charter Cannes Experience

Pricing is transparent but variable. A half-day (4 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht in Puerto Banús starts from around EUR 1,200. A full day (8 hours) on a 15-metre catamaran is about EUR 2,500. Superyachts over 20 metres are price on request, but expect EUR 4,000-8,000 per day. Fuel is included in most quotes, check when you book. Extras like food, drinks, water toys, or a photographer cost extra. The high season (June to September) is 20-30% more expensive than May or October. You can save money by booking a weekday or a morning charter. Payment is typically 50% deposit by bank transfer or card, with the balance due on the day. Cancellation policies vary, but most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days in advance. No hidden fees, no tips required (but appreciated). For the best value, book a catamaran from Cabopino or Estepona, they are cheaper than Puerto Banús and just as beautiful.

Best Time of Year for a Yacht Charter Cannes Style Trip

The Costa del Sol has over 300 days of sunshine a year, so you can book a yacht charter Cannes alternative in any season. The best months are May, June, September and October. The sea temperature is 18-22 degrees C in May, rising to 24-26 degrees C in August. July and August are the hottest (30-35 degrees C) and busiest, the marinas are full, the anchorages are crowded, and the prices are high. April and November are cooler (16-20 degrees C) but still pleasant for a cruise, you will need a light jacket on the water. December to March is the low season: the weather is mild (12-16 degrees C), the sea is choppier, and many boats are in dry dock. If you want a guaranteed swim, book between June and September. If you want solitude and lower prices, book in May or October. The wind is usually light in the morning, picking up in the afternoon, your skipper will choose the best route based on the forecast.

What is Included in Your Yacht Charter Cannes Booking

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and basic safety equipment (life jackets, flares, first aid kit). The skipper is not a waiter, they drive the boat, handle the mooring, and give you a safety briefing. You can ask them to anchor for a swim, take you to a beach club, or show you the local landmarks. Some skippers speak English, Spanish, and sometimes French or German, confirm when you book. Most boats include a cooler with ice, a sound system (Bluetooth), and a basic galley with a sink and fridge. You need to bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package (EUR 30-50 per person). Water toys like a paddleboard, snorkel gear, or a floating mat can be added for EUR 50-100. Toilet facilities vary, larger boats have a marine toilet, smaller RIBs do not. All boats have a VHF radio and a GPS chart plotter. The skipper will not let you do anything dangerous, but they will let you have fun. Read our blog for tips on what to bring.

Who is a Yacht Charter Cannes For

A yacht charter Cannes alternative on the Costa del Sol is for anyone who wants a private, flexible day on the water. Couples book a motor yacht for a romantic sunset cruise. Families book a catamaran for a safe, stable day with the kids, the trampoline is a hit. Groups of friends book a RIB for a high-speed trip to the beach clubs of Puerto Banús. Corporate groups book a superyacht for a client entertainment day, the skipper will keep the drinks cold and the itinerary flexible. Fishing enthusiasts book a fishing boat for a half-day chasing sea bass or bluefin tuna. Solo travellers can join a shared charter if they want to meet people, but most boats are private. The minimum age is usually 2 years, and there is no maximum. You do not need a licence, experience, or even a sense of direction, the skipper does everything. Just bring sunscreen, a towel, and a good attitude.

How to Book Your Yacht Charter Cannes with BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24, enter your preferred date, number of guests, and port. Browse the boats, read the specs, and check the photos. Click on a boat to see the full description, included extras, and the cancellation policy. Send an enquiry through the site, and the operator will confirm availability and send you a quote. You can also call or WhatsApp the number on the listing. Expect a response within a few hours during business hours. Once you accept the quote, you pay a 50% deposit to secure the booking. The remaining 50% is paid on the day, usually in cash or by card. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details, the meeting point, and a suggested itinerary. Arrive at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The skipper will meet you at the dock, give you a safety briefing, and answer any questions. Then you cast off and enjoy your yacht charter Cannes style day on the Costa del Sol.

Local Attractions and Itineraries for Your Yacht Charter Cannes

Your skipper can suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences. A classic itinerary from Puerto Banús goes west to the Cala del Faro, a small cove with clear water and a beach bar. From there, you can continue to Estepona old town, where the whitewashed houses and flower pots make a good photo stop. Another route goes east to Cabopino, a naturist beach with dunes and a chiringuito. Further east is Marbella Marina, where you can dock for lunch at a seafood restaurant. For a longer trip, head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar, you will pass the Rock of Gibraltar and, if you are lucky, see pods of common dolphins and pilot whales. The Strait is also a migratory route for whales in spring and autumn. If you want a full day, go all the way to the Nerja Caves, the boat can anchor near the cliffs, and you can swim into the sea caves. Your skipper will know the best anchorages for each wind direction.

Safety and Skipper Qualifications on a Yacht Charter Cannes

All skippers on BoatHire24 hold a valid Spanish licence (Patrón de Yate or similar) and have commercial insurance. They are trained in first aid and fire safety. The boat is inspected annually by the Spanish maritime authority. You will be given a safety briefing at the start of the charter, including the location of life jackets, the emergency radio channel, and the fire extinguisher. The skipper will not take the boat out in dangerous weather, if the forecast is bad, they will suggest a reschedule or a different route. You are not allowed to operate the boat yourself unless you have a licence and the skipper agrees. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper stays sober. If anyone on board becomes a danger to themselves or others, the skipper has the right to terminate the charter and return to port. This is rare, but it happens. Respect the skipper, follow their instructions, and you will have a safe, enjoyable day.

Comparing the Cost of a Yacht Charter Cannes with a Costa del Sol Charter

The price difference between Cannes and the Costa del Sol is significant. A 12-metre motor yacht in Cannes costs from around EUR 2,500 for a half-day in July. The same boat from Puerto Banús starts at EUR 1,200. That is a 50% saving. The reason is simple: the Costa del Sol has lower berthing fees, cheaper crew costs, and less demand relative to supply. You also get more boat for your money. A 15-metre catamaran that costs EUR 4,000 in Cannes is available for EUR 2,500 here. The fuel is included in most Costa del Sol charters, in Cannes it is often extra and can add EUR 500-1,000 to the bill. If you are looking for a yacht charter Cannes experience on a budget, the Costa del Sol is the smarter choice. You can book a 10-metre RIB for EUR 600 for a half-day, something you would struggle to find for under EUR 1,200 in Cannes. The quality of the boats is the same, the skippers are just as professional, and the scenery is arguably more varied.

How the Weather Compares for Your Yacht Charter Cannes Alternative

The Costa del Sol has a microclimate that gives it an edge over the French Riviera. In July, Cannes averages 27 degrees C with a 60% chance of a thunderstorm in the afternoon. Marbella averages 30 degrees C with a 10% chance of rain. The sea temperature in August is 26 degrees C on both coasts, but the Costa del Sol has less wind in the morning, making for a smoother cruise. The Levante wind can pick up in the afternoon, but your skipper will plan around it. In May, Cannes is still cool at 19 degrees C with a 40% chance of rain. Marbella is 23 degrees C and mostly dry. If you want a guaranteed sunny day for your yacht charter Cannes style trip, book between May and October on the Costa del Sol. The water is warm enough for swimming from June to September, and the evenings are balmy enough for a sunset dinner on deck. The Strait of Gibraltar can be choppy in spring, but the coastal routes are protected by the mountains.

Specific Itineraries for a Yacht Charter Cannes Style Day

Your skipper can customise the route to your preferences. For a Cannes-style glamour day, start from Puerto Banús at 11:00, cruise west to the Cala del Faro for a swim and a glass of cava. Then head to Estepona for lunch at the marina restaurant La Escollera, known for its grilled fish. After lunch, cruise back to Puerto Banús for a late afternoon at the beach club Ocean Club. For a family day, start from Cabopino, anchor off the dunes of Artola for a swim, then motor east to Marbella Marina for a paella lunch at El Puerto. The kids can play on the beach while you finish your wine. For an adventure day, take a RIB from Sotogrande south to the Strait of Gibraltar. You will see the Rock of Gibraltar up close, and if the dolphins are active, you can watch them bow-ride. The trip takes about 2 hours each way, so you need a full-day charter. Your skipper will know the best spots for each wind direction, so trust their advice.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind for Your Yacht Charter Cannes

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a change of clothes. Leave the high heels at home, they damage the deck and are dangerous on a moving boat. Bring soft-soled shoes or go barefoot. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The skipper can provide ginger tea or acupressure bands, but medication is more reliable. Bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package. Most boats have a cooler with ice, but the capacity is limited, so bring a separate cooler for extra drinks. Do not bring glass bottles, they break and cut feet. Bring plastic cups and plates. If you want to swim, bring a snorkel mask and fins, some boats have them on board, but it is better to bring your own. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos. Leave any valuables in the car or the marina locker, the boat is safe, but the sea is not. The skipper will store your bags in a dry cabin if available.

intro:

bodyHtml:
What’s Included in Your Phuket Yacht Rental

Every yacht rental through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the currents around the Phi Phi Islands, and the best spots to anchor for lunch. The price includes fuel for a standard itinerary (usually 6-8 hours of cruising), basic insurance, and the use of onboard facilities: sun pads, a sound system, a galley kitchen, and a toilet or two. You can add a hostess or a chef for around EUR 100-150 extra per day, or bring your own food and drinks. Some catamarans and larger motor yachts include stand-up paddleboards and snorkelling gear.

What’s not included: your transport to the marina, any docking or national park fees (typically EUR 5-15 per person for the Similan or Phi Phi islands), and gratuities. The skipper will handle all navigation and safety briefings. You just decide the itinerary, within reason. Want to spend the whole day at Maya Bay and then cruise to Bamboo Island for sunset? Doable. Want to go fishing off the west coast? Also doable, as long as the weather plays along.

Phuket Marinas and Departure Ports

Your yacht rental Phuket experience starts at one of these marinas. Yacht Haven Marina, on the north-east coast, is the most popular for luxury charters heading to Phang Nga Bay and James Bond Island. It’s a 20-minute drive from Phuket International Airport. Phuket Boat Lagoon, also on the east coast, is a bit further south and offers a quieter departure point with fewer crowds. Ao Po Grand Marina, near the top of the island, is where many of the larger catamarans dock, and it’s the closest to the Similan Islands (about a 2-hour cruise). Chalong Bay, on the south-east coast, is the main departure point for day trips to the southern islands: Coral Island, Racha Island, and the Phi Phi archipelago. Each marina has parking, a café or restaurant, and a small shop for last-minute supplies.

If you’re staying in Patong, Kata, or Karon, the drive to Yacht Haven or Chalong Bay is about 40 minutes. Most skippers will meet you at the marina gate and walk you to the boat. No need to worry about finding the slip number.

Boat Types Available for Phuket Charters

Our Phuket fleet covers four main categories. Motor yachts from 30 to 60 feet, typically with a flybridge and a spacious saloon. These are the fastest option, cruising at 18-25 knots, so you can cover more ground in a day. Catamarans from 38 to 54 feet, stable and spacious, ideal for families or groups of 8-12 people. They have a shallower draft, so you can anchor closer to beaches. Sailing yachts from 40 to 55 feet, for those who want the experience of sailing (though the skipper will handle the sails). They are slower but quieter, and you can often charter them for multi-day trips at a lower cost per day. And RIBs or speedboats, between 25 and 35 feet, for a more adrenaline-fuelled trip to the Similans or for fishing. These are the cheapest option, starting from around EUR 350 for a half-day.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Rental Phuket

Prices vary by boat size, age, and inclusions. A 30-foot motor yacht for a half-day (4 hours) starts from around EUR 450. A full-day (8 hours) on a 40-foot motor yacht is typically EUR 800-1,200. A 50-foot catamaran for a full day runs EUR 1,500-2,500. Luxury 60-foot motor yachts with a full crew (skipper, hostess, chef) cost EUR 3,000-5,000 per day. Multi-day charters: a 3-day sailing trip to the Similan Islands on a 45-foot sailing yacht starts from around EUR 2,500 total, including food and fuel. Prices are seasonal: high season (November to April) is 20-30% more expensive than low season (May to October). All prices are in EUR and include VAT. You can pay by bank transfer or credit card, with a 50% deposit to confirm the booking and the balance due 14 days before departure.

Best Time to Rent a Yacht in Phuket

The best time for a yacht rental Phuket is from November to April, the dry season. The sea is calm, visibility is 20-30 metres, and the wind is light, making for comfortable cruising. Average air temperature is 28-32 degrees C, water temperature 27-29 degrees C. The monsoon season (May to October) brings stronger winds, rain and rougher seas, especially on the west coast. However, the east coast (Phang Nga Bay) is more sheltered and remains navigable year-round. If you’re on a budget, low season offers discounts of 20-30% on charter rates, and you’ll have the islands to yourself. Just be prepared for the occasional downpour and check the forecast with your skipper before departing.

How to Book Your Phuket Yacht Charter

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter Phuket as your destination, pick your dates and boat type. You’ll see a list of available yachts with photos, specs, and prices. Choose one, fill in your details, and pay the deposit. We’ll confirm within 24 hours. If you want a custom itinerary or a specific boat not listed, BoatHire24 can source it for you. Most charters require a minimum of 2-3 days' notice, but last-minute bookings (within 24 hours) are sometimes possible, especially in low season. For multi-day charters, we recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance. You can cancel up to 14 days before departure for a full refund, minus a 10% admin fee. Within 14 days, the deposit is non-refundable, but we’ll try to reschedule if the weather is bad.

Who Is Phuket Yacht Rental For

This is for anyone who wants to explore the Andaman Sea without the responsibility of skippering. It’s for couples celebrating an anniversary, families with kids who want a safe, stable catamaran to swim from, groups of friends wanting a party boat with a sound system and a cooler, or business clients looking for a corporate day out. It’s also for photographers and divers who want to reach remote spots like the Similan Islands or the Surin Islands. If you have a licence and want to charter a bareboat, we can arrange that for certain boats, but the default is skippered. We do not rent to stag or hen parties that plan to cause trouble. Everyone must be at least 18 years old to consume alcohol on board.

Popular Phuket Yacht Rental Itineraries

Most charters follow one of these routes. The Phang Nga Bay tour: depart from Yacht Haven, cruise past the limestone karsts, stop at James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), canoe through the sea caves at Hong Island, have lunch at a floating restaurant, and return by 5 pm. The Phi Phi Islands tour: depart from Chalong Bay, cruise 45 minutes to Maya Bay (if open), then to Loh Samah Bay for snorkelling, lunch at Phi Phi Don, and a stop at Bamboo Island for sunset. The Coral and Racha Islands tour: a shorter trip, 30 minutes from Chalong Bay, with swimming, snorkelling, and lunch on the beach at Racha Island. The Similan Islands multi-day: depart from Ao Po, cruise 2 hours to the Similan Islands, spend 2-3 days diving, snorkelling, and sleeping on the boat or at a bungalow on the island. Each itinerary can be customised. Your skipper will advise on the best route based on the wind and tide.

What About Safety and Insurance

All boats in our Phuket fleet are licensed by the Phuket Marine Office and undergo annual safety inspections. They carry life jackets for all passengers, a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher, and a VHF radio. The skipper holds a valid Thai skipper’s licence and has at least 5 years of experience in Phuket waters. You are covered by third-party liability insurance, but you should check your own travel insurance for personal accident and medical evacuation cover. We recommend taking out a policy that covers water sports and boat trips. If the weather is deemed unsafe by the skipper or the harbour master, the charter will be rescheduled or refunded. No one wants to be out in a 40-foot boat in a 30-knot squall.

Local Colour: What Makes Phuket Special

Phuket isn’t just about the beaches. The old town has Sino-Portuguese shophouses, a Sunday walking street market, and some of the best street food in Thailand: try the Hokkien noodles and the roti. The Big Buddha on Nakkerd Hill offers panoramic views of the island. Andaman Sea water is warm all year, and you’ll see flying fish, sea eagles, and if you’re lucky, dolphins. The limestone karsts in Phang Nga Bay are reminiscent of Halong Bay but less crowded. If you have time, a day trip to the Similan Islands (only open from October to May) is worth the longer cruise. The visibility there can reach 30 metres, and the coral is vibrant. For more tips, check out our blog on Phuket yacht charters.

How to Get to Phuket and Around

Fly into Phuket International Airport (HKT). Direct flights from Bangkok (1 hour 20 minutes), Singapore (2 hours), Kuala Lumpur (1 hour 30 minutes), and many other Asian hubs. From the airport, a taxi to Yacht Haven Marina costs around EUR 15-20 and takes 20 minutes. To Chalong Bay, it’s EUR 25-30 and 45 minutes. You can rent a car or scooter, but parking at the marinas is limited. Most hotels in Patong, Kata, and Karon will arrange a transfer for you. If you’re staying on the east coast (Cape Panwa, Rawai), you’re closer to Chalong Bay. If you’re on the west coast (Kamala, Surin), you’re closer to Yacht Haven. Plan your departure port based on your accommodation to minimise travel time.

What to Pack for Your Phuket Yacht Charter

You want to enjoy the sun without getting fried. Bring reef-safe sunscreen (SPF 50+), a wide-brimmed hat, polarised sunglasses, and a rash guard or light long-sleeve shirt for snorkelling. A waterproof phone pouch is useful for photos at Maya Bay. If you plan to swim, pack a towel and a change of clothes. The boat will have a small fridge, so bring your own drinks and snacks if you didn't order catering. Most skippers provide a cooler with ice. For multi-day charters, bring a light jacket for the evening breeze and seasickness tablets if you're prone to queasiness. The pharmacy at any 7-Eleven sells Dramamine for about EUR 2. Leave your high heels onshore; barefoot or soft-soled shoes are best on a boat.

Food and Drink Options on Board

You can bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package. Standard lunch options cost around EUR 15-25 per person and include Thai dishes like pad Thai, green curry, fried rice, spring rolls, and fresh fruit. Some boats offer a barbecue on the back deck with prawns, chicken, and sausages. For drinks, you can bring your own alcohol (beer, wine, spirits) and the skipper will provide mixers and ice. Alternatively, the boat can stock a bar with local beer (Singha, Chang) at EUR 2-3 per can, wine at EUR 10-15 per bottle, and soft drinks at EUR 1-2 each. If you have dietary requirements (vegetarian, gluten-free), let us know at booking and we'll arrange it. For a special occasion, a private chef costs around EUR 100-150 extra and can prepare a multi-course meal.

Environmental Considerations for Phuket Charters

Phuket's marine environment is fragile. Maya Bay was closed for years to allow coral recovery. You should follow basic rules: do not touch or step on coral, do not feed the fish, and take all rubbish back to shore. Many boats now use biodegradable sunscreen and avoid single-use plastics. Your skipper will anchor in designated areas to avoid damaging seagrass beds. If you see a sea turtle or a reef shark, admire from a distance. The Similan Islands have a daily visitor limit, so your skipper will have permits arranged. Fines for damaging coral or littering can be up to EUR 500. It's not hard to be responsible, and it keeps the islands beautiful for everyone.

Alternatives to Phuket for Yacht Charters

If you've done Phuket before or want something different, consider Krabi (from Ao Nang or Railay Beach), Koh Samui (in the Gulf of Thailand), or the Maldives (further south but with similar water clarity). Krabi is closer to the Phi Phi Islands and has dramatic limestone cliffs. Koh Samui offers a different vibe with full-moon parties and quieter anchorages. The Maldives requires a longer flight but has overwater bungalows and world-class diving. For a shorter trip, Phang Nga Bay is unique to Phuket and can't be replicated elsewhere. Each destination has its own season, so check the weather before booking. For more comparisons, read our blog on the best yacht charter destinations in Thailand.

Common Mistakes to Avoid When Renting a Yacht in Phuket

First mistake: booking a boat that's too small for your group. A 40-foot motor yacht fits 10-12 people comfortably for a day trip, but if everyone wants to sunbathe on the foredeck, it gets cramped. Second mistake: not checking the itinerary with the skipper. Some routes are weather-dependent, and you might end up at a different beach than planned. Third mistake: forgetting cash for national park fees. Most islands charge EUR 5-15 per person, and not all boats accept card payments. Fourth mistake: assuming the boat has Wi-Fi. Some do, but it's slow. Download your playlist before boarding. Fifth mistake: arriving late. The skipper will wait 30 minutes, then charge you for the delay or cancel. Sixth mistake: drinking too much in the heat. You'll dehydrate faster on the water. Pace yourself and drink water between beers.

How to Combine a Phuket Yacht Charter with Other Activities

You can extend your yacht rental into a multi-day adventure. After a day on the water, head to Phuket Old Town for the Sunday night market (if it's a weekend). Or book a cooking class at a local farm to learn Thai cuisine. For divers, the Similan Islands liveaboard trips combine a yacht charter with 3-4 dives per day. For families, a day at the Splash Jungle Water Park near the airport is a good alternative if the sea is rough. For couples, a sunset dinner cruise on a catamaran around Phang Nga Bay is romantic and costs around EUR 800-1,200 for two. You can also combine a yacht charter with a visit to the Gibbon Rehabilitation Centre or the Elephant Sanctuary in Phuket. Just leave a day between activities to avoid rushing.

title: Boat Captains For Hire
metaDescription: Need a licensed skipper for your boat rental in Marbella? Boat captains for hire on the Costa del Sol. Private charters from Puerto Banús, Estepona, Sotogrande. Book online.
h1: Boat Captains For Hire on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You want to take a boat out on the water around Marbella, but you don't have a licence, or you just don't fancy steering yourself while you're trying to drink a cold beer and watch the sunset. That's where boat captains for hire come in. Every single charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper as standard, so you never have to worry about navigation, mooring, or the paperwork. You just turn up, step aboard, and tell the captain where you want to go. They handle the rest.

The Costa del Sol has a lot of coastline, from the glitzy marina of Puerto Banús to the quiet coves near Estepona and the dolphin-filled waters off Tarifa. With your own captain, you can explore it all without the stress of anchoring in a crowded bay or reading a chart. Whether you want a fast RIB for a fishing trip, a catamaran for a party, or a superyacht for a full-day cruise, there's a boat and a skipper ready for you.
bodyHtml:
What Does a Boat Captain For Hire Include?

When you hire a boat through BoatHire24, the skipper is part of the package. You don't pay extra or negotiate separately. The captain knows the local waters, the weather patterns, and the best spots for swimming, lunch, or dolphin watching. They also handle all safety briefings, fuel costs (usually included in the charter price), and any docking fees. You are free to relax, swim, eat, drink, and enjoy the scenery. The captain will not join you for dinner unless you invite them, and they will keep a professional distance while being friendly and informative.

Most skippers speak English and Spanish, sometimes German or French too. They have the relevant Spanish qualifications (Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo or higher) and insurance. You can ask for a specific language or preference at the time of booking, but generally the captains are flexible and used to dealing with international guests.

Departure Ports for Your Charter

You can start your trip from any of the main marinas along the Costa del Sol. The most popular is Puerto Banús, the luxury port in Marbella lined with superyachts, designer shops, and seafood restaurants. From there, you can head east towards Marbella's own marina (Puerto Deportivo) or west towards the sand dunes of Cabopino. Another common departure is Estepona, a charming town with a pretty old quarter and a quieter marina. Sotogrande is further west, near Gibraltar, and is ideal for longer cruises towards the Strait of Gibraltar where you can see pilot whales and dolphins. Benalmádena on the eastern side of the coast offers easy access to the open sea and the beaches of Torremolinos.

Each port has its own character. Puerto Banús is flashy and busy, perfect for people-watching. Estepona is more relaxed, with good anchorages near the Cala del Faro. Cabopino has a natural dune system and a small, less crowded marina. Your captain will know the best route based on the wind and your preferences.

Types of Boats With Captains

The range of boats available with a skipper is wide. You can choose a motor yacht for speed and comfort, typically 10 to 20 metres long, with cabins, a galley, and a flybridge. These are good for day trips or overnight stays. Catamarans are stable and spacious, ideal for groups of 10 to 20 people. They have a shallow draft, so you can anchor close to beaches. Sailing yachts offer a quieter, more traditional experience. You can help the crew if you want, or just lie on the deck and listen to the rigging. RIBs and speedboats are smaller and faster, perfect for a few hours of water sports or a quick run to the Marbella coast. Fishing boats come with a captain who knows the local marks for bream, tuna, and mahi-mahi. Licence-free day boats are small motorboats that you can drive yourself without a licence, but you can also hire a captain for those if you prefer to be a passenger. Finally, superyachts are available for the high end, with full crew including a captain, chef, and stewardesses. Prices for those are on request.

All boats are maintained to Spanish safety standards and have life jackets, first aid kits, and communication equipment. The captain will do a safety briefing before departure.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Captains For Hire

Prices vary depending on the boat size, type, duration, and season. For a half-day (4 hours) on a motor yacht around 12 metres, expect to pay from around EUR 800 to EUR 1,500. A full day (8 hours) might be EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. Catamarans for groups of 12 to 20 people start from about EUR 2,000 for a half-day and go up to EUR 4,500 for a full day. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper, from EUR 400 for two hours to EUR 1,200 for a half-day. Fishing charters are usually priced per person or per boat, starting at EUR 600 for a half-day. Superyacht charters are bespoke, so you need to request a quote.

Fuel is generally included in the price, but check when you book. Some charters include food and drinks, others are BYO or you can order a catering package. The captain's gratuity is not included, but 10-15% of the charter fee is customary if you are happy with the service.

Best Seasons for a Private Charter

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and hot summers. The peak season is June to September, when temperatures hit 30-35 degrees Celsius and the sea is warm. This is when most charters happen, and you should book at least a week in advance. Spring (April to May) and autumn (October to November) are also good, with temperatures around 20-25 degrees, fewer crowds, and lower prices. Winter charters are possible but less common; the sea can be choppy, and some boats are laid up for maintenance. However, on a calm day in December, you can have the coast almost to yourself. The best time for dolphin watching is from April to October, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar.

Your captain will advise on the best departure time. Mornings are usually calmer, with less wind, while afternoons can have a sea breeze that makes for a pleasant sail but a bumpier ride in smaller boats.

How to Book a Boat Captain For Hire

Booking is straightforward on BoatHire24. You browse the available boats, select your preferred date and duration, and add any extras like catering or water toys. The system will show you the total price including the captain. You pay a deposit online (usually 30-50% of the total) and the balance on the day, either in cash or by card. You can also contact the owner or the booking team if you have special requests, such as a specific route, a celebration (birthday, anniversary), or a corporate event.

We recommend booking at least 48 hours in advance, especially in summer. For last-minute bookings, you can check the search page for availability. Cancellations are usually free up to 48 hours before departure, but check the terms of each listing.

Who Is This For?

Hiring a boat with a captain is for anyone who wants to enjoy the sea without the responsibility of driving. It is popular with couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise, families with children who want a safe day out, groups of friends celebrating a stag or hen party (though the captain will enforce responsible drinking), and corporate clients entertaining clients. It is also ideal for solo travellers who want to join a shared charter, though most boats are private. If you have never been on a yacht before, the captain will make you feel comfortable and show you how things work.

If you are a seasoned sailor and want to charter a bareboat (without a captain), that is a different service. But for most people on holiday, the convenience of a skipper is worth the cost. You get local knowledge, safety, and the freedom to relax completely.

Local Highlights You Can Visit With Your Captain

With a captain, you can access places that are tricky to reach by land or without local knowledge. From Puerto Banús, you can cruise to the Cala del Faro near Estepona, a secluded cove with clear water. From Marbella, head to the Río Verde estuary, where you can anchor and see birdlife. From Sotogrande, a trip towards the Strait of Gibraltar offers the chance to spot migrating whales and pods of common dolphins. Further east, the Nerja caves are visible from the sea, and you can stop at the beach of Burriana for lunch.

Your captain will also know the best beach clubs and chiringuitos (beach bars) that are only accessible by boat, like the ones at Cabopino or the sandbank of El Rincón. They can recommend where to get fresh grilled fish or a good paella.

Safety and Regulations

All captains on BoatHire24 hold a valid Spanish recreational boating licence and have passed a medical check. They are required to carry safety equipment including life jackets for all passengers, a fire extinguisher, flares, and a VHF radio. The boat itself must have a valid navigation permit and insurance. Before departure, the captain will give a safety briefing and show you where the life jackets are stored. They will also check the weather forecast and may cancel or postpone the trip if conditions are dangerous. You can trust their judgment; they want to keep you safe and also protect their boat.

Alcohol is allowed on board, but the captain cannot drink while operating the vessel. You can bring your own drinks or order them through the charter. If you are planning a party, let the captain know in advance so they can manage the situation responsibly.

Frequently Asked Questions

If you have never hired a captain before, you might have questions about what to bring, how to tip, or whether you can change the itinerary. The answers are straightforward: bring sunscreen, a towel, and a hat. The captain will provide water and ice. You can change the route during the trip if you agree with the captain, but if you want a significant detour, it may affect the fuel consumption and time. Tips are appreciated but not mandatory. If you have a specific dietary requirement, inform the charter at booking time so they can arrange catering.

For more detailed information, read the blog articles on the BoatHire24 website, which cover topics like what to wear, how to choose the right boat, and the best anchorages on the Costa del Sol.

How to Choose the Right Captain for Your Group

Not all captains are the same, and matching them to your group makes a difference. If you have young children, look for a skipper who has experience with families and knows calm anchorages like the shallow waters of Cabopino or the sheltered bay of Estepona. For a corporate event, you might want a captain who speaks fluent English and can host a professional lunch on the flybridge. If you are a group of divers or snorkellers, some captains carry extra gear or know the best reefs near the Cala del Faro. You can mention your group composition when you book, and the BoatHire24 team will suggest a suitable captain from the fleet. The cost does not change, but the experience will be better tailored.

What Happens on a Typical Day With a Captain

You meet at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The captain greets you, shows you the boat, and runs through the safety briefing. You leave the dock and head to your first stop, maybe a swim stop off the coast of Marbella near the Río Verde. The captain anchors, and you jump in. After an hour, you move on to a beach club for lunch, or the captain can grill food on the boat if you have a catering package. In the afternoon, you cruise along the coast towards Puerto Banús, passing the luxury villas and the La Concha mountain backdrop. You return to the marina by the agreed time. The captain handles all the mooring and cleaning. You just step off and head home. It is that simple.

Hidden Costs and How to Avoid Them

The listed price usually covers the boat, captain, fuel, and basic safety equipment. But there are extras you might not expect. Some charters charge extra for water toys like jet skis, paddleboards, or snorkel gear. Others add a fee for cleaning if you leave the boat very messy. Dockage fees at beach clubs or restaurants are sometimes not included, so if you want to stop for lunch at a place like the Trocadero in Puerto Banús, you might pay EUR 50 to EUR 100 for mooring. Ask the captain or the booking team beforehand what is included. Most listings on BoatHire24 are transparent, but it is worth confirming. Also, if you want to extend the trip on the day, expect to pay a pro-rata rate plus extra fuel. Cash is easiest for on-the-day extras.

Last-Minute Bookings and Same-Day Charters

If you wake up in Marbella and decide you want to go out on the water that day, you can often find a captain available. Many boats have a 24-hour cancellation policy, so last-minute slots open up. Use the search page and filter by availability for today or tomorrow. You might pay a slight premium for urgency, but it is usually the same price as an advance booking. The captain will need at least 2 hours notice to prepare the boat, refuel, and get to the marina. For evening charters, like a sunset cruise from Puerto Banús, same-day booking is common in summer. Just be flexible on the boat size and type, and you will find something.

Weather and Sea Conditions You Should Know

The Costa del Sol has a local wind called the Poniente (west wind) that blows from the Strait of Gibraltar. It can pick up in the afternoon, making the sea choppy on the western side, near Sotogrande and Estepona. The Levante (east wind) is less common but can bring haze and bigger waves. Your captain will check the forecast and may suggest a different route or an earlier departure to avoid rough conditions. In July and August, the sea is usually calm in the morning, with a light breeze by 2 PM. In winter, swells from the Atlantic can affect the coast, especially near Gibraltar. If you are prone to seasickness, book a catamaran or a large motor yacht, and take medication an hour before departure. The captain can also recommend a sheltered route along the coast.

What to Bring and What the Boat Provides

The boat will have life jackets, a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher, and basic navigation equipment. Most boats also have a cooler with ice, bottled water, and soft drinks. Some have a Bluetooth speaker for music. You should bring sunscreen (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. If you plan to swim, bring a swimsuit and a change of clothes. Cameras and phones are fine, but keep them in a waterproof pouch. Do not bring glass bottles, as broken glass on deck is dangerous. The captain will provide a bin for rubbish. If you want to bring your own food, that is usually fine, but check if the boat has a galley or just a fridge. For a full-day charter, a packed lunch or a catering order is recommended.

title: Yacht Charter Split
metaDescription: Book a yacht charter Split with BoatHire24. Compare motor yachts, catamarans, and sailing yachts with licensed skippers. Instant online quotes available.
h1: Yacht Charter Split, Compare Boats with Skipper
intro:
You want a yacht charter Split because the Dalmatian coast is one of the best cruising grounds in the Mediterranean, and Split is the logical starting point. The old town, the Marjan hill, the islands of Brač, Hvar, and Vis, they are all within a few hours’ sail. BoatHire24 lets you compare motor yachts, catamarans, and sailing yachts, all with a licensed skipper included, so you can skip the paperwork and just enjoy the Adriatic.

We operate in Marbella and the Costa del Sol, but we know the Split charter scene well enough to give you a straight answer. You will find boats from 8 m RIBs up to 25 m motor yachts, prices from around EUR 400 per day for a small sailing yacht to EUR 3,500 for a crewed catamaran. Every booking includes a professional skipper, insurance, and basic safety gear. No hidden fees, no surprise charges.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Split Yacht Charter with BoatHire24

Every charter through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters. That means you do not need a boating licence, and you do not have to worry about navigation, docking, or fuel logistics. The skipper handles all of that. You also get a safety briefing, life jackets, a first aid kit, and a VHF radio. Most boats include a Bluetooth sound system, a cooler, and a bimini top for shade. Fuel is usually extra, about EUR 100-200 per day for a motor yacht, less for a sailing yacht. You pay for mooring fees and port taxes separately, typically EUR 20-50 per night depending on the marina. Food and drinks are on you, but the skipper can recommend a supermarket or a local konoba for provisions.

You can add extras like a hostess, a chef, or water toys (SUP boards, snorkel gear, a seabob) for an additional fee. The base price covers the boat, the skipper, and standard safety equipment. We do not charge a booking fee, and you get a full breakdown before you confirm.

Departure Ports for Your Split Yacht Charter

Split is the main hub, but you can also start from Trogir, Makarska, or even Dubrovnik if you prefer a one-way charter. Split’s port is central, with good connections to the islands. The main departure points are:

  • Split Riva, the main seafront, close to Diocletian’s Palace. Ferries and charter boats depart from here. It is busy but convenient.
  • Marina Baotić, about 10 km west, in Seget. Larger yachts and catamarans often base here. Free parking and a quieter vibe.
  • ACI Marina Split, a modern marina with good facilities, fuel dock, and security. Popular for motor yachts.
  • Trogir, 20 km west, a UNESCO town with a smaller marina. Good if you want to avoid the Split crowds.
  • Makarska, 60 km south, a good start for the southern islands like Hvar and Korčula.

Each port has its own character. Split is lively, Trogir is historic, Makarska is relaxed. Choose based on your itinerary and the type of boat you want.

Boat Types Available for Split Charter

You can filter by boat type on our search page. The options are:

  • Motor yachts, from 10 m to 25 m, speeds up to 30 kts. Good for covering distance or island hopping. Prices from around EUR 800 per day.
  • Catamarans, 12-20 m, stable and spacious. Ideal for families or groups. Prices from EUR 1,200 per day.
  • Sailing yachts, 9-15 m, slower but more authentic. Prices from EUR 400 per day.
  • RIBs and speedboats, 6-9 m, fast and nimble. Good for day trips to Blue Cave or Hvar. Prices from EUR 300 per day.
  • Fishing boats, 7-10 m, equipped for trolling and bottom fishing. Prices from EUR 500 per day.
  • Superyachts, over 24 m, with crew and luxury amenities. Price on request.

Each boat is inspected and insured. The skipper will give you a full tour before departure.

Pricing Guidance for Split Yacht Charter

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. As a rough guide:

  • Low season (April-May, October): from around EUR 400 per day for a 9 m sailing yacht, EUR 700 for a 12 m motor yacht.
  • Mid season (June, September): from EUR 600 for sailing, EUR 1,000 for motor.
  • High season (July-August): from EUR 900 for sailing, EUR 1,500 for motor. Catamarans start at EUR 2,000.

These are base rates. Fuel, food, mooring, and crew tips are extra. A week-long charter in July on a 15 m motor yacht with a skipper might cost EUR 10,000-15,000 all-in. You can get a better deal in May or September.

We do not show exact prices for every boat because they change with demand. Use our BoatHire24 homepage to get a custom quote for your dates.

Best Time for a Split Yacht Charter

The Adriatic season runs from April to October. July and August are peak: air temperatures 30-35°C, water 25°C, and the sea is calm. But the ports and anchorages get crowded. You will need to book well ahead, and mooring fees are higher. May, June, and September are better for a relaxed trip: 22-28°C, fewer boats, and lower prices. October is still warm but the winds pick up, especially the bura and jugo, which can make sailing choppy. The best months for guaranteed sun and light winds are June and September.

If you want to see dolphins, the Strait of Gibraltar is better, but the islands around Split have some resident bottlenose dolphins. You might spot them near Vis or the Pakleni Islands.

How to Book a Split Yacht Charter with BoatHire24

Go to our search page, enter Split as the destination, your dates, and the number of guests. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. You can filter by boat type, length, and price range. Once you find one you like, click to see the full details: what is included, the skipper’s bio, and the cancellation policy. You can then request a booking. We will confirm availability within 24 hours and send you a payment link. A 30% deposit secures the booking, the balance is due 14 days before departure. You can pay by bank transfer or credit card. We do not charge a booking fee.

If you have special requests, like a specific departure time, a custom itinerary, or extra crew, let us know in the booking request. The skipper will work with you to plan the route.

Who Is a Split Yacht Charter For

This is for anyone who wants to see the Dalmatian coast without the hassle of owning a boat or having a licence. It works for:

  • Families, catamarans are stable and have plenty of space for kids. The skipper can take you to shallow coves for swimming.
  • Couples, a sailing yacht for two, with a skipper who doubles as a guide. Romantic and private.
  • Groups of friends, motor yachts with a sound system and a flybridge for sunbathing. You can island hop and party at beach clubs.
  • Corporate groups, a catamaran or motor yacht for a day event. The skipper can handle logistics while you network.
  • Solo travellers, join a shared charter if you want to meet people, or book a small RIB for a solo adventure.

The skipper is there to ensure safety and to share local knowledge. You do not need any boating experience.

What to Expect on the Day of Your Charter

You will meet the skipper at the agreed marina at the scheduled time. They will check your ID, give a safety briefing, and show you the boat. You can leave your bags on board, and then you are off. The skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences. Typical day trips include:

  • Split to Brač (Zlatni Rat beach), 1.5 hours by motor yacht.
  • Split to Hvar town, 2 hours, with a stop at the Pakleni Islands for lunch.
  • Split to Vis (Blue Cave), 2.5 hours, best done in the morning to avoid queues.
  • Split to Šolta, 1 hour, quieter and less touristy.

You can also do a multi-day charter, staying overnight in different marinas or anchoring in secluded bays. The skipper will handle mooring and docking. You just relax.

Local Highlights Near Split

Split itself is a UNESCO site with Diocletian’s Palace, the Riva promenade, and the Marjan hill for hiking. The nearby islands each have their own character. Brač has the famous Zlatni Rat beach, a white pebble spit that changes shape with the current. Hvar has a lively nightlife and a fortress with views. Vis is more remote, with the Blue Cave and the abandoned submarine tunnels. The Pakleni Islands are a chain of islets with coves and beach bars. If you have time, a day trip to the Krka National Park (waterfalls) is worth it, but you need a car or a tour bus from Split.

For a longer charter, you can sail south to Korčula, Dubrovnik, or even the Pelješac peninsula for wine tasting. The distances are manageable: Split to Dubrovnik is about 70 NM, a 4-5 hour motor trip.

Common Questions About Split Yacht Charter

We get asked about licences, insurance, and cancellation policies. You do not need a licence because the skipper is licensed. Insurance is included in the price, but you should check the excess for damage. Cancellation policies vary by boat, but typically you get a full refund if you cancel 30 days before departure, 50% refund 14-30 days, and no refund after that. We recommend travel insurance that covers charter cancellations.

If you want to know more about the local area, read our blog for tips on the best anchorages, restaurants, and hidden spots around Split. We update it regularly with local knowledge.

Navigating the Split Charter Season: Wind and Wave Patterns

The Adriatic has a predictable rhythm, and knowing it helps you pick the right boat. The maestral, a northwesterly wind, blows from June to August, usually from midday until sunset. It is light, 10-15 kts, perfect for sailing. The bura, a cold northeasterly, can hit 40 kts in winter, but in summer it is rare. The jugo, a southeasterly, brings rain and rough seas, mostly in spring and autumn. If you charter in July, expect flat calm mornings and a gentle breeze by 2 pm. In September, the jugo is more likely, so a motor yacht or a catamaran is a safer bet than a sailing yacht. Skippers know the forecasts and will adjust the route. They will not take you out in a bura if it is unsafe.

Island Hopping Itineraries from Split: Time and Distance

A week-long charter gives you time to see three or four islands without rushing. A typical five-day route: Day one, Split to Brač (12 NM, 1 hour by motor yacht). Anchor at Zlatni Rat or Lovrečina bay. Day two, Brač to Hvar (15 NM, 1.5 hours). Spend the afternoon in Hvar town or the Pakleni Islands. Day three, Hvar to Vis (20 NM, 2 hours). Visit the Blue Cave in the morning, then anchor in Stiniva cove. Day four, Vis to Korčula (30 NM, 3 hours). Explore the old town and walk the walls. Day five, Korčula back to Split (50 NM, 4-5 hours). That is about 130 NM total, easy for a motor yacht or a catamaran. A sailing yacht would need more time, maybe two days for the return leg. If you only have three days, stick to Brač, Hvar, and Šolta. Each leg is under 20 NM, so you have time for swimming and lunch.

Mooring Fees and Marina Costs Around Split

Mooring costs vary by location and season. In Split, ACI Marina charges about EUR 60-80 per night for a 12 m boat in July. The town quay in Hvar is around EUR 50-70, but it fills up fast. The Pakleni Islands have seasonal buoys for EUR 30-40, with no facilities. Free anchoring is possible in most coves, but you need to carry your own fenders and lines. The skipper will know the free spots, like Stiniva bay on Vis or Lučišća on Brač. If you want a marina with electricity, water, and showers, budget EUR 50-100 per night. In low season, prices drop by about 30%. You pay on arrival, usually in cash or by card. Some marinas require a reservation in July and August, so the skipper will book ahead.

Fuel Costs for Different Boat Types

Fuel is one of the biggest variable costs. A 12 m motor yacht with twin 300 hp engines burns about 40-60 litres per hour at cruising speed (20 kts). At EUR 1.50 per litre, that is EUR 60-90 per hour. A day trip of 4-5 hours of running time costs EUR 240-450 in fuel. A sailing yacht uses the engine for manoeuvring and when the wind drops, about 5-10 litres per hour, so EUR 8-15 per hour. A catamaran with two 50 hp engines burns 15-25 litres per hour, EUR 23-38. A RIB with a 250 hp outboard burns 30-40 litres per hour, EUR 45-60. The skipper will estimate fuel based on your itinerary. You pay for what you use, usually at the end of the charter. Some boats include fuel in the price, but most do not. Ask before you book.

Best Anchorages for Swimming and Snorkelling

The Dalmatian coast has clear water and rocky bottoms, ideal for snorkelling. Stiniva bay on Vis is a narrow cove with a pebble beach and cliffs. It gets crowded by midday, so go early. Lučišća on Brač is a sheltered bay with a small village and a beach bar. The water is calm and shallow, good for kids. The Pakleni Islands have several coves, like Palmizana and Mlini, with turquoise water and pine trees for shade. You can anchor off the beach and swim ashore. On Šolta, Maslinica bay has a sandy bottom and a few restaurants. For something more remote, the Blue Cave on Vis is a sea cave with a light effect, but you can only enter by small boat. The skipper will take you in a tender if the boat is too big.

Local Specialities and Provisions for Your Charter

You can bring your own food and drinks, or the skipper can arrange a provisioning service. In Split, the main market (Pazar) is near the Riva, open daily until 2 pm. You can buy fresh bread, cheese, olives, prosciutto, and fruit. The Konzum supermarket near the ferry terminal has everything else. If you want local wine, look for Pošip from Korčula or Plavac Mali from Pelješac. A bottle costs EUR 8-15 in a shop. For lunch, you can stop at a konoba on the islands. On Brač, try the lamb roasted under a bell (ispod peke). On Hvar, the seafood at Konoba Menego is good. The skipper can recommend places that are not tourist traps. If you want a chef on board, that costs extra, around EUR 150-250 per day plus the cost of ingredients. They will cook local dishes like black risotto or grilled fish.

Booking a Skipper with Local Knowledge

All our skippers are licensed and speak English. Some speak German, Italian, or French as well. They have been working in the Adriatic for years and know the hidden spots. If you want a skipper who is also a dive instructor or a fishing guide, you can request that in the booking form. The skipper lives on the boat during multi-day charters, so they need a cabin. Most boats have a separate crew cabin. If not, the skipper sleeps on deck or in the saloon. You do not need to feed them, but it is polite to offer a meal. The skipper will not drink alcohol while on duty. They are there to ensure safety and to make your trip enjoyable. If you have any issues, contact us and we will sort it out.

h1: Boat Rental Malta, Skippered Charters on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You are looking for a boat rental Malta, but you have probably noticed that most options there are either overpriced or require a skipper’s licence you do not have. On BoatHire24, we offer a different route: skippered boat rentals based on the Costa del Sol, with departure ports from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande. Our fleet covers motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, RIBs, fishing boats and even superyachts. You can book a half-day trip to see dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar, a full-day cruise to the Nerja caves, or a sunset sail from Marbella Marina.
