If you are set on Malta, we get it, the island has its charm. But the Costa del Sol gives you more variety, better value and a guaranteed skipper. Check our BoatHire24 homepage to see the full range, or jump straight to search available boats.
bodyHtml:
Why Choose a Skippered Boat Rental on the Costa del Sol Over Malta

Malta is a classic destination for boat hire, but the reality is that many boats there are self-drive only, requiring a licence you may not have. On the Costa del Sol, every rental through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That means you can focus on swimming, sunbathing and sipping a drink while someone else navigates. The water clarity here rivals Malta, the coves are less crowded, and the backdrop of La Concha mountain is hard to beat. Plus, you get access to five departure ports, Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona and Sotogrande, each with its own character. Malta has just a few main marinas, and prices there have climbed steeply in recent years.

What’s Included in Every Boat Rental Malta-Style Charter

When you book a boat rental through BoatHire24, you get more than just a hull and an engine. The skipper is included in the price, along with fuel for the trip, basic safety equipment and VAT. Most charters also include a cooler with ice, snorkelling gear and a Bluetooth speaker. What is not included: food and drinks (you can bring your own or order a catering package), dockage fees at private ports (usually EUR 30-60 extra) and any extra hours beyond the agreed time. For a half-day (4 hours) you can expect to pay from around EUR 500 for a RIB, EUR 800 for a small motor yacht and EUR 1,200 for a catamaran. Full-day (8 hours) rates are roughly 1.5x the half-day price. Superyachts are price on request.

Departure Ports for Your Costa del Sol Boat Rental

Each port has its own vibe. Puerto Banús is the glitzy one, superyachts, designer boutiques and a lively promenade. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more relaxed, with good restaurants and easy parking. Cabopino is a small, sandy harbour near the dunes of Artola, perfect for a quiet start. Estepona marina is charming, with a flower-filled old town a short walk away. Sotogrande is upmarket and quieter, closer to the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin watching. Benalmádena offers a mix of nightlife and family fun. All ports are within 30-90 minutes of each other by sea, so you can pick up in one and drop off in another for a small fee.

Boat Types Available, From RIBs to Superyachts

We have five main categories. Motor yachts (10-20 metres) are the most popular for groups of 6-12 people, think Azimut, Sunseeker or Princess. Catamarans (12-18 metres) offer huge deck space and stability, ideal for families or those prone to seasickness. Sailing yachts (10-15 metres) are for purists who want to feel the wind, they are slower but more authentic. RIBs and speedboats (6-9 metres) are fast and nimble, great for a day of exploring coves. Fishing boats (7-10 metres) come with basic tackle and a skipper who knows the best spots. Licence-free day boats (5-7 metres) are small, simple and perfect for a couple. Superyachts (20+ metres) are available on request for VIP events or corporate charters.

Pricing Guidance, What a Boat Rental Malta Alternative Costs

Prices vary by boat type, season and duration. As a general guide: a half-day RIB hire starts from around EUR 500; a half-day motor yacht from EUR 800; a half-day catamaran from EUR 1,200; a full-day sailing yacht from EUR 900; a fishing boat half-day from EUR 600. Superyachts from EUR 3,000 per day. Peak season (July-August) can add 20-30% to these figures. Low season (May, June, September, October) offers better deals. Always check the exact price on the boat listing, some include extras like paddleboards or a barbecue. You can filter by price on our search page.

Best Seasons for a Boat Rental on the Costa del Sol

The season runs from May to October, with water temperatures from 22°C in June to 28°C in August. July and August are the hottest (air temp 30-35°C) and busiest, book at least two weeks ahead. May, June and September are quieter and more pleasant, with fewer crowds and lower prices. October is still warm (water 22°C) but risk of wind increases. Winter charters are possible on calm days, but most boats are laid up from November to March. If you want to see whales and dolphins, the best time is May to September when they migrate through the Strait of Gibraltar.

How to Book Your Skippered Boat Rental Malta Alternative

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Browse the fleet on our homepage, filter by port, boat type and budget. Select your date and time, most charters start at 10:00 or 16:00 for half-day, 10:00 for full-day. Pay a 30% deposit online; the balance is due on the day, in cash or card. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper’s contact details and meeting point. Cancel up to 48 hours in advance for a full refund. On the day, arrive 15 minutes early, meet the skipper, go through a safety briefing and you are off. No licence, no stress.

Who Is This Boat Rental For, Families, Couples, Groups

This works for almost anyone. Families with kids love catamarans for the space and stability, kids can swim off the back while parents relax. Couples often book a RIB or small motor yacht for a romantic sunset cruise. Groups of friends go for a motor yacht with a sound system and a photographer. Corporate groups use superyachts for client entertainment. Solo travellers can join a shared charter on a catamaran (ask us for details). The only people who might not enjoy it are those who get seasick easily, but the Costa del Sol is generally calm, and catamarans are very stable.

Local Attractions You Can Visit on Your Boat Rental

From the water you can see the best of the Costa del Sol. Puerto Banús itself is a sight, the marina full of superyachts, the golden sand of the beach. Head east and you reach Cala del Faro, a small cove with a lighthouse. Further east, the Río Verde estuary is a nature spot with birdlife. Westwards, you can cruise past Estepona’s old town (white-washed houses) and on to the Strait of Gibraltar, where dolphins and even whales appear. A longer trip takes you to the Nerja caves, the cliffs are spectacular from the sea. Most skippers know the best anchorages for lunch, like Cabopino or the dunes of Artola.

Why BoatHire24 Is Different from Other Boat Rental Malta Options

We are not a faceless aggregator. BoatHire24 is run by a small team based in Marbella who personally know every boat and skipper. We do not list boats we have not inspected. Our pricing is transparent, no hidden fees for cleaning or fuel. And we offer a price-match guarantee: if you find the same boat cheaper elsewhere, we will match it. Plus, we have a blog with guides on local spots, weather tips and skipper recommendations, check it out at our blog. Malta might have the name, but the Costa del Sol has the experience.

Frequently Asked Questions About Boat Rental Malta Alternatives

How to Compare a Boat Rental Malta Trip with the Costa del Sol

If you are weighing up a boat rental Malta versus the Costa del Sol, start with the practical details. Malta’s coastline is about 200 km, the Costa del Sol is roughly 150 km but with more varied scenery, from cliffs to sandy coves. Malta’s water is clear, around 25-30 metres visibility in summer, the Costa del Sol averages 15-20 metres but the backdrop of the Sierra Blanca mountains adds drama. Malta has a limited number of departure points, mostly Sliema, St Julians and Bugibba. Here you have five ports, each with different vibes and access to different stretches of coast. Fuel costs in Malta have risen sharply, a half-day charter there can cost EUR 600-1,000 for a basic motorboat. On the Costa del Sol, a comparable half-day skipper-included RIB starts at EUR 500. The skipper in Malta is often an extra EUR 100-200 per day, here it is built into the price. For a family of four, the Costa del Sol option usually works out cheaper and less hassle.

Specific Anchorages and Coves for Your Boat Rental Day

Your skipper will know the best spots based on wind and season. On the eastern side of Marbella, Cala del Faro is a reliable stop, a small pebble cove with a lighthouse and clear water, depth about 3-5 metres, good for snorkelling. Further east near Cabopino, the Artola dunes form a natural bay with sandy bottom, popular for lunch stops, you can tie up to a buoy or anchor. West of Marbella, the coast around Estepona has a series of small coves like Cala Sardina, a rocky inlet with good fishing. Near Sotogrande, the Guadiaro river mouth is a calm spot for swimming, but watch for currents. For a longer trip, the Strait of Gibraltar offers a chance to see common dolphins, striped dolphins and even pilot whales from May to September. Your skipper will know the best time of day, usually early morning, and will stay a safe distance. Most charters include a stop at one or two coves, plus a lunch anchorage.

What a Typical Half-Day Itinerary Looks Like

A half-day charter (4 hours) from Puerto Banús might go like this. Depart at 10:00, motor east along the coast past the Marbella skyline. First stop at Cala del Faro at 10:45, anchor for a swim and snorkel for 45 minutes. Then cruise back west, passing the Puerto Banús entrance, and head towards the Río Verde estuary around 12:00 for a quick look at the birdlife. Final stop at a quiet cove near the Marbella Club hotel for a final swim before returning to port at 13:45. Total distance about 10 nautical miles. Fuel consumption for a 12-metre motor yacht is roughly 80-100 litres, included in the price. If you choose a catamaran, the trip is more leisurely, fuel burn is lower, around 30-50 litres for the same distance. A RIB would cover the same route in half the time, allowing extra stops at Cabopino or even Estepona if you push further.

Understanding the Boat Rental Malta Price Structure on the Costa del Sol

Pricing on BoatHire24 is straightforward but worth understanding. The base price includes the boat, skipper, fuel, insurance and VAT. Extra costs to budget for: food and drinks (bring your own or order a catering platter from around EUR 25 per person), dockage fees at private marinas if you stop for lunch (EUR 30-60), and a tip for the skipper (10-15% is standard if service is good). Some boats charge an extra EUR 50 for a paddleboard or kayak. Half-day prices are for 4 hours, full-day for 8 hours. A sunset cruise is usually 2-3 hours and costs about 60% of a half-day. For a group of 8 people, a half-day catamaran at EUR 1,200 works out to EUR 150 per person, cheaper than a comparable boat rental Malta option where per-person costs often exceed EUR 200. Always check the listing for what is included, some boats offer a free bar or a barbecue on board.

Practical Tips for Your Boat Rental Day

Arrive 15 minutes early to meet the skipper and do the safety briefing. Bring sunscreen (factor 50), a hat, sunglasses and a towel. The sun is strong from 11:00 to 16:00, even in May. Seasickness is rare on the Costa del Sol because the water is usually calm, but if you are prone, take a tablet an hour before departure. The skipper will have a cooler with ice, but bring your own drinks and snacks. Alcohol is fine in moderation, but the skipper will stay sober. If you want to swim, bring a snorkel mask, most boats supply basic ones. Cameras and phones are safe in a dry bag, the skipper usually has one onboard. For families with young children, ask for a boat with a swim platform and ladder. Most motor yachts have a bathing platform at the stern. If you are booking for a special occasion, like a birthday or proposal, let us know in advance, the skipper can arrange decorations or a photographer.

How the Boat Rental Malta Season Compares to the Costa del Sol

Malta’s boating season runs from April to October, similar to the Costa del Sol. But Malta can be windy in spring, with the Gregale wind causing choppy seas in April and May. The Costa del Sol is sheltered by the Sierra Blanca mountains, so the sea is often calmer, especially in the morning. Water temperatures in Malta reach 26-28°C in August, the same as here. Air temperatures are similar, 30-35°C in peak summer. The key difference is crowds: Malta’s popular anchorages like Comino and the Blue Lagoon get packed in July and August, with dozens of boats jostling for space. On the Costa del Sol, coves like Cala del Faro and Cabopino are less crowded, and skippers know quieter spots. October in Malta is still warm but can be windy, the Costa del Sol has more settled weather in autumn, with calm days well into October. If you are flexible, book in late May or early September for the best balance of good weather and fewer people.

Why a Skipper Makes Your Boat Rental Malta Alternative Better

On a boat rental Malta, many charters are self-drive, meaning you need a licence (ICC or equivalent) and local knowledge. Without a skipper, you are responsible for navigation, anchoring and safety. On the Costa del Sol, every BoatHire24 charter includes a licensed skipper who knows the coast, the wind patterns and the best anchorages. They handle all the tricky bits, like mooring in a busy marina or spotting hidden rocks. They also know where to find dolphins, which coves have the clearest water, and where to get a good lunch. For a group of friends, the skipper becomes part of the day, pointing out landmarks and sharing local stories. For a family, they give you peace of mind, especially with kids. The cost of the skipper is built into the price, so you are not paying extra. In Malta, adding a skipper can cost EUR 100-200 on top of the boat hire. Here, it is included, making the total price more competitive.

What to Do If You Have Never Been on a Boat Rental Before

Do not worry. The skipper will give a full safety briefing before departure, including where the life jackets are, how to use the toilet (if fitted), and what to do in an emergency. Most boats have a VHF radio and a first aid kit. You do not need any experience. Wear non-slip shoes, trainers or boat shoes are fine, no high heels on deck. If you are prone to seasickness, take a travel sickness tablet an hour before. The Costa del Sol is generally calm, but if the wind picks up, the skipper will adjust the route. You can bring a small bag with your belongings, the skipper will stow it safely. Children must be supervised at all times, especially near the edge of the boat. Most boats have a Bimini top for shade. If you are unsure about anything, ask the skipper, they are there to help. The whole experience is designed to be relaxing, not stressful.

h1: Yacht Charter Malta, Skippered Boats for Your Day on the Water
intro:
You want a yacht charter Malta, and you want it to be straightforward. No hidden fees, no surprise skippers you have to tip separately, no boats that look nothing like the photos. BoatHire24 connects you with boat owners and charter companies along the Maltese coast, from Sliema to St Julian's to Valletta. Malta's coastline is 197 km of rocky coves, sandy beaches and limestone cliffs. The water is clear enough to see the sandy bottom at 10 metres. A yacht charter Malta means you can explore the Blue Lagoon on Comino, drop anchor off Gozo's Ramla Bay, or cruise past the fortifications of Valletta. bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Yacht Charter Malta

When you book a yacht charter Malta through BoatHire24, the skipper is included in the price. That is not always the case with other platforms, where the skipper is an optional extra that doubles the cost. Here, the skipper is part of the deal. He or she knows the local waters, the best anchorages and the spots where the sea is calm even when the wind picks up. Fuel is usually included for a standard day trip (8-10 hours), but check the listing details because some larger yachts charge fuel separately. Snorkelling gear, paddleboards and a cool box with ice are standard on most boats. Some catamarans also include a small inflatable tender for reaching shallow beaches.

What is not included: your food and drink (though you can bring your own or order catering through the charter company), dockage fees if you decide to stay overnight in a marina, and crew gratuity (10-15% is customary if the service is good). The boat will be cleaned before you board, so you do not need to tidy up afterwards. Just leave the cabin as you found it.

Departure Ports for Your Yacht Charter Malta

Most yacht charter Malta bookings start from one of three main ports. Sliema is the most popular, with dozens of charter companies based along the Sliema waterfront. From there you can be at Comino in 45 minutes or Gozo in 90 minutes, depending on the boat speed. St Julian's (Portomaso) is a close second, with a modern marina and plenty of restaurants for a pre-charter breakfast. Valletta Grand Harbour is the third option, more dramatic because you sail past the 16th-century fortifications before hitting open water. Less common departure points include Marsaxlokk (south-east Malta) and Mġarr (Gozo), which are useful if you want to spend most of the day on the Gozo side without crossing the channel twice.

If you are staying in a hotel near Golden Bay or Mellieħa Bay, some operators will pick you up from the local jetty by tender. Ask when you enquire. The distance from the marina to the open sea is never more than 15 minutes, so you are not wasting time motoring through a canal.

Types of Boats Available for a Yacht Charter Malta

The fleet in Malta is varied, and the right choice depends on your group size and what you want to do. Motor yachts are the fastest option, typically 12-18 metres, with a cruising speed of 20-25 knots. They are ideal for a day trip to the Blue Lagoon because you can get there in under an hour and have more time to swim. Catamarans are wider, more stable and have more deck space. A 14-metre catamaran can comfortably seat 12 people for lunch. If you are prone to seasickness, a catamaran is the better choice because it does not roll as much as a monohull. Sailing yachts are slower but quieter, and you can ask the skipper to cut the engine once you are clear of the harbour. The experience is more relaxed, more about the journey than the destination.

RIB speedboats are available for smaller groups (up to 6 people) and are the cheapest option, from around EUR 400 for a half day. They are not comfortable for lounging, but they are fun for a fast trip to a beach club. Fishing boats are tricked out with rods and fish-finders, and the skipper will take you to the best spots off the south coast. Superyachts (over 24 metres) are available for VIP groups, with prices on request and a crew of 3-4. You do not need a boating licence for any of these boats because the skipper holds the Maltese licence required by law.

Pricing Guidance for a Yacht Charter Malta

Prices for a yacht charter Malta vary by season, boat size and duration. A half-day (4-5 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht starts from around EUR 800 in the low season (October to April) and EUR 1,200 in the high season (June to September). A full day (8-10 hours) on a 14-metre catamaran is typically EUR 1,800-2,800. Superyachts are price on request, but expect EUR 5,000+ for a day. Fuel surcharges are uncommon but not unheard of for long trips to Gozo or the south coast. Always confirm the total cost before paying the deposit. The deposit is usually 30-50% of the total, with the balance due on the day, either in cash or by card.

There are no hidden cleaning fees or port taxes to pay separately. The price you see on the listing is the price for the boat, the skipper and the standard equipment. Extras like a photographer, a chef or a DJ are charged separately, usually EUR 200-500 per service. If you want to book a wedding reception on a yacht, expect a premium of 50-100% on the standard charter price, plus catering costs.

Best Season for a Yacht Charter Malta

The Mediterranean climate means the season for a yacht charter Malta runs from April to October, with July and August being the peak. Water temperature in August is 26-28 degrees C, and air temperature is 30-35 degrees C. The sea is calm most days, though a north-westerly wind can create a chop in the afternoon. The shoulder months of May, June and September are the sweet spot: warm enough to swim, fewer crowds, and lower prices by 20-30%. October is still pleasant, with water at 22 degrees C, but the chance of a windy day is higher.

Winter charters (November to March) are possible but less common. The boats still operate, but the water is 15-17 degrees C, and the air temperature rarely exceeds 18 degrees C. If you are interested in a winter charter for a special event or a photography trip, contact the charter companies directly. The prices are lower, but you will need a jacket on deck.

Malta is famous for its clear water, which is due to the lack of rivers carrying sediment into the sea. Visibility underwater is 20-30 metres on a calm day. The Blue Lagoon is the most famous spot, but it gets crowded in summer. Your skipper can take you to Crystal Lagoon (south of Comino) or the caves at Ghar Lapsi instead. Those spots are quieter and just as clear.

How to Book a Yacht Charter Malta on BoatHire24

Booking a yacht charter Malta on BoatHire24 takes a few minutes. Use the search page to filter by date, boat type, group size and budget. Each listing shows photos, a detailed description, the equipment list and the cancellation policy. Most operators offer free cancellation up to 14 days before the charter date. After that, you lose the deposit. Some allow rescheduling for a fee of EUR 100-200, depending on the boat.

Once you select a boat, you submit a booking request through the platform. The operator confirms availability within 24 hours. Payment is made via bank transfer or credit card. The deposit is refundable if the operator cancels due to weather or mechanical issues. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance in the high season, because the best boats go quickly. If you are booking last minute, try calling the operator directly; they sometimes have cancellations at a discount.

After the booking is confirmed, the operator sends you the skipper's contact details and the exact meeting point. The skipper will meet you at the marina 15 minutes before departure. They speak English, Maltese and usually Italian. If you have specific dietary requirements or want a particular route, tell the skipper at the start of the day. They are flexible.

Who Is a Yacht Charter Malta For

A yacht charter Malta works for families with children (the skipper is experienced with kids), couples looking for a romantic day, groups of friends celebrating a birthday or a stag do (within reason), and corporate groups for a team-building day or client entertainment. The boats are not suitable for large parties where people are going to be rowdy and disrespect the crew. The skipper has the right to cut the trip short if the behaviour is unsafe. Most groups of 6-12 people get along fine, and the skipper usually knows a good spot for lunch on the water.

If you are a solo traveller, you can book a shared charter on some boats, where you join a group of strangers. That is cheaper (from EUR 150 per person) but you have less control over the itinerary. Check the listing for shared charter options. Otherwise, you need to book the whole boat.

If you have a disability, contact the operator before booking. Some boats are wheelchair accessible (ramps to the main deck, wide doors to the cabin), but many are not. The skipper can help with boarding, but the toilets on smaller boats are cramped. Larger catamarans and motor yachts over 15 metres usually have accessible heads.

Local Tips for Your Yacht Charter Malta

Malta is small, so you can see most of the coast in a single day if you start early. A typical itinerary for a full-day yacht charter Malta: depart Sliema at 9 am, head to Comino (45 minutes), spend two hours at the Blue Lagoon, then cross to Gozo (30 minutes), anchor off Ramla Bay for lunch and a swim, then cruise back via the north coast, passing the cliffs of Dingli. You are back at the marina by 5 pm. If you want to add a stop at the Valletta waterfront, that adds 30 minutes.

Bring a towel, sun cream (SPF 50, the Maltese sun is strong), a hat and a light jacket for the wind. The boat has a shaded area, but the deck gets hot. Snorkelling gear is provided, but if you have your own mask, bring it. The water is so clear you can see the fish without a mask, but it is nicer with one. Do not feed the fish; it disrupts the ecosystem and the skipper will tell you off.

Malta has a strong boating culture, and the Maltese are proud of their maritime history. The Grand Harbour is one of the deepest natural harbours in the Mediterranean, and the fortifications are UNESCO-listed. Your skipper can give you a short history tour if you ask. The price is the same whether you ask or not.

Why Book Through BoatHire24 Rather Than Directly

You can book a yacht charter Malta directly with a charter company, and sometimes it is cheaper by 10-15% because there is no platform fee. But BoatHire24 offers three advantages. First, we verify the boats and the skippers before listing them. Every boat on the platform has a valid commercial licence, insurance and a safety certificate. Second, we handle the payment and the deposit, so you are not handing cash to a stranger at a marina. Third, we have a dispute resolution process if something goes wrong: the boat breaks down, the skipper does not show up, or the photos misrepresent the condition. You are protected for up to EUR 5,000 through our insurance policy.

We also have a blog with guides to the best anchorages, the latest regulations and tips for first-time charterers. It is updated monthly. The BoatHire24 homepage has a map view of all available boats, so you can see which ones are closest to your hotel. We do not charge a booking fee; the price you see is the price you pay, minus any extras you add.

Malta is a small island, but the variety of boats and itineraries is large. A yacht charter Malta is the best way to see the coast without the crowds of the beach clubs. The water is warm, the sun is hot, and the skipper handles the rest.

title: Boat Rental Bali

h1: Boat Rental Bali, Find Your Perfect Charter
intro:
You want to explore Bali from the water, right. Maybe you’ve seen the photos of turquoise lagoons and limestone cliffs and wondered how to get there without the crowds. A boat rental in Bali is the answer, and it’s more straightforward than you think. BoatHire24 connects you with skippered charters across the island, from motor yachts in Seminyak to traditional phinisi boats in Labuan Bajo. You pick the boat, we handle the rest.

This page covers what you need to know about renting a boat in Bali: the types of vessels, the best areas to sail, typical costs, and how to book. No fluff, just the facts. We operate in Spain primarily, but our platform includes listings for Bali too, so you get the same no-nonsense booking process.
bodyHtml:
What a Boat Rental in Bali Includes

Every boat rental in Bali through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper and crew. That means you don’t need a licence or any sailing experience. The skipper knows the local waters, the currents around Nusa Penida, the best snorkelling spots at Blue Lagoon, and the quiet coves near Uluwatu. You just sit back or take the helm if you want. Fuel is usually included in the price, but confirm with the listing. Some charters include lunch, drinks, and snorkelling gear. Others charge extra. Check the boat details before you book.

Typical rental durations are half-day (4-5 hours) or full-day (8-9 hours). Sunset cruises are popular too, running from around 4pm to 8pm. For longer trips, like a week-long sail around the Komodo islands, you can arrange multi-day charters. The crew stays on board, and you sleep in cabins or on deck. Prices vary widely, so we’ll get to that later.

Popular Ports and Departure Points for Your Bali Charter

Bali has several main departure points for boat rentals. The most common is Benoa Harbour in the south, near Nusa Dua. It’s the busiest marina on the island and gives you quick access to the southern islands: Nusa Lembongan, Nusa Ceningan, and Nusa Penida. From Benoa, you can reach these spots in 30-45 minutes by speedboat. Another option is Padang Bai, a smaller port on the east coast, closer to the Gili Islands and Lombok. If you’re staying in Ubud or the east, Padang Bai saves you time.

For the west coast, consider the harbour at Gilimanuk, though it’s mainly for ferries. Most charters start from Benoa or Padang Bai. Some luxury yachts also depart from the marina at Sanur or Serangan Island. If you’re after a sunset cruise, many boats leave from the beach at Jimbaran or Seminyak. You just wade out to the boat. No dock needed. Check the listing for the exact meeting point. BoatHire24 shows the departure port on each boat page.

Types of Boats Available for Rent in Bali

Bali’s boat rental scene covers a range of vessels. Here are the main types you’ll find on BoatHire24.

Motor yachts. These are the most common for day charters. Sizes from 40 to 80 feet. They’re fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space for sunbathing. A 50-foot motor yacht can take up to 20 guests. Prices start from around EUR 800 for a half-day. You get a flybridge, cabin, and usually a sound system. Good for parties or family trips.

Catamarans. Bigger, more stable, and ideal for groups. A 60-foot catamaran can hold 30-40 people. They have wide decks, trampolines at the front, and often a jacuzzi. Catamarans are popular for sunset cruises and day trips to Nusa Penida. Prices from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day.

Phinisi boats. Traditional Indonesian sailing vessels, made of ironwood. They’re slower but offer a unique experience. Phinisi boats are usually used for multi-day charters around Komodo or the Raja Ampat islands. Prices are higher, from EUR 2,000 per day for a basic model, up to EUR 10,000 for a luxury one.

Speedboats and RIBs. Small, fast, and no-frills. Good for a quick trip to the islands or watersports. A 30-foot RIB can take 8-12 people. Prices from EUR 400 for a half-day. Not much shade, so bring sunscreen.

Sailing yachts. For the purist. A 40-foot monohull takes 6-10 guests. Slower but quieter. Prices from EUR 600 for a half-day. You can help with the sails if you want, or just relax.

Pricing Guidance for Bali Boat Rentals

Prices for boat rental in Bali vary based on boat type, size, duration, and season. As a rough guide:

  • Half-day (4-5 hours): EUR 400-1,500 for a standard motor yacht, EUR 800-2,000 for a catamaran.
  • Full-day (8-9 hours): EUR 800-3,000 for a motor yacht, EUR 1,500-4,000 for a catamaran.
  • Sunset cruise (3-4 hours): EUR 300-1,000 for a motor yacht, EUR 500-1,500 for a catamaran.
  • Multi-day charter (per day): EUR 1,000-5,000 for a phinisi or luxury yacht.
  • Yacht Charter Malta, Skippered Boats for Your Day on the Water

These are estimates. The actual price depends on the boat’s age, amenities, and the season. High season (July-August, Christmas, New Year) can be 20-30% higher. Low season (February-March, October-November) offers better deals. Always check the listing for exact rates. BoatHire24 shows prices in EUR, but you can pay in your local currency.

Additional costs to consider: port fees (EUR 10-30 per person), food and drinks (if not included), and snorkelling equipment rental (EUR 5-15 per set). Some charters include everything. Others itemise. Read the fine print.

Best Seasons for a Bali Boat Charter

Bali has two main seasons: dry (April to October) and wet (November to March). The dry season is the best time for a boat rental. The sea is calm, visibility is good for snorkelling, and the sun is reliable. June to August is peak season, with more tourists and higher prices. September and October are also good, with fewer crowds.

The wet season brings rain and rough seas, especially from December to February. Charters still run, but you might face cancellations due to weather. The upside is lower prices and fewer boats on the water. If you’re flexible, you can get a deal. Check the forecast before booking.

Water temperature in Bali is around 27-29 degrees C year-round. Air temperature averages 30 degrees C in the dry season, 28 degrees C in the wet. You’ll be fine in a swimsuit and a light cover-up.

How to Book a Boat Rental in Bali with BoatHire24

Booking is simple. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and use the search bar. Enter “Bali” as the destination, select your dates, and pick the boat type. The search page will show you available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Each listing has a “Book Now” button. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) online via credit card or PayPal. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or card. Cancellation policies vary, but most allow free cancellation up to 48 hours before.

If you need help, contact us via the chat or email. We speak English, Spanish, and Indonesian. We can also arrange extras like catering, decorations for a wedding, or a photographer. Just ask.

Who Is a Bali Boat Rental For

A boat rental in Bali suits almost anyone. Families with kids: the crew are experienced with children, and most boats have safety equipment. Groups of friends: party boats with sound systems and coolers. Couples: a private sunset cruise or a romantic dinner on a catamaran. Solo travellers: join a group charter or book a small speedboat. Business groups: corporate charters for team building or client entertainment.

If you’re not a confident swimmer, no problem. The crew provides life jackets and can take you to shallow spots. If you’re prone to seasickness, stick to catamarans or large motor yachts, and take medication beforehand. The skipper will advise on the best anchor spots based on the weather.

Popular Itineraries for a Bali Boat Trip

Most boat rentals from Benoa or Padang Bai follow similar routes. Here are three common ones.

Nusa Penida and Nusa Lembongan. A full-day trip. You leave around 8am, arrive at Nusa Penida by 9am. Snorkel with manta rays at Manta Point. Then head to Nusa Lembongan for lunch at a beach club. Visit the mangroves or the Devil’s Tear cliffs. Back by 4pm. This is the most popular itinerary.

Gili Islands. From Padang Bai, it’s 1-2 hours by speedboat to the three Gilis: Trawangan, Meno, and Air. You can circle the islands, snorkel with turtles, and have lunch on Gili Trawangan. A full-day trip covers all three. Multi-day charters can include Lombok and the south coast.

Uluwatu and the west coast. A sunset cruise from Jimbaran or Seminyak. You sail past the cliffs of Uluwatu, anchor at a quiet cove for swimming, then watch the sunset over the Indian Ocean. This is a half-day option, usually 3-4 hours. Drinks and snacks included.

For longer trips, consider a 3-5 day charter to Komodo National Park. You sail east from Bali, overnight at Labuan Bajo, then explore the islands. You’ll see Komodo dragons, pink beaches, and world-class diving. This requires a larger boat with cabins. Prices from EUR 3,000 for a 3-day trip.

Safety and Regulations for Bali Boat Rentals

Bali has safety standards, but they’re not always enforced. With BoatHire24, all listed boats have valid licences, insurance, and safety equipment (life jackets, fire extinguishers, flares, first aid kit). The skipper holds a local licence and knows the waters. If you have concerns, ask the skipper before departure. You can also check the boat’s registration number.

Weather conditions can change quickly. The skipper will cancel if there’s a storm warning. You get a full refund in that case. For seasickness, bring your own medication or ask the crew for ginger tea. Drinking alcohol is fine, but don’t overdo it. The skipper reserves the right to refuse service to intoxicated guests.

For more tips on boat safety and etiquette, read our blog.

Environmental Considerations When Renting a Boat in Bali

Bali’s marine environment is fragile. Coral reefs are damaged by anchors, sunscreen, and plastic waste. When you rent a boat, choose a charter that follows sustainable practices. Many of our listed boats use mooring buoys instead of anchoring. They also provide reef-safe sunscreen and collect any rubbish. You can help by not touching coral, not feeding fish, and taking your trash back to shore.

Some charters support local conservation projects. Ask the skipper if they contribute to reef restoration or sea turtle protection. A small extra cost can go a long way.

Final Thoughts on Boat Rental Bali

Renting a boat in Bali opens up the islands in a way that land travel can’t. You avoid traffic, reach remote beaches, and see marine life up close. BoatHire24 makes it easy to find and book a skippered charter. Whether you want a party boat, a family day out, or a luxury escape, there’s an option for you. Use the search page to start, or contact us for a personalised recommendation. The water is waiting.

Comparing Departure Points: Benoa vs Padang Bai

If you’re staying in Seminyak, Canggu, or Nusa Dua, Benoa Harbour is your best bet. It’s 20 minutes from Ngurah Rai airport and has plenty of parking. Padang Bai, on the other hand, is 45 minutes from Ubud and 1.5 hours from the airport. The choice affects your trip time. From Benoa to Nusa Penida is 30 minutes by speedboat. From Padang Bai, it’s 45 minutes to the same spot. But Padang Bai gets you 20 minutes closer to the Gili Islands. Factor in traffic on the Bypass Ngurah Rai road, which can add 30 minutes in peak hours. BoatHire24 lists the exact departure coordinates for each boat, so you can plan your taxi or driver pickup.

Hidden Costs You Should Budget For

Beyond the base rental, expect to pay for port clearance fees. In Benoa, this is around EUR 15 per person for a day charter. Padang Bai charges EUR 10 per person. Some boats include these in the price, but many don’t. Snorkelling gear rental is another EUR 10-20 per set if not provided. If you want a photographer or videographer on board, budget EUR 150-300 for the day. Drinks and meals vary: a basic lunch spread costs EUR 15-25 per person, while a premium barbecue with seafood and cocktails runs EUR 40-60 per person. Tipping the crew is customary, usually 10-15% of the charter fee. Ask the skipper if the boat has a cash-only policy for extras, as some remote anchorages have no card machines.

Best Boat Types for Specific Activities

For snorkelling trips to Manta Point, choose a catamaran or a large motor yacht. They anchor steadily, and the crew can assist with gear. For a fishing charter, a speedboat or a dedicated fishing boat with outriggers works best. These boats have rod holders, bait tanks, and fish finders. Prices for a half-day fishing trip start around EUR 500. For a wedding or proposal, a luxury motor yacht with a flybridge and interior cabin is ideal. You get privacy, a sound system, and a dedicated space for decorations. The crew can arrange flowers, a cake, and a photographer. For a party with 20+ guests, a catamaran with a wide deck and a bar is the obvious choice. The trampolines at the front are great for lounging, and the jacuzzi adds a premium touch.

Seasonal Variations in Weather and Sea Conditions

July and August are the busiest months. The sea is calm, with wave heights rarely exceeding 1 metre. Visibility for snorkelling is 15-20 metres. In January and February, the wet season brings rougher seas, with waves of 2-3 metres in the Lombok Strait. Charters to the Gili Islands are often cancelled during these months. The best compromise is May or September. The weather is still good, but prices are 10-20% lower than peak season. October can be hit or miss, with occasional storms. If you book in the wet season, choose a boat with a covered deck and a cabin. The crew will monitor the weather and may change the itinerary to avoid storms. BoatHire24’s blog has monthly weather guides for Bali.

Multi-Day Charter Itineraries Beyond Komodo

If you have 5-7 days, consider a charter to the Raja Ampat islands in West Papua. This is a bucket-list trip for divers and nature lovers. You fly from Bali to Sorong, then board a liveaboard phinisi. Prices start from EUR 3,500 per person for a 7-day trip, including flights. The crew handles all logistics. You visit islands with limestone karsts, hidden lagoons, and some of the best coral reefs in the world. Alternatively, a 3-day charter to the Gili Islands and Lombok is more accessible. You sail from Padang Bai, spend a night on Gili Trawangan, then explore the south coast of Lombok, including the pink beach at Tangsi. This costs around EUR 2,000-3,000 for a group of 6-8 people, including meals and accommodation on the boat.

Practical Tips for First-Time Renters

Book at least two weeks in advance during peak season. For last-minute bookings, check the BoatHire24 search page for available boats. Bring a waterproof phone case and a dry bag for valuables. The crew can store your bag in a dry cabin, but it’s safer to keep it with you. Wear non-slip shoes on deck, especially on wet surfaces. If you plan to swim, bring a rash guard to protect against jellyfish stings, which are common from November to March. Ask the skipper about the current direction before jumping in. A strong current can pull you away from the boat quickly. The crew will deploy a line with a float for you to hold onto. For sunset cruises, bring a light jacket. The wind picks up after sunset, and temperatures drop to around 24 degrees C.

h1: Yacht Charter Maldives, Book Your Luxury Boat Holiday
intro:
You are probably looking at this page because you typed "yacht charter Maldives" into Google. We get it. The Maldives are stunning, but you are on the Costa del Sol, and you want the same turquoise water, private skipper, and luxury vibe without the 11-hour flight. Good news. BoatHire24 runs the largest boat-rental marketplace in Marbella, Puerto Banús, and the whole Costa del Sol. You can charter a yacht here that rivals anything in the Indian Ocean, and your skipper comes included. No licence needed. Just pick your boat, pick your port, and go.

This page explains exactly how a yacht charter in Marbella works, what you get, where you can sail, and how much it costs. We keep it honest. No marketing fluff. If you want a yacht charter that feels like the Maldives but is a 20-minute drive from your hotel, keep reading.
bodyHtml:
What You Get on a Yacht Charter in Marbella

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. You do not need a boating licence. You do not need to know how to dock. You just show up with your group, and the skipper handles everything. The boat is fully fuelled, cleaned, and equipped with safety gear, a sound system, and usually a cooler with ice. Some charters include a welcome drink or a small tapas platter. Most allow you to bring your own food and drinks, including alcohol. The skipper will take you to the best coves, help you anchor, and point out dolphins if they are around. You can swim, snorkel, paddleboard, or just sunbathe on the foredeck. The skipper stays out of your way but is always available. This is your private yacht for the day.

Ports You Can Depart From

You are not limited to one marina. BoatHire24 lists boats from six ports along the Costa del Sol. Puerto Banús is the most famous, with its superyachts and designer shops. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is smaller but central, with easy parking. Cabopino is a quiet, sandy-beach port near the dunes. Estepona has a charming old town and a long promenade. Sotogrande is the luxury enclave with huge villas and a golf course. Benalmádena is close to Malaga airport and has a lively marina with restaurants. You can choose the port that is closest to your accommodation or the one that offers the best route to the spots you want to visit. Each port has its own character, and the sailing time to the open sea is usually under 15 minutes.

Boat Types: From RIBs to Superyachts

You can charter almost any type of boat on BoatHire24. Motor yachts are the most popular: they are fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space. You can get a 40-foot motor yacht for around EUR 1,200 for a half day, or a 60-foot one for EUR 2,500. Catamarans are wider and more stable, great for families or large groups. A 40-foot catamaran costs from around EUR 1,500 for a full day. Sailing yachts are quieter and more traditional; a 36-foot sailing yacht starts at EUR 800 for a half day. RIBs and speedboats are fast and fun, ideal for a quick trip to a beach club. A 25-foot RIB costs from EUR 500 for two hours. Fishing boats are fully equipped with rods and a cooler; a half-day fishing charter starts at EUR 600. Licence-free day boats are small motorboats you can drive yourself without a licence, but they are limited to 10 hp and a 2-mile radius. Superyachts over 80 feet are available on request, with prices from EUR 10,000 per day.

Pricing Guidance: What You Will Actually Pay

We do not list exact prices for every boat because they change with season, demand, and duration. But here are realistic ranges. A half-day (4 hours) charter for a 40-foot motor yacht in low season (October to March) starts around EUR 900. In high season (June to September), the same boat costs from EUR 1,400. A full day (8 hours) for a 50-foot motor yacht in high season is around EUR 2,800. Catamarans are slightly more expensive because they are wider and newer. A 45-foot catamaran full day in high season costs from EUR 3,200. Sailing yachts are cheaper: a 40-foot sailing yacht full day in high season is around EUR 1,800. RIBs and speedboats are the most affordable: a 30-foot RIB for 2 hours costs from EUR 400. All prices include the skipper, fuel, insurance, and basic equipment. You pay extra for food, drinks, and any special requests like a photographer or a private chef. Always ask the owner for a full breakdown before booking.

Seasons: When to Go and What to Expect

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days a year. The high season for yacht charters is June through September. July and August are the busiest, with temperatures around 30 degrees C and sea temperatures of 24-26 degrees C. The water is warm, the beaches are full, and the marinas are buzzing. You should book at least two weeks in advance. May and October are shoulder months: temperatures are 22-26 degrees C, sea is 20-22 degrees C, and there are fewer crowds. You can often get a discount of 20-30 percent. November through March is low season. The weather is still good for sailing if you pick a sunny day, but you will need a jacket. Prices are at their lowest, and you can often book last-minute. April is a transition month, with flowers blooming and the sea warming up. If you want the Maldives experience of calm, clear water and hot sun, aim for July or August. If you prefer quieter anchorages and lower prices, try May or October.

Local Colour: What You Will See on the Water

The Costa del Sol is not just beaches. From the water, you see the Sierra Blanca mountains, with La Concha peak rising 1,270 metres behind Marbella. The Río Verde flows into the sea near Puerto Banús, creating a small estuary. Cala del Faro is a hidden cove east of Marbella, with a lighthouse and rocky cliffs. Estepona old town is visible from the sea, with whitewashed houses and a long beachfront. If you head south towards Gibraltar, you can spot dolphins playing in the Strait of Gibraltar. The current there is strong, so your skipper will know the best spots. North of Marbella, the coastline becomes more rugged, with cliffs and small coves near Cabopino. The Nerja caves are further east, but you cannot see them from the water; you can, however, anchor near the beach and take a short walk. Every charter is a mini adventure, and the skipper will tailor the route to what you want to see.

How to Book a Yacht Charter on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter your dates, group size, and preferred port. The search results show you available boats with photos, specifications, and prices. You can filter by boat type, length, and price range. Click on a boat to see the full listing, including what is included, the cancellation policy, and the skipper’s bio. You can message the owner directly through the platform to ask questions or negotiate the itinerary. Once you are happy, you book and pay securely online. The platform holds your payment until after the charter, so you are protected. You receive a confirmation with the skipper’s contact details and meeting point. On the day, you meet the skipper at the marina, sign a waiver, and board. It is that simple. No hidden fees, no surprises.

Who Is a Yacht Charter For

A yacht charter on the Costa del Sol works for almost everyone. Couples celebrating an anniversary or a honeymoon can book a private sailing yacht for a romantic sunset cruise. Families with children love catamarans because they are stable and have plenty of shade. Groups of friends rent motor yachts for party days with music and swimming. Business clients use superyachts for corporate events or client entertainment. Fishermen can charter specialised fishing boats with gear and bait. Even solo travellers can join a shared charter if they want to meet people. The only people who should not book are those who get seasick easily (though the Mediterranean is usually calm) or those on a very tight budget (a half-day charter costs at least EUR 400). For everyone else, it is a fantastic way to see the coast from a different perspective.

What to Bring and What to Expect on the Day

You need swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe is best), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket or long-sleeve shirt for the wind. Bring your own food and drinks unless you arranged catering. Most boats have a small fridge and a cooler. You can bring a Bluetooth speaker if the boat does not have one. The skipper will provide life jackets and a safety briefing. The boat will have a bathroom (called a head) and a small cabin for changing. On the water, you can swim, snorkel (bring your own mask or ask the skipper if they have one), or paddleboard if the boat includes one. The skipper will anchor in a calm cove for lunch. You can also stop at a beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club for a drink and a bite, but you need to arrange that in advance. The skipper will have a suggested itinerary, but you can ask to change it. The day is yours.

Why the Costa del Sol Beats the Maldives for a Yacht Charter

We are not saying the Maldives are bad. They are incredible. But for a yacht charter, the Costa del Sol has advantages. No long-haul flight. No jet lag. No time difference. You can fly into Malaga from almost any European city in under three hours, and be on a boat within an hour of landing. The cost is lower: a full-day luxury yacht charter here costs roughly half of what you would pay in the Maldives. You have more boat options: from RIBs to superyachts, all in one marketplace. You have more ports to choose from, each with its own vibe. You have the option to combine your charter with a visit to a beach club, a gourmet restaurant, or a historic town. And the water is warm enough for swimming from May to October. If you want the Maldives experience without the hassle, the Costa del Sol delivers.

Frequently Asked Questions About Yacht Charters in Marbella

We hear the same questions every day. Here are the answers. Do I need a licence? No, the skipper is included. What is included in the price? The boat, skipper, fuel, insurance, and basic equipment. Can I bring my own food? Yes, almost all charters allow it. Can I cancel? Yes, but check the cancellation policy on the listing. Most offer full refund if you cancel 7 days before. What happens if the weather is bad? The skipper will decide if it is safe to sail. If not, you can reschedule or get a refund. Can I swim? Yes, in designated coves. The skipper will choose a safe spot. How many people can I bring? The boat’s capacity is listed on the page. Do not exceed it. Can I bring a pet? Ask the owner; some allow small dogs. Is there a toilet on board? Yes, all boats over 30 feet have a head. What time do charters start? Usually 10am or 11am, but you can arrange a different time.

Ready to Book Your Yacht Charter

If you are still reading, you are probably serious about booking. The next step is simple. Go to the search page on BoatHire24, enter your dates and group size, and browse the available yachts. You can also read our blog for tips on the best coves, beach clubs, and itineraries. We have helped thousands of people charter yachts on the Costa del Sol, and we are confident you will find the perfect boat for your trip. Book now and secure your spot for the summer.

h1: Yacht Charter Corfu, Compare Boats with Skipper
intro:
You want a yacht charter Corfu, and you want it sorted without the usual holiday faff. Corfu has over 200 kilometres of coastline, turquoise coves and a hinterland that smells of olive groves and cypress. But renting a boat here can be a minefield of hidden fees, dodgy operators and boats that look nothing like the photos. BoatHire24 lists only verified vessels with licensed skippers, so you know exactly what you are getting.

Whether you want a sleek motor yacht for a wedding proposal, a catamaran for a family day out, or a RIB to chase the sunset along the north-east coast, we have options from EUR 450 for a half-day to several thousand for a superyacht. All charters include a professional skipper, fuel is usually extra, and you can depart from Corfu Town, Gouvia Marina, or smaller ports like Kassiopi and Petriti.

This page covers everything you need to know about booking a yacht charter in Corfu: boat types, ports, pricing, seasons, and how to book without getting stung. No fluff. Just the facts.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Yacht Charter Corfu

Every boat listed on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a boating licence, and you do not have to navigate the Ionian Sea yourself. The skipper knows the local waters, the best swimming spots, and where to find the quieter bays away from the day-tripper crowds. Most charters include the skipper’s fee in the base price, but always check the booking details because some operators charge extra for longer trips.

Fuel is typically not included. For a half-day charter (4-5 hours), expect to pay around EUR 80-150 in fuel for a motor yacht or RIB. Catamarans and sailing yachts use less fuel, often EUR 50-100. The skipper will refuel at the end of the trip, and you pay the actual cost. Food and drinks are not included, but you can bring your own or ask the operator to arrange catering (EUR 25-50 per person for a decent lunch).

Standard inclusions: life jackets, basic safety equipment, snorkelling gear (often), and a cooler with ice. Some boats have a Bluetooth speaker, a sun deck, and a small kitchenette. If you want extras like a water slide, paddleboard, or jet ski, those come at an additional cost, usually EUR 100-300 per item per day.

Corfu Departure Ports for Your Charter

Corfu has several departure points, and your choice affects the itinerary. The main port is Corfu Town (the New Port or the Old Port). From there, you can head north to the Diapontia Islands (Othonoi, Erikoussa, Mathraki) or south to the beaches of Agios Gordios and the southern tip. Gouvia Marina is the largest marina on the island, about 6 km north of Corfu Town, with plenty of parking and facilities. It is the most common departure point for motor yachts and catamarans.

Kassiopi, on the north-east coast, is a smaller port with a handful of charter operators. It is ideal if you are staying in the north and want quick access to the Albanian coast or the island of Corfu’s rugged north coast. Petriti, on the south-east coast, is a fishing village with a few RIB and speedboat rentals. It is quieter and cheaper, but boat options are limited.

For a full list of available boats and ports, check our search page and filter by location. You can also read our blog for detailed guides on each port.

Types of Boats for a Yacht Charter Corfu

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for a yacht charter Corfu. They range from 30 feet (around 9 metres) to 80 feet (24 metres). A 40-foot motor yacht sleeps 6-8 guests comfortably for a day trip and costs from EUR 800 for a half-day to EUR 1,500 for a full day. Larger yachts with flybridges, sun decks, and more powerful engines cost EUR 2,000-5,000 per day.

Catamarans are a good option if you value stability and space. A 40-foot catamaran has a wide beam, so it does not roll as much as a monohull. Perfect if anyone in your group gets seasick. Prices start from EUR 900 for a half-day and go up to EUR 2,000 for a full day. Sailing yachts are cheaper, from EUR 500 for a half-day, but they are slower and require more wind. If you just want to relax and let the skipper handle the sails, a sailing yacht is a romantic choice.

RIBs and speedboats are for the adrenaline seekers. A 7-metre RIB with a 200 HP outboard can hit 40 knots. Half-day from EUR 450, full day from EUR 700. They are open boats, so expect to get wet. Fishing boats are available for anglers, from EUR 600 for a half-day, with tackle and bait included. Licence-free day boats (under 10 HP) are also available from EUR 300 for a day, but you drive them yourself and they are limited to calm bays.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Charter Corfu

Prices vary wildly depending on the boat, season, and duration. As a rule of thumb, a half-day (4-5 hours) on a motor yacht starts from around EUR 800. A full day (8 hours) from EUR 1,200. Catamarans are slightly more expensive: half-day from EUR 900, full day from EUR 1,500. Sailing yachts are the cheapest: half-day from EUR 500, full day from EUR 800.

RIB/speedboat charters: half-day from EUR 450, full day from EUR 700. Fishing boats: half-day from EUR 600, full day from EUR 1,000. Superyachts (over 80 feet) are price on request, but expect EUR 5,000-15,000 per day. All prices are for the boat and skipper only. Fuel, food, drinks, and mooring fees are extra. Mooring fees at popular spots like the Blue Lagoon or Paxos can be EUR 20-50.

BoatHire24 does not add booking fees. You pay the same price as booking directly with the operator, and you get the security of our verification process. For exact prices on specific boats, check the search page.

Best Time of Year for a Yacht Charter Corfu

The season runs from April to October. May and June are the best months: warm (25-30 degrees C), low wind, and the water is clean. July and August are peak season: hot (35 degrees C), crowded, and prices are 20-30% higher. September is also good: still warm, fewer crowds, and the sea temperature is at its highest (26 degrees C). October is a gamble: you might get perfect weather or a storm.

If you are on a budget, book in May or late September. The water is still swimmable (20-22 degrees C), and you will have the coves mostly to yourself. Avoid August if you hate crowds, unless you want to party in the beach bars of Kavos or the north coast.

Wind conditions: the Meltemi wind can blow in July and August, making the sea choppy on the east coast. The west coast is usually calmer. Your skipper will adjust the route accordingly.

Popular Itineraries for a Yacht Charter Corfu

Most charters start from Corfu Town or Gouvia and head south or north. A typical half-day itinerary: depart at 10:00, cruise south to the beaches of Agios Gordios or the tiny islet of Vidos, swim and snorkel, then stop for lunch at a seaside taverna in Benitses or Perama. Return by 15:00.

A full-day itinerary: head north to the Diapontia Islands, about 1.5 hours from Corfu Town. Visit Othonoi (the westernmost point of Greece), swim in the Blue Cave of Erikoussa, and have lunch at a fish taverna on Mathraki. Return by 18:00. Alternatively, go south to the island of Paxos and Antipaxos, about 2 hours from Corfu. Swim in the turquoise waters of Antipaxos, explore the caves of Paxos, and eat in Gaios. This is a longer day, usually 9-10 hours.

For a shorter trip, stay on the east coast: visit the old fortress of Kassiopi, swim at Avlaki beach, and see the Albanian coast from the water. Your skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences.

Who Is a Yacht Charter Corfu For

Couples looking for a romantic day out, families with kids who want a safe and fun boat trip, groups of friends wanting to party on a catamaran, and corporate clients needing a professional event. The skipper handles everything, so you can relax. If you have a specific request, like a wedding ceremony at sea or a birthday celebration, let us know when you book.

BoatHire24 also caters to experienced sailors who want a bareboat charter (no skipper). But for a yacht charter Corfu, we recommend a skipper unless you know the Ionian waters well. The coast has hidden rocks, strong currents near the straits, and busy shipping lanes in the summer.

How to Book a Yacht Charter Corfu with BoatHire24

Go to BoatHire24 and enter Corfu as your destination. Use the filters to choose boat type, number of guests, and budget. You will see a list of boats with photos, specifications, and prices. Click on a boat to see the full details, including the cancellation policy, what is included, and the operator’s reviews.

Once you find a boat you like, select the date and duration, and proceed to checkout. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking, and the balance is due on the day of the charter, paid directly to the skipper. We send you a confirmation email with all the details. If you have questions before booking, use the contact form on the boat’s page to message the operator directly.

We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for July and August. For May and June, a week is usually enough. Last-minute bookings (1-2 days) are possible but limited.

Why Use BoatHire24 for Your Yacht Charter Corfu

We are a marketplace, not a charter company. We list boats from multiple operators, so you can compare prices and boats in one place. Every operator is vetted: we check their licences, insurance, and safety equipment. If something goes wrong, we mediate. We do not add booking fees, and we do not sell your data.

We also have a blog with detailed guides on Corfu, including the best beaches, restaurants, and hidden coves. Check it out for tips on planning your trip.

Licence-Free Day Boats in Corfu

If you want to drive a boat yourself without a licence, Corfu has a few options. Licence-free day boats are typically small motorboats under 10 HP, limited to calm bays and slow speeds. They cost from EUR 300 for a full day, and you get a quick briefing from the operator. You cannot go far from the departure port, but you can explore the coves around Gouvia or the east coast. These boats are popular with families who want a private picnic day. Book through BoatHire24 to see what is available in Corfu.

Corfu West Coast Charters

The west coast of Corfu is wilder and less developed than the east. Departing from Corfu Town, you can head west to Paleokastritsa, a resort with six beaches and a monastery on a cliff. The water is deep blue, and there are sea caves to explore. A half-day charter from Corfu Town to Paleokastritsa costs around EUR 800-1,000 for a motor yacht. Further south, you reach Agios Gordios, a long sandy beach with a rock formation called the "Ortholithi." The west coast has more swell than the east, so check with your skipper if you are prone to seasickness.

Diapontia Islands Itinerary Details

A full-day trip to the Diapontia Islands (Othonoi, Erikoussa, Mathraki) is a popular choice for a yacht charter Corfu. From Gouvia Marina, it takes about 1.5 hours to reach Othonoi at 20 knots. Othonoi has a Blue Cave that you can swim into, and a small village with a taverna serving fresh fish. Erikoussa is flatter, with a long sandy beach and a shipwreck. Mathraki has a single beach with a bar. Fuel for this trip is around EUR 100-150 for a motor yacht. The total cost for a full day is from EUR 1,200 plus fuel and food.

Paxos and Antipaxos Extended Trip

If you have a full day and want to see the famous turquoise waters of Antipaxos, you need a boat that can cruise at 25 knots or more. From Corfu Town, it is a 2-hour run south. Antipaxos has three main beaches: Voutoumi, Vrika, and Mesovrika. The water is so clear you can see the bottom at 10 metres depth. Paxos has the port of Gaios, with tavernas and shops. This trip is longer, usually 9-10 hours, and costs from EUR 1,500 for a motor yacht, plus fuel (EUR 150-200). Catamarans take longer but use less fuel. Check the search page for boats that offer this itinerary.

Evening Cruises and Sunset Charters

Sunset charters are a popular option in Corfu. A 3-hour evening cruise from Corfu Town or Gouvia costs from EUR 500 for a motor yacht. You cruise along the coast, watch the sunset over the Ionian Sea, and stop for a swim if the light allows. Some operators include a glass of wine or a light snack. For a more romantic experience, book a sailing yacht for EUR 400 for 3 hours. Sunset charters are available from May to September, with the best light in June and July. Bring a jacket, as it gets cooler after dark.

Booking Tips for Peak Season

In July and August, demand for a yacht charter Corfu is high. Book at least 3 weeks in advance for the best selection. Prices are 20-30% higher than in May or June. If you are flexible, consider a half-day charter instead of a full day, as many operators have availability for shorter trips. For last-minute bookings (1-3 days), call the operator directly through the contact form on BoatHire24. Some operators offer discounts for bookings made within 48 hours, but this is rare in August.

What to Bring on a Yacht Charter Corfu

Pack sunscreen (SPF 50, as the sun is strong), a hat, and sunglasses. Bring a towel, swimwear, and a change of clothes. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful for the evening. If you plan to snorkel, bring your own mask if you have one, as the ones provided are basic. For food and drinks, most operators allow you to bring a cooler. Some have a small fridge on board. Alcohol is fine, but do not overdo it, as the skipper may refuse to sail if anyone is dangerously drunk. For more tips, read our blog on preparing for a day at sea.
