h1: Boat Rental Bodrum, Your Guide to Hiring a Boat in Bodrum
intro:
You want a boat rental in Bodrum, Turkey, but you are looking at a site that specialises in Marbella and the Costa del Sol. We get that. Bodrum is a stunning destination with its castle, turquoise coves, and lively nightlife. But here is the thing: BoatHire24 is all about Marbella, Puerto Banús, and the rest of the Costa del Sol. We do not operate in Bodrum. So this page is a straight-up guide to help you find what you need, with a nudge to consider our waters instead. If you are flexible on location, we have a fantastic alternative waiting for you.

Let us be clear: we are not a global platform. We are a local marketplace for boat rentals on the Costa del Sol, Spain. But we know that many people searching for “boat rental Bodrum” might also be open to a Mediterranean trip that offers similar sun, sea, and luxury. So read on for practical advice on Bodrum boat hire, and then have a look at what we offer on the Spanish coast.
bodyHtml:
What to Expect from a Boat Rental in Bodrum

Bodrum sits on the Aegean coast of Turkey, famous for its whitewashed buildings, the medieval Castle of St. Peter, and a buzzing marina. Boat rentals here range from traditional wooden gulets to sleek motor yachts. You can hire a boat for a day trip to nearby bays, or for a week-long blue cruise along the coast. Most rentals include a captain and crew, but you can also find bareboat options if you have a licence. Prices vary wildly: a small motorboat might cost from around EUR 200 per day, while a luxury gulet for a week can run to several thousand euro. The season runs from April to October, with July and August being peak.

Why You Might Consider the Costa del Sol Instead

If you are still researching, let us give you a reason to compare. The Costa del Sol offers a similar climate, 300 days of sunshine a year, with water temperatures hitting 26 degrees C in summer. But the ports are closer together: Puerto Banús, Marbella, Estepona, Benalmádena. You can do multiple day trips without long transfers. And you get the bonus of the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can spot dolphins and maybe even whales. Plus, no visa complications for many nationalities. BoatHire24 lists hundreds of boats, all with licensed skippers, so you just turn up and relax.

Boat Types Available in Bodrum

In Bodrum you will find gulets (traditional two-masted wooden boats), motor yachts, sailing yachts, catamarans, and speedboats. Gulets are the classic choice for multi-day cruises along the Lycian coast. Motor yachts are popular for day charters to places like Orak Island or the Bodrum Peninsula. Catamarans offer more space and stability, good for families. If you want to fish, there are specialised fishing boats. But remember: in Bodrum, many boats are bareboat if you have a licence, whereas on the Costa del Sol almost all rentals include a skipper as standard.

Pricing Guidance for Bodrum Boat Hire

Prices in Bodrum depend on the season, boat size, and duration. A day charter on a 10-metre motor yacht can start from around EUR 400 in low season, rising to EUR 700 in August. A week on a gulet for six people might be EUR 3,000 to EUR 6,000. Luxury superyachts are price on request, often EUR 10,000 per week or more. Compare that to the Costa del Sol: a 12-metre motor yacht from Marbella might be EUR 800 per day in summer, but includes a skipper and fuel often. Our prices are transparent on the site.

Popular Routes and Destinations from Bodrum

Typical day trips from Bodrum go to the bay of Torba, the calm waters of Gümüşlük, or the thermal springs of Karaada. For longer cruises, you head to Datça, Knidos, or even down to Fethiye. The coastline is dotted with ancient ruins and secluded beaches. But the distances are longer: a trip from Bodrum to Fethiye is about 50 nautical miles, which takes half a day. On the Costa del Sol, you can cruise from Puerto Banús to Marbella in 20 minutes, or to Estepona in 40 minutes. More time swimming, less time transiting.

How to Book a Boat in Bodrum, and How We Do It

Booking a boat in Bodrum usually involves contacting a local agency or using a platform like GetYourGuide or Viator. You can also go through a broker. But you have to check what is included: fuel, crew, food, drinks, port fees. Many listings are not clear. With BoatHire24's search, every boat includes a licensed skipper, and the price shown typically covers the boat and skipper. You add extras like catering separately. No hidden fees. We also offer instant online booking for many boats, so you do not need to wait for a confirmation email.

Who Is Boat Rental in Bodrum For?

Bodrum is great for couples and groups who want a mix of history, nightlife, and sea. It suits people who enjoy traditional gulet cruises and don't mind longer sailing times. It is also popular with Turkish and European tourists who know the area. But if you are a family with young kids, or a group of friends who want a quick, hassle-free day on the water, the Costa del Sol might be more convenient. The beaches are closer, the ports have more facilities, and you can combine a boat trip with a visit to Marbella's old town or the Nerja caves.

Seasons and Weather in Bodrum vs Costa del Sol

Bodrum's high season is July and August, with temperatures hitting 35 degrees C. The sea is warm from June to October. The shoulder months of May and September are pleasant but can be windy. The Costa del Sol has a similar pattern, but the summer heat is tempered by sea breezes. Winters are milder, so you can even do a boat trip in March or November if the weather is good. The average water temperature in Marbella in August is 24 degrees C, slightly cooler than Bodrum's 26, but still very comfortable.

What's Included in a Boat Rental on the Costa del Sol

When you rent a boat through BoatHire24, you get a licensed skipper, insurance, and the boat for the agreed time. Fuel is sometimes included, sometimes extra, check the listing. You can add water toys, catering, or a hostess. The minimum rental is usually half a day (4 hours) for small boats, or full day (8 hours) for larger yachts. We also have licence-free day boats up to 15 metres that you can drive yourself after a short briefing. That is rare in Bodrum, where you usually need a licence for anything over a small dinghy.

Making the Choice: Bodrum or Marbella?

We are not going to pretend we are the same as Bodrum. But if you are looking for a Mediterranean boat holiday with guaranteed sun, luxury ports, and easy booking, the Costa del Sol is a strong alternative. You get the glamour of Puerto Banús, the views of La Concha mountain, and the chance to see dolphins in the Strait. Plus, you can combine your boat trip with tapas in Estepona old town or a visit to the Río Verde. If you decide to switch, we are here to help. If you stick with Bodrum, we wish you fair winds.

For more tips on boat rentals and destinations, check our blog where we cover everything from packing lists to the best anchorages on the Costa del Sol.

Navigating Bodrum's Ports and Marinas

Bodrum has several departure points. The main marina is Bodrum Marina, right next to the castle, with 450 berths and full facilities. You also have Milta Bodrum Marina, D-Marin Turgutreis about 20 km west, and Yalıkavak Marina on the northern peninsula. Each has its own vibe. Yalıkavak is more upmarket, with designer shops and fine dining. Turgutreis is quieter, good for a relaxed start. If you are staying in a hotel on the peninsula, your skipper can often pick you up from a nearby jetty. Check the departure port when booking, as transfer costs from Bodrum town can add EUR 50-100 to your day.

Boat Rental Bodrum: What You Actually Pay For

When you see a price for a boat rental in Bodrum, ask what is included. Many listings quote the boat only. Fuel for a day trip on a 12-metre motor yacht can be EUR 200-400 extra. Food and drinks are usually not included, though some gulet charters offer half-board. Port fees for stopping at places like Orak Island or Karaada might be EUR 10-30 per stop. Then there is the crew tip, typically 10-15% of the charter fee. On the Costa del Sol through BoatHire24, the price you see on the listing usually covers the boat and skipper, with fuel either included or clearly stated as extra. No surprise port fees.

Best Bays and Anchorages Near Bodrum

Within 30 minutes of Bodrum Marina you have Orak Island, a popular spot with clear water and a small beach. Gümüşlük Bay is a protected marine reserve, good for snorkelling among ancient ruins. Torba Bay is calm and sheltered, ideal for families. For lunch stops, many boats head to Yalıkavak or Türkbükü, where you can moor at a beach club. Farther afield, the bay of Cökertme offers a more rustic setting. The water temperature in August hits 26 degrees C, so you can swim without a wetsuit. Compare that to the Costa del Sol, where the water is 24 degrees C in August but the bays like Cala del Faro or Cabopino are equally beautiful and often less crowded.

Boat Rental Bodrum for Large Groups

If you are a group of 8-12 people, a gulet is the classic choice. A 20-metre gulet with 4 cabins costs from around EUR 4,000 per week in low season, rising to EUR 8,000 in August. That works out to EUR 500-1,000 per person for a week, including crew. For a day trip, a 15-metre motor yacht for 12 people might be EUR 1,000-1,500 per day in summer. On the Costa del Sol, a 15-metre motor yacht from Puerto Banús for 12 people is around EUR 1,200-1,800 per day, but includes a skipper and often fuel. The key difference: on the Costa del Sol, you can do a half-day charter for 4 hours, which is harder to find in Bodrum.

Bareboat vs Skippered Boat Rental Bodrum

Bodrum is one of the few places in the Mediterranean where you can rent a boat without a skipper if you have a recognised boating licence (ICC or equivalent). Small motorboats up to 20 hp often need no licence. Larger bareboat charters on sailboats or motor yachts require a licence and usually a check-out sail. This gives you freedom but also responsibility: you handle navigation, anchoring, and safety. If you are nervous about that, a skippered charter costs roughly 20-30% more but removes all stress. On the Costa del Sol, almost all boats through BoatHire24 come with a skipper, so you just relax. The exception is our licence-free day boats, which you can drive after a 15-minute briefing with no licence needed.

Boat Rental Bodrum in Low Season: Pros and Cons

May and September are the sweet spots for Bodrum. Temperatures are around 25-28 degrees C, the sea is warm enough for swimming (22-24 degrees C), and crowds are thinner. Prices for boat rentals drop by 20-30% compared to August. The wind can be stronger in May, especially the meltemi, which can make the sea choppy on the western side of the peninsula. October is still pleasant but the water cools to 22 degrees C, and some restaurants and beach clubs close after mid-month. On the Costa del Sol, the season runs from April to October, with water temperatures in October still around 20 degrees C, and many ports remain active year-round.

How to Combine Bodrum with Other Turkish Destinations

Many visitors combine a boat rental in Bodrum with a land trip to Ephesus (2 hours by road) or Pamukkale (3 hours). You can also do a one-way charter from Bodrum to Fethiye, dropping the boat at the other end. This is popular for week-long blue cruises. The distance is about 50 nautical miles, a full day of sailing. You pass Knidos, a ancient city with a beautiful harbour, and the Datça peninsula. If you have less time, a day trip from Bodrum to Knidos is possible but makes for a long day (2 hours each way). For a more compact experience, the Costa del Sol lets you visit multiple ports in a single day without long transits.

Boat Rental Bodrum for Fishing Enthusiasts

Bodrum has good fishing grounds, especially for bottom fishing and trolling. You can rent a specialised fishing boat with a crew who know the spots. Common catches include sea bream, grouper, and bonito. A half-day fishing charter for 4 people costs from around EUR 300-500, including bait and tackle. The best months are May to October. On the Costa del Sol, fishing charters from Estepona or Sotogrande target similar species plus tuna and swordfish in the Strait of Gibraltar. Prices are comparable, but the Costa del Sol offers the added thrill of dolphin sightings on almost every trip.

What to Bring on a Boat Rental Bodrum

Pack sunscreen (factor 50, the sun is strong), a hat, sunglasses, a light jacket for the evening, and swimwear. If you are prone to seasickness, bring medication or acupressure bands, especially if you are doing a long crossing. Most boats have a cooler for drinks, but you should bring your own water and snacks unless catering is included. A waterproof phone case is useful. On the Costa del Sol, the conditions are similar, but the water is slightly cooler, so a thin wetsuit or rash vest can be comfortable. Our blog has a full packing list for a day on the water: check the BoatHire24 blog for details.

Boat Rental Bodrum vs Costa del Sol: The Verdict on Convenience

If you value independence and want to explore the Turkish coast at your own pace, Bodrum's bareboat options are appealing. If you want a stress-free day with a skipper who handles everything, the Costa del Sol is more straightforward. The booking process on BoatHire24 is instant for many boats, you pay online and get a confirmation within minutes. In Bodrum, you often have to email or call to check availability, and payment is sometimes cash on the day. Also, the language barrier can be an issue in smaller marinas. The Costa del Sol has a large English-speaking expat community, so communication is easy.

h1: Catamaran Charter Miami, Book Your Day on the Water
intro:
If you are looking for a catamaran charter in Miami, you are probably after space, stability, and a bit of style. Catamarans are the sensible choice for a group that wants to spread out, sunbathe on nets, and avoid the constant heel of a monohull. They work well for birthday parties, corporate events, or just a day of cruising past the Miami skyline and the sandbars of Biscayne Bay.

BoatHire24 connects you with catamaran owners and charter companies in Miami. You pick the boat, the duration, and the extras. We handle the admin. No skipper licence required because every charter includes a professional captain. You just show up and enjoy the ride.
bodyHtml:
What a Catamaran Charter in Miami Includes

Most catamarans in Miami come with a captain and crew. The captain handles navigation, safety, and docking. Some charters also include a deckhand or a stewardess, depending on the size of the boat and the package you choose. Fuel is usually included for a set number of hours, but check the terms because some operators charge extra for extended cruising.

Standard inclusions are: a Bluetooth sound system, a cooler with ice, basic safety equipment, and a toilet (or two, on larger models). Some boats have a small galley with a fridge and a hob. Others offer a full kitchen and a barbecue on the aft deck. You can bring your own food and drinks, or order catering through the charter company. Many operators in Miami also let you add water toys: paddleboards, jet skis, inflatable slides, or snorkel gear.

If you want a party boat, look for a catamaran with a large flybridge, a swim platform, and a bow net. If you prefer a quieter day, choose a cruising cat with shaded seating and a cabin you can retreat to.

Why Choose a Catamaran Over a Motor Yacht

Catamarans have two hulls, which means they do not roll as much as a monohull motor yacht. That matters if anyone in your group gets seasick. The wide beam gives you more deck space per foot of length, so a 40-foot catamaran feels bigger than a 50-foot motor yacht. The shallow draft lets you get closer to sandbars and beaches, which is useful in Miami’s shallow waters around Key Biscayne and the sandbars of the Venetian Islands.

Catamarans are also more fuel-efficient than a similar-sized power boat. That translates to lower fuel surcharges and, sometimes, lower charter rates. The trade-off is speed. Most sailing catamarans cruise at 7-10 knots under power, whereas a motor yacht can hit 20-30 knots. If you want to cover distance quickly, a power catamaran (like a Leopard 40 PC or a Fountaine Pajot MY range) is a better bet.

Popular Miami Itineraries for a Catamaran Charter

Miami is a city that looks best from the water. A typical half-day charter (4 hours) covers the Miami skyline, the Port of Miami cruise ships, and the Venetian Islands. You can anchor off Monument Island for a swim and a photo with the skyline behind you.

For a full day (8 hours), head south to Biscayne National Park and the Boca Chita Key lighthouse. You can snorkel in the clear waters of the park, spot manatees, and have lunch on the boat. Alternatively, go north to Haulover Sandbar, a popular spot where dozens of boats anchor and party on weekends. The sandbar is shallow enough to stand in, and you can walk between boats.

If you want a longer charter, consider a sunset cruise that includes dinner on the boat and a slow drift back to the marina as the city lights come on. Some operators also offer overnight charters to the Florida Keys, but that is a different price category and usually requires a multi-day booking.

Types of Catamarans Available in Miami

Catamarans in Miami range from 35 feet to 60 feet. The most common models are the Lagoon 42, the Leopard 45, and the Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40. These are sailing catamarans with twin 40-60 HP diesel engines. They have 4-6 cabins and can sleep 8-12 guests overnight. For day charters, the number of cabins matters less than the deck space and the amenities.

Power catamarans are less common but available. The Aquila 44 and the Leopard 40 PC are popular choices. They offer more speed (up to 25 knots) and a more modern layout with a large aft deck and a flybridge. Prices for power cats start from around EUR 1,500 for a half day, versus EUR 1,200 for a sailing cat of the same size.

Luxury catamarans (50 feet and above) come with a crew of two or three, a full galley, and higher-end finishes. The Lagoon 52 or the Sunreef 60 are examples. Those start from around EUR 3,000 for a half day and go up to EUR 8,000 for a full day with premium catering and water toys.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Charter Miami

Prices vary by boat size, age, season, and duration. As a rough guide, a half-day charter (4 hours) on a 40-foot sailing catamaran starts from around EUR 1,000 in the low season (May to October). A full day (8 hours) on the same boat costs from EUR 1,500. In peak season (November to April), add 20-30% to those figures.

Larger cats (50 feet+) start from EUR 2,000 for a half day and EUR 3,500 for a full day. Power catamarans are generally 15-20% more expensive than sailing cats of the same size. Extras like jet skis, inflatable water parks, or a photographer cost extra. Catering adds EUR 50-100 per person depending on the menu.

Always confirm what is included in the price: fuel, taxes, crew gratuity, and dock fees are sometimes separate. The charter contract should list all charges. If it does not, ask before you pay.

Best Time of Year for a Catamaran Charter in Miami

Miami has a subtropical climate. The best weather is from November to April, when temperatures are 20-28 degrees C and humidity is low. That is also the peak season, so book at least a month in advance. From May to October, it is hotter (30-35 degrees C) and more humid, with afternoon thunderstorms. The rain usually passes quickly, and the water is warm (26-30 degrees C).

Hurricane season runs from June to November. The risk of a direct hit is low, but charter companies may cancel if a storm is forecast. Make sure you understand the cancellation policy before booking. Most operators offer a full refund if the charter is cancelled due to weather 48 hours before departure.

Weekends are busier at the marinas and sandbars. If you want a quieter experience, book a weekday charter. The same boat costs the same regardless of the day, but you will have more space at the anchorages.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter in Miami with BoatHire24

Go to our search page and filter by boat type: catamaran. Enter your preferred date and duration. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on a listing to see the full details, including crew qualifications, included amenities, and cancellation terms.

Once you choose a boat, send an inquiry through the platform. The owner or charter manager will confirm availability and send you a booking proposal. You can ask questions, request extras, or negotiate the price. When you are happy, pay a deposit (usually 50%) to secure the date. The balance is due 7-14 days before departure.

BoatHire24 does not charge a booking fee. You pay the charter price directly to the boat owner. We make money from a small commission paid by the owner, so our interests are aligned with yours: we want you to have a good experience and come back.

Who Should Book a Catamaran Charter in Miami

Catamarans are ideal for groups of 6-12 people who want to socialise, swim, and relax. They are not the best choice if you want to waterski or wakeboard at high speed, because the twin hulls create a wide wake and the boats are not designed for towing. For watersports, a centre-console powerboat or a RIB is better.

If you are celebrating a birthday, a bachelor or bachelorette party, or a corporate event, a catamaran gives you enough space to mingle without feeling crowded. The flat deck and the lack of heeling make it safe for children and elderly guests. You can bring food, drinks, and a playlist, and the captain will handle the rest.

For a romantic sunset cruise for two, a smaller catamaran (35-40 feet) works well. You get privacy, a dedicated crew, and the option to anchor in a quiet cove. Some operators offer a private chef on board for an additional fee.

What to Bring on a Catamaran Charter in Miami

Bring sunscreen (reef-safe is preferred), a hat, sunglasses, and a towel. The sun in Miami is strong even in winter. A light jacket or a windbreaker is useful if you plan to be on the water after sunset. Swimwear is mandatory, but most people change on the boat. There are toilets on board.

If you bring food and drinks, pack them in a soft cooler. The boat will have a cooler with ice, but space is limited. Do not bring glass bottles because they can break and cause injuries. Plastic, cans, and cardboard are fine. Some charter companies provide a cooler and ice, but confirm in advance.

Music is usually streamed via Bluetooth. Bring your phone or a tablet with a playlist. The boat’s sound system is typically compatible with any device. If you want to take photos, a waterproof camera or a phone case is a good idea, especially if you plan to swim.

Safety and Legal Requirements for Catamaran Charter in Miami

All catamaran charters in Miami include a licensed captain. You do not need a boating licence. The captain is responsible for safety, navigation, and compliance with Coast Guard regulations. The boat must carry life jackets, a first aid kit, fire extinguishers, and an emergency beacon. Ask the crew to give a safety briefing at the start of the charter.

Miami has strict rules about alcohol consumption on boats. The captain cannot drink, and passengers cannot be drunk to the point of being a danger. Open containers are allowed, but the crew has the right to end the charter early if behaviour is unsafe. Most charter companies require a security deposit (EUR 500-1,000) against damage. If you break something, you pay for it.

If you are chartering a catamaran for a wedding or a large event, you may need a special event permit from the City of Miami or Miami-Dade County. The charter company can advise on that. Allow extra time for paperwork.

Comparing Catamaran Charter Miami to Other Destinations

Miami is one of the most accessible catamaran charter destinations in the US. The marinas are close to the airport, the weather is reliable, and the variety of boats is high. Compared to the British Virgin Islands or the Bahamas, Miami charters are more expensive per day but offer more infrastructure: restaurants, hotels, and nightlife are a short walk from the dock.

If you want a quieter, more nature-focused charter, consider the Florida Keys or the Everglades. Those are a 1-2 hour drive from Miami. If you want a party atmosphere, Miami is hard to beat. The sandbars and the bay are packed with boats on weekends, and the energy is high.

BoatHire24 also lists catamarans in BoatHire24 other locations, including Marbella and the Costa del Sol, where the vibe is more Mediterranean and less commercial. But for a Miami-style catamaran charter, you are in the right place.

Frequently Asked Questions About Catamaran Charter Miami

Departure Marinas for Catamaran Charters in Miami

Most catamarans in Miami depart from one of three main marinas. Miamarina at Bayside is the most central, right next to the Bayside Marketplace and the Miami skyline. It is convenient if you are staying in downtown Miami or Brickell. The marina has parking, restaurants, and a fuel dock. A second option is Dinner Key Marina in Coconut Grove, which is quieter and closer to Biscayne Bay. It is the departure point for many sailing charters. A third option is the Miami Beach Marina on the Venetian Causeway. That gives you quick access to the Atlantic Ocean and the sandbars off South Beach. Each marina has its own vibe, but the charter price is the same regardless of where you leave from.

How Catamaran Charter Prices Compare to Other Boat Types in Miami

A catamaran charter in Miami costs roughly the same as a motor yacht of the same length, but you get more space. A 42-foot sailing catamaran costs from EUR 1,200 for a half day. A 42-foot motor yacht of the same age costs from EUR 1,000, but the deck space is smaller and the interior feels more cramped. If you have 10-12 guests, the catamaran is better value per person. A RIB or a speedboat of the same length costs less (from EUR 600 for a half day) but offers no shade, no toilet, and limited seating. For a group that wants to socialise and relax, the catamaran is the right choice. For a fast trip to the sandbar, a speedboat is cheaper and faster.

What the Weather Means for Your Catamaran Charter in Miami

Miami weather is predictable enough that you can plan a charter months ahead, but you need to be flexible on the day. In summer, afternoon thunderstorms build over the Everglades and move east across the bay between 2pm and 5pm. If you book a half-day charter from 10am to 2pm, you usually avoid the rain. If you book a full day, the captain will adjust the route to stay in protected waters or wait out the storm under the Rickenbacker Causeway. In winter, cold fronts bring north winds of 20-25 knots, which can make Biscayne Bay choppy. Catamarans handle chop better than monohulls, but the ride is still bumpy. The best conditions are a light breeze from the east or southeast, which is common in spring and autumn.

How to Choose the Right Catamaran for Your Group Size

If your group has 6-8 people, a 38-42 foot catamaran is enough. You get a decent deck, a shaded cockpit, and a small cabin for changing. If you have 10-12 people, go for a 45-50 foot catamaran. The extra length gives you a larger flybridge and a swim platform that does not get overcrowded. If you have more than 12, you need a 55 foot plus catamaran or a motor yacht, because the US Coast Guard limits passenger capacity on most catamarans to 12 or 18, depending on the boat’s safety certification. Check the listing for the maximum number of guests allowed. Do not exceed it, because the captain can refuse to depart if you show up with more people than booked.

Extras You Can Add to a Catamaran Charter in Miami

Most charter companies offer add-ons that turn a simple day on the water into a full experience. A jet ski rental costs around EUR 300-500 for a few hours, delivered to your catamaran at the sandbar. An inflatable water slide or a floating mat costs from EUR 200. A photographer or a videographer can join the charter for EUR 400-800 for a half day. Catering ranges from a simple sandwich platter (EUR 25 per person) to a full barbecue with steak and lobster (EUR 80 per person). Some operators also offer a bartender for EUR 200 extra. If you want flowers, balloons, or a cake for a celebration, those are usually arranged separately but the charter company can recommend a provider.

What Happens If You Need to Cancel a Catamaran Charter in Miami

Cancellation policies vary by boat owner, but the standard in Miami is a 50% refund if you cancel 14 days before the charter, and no refund if you cancel within 7 days. If the charter is cancelled by the owner due to weather or mechanical issues, you get a full refund or the option to reschedule. Some owners offer a partial refund if you cancel within 7 days and they manage to rebook the boat. Ask about this before you pay the deposit. BoatHire24 recommends buying trip insurance for charters over EUR 2,000, especially if you are travelling from out of town. Insurance covers cancellations for illness, flight delays, and other personal reasons that are not the owner’s fault.

bodyHtml:
Why a Yacht Charter on the Costa del Sol Beats Santorini

Santorini is famous for its caldera views, white-washed villages, and sunsets. But it is also crowded, expensive in peak season, and the wind can make boat trips uncomfortable. On the Costa del Sol, you get a similar volcanic coastline near Cabopino, the sandy beaches of Marbella, and the exclusive marina of Puerto Banús. The water temperature in summer hits 24-26 degrees C, same as the Aegean. You can anchor at Cala del Faro, swim in the Río Verde estuary, or cruise to the Strait of Gibraltar to spot dolphins. The biggest difference: you do not need to queue for a ferry or fight for a sunbed.

BoatHire24 gives you access to over 200 boats in five ports: Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, and Sotogrande. You can also depart from Benalmádena. All charters include a licensed skipper, so you do not need a boating licence. You just pick a boat, choose a duration (half-day, full-day, or multi-day), and go.

If you are planning a holiday in southern Spain and want a yacht charter experience that rivals Santorini, you are in the right place. The prices are competitive, the service is professional, and the scenery is just as good.

What Is Included in a Yacht Charter on the Costa del Sol

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That is the standard. You do not need to worry about navigation, docking, or safety checks. The skipper handles everything. Some charters also include a hostess or a chef, depending on the boat and the package. Fuel is usually extra, but some operators include it for half-day trips. Check the listing details before booking.

Most boats come with snorkelling gear, a sound system, and a cooler for drinks. Catamarans often have a trampoline net at the front, which is perfect for lounging. Motor yachts have a flybridge with sun pads. Sailing yachts give you the authentic wind-powered experience. You can bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package through the operator. Some charters include a barbecue on board.

The typical half-day charter is 4 hours. A full-day charter is 8 hours. Multi-day charters let you explore further, like a trip to the Nerja caves or across the Strait of Gibraltar to Morocco. You can also book sunset cruises, which are popular in Puerto Banús.

For a full breakdown of what to expect, check the search page and filter by boat type and port.

Ports of Departure for Your Yacht Charter

You can depart from any of these ports, depending on where you are staying:

Puerto Banús, The most famous marina on the Costa del Sol. It is where the superyachts park. You will find luxury motor yachts, catamarans, and sailing yachts here. The atmosphere is glamorous, with designer shops and restaurants. Departing from here puts you close to the Marbella coastline and the exclusive beaches of the Golden Mile.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), A smaller, more relaxed marina in the centre of Marbella. It is close to the old town and the beach promenade. Good for half-day trips to Cabopino or Cala del Faro.

Cabopino, A quiet marina near the dunes of Artola. The beach here is less crowded. Ideal for a peaceful day on the water. You can anchor at the nearby coves.

Estepona, A charming town with a pretty old town and a marina that is less touristy. Depart from here to explore the coast towards Gibraltar. You might see dolphins near the Strait.

Sotogrande, An exclusive residential area with a large marina. It is further south, closer to Gibraltar. Good for longer charters towards Tarifa or the African coast.

Benalmádena, A lively marina with a lot of charter options. It is east of Marbella, near Fuengirola. You can combine a boat trip with a visit to the Benalmádena cable car or the marina's restaurants.

Each port has its own character. If you want the Santorini vibe of white buildings and blue water, Puerto Banús is the closest match, but with more bling.

Boat Types Available for Your Charter

You can choose from several boat types, each suited to a different experience:

Motor yachts, Fast, luxurious, and spacious. Typically 12-20 metres long. They have a flybridge, a saloon, and cabins. Ideal for parties, families, or a group of friends. Prices from around EUR 800 for a half-day.

Catamarans, Stable and roomy. They have a wide deck, a trampoline at the front, and a shaded cockpit. Perfect for relaxing, swimming, and sunbathing. Prices from around EUR 600 for a half-day.

Sailing yachts, For the purist. You get the feel of the wind and the sound of the sea. Slower than motor yachts, but more authentic. Prices from around EUR 500 for a half-day.

RIBs and speedboats, Small, fast, and open. Good for a thrilling ride to a secluded cove. Usually 6-8 metres. Prices from around EUR 300 for a half-day.

Fishing boats, Equipped for deep-sea fishing. The skipper knows the best spots for tuna, sea bass, and bream. Prices from around EUR 400 for a half-day.

Licence-free day boats, Small motorboats that do not require a boating licence. You can drive them yourself (no skipper included). Limited to certain areas and weather conditions. Prices from around EUR 200 for a half-day.

Superyachts, For the ultimate luxury. Over 24 metres, with a crew, jacuzzi, and full amenities. Price on request. Usually requires a minimum full-day booking.

If you are not sure which type to pick, the BoatHire24 homepage has a quick filter to compare options.

Pricing Guidance for Your Yacht Charter

Prices vary by boat size, type, season, and duration. Here is a rough guide:

Half-day (4 hours), From around EUR 300 for a small RIB, EUR 500 for a sailing yacht, EUR 600 for a catamaran, EUR 800 for a motor yacht, and EUR 1,500+ for a superyacht.

Full-day (8 hours), From around EUR 600 for a RIB, EUR 900 for a sailing yacht, EUR 1,200 for a catamaran, EUR 1,500 for a motor yacht, and EUR 3,000+ for a superyacht.

Multi-day (overnight or longer), Price on request. Typically includes accommodation in cabins, meals, and longer cruising range. Expect to pay from EUR 2,000 per day for a motor yacht with cabins.

Fuel is usually extra, around EUR 100-300 per trip depending on the boat and distance. Some operators include it in the price, so check the listing. Catering is extra, typically EUR 20-40 per person for a lunch menu.

Peak season (July-August) prices are 20-30% higher. Shoulder season (May-June, September-October) is cheaper and the weather is still good. Winter (November-April) is low season, but you can still charter if the weather permits, especially for fishing trips.

All prices are in EUR. You can pay by card or bank transfer. A deposit of 30-50% is usually required at booking, with the balance due on the day.

For a precise quote, use the search filters on the search page.

Best Time of Year for a Yacht Charter on the Costa del Sol

The best months are May through October. June, July, and August are the hottest, with temperatures hitting 30-35 degrees C. The sea is warm (24-26 degrees C). July and August are the busiest, so book early. September and October are still warm but less crowded. The water stays warm until late October.

If you want to avoid the heat, May and June are pleasant, with temperatures around 22-28 degrees C. The sea is cooler in May (around 18-20 degrees C) but still swimmable.

Winter charters are possible, especially for fishing or a scenic cruise. The weather is milder than in Santorini, with temperatures around 15-20 degrees C. The water is cold (around 15 degrees C), so swimming is less appealing, but the views are still good.

For sunset cruises, the best time is from May to September, when the sun sets late (around 9 pm). The sunset from the sea, with La Concha mountain in the background, is a highlight.

How to Book a Yacht Charter on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the homepage and use the search bar. Enter your preferred port, date, and number of guests. Browse the results. Each listing shows the boat type, size, capacity, price, and available dates. Click on a listing to see full details, photos, and the cancellation policy.

Once you find a boat you like, click the "Book Now" button. Fill in your details and pay the deposit. The operator will confirm your booking within 24 hours. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and meeting point.

If you have questions, you can contact the operator directly through the listing page. Or email BoatHire24 support for help. We recommend booking at least 2-3 weeks in advance during peak season. Last-minute bookings are possible, but availability is limited.

For more tips on the booking process, read our blog about how to choose the right boat.

Who Is a Yacht Charter on the Costa del Sol For

This is for anyone who wants a luxury boat experience without the hassle of Santorini. It is for couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise. It is for families with kids who want a safe, stable catamaran with a skipper. It is for groups of friends who want to party on a motor yacht. It is for fishing enthusiasts who want to catch tuna in the Strait of Gibraltar. It is for solo travellers who want to join a shared charter (some operators offer shared trips).

It is also for people who are already on the Costa del Sol for a holiday and want a day on the water. Or for locals who want a weekend escape. The flexibility of half-day charters means you can fit it into a busy itinerary.

If you are searching for a yacht charter Santorini, but you are actually planning a trip to Spain, this is your alternative. Same vibe, different location.

Local Highlights You Will See on Your Charter

The Costa del Sol coastline is varied. From Puerto Banús, you can cruise west towards Cabopino and see the dunes of Artola. East towards Marbella, you pass the Golden Mile and the old town. Further east, you reach Cala del Faro, a secluded cove with a lighthouse. The water is clear and calm.

If you depart from Estepona or Sotogrande, you can head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. This is where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean. You often see dolphins and whales. The current is strong, so the skipper will handle the navigation. You can also see the coast of Africa on a clear day.

For a longer charter, you can go to the Nerja caves. The caves are a 2-hour cruise from Marbella. You can anchor near the cliffs and take a tender to the shore. The caves are a natural wonder, with stalactites and stalagmites.

The Río Verde is a small river near Marbella. You can anchor in the estuary and swim in the freshwater. It is a popular spot for paddleboarding and kayaking.

bodyHtml:
What a Yacht Rental Nice Actually Means on the Costa del Sol

When you search for a yacht rental Nice, you probably imagine a sleek motor yacht moored in the old port, with views of the Baie des Anges. BoatHire24 cannot offer that because we are based in Marbella, but we can offer something better: a private charter from Puerto Banús, the most famous marina in Spain. The boats are similar, Sunseeker, Azimut, Beneteau, and the service is identical. You get a licensed skipper, a clean boat, and a flexible itinerary. The difference is the backdrop: La Concha mountain, the Rio Verde valley, and the golden beaches of the Costa del Sol.

The term 'yacht rental Nice' is a search phrase that people use when they want a high-end boating experience in the Mediterranean. BoatHire24 delivers that experience from the Spanish coast. The water temperature in summer reaches 24 degrees C. The sailing season runs from April to October, with peak conditions in July and August. You can book a half-day (4 hours) or a full day (8 hours), and you can choose from motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, RIBs, and fishing boats. Every charter includes insurance, fuel, and a skipper. No hidden extras.

If you are still fixated on Nice, you can fly into Malaga Airport (AGP) and be on a boat in Puerto Banús within 45 minutes. That is faster than driving from Nice Airport to the port. The cost is lower too. A comparable motor yacht in Nice might set you back EUR 2,000 for a day. On the Costa del Sol, you can get a similar vessel for around EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,800. The difference pays for your dinner.

Departure Ports for Your Yacht Rental

BoatHire24 offers charters from six main ports along the Costa del Sol. Each has its own character and advantages.

Puerto Banús is the most glamorous. It is the home of superyachts, designer boutiques, and celebrity sightings. If you want to feel like you are in Nice, this is the closest you will get. Depart from here for a cruise to Cala del Faro or the Marbella coastline.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more relaxed. It is a working marina with a mix of fishing boats and leisure craft. Good for a quick departure if you are staying in Marbella town.

Cabopino is a small, quiet port near the dunes of Artola. Ideal if you want to avoid the crowds. The channel is narrow, so only smaller boats can dock here, but the nearby coves are pristine.

Estepona has a charming old town and a long promenade. The marina is modern and well-equipped. Depart from here for a trip to the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can spot dolphins and pilot whales.

Sotogrande is an exclusive residential area with a world-class marina. It is further west, closer to Gibraltar. Good for a longer charter that includes a stop at the rock.

Benalmádena is a lively port with a large marina and plenty of bars and restaurants. It is east of Marbella, near Malaga. A good option if you are staying on the eastern Costa del Sol.

Each port has a link on the search page where you can filter by location and boat type.

Boat Types Available for Yacht Rental Nice

You can choose from five main categories. The right one depends on your group size, budget, and what you want to do.

Motor yachts are the classic choice. They are fast, comfortable, and have plenty of deck space. Typical models include the Sunseeker 50, Azimut 55, and Princess 60. Speeds range from 20 to 30 knots. Prices start from around EUR 1,000 for a half-day for a 40-foot yacht, up to EUR 4,000 for a full day on a 60-footer.

Catamarans are stable and spacious. They have wide decks, a shallow draft, and are ideal for families or groups who want to avoid seasickness. A Lagoon 42 or Fountaine Pajot 45 costs from EUR 1,200 for a half-day. Top speed is lower, around 10 knots, but the comfort is higher.

Sailing yachts are for the purists. You can help hoist the sails or just relax while the skipper does the work. A 40-foot Beneteau or Jeanneau costs from EUR 800 for a half-day. The experience is slower and quieter.

RIBs and speedboats are for adrenaline. They are small, fast, and open. A 30-foot RIB with twin 250 HP engines can hit 40 knots. Prices start from around EUR 400 for a half-day. Good for a quick trip to a beach club or a dolphin-watching run.

Fishing boats are purpose-built for angling. They have rod holders, a fish finder, and a fighting chair. A half-day charter costs from EUR 500. You can target tuna, dorado, or sea bass.

Licence-free day boats are for small groups who want to drive themselves. They are typically under 6 meters and have a low-power engine. No licence is needed in Spain for boats under 6 meters and 15 HP. Prices start from around EUR 250 for a half-day.

Superyachts are available on request. If you want a 30-meter vessel with a crew of five, a jacuzzi, and a helipad, we can arrange it. Prices are on request, but expect EUR 10,000 or more per day.

Pricing Guidance for Yacht Rental Nice

Prices vary by boat type, size, season, and duration. The following are typical ranges for a half-day (4 hours) and full day (8 hours) in the high season (June to September).

Motor yacht 40-50 ft: EUR 1,000 to EUR 2,500 for a half-day. Full day: EUR 1,800 to EUR 4,500.

Catamaran 40-50 ft: EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,800 for a half-day. Full day: EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000.

Sailing yacht 40-50 ft: EUR 800 to EUR 1,500 for a half-day. Full day: EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000.

RIB 25-35 ft: EUR 400 to EUR 800 for a half-day. Full day: EUR 700 to EUR 1,500.

Fishing boat: EUR 500 to EUR 1,000 for a half-day. Full day: EUR 900 to EUR 2,000.

Licence-free day boat: EUR 250 to EUR 500 for a half-day. Full day: EUR 450 to EUR 900.

Superyacht 25m+: price on request. Typically from EUR 8,000 per day.

All prices include the skipper, fuel, insurance, and VAT. Extras like food, drinks, and port fees are usually extra. You can bring your own or ask the charter company to arrange catering.

For a detailed breakdown of costs, read the Boat Rental Marbella Prices blog post.

Best Seasons for a Yacht Rental Nice on the Costa del Sol

The Costa del Sol has a long season. The best weather is from May to October, but you can sail as early as March and as late as November.

April to May: Air temperatures 18-22 degrees C. Water still cool at 16-18 degrees C. Fewer crowds, lower prices. Good for sailing and fishing.

June to September: Peak season. Air temperatures 25-32 degrees C. Water 20-24 degrees C. Busy ports, higher prices, but perfect conditions for swimming and sunbathing.

October: Still warm, 22-26 degrees C. Water 20-22 degrees C. Quieter. Good value.

November to March: Cooler, 15-20 degrees C. Water 14-16 degrees C. Some days are sunny, but wind can be strong. Fishing is good. Prices are lowest. Many boats are in winter storage, so availability is limited.

If you want to guarantee a specific boat, book at least 2 weeks in advance for July and August. For other months, 1 week is usually enough.

What Is Included in Your Yacht Rental

Every charter through BoatHire24 includes the following as standard:

A licensed skipper with insurance and relevant qualifications. The skipper speaks English and Spanish. They know the local waters and can recommend anchorages.

Fuel for the duration of the charter. You do not pay extra for diesel or petrol.

Insurance for the boat and third-party liability. You are not responsible for damage unless it is caused by gross negligence.

Safety equipment: life jackets, flares, fire extinguisher, first aid kit. All boats comply with Spanish maritime regulations.

Cleaning and linen. The boat is handed over clean, and towels and bedding are provided for overnight charters.

Not included: food and drinks, port fees for overnight stays, transfer to the marina, and tips for the skipper (10-15% is customary).

Some charters include a paddleboard, snorkel gear, or a Bluetooth speaker. Check the listing details on the search page.

How to Book Your Yacht Rental Nice

Booking is straightforward. Follow these steps:

1. Go to the BoatHire24 search page. Enter your preferred date, group size, and port. You can filter by boat type and budget.

2. Browse the listings. Each boat has photos, a description, and a price. Read the terms carefully.

3. Click 'Request to Book'. You will be asked to provide your contact details and any special requests (e.g., catering, a specific route).

4. The charter company will confirm availability within 24 hours. You will receive a booking confirmation with payment instructions.

5. Pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the date. The balance is due 7 days before departure.

6. On the day, arrive at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The skipper will meet you at the boat.

Cancellations: Free cancellation up to 14 days before the charter. After that, a partial refund may be given depending on the policy.

If you have questions, contact the BoatHire24 support team via the website. We do not take phone calls, but we reply to emails within 2 hours during business hours.

Who Is a Yacht Rental Nice For

A private yacht charter is not for everyone. It is for people who value privacy, flexibility, and a premium experience. You are not sharing the boat with strangers. You decide the itinerary, the music, and the menu.

It is ideal for:

Couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise. A sailing yacht or catamaran with a bottle of Cava and a charcuterie board.

Families with children. Catamarans are stable and have plenty of space. Kids can swim off the back of the boat.

Groups of friends celebrating a birthday or bachelor party. A motor yacht with a sound system and a cooler full of drinks.

Corporate events. A day charter for team building or client entertainment. Superyachts can host up to 30 guests.

Fishing enthusiasts. A dedicated fishing boat with a skipper who knows the best spots.

It is not for solo travellers on a budget, or for people who want a party boat with a DJ and a bar. Those exist, but they are not what BoatHire24 offers. We focus on private, skippered charters.

For more ideas on what to do on a boat charter, read the Marbella Boat Charter Itineraries blog post.

Local Attractions You Can Visit on Your Charter

The Costa del Sol has plenty of sights accessible only by boat.

Cala del Faro is a small cove near Marbella with a lighthouse. Good for swimming and snorkelling. The water is clear and calm.

Puerto Banús itself is a spectacle. The marina is filled with superyachts, and the promenade is lined with luxury shops. You can dock and have lunch at one of the beach clubs.

Estepona old town is visible from the sea. The whitewashed houses and flower-filled balconies make a pretty backdrop. You can anchor offshore and take a tender in.

The Strait of Gibraltar is a 30 NM run from Estepona. It is one of the best places in Europe for dolphin and whale watching. Common sightings include common dolphins, striped dolphins, and pilot whales. In summer, you might see fin whales.

Nerja caves are further east, about 60 NM from Marbella. A day trip is possible on a fast motor yacht. The caves are a 3-hour tour, and you can combine it with a swim at the nearby Balcony of Europe.

Gibraltar is a 45-minute crossing from Sotogrande. You can see the Rock, the Barbary macaques, and the airport runway from the water. You can dock at the marina and go ashore.

Your skipper can suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences. The standard itinerary is a 4-hour cruise to a nearby cove, with a stop for swimming and lunch.

Safety and Skipper Qualifications

All skippers on BoatHire24 hold a valid Spanish Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo (PER) or a higher qualification. They have completed first aid training and have logged at least 500 hours at sea. The boats are inspected annually by the Spanish Maritime Authority.

Before departure, the skipper will give a safety briefing. Life jackets are available for all passengers, including children. The boat has a VHF radio and a GPS plotter.

In the unlikely event of an emergency, the skipper will contact the local coastguard. The response time is typically 15 minutes within 5 NM of the coast.

Weather cancellations are rare but possible. If the wind exceeds 30 knots or visibility drops below 1 NM, the charter will be postponed or refunded. The skipper has the final say.

For more information on safety regulations, see the Boat Rental Safety Tips blog post.

faqs.q: Can I rent a yacht in Nice through BoatHire24?
faqs.a: No. BoatHire24 operates from Marbella and the Costa del Sol, Spain. The page title is a search-friendly term for people looking for yacht rental in the Mediterranean. You will get a similar experience from Puerto Banús or Estepona, with the same quality of boats and service.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to rent a boat?
faqs.a: No. Every charter includes a licensed skipper who handles the navigation. If you want to drive a small licence-free day boat (under 6 meters and 15 HP), no licence is required. Those are available from around EUR 250 for a half-day.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest yacht rental option?
faqs.a: The cheapest option is a licence-free day boat from around EUR 250 for a half-day. For a skippered charter, a RIB or small motor yacht starts at EUR 400 for a half-day. Prices increase with boat size and season.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks?
faqs.a: Yes. You can bring your own food and drinks on board. Some charter companies offer catering packages, but they are optional. Check the listing details for restrictions on glass bottles or red wine.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book?
faqs.a: For July and August, book at least 2 weeks in advance. For other months, 1 week is usually enough. Last-minute bookings are possible if a boat is available, but selection will be limited.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.a: The skipper will assess the conditions. If the wind exceeds 30 knots or visibility is poor, the charter will be postponed or cancelled. You will receive a full refund or the option to reschedule. The decision is at the skipper's discretion.

faqs.q: Can I request a specific route?
faqs.a: Yes. You can discuss the itinerary with the skipper before departure. Common routes include a cruise to Cala del Faro, a dolphin-watching trip to the Strait of Gibraltar, or a stop at a beach club in Puerto Banús. The skipper will advise on feasibility based on weather and time.

intro:
You want a yacht charter Capri, but you're in Marbella. That's a 1,300 km drive or a two-hour flight. So here's the thing: you don't need to go to Capri to get the Capri experience. Puerto Banús has the same glamour, the same superyachts, the same Aperol Spritz at sunset. And with a BoatHire24 charter, you get a licensed skipper, a boat that turns heads, and the Mediterranean on your terms.

We run yacht charters from five ports on the Costa del Sol: Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. bodyHtml:
What You Get on a Yacht Charter Capri (From Marbella)

Every charter includes a licensed skipper who knows the coast. That means no need for a boating licence, no stress about anchoring, and no worrying about the weather. You get a private boat for your group, typically up to 12 passengers, with a cooler, ice, and basic safety gear. Most charters also include paddleboards, snorkelling masks, and a Bluetooth speaker. Fuel is included in the price, so you don't get a surprise bill at the end.

The skipper will take you to the best spots depending on the wind and sea state. That might be the cliffs at Cala del Faro, the dolphin-sighting waters off Estepona, or the calm bay of Cabopino. You decide the itinerary, but the skipper knows the local anchorages and chiringuitos. You just sit back, drink something cold, and pretend you're in Capri.

Ports of Departure for Your Capri-Style Charter

You can start your yacht charter from any of our six ports. Each has its own vibe and proximity to different beaches and attractions.

Puerto Banús, The obvious choice if you want the full Marbella glamour. Superyachts, designer shops, and a buzzing marina. From here you can reach the sandbank at Río Verde in 20 minutes, or head east to the cliffs at Cabo de Marbella.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Less flashy than Banús, but closer to the old town and the beachfront promenade. Good for a relaxed start with easy parking.

Cabopino, Small, quiet, and near the Artola dunes. Ideal if you want to escape the crowds and anchor in a natural cove.

Estepona, A working marina with a charming old town. From here you can head towards the Strait of Gibraltar and spot dolphins, or cruise west to the Costa del Sol's quieter beaches.

Sotogrande, Upmarket and exclusive, near the Guadiaro River mouth. Great for a luxury charter with access to the Sotogrande marina facilities.

Benalmádena, A lively marina with plenty of restaurants and bars. Good for a day trip to the beaches of Torremolinos or Fuengirola.

All ports are within 30 minutes of each other by road, so you can choose based on where you're staying. We recommend Puerto Banús for the full Capri feel.

Types of Boats Available for Your Charter

We have over 200 boats on our platform, ranging from small RIBs to superyachts. Here's what you can expect.

Motor yachts, The most popular choice for a day charter. Speeds of 20-30 knots, sun pads, a bow sundeck, and a shaded cockpit. Typical sizes: 30-50 feet. Prices from around EUR 1,200 for a half day.

Catamarans, More stable and spacious. Great for groups who want to spread out. A 40-foot catamaran has a flybridge, trampoline nets, and a large saloon. Prices from around EUR 1,500 for a half day.

Sailing yachts, For a quieter, more traditional experience. You can help with the sails if you want, or just let the skipper do it. Prices from around EUR 800 for a half day.

RIBs and speedboats, Smaller, faster, and cheaper. Perfect for a couple or a small family. Typical sizes: 6-9 metres. Prices from around EUR 400 for a half day.

Fishing boats, Fully equipped for deep-sea fishing. The skipper knows the best spots for tuna, dorado, and sea bass. Prices from around EUR 600 for a half day.

Licence-free day boats, Boats under 6 metres that you can drive without a licence. Good for a quick trip to a nearby beach. Prices from around EUR 200 for a half day.

Superyachts, 70 feet and above, with a crew, jet skis, and a full bar. Price on request, but expect EUR 10,000+ per day.

You can browse all options on our search page and filter by size, type, and price.

Pricing Guidance for a Yacht Charter Capri Experience

We don't set prices, each boat owner sets their own. But here's a rough guide based on what you'll find on BoatHire24.

Half-day charters (4 hours) start at around EUR 400 for a small RIB and go up to EUR 2,500 for a large motor yacht. Full-day charters (8 hours) range from EUR 600 to EUR 5,000. Most charters include fuel, skipper, and basic amenities. Extras like food, drinks, and water toys are usually extra.

High season (June to September) is the most expensive. You'll pay 20-30% more than in May or October. Book early, popular boats go weeks in advance. Low season (November to March) is cheaper but the weather is cooler (15-20 degrees C) and the sea can be choppy.

For a group of 8-12 people, expect to pay around EUR 1,500-2,500 for a full day on a decent motor yacht. That works out at EUR 150-250 per person, which is less than a day ticket to a water park. And you get a private boat with a skipper.

Best Time of Year for a Yacht Charter on the Costa del Sol

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 days of sunshine a year. You can charter a boat year-round, but the experience varies.

June to September, Peak season. Temperatures 28-35 degrees C, sea temperature 22-26 degrees C. Calm seas, light winds, and long evenings. Perfect for swimming, sunbathing, and sunset cruises. Book at least a month in advance.

May and October, Shoulder season. Temperatures 20-28 degrees C, sea temperature 18-22 degrees C. Fewer crowds, lower prices, and still plenty of sun. Good for sailing and fishing.

November to April, Low season. Temperatures 15-20 degrees C, sea temperature 15-18 degrees C. Possible rain and stronger winds. Some boats are in maintenance. Still doable for a day trip, but bring a jacket.

If you want the Capri vibe, hot, glamorous, and buzzing, go in July or August. If you want peace and quiet, go in May or September.

How to Book Your Yacht Charter Capri with BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter your port, date, and group size. Filter by boat type and price. You'll see photos, specs, and the owner's profile. Read the description, check the cancellation policy, and click 'Book Now'.

You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) at the time of booking. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, usually in cash or by card. We recommend reading the terms carefully, some owners require a damage deposit (refundable).

If you're not sure what to choose, call us or email. We know the boats and the skippers. We can recommend a specific boat for your group size and budget. We don't charge extra for advice.

Who Is a Yacht Charter Capri For?

This is for anyone who wants a private, flexible day on the water. It's for couples who want a romantic sunset cruise. It's for families who want to escape the hotel pool and find a hidden beach. It's for groups of friends who want to party on a catamaran. It's for business clients who want to impress. It's for you, if you're tired of crowded beaches and overpriced sun loungers.

It's not for you if you want to drive the boat yourself without a licence (though we have licence-free day boats for that). It's not for you if you're on a tight budget, charters start at EUR 400, which is more than a ferry ticket. But for a private, skippered experience with a group, it's good value.

Local Highlights You Can Visit on Your Charter

Your skipper will know the best spots, but here are a few to mention when you plan your route.

Puerto Banús, The marina itself is a sight. Superyachts, Lamborghinis, and people watching. Anchor nearby and take the tender in for lunch at a beach club.

La Concha mountain, Not a sea spot, but the backdrop to Marbella. You'll see it from the water. Good for photos.

Río Verde sandbank, A sandbar at the mouth of the Río Verde river. Shallow, clear water. Popular for anchoring and swimming.

Cala del Faro, A cliffside cove near Estepona. Secluded, with a small beach and a lighthouse. Good for snorkelling.

Estepona old town, You can dock at the marina and walk into the old town. Cobbled streets, flower pots, and tapas bars.

Strait of Gibraltar, A longer trip (2-3 hours from Estepona), but you'll see dolphins, and maybe whales. The skipper will know the best times.

Nerja caves, Too far for a day trip by boat (about 50 NM east), but you can combine a charter with a road trip. The caves are worth a visit.

For more ideas, read our blog on the best anchorages on the Costa del Sol.

Frequently Asked Questions About Yacht Charter Capri

Why Call It a Yacht Charter Capri When You're in Marbella

Capri is shorthand for a certain kind of day. White deck shoes, Aperol spritzes, a gentle swell, and a view of cliffs that look like they were designed by a film director. The Costa del Sol has its own version. The water is warmer, the sun is stronger, and the marinas are flashier. You get the same feeling of floating above your normal life for a few hours. The difference is you don't need a flight to Naples. You drive to Puerto Banús, step onto a 40-foot motor yacht, and within 20 minutes you're anchored off a sandbank with a cold drink in your hand. The skipper might even put on some Italian music if you ask nicely.

If you've done Capri before, you'll recognise the rhythm. Slow morning, gentle cruise, a swim stop, lunch at a chiringuito on the beach, then a lazy return as the sun drops behind La Concha. The boats are similar, the service is similar, and the price is often better. A full-day charter for eight people on a decent motor yacht costs around EUR 1,800. That's less than a comparable day in Capri, where the port fees alone can be EUR 200. And you don't have to queue for the funicular.

Which Port Gives You the Closest Capri Vibe

Puerto Banús is the obvious answer. It's built for showing off. The marina is full of Azimuts and Sunseekers, the bars are loud, and the people are dressed like they're about to be photographed. If you want the full Capri experience, start here. You'll feel like you're in the Marina Grande, but with more Range Rovers.

But if you want something quieter, closer to the Anacapri feel, choose Cabopino or Estepona. Cabopino has a small marina with a sandy beach and a dune system behind it. Estepona has a proper old town with flower-filled streets and a working fishing port. Both are less crowded and cheaper for mooring. From Cabopino you can reach the Cala del Faro in 30 minutes. From Estepona you can head towards the Strait of Gibraltar and see dolphins within an hour. The choice depends on whether you want to be seen or to see things.

What to Expect on a Typical Day Itinerary

A standard half-day charter (4 hours) usually goes like this. You meet the skipper at the marina at 10am. He shows you the boat, runs through the safety briefing, and asks where you want to go. You say the first nice beach you can think of. He nods and casts off. Within 15 minutes you're out of the marina and the coast opens up. The sea is calm, the sky is blue, and the boat cuts through the water at 20 knots. You settle into a sun pad and watch the hotels shrink.

After 30 minutes you anchor in a cove. The skipper drops the anchor, hands out snorkel masks, and points to the clearest patch of water. You swim, float, and drink something cold. After an hour he suggests lunch. You motor to a beach club or a chiringuito. He ties up to a buoy or drops you on the beach. You eat grilled fish and drink a cold beer. Then you have another swim before heading back. By 2pm you're back at the marina, sunburned and relaxed. For a full-day charter (8 hours), add another swim stop, a longer lunch, and maybe a visit to a second beach or a dolphin sighting.

Boat Size and Group Dynamics

The boat you choose depends on your group size and what you want to do. For a couple or a small family, a 25-foot RIB is fine. It's fast, easy to board, and cheap. You can beach it on sand and jump off the side. But it has no toilet, no cabin, and limited shade. For a group of six to eight, a 35-foot motor yacht is the sweet spot. It has a cabin with a toilet, a bow sundeck, a shaded cockpit, and a small galley. You can spend the whole day on board without feeling cramped.

For eight to twelve people, a 40-foot catamaran is better. The beam (width) gives you space to spread out. The trampoline nets at the bow are good for lounging. The flybridge gives the skipper a view and gives you a sunbathing spot. Catamarans are more stable, so less seasickness. They're also slower, so you spend more time at anchor and less time travelling. If you want to party, a catamaran with a sound system and a cooler full of ice is hard to beat.

Extra Costs You Should Know About

The headline price includes the boat, the skipper, fuel, and basic safety gear. But there are extras. Food and drink are not included unless you negotiate with the owner. Some boats have a catering option, usually EUR 30-50 per person for a simple lunch of paella, salad, and drinks. Others let you bring your own. We recommend bringing your own, it's cheaper and you can choose what you want.

Water toys are another extra. Paddleboards and snorkel gear are usually included. But jet skis, seabobs, and inflatable slides are not. If you want a jet ski, expect to pay EUR 150-250 for an hour. Some superyachts include them in the price, but they cost EUR 10,000+ per day. Also check the cancellation policy. Most owners offer a full refund if you cancel 7 days before. Closer than that, you might lose your deposit. Read the terms before you book.

How to Avoid Seasickness on Your Charter

The Costa del Sol is generally calm, especially in summer. But the western end near the Strait of Gibraltar can get choppy. If you're prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before you board. Brands like Stugeron or Kwells work. Also choose a catamaran over a monohull. Catamarans roll less. Sit in the middle of the boat, keep your eyes on the horizon, and avoid alcohol until you're anchored. Once you're stationary, the feeling passes quickly. Most people are fine after a swim.

If you're chartering in winter or spring, the sea can be rougher. Check the forecast before you book. The skipper will advise you if conditions are unsafe. They won't take you out in a storm. But a 2-metre swell is normal in March. If you're not a confident sailor, stick to summer months.

What to Wear and Bring on the Day

You're on a boat, so dress for the sun and the water. Swimwear, a light cover-up, and non-slip shoes. Flip-flops are fine, but they can slip on wet decks. Bring a towel, sunscreen (factor 50, reapply), a hat, and sunglasses. A windbreaker is useful even in summer, the breeze can feel cool when you're moving at 20 knots. Bring a dry bag for your phone and wallet. Most boats have a small safe, but it's not guaranteed.

For food and drink, bring a cooler bag with ice packs. The boat will have a cooler, but it's usually small. Bring more water than you think you need. You'll get dehydrated faster on the water. Beer, wine, and soft drinks are fine. Avoid glass bottles, they're banned on most boats. Use cans or plastic. And bring a speaker if the boat doesn't have one. The skipper will have a Bluetooth speaker, but it's worth checking.

Why You Should Book Through BoatHire24

We're a marketplace, not a charter company. That means we list boats from multiple owners, so you can compare prices, sizes, and features in one place. You don't have to call five different companies and wait for quotes. You search, filter, and book online. We handle the deposit and the communication. The owner handles the boat and the skipper.

We also have local knowledge. We know which boats are well-maintained and which skippers are reliable. If you're unsure, read the reviews on each listing. They're from real customers, not fabricated. And if you have a problem, we'll help resolve it. We don't take a commission from the owner, we charge a small booking fee. So you're not paying extra for using us. Start your search on our BoatHire24 homepage and find your Capri-style charter today.

What About Insurance and Safety
