bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

A catamaran charter Sardinia with BoatHire24 includes the boat, a licensed skipper, fuel for standard cruising, and insurance. You also get use of the onboard kitchen, bathrooms, cabins, and deck spaces. Most boats come with a dinghy, snorkeling gear, and a sound system. What is not included is food, drinks, and port mooring fees (usually EUR 30-80 per night). Gratuity for the skipper is optional, around 10-15% of the charter price if you are happy with the service.

Some premium catamarans include a hostess or chef for an extra fee, around EUR 200-400 per day. You can also add water toys like paddleboards or a jet ski, price on request. Check the listing details for each boat on our search page.

Why Choose a Catamaran Over a Monohull

Catamarans have two hulls, which means more deck space, no heeling, and shallower draft. In Sardinia, where many anchorages have shallow water, a catamaran lets you get closer to beaches and coves. The stability is a big plus if anyone in your group gets seasick. You also get separate cabins in each hull, giving more privacy than a monohull of the same length.

The trade-off is that catamarans are wider, so some marinas charge higher berth fees. But for a week-long itinerary hopping between the Costa Smeralda and La Maddalena, the space and comfort win. For a comparison of boat types, read our catamaran vs monohull charter blog post.

Best Departure Ports for a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

You can start your catamaran charter Sardinia from several ports. Olbia and Porto Cervo are the main hubs for the Costa Smeralda. Cagliari in the south gives access to the Gulf of Cagliari and the islands of Sant'Antioco and San Pietro. Alghero in the northwest is close to the Neptune's Grotto and the Capo Caccia cliffs. Porto Torres is a quieter option for the Asinara National Park.

Each port has its own character. Porto Cervo is glitzy, with designer shops and expensive restaurants. Olbia is more practical, with a large marina and easy airport access. Cagliari is a proper city with a historic centre. Alghero has Catalan architecture and a laid-back vibe. We recommend booking a port that matches your itinerary plans. If you want to explore the Maddalena archipelago, start from Olbia or Porto Cervo. For the south coast, start from Cagliari.

Popular Itineraries for a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

A typical week-long catamaran charter Sardinia from Olbia might go: Day 1, Olbia to Cala di Volpe (15 NM). Day 2, Cala di Volpe to Porto Cervo (5 NM) and explore the town. Day 3, Porto Cervo to Cala Coticcio (10 NM), also called Tahiti beach. Day 4, Cala Coticcio to La Maddalena island (8 NM), visit the town and Caprera. Day 5, La Maddalena to Spargi and Budelli (5 NM), swim at the pink beach. Day 6, Budelli to Palau (10 NM) and return to Olbia. Day 7, disembark.

For a southern itinerary from Cagliari: Day 1, Cagliari to Villasimius (25 NM). Day 2, Villasimius to Costa Rei (10 NM). Day 3, Costa Rei to Cala Sinzias (5 NM). Day 4, Cala Sinzias to Capo Carbonara (10 NM). Day 5, Capo Carbonara to Cagliari (20 NM). Day 6, explore Cagliari. Day 7, disembark. Your skipper will adjust based on weather and your preferences.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Charter Sardinia

Prices for a catamaran charter Sardinia vary by boat size, age, and season. A 40-foot catamaran from 2015 sleeps 8 and costs from around EUR 2,500 per day in July and August. A newer 50-foot catamaran with 4 cabins and a flybridge can be EUR 4,000-6,000 per day in peak season. In May, June, or September, prices drop by 20-30%. October and April are cheaper still, but some boats are laid up.

Weekly charters are common and often get a discount of one free day on a 7-day booking. For example, a boat that costs EUR 3,000 per day might be EUR 18,000 for 7 days instead of EUR 21,000. Always ask for the weekly rate. Fuel is extra if you cruise more than 4 hours per day, typically EUR 200-400 per week. Mooring fees at popular spots like Porto Cervo can be EUR 100-200 per night. For a full breakdown, see our Sardinia charter costs blog post.

Best Time for a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

The best time for a catamaran charter Sardinia is from May to October. July and August are the hottest and busiest, with water temperatures around 25-27 degrees C. June and September offer warm weather, fewer crowds, and lower prices. May and October are cooler, air temperature 20-24 degrees C, but still pleasant for sailing. The wind in Sardinia is mostly from the northwest, the Mistral, which can be strong in spring and autumn. Your skipper will choose sheltered routes.

If you want to swim and sunbathe, aim for June to September. If you prefer hiking and exploring towns, May and October are fine. Avoid November to March unless you are a hardcore sailor, as many marinas have limited services and weather can be rough.

What to Expect Onboard a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

Onboard a catamaran charter Sardinia, you get a saloon with a galley (kitchen), dining table, and seating. Cabins have double beds or twin singles, with en-suite bathrooms (heads) in most cases. The cockpit has a table and bench seating for al fresco meals. The foredeck often has sun loungers or a trampoline net. The flybridge, if the boat has one, gives a panoramic view and a helm station. Air conditioning is available on most boats but may cost extra, around EUR 200-400 per week.

Your skipper lives in a separate cabin or on deck, depending on the boat. They handle navigation, docking, and cooking if you pay for meal preparation. You are free to relax, swim, or help with sailing if you want. The skipper speaks English and Italian. They know the local anchorages and restaurants.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter Sardinia with BoatHire24

Booking a catamaran charter Sardinia on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to our search page, filter by boat type (catamaran), number of guests, and your preferred port. You will see available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on a listing to see the full details, including what is included and any extras. Use the inquiry form to send a booking request. We will confirm availability and send you a contract and payment link.

We require a 50% deposit to secure the booking, with the balance due 4 weeks before departure. We accept bank transfer and credit card. Cancellation policy: full refund if cancelled 60 days before, 50% refund 30-60 days, no refund within 30 days. We recommend travel insurance that covers charter cancellations. For any questions, contact us via the website or email. We respond within 24 hours.

Who Is a Catamaran Charter Sardinia For

A catamaran charter Sardinia suits families, groups of friends, and couples who want a spacious, stable boat. It is ideal for people who want to swim, snorkel, and explore islands without the work of sailing. The catamaran's shallow draft means you can anchor close to beaches, so it works well for families with young children. It is also popular for corporate events or birthday celebrations, as the deck space allows for parties.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a cabin charter, where you book a single cabin on a catamaran with other guests. This is cheaper, from around EUR 1,500 per person per week. Check our listings for cabin charter options. For more ideas, read our Sardinia charter guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

What to Pack for a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

Pack light but smart for a catamaran charter Sardinia. Bring swimwear, a rash guard or UV shirt for sun protection, and a light jacket for evenings. The wind can pick up, so a windproof top is useful. Soft-soled shoes or deck shoes are mandatory on most boats, no black soles that mark the deck. A sun hat, sunglasses with a strap, and reef-safe sunscreen are essentials. If you plan to eat out, pack smart casual clothes, as some restaurants in Porto Cervo and Cagliari expect collared shirts and dresses.

Bring a reusable water bottle, as the boat has a water tank. A dry bag for phones and cameras is handy when you take the dinghy ashore. If you are prone to seasickness, bring medication or acupressure bands, though the catamaran's stability makes it unlikely. Most boats have a first aid kit, but bring your own painkillers and plasters. A small backpack for day trips is useful. Leave hard suitcases at home, duffel bags are easier to store in the cabins.

Local Cuisine and Dining Options on a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

Sardinia has a distinct food culture that you should experience during your catamaran charter Sardinia. The island is known for porceddu (roast suckling pig), pane carasau (crispy flatbread), and pecorino cheese. Seafood is excellent, with bottarga (cured fish roe), spaghetti with sea urchins, and lobster from Alghero. Onboard, your skipper can recommend local markets where you can buy fresh produce. In Olbia, the morning market at Via Mameli has fish, vegetables, and cheese. In Cagliari, the Mercato di San Benedetto is one of the largest in Italy.

For dining ashore, book a table at a restaurant in Cala di Volpe or Porto Cervo for high-end Italian cuisine, expect EUR 80-150 per person. For a more casual meal, try a trattoria in Palau or La Maddalena, where a full meal costs EUR 30-50. Many catamarans have a barbecue on the aft deck, so you can grill fresh fish and meat while anchored. Your skipper can help arrange provisioning before departure. Some charters include a hostess who cooks breakfast and lunch, price on request.

How to Choose the Right Catamaran Size for Your Sardinia Charter

Choosing the right catamaran size for your catamaran charter Sardinia depends on your group size and budget. A 38-40 foot catamaran sleeps 6-8 people in 3-4 cabins. This is suitable for a family or a small group of friends. The saloon and cockpit are compact but functional. A 44-48 foot catamaran adds more deck space, a larger saloon, and 4-5 cabins, sleeping 8-10 guests. This is better for two families or a group of couples who want more privacy and living area.

A 50-55 foot catamaran is a luxury option with a flybridge, spacious cabins with en-suite bathrooms, and a crew cabin for the skipper. Prices for these boats start from around EUR 5,000 per day in peak season. If you have a large group of 10-12 people, a 55-foot catamaran is ideal. For smaller groups, a 40-foot catamaran is more cost-effective and easier to handle in tight marinas. Check the beam (width) of the boat, as some older marinas in Sardinia have narrow berths that cannot accommodate wide catamarans.

Environmental Considerations for a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

Sardinia has strict environmental rules that you must follow during your catamaran charter Sardinia. The La Maddalena Archipelago is a national park, and anchoring is prohibited in some areas to protect seagrass meadows (Posidonia oceanica). Your skipper will know the designated mooring buoys, which cost around EUR 20-40 per night. Do not throw rubbish overboard, all waste must be stored and disposed of at port facilities. Many marinas have recycling bins, and some enforce a deposit system for glass bottles.

Use biodegradable sunscreen and avoid touching coral or marine life. The waters around Sardinia are home to dolphins, sea turtles, and occasional whales. If you see them, keep a distance of at least 100 metres. Do not feed the fish or disturb nesting birds on the islands. Some catamarans have eco-friendly features like solar panels or water makers, which reduce reliance on generators and shore water. Ask about these when booking if sustainability is important to you.

Combining a Catamaran Charter Sardinia with Other Activities

A catamaran charter Sardinia can be combined with land-based activities for a fuller holiday. If you start from Alghero, visit the Neptune's Grotto, a sea cave with stalactites and a 654-step staircase. From Olbia, take a day trip to the Costa Smeralda golf courses or the archaeological site of Nuraghe La Prisgiona. From Cagliari, explore the Roman amphitheatre and the Bastione di Saint Remy. Your skipper can arrange a day ashore while the boat stays at a mooring.

For adventure, try scuba diving at the Capo Carbonara marine reserve or the wrecks off the coast of Villasimius. Hiking on the island of Caprera has trails with views of the archipelago. In the evening, many ports have live music or festivals, especially in August. If you have extra days, consider a land tour of the interior, including the Gola Su Gorropu canyon or the town of Orgosolo with its murals. We can help arrange transfers and accommodation, price on request.

What Happens in Bad Weather on a Catamaran Charter Sardinia

Bad weather can affect a catamaran charter Sardinia, but your skipper will adjust the itinerary to keep you safe and comfortable. The Mistral wind can reach 30-40 knots in spring and autumn, making the open sea rough. Your skipper will choose sheltered routes along the coast or stay in port until the wind drops. The catamaran's shallow draft and twin engines allow it to navigate in protected bays and channels. If a storm is forecast, you may stay overnight at a marina instead of anchoring.

BoatHire24 monitors weather forecasts and will notify you of any changes before departure. If the weather is unsafe for several days, we may offer alternative dates or a partial refund. Travel insurance that covers weather-related cancellations is recommended. In July and August, storms are rare and usually pass quickly. Your skipper has local knowledge of anchorages like Cala del Faro on the Costa Smeralda, which offers protection from the prevailing wind.

But if you want a high-end catamaran with a licensed skipper, departure from a mainland port, and the flexibility to head to Ibiza, you are in the right place.
bodyHtml:
What a Catamaran Charter Ibiza Actually Means on BoatHire24

When you search for a catamaran charter Ibiza on this site, you are looking at boats that are berthed in Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. These are not Ibiza-based vessels. The reason we list them under an Ibiza keyword is that many clients want to sail from the Costa del Sol to Ibiza for a week or longer. A catamaran charter from Marbella to Ibiza is a popular multi-day route, especially in July and August. You get the stability and space of a catamaran, a licensed skipper who knows the Mediterranean, and the freedom to explore both the mainland coast and the Balearics. If you want a day charter in Ibiza itself, you need a different platform. But if you want a week-long catamaran charter that includes Ibiza as a destination, BoatHire24 can help.

The boats available are mostly Lagoon, Fountaine Pajot, and Bali models, ranging from 38 to 50 feet. They typically sleep 6 to 12 guests in cabins, with a skipper cabin separate. Prices for a weekly catamaran charter start from around EUR 8,000 in low season and go up to EUR 20,000 or more in August, depending on the boat age, size, and equipment. Day charters from the Costa del Sol to nearby spots like Cala del Faro or the Strait of Gibraltar are cheaper, around EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 for a full day. But a true catamaran charter Ibiza itinerary involves a multi-day booking.

Departure Ports for Your Catamaran Charter

Your catamaran charter Ibiza trip will start from one of these ports. Each has its own advantages.

Puerto Banús. The most famous marina on the Costa del Sol. You depart from the heart of Marbella's luxury scene. The port has fuel, water, provisioning, and parking. It is a 12-hour sail to Ibiza, so most skippers will leave early morning and arrive by evening. You can also stop overnight in Almería or Cartagena if you want to break the journey.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo). Slightly less flashy than Puerto Banús, but closer to Marbella town centre. Good for provisioning and crew changes. Same sailing time to Ibiza.

Estepona. A quieter departure point. Estepona old town is worth a visit before you set off. The marina is modern and well-equipped. Sailing time to Ibiza is about 13 hours.

Sotogrande. Near Gibraltar. This is a good option if you want to combine a catamaran charter with a visit to the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins. The crossing to Ibiza from here is about 14 hours.

Benalmádena. East of Marbella. This port is close to Málaga airport, which makes it convenient for international guests. Sailing time to Ibiza is about 11 hours.

Cabopino. A small, charming marina near Marbella. Less crowded, but with limited services. Good for a relaxed start.

All these ports have direct access to the Mediterranean. Your skipper will plan the route based on weather, currents, and your preferences.

Boat Types Available for a Catamaran Charter

When you book a catamaran charter Ibiza through BoatHire24, you are not limited to catamarans. The site lists motor yachts, sailing yachts, RIBs, fishing boats, licence-free day boats, and superyachts. But for a multi-day trip to Ibiza, a catamaran is the best choice for stability and space. Here are the typical options.

Catamarans. The main focus. Expect boats like a Lagoon 42, Fountaine Pajot Isla 40, or Bali 4.1. These have 4 to 6 cabins, a large saloon, a flybridge, and a spacious deck. The skipper has a separate cabin. You get good fuel efficiency and a shallow draft, which lets you anchor close to beaches.

Sailing catamarans. Some catamarans are sailing versions, not motor. They are quieter and more eco-friendly, but slower. If you want to sail to Ibiza under canvas, this is the option. Average speed is around 8 knots. The crossing takes 14 to 16 hours.

Motor catamarans. These are rare but available. They combine catamaran stability with motor yacht speed. You can do the crossing in 8 to 10 hours. They consume more fuel, which is reflected in the charter price.

Luxury catamarans. Some boats are crewed with a skipper and a hostess or chef. These are more expensive, from around EUR 15,000 per week. They include gourmet meals, cocktails, and premium service.

If you want a day charter instead of a multi-day trip, you can book a catamaran for a few hours from any of the ports. Day charters typically go to Cala del Faro, the Marbella coastline, or the Strait of Gibraltar. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half day.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Charter Ibiza

Exact prices depend on the boat, season, duration, and extras. Here is a realistic range.

Day charter (8 hours). From around EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 for a catamaran. Includes skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. Food and drinks are extra or you can bring your own.

Weekend charter (2-3 days). From around EUR 3,000 to EUR 6,000. You can sail to a nearby port like Estepona or Gibraltar, but not to Ibiza in that time.

Weekly charter (7 days). From around EUR 8,000 in May or October to EUR 20,000 in August. This includes the skipper and standard insurance. Fuel for the crossing to Ibiza is extra, typically EUR 500 to EUR 1,000 depending on the boat and engine hours.

Luxury weekly charter. With a full crew (skipper, chef, hostess), prices start from EUR 15,000 and can exceed EUR 30,000 for a 50-foot catamaran in high season.

Additional costs: port fees in Ibiza (around EUR 50 to EUR 150 per night), food and drinks (you can provision yourself or ask the skipper to arrange), and optional extras like water toys (paddleboards, snorkel gear, jet skis). Always ask for a full quote before booking.

Seasons and Weather for a Catamaran Charter

The best time for a catamaran charter Ibiza is from May to October. The weather is warm, the sea is calm, and the days are long.

May and June. Air temperatures around 22-28 degrees C. Water temperature around 18-22 degrees C. Less crowded in Ibiza. Prices are lower. The crossing from the Costa del Sol is usually smooth, with light winds.

July and August. Peak season. Air temperatures 30-35 degrees C. Water 24-27 degrees C. Ibiza is busy, so book ports and anchorages in advance. Prices are highest. The crossing can be choppy if the Levante wind blows, but your skipper will choose the best window.

September and October. Air temperatures 25-30 degrees C. Water still warm. Fewer crowds. Good value. The weather is still stable, though occasional storms are possible in late October.

November to April. Low season. Many catamarans are laid up or used for maintenance. The crossing to Ibiza is riskier due to storms. You can still charter a catamaran for a day trip along the Costa del Sol, but a weekly trip to Ibiza is not recommended.

Your skipper will monitor the forecast and adjust the route. The Strait of Gibraltar can have strong winds and currents, but the Costa del Sol coast is generally sheltered by the mountains.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter Ibiza on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the search page and filter by boat type (catamaran), port, and date. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specifications, and prices. Each listing has a contact form or phone number for the owner or charter company.

Because every charter includes a licensed skipper, you do not need a boating licence. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and docking. You just relax and enjoy.

For a multi-day trip to Ibiza, you should book at least 2 weeks in advance in high season. The skipper will need time to plan the route, provision the boat, and check the weather. For day charters, you can often book a few days ahead.

Payment is typically 50% deposit and 50% on the day of departure. Some operators accept credit cards, others prefer bank transfer. Always read the cancellation policy. Most are flexible if bad weather prevents sailing, but not if you change your mind.

If you want a custom itinerary, contact the BoatHire24 team and we can match you with a suitable catamaran and skipper. We do not own the boats, but we know the fleet and can advise.

Who Is a Catamaran Charter Ibiza For

This type of charter suits groups who want a private, comfortable, and stable boat for a week-long holiday. Families with children appreciate the space and safety of a catamaran. Groups of friends can party on deck without disturbing the skipper. Couples looking for a romantic getaway might prefer a smaller sailing catamaran with a chef.

If you are a solo traveller, a catamaran charter is expensive unless you join a shared charter (rare on this site). Most boats are booked by groups of 6 to 12 people.

If you want to visit Ibiza but do not want to fly or take a ferry, a catamaran charter from the Costa del Sol is a unique way to arrive. You see the coast, the sea, and the Balearics from the water. The skipper can stop at hidden coves along the way.

If you are not interested in a multi-day trip, you can still book a catamaran for a day charter from Puerto Banús or Marbella. That is a different experience, but still enjoyable. You can read more about day charters on the BoatHire24 blog.

Local Colour and Attractions Along the Way

If you do the crossing from the Costa del Sol to Ibiza, you pass several interesting spots. Your skipper might suggest a stop at the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins and whales. The strait is a migration route for pilot whales, orcas, and common dolphins. The water is deep and the currents strong, but a catamaran handles it well.

You also pass near the Cabo de Gata Natural Park in Almería. This is a protected coastline with volcanic cliffs and hidden beaches. Good for an overnight anchorage.

Once you reach Ibiza, you can anchor at Cala d'Hort, Cala Comte, or Cala Bassa. These are famous for clear water and sunset views. The skipper will know the best spots for swimming and snorkelling.

Back on the Costa del Sol, you can explore Puerto Banús with its shops and restaurants, Marbella's old town, Estepona's flower-lined streets, or the Nerja caves (a 45-minute drive from Marbella). If you have time before or after the charter, these are worth visiting.

The La Concha mountain dominates the Marbella skyline. It is a good landmark for navigation and a popular hike if you want to stretch your legs before boarding.

Why Choose a Catamaran Over a Motor Yacht for the Ibiza Crossing

The crossing from the Costa del Sol to Ibiza is roughly 130 nautical miles. A motor yacht of similar size burns more fuel and has a narrower beam, meaning more roll in a swell. A catamaran, with its twin hulls, offers a stable platform. You can walk around, cook, and sleep during the crossing without feeling seasick. The shallow draft (typically 1.2 to 1.5 metres) lets you anchor closer to Ibiza's sandy coves than a deep-keel motor yacht. Fuel costs for a catamaran on this route are around EUR 400 to EUR 700 for the crossing, compared to EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,000 for a motor yacht. If you are splitting the cost among 8 people, the saving is noticeable.

Specific Catamaran Models You Might Find on BoatHire24

Not all catamarans are the same. A Lagoon 42 from 2020 has a different layout to a Fountaine Pajot Saona 47. On BoatHire24, you will see listings for the Lagoon 380, 400, 42, and 450; the Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40, Isla 40, and Astrea 42; and the Bali 4.1, 4.2, and 4.6. The Bali models have a distinctive open saloon that connects directly to the cockpit, which groups like for socialising. The Lagoon 42 is a common choice for the Ibiza route because it balances speed (8-10 knots) with comfort. If you want a newer boat, look for 2022 or 2023 models. They have better insulation, more efficient engines, and updated electronics. Older boats (2010-2015) are cheaper but may have worn upholstery and older navigation gear.

What the Skipper Does During the Ibiza Crossing

Your skipper is a licensed professional, usually with a Spanish Patrón de Yate qualification or equivalent. They handle the navigation, radio, engine checks, and docking. During the crossing to Ibiza, they will set a course that avoids shipping lanes and optimises for wind and current. They will also monitor the weather via AIS and radar. You do not need to help, but you can if you want. The skipper will brief you on safety procedures at the start. They live in a separate cabin, so you have privacy. Some skippers speak English, Spanish, and French. Confirm the language when booking. The skipper's fee is included in the charter price, but you should tip 10-15% at the end if the service is good.

How to Provision for a Week-Long Catamaran Charter

Most charters do not include food or drinks. You can bring your own or ask the skipper to arrange provisioning. In Puerto Banús, there is a Supercor supermarket in the marina. In Marbella, there is a Mercadona a 10-minute walk from the port. For a group of 8, budget around EUR 50-70 per person per day for groceries and drinks. If you want to eat out, Ibiza's restaurants are expensive: a dinner with wine can cost EUR 60-80 per person. Many groups do a mix: breakfast and lunch on the boat, dinner at a beach club or restaurant. The catamaran's fridge and freezer are large enough for a week's supplies. Bring your own snacks and alcohol to save money. The skipper can also recommend local markets for fresh fish and produce.

bodyHtml:
What a Catamaran Charter in Marbella Includes

When you book a catamaran charter through BoatHire24, you get a boat with a professional skipper. You do not need a licence. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and mooring. Most charters include fuel, water toys (paddleboards, snorkel gear), and a basic welcome pack. Some include food and drinks, but check the listing. You can customise the itinerary, within reason. The skipper knows the coast and will suggest anchorages like Cala del Faro or the coves near Cabopino. You pay from around EUR 200 per person for a half-day trip, depending on the boat and season.

Departure Ports on the Costa del Sol

You can start your catamaran charter from any of our ports. Puerto Banús is the most famous, with its superyachts and designer shops. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and closer to the old town. Cabopino is small and relaxed, near the Artola dunes. Estepona has a modern marina and a charming old town. Sotogrande is exclusive, with a polo club and golf courses. Benalmádena is lively, with a large marina and waterpark. Each port gives you access to different stretches of coast. From Puerto Banús, you can reach the Marbella coastline in 15 minutes. From Estepona, you are closer to Gibraltar and the dolphin pods.

Boat Options: Catamarans and More

We list catamarans from 30 to 50 feet, with capacities from 8 to 20 guests. Lagoon and Fountaine Pajot are common brands. Catamarans are stable, spacious, and have shallow drafts, so you can anchor close to beaches. If you want something faster, try a motor yacht or a RIB. If you prefer sailing, we have sailing yachts. For fishing, there are fishing boats with gear. For a day without a skipper, look at licence-free day boats (up to 15 hp). Superyachts are available on request. Prices vary: a half-day catamaran charter for 10 people costs from around EUR 1,000 to EUR 2,500, depending on the boat and extras. Full-day charters start from EUR 1,800.

Pricing Guidance and What Affects the Cost

Catamaran charter prices depend on several factors. Boat size and age matter. Newer, larger catamarans cost more. Season is a big factor: July and August are peak, with prices 30-50% higher than May or October. Half-day (4 hours) is cheaper than full-day (8 hours). Extras like food, drinks, jet skis, or a hostess add cost. You can often negotiate for a group booking. Always ask the owner or broker for a detailed quote. We list prices as from around EUR X, but the final price is confirmed when you book. For a group of 10, expect to pay EUR 100 to EUR 300 per person for a half-day, including the skipper and fuel.

Best Seasons for a Catamaran Charter

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate. Summer (June to September) is hot, 28-32 degrees C, with calm seas and long days. This is the busiest season, so book early. Spring (April to May) and autumn (October) are milder, 20-26 degrees C, with fewer crowds and lower prices. Winter (November to March) is cooler, 15-20 degrees C, but sunny. Some boats operate year-round, but many are dry-docked for maintenance. If you want to swim, summer is best. If you want to sail without sweating, spring and autumn are ideal. The wind is light in summer, stronger in spring and autumn, making for better sailing.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter with BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page and filter by catamaran, port, date, and number of guests. You will see available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on a listing to see the full description and inclusions. Send an enquiry through the form, and the owner or broker will reply with availability and a quote. You can also call or email us. We do not take payment directly; you pay the owner. We act as a marketplace. Once you agree on a price and date, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is paid on the day, often in cash. Read the cancellation policy before booking.

Who Is a Catamaran Charter For

A catamaran charter works for families, groups of friends, couples, and corporate events. The stable platform suits people who get seasick. The space works for parties, with a large deck and trampolines. Kids can swim and snorkel safely. For a romantic trip, a sunset cruise on a catamaran is hard to beat. For a bachelor or bachelorette party, you can bring music and drinks. For a team-building event, you can do a day sail with a barbecue. The skipper handles everything, so you just relax. If you want a private chef or a photographer, ask the owner. Most are flexible.

Local Attractions and Activities on Your Charter

On a catamaran charter from Marbella, you can visit Cala del Faro, a secluded cove with clear water. You can see La Concha mountain from the sea. You might spot dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar if you go south from Estepona. You can anchor off Puerto Banús and watch the superyachts. You can visit the Nerja caves from the sea (you need a full-day trip and a car from the port). You can stop for lunch at a chiringuito on the beach, like the ones at Cabopino. Your skipper will know the best spots. If you want to fish, some catamarans have fishing rods. If you want to snorkel, the water is clearest in summer.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Catamaran Charter

BoatHire24 lists only verified boats with licensed skippers. We do not list unskippered boats. We show real photos and prices. You can compare multiple boats in one place. We cover all major ports on the Costa del Sol. We do not charge a booking fee. We are based in Marbella, so we know the area. If you have questions, you can call us. We are not a big aggregator; we are a small team. Our BoatHire24 homepage has more information. You can also read our blog for tips on charters and destinations. If you are still set on Cancun, we cannot help. If you want the Mediterranean, we can.

Comparing Catamarans by Size and Capacity

Not all catamarans are the same. A 32-foot Lagoon 380 sleeps 8 but works well for a day charter with 10 to 12 guests. A 40-foot Fountaine Pajot Lucia can take 12 to 15 people comfortably, with a larger saloon and better galley. A 50-foot Lagoon 500 or similar handles up to 20 guests, with a flybridge, multiple seating areas, and a proper kitchen. For a group of 6, a smaller catamaran keeps costs down. For a party of 15, you need the bigger boat. Check the deck space: trampolines at the bow are great for sunbathing, while a flybridge gives shade and a better view. The skipper will brief you on safety and layout before you leave port.

Puerto Banús: The Glamour Option

Starting from Puerto Banús puts you in the heart of Marbella's luxury scene. The marina is full of superyachts, sports cars, and designer boutiques. You can board your catamaran right next to the famous casino. From here, you can head west to the San Pedro coast or east to the Marbella shoreline. The sea is usually calm in summer. You can anchor near the beach of Puerto Banús itself, but it gets busy. A better spot is the cove at Cala del Faro, 15 minutes east. That cove has clear water and fewer boats. If you want lunch, the chiringuito at El Faro serves fresh fish. The skipper can drop you off by dinghy. Expect to pay a premium for departing from this port, but the convenience and atmosphere justify it.

Marbella Marina: Quiet and Central

Marbella Marina, also called Puerto Deportivo, is a less flashy alternative to Puerto Banús. It is closer to Marbella old town, with its orange trees and tapas bars. The marina has fewer superyachts, so it feels more relaxed. Catamaran charters from here cost slightly less than from Puerto Banús, sometimes by EUR 100 to EUR 200 for a half-day. The coast east of the marina has small beaches like Playa de la Venus and Playa del Faro. You can anchor there for swimming. The marina has good parking and is walkable from the town centre. If you are staying in Marbella, this is the easiest port to use. The skipper can pick you up from the marina office.

Cabopino: Small and Secluded

Cabopino is a tiny marina near the Artola sand dunes, a protected natural area. It is quieter than the big ports, with fewer bars and restaurants. The beach at Cabopino is wide and sandy. The marina has a small boatyard and a few cafes. Catamaran charters from here are ideal if you want a peaceful start. You can reach the coves of Calahonda and Cala del Moral in 20 minutes. The water is clearer here than near the busy ports. The marina has limited parking, so arrive early. Cabopino is good for families who want to avoid crowds. The prices are similar to Marbella Marina, but the experience is more low-key. The skipper might suggest a stop at the chiringuito on the beach for a simple lunch.

Estepona: Old Town Charm and Dolphin Spotting

Estepona marina is modern and well-equipped, with a promenade and restaurants. The old town is a 10-minute walk, with whitewashed houses and flower pots. Catamaran charters from Estepona can head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you often see dolphins and pilot whales. The trip to Gibraltar takes about 90 minutes by catamaran. You can anchor off the coast and watch the monkeys on the Rock. Alternatively, go east to the beaches of Guadalmina or San Pedro. The water is cooler here than in Marbella, but still swimmable in summer. Estepona is less crowded than Puerto Banús, so prices are lower. A half-day charter for 10 people might cost from EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,000. The marina has good facilities, including showers and a chandlery.

Sotogrande: Exclusive and Spacious

Sotogrande is a gated community with a marina, golf courses, and polo fields. The marina is large and well-maintained, with plenty of space. Catamaran charters from here are popular with families and corporate groups. The coast south of Sotogrande has long, empty beaches like Playa de Torreguadiaro. You can anchor there for a quiet swim. The marina has restaurants and a supermarket. Sotogrande is further from Marbella, so you need a car or taxi. Prices are similar to Puerto Banús, but the atmosphere is more exclusive. The skipper can arrange a barbecue on the beach or a visit to the nearby town of San Roque. If you want privacy, this is a good choice.

Benalmádena: Lively and Family-Friendly

Benalmádena marina is one of the largest on the Costa del Sol, with a waterpark, aquarium, and many restaurants. Catamaran charters from here are good for families with children. The marina has a beach and a promenade. You can head east to the cliffs of Torremolinos or west to the beaches of Fuengirola. The water is warm in summer. Benalmádena is less expensive than Puerto Banús, with half-day charters from around EUR 900 for a 10-person catamaran. The marina has plenty of parking. The skipper can recommend a stop at a chiringuito for lunch. If you want a lively atmosphere, this port works. The downside is the noise from the beach bars, but you leave it behind once you sail out.

Practical Tips for Your Catamaran Charter Day

Arrive 15 minutes before departure to meet the skipper and stow your bags. Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, and a towel. The sun is strong even in spring. Wear non-marking shoes, as the deck can get hot. Most catamarans have a cooler with ice, but you can bring your own drinks. The skipper will provide water and soft drinks in the welcome pack. If you want alcohol, check the policy; some charters allow it, others do not. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and wallet. The sea can be choppy in the afternoon, so take seasickness tablets if you are prone. The skipper will anchor in calm coves for swimming. If you want to snorkel, bring your own mask or use the boat's gear. Respect the skipper's instructions, especially about safety and mooring.

How Weather Affects Your Charter

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, but weather can still change your plans. In summer, the Levante wind blows from the east, creating choppy seas in the afternoon. The skipper might adjust the itinerary to stay in sheltered coves. In spring and autumn, the Poniente wind from the west brings calmer seas. If the forecast is bad, the owner may cancel or reschedule. Check the forecast before you book. Most charters have a cancellation policy that covers bad weather. If the sea is too rough, you get a refund or a new date. The skipper will not take risks. In winter, some catamarans are not available, so check the listing. The water temperature in summer is 24-26 degrees C, comfortable for swimming. In spring, it is cooler, around 18-20 degrees C.

What to Eat and Drink on Board

Most catamaran charters include a basic welcome pack with water, soft drinks, and sometimes beer or wine. Some owners offer a catering option with tapas, paella, or a barbecue. You can also bring your own food. The galley on a catamaran has a fridge, stove, and sink. The skipper can prepare simple meals. For a special occasion, hire a private chef. The cost is around EUR 50 to EUR 100 per person for a three-course meal. Popular dishes include grilled fish, seafood paella, and Spanish tortilla. For drinks, sangria and cava are common. If you want a specific wine, bring it. The skipper will provide glasses and ice. For a sunset charter, champagne is a good choice. Check the listing for what is included. Some charters offer a full bar, others just basics.

Extras and Add-Ons to Enhance Your Trip

You can add extras to your catamaran charter. Jet skis are available for rent at some ports, costing around EUR 150 per hour. A hostess or steward can serve drinks and food, adding EUR 100 to EUR 200 for the day. A photographer or videographer can capture the trip, from EUR 300 for a half-day. Water toys like a floating mat, kayak, or inflatable slide can be included or added for a fee. Some catamarans have a sound system for music. If you want a specific playlist, bring a phone or USB. For a special event like a birthday or proposal, the owner can arrange decorations and cake. Ask when you book. These extras are not standard, so confirm the price before the trip. The skipper can also arrange a beach barbecue if you anchor near a chiringuito.

Safety and Insurance on Your Charter

All catamarans on BoatHire24 have licensed skippers with valid qualifications. The boat is insured for liability and damage. You do not need personal insurance for the boat, but you should have travel insurance for personal injury or cancellation. The skipper will do a safety briefing before departure. Life jackets are available for all guests, including children. The boat has a first aid kit and a VHF radio. In an emergency, the skipper will contact the coastguard. The Costa del Sol has a good safety record for charters. The main risks are sunburn, seasickness, and minor injuries from slipping on the deck. Wear shoes with grip. Do not dive from the boat without checking the depth. The skipper will advise on safe swimming areas. If you have medical conditions, inform the skipper before the trip.

h1: Boat Rental Tenerife, Book Your Charter with Skipper
intro:
You want to charter a boat in Tenerife but don’t have a skipper licence. That’s fine, every rental on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper, so you just turn up and enjoy the sun, the sea, and the views of Mount Teide. We list motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, and RIBs from ports all around the island, from Los Cristianos to Puerto Colón. Prices start from around EUR 250 for a half-day on a speedboat, and go up to EUR 3,000 for a luxury catamaran with crew. No hidden fees, no licence checks, just a straight-up booking.

This page is your practical guide to boat rental Tenerife. You’ll find what’s included, which ports to depart from, what types of boats are available, and how to book without the usual headaches. We cover weather, seasons, and who this is for, whether you’re a family, a group of friends, or a couple wanting a private sunset cruise. Let’s get you on the water.
bodyHtml:
What’s Included in Every Boat Rental Tenerife

Every charter you book through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That means you don’t need a boating licence, and you don’t have to worry about navigation, docking, or safety. The skipper handles all that, and they know the local waters, hidden coves, dolphin hotspots, and the best spots for swimming. Most rentals also include fuel, a safety briefing, and basic insurance. Some include food and drinks, but check the listing details. You can also add extras like a barbecue, snorkelling gear, or a photographer. The price you see is the price you pay, except for a refundable damage deposit on some boats.

Departure Ports for Boat Rental Tenerife

Tenerife has several marinas and ports where you can start your charter. The most popular are Los Cristianos (south-west, sheltered bay, lots of restaurants), Puerto Colón (Costa Adeje, close to Playa del Duque and fancier hotels), and Santa Cruz (main city, for east coast trips). You can also depart from Playa de las Américas, Puerto de la Cruz (north), or smaller harbours like Radazul and San Miguel. Each port gives you access to different parts of the coast, from the cliffs of Los Gigantes to the black sand beaches of the north. Pick the one closest to your accommodation to save travel time.

Types of Boats Available

Motor yachts are the most common, fast, stable, and good for covering distance. You’ll find everything from 6-metre speedboats (around EUR 250 for 3 hours) to 15-metre luxury yachts with cabins (EUR 1,500+ for a full day). Catamarans are great for larger groups and stability, they don’t roll as much, so less seasickness. Sailing yachts are quieter and more eco-friendly, but slower. RIBs and speedboats are for thrill-seekers who want to bounce over waves and explore caves. Fishing boats are also available, with rod hire included. Licence-free day boats (under 6 metres, no skipper needed) are rare in Tenerife because of local regulations, most require a skipper anyway, so we include one.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Tenerife

Prices vary by boat size, type, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 6-metre RIB costs from around EUR 250. A half-day on a 10-metre motor yacht is about EUR 600-800. Full-day catamaran charters (8 hours) for up to 12 people start at EUR 1,200 and go to EUR 3,000 for premium vessels with crew. Superyachts (over 20 metres) are price on request, expect EUR 5,000+ per day. Most operators offer morning (10:00-14:00) or afternoon (15:00-19:00) slots, and sunset charters are popular for 2-3 hours at a lower price. Always check what’s included, fuel is usually included, but extras like food, drinks, or water toys cost more.

Best Seasons for Boat Rental Tenerife

Tenerife has a subtropical climate, so you can charter a boat year-round. Summer (June to September) is the busiest, air temperatures hit 30 degrees C, sea water is 24 degrees C, and the trade winds blow from the north-east, making the south coast calmer. Winter (December to February) is cooler (20-22 degrees C) but still pleasant, with fewer crowds and lower prices. Spring and autumn are the sweet spots, warm, calm seas, and good visibility for spotting dolphins and whales. The only months to avoid are when there’s a calima (dust from the Sahara) or strong Atlantic swells, but these are rare and usually pass in a day or two.

How to Book Your Boat Rental Tenerife

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Use the search page to filter by port, boat type, date, and budget. You’ll see a list of available charters with photos, specs, and skipper details. Click on one that suits you, check the inclusions (fuel, food, cancellation policy), and book online with a deposit (usually 30-50%). The remaining balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or card. We recommend booking at least a week in advance during summer, and 2-3 days for winter. You can also contact the operator directly through the platform if you have questions about itineraries or special requests. For more tips, read our blog on chartering in the Canary Islands.

Who Is Boat Rental Tenerife For

This is for anyone who wants to explore Tenerife’s coastline without the hassle of owning or driving a boat. Families with kids, the skipper keeps everyone safe, and you can stop for swimming at places like Playa de las Teresitas or the natural pools of Garachico. Groups of friends, take a party boat to the cliffs of Los Gigantes, play music, and drink cava. Couples, book a sunset cruise for two, with champagne and views of Teide. Solo travellers, join a shared charter (if available) or hire a small RIB for a solo adventure. It’s also for corporate groups, many yachts can host up to 20 people for a day trip with catering. No licence needed, no experience required.

What to Expect on the Day

On the day of your charter, arrive at the port 15 minutes early. Meet the skipper, who will do a safety briefing and show you the boat. You’ll then head out, typical itineraries include cruising along the coast, stopping for a swim at a quiet beach or cove, maybe seeing dolphins or turtles (common off the south coast). Some skippers take you to Masca Bay or the cliffs of Los Gigantes for photos. Lunch is usually at a beachside restaurant or on board if you’ve ordered catering. The skipper returns you to the port on time. Be aware that sea conditions can change, the skipper may adjust the route for safety. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a towel. Most boats have a toilet, but not all have a shower.

Local Attractions and Highlights

Tenerife’s coast is packed with things to see. The cliffs of Los Gigantes are a must, 600-metre vertical drops into the sea, only accessible by boat. The whale and dolphin watching around the south-west coast is excellent, you’ll often see pilot whales, bottlenose dolphins, and even sea turtles. The black sand beaches of the north (like Playa Jardín in Puerto de la Cruz) are unique. For a longer trip, you can sail to the nearby island of La Gomera (about 30 NM from Los Cristianos), a full-day charter, but worth it for the remote beaches. The Teide National Park is visible from the water, especially at sunset. Some skippers offer a stop at the Cueva del Viento (wind cave) near Icod de los Vinos, though it’s a short walk from the beach.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Tenerife Charter

BoatHire24 is a marketplace that connects you with local operators in Tenerife. We don’t own boats, so we can offer a wide range, from budget speedboats to luxury superyachts. Every listing includes a licensed skipper, transparent pricing, and real photos. You book online, pay a deposit, and the rest on the day. We don’t add booking fees, and we have a cancellation policy that’s fair, full refund if you cancel 48 hours before, subject to operator terms. Our customer support team speaks English and Spanish, and we can help with special requests like dietary requirements or extra activities. We’ve been operating in the Canary Islands since 2018, and we know the local market. For more details, check our blog for destination guides and booking tips.

Detailed Port Profiles for Your Tenerife Charter

Each departure port gives you a different starting point and a different day. Los Cristianos is the busiest, with the most charter boats and a sheltered harbour. From here you can reach the whale-watching grounds off the south-west coast in 20 minutes. Puerto Colón in Costa Adeje is more upmarket, surrounded by five-star hotels and the fancier end of Playa del Duque. It is a 15-minute walk from the beach, and the marina has a few decent restaurants for a pre-charter coffee. Santa Cruz de Tenerife is the capital, in the north-east. Departing from here lets you explore the Anaga mountains coast, which is rugged and less touristy, with small coves like Playa de Benijo. Puerto de la Cruz in the north is quieter, and from here you can head to the Orotava Valley coast or the natural pools of Garachico. Radazul and San Miguel are small, local marinas with fewer charter options but lower prices and less crowding. Choose your port based on where you are staying, and if you are flexible, pick one with the boat type you want, as some ports specialise in catamarans (Los Cristianos) while others have more RIBs (Puerto Colón).

Specific Boat Models and Their Costs

To give you a concrete idea, a 4.5-metre RIB with a 40hp engine, seating 4 people, costs from around EUR 200 for 2 hours. A 6-metre RIB with 115hp, seating 6, is EUR 300 for 3 hours. A 8-metre motor yacht (like a Jeanneau or Beneteau) with a cabin, toilet, and sunpad, seating 8, costs from EUR 600 for 4 hours. A 12-metre catamaran (like a Lagoon 42) with 4 cabins, 2 toilets, and a flybridge, seating 12, is EUR 1,200 for 4 hours and EUR 1,800 for 8 hours. A 15-metre luxury motor yacht (like a Azimut or Sunseeker) with full crew, air conditioning, and water toys, starts at EUR 2,500 for 8 hours. A sailing yacht of 10 metres (like a Bavaria 36) costs from EUR 400 for 4 hours, but it is slower and more weather-dependent. Fishing boats are usually 6-8 metres with rod holders and a fish finder, costing EUR 350 for 4 hours. These prices are for the boat and skipper only; fuel is included in most cases, but confirm when booking.

Seasonal Price Variations and Booking Tips

Peak season in Tenerife is July, August, and Christmas/New Year. Prices can be 30-50% higher than in low season (November, February, except Christmas). For example, a catamaran that costs EUR 1,200 in April might be EUR 1,800 in August. Shoulder months (March, May, June, September, October) offer a good balance of decent weather and lower prices. If you are on a budget, book a morning slot (10:00-14:00) rather than a full day, as you still get 4 hours of sun and sea. Sunset charters (17:00-20:00 in summer, 16:00-19:00 in winter) are cheaper, often EUR 100-200 less than the same boat in a daytime slot. Book at least 2 weeks ahead for peak season, 1 week for shoulder, and 3-4 days for low season. Last-minute bookings (1-2 days before) can sometimes get discounts of 10-20%, but only if the boat is not already chartered. Use the search page to compare prices across multiple operators for the same date.

Weather and Sea Conditions in Detail

The trade winds blow from the north-east, so the south coast (Los Cristianos, Costa Adeje) is generally calmer than the north (Puerto de la Cruz). In summer, the wind is lighter, often 10-15 knots, making for smooth seas. In winter, the wind can be 20-25 knots, with swells of 1-2 metres on the south coast and 2-3 metres on the north coast. Most skippers will not go out if the swell is over 2.5 metres, as it is uncomfortable. The sea temperature is 19 degrees C in February and 24 degrees C in August. The calima (Saharan dust) can reduce visibility and make the air hazy, but it rarely lasts more than 2 days. Check the wind forecast on Windy or Windguru before your charter. If the forecast is bad, ask the operator if you can reschedule, most will allow it for free if done 24 hours in advance. The best months for calm seas and clear skies are April, May, September, and October.

Whale and Dolphin Watching Specifics

The waters off the south-west coast of Tenerife are a year-round habitat for pilot whales and bottlenose dolphins. You are almost guaranteed to see them on any charter from Los Cristianos or Puerto Colón, especially in the morning. The whales are often found between the coast and the island of La Gomera, about 5-10 NM offshore. Some operators offer dedicated whale-watching charters with a marine biologist on board, costing from EUR 50 per person for a 2-hour trip. On a private charter, the skipper will take you to the known spots, but it is not guaranteed. If you want a higher chance, book a charter that specifically mentions whale watching in the listing. You can also see sea turtles, flying fish, and occasionally orcas (killer whales) in winter. Do not feed or touch the animals, it is illegal and harmful. The skipper will keep a safe distance, 50 metres for whales, 30 metres for dolphins.

Food and Drink Options on Board

Most charters include water and soft drinks, but not alcohol. You can bring your own food and drink, as long as you clean up afterwards. Some operators offer catering as an extra, ranging from a simple sandwich platter (EUR 15 per person) to a full paella lunch with wine (EUR 40 per person). For a sunset charter, champagne and canapés are common, costing around EUR 25 per person. If you are on a budget, buy your own supplies from a local supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) and bring a cooler bag. The boat will have a small fridge, but space is limited. For longer charters (full day), the skipper can recommend a beachside restaurant where you can moor and eat ashore. This is common in Masca Bay or Playa de la Tejita. Always confirm the food and drink policy when booking, as some operators do not allow you to bring glass bottles for safety reasons.

Special Itineraries and Day Trip Ideas

For a half-day (4 hours), a classic route from Los Cristianos is south-west to the cliffs of Los Gigantes, stopping for a swim at Playa de la Arena or the small cove of Masca. You can also head east to the abandoned hotel at Playa de la Tejita and the Montaña Roja volcano. For a full day (8 hours), you can cross to La Gomera, 30 NM from Los Cristianos, and anchor at the beach of Valle Gran Rey. This is a 1-hour crossing each way, leaving 6 hours for swimming and lunch. Another full-day option is to go north from Santa Cruz to the Anaga mountains, stopping at the black sand beach of Playa de Benijo and the fishing village of Taganana. For a sunset charter, stay local in Costa Adeje, cruise past the hotels, and watch the sun set behind La Gomera. Some operators offer a “party boat” with a DJ and unlimited drinks, costing from EUR 80 per person for 3 hours. Always discuss the itinerary with the skipper before departure, they can tailor it to your interests.

Safety and Practical Considerations

All boats have life jackets for every passenger, a first aid kit, and a VHF radio. The skipper is licensed and trained in first aid. If you are prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure, and avoid a heavy breakfast. The boat will have a toilet, but not all have a shower. Bring biodegradable sunscreen and a rash guard, as the sun is strong even on cloudy days. Do not wear black clothing, it gets hot and shows every mark. The skipper will provide a briefing on emergency procedures and where the life jackets are. If you have any medical conditions, inform the skipper before departure. Children under 12 must wear a life jacket at all times on deck. Do not jump off the boat unless the skipper says it is safe, as currents can be strong near cliffs. The skipper has the final say on the route and schedule, they will not take risks with safety. For more safety tips, read our blog on boating in the Canary Islands.

title: Catamaran Charter Phuket
metaDescription: Book a catamaran charter Phuket with BoatHire24. Compare power and sailing catamarans, see prices from EUR 900, and reserve your day on the Andaman Sea.
h1: Catamaran Charter Phuket, Your Guide to Booking
intro: You want a catamaran charter in Phuket, but you're based in Marbella or visiting the Costa del Sol. That's fine because BoatHire24 can help you compare options and book a catamaran in Phuket through our network of trusted partners. We focus on Marbella and the Costa del Sol for most charters, but we also offer curated bookings for top global destinations like Phuket. The process is the same: you tell us what you need, we find the right boat with a skipper, and you pay securely online. Expect to pay from around EUR 900 for a half-day on a 40-foot sailing catamaran, up to EUR 3,500 for a full day on a luxury power catamaran with crew. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. You just bring your swimsuit and sunscreen.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Charter Phuket

Every catamaran charter in Phuket booked through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, fuel, and basic third-party insurance. The skipper handles navigation and safety, so you can relax. Most charters also include snorkel gear, paddleboards, and a cooler with ice. Food and drinks are usually extra, but you can pre-order a catering package (from EUR 25 per person) or bring your own. Some luxury catamarans include a hostess who serves lunch and drinks. Always check the specific inclusions on the boat listing before booking.

Why Choose a Catamaran Over a Motor Yacht in Phuket

Catamarans have two hulls, which means more deck space and better stability than monohull motor yachts. In Phuket, where the Andaman Sea can get choppy in the afternoon, a catamaran offers a smoother ride. You also get shallower draft, so you can anchor closer to beaches like Freedom Beach or Coral Island. The trade-off is speed: a typical sailing catamaran does 6-8 knots, while a power catamaran does 12-18 knots. If you want to cover more ground, go for a power catamaran. If you want a quiet, eco-friendly day, choose a sailing catamaran.

Popular Catamaran Types for Phuket Charters

You have three main options. Sailing catamarans (35-50 feet, from EUR 900 half-day) are great for couples or small groups who enjoy the wind. Power catamarans (40-55 feet, from EUR 1,500 half-day) offer more speed and luxury, with flybridge lounges and sun pads. Luxury catamarans (50-65 feet, from EUR 2,500 full-day) include crewed service, gourmet meals, and water toys like jet skis. For a large party, a 50-foot sailing catamaran sleeps 10-12 guests comfortably. For a romantic trip, a 40-foot power catamaran with a private cabin works well.

Best Departure Ports for Catamaran Charters in Phuket

Most catamaran charters depart from Chalong Bay, the main marina in southern Phuket. Chalong has easy parking and a few cafes. Other departure points include Ao Po Grand Marina (north, closer to Phang Nga Bay) and Yacht Haven Marina (also north, near the airport). If you're staying on the west coast (Patong, Karon, Kata), you can ask for a pickup by tender from the beach, but expect an extra fee of around EUR 100-200. For the best scenery, depart from Chalong and head south to Coral Island or Racha Island.

Typical Itineraries for a Phuket Catamaran Day Trip

A half-day (4 hours) usually covers Coral Island or Maiton Island. You anchor, snorkel, have lunch, and return. A full day (8 hours) can include Coral Island, Racha Island, and a stop at the famous Phromthep Cape viewpoint from the water. For a longer charter (12 hours or overnight), you can explore Phang Nga Bay with its limestone karsts, James Bond Island, and the floating village of Koh Panyee. All itineraries are flexible, but the skipper has final say based on weather and sea conditions.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Charter Phuket

Prices vary by boat size, age, and season. In low season (May-October), a 40-foot sailing catamaran starts at around EUR 800 for a half-day and EUR 1,200 for a full day. In high season (November-April), the same boat costs EUR 1,100 half-day and EUR 1,800 full-day. Power catamarans are 30-50% more expensive. Luxury catamarans with crew and premium catering start at EUR 2,500 for a full day. All prices include skipper, fuel, and insurance. You pay a 50% deposit to confirm the booking, and the balance 7 days before departure. Cancel up to 14 days before for a full refund.

Best Seasons for Catamaran Charter Phuket

The best time for a catamaran charter in Phuket is November to April, when the sea is calm, skies are clear, and temperatures are 28-32 degrees C. This is high season, so book at least 2-3 months ahead. May to October is low season, with rain and rougher seas, but you get lower prices and fewer crowds. The sea is still navigable most days, but afternoon storms are common. If you're flexible, low season can be a good deal. Avoid the monsoon peaks in September and October, when many charters are cancelled.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter Phuket with BoatHire24

Go to our BoatHire24 homepage and use the destination search bar. Type "Phuket" and select the date and number of guests. You'll see a list of available catamarans with prices, photos, and reviews. Click on one to see full details, then use the booking form to send an enquiry. Our team will confirm availability within 24 hours and send a payment link. You can also call or WhatsApp us for a custom quote. For last-minute bookings (less than 48 hours), call us directly. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for the best selection.

Who Should Book a Catamaran Charter in Phuket

Catamaran charters suit families with kids (stability and space), couples wanting a romantic day, and groups of friends looking for a party boat. They are less suitable for watersports enthusiasts who want speed (choose a RIB instead) or for solo travellers (join a shared charter, which costs around EUR 150 per person). If you're celebrating a birthday or anniversary, a catamaran with a crew and catering is a solid choice. For corporate events, luxury catamarans can host up to 20 guests for a day meeting at sea.

Comparing Catamaran Charter Phuket with Costa del Sol Options

If you're in Marbella, you might wonder why we offer Phuket charters. The answer is simple: we have partners worldwide, and we can arrange a catamaran in Phuket just as easily as in Puerto Banús. The main difference is cost: a 45-foot sailing catamaran in Phuket costs about EUR 1,200 for a full day, while the same boat in Marbella costs EUR 1,800. Phuket also offers more exotic scenery (limestone islands, emerald water) compared to the Costa del Sol's rocky coves. However, the Costa del Sol has better infrastructure and more consistent wind for sailors. If you want a tropical experience, go to Phuket. If you want convenience and proximity, stay in Marbella. Browse our search page to compare both destinations.

Local Tips for Your Phuket Catamaran Day

Bring reef-safe sunscreen because the marine park fees (around EUR 10 per person) support conservation. Pack a light jacket for the afternoon breeze. Most catamarans have a bluetooth speaker, but you can bring your own. Tip the skipper and crew 10-15% if service is good. Avoid booking on a full moon (unless you want a full moon party) because anchorages get crowded. For a quieter experience, go on a weekday. If you have time, combine your charter with a visit to the Big Buddha or a cooking class in Phuket Town.

For more tips on boat rentals, check our blog. And if you decide to stay local, we have plenty of catamarans in Marbella and the Costa del Sol. Just search for "catamaran charter Marbella" on our site.

Detailed Breakdown of Phuket's Catamaran Charter Costs by Season

To give you a clearer picture, here are some real-world price ranges for Phuket catamaran charters in 2025. In high season (November to April), a 45-foot Lagoon sailing catamaran for a full day (8 hours) runs from EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,000. The same boat in low season (May to October) drops to EUR 1,000 to EUR 1,400. A 50-foot power catamaran like a Fountaine Pajot MY44 costs EUR 2,500 to EUR 3,500 in high season and EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,500 in low season. Add EUR 150 to EUR 300 for a hostess or chef. Marine park fees are extra: EUR 10 per person for Coral Island, EUR 20 for Racha Island, and EUR 40 for Phang Nga Bay. Always confirm the total price before booking, including any fuel surcharges.

Best Catamarans for Large Groups in Phuket

If you have a group of 12 to 20 people, you want a boat with a wide beam and plenty of deck space. The Lagoon 52 (52 feet, sailing) sleeps 12 overnight but can take 20 for a day charter. It has a large flybridge, a forward seating area, and a spacious saloon. The Sunreef 60 (60 feet, sailing or power) is another option, with a hydraulic swim platform and a jacuzzi, but it costs EUR 3,000 to EUR 4,500 for a full day. For power catamarans, the Fountaine Pajot Power 67 (67 feet) can host 25 guests and has three decks with a flybridge bar. All these boats include two crew members. Book at least three months ahead for large groups in high season.

Phuket Catamaran Charter for Weddings and Proposals

Catamarans are popular for weddings and proposals in Phuket because they offer a private setting with sunset views. A typical wedding package includes a catamaran for 4-6 hours, a photographer, a bouquet, and a cake, starting at EUR 1,500 for a 40-foot sailing catamaran. For a proposal, you can charter a 50-foot luxury catamaran with a private chef and a sunset cruise around Koh Yao Noi. The crew can help with decorations and timing. Avoid the rainy season (September-October) for outdoor ceremonies. Most boats have a sound system for music, but you need a special permit for fireworks. Check with your charter company about local marriage registration requirements if you want a legal ceremony at sea.

Comparing Phuket Catamaran Charter with Other Thai Destinations

Phuket is the most accessible place for a catamaran charter in Thailand, with direct international flights and a wide range of boats. But you also have options in Krabi (departing from Ao Nang or Railay) and Koh Samui (departing from Bophut or Nathon). Krabi offers similar limestone scenery but fewer luxury catamarans. Koh Samui has calmer seas in the Gulf of Thailand but less dramatic landscapes. Phuket's advantage is the variety of itineraries: you can go south to the Andaman islands or north to Phang Nga Bay. Prices in Krabi are about 10-15% lower than Phuket, but the boat selection is smaller. If you want the best mix of convenience, boat quality, and scenery, Phuket is your best bet.

What to Pack for a Catamaran Charter in Phuket

Packing smart makes your day more comfortable. Bring a rash guard or long-sleeve UV shirt for snorkelling, because the sun is intense even through clouds. A dry bag for your phone and wallet is essential, as is a waterproof camera. Most catamarans have a freshwater shower on the swim platform, so bring a towel. If you get seasick, take motion sickness tablets 30 minutes before departure, even though catamarans are stable. Wear non-marking, soft-soled shoes to avoid scratching the deck. Bring cash for tips and marine park fees, because some boats don't accept cards. Avoid heavy perfume or aftershave, as it attracts insects on the islands.

Phuket Catamaran Charter for Fishing Enthusiasts

Some catamarans in Phuket are configured for fishing, with rod holders, a live bait well, and a fighting chair. These are usually power catamarans between 40 and 50 feet. You can target mahi-mahi, tuna, and barracuda in the Andaman Sea, especially around the Similan Islands (a 2-hour ride from Phuket). A full-day fishing charter on a catamaran costs from EUR 1,800, including tackle and bait. The crew will clean and fillet your catch, and you can arrange for a local restaurant to cook it. Note that fishing is banned in marine park areas like Phang Nga Bay, so you need to go offshore. Check the season: November to May is best for pelagic fish.

How to Avoid Crowds on Your Phuket Catamaran Charter

Phuket's popular spots like Coral Island and Phi Phi can get busy, especially in high season. To avoid crowds, leave early (depart by 8:00 AM) and head to less visited islands like Koh Mai Thon (Maiton Island) or Koh Racha Yai. These have fewer boats and better snorkelling. Another trick is to book a full-day charter and visit Phang Nga Bay, which is large enough to find quiet corners. Avoid weekends and Thai public holidays (Songkran in April, Loy Krathong in November) when locals also go out. If you want complete solitude, ask your skipper to anchor at Koh Yao Noi's eastern coast, which has few charters. The boat will cost the same, but the experience is much better.

Catamaran Charter Phuket for Digital Nomads and Remote Workers

If you work remotely and want a day on the water without missing deadlines, some catamarans offer stable WiFi via a 4G router. A 45-foot power catamaran with a flybridge and a shaded saloon works well as a floating office. You can work during the morning sail, anchor for lunch and a swim, then work again on the return. Expect to pay EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,000 for a full day with WiFi included. Check the signal strength before booking, because some areas like Phang Nga Bay have poor coverage. Bring a power bank, because the boat's outlets may be limited. This is a good option if you want to combine work with a sunset cruise.
