title: Catamaran Charter Bali
metaDescription: Book a catamaran charter Bali style on the Costa del Sol. Spacious decks, sunbathing nets, and a licensed skipper from Puerto Banús or Marbella. Browse now.
h1: Catamaran Charter Bali, Costa del Sol Style
intro:
You want a catamaran charter Bali vibes but you are on the Costa del Sol. That is fine. The Mediterranean has the same sun, better infrastructure, and no jet lag. A catamaran from BoatHire24 gives you the same wide decks, the same net for lounging over the water, and a skipper who knows where the dolphins hang out. You will start from Puerto Banús, Marbella, or one of five other ports, and you will spend the day anchored off a cove that looks like it was designed for a postcard. No flights required.

Catamarans are the best option for groups who want stability, space, and a shallow draft that lets you get close to beaches. The Bali brand is a popular choice in the charter fleet because of its open-plan layout and those forward cockpits that turn into a sunbathing area. You can rent one for a half-day, a full day, or a week. Every charter includes a licensed skipper. You just bring the drinks, the playlist, and the sunscreen.
bodyHtml:
Why a Catamaran Charter Bali on the Costa del Sol

The Bali catamaran is not a boat. It is a floating apartment with a sun deck. The model you will find in the Marbella fleet is usually the Bali 4.0 or Bali 4.2, both of which have the trademark solid foredeck instead of a trampoline net. That means you can walk from the saloon to the bow without climbing over a net. It also means you can put cushions, a table, or a sun lounger up front. The open-plan saloon connects directly to the aft cockpit, so the whole living area is one continuous space. You get four or five cabins, two or three heads, and a galley that can handle a paella for ten people.

The skipper lives in a separate crew cabin. You do not have to share your bathroom with him. He will handle the mooring, the navigation, and the anchorage spots. You just decide where you want to go. Typical day trips include a run west to Estepona, where the old town has a terrace for a late lunch, or east to Cala del Faro, a small cove with clear water and a beach bar that only serves seafood. If you want a longer charter, you can cross the Strait of Gibraltar and spend a day in Morocco. The Bali can do 8-10 knots, so the crossing takes about an hour. You will see dolphins on the way.

Which Ports Can You Depart From

You have six departure ports to choose from. The most popular for a catamaran charter Bali is Puerto Banús because it is the centre of the Marbella social scene. You step off the boat and you are on the Golden Mile. The marina has fuel docks, water, and a supermarket for provisioning. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and closer to the old town. Cabopino is a small marina near the Artola sand dunes, good if you want to anchor off the naturist beach. Estepona is further west, closer to Gibraltar and the dolphin watching zone. Sotogrande is a luxury residential marina with a golf course next door. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near the Tivoli theme park and the Selwo Marina dolphinarium.

Each port has its own character. If you want to be in the middle of the action, pick Puerto Banús. If you want a relaxed start with easy parking, pick Cabopino or Estepona. The skipper will meet you at the boat, give you a safety briefing, and cast off within 15 minutes. You do not need to check in at an office. Everything is arranged online through BoatHire24.

What Is Included in the Charter Price

The base price includes the boat hire, the licensed skipper, fuel for a standard day trip (usually up to 4 hours of cruising), VAT, and insurance. You do not pay extra for the skipper or the fuel if you stay within the typical itinerary. If you want to go further, for example to Gibraltar or Morocco, the fuel cost is extra and you pay it directly at the fuel dock. The skipper will give you an estimate before you leave. You also pay for food, drinks, and any marina fees if you stop for lunch at a port. Some charters include a paddleboard or snorkelling gear. Check the listing on the search page for the specific inclusions.

Prices for a Bali catamaran start from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day and EUR 1,800 for a full day in low season. High season (July, August, September) can go up to EUR 2,500 for a full day. A week-long charter starts from around EUR 8,000. You can negotiate a discount for multi-day bookings or for last-minute availability in shoulder season. The booking platform shows live availability and you can reserve with a 30% deposit. The balance is due 14 days before departure.

Boat Options: Bali 4.0 vs Bali 4.2

The Bali 4.0 is 12 metres long with four cabins and two heads. It sleeps eight guests comfortably. The forward cockpit is the standout feature: a U-shaped seating area that converts into a sunbed. The saloon has a galley down and a dinette that seats ten. The helm station is on the flybridge, so the skipper has a clear view over the bow. The Bali 4.2 is the larger version, 12.8 metres with four cabins and three heads. It has a bigger galley and a separate crew cabin. Both boats have a shallow draft of around 1.1 metres, so you can anchor close to the beach. You can also beach the stern on a sandy shore for easy boarding.

If you want a sailing catamaran with the Bali layout, you can charter a Bali 4.0 or 4.2 with the standard rig. The sails are easy to handle and the skipper will use them when the wind is favourable. If the wind drops, you motor. The fuel consumption is low because the catamaran hull is efficient. You can also charter a motor catamaran, but those are less common in the Marbella fleet. For a full list of available Bali models, check the BoatHire24 blog for the latest fleet updates.

Seasons and Weather

The Costa del Sol has 300 days of sunshine a year. The best months for a catamaran charter Bali are May to October. In May and June, the sea temperature is 18-20 degrees C, the air is 25-28 degrees C, and the wind is light from the west. July and August are hot, 30-35 degrees C, with a sea breeze that picks up in the afternoon. The water temperature reaches 24-26 degrees C. September is the sweet spot: still warm, fewer crowds, and a stable easterly wind that makes for a comfortable sail. October is good but the water cools to 20 degrees C and the chance of rain increases.

Winter charters are possible but less popular. The air temperature in December is 15-18 degrees C, the sea is 16 degrees C. You will need a jacket and a windbreaker. The advantage is that the marinas are quiet, the prices are lower, and you can book a Bali catamaran for around EUR 800 for a half-day. The skipper will still take you out, but you will spend more time in the saloon than on the deck. If you are a cold-weather person, it is fine. If you want to swim, wait until June.

How to Book Your Catamaran Charter Bali

Booking is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 website, select the Bali catamaran model, choose your date and port, and submit a booking request. The system sends a confirmation within 24 hours. You will receive a contract by email with the terms and conditions. Read it carefully, especially the cancellation policy. Most charters allow free cancellation up to 30 days before departure. After that, you lose the deposit. If the weather is unsafe, the skipper will cancel and you get a full refund or a reschedule. You do not need a boating licence. The skipper has all the necessary qualifications and insurance.

On the day of the charter, arrive at the marina 15 minutes before the scheduled time. The skipper will be at the boat. You will do a quick safety briefing, sign a waiver, and then you are off. Bring sunscreen, a towel, and a hat. The boat has a fridge, a freezer, and an ice maker. You can bring your own food and drinks or order a catering package through the charter company. Some companies offer a barbecue on the aft deck. If you want to stop for lunch at a beach club, tell the skipper in advance so he can reserve a mooring buoy.

Who Is a Catamaran Charter Bali For

This charter is for groups of 6 to 10 people who want to party, relax, or explore. It is ideal for a birthday, a bachelor or bachelorette party, a family reunion, or a corporate day out. The stability of the catamaran means nobody gets seasick, even in a light chop. The shallow draft means you can anchor right off the beach at Cala del Faro or Cabopino. The open layout means nobody is stuck in a cabin. You can all hang out in the saloon, on the foredeck, or on the flybridge. The skipper will serve as a host and a guide. He knows the best spots for swimming, snorkelling, and lunch.

If you are a couple looking for a romantic charter, a catamaran might be too big. Consider a sailing yacht or a RIB. If you are a solo traveller, a catamaran is not cost-effective unless you join a shared charter. Some companies offer shared trips on catamarans during July and August. Check the listings on the search page for shared charter options. Otherwise, gather your friends and split the cost. It works out at around EUR 200 per person for a full day, which is cheaper than a beach club with a sunbed and a bottle of cava.

Local Highlights You Will See

From the deck of a Bali catamaran, you will see the Sierra Blanca mountains, with La Concha peak at 1,270 metres. Along the coast, you will pass the dunes of Artola, the lighthouse at Calaburras, and the fishing port of La Cala de Mijas. If you go west, you will see the Rock of Gibraltar from the water. The skipper will point out the caves and the Barbary macaques. If you go east, you will see the cliffs of Maro and the entrance to the Nerja caves. You can anchor near the caves and swim into a small sea cave. The water is turquoise and the rock formations are dramatic. Do not skip this stop.

You will also see dolphins. Common dolphins and striped dolphins live in the Strait of Gibraltar year-round. The skipper will know where to find them. They often swim alongside the catamaran, especially in the morning. If you are lucky, you might see a pilot whale or a fin whale. The Strait is a migration corridor. The best time for whale watching is April to June. The skipper will not guarantee sightings, but he will try. If you are specifically interested in marine life, mention it when you book. The skipper can adjust the route to spend more time in the dolphin zones.

What to Bring and What Not to Bring

Bring a soft-sided cooler if you have one. The boat has a fridge but it fills up fast with drinks. Bring a reusable water bottle. The boat has a water maker, but it is polite to use it sparingly. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and a rash guard for long exposure. Bring a waterproof phone case. Bring a change of clothes for the evening. Do not bring glass bottles. The skipper will ask you to transfer drinks into plastic or cans. Glass breaks and bare feet on a catamaran are common. Do not bring high heels. The deck is non-slip but heels will leave marks. Do not bring a drone unless you have permission from the skipper. Some marinas and national parks have restrictions. Do not bring a bad attitude. The skipper is there to help you have a good time. If you are rude or aggressive, he has the right to terminate the charter and return to port. You will not get a refund.

Do bring a sense of adventure. A catamaran charter Bali on the Costa del Sol is one of the best ways to see the coast. You will see places you cannot reach by car. You will eat lunch with your feet in the sand. You will swim in water that is clear enough to see the anchor chain. You will come back with a tan and a story. Book now on BoatHire24 and start planning.

title: Boat Rental Algarve
metaDescription: Looking for boat rental Algarve? We offer skippered yacht charters from Marbella to the Algarve. Book your next adventure with BoatHire24 today.
h1: Boat Rental Algarve, Skippered Charters from Spain
intro:
You’re searching for boat rental Algarve, and you probably want sun, sea, and a skipper who knows the best coves. Here’s the catch: we operate from the Costa del Sol, not the Algarve itself. But that doesn’t mean you’re stuck. Our fleet of motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs can take you from Puerto Banús or Estepona across to the Algarve coast in a few hours. You get the same crystal-clear water, dramatic cliffs, and seaside towns, just with a Spanish departure point. And yes, every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you can focus on the sangria.

Think of it as a two-country trip in one day. You leave from Marbella, cruise past Gibraltar (dolphins guaranteed most of the year), and arrive at places like Lagos or Albufeira. The boat is yours, the itinerary is flexible, and the skipper handles the navigation. No paperwork, no stress. Just you, your crew, and the Atlantic.
bodyHtml:
Why Choose Boat Rental Algarve from the Costa del Sol?

You might wonder why you’d rent a boat from Spain to visit the Algarve. Simple: choice and convenience. Marbella’s marinas, especially BoatHire24, offer a wider range of boats than most Algarve ports. You can pick a 12-metre motor yacht for a fast crossing (about 2 hours to Faro) or a catamaran for a more relaxed sail. Plus, you get the added bonus of seeing the Strait of Gibraltar, where pods of common dolphins and pilot whales hang out. The Algarve’s coastline is stunning, but so is the journey there.

The Algarve itself has plenty of charter companies, but they often lack the variety or the English-speaking skippers you’ll find here. Our skippers are all licensed, experienced, and speak fluent English. They know the best anchorages on both sides of the border. And because you’re booking through a marketplace, you can compare prices and boat types without calling ten different operators.

What’s Included in Your Skippered Charter

Every charter through our platform includes a professional skipper who handles the boat, safety, and navigation. You don’t need a licence or any experience. The skipper will also act as a guide, pointing out landmarks like the Rock of Gibraltar or the caves at Benagil. Fuel is typically extra unless stated otherwise, but we’ll give you an estimate before you book. Some boats include snacks and soft drinks; others have a full bar. Check the listing details.

You also get insurance, life jackets, and a safety briefing. The skipper will decide the route based on weather and your preferences. Want to stop for a swim near the Ponta da Piedade cliffs? No problem. Prefer to anchor in a quiet cove for lunch? The skipper knows the spots. The boat is yours for the agreed hours, usually 4, 6, or 8 hours, with the option to extend.

Departure Ports for Your Algarve Adventure

We operate from six ports on the Costa del Sol, all within easy reach of the Algarve. The closest is Estepona, just 40 nautical miles from Faro. A fast RIB or motor yacht can make the crossing in under 90 minutes. Puerto Banús is a bit further (50 NM) but offers the flashiest boats and the best pre-departure people-watching. Marbella Marina is central and easy to reach from Málaga airport. Cabopino and Sotogrande are quieter options, ideal if you want a more relaxed start. Benalmádena is further east but still doable for a full-day charter.

Your skipper will pick the best departure time based on tides and wind. Most crossings happen in the morning when the sea is calm. You’ll arrive in the Algarve by late morning, with the whole afternoon to explore. Return is usually by early evening, but you can arrange an overnight stay if you want more time. Just let us know when booking.

Boat Options for the Algarve Crossing

Not all boats are suited for a crossing of 30-50 nautical miles. We’ll help you choose the right one. Motor yachts from 10 to 15 metres are the most popular for this trip. They’re fast (20-30 knots), stable, and have plenty of deck space. Catamarans are slower but more spacious and fuel-efficient; a 12-metre cat can do the crossing in 3 hours. Sailing yachts are an option if you have a full day and want the experience, but they’re slower (5-8 knots). RIBs and speedboats are best for small groups who want a thrill; they’re fast but bumpy in choppy seas.

We also have licence-free day boats (up to 15 hp) for the Algarve’s protected waters, but they’re not suitable for the crossing. You’d need to pick one up from a local Algarve port. For superyachts (20 metres plus), the crossing is a breeze, and you can bring a larger group. Prices vary widely: expect from around EUR 800 for a 4-hour RIB trip to EUR 3,000 for a full-day motor yacht. Superyachts are price on request.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Algarve

You’re not getting a cheap day out. A standard 8-hour charter on a 12-metre motor yacht with skipper starts from around EUR 1,200, including fuel for the crossing. Add another EUR 200-300 for fuel on longer trips. Catamarans are similar, around EUR 1,500 for a full day. RIBs are cheaper, from EUR 600 for 4 hours, but you’ll feel the waves. Fishing boats are available too, from around EUR 700 for a half day, but they’re slower.

Prices drop in the shoulder season (April-May, September-October) by about 20%. July and August are peak, so book early. We don’t set prices; each owner sets their own. You can search our listings for current rates. Always check what’s included: some boats include fuel, others don’t. We recommend budgeting EUR 150-300 extra for food, drinks, and tips for the skipper (10-15% is standard if you’re happy).

Best Time for a Boat Rental Algarve Trip

The Algarve is a year-round destination, but the best time for a boat trip is May to October. Sea temperatures range from 18°C in May to 24°C in August. Air temperatures hit 30°C in summer. The wind is usually light in the morning, picking up in the afternoon. The crossing from Spain is most comfortable in calm conditions, which are common from June to September. April and October can be windy, so check the forecast.

Winter charters (November-March) are possible but less popular. The water is cooler (16-18°C), and the crossing can be rougher. However, you’ll have the Algarve’s beaches almost to yourself, and prices are lower. Dolphin sightings are still common. Just bring a jacket for the wind on deck.

What to See and Do in the Algarve by Boat

The Algarve coastline is famous for its limestone cliffs, sea caves, and golden beaches. From the water, you can explore the Benagil Sea Cave (a must-see), the Ponta da Piedade rock formations near Lagos, and the Ria Formosa Natural Park, a lagoon system with islands and birdlife. Your skipper will know which spots are accessible and less crowded. Most charters include a stop for swimming and snorkelling. The water is clear, and you might see octopus or bream.

If you want to go ashore, popular stops include the town of Lagos (historic centre, marina, and restaurants), Albufeira (lively beaches and nightlife), and Faro (old town and airport). Some skippers will arrange a lunch stop at a beachside restaurant. Just ask. For a longer trip, you can head to the western Algarve, near Sagres, where the cliffs are dramatic and the surfing is world-class. That’s a full-day trip from Marbella, but doable.

How to Book Your Boat Rental Algarve Charter

Booking is straightforward. Go to our website, BoatHire24, and use the search filters to pick your port, boat type, and date. You’ll see a list of available boats with photos, specifications, and prices. Click on a listing to see the full details, including what’s included and the skipper’s bio. You can request a booking directly through the site. We’ll confirm availability within 24 hours. Payment is secure via card or bank transfer.

We recommend booking at least a week in advance for summer, especially for popular boats. Last-minute bookings (within 48 hours) are sometimes possible, but you’ll have fewer options. If you’re unsure which boat suits your group, call or email us. We’ve done this trip ourselves and can advise. We also have a blog with more details on routes and tips.

Who Is This Boat Rental Algarve For?

This trip works for groups of friends, families, couples, or corporate events. The boat can accommodate from 6 to 12 guests depending on size. Children are welcome; the skipper will adjust the speed and stops accordingly. If you’re celebrating a birthday or anniversary, the skipper can help arrange catering or decorations (extra cost). The Algarve is also popular for bachelor/bachelorette parties, but keep it respectful, the skipper can refuse if the group is unruly.

Not for you if you’re prone to seasickness (the crossing can be bumpy) or if you want a budget option. This is a premium experience. But if you want a unique day out that combines two countries, stunning scenery, and a private boat, it’s hard to beat.

Crossing the Strait: What to Expect on the Journey

The crossing from the Costa del Sol to the Algarve takes you through the Strait of Gibraltar, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Your skipper will navigate around cargo ships and tankers, so you’re in safe hands. The good news is that this area is also a marine wildlife hotspot. On a typical crossing, you’ll see common dolphins riding the bow wave, and if you’re lucky, pilot whales or even a sunfish. The skipper will slow down or stop if there’s a pod nearby, giving you time to take photos. The crossing itself takes 1.5 to 3 hours depending on the boat and conditions. Bring a light jacket, sunscreen, and a hat, the wind can be strong even on a sunny day. If you’re prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure; the skipper can recommend a pharmacy in Marbella.

Ports in the Algarve Where You Can Dock

Once you arrive in the Algarve, you can dock at several marinas. The most common is Portimão Marina, a large facility with restaurants, shops, and fuel docks. It’s close to the Benagil caves and the Ferragudo fishing village. Another option is Vilamoura Marina, a more upscale spot with a casino and golf courses nearby. Lagos Marina is smaller but charming, with easy access to the Ponta da Piedade cliffs. Faro Marina is convenient if you want to fly home from Faro airport, but it’s less scenic. Your skipper will arrange docking fees (usually EUR 20-50 for a few hours) and handle the paperwork. If you want to stay overnight, most marinas have visitor berths, but book ahead in summer. Some boats allow you to anchor off a beach and use a dinghy to go ashore, which saves docking fees and feels more adventurous.

Licence-Free Day Boats in the Algarve

If you don’t want to cross the Strait but still want to explore the Algarve by boat, we can arrange a licence-free day boat for you. These are small motorboats (up to 15 hp) that don’t require a licence to operate. You can rent one from a local Algarve port like Portimão or Albufeira, and we’ll help you book it through our network. The boat comes with a safety briefing, a map, and a VHF radio. You can drive it yourself to the Benagil cave, the Marinha beach, or the Ria Formosa islands. The cost is lower, from around EUR 150 for a half day, but you’re limited to protected coastal waters and calm weather. It’s a good option for a small group (up to 5 people) who want flexibility and independence. Just remember, you’re responsible for the boat, so don’t go too far from shore and check the wind forecast.

Seasonal Variations in the Algarve Boat Rental Market

The Algarve boat rental market changes with the seasons. In summer (June to August), demand is high, and you’ll need to book at least two weeks in advance. Prices are at their peak, and marinas are crowded. The water is warmest (22-24°C), and the sea is calmest. In spring (April to May) and autumn (September to October), the weather is still pleasant (20-25°C air temperature), but there are fewer tourists. You can often negotiate a discount, and you’ll have more choice of boats. The water is cooler (18-20°C), but still swimmable. In winter (November to March), many charter companies reduce their fleet or close entirely. You can still find a few boats, but the crossing can be rough, and some Algarve marinas have limited services. We recommend spring or autumn for the best balance of price, weather, and availability. If you’re flexible with dates, you can save up to 30% compared to July.

Customising Your Itinerary: Examples of Day Trips

You can tailor your Algarve boat trip to your interests. Here are three examples. Example one: a 4-hour fast trip from Estepona to Benagil. You leave at 8am, arrive at the cave by 10am, spend an hour swimming and taking photos, then head to Marinha beach for a quick stop, and return by noon. This works well with a RIB or small motor yacht. Example two: a full-day cultural trip from Puerto Banús to Lagos. You cross to Portimão, dock for lunch at a seafood restaurant in Lagos old town, then explore the Ponta da Piedade grottoes by dinghy, and return by 6pm. This suits a catamaran or larger motor yacht. Example three: a wildlife-focused trip from Marbella to the Strait of Gibraltar. You spend the morning dolphin-watching near the Rock, then cross to the Algarve for a late lunch in Faro, and return via the Ria Formosa. This is best with a sailing yacht or a quiet motor yacht that doesn’t scare the animals. Your skipper will help you plan the route based on your preferences and the weather.

Practical Tips for Your Boat Rental Algarve Day

A few things to make your trip smoother. Pack a waterproof bag for your phone and camera, spray from the sea can damage electronics. Bring cash in euros for tips, drinks, and any unexpected costs (like a taxi from the marina to a restaurant). The sun in the Algarve is strong, even in spring, so use reef-safe sunscreen and reapply every two hours. If you’re prone to seasickness, take medication 30 minutes before departure; the skipper will have ginger biscuits or wristbands as backup. Wear non-slip shoes, boat decks get slippery. And don’t forget your passport or ID card, you’re crossing an international border, and the Spanish or Portuguese authorities might do a spot check. The skipper will carry the boat’s registration and insurance documents, but you need to prove your identity. Finally, confirm the exact meeting point with the skipper the day before. Some marinas have multiple docks, and getting lost is stressful.

Combining a Boat Rental Algarve with a Stay in Marbella

You can make a holiday of it by staying in Marbella before or after your boat trip. Marbella has plenty of accommodation, from luxury hotels like the Marbella Club to budget apartments in the old town. You can spend a day exploring Puerto Banús, with its designer shops and yachts, or hike up La Concha mountain for the views. The drive from Málaga airport to Marbella is 40 minutes, and from there to Estepona is another 20 minutes. If you book a boat trip early in your stay, you’ll have time to adjust to the time zone and weather. We can recommend restaurants in Marbella for a pre-trip dinner, like a beachfront chiringuito with fresh grilled fish. After your Algarve trip, you’ll be back in Marbella by evening, ready for a relaxing sunset drink. This combination works well for a week-long holiday: three days on land, one day on the boat, and the rest for recovery or exploration.

metaDescription: Book a catamaran charter Corfu with a licensed skipper. Compare prices, boats, and ports. Instant online booking. Start your Greek island adventure today.
h1: Catamaran Charter Corfu
intro:
You want a catamaran charter in Corfu, but you are not sure where to start. The good news is that Corfu is one of the best places in the Ionian Sea for a catamaran trip, with flat waters, reliable winds, and dozens of secluded coves. The bad news is that sorting through the options can be a pain. That is where BoatHire24 comes in. We list catamarans from private owners and local charter companies, all with a licensed skipper included, so you can just turn up and enjoy the day.

Whether you want a half-day cruise along the coast, a full-day island hop to Paxos and Antipaxos, or a week-long liveaboard adventure, we have the boat for you. Departure ports include Corfu Town, Gouvia Marina, and Kassiopi. Prices start from around EUR 800 for a half-day on a 40-foot catamaran for up to 8 guests. You can browse our full inventory on the BoatHire24 homepage and filter by size, duration, and price.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Charter Corfu

Every catamaran charter listed on BoatHire24 includes a professional skipper who knows the local waters. That means you do not need a boating licence or any previous experience. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and mooring, so you can focus on swimming, sunbathing, and eating. Fuel costs are usually extra and are charged at the end of the trip based on hours used. Some charters also include a hostess or a chef for an additional fee. Standard inclusions are life jackets, snorkelling gear, a cooler with ice, and a Bluetooth speaker. You should confirm the exact inclusions with the owner before booking.

Why Corfu Is Perfect for a Catamaran Trip

Corfu sits in the northern Ionian Sea, where the water is calm and the coastline is rugged. The island has a mix of sandy beaches, pebble coves, and dramatic cliffs. The prevailing wind is the northwesterly Maistro, which is gentle in summer, rarely exceeding 15 knots. That makes catamaran sailing comfortable even for guests who get seasick. You can anchor at Paleokastritsa, swim in the Blue Lagoon, or visit the tiny island of Vido. The water temperature in July and August is around 26 degrees C, so you can stay in for hours.

Departure Ports for Catamaran Charter Corfu

Most catamarans depart from Corfu Town, specifically the old port or the new marina. Gouvia Marina is the largest and best equipped, with parking, restaurants, and a supermarket. Kassiopi, in the northeast, is a good option if you want to sail towards Albania or the Diapontia Islands. Some smaller boats can also be chartered from Benitses or Petriti on the south coast. Each port has its own advantages. Corfu Town gives you quick access to the west coast beaches. Kassiopi is closer to the mainland and the islands of Othonoi and Erikoussa.

Types of Catamarans Available

You can find catamarans from 36 to 50 feet on BoatHire24. The most common are the Lagoon 42, the Bali 4.2, and the Fountaine Pajot Saba 50. These boats have 4 to 6 cabins and can sleep 8 to 12 guests, though day charters usually limit the number to 10 or 12 due to safety regulations. If you want something smaller, there are 38-foot catamarans with 3 cabins. For a premium experience, look for a newer model with a flybridge, a bowsprit net, and a hydraulic swim platform. Every listing includes photos, a layout diagram, and a list of onboard equipment.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Charter Corfu

Prices vary depending on the boat size, age, season, and duration. A half-day charter (4 to 5 hours) on a 40-foot catamaran starts from around EUR 800 in low season and goes up to EUR 1,200 in August. A full day (8 hours) costs between EUR 1,200 and EUR 2,000. Weekly charters for a liveaboard experience start from around EUR 4,000 in June and can reach EUR 8,000 in August. All prices include the skipper. Fuel is extra and typically costs EUR 100 to EUR 200 per day. You should also budget for a tip for the skipper, usually 10% to 15% of the charter fee. For exact prices, use the search page and filter by your dates.

Best Time to Book a Catamaran Charter Corfu

The season runs from April to October. May and June are the best months for sailing because the weather is warm but not too hot, and the wind is steady. July and August are peak season, with higher prices and more crowded anchorages. September is also excellent, with water temperatures still around 24 degrees C and fewer tourists. October can be windy, but it is still possible for a day trip if you are flexible. If you want to book a specific boat for August, do it at least 2 months in advance. For May or September, 2 to 4 weeks ahead is usually enough.

Popular Itineraries for a Corfu Catamaran Charter

Most day charters head south to the beaches of Agios Gordios, Glyfada, and Myrtiotissa. A full-day trip can reach the famous Blue Lagoon on the east coast near the Albanian border, where the water is shallow and turquoise. Another popular route is to the west coast caves near Paleokastritsa. For a longer trip, you can sail to the island of Paxos and Antipaxos, which is about 2 hours from Corfu Town. There you will find the Voutoumi beach and the blue caves. Some charters also offer a sunset cruise with dinner included. You can read more about these itineraries on our blog.

Who Should Book a Catamaran Charter Corfu

Catamaran charters are ideal for families with children, because the boat is stable and has plenty of deck space. They are also great for groups of friends who want to party without the risk of seasickness. Couples looking for a romantic sunset sail will appreciate the comfort and privacy. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared catamaran day trip, which is cheaper and a good way to meet people. Corporate groups often book catamarans for team-building events or client entertainment. The skipper can organise a barbecue on board or arrange a stop at a beachside taverna.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter Corfu on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 website, enter your destination as Corfu, and select your dates. You will see a list of available catamarans with prices, photos, and skipper profiles. Click on a listing to see the full details, including cancellation policy, what to bring, and the exact meeting point. Once you choose a boat, you can send an inquiry or book directly if the calendar shows instant booking. You pay a deposit of 30% to 50% online, and the balance is due on the day of the charter. The skipper will meet you at the port 15 minutes before departure.

What to Bring on a Catamaran Charter Corfu

Pack sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a swimsuit, and a towel. The sun in Corfu is strong, even in spring. Bring a light jacket or a windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. If you plan to eat on board, you can bring your own food and drinks, or ask the owner if they provide a catering service. Most catamarans have a fridge and a gas stove. Alcoholic drinks are allowed, but the skipper will limit consumption if it becomes unsafe. Do not forget a camera or a phone with a waterproof case. The views of the Corfu coastline from the sea are spectacular.

Safety on Catamaran Charter Corfu

All catamarans on BoatHire24 are fully insured and comply with Greek maritime regulations. The skipper holds a valid license and has passed a safety briefing. Life jackets are provided for all guests, and there is a liferaft on board. The skipper will give a short safety talk before departure. You should listen carefully and ask questions if something is unclear. In case of bad weather, the skipper has the authority to cancel or modify the itinerary. Your deposit will be refunded if the cancellation is due to unsafe conditions. We recommend travel insurance that covers trip cancellation.

Local Highlights Near Corfu

Corfu Town is a UNESCO World Heritage site with Venetian architecture, narrow streets, and a lively square called Spianada. The old fortress and the new fortress offer panoramic views. If you have time before or after your charter, visit the Achilleion Palace, built for Empress Elisabeth of Austria. The nearby island of Vido has a small beach and a cafe. For a taste of local food, try pastitsada, sofrito, and bourdeto. The local wine is mostly white and pairs well with seafood. You can find tavernas in the old town and along the waterfront in Gouvia.

Frequently Asked Questions

Comparing Corfu Catamarans with Other Boat Types

If you are deciding between a catamaran and a monohull sailing yacht, the main difference is stability. A catamaran has two hulls, so it does not heel over when sailing. That means you can walk around, pour a drink, and use the toilet without holding on. Monohulls are cheaper to charter, but they lean and can make some guests uncomfortable. A motor yacht is faster but burns more fuel and has less deck space. For a day trip with a group of 8 to 12 people, a catamaran is the best compromise of space, comfort, and cost. You can filter by boat type on the search page to compare options side by side.

How to Choose the Right Catamaran Size for Your Group

The number of guests determines the minimum size you need. For a group of 6 to 8 people, a 38 to 40 foot catamaran is fine. For 10 to 12 guests, go for 44 feet or larger. The extra length gives you more deck space, a bigger trampoline at the front, and a more comfortable saloon. If you want to eat lunch on board, check that the cockpit table seats everyone. Some catamarans have an outdoor grill or a wet bar, which is useful for longer trips. The skipper will usually stay in the forward cabin or the saloon, so do not count that cabin for guests. Ask the owner about the exact sleeping configuration if you plan an overnight charter.

What to Expect from the Skipper on a Corfu Catamaran Charter

The skipper is a local professional who knows the Corfu coastline well. They will navigate, handle the sails, anchor, and dock. They will also point out landmarks, recommend swimming spots, and suggest tavernas for lunch. Most skippers speak English and Greek. They are not tour guides, but they will share their knowledge if you ask. You can request a specific route or activity, but the skipper has the final say on safety. If you want a more relaxed experience, let the skipper choose the itinerary based on the wind and weather. Some skippers are also qualified to teach basic sailing skills if you ask in advance.

How the Weather Affects Your Catamaran Charter in Corfu

The Ionian Sea is generally calm in summer, but conditions can change. The Maistro wind usually picks up in the afternoon, reaching 10 to 15 knots. That is perfect for sailing, but it can create a short chop in exposed areas. The west coast of Corfu is more exposed to the open sea, so the water can be rougher there. The east coast and the channel to Albania are usually flat. If the forecast shows strong winds above 25 knots, the skipper may cancel or change the itinerary. In July and August, the risk of thunderstorms is low, but isolated storms can occur. Always check the forecast a day before your charter and stay flexible.

Hidden Costs to Budget for on a Corfu Catamaran Charter

Besides fuel, there are a few extra costs you should plan for. Some ports charge a mooring fee if you stop at a town quay or a marina. In Corfu Town, the marina fee for a catamaran is around EUR 20 to EUR 40 per night. If you take a taxi from your hotel to the port, that is another EUR 20 to EUR 40 depending on the distance. Food and drinks you bring on board are your responsibility. If you want a catered lunch, some owners offer a menu with prices starting from EUR 25 per person. A tip for the skipper is customary, usually 10% to 15% of the charter fee. You can give it in cash at the end of the trip. For a full-day charter, budget an extra EUR 200 to EUR 300 for all incidentals.

How to Combine a Catamaran Charter with a Corfu Land Holiday

Many visitors spend a week in Corfu and book a catamaran for one or two days. That works well because you can explore the coast from the water and still have time for beaches, museums, and restaurants on land. You can base yourself in Corfu Town for easy access to the port, or stay in a resort like Gouvia or Dassia, which are close to the marina. If you are staying in the south, consider a charter from Benitses or Petriti to save travel time. A half-day charter is a good introduction if you are unsure about spending a full day on the water. You can also combine a catamaran trip with a visit to the Achilleion Palace or a wine tasting in the countryside.

What to Do If You Have Never Been on a Catamaran Before

If you are a first timer, a catamaran is a good choice because it is stable and easy to move around. You do not need any sailing skills. The skipper will handle everything. You should arrive at the port with a positive attitude and a willingness to follow safety instructions. If you feel seasick, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. Ginger tea or wristbands can also help. Do not wear high heels or shoes with dark soles, as they can mark the deck. Barefoot or with non marking white soles is standard. The skipper will show you how to use the toilet on board, which is called the head. It works differently from a land toilet, so listen to the briefing.

How to Find the Best Deals on Catamaran Charter Corfu

The cheapest rates are in May and September, when demand is lower. You can find half day charters for around EUR 700 in May. Booking midweek, Tuesday to Thursday, is often cheaper than weekends. Last minute deals are rare in August, but you might find a discount if a boat is still available a week before. On the BoatHire24 platform, you can compare prices across multiple owners. Look for listings that include fuel in the price, as that can save you EUR 100 to EUR 200. Some owners offer a discount for repeat customers or for booking two days in a row. Always read the cancellation policy before paying a deposit.

What to Do on a Rainy Day in Corfu Instead of a Catamaran Charter

If the weather turns bad and your charter is cancelled, you still have plenty of options. Visit the Corfu Aquarium in the old town. Explore the Mon Repos estate, where the gardens are free to walk through. Go to the Archaeological Museum to see artefacts from the ancient city of Corfu. Drive to the top of Mount Pantokrator for views over the island, even in cloudy weather. Spend an afternoon in the Liston arcade, drinking coffee and watching people. If the rain is light, you can still walk through the old town streets and visit the churches. The weather in Corfu changes quickly, so do not cancel your whole trip based on a morning shower.

h1: Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day, Rentals for Groups
intro:
You want a private yacht charter Marbella day for your group, and you want it sorted without the fluff. A day on the water with a licensed skipper, cold drinks, and the Costa del Sol sun. BoatHire24 lists boats from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. Motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, RIBs, fishing boats, licence-free day boats, and superyachts. Every charter includes a skipper, so you sit back and enjoy.

Forget the endless scrolling through charter company sites. We’ve done the legwork, pulling together real boats, real prices, and real availability. Whether it’s a birthday, a corporate do, or just because you fancy a day off dry land, you can filter by size, type, and port. Prices start from around EUR 800 for a half-day on a 10-metre motor yacht, and go up to price on request for a 30-metre superyacht. You book directly through the platform, no middleman markup.

This page covers what you get, which ports work best, the boat types that suit groups, pricing guidance, the best months to go, how to book, and who this kind of charter is for. If you’re after a BoatHire24 experience that doesn’t involve a timeshare pitch or hidden fees, read on.
bodyHtml:
Browse the full fleet at BoatHire24.

What a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day Includes

A private yacht charter Marbella day means the whole boat is yours. No strangers, no sharing, just your group and the crew. The standard package includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation, mooring, and safety. Some boats also come with a host or stewardess, especially the larger motor yachts and catamarans. Fuel is usually included for the agreed itinerary, but check the booking details because some operators charge extra for fuel beyond a set number of hours.

Food and drink are not automatically included. Many charters offer a catering upgrade: a tapas platter, a paella lunch, or a BBQ on the aft deck. You can also bring your own food and drink, as long as you don’t expect the crew to cook it. Ice and coolboxes are standard. Snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and inflatable water toys are often available on request, sometimes at an extra cost of around EUR 50-100 per item.

The itinerary is flexible within reason. You tell the skipper where you want to go: Cala del Faro for a swim, the coast off Estepona old town for a view of the castle, or out towards the Strait of Gibraltar to spot dolphins. The skipper knows the local anchorages and weather patterns, so they’ll advise on the best route. If you want to dock for lunch at a chiringuito, that’s doable too, but you pay the mooring fee if there is one.

Every charter includes insurance, life jackets, and a safety briefing. The boats are inspected and licensed, so you’re not taking a gamble. For a search on BoatHire24, you can filter by included amenities like WiFi, sound system, or flybridge.

Which Ports Work Best for a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice. It’s the glitzy marina in Marbella, full of superyachts and flashy motor yachts. Departing from here gives you quick access to the coast west towards Estepona and east to Cabopino. The marina itself is a tourist attraction, with designer shops and restaurants. If you want to impress your group, start from Banús. The downside is that berthing fees are higher, so charter prices from this port tend to be slightly above average.

Marbella Marina, also called Puerto Deportivo, is a more laid-back alternative. It’s in the town centre, close to the old town and the beach. Boats from here are often a bit cheaper than Banús, and you still get the same sea access. It’s a good option if your group is staying in Marbella town and wants to walk to the boat.

Cabopino is a small marina east of Marbella, near the dunes of Artola. It’s quieter and less commercial. The boats here are mostly smaller motor yachts and fishing boats. If you want a low-key day without the glamour, Cabopino works. It’s also closer to the Nerja caves if you fancy a longer trip east.

Estepona marina is west of Marbella, near the old town with its flower-filled streets. The charter options here are a mix of sailing yachts and motor boats. It’s a good starting point for heading towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can see dolphins and, on a clear day, the coast of Africa.

Sotogrande is further west, a luxury residential area with a large marina. It’s less touristy and more exclusive. Boats from here are often larger, and the charter prices reflect that. Benalmádena, east of Marbella, has a marina with a range of boats, from RIBs to catamarans. It’s convenient if you’re staying on the Costa del Sol between Fuengirola and Torremolinos.

Boat Types for a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for groups. They have spacious decks, a saloon with air conditioning, and a bathroom. A 12-metre motor yacht can take up to 12 guests. Prices for a half-day start from around EUR 1,200. Full-day rates are typically EUR 1,800-2,500. You get speed, comfort, and a sun pad at the bow.

Catamarans are the party boats. They have a wide beam, so they’re stable and don’t roll much. The deck space is massive, often with a trampoline at the front. A 13-metre catamaran can hold 12 guests. Half-day prices start from EUR 1,500. Catamarans are great for groups that want to swim, lounge, and eat. They’re slower than motor yachts, but that’s not the point.

Sailing yachts are for the purists. A 14-metre sailing yacht with a skipper can take 8-10 guests. Half-day from EUR 1,000. You get the experience of sailing, the quiet, and the chance to help with the ropes if you want. They’re less about partying and more about cruising. If your group wants to sail under the La Concha mountain view, this is the option.

RIBs and speedboats are for the adrenaline crowd. A 6-metre RIB can take 6-8 guests. Half-day from EUR 500. They’re fast, open, and wet. You’ll get a thrill ride to Cala del Faro or a dolphin-watching trip. Not ideal for lounging, but perfect for a quick blast.

Fishing boats are specialised. A 7-metre fishing boat with a skipper costs from EUR 600 for a half-day. You get rods, bait, and local knowledge. The fishing off Marbella is decent for bream, sea bass, and sometimes tuna. Licence-free day boats are small motorboats you can drive yourself without a licence. They’re limited to 10 metres and 6 guests. Half-day from EUR 300. You don’t get a skipper, so you’re on your own. Good for a couple or a small group who want independence.

Superyachts are the top end. 25 metres and above, with crew, jetskis, and a tender. Price on request. If you have to ask, you can probably afford it. They’re available from Puerto Banús and Sotogrande.

Pricing Guidance for a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Prices vary by boat size, type, season, and port. A half-day is usually 4 hours, a full day is 8 hours. Half-day charters are more common for groups who want a shorter experience. Full-day allows for a longer cruise, lunch at a beach club, and more swimming stops.

For a motor yacht up to 12 metres, half-day from EUR 800, full day from EUR 1,500. For a catamaran up to 14 metres, half-day from EUR 1,200, full day from EUR 2,000. For a sailing yacht up to 14 metres, half-day from EUR 900, full day from EUR 1,600. For a RIB up to 8 metres, half-day from EUR 500, full day from EUR 900. These are starting prices. High season (July, August) adds 20-30%. Easter and September are also busy.

Extras: catering from EUR 30 per person, paddleboard EUR 80, jetski tow EUR 150. Some charters include a photographer or a DJ for an extra fee. You can negotiate directly with the operator through the platform, but the listed price is what you pay plus any extras you add.

Deposits are typically 30-50% at booking, with the balance due on the day. Cancellation policies vary: most allow free cancellation up to 14 days before, then 50% refund up to 7 days. Check the terms on the specific boat listing.

Best Months for a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day

May, June, September, and October are the sweet spots. The weather is warm (22-28 degrees C), the sea is calm, and the crowds are thinner. July and August are hot (30-35 degrees C) and busy, but the water is perfect for swimming. The afternoon Levante wind can pick up in summer, making the sea choppy, but the skipper will adjust the route.

April and November are borderline. You might get a good day, but it’s riskier. Water temperature in April is around 17 degrees C, so swimming is cold. December to March is low season. Some boats still operate, but expect cooler temperatures (15-20 degrees C) and a higher chance of wind. Prices are lower, though, so if you’re flexible, you can get a bargain.

The best time of day for a charter is 10:00 to 18:00. Sunset charters (18:00-21:00) are popular for groups who want a relaxed evening with drinks. The light over the La Concha mountain is spectacular.

How to Book a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day on BoatHire24

Go to the homepage, enter your dates, group size, and port. The search results show you available boats with photos, specs, and prices. You can filter by boat type, length, and amenities. Each listing has a booking calendar and a direct message option to ask the operator questions.

Once you find a boat you like, you book and pay the deposit through the platform. The operator confirms the booking within 24 hours. You get a confirmation email with the meeting point and skipper contact. On the day, you turn up at the marina, meet the crew, and go. No hidden fees, no bait and switch.

If you’re unsure, you can read the boat reviews from previous guests. All reviews are verified. You can also check the BoatHire24 blog for tips on what to bring, how to avoid seasickness, and the best anchorages.

Who a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day Is For

Groups of friends celebrating a birthday, a stag or hen do, or a reunion. Families with kids who want a safe day on the water. Corporate groups for team building or client entertainment. Couples who want a romantic day with a private skipper. Photographers who want access to remote coves and the best light.

It’s not for solo travellers unless you want to book the whole boat yourself, which is expensive. It’s not for budget backpackers, because even the cheapest charter is a few hundred euros. But if you have a group of 6-12 people, the per-person cost is reasonable. For example, a EUR 1,200 half-day on a motor yacht split 8 ways is EUR 150 each. That’s cheaper than a day at a water park and infinitely better.

If you’re visiting Marbella for a week and want a standout day, a private yacht charter is the move. You get the coast, the sea, the sun, and the service. No queues, no crowds, no stress.

Local Highlights You Can See on a Private Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Puerto Banús from the water is a different perspective. The superyachts lined up, the tower blocks behind, and the mountains beyond. Cala del Faro is a small cove east of Marbella, with a lighthouse and clear water. It’s a popular swim stop. The Río Verde is a river mouth near Banús where you sometimes see flamingos.

Estepona old town is visible from the sea, with its white buildings and castle. If you go further west, you reach the Strait of Gibraltar, where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean. Dolphin and whale sightings are common there. On a clear day, you can see the Rif Mountains of Morocco. East of Marbella, the Nerja caves are a landmark you can see from the water, though you need a longer trip to get there.

The La Concha mountain is the backdrop for most of the coast. It’s 1,270 metres high and often has a cloud cap. The view from the sea is iconic. If you’re on a sailing yacht, the silhouette against the sunset is worth the price alone.

title: Catamaran Hire Puerto Banus for Birthday Parties
metaDescription: Book catamaran hire Puerto Banus for birthday parties. Private skipper, open bar, sunset cruises from EUR 1,500. Reserve your celebration on the Costa del Sol.
h1: Catamaran Hire Puerto Banus for Birthday Parties
intro:
If you are planning a birthday party on the Costa del Sol, catamaran hire in Puerto Banus is the most relaxed way to do it. You get a private boat with a licensed skipper, a floating party deck, and views of the Marbella coastline that no restaurant can match. No need to worry about driving, queuing for drinks, or finding a table. You just turn up, celebrate, and let the crew handle the rest.

BoatHire24 lists dozens of catamarans based in Puerto Banus, from 40-foot day cruisers to 70-foot vessels with full bars, sound systems, and sun pads. Every charter includes a skipper, so you can focus on your guests. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day trip, depending on the boat size, season, and extras like catering or a DJ.

This page covers exactly what you get, which boats work best for birthdays, how to book, and the local spots you’ll visit. No fluff, just the details you need to decide.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Birthday Party in Puerto Banus

When you book catamaran hire in Puerto Banus for a birthday, the basics are straightforward. You get the boat for a set time, usually 4 or 8 hours, with a skipper who knows the coast. Most catamarans also include a host or stewardess to serve drinks and food. The boat comes with a sound system, often Bluetooth or AUX, so you can plug in your own playlist. Sun decks, a shaded saloon, and a bathroom are standard on all but the smallest catamarans.

Extras vary by boat and operator. You can add an open bar (beer, wine, soft drinks, sometimes cava) for a flat fee, usually EUR 25-40 per person. Catering ranges from tapas platters to full barbecues, with prices around EUR 30-60 per head. Some boats allow you to bring your own food and drink, but check the terms first. A DJ or live musician can be arranged for an extra EUR 300-800. The skipper will also handle the anchor, docking, and safety briefings, so you don’t have to think about any of that.

Every charter includes basic insurance and life jackets. You do not need a boating license. The skipper holds a valid Spanish professional qualification. If you want to swim, the skipper will find a calm spot, often near the Cabopino dunes or the Cala del Faro.

Puerto Banus: The Best Departure Port for Birthday Cruises

Puerto Banus is the obvious choice for a birthday party on the water. It is the most famous marina on the Costa del Sol, packed with restaurants, bars, and shops. You can start your celebration with a drink on the dock before boarding, or head straight out to sea. The marina has plenty of parking, taxi ranks, and a heliport if you want to arrive in style.

From Puerto Banus, the typical route goes west towards the Strait of Gibraltar or east towards Marbella’s golden beaches. The water is calm in summer, with average sea temperatures of 22-26 degrees C from June to September. You will see the La Concha mountain behind you, and if you head west, the coast of Africa on a clear day. Dolphins are common, especially near the Cabo de la Plata.

The marina itself has a party vibe, but once you are out on the water, it is quieter. You can anchor off the coast of San Pedro Alcántara or near the Rio Verde estuary. The skipper will know the best spots for swimming, photos, and avoiding crowds.

Best Catamarans for Birthday Parties in Puerto Banus

The catamarans available for hire in Puerto Banus range from 40 to 70 feet. For a birthday party, the sweet spot is 50-60 feet. That gives you enough deck space for dancing, seating for 12-20 guests, and a decent sound system. Smaller catamarans (40-45 feet) work for groups of 8-10, but the space is tighter. Larger catamarans (65-70 feet) can host 25-30 people, with separate lounges, a kitchen, and sometimes a jacuzzi.

Popular models include the Lagoon 52, the Bali 4.6, and the Fountaine Pajot Saba 50. These boats have wide beams, stable platforms, and plenty of sunbathing areas. Some are equipped with water toys like paddleboards, snorkel gear, or even a small inflatable slide. If you want a party-focused boat, look for one with a flybridge where the DJ can set up, leaving the main deck for guests.

For a truly memorable birthday, consider a catamaran with a jacuzzi or a grill on the back deck. The combination of hot water, cold drinks, and the Mediterranean sunset is hard to beat. You can see the full list on our catamaran search page.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Birthday Parties

Prices for catamaran hire in Puerto Banus vary by season, boat size, and duration. A half-day charter (4 hours) in the low season (October to May) starts from around EUR 1,500 for a 45-foot catamaran. In high season (June to September), the same boat costs EUR 2,000-2,500. A full day (8 hours) adds roughly 60-80% to the half-day price.

Larger catamarans (60-70 feet) cost EUR 3,000-5,000 for a half-day in peak season. Full-day charters on these boats can reach EUR 7,000-10,000. Open bar and catering are usually extra, as mentioned above. Some operators offer all-inclusive packages for birthday parties, bundling the boat, bar, and food for a per-person price of EUR 150-300.

You should also budget for a tip for the crew, typically 10-15% of the charter fee. If you book through BoatHire24, there are no hidden fees. The price you see includes the boat, skipper, fuel for the standard itinerary, and basic insurance. VAT is usually included, but confirm when you book.

For a precise quote, contact the boat owner directly via our platform. Prices are always negotiable in the low season, and last-minute bookings sometimes get discounts.

Best Time of Year for a Catamaran Birthday Party

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days a year. The best months for a catamaran birthday party are May, June, September, and October. The weather is warm (24-30 degrees C), the sea is calm, and the marinas are less crowded than July and August. July and August are hotter (30-35 degrees C) and busier, but the water is at its warmest (26 degrees C) and the sunset is later, around 9:30 PM.

If you are planning a winter birthday (November to March), you can still charter a catamaran, but the weather is cooler (15-20 degrees C) and the sea can be choppy. The advantage is much lower prices and availability. You will want a boat with a heated saloon or a covered deck. Some operators offer winter charters with hot drinks and blankets, but check the forecast carefully.

For a sunset party, aim for a 5 PM to 9 PM charter in summer. The light over the Mediterranean is spectacular, and you can watch the sky turn orange behind La Concha mountain. In spring and autumn, sunset is earlier, around 7-8 PM.

How to Book a Catamaran for a Birthday Party

Booking through BoatHire24 is simple. Go to our catamaran search page, filter by port (Puerto Banus) and boat type (catamaran). You will see photos, specs, and prices for each boat. Click on a listing to see the full details, including what is included, the maximum guest count, and the cancellation policy.

To confirm a booking, you typically pay a 30-50% deposit via bank transfer or credit card. The balance is due on the day of the charter, usually in cash or by card on board. Some operators offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days or more before the trip. Others have stricter policies, so read the terms carefully.

If you are unsure which boat suits your group, contact the owner directly through the platform. They can advise on the best boat for your guest count, budget, and party style. You can also request extras like a DJ, photographer, or custom decorations. Most operators are flexible and will work with you to create the perfect birthday experience.

For last-minute bookings (within 48 hours), call the owner or send a message via the platform. Availability is limited in summer, so book at least 2-4 weeks ahead for July and August.

Who Is Catamaran Hire for Birthday Parties For

Catamaran hire in Puerto Banus works for most types of birthday celebrations. It is ideal for adults celebrating a milestone birthday, like 30, 40, or 50. The relaxed atmosphere suits groups of friends who want to chat, swim, and drink without the noise of a nightclub. It also works for families with children, as catamarans are stable and have plenty of space. Some boats have cabins where kids can nap or change.

If you are planning a surprise birthday, the crew can help. They can arrange a cake, decorations, or a special announcement. Just let them know in advance. The skipper will also coordinate with you on the timing and route, so the surprise is not ruined by a late arrival or a change of plans.

For corporate birthday parties or team celebrations, catamarans offer a professional yet fun setting. You can combine a short meeting with a party, or just use the boat for networking and socialising. The crew will handle the logistics, so you can focus on your guests.

If you are looking for a more adventurous birthday, consider a catamaran that offers water sports like wakeboarding, tubing, or jet skiing. Some boats tow a small inflatable or have a tender for exploring hidden coves. You can find options on our catamaran search page.

Local Highlights: What You Will See on Your Birthday Cruise

From Puerto Banus, your catamaran will likely head west towards Estepona or east towards Marbella. West of Puerto Banus, you will pass the Cabopino dunes, a protected area with white sand and clear water. Further west is the Cala del Faro, a rocky cove with a lighthouse that offers great photo opportunities. If you go all the way to Estepona, you can see the old town from the water, with its whitewashed houses and flower pots.

East of Puerto Banus, you will cruise past the Marbella marina (Puerto Deportivo), the Golden Mile, and the beaches of Nagüeles and Puente Romano. The La Concha mountain dominates the skyline, and on a clear day you can see the Rif mountains of Morocco. If you head further east towards Benalmádena, you will pass the cliffs of Cabopino and the fishing village of La Carihuela.

Dolphins are common in the Strait of Gibraltar, about 30 nautical miles west of Puerto Banus. Some catamarans offer dolphin-watching trips as part of the itinerary. The best time for dolphin sightings is early morning or late afternoon. The skipper will adjust the route based on the conditions and your preferences.

If you want to swim, the skipper will anchor in a sheltered bay. Popular spots include the Rio Verde estuary, the Cabopino beaches, and the Cala del Moral. The water is clear and warm, with visibility of 10-20 metres in summer.

What to Bring and What to Wear

For a catamaran birthday party, dress for the weather. In summer, bring swimwear, a towel, sunglasses, and a hat. The sun is strong, so use high-SPF sunscreen and reapply every two hours. A light jacket or sweater is useful for the evening, as the sea breeze can be cool after sunset. Wear non-marking shoes, as many boats require you to remove heels or black-soled shoes.

If you are bringing gifts or decorations, check with the owner first. Some boats allow balloons and banners, but others have rules about what you can attach to the boat. Avoid confetti or glitter, as it is hard to clean up and can damage the marine environment. A birthday cake is fine, but the crew will need to store it in the fridge, so let them know in advance.

You can bring your own drinks and food, but some operators charge a corkage fee for alcohol. It is often easier to use the boat’s open bar and catering packages, as they include glassware, ice, and service. If you have dietary restrictions, the crew can usually accommodate them with advance notice.

For photos and videos, bring a waterproof camera or a phone with a waterproof case. The light on the water is excellent, especially during the golden hour before sunset. You will want to capture the views of the coast, the boat, and your guests enjoying themselves.

Safety and Regulations

Catamaran charters in Spain are regulated by the Spanish Merchant Marine. The skipper holds a valid license and the boat is inspected annually. Life jackets are provided for all guests, and the skipper will give a safety briefing before departure. The boat has a VHF radio, flares, and a first aid kit. In case of bad weather, the skipper will decide to cancel or reschedule the trip. You will get a full refund if the charter is cancelled due to unsafe conditions.

Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper will not tolerate excessive drinking that endangers guests or the crew. If someone becomes unruly, the skipper has the authority to end the charter early. Most parties are fine, but it is worth setting expectations with your guests beforehand.

Children are welcome, but they must be supervised at all times. Some catamarans have nets around the deck for safety, but younger children should wear life jackets when near the water. The crew can provide life jackets for kids if you request them in advance.

If you are planning a fireworks display or a drone flight, check with the owner first. Fireworks are generally not allowed on charter boats due to fire risk. Drones are permitted in some areas, but you need a permit from the Spanish aviation authority for commercial use. For personal use, keep the drone within sight and avoid flying over crowds or wildlife.
