title: Speedboat Rental Marbella No Licence Needed – Affordable Fun
metaDescription: Speedboat rental Marbella no licence needed. Drive a RIB or day boat from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina. Book affordable fun with BoatHire24 today.
h1: Speedboat Rental Marbella No Licence Needed, Affordable Fun
intro:
You don't need a boating licence to rent a speedboat in Marbella. That's the short answer. The longer answer is that BoatHire24 lists boats you can drive yourself without any paperwork, provided you're over 18 and sober. Think RIBs with 150 HP outboards, small motorboats for zipping along the coast, and licence-free day boats from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and Cabopino. Prices start from around EUR 250 for a half-day, and every booking includes a quick safety briefing. No test, no exam, no fuss.

You get the keys, a map of no-go zones (nature reserves, swimming areas), and a radio for emergencies. The boat is yours for a few hours. You can anchor off Cala del Faro, cruise past La Concha mountain, or just find a quiet cove near Estepona. It's cheaper than a charter with a skipper, and you set the pace.
bodyHtml:
What Does No Licence Mean Exactly

In Spain, boats under 15 metres and with engines under 40 HP used to require a licence. That changed. Now, for small boats (up to 6 metres, under 15 HP), you can rent without any licence at all. For slightly bigger RIBs and speedboats (up to 8 metres, engines up to 40 HP), you need a quick online test or a one-day course. Most rental companies on BoatHire24 handle this for you. You show up, they run through a 30-minute briefing, and you sign a waiver. You are legally allowed to drive. No prior experience needed.

The boats are designed for ease: tiller steering, simple throttle, and a kill-cord lanyard. You will not be given a 40-knot rocket unless you prove you can handle it. But you will get a fun, fast boat that planes on the water. Maximum speed is usually 25-30 knots, which is plenty for a day out.

Ports Where You Can Pick Up a Licence-Free Speedboat

BoatHire24 works with operators in five ports along the Costa del Sol. For speedboat rental Marbella no licence, the best options are:

  • Puerto Banús, the glamour port. You pick up from the main dock near the yacht club. Easy access to the open sea and the coast towards Estepona.
  • Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), quieter, cheaper parking, and closer to the town centre. Good for a quick blast to Cabopino or Cala del Faro.
  • Cabopino, small marina near Artola dunes. Less crowded, ideal for a relaxed afternoon.
  • Estepona, the old town is a 10-minute walk from the port. You can cruise along the coast to the Gibraltar strait and spot dolphins.
  • Benalmádena, near the marina and the cable car. A bit further from Marbella, but still within easy reach for a day trip.
  • Catamaran Hire Puerto Banus for Birthday Parties

Each port has its own character. If you want the full Marbella experience, start from Puerto Banús. If you prefer a quieter launch, try Cabopino or Estepona.

What Speedboats Are Available Without a Licence

You will find three main types of licence-free boats on BoatHire24:

RIBs (Rigid Inflatable Boats). These are the most common. They're fast, stable, and easy to handle. Typically 4.5 to 6 metres long with a 40 HP outboard. Can carry 4-6 people. Prices from around EUR 250 for 4 hours.

Small motorboats / day boats. Fibreglass hulls, usually under 5 metres. Slower than RIBs (15-20 knots), but more comfortable for lounging. Some have a small sunpad. Good for families with kids. Prices from EUR 200 for half-day.

Licence-free speedboats (up to 8 metres). These require a quick online test or an in-person briefing. They have bigger engines (up to 40 HP) and can reach 30 knots. More fun for adrenaline seekers. Prices from EUR 350 for 4 hours.

Check the listing details on our search page for exact specs and what's included (fuel, insurance, life jackets).

Pricing Guidance for Speedboat Rental Marbella No Licence

Prices vary by boat size, duration, and season. Here is a rough guide:

  • Half-day (4 hours): EUR 200 to EUR 400
  • Full day (8 hours): EUR 350 to EUR 700
  • Fuel: Usually not included. Budget EUR 50-100 for a half-day, depending on how far you go.
  • Insurance: Liability insurance is included. Collision damage waiver (CDW) is optional, around EUR 30-50 extra.
  • Deposit: EUR 300-500, refundable if you return the boat undamaged.

For exact prices, use the BoatHire24 search filters. Prices drop significantly outside July and August. October can be half the summer rate, and the weather is still warm (22-26 degrees C).

Best Time of Year for Speedboat Rental in Marbella

The season runs from April to October. Peak is July and August, when the sea is calm and the air temperature hits 30 degrees C. But you pay a premium. June and September are the sweet spots: warm water, fewer crowds, and lower prices. May and October are still good, but you might get some wind. Winter rentals are possible but rare; the sea can be rough, and many operators close from November to March.

If you want to avoid the crowds, go early morning (10-12) or late afternoon (15-18). The afternoon sea breeze picks up around 14:00, making the water choppier. Morning is glassy flat, especially in the summer.

Where to Go With Your Licence-Free Speedboat

You have the whole Costa del Sol coast to explore within a 20 NM radius. Some highlights:

  • Cala del Faro, a small cove near Marbella with a lighthouse. Good for a swim stop. No beach, but you can anchor and jump off the boat.
  • Estepona Old Town, moor up at the marina and walk into the whitewashed streets for lunch. The port has a fuel dock and a small supermarket.
  • Puerto Banús, cruise past the superyachts and the famous marina. You can't moor there without a reservation, but you can slow-roll through the entrance.
  • Strait of Gibraltar, if you start from Estepona, you can head south towards Gibraltar. You might see dolphins, pilot whales, and even orcas (keep a safe distance).
  • Cabopino Dunes, a nature reserve with a beach. You can anchor off the sand and swim ashore.

Most rental operators give you a map with restricted areas. Respect them. The Guardia Civil do patrol and fine for illegal anchoring in posidonia seagrass meadows.

How to Book a Licence-Free Speedboat on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24, enter Marbella as your destination, and filter by "no licence" in the boat type. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Choose your date and time, pay a deposit (usually 30-50%), and the rest on the day. The operator will confirm by email with a meeting point and a contact number.

On the day, you arrive 15 minutes early. The operator checks your ID (passport or driving licence), runs through the safety briefing, and hands over the boat. You sign a rental agreement. That's it. You are on the water.

For more tips, read our blog posts on boating in Spain without a licence.

Who Is This For

Speedboat rental Marbella no licence is ideal for:

  • Tourists who want a spontaneous day on the water without planning a course.
  • Groups of friends or families (up to 6 people) looking for a fun, self-guided outing.
  • People who already have a driving licence and are comfortable with basic boat handling.
  • Anyone who wants to avoid the cost of a skipper (saving EUR 100-200 per day).

It is not for everyone. If you have never driven any vehicle on water before, consider a half-day charter with a skipper first. The sea can be unpredictable, and you are responsible for the boat. But if you are confident, go for it.

Safety and Legal Requirements

You must be over 18. You must not be under the influence of alcohol or drugs. You must wear the kill-cord at all times. Life jackets are provided and must be worn by children and non-swimmers. The boat must have a VHF radio, flares, and a fire extinguisher. The operator will check all of this before you depart.

If you break down, call the operator or the coastguard (channel 16). Most operators have a support boat that can reach you within 30 minutes. Do not anchor in prohibited areas. Do not exceed the speed limits in the marina (usually 3 knots). Fines can be steep.

Frequently Asked Questions

How to Handle the Boat: A Quick Practical Guide

If you have never driven a speedboat, the controls are simpler than a car. There is a throttle lever (push forward to go, pull back to neutral or reverse). Steering is with a tiller or a small wheel. The kill-cord clips to your life jacket or shorts; if you fall overboard, the engine cuts dead. That is your main safety feature.

To get on the plane (the boat lifts up and skims the water), push the throttle fully forward for a few seconds, then ease back to about two-thirds. You will feel the bow drop and the speed increase. That is the sweet spot. Do not turn sharply at speed; the boat can spin out. Slow down to 5-10 knots before turning. Practice in open water away from other boats for the first ten minutes.

Most rental operators give you a laminated card with local hazards: shallow rocks near Cala del Faro, the sandbar at Cabopino, and the busy shipping lanes off Gibraltar. Keep it on the dashboard. If in doubt, idle and call the operator.

Fuel Costs and How to Avoid Running Out

Fuel is not included in the rental price for most licence-free speedboats. You pay for what you use. A typical RIB with a 40 HP outboard burns about 10-15 litres per hour at cruising speed (20 knots). At EUR 1.60 per litre (current prices on the Costa del Sol), that is EUR 16-24 per hour. For a 4-hour half-day, budget EUR 60-100 for fuel.

The boat comes with a full tank. You return it with the same amount. The operator will point out the nearest fuel dock: Puerto Banús has a fuel station at the entrance, Marbella Marina has one near the slipway, and Estepona has one at the end of the main pier. Do not run the tank dry; the engine can suck debris from the bottom of the tank. Fill up with at least 10 litres left.

If you plan a long trip (say, Marbella to Estepona and back, about 30 NM round trip), you will use roughly 20-30 litres. Ask the operator for a fuel estimate before you leave. They know the local consumption patterns.

What to Wear and Bring for a Day on the Water

You will get wet. Not necessarily soaked, but spray from the bow will hit you at speed. Bring a quick-dry top or a light waterproof jacket. Swim shorts or a bikini under your clothes is smart. Sunblock (SPF 50, water-resistant) is non-negotiable; the reflection off the water doubles UV exposure. A hat with a strap (wind will take a loose one). Polarised sunglasses cut glare and let you see shallow rocks.

Do not bring hard suitcases, glass bottles, or heavy coolers. The boat has limited storage: a small locker under the bow seat or a dry bag. Most operators provide a waterproof bag for phones and wallets. Leave your passport onshore; a photocopy or a photo on your phone is enough for ID checks. Bring cash for the fuel dock (some do not take cards) and for lunch at a beach chiringuito.

If you are prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure. The chop in the afternoon can be uncomfortable for some. Ginger biscuits or a flat Coke help settle the stomach.

How to Avoid Fines and Common Mistakes

The Guardia Civil patrol the coast in rigid inflatables and helicopters. They check for licences, life jackets, and kill-cords. If you are stopped without a kill-cord attached, the fine is EUR 200-300. If you are in a restricted area (nature reserves, swimming zones, or within 200 metres of a beach where flags indicate swimming), the fine can be EUR 500-1,000.

Do not anchor in posidonia seagrass meadows. They are protected by EU law. The seagrass looks like dark patches underwater. Anchor only on sand or bare rock. Most operators give you a map of safe anchoring spots. If you are unsure, drop anchor in 5-8 metres of water where the bottom is light-coloured sand.

Do not drink alcohol while driving. The legal limit is 0.25 mg/l in breath, lower than for cars. A single beer can put you over. The Guardia can breathalyse you on the water. If you fail, you lose the boat and face a fine of up to EUR 1,000. Save the drinks for when you are anchored and swimming.

Best Routes for a Half-Day Licence-Free Trip

If you start from Puerto Banús, head east towards Marbella. The coast is lined with villas and small beaches. In 20 minutes at 20 knots, you reach Playa de la Fontanilla, where you can anchor off the sand for a swim. Continue east to Cabopino (another 15 minutes) and see the Artola dunes from the water. Total distance: about 12 NM round trip. Fuel: 10-15 litres.

From Marbella Marina, go west to Cala del Faro. It is a 10-minute run. The cove is sheltered from the prevailing wind. Anchor in 5 metres and swim to the rocky shore. There is a small lighthouse and a path up to a viewpoint. From there, you can go further west to Puerto Banús (another 10 minutes) and slow-roll past the superyachts. Do not stop in the marina without a reservation; the harbourmaster will ask you to leave.

From Estepona, head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar. In 30 minutes, you reach the waters off Punta de la Doncella, where dolphins are common. Keep a distance of 50 metres. Do not chase them. Continue to the Guadalmina River mouth, a shallow estuary good for a quiet lunch stop. Total distance: about 20 NM round trip. Fuel: 20-25 litres.

What Happens if the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is known for calm seas, but the afternoon Levante wind can pick up suddenly. If the wind exceeds 15 knots (Force 4), the sea becomes choppy, especially west of Marbella. Most operators will cancel or postpone your rental if the forecast is bad. You get a full refund or a reschedule.

If you are already on the water and the wind picks up, head back to port immediately. Do not try to ride it out. The boat can handle waves up to 1 metre, but a 4-metre RIB in 1.5-metre swell is uncomfortable and dangerous. Use the VHF radio on channel 16 to call for help if needed. The operator will give you a contact number for the coastguard.

Check the weather forecast on Windy or AEMET before you go. Look for wind under 10 knots and wave height under 0.5 metres. That is ideal for a licence-free speedboat. If the forecast shows a yellow or orange warning, stay ashore.

How to Save Money on Speedboat Rental Marbella No Licence

Book in advance. Last-minute rentals in July and August cost 20-30% more. Use the BoatHire24 search page to compare prices across operators. Midweek (Monday to Thursday) is cheaper than weekends. Morning slots (09:00-13:00) are often discounted because the sea is calm and demand is lower.

Share the cost with friends. A 4-hour rental for EUR 300 split between 4 people is EUR 75 each. That is cheaper than a jet ski (EUR 100 per hour) and you get a whole boat. Bring your own food and drink; buying lunch at a beach club adds EUR 30-50 per person.

Avoid extras you do not need. Collision damage waiver (CDW) is optional. If you are a careful driver and the sea is calm, you can skip it. The deposit (EUR 300-500) is refundable as long as you do not damage the boat. Check the operator's policy on scratches and minor dings; some are strict, others lenient.

What to Do if You Have Never Been on a Speedboat Before

Start with a short rental: 2 hours, not 4. That is enough to get a feel for the boat, visit one cove, and return. You will not be exhausted or stressed. Choose a calm morning slot. Avoid the first day of your holiday; do a test run on day two or three after you have settled in.

Ask the operator for a thorough briefing. Make them show you how to start the engine, use the throttle, and steer. Practice in the marina at idle speed before opening the throttle. If you feel uncomfortable after 15 minutes, you can return to the dock and the operator will help. Most are used to nervous beginners and will not judge.

Consider a guided tour. Some operators offer a "self-drive with a lead boat" option: you follow a guide in another speedboat for the first hour. That costs an extra EUR 50-80 but gives you confidence. You can then go solo for the rest of the rental.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Licence-Free Speedboat

BoatHire24 aggregates operators that are licensed, insured, and vetted. You are not renting from a random private owner. Each listing includes the boat's specs, the operator's contact details, and the exact meeting point. You book online with a deposit, and the balance is paid on the day. No hidden fees.

The search filters let you narrow down by "no licence", boat type, capacity, and price. You can see availability in real time. The operators speak English and Spanish. If you have questions, use the live chat on the BoatHire24 website. The team is based in Marbella and knows the local conditions.

For more detailed advice on boating in Spain without a licence, read our blog posts. They cover the legal changes, port guides, and seasonal tips. You will find everything you need to plan a hassle-free day on the water.

title: Private Boat Charter Marbella for Fishing – Expert Skippers
metaDescription: Book a private boat charter Marbella fishing with a licensed skipper. Expert crew, top gear, and prime spots from Puerto Banús. Check availability now.
h1: Private Boat Charter Marbella for Fishing, Expert Skippers
intro:
You want to fish the Mediterranean, but you don't own a boat, you don't know the best spots, and you definitely don't want to spend your holiday wrestling with a hire-car sat-nav to find a public pier. A private boat charter in Marbella for fishing solves all that. You get a fully equipped boat, a licensed skipper who knows exactly where the dentex and amberjack are hiding, and you leave from a marina that's probably a ten-minute taxi from your hotel. No paperwork, no stress, just you, a rod, and a cold beer while someone else handles the anchor.

This page is the straight-talking guide to booking a fishing charter through BoatHire24. We cover what you get, which ports work best, what you'll catch, and how to avoid the tourist-trap boats that charge you extra for bait. If you want to skip the fluff and go straight to available boats, hit the search page.
bodyHtml:
What a Private Boat Charter Marbella for Fishing Actually Includes

First, the skipper. Every boat on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed professional. That means you don't need a Spanish boating licence, you don't need to worry about navigation rules, and you won't be the one untangling a snagged line at 30 knots. The skipper handles the boat, the safety briefings, and the local fishing knowledge. They know the reefs, the drop-offs, and the times of day when the fish feed. You just cast, reel, and drink your Estrella.

Second, the gear. Most fishing charters supply rods, reels, and terminal tackle. But you need to check the listing details because some budget boats charge extra for lures or bait. Look for listings that say "all tackle included" or "bait provided." If you are after specific species like bluefin tuna or swordfish, you might need heavy-duty gear that not every boat carries. Ask the owner before you book.

Third, the duration. Half-day charters (4-5 hours) are the most common, and they work fine for inshore fishing around Marbella. Full-day trips (8-10 hours) let you run further out to the deeper grounds where the bigger fish live. Some operators also offer sunset fishing trips, which are more about the atmosphere than the catch, but you can still hook a decent sea bass as the sun drops behind La Concha.

Fourth, the extras. Some charters include drinks, snacks, and even a freshly grilled catch for lunch. Others are strictly boat and skipper. Read the fine print. And always confirm the maximum number of anglers. A 30-foot motor yacht might legally carry 10 people, but you don't want 10 rods tangling on a small deck.

Which Departure Ports Work Best for Marbella Fishing Charters

Marbella's coastline runs from Cabopino in the east to the outskirts of Estepona in the west. Each port has different access to fishing grounds. Here is the breakdown.

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice. It is the most famous marina on the Costa del Sol, packed with superyachts and flashy restaurants. The fishing grounds directly offshore are good for dentex, sea bream, and mackerel. You can also run south-west towards the Strait of Gibraltar in about 40 minutes. That is where the dolphin pods hang out and the tuna migrate. Charters leaving from Banús tend to be pricier, but you get convenience and a skipper who speaks English.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a quieter alternative, right next to the old town. It is less glitzy but the fishing is just as good. You save a bit on the charter fee because the berthing costs are lower. The marina is a five-minute walk from the Paseo Marítimo, so you can grab breakfast before you sail.

Cabopino is a small, sandy-bottomed harbour east of Marbella. It is popular with locals and a good launch point for the reefs around Cala del Faro. The fish here are less pressured than the Banús grounds, so you might have better luck. Cabopino is also close to the Dunas de Artola nature reserve, which keeps the water clean.

Estepona and Sotogrande are further west. Estepona's old town is charming, and the fishing off its coast is productive for bottom species. Sotogrande is more exclusive, with a long channel that leads straight to the Mediterranean. If you are staying near the Sotogrande polo fields, this is your port. Benalmádena is a bit of a drive from Marbella (about 45 minutes), but it offers some of the best offshore wreck fishing on the coast. The deep-water wrecks near the port hold big conger eels and groupers.

What Fish You Can Expect to Catch on a Marbella Fishing Charter

The Mediterranean is not the tuna-rich Pacific, but the Costa del Sol has a decent variety. Inshore you will find sea bream, sea bass, mackerel, and dentex. These are the reliable catches for half-day trips. Move out to depths of 50-100 metres and you can hook amberjack, greater forkbeard, and the occasional grouper. If you go deeper, around 200 metres, you might find redfish and John Dory.

Seasonal species matter. Bluefin tuna run through the Strait of Gibraltar from June to October. You need a serious boat and a skipper who knows the migration patterns. Swordfish are around from May to September, usually caught on overnight trips using drift lines. Winter is slower, but you can still catch hake and whiting. The best all-round season for fishing in Marbella is April to October, when the water temperature sits between 18 and 25 degrees C.

Pricing for a Private Fishing Charter in Marbella

Prices vary wildly depending on boat size, duration, and included extras. A half-day private charter for a group of 4-6 people on a well-equipped motor yacht starts from around EUR 600. Full-day trips run from EUR 1,200. If you want a luxury superyacht with a dedicated fishing crew, the price goes up to EUR 3,000 or more. Some operators charge extra for fuel, so always ask if the price includes fuel or if it is a fuel surcharge on the day. BoatHire24 listings usually show the total price, but double-check the terms.

You can also find licence-free day boats for smaller groups. These are rigid inflatables or small motorboats that do not require a licence to rent. They come with a skipper who doubles as a fishing guide. Prices for these start around EUR 350 for a half-day. They are not as comfortable as a 40-foot yacht, but they get you to the fish without breaking the bank.

Best Seasons for Fishing Charters in Marbella

Spring (March to May) is good for sea bream and mackerel. The water is warming up, and the fish start feeding more actively. Summer (June to September) is peak season for tuna and swordfish, but also the busiest time on the water. You need to book at least two weeks in advance for a private charter. Autumn (October to November) is the sweet spot: the summer crowds are gone, the water is still warm, and the dentex are fat before winter. Winter (December to February) is quiet. You can still catch fish, but the sea can be rough. Some charter boats do not operate in December and January. Check availability on the search page to see which boats are running.

What to Bring on Your Fishing Charter

Sun cream, sunglasses, and a hat. The Mediterranean sun is brutal even in spring. A windbreaker or light jacket, because the sea breeze can be cold at speed. Your own food and drink if the charter does not supply it. A camera for the dolphin sightings. And cash for the skipper's tip. 10-15% of the charter fee is standard if you had a good day. Do not bring your own fishing rod unless you have a specific preference. The boat's gear is usually better suited to the local conditions.

Who Is a Private Fishing Charter in Marbella For

It is for anyone who wants to fish without the hassle of owning a boat. Families with kids who want a safe, guided day on the water. Groups of friends who want to combine fishing with a booze cruise. Serious anglers who want to target specific species with an expert skipper. And tourists who just want to see the coast from a different angle and maybe catch dinner. It is not for people who get seasick easily. If you are prone to motion sickness, take a tablet an hour before you sail and stick to half-day trips in the morning when the sea is calmest.

How to Book a Private Boat Charter for Fishing in Marbella

Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters. Select your port, date, and group size. Look for the "fishing" tag or read the description to confirm the boat is set up for angling. Contact the owner through the platform to ask about gear and bait. Book online to secure your slot. Most operators require a deposit, with the balance paid on the day. Cancel at least 48 hours in advance for a full refund. If you are unsure which boat is right for you, read the blog for detailed guides on each charter type.

Why Use BoatHire24 for Your Marbella Fishing Charter

Because we list only boats with licensed skippers. Because we show real availability and real prices. Because we are based in Marbella and know the local operators. And because we do not charge you extra. The price you see is the price the owner sets. No hidden booking fees. If you want to fish the Costa del Sol without the nonsense, start your search on BoatHire24.

How the Skipper’s Local Knowledge Transforms Your Catch Rate

An expert skipper isn’t just there to drive the boat. On a private boat charter Marbella fishing trip, they’ve spent years mapping the seabed. They know the exact coordinates of a wreck off Cabopino that holds dentex. They know that in July, the mackerel school at 25 metres depth off the Río Verde estuary. They can read the seabird activity and tell you when to drop the line. Without that knowledge, you’re essentially guessing. A good skipper will also adjust the drift speed and bait presentation based on the current. Ask your skipper about their favourite spots before you leave the marina. You’ll get a better trip than if you just let them take you to the same generic grounds every tourist uses.

What Boat Size and Type Works Best for Fishing

Not every boat on BoatHire24 is set up for serious fishing. A 40-foot motor yacht with a flybridge gives you space, shade, and a stable platform for trolling. It can handle the 25 NM run to the deeper tuna grounds without bouncing you off the gunwales. A 7-metre RIB is faster and cheaper, but it’s a wet ride in a chop and you’ve got limited deck space for rods. For bottom fishing inshore, a 30-foot sailing yacht works fine if the skipper knows how to rig it. But if you’re targeting bluefin, you want a purpose-built fishing boat with outriggers, a fighting chair, and a live bait well. Check the boat’s length and engine power in the listing. A 200 HP outboard can get you to the grounds quickly. A 50 HP inboard will take longer but use less fuel.

Specific Fishing Grounds You Can Hit from Each Port

From Puerto Banús, the most common run is south-west towards the Punta de Calaburras lighthouse. The rocky bottom there holds sea bream and amberjack. If you go further, about 12 NM south, you hit the Banco de la Manga, a shallow plateau where tuna feed in summer. From Marbella Marina, the grounds off the Cabopino pines are productive for bottom species. From Estepona, the area around the Punta de la Doncella has good structure for dentex. From Sotogrande, you can run straight south to the Strait of Gibraltar in 30 minutes. That’s where the current pushes baitfish, and the dolphins and tuna follow. From Benalmádena, the wreck of the SS Politician (yes, the same one from the film) sits at 35 metres and holds conger eels. Each port gives you a different set of options. Choose based on where you’re staying and what you want to catch.

Cost Breakdown: What You Actually Pay for a Fishing Charter

Let’s be realistic about the numbers. A half-day private boat charter Marbella fishing trip on a 30-foot motor yacht with a skipper and basic tackle costs around EUR 600-800. That covers the boat, the skipper’s fee, and fuel for a 4-5 hour trip. If you want a full day with a larger boat (35-40 feet) and premium gear, expect EUR 1,200-1,800. For a superyacht with a dedicated fishing crew and gourmet lunch, you’re looking at EUR 3,000-5,000. Fuel surcharges are common in summer when prices spike. Some operators add a 10% fuel supplement if the price of diesel goes above a certain threshold. Ask about this before you book. Also, some charters charge extra for filleting and packing your catch. That’s usually EUR 20-40. It’s worth it if you want to take the fish home.

How to Avoid the Worst Fishing Charter Mistakes

First, don’t book a boat that’s too big for your group. A 50-foot yacht for two people is a waste of money. You’ll pay for fuel and space you don’t need. Second, don’t assume all skippers speak fluent English. Most do in Puerto Banús, but in Cabopino or Estepona you might get a skipper with basic English. Confirm on the platform. Third, don’t turn up late. The skipper has a schedule and the best fishing windows are early morning and late afternoon. If you’re 30 minutes late, you lose prime time. Fourth, don’t drink too much. One beer is fine. Six beers and you’ll be leaning over the rail instead of reeling in a fish. The skipper will not be impressed. Fifth, don’t forget to check the weather forecast. A force 4 wind from the east makes the sea lumpy and the fish stop biting. Reschedule if the forecast is bad.

What to Do with Your Catch After the Charter

If you catch fish, you have options. Some charters include a grill on board and the skipper will cook your catch for lunch. That’s the best option. If not, you can take the fish to a local restaurant in Marbella or Puerto Banús. Many places will cook your catch for a fee, usually EUR 10-15 per person. Ask before you walk in. Or you can take it back to your holiday rental and cook it yourself. Sea bream and sea bass are excellent grilled with olive oil and lemon. Mackerel is good smoked or pickled. Tuna is best eaten as sashimi or seared. If you don’t want the fish, release it. Catch and release is common on the Costa del Sol, especially for smaller fish. Just handle them with wet hands to avoid damaging the slime coat.

How to Combine Fishing with Other Activities on the Same Day

A private boat charter Marbella fishing trip doesn’t have to be all rods and reels. Many boats let you split the day. Start with two hours of fishing off the coast, then anchor near Cala del Faro for a swim and snorkel. The water there is clear and the rocky shoreline has plenty of marine life. Or fish in the morning, then cruise along the coast to Puerto Banús for lunch at a beach club. Some skippers will even take you to see the dolphin pods in the Strait of Gibraltar if you’re not having luck with the fish. Just tell the skipper your preferences when you book. They’ll plan the route accordingly. It’s your charter. You’re paying for the boat and the skipper’s time. Use it how you want.

Why Booking Through BoatHire24 Gives You More Options

We aggregate boats from multiple operators across the entire Costa del Sol. That means you can compare a 28-foot fishing boat from Cabopino with a 45-foot motor yacht from Puerto Banús in one search. You can filter by price, boat type, and included gear. You can message the owner directly to ask about bait and target species. And you book through a platform that’s based in Marbella, not a call centre in another country. If there’s a problem, we can sort it locally. Start your search for a private boat charter Marbella fishing trip on BoatHire24. We’ll get you on the water with a skipper who knows where the fish are hiding.

h1: Luxury Motor Yacht Hire Marbella for a Day, Premium Experience
keyword: luxury motor yacht hire Marbella day
intro:
If you want to spend a day on the Costa del Sol in style, luxury motor yacht hire Marbella for a day is the only way to do it. You get a private vessel, a professional skipper, and the freedom to explore the coast at your own pace. No queues, no crowded beaches, no mediocre lunch spots. Just you, your group, and the Mediterranean.

BoatHire24 connects you with the best motor yachts available for day hire from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and other ports along the coast. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you can relax and enjoy the experience. Whether you want to anchor at Cala del Faro, spot dolphins near Gibraltar, or simply cruise past La Concha mountain, we have the boat for you.

Below, you will find everything you need to know about booking a luxury motor yacht for a day in Marbella. What is included, which ports to depart from, how much it costs, and how to make the most of your time on the water.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Luxury Motor Yacht Day Hire

When you book a luxury motor yacht hire Marbella for a day through BoatHire24, the standard package includes a professional skipper who knows the local waters inside out. You do not need a licence. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety. Fuel is usually included in the price, but check with the specific yacht listing. Most charters also include a welcome pack with soft drinks, water, and ice. Some premium yachts offer a choice of gourmet catering, ranging from a Mediterranean platter to a full barbecue on board. Snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and inflatable water toys are often available at no extra cost. Towels and sun cream are not always provided, so bring your own.

Every yacht is fully insured and undergoes regular maintenance. The crew will brief you on safety procedures before departure. You can bring your own food and drink, but many charters have a corkage fee for alcohol you bring on board. Ask the boat owner or our team for details.

Which Ports Can You Depart From

Luxury motor yacht hire Marbella for a day typically departs from one of five ports. Puerto Banús is the most famous, with its superyacht marina and designer boutiques. You can step straight from the dock onto your yacht. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a short walk from the old town and offers a more relaxed vibe. Cabopino is a smaller marina near the Artola sand dunes, ideal if you want to avoid the crowds. Estepona port is further west, close to the charming old town with its flower-filled streets. Sotogrande is the most exclusive option, with a private estate and a quieter atmosphere. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near the marina with its lively bars and restaurants.

Each port gives you access to different stretches of the coast. From Puerto Banús, you can head east to Marbella or west to the Strait of Gibraltar. From Estepona, you are closer to Gibraltar and the dolphin-watching spots. Choose the port that suits your itinerary and travel plans.

What Size of Motor Yacht Can You Hire for a Day

Luxury motor yachts for day hire in Marbella range from around 10 metres to 30 metres or more. A 10-12 metre yacht is perfect for a couple or a small group of up to 6 people. It has a sun deck, a small cabin, and a basic galley. For a group of 8-12, look at yachts in the 14-18 metre range. These have a larger saloon, a proper kitchen, and often a flybridge with a second helm station. The top-end yachts, 20 metres and above, offer multiple cabins, a spacious sundeck, a jacuzzi, and a crew of two or three. These are the yachts you see in Puerto Banús.

Examples include the Sunseeker Predator models, Princess V-series, and Azimut Flybridge yachts. Each has its own character. A Sunseeker is sporty and fast. An Azimut is more about comfort and cruising. You can filter by size, capacity, and price on our search page.

How Much Does a Luxury Motor Yacht Day Hire Cost

Prices for luxury motor yacht hire Marbella for a day start from around EUR 1,500 for a 10-metre yacht in low season. A mid-range 15-metre yacht costs from EUR 3,000 to EUR 5,000 per day. A 20-metre-plus superyacht can cost EUR 8,000 to EUR 15,000 or more, depending on the age, amenities, and crew. High season (July and August) pushes prices up by 20-30 percent. Fuel is usually included, but for longer trips or high-speed cruising, there may be a surcharge.

Additional costs include catering (EUR 30-80 per person), drinks, and optional extras like a waterskiing session or a photographer. Tipping the crew is customary, usually 10-15 percent of the charter fee. You can get a precise quote by entering your dates and group size on our booking platform. We do not invent exact prices because they vary by yacht and availability.

What Is the Best Season for a Day Charter

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 days of sunshine a year. The best time for luxury motor yacht hire Marbella for a day is from May to October. In May and June, the sea temperature is around 18-20 degrees C, and the air temperature is 25-28 degrees C. July and August are the hottest months, with air temperatures reaching 35 degrees C and sea temperatures hitting 24-26 degrees C. September and October are still warm, with fewer crowds and lower prices.

Winter charters are possible but less popular. The sea can be choppy, and the air temperature drops to 15-18 degrees C. You will still get sunny days, but the experience is better suited to a hot drink and a blanket than swimming. We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance during peak season, as the best yachts get snapped up quickly.

What You Can Do on a Day Charter

A typical day charter lasts 8 hours, usually from 10:00 to 18:00 or 11:00 to 19:00. You can customise the itinerary with your skipper. The most popular route is a cruise east from Puerto Banús past Marbella to Cabopino, with a stop at Cala del Faro for swimming and lunch. The water is clear, and the cliffs provide shelter from the wind. Another option is to head west towards Estepona and Gibraltar. The Strait of Gibraltar is a prime spot for dolphin and whale watching. You might see common dolphins, striped dolphins, or even pilot whales.

If you want a longer trip, some yachts can take you as far as Nerja, but that is a 2-hour cruise each way. You can also anchor near the Río Verde estuary for a quiet swim. On board, you can sunbathe on the deck, use the sound system, or relax in the saloon with air conditioning. Many yachts have a barbecue grill on the aft deck.

Who Is Luxury Motor Yacht Hire For

This type of charter suits a wide range of groups. Couples celebrating an anniversary or a honeymoon appreciate the privacy and romance. Families with older children enjoy the space and the water toys. Corporate groups use day charters for team-building or client entertainment. Bachelor and bachelorette parties are common, but the skipper will enforce a reasonable noise limit and safety rules. If you want a party boat, there are specific yachts that allow DJ equipment and larger groups.

We do not recommend luxury motor yacht hire for very young children or people with mobility issues, as the steps and deck hatches can be hazardous. Check with the specific yacht before booking.

How to Book a Luxury Motor Yacht for a Day in Marbella

Booking is straightforward. Go to our BoatHire24 homepage and use the search bar to enter your preferred date, group size, and port. You can filter by boat type and price range. Each listing shows photos, specifications, and the exact inclusions. Once you find a yacht you like, you can send an inquiry or book directly through our secure payment system. We require a 50 percent deposit to confirm the booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure.

Our team is available by phone and email to answer any questions. We can also arrange catering, transfers, and additional services. Cancellation policies vary by yacht, but most offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days or more in advance. For last-minute bookings, contact us directly, and we will check availability.

For more tips on planning your day, read our blog on the best anchorages and restaurants along the coast.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Day Charter

We have been operating in Marbella since 2015 and have built relationships with the best yacht owners and skippers. Every yacht on our platform is vetted for safety, cleanliness, and reliability. We offer transparent pricing with no hidden fees. You can compare multiple yachts side by side and read verified reviews from previous guests. Our customer support team is based in Marbella and speaks English, Spanish, and German.

We also offer a price-match guarantee. If you find the same yacht on another site for less, we will match the price and give you a 5 percent discount. This applies to direct competitors only.

Start your search on our search page to see all available luxury motor yachts for day hire in Marbella.

What Are the Best Luxury Motor Yacht Models Available in Marbella

Marbella’s charter fleet includes several standout motor yacht models that define the luxury day-hire experience. The Sunseeker Manhattan 52, a 16-metre flybridge yacht, offers a spacious saloon, a large sun deck, and a top speed of around 30 knots. It is a popular choice for groups of 8 to 10 who want both style and performance. The Princess V58, at 18 metres, has a more enclosed flybridge and a generous aft deck for dining. Its deep-V hull handles the chop near Cabopino well. For something faster, the Azimut 68S is a 21-metre sport yacht with a top speed of 35 knots and a striking exterior. It can accommodate up to 12 guests and has a jacuzzi on the foredeck. The Pershing 70, another high-performance option, is 22 metres long and can reach 40 knots. It is ideal if you want to cover more distance in a day, say from Puerto Banús to Estepona and back. Each model has its own feel, so browse the listings to see which layout suits your group.

How to Choose Between a Flybridge and a Sport Motor Yacht

The choice between a flybridge and a sport motor yacht depends on how you plan to spend the day. A flybridge yacht, like the Princess V-class or Azimut Flybridge, has an upper deck with a second helm station, seating, and often a sun pad. This gives you panoramic views and a shaded area under the hardtop. It is better for cruising and socialising in a group. A sport yacht, like the Sunseeker Predator or Pershing, has a lower profile and a more streamlined design. The main deck is open at the back, with a sun lounge area that converts into a seating area. Sport yachts are faster and more agile, making them fun for a shorter, more adrenaline-fuelled trip. They also have less interior space, so if you want to escape the sun in an air-conditioned saloon, a flybridge is the better bet. For a day charter in Marbella, where the sun is strong from June to September, a flybridge with a bimini top or hardtop provides welcome shade.

What Are the Best Anchorages for a Day Charter from Puerto Banús

Leaving from Puerto Banús, you have several excellent anchorages within a 30-minute cruise. Cala del Faro, just east of the port, is a small cove with a rocky shoreline and clear turquoise water. It is sheltered from the westerly winds and has a depth of around 5 metres, perfect for anchoring and swimming. The backdrop of La Concha mountain adds to the setting. A little further east, the coast near the Río Verde estuary offers a sandy bottom and calm water, though it can get busy in August. Heading west, you reach the area off the Marbella Club Hotel, where the water is deeper and the views of the Sierra Blanca mountains are striking. For a longer trip, the waters off Estepona, near the marina, have a sandy seabed and good visibility. Your skipper will know which spots are calm on the day, as the wind direction changes the conditions. Always ask for a recommendation when you board.

Can You Combine a Day Charter with a Visit to Estepona Old Town

Yes, you can combine a luxury motor yacht hire Marbella day with a stop in Estepona old town, but it requires a longer cruise. From Puerto Banús, it is about 12 nautical miles west, taking roughly 45 minutes at cruising speed. You can anchor in the bay off Estepona marina and take the tender to the shore. The old town is a 10-minute walk from the marina. Its narrow streets are lined with flower pots, whitewashed buildings, and small tapas bars. You can spend an hour or two exploring before returning to the yacht for lunch. This works best if you start early, around 09:00, and extend the charter to 10 hours. Some yachts offer a full-day itinerary that includes a morning cruise, a lunch stop at Estepona, and an afternoon swim at Cala del Faro. The skipper will adjust the plan based on the weather and your preferences. It is a good option if you want to see more of the coast than just the Marbella strip.

What Are the Additional Costs You Should Budget For

Beyond the base charter fee, you should budget for several extras. Catering is the most common add-on. A basic Mediterranean platter with cold meats, cheeses, olives, and bread costs around EUR 30 per person. A full barbecue with grilled fish, meat, and salads is EUR 50-80 per person. Drinks packages, including beer, wine, and soft drinks, add EUR 15-25 per person. If you want a premium bar with champagne and spirits, expect EUR 40-60 per person. Some yachts charge a corkage fee of EUR 10-20 per bottle if you bring your own alcohol. Water toys like a jet ski or a towable banana boat cost extra, usually EUR 100-200 per hour. A photographer to capture the day is around EUR 300-500 for the charter. Tipping the crew is customary at 10-15 percent of the total fee. If you book a yacht with a crew of two, a tip of EUR 200-300 is standard for a good day. Always confirm what is included in the quoted price before booking to avoid surprises.

How to Prepare for a Day on a Luxury Motor Yacht

Preparation makes the day more comfortable. Bring a swimsuit, a towel, and a change of clothes. Sun cream with SPF 50 is essential, as the reflection off the water intensifies the rays. A hat and sunglasses with a strap help prevent them blowing away. A light jacket or a windbreaker is useful even in summer, as the wind on the water can feel cool at 25 knots. Seasickness is rare on a motor yacht in calm conditions, but if you are prone to it, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. Wear non-marking shoes on board; many yachts ask you to remove shoes or wear deck shoes. Pack a waterproof bag for your phone and camera. If you plan to swim, bring a snorkel mask if you have one, though most yachts provide basic gear. Let the skipper know if anyone in your group has a medical condition or dietary restriction. The crew can adjust the lunch menu or the itinerary accordingly.

What Is the Cancellation Policy for a Day Charter

Cancellation policies vary by yacht owner, but there are common patterns. Most charters offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days or more before the departure date. Between 7 and 14 days, you usually get a 50 percent refund. Less than 7 days, the deposit is non-refundable unless the charter is rescheduled. In case of bad weather, the skipper has the final say. If the sea state is unsafe, the charter can be postponed or cancelled with a full refund. This is rare in summer, but possible in winter. We recommend taking out travel insurance that covers charter cancellations. For bookings made within 7 days of departure, we require full payment upfront, and the cancellation policy is stricter. Always read the terms on the yacht listing before paying. Our team can explain the specific policy for your chosen yacht if you have questions.

bodyHtml:
What a Catamaran Charter in Estepona for Groups Includes

When you book a catamaran charter in Estepona for groups through BoatHire24, you get a few things standard. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you don’t need a boat licence or any experience. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety. You also get fuel, insurance, and basic safety equipment. Most catamarans come with a sound system, a fridge, a cooler, and a grill or BBQ. Some have a water slide, a trampoline net at the front, and a flybridge for sunbathing. You can bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package. The typical group size is 10 to 30 people, depending on the boat. A 15-metre catamaran usually takes around 12 to 15 guests comfortably. A 20-metre one can handle 25 to 30.

Why Estepona for a Group Party at Sea

Estepona is a bit of a hidden gem on the Costa del Sol. It has a proper fishing port turned modern marina, the Puerto Deportivo, with bars and restaurants right on the water. The old town is full of whitewashed houses and flower pots. But the real draw for a group is the coastline. You have the Sierra Bermeja mountains behind you, the Strait of Gibraltar to the west, and the African coast visible on clear days. The water is calmer than in the open sea, so even people prone to seasickness are fine. You can anchor near the Playa del Cristo, a sheltered beach with a chiringuito, or go further east to the dunes of Artola in Cabopino. The sunset from a catamaran off Estepona is genuinely good. And because Estepona is less flashy than Marbella, the prices are a bit more reasonable.

Boat Options for Your Group Charter

We have a range of catamarans suitable for groups. The most popular size is 14 to 18 metres, with a beam of 7 to 9 metres, giving you a lot of deck space. These boats have a main deck with a saloon and a kitchen, plus a flybridge with seating and a sun pad. Some examples include the Lagoon 450 or the Bali 4.6, both around EUR 2,800 to EUR 4,500 for a full-day charter (8 hours). For larger groups, up to 30 people, a 20-metre catamaran like the Sunreef 60 costs from around EUR 5,500 to EUR 8,000 per day. Half-day charters (4 hours) are available from around EUR 1,800. You can also book a sunset cruise for 2 to 3 hours, starting from EUR 1,200 for a group of 12. All prices include skipper and fuel. Check our search page for current availability and exact prices.

Pricing Guidance for a Catamaran Charter Estepona Group

Pricing depends on the boat size, season, and duration. High season (June to September) is the most expensive. A full-day charter for 12 to 15 people in July costs between EUR 3,000 and EUR 4,500. In May or October, the same boat is around EUR 2,500 to EUR 3,500. Half-day charters in high season start at EUR 2,000 for a 14-metre catamaran. Low season (November to March) drops to EUR 1,500 for half a day. You can also add extras: a catering menu with paella, tapas, and drinks costs about EUR 50 to EUR 80 per person. A DJ or live musician adds EUR 300 to EUR 600. Water toys like a jet ski or a paddleboard are extra, around EUR 150 to EUR 250 each. The cheapest option for a group of 10 is a half-day in low season on a 12-metre catamaran, from around EUR 1,200. For a premium experience with a 20-metre boat and full catering, budget EUR 6,000 to EUR 8,000.

Best Seasons for a Group Party at Sea

The best time for a catamaran charter in Estepona for groups is May to October. June, July, and August are hot, with temperatures hitting 30 to 35 degrees C. The water is warm, 22 to 26 degrees C, so swimming is great. The sea is usually calm, though the afternoon Levante wind can pick up. September and October are slightly cooler but still pleasant, with fewer crowds. April and November are marginal: you might get a good day, but the water is cooler and the wind more unpredictable. December to March is low season, and many boats are in maintenance. If you want a guaranteed sunny party, book between mid-May and mid-September. The sunset in July is around 9:30 PM, giving you a long evening for a dinner cruise. In October, sunset is around 7:30 PM, so a sunset charter needs an earlier start.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter in Estepona for Groups

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You select your date, group size, and preferred boat. You can filter by catamaran, capacity, and price. Once you pick a boat, you request a booking. We confirm availability with the owner and send you a quote. You pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) to secure the date. The balance is due 2 to 4 weeks before the charter, or on the day for last-minute bookings. You get a confirmation with the skipper’s contact details and the departure time. The departure port is the Puerto Deportivo de Estepona, which is easy to reach by car or taxi from Marbella (30 minutes) or Malaga airport (1 hour). Parking is available at the marina for around EUR 15 per day. You need to arrive 15 minutes before departure. The skipper will give a safety briefing and then you’re off. You can also book a private transfer if you’re a large group staying in a hotel.

Who Is This Charter For

This is for groups of friends, families, or colleagues who want a private party on the water. It works for birthdays, bachelor or bachelorette parties, anniversaries, corporate events, or just a big day out. The catamaran is stable enough for all ages, from kids to grandparents. The skipper keeps things safe, so you can drink and dance without worry. It is not a rowdy club boat, you bring the vibe. Some groups hire a DJ, others just use a Bluetooth speaker. The boat has a toilet and a small cabin for changing. If you want a more exclusive experience, you can book a catamaran with a jacuzzi or a flybridge lounge. For a quieter group, a sailing catamaran with less motor noise is an option. For a full-on party, a motor catamaran with a powerful sound system is better. We can advise on the best fit. Check our blog for tips on planning a group charter.

What to Bring on a Catamaran Charter for Groups

Bring swimwear, sunscreen, a towel, and a light jacket for the evening. Sunglasses and a hat are essential. If you’re prone to sunburn, bring factor 50. The sun reflects off the water, so you burn faster. You can bring your own food and drinks, but glass bottles are usually not allowed because they break. Use plastic cups and cans. Some boats have a cooler with ice, but bring extra ice packs. If you order catering, you don’t need to bring anything except your appetite. Music: bring a playlist on your phone, but check if the boat has Bluetooth or an aux cable. Most catamarans have a standard audio system. For a party, bring a portable speaker as backup. You can also bring snorkelling gear, a GoPro, or a drone (check with the skipper first). The boat has a first aid kit, but bring any personal medication. And bring cash for tips or for buying drinks from the skipper’s bar if available.

Local Attractions Near Estepona for Your Group

Estepona itself is worth a visit before or after the charter. The old town has narrow streets with flower pots, a nice square, and plenty of tapas bars. The Paseo Marítimo is a long promenade along the beach. The marina has restaurants serving fresh fish and paella. If you want to extend the trip, you can combine the catamaran charter with a visit to Gibraltar, 30 minutes by car, where you can see the monkeys and the rock. Or go to the Sierra Bermeja for hiking. For a longer day, you can sail towards Marbella and see the Puerto Banús skyline from the water. The skipper can anchor near the Cala del Faro, a small cove with clear water, or near the Playa del Saladillo. If you book a full-day charter, you can stop for lunch at a beach club like the Guadalmina or the Cabopino. The skipper will recommend the best spots based on the weather and your preferences.

Safety and Regulations for Group Charters

All catamarans on BoatHire24 are licensed and insured. The skipper has the required qualifications and local knowledge. The boat has life jackets for all passengers, a fire extinguisher, flares, and a VHF radio. The skipper will give a safety briefing at the start. You must follow the skipper’s instructions, especially when anchoring or mooring. The maximum number of passengers is set by the boat’s licence and is not negotiable. If you have more people than the limit, the charter may be cancelled. Children count as passengers. The boat has a toilet and a small cabin. If anyone feels seasick, the skipper can head to calmer waters. The boat is not allowed to operate in bad weather, so if the forecast is rough, we can reschedule or refund. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper has the right to refuse service if someone is dangerously drunk. You are responsible for your own behaviour. Damage to the boat caused by guests will be charged.

Frequently Asked Questions

Comparing Estepona with Other Departure Ports for Group Charters

Estepona sits at the western edge of the Costa del Sol, which gives it a few advantages over Puerto Banús or Marbella for a group charter. The marina is quieter and less crowded, so boarding is faster and you don’t fight for parking. The sea here is generally calmer because you’re closer to the Strait of Gibraltar and protected by the coast. From Estepona, you can sail east to the Cabopino dunes or west towards Gibraltar in about 45 minutes. If you depart from Puerto Banús, you’re in the busiest port on the coast and pay more for parking and marina fees. Marbella’s Puerto Deportivo is a middle ground, but the water can be choppier near the Cabo de Calaburras. Benalmádena is further east and adds 20 minutes of transit time to reach open water. For a group that wants a relaxed start and easy access to calm anchorages, Estepona is the best choice. You can check our search page to compare boats available from each port.

Realistic Itinerary for a Full-Day Group Charter from Estepona

A typical full-day catamaran charter from Estepona for groups runs from 10:00 to 18:00 or 11:00 to 19:00. You meet at the Puerto Deportivo, load your gear, and get the safety briefing. The skipper motors out of the harbour, which takes about 10 minutes. First stop is usually Playa del Cristo, a sheltered bay with a beach bar, 15 minutes from the marina. You anchor for swimming and snorkelling for an hour. Then you head east along the coast towards the Cala del Faro, a small cove with clear water and fewer boats. You anchor again for lunch around 13:00. The skipper can grill on the BBQ or you serve the catering. After lunch, you motor further east to the area near the Río Verde or even as far as Cabopino if the sea is calm. You stop for a third swim and some music. Around 16:00, you start heading back. The return journey takes 30 to 45 minutes, depending on wind. You dock at 18:00. For a sunset charter, you depart at 16:00, anchor near the coast, watch the sun go down around 20:30 in summer, and return by 21:30.

What a 15-Metre Catamaran Looks Like for Your Group

A 15-metre catamaran is the sweet spot for a group of 12 to 15 people. You get two hulls connected by a wide deck. The front has a trampoline net where people sit or lie down. The main deck has an indoor saloon with a table and seating, plus an outdoor cockpit with another table and benches. The flybridge on top has a helm station, a sun pad, and extra seating. The kitchen is small but functional with a fridge, a sink, and a two-burner stove. The toilet is in one of the hulls, usually a single cabin with a marine head. There is a small cabin for changing or storing bags. The sound system is Bluetooth or aux, with speakers on the main deck and sometimes on the flybridge. The boat has a bimini top for shade. The beam is around 7.5 metres, which makes it stable even with 15 people moving around. You can walk around without bumping into each other. The top speed is around 8 to 10 knots, so it’s a relaxed cruise, not a speedboat ride. For a group that wants space without paying for a 20-metre boat, this is the standard option.

Adding Water Toys and Activities to Your Charter

Most catamarans in Estepona can be equipped with extra water toys for an additional cost. A stand-up paddleboard costs around EUR 50 to EUR 100 for the day. A kayak for two is similar. A towable inflatable sofa or a banana boat costs EUR 150 to EUR 250, but you need a RIB or a speedboat to tow it, which is not always available on a catamaran. A jet ski can be delivered to the boat at anchor for about EUR 200 to EUR 300 per hour. Snorkelling gear is sometimes included, but bring your own mask for a better fit. A floating mat or a water trampoline is popular for groups and costs EUR 100 to EUR 150. If you want to fish, the skipper can take you to a spot near the coast, but you need a fishing licence, which costs around EUR 10 per person for a day. You can also book a photographer or a videographer to capture the day, from EUR 200 to EUR 500. For a party, a smoke machine or bubble machine is possible, but check with the owner first. The skipper will help you arrange any extras before the charter.

Weather and Wind Patterns for Estepona Group Charters

The weather in Estepona is Mediterranean, with over 300 sunny days a year. The main wind is the Levante, which blows from the east and can pick up in the afternoon, especially from June to August. The Levante creates choppy seas near the coast, but Estepona is somewhat sheltered by the Sierra Bermeja. The Poniente wind from the west is lighter and brings calmer seas. In the morning, the sea is usually flat, with the wind building around 14:00. For a group charter, the best strategy is to anchor in a sheltered bay like Playa del Cristo or the Cala del Faro before the wind picks up. The water temperature in July and August is 24 to 26 degrees C. In May and October, it’s 18 to 22 degrees C, still swimmable for most people. The air temperature in high season is 30 to 35 degrees C, so bring plenty of water and sunscreen. Rain is rare from May to September. If a storm is forecast, the charter can be rescheduled or cancelled with a full refund. The skipper monitors the weather and will adjust the route if needed.

Food and Drink Options for a Group Catamaran Charter

You have three options for food and drink on a catamaran charter in Estepona for groups. First, you bring your own. Most boats allow this, but no glass bottles, so transfer drinks into plastic containers. You can bring a cooler bag with ice, but the boat’s fridge is small, so plan accordingly. Second, you order a catering package from the boat owner or a local company. Typical menus include a Spanish spread with jamón, cheese, olives, and bread, plus paella or grilled meat and fish. Drinks can be beer, wine, soft drinks, and water. Catering costs EUR 50 to EUR 80 per person, including disposable plates and cups. Third, you stop at a beach club for lunch. The chiringuito at Playa del Cristo serves grilled fish and salads, and you can moor the catamaran nearby. The skipper can also arrange a BBQ on board, with the boat owner providing the meat and charcoal. For a party, you can order a cocktail package with premixed drinks and a bartender for an extra EUR 200 to EUR 400. Whatever you choose, let the owner know at least 48 hours in advance.
