h1: Catamaran Rental Benalmadena: Book Your Cat
intro:
If you want to spend a day on the water around Benalmadena without the heeling and the winch-grinding, a catamaran is the obvious choice. These wide, stable boats give you a platform for swimming, sunbathing and eating tapas while the coast slides by. At BoatHire24 we list catamarans based in Benalmadena Marina (Puerto Deportivo) and the neighbouring port of Puerto Banús, all with a licensed skipper included. You turn up, they sail, you enjoy.

Benalmadena sits between Torremolinos and Fuengirola, with the Sierra de Mijas mountains behind it and the Mediterranean in front. The marina has direct access to open water, so you are not wasting time motoring through narrow channels. Most catamaran charters here are half-day or full-day trips, with prices starting from around EUR 800 for a half-day on a 40-foot cat. For a full-day on a larger 50-footer expect EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500, fuel and skipper included.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Catamaran Rental in Benalmadena

A catamaran charter from Benalmadena includes the boat, the skipper and the fuel for the day. The boat is yours for the agreed hours, usually 4 hours for a half-day or 8 hours for a full day. The skipper handles the navigation, the anchoring and the safety briefings. You do not need a boating licence. You do not need to know how to dock. You just need to decide where you want to go and how many beers to bring.

Most catamarans in our fleet have a flybridge with a bimini top, a forward sunbathing area with cushions, a rear platform for swimming and a saloon with a fridge and a basic galley. Some have a grill or a barbecue on the back. Some have a water slide or a paddleboard. The skipper will usually anchor in a calm bay for a swim stop, typically at Cala del Faro or off the coast of Cabopino. You can also request a route past the marina of Puerto Banús to see the superyachts.

Benalmadena Marina and Departure Points

Benalmadena Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Benalmadena) is the main departure point for catamaran rentals in this area. It is a large marina with around 900 berths, a few restaurants and a small beach at the entrance. Parking is available but can be tight in summer. The marina is about 15 minutes from Malaga Airport and 10 minutes from the A-7 motorway.

If you are staying in Torremolinos or Fuengirola, Benalmadena is the closest departure port. If you are in Marbella or Puerto Banús, you might prefer to depart from there instead. We also list catamarans departing from Cabopino, Estepona and Sotogrande, so you can choose the port that suits your accommodation.

Catamaran Sizes and Capacities

Catamarans for charter in Benalmadena range from 38 feet to 55 feet. A 38-foot cat typically sleeps 4 to 6 people overnight and can take up to 12 passengers for a day charter. A 50-foot cat can take up to 20 passengers, with more deck space and a larger saloon. The legal limit for passenger capacity is set by the boat's licence and the skipper's endorsement, so we list the maximum number of guests for each boat.

For a group of 6 to 8 people, a 40-foot catamaran is comfortable. For a group of 10 to 12, go for a 45-footer or bigger. If you want to party, you want a cat with a large flybridge and a good sound system. If you want to relax, a quieter boat with more shade might be better. Check the photos and the amenities list on each listing.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Rental Benalmadena

Prices for catamaran rental in Benalmadena vary by boat size, season and duration. Half-day charters (4 hours) start from around EUR 800 for a 38-foot cat in the low season. Full-day charters (8 hours) start from around EUR 1,200 for the same boat. In July and August, prices increase by 20 to 30 percent. A 50-foot cat in high season can cost EUR 2,500 to EUR 3,500 for a full day.

Fuel is included in the price, but you should check if the marina fees or the cleaning fee are extra. Most listings include everything except food and drinks. You can bring your own catering or order a catering package from the skipper. Some boats have a fridge and a freezer, so you can bring your own supplies.

For a precise price, use the search on BoatHire24 and filter by Benalmadena, date and number of guests. You will see live availability and instant booking options.

Best Time of Year for a Catamaran Charter

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and hot summers. The best months for a catamaran rental in Benalmadena are May through October. In May and June the water temperature is around 18 to 21 degrees C, the air temperature is 25 to 30 degrees C, and the sea is calm. July and August are the busiest and hottest, with air temperatures above 30 degrees C and water at 24 degrees C. September and October are still warm, with fewer crowds and lower prices.

Winter charters are possible from November to April, but the sea can be rougher and the weather less predictable. Some boats are laid up for maintenance during the winter. If you want to go in the off-season, contact us and we will check availability.

Typical Itineraries from Benalmadena

A common half-day itinerary from Benalmadena heads west towards Cabopino and Cala del Faro. You motor out of the marina, turn left along the coast, and anchor in the sandy bay of Cala del Faro for a swim. The skipper will serve drinks and snacks while you float. Then you cruise back past the marina and into the port. Total distance is about 6 to 8 nautical miles.

A full-day itinerary can go further west to Puerto Banús or east to Nerja. If you go east, you can see the cliffs of the Costa del Sol and the mountains behind. The skipper will choose a calm anchorage for lunch and swimming. Some trips include a stop at a beach club or a restaurant on the water. You can also request a dolphin-watching route towards the Strait of Gibraltar, but that is a longer trip and requires a full day.

What to Bring and What to Expect

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a towel and a swimsuit. The sun on the water is stronger than on land. Bring a light jacket or a windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. Bring food and drinks unless you have ordered a catering package. Most catamarans have a fridge and a cooler, so you can keep things cold.

The skipper will give a safety briefing before departure. Life jackets are on board for all passengers. The boat has a VHF radio, a first aid kit and a fire extinguisher. If you have any medical conditions or mobility issues, tell the skipper when you book.

Children are welcome on most catamarans. Some boats have a minimum age of 2 or 3 years. Check the listing details or ask the skipper. Dogs are allowed on some boats, but not all. Again, check before you book.

How to Book a Catamaran Rental in Benalmadena

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage, select Benalmadena as the port, choose your date and the number of guests, and browse the available catamarans. Each listing shows the boat details, the price, the availability calendar and the cancellation policy. You can book online with a deposit and pay the balance on the day.

If you have questions about a specific boat or want to customise your itinerary, use the contact form on the listing. The skipper will get back to you within a few hours. We recommend booking at least a week in advance in high season, especially for weekends and holidays.

For more tips on choosing the right boat, read our blog posts on catamaran charters in Spain.

Who Is a Catamaran Rental in Benalmadena For?

A catamaran rental is for anyone who wants a stable, spacious boat with plenty of deck space. It is good for families with children, because the boat does not heel like a monohull. It is good for groups of friends who want to party, because you can dance on the flybridge without falling over. It is good for corporate events and team-building, because you can fit 12 to 20 people on one boat.

It is also good for people who get seasick. The catamaran's twin hulls make it much more stable than a monohull sailing yacht or a motorboat. If you have had trouble with motion sickness on boats before, a catamaran is a safe bet.

If you want a more active sailing experience, you might prefer a sailing yacht where you can help with the sails. If you want speed, a RIB or a speedboat might be better. But for a relaxing day on the water with maximum comfort, a catamaran is the best option.

Catamaran vs Other Boat Types in Benalmadena

Catamarans are not the only option in Benalmadena. You can also rent motor yachts, sailing yachts, RIBs and fishing boats. Motor yachts are faster and more luxurious, but they use more fuel and have less deck space. Sailing yachts are more traditional and cheaper, but they heel and are less stable. RIBs are fast and fun for a short trip, but they are not comfortable for a full day. Fishing boats are purpose-built for angling, with rod holders and a fish finder.

Catamarans sit in the middle: they are stable, spacious and comfortable, but they are slower than motor yachts and more expensive than sailing yachts. If you want to cover a lot of distance in a day, a motor yacht is better. If you want to anchor and swim for hours, a catamaran is better.

Why Benalmadena Works Better for a Catamaran Than Marbella or Puerto Banus

Benalmadena Marina is less flashy than Puerto Banus, which means lower berthing fees and slightly cheaper charter prices. The marina is also closer to Malaga Airport, saving you 20 minutes of driving compared to Puerto Banus. The coastline east of Benalmadena is less developed than the Marbella strip, with more open water and fewer superyacht traffic jams. You get a more relaxed vibe and a quicker exit from the harbour. The downside is that the beach clubs are less glamorous. If you want to be seen, go to Puerto Banus. If you want to actually enjoy the boat, start from Benalmadena.

Fuel Consumption and Range on a Benalmadena Catamaran

A 40-foot catamaran with twin 30hp diesel engines burns roughly 15 to 20 litres per hour at cruising speed (8 to 10 knots). For a 4-hour trip covering 20 to 25 nautical miles, you are looking at 60 to 80 litres of fuel. Since fuel is included in the charter price, you do not need to worry about the cost, but it helps to understand the range. From Benalmadena, you can comfortably reach Fuengirola (5 NM west), Torremolinos (3 NM east) or Cala del Faro (8 NM west) on a half-day. A full-day trip can extend to Marbella (15 NM west) or Nerja (25 NM east). The skipper will plan the route to keep a safety margin of at least 20 percent fuel reserve.

What Happens If the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is known for calm seas, but the Poniente wind can pick up in the afternoon, especially from June to August. If the wind exceeds 20 knots or the waves go above 1.5 metres, the skipper may cancel or modify the itinerary. You do not lose your money. Most charters have a weather clause that allows a free reschedule or a full refund if the skipper deems it unsafe. The decision is the skipper's, not yours. If you are prone to seasickness even on a catamaran, book a morning departure when the sea is usually flatter. The afternoon breeze can create a short chop that makes some people queasy, even on a stable cat.

Private Chef and Catering Options for Your Catamaran Trip

Most catamaran rentals in Benalmadena allow you to bring your own food and drinks. If you want something more organised, several skippers offer catering packages. A basic option is a cold buffet with sandwiches, salads and fruit, costing around EUR 20 to EUR 30 per person. A premium option includes a barbecue on the rear platform with grilled meat or fish, plus drinks, for around EUR 50 to EUR 70 per person. Some boats have a built-in barbecue, but the skipper will usually bring a portable grill if not. You can also order a paella cooked on board, which is popular with Spanish groups. Alcoholic drinks are allowed, but the skipper will cut you off if you get too drunk for safety reasons. Bring your own speaker if the boat's sound system is weak.

How to Choose the Right Catamaran for Your Group Size

For a group of 4 to 6 people, a 38 to 40-foot catamaran is fine. You get a forward sunbathing area, a small saloon and a rear platform. For 8 to 10 people, go for 44 to 48 feet. The extra deck space means you are not tripping over each other. For 12 to 20 people, you need 50 feet or more. At that size, the boat has a proper flybridge with seating for everyone, a large saloon with air conditioning and a bigger galley. The skipper will also have an assistant or a hostess on board for larger groups. Check the maximum capacity on each listing carefully. If you book a boat for 12 passengers and 13 show up, the skipper will refuse to leave the dock. No exceptions.

What to Do If You Want to Stay Overnight on the Catamaran

Some catamarans in Benalmadena are available for overnight charters. You can anchor in a quiet bay or moor at the marina for the night. Overnight charters usually start from around EUR 1,500 for a 40-foot cat in low season, including dinner and breakfast if you arrange it with the skipper. The boat has cabins with beds, a bathroom with a shower and a small kitchen. You sleep on the boat, wake up, swim and then cruise back in the afternoon. This is a good option for a birthday or an anniversary. Book well in advance because the number of overnight-capable catamarans is limited. The skipper will stay on board overnight in a separate cabin or on the deck, so you have privacy.

How to Get to Benalmadena Marina Without a Car

Benalmadena Marina is accessible by train and bus. The C1 Cercanias train from Malaga Centro-Alameda station stops at Benalmadena-Arroyo de la Miel station, which is a 15-minute walk or a 5-euro taxi ride to the marina. The bus line M-110 from Malaga bus station stops right at the marina entrance. From Malaga Airport, take the C1 train to Benalmadena-Arroyo de la Miel and then a taxi. If you are staying in Torremolinos, it is a 10-minute taxi ride costing around EUR 15. If you are in Fuengirola, it is 15 minutes by train or taxi. The marina has a taxi rank at the main entrance. Parking at the marina costs around EUR 15 to EUR 20 per day in summer, so a taxi might be cheaper if you are a group of 4 or more.

What to Do in Benalmadena Before or After Your Catamaran Trip

If you arrive early, walk along the marina promenade and look at the boats. There is a small aquarium called Sea Life Benalmadena at the marina entrance, which is good for kids. The cable car to the top of Mount Calamorro runs from the marina and takes about 15 minutes. At the top you get a view of the entire coast from Gibraltar to Nerja. The bird of prey show at the summit is worth watching. For lunch, the marina has several seafood restaurants, but they are tourist-priced. Walk 10 minutes into the town of Arroyo de la Miel for cheaper tapas. The Selwo Marina dolphinarium is a 5-minute drive from the marina if you want to see dolphins before you see them in the wild on your catamaran trip.

h1: Boat Rental Marbella Port Group: Best Deals for Your Crew
intro:
If you are looking for a boat rental Marbella port group option, you have come to the right place. The idea is simple: you get a group together, we find you a boat with a licensed skipper, and you spend the day cruising the Costa del Sol. No licence needed, no hidden stress, just sun, sea, and a bit of sangria. The best part? You can split the cost between everyone, making it far cheaper than you might think.

Marbella port, specifically Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), is a prime departure point. It is central, easy to reach from the town centre, and surrounded by bars and restaurants for a pre-sail coffee or post-sail beer. From here, you can head east towards the Cabopino sand dunes or west towards Puerto Banús and the fancy yachts. A typical group charter includes a skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. You just bring your group, your music, and your appetite for a good time.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Group Boat Rental in Marbella Port

When you book a boat rental Marbella port group charter, the basics are usually the same. The boat comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters. They handle all the navigation, docking, and safety stuff. You get the boat for a set number of hours, typically 4, 6, or 8 hours for a day charter. Fuel is included in the price, which is a relief because it can add up. Some charters also include a welcome drink, ice, and basic snorkelling gear. You can often bring your own food and drink, or order a catering package for an extra fee. The skipper will help you plan a route, whether you want to head to a quiet cove for swimming or cruise past the Puerto Banús marina to see the superyachts.

Why Choose Marbella Port as Your Departure Point

Marbella port, officially called Puerto Deportivo de Marbella, is a solid choice for a group trip. It is right in the heart of Marbella, so you can walk from the old town or the beachfront. The port has ample parking nearby, though it can get busy in summer. From here, you have quick access to the best spots on the coast. Head east to Cabopino, a nature reserve with dunes and a nudist beach if that is your thing. Or go west to the famous Puerto Banús, where you can gawk at the superyachts and maybe spot a celebrity. The skipper will know the best anchorages, like Cala del Faro near Estepona or the calm waters off the Río Verde. The water is warm from June to October, around 22-26 degrees C, so you can swim comfortably.

Types of Boats for a Group Charter in Marbella

You have several options the boat itself. The most popular for groups is a motor yacht, typically 40 to 60 feet long, with a flybridge, a saloon, and a cabin or two. These can take up to 12 passengers and offer a good balance of space and speed. Catamarans are also a favourite, especially if your group is prone to seasickness. They are more stable, have a large deck area, and are great for lounging. Sailing yachts are available if you want a more traditional experience, but they are slower and require more coordination. For a smaller group of 6 to 8, a RIB or speedboat can be fun for a fast trip to a beach club or a quick dolphin-watching run towards the Strait of Gibraltar. Fishing boats are also an option if your group wants to try catching some local species like sea bass or bream. Prices vary by boat type and size, but expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day on a decent motor yacht for up to 10 people, or from EUR 800 for a smaller RIB.

Pricing Guidance for Group Boat Rentals in Marbella Port

Pricing for a boat rental Marbella port group charter depends on the boat, the duration, and the season. In low season (April, May, October), you can find deals from around EUR 900 for a 4-hour trip on a 40-foot motor yacht for up to 10 people. In high season (June to September), prices go up, often starting at EUR 1,500 for the same boat. Catamarans tend to be more expensive, from EUR 1,800 for a half-day. Larger yachts for 12 people can go from EUR 2,500. Superyachts are price on request, but expect to pay several thousand euros per day. The key is to book early for summer, as availability drops. You can also save by booking a morning slot (9 AM to 1 PM) instead of the more popular afternoon slot (2 PM to 6 PM). Always check what is included: some operators charge extra for food, drinks, or fuel if it is not explicitly stated. For a full breakdown, see our search page for live prices and availability.

Best Seasons for a Group Boat Trip from Marbella Port

The best time for a group boat trip is from late May to early October. The weather is warm, the sea is calm, and the sun is reliable. July and August are peak season, with temperatures hitting 30-35 degrees C. The water is at its warmest, around 26 degrees C, making swimming a pleasure. The downside is that the coast gets crowded, and anchorages can fill up by midday. September is a sweet spot: still warm, fewer crowds, and the sea is often flat calm. April and October can be hit or miss. You might get a perfect 25-degree day, or you might get a cloudy one with a breeze. If you are flexible, you can find great last-minute deals in these months. Winter charters are rare but possible for hardy groups, though the water is cold (around 15 degrees C) and the days are short.

How to Book a Group Boat Rental in Marbella Port

Booking a boat rental Marbella port group charter is straightforward on BoatHire24. You start by entering your group size, desired date, and preferred port (Marbella Marina). The system shows you available boats with prices and photos. You can filter by boat type, capacity, and duration. Once you pick a boat, you make a secure online payment to confirm the booking. The company sends you a confirmation with the skipper's contact details and meeting point instructions. You show up at the port at the agreed time, meet the skipper, and off you go. Cancellation policies vary, but most operators offer a full refund if you cancel at least 7 days in advance. For last-minute bookings, call us directly and we can often find something within 24 hours. We recommend booking at least two weeks ahead in summer, but for smaller groups, you can sometimes find availability a few days before.

Who Is a Group Boat Rental in Marbella Port For

A group boat rental in Marbella port is ideal for stag and hen parties, family reunions, corporate outings, and friend groups. It works well for birthdays, anniversaries, or just a day out to escape the hotel pool. The skipper handles the boat, so you can focus on having fun. For stag and hen groups, expect to bring your own speaker and a cooler of drinks. Just be respectful to the skipper and the boat, as damage deposits can be hefty. Families with kids will appreciate the calm waters and the chance to swim in a safe cove. Corporate groups often use these charters for team-building or client entertainment; you can even arrange a catered lunch on board. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter, but that is a different product. For groups of 6 to 12, a private charter offers the best value and flexibility.

Local Highlights You Can Visit from Marbella Port

Once you leave Marbella port, you have a few classic destinations. Heading west, you can cruise past Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina with its designer shops and mega-yachts. The skipper can slow down so you can take photos. Further west is Estepona, where you can anchor near the old town and walk up to the colourful flower streets. The Cala del Faro is a quiet cove with a lighthouse, perfect for a swim stop. Heading east, you have Cabopino, a natural dune system with a beach bar called Chiringuito Cabopino that does good grilled fish. If you have a full day, you can go further east to the Nerja caves, though that is a 2-hour sail each way. For dolphin watching, the Strait of Gibraltar is about an hour south by speedboat, where you can see common dolphins and sometimes pilot whales. The skipper will tailor the route to your group's preferences, within the time limit.

What to Bring on Your Group Boat Trip

Packing for a group boat trip is easy. Bring sunscreen (factor 50, you will burn), a hat, and sunglasses. A towel and a change of clothes are useful if you plan to swim. You can bring your own food and drink, but check with the operator first. Most allow it, but some have restrictions on glass bottles or red wine (it stains). A cooler with ice is usually provided. Bring a Bluetooth speaker for music, but keep it at a reasonable volume so you do not annoy other boats. Seasickness tablets are a good idea if anyone in the group is prone to it; you can buy them at any pharmacy in Marbella. A waterproof phone case is handy for photos. And bring cash for tips for the skipper, though it is not mandatory. The skipper will appreciate a 10-15% tip if they do a good job.

Safety and Rules for Group Boat Charters

Safety is taken seriously on all group charters. The skipper is licensed and trained in first aid. Life jackets are available for all passengers, though you are not required to wear them unless the skipper says so. The boat has a VHF radio and GPS. You are not allowed to operate the boat yourself unless you have a valid licence, which is why every charter includes a skipper. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper will not let anyone who is dangerously drunk swim or operate any equipment. The boat has a maximum capacity, usually 12 passengers for most motor yachts and catamarans. This is a legal limit, so do not try to sneak extra people on board. If you have a larger group, you may need to charter two boats or look for a superyacht that can take more. For more tips, check our blog on group charter etiquette.

Comparing Marbella Port with Other Departure Points

Marbella port is not the only option for a group boat rental. Puerto Banús is more glamorous and has more superyachts, but it is also more expensive and can be harder to park. Cabopino is quieter and closer to the dunes, but has fewer boat options. Estepona port is smaller and more relaxed, good if you want to avoid the crowds. Sotogrande is further west, near the golf resorts, and Benalmádena is east, closer to Málaga airport. For most groups staying in Marbella, Marbella port is the most convenient. It offers a good range of boats, easy access, and reasonable prices. You can also combine a charter with a walk into Marbella old town afterwards, which is a nice touch. If you are unsure which port suits your group, contact us and we can advise based on your itinerary.

Final Thoughts on Group Boat Rentals in Marbella Port

A boat rental Marbella port group charter is one of the best ways to spend a day on the Costa del Sol. It is social, affordable when split, and gives you a unique perspective of the coastline. You do not need any boating experience, just a willingness to relax and enjoy. The skipper takes care of everything, so you can focus on swimming, eating, and laughing with your friends. Whether you are celebrating something special or just want a break from the beach, it is a solid choice. Book early for the best deals, especially in summer. And if you have any questions, the team at BoatHire24 is here to help you find the perfect boat.

h1: Private Yacht Charter Marbella Hen Party
keyword: private yacht charter marbella hen party
intro:
You want a hen party that doesn’t involve sticky carpets, overpriced shots, and a hangover you vaguely remember. A private yacht charter in Marbella for a hen party is the answer. You get the sun, the sea, and a floating venue that moves from beach club to beach club. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so no one has to steer while wearing heels. Departures from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. You decide the route, the playlist, and the prosecco intake.

This page is for you if you’re organising a hen do and want something that actually impresses the bride. We’ll cover what’s included, which ports work best, boat options, pricing, seasons, and how to book without the stress. No fluff, just the details you need to get a deposit down and start planning the Instagram grid.
bodyHtml:
What’s Included in a Private Yacht Charter for a Hen Party

A private yacht charter for a hen party in Marbella isn’t just a boat ride. You get the whole vessel to yourselves, a professional skipper who knows the coast, and the freedom to set your own schedule. Most charters include fuel, insurance, and basic amenities like a sound system, fridge, and sun pads. Some boats come with a crew member who can serve drinks or help with food setup. You bring your own catering or order from a local supplier, the skipper can recommend one. No hidden fees for cleaning or docking at beach clubs, but always check the terms because some operators charge extra for overnight stays or specific routes.

The skipper handles navigation, anchoring, and safety. They’ll also point out dolphin spots near the Strait of Gibraltar or the best coves for a swim stop. You don’t need a boating licence, and you don’t have to worry about parking. For a hen party, the key inclusions are: private use of the boat, a skipper, fuel, and basic amenities. Extras like water toys (SUP boards, snorkel gear), a DJ, or a photographer can be added for an additional fee. Ask the charter company directly when you enquire.

Best Departure Ports for a Hen Party Yacht Charter

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice for a hen party. It’s flashy, full of superyachts, and close to the famous beach clubs like Ocean Club and Pangea. You can step off the boat and straight into a VIP table. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a bit more laid back but still central, with easy access to the old town for dinner after the charter. Cabopino is quieter, with a sandy beach and a couple of chiringuitos, good if you want a more relaxed vibe. Estepona offers a charming old town and a marina that’s less crowded, while Sotogrande is upscale and quieter, better for a sophisticated group. Benalmádena is lively and slightly cheaper, with a big marina and plenty of bars nearby.

For a hen party, Puerto Banús is the most popular because the whole area is geared towards celebration. You can dock at a beach club for lunch, then cruise along the coast to see the mansions of the rich and famous. If you want a more private experience, consider departing from Cabopino or Estepona, you’ll have more space and fewer crowds. The choice of port also affects the route: from Puerto Banús, you can head east to Cala del Faro or west to the Strait of Gibraltar. From Estepona, you’re closer to the dolphin sightings. Discuss your preferences with the charter company when you book.

Boat Options for a Hen Party: Which Type Suits Your Group

Motor yachts are the default for hen parties. They’re sleek, fast, and have plenty of deck space for lounging and dancing. A 40-50 foot motor yacht typically fits 10-12 guests comfortably, with a flybridge for sunbathing and a saloon for escaping the heat. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day charter. Catamarans are better if your group is larger (12-20 guests) or if you want more stability, they don’t roll as much, which helps if someone’s had one too many rosés. They also have a wider beam, meaning more deck space and a trampoline net at the front for lounging.

Sailing yachts are an option if the bride is into the whole nautical aesthetic, but they’re slower and have less deck space. RIBs and speedboats are for smaller groups (6-8 people) who want a thrill ride and don’t mind getting wet, not ideal for a full hen party unless it’s a pre-club warm-up. Licence-free day boats are available for groups who want to drive themselves, but for a hen party, a skipper is recommended so you can all relax. Superyachts are available for groups of 20+ with a budget of EUR 5,000 or more. They come with a full crew, including a chef, and offer the ultimate luxury experience. For most hen parties, a motor yacht or catamaran is the sweet spot.

Pricing Guidance for a Hen Party Yacht Charter in Marbella

Prices vary by boat size, duration, and season. A half-day charter (4 hours) on a 40-foot motor yacht starts from around EUR 1,500 in the low season (May, June, September). Full-day charters (8 hours) range from EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,000 for the same boat. Catamarans are slightly more expensive due to their size and stability: expect from EUR 2,000 for a half day. Superyachts are price on request, but you’re looking at EUR 5,000 to EUR 15,000 per day depending on the vessel and crew.

High season (July, August) sees prices increase by 20-30%. If you’re flexible with dates, aim for a weekday charter in June or September, you’ll get better availability and lower rates. Some operators offer discounts for full-day bookings or for groups that book multiple boats. Always ask about deposit structure and cancellation policies. Most require a 30-50% deposit to secure the date, with the balance due a week before the charter. For a hen party, it’s common to split the cost among the group, so calculate per person: for 12 guests on a EUR 2,000 half-day charter, that’s about EUR 167 each. Not bad for a private yacht in Marbella.

Best Seasons for a Hen Party Yacht Charter

The Costa del Sol has a long season. April to October is the sweet spot, with May, June, and September offering the best balance of good weather and reasonable prices. July and August are peak season: temperatures hit 30-35 degrees C, the sea is warm (22-26 degrees C), and the beach clubs are buzzing. But it’s also crowded, and prices are at their highest. For a hen party, June is ideal, long days, warm but not scorching, and the water is pleasant for swimming. September is also great, with the summer crowds thinning out but the weather still holding up.

April and October are shoulder months. You might get a cooler day (20-25 degrees C) and the sea can be a bit fresh (18-20 degrees C), but you’ll have more choice of boats and lower prices. If you’re on a tight budget, consider a charter in late April or early October. Just bring a light jacket for the evening. The wind picks up in the afternoon, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar area, but modern yachts handle it fine. The skipper will adjust the route to keep things comfortable.

How to Book a Private Yacht Charter for a Hen Party

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter your preferred date, group size, and port. You’ll see a list of available boats with prices, photos, and specifications. Filter by boat type, duration, and price range. Once you find a boat that fits, click ‘Enquire’ or ‘Book Now’. You’ll be asked for your contact details and any special requests (e.g., catering, decorations, music). We’ll confirm availability and send you a quote within 24 hours. For hen parties, it’s best to book at least 2-4 weeks in advance, especially in high season.

If you’re unsure about which boat or port suits your group, call us or use the live chat on the site. We can recommend options based on your budget and vibe. Some operators allow a site visit to see the boat beforehand, ask when you enquire. For larger groups (12+), we may suggest a catamaran or a superyacht. Payment is typically by bank transfer or credit card. We recommend reading the terms and conditions carefully, particularly the cancellation policy. Most charters require a 30% deposit, with the balance due 7 days before departure. For last-minute bookings (within a week), full payment is usually required upfront.

Who Is a Private Yacht Charter for a Hen Party For

This is for the bride who wants something more than a pub crawl. It’s for groups of 6 to 20 women who want to celebrate in style without the stress of organising transport, venues, and timings. It works for all ages, from 18 to 50-plus. The vibe can be as relaxed or as lively as you want, some groups bring a Bluetooth speaker and just chill, others hire a DJ and turn the boat into a floating club. The skipper will accommodate your preferences, within reason. No rowdy behaviour that puts the boat at risk, but you can dance, drink, and take as many photos as you like.

It’s also for groups that want to combine a boat trip with other activities. You can stop at a beach club for lunch, go snorkelling in a cove, or watch the sunset with a glass of cava. The charter is private, so you control the itinerary. If you’re planning a surprise for the bride, let the skipper know, they can help with timing and location. For a truly unforgettable hen party, a private yacht charter in Marbella is hard to beat. Check out our blog for more ideas on planning the perfect day on the water.

Sample Itineraries for a Hen Party Yacht Charter

You can tailor the route to your group’s mood. A classic half-day from Puerto Banús heads east along the Golden Mile, past Marbella’s luxury hotels, then drops anchor at Cala del Faro for swimming. The skipper will pull up near the cliffs, you’ll have crystal-clear water and a view of La Concha mountain. After an hour or two, cruise back to Puerto Banús and stop at a beach club for lunch, Ocean Club is the obvious choice but Pangea or La Plage are less crowded. If you want a full-day trip, go west from Estepona towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You’ll likely spot dolphins, maybe even pilot whales. The skipper will find a quiet cove near Punta de la Chullera for a swim stop. Then head back to Estepona old town for a late lunch at a chiringuito on the seafront.

For a sunset charter, depart from Cabopino or Marbella Marina around 6pm in summer. Cruise along the coast as the sun drops behind La Concha, the light turns golden, and the sea calms. Anchor near a quiet beach, break out the cava, and watch the sky change colour. The skipper will have the boat back at port by 9pm, just in time for dinner at a restaurant in the old town. If your group wants to party, consider a charter that ends at a beach club with a DJ, you can dock directly at the club’s jetty and walk in. This works well from Puerto Banús or Benalmádena.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind on a Hen Party Charter

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe if you care about the marine life), a hat, and sunglasses. A light cover-up or a dress for when you get off the boat. Footwear should be non-marking, boat shoes or barefoot, no black-soled heels. Bring a cooler bag with drinks and snacks if the boat doesn’t supply them, most allow you to bring your own catering. A Bluetooth speaker is fine, but check if the boat already has one. Leave behind glass bottles, some operators ban them for safety. No red wine, it stains the upholstery. No illegal substances, the skipper will abort the trip and you’ll lose your deposit. Keep valuables minimal, there’s no safe on smaller boats, but the crew will look after your bags.

If you’re planning decorations, ask the charter company first. Some allow balloons and banners, others don’t because they can get tangled in the engine or blow overboard. A photo backdrop or a polaroid camera adds fun without mess. For the bride, consider a small cake or a personalised banner, but keep it simple. The boat is the main attraction. If you’re prone to seasickness, bring motion sickness tablets (the pharmacist in Marbella sells Biodramina). Take them an hour before departure. Catamarans are more stable than motor yachts, so if anyone in the group is nervous, book a cat.

How the Weather Affects Your Hen Party Charter

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, but the wind can be a factor. The Poniente wind blows from the west and brings calm seas, ideal for a smooth cruise. The Levante wind from the east can kick up waves, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar area. The skipper will monitor forecasts and adjust the route or cancel if conditions are unsafe. In summer, the sea is usually flat in the morning, with a light breeze picking up in the afternoon. July and August can have a heatwave, 35 degrees C on deck, so bring plenty of water and SPF 50. The boat’s saloon has air conditioning, so you can cool down inside.

If a storm is forecast, the charter company will contact you the day before to discuss options, reschedule or cancel with a full refund. For a hen party, it’s wise to have a backup plan if the weather turns, like a lunch at a beach club or a spa session. The skipper has the final say on safety, so trust their judgement. If the sea is rough, they might suggest a sheltered route along the coast instead of open water. You’ll still have a good time, just with less swimming.

Extras and Upgrades for a Hen Party Yacht Charter

Most charters offer add-ons. A crew member who serves drinks and helps with catering costs around EUR 100-200 extra. A DJ with a sound system for a floating party can be arranged, expect EUR 300-500 for a few hours. Some boats have a waterslide or a trampoline, popular with hen parties. Water toys like SUP boards, kayaks, or snorkel gear are usually EUR 50-100 per item. A photographer to capture the day, including drone shots, costs from EUR 300 for a half-day. If you want a chef to prepare a meal on board, that’s available on larger yachts and catamarans, expect EUR 50-100 per person for a multi-course lunch with local ingredients.

For a truly bespoke experience, some operators can arrange a flamenco dancer to perform on the boat, or a private yoga session on deck at sunrise. Ask when you book. The charter company can also organise a meet-and-greet at the port with a sign for the bride, or a bottle of cava on arrival. These small touches don’t cost much but make the day feel special. For a hen party, the most popular extras are a DJ, a photographer, and a catered lunch. Budget an additional 20-30% on top of the base charter price for these.

Legal and Safety Requirements for a Hen Party Charter

All boats on BoatHire24 are fully licensed and insured. The skipper holds a professional qualification, usually a Spanish Patrón de Yate or equivalent. They are responsible for safety, so they’ll do a brief safety drill at the start. Life jackets are available for all guests, though you’re not required to wear them unless the skipper deems it necessary. The boat has a first aid kit and a VHF radio for emergencies. For a hen party, the skipper will ask about any medical conditions or dietary restrictions beforehand, so be honest.

Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper will not tolerate excessive drunkenness that endangers the group. They have the right to terminate the charter early if anyone is aggressive or unsafe, with no refund. The legal drinking age in Spain is 18, but if you look under 25, bring ID. Smoking is usually allowed on the deck but not inside the saloon. Vaping is fine. If you’re planning to swim, the skipper will check for currents and jellyfish, they’ll advise if it’s safe. The Costa del Sol rarely has dangerous marine life, but occasionally jellyfish appear in late summer. The skipper will know the local conditions.

title: Catamaran Charter Marbella for Weddings – Romantic Celebration
metaDescription: Plan your romantic catamaran charter Marbella wedding on the Costa del Sol. Private skipper, sunset vows, and champagne. Book your celebration at BoatHire24.
h1: Catamaran Charter Marbella for Weddings
intro:
You want a wedding that doesn't feel like a conference with canapés. A catamaran charter Marbella wedding swaps the hotel ballroom for open sea, the DJ for the sound of waves, and the seating plan for a sun-drenched deck. At BoatHire24, we connect you with licensed skippers and private catamarans from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and Estepona. No crowds, no awkward small talk, just you, your partner, and up to 50 guests on a boat that moves with the Mediterranean swell.

The idea is simple: you hire the whole catamaran, the skipper handles navigation, and you focus on the ceremony, the photos, and the first dance as the sun drops behind La Concha mountain. We have seen couples exchange vows off Cala del Faro, sip cava while dolphins play near the Strait of Gibraltar, and cut cake on the foredeck with Marbella's skyline as the backdrop. This page tells you what to expect, how much it costs, and how to book without the fluff.
bodyHtml:
What a Catamaran Wedding Charter Includes

When you book a catamaran charter Marbella wedding through BoatHire24, the boat comes with a professional skipper who knows the coast. You do not need a licence, and you do not need to worry about anchoring or docking. The skipper will take you to calm spots like the bay off Cabopino or the quieter side of Puerto Banús. Most catamarans we list have a flybridge, a salon with AC, a galley, and a bow area big enough for a ceremony setup. Some boats include a sound system, a BBQ, and a bimini for shade. You can bring your own decorations, flowers, and caterer, or ask the skipper to recommend a local supplier. The charter is private, meaning no other passengers, just your party.

Typical inclusions are: fuel for up to 4-6 hours of cruising, ice, water, soft drinks, and sometimes a welcome glass of cava. You should confirm the exact package with the owner before booking. Most boats allow you to bring your own alcohol, but some charge a corkage fee. The skipper will stay sober and professional, so you can relax and enjoy the day.

Departure Ports for Your Wedding Charter

The Costa del Sol has several marinas where you can start your catamaran charter Marbella wedding. Puerto Banús is the obvious choice if you want glitz and proximity to the Golden Mile. From here, you can cruise towards the Río Verde or anchor near the dunes of Artola. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is smaller and more relaxed, with easy parking and a short walk to the old town for post-charter drinks. Cabopino, near the Artola sand dunes, offers a quieter departure with a natural beach close by. Estepona Marina is a 20-minute drive west of Marbella and gives you access to the calm waters of the Estepona bay and the Sierra Bermeja views. Sotogrande, further west, is more exclusive and ideal for intimate weddings with a focus on privacy. Benalmádena, east of Marbella, is a bit further but offers a large marina with plenty of boat options.

Each port has its own character. Puerto Banús is the most famous, but it can be busy in July and August. Estepona is quieter and more romantic. Your choice depends on where you are staying and the vibe you want. We recommend picking a port within 30 minutes of your venue or hotel to minimise travel time on the day.

Boat Options for a Wedding Celebration

Not all catamarans are the same. For a wedding, you want a boat with enough deck space for a ceremony, a shaded area for the reception, and a toilet or two. The most common sizes for weddings are 40 to 55 feet, which can hold 12 to 30 guests comfortably. Larger catamarans up to 70 feet can take up to 50 guests. Some boats come with a built-in sound system, a DJ booth, or a projector for a video montage. You can also find catamarans with a water slide or a paddleboard for the more adventurous guests.

If your party is small, say 6 to 10 people, a 35-foot catamaran might be enough. For larger groups, look at the Lagoon 52 or Bali 4.6 models, which have wide beams and stable platforms. The skipper will handle the anchoring and the route, so you can focus on the ceremony. We also have sailing catamarans and motor catamarans. Sailing catamarans are quieter and more romantic, while motor catamarans are faster and have more deck space. Both are stable and comfortable, even in a light chop.

Pricing Guidance for a Catamaran Wedding

Prices for a catamaran charter Marbella wedding vary depending on the boat size, season, and duration. For a half-day charter (4 hours), expect to pay from around EUR 1,500 for a 40-foot catamaran in low season. A full day (8 hours) on a 50-foot catamaran in high season can cost from EUR 3,500 to EUR 6,000. Superyacht catamarans with crew and luxury amenities are price on request and can go above EUR 10,000 per day. These prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic amenities. Catering, decorations, photography, and extra crew (like a hostess) are additional.

We recommend booking at least 2-3 months in advance for summer weddings, as popular boats get snapped up quickly. Winter and spring rates are lower, and the weather is still pleasant, with average temperatures of 18-22 degrees C from March to May. Your skipper will advise on the best route based on the wind and sea conditions. Always ask for a detailed quote before paying a deposit, and check what happens if the weather turns bad.

Best Seasons for a Wedding on the Water

The Costa del Sol has a long season for catamaran charters. May to October is the most reliable, with sunshine, calm seas, and water temperatures above 20 degrees C. July and August are the hottest and busiest, with afternoon temperatures hitting 32 degrees C. If you want a sunset wedding, aim for a late afternoon departure around 5-6 PM, when the light is golden and the heat eases. September and October are ideal for smaller weddings, with fewer crowds and still warm weather. April and November can work, but you risk a cooler breeze and occasional rain. The skipper will monitor the forecast and can adjust the route or cancel if conditions are unsafe.

For a wedding, we suggest avoiding the peak of August if you want a quiet ceremony, as the marinas are packed and anchorages can be busy. May, June, and September are the sweet spots. The sun sets around 8:30-9:30 PM depending on the month, giving you plenty of time for photos and dinner on deck.

How to Book Your Catamaran Wedding Charter

Booking a catamaran charter Marbella wedding on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to our search page, filter by boat type (catamaran), number of guests, and port. You will see available boats with photos, specs, and pricing. Contact the owner directly through the platform to ask about wedding packages. Most owners are flexible and can arrange a custom setup. We recommend having a clear idea of your guest count, preferred date, and budget before reaching out. The owner will confirm availability and send a contract with cancellation terms.

Deposits are usually 30-50% of the total, with the balance due a week before the charter. Payment is typically by bank transfer or card. Once booked, you can coordinate with the skipper on the itinerary, catering, and any special requests. If you need a photographer, florist, or caterer, the owner can recommend trusted local vendors. We also have a blog with tips on planning a wedding charter, including what to wear and how to manage seasickness.

Who Should Consider a Catamaran Wedding

A catamaran charter Marbella wedding is not for everyone. If you want a traditional church ceremony or a sit-down dinner for 100 people, this is not the right choice. But if you want an intimate, flexible celebration with a small group of close friends and family, it is hard to beat. It works well for elopements, renewal of vows, or a micro-wedding. The boat gives you a natural backdrop for photos, a moving venue that changes scenery, and a sense of exclusivity. It is also a good option if you are already on holiday in Marbella and want a low-stress ceremony without organising a full venue.

The skipper will take care of navigation, so you do not need any boating experience. Just bring your wedding attire, a sense of adventure, and maybe some seasickness patches if you are prone to motion. Most catamarans are stable, but the open sea can still rock a little. If you have elderly guests or anyone with mobility issues, check the boat's accessibility beforehand. Some catamarans have a ladder to the flybridge and a step up from the dock.

Local Colour and Photo Opportunities

The Costa del Sol offers plenty of scenic spots for a wedding charter. From Puerto Banús, you can cruise towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro, where the rocks turn orange at sunset. From Estepona, you can anchor near the old town's beach and see the whitewashed houses from the water. If you head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar, you might spot dolphins and even a glimpse of Africa on a clear day. The Nerja caves are too far for a half-day charter, but you can combine a full-day trip with a stop at the beaches of Maro. La Concha mountain looms over Marbella and provides a dramatic backdrop for photos.

Your skipper will know the best anchorages for calm water and good lighting. Some popular spots include the bay of Cabopino, the area off the Río Verde, and the cove near the Marbella Club Hotel. For a truly unique experience, you can time the charter to coincide with a full moon or a local festival. The skipper will also advise on anchoring regulations and protected areas.

What to Bring and What to Expect

On the day of your catamaran charter Marbella wedding, you will meet the skipper at the marina. Arrive 15 minutes early to load decorations, food, and personal items. The boat will have a fridge, a stove, and usually a BBQ. You can bring your own cake, but avoid anything that melts quickly in the sun. Bring sunscreen, hats, and a light jacket for the evening. The skipper will give a safety briefing and then cast off. The ceremony can take place at anchor or while cruising slowly. Most couples choose a calm anchorage where the boat is stable and the background is scenic.

After the vows, you can enjoy drinks, music, and a meal on deck. The skipper will return to port at the agreed time. You can also extend the charter if you want to watch the sunset at sea. Just confirm the extra cost beforehand. The entire experience is private, so you will not share the boat with strangers. The skipper stays in the wheelhouse or on the flybridge, giving you space to celebrate.

If you have any questions, contact the owner through the BoatHire24 platform. We are here to help you find the perfect catamaran for your wedding. Start your search on our BoatHire24 homepage and filter by catamaran and Marbella. We look forward to helping you create a memorable day on the water.

Choosing the Right Catamaran Layout for Your Ceremony

The physical layout of the catamaran matters more than you might think for a wedding. Look for boats with a wide, open bow area where you can set up an arch or a simple altar. The Lagoon 42 and 450 models have a forward seating area that works well for a small crowd of 10-15 people. For a larger group, the Bali 4.6 has a huge forward cockpit that can accommodate a ceremony for up to 25 guests. Some catamarans have a fixed table on the bow that you can use as a cake table or gift table. Check the photos carefully for deck space, and ask the owner if you can remove cushions or move furniture on the day. The flybridge is another option for the ceremony if the main deck is too small, but it usually has less shade and more wind. A 50-foot catamaran typically has two toilets and one shower, which is fine for a half-day charter but might be tight for a full day with 30 guests. Consider a boat with three or four cabins if you need changing rooms for the wedding party.

Specific Anchorages for Wedding Photos and Privacy

Not all anchorages are created equal for a wedding. The bay off Cabopino is a favourite because the Artola sand dunes create a natural backdrop with no buildings in sight. You can anchor in about 4 metres of water and the boat will stay steady even with a light breeze. From Puerto Banús, the area near the Río Verde mouth offers views of the Marbella mountains and the La Concha peak. If you want a more tropical feel, head towards the cove at Cala del Faro, where the cliffs are reddish-orange and the water is turquoise. From Estepona, the best spot is just west of the marina, where you can see the old town's white facades from the water. For a longer charter, the waters off Sotogrande are very calm and exclusive, with fewer other boats around. Your skipper will know the no-anchor zones and protected areas, so you do not get fined. Always ask the skipper to recommend a specific GPS coordinate for the ceremony spot a few days before the charter.

Managing the Weather and Backup Plans

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, but the wind can pick up in the afternoon, especially from May to July. The typical pattern is a calm morning, a breeze starting around 2 PM, and stronger winds by 5 PM. If you plan a ceremony for 4 PM, you might face a choppy anchorage. A better option is a 11 AM ceremony with a lunch cruise, or a 6 PM ceremony with a sunset dinner. The skipper will have a backup anchorage in a more sheltered bay, like the lee side of the Cabopino dunes or inside the Puerto Banús breakwater. If the wind is too strong, the skipper may recommend staying in the marina and doing the ceremony on the dock, which is less romantic but safer. Most contracts allow a free reschedule if the weather is deemed unsafe by the captain. Check the cancellation policy before booking, especially in shoulder months like April and November. A good rule is to book a boat with a bimini or hardtop so you have shade if the sun is too bright, and a cabin with AC so guests can cool down.

Catering and Drinks on a Catamaran Wedding

Most catamarans have a galley with a stove, fridge, and sink, but the oven is often small. You can bring pre-prepared food or hire a private chef who cooks on board. Some owners offer a catering add-on for around EUR 30-50 per person for a cold buffet with salads, meats, and bread. A hot meal with paella or grilled fish costs more, around EUR 60-80 per person. You can also bring your own food from a local supermarket or a caterer in Marbella. For drinks, the boat usually provides water, soft drinks, and ice. You can bring your own wine, beer, and spirits, but some owners charge a corkage fee of EUR 5-10 per bottle. A welcome glass of cava is often included. If you want a champagne toast, bring your own bottle and glasses. The fridge space is limited, so bring a cooler bag for extra drinks. For a sunset wedding, consider a signature cocktail like a gin and tonic with local Spanish gin. The skipper will not drink, so you can relax and enjoy the open bar.

faqs.q: How many guests can I have on a catamaran wedding charter in Marbella?
faqs.a: Most catamarans for weddings hold between 12 and 30 guests. Larger boats up to 70 feet can take up to 50 people. Check the boat's maximum capacity on the listing before booking. The skipper will enforce the limit for safety.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to rent a catamaran for my wedding?
faqs.a: No. Every catamaran charter Marbella wedding through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles all navigation. You do not need any boating experience or licence.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and decorations?
faqs.a: Yes, most owners allow you to bring your own catering, flowers, and decorations. Some boats have a galley and a BBQ. Confirm with the owner beforehand, as some may charge a small fee for setup or cleaning.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad on my wedding day?
faqs.a: The skipper will check the forecast and might suggest a different route or time. If conditions are unsafe, the charter can be rescheduled or cancelled. Check the cancellation policy in your contract before booking.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book a catamaran wedding charter?
faqs.a: For summer weddings, book at least 2-3 months ahead. Popular boats fill up quickly. For spring or autumn, 4-6 weeks is usually enough. Last-minute bookings are possible but the selection will be limited.

faqs.q: Can we have a legal wedding ceremony on a catamaran in Marbella?
faqs.a: Yes, but you need to arrange the legal paperwork with a local registrar or officiant. The boat can host the symbolic ceremony, but the legal marriage must be registered on land. The skipper can recommend a local officiant.

faqs.q: What is the best time of day for a wedding charter?
faqs.a: Late afternoon, around 5-6 PM, is ideal for a sunset wedding. The light is golden, the heat is lower, and the sea is usually calm. You can combine the ceremony with dinner and drinks as the sun goes down.

title: Speedboat Hire Marbella Hourly – Affordable Rates
metaDescription: Looking for speedboat hire Marbella hourly? Compare affordable rates for RIBs & speedboats with skipper. Book by the hour from Puerto Banús. Instant confirmation.
h1: Speedboat Hire Marbella Hourly, Affordable Rates
intro: You want to get on the water in Marbella without committing to a full day or blowing your budget. Speedboat hire Marbella hourly is the answer. You pay for the time you actually use, the boat comes with a licensed skipper, and you can blast along the Costa del Sol coast from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or Cabopino. Rates typically start from around EUR 200 per hour for a 6-metre RIB and go up from there depending on size, power, and season. No hidden costs, no fuel surcharges in the quoted price, and you can book for as little as one hour.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with Hourly Speedboat Hire in Marbella

Every speedboat hire on BoatHire24 includes a professional skipper who holds a Spanish licence. You don't need a boating licence yourself. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and mooring while you relax or take the helm under supervision. Boats are cleaned and fuelled before departure. Life jackets, basic safety equipment, and insurance are included. Some operators also supply snorkelling gear or a Bluetooth speaker, but check the listing. You can extend your hire on the day if the boat is available, but you pay for the extra time at the same hourly rate.

Ports Where You Can Depart

Hourly speedboat hire is available from five main ports on the Costa del Sol. Puerto Banús is the most popular starting point: you are out of the marina and past the breakwater in under ten minutes, heading toward the Marbella coastline or the cliffs of Cabopino. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a quieter alternative, closer to the old town and the beach clubs. Cabopino gives you quick access to the Cabopino dunes and the nature reserve. Estepona port is a good base for exploring the western coast toward Gibraltar. Sotogrande and Benalmádena also have options, but availability varies. Check the listing for the exact departure port before booking.

Types of Boats Available for Hourly Hire

The term speedboat covers a few different hull types. RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) are the most common: light, fast, and stable. Typical sizes are 6 to 8 metres, with outboard engines from 150 to 300 hp. You can expect speeds of 35 to 50 knots in calm conditions. Some operators offer centre-console boats with more deck space and a small cabin. A few have classic wooden runabouts for a more stylish cruise, though those are slower. Fishing boats with outboard engines also appear in the hourly category, but they are usually less powerful. If you want pure adrenaline, look for a RIB with a twin-engine setup. All boats have a maximum capacity of 8 to 12 passengers, depending on the licence category.

Pricing Guidance for Hourly Speedboat Hire Marbella

Rates are seasonal and depend on boat size and engine power. In low season (October to April), a 6-metre RIB with a 150 hp engine starts from around EUR 200 per hour. Mid-season (May, June, September) the same boat goes for EUR 250 to EUR 300 per hour. High season (July, August) you pay EUR 300 to EUR 400 per hour. An 8-metre RIB with twin 200 hp engines costs from EUR 400 per hour in low season and up to EUR 600 in August. Some operators offer a two-hour minimum in high season. Fuel is included in the hourly rate for most listings, but a few charge extra for fuel based on usage. Always read the terms before confirming. You can find the exact price on the search page by filtering by port and date.

Best Seasons for Speedboat Hire by the Hour

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, so you can hire a speedboat almost any month. The water is warmest from June to October (22 to 26 degrees C). July and August are the busiest months, so book at least a week ahead. May, June, and September offer good weather with fewer crowds and lower rates. From November to March, the sea can be choppy, especially in the afternoon when the Levante wind picks up. Morning hires are smoother in winter. April and October are transitional months: you might get flat calm or a bit of swell. Check the marine forecast on the day. If the skipper cancels due to bad weather, you get a full refund.

What You Can Do in One or Two Hours

With one hour, you can cruise along the Marbella coastline from Puerto Banús to the Marbella Marina and back, or head south toward the Cabopino lighthouse. Two hours gives you time to reach Cala del Faro, a small cove west of Estepona, or anchor near the Cabopino dunes for a quick swim. Three hours lets you go further: you can cross the bay toward the Strait of Gibraltar and see dolphins, or head east toward the Nerja caves (though that is a longer run, more like four hours round trip). Most hourly hire is used for coastal sightseeing, sunset cruises, or a fast transfer between beach clubs. You cannot go far offshore in one hour because the skipper needs to stay within a reasonable distance from the port.

How to Book Hourly Speedboat Hire on BoatHire24

Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and use the search bar. Enter Marbella as the location, set the date and time, and filter by boat type: RIB or speedboat. The results show available boats with hourly rates. Click on a listing to see the full description, photos, and terms. You can book directly online with instant confirmation. Payment is by credit card or PayPal. You receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and the exact meeting point at the port. Cancel up to 48 hours before departure for a full refund. For last-minute bookings, call the number on the listing. The platform charges no booking fee.

Who Should Hire a Speedboat by the Hour

Hourly hire suits small groups who want a quick experience without a full-day commitment. Couples, families with older children, and small friend groups use it for a sunset cruise or a fast run to a beach club. Business travellers with a few hours free between meetings hire speedboats for a coastal sightseeing tour. Photographers and videographers use them to get shots of the coastline from the water. If you are planning a party or a large group, a catamaran or motor yacht might be better value for the whole day. Speedboats are not ideal for long-distance cruising or for people who get seasick easily at high speeds. The skipper can adjust the pace, but the boat is designed for speed, not comfort.

Safety and Licensing Requirements

All skippers on BoatHire24 hold a Spanish recreational boating licence (Patrón de Navegación Básica or higher) and a valid VHF radio certificate. They are trained in first aid and safety procedures. The boat carries life jackets for all passengers, a first aid kit, flares, fire extinguisher, and a VHF radio. The skipper gives a safety briefing before departure. You must follow the skipper's instructions at all times. Children under 12 must wear a life jacket while the boat is moving. The maximum passenger number is strictly enforced. Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper will not operate the boat if the person at the helm has been drinking. The boat is equipped with an automatic identification system (AIS) and GPS tracking for safety.

Local Highlights You Can See from the Water

From a speedboat, you get a different perspective on Marbella's landmarks. The La Concha mountain rises behind the town, visible from miles offshore. The Puerto Banús marina looks like a toy harbour from the water, with superyachts lined up. The Río Verde mouth is a good spot for birdwatching. Cala del Faro near Estepona has a small lighthouse and clear water for swimming. In the Strait of Gibraltar, you can spot common dolphins, bottlenose dolphins, and occasionally pilot whales. The Nerja caves are visible from the sea as a series of white cliffs with cave openings, but you need a longer hire to get there. The coastline between Marbella and Estepona has several small coves accessible only by boat. Your skipper knows the best spots and can adjust the route based on your interests.

Comparing Hourly Hire with Half-Day and Full-Day Options

Hourly hire is cheaper per trip but more expensive per hour if you compare rates. A half-day (4 hours) might cost EUR 600 to EUR 800, which works out at EUR 150 to EUR 200 per hour. A full day (8 hours) can be EUR 1,000 to EUR 1,500, around EUR 125 to EUR 190 per hour. So if you want more than two hours, consider a half-day or full-day booking for better value. Hourly hire is best for short trips, sunset cruises, or when you are not sure how long you want to stay on the water. You can always extend on the day if the boat is free, but you lose the bulk discount. Use the BoatHire24 blog to read comparisons of different hire durations and find the best option for your plans.

Frequently Asked Questions about Speedboat Hire Marbella Hourly

How Hourly Speedboat Hire Compares to Licence-Free Day Boats

You might see licence-free day boats advertised for similar hourly rates. Those are typically small motorboats with a 5 hp engine limit, maxing out at 6 knots. A speedboat with 150 hp is a different experience entirely. You get planing speeds, the ability to cover more coastline, and the thrill of acceleration. Licence-free boats are cheaper to rent but you drive them yourself, which means you also handle mooring and navigation. With a speedboat hire you have a skipper who knows the local waters, so you can focus on the view and the ride. If you want to drive yourself and save money, look for a licence-free boat. If you want speed, comfort, and local knowledge, hourly speedboat hire is the better choice.

Best Routes for a One-Hour Speedboat Trip from Puerto Banús

From Puerto Banús, a one-hour trip works well heading east toward the Marbella Marina. You pass the Golden Mile beach clubs, the Marbella Club Hotel, and the Puerto Deportivo entrance. The skipper can slow down near the old town so you can take photos of the castle and the promenade. Alternatively, head west toward the Cabopino lighthouse. That route takes you past the dunes and the naturist beach, with a possible stop for a quick swim if you have 10 minutes to spare. You cannot go far inland or explore coves in one hour, but you get a solid coastal tour. For a sunset option, leave 30 minutes before sunset and watch the sun drop behind La Concha from the water.

What to Bring and Wear for an Hourly Speedboat Trip

The boat moves fast, so wind chill is a factor even on a 30-degree day. Bring a light jacket or a windbreaker, especially for evening trips. Sunscreen with high SPF is essential because the sun reflects off the water. Wear non-slip shoes or barefoot-friendly sandals; the deck can get slippery. A small dry bag for your phone, wallet, and keys is useful because spray can wet the seats. Sunglasses with a strap are better than loose ones. If you plan to swim, bring a towel and change of clothes, but keep the bag compact because storage on a 6-metre RIB is limited. The boat usually has a small cooler for drinks, but check the listing to confirm.

How Weather Affects Hourly Speedboat Hire in Different Seasons

In summer, the thermal wind from the west picks up around midday, creating a chop of 0.5 to 1 metre. Morning hires from 9 am to 12 pm are usually the calmest. Afternoon hires can be bumpier, but most speedboats handle a metre of swell without issue. In spring and autumn, the Levante wind from the east can bring stronger winds and bigger waves, especially in the afternoon. Skippers may recommend a shorter route or a different departure time to avoid rough conditions. Winter hires are possible on calm days, but the water temperature drops to 15-17 degrees C, making swimming less appealing. Always check the forecast on the day and ask the skipper if conditions are suitable for your planned route.

Extra Costs and Hidden Charges to Watch For

Most hourly speedboat listings include fuel, skipper, and insurance. But some operators charge extra for fuel based on consumption, which can add EUR 50 to EUR 100 per hour if you run the engines hard. A few listings charge a cleaning fee of EUR 20 to EUR 50 if you leave the boat messy. Snorkelling equipment is sometimes an add-on at EUR 10 to EUR 20 per set. Food and drinks are not included unless specified. Gratuity for the skipper is not mandatory but is appreciated if you had a good time. Read the terms section on each listing carefully. If you see "fuel not included" or "extras may apply," factor those into your budget. The total price shown on the search page usually includes all mandatory costs, but confirm before booking.

How to Choose the Right Speedboat for Your Group Size

A 6-metre RIB seats 6 to 8 passengers comfortably. For 4 people, that size is fine with room to move. For 8 people, it gets tight, especially if you want to swim or store bags. An 8-metre RIB seats 8 to 12 passengers and has more deck space, a larger sun pad at the bow, and often a small bathroom in the console. If you have 6 or more people, book the larger boat. Some centre-console boats have a T-top roof for shade, which is useful in summer. Classic wooden runabouts look great but have less space and no shade. Fishing boats have a low freeboard and more deck space but are slower. Use the filter on the search page to narrow by passenger capacity and boat length.

What Happens If You Are Late or Want to Extend

Most operators allow a 15-minute grace period for late arrivals. After that, the hire time is reduced because the boat has a fixed return time for the next booking. If you want to extend, ask the skipper during the trip. Extensions are subject to availability and you pay the same hourly rate for the extra time. Some operators require a minimum extension of 30 minutes. If you extend, the skipper will adjust the route to ensure you return on time for the next slot. Late returns without prior agreement may incur a penalty fee of EUR 50 to EUR 100. To avoid issues, arrive at the port 15 minutes before your booked time. The meeting point is usually at the fuel dock or a specific pontoon number listed in the confirmation email.

Why BoatHire24 Is the Best Platform for Hourly Speedboat Hire in Marbella

You can read the boat description, see photos, and check the exact departure port before booking. The search page lets you filter by price, boat type, passenger capacity, and departure port.
