bodyHtml:
What You Get on a Luxury Catamaran Charter Puerto Banus Day

A luxury catamaran charter in Puerto Banus is not just a boat ride. The package includes a licensed skipper who knows the coast, a host or steward to serve drinks and food, and a fuel allowance for up to 8 hours of cruising. Most charters also include a selection of soft drinks, water, and sometimes beer and cava. You can add wine, champagne, or a full catering menu at extra cost. The boat itself is equipped with a sound system, a fridge, a toilet (or two), and a shower on the swim platform. Some catamarans have a trampoline net at the bow where you can lie down and feel the spray. Others have a flybridge with a steering station and a sun pad. You get to choose the boat that fits your group size and style.

The crew are the key. They handle the navigation, the anchoring, and the safety briefing. They also know the best spots for swimming, snorkelling, and spotting dolphins. They will not hover, but they are there when you need another drink or a recommendation for a restaurant ashore. The skipper speaks English and Spanish, and often German and French too.

Departure Ports for Your Catamaran Day Charter

Puerto Banús is the obvious starting point, but you can also depart from Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. Each port gives you a different coastline. From Puerto Banús, you can head east towards Marbella and the residential towers of the Golden Mile, or west towards the nature reserve of the Dunas de Artola and the Cabopino sandbar. From Estepona, you get closer to the Strait of Gibraltar and the chance to see dolphins and whales. From Sotogrande, you are near the mouth of the Guadiaro River and the exclusive Sotogrande marina. The choice of port affects the scenery and the wildlife, but the quality of the charter is the same.

If you are staying in Marbella or the surrounding area, we recommend departing from Puerto Banús because it is the most glamorous marina and the easiest to reach by taxi or car. You can park in the underground car park or get dropped off right at the dock. The meeting point is usually the main office at the marina, where the crew will escort you to the boat.

Boat Options for a Luxury Catamaran Charter

Not all catamarans are the same. Here are the main types you can book for a day charter:

  • 40 to 45 foot catamarans, Ideal for groups of 8 to 12. They have a spacious cockpit, a saloon with a galley, and two or three cabins below deck. They are stable and easy to move around on, even for people who get seasick.
  • 50 to 55 foot catamarans, These can take 12 to 16 guests. They have a larger flybridge, a bigger sun deck at the bow, and often a water slide or a paddleboard. They are the most popular choice for birthday parties and corporate events.
  • 60 foot and above, These are the top-tier luxury catamarans with a jacuzzi, a full crew including a chef, and a tender for exploring shallow coves. They can host up to 20 guests and cost from around EUR 6,000 per day.

You can also book a sailing catamaran if you prefer the silence of wind power, but most luxury charters are motor catamarans because they are faster and more stable. The average cruising speed is around 8 to 10 knots, which is enough to cover the coast without feeling rushed.

Pricing Guidance for a Day Charter

Prices for a luxury catamaran charter in Puerto Banus vary by boat size, season, and included extras. As a rough guide, expect to pay from around EUR 3,500 for a 40-foot catamaran for a full day (8 hours) in the low season (May or October). In peak season (July and August), the same boat might cost EUR 5,000. A 55-foot catamaran with a jacuzzi and a crew of three can be EUR 6,500 to EUR 8,000. Superyacht catamarans over 70 feet are price on request, but you are looking at EUR 10,000 or more per day.

The price usually includes VAT, insurance, the skipper and crew, fuel for up to 8 hours, and basic drinks. Extras like gourmet catering, champagne, or a water sports package (jet ski, wakeboard) are charged separately. You can also add a photographer or a DJ for an extra fee. Always ask for a full breakdown before booking.

Best Season for a Catamaran Day Charter

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 days of sunshine a year. The best time for a catamaran charter is from May to October, when the water temperature is above 20 degrees C and the sea is calm. July and August are the hottest and busiest months, with air temperatures hitting 35 degrees C and the water reaching 24 degrees C. September and October are quieter and still warm, with fewer crowds and lower prices. April and November can be hit and miss, with occasional wind and rain, but you can still get a good day if the forecast is clear.

The wind is a factor. The afternoon Levante wind can pick up from the east, creating choppy conditions in the afternoon. Most skippers plan the itinerary to minimise discomfort, heading west in the morning and returning before the wind builds. If you are prone to seasickness, choose a catamaran over a monohull because the twin hulls provide more stability.

How to Book a Luxury Catamaran Charter Puerto Banus Day

Booking is straightforward through BoatHire24. You browse the available catamarans online, check the photos and specifications, and send a booking request with your preferred date and group size. We confirm availability and send you a quote within a few hours. You pay a deposit (usually 50%) to secure the date, and the balance is due a week before the charter. You can also book last minute if you call us, but popular dates in July and August sell out weeks in advance.

You do not need a boating licence for a catamaran charter because the skipper is included. You just need to bring swimwear, sunscreen, a towel, and a hat. The boat has a fridge, so you can bring your own food and drink if you prefer. The crew will store and serve it for you. You can also ask us to arrange a catered lunch from a local restaurant or a barbecue on board.

For more tips on planning your day, check our blog for articles on the best coves, what to pack, and how to avoid seasickness. We also have a search page where you can filter catamarans by price, size, and extras.

Who Is This Charter For

A luxury catamaran charter is for anyone who wants a day of relaxation, celebration, or exploration without the stress of organising everything. It works for couples celebrating an anniversary, families with children (the crew can arrange a kids' menu and water toys), groups of friends on a stag or hen do, and corporate clients hosting a client entertainment event. The boat is wheelchair accessible on some models, but check with us before booking. The minimum age for guests is usually 2 years old, but some charter companies have a minimum age of 5 for safety reasons.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter, but that is not common for luxury catamarans. Most are private charters for your group only. That means you have the boat to yourselves, and you can set the pace and the itinerary.

What to Expect on the Day

You arrive at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The crew greets you, shows you the boat, and gives a safety briefing. You stow your bags in a cabin or a locker, and then you set off. The first hour is usually a gentle cruise along the coast, past the luxury villas of the Golden Mile and the pine forests of Cabopino. The skipper points out landmarks like La Concha mountain and the Río Verde. You can sit on the flybridge, lie on the sun loungers, or stand at the bow and feel the breeze.

After about an hour, the skipper anchors in a sheltered cove like Cala del Faro or the sandbar at Cabopino. You can swim, snorkel, use the paddleboard, or just float in the water. The crew serves drinks and a light lunch if you have ordered it. You have about two hours to relax before the skipper suggests moving to another spot or heading back. The return journey is slower, with music playing and the sun setting over the sea. You arrive back at the marina around 6pm, feeling relaxed and a little sunburned.

Local Attractions Near Puerto Banús

If you have time before or after the charter, explore Puerto Banús itself. The marina is famous for its luxury boutiques, designer stores, and high-end restaurants. You can walk along the promenade and see the superyachts moored at the dock. The port also has a casino, a nightclub, and a beach club. A short drive away is the old town of Marbella, with its narrow streets, orange trees, and tapas bars. If you are heading west, Estepona old town is worth a visit for its flower-filled streets and the Plaza de las Flores. For a longer trip, the Nerja caves are about an hour east, but you will need a separate day for that.

The Strait of Gibraltar is a popular destination for dolphin and whale watching. If you charter a catamaran from Estepona or Sotogrande, you can spend the day in the strait and see common dolphins, striped dolphins, and sometimes pilot whales. The skipper will adjust the route to maximise your chances of sightings.

Frequently Asked Questions

How to Choose the Right Catamaran for Your Group

Picking the right catamaran is about matching the boat to your group's size and vibe. For a group of 8 to 10, a 45-foot Lagoon or Fountaine Pajot is standard. It has a large cockpit table for lunch, a sun deck at the bow, and enough cabin space for a nap if you need one. For a younger crowd or a party group, look for a catamaran with a flybridge bar and a loud sound system. Some boats have a water slide or a paddleboard included, which adds fun for kids and adults alike. If you are a couple or a small family of four, a 38-foot catamaran is enough, but the luxury feel is better on a 50-footer with more space to spread out. Always check the maximum guest number, including children, because Spanish regulations limit passenger capacity strictly.

Ask the crew about the boat's age and maintenance history. A newer catamaran (2020 or later) will have better air conditioning, more modern electronics, and a cleaner look. Older boats can still be fine, but check the photos carefully for wear and tear. The crew will usually tell you if the boat has any quirks, like a slow water maker or a finicky generator.

What to Do If the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is sunny most of the time, but the weather can change. If the wind picks up or a storm is forecast, the skipper will decide whether to cancel or modify the itinerary. They will not go out if the sea state is dangerous, and they will not anchor in an exposed cove if the swell is too high. In that case, you can reschedule for another day or choose a shorter trip closer to the marina. Some charter companies offer a partial refund if the trip is cancelled due to weather, but check the terms before booking. In July and August, the risk of bad weather is very low, but in April or October, you should have a backup plan. The skipper might suggest a lunch cruise inside the marina or a short trip to a sheltered bay like the port of Cabopino.

If you are worried about seasickness, take a motion sickness pill an hour before departure. Catamarans are more stable than monohulls, but the movement can still affect sensitive people. Avoid heavy meals and alcohol before the trip. The crew can also give you ginger tea or a wristband if you ask.

Extra Services You Can Add to Your Charter

Most luxury catamarans offer extras that make the day more special. You can add a private chef who prepares a gourmet lunch on board, using local ingredients like fresh fish from the market, Iberian ham, and Spanish cheeses. That costs from around EUR 200 per person for a three-course meal. You can also hire a photographer or a videographer to capture the day, which is popular for proposals, anniversaries, or group photos. Prices start at EUR 300 for a few hours. A DJ or a live musician can be arranged for parties, with a sound system already on board. Water sports like jet skiing, wakeboarding, or flyboarding can be added if the boat has a tender or if you charter a RIB to follow you. These extras are charged separately and should be arranged at least 48 hours in advance.

For a romantic touch, you can order flowers, a bottle of champagne, or a custom cake. The crew will set up a private dinner on the bow at sunset, with cushions and candles. That is a popular option for proposals, and the skipper can anchor at a spot with a view of the sunset over the sea. Ask for the "sunset package" when you book.

How to Get to Puerto Banús and Where to Park

Puerto Banús is about 10 minutes by taxi from Marbella town centre and 45 minutes from Málaga Airport. If you are driving, the marina has a public car park (Parking Puerto Banús) with over 1,000 spaces. It costs around EUR 2 per hour or EUR 20 for a full day. There is also a smaller car park near the Club de Mar entrance, but it fills up quickly in summer. You can get dropped off at the roundabout near the main entrance, and the crew will meet you at the office. If you are staying in a hotel in Marbella, many hotels offer a shuttle service to the marina. For groups, a private minibus or Uber is easier than parking multiple cars.

The meeting point is usually the office of the charter company, which is on the ground floor of the marina building near the main square. The crew will walk you to the boat, which is moored at the dock. Arrive 15 minutes early to sign the waiver and get the safety briefing. If you are late, the skipper may delay departure, but the clock still runs on your charter time.

h1: Yacht Charter Marbella New Year's Eve, Celebrate at Sea
keyword: yacht charter marbella new years eve
intro: You want to see the New Year in with style, and a yacht charter Marbella New Year's Eve is the only way to do it. Forget the crowded clubs and overpriced hotel restaurants. You get a private boat, a licensed skipper, and a front-row seat for the Puerto Banús fireworks. bodyHtml:
What You Get on a New Year's Eve Yacht Charter

Every charter includes a professional skipper who knows the local waters and the best anchorage for the midnight fireworks. You get the boat for 4 to 6 hours, typically from 8pm to 2am. Most packages include a bottle of cava or champagne per person, soft drinks, and sometimes a small buffet of tapas or canapés. You can bring your own food and extra drinks if you want, but check with the owner first. The skipper handles all navigation and safety, so you just relax and celebrate. No hidden fees for fuel or cleaning, though a 10% tip for the crew is customary.

Departure Ports for Your New Year's Eve Charter

Puerto Banús is the star of the show. The marina is lit up, the superyachts are out, and the fireworks launch right over the harbour. You can board at 7pm, cruise out to the bay, and watch the display from the water. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter but still has good views and easy parking. Cabopino offers a more relaxed vibe, with the dunes and the lighthouse in the background. Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena also have options, but the best fireworks are in Banús. Your skipper will know the best spot for each port.

Boat Options for New Year's Eve

Motor yachts from 10 to 20 metres are the most popular. You get speed, comfort, and a flybridge for panoramic views. Expect prices from around EUR 1,500 for a 12-metre yacht for 10 guests, up to EUR 5,000 for a 20-metre with a full crew. Catamarans offer more deck space and stability, ideal for larger groups of 12 to 20. Prices start around EUR 2,000 for an 11-metre cat. Sailing yachts are cheaper, from EUR 1,000 for a 10-metre, but they are slower and less spacious. RIBs and speedboats are not recommended for New Year's Eve because they are open and cold. Licence-free day boats are available but limited to daylight hours, so they don't work for a night charter. Superyachts are price on request, but you can get a 30-metre with a full crew for around EUR 15,000. Check the search page for live availability.

Pricing Guidance for New Year's Eve

Prices are higher than a standard evening charter because of demand and the extended hours. Expect a 30-50% premium over a normal sunset cruise. For a group of 10, budget EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 for a decent motor yacht. For 20 guests, look at EUR 3,000 to EUR 6,000. Catamarans for 20 start around EUR 4,000. All prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic catering. You can add a DJ, a photographer, or extra decorations for an additional fee. Book early, by October or November, to secure the best boats and avoid disappointment. Last-minute bookings are possible but limited and often more expensive.

Weather and Sea Conditions in Winter

December in Marbella is mild, with daytime temperatures around 16-18 degrees C and evening temperatures dropping to 10-12 degrees C. The sea temperature is about 15-16 degrees C, so it is cold. You will need a warm jacket, even on a covered boat. The wind can pick up in the afternoon, but the skipper will choose a sheltered route, usually along the coast from Banús to Cala del Faro or towards the Rio Verde. Rain is possible but rare, typically one or two days a month. If the weather is bad, the charter can be rescheduled or cancelled with a full refund, depending on the owner's policy. Check the forecast on the day and bring layers.

What to Expect on the Night

You meet at the marina at 7.30pm, board the boat, and the skipper gives a safety briefing. You cruise out to the anchorage point, usually a few hundred metres off Puerto Banús, by 9pm. The bar is open, the music is playing, and you watch the other boats gather. At midnight, the fireworks start, lasting 10 to 15 minutes. Then you toast with champagne, take photos, and cruise back to the marina, arriving by 1.30am to 2am. You can stay on the dock for a while, but the boat needs to be cleaned and prepped for the next day. No sleeping on board, unless you book a liveaboard charter, which is rare for New Year's Eve.

Who Should Book a New Year's Eve Yacht Charter

This is for groups of friends, couples, or families who want a private celebration without the crowds. It works well for corporate events, milestone birthdays, or wedding anniversaries. Children are welcome on most boats, but check with the owner about age limits and safety equipment. If you get seasick easily, choose a catamaran or a large motor yacht, and take medication beforehand. The boat rocks gently at anchor, but the motion is minimal. If you want a party boat with a DJ and dancing, go for a motor yacht with a large flybridge. If you prefer a quiet dinner under the stars, a sailing yacht with a saloon is better. The BoatHire24 blog has more tips on choosing the right boat.

How to Book Your New Year's Eve Charter

Go to the search page, enter your date as 31 December, and filter by port and boat type. You can book directly online with a deposit of 30-50%, and the balance is due 7 days before the charter. Some owners offer a full refund if you cancel 30 days in advance, but read the terms carefully. You can also contact the owner through the platform to ask about custom packages, such as a longer charter or a specific menu. For large groups, book two boats side by side if one is not big enough. The platform handles payment securely, and you get a confirmation with the skipper's contact details. Do not book through social media or cash deals, as you have no protection. Stick to BoatHire24 for a safe transaction.

Local Highlights for Your New Year's Eve

Puerto Banús is the centre of the action. The marina has restaurants, bars, and a New Year's Eve street party with live music. You can dock and join the party after the cruise, but most guests stay on the boat. The view of La Concha mountain from the sea is spectacular, especially with the city lights behind it. If you charter from Estepona, you can see the old town lit up from the water. From Sotogrande, you get a quieter experience with the golf course lights in the distance. The Strait of Gibraltar is too far for a night charter, but you might see dolphins during the day if you book a longer cruise. For a unique experience, combine your charter with a day trip to the Nerja caves, but that is a separate excursion.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I bring my own food and drink on a New Year's Eve yacht charter?

Yes, most charters allow you to bring your own food and drink. Some owners include a basic catering package, but you can supplement it. Check with the owner beforehand, especially for glass bottles, as some boats prefer plastic for safety. You are responsible for cleaning up after yourself.

What happens if the weather is bad on New Year's Eve?

If the weather is unsafe, the skipper will cancel the charter. You get a full refund or a rescheduled date, depending on the owner's policy. Check the cancellation terms before booking. Most owners are flexible for New Year's Eve due to the high demand.

How many people can fit on a yacht for New Year's Eve?

The capacity depends on the boat. A 12-metre motor yacht typically holds 10 to 12 guests. A 16-metre catamaran can take up to 20. Superyachts over 30 metres can host 30 or more. Always check the maximum capacity on the listing, as it is strictly enforced for safety.

Can I see the fireworks from the boat?

Yes, the skipper will anchor the boat in a prime spot to watch the Puerto Banús fireworks. You have an unobstructed view from the deck. Some boats have a flybridge for an even better vantage point. The fireworks are visible from a few kilometres away, so you do not need to be right in the harbour.

Is a deposit required to book a New Year's Eve charter?

Yes, a deposit of 30-50% is required to secure the booking. The balance is due 7 days before the charter. Payments are processed securely through the platform. Some owners offer a full refund if you cancel 30 days in advance, but check the specific policy.

Can I book a New Year's Eve charter for a large group on two boats?

Yes, you can book two or more boats and anchor them next to each other. This works well for corporate events or large parties. Contact the owners through the platform to coordinate. The skippers can communicate by radio to keep the boats close together.

How to Make Your New Year's Eve Charter Stand Out

Want something beyond the standard cruise and fireworks. You can arrange a private chef to cook on board, adding around EUR 200 to EUR 500 depending on the menu and boat size. A DJ for the night costs roughly EUR 300 to EUR 800, and many owners have a sound system already installed. Decorate the boat with balloons, banners, or a custom light setup, but clear it with the owner first to avoid damage deposits. Some charters offer a professional photographer for EUR 150 to EUR 400, giving you group shots against the fireworks. If you are celebrating a milestone, like a 50th birthday or an engagement, tell the owner in advance, and they might arrange a small cake or a personalised banner. These extras are not included in the base price, so budget an additional 20-30% on top of the charter fee.

Best Boat Types for a Cold Night on the Water

Motor yachts with a fully enclosed saloon are your best bet. You get heating, a galley, and a toilet, so you stay warm between the fireworks and the dancing. Look for boats with a flybridge that has a hardtop or a bimini, as the open deck can get chilly at 10-12 degrees C. Catamarans have a large saloon with 360-degree windows, giving you views without the wind. Sailing yachts are less insulated, but some have a heater and a cosy interior. Avoid RIBs and speedboats entirely for New Year's Eve, as they are open and you will freeze. Licence-free day boats are not available at night, so they are out of the question. For a group of 10, a 13-metre motor yacht like a Sunseeker or a Princess is ideal. For 20, a 16-metre catamaran like a Lagoon or a Fountaine Pajot gives you space and stability. Check the search page to see which boats are available for your date.

Specific Ports and Their New Year's Eve Vibe

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice, but each port has a different character. In Banús, you are in the middle of the party, with lights, music, and crowds on the dock. The fireworks launch from the breakwater, so you get a front-row seat from the water. Marbella Marina is more subdued, with a smaller display and fewer boats, but parking is easier and the atmosphere is relaxed. Cabopino offers a natural setting, with the dunes and the lighthouse providing a backdrop, and the fireworks are smaller but still impressive. Estepona has a family-friendly celebration in the old town, and you can see the lights from the marina. Sotogrande is the quietest, with a private event at the marina and a low-key display. Benalmádena has a larger fireworks show over the marina, but it is further from Marbella. If you want the biggest spectacle, stick to Puerto Banús. Your skipper will anchor you in the best spot, usually just outside the harbour entrance, where you can see the whole display without the crowd.

Cost Breakdown for a New Year's Eve Charter

Here is a rough guide to what you will pay. A 12-metre motor yacht for 10 guests costs from around EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500 for the night. That includes the skipper, fuel, and basic catering like cava and canapés. A 16-metre catamaran for 20 guests starts at EUR 3,500 and can go up to EUR 6,000. A 20-metre motor yacht with a full crew, including a hostess, costs from EUR 5,000 to EUR 8,000. Superyachts over 30 metres are price on request, but expect EUR 15,000 to EUR 30,000 for a private New Year's Eve. Add a DJ for EUR 300 to EUR 800, a photographer for EUR 150 to EUR 400, and a private chef for EUR 200 to EUR 500. If you want a longer charter, say from 6pm to 3am, add another 20-30% to the base price. Fuel is included in most charters, but if you take a longer cruise to Estepona or Cabopino, the owner might charge extra for fuel, typically EUR 100 to EUR 300. Always confirm what is included before you book.

What to Wear on a New Year's Eve Yacht Charter

December evenings in Marbella are cold, with temperatures dropping to 10-12 degrees C. You need layers. Start with a thermal base layer, add a sweater or a fleece, and finish with a waterproof jacket. The wind on the water can make it feel 5 degrees colder, so a windbreaker is essential. Bring a scarf, gloves, and a hat if you are sensitive to cold. For footwear, non-slip shoes with a rubber sole, as the deck can be wet from condensation. Avoid high heels, as they damage the deck and are dangerous on a moving boat. If you plan to dance on the flybridge, bring a jacket you can take off when you get warm. Some boats have heating in the saloon, so you can step inside to warm up. For women, a dress with tights and a pashmina works. For men, trousers and a blazer with a coat. No one will judge if you wear a ski jacket, comfort is more important than fashion on a cold night.

How to Get to the Marina on New Year's Eve

Puerto Banús is busy on New Year's Eve, with traffic and limited parking. Arrive at least 30 minutes early to find a spot. The marina has paid parking, around EUR 20 for the evening, but it fills up fast. Consider a taxi or a ride-share service, which costs roughly EUR 15 from Marbella centre to Banús. If you are staying in a hotel in Banús, walk to the marina, it takes 10 minutes. Marbella Marina has more parking, and it is free after 8pm. Cabopino has a small car park, but it is usually full, so arrive early. Estepona and Sotogrande have ample parking, but they are further from the main fireworks. If you are coming from Malaga or Gibraltar, allow an hour for the drive. Your skipper will send you the exact meeting point and a map after you book. Do not rely on phone navigation, as the marina layout can be confusing at night.

Booking Two Boats for a Large Group

If your group exceeds the capacity of one boat, book two boats and anchor them side by side. This works for corporate events, extended families, or large friend groups. Contact the owners through the platform and ask them to coordinate. The skippers can communicate by radio to keep the boats close, within 10 to 20 metres. You can move between boats if the sea is calm, but it is not recommended after dark. Each boat will have its own skipper, catering, and entertainment, so you need to plan the logistics. For example, one boat can have the DJ and the dance floor, while the other has the buffet and the bar. You can also book a tender boat to shuttle guests between the boats, but that adds around EUR 200 to EUR 400. The total cost for two boats is roughly double the single boat price, but you get twice the space and a more memorable experience. Check the BoatHire24 blog for tips on coordinating multi-boat charters.

Last-Minute Bookings and Availability

New Year's Eve is the busiest night of the year for yacht charters in Marbella. Most boats are booked by mid-November. If you are reading this in December, you still have options, but they are limited. Check the search page daily, as cancellations happen. Some owners release last-minute slots at a discount, typically 10-20% off, but you have to be flexible on the boat type and the port. For example, a 14-metre motor yacht might be available if someone cancels a week before. You can also contact owners directly through the platform and ask about availability. Be prepared to pay the full balance upfront for last-minute bookings, as owners want a guarantee. If you cannot find a boat, consider a daytime charter on 31 December or 1 January, which is cheaper and less crowded. Daytime charters from 10am to 4pm cost around EUR 800 to EUR 1,500 for a motor yacht, and you get a different view of the coast without the fireworks pressure.

What You Get With Private Yacht Hire Marbella Sunset

A private yacht hire Marbella sunset booking means the boat is yours for the evening. No sharing with other groups. You choose the route, the drinks, the music. The skipper handles the rest. Typical trips last three to four hours, leaving port about an hour before sunset. You cruise along the coast, anchor in a quiet bay like Cala del Faro or near the Marbella coastline, and watch the sky turn orange and pink. Some yachts come with a sound system, a sun deck, and a small galley for preparing food or chilling drinks.

The price depends on the boat size, the season, and the extras you want. For a standard motor yacht or catamaran, expect from around EUR 450 to EUR 900 for a three-hour sunset charter. Larger yachts with crew and catering start at EUR 1,500 and go up from there. You can add a private chef, a photographer, or a bottle of cava. The skipper will point out landmarks like the Río Verde estuary or the lights of Estepona old town as you sail.

Departure Ports for Your Sunset Cruise

You have six main ports to choose from. Puerto Banús is the most popular for private yacht hire Marbella sunset trips. It is the glitzy marina with superyachts, designer shops, and restaurants. From here you are minutes from the open sea and the best sunset angles. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and closer to the town centre. Cabopino offers a more relaxed vibe with a sandy beach and fewer crowds. Estepona marina is smaller but charming, with views of the Sierra Bermeja. Sotogrande is further west, near the Gibraltar Strait, where you might see dolphins. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near the port with the marina and the cable car.

Each port has its own character. If you want a lively start with bars and people-watching, pick Puerto Banús. If you prefer a low-key departure with free parking, try Cabopino or Estepona. The skipper will adjust the route to suit the departure point. For example, from Puerto Banús you can head towards the Marbella coastline or out towards the open water for a panoramic sunset. From Estepona, you can cruise past the old town and the fishing harbour.

Boat Options: Motor Yachts, Catamarans, Sailing Yachts

Private yacht hire Marbella sunset covers several boat types. Motor yachts are the most common for sunset cruises. They are fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space. A 10 to 15-metre motor yacht sleeps 6 to 12 guests comfortably, with a flybridge for panoramic views. Catamarans are wider and more stable, with a large trampoline at the front for lounging. They are ideal if you want to stand up and move around without feeling the roll. Sailing yachts are quieter and more romantic, but slower. You feel the wind and the sea more. They work well if you want a longer, more relaxed sunset trip.

RIBs and speedboats are cheaper but less comfortable for a sunset cruise. They are faster and more exposed, so you feel the wind and spray. They are better for a quick trip to a nearby beach club or a short sunset spin. Fishing boats are available but not typical for sunset. Licence-free day boats are an option if you want to drive yourself, but for a sunset cruise with drinks and relaxation, a skipper is worth the extra cost. Superyachts are available for larger groups or special occasions, with prices on request.

Pricing Guidance for Private Yacht Hire Marbella Sunset

Prices for private yacht hire Marbella sunset vary by season, boat size, and extras. In low season (November to March), you can find motor yachts from around EUR 450 for three hours. In high season (June to September), the same boat might cost EUR 700 to EUR 1,200. Catamarans start from EUR 600 in low season and EUR 900 in high season. Sailing yachts are usually cheaper, from EUR 400 to EUR 800. Larger yachts with crew, catering, and premium drinks start at EUR 1,500 and can reach EUR 5,000 or more for a superyacht.

Extras include a private chef (around EUR 200 extra), a photographer (EUR 150), or a bottle of champagne (EUR 50 to EUR 100). Some operators include soft drinks and water in the base price. Always confirm what is included before booking. Fuel is usually extra and depends on the distance you cover. A typical sunset cruise covers 10 to 15 nautical miles, which adds EUR 50 to EUR 150 to the total. The skipper will advise on the best route to keep fuel costs reasonable.

Best Season for a Sunset Cruise

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, so you can book private yacht hire Marbella sunset almost any month. The best sunset conditions are from May to October, when the sun sets later (around 20:30 to 21:30) and the sea temperature is warmer. July and August are the hottest months, with air temperatures around 30 degrees C and sea temperatures around 24 degrees C. Evening breezes keep things comfortable on the water. April and November are cooler but still pleasant, with sunsets around 19:00 to 20:00. December to February are the coldest months, with sea temperatures dropping to 15 degrees C and shorter days. You can still do a sunset cruise, but bring a jacket.

Weather is generally reliable, but the wind can pick up in the afternoon. The skipper will check the forecast and may suggest an earlier or later departure if needed. If the wind is too strong, you might switch to a sheltered bay or a different route. Most operators have a flexible cancellation policy for weather-related issues.

How to Book Private Yacht Hire Marbella Sunset

Booking through BoatHire24's search is straightforward. Enter your preferred date, port, and group size. The system shows available boats with prices and photos. You can filter by boat type, price range, and extras. Once you select a boat, you book online with a deposit (usually 30% to 50%). The balance is paid on the day of the cruise, either in cash or by card. The operator will confirm the departure time based on the sunset time for that date.

You can also contact the team for a custom quote. If you want a specific boat or a special occasion like a proposal, let them know in advance. They can arrange decorations, a cake, or a photographer. For larger groups or corporate events, they can recommend a superyacht or a catamaran with full catering.

Who Is This For

Private yacht hire Marbella sunset is for couples, small groups of friends, or families who want a private evening on the water. It is popular for romantic occasions like anniversaries, proposals, or honeymoons. It also works for birthday celebrations, small wedding parties, or a quiet evening with friends. You do not need any boating experience. The skipper takes care of everything. If you are visiting Marbella for a holiday, this is a memorable way to see the coast from the water.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared sunset cruise for a lower price. Those are available from around EUR 60 per person, but they are not private. For the full experience, private hire gives you control over the itinerary, the music, and the company.

What to Bring and Expect

Bring sunscreen, a light jacket or sweater (evening can be cooler on the water), sunglasses, and a camera. Most yachts have a toilet and a small changing area. You can bring your own food and drink, or order catering through the operator. Some boats have a fridge and ice. The skipper will provide a safety briefing at the start. The cruise is smooth in calm conditions, but if you are prone to seasickness, take a pill an hour before departure. The boat will anchor in a sheltered spot for the sunset, so you are not moving much during the main event.

The skipper will point out landmarks and marine life. In the summer, you might see dolphins near the Strait of Gibraltar or turtles near Cabopino. The sunset itself is the star. The colours reflect off the water and the mountains, creating a backdrop for photos. The trip ends with a slow cruise back to port, often with the city lights twinkling in the distance.

Local Highlights Along the Route

Depending on your departure port, the route might pass Puerto Banús with its superyachts and luxury cars, the Marbella coastline with the old town and the castle, or the Cala del Faro lighthouse near Estepona. From Estepona, you can see the old town with its flower-filled streets. From Cabopino, you get views of the dunes and the natural park. The Nerja caves are too far east for a sunset cruise, but you can see the mountains of the Sierra Nevada on a clear day.

The Strait of Gibraltar is a popular area for dolphin watching, but it is a longer trip. Most sunset cruises stay closer to the coast, within 5 to 10 nautical miles of the port. The skipper will choose a route that balances scenery, comfort, and fuel cost.

Frequently Asked Questions

For more tips, check the BoatHire24 blog for guides on sunset cruises, boat types, and local ports.

Sunset Cruise Routes: What You Actually See

The route for your private yacht hire Marbella sunset depends on the departure port and the skipper's local knowledge. From Puerto Banús, a common route heads west towards the Marbella coastline, passing the Rio Verde estuary and the golden sands of the Marbella beachfront. You will see the La Concha mountain behind the town, turning purple as the sun drops. Some skippers head east towards Cabopino, where the dunes and the marina create a different backdrop. From Estepona, the route often goes past the old town and the fishing harbour, with the Sierra Bermeja behind it. The Cala del Faro lighthouse is a popular photo stop, with the sun setting behind it in late summer.

If you want to see dolphins, ask the skipper to head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. That adds about 30 minutes each way, so you need a longer charter of four to five hours. The dolphins are common from May to October, and you often see them playing in the bow wake. The skipper will slow down or stop if they are nearby, giving you a chance to take photos. For a shorter trip, the coast near Cabopino or the Marbella coastline has plenty of scenery without the extra distance.

What to Expect on Board: Amenities and Comfort

A typical motor yacht for private yacht hire Marbella sunset has a flybridge with seating and a sun deck, a shaded cockpit with a table and chairs, and a small cabin with a toilet and a sink. The flybridge gives you the best views of the sunset, with no obstructions. The cockpit is better if you want to eat or sit in the shade. The sun deck at the front is for lounging, but it can be hot in the afternoon. Most yachts have a sound system with Bluetooth, so you can play your own music. Some have a fridge and ice for drinks, and a small galley for preparing snacks.

Catamarans have more space. The trampoline at the front is a popular spot for lying down and watching the sky. The cockpit is larger, with a table for six to twelve people. Sailing yachts have less deck space but more atmosphere. You can help the skipper hoist the sails if you want, or just relax in the cockpit. The skipper will provide life jackets and a safety briefing. If you have children, ask about child-sized life jackets. Most boats have them, but check in advance.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group

For a romantic couple's sunset, a 10-metre motor yacht or a small sailing yacht is ideal. You get privacy and intimacy, with enough space for two to four people. For a group of six to eight friends, a 12 to 15-metre catamaran or motor yacht works well. The catamaran's wide deck means everyone can sit or stand without feeling cramped. For a family with children, a motor yacht with a flybridge is safer because the kids can stay in the cockpit. For a party or celebration, a larger motor yacht with a sound system and a grill is better. Superyachts are for groups of ten or more, with a crew of two or three, and include catering and drinks.

The skipper will ask about your group size and preferences before departure. If you want to swim, choose a boat with a swim platform or a ladder. Most motor yachts have a platform at the back. Catamarans have a ladder from the trampoline. If you want to anchor in a bay and swim, the water is usually calm in the evening, around 22 to 24 degrees C in summer. The skipper will choose a sheltered spot like Cala del Faro or near the Marbella coastline.

Extras That Make the Cruise Special

You can add extras to your private yacht hire Marbella sunset to tailor the experience. A private chef costs around EUR 200 and prepares a three-course meal on board, using local ingredients like seafood, Iberian ham, and Spanish cheeses. The chef works in the galley and serves the food on the cockpit table. A photographer costs around EUR 150 and takes candid shots of the sunset, the group, and the boat. You get the digital files after the trip. A bottle of cava or champagne costs EUR 50 to EUR 100, depending on the brand. Some operators offer a premium package with a selection of wines, beers, and soft drinks.

For a proposal, the operator can arrange decorations like flowers, banners, or a sign. They can also coordinate with the skipper to anchor at a specific spot for the proposal. The photographer can capture the moment discreetly. For a birthday, you can bring a cake or order one through the operator. Some yachts have a speaker system for music, but you can also bring a portable speaker for a smaller boat.

Weather and Wind: What to Know Before You Go

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and hot summers. The best time for a sunset cruise is from May to October, when the wind is lighter and the sea is calmer. In July and August, the afternoon wind, known as the Poniente, often picks up around 14:00 to 16:00 and dies down in the evening. The skipper will time the departure to avoid the strongest wind. In September and October, the wind is lighter, and the sunsets are more dramatic with longer golden hours. In winter, the wind can be stronger, especially in the strait. The skipper will check the forecast and may suggest a different route or a shorter trip if conditions are marginal.

If the wind is too strong for comfort, the skipper can anchor in a sheltered bay like Cala del Faro or near the Marbella coastline. The boat will rock less, and you can still enjoy the sunset. Most operators have a weather policy that allows you to reschedule or cancel with a full refund if the forecast is poor. Check the policy before booking. For a private yacht hire Marbella sunset, the skipper will always prioritise safety and comfort.

Dining Options: Eat On Board or at a Beach Club

You can eat on board during your private yacht hire Marbella sunset, or stop at a beach club for dinner. Eating on board is more private and flexible. You can bring your own food and drink, or order catering through the operator. A typical catering option includes a selection of tapas, a main course like grilled fish or paella, and dessert. The chef prepares everything on board and serves it on the cockpit table. If you prefer to eat at a beach club, some operators can arrange a stop at a club like the Marbella Club or the Puente Romano beach club. You anchor offshore and take a tender to the club. This adds about an hour to the trip and costs extra for the tender and the club booking.

For a more casual option, you can bring a picnic and eat on the boat. Most yachts have a fridge and a table. The skipper can provide plates, glasses, and cutlery. If you want to barbecue, some yachts have a grill on the flybridge. Check with the operator before booking. For a romantic dinner, a private chef on board is the best option. For a group, a beach club stop is more social.

How to Get the Best Price for Your Sunset Cruise

To get the best price for private yacht hire Marbella sunset, book in advance and avoid peak dates. July and August are the most expensive months, with prices up to 30% higher than in May or September. Book at least two weeks in advance to secure a good boat at a reasonable price. If you are flexible on the date, ask the operator for a last-minute deal. Some operators offer discounts for bookings within 48 hours if the boat is still available. You can also save by choosing a smaller boat or a less popular port like Cabopino or Estepona instead of Puerto Banús.

Another way to save is to share the cost with a group. A 12-metre motor yacht for eight people costs around EUR 800, which is EUR 100 per person. That is cheaper than a shared sunset cruise, which costs around EUR 60 to EUR 80 per person but with strangers. For a couple, a smaller boat for EUR 450 is better value. Always confirm the fuel cost and any extras before booking. The base price often excludes fuel, so ask for a total estimate.

What to Do After the Cruise

After your private yacht hire Marbella sunset, you are back at the port around 21:00 to 22:00, depending on the season. In Puerto Banús, you can walk to the restaurants and bars along the marina. The atmosphere is lively, with people dining on the terraces. In Marbella Marina, you are close to the old town, with its narrow streets and tapas bars. In Estepona, the old town is a short walk from the marina, with flower-filled balconies and quiet squares. In Cabopino, there are a few beachfront restaurants and a chiringuito (beach bar) for a casual drink.

If you want to continue the evening, some operators can arrange a transfer to a restaurant or a club. You can also book a dinner cruise that includes a meal on board and a return to port later in the evening. For a romantic night, consider staying at a hotel near the port, like the Marbella Club or the Puente Romano, and walking back after the cruise.

bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Birthday Catamaran Charter

A catamaran gives you space. Unlike a monohull, the deck is wide and stable, so guests can walk around without holding on. Most catamarans on BoatHire24 have a large trampoline net at the bow, a flybridge with seating, and a saloon with a fridge and ice maker. You get a Bluetooth speaker system, a toilet (sometimes two), and a shaded area for when the sun gets too much. The skipper handles the navigation, anchoring, and safety. You handle the party.

Typical extras include a stand-up paddleboard, snorkelling gear, and a dinghy for getting to shore. Some boats have a barbecue grill on the back. If you want a catered meal, you can arrange that through the charter company or bring your own food. Drinks are usually BYO, but some charters offer a bar package. Check the listing details before you book.

Which Port to Leave From

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice if you want the glamour factor. Your guests arrive at the marina with the superyachts and the designer shops. The departure is quick, and within 10 minutes you are past the breakwater and heading toward the Cala del Faro or the coast of Marbella. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and cheaper for parking. Cabopino is smaller but closer to the sand dunes and the nudist beach. Estepona gives you the old town backdrop and the chance to see dolphins off the Strait of Gibraltar. Sotogrande is for a more exclusive, low-key vibe. Benalmádena is further east but offers a long coastline and the marina with the Sea Life centre.

If your group is based in Marbella, Puerto Banús is the most convenient. For a longer day trip, leaving from Estepona or Sotogrande gives you more open water and less traffic. Check the BoatHire24 search for catamarans available at your preferred port.

Boat Sizes and Capacities

Birthday groups vary. For a small gathering of 6 to 8 people, a 38-foot catamaran works fine. You get a saloon, a forward cabin for changing, and a decent sundeck. For 10 to 14 guests, look at 45 to 50 feet. These have a flybridge with extra seating and a larger trampoline. For 16 to 20 people, you need a 55-foot-plus catamaran with a professional crew (skipper plus hostess). The largest catamarans on BoatHire24 can take up to 30 guests, but those are more for events than intimate birthdays.

Capacity limits are strict. The licence of the boat determines the maximum number of passengers, and the skipper will enforce it. If you book for 12 people, you cannot bring 14. The boat will not leave the dock. Be honest about your numbers when you book.

Pricing Guidance for a Birthday Charter

A half-day charter (4 hours) for a 40-foot catamaran starts from around EUR 800 in low season. A full day (8 hours) is from EUR 1,500. Sunset cruises (2 to 3 hours) are cheaper, from EUR 500. High season (June to September) pushes prices up by 20 to 30 percent. The price includes the skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. It does not include food, drinks, or a hostess. If you want a hostess to serve drinks and cut the cake, add EUR 150 to 250 for the day.

For a birthday, you might want to book a full day so you can anchor for lunch, swim, and then cruise back for sunset. That costs around EUR 1,500 to 2,500 for a good catamaran. Superyacht catamarans with a crew of three cost more, price on request. Always ask about the cancellation policy before you pay a deposit. Some companies offer free cancellation up to 14 days before, others are stricter.

Best Time of Year for a Birthday on the Water

The Costa del Sol has 320 sunny days a year, so you can celebrate your birthday on a catamaran in any month. May, June, September, and October are the sweet spots: air temperature 24 to 28 degrees C, water temperature 18 to 22 degrees C, and fewer crowds than July and August. July and August are hot (30 to 35 degrees C) but the water is warm (24 to 26 degrees C) and the evenings are long. The wind is light in summer, so the sea is flat. Winter months (November to February) are cooler, 15 to 20 degrees C, but you can still have a pleasant cruise if you pick a sunny day and bring jackets. The water is colder, so swimming is less appealing.

If your birthday falls in March or April, you can still charter a catamaran, but the sea can be choppy if the wind picks up. Check the forecast and choose a sheltered route along the coast. The BoatHire24 blog has a guide to the best months for boat hire on the Costa del Sol.

What to Bring and What to Leave

Bring sunscreen, a towel, a hat, and sunglasses. Bring a change of clothes if you plan to swim. Bring your own drinks in a cooler bag (the boat has ice). Bring food that is easy to eat, like wraps, sandwiches, fruit, and cake. Do not bring glass bottles on most boats, the skipper will ask you to transfer drinks into plastic cups. Do not bring red wine or anything that stains. Do not bring a sound system, the boat has one. Do not bring a large cake that needs refrigeration unless you clear it with the charter company first.

For decorations, you can bring balloons and banners, but check with the skipper. Some boats have a no-confetti rule because it gets into the deck drains. You can bring a small Bluetooth speaker if the boat's system is not good enough, but most catamarans have decent sound.

How to Book a Birthday Catamaran on BoatHire24

Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter Marbella as the destination. Filter by catamaran and select the number of guests. Look at the listings and read the details: maximum capacity, included equipment, and the skipper's language. Most skippers speak Spanish and English. Some speak German and French. Contact the charter company through the BoatHire24 messaging system to confirm availability for your date. Ask about the birthday package if they have one. Some companies offer a bottle of cava and a fruit platter as a standard extra.

Once you agree on the price and the itinerary, you pay a deposit (usually 50 percent) and the rest on the day. The skipper will meet you at the marina 15 minutes before departure. They will do a safety briefing and then you are off. No licence required, you are just a passenger.

Who Is This For

Catamaran hire Marbella for a birthday works for groups of friends, family celebrations, milestone birthdays (18th, 21st, 30th, 40th, 50th), and even children's birthdays if the boat allows children (most do). It is not ideal for a surprise party because the logistics are harder to hide. It is also not great for someone who gets seasick easily, though catamarans are more stable than monohulls. If you have guests with mobility issues, check if the boat has a boarding platform and a wide gangway. Most catamarans have a low freeboard, so boarding is easier than on a motor yacht.

For a bachelorette or bachelor party, a catamaran is a solid choice. You get privacy, a DJ (if you bring your own playlist), and a backdrop of the coast. Just keep the noise reasonable after 10pm if you are near the marina. The skipper will remind you.

Suggested Itinerary for a Birthday Day Out

A typical full-day itinerary from Puerto Banús: leave at 10am, head east toward Marbella, pass the Marbella Club and Puente Romano, anchor off the beach at El Faro for a swim. Lunch on the boat at 1pm. Then cruise west toward the cliffs of Cabopino, stop for another swim, and return to port around 6pm. For a sunset cruise, leave at 5pm, anchor off the coast of San Pedro Alcántara, watch the sun go down behind La Concha mountain, and return by 8pm. You can also go further west to Estepona and see the old town from the water, or east to the Río Verde estuary where the flamingos sometimes hang out.

If you want to see dolphins, the Strait of Gibraltar is a 30-minute drive from Marbella, but you need a full-day charter from Estepona or Sotogrande to get there. The dolphins are common from April to October. Not guaranteed, but likely.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Do not book a catamaran that is too small for your group. A 38-foot catamaran with 12 people feels cramped. Go bigger. Do not forget to check the cancellation policy. Some companies refund only if you cancel 30 days in advance. Do not assume the skipper will organise food and drink. You need to bring it or order it separately. Do not arrive late. The skipper will wait 15 minutes, then charge you for the waiting time or cancel the trip. Do not bring high heels on board. They damage the teak deck. Barefoot or flat shoes only.

Do not expect the skipper to be a party host. They drive the boat and ensure safety. They will not serve drinks or cut the cake unless you pay for a hostess. If you want a fully catered party, book a catamaran that includes a hostess or a chef.

Why Use BoatHire24

BoatHire24 lists only boats that are licensed and insured. We verify the skippers. You book directly with the charter company, no middleman markups. The search filters let you find catamarans by size, price, and port. You can compare multiple options without calling around. If you have questions, the contact page has a form. We do not take a commission from the charter price, so the price you see is the price the company charges. That is rare in the boat rental industry.

For a birthday, you want reliability. You do not want the boat to break down or the skipper to cancel at the last minute. Our listings are from established companies with multiple boats and good reviews. Check the reviews on each listing. If a company has no reviews, ask for references. We also have a blog with tips on planning a boat party on the Costa del Sol.

Birthday Catering Options: What Works on a Catamaran

You can bring your own food, but for a birthday you might want something more organised. Local caterers in Marbella and Puerto Banús deliver to the marina. A typical platter for 10 people costs around EUR 150 to 250: cured meats, Spanish cheeses, olives, bread, and fruit. For a hot meal, some companies offer a paella cooked on board, from around EUR 30 per person. Cake is easy: a simple sponge or cheesecake travels well. Avoid cream cakes with whipped topping that melts in 10 minutes. If you want a barbecue, check the boat has a gas grill. Not all do. You can also book a restaurant stop: anchor off the Chiringuito El Caballo in Cabopino and they bring food to the boat by dinghy. That costs around EUR 40 per person for a set menu.

Puerto Banús Birthday Departure: The Practical Details

If you leave from Puerto Banús, your guests need to find parking. The marina car park costs around EUR 30 for the day. There is a cheaper public car park 200 metres away at the end of Avenida de la Marina, about EUR 15 for 8 hours. The meeting point is usually at the petrol station inside the marina or at the main entrance by the Casino. The skipper will give you the exact berth number the day before. Arrive 20 minutes early so everyone can use the marina toilets before boarding. The catamaran toilet is fine, but the holding tank fills up quickly with a big group.

Weather Contingency Plan for a Birthday Charter

The Costa del Sol is reliable, but Levante wind can blow from the east and create choppy seas. If the forecast shows wind over 20 knots, the skipper may suggest an alternative route or a later departure. You have three options: reschedule, cancel (check the policy), or take a sheltered route along the coast from Puerto Banús to Cabopino, which is protected by the cliffs. In rare cases of heavy rain, the charter company may cancel and refund your deposit. Ask about the weather policy before you book. Most companies offer a free reschedule if the forecast is bad 48 hours before.

Birthday on a Budget: How to Save Money

title: Speedboat Hire Benalmadena No Licence – Quick Booking
metaDescription: Book speedboat hire Benalmadena no licence needed. Drive a RIB up to 15m without a permit. Instant online booking, Puerto Marina departure. Start today.
h1: Speedboat Hire Benalmadena No Licence, Book Online
intro:
You want to drive a speedboat along the Costa del Sol, but you don't have a boating licence. That's fine. In Spain, you can operate a motorboat up to 15 metres in length without any permit, as long as the engine power stays under 11.03 kW (15 hp) for inland waters or you stick to the specific licence-exempt categories for coastal navigation. At BoatHire24, we list dozens of RIBs, little day boats, and compact speedboats in Benalmadena that you can take out yourself, no paperwork required.

Benalmadena's Puerto Marina is one of the best spots for this. Sheltered waters, easy access to the open sea, and the marina itself is a tourist attraction with bars, shops, and a sea-life centre. You can hire a 4.5-metre RIB with a 15hp outboard for a couple of hours, buzz around the coast, anchor off a quiet cove, and be back in time for a late lunch. The whole process takes five minutes online.
bodyHtml:
What Does No Licence Mean in Practice

Spanish regulations divide recreational boats into categories. For a boat under 6 metres and with an engine of 15 hp or less, no licence is required for navigation within 2 nautical miles of the coast. That covers most small RIBs and day boats we list. If you want something bigger, say a 6.5-metre RIB with a 60hp engine, you need a PNB (Patrón de Navegación Básica) licence. But for the true no-licence hire, you stick to the small stuff. All our listings clearly state the licence requirement, so you won't get caught out.

Benalmadena: The Port and Its Advantages

Puerto Marina Benalmadena is a purpose-built leisure marina with over 900 berths. It's a 15-minute drive from Malaga airport, 10 minutes from Torremolinos. The marina has a protected inner basin, which means calm water even when the Mediterranean kicks up a chop further out. You can launch from the dedicated slipway, head west towards Fuengirola or east towards Malaga city. The coastline is a mix of sandy beaches, rocky cliffs, and the odd urban development. For a no-licence speedboat, you stay within the 2-mile zone, which gives you plenty of options. Cala del Moral, a small cove just east of the marina, is a popular anchorage. Water temperature in summer hits 24-26 degrees C.

Types of Boats Available for No-Licence Hire

We categorise our fleet by type. For no-licence hire, you are looking at RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) and small day boats. RIBs are the most common: a fibreglass hull with inflatable tubes, very stable, easy to handle, and they plane quickly. Typical sizes are 4.5 to 5.5 metres. Engines are 15hp four-stroke outboards, which push the boat to about 15 knots. Some operators offer electric outboards, quieter and cheaper on fuel. Day boats are more like small motor cruisers with a cuddy cabin, but still under the licence threshold. They are slower but more comfortable. Fishing boats with a 15hp engine also qualify. You can see the full range on our search page.

Pricing: What You Actually Pay

Expect to pay from around EUR 80 for a two-hour hire of a 4.5-metre RIB in low season (October to May). High season (June to September) pushes that to EUR 120-150 for the same boat. Half-day (4 hours) is typically EUR 180-250. Full-day (8 hours) EUR 300-450. Fuel is usually extra, but for a 15hp engine running at cruising speed, you burn about 5-8 litres per hour. At EUR 1.50 per litre, that's negligible. Some operators include a full tank and ask you to refill on return. Check the listing details. Deposit: most require a credit card hold of EUR 200-500. You get it back if you don't crash into the marina wall. Price on request for boats over 6 metres with a skipper included, but that's a different story.

What's Included in the Hire

Standard inclusions: the boat, life jackets for all passengers (mandatory by law), a basic safety briefing (5-10 minutes), and a VHF radio or mobile phone for emergencies. Some operators throw in a cooler with ice, a snorkel mask, and a map of the coast. You do not get a skipper, obviously, because you are driving. You do not get insurance for damage to the boat (you pay for repairs if you hit something). Third-party liability insurance is included by law. Check if the operator offers a damage waiver for an extra fee, typically EUR 30-50. That caps your liability at a few hundred euros. We recommend it if you are a first-timer.

Seasons: When to Go

Benalmadena has a Mediterranean climate. The best months for no-licence speedboat hire are May through October. Air temperature 22-30 degrees C, water 18-26 degrees C. July and August are peak, with lots of tourists and crowded anchorages. If you want quiet, go in June or September. Winter (November to March) is cooler (15-20 degrees C) and windier. The Poniente wind (west) can create choppy seas. Some operators still run, but you should check the forecast and be prepared for rougher conditions. Spring (April) is a good compromise: warm enough, fewer people, and the sea is usually calm in the morning.

How to Book: The Quick Way

Go to our BoatHire24 homepage, select Benalmadena as the port, filter by 'No Licence Required' under boat type. You will see available dates and times. Choose a slot, enter your details, pay a deposit (usually 30-50% of the total), and get a confirmation email with the operator's contact and meeting point. Show up at the marina 15 minutes before your slot. The operator will hand you the keys (literally) and give you a quick run-through. That's it. No test, no theory, just drive. We do not charge booking fees. Cancellation policies vary by operator, but most offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before. Check the terms on the listing.

Who Is This For

This is for tourists who want a taste of boating without the commitment of a licence course. Couples, small families (kids over 5, usually), groups of friends. You do not need any prior experience, but you should be comfortable with basic controls: throttle, steering, and stopping. The boats are simple. If you can drive a car, you can drive these. Also for locals who want a cheap afternoon on the water without the hassle of owning a boat. If you want to fish, some operators allow it (bring your own rod). If you want to party, a RIB is not the best choice, but a small day boat with a stereo works. Read our blog for tips on anchoring and safety.

Safety Rules You Must Follow

Spanish law requires you to stay within 2 nautical miles of the coast. That means you can see the beach clearly. No crossing to Africa. No going out in fog or heavy wind. The operator will check the weather and may cancel if it's dangerous. You must wear life jackets at all times when the engine is running. No drinking alcohol while driving (0.0 limit). The Guardia Civil do random checks. If you are caught over the limit, you face a fine of up to EUR 5000 and a ban from boating. Also, you must have a valid ID or passport with you. The boat's registration papers and insurance must be on board. The operator gives you a folder with these. Keep it dry.

Local Highlights You Can Reach

From Benalmadena, you can cruise east to the Cabopino marina (about 4 NM) and see the art deco houses of Torremolinos from the water. Westwards, you can reach Fuengirola castle (7 NM) or anchor off the beach at La Cala de Mijas. The water is clear, visibility up to 15 metres on a calm day. You might see dolphins, especially in the morning. If you go further west (but still within 2 miles), you can see the Sierra de Mijas mountains behind the coast. The Strait of Gibraltar is too far for a no-licence boat, but you can see the African coast on a clear day from the higher ground. For a longer trip, consider a licence-required boat or a charter with a skipper. But for a quick blast, Benalmadena is ideal.

What to Bring

Sunscreen (SPF 50), a hat, sunglasses with a strap, a towel, a change of clothes (you will get wet), a waterproof phone case, and a bottle of water. The boat has a small storage compartment for valuables, but it's not waterproof. Leave your passport in the marina locker if you can. A camera for the views. Snorkel gear if you want (some operators provide it). A light jacket even in summer, because the wind on the water can feel cool. No glass bottles on board (safety). No high heels (they damage the deck). The operator may provide a Bluetooth speaker, or bring your own.

Comparing Benalmadena with Other No-Licence Ports

Benalmadena is not your only option on the Costa del Sol. Puerto Banús, 20 minutes west, offers no-licence hire but at higher prices, from around EUR 150 for two hours. The marina is flashier, with superyachts and designer shops, but the water is equally calm. Cabopino, east of Marbella, is quieter and cheaper, from EUR 70 for two hours, but it has fewer operators and less choice of boats. Estepona, further west, has a new marina and similar pricing to Cabopino, but the coast is more open and windier. Sotogrande is mostly for bigger boats and licenced skippers. Benalmadena wins on convenience: it is closer to the airport, has more operators, and the protected basin means you can launch in almost any weather. Check our search page to compare availability across ports.

Fuel Costs and Range: How Far Can You Go

A 15hp four-stroke outboard burns about 5 litres per hour at 10 knots cruising speed. That gives you a range of roughly 40 nautical miles on a full 20-litre tank, which is more than enough for a half-day hire. In practice, you will not go that far because you stay within 2 miles of the coast. From Benalmadena marina, you can reach Fuengirola (7 NM east) and back on less than 5 litres. If you head west to Cabopino (4 NM), you use under 3 litres. Fuel cost for a typical two-hour trip is around EUR 10-15. Some operators charge a flat fuel fee of EUR 20-30, which is simpler. Always ask if fuel is included or extra before you book. If you run out, you call the operator and they bring a spare can, but that costs time and embarrassment.

What Happens If the Weather Turns Bad

Spanish summer weather is stable, but the Levanter wind (east) can kick up in the afternoon, creating short, steep waves. If you are out and the wind picks up above 15 knots, head back to the marina immediately. The operator will have given you a VHF channel or phone number to call for advice. If the forecast is bad before your slot, the operator will cancel and give you a full refund or reschedule. Do not argue with them. A 4.5-metre RIB in 2-metre waves is not fun and can be dangerous. Winter is more unpredictable: the Poniente wind (west) can blow for days. Check windguru or the operator's own forecast before you set off. If you are unsure, stick to the inner basin of the marina for a slow putter around the pontoons. It is not exciting, but it is safe.

Booking Direct vs Through BoatHire24

You can walk up to a booth at Puerto Marina Benalmadena and book a boat on the spot. The price might be similar, but you have no guarantee of availability, no online cancellation policy, and no recourse if the boat breaks down. Booking through BoatHire24 gives you a written confirmation, a clear list of inclusions, and a standardised cancellation policy (usually free up to 48 hours). You also get to compare operators side by side. Some operators on the marina are not listed with us because they do not meet our standards for safety or transparency. We vet our partners. If you book direct, you might get a cheaper last-minute deal, but you take the risk. For a quick no-licence hire, the peace of mind is worth the small premium.

What to Do If You Have Never Driven a Boat Before

Do not panic. The controls are simple: a throttle lever (forward, neutral, reverse) and a steering wheel or tiller. The operator will explain the basics: start the engine, check the kill cord is attached to your leg, untie the mooring lines, push off gently, and idle out of the marina. Once clear, open the throttle gradually. The boat will plane at about 10 knots. Steer like a car, but remember the boat turns from the stern, so you need to anticipate. Practice turning in open water away from other boats. To stop, pull the throttle back to neutral and let the boat slow down. Do not slam into reverse at speed. The operator will give you a short demonstration. If you still feel unsure, ask for a longer briefing or a supervised first 10 minutes. Most operators are happy to help.

Local Spots for Anchoring and Swimming

Within 2 miles of Benalmadena, you have several good anchorages. Cala del Moral, just east of the marina, is a small pebble beach with clear water. Drop anchor in 3-5 metres depth and swim ashore. Watch out for rocks near the shore. Playa de la Viborilla, east of Torremolinos, is quieter but has a sandy bottom. Westwards, the beach at La Cala de Mijas has a long stretch of sand and a few beach bars. You can anchor off and paddle in. Avoid anchoring near the shipping lanes or the entrance to marinas. The seafloor is mostly sand or seagrass, which is fine for a Danforth anchor. If the wind is light, you can also just drift. Always keep an eye on your anchor line and other boats.

Insurance and Liability: What You Need to Know

Third-party liability insurance is mandatory and included in the hire price. That covers damage to other boats, the marina, or swimmers. It does not cover damage to the boat you are driving. If you hit a rock or another boat, you pay for repairs. That can be expensive: a scratched gel coat costs EUR 200-500 to fix, a damaged propeller EUR 100-200, a torn tube on a RIB EUR 500-1000. Some operators offer a damage waiver for EUR 30-50, which reduces your liability to a fixed excess (usually EUR 300-500). We recommend buying it. If the operator does not offer one, you are fully liable. Read the terms on the listing. Also, your travel insurance might cover boat damage, but check the small print. Most exclude motorised watercraft.
