faqs.q: Do I need any experience to drive a no-licence speedboat in Benalmadena?
faqs.a: No. The operator gives a 5-10 minute briefing covering controls, safety, and the local area. If you can drive a car, you can handle a 4.5-metre RIB with a 15hp engine. Speed is limited to about 15 knots, so it's manageable.

faqs.q: What is the maximum number of people on a no-licence boat?
faqs.a: Most boats carry up to 6 passengers including the driver. The boat's capacity plate shows the exact number. For a 4.5-metre RIB, that's usually 4 adults plus 2 children. Overloading is illegal and dangerous.

faqs.q: Can I take the boat out at night?
faqs.a: No. No-licence hire is restricted to daylight hours only. You must return the boat before sunset. The operator will specify the exact return time, usually 8pm in summer, 6pm in winter.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather turns bad while I'm out?
faqs.a: Head back to the marina immediately. If you are unsure, call the operator on the VHF or mobile. They will guide you. Do not try to ride out a storm in a small boat. The deposit covers towing if needed.

faqs.q: Can I fish from the speedboat?
faqs.a: Yes, if the operator allows it. Most do, but you need your own fishing rod and a valid fishing permit for the Mediterranean (available online for about EUR 10). Spearfishing is not allowed from a rental boat.

faqs.q: Is there an age limit for driving?
faqs.a: You must be at least 18 years old with a valid driving licence or ID. Some operators set a minimum of 21. There is no upper age limit, but you should be physically able to operate the controls and handle the boat.

faqs.q: What is the cancellation policy?
faqs.a: Most operators offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before the booking. Within 48 hours, you may lose the deposit. If the operator cancels due to weather, you get a full refund or a reschedule. Check the specific listing's terms.

title: Luxury Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day – Exclusive
metaDescription: Book a luxury motor yacht charter Marbella day trip. Explore Puerto Banús, Costa del Sol. Skipper included. Instant online booking at BoatHire24.
h1: Luxury Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day
keyword: luxury motor yacht charter marbella day
intro:
You want a day on a luxury motor yacht in Marbella, and you want it sorted without the nonsense. A private charter with a licensed skipper, a gleaming motor yacht, and a route that takes you past Puerto Banús, the Marbella coastline, and maybe even a dolphin-spotting detour towards Estepona. That is exactly what BoatHire24 does. No hidden fees, no deckhand tipping confusion, just a boat and a captain for the day.

The standard day charter runs from 10am to 6pm, though you can tweak the hours. You get the yacht, the skipper, fuel for a reasonable itinerary, and all the onboard toys (snorkel gear, paddleboard, sometimes a jet ski). What you do not get is a floating nightclub or a booze cruise. This is a luxury motor yacht charter Marbella day experience for adults who want to swim, sunbathe, and eat grilled prawns at a cala, not a foam party.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Luxury Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Every charter at BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the wind patterns off La Concha, and the best anchor spots. The price covers the yacht, the skipper, fuel for a standard day itinerary (usually up to 40 nautical miles), and basic insurance. You also get a cooler with ice, towels, snorkelling masks, and a Bluetooth speaker. Some yachts throw in a stand-up paddleboard or a Seabob. What is not included: food and drinks (you bring your own or order catering through us), dockage fees if you decide to stop at a marina restaurant, and any extra fuel if you go on a long run to Marbella or Cabopino.

You are not paying per person. You charter the whole yacht for your group. That means you control the guest list, the music, and the itinerary. The skipper will suggest a route, but you can override it within reason. Want to spend three hours anchored off Cala del Faro instead of cruising to Benalmádena? No problem. The skipper works for you, not the marina.

Departure Ports for Your Day Charter

You can start your luxury motor yacht charter Marbella day from any of the main Costa del Sol ports. Puerto Banús is the most popular departure point, because it is the flashy one with the superyachts and the Gucci store. But you can also leave from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), which is closer to the old town and a bit quieter. Cabopino is a good option if you want to head east towards the Cala del Moral and the dunes. Estepona works for a westbound trip towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you often see dolphins. Sotogrande is further west, more exclusive, and good for a longer day trip. Benalmádena is east of Marbella and gives you quick access to the Málaga coastline.

Your skipper will meet you at the port 15 minutes before departure. You board, do a quick safety briefing, and cast off. The boat is fuelled and ready. No waiting around.

Boat Options for a Luxury Day Charter

We have motor yachts from 35 feet to over 80 feet. A 40-foot Azimut or a 50-foot Princess is the sweet spot for a group of 8 to 12. You get a flybridge with sun pads, a spacious saloon with air conditioning, a galley, a bow sunbathing area, and a swim platform at the stern. Larger yachts, like a 70-foot Ferretti or a 90-foot Sunseeker, come with a master cabin, a crew cabin, and more deck space. Those are for groups up to 20 or for clients who want a bit more luxury. Prices start from around EUR 2,500 for a 40-foot motor yacht for the day, and go up to EUR 8,000 or more for a 70-foot plus yacht. You can also charter a catamaran if you prefer stability and more deck space, but for speed and style, a motor yacht is the way to go.

All boats are fully equipped with safety gear, navigation electronics, and a sound system. You do not need to bring anything except swimwear, sunscreen, and a credit card for the deposit (usually EUR 500 to EUR 1,000, refunded after the charter).

Pricing Guidance for a Day Charter

Prices vary by boat size, season, and duration. A standard 8-hour day charter in June for a 40-foot motor yacht starts at around EUR 2,500. In August, the same boat might be EUR 3,200. A 60-foot yacht in high season can be EUR 5,500 to EUR 7,000. Superyachts over 80 feet are price on request, but expect EUR 10,000 plus. These prices include VAT and the skipper. You do not tip the skipper unless you want to, but it is not mandatory. Fuel is included for a standard day itinerary of up to 40 nautical miles. If you want to go to Nerja or Gibraltar, you pay extra fuel. The deposit covers potential damage; if you return the boat clean and undamaged, you get it back within 48 hours.

You can also book a half-day (4 hours) from around EUR 1,500 for a smaller motor yacht. But for a proper luxury motor yacht charter Marbella day, go for the full 8 hours. That gives you time to cruise, anchor, swim, eat, and cruise back without rushing.

Best Seasons for a Luxury Day Charter

The Costa del Sol has a long season. April to October is the sweet spot. In April and May, the water temperature is around 18-20 degrees C, and the air temperature is 22-25 degrees C. You will not get the scorching heat, but the sea is calm and the ports are less crowded. June and September are ideal: warm water (22-24 degrees C), long daylight hours, and fewer tourists than July and August. July and August are hot (30-35 degrees C air temperature) and busy, but the sea is warmest (25-26 degrees C). You will share the anchorages with more boats, but the atmosphere is lively. November to March is low season. You can still charter, but the weather is cooler (15-20 degrees C) and the sea can be choppy. Some boats are out of the water for maintenance. If you want a guaranteed sunny day with flat seas, book between June and September.

Wind is a factor. The Levante wind from the east can pick up in the afternoon, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar. Your skipper will know the sheltered spots, like the coves around Cabopino or the lee side of La Concha. Do not worry about sea sickness; modern motor yachts are stable, and the skipper will avoid rough areas.

How to Book Your Luxury Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter your date, group size, and port. You will see available yachts with photos, specs, and prices. Select a boat, choose your extras (catering, water toys, extra hours), and pay a 50% deposit online. The remaining 50% is due 14 days before the charter. You get a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and the meeting point. If you need to cancel, check the policy: full refund up to 30 days before, 50% refund up to 14 days before, no refund after that. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for summer dates, especially for larger yachts.

You can also call or email us if you want a bespoke itinerary. We can arrange a chef, a photographer, or a special celebration (birthday, anniversary, proposal). Just ask.

Who Is This Charter For

A luxury motor yacht charter Marbella day is for groups of friends, families with older children (the skipper can handle safety), couples, or corporate clients. It is not for stag or hen parties that want to get drunk and loud. The skipper has the right to refuse boarding if the group is intoxicated or aggressive. You are expected to behave like adults. The vibe is relaxed luxury: sunbathing, swimming, snorkelling, eating good food, and enjoying the view of the Marbella coastline and the Sierra Blanca mountains. If you want a party boat, look elsewhere. If you want a classy day on the water with a professional crew, this is it.

Children are welcome on most yachts, but you need to bring life jackets for kids under 12 (the boat has a few, but not in all sizes). The skipper will not let children operate the boat or swim unsupervised. That is your responsibility.

Local Highlights You Can Visit on Your Charter

Your skipper can take you to Cala del Faro, a small cove near Marbella with clear water and a beach bar. Or head to the Río Verde estuary, where you can see birds and maybe a glimpse of the Marbella Club. Puerto Banús is worth a slow cruise through to see the superyachts and the flash cars on the promenade. If you go west towards Estepona, you can anchor near the old town and walk up for lunch. Eastwards, Cabopino has a sandy beach and a dune reserve. Further east, the Nerja caves are a long run (about 30 nautical miles from Marbella), but doable if you have a fast motor yacht and want a full-day adventure. The Strait of Gibraltar is a 45-minute cruise from Estepona, and you almost always see dolphins and sometimes pilot whales.

Your skipper knows the best anchor spots for swimming, the quietest coves, and the restaurants that will send a water taxi to your boat. Ask for recommendations.

What to Bring and What to Wear

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe if possible), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the afternoon breeze. Shoes should be non-marking boat shoes or barefoot. High heels damage the deck. You can bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package through us (EUR 50-100 per person for a seafood platter, paella, and drinks). The boat has a fridge, a freezer, and a grill. You can also stop at a chiringuito on the beach for lunch. Alcohol is allowed, but do not get wasted. The skipper reserves the right to cut the charter short if anyone is dangerously drunk.

Cameras and phones are fine, but secure them when the boat is moving. The skipper will point out photo spots, like the view of La Concha from the sea or the entrance to Puerto Banús.

Frequently Asked Questions About Luxury Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Can I drive the yacht myself?

No. All charters include a licensed skipper. You cannot drive the yacht. You can steer for a photo if the skipper allows, but that is it. The skipper is responsible for safety, navigation, and mooring.

Is the skipper included in the price?

Yes. The price includes the skipper. You do not pay extra. Tipping is optional but appreciated if the service is good.

Can I bring my own food and drink?

Yes. You can bring your own food and drinks. The boat has a fridge and a cooler. You can also order catering through us. Glass bottles are allowed but be careful.

What happens in bad weather?

If the weather is dangerous (storms, high winds), the skipper will cancel or reschedule. You get a full refund or alternative date. For light rain or choppy seas, the trip goes ahead. The skipper will choose a sheltered route.

How many people can I bring?

It depends on the yacht. A 40-foot motor yacht typically holds up to 12 guests. A 60-foot yacht can take up to 20. Check the boat spec on the listing. The number includes children and infants.

Can I choose the itinerary?

Yes, within reason. The skipper will suggest a route, but you can ask for a different destination. The skipper will advise if it is safe and within the fuel allowance. Extra fuel costs apply for long distances.

What is the cancellation policy?

Full refund up to 30 days before the charter. 50% refund up to 14 days before. No refund after that. For weather cancellations by the skipper, you get a full refund or reschedule.

For more details on boat types and destinations, read our blog about Costa del Sol charters.

h1: Private Catamaran Hire Puerto Banus
intro:
If you want to see Marbella from the sea, a private catamaran hire in Puerto Banus is the most civilised way to do it. You get a whole boat to yourself, a licensed skipper who knows the coast, and none of the queuing or crowding that comes with shared excursions. The real question is whether you want to anchor off Cabopino for lunch, drift past the mansions of the Golden Mile, or head south to spot dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar.

BoatHire24 lets you compare catamarans moored in Puerto Banus and other Costa del Sol ports, see real availability, and book online. No phone tag, no hidden fees. Every charter includes the skipper, fuel, and insurance. You just turn up with your drinks and your playlist.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Private Catamaran Charter

A private catamaran charter means the boat is yours for the day, the half day, or the sunset slot. You decide the itinerary, the pace, and the guest list. The skipper handles the navigation, the anchoring, and the safety briefings. You handle the sunbathing, the swimming, and the decision about when to open the rosé.

Catamarans are wider than monohulls, so you get more deck space, a steadier ride, and usually a trampoline net at the bow where you can lie down and watch the water pass under you. Most boats in this category have a flybridge, a shaded saloon, a galley, and at least one cabin if you want to freshen up. Capacity ranges from 6 to 12 guests, depending on the model and the port regulations.

All charters on BoatHire24 include a professional skipper, fuel for the agreed itinerary, insurance, and basic safety equipment. You can add extras like a paddleboard, a seabob, or a catered menu. Some boats also have a sound system with Bluetooth, so you can play your own music.

Puerto Banus: The Main Departure Point

Puerto Banus is the obvious starting point for a luxury catamaran hire. The marina is right next to the designer shops and beach clubs, and the port exit takes you straight into the Bay of Marbella. From here you can head west toward Estepona or east toward Cabopino and Cala del Faro.

The harbour itself is worth a stroll before you board. You will see superyachts, sports cars, and a lot of people who have dressed for the occasion. The catamarans are usually moored on the outer pontoons, so you get a clear view of La Concha mountain as you cast off.

Departure time matters in Puerto Banus because the wind picks up in the afternoon. Mornings are glassy, good for a relaxed cruise. Afternoons bring a breeze that makes sailing more fun but can make anchoring a bit lumpy. Sunset charters are popular because the light turns the sea gold and the beach clubs start playing music.

Other Ports for Catamaran Hire on the Costa del Sol

If you are staying outside Marbella, you can also hire a private catamaran from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmadena. Each port has its own character and access to different stretches of coast.

Cabopino is smaller and quieter, with a sandy beach and a nature reserve behind it. The catamarans here tend to be a bit more modest in size, but the anchorage at Cabopino beach is excellent. Estepona has a long promenade and a marina that is less flashy than Banus but more authentic. Sotogrande is further west, closer to Gibraltar, and a good base if you want to cross the bay to Algeciras or head out toward the dolphin pods.

Benalmadena, east of Marbella, gives you access to the coast toward Malaga and the Nerja caves. The marina is large and well equipped, with plenty of restaurants and a cable car up to the mountain. You can find catamarans for 8 to 12 guests in all these ports, and the booking process on the search page is the same.

Boat Options: Size, Layout, and Extras

Catamarans available for private hire range from 38 to 50 feet, with some larger models up to 60 feet. The layout usually includes a flybridge with a helm station and sun pads, a main deck with a saloon and aft seating, and a foredeck with a trampoline or sun loungers.

The smaller catamarans (38-42 feet) work well for groups of 6 to 8. They have a single cabin and a basic galley. The mid-range (44-48 feet) can take up to 10 guests, with two cabins, a proper kitchen, and a fridge that can hold a serious amount of drinks. The larger ones (50 feet plus) are for 12 guests and come with a full galley, multiple cabins, and often a hydraulic platform for easy swimming access.

Extras vary by boat but commonly include stand-up paddleboards, snorkel gear, inflatable towables, and a Bluetooth sound system. Some operators offer a barbecue on the aft deck or a paella cooked on board. You can also arrange catering from a local restaurant that delivers to the marina. Prices for extras are usually listed on the boat profile page.

Pricing Guidance for Private Catamaran Hire

Prices for private catamaran hire in Puerto Banus start from around EUR 1,200 for a half day on a 38-foot boat for up to 8 guests. Full-day charters on the same boat range from EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,400. Larger catamarans (48-50 feet) for 10 to 12 guests start from about EUR 2,000 for a half day and EUR 3,000 for a full day.

Sunset charters are usually shorter (3-4 hours) and cost less than a full day, typically EUR 800 to EUR 1,500 depending on the boat. High season (July and August) sees a premium of roughly 20-30 percent. Low season (November to February) can be 15-20 percent cheaper, and you get calmer seas and emptier anchorages.

These prices include the skipper, fuel for the standard itinerary, and insurance. They do not include food and drink, marina fees for overnight stays, or extras like water toys. You can find exact prices on each boat listing, and you can filter by budget on the search page.

Seasons and Weather for Catamaran Charters

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and hot summers. The best months for catamaran hire are May through October, when the sea temperature is above 18 degrees C and the wind is moderate. July and August are the hottest, with air temperatures reaching 32 degrees C and the sea around 24 degrees C. The wind in summer is usually a light thermal breeze from the west, perfect for a gentle sail.

April and November are shoulder months. You can still get good days, but you need to check the forecast. The wind can be stronger, and there is a higher chance of rain. December to February is low season. The sea is colder (around 14 degrees C), and the days are shorter. Some operators run winter charters for whale watching or sunset trips, but availability is limited.

If you are booking in summer, aim for a morning departure to avoid the afternoon heat and the build-up of wind. In spring and autumn, the middle of the day is usually the calmest. Sunset charters work year-round, but in winter the sun sets before 6 pm, so you get a shorter window.

How to Book a Private Catamaran on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter the number of guests, the date, and the port (Puerto Banus or another). The system will show you available catamarans with prices, photos, and a list of included items. You can filter by boat size, price range, and extras.

Once you pick a boat, you can see the full itinerary options: half day, full day, sunset, or multi-day. You can also add extras like a catered menu or water toys. The booking process takes your payment and sends you a confirmation with the skipper's contact details and the departure instructions.

You can cancel up to 48 hours before departure for a full refund. Less than 48 hours, you lose the deposit. Weather cancellations are handled case by case. If the port authority closes the harbour due to wind or storms, you get a full refund or a reschedule.

For more tips on choosing the right boat and itinerary, check the BoatHire24 blog for guides on catamaran charter etiquette, the best anchorages, and what to pack.

Who Is Private Catamaran Hire For

Private catamaran hire works for a few different types of groups. Couples or small families who want a quiet day on the water with space to spread out. Groups of friends celebrating a birthday, a hen or stag do, or just a reunion. Corporate groups who need a floating meeting room with a better view than a hotel conference suite.

It also works for people who have never sailed before. The skipper handles everything, so you do not need any experience. The stable platform of a catamaran means even people prone to seasickness usually manage fine. You can spend the whole day on the water without once feeling the need to hold on to something.

If you are travelling with young children, catamarans are a good choice because of the space and the low freeboard. Kids can play on the trampoline net under supervision, and there is usually a cabin where they can nap. Just bring plenty of sun cream and a change of clothes.

Popular Itineraries from Puerto Banus

A typical half-day charter from Puerto Banus heads west along the coast toward the Marbella Club Hotel and the old town. You anchor off the beach near the Venus statue, where the water is calm and the seabed is sandy. Swim, use the paddleboard, or just float and watch the yachts go by. The skipper will bring out the cold drinks and maybe a plate of jamón if you arranged it.

A full-day itinerary usually goes further west to Estepona. You cruise past the luxury villas of the Golden Mile, the lighthouse at Punta de Calaburras, and the long beach of El Saladillo. You anchor in the bay of Estepona, near the port, and have lunch on board or go ashore to eat in the old town. The return trip in the afternoon gives you a different angle on the coast and the mountains behind it.

If you want to go east, you can head toward Cabopino and Cala del Faro. The coves around Cabopino are protected by the dunes of the Artola nature reserve, so the water is clear and the crowds are thinner. Cala del Faro is a rocky cove with a small beach and a lighthouse. It is a good spot for snorkelling because the rocks hold fish.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind

Bring swimwear, a towel, sun cream (factor 50, the Spanish sun is no joke), a hat, and a light jacket or jumper for the evening. Sunglasses with a strap are a good idea because the wind will take them off your face. A dry bag is useful for your phone and wallet.

Leave behind high heels, black soles that mark the deck, and glass bottles. Most catamarans have a strict no-glass policy because broken glass on deck or in the water is a nightmare. Plastic cups and cans are fine. The boat will have a cooler with ice, so you can bring your own drinks or buy them from the marina supermarket before boarding.

If you are prone to seasickness, take a travel sickness tablet an hour before departure. The Bay of Marbella is usually calm, but if you go further out toward the Strait of Gibraltar, the swell can pick up. Ginger sweets or a can of Coke also help settle the stomach.

Dolphin Watching on a Catamaran Charter

The waters off the Costa del Sol are home to several species of dolphin, including common dolphins, striped dolphins, and bottlenose dolphins. The best area for dolphin watching is between Estepona and the Strait of Gibraltar, where the nutrient-rich currents attract pods of up to 100 animals. You can also see pilot whales and, in summer, fin whales.

A private catamaran charter gives you the flexibility to spend time in the areas where dolphins are most likely to appear. The skipper will know the recent sightings and can adjust the route. Dolphins often ride the bow wave of the catamaran, so you get a close-up view from the trampoline net. The experience is better in the morning when the sea is calm and the animals are more active.

If dolphin watching is your main goal, book a full-day charter from Estepona or Sotogrande, which are closer to the Strait. The crossing from Puerto Banus adds about 45 minutes each way, so you need a longer trip to make it worthwhile.

Sunset Charters: What to Expect

Sunset charters are the most popular time slot on BoatHire24, and for good reason. The light in the evening is warm and soft, the wind drops, and the sea turns a deep orange. You leave Puerto Banus around 6 pm in summer or 4 pm in winter, cruise along the coast for an hour, and anchor in a quiet spot to watch the sun go down behind La Concha mountain.

The skipper will usually have a selection of drinks and maybe some tapas. You can bring your own food, or order a catering package from the marina. The atmosphere is relaxed, and the group size is often smaller than on a day charter. Most sunset charters last 3 to 4 hours, and you are back at the marina before the nightlife kicks off.

One practical point: the sun sets fast on the Costa del Sol. From the moment it touches the horizon to the moment it disappears is about 5 minutes. So have your phone or camera ready, and do not blink.

Special Occasions: Birthdays, Proposals, and Celebrations

Private catamaran hire is a common choice for milestone birthdays, anniversaries, and marriage proposals. The privacy and the scenery make it easy to create a memorable moment. You can arrange for a bottle of cava, a cake, or even a photographer to meet you at the marina. Some operators allow decorations on board, but check first because some boats have strict rules about confetti and glitter.

For a proposal, the skipper can anchor in a secluded cove at sunset and give you the space you need. The trampoline net at the bow is a popular spot, or the flybridge if you want a higher viewpoint. Just let the booking team know in advance so they can coordinate with the skipper.

Hen and stag groups are also common, but the boats have rules about noise and behaviour. No glass, no jumping off the flybridge, and no excessive drinking that puts the group at risk. The skipper has the authority to end the charter early if things get out of hand, so keep it civil.

How to Compare Catamaran Listings on BoatHire24

When you look at catamaran listings on the search page, focus on three things: capacity, included items, and the skipper's experience. Capacity is the legal limit, not a suggestion. If the listing says 10 guests, that includes you and everyone else, not 10 plus the skipper. The skipper is separate.

Included items vary by boat and operator. Some include a stand-up paddleboard and snorkel gear as standard. Others charge extra. Check the "What's included" section on the listing. If it says "fuel for 4 hours of cruising," that means the itinerary is limited to that distance. If you want to go further, you pay extra for fuel.

The skipper's experience matters because a good skipper knows the best anchorages, the wind patterns, and the local restaurants that deliver to the boat. Look for listings that mention the skipper's years of experience or the languages they speak. English and Spanish are the norm, but some skippers also speak German, French, or Italian.

intro:
You want a hen do that doesn't involve a sweaty club in some rainy city. You want sun, sea, and a boat that turns heads. bodyHtml:
What’s Included in a Hen Do Boat Charter

Every charter through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That means you don’t need a boating licence, and someone else handles the mooring, the navigation, and the awkward reversing into a berth. You just bring the party. Most charters include basic safety equipment, fuel for a standard itinerary, and a welcome briefing. Some include a cooler with ice, a Bluetooth speaker, and basic tableware. You can usually add extras like a hostess, a photographer, or a DJ. Check the listing details before you book.

The standard duration is four hours, but you can go for six or eight if you want to hit a second cove or stop for lunch at a beach club. The skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and your vibe. You might cruise past the golden sands of Puerto Banus, drop anchor off Cabopino, or head towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro. The boat is yours for the time you pay for.

Puerto Banus, The Starting Point

Puerto Banus is the obvious departure port for a hen do. It’s flashy, it’s loud, and it’s full of superyachts, sports cars, and people who look like they’ve just stepped off a reality show. The marina itself has a string of restaurants, shops, and bars that stay open late. You can start your charter from the main dock, wave at the Lamborghinis on the promenade, and be out on open water within ten minutes.

The port sits right next to the Rio Verde, a short walk from the beach. If you’re staying in Marbella or Nueva Andalucia, it’s a quick taxi ride. Parking is expensive and scarce, so get dropped off or take a transfer. Once you’re on the boat, you don’t need to think about traffic again until you dock.

Other departure ports on the Costa del Sol include Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmadena. Each has its own character. Marbella Marina is quieter and more local. Cabopino has a small, sandy beach and a dune system. Estepona has a pretty old town and a longer coastline. Sotogrande is posh and spread out. Benalmadena is lively and close to Torremolinos. For a hen do, Puerto Banus is the most central and the most fun.

Boat Types for a Hen Party

Not all boats are equal a hen do. You want space, a sun deck, and a decent sound system. Here are the options you’ll find on BoatHire24.

Motor yachts are the most popular choice. They’re fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space. A 40-foot motor yacht sleeps about 12 guests for a day charter. You get a bow sun pad, a shaded cockpit, and a cabin for changing or storing bags. Expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for four hours in the summer.

Catamarans are wider and more stable. They have a huge foredeck, a trampoline net at the front, and often a flybridge. They’re ideal if anyone in your group gets seasick. A 40-foot cat can take up to 12 guests. Prices start around EUR 1,500 for a half-day.

Sailing yachts are slower and quieter. They’re good if you want a more relaxed vibe, but they have less deck space and you might have to help with the sails. Not ideal for a big party. A 50-foot sailing yacht costs from EUR 1,000 for four hours.

RIBs and speedboats are small and fast. They’re fun for a quick blast, but they don’t have a toilet, a cabin, or much shade. Max four to six guests. Prices from EUR 500 for two hours.

Licence-free day boats are small motorboats you can drive without a licence. They’re cheap, but they don’t come with a skipper, so you’re on your own. For a hen do, you’re better off with a skipper who knows the coast.

Superyachts start at around EUR 5,000 for a half-day and go up to EUR 50,000 or more. They come with a crew, a chef, and everything else. If you have the budget, go for it. Otherwise, stick with a motor yacht or cat.

Pricing Guidance for Hen Do Charters

Prices vary by boat, season, duration, and extras. Here’s a rough guide for a half-day (four hours) in peak summer (June to September) from Puerto Banus.

Motor yacht (40-50 ft): EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,500. Catamaran (40-50 ft): EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. Sailing yacht (50 ft): EUR 1,000 to EUR 2,000. RIB/speedboat: EUR 500 to EUR 1,000. Superyacht (80+ ft): from EUR 5,000.

Extras add up. A hostess costs around EUR 200 for the day. A photographer is EUR 300 to EUR 500. Food catering starts at EUR 30 per person for a platter. Drinks are usually bring your own or pay a corkage fee. Some charters include a cooler and ice. Check the listing for what’s included.

Off-peak months (April, May, October) are cheaper by 20-30%. November to March is low season, but you can still charter if the weather holds. Book early for June to September, because boats get snapped up by hen parties, corporate groups, and tourists.

Best Times of Year for a Hen Do on the Water

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with hot summers and mild winters. The best time for a hen do on a boat is May to October. In May and June, the water is around 18-20 degrees C, the air is 25-28 degrees C, and the crowds are smaller. July and August are peak season: air temperatures hit 32-35 degrees C, water is 22-25 degrees C, and the coast is busy. September and October are still warm, with fewer tourists and lower prices.

April and November are gamble months. You might get a sunny day, but you might also get wind and rain. If you’re flexible, you can find a bargain. December to March is cold for swimming, but you can still cruise and have lunch on board.

If you want to swim, anchor in a cove, or sunbathe on the deck, aim for June to September. If you just want to cruise, drink, and take photos, the shoulder months work fine.

How to Book a Hen Do Yacht Rental in Puerto Banus

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter Puerto Banus as the departure port, your date, and the number of guests. Filter by boat type and price range. You’ll see listings from local charter companies. Each listing shows the boat, the price, the skipper, and what’s included. Click through to see photos, reviews, and availability.

Once you find a boat you like, send an enquiry through the platform. The charter company will confirm availability and send a quote. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking, and the balance on the day. Read the cancellation policy before you pay. Most companies offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days ahead, but check the terms.

If you’re not sure what you need, BoatHire24 has a blog with guides on boat types, packing lists, and local tips. You can also call or email us, and we’ll point you to the right boats. We don’t take a commission from you; the charter companies pay us a listing fee. So the price you see is the price they charge.

Who Is This For

A yacht rental for a hen do in Puerto Banus works for groups of 6 to 12 people. It’s not ideal for a big party of 20 or more, because most boats have a max capacity of 12 guests. If you have a larger group, you can book two boats and cruise together. The skipper will coordinate the route so you can raft up and mingle.

It’s also good for a quieter hen do, where the focus is on relaxing, swimming, and eating. You don’t have to drink or dance. You can just lie on the sun pad and watch the coast go by. The skipper will adjust the pace to what you want.

If you’re the organiser, you’ll need to collect the deposit from the group, sort out the guest list, and communicate with the charter company. Most companies require a final guest count 48 hours before departure. Make sure everyone knows the meeting point and the time. Late arrivals hold up the whole charter.

For more ideas on what to do on the Costa del Sol, check the BoatHire24 blog. We cover everything from dolphin watching off Estepona to visiting the Nerja caves. The blog also has a packing list for a day on the water, which includes sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a change of clothes. Don’t forget the suncream, because the reflection off the water burns faster than you think.

What to Bring on a Hen Do Boat Party

You need to pack smart for a day on the water. Bring sunscreen with at least SPF 50, because the sun reflects off the sea and burns you twice as fast. A hat and sunglasses are non-negotiable. Take a towel, a change of dry clothes, and a light jacket or hoodie for the evening breeze. If you plan to swim, bring a swimsuit and a waterproof phone case. Most boats have a small cabin where you can change, but space is tight.

For music, check if the boat has a Bluetooth speaker. If not, bring your own portable one. Make a playlist beforehand, because signal can be patchy on the water. For drinks, most charters let you bring your own alcohol. Take cans or plastic bottles, not glass, because glass breaks and the skipper will tell you off. A cooler with ice is often included, but confirm it before you arrive. Snacks are a good idea, but avoid anything that melts or crumbles easily. Think grapes, crisps, and sandwiches.

If you’re prone to seasickness, take a pill an hour before you board. The Costa del Sol is generally calm in summer, but the swell can pick up in the afternoon. Ginger biscuits and fresh air help. Don’t drink on an empty stomach, and pace yourself. The combination of sun, movement, and alcohol hits harder than you expect.

Best Itineraries for a Hen Do from Puerto Banus

A typical four-hour charter from Puerto Banus heads west towards Cabopino or east towards Marbella. The skipper will decide based on the wind and swell. One popular route goes west to Cabopino, where you can anchor off the sand dunes and swim in clear, shallow water. Cabopino has a small beach bar called Chiringuito Cabopino, but you can’t dock there, so you swim ashore or use the boat’s tender.

Another route goes east to Cala del Faro, a rocky cove near Marbella. It’s quieter than Cabopino and has good snorkelling. You can also stop at the Marbella Marina for a photo with the yachts. If you have six hours, you can push further east to the cliffs of Elviria or even to the mouth of the Rio Verde. For a full-day charter (eight hours), you might go all the way to Estepona, anchor off the old town, and have lunch at a beach club like El Ancla or Bahia de Estepona.

If your group wants to see dolphins, ask the skipper to head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The trip takes about an hour from Puerto Banus, and you’re likely to see common dolphins, striped dolphins, and sometimes pilot whales. The best time is early morning. This works well for a longer charter of six to eight hours, because you need time to get there, watch them, and come back.

How to Split Costs and Organise the Group

Hen do budgets vary wildly. A typical split for a group of 10 on a motor yacht at EUR 1,800 is EUR 180 per person. If you add a hostess (EUR 200), food (EUR 30 per person), and drinks (say EUR 20 per person), the total per person comes to around EUR 250. That’s cheaper than a night out in Puerto Banus, and you get a private boat for the day.

To collect money, use a group payment app like Splitwise or Revolut. Ask everyone to pay a non-refundable deposit upfront to cover the booking deposit. Most charter companies want 30-50% to secure the date. The balance is due on the day, so collect that a week before. Have a backup plan if someone drops out. A spare guest or a small increase for the rest of the group is easier than cancelling.

Make sure everyone knows the meeting point. The main dock at Puerto Banus is easy to find, but specify the pontoon number. Arrive 15 minutes early. The skipper will do a safety briefing and a quick tour of the boat. Late arrivals mean less time on the water, and the skipper won’t wait.

What Not to Do on a Hen Do Boat Charter

Don’t bring glass bottles. They break, they cut feet, and they’re a hazard on deck. Use plastic cups or cans. Don’t play music so loud that the skipper can’t hear the radio or other boats. The skipper has the final say on volume. Don’t jump off the boat without checking with the skipper first. They need to know where you are at all times, especially in open water.

Don’t expect to dock at a beach club. Most beach clubs have small jetties for tenders, not for charter boats. You anchor offshore and swim in, or the skipper drops you off in the tender. Don’t assume the boat has a toilet that works while underway. Some marine heads are finicky. Use the marina facilities before you leave. Don’t leave rubbish on the boat. Take everything back to shore. The charter company will charge you a cleaning fee if you leave a mess.

Don’t be late back to the dock. The skipper has a schedule, and the next charter might be waiting. If you’re late, you might lose your deposit or pay an overtime fee. Respect the skipper’s time and the boat. They work hard to keep it clean and safe.

Alternatives to Puerto Banus for a Hen Do

If Puerto Banus is too flashy or too expensive, consider Marbella Marina. It’s a ten-minute taxi ride from Puerto Banus, and the boats are similar. The marina itself is quieter, with a few restaurants and a supermarket. You can still cruise the same coastline. Cabopino is another option. It’s smaller and more laid back, with a sandy beach and a beach bar. The boats are smaller too, so max capacity is usually eight guests.

Estepona is a good choice if you want a longer cruise. The old town is pretty, with whitewashed buildings and flower pots. The marina has a range of boats, from small RIBs to 50-foot motor yachts. Sotogrande is for the luxury crowd. It’s quieter, more exclusive, and further from the main party scene. Benalmadena is lively and close to Torremolinos, but the boats are often older and cheaper. For a hen do, Puerto Banus is still the best starting point, but these alternatives work if you want something different.

intro:
You're planning a stag do in Marbella and you want something that doesn't involve a sweaty club at 2am. You want the sun, the sea, and a floating bar that moves. Motor yacht hire Marbella for stag parties is exactly that: a private boat with a licensed skipper, a sound system, and a crew that will keep the drinks coming. No queues, no dress code, no last orders.

BoatHire24 connects you with the best motor yachts in Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and the rest of the Costa del Sol. Every charter includes a skipper, so you can focus on the stag and the champagne. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day, depending on the yacht size and extras. You book online, you turn up, you party.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with Motor Yacht Hire for a Stag

A motor yacht for a stag do isn't just a boat. It's a private venue with no capacity limits, no noise complaints, and no closing time. You get a spacious deck for dancing, a flybridge for sunbathing, a cabin for the inevitable nap, and a kitchen for the barbecue. The skipper handles the navigation, the crew handles the drinks, and you handle the stag.

Most charters include a standard sound system, but you can upgrade to a DJ setup or a Bluetooth speaker that shakes the hull. Some yachts have a water slide, a paddleboard, or a jet ski tow. You can add catering, from tapas to a full paella feast, or bring your own food and drink. The skipper will anchor in a quiet cove like Cala del Faro or off the coast of Estepona, where the water is calm and the views are ridiculous.

You don't need a boating licence. The skipper has one. You just need to decide how long you want to party: half-day (4 hours), full-day (8 hours), or sunset cruise (3 hours). Sunset is popular because the light turns the sea gold and the clubs haven't started yet.

Best Departure Ports for a Stag Party

You have options. The most famous is Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina with the superyachts and the champagne bars. Your stag party will arrive at the port, walk past the Lamborghinis, and board your yacht right next to the billionaires. It sets the tone.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more relaxed but still central. You're a short walk from the old town and the beach clubs. Cabopino is quieter, with a sandy beach and a dune reserve, good if you want to avoid the crowds. Estepona has a charming old town and a long promenade, and the marina is modern and well-equipped. Sotogrande is the polo crowd, a bit more understated but still luxurious. Benalmádena is lively and close to the nightlife of Torremolinos.

Your skipper will know the best spots for swimming, dolphin watching, and anchoring. The Strait of Gibraltar is a short cruise from Estepona or Sotogrande, where you can see dolphins and maybe a whale. The Nerja caves are a longer trip but worth it if you have a full day.

Motor Yacht Options for Stag Parties

You don't need a superyacht to have a good time, but you can rent one if the budget allows. For a stag of 10 to 20 people, a 40-50 foot motor yacht is ideal. It has enough deck space for dancing, a cabin for the stag to get ready, and a bathroom. For larger groups, 60-80 foot yachts can handle up to 30 guests comfortably.

Catamarans are also an option, but motor yachts are faster and more stable for a party. You can cover more distance, visit more coves, and get back to port in time for the evening. RIBs and speedboats are for the adrenaline crowd, but they lack the space for a proper party. Fishing boats are not recommended for stags. Licence-free day boats are small and slow, fine for a quiet couple but not a stag.

Most motor yachts on BoatHire24 are from 2010 or newer, with modern interiors and clean lines. You can filter by size, price, and availability. The skipper will meet you at the port and give you a safety briefing. Then you're off.

Pricing Guidance for Motor Yacht Hire Marbella Stag

Prices vary by yacht, season, and duration. As a rough guide, a half-day charter for a 40-foot motor yacht starts from around EUR 1,500. A full day is from EUR 2,500. A sunset cruise (3 hours) is from EUR 1,000. These prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. Extras like catering, drinks, water toys, and DJ equipment cost more.

High season (June to September) is the most expensive. Low season (October to May) is cheaper and the weather is still good, with average temperatures of 20-25 degrees C in spring and autumn. You can book a last-minute charter if the yacht is available, but it's better to book a few weeks ahead for a stag group.

You can split the cost among the group. For 10 people, a EUR 1,500 half-day works out at EUR 150 per person. That's less than a club table and you get the sea, the sun, and the privacy. Some yachts require a deposit, usually 30-50% of the total, with the balance paid on the day. Payment is by bank transfer or card.

Best Seasons for a Stag Party on a Motor Yacht

The obvious answer is summer: June, July, August, and September. The sea is warm, the sun is out, and the evenings are long. But the Costa del Sol has over 300 days of sunshine a year, so you can do a stag party in April, May, or October without the crowds. The water is cooler, but you can still swim. The clubs are less busy, but the yachts are cheaper.

Winter is not ideal for swimming, but you can still charter a motor yacht for a sightseeing cruise or a lunch trip. The mountains behind Marbella, especially La Concha, are often snow-capped in January, which makes for a dramatic backdrop. The Strait of Gibraltar is a good winter destination for dolphin watching.

For a stag party, the best balance is late May or early September. The weather is hot, the water is warm, and the prices are lower than peak July and August. You also avoid the school holiday crowds.

How to Book Motor Yacht Hire for a Stag in Marbella

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You search for motor yachts in Marbella, filter by date, group size, and budget, then send an enquiry. The platform connects you directly with the yacht owner or charter company. You get a confirmation with the skipper's contact details and the meeting point.

You can add extras like a photographer, a DJ, or a catering package. Some companies offer a stag package that includes a bottle of champagne, a fruit platter, and a personalised banner. You can also arrange a transfer from your hotel or apartment to the port.

Read the cancellation policy before you book. Most charters allow free cancellation up to 7 days before. After that, you may lose the deposit. Make sure the group is confirmed before you commit.

Who Should Charter a Motor Yacht for a Stag

This is for a stag who wants something different. Not the lads who want to get drunk in a pub and then fall asleep on a bench. This is for a group that wants to swim in the Mediterranean, see the coastline from the water, and have a party that doesn't end at 2am because the bar closes. It works for groups of 8 to 30 people. If you have fewer than 8, a RIB or a smaller motor yacht might be more cost-effective. If you have more than 30, you need a superyacht or a catamaran.

It also works for mixed groups, not just all-male. The skipper is professional and discreet. You can bring your own playlist, your own food, and your own drinks. The crew will help with the barbecue and the cleanup. It's your private party on the water.

For more ideas on planning a stag do in Marbella, check out our blog for tips on the best bars, restaurants, and activities.

What to Bring on Your Stag Yacht Charter

You need swimwear, sunscreen (factor 50, the Spanish sun is relentless), a towel, and a change of clothes for the evening. Bring a hat and sunglasses. If you plan to drink, bring more water than you think you need. Dehydration on a boat is faster than on land. A portable speaker is fine, but check with the skipper first. Some yachts have a fixed sound system and you don't want to cause a feedback loop. Bring a cooler if the yacht doesn't have one, but most do. A camera or a waterproof phone case is worth it. The photos from the water are better than any club selfie.

For the stag himself, a crown, a sash, or a custom t-shirt works. Some groups bring a banner with a photo of the stag. The crew will help hang it on the flybridge. You can also bring a cake or a bottle of cava for a toast. Just check with the charter company first. Some have corkage fees if you bring your own alcohol, but most allow it for stags.

How to Choose the Right Motor Yacht for Your Group Size

For a stag of 8 to 12 people, a 40-foot motor yacht like a Sunseeker Portofino or a Princess V42 is perfect. It has a large aft deck for standing, a saloon with seating, and a cabin for the stag to get changed. For 12 to 20 people, go for a 50-60 foot yacht like a Sunseeker Predator or a Ferretti 550. These have a flybridge with a sunpad and a bar area. For 20 to 30 people, you need a 70-80 foot yacht, like a Princess 72 or a Pershing 76. These have multiple decks, a crew cabin, and a galley.

If your group is smaller than 8, consider a RIB or a smaller motor yacht. A 30-foot RIB can take 8 people and is fast, but it has no cabin and limited shade. A 30-foot motor yacht like a Jeanneau Leader 33 can take 6 to 8 people and has a small cabin and a toilet. For a stag, the minimum is a 40-footer. Anything smaller feels cramped when everyone is dancing.

Adding Water Toys to Your Stag Charter

A motor yacht with a jet ski tow is a popular add-on for stags. The skipper will tow the jet ski behind the yacht, and you take turns riding it in the cove. Prices start from around EUR 200 for an hour. A paddleboard is cheaper, around EUR 50 for the day, and it's good for the hangover. A water slide attached to the side of the yacht is a crowd-pleaser. It costs around EUR 150 to rent and fits most yachts over 40 feet.

Some yachts have a seabob, a underwater scooter that lets you swim like a dolphin. It's a novelty and costs around EUR 100 per hour. If you want to fish, the skipper can provide a basic fishing rod and bait. The best spots are off the coast of Estepona and near the Strait of Gibraltar. You can catch bream, mackerel, and sometimes sea bass. The crew will clean and cook it for you if you want.

Best Coves and Beaches for a Stag Party Anchor

Cala del Faro is the most popular anchor spot for stags. It's a small cove near Marbella with clear water and a rocky beach. The water is deep enough for swimming and jumping off the yacht. There are no restaurants or bars, so you need to bring everything. The skipper will anchor near the cliffs, and you can swim to the beach if you want.

Another good spot is the coast between Cabopino and Marbella. There are several sandy coves with calm water and good visibility. The area near the Río Verde is shallow and warm, good for paddleboarding. Off the coast of Estepona, there are larger coves with more space. The water is cleaner here because it's further from the marinas. If you have a full day, the skipper can take you to the Nerja coast, where the cliffs are dramatic and the water is turquoise. It's about an hour from Marbella by motor yacht.

How to Plan the Timing of Your Stag Yacht Charter

A full-day charter from 10am to 6pm gives you time to swim, eat, drink, and explore. You can anchor in a cove for lunch, then move to another spot for the afternoon. A half-day from 2pm to 6pm is good if you want to party in the afternoon and then go to a club in the evening. A sunset charter from 6pm to 9pm is the most Instagrammable. The light is golden, the sea is calm, and the temperature drops to a comfortable 25-28 degrees C in summer.

If you book a sunset charter, you can go straight from the yacht to a club in Puerto Banús. The marina is a 5-minute walk from the port. Some clubs offer a VIP table package for yacht guests. You can arrange this through the charter company or directly with the club. The advantage of a sunset charter is that you don't waste the whole day on the water. You can spend the morning at the beach or the pool, then board the yacht at 6pm.

What the Skipper Does and Doesn't Do

The skipper is a licensed professional who handles the navigation, safety, and anchoring. They will give you a safety briefing at the start, including where the life jackets are and how to use the VHF radio. They will not serve drinks or clean up after you. That's the crew's job, if you have one. Most motor yachts under 50 feet have a skipper only. Yachts over 60 feet usually have a skipper and a deckhand or stewardess.

The skipper will not let you drive the yacht unless you have a boating licence and they agree. Some skippers allow it for a photo, but not for long. They will not tolerate dangerous behaviour, like jumping from the flybridge or drinking too much. If someone is sick or aggressive, the skipper can return to port early. You lose the remaining time and the money. Keep it civil and the skipper will stay out of your way.

Understanding the Costs of Fuel and Extras

Fuel is usually included in the charter price for a fixed itinerary. If you want to go further, like to the Strait of Gibraltar or Nerja, the skipper will charge extra for fuel. A 40-foot motor yacht burns around 100 litres per hour at cruising speed. At EUR 1.50 per litre, that's EUR 150 per hour. A trip to the Strait of Gibraltar from Marbella is about 2 hours each way, so an extra EUR 600 in fuel. The skipper will give you an estimate before you go.

Other extras include catering, drinks, water toys, and a photographer. A catering package with tapas and drinks starts from around EUR 30 per person. A full paella feast with wine is from EUR 50 per person. A photographer for the day is from EUR 300. A DJ setup with a sound system is from EUR 500. You can negotiate a package deal if you book through BoatHire24. The platform allows you to compare quotes from different owners.

How to Avoid Common Stag Party Charter Mistakes

The biggest mistake is booking a yacht that is too small for the group. A 30-foot yacht for 12 people is a disaster. Everyone is cramped, there is no space to dance, and the toilet queue is long. Always book a yacht with at least 2 feet of length per person. A 40-foot yacht for 12 people is fine. A 50-foot yacht for 20 people is fine. The second mistake is not confirming the extras. If you want a DJ, book it in advance. Don't assume the yacht has one. The third mistake is not checking the weather. The Costa del Sol is mostly calm, but the wind can pick up in the afternoon. The skipper will decide if it's safe to go out. If the sea is rough, you can reschedule or get a refund if the charter is cancelled by the owner.

Another mistake is not agreeing on the music policy. Some yachts have noise restrictions in the marina. You can play loud music once you are at sea, but not at the dock. The skipper will tell you when you can turn it up. Finally, don't bring glass bottles on the yacht. They break and the crew has to clean up the shards. Use plastic cups and cans. The skipper will provide a bin for the empties.

intro:
If you are looking for a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week, you want the best boat, the best crew and the best itinerary without the usual booking headache. Puerto Banus is the superyacht capital of the Costa del Sol, but a week-long charter here is not only for billionaires. You can rent a 12-metre motor yacht for a family holiday, a spacious catamaran for a group of friends or a sleek sailing yacht for a romantic getaway. The prices vary by season, boat size and included extras, but you can expect to pay from around EUR 8,000 to EUR 25,000 for a week in high season, depending on the boat. For larger yachts or superyachts, prices are on request.

This page covers everything you need to know about booking a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week: what is included, which ports you can depart from, what boat types suit different groups, how the weather works, how to book and who this kind of trip is really for. No fluff, no fake reviews, just straight answers.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Luxury Yacht Charter Puerto Banus Week

When you book a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week through BoatHire24, the base price typically includes the yacht itself, a professional skipper and standard safety equipment. The skipper lives aboard for the duration, so you do not need to worry about docking, anchoring or navigating the tricky currents around the Strait of Gibraltar. Fuel costs are usually extra and depend on how many nautical miles you cover. A typical week might involve 20 to 40 engine hours, which at current fuel prices adds around EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 for a mid-size motor yacht. Catamarans and sailing yachts use less fuel, so those costs are lower.

Most charters also include bed linen, towels and basic galley equipment. Some operators offer a welcome pack with water, soft drinks and a bottle of cava. Food and drinks are not included unless you book a fully crewed option with a chef. You can either bring your own provisions, order a provisioning service or ask the skipper to stop at a supermarket in Puerto Banus or Estepona before departure. Many guests prefer to eat ashore at beach clubs or chiringuitos during the day and cook on board in the evening.

Extras like jet skis, paddleboards, snorkelling gear or a water slide can be added for an additional fee. If you want a crewed charter with a stewardess or a chef, expect to pay 20 to 30 percent more on top of the base rate. For a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week, the total cost including fuel, food and extras can easily reach EUR 15,000 to EUR 40,000 for a high-end motor yacht, but you can also find more affordable options if you book early or travel in the shoulder season.

Departure Ports for Your Week-Long Charter

Your luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week can start from any of the six main ports we cover on the Costa del Sol. Puerto Banus itself is the obvious choice if you want to step straight into the glamour of designer boutiques and champagne bars. The marina has 915 berths and can accommodate yachts up to 60 metres. Departing from here gives you quick access to the Marbella coastline and the Cala del Faro, a secluded cove just 15 minutes west.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a more laid-back alternative, with cheaper berthing fees and easy parking. It is located right next to the old town, so you can stock up on supplies or enjoy a pre-charter dinner at one of the tapas bars on Calle Alcazabilla. Cabopino, near the dunes of Artola, is a smaller, quieter port with a sandy beach and a handful of restaurants. It is ideal if you want a low-key start to your week, especially if you plan to head west towards Estepona and Gibraltar.

Estepona port is another excellent option, especially for longer charters. The town has a charming old quarter with flower-filled streets and a good selection of supermarkets and chandleries. Sotogrande is further west, near the border with Cadiz, and is popular for sport fishing and golf holidays. Benalmadena, east of Marbella, offers a different perspective, with views of the Mijas mountains and quicker access to the Nerja caves if you want to combine sailing with a cultural excursion.

Whichever port you choose, your skipper will plan a route that matches your interests, whether that means anchoring in quiet coves, visiting beach clubs or exploring the Strait of Gibraltar to watch dolphins and whales. The distance between Puerto Banus and Gibraltar is about 40 nautical miles, which is a comfortable four- to five-hour cruise at 10 knots.

Boat Types for a Luxury Yacht Charter Puerto Banus Week

The boat you choose for your luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week depends on your group size, budget and preferred style of cruising. Motor yachts are the most popular option for a week-long charter because they offer speed, luxury and plenty of deck space. A typical 15-metre motor yacht sleeps six to eight guests in three or four cabins, with a flybridge, a salon and a sun pad area. Expect to pay from around EUR 12,000 to EUR 18,000 for a week in July or August. If you want something bigger, a 20-metre motor yacht with a master suite and VIP cabins can cost EUR 20,000 to EUR 30,000 per week.

Catamarans are a great choice for groups who value stability and space. A 14-metre catamaran has a wide beam, so it does not heel like a monohull, making it ideal for guests who get seasick. The living area is usually on one level, with a large saloon and an open cockpit. Catamarans also have shallow drafts, so you can anchor closer to the beach. Prices for a week on a catamaran start at around EUR 9,000 for a 12-metre and go up to EUR 20,000 for a 16-metre with four cabins.

Sailing yachts offer a more traditional experience, with the romance of hoisting sails and the quiet of wind power. A 14-metre sailing yacht sleeps six to eight and costs roughly EUR 8,000 to EUR 14,000 per week. You will need to enjoy a bit of heeling, but modern sailing yachts are comfortable and well-equipped. RIBs and speedboats are not really suitable for a week-long charter because they lack cabins and amenities, but you can rent them for day trips from Puerto Banus. Licence-free day boats, which are small motorboats under 15 hp, are also available for short excursions but are not suitable for overnight stays.

Superyachts over 30 metres are available for those who want the ultimate luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week. These come with a full crew, including a captain, engineer, stewardess and chef. Prices start at around EUR 50,000 per week and can exceed EUR 200,000 for the most exclusive vessels. You can browse our selection on the search page.

Pricing Guidance for a Week-Long Charter

Pricing for a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week varies significantly depending on the season, the boat size and the level of service. High season runs from June to September, with July and August being the most expensive. In these months, a 15-metre motor yacht costs around EUR 14,000 to EUR 18,000 per week, while a 12-metre catamaran is EUR 10,000 to EUR 13,000. Shoulder months like May, June and October are 20 to 30 percent cheaper, and the low season from November to April offers the best value, with prices dropping by up to 40 percent. However, the weather can be cooler and windier in winter, so you may not get the full beach experience.

Fuel is a major variable. A motor yacht burning 60 litres per hour at cruising speed will consume around 1,440 litres over a week of moderate use (24 hours of engine time at 10 knots). At current diesel prices of about EUR 1.40 per litre, that is roughly EUR 2,016. Catamarans and sailing yachts use much less, often half that amount. Some operators include a fuel allowance, but most charge actual consumption. Always ask for an estimate before booking.

Extras like jet skis (EUR 300 to EUR 500 per day), paddleboards (EUR 50 to EUR 100 per day) and chef services (EUR 200 to EUR 400 per day) add up quickly. If you want a fully crewed charter with a chef, expect to pay around EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 extra for the week. To get an accurate price for your specific dates and requirements, contact us via the BoatHire24 homepage and we will send you a detailed quote from our partner operators.

Best Season for a Luxury Yacht Charter Puerto Banus Week

The best time for a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week is from May to October, when the weather is warm and the sea is calm. July and August are the peak months, with average air temperatures of 28 to 32 degrees Celsius and water temperatures of 24 to 26 degrees. The sea breeze usually picks up in the afternoon, making sailing conditions pleasant. However, these months are also the busiest, so you need to book at least three to six months in advance to secure the boat you want.

June and September are excellent shoulder months. The weather is still hot, with air temperatures around 26 to 30 degrees, and the water is warm enough for swimming. Crowds are smaller, and prices are lower. October can also be good, with temperatures around 22 to 25 degrees, but you might get some rain. The wind tends to be stronger in spring and autumn, which is great for sailors but can make anchoring uncomfortable in exposed coves.

Winter charters are possible but less common. From November to March, temperatures range from 15 to 20 degrees, and the water is too cold for most people to swim comfortably. However, you can still enjoy sightseeing, dolphin watching in the Strait of Gibraltar or visiting the Nerja caves. If you are flexible with dates and want a bargain, a winter luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week can cost half the summer price. Just pack a jacket.

How to Book Your Luxury Yacht Charter Puerto Banus Week

Booking a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Start by using the search page to filter by port, boat type, number of guests and dates. You will see a list of available yachts with photos, specifications and approximate prices. Once you find a boat you like, click on it to view the full details, including the layout, amenities and the operator's contact information.

If you prefer a more personalised service, you can fill in the contact form on our website with your requirements, and we will match you with suitable operators. We work with vetted local companies who have years of experience in the Marbella area. They will send you a customised itinerary and a quote. After you agree on the terms, you pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) to secure the booking, with the balance due two to four weeks before departure.

We recommend taking out travel insurance that covers cancellation and damage deposits. Most operators require a damage deposit of EUR 1,000 to EUR 3,000, which is refunded after the charter if the boat is returned in good condition. For more tips on the booking process, read our blog post on how to avoid common charter mistakes.

Who Is a Luxury Yacht Charter Puerto Banus Week For

A luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week is ideal for groups of friends, families or couples who want a private, flexible holiday on the water. If you are celebrating a milestone birthday, an anniversary or a family reunion, renting a yacht for a week gives you the freedom to explore the coast at your own pace without the crowds of a resort. You can wake up in a different cove every morning, swim in crystal-clear water and dine at beach clubs that are only accessible by boat.

The trip is also suitable for corporate groups or team-building events, provided the group size does not exceed the boat's capacity. Many operators offer corporate packages with catering and AV equipment. However, note that most charters have a maximum of 12 guests for safety and insurance reasons, even if the boat can sleep more. If you have a larger group, you can charter two yachts and travel together.

This type of charter is not for everyone. If you prefer all-inclusive resorts with non-stop entertainment, or if you get seasick easily, a week on a yacht might not be your best option. Also, if you are on a tight budget, a week-long charter is a significant investment, though the per-person cost can be comparable to a luxury hotel when split among a group. For a more affordable option, consider a day charter or a weekend trip instead.

Local Highlights to Include in Your Itinerary

When planning your luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week, your skipper will suggest a route that takes in the best of the Costa del Sol. Start by heading west from Puerto Banus towards the Cala del Faro, a quiet cove with a small beach and a lighthouse. It is a great spot for a morning swim before the crowds arrive. Continue to Estepona, where you can moor in the marina and explore the old town with its colourful flower pots and tapas bars. The marina has a fuel station and a supermarket, so you can restock supplies.

The Strait of Gibraltar is a must-see for wildlife enthusiasts. The area is one of the best places in Europe to spot dolphins, pilot whales and even orcas. The crossing from Estepona to Gibraltar takes about two hours at 20 knots. You can anchor near the Rock of Gibraltar and take a tender ashore to see the Barbary macaques or visit the caves. If you have time, head further west to Tarifa, the windsurfing capital, where the water is turquoise and the beaches are wild.

If you prefer to go east, sail from Puerto Banus towards Marbella and then on to Cabopino, where the Artola dunes form a protected natural park. Further east, you can reach Benalmadena and then Malaga, the birthplace of Picasso. For a longer excursion, continue to the Nerja caves, a stunning series of caverns with prehistoric paintings. The journey from Puerto Banus to Nerja is about 50 nautical miles, so it is best done as an overnight stop. Your skipper will help you plan a realistic itinerary based on the weather and your preferences.

What to Expect Onboard

Onboard a luxury yacht charter Puerto Banus week, you can expect a high standard of comfort and service. Most yachts have air conditioning, a fully equipped galley, a sound system and a TV. Cabins are typically en-suite, with fresh towels and bed linen provided. The deck area usually has a bimini or hardtop for shade, plus sun loungers and a table for outdoor dining. Some yachts have a grill or a barbecue on the aft deck.

The skipper will give you a safety briefing on the first day and explain the rules of the boat. They will also help you plan the daily schedule, but the itinerary is flexible. You can decide to stay in one place for two days if you like a particular cove, or move every day if you want to cover more ground. The skipper lives in a separate cabin and is available 24/7 for questions or assistance.

Keep in mind that space on a yacht is limited compared to a hotel room. Storage is at a premium, so pack light. Soft bags are better than hard suitcases because they fit into lockers more easily. Also, bring sunscreen, a hat and a light jacket for the evenings, as the sea breeze can be cool even in summer.

title: Private Boat Hire Marbella for Fishing – Book Trip
