title: Luxury Yacht Hire Marbella for Events – Exclusive
metaDescription: Book luxury yacht hire Marbella for events with a licensed skipper. Private parties, corporate events, weddings from Puerto Banús. Compare yachts now.
h1: Luxury Yacht Hire Marbella for Events, Exclusive Charters
intro:
You want to host an event on the Costa del Sol that people actually remember. Not another hotel ballroom or beach club where the canapés go soggy. You want the Mediterranean as your backdrop, a deck under your feet, and a crew who makes sure the champagne stays cold. That is exactly what luxury yacht hire Marbella for events delivers.

On BoatHire24, every charter comes with a licensed skipper, so you don't need a licence or any nautical experience. You just pick the boat, choose your port (Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande or Benalmádena), and plan the kind of event that makes your guests text you the next day asking when the next one is. Whether it is a birthday, a corporate bash, a wedding reception or a milestone anniversary, the yacht is yours for the duration.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Luxury Yacht Hire for Events

When you book a luxury yacht for an event through BoatHire24, you are not just renting a boat. You are renting a private venue that moves. Every charter includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation and safety, so you can focus on your guests. The crew can be extended to include stewards, hostesses or even a private chef, depending on the package you choose. Standard inclusions on most yachts are: use of the onboard sound system (Bluetooth or aux), a cooler or fridge for your drinks, a shaded deck area, and a swim platform if you want to take a dip between courses. Some larger motor yachts and catamarans come with a barbecue grill, a Jacuzzi or even a slide. You can bring your own catering, or arrange it through the charter company. The key point is that everything is customisable, and the crew works to your timeline.

Ports of Departure for Your Event Charter

Where you set off matters. Puerto Banús is the obvious choice for glamour: superyachts in the marina, designer shops on the quay, and a short cruise to the exclusive Cala del Faro for a swim stop. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more laid back and closer to the old town, ideal if you want to combine a yacht party with a dinner at a chiringuito later. Cabopino is smaller and quieter, perfect for a private event without the paparazzi. Estepona gives you access to the Strait of Gibraltar and its dolphin pods, plus the charming old town for an after-party. Sotogrande is the choice for high-end corporate events, with its golf courses and polo fields nearby. Benalmádena offers a family-friendly vibe and easy access from Málaga airport. Each port has its own character, and your skipper will advise on the best anchorage for your specific event type.

Boat Types Available for Events

Not all yachts are the same for events. Motor yachts from 12 to 30 metres give you speed, space and a sleek profile. They are the best choice for a cocktail party or a corporate reception where you want to impress. Catamarans (20 to 24 metres) are stable, with huge deck areas and a shallow draft that lets you anchor close to the beach. They work well for wedding receptions or larger groups (up to 50 guests). Sailing yachts offer a more classic, romantic feel, ideal for an intimate anniversary or a small wedding ceremony. RIBs and speedboats are for smaller, more active groups who want to combine the event with water sports. Licence-free day boats (up to 15 metres without a licence requirement) are available for smaller parties, but note that you still get a skipper included on BoatHire24 charters. Superyachts (30 metres plus) are for the ultimate statement: think helipad, cinema, and full crew. All options are listed on our search page with real-time availability.

Pricing Guidance for Luxury Yacht Events

Prices vary widely depending on the yacht size, season, duration and extras. As a rough guide, a half-day charter (4 hours) on a 12-metre motor yacht in the low season starts from around EUR 1,200. A full day on a 20-metre catamaran in high season can be EUR 4,500 to EUR 7,000. For a 30-metre superyacht with full crew and catering, expect from EUR 15,000 per day. These are exclusive charter prices, not per person. The rate includes the skipper, fuel for standard cruising, and basic insurance. Extras like gourmet catering, premium bar, water toys (jetski, seabob, inflatables) and additional crew are charged separately. You can request a custom quote on any yacht via the BoatHire24 platform, and the charter company will respond within 24 hours. For large events (40+ guests), you may need to charter a catamaran or a larger motor yacht, and prices are generally on request.

Best Seasons for a Yacht Event in Marbella

The Costa del Sol has a long season. May to October is the sweet spot, with average temperatures of 22 to 30 degrees C and calm seas. July and August are peak season: hot, busy, and the highest prices. If you want good weather and fewer crowds, book in June or September. April and October can still be pleasant, but you might get a cooler breeze and the odd shower. For a sunset cocktail event, the long evenings from June to August give you light until 9.30pm. For a daytime party, the morning or early afternoon slots are best to avoid the midday heat. Winter charters are possible (November to March) but less common for events, as the sea can be choppier and temperatures drop to 15 degrees C. However, if you want a unique Christmas or New Year's Eve party, some yachts are available with heated interiors.

How to Book Your Event Yacht on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters to select your port, date, number of guests and boat type. Each listing shows the maximum capacity, amenities and a photo gallery. Click on a yacht to see the full description and the charter company's contact details. You can send a booking request directly through the platform, specifying your event type, duration and any extras. The charter company will confirm availability and send you a quote. Payment is handled securely online, and you receive a confirmation voucher. For complex events (weddings, corporate functions), we recommend contacting the charter company at least two weeks in advance to arrange catering and crew. You can also read our blog for tips on planning a yacht event, including playlist suggestions and catering ideas.

Who Should Book a Luxury Yacht for an Event

This type of charter is for anyone who wants a private, movable venue. It suits: milestone birthdays (30th, 40th, 50th), wedding receptions or proposals, corporate team-building days or client entertainment, anniversary celebrations, and even small music or art events. If you are planning a bachelor or bachelorette party, a yacht adds a level of class that a bar cannot match. For business events, the quiet setting of a yacht allows for productive meetings with a view. Families celebrating a reunion also find yachts work well, because kids can swim off the back while adults socialise. The only real limitation is the number of guests: most yachts in the Marbella area can accommodate between 8 and 50 guests comfortably. For larger groups, you can charter multiple yachts or a superyacht.

Local Highlights You Can Include in Your Event Itinerary

Your skipper can tailor the route to include some of the Costa del Sol's best spots. A typical event cruise from Puerto Banús might head east to Cala del Faro, a secluded cove with turquoise water, perfect for a swim stop and photos. From Marbella Marina, you can cruise past the golden beaches and see La Concha mountain in the background. From Estepona, the route can go west towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you often see dolphins and even whales. If you have a full-day charter, you can go as far as the Nerja caves (east of Málaga) for a dramatic coastal view, but that is a long day (about 6 hours cruising each way). A more relaxed option is to anchor near the Río Verde estuary for a barbecue. The crew can also arrange for a local guitarist or flamenco dancer to come aboard for a short performance, adding a genuine Andalusian touch.

What to Bring and What Not to Bring

Most charter companies provide the basics: life jackets, first aid kit, and basic crockery. You should bring your own food and drink unless you have arranged catering. Many yachts have a fridge and ice maker, but check the size if you are bringing a lot of bottles. Bring non-marking shoes (white soles) to avoid damaging the deck. Sunscreen, hats and sunglasses are essential. Do not bring glass bottles if the yacht has a policy against them (some do, to avoid breakages). Do not bring illegal substances, as the skipper will cancel the charter. Also avoid bringing too many heavy bags, as space is limited. If you are bringing a cake or decorations for a birthday, confirm with the charter company first. For weddings, some yachts allow a small arch or floral arrangements, but it must be set up by the crew.

Frequently Asked Questions

How the Crew Enhances Your Luxury Event Experience

The skipper is not just a driver. On a luxury yacht hire for a Marbella event, the crew can make or break the day. A good skipper knows the best anchorages for your specific event, whether that is a quiet cove for a proposal or a lively spot near Puerto Banús for a party. They also handle all safety briefings, mooring and navigation, so you never have to think about it. For larger events, you can add a steward or hostess to serve drinks and canapés, keeping the party flowing without you lifting a finger. Private chefs are available on many yachts, preparing everything from sushi platters to a full Spanish paella cooked on the barbecue. Some charter companies even offer a DJ or a saxophonist for an extra charge. The crew works to your schedule, not the other way around, which is the whole point of a private charter.

Comparing Motor Yachts vs Catamarans for Events

If you are deciding between a motor yacht and a catamaran for your event, think about the experience you want. Motor yachts, like a 15-metre Azimut or a 20-metre Sunseeker, offer sleek lines and a sense of speed. They are ideal for a corporate event where you want to arrive in style, or a cocktail party with a sophisticated vibe. The interior saloon is usually air-conditioned, which matters in July. Catamarans, such as the Lagoon 620 or a 22-metre Fountaine Pajot, give you two or three times the deck space of a monohull of the same length. They are stable, so guests who get seasick will thank you. The wide aft deck is perfect for a buffet lunch or a dance floor. Catamarans also have a shallow draft, letting you anchor closer to beaches like Cala del Faro. For a wedding reception with 40 guests, a catamaran is often the better choice. For a small, intimate dinner for 10, a motor yacht wins on luxury.

What a Typical Event Itinerary Looks Like

Let us walk through a real example. You book a 18-metre motor yacht from Puerto Banús for a 40th birthday party, 15 guests, 4 hours (12pm to 4pm). The skipper picks you up at the dock at noon. You cruise east along the coast for 20 minutes, passing the Marbella skyline with La Concha mountain behind it. The crew serves welcome drinks (cava or gin and tonic) and canapés. You anchor at Cala del Faro for 90 minutes. Guests swim off the back platform, use the paddleboard, or just lounge on the foredeck cushions. Lunch arrives: a catering platter of jamón ibérico, prawns, salads and bread, or a paella cooked onboard. After lunch, you cruise back towards Puerto Banús, with music playing over the sound system. The skipper drops you at the dock at 4pm. Total cost: around EUR 2,800 for the yacht, plus EUR 600 for catering and drinks. No stress, no logistics, just a private party on the water.

Why Puerto Banús Is the Top Port for Event Charters

Puerto Banús is the most popular departure port for luxury yacht hire for events in Marbella, and for good reason. The marina itself is a spectacle: superyachts, luxury car dealerships and high-end boutiques create a glamorous atmosphere from the moment you arrive. Your guests can park easily in the underground car park or arrive by taxi. The port is a 10-minute drive from Marbella town centre and 45 minutes from Málaga airport. From the dock, you are minutes from the open sea. The sheltered bay means calm waters even on windy days. For evening events, the marina lights up, and you can return to a table at a beach club like Ocean Club or Purobeach. If you want a quieter start, consider Cabopino or Estepona, but for sheer wow factor, Puerto Banús is hard to beat.

How to Handle Catering and Drinks on Your Yacht Event

You have two options for food and drink on a luxury yacht event. First, you can bring everything yourself. Most yachts have a fridge, ice maker and basic plates and glasses. You stop at a supermarket like Mercadona or Carrefour on the way to the port. This works well for a casual barbecue or a bring-your-own picnic. Second, you can arrange catering through the charter company. Typical costs are EUR 30 to EUR 80 per person for a menu that includes starters, main course and dessert. Drinks can be BYO or supplied by the crew at cost plus a corkage fee. For a premium experience, a private chef costs around EUR 200 to EUR 400 extra, plus ingredients. Some yachts have a built-in barbecue on the aft deck, perfect for grilling fresh fish or meat. Always confirm the catering setup before the day, especially for dietary restrictions like gluten-free or vegan options.

What Happens in Bad Weather or Sea Conditions

The Costa del Sol is generally sunny, but the sea can get choppy, especially in winter or during a Levante wind. If the forecast shows high winds or rough seas, the skipper has the final say on whether to sail. Your safety comes first. In most cases, the charter company will offer you alternatives: a different route in sheltered waters, a later time slot when the wind drops, or a full refund if the trip is cancelled due to unsafe conditions. For events, it is wise to have a backup date, especially for weddings or milestone birthdays. The booking contract on BoatHire24 usually includes a weather clause. If you are flexible, the skipper might suggest a coastal cruise instead of anchoring, or a visit to a marina like Sotogrande where the water is calmer. Do not worry too much in summer: May to September sees calm seas 90% of the time.

How to Make Your Yacht Event Instagram-Worthy

Let us be honest, part of the appeal of a luxury yacht event is the photos. To get the best shots, book a yacht with a clean white exterior and a spacious foredeck. The golden hour (one hour before sunset) gives you the best light, especially with La Concha mountain or the Marbella coastline in the background. Bring a polarised lens filter to cut glare from the water. For group shots, the bow of the yacht or the flybridge works well. If you are celebrating a proposal or anniversary, ask the crew to anchor near Cala del Faro for a dramatic cliff backdrop. Some yachts have a distinctive feature like a Jacuzzi or a slide that makes for fun candid shots. Avoid using flash on the deck at night, as it creates harsh shadows. Instead, rely on the yacht's ambient lighting and the marina lights. And remember, the crew are happy to take photos for you while they handle the boat.

What to Expect When You Arrive at the Marina

On the day of your event, you arrive at the designated marina 15 minutes before departure. The skipper meets you at the designated berth, usually signposted with the yacht name. You will need to sign a charter agreement and provide a damage deposit (typically EUR 500 to EUR 2,000, held on your card and refunded after the trip). Bring ID for all guests, as the port authority may require a passenger list. The crew loads your bags, food and drinks onto the yacht. They give a short safety briefing: where the life jackets are, how to use the toilet, and the no-glass rule if applicable. Then you set off. There is no boarding pass, no security queue, no waiting. You walk from the car to the yacht in under five minutes. That is the whole point of a private charter: zero friction, maximum enjoyment.

For a standard group of 12 to 20, you are looking at catamarans in the 40 to 60 foot range, which have plenty of deck space, a trampoline net at the front for lounging, and a shaded saloon with a table for lunch.

You can depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, or Estepona. Most group charters head west towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro or east towards the dunes of Cabopino. If you want dolphins, the Strait of Gibraltar is a longer trip, but doable from Estepona or Sotogrande. The skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and your group’s preferences. You can anchor for a swim, use the paddleboard or kayak that some catamarans carry, or just float about with a cold drink. The point is that you are in control of the day, not a timetable.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Charter for a Group in Marbella

When you book a catamaran charter for a group in Marbella through BoatHire24, the base price includes the boat, the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary (usually up to 4 to 6 hours), and basic safety equipment. Some boats also include a host or hostess to serve drinks and food, but that is not always the case, so check the listing details or ask the owner before booking.

You are allowed to bring your own food and drink on most catamarans. Some owners charge a corkage fee if you bring alcohol, but many do not. If you want catering, the skipper can arrange a platter of Spanish ham, cheese, olives, bread, and fruit for around EUR 15 to EUR 25 per person. For a full sit-down meal, you might pay EUR 40 to EUR 60 per person, depending on the menu. Soft drinks, water, and ice are usually provided by the boat owner as part of the charter, but again, confirm that when you book.

Snorkelling equipment, paddleboards, and kayaks are often included or available for a small extra fee. Inflatables like a giant floating mat or a towable banana are sometimes available for an additional EUR 50 to EUR 100 per day. If you want a DJ on board, some catamarans have a sound system that you can connect your phone to, but a proper DJ setup with speakers and lights will cost extra, around EUR 200 to EUR 400 depending on the duration.

Fuel is included for the standard itinerary, but if you want to go further, like from Marbella to Gibraltar or up to Nerja, the skipper will charge extra for fuel. That can add EUR 100 to EUR 300 to the bill, depending on the distance and the boat's engine size. Always ask the owner about fuel policy before you confirm the booking.

Which Ports Can You Depart From for a Group Catamaran Charter

The most popular departure port for a catamaran charter Marbella group trip is Puerto Banús. It is the glitzy marina with the big yachts, the designer shops, and the restaurants. Your group can meet at the boat, have a coffee at a nearby cafe, and then set off. Puerto Banús is well connected by taxi and bus from Marbella town, and there is a large car park if people drive.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is another option, slightly less flashy but still central. It is closer to the old town, so you can combine a boat trip with a walk around the historic centre and a tapas lunch after the charter. Catamarans from Marbella Marina tend to be a bit cheaper than those from Puerto Banús because the berthing fees are lower, and that saving sometimes gets passed on to you.

Cabopino is a small marina east of Marbella, near the Artola dunes and the Cabopino beach. It is quieter and more laid-back. If your group wants a relaxed day with fewer crowds, Cabopino is a good choice. The catamarans there are usually smaller, up to 20 people, but the sailing area is beautiful, with the Cabopino dunes on one side and the open sea on the other.

Estepona marina is further west, about 15 minutes by car from Puerto Banús. It is a modern marina with good facilities and easy access to the coast. From Estepona, you can head towards the Strait of Gibraltar and see dolphins, or go east towards the Cala del Faro cliffs. Estepona has a charming old town with whitewashed buildings and flower-filled streets, so you could make a day of it before or after the charter.

Sotogrande is the most exclusive port on this list, located about 40 minutes west of Marbella. It is a private resort with a marina, golf courses, and polo fields. Catamarans from Sotogrande are often larger and more luxurious, suitable for groups of 20 to 40 people. The sailing area includes the Strait of Gibraltar and the coast of Algeciras. If your group is looking for a premium experience and does not mind the drive, Sotogrande is a solid option.

Benalmádena is east of Marbella, about 20 minutes by car. It has a large marina with plenty of restaurants and bars. Catamarans from Benalmádena can head towards the Costa del Sol coastline or go further east towards Málaga. This port is a good alternative if you are staying in the Benalmádena or Torremolinos area and do not want to travel all the way to Marbella.

How Much Does a Catamaran Charter for a Group in Marbella Cost

Prices for a catamaran charter Marbella group trip vary depending on the boat size, the duration, the season, and the departure port. For a half-day charter (4 hours) on a 40-foot catamaran that takes up to 12 people, you can expect to pay from around EUR 800 to EUR 1,200 in the low season (October to May). In the high season (June to September), the same boat costs from EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,800 for half a day.

For a full day (8 hours) on the same boat, the price ranges from EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500 in low season and EUR 2,000 to EUR 3,500 in high season. If you have a larger group of 20 to 30 people, you need a bigger catamaran, 50 to 60 feet, which costs from EUR 2,000 to EUR 3,500 for half a day and EUR 3,000 to EUR 5,000 for a full day in low season. High season prices can be 30 to 50 percent higher.

Luxury catamarans with crew, catering, and premium amenities can cost EUR 5,000 to EUR 10,000 or more for a full day. Superyacht catamarans that take 40 to 50 people are price on request, but expect to pay upwards of EUR 10,000 for a day charter. You can browse current prices and availability for different group sizes on the BoatHire24 search page.

Additional costs to consider: a deposit (usually EUR 500 to EUR 1,000, refundable if no damage), fuel surcharge for long distances, catering, extra water toys, and gratuity for the crew (10 to 15 percent of the charter fee is standard if you are happy with the service).

Best Time of Year for a Catamaran Charter Marbella Group Trip

The best months for a catamaran charter Marbella group trip are May, June, July, August, September, and October. July and August are the hottest, with average temperatures around 30 to 35 degrees Celsius, and the sea temperature is 22 to 26 degrees. These months are also the busiest, so you need to book at least two to three weeks in advance for a weekend charter. Weekdays are easier to get.

June and September are slightly cooler, 25 to 30 degrees, with fewer crowds and lower prices. The sea is still warm enough for swimming. May and October are shoulder months, with temperatures of 20 to 25 degrees and cooler evenings. You can still swim in May if the sun is out, but October can be a bit chilly for a dip unless you are hardy. The advantage of May and October is that prices are lower and availability is better.

Winter months (November to March) are not ideal for a group catamaran charter unless you are just going out for a short trip and staying in the marina area. The sea can be rough, and the weather is unpredictable. Some catamarans do not operate at all in winter, so check with the owner if you are considering a charter during that period.

What to Expect on the Day of Your Group Catamaran Charter

On the day of your catamaran charter Marbella group trip, you and your guests meet the skipper at the designated port at the agreed time. The skipper will give a short safety briefing, explain where the life jackets are, how to use the toilet, and what the itinerary is. Then you cast off and head out.

Most group charters start with a cruise along the coast, past the golden beaches and the cliffs of Cala del Faro. The skipper will find a sheltered spot to anchor for swimming, usually in a calm bay or near a beach. You can jump off the boat, use the paddleboard, or just lie on the trampoline net and soak up the sun. The crew will serve drinks and food if you arranged catering, or you can help yourself to what you brought.

After a couple of hours at anchor, you might cruise to another spot for a different view, or head back to port if you booked a half-day charter. For a full-day charter, you will have a longer stop for lunch, maybe at a beachside chiringuito where the skipper can moor the boat and you can go ashore, or you can eat on board. The skipper will then return to port at the end of the charter.

If you want to see dolphins, the best area is off the coast of Estepona and towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The skipper can take you there if the weather permits and if you have enough time. Dolphins are wild animals, so sightings are not guaranteed, but the chances are high in that area, especially in the morning.

Who Should Book a Catamaran Charter for a Group in Marbella

A catamaran charter Marbella group trip is suitable for almost any group that wants a private day out on the water. It works well for stag and hen parties because the boat is a contained space where everyone can socialise without worrying about other passengers. You can play your own music, drink your own drinks, and do your own thing. Just be aware that some boat owners have a no-stag or no-hen policy, so check the listing or ask before booking if you are a large group of 10 or more people in matching t-shirts.

Family reunions are another common use. Grandparents, parents, kids, and teenagers can all find something to do on a catamaran. The shallow draft of a catamaran means it can get close to beaches, so you can wade ashore easily. The stable platform is good for people who get seasick on monohulls. Kids can swim off the back or play on the paddleboard while adults relax on the deck.

Corporate groups use catamarans for team-building days, client entertainment, or celebratory events. The boat can be dressed up with banners or decorations if you want, and the crew can arrange a proper lunch or cocktail service. Some catamarans have a projector and screen for presentations, but that is rare; most corporate charters are about networking and having fun rather than working.

Friends celebrating a birthday, an anniversary, or just a weekend away also book group catamaran charters. It is a memorable way to spend a day together, and the photos from the boat look great on Instagram. The cost per person is lower than you might think, especially if you split it among a group of 10 or more. For example, a half-day charter for EUR 1,200 split among 12 people works out at EUR 100 per person, which is less than a day ticket for a theme park or a night out in a club.

How to Book a Catamaran Charter for a Group in Marbella on BoatHire24

Booking a catamaran charter Marbella group trip on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter your group size, the date you want, and your preferred departure port. The system will show you available catamarans that match your criteria. You can filter by price, boat length, amenities, and duration.

Once you find a boat you like, you can send an enquiry to the owner directly through the platform. You can ask questions about the itinerary, catering, cancellation policy, and anything else. The owner will respond with a quote and availability. If you are happy, you can book and pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent of the total) to secure the date. The balance is due on the day of the charter, usually in cash or by bank transfer.

Read the terms and conditions carefully before booking. Some owners have a minimum number of guests, a maximum number, a no-smoking policy, or a strict cancellation policy. If you need to cancel, you may lose your deposit or part of the fee, depending on how far in advance you cancel. Travel insurance that covers trip cancellation is a good idea for group bookings.

For more tips on planning a group boat trip, read our blog posts about group charters on the Costa del Sol. We cover topics like what to bring, how to choose the right boat, and how to keep everyone happy on the water.

What to Bring on a Group Catamaran Charter in Marbella

You do not need much for a catamaran charter Marbella group trip, but a few things make the day better. Bring sunscreen with a high SPF (the sun is strong on the water), a hat, sunglasses, and a towel. A light jacket or hoodie is useful for the afternoon breeze, even in summer. Swimwear is essential if you plan to swim. A change of dry clothes for the trip back is a good idea.

If you are bringing your own food and drink, pack it in a cool box or a bag that can be stored in the boat's fridge. Glass bottles are often not allowed on boats because broken glass is dangerous, so use plastic or cans. Bring plenty of water, especially if it is hot. Alcohol is fine, but pace yourself; the sun and the motion of the boat can amplify the effects.

If you have kids, bring their life jackets if they have specific ones they prefer, though the boat will have child-sized life jackets on board. Snorkel masks, fins, and wetsuits can be brought from home if you have them, or you can use the boat's equipment. A waterproof phone case or a dry bag is handy for keeping your phone and wallet dry.

Music is important for the vibe. Most catamarans have a Bluetooth speaker or a sound system that you can connect your phone to. Make a playlist beforehand so you do not have to fiddle with tracks while you are on the water. If you want a specific genre or a DJ, arrange that with the owner ahead of time.

Group Catamaran Charter Itinerary Ideas for Marbella

A standard itinerary for a catamaran charter Marbella group trip from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina heads west towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro. You cruise past the beach clubs of Puerto Banús, the golden sand of Marbella, and then the rocky coastline. The skipper will anchor in a sheltered cove near Cala del Faro for swimming and lunch. After lunch, you can cruise back along the coast, maybe stopping at a beach for a quick swim before returning to port.

From Cabopino, you can head east towards the Cabopino dunes and then into the open sea. A popular stop is the area near the Calahonda beach, where the water is calm and clear. You can also go west towards Marbella and Puerto Banús, but that is a longer trip. Cabopino is a good starting point if you want to avoid the crowds of the main marinas.

From Estepona, you have two main options. One is to go east towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro and the coast of Marbella. The other is to go west towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can see dolphins and maybe even whales if you are lucky. The Strait is about 30 minutes by boat from Estepona, so it is feasible for a half-day charter if you do not stop for long. A full-day charter from Estepona can take you to Gibraltar, where you can anchor near the Rock and see the monkeys from the water.

From Sotogrande, the most common itinerary is west towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You can combine dolphin watching with a stop at a beach near Tarifa or Algeciras. The water in this area is often choppier than the Marbella coast, so be prepared for a bit of motion. If the weather is calm, you can cross the Strait to the coast of Africa, but that is a full-day trip and requires a larger boat.

From Benalmádena, you can head east towards the beaches of Torremolinos and Málaga, or west towards Marbella. The coastline is more urbanised than the Marbella area, but there are still some nice coves near the cliffs of La Cala del Moral. The advantage of Benalmádena is that it is close to Málaga airport, so it is convenient if your group is flying in.

For a longer trip, you can charter a catamaran for multiple days and sail to the Nerja caves or even across to Morocco. That requires a different kind of booking, usually with a crew that stays on board overnight. Multi-day charters are available on request, and the price is typically EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000 per day depending on the boat and the crew.

faqs.q: How many people can a catamaran charter in Marbella hold for a group?
faqs.a: Most catamarans for group charters in Marbella hold between 10 and 30 people. Smaller catamarans (40 feet) take up to 12, while larger ones (50 to 60 feet) take up to 30 or 40. A few superyacht catamarans take 50 or more, but those are rare and more expensive.

faqs.q: Do I need a boating licence to charter a catamaran for a group in Marbella?
faqs.a: No. Every catamaran on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who handles navigation and safety. You and your group just relax and enjoy the day. No licence required.

faqs.q: Can we bring our own food and drink on a group catamaran charter?
faqs.a: Yes, on most catamarans you can bring your own food and drink. Some owners charge a corkage fee for alcohol, but many do not. Check the listing or ask the owner before booking. You can also arrange catering through the owner for an extra fee.

faqs.q: What is the cancellation policy for a group catamaran charter in Marbella?
faqs.a: Cancellation policies vary by owner. Typically, you lose your deposit if you cancel less than 7 to 14 days before the charter. Some owners offer a full refund if you cancel more than 30 days in advance. Read the terms before booking and consider travel insurance.

faqs.q: Can we see dolphins on a catamaran charter from Marbella?
faqs.a: Yes, dolphins are common off the coast of Estepona and towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The skipper can take you to areas where dolphins are frequently spotted, especially in the morning. Sightings are not guaranteed, but the chances are high in that area.

faqs.q: What time of day is best for a group catamaran charter in Marbella?
faqs.a: Morning charters (10:00 to 14:00) are cooler and calmer, with better chances of seeing dolphins. Afternoon charters (14:00 to 18:00) are warmer and sunnier, ideal for swimming. Full-day charters (10:00 to 18:00) give you the best of both.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book a catamaran for a group in Marbella?
faqs.a: In July and August, book at least two to three weeks in advance for weekends. Weekdays are easier. In May, June, September, and October, one to two weeks ahead is usually enough. For large groups (20+), book a month in advance to secure the best boats.

title: Speedboat Hire Puerto Banus Hourly – Quick Booking
metaDescription: Need speedboat hire Puerto Banus hourly? Quick booking for RIBs and speedboats from EUR 150/hr with skipper. Check availability now on BoatHire24.
h1: Speedboat Hire Puerto Banus Hourly, Quick Booking
intro:
If you want to get on the water fast without committing to a full-day charter, speedboat hire Puerto Banus hourly is the answer. You rent a RIB or speedboat by the hour, a licensed skipper handles the driving, and you can zip from Puerto Banus to the Marbella coastline, Cala del Faro, or even the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin spotting. No boating licence needed, no long-term commitment. Just pick a slot, pay for the hours you want, and go.

BoatHire24 lists hourly options from several operators based in Puerto Banus and nearby ports. Prices start from around EUR 150 per hour for a 30-40 hp RIB that seats 6-8 people. For a bigger speedboat with more power (100-250 hp), expect EUR 250-400 per hour. Every booking includes a skipper, fuel, and basic safety gear. You can book online in a few minutes and be at the dock within the hour if availability allows.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with Hourly Speedboat Hire in Puerto Banus

Hourly hire means you pay only for the time you use. Most operators offer 1-hour, 2-hour, or 3-hour slots. A 1-hour trip is enough for a quick blast along the coast to see the Golden Mile from the sea. Two hours lets you reach Cabopino beach or the dunes of Artola. Three hours opens up Estepona or even a run past the Gibraltar strait if conditions are calm.

Every boat comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, so you can relax and enjoy the ride. The skipper handles mooring, navigation, and safety. You don't need a boating licence or any previous experience. Fuel is included in the hourly rate, which is unusual for longer charters but standard for these short trips. Life jackets, first aid kit, and VHF radio are onboard.

Typical boats are rigid inflatable boats (RIBs) or small motor yachts. RIBs are fast, stable, and ideal for groups of 4-8. Some operators also offer smaller speedboats with outboard engines. All are well maintained and inspected before each trip.

Departure Ports for Hourly Speedboat Hire

Puerto Banus is the main departure point, but you can also hire from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, Benalmadena, or Sotogrande. If you stay near Puerto Banus, you can walk to the port and board within minutes. For other ports, check the distance from your accommodation.

Each port has its own character. Puerto Banus is glitzy, full of superyachts and designer shops. Marbella Marina is more relaxed with a fishing vibe. Cabopino is quieter, near the Artola dunes. Estepona has a charming old town. Benalmadena is lively with a large marina. Sotogrande is exclusive, near the Gibraltar border.

Most hourly rentals operate from Puerto Banus because it's the most popular base. Operators there have quick turnaround times and multiple boats available. You can book a slot as early as 9am or as late as 7pm, depending on the season.

Boat Options for Hourly Hire

The most common boats for hourly hire are RIBs (rigid inflatable boats). They range from 4.5m to 8m in length. A 4.5m RIB with a 30hp engine is fine for a couple or small family. A 6m RIB with 100hp can seat 6-8 and reach 30-40 knots. An 8m RIB with 250hp is a serious speed machine, hitting 50+ knots.

Some operators also offer small motor yachts (6-8m) for hourly hire. These are slower but more comfortable, with a cabin and seating area. They're better if you want a relaxed cruise rather than a speed thrill. A few places have licence-free day boats (no skipper required), but those are usually rented by the half-day or full day, not hourly.

For a true speed experience, go for a RIB. For a more luxurious feel, choose a small motor yacht. Prices vary accordingly: RIBs from EUR 150/hr, motor yachts from EUR 250/hr.

Pricing Guidance for Hourly Speedboat Hire

Prices depend on boat size, engine power, and season. In low season (November to March), you might find deals from EUR 120/hr for a small RIB. In high season (June to September), peak hours (afternoon) can cost EUR 200-300/hr. Evening slots (sunset trips) are often priced higher because demand is strong.

Here are typical price bands for hourly hire in Puerto Banus (2025):

  • Small RIB (4.5-5m, 30-60hp): EUR 150-200/hr
  • Medium RIB (6-7m, 100-150hp): EUR 250-350/hr
  • Large RIB (7-8m, 200-250hp): EUR 350-500/hr
  • Small motor yacht (6-8m, 150-200hp): EUR 250-400/hr

Prices are per boat, not per person. So if you have 6 people, a EUR 300/hr boat costs EUR 50 each per hour. That's cheaper than a cocktail at some Banus bars. Fuel and skipper are included, so no hidden costs. Some operators ask for a deposit (EUR 100-200) refunded after the trip, paid by credit card.

Best Seasons for Hourly Speedboat Hire

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and hot summers. The best months for speedboat hire are May to October, when sea temperatures are above 18 degrees C and the wind is light. July and August are peak season, with air temperatures around 30-35 degrees C and calm seas. The water is warm enough for swimming at stops.

In winter (November to March), the sea can be choppy and the wind stronger. Some operators still run hourly charters, but you'll need a windproof jacket. The advantage is lower prices and fewer crowds. Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) offer a good balance: pleasant weather, reasonable prices, and still enough daylight for a 2-hour trip.

Always check the marine forecast before booking. Wind above 20 knots can make small RIBs uncomfortable. Operators will cancel or reschedule if conditions are unsafe, and you'll get a full refund.

How to Book Hourly Speedboat Hire

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, select Puerto Banus as the port, choose the date and time, and filter by hourly rental. You'll see available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Select the boat, enter your group size, and complete the booking with a deposit. The balance is paid on the day.

You can also call or WhatsApp the operator directly via the contact details on the listing. Many operators offer last-minute bookings if they have availability. For a guaranteed slot, book at least 24 hours in advance, especially in summer.

What to bring: swimwear, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and a camera. The skipper will have water onboard, but you can bring your own drinks and snacks. No glass bottles on most boats. Leave valuables at your accommodation; there's limited dry storage on a RIB.

Who Is Hourly Speedboat Hire For?

Hourly hire suits anyone who wants a quick, flexible experience without a full-day commitment. It's popular with:

  • Couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise
  • Small groups of friends wanting a fun afternoon on the water
  • Families with kids who might get bored on a long charter
  • Business travellers with a few hours free
  • People staying in Marbella or Puerto Banus for a short break

It's not ideal for large groups (more than 8 people) or those who want to go far (e.g., to Nerja or Gibraltar). For longer distances, consider a half-day or full-day charter. For big groups, look at catamarans or larger yachts.

Local Highlights You Can See on an Hourly Trip

From Puerto Banus, you can see the La Concha mountain behind Marbella, the luxury villas along the Golden Mile, and the sandy beaches of San Pedro. If you head west, you pass the Cala del Faro lighthouse and the dunes of Cabopino. Eastward takes you past Marbella's old town and the marina. In 30 minutes, you're at the mouth of the Rio Verde, where you might spot seabirds.

Further out, if you take a 2-hour trip, you can reach Estepona's coastline or the dolphin-rich waters of the Strait of Gibraltar. The skippers know the best spots for dolphin watching (common dolphins, striped dolphins, sometimes pilot whales). Bring binoculars for a better view.

For a unique perspective, the hourly trip can include a stop for swimming in a secluded cove. The skipper will anchor off a quiet beach where you can jump in. The water is clear and refreshing, especially in summer.

Safety and Regulations

All hourly charters comply with Spanish maritime regulations. The skipper holds a valid Spanish licence (Patron de Embarcaciones de Recreo or higher). The boat is registered and insured. Life jackets are provided for all passengers, and children must wear them at all times. The skipper will give a safety briefing before departure.

You must be at least 18 years old to book. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. No alcohol is allowed for the skipper, but passengers can drink responsibly. The skipper reserves the right to cancel if passengers are intoxicated or behaving dangerously. In that case, no refund is given.

Weather cancellations are rare but happen. If the operator cancels due to bad weather, you get a full refund or can reschedule. If you cancel less than 48 hours before the trip, you may lose the deposit. Check the cancellation policy on the listing before booking.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a boating licence for hourly speedboat hire in Puerto Banus?

No. Every hourly hire includes a licensed skipper who operates the boat. You can just sit back and enjoy. This applies to all boats listed on BoatHire24.

Can I drive the speedboat myself?

No, for hourly hire the skipper stays onboard. If you want a self-drive experience, look for licence-free day boats (up to 15hp) rented by the half-day or full day. Those are available in Marbella and Estepona.

What is the maximum group size for an hourly speedboat?

Most RIBs seat 6-8 passengers including the skipper. Some larger RIBs can take up to 10. Check the boat's capacity on the listing. For bigger groups, consider a catamaran or motor yacht charter.

Can I bring my own food and drinks?

Yes, you can bring snacks and drinks. No glass bottles on most boats. The skipper will have water onboard. Some operators offer a cooler, but check in advance. Alcohol is allowed for passengers, but not for the skipper.

What happens if the weather is bad?

If the operator cancels due to unsafe weather, you get a full refund or can reschedule. If you cancel less than 48 hours before, you may lose the deposit. Check the specific policy on the listing.

How far can I go in one hour?

In one hour, you can cover about 15-20 NM (nautical miles) at cruising speed. That's enough to reach Cabopino from Puerto Banus or go past Marbella to the Rio Verde. Two hours gets you to Estepona or the Gibraltar area.

Is fuel included in the price?

Yes, fuel is included in the hourly rate for all listings on BoatHire24. No extra charges for fuel. The only extras might be a deposit (refundable) or optional extras like a GoPro rental.

Why Choose Puerto Banus for Hourly Speedboat Hire

Puerto Banus is the epicentre of luxury on the Costa del Sol, and hiring a speedboat by the hour lets you tap into that vibe without the full-day price tag. The marina itself is a spectacle: rows of superyachts, designer boutiques like Louis Vuitton and Gucci, and restaurants where a plate of jamon costs EUR 40. But from the water, you get a different perspective. You can cruise past the mega-yachts moored in the outer harbour, then open the throttle and leave the glitz behind in seconds. The contrast is part of the appeal. One minute you are staring at a EUR 20 million Azimut, the next you are skimming across open water with La Concha mountain as your backdrop. For a quick hit of adrenaline and a dash of Marbella glamour, hourly hire from Puerto Banus is hard to beat.

How Hourly Hire Compares to Half-Day or Full-Day Charters

If you are short on time or budget, hourly hire makes sense. A half-day charter (4 hours) typically costs EUR 600-1,200, and a full day (8 hours) can run EUR 1,200-2,500. With hourly hire, you pay EUR 150-500 per hour and can choose exactly how long you want. For a couple who just want to see the coast from the sea for an hour, that is a better deal. For a family with kids who might lose interest after 90 minutes, a 2-hour slot is ideal. The downside is that you cannot go as far. In one hour, you cover roughly 15-20 NM, which limits you to the coastline between Cabopino and Estepona. If you want to reach Nerja, Gibraltar, or the dolphin grounds near Tarifa, you need a half-day or full-day charter. Also, hourly hire usually means a fixed route determined by the skipper, whereas longer charters let you customise the itinerary.

Specific Boats Available for Hourly Hire in Puerto Banus

On BoatHire24, you will find several specific models for hourly hire. A common choice is the Zodiac Pro 650, a 6.5m RIB with a 115hp outboard, seating 6 passengers. It cruises at 25 knots and tops out at 35 knots. Another is the Brig Falcon 750, a 7.5m RIB with a 200hp engine, seating 8 and reaching 40 knots. For something smaller, the Highfield 540 (5.4m, 60hp) is good for 4 passengers and costs from EUR 150/hr. Some operators also offer the Quicksilver 675 (6.7m, 150hp) which is a bit more stable in choppy conditions. If you prefer a motor yacht, look for the Jeanneau Leader 8 (8m, 200hp) which has a small cabin and a toilet, priced from EUR 300/hr. Each listing on the site includes photos, specs, and the exact hourly rate, so you can compare before booking.

Best Times of Day for an Hourly Speedboat Trip

The time of day affects both the experience and the price. Morning slots (9am-11am) are the cheapest because demand is lower. The sea is often calmer, and the light is good for photos. Midday (12pm-2pm) is hot, especially in July and August, with air temperatures hitting 35 degrees C. The water is warm for swimming, but the sun is intense. Afternoon slots (3pm-5pm) are the most popular and most expensive. The sea breeze picks up, making the ride more exciting. Sunset trips (6pm-8pm) are also in high demand, particularly for couples. The price can be 20-30% higher than a morning slot. If you want to save money, book a 9am or 10am slot. If you want the best light and atmosphere, go for late afternoon or sunset. Just be aware that in winter, sunset is around 6pm, so a 2-hour trip starting at 4pm gives you the golden hour.

How to Combine Hourly Hire with Other Activities in Puerto Banus

An hourly speedboat trip fits neatly into a day of other activities. You can start with a morning coffee at one of the marina cafes, then take a 1-hour boat ride at 11am. After that, have lunch at a chiringuito on the beach, like the one at San Pedro de Alcantara. In the afternoon, visit the Puerto Banus designer shops or the nearby Rio Verde shopping centre. If you are staying at a hotel like the Marbella Club or Puente Romano, the boat can pick you up from the hotel's beach club. Some operators offer a "boat and beach" package: a 2-hour hire that includes a stop at a beach club where you can have a drink and swim. This is a good option if you want a mix of speed and relaxation. You can also combine hourly hire with a visit to the Estepona old town, which is a 15-minute drive from Puerto Banus. The boat drops you back at the marina, and you walk to the port.

What to Expect from the Skipper on an Hourly Charter

The skipper is not just a driver. They are a local guide who knows the coastline, the best swimming spots, and where to find dolphins. On an hourly charter, the skipper will take a route that shows you the highlights within the time limit. They will point out landmarks like the Cala del Faro lighthouse, the Artola dunes, and the luxury villas of the Golden Mile. They can also adjust the speed based on your preference: if you want a smooth cruise, they will keep it at 15-20 knots. If you want thrills, they will open it up to 30-40 knots, subject to sea conditions. The skipper will handle all mooring and anchoring, so you can jump straight into the water for a swim. They will also provide a safety briefing and ensure life jackets are worn. Most skippers speak English and Spanish, and some speak German or French. You can tip the skipper at the end if you are happy with the service, but it is not mandatory.

Hidden Costs and How to Avoid Them

Hourly hire on BoatHire24 is transparent: the price includes the boat, skipper, and fuel. But there are a few potential extras. Some operators charge a cleaning fee if the boat is left dirty (e.g., sand or food spills). To avoid this, use the onboard bin and wipe down seats before returning. If you break or damage equipment, you may be charged for repairs. Check the boat for existing damage before departure and take photos. A refundable deposit of EUR 100-200 is common, paid by credit card. This is returned after the trip if there is no damage. Some operators offer optional extras like a GoPro rental (EUR 30-50), a cooler with ice (EUR 20), or a bottle of cava (EUR 25). These are not required. For a group of 6, the total cost is the hourly rate divided by 6, so a EUR 300/hr boat costs EUR 50 per person per hour. No hidden fees for life jackets or safety equipment.

How to Get the Best Deal on Hourly Speedboat Hire

To get the best price, book in advance. Last-minute bookings in summer are often at full price. If you are flexible, try a morning slot (before 11am) or a weekday (Monday to Thursday). Weekends and holidays are the most expensive. Booking through BoatHire24 gives you access to multiple operators, so you can compare prices directly. Look for listings that say "fuel included" and "no hidden fees". Some operators offer a discount for booking 2 or 3 hours at once: for example, a 2-hour hire might be EUR 500 instead of EUR 300 per hour. Check the cancellation policy: a flexible policy (free cancellation up to 24 hours before) is better if your plans might change. Avoid booking through third-party aggregators that add service fees. BoatHire24 lists direct from operators, so you pay the same as walking into the marina office. If you are a returning customer, some operators offer a loyalty discount of 10-15%.

title: Motor Yacht Rental Marbella for Stag – Ultimate Fun
metaDescription: Motor yacht rental Marbella stag party with skipper, drinks, and DJ. Book your ultimate fun on the Costa del Sol. From Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina.
h1: Motor Yacht Rental Marbella Stag, Ultimate Fun at Sea
intro: You're planning a stag do in Marbella and you want something that doesn't involve another sweaty club or a hangover on a sun lounger. A motor yacht rental Marbella stag trip is the answer. You get a private boat, a licensed skipper who knows the coast, and enough space for the lads to let loose without bothering anyone else. Depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or any port on the Costa del Sol, and spend the day drinking, swimming, and pretending you're in a music video. No hidden fees, no dodgy deals, just a boat and a crew that handle everything.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Motor Yacht Rental Marbella Stag

A motor yacht rental Marbella stag isn't just a boat trip. It's a floating party base. You get the yacht for a set number of hours, usually 4, 6, or 8, with a professional skipper who knows the local waters. That means you don't need a licence or any experience. The boat comes with a sound system, a sun deck, a shaded saloon, and a toilet. Most yachts also have a fridge for your drinks and a grill if you want to cook. You can bring your own food and booze, or add on catering packages. Some operators even offer a DJ or a hostess if you want to go all out. The key point is that the skipper stays sober and handles the navigation, so you can focus on the fun.

Departure Ports for Your Stag Yacht Charter

You can start your motor yacht rental Marbella stag from several ports along the Costa del Sol. The most popular is Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina in Marbella where you'll see superyachts and Ferraris. It's close to the nightlife and has plenty of bars for a pre-boat drink. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a bit more relaxed and often cheaper. Cabopino is smaller and quieter, good if you want to avoid crowds. Estepona and Sotogrande are further west, with calmer waters and less traffic. Benalmádena is east of Marbella and has a lively port with restaurants. Each port gives you different scenery and sailing times. For a stag party, Puerto Banús is the classic choice, but any port works as long as you book the right boat.

Boat Options for a Stag Party

Not all motor yachts are the same. For a stag do, you want something with space, speed, and a bit of flash. A 40-foot motor yacht (around 12 metres) suits a group of 8 to 12 people. It has a flybridge, a sun pad at the bow, and a cabin below deck. A 50 to 60-foot yacht (15 to 18 metres) fits up to 20 guests and often has a bigger sound system and a more spacious saloon. For larger groups, a superyacht over 20 metres can take 30 or more, but those are price on request. RIBs and speedboats are faster and more adrenaline-focused, but they have less space and no toilet, so they're better for a short blast rather than a full party. Stick with a motor yacht for the full stag experience. You can see available models on the search page.

Pricing Guidance for a Motor Yacht Rental Marbella Stag

Prices vary by yacht size, duration, season, and extras. For a standard 40-foot motor yacht for 4 hours, expect from around EUR 1,200 in low season (October to April) and from around EUR 1,800 in high season (June to September). A 50-foot yacht for 6 hours starts from around EUR 2,500. Superyachts are price on request and can run into thousands. Fuel is usually included in the price, but check. Some operators charge extra for a DJ, a hostess, or a barbecue. The best way to get an accurate quote is to use the booking form on BoatHire24 and specify your group size and preferences. You pay a deposit upfront and the balance on the day, usually in cash or card.

Best Season for a Stag Yacht Party

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days a year. The best time for a motor yacht rental Marbella stag is May to September, when temperatures hit 25 to 35 degrees C and the sea is calm. July and August are peak season, so book at least two weeks in advance. April and October are cooler but still pleasant, with highs around 20 degrees C and fewer crowds. November to March is possible but risky, as the sea can be choppy and the wind strong. For a stag party, you want warm weather and flat water, so aim for late spring or summer.

What to Do on a Stag Yacht Charter

A motor yacht rental Marbella stag is about chilling, drinking, and messing about on the water. Most trips include a stop for swimming at a cove like Cala del Faro or Playa de la Vibora, where you can jump off the boat and snorkel. You can also anchor near Puerto Banús and watch the other yachts go by. Some groups bring a Bluetooth speaker and a playlist, but many yachts already have a sound system. If you want to add a bit of adventure, you can tow a inflatable banana or a doughnut ring, but that costs extra and requires a RIB. For a more relaxed vibe, just sunbathe on the deck and drink beer. The skipper will point out landmarks like La Concha mountain and the Río Verde estuary. If you head west, you might spot dolphins near the Strait of Gibraltar, but that's a longer trip of 6 to 8 hours.

How to Book a Motor Yacht Rental Marbella Stag

Booking is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage, enter your dates, group size, and port. You'll see available yachts with photos, specs, and prices. Choose one and send an enquiry. The operator will confirm availability and send a quote. You pay a deposit to secure the booking, usually 30 to 50 percent. The rest is due on the day. Make sure you read the terms: cancellation policies, weather clauses, and what's included. For a stag party, it's wise to book a boat with a toilet and a shaded area, because the Spanish sun is brutal. Also, check the maximum guest count, including the skipper. Some boats have a strict limit, and exceeding it can get you fined. If you have questions, the BoatHire24 blog has guides on what to expect.

Who Should Book a Motor Yacht Rental Marbella Stag

This is for groups of friends who want a private, no-BS party on the water. It's not for people who get seasick easily or who want a quiet day out. It works for stags of 6 to 20 people, but you can go smaller or larger if you find the right boat. The skipper is included, so no one has to worry about driving. You can drink as much as you want without risking a DUI. It's also a good option for bachelor parties where the groom wants something different from the usual strip club or golf. The yacht gives you a base to move around, swim, and party without being stuck in one spot. And because you're on the water, you get a different view of Marbella's coast, from the Nerja caves in the east to the Estepona old town in the west.

Legal and Safety Stuff

Every motor yacht rental Marbella stag includes a licensed skipper who is responsible for safety. The boat has life jackets, a first aid kit, and a VHF radio. The skipper will give a safety briefing at the start. You are allowed to bring your own alcohol, but glass bottles are often banned on board because they break and cut feet. Use plastic cups or cans. The skipper has the final say on where you go and when you return, especially if the weather turns. If you want to swim, the skipper will anchor in a safe spot. Smoking is usually allowed on the deck, but not inside the cabin. If you cause damage or leave a mess, you might lose your deposit. Keep it civil, and everyone has a good time.

Why Book with BoatHire24

BoatHire24 lists verified operators on the Costa del Sol with real photos and transparent pricing. You don't have to chase multiple companies or worry about scams. The platform handles the booking process and gives you direct contact with the boat owner. For a motor yacht rental Marbella stag, you can compare options side by side and read the details before you commit. The search page lets you filter by boat type, price, and port. The blog has tips on party planning and local recommendations. No fluff, just boats that work.

Choosing the Right Motor Yacht Layout for a Stag Do

The layout of the boat matters more than you think for a stag party. A flybridge motor yacht gives you an upper deck with a helm station and seating, which becomes the main social area. The bow sun pad is where people nap or tan. The aft deck usually has a table and bench seats for eating. Below deck, there is a cabin with a bed and a toilet, which is handy for changing or escaping the sun. For a group of 10 to 14, a 45-foot Sunseeker or Princess model works well because the cockpit is open and the sound system reaches everywhere. Avoid boats with too many enclosed spaces, as they trap heat and limit movement. If you want to impress the groom, go for a model with a hydraulic swim platform, which makes getting in and out of the water easier. Check the deck plan on the listing before you book.

Puerto Banús: The Obvious but Best Option for Stags

Puerto Banús is the epicentre of Marbella's party scene, so it is the natural starting point for a motor yacht rental Marbella stag. The marina itself is a spectacle, with 900 berths filled with superyachts, designer shops, and restaurants like Babilonia and Ocean Club. Your group can meet at a bar on the waterfront before boarding. The departure point is usually at the end of the main pier, near the statue of the bull. From Puerto Banús, you can cruise east towards Marbella's Golden Mile or west towards the exclusive villas of Sierra Blanca. The port is also close to the A-7 motorway, making it easy to reach from Málaga airport or your accommodation. The downside is that parking is expensive and the area is crowded in summer. Arrive 30 minutes early to avoid stress.

Cabopino and Estepona: Quieter Alternatives for Smaller Groups

If your stag group prefers a more laid-back vibe, consider departing from Cabopino or Estepona. Cabopino is a small marina east of Marbella with a sandy beach and a few chiringuitos. It is less flashy than Puerto Banús but has a friendly atmosphere. The waters around Cabopino are calmer, which is good if anyone in the group is prone to seasickness. Estepona, further west, has a renovated port with modern facilities and a promenade lined with restaurants. The old town of Estepona is worth a visit after the boat trip, with its whitewashed buildings and flower pots. Both ports offer cheaper berthing fees, so the charter price can be slightly lower than from Puerto Banús. For a group of 6 to 8, a 35-foot motor yacht from Cabopino costs from around EUR 900 for 4 hours in shoulder season. You get the same experience with less hassle.

What to Bring on a Stag Yacht Charter

Packing smart makes the day better. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen with SPF 50, and a hat. The sun reflects off the water and burns fast. Sunglasses are essential, preferably polarised to cut glare. Bring a dry bag for your phone and wallet, because splashes happen. For drinks, cans of beer, premixed cocktails, and plastic bottles of water are best. Glass is banned on most boats, so decant spirits into plastic flasks. Bring a cooler bag if the boat's fridge is small. Food wise, finger food like sandwiches, crisps, and fruit works well. A barbecue on the aft deck is possible on some yachts, but you need to pre-order the grill and bring your own meat. A Bluetooth speaker is redundant if the boat has a stereo, but bring one as backup. Do not bring valuables or white clothing, as stains from sunscreen and drinks are inevitable.

Typical Itinerary for a 4-Hour Stag Charter

A standard 4-hour motor yacht rental Marbella stag follows a predictable but effective route. You board at 11:00 or 15:00 from Puerto Banús. The skipper casts off and heads west towards the Marbella coastline. The first 30 minutes are spent cruising past the luxury hotels and villas of the Golden Mile. The skipper points out landmarks like La Concha mountain and the Marbella Club Hotel. After 20 minutes, the boat anchors at a calm spot near Cala del Faro or Playa de la Vibora. You swim, drink, and eat for about 90 minutes. The skipper then cruises back towards Puerto Banús, passing the Rio Verde estuary where you might see flamingos. The last 30 minutes are spent docking and settling the bill. Four hours is enough for a relaxed party, but if you want to go further or include a stop for lunch at a beach club, book 6 hours.

6-Hour and 8-Hour Stag Itineraries

A 6-hour charter opens up more options. You can head west towards Estepona and the Strait of Gibraltar, where dolphin sightings are common. The trip from Puerto Banús to the strait takes about 90 minutes each way, leaving 3 hours for swimming and lunch. Some groups combine a stop at a beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club, but that requires advance booking and a minimum spend. An 8-hour charter allows you to go east towards Cabopino and even as far as the Nerja caves, though that is a 2-hour cruise each way. For a stag party, 6 hours is the sweet spot, giving you time to relax without feeling rushed. The cost for a 50-foot yacht for 6 hours in high season is from around EUR 2,800. Make sure the itinerary is agreed with the skipper beforehand, as fuel costs can vary if you go further.

Adding Extras to Your Stag Charter

You can upgrade your motor yacht rental Marbella stag with optional extras. A DJ costs from around EUR 300 for 4 hours and brings his own equipment. A hostess or stewardess costs from around EUR 150 for 4 hours and helps with serving drinks and cleaning. A barbecue setup costs from around EUR 100 and includes a gas grill and utensils. Some operators offer a photographer or videographer for around EUR 200, which gives you a drone shot of the group on the bow. Inflatable toys like a banana boat or a doughnut ring cost from around EUR 150 and require a RIB to tow them. Food catering starts from around EUR 25 per person for a basic platter of Spanish ham, cheese, and bread. Premium packages with seafood and paella cost from around EUR 50 per person. Always confirm the extras in writing before the day.

Weather and Cancellation Policies

The Costa del Sol is sunny, but the weather can change. The skipper has the final say on whether the trip goes ahead based on wind speed and wave height. If the forecast is bad, the operator may cancel or reschedule. Most operators have a weather clause that allows a full refund or rebooking if the cancellation is made 24 to 48 hours in advance. If you cancel for non-weather reasons, you usually lose the deposit. For a stag party, it is wise to book a backup indoor activity like a paintball session or a brewery tour in case the sea is too rough. The best months for stable weather are June, July, and August, when the Levante wind is rare. September is also good, but the chance of afternoon storms increases. Check the marine forecast on Windy or similar apps before you confirm.

Cost Comparison by Season and Group Size

To give you a rough idea, here is a cost breakdown for a motor yacht rental Marbella stag based on typical listings. For a group of 8, a 40-foot yacht for 4 hours in May costs from around EUR 1,200. In August, the same boat costs from around EUR 1,800. For a group of 12, a 50-foot yacht for 6 hours in June costs from around EUR 2,500. For a group of 20, a 60-foot yacht for 8 hours in July costs from around EUR 4,500. These prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic equipment. Extras like a DJ or catering add 20 to 50 percent. The cheapest option is a 4-hour trip in April or October for a small group, from around EUR 800. The most expensive is a superyacht for 30 people in August, price on request but easily over EUR 10,000. Use the search page to get real-time quotes for your exact dates.
