bodyHtml:
What a Luxury Yacht Rental Puerto Banus Day Includes

A day charter typically runs from 10:00 to 18:00, though you can adjust start and end times. The boat comes with a professional skipper and sometimes a steward or host. Fuel, port fees, and VAT are usually included in the price. Onboard you get a sound system, sun pads, a shaded cockpit, and a bathroom. Some boats offer a paddleboard, snorkel gear, or a small tender for beach landings. You bring your own food and drink, or arrange catering through the charter company. The skipper knows the best spots along the coast: Cala del Faro for a quiet swim, Cabopino for lunch at a chiringuito, or the stretch near Estepona where dolphins often appear.

Puerto Banús: The Starting Point

Puerto Banús is the most famous marina on the Costa del Sol. It is where the superyachts dock and the shopping is a mix of Louis Vuitton and local jewellery. Departing from here means you are on the water within minutes of stepping off the dock. The marina has plenty of parking, a taxi rank, and restaurants for a pre-charter breakfast. If you are staying in Marbella town or the Golden Mile, it is a ten-minute drive. For a luxury yacht rental Puerto Banus day, this is the natural base. The boat will cruise past the iconic La Concha mountain, then head west towards the Strait of Gibraltar or east towards Cabopino and Cala del Faro.

Boat Options for Your Day Charter

Motor yachts from 12 to 30 metres are the most common choice for a luxury day out. They offer speed (20-30 knots), multiple decks, and cabins if you want to change or nap. Catamarans are more stable and have more deck space, ideal for groups who want to sunbathe and socialise. Sailing yachts give a quieter, more traditional feel, but they are slower. RIBs and speedboats are for thrill-seekers who want to reach a destination fast. Fishing boats are available if you want to combine luxury with a catch. Superyachts over 30 metres come with a full crew, Jacuzzi, and sometimes a helipad. Prices for a motor yacht start from around EUR 1,500 for a 12-metre boat, and go up to EUR 10,000 or more for a 25-metre superyacht. Catamarans are similar, while sailing yachts are slightly cheaper. Superyachts are price on request.

Where You Can Go on a Day Trip

From Puerto Banús, you have several options. Head east to Marbella Marina (20 minutes), Cabopino (30 minutes), or Cala del Faro (40 minutes). Cabopino has a sandy beach and a small marina with a beach club. Cala del Faro is a rocky cove with clear water, popular for swimming and snorkelling. Westbound takes you to Estepona (30 minutes), where you can anchor near the old town and walk up for tapas. Further west, the Strait of Gibraltar (90 minutes) is where you see dolphins and sometimes whales. If you have a fast boat, you can reach the Nerja caves (2 hours east), but that is a long day. Most charters stay within 15 nautical miles of the coast, so you can always see the mountains.

Pricing Guidance for a Luxury Yacht Rental Puerto Banus Day

Prices vary by boat size, age, and season. High season (June to September) is more expensive. A 12-metre motor yacht costs around EUR 1,500-2,500. A 15-metre catamaran is EUR 2,000-3,500. A 20-metre motor yacht with a flybridge is EUR 4,000-6,000. Superyachts over 25 metres start at EUR 8,000 and go up. All prices include skipper, fuel, and port fees. Catering is extra, typically EUR 30-50 per person for a lunch menu. Drinks are usually BYO. You can also book a half-day (4 hours) for about 60% of the full-day rate. Always confirm what is included before booking. Some boats charge extra for water toys or a host.

Best Seasons for a Day Charter

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, but the best months for a luxury yacht rental Puerto Banus day are May to October. Sea temperatures range from 18 degrees C in May to 26 degrees C in August. July and August are peak season, with calm seas and long daylight hours. April and November can be pleasant but cooler, with occasional wind. December to March is low season; many boats are in dry dock or undergoing maintenance. If you want a winter charter, check availability in advance. The water is too cold for swimming, but the views are still good.

How to Book a Luxury Yacht Rental Puerto Banus Day

You can browse boats on BoatHire24 and filter by size, type, and price. Each listing shows photos, specifications, and the skipper's experience. Once you find a boat, you send an enquiry or book directly through the platform. The operator will confirm availability and send a contract. Deposit is usually 30-50% of the total, with the balance due on the day. You can also call or email us for personalised recommendations. We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance in summer, one week in shoulder season. Last-minute bookings are possible but limited.

Who Is This Charter For

Couples celebrating an anniversary, groups of friends, corporate clients, or families with older children. The minimum age for passengers is usually 2, but check with the boat. Most boats have a maximum capacity of 10-12 passengers for safety and comfort. If you want a party boat, some operators allow up to 18. The skipper is responsible for safety and will enforce the rules: no glass bottles on deck, no jumping from the flybridge, and no excessive noise near other boats. This is a luxury experience, not a booze cruise. If you want a relaxed day with good food and a swim, this is it.

Local Highlights and Hidden Gems

Estepona old town is a short walk from the marina, with whitewashed buildings and flower pots. The Río Verde estuary is a nature reserve where you see birds and sometimes turtles. The Strait of Gibraltar is a marine protected area with a resident pod of common dolphins. If you anchor near Cabopino, you can walk to the sand dunes and have lunch at a beach bar. The Nerja caves are a longer trip but worth it if you have a fast boat and a full day. Your skipper knows the local conditions and will advise on the best route based on wind and swell.

What to Bring and Wear

Swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe preferred), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the evening. Non-slip shoes are useful on deck. If you plan to eat on board, bring your own food or arrange catering. Most boats have a fridge and a cooler. Alcoholic drinks are allowed, but the skipper cannot drink. Bring cash for tips (optional) or for buying from a beach vendor. The boat will have life jackets and safety equipment. You do not need a licence or any experience.

Frequently Asked Questions

Check our blog for more detailed guides on specific routes and boat types. You can also search for available boats directly on our site.

The Difference Between a Luxury Yacht and a Standard Charter

A luxury yacht rental Puerto Banus day is not the same as hiring a basic speedboat or a small fishing vessel. The difference is in the details: a professional crew (skipper plus steward or host), a higher level of finish on the boat (teak decks, leather upholstery, air conditioning in the saloon), and extras like a Jacuzzi, a swim platform, or a water slide. Standard charters might offer a clean boat with a skipper, but luxury means you are paying for comfort, service, and the ability to customise the day. If you want to arrive at a beach club in style, or have a gourmet lunch served on deck, you need a luxury yacht. The crew will handle the anchoring, the music, and the drinks. You just relax.

Puerto Banús vs Other Departure Ports for a Day Charter

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice for a luxury yacht rental Puerto Banus day, but it is worth comparing it to the other ports. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is closer to Marbella town and the Golden Mile, and it has slightly cheaper parking. Cabopino is smaller and quieter, with a sandy beach and a nature reserve. Estepona marina is modern but less glamorous, and it gives you quicker access to the Strait of Gibraltar. Sotogrande is exclusive but further south, and Benalmádena is east of Marbella. If you are staying in Puerto Banús, you save time and taxi fare. The marina itself is a spectacle: superyachts, Ferraris, and people watching. Departing from here adds to the experience.

Typical Itinerary for a Day Charter from Puerto Banús

A typical day starts at 10:00. You meet the skipper at the dock, load your bags and food, and do a safety briefing. The boat leaves the marina at 10:15. You cruise west for 20 minutes to the coast near Estepona, where the water is calm and the views of La Concha are clear. You anchor at 11:00 for a swim and snorkel. The crew serves drinks and snacks. At 13:00, you move to a spot near Cabopino or Cala del Faro for lunch. You can either eat on board or go ashore to a chiringuito. At 15:00, you cruise back towards Puerto Banús, passing the Marbella coastline. You arrive at 16:30, with time to shower and change before dinner. This is a relaxed pace. If you want a faster trip, you can go to the Strait of Gibraltar and be back by 17:00.

Cost Breakdown: What You Actually Pay For

When you book a luxury yacht rental Puerto Banus day, the price covers the boat hire, the skipper's fee, fuel for up to 8 hours of cruising, port fees for departure and return, and VAT at 21 percent. Some operators include a host or steward, others charge extra (around EUR 200-300 for the day). Water toys like a paddleboard, a kayak, or a floating mat are sometimes included, sometimes EUR 50-100 extra. Catering is always extra: a basic lunch menu for 10 people costs EUR 300-500, or EUR 30-50 per person. Drinks are BYO, but some boats have a bar package for EUR 15-25 per person. Tips for the crew are optional but common at 10-15 percent of the charter price. Always ask for a full breakdown before you pay the deposit.

Seasonal Variations in Weather and Availability

In May, the sea temperature is around 18 degrees C, and the air is 22-25 degrees C. You can swim, but it is brisk. June is warmer, 22-24 degrees C water, 28 degrees C air. July and August are peak: water 24-26 degrees C, air 30-35 degrees C, and the sea is flat calm most days. September is still warm, with water at 22 degrees C and fewer crowds. October is a gamble: water 18-20 degrees C, air 22-25 degrees C, but the wind can pick up. November to March is low season: many luxury yachts are in dry dock, and the ones that are available are often smaller. If you want a superyacht in winter, you need to book months ahead. The best value is in May, June, and September, when prices are 10-20 percent lower than July and August.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group

For a couple or a small group of 4-6, a 12-15 metre motor yacht is perfect. It has a cabin, a bathroom, and a decent deck space. For 8-12 people, a 15-20 metre catamaran gives you more room to spread out, with a large trampoline net at the front and a shaded cockpit at the back. For a party of 12-18, you need a 20-25 metre motor yacht with a flybridge. The flybridge is the best spot for socialising, with a bar, sun pads, and a second helm. Superyachts over 30 metres are for 18+ guests, with multiple decks, a Jacuzzi, and a full crew. RIBs and speedboats are fun for 6-8 people but not luxury in the traditional sense. Think about what you want to do: swim, eat, dance, or just cruise.

Hidden Costs and How to Avoid Them

The biggest hidden cost is fuel surcharges. Some operators quote a price that includes fuel for a certain number of hours, then charge extra if you go further or run the engines at high speed. Always confirm the fuel policy. Another cost is the host or steward: some boats include a crew member who serves food and drinks, others charge EUR 200-400 extra. Water toys are often listed as optional, so ask if they are included. Port fees at some destinations (like Cabopino or Estepona) are sometimes extra, around EUR 50-150. If you want to dock at a beach club for lunch, that is also extra. The best way to avoid surprises is to get a written quote that lists everything. On BoatHire24, we require operators to be transparent about what is included.

What to Expect from the Crew

The skipper is a licensed professional with years of experience on the Costa del Sol. They know the local waters, the wind patterns, and the best spots for swimming. They are not a tour guide, but they will offer suggestions. The host or steward (if included) will serve drinks, prepare food, and clean up. The crew works for tips, so treat them well. They are not allowed to drink alcohol while on duty. They will enforce safety rules: no running on deck, no jumping from high points, and no glass near the water. They are there to ensure you have a safe and enjoyable day. If you have special requests, tell them at the start. They can adjust the route, the music, or the menu.

Booking a Superyacht for a Day Charter

Superyachts over 30 metres are available for day charters from Puerto Banús, but they are rare and expensive. Prices start at around EUR 15,000 for a 30-metre boat and go up to EUR 50,000 or more for a 50-metre vessel. They come with a full crew of 4-8 people, including a captain, a chef, a stewardess, and a deckhand. Onboard you get a Jacuzzi, a saloon with a TV, a full galley, and multiple cabins. The experience is closer to a private resort than a boat trip. You can anchor off Cala del Faro and have a five-course lunch served on deck. Booking a superyacht requires at least a month of notice, and you will need to sign a detailed contract. Contact us for a quote.

Combining a Day Charter with a Beach Club Visit

Many luxury yacht rentals Puerto Banus day charters include a stop at a beach club. The most popular is Nikki Beach Marbella, located on the coast near Estepona. You anchor off the beach, and the club sends a tender to pick you up. You can have lunch on the beach or at a table, then return to the boat. Another option is the Ocean Club at Cabopino, which has a swimming pool and a restaurant. Some beach clubs require a minimum spend, typically EUR 50-100 per person for a sunbed and lunch. The skipper can arrange the booking in advance. This adds a land-based element to the day, giving you the best of both worlds: a boat ride and a beach club experience.

Environmental Considerations and Eco-Friendly Options

The Costa del Sol has strict rules about anchoring in seagrass meadows and protected areas. Your skipper will know where you can and cannot anchor. Some luxury yachts now offer eco-friendly features like electric engines for slow cruising, solar panels for power, and biodegradable cleaning products. If you care about the environment, ask the operator about their practices. You can also bring reef-safe sunscreen and avoid single-use plastics. The Strait of Gibraltar is a marine protected area, and dolphins are sensitive to noise. The skipper will keep a respectful distance. A luxury yacht rental Puerto Banus day can be sustainable if you choose the right boat and behave responsibly.

What a Catamaran Rental Estepona Sunset Includes

A typical sunset charter runs from around 18:30 to 21:30, depending on the season. You get a private catamaran, a professional skipper, and the freedom to cruise along the coast or drop anchor at a quiet cove. Most packages include a welcome drink, sometimes a small tapas platter, and an onboard sound system. You can bring your own wine or arrange catering through the charter company. Catamarans are ideal for sunsets because of their stability and wide deck space. You can sit on the forward netting, lounge on the aft deck, or stand at the helm. The shallow draft lets you get close to the shore, so you feel the warmth of the land meeting the sea. Expect a gentle breeze, not a rocking motion. That is the catamaran advantage.

Why Estepona for a Sunset Charter

Estepona has the best sunset position on the Costa del Sol. The town sits at the western edge of the coast, so the sun sets directly over the water, not behind hills or buildings. From the deck of a catamaran, you watch the sun slide into the Atlantic with no obstruction. The light changes every minute, deep orange, then violet, then a soft grey that lasts for another half hour.

The Estepona waterfront is less crowded than Puerto Banús or Marbella. You launch from the marina (Puerto Deportivo de Estepona), which is small and easy to navigate. No long queues, no security checks. You are on the water within ten minutes of arriving. The old town of Estepona is a short walk from the marina, with whitewashed streets and flower pots that look even better in the evening light. You can combine a pre-charter stroll with your sunset sail.

Available Catamarans for Sunset Charters

We list catamarans from 32 to 50 feet in Estepona. A 38-foot Lagoon or a 40-foot Bali are common choices. They sleep 6 to 12 people, but for a romantic evening you will want a smaller group, maybe just the two of you, or a couple of friends. The larger cats have a flybridge, which gives you a higher viewpoint for photos. The smaller ones are more intimate and easier to manoeuvre close to the coast.

Every catamaran has a bimini or hardtop for shade, but you will not need it at sunset. You want the open deck. Check the listing for details on the sound system, the galley, and the toilet facilities. Some catamarans have a grill on the back, so you can cook fresh fish if you book a longer charter. For a sunset trip, you are better off with pre-prepared food and a cooler full of Spanish wine.

Pricing Guidance for a Sunset Catamaran in Estepona

A private catamaran rental Estepona sunset starts from around EUR 400 for a two-hour evening charter on a 35-foot cat, up to EUR 1,200 for a four-hour trip on a 50-foot Lagoon with full catering. The price includes the skipper, fuel for the local area, and basic insurance. Extras like gourmet catering, open bar, or a photographer cost more. You can book through BoatHire24 with transparent pricing, no hidden fees.

Peak season (June to September) is more expensive and books out weeks in advance. Shoulder months (May and October) offer better value and still have warm evenings. Off-season (November to April) can work if you pick a clear day, but the sunset is earlier and the temperature drops. The best compromise is late May or early September, warm, fewer crowds, and lower prices.

Best Sunset Routes from Estepona Marina

The classic sunset route heads west towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You cruise past the Punta de la Doncella lighthouse, then open up the throttle towards the Bahía de Estepona. The water is calmer here, and you can see the African coast on a clear day. Dolphins are common in this area, they feed in the late afternoon. The skipper will slow down if they appear.

Another option is to head east towards the Costalita cove and the Cala del Faro. This route keeps you closer to the shore, with views of the Estepona hills and the Sierra Bermeja mountains. The sunset light reflects off the white houses of the old town. You can anchor at Cala del Faro for a swim if the water is still warm enough. The depth is shallow, so you can step off the catamaran into the sea.

A third route goes to the Río Guadalmina area, where the river meets the sea. This is quieter, with fewer boats. The water is clearer here because of the sand bottom. You can watch the sunset from the anchor, then cruise back to the marina under the stars. The skipper will turn on the navigation lights, and you get a second show, the lights of Estepona reflecting on the water.

What to Bring for a Sunset Catamaran Trip

Pack light but smart. A jumper or a light jacket is essential, the wind picks up after sunset and the temperature drops by 5 to 10 degrees Celsius. Non-slip shoes are a good idea, but barefoot is fine on the deck. Sunscreen is still needed even at 6pm, the UV reflects off the water. Bring a camera or a phone with a good night mode. The photos from a catamaran at sunset are the ones you will frame.

If you are planning a romantic evening, bring a small gift, a bottle of Cava, some chocolate, or a playlist. The skipper can handle the rest. Do not bring glass bottles unless they are allowed by the charter company; some prefer plastic or cans for safety. A waterproof bag for your phone is useful if you want to take photos from the netting.

How to Book a Catamaran Rental Estepona Sunset

Booking through BoatHire24 takes five minutes. Select Estepona as the port, choose a catamaran from the list, and pick your date. You will see the available time slots, sunset trips are usually listed as "evening charter" or "sunset cruise". Enter the number of guests, confirm the extras, and pay a deposit. The balance is due on the day, usually in cash or card to the skipper.

We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance for summer dates. For a last-minute trip, check the availability page, some charters have cancellations that open up slots. You can also contact the charter company directly through the listing. The skipper will send you the exact meeting point at the marina and a contact number. Arrive 15 minutes early to park and find the boat.

Who Is This For

A catamaran rental Estepona sunset is for couples, small groups of friends, or anyone who wants a private experience without the hassle of a public tour. It works for proposals, anniversaries, birthdays, or just a memorable evening. It is not for large parties or loud events, the catamaran is a quiet space. If you want a party boat, look at a motor yacht with a sound system and a dance floor.

Families with children are welcome on most catamarans, but check the age policy, some skippers prefer no children under 5 for evening charters due to safety. The skipper is responsible for the boat and the itinerary, so you can relax without worrying about navigation or weather. The only decision you need to make is whether to have another glass of wine.

Combining Your Sunset Charter with Estepona

Estepona has a lot to offer beyond the marina. The old town is a 10-minute walk from the port, with tapas bars, ice cream shops, and the famous Orchidarium. You can have a late dinner after the charter at a seafood restaurant on the waterfront, try the grilled sardines or the fried squid. The sunset charter ends around 9pm, so you have the whole evening ahead.

If you are staying in the area, consider a day charter to the Nerja caves or a dolphin-watching trip in the Strait of Gibraltar. The same catamaran can be booked for a full day, but the sunset slot is the most popular. For more ideas, check the BoatHire24 blog for guides on Estepona, Costa del Sol boat trips, and the best sunset spots.

Weather and Sea Conditions for Sunset Charters

The Costa del Sol has consistent weather from May to October. Afternoon winds (the Poniente) pick up around 3pm and drop by 6pm, so the sunset cruise is usually calm. The sea temperature in summer is 22 to 26 degrees Celsius, comfortable for a quick swim. In winter, the temperature drops to 15 degrees, and the wind can be stronger. The skipper will check the forecast and may suggest a different route or time if conditions are marginal.

If the weather is bad, the charter company will offer a reschedule or a refund. We recommend booking a flexible policy or choosing a date with a backup day. The sunset is guaranteed to happen, but the visibility depends on the clouds. Even a partly cloudy sky makes for a dramatic sunset, the colours bounce off the clouds and create a show that lasts longer.

Why Book Through BoatHire24

BoatHire24 is a marketplace, not a tour operator. We list catamarans from multiple charter companies in Estepona, so you can compare prices, boat sizes, and inclusions. Every listing has real photos, a detailed description, and verified contact information. You book directly with the charter company, and we provide support if anything goes wrong. No markups, no hidden fees.

We have been operating on the Costa del Sol for years, and we know the local skippers and the best sunset spots. Our team can recommend a specific catamaran based on your group size and budget. Call or email us before booking if you have questions. We want you to have the best sunset of your life, and we know exactly how to make that happen.

The Best Catamarans for a Romantic Sunset in Estepona

For two people, a 32-foot Lagoon 380 is a solid choice. It has a forward sunbathing area, a small galley, and a cabin if you want to freshen up. The cockpit is shaded by a bimini, but you will want to sit on the bow netting for the sunset. A 40-foot Bali Catamarans Open Space has a folding transom that creates a swim platform. You can sit with your feet in the water while the sun goes down. The Bali is wider than the Lagoon, so you get more deck space per person.

If you want a flybridge, the Lagoon 450 or the Fountaine Pajot Astrea 42 have a raised helm station with a second seating area. The flybridge gives you a 360-degree view, which is useful for spotting dolphins and for taking photos without other passengers in the frame. The downside is the stairs, but for a sunset charter you are not moving around much. The skipper will anchor early, so you can sit on the flybridge with a drink and watch the show.

What You Pay for a Sunset Catamaran in Estepona

A two-hour sunset charter on a 35-foot catamaran costs from around EUR 400 to EUR 600. A three-hour trip on a 40-foot cat with a flybridge and basic catering runs EUR 800 to EUR 1,000. A four-hour premium charter on a 50-foot Lagoon with a full bar and gourmet tapas is EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,600. These are private charters, not shared tours. The price includes the skipper, fuel for the local area, and standard insurance.

Extras that add cost: an open bar with premium spirits (EUR 150 to EUR 300), a photographer (EUR 200 to EUR 400), flowers or decorations (EUR 50 to EUR 150), and a custom menu from a private chef (EUR 100 to EUR 200 per person). Some charter companies offer a "romance package" that includes a bottle of Cava, strawberries, and a bouquet. Ask when you book. The deposit is usually 30% to 50% of the total, and the balance is due in cash or card on the day.

When to Book for the Best Sunset Experience

The sunset time in Estepona varies by season. In June, the sun sets around 21:40, so a 19:00 to 22:00 charter gives you the golden hour and the afterglow. In September, sunset is around 20:30, so a 18:00 to 21:00 trip works. In October, sunset is around 19:30, and the temperature drops to 18 degrees by the end. The best months for a sunset charter are June, July, August, and September. The air temperature is 28 to 32 degrees during the day and 22 to 26 degrees at sunset.

Book a Monday to Thursday charter for lower prices and fewer boats on the water. Friday and Saturday evenings are the most popular, so prices are higher and availability is tighter. If you want a specific catamaran, book three to four weeks ahead in summer. For a last-minute booking, check the listings on BoatHire24 for cancellations. Some charter companies offer a discount if you book within 48 hours, but the selection is limited.

What Happens If the Weather Is Bad

The skipper will cancel if the wind is above 25 knots or if there is a risk of thunderstorms. The Costa del Sol has reliable weather, but the Levante wind can blow from the east and create choppy seas. In that case, the charter company will offer a reschedule or a full refund. If the weather is marginal, the skipper may suggest a shorter route or a later start time. You can also choose a catamaran with a full enclosure, which blocks the wind and keeps you warm.

We recommend booking a flexible cancellation policy. Some charter companies offer free rescheduling up to 48 hours before the charter. Others charge a fee. Check the terms before you pay the deposit. If you are visiting for a short time, book a backup date. The weather in Estepona is good 80% of the time in summer, but it is better to have a plan B.

How to Get to Estepona Marina

Estepona Marina is at Avenida de España, just west of the old town. Parking is available at the underground car park next to the marina, cost around EUR 2 per hour. If you are staying in Marbella, it is a 20-minute drive west on the A-7. From Puerto Banús, it is 15 minutes. From Sotogrande, it is 25 minutes east. The marina entrance is easy to find, look for the large white building with the "Puerto Deportivo" sign.

The meeting point is usually at the fuel dock or the main pier. The skipper will send you the exact location and a contact number the day before. Arrive 15 minutes early to park and find the boat. If you are late, the skipper may shorten the charter or charge a waiting fee. The marina has a small supermarket and a few cafes if you need to buy snacks or drinks before boarding.

What to Do After the Sunset Charter

Estepona old town has dozens of restaurants within a 10-minute walk from the marina. Try La Escollera for grilled fish, El Rincón de Estepona for tapas, or La Casa del Rey for paella. Most places serve dinner from 20:00 to 23:00, so you can eat after the charter. If you want a late drink, the bars on the marina front stay open until 01:00. The atmosphere is relaxed, not loud.

For a romantic evening, book a table at a restaurant with a sea view. The sunset charter ends around 21:00 to 22:00, so you can walk from the marina to the restaurant in five minutes. The old town streets are lit with string lights, and the flower pots on the walls make for a good photo. If you want to stay on the water, some charter companies offer a dinner option where the caterer brings the food to the boat. You eat at anchor while the stars come out.

Who Should Not Book a Sunset Catamaran

If you get seasick easily, a catamaran is the best choice, but even a catamaran can rock in a swell. If the sea is choppy, you may feel movement. Take a motion sickness pill an hour before the charter. If you are on a tight budget, a sunset catamaran is not the cheapest option. A shared sunset cruise on a motor yacht costs from EUR 50 per person, but you share the boat with strangers. A private catamaran is for people who want privacy and flexibility.

If you want a party with loud music and dancing, a catamaran is too quiet. Look for a motor yacht with a DJ and a dance floor. If you want to fish, a sunset charter is not the right time. Fish feed in the early morning or late afternoon, but the sunset charter is for relaxing, not for catching. If you want to swim, check the water temperature. In winter, the sea is 15 degrees, too cold for a comfortable swim. In summer, it is fine.

How to Make the Sunset Charter More Special

Bring a bluetooth speaker if the catamaran does not have a good sound system. Create a playlist of slow songs, jazz, or Spanish guitar. Ask the skipper to anchor at a quiet spot away from other boats. The Cala del Faro area is usually empty in the evening. If you are celebrating an anniversary or a proposal, tell the skipper in advance. They can help with timing and positioning. Some skippers have a bottle of Cava ready for the toast.

Take photos during the golden hour, which starts about an hour before sunset. The light is warm and soft. Use a tripod or a stabiliser for video. The reflection of the sunset on the water is better from the bow netting than from the cockpit. If you have a drone, check the local regulations. You cannot fly over the marina or near the port, but you can launch from the catamaran once you are away from the shore. The skipper can advise on the best spots.

h1: Motor Yacht Hire Puerto Banus for Party
keyword: motor yacht hire puerto banus party
intro:
So you want to throw a party on a motor yacht in Puerto Banus. Good call. The marina is the epicentre of Marbella's nightlife, and a private yacht is the only way to do it without queuing for a drink or fighting for a seat. You get your own floating club with a skipper, a sound system, and a crew who won't judge your playlist. We'll tell you what you need to know to make it happen, from boat sizes to budgets and the best spots to anchor.

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, so you don't need a licence or any experience. The boat is yours for the day or evening. You bring the guests, we bring the boat. Here's how to get your motor yacht party sorted in Puerto Banus.
bodyHtml:
Why Puerto Banus for a Motor Yacht Party

Puerto Banus is the obvious choice for a party on the water. The marina is lined with bars, restaurants, and superyachts, and the atmosphere is loud and unapologetic. You can start the evening on your yacht, then head to one of the beach clubs or continue at a port-side spot. The harbour itself is a spectacle, and your boat becomes part of the show.

The water around Puerto Banus is calm, sheltered by the coast and the breakwater. That means you can anchor close to the shore, swim off the back, and still be within walking distance of the marina if you need to pick up more ice or forgot the speaker. The sunsets are reliably good, and the sea temperature in summer hits 24 degrees C, so swimming is optional but recommended.

If you want to escape the crowds, you can head east towards Cala del Faro or west to the coast near Estepona. Both are short cruises and give you a quieter spot to drop anchor. Your skipper will know the best coves for the conditions and your vibe.

What's Included in a Motor Yacht Party Charter

When you book a motor yacht for a party through BoatHire24, the basics are always the same. You get the boat, the skipper, and fuel for a standard itinerary. Most boats also include a host or stewardess to keep the drinks flowing and the canapes coming. Some come with a barbecue on the back deck, a sound system with Bluetooth, and a freshwater shower for rinsing off after a swim.

What you don't get automatically is food and drink. You can bring your own, or ask the charter company to arrange catering. Many will offer a menu of options from simple platters to full sit-down dinners. For a party, you probably want finger food and plenty of ice. Some boats have a fridge and an ice maker, but check before you rely on it.

If you want a DJ, a photo booth, or a specific type of music, you need to arrange that separately. The crew will usually accommodate reasonable requests, but don't expect a full production unless you pay for it. The boat is the venue, not the event planner.

Motor Yacht Sizes for a Party

The size of the motor yacht you need depends on how many people you want to invite and how much space you want. A 12-metre motor yacht can comfortably host 8 to 10 guests for a party. You get a saloon, a rear deck, and maybe a small sun pad. It's cosy but workable.

For 15 to 20 guests, you want something around 15 to 18 metres. These boats have a larger flybridge, a proper saloon with seating, and a decent swim platform. You can spread out and not feel like you're in a lift.

If you're planning a blowout for 30 or more, you need a 20-metre-plus motor yacht or a superyacht. These have multiple decks, a bar, a dance floor, and cabins you can use for changing or storage. Prices go up sharply, but so does the wow factor. Check the search page for boats by guest capacity and length.

Pricing Guidance for Motor Yacht Party Hire

Prices for motor yacht hire in Puerto Banus vary by size, season, and duration. For a half-day party charter (4 hours) on a 12-metre motor yacht, expect from around EUR 2,000. A full day (8 hours) on a 15-metre boat starts around EUR 3,500 to EUR 5,000. For a 20-metre-plus yacht with a crew of four, you are looking at EUR 8,000 to EUR 15,000 for a full day.

Evening charters are generally the same price as day charters, but some companies offer a discount if you start after 6pm. Fuel is often included for a standard itinerary within 15 nautical miles of the port. If you want to go further, say to Marbella or Estepona, there may be a fuel surcharge. Always ask for a full quote before booking.

High season (June to September) commands a premium of 20 to 30 percent over spring and autumn. July and August are the most expensive and the busiest. If you want a specific boat, book at least two weeks ahead. For a Saturday in August, book a month in advance.

Departure Ports for Your Party

Puerto Banus is the most popular departure port for a party, but you are not limited to it. You can also charter from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmadena. Each has its own character and proximity to different anchorages.

If you leave from Puerto Banus, you are right in the action. The marina itself is a party destination, and you can step off the boat straight into a restaurant or club. If you want a more relaxed start, consider Cabopino, which is quieter and has a smaller, sandier beach nearby. Estepona is a good choice if you want to combine the party with a visit to the old town or the port itself.

For a truly exclusive feel, charter from Sotogrande, which is about 30 minutes west of Puerto Banus. The marina is upmarket and less crowded. Your party will feel like a private event rather than one among many. Benalmadena is further east, near Torremolinos, and is a good option if you are staying on that side of the coast.

Best Time of Year for a Motor Yacht Party

The summer months from June to September are the obvious choice. The weather is hot, the sea is warm, and the evenings are long. July and August are peak season, with temperatures around 30 degrees C and water at 24 degrees C. The downside is that the coast is busy, and you may need to share anchorages with other boats.

May and October are underrated. The temperature is still in the mid-20s, the water is swimmable, and the crowds are thinner. You might get an occasional cloudy day, but the party won't be ruined. Prices are lower, and availability is better.

Winter charters are possible but less common. The temperature drops to around 15 degrees C, and the sea can be choppy. If you are set on a winter party, choose a motor yacht with a heated saloon and enclosed flybridge. It can still be a good time, but it is not the same as a summer blowout.

How to Book Your Motor Yacht Party

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You browse the available motor yachts, check the guest capacity and amenities, and send an enquiry. The team will confirm availability and send you a quote. Once you accept, you pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) and the balance is due two weeks before the charter.

You can also add extras like catering, a DJ, or water toys. The charter company will arrange these for an additional fee. Make sure you communicate your requirements clearly when you book. The crew will appreciate knowing what kind of party you want so they can prepare accordingly.

If you are unsure which boat to choose, call or email. The team can recommend a boat based on your group size, budget, and preferred vibe. They have been on most of the boats and know which ones have the best sound systems and the biggest sun decks.

Who This Is For

Motor yacht hire for a party in Puerto Banus is not for everyone. It is for groups who want to celebrate something specific: a birthday, a bachelor or bachelorette, a corporate milestone, or just a weekend with friends who like to have a good time. It works best when everyone is on board with the plan and the vibe is social.

It is less suited to quiet family outings or romantic dinners. If you want a peaceful day on the water, consider a sailing yacht or a catamaran. They are more stable and generally quieter. For a party, a motor yacht is the right tool. It is fast, loud, and built for socialising.

If you are looking for a licence-free day boat, those are available too, but they are smaller and less suited to a party. They are fine for a small group who want to drive themselves, but for a proper party, you want a skipper and a bigger boat.

Local Colour and Things to Do Around Puerto Banus

Puerto Banus is not just the marina. The area has plenty to offer if you want to extend your party into the evening. The beach clubs like Ocean Club and Nikki Beach are within walking distance. The old town of Marbella is a short taxi ride away and has a different, more traditional vibe.

If you are anchoring near Cala del Faro, you can swim to the beach or take a tender ashore. The cove is quiet and has a small restaurant on the sand. Estepona old town is worth a visit if you have time. It has whitewashed streets and flower-filled balconies, a contrast to the glitz of Puerto Banus.

For a longer trip, you can head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The crossing can be choppy, but the reward is the chance to see dolphins and maybe even whales. The crew will know the best spots and the conditions. It makes for a memorable party backdrop.

If you want to read more about the local scene, check the blog for guides to Puerto Banus nightlife, the best anchorages, and tips for chartering on the Costa del Sol.

Sound Systems and Party Tech on Board

Not all motor yachts have the same audio setup. Some come with a basic Fusion stereo and four speakers, fine for background music. Others have a full JL Audio system with a subwoofer, amplifiers, and speakers on every deck. If you want to dance, ask for a boat with a decent flybridge setup. The best party boats have a dedicated DJ area on the aft deck or flybridge, with a mixer and XLR inputs. You can plug in a laptop or USB stick. Bluetooth is common, but it can drop out over distance. Bring a wired backup. Some superyachts have a built-in karaoke system or a projector for visuals. Check the spec list before you book. The crew can usually set up a playlist, but they are not DJs. If you want a proper set, hire one separately. Expect to pay EUR 300 to EUR 800 for a DJ for the day, depending on their gear and reputation.

Food and Drink Logistics for a Party Charter

Most charter companies allow you to bring your own alcohol. That saves money compared to buying from the boat's bar, but you need to bring enough ice. A typical party of 15 people will go through 20 to 30 kg of ice in a day. Some boats have an ice maker, but it is usually small. Bring coolers or ask the crew to stock extra ice. For food, finger food works best on a moving boat. Think sliders, skewers, sushi, dips, and fruit platters. A sit-down meal is possible on larger yachts with a dining table, but it takes up space and time. If you want a barbecue, check the boat has a fixed grill. Many catamarans have one, but motor yachts often rely on the galley. You can order catering from companies like Taste of Marbella or La Sala, who deliver to the marina. Allow EUR 40 to EUR 80 per person for decent catering, depending on the menu. If you want a full bar setup, some companies offer a mixologist for an extra EUR 200 to EUR 400. They will make cocktails, mocktails, and keep the glasses clean.

Anchorage Spots for Party Boats Near Puerto Banus

The best anchorage for a party is just outside Puerto Banus, near the sandbar off the mouth of the Rio Verde. The water is shallow, about 5 to 8 metres deep, and the bottom is sand. You can anchor close to other boats and the vibe is social. The beach is a short swim away. Another option is Cala del Faro, a small cove east of Puerto Banus. It is quieter but still within 15 minutes of the marina. The water is clear and there is a beach bar on the sand. If you want more space, head west to the coast near Estepona. The area around the Estepona lighthouse has wide sandy beaches and good holding. You can anchor in 10 metres and have room for water toys. For a sunset party, the stretch between Puerto Banus and Marbella is hard to beat. The sun sets over La Concha mountain, and the light is golden. Your skipper will know the best spot for the wind and swell. Avoid anchoring near the main shipping channel or the entrance to Puerto Banus. The wake from passing boats will ruin the party.

Water Toys and Activities to Add to Your Party

A party on a motor yacht does not have to be static. Most charter companies offer water toys as add-ons. A Seabob runs about EUR 200 to EUR 350 for a half-day rental. A jet ski is EUR 300 to EUR 500 for an hour. A paddleboard or kayak is usually included or costs EUR 50 to EUR 100. If you want a towable inflatable, like a banana boat or a donut, that is EUR 150 to EUR 250 for a session. For a bigger group, consider a floating platform or a water trampoline. These are rare on motor yachts but can be arranged with a support boat. Some superyachts have a slide off the deck, but you need to check the boat's insurance. The crew will supervise all activities. They will not let you use the jet ski if you have been drinking heavily. That is a safety rule, not a killjoy. If you want to swim, bring your own towels. The boat provides a freshwater shower to rinse off. The sea temperature in summer is 24 degrees C, so swimming is comfortable for hours.

What to Wear and Bring for a Motor Yacht Party

Dress code on a charter boat is casual but smart. Swimwear with a cover-up is fine during the day. For evening, a sundress or linen shirt and shorts work. Heels are a bad idea on a boat deck. They damage the teak and you will slip. Barefoot or deck shoes only. Bring a light jacket or a hoodie for the evening. The wind on the water drops the temperature by 5 to 10 degrees C. Sunscreen is essential. The reflection off the water burns fast. SPF 50, applied every two hours. Sunglasses with polarised lenses help you see the water. A hat is useful. Bring a waterproof phone pouch or leave the phone in a dry bag. The crew will have a safe for valuables. If you take prescription medication, bring it in its original packaging. The boat has a first aid kit, but it is basic. For seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure even if you think you do not need it. The water is calm, but the party motion can unsettle some people. Bring cash for tips. The crew works hard, and a tip of 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee is standard if they do a good job.

h1: Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Group, Book Now
intro:
You want a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group trip that actually works for everyone. No fighting over who drives, no hidden fees, no rubbish boat. On BoatHire24 you compare real catamarans from local operators, each with a licensed skipper included, and you book the one that fits your crowd. Departure ports range from Puerto Banús to Estepona, and you can head to Cala del Faro, the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphins, or just anchor off La Concha for a swim. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day for up to 12 guests, but you can spend EUR 5,000+ for a full-day with a bigger group and more toys.

This page covers exactly what you get, which ports work best, how many people you can bring, what the weather does, and how to lock in your date without the nonsense. If you have 10, 15, or 20 people and want a proper boat day, this is the page to read.
bodyHtml:
What a Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Group Includes

Every luxury catamaran charter Marbella group booking on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That means you sit back, drink, swim, and let someone else handle the navigation. Most boats also include fuel for the agreed itinerary, though some operators charge extra for longer runs. You get a sound system, usually a Bluetooth speaker or built-in marine stereo, a shaded flybridge or bimini, and a swim platform with ladder. Many catamarans have a paddleboard, snorkel gear, or even a small inflatable kayak. Catering is optional, you can bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package (paella, tapas, BBQ) from around EUR 30, 50 per person. Some boats have a fridge and ice box, so bring your own beer and wine.

Typical group size for a luxury catamaran is 10 to 16 guests, but some larger models take up to 30. Check the max capacity on the listing, it is a legal limit, not a suggestion. If you exceed it, the port authority can fine you and the skipper can cancel the trip. So be honest about your numbers.

Which Ports Work for a Group Catamaran Charter

You have five main departure ports for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group: Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, and Sotogrande. Puerto Banús is the flashy one, you step off the boat straight into the port's restaurants and shops. It is also the most expensive for mooring fees, which operators pass on to you. Marbella Marina is a bit quieter, closer to the old town, and often EUR 100, 200 cheaper per trip. Cabopino is small and sandy, good if you want a quick exit to the dunes. Estepona is further west, near the Strait of Gibraltar, so you can spot dolphins on the way. Sotogrande is further west again, more exclusive, with a longer run to the best swimming spots.

For a group, Puerto Banús is the easiest because you can walk from the boat to dinner. But if you want a more relaxed vibe, Estepona or Cabopino work well. The skipper will advise on the best route based on wind and sea state.

Boat Types and Sizes for Your Group

Not all catamarans are equal. A luxury catamaran charter Marbella group can mean a 40-foot Lagoon with four cabins and a flybridge, or a 50-foot Bali with a spacious cockpit and forward lounge. The bigger the boat, the more deck space for lounging and dining. For a group of 10 to 12, a 40- to 45-foot catamaran is fine. For 16 to 20, go 50 feet or larger. Some operators have luxury catamarans with hydraulic swim platforms, water slides, and even a Jacuzzi on the foredeck. Those are price on request, but expect EUR 6,000 to EUR 10,000 for a full day.

If you want a faster trip or a more sporty vibe, you can also consider a luxury motor yacht or a sailing yacht, but catamarans offer the best stability and space for groups. They do not heel over, so nobody gets seasick, and the shallow draft lets you anchor close to beaches.

Pricing Guidance for a Group Catamaran Charter

Prices for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group vary by season, boat size, and duration. In low season (November to February), a half-day (4 hours) for up to 12 guests starts from around EUR 1,200. In high season (June to September), the same boat costs EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,500. Full-day (8 hours) in high season for a 45-foot catamaran with 12 guests is typically EUR 3,000 to EUR 4,500. For 16 guests on a 50-foot catamaran, expect EUR 4,500 to EUR 6,500. Super-luxury catamarans with crew and premium catering can hit EUR 8,000 to EUR 12,000 for a full day.

Always ask what is included. Some operators charge extra for fuel (EUR 300, 500 per trip), port fees (EUR 100, 200), and cleaning (EUR 50, 100). Catering is separate. BoatHire24 shows the base price and the extras, so you can compare apples to apples.

Best Time of Year for a Group Catamaran Charter

The best weather for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group is May to October. Sea temperatures are 18, 24 degrees C, air temperatures 25, 35 degrees C. July and August are the busiest and most expensive, with calm seas and long daylight hours (sunset around 9:30 PM). June and September are slightly cooler but still excellent, with fewer crowds. April and November are borderline, you might get a warm day, but the sea is cooler and windier. December to March is low season, with some operators still running but sea temperatures around 15 degrees C and a higher chance of wind. If you are flexible, June or September give you the best balance of price and conditions.

For dolphin watching, the Strait of Gibraltar is best from April to October. The dolphins are resident, but they are more active in warmer months.

How to Book a Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Group

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, filter by boat type "catamaran" and group size, then pick your preferred port and date. Each listing shows the boat, photos, capacity, price, and what is included. You can message the operator directly through the platform to ask about availability or special requests. Once you agree, you pay a deposit (usually 30, 50%) via secure link, and the balance is due on the day. No cash needed. The operator will send you a confirmation with meeting point and skipper contact. If the weather is bad, most operators offer a free reschedule or full refund.

If you want a bespoke itinerary, say, a sunset cruise with a DJ or a full-day trip to the Nerja caves, contact us via the BoatHire24 homepage and we will match you with a suitable operator.

Who Is This For

A luxury catamaran charter Marbella group is for anyone with 10 or more people who want a private boat experience without the hassle of skippering. It works for stag and hen parties (with respectful behaviour), family reunions, corporate team days, birthday celebrations, or just a group of friends who want to swim, eat, and drink in style. The skipper keeps things safe and legal, so you do not have to worry about alcohol limits or navigation. If you have kids, catamarans are safer than motor yachts because the deck is flat and there is no exposed propeller. Most operators allow children, but check the policy, some have a minimum age for the water toys.

If your group is smaller than 8, a motor yacht or RIB might be cheaper. But for 10 to 20 people, a catamaran is the best value in terms of space per person.

Local Highlights You Can See on Your Charter

From Puerto Banús, you can head east to see the Marbella coastline and the La Concha mountain backdrop, then stop at Cala del Faro for a swim. From Estepona, you can go west to the Strait of Gibraltar where you often see bottlenose dolphins and pilot whales. For a longer trip, some catamarans go to the Nerja caves (2.5 hours from Marbella), the caves are visible from the sea, and you can anchor nearby for a swim. The Río Verde area, between Marbella and Estepona, has clear waters and secluded coves. Your skipper will know the best spots based on wind direction and sea state.

If you want to combine the charter with a meal, many operators allow you to dock at a beach club or restaurant for lunch. Popular options include the beach clubs at Cabopino or the chiringuitos at Estepona. Just tell the skipper in advance.

What to Bring and What Not to Bring

Bring sunscreen (factor 50, not spray, it leaves oily residue on the deck), a towel, sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the evening. Swimwear, obviously. If you bring food and drink, avoid glass bottles, most operators ban glass for safety reasons. Plastic cups and cans are fine. Bring a cooler if the boat does not have one. Do not bring illegal drugs or excessive alcohol that could cause trouble. The skipper has the right to terminate the trip if anyone is unsafe, and you will not get a refund.

If you want music, bring a playlist on your phone. Most boats have AUX or Bluetooth. Do not bring your own speaker unless the boat's system is weak, check with the operator.

Frequently Asked Questions About Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Group

If you still have questions, check the BoatHire24 blog for more detailed guides on catamaran charters, group itineraries, and what to expect from Marbella's boating scene. Or contact us directly via the website.

Comparing Catamaran Models for Your Group

When you search for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group, you will encounter a few common models. The Lagoon 42 is a popular choice for 10 to 12 guests, with four double cabins and a spacious saloon. The Bali 4.3 offers a unique open-plan cockpit and forward lounge, giving you more outdoor space for lounging. For larger groups of 16 to 20, the Lagoon 52 or the Fountaine Pajot Samana 59 provide extra cabins and deck area. Some operators in Puerto Banús have the Nautitech 46 Open, which has a sportier feel and a large flybridge. Ask the operator which model they offer and check the photos carefully. A 2020 or newer model will have better amenities, like a hydraulic platform and upgraded sound system.

For a group that wants a party vibe, some catamarans have a built-in BBQ grill, a wet bar, and even a DJ booth. These are more common on boats over 50 feet and cost from EUR 5,000 for a full day. If you want a quieter, more relaxed trip, a standard 40-foot catamaran with a simple bimini and basic sound system might be enough. The key is matching the boat's features to your group's expectations.

Specific Itineraries for a Group Catamaran Charter

A typical itinerary from Puerto Banús for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group heads east towards Marbella's coastline. You cruise past the Golden Mile, see the La Concha mountain rising behind the city, and anchor at Cala del Faro for a swim. This cove has clear water and is sheltered from the wind. From there, you can continue to Cabopino, where the sand dunes and beach club offer a lunch stop. The total distance is about 8 to 10 nautical miles, taking 45 minutes each way. For a full day, you can go further east to the Río Verde, where the water is deeper and you can spot sea turtles. The skipper can also take you to the island of Isla de las Palomas, near Estepona, which is a popular spot for snorkelling.

If you depart from Estepona, the itinerary often goes west towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You can anchor near the Punta de la Doncella for a swim, then head to the Bay of Gibraltar for dolphin watching. This route is about 12 to 15 nautical miles and takes 1.5 hours each way. The dolphins are almost guaranteed, and you might see pilot whales or even orcas in late summer. For a sunset trip, leave at 5 PM, anchor for a swim, then watch the sun set over the water while you have drinks. Many operators offer a sunset option from 6 PM to 9 PM, costing around EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500 depending on the boat.

Additional Costs and Hidden Fees to Watch For

While the base price for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group covers the boat and skipper, there are extras you need to budget for. Port fees vary by marina: Puerto Banús charges around EUR 150 to EUR 250 for a catamaran, Marbella Marina is EUR 80 to EUR 120, and Cabopino is EUR 60 to EUR 100. Some operators include these in the price, but many do not. Fuel is another variable. For a 40-foot catamaran, a full day of cruising (6 engine hours) costs about EUR 200 to EUR 350 in fuel. Larger boats use more, up to EUR 500. You should ask the operator if fuel is included or charged separately. Cleaning fees are usually EUR 50 to EUR 100, and some operators add a service charge of 5 to 10 percent. Always request a full breakdown before you pay the deposit.

Catering packages are optional but common. A basic paella and salad lunch for 12 people costs around EUR 360 to EUR 480 (EUR 30 to EUR 40 per person). A premium BBQ with prawns, steak, and wine is EUR 600 to EUR 900 (EUR 50 to EUR 75 per person). You can also order individual platters or a tapas selection. If you bring your own food, there is no corkage fee on most boats, but check the policy. Some operators charge a small fee for ice or for using their cooler.

How to Choose the Right Group Size for Your Charter

When you book a luxury catamaran charter Marbella group, the capacity listed is the maximum number of people allowed on board, including children and infants. For comfort, you should aim for 80 percent of the max capacity. A 12-person catamaran is comfortable for 8 to 10 adults. If you have 12 adults, the seating and sunbathing areas will be tight, and you might have to rotate who sits on the flybridge. For a group of 16, you need a catamaran with a max capacity of 20 or more, such as a 50-foot model. The deck space on a 40-foot catamaran is roughly 400 square feet, while a 50-foot catamaran has about 600 square feet. More space means less crowding and a better experience.

If your group is uneven, say 15 people, you might need to book a boat that holds 18 or 20. Some operators allow up to 30 guests on larger catamarans, but these are rare and cost more. For stag or hen parties, keep the group to 12 or fewer to maintain a manageable vibe. The skipper will appreciate a group that is easy to manage, especially if alcohol is involved.

Booking Tips for a Smooth Experience

To secure the best luxury catamaran charter Marbella group, book at least two weeks in advance during high season. July and August weekends sell out quickly, especially for boats departing from Puerto Banús. If you want a specific model, like a Lagoon 52, book a month ahead. For last-minute bookings, try weekdays or low season. When you message the operator through BoatHire24, state your group size, preferred date, and any special requests. Ask about the cancellation policy: most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 7 days before, but some have a 14-day policy. If the weather is bad, you can reschedule for free. Confirm the meeting point and time in advance. Most charters start at 10 AM for a full day or 2 PM for a half day. Arrive 15 minutes early to load your gear.

If you have a large group, consider splitting into two boats if the total exceeds 20 people. Two 40-foot catamarans can travel together, and you can anchor near each other. This often costs less per person than one massive boat. Ask the operator for a quote on multiple boats.

faqs.a: Most catamarans take 10 to 16 guests. Some larger models go up to 30. The legal limit is on the boat's license, not a suggestion. Always check the listing for max capacity and do not exceed it.

faqs.q: What is included in the price for a group catamaran charter?
faqs.a: The price usually includes the boat, licensed skipper, fuel for the agreed itinerary, and basic safety equipment. Extras like catering, drinks, water toys, and port fees are often separate. Read the listing details carefully.

faqs.q: Can we bring our own food and drinks?

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day of our charter?
faqs.a: The skipper decides if it is safe to sail. If conditions are unsafe, you can reschedule for free or get a full refund. Most operators have a weather policy in their terms.

faqs.q: Do we need to tip the skipper?
faqs.a: Tipping is not mandatory but is appreciated. A typical tip is 10, 15% of the charter price, given in cash at the end of the trip. Some groups pool money beforehand.

faqs.q: Can we choose the itinerary for the day?
faqs.a: Yes, you can discuss the itinerary with the skipper before departure. They will advise on the best spots based on wind, sea state, and time. Popular stops include Cala del Faro, the Strait of Gibraltar, and the Nerja coastline.

faqs.q: How far in advance should we book a group catamaran charter?
faqs.a: In high season (June, September), book at least 2, 4 weeks in advance. For larger groups (15+), book a month ahead. In low season, a week is usually fine. BoatHire24 shows real-time availability.

title: Catamaran Charter Puerto Banus Wedding – Dream Day
metaDescription: Plan your dream catamaran charter Puerto Banus wedding. Luxury boats, licensed skipper, sunset vows. Book your perfect day with BoatHire24.
h1: Catamaran Charter Puerto Banus Wedding, Dream Day
intro:
If you are planning a wedding on the Costa del Sol and want something far more memorable than a hotel function room, a catamaran charter in Puerto Banus is the answer. You get the Mediterranean as your backdrop, La Concha mountain watching from the distance, and a floating party that moves from the marina to the open sea. No need to worry about the skipper or the licence, because every BoatHire24 charter includes a licensed professional who handles the navigation while you focus on the vows, the champagne, and the photos.

This page is for couples who want the details upfront: what you actually get, which ports work best, how much it might cost (roughly), and the practical steps to make it happen. No fluff, no fake testimonials, just the real picture of a wedding on a catamaran in Puerto Banus.
bodyHtml:
What a Catamaran Wedding Charter Includes

A catamaran wedding charter from BoatHire24 is not a standard boat hire with a few extras thrown in. It is a private charter for your group, with the boat yours for the duration. The licensed skipper is included, fuel is included, and the boat is cleaned before you board. You can bring your own catering or arrange it through the charter company, and most catamarans have a sound system, a sun deck, and a shaded saloon. For a wedding, you typically get the boat for three to six hours, depending on the package. Some operators offer a ceremony at anchor with a captain who can officiate, but that depends on the crew and local regulations. You can also bring a registrar or a friend to conduct the ceremony, but you need to check the legal requirements in Spain for a civil ceremony at sea.

Puerto Banus as Your Departure Port

Puerto Banus is the obvious choice for a wedding charter because of the glamour factor. The marina is full of superyachts, designer shops, and restaurants, and the atmosphere is pure luxury. Your guests can arrive by taxi or car, and there is parking nearby (paid, so budget for that). The departure point is the main dock, and the crew will be there to welcome you. From Puerto Banus, you can head west towards Estepona or east towards Marbella, depending on the wind and the plan. The advantage of Puerto Banus is the proximity to the open sea, so you are not wasting time motoring through a narrow channel. You can be sipping cava within ten minutes of leaving the dock.

Other Departure Ports on the Costa del Sol

If Puerto Banus feels too flashy or too busy, you have other options. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a ten-minute drive east, and it is slightly quieter. Cabopino, near Cala del Faro, is smaller and more relaxed, with a sandy beach nearby. Estepona marina is west of Puerto Banus, and it has a lovely old town for a reception afterwards. Sotogrande is further west, close to Gibraltar, and it is a more exclusive, residential area. Benalmadena is east of Marbella, near the Nerja caves direction, and it has a large marina with plenty of charter options. Each port has its own character, and the choice depends on your venue for the reception and the vibe you want. BoatHire24 covers all these ports, so you can compare the options on the search page.

Boat Options for a Wedding Charter

Catamarans are the most popular choice for weddings because they are stable, spacious, and have a large deck area. A typical catamaran for a wedding is around 40 to 50 feet, with capacity for 12 to 20 guests. Some larger catamarans can take up to 30 people, but the rules in Spain limit the number of passengers on a charter, so check the specifics. Sailing catamarans are quieter and more romantic, while motor catamarans offer more deck space and a smoother ride. You can also consider a motor yacht for a more formal feel, or a sailing yacht for a classic vibe. RIBs and speedboats are not suitable for a wedding unless you are eloping with just two guests. Superyachts are available for a price on request, and they come with a full crew, including a chef and stewardesses. The choice depends on your budget and the size of your party.

Pricing Guidance for a Wedding Charter

Pricing for a catamaran wedding charter in Puerto Banus varies a lot. A basic three-hour charter for a small group on a 40-foot catamaran might start from around EUR 1,500. For a larger boat with a full wedding package, including decoration, food, and drinks, you could pay EUR 3,000 to EUR 6,000 for a half-day. Superyacht charters start at EUR 10,000 and go up quickly. The season matters: July and August are peak, and prices are higher. May, June, September, and October are shoulder season, with better availability and slightly lower rates. Winter months (November to March) are cheaper but the weather is less reliable. You should always ask for a detailed quote that includes the base price, fuel, skipper, and any extras like catering or decoration. Do not assume anything is included. The BoatHire24 platform lets you compare options and request quotes from multiple operators.

Best Seasons for a Wedding at Sea

The best months for a catamaran wedding in Puerto Banus are May, June, September, and October. The air temperature is around 25 to 30 degrees C, the water is warm enough for a swim, and the sea is generally calm. July and August are hot (35 degrees C plus) and crowded, but the evenings are beautiful for a sunset ceremony. The wind in summer is usually light, so the boat stays steady. Winter can work if you want a small, intimate ceremony, but expect cooler temperatures (15 to 20 degrees C) and a higher chance of wind or rain. The sunset in summer is around 9:30 PM, so a 6 PM to 9 PM charter gives you golden hour light for photos. In spring and autumn, sunset is earlier, around 8 PM, so plan accordingly.

How to Book a Wedding Charter

Booking a wedding charter on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter Puerto Banus as the port, select the date and number of guests, and filter by catamaran. You will see a list of available boats with prices and details. Each listing has a contact button that lets you send a message to the operator. You can ask questions about the wedding package, the crew, and any specific requirements. The operator will reply with a quote and availability. Once you are happy, you pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) to secure the date. The balance is due a few days before the charter. Make sure you read the cancellation policy carefully, especially for a wedding where you have other suppliers depending on the date.

Who This Is For

A catamaran wedding charter is for couples who want a small to medium-sized wedding (up to 30 guests) in a unique setting. It works well for elopements, vow renewals, or a ceremony with immediate family and close friends. It is not ideal for a large wedding with 100 guests because the boat capacity is limited. It is also not for people who get seasick easily, although catamarans are very stable. If you want a party atmosphere, a catamaran is perfect because you can dance on the deck, play your own music, and stop for a swim. The skipper handles the navigation, so you can relax and enjoy the day. For more ideas and tips, check the BoatHire24 blog for articles on wedding planning on the Costa del Sol.

Local Colour and Photo Spots

The Costa del Sol has some stunning backdrops for wedding photos. From Puerto Banus, you can cruise past the luxury villas of the Golden Mile, with La Concha mountain in the background. Further west, the coast gets wilder, with cliffs and coves like Cala del Faro near Cabopino. East of Marbella, you have the dunes of Cabopino and the distant view of the Sierra Blanca mountains. If you head towards Estepona, the old town's whitewashed buildings are visible from the sea. On a clear day, you can see the Strait of Gibraltar and even the coast of Africa. Dolphins are common in the area, especially near the Strait, so you might get a surprise appearance during your ceremony. The crew can help you find the best spots for photos, and you can anchor in a quiet cove for a private moment.

Practical Details and Tips

Here are a few practical things to consider for a catamaran wedding in Puerto Banus. First, check the weather forecast a few days before, and have a backup plan. The skipper can adjust the route to avoid rough seas, but if the wind is too strong, the charter might be cancelled. Second, think about the food and drink. You can bring your own catering, but the boat might have restrictions on glassware or hot food. Some operators offer a catering package with canapes, a buffet, or a barbecue. Third, consider the dress code. Heels can damage the deck, so flat shoes or barefoot is better. The boat will have a sound system, but you can bring your own playlist. Fourth, inform the crew about any special requests, like a specific route or a stop for a swim. They are there to make your day special, but they need to know in advance. Finally, book early, especially for summer weekends. Popular boats are booked months ahead.

Wedding Ceremony Options at Sea

You have a few ways to handle the legal side of a catamaran wedding in Puerto Banus. A civil ceremony on a Spanish-registered boat is possible if the captain is authorised to perform marriages, but this is rare. Most couples opt for a symbolic ceremony on board, then do the legal paperwork at the registry office in Marbella or Estepona before or after the charter. You can bring a non-denominational officiant or ask a friend to lead the vows. Some operators offer a "captain's ceremony" where the skipper reads a script and you exchange rings, but this has no legal standing. If you want a fully legal wedding at sea, you need to hire a Spanish notary or registrar to come on board, which costs extra and requires advance booking. Check with your chosen operator about their specific policy on ceremonies.

Decorating the Catamaran for Your Wedding

Most charter companies allow you to decorate the catamaran, but with limits. You can bring flowers, bunting, and fabric drapes, but avoid anything that might damage the deck or rigging. No confetti or rice, as it ends up in the sea. Biodegradable confetti is sometimes allowed, but check first. Balloons are a bad idea because they can blow away and become marine litter. A popular option is to hire a local wedding stylist who specialises in boat decorations. They can set up an arch on the bow, arrange flowers on the table, and add cushions and throws to the seating area. Expect to pay EUR 300 to EUR 800 for basic decoration, depending on the complexity. Some operators offer a decoration package as an add-on, which saves you the hassle of sourcing everything yourself. Just confirm what is included in the price before you book.

Sunset Timing and Route Planning

The sunset time in Puerto Banus changes significantly through the year. In June and July, the sun sets around 9:30 PM to 9:45 PM, so a 6 PM to 9 PM charter gives you two hours of golden light and the actual sunset at the end. In September, sunset is around 8:30 PM, so a 5 PM to 8 PM slot works. In May and October, sunset is around 8 PM to 8:30 PM, so aim for a 4 PM to 7 PM charter. The skipper can plan the route to face the setting sun for photos. A typical route from Puerto Banus is west towards the cliffs of Cabopino or east towards the Marbella coastline. For a more dramatic backdrop, head west towards Estepona where the mountains meet the sea. The crew will know the best spots for a sunset anchor, so trust their local knowledge.

What to Wear on a Catamaran Wedding

Dress code for a catamaran wedding is smart casual with a nautical twist. For the bride, a lightweight dress or a short train works best. Avoid heavy satin or long trains that will get dirty on the deck. Heels are a problem because they can slip through the teak deck gaps or scuff the surface. Wedge heels or flat sandals are better. For the groom, linen trousers and a linen shirt are comfortable and look good in photos. Jackets are optional but can be hot in summer. Guests should avoid stilettos and wear flat shoes or barefoot if the crew allows it. Bring a light jacket or pashmina for the evening, as the breeze picks up after sunset. Sunscreen is essential, even in the evening, because the reflection off the water is strong. The crew will have a shaded saloon where guests can cool down if needed.

Catering Options for a Wedding Charter

You have three main catering options for a catamaran wedding. First, you can bring your own food and drink. This is the cheapest option, but you need to check if the boat allows it and if there are any corkage fees. Most operators charge a small fee for catering setup, around EUR 50 to EUR 100. Second, you can order from a local catering company that delivers to the dock. Many caterers in Marbella and Puerto Banus specialise in boat events and can provide canapes, a buffet, or a sit-down meal. Prices range from EUR 30 to EUR 80 per person for a good spread. Third, some catamarans have a crew who can cook on board, offering a barbecue or a paella lunch. This is the most convenient option but costs more, typically EUR 50 to EUR 100 per person plus a service charge. Drinks are usually BYO or ordered through the operator. A standard package might include cava, wine, beer, and soft drinks for EUR 15 to EUR 25 per person.

Music and Entertainment on Board

Every catamaran has a sound system, but the quality varies. Most have Bluetooth connectivity, so you can play your own playlist from a phone or tablet. Some have a DJ setup with better speakers and a mixer, which you can request for an extra fee. If you want live music, a guitarist or a saxophonist can fit on the deck, but you need to check the boat's capacity and the noise restrictions in the marina. Dancing on a catamaran is possible, but the space is limited. The bow and the flybridge are the best spots for a dance floor. For a more relaxed vibe, you can have background music while you eat and then turn it up later. The crew can help you manage the volume so it does not disturb other boats. Avoid fireworks or sparklers, as they are dangerous on a fibreglass boat and illegal in many marinas.

Weather Contingency Plans

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, but the sea can still be unpredictable. If the wind is too strong, the skipper may recommend staying close to the coast or cancelling the charter. Most operators have a weather clause in their contract. If they cancel due to unsafe conditions, you get a full refund or a reschedule. If you cancel because you do not like the forecast, you may lose your deposit. A good backup plan is to book a restaurant on the marina as an alternative venue. Puerto Banus has dozens of waterfront restaurants that can host a small wedding party at short notice. Another option is to choose a catamaran with a large, enclosed saloon so you can still have the party indoors if the weather turns. Ask the operator about their weather policy before you pay the deposit.

Photography and Videography Tips

Professional photos on a catamaran require some planning. The best light is in the late afternoon, so schedule the ceremony for 5 PM to 7 PM. The photographer should arrive early to scout the boat and find the best angles. A drone can capture stunning aerial shots of the boat at anchor, but you need permission from the marina and the skipper. Some marinas ban drones for safety reasons. Underwater photography is possible if you stop for a swim, but you need a waterproof camera or a GoPro. The crew can help position the boat for photos, turning the bow into the sun or finding a calm spot. Make sure the photographer is comfortable on a moving boat and has non-slip shoes. If you are hiring a local photographer, ask to see examples of their boat work. The reflection of the water can cause exposure issues, so an experienced marine photographer is worth the extra cost.

faqs.a: A civil ceremony at sea is possible if you arrange a registrar or a captain authorised to officiate. Most charters offer a symbolic ceremony, and you can make it legal later on land. Check with the charter operator for their specific options.
