title: Speedboat Rental Puerto Banus Group – Fun Day
metaDescription: Speedboat rental Puerto Banus group. Hire a RIB or speedboat for a fun day on the Costa del Sol. Includes skipper, fuel, snorkel gear. Book your group trip now.
h1: Speedboat Rental Puerto Banus Group, Fun Day on the Water
intro:
You want a speedboat rental Puerto Banus group trip that actually delivers. No queues, no crowds, just you and your mates tearing across the Mediterranean with the wind in your hair. That’s exactly what we do at BoatHire24. We connect you with boat owners in Puerto Banus and along the Costa del Sol who provide licensed skippers, fuel, and all the gear you need for a day out. Forget the hassle of organising a big group activity, we make it simple, safe, and surprisingly affordable if you split the cost.

Puerto Banus is the obvious starting point. It’s the superyacht capital of Spain, but you don’t need a superyacht budget to have a great time. A RIB or a smaller speedboat can handle your group of 6 to 12 people easily. You’ll blast past the marina’s flashy boats, head out to the open sea, maybe spot some dolphins off the coast of Estepona, and drop anchor for a swim and some snorkelling. The skipper handles everything, navigation, safety, even the music if you ask nicely.

We’ve put together this guide to help you understand exactly what you get with a speedboat rental Puerto Banus group booking. Prices, ports, boat types, what’s included, and how to secure your slot. No fluff, just the details you need to plan your fun day on the water.
bodyHtml:
What’s Included in a Speedboat Rental Puerto Banus Group Booking

Every speedboat rental we arrange comes with a licensed skipper as standard. That’s not optional, it’s the law in Spain for most powerboats over 15 hp. The skipper is local, speaks English, and knows the best spots along the coast. You don’t need a boating licence, you don’t need to navigate, you just turn up and enjoy.

Fuel is included in the price. That’s a big one because fuel costs on a RIB can add up quickly, especially if you’re covering 20 or 30 nautical miles. Most charters include up to 4 hours of cruising, which is enough to head south to the beaches of Estepona or north to the cliffs of Cala del Faro. Some packages also include snorkel gear, a cooler with ice, and sometimes soft drinks. Check with the owner before booking, but expect the basics to be covered.

Insurance and safety equipment are mandatory. Every boat has life jackets, a first aid kit, and a VHF radio. The skipper will give a brief safety talk when you board. You don’t need to worry about hidden extras, the price you see on BoatHire24 includes everything except tips and any food or drinks you bring yourself.

Which Ports Can You Depart From?

Puerto Banus is the main launch point for group speedboat rentals, but you have other options along the Costa del Sol. Here’s a quick rundown of the departure ports we cover.

Puerto Banus, The most glamorous marina in Spain. You’ll see yachts worth millions, but your speedboat rental will be tied up in the guest berths near the entrance. Easy parking nearby, plenty of restaurants for a pre-boat breakfast. Perfect for groups staying in Marbella or the Golden Mile.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), A bit less flashy than Banus, but still a solid choice. It’s closer to Marbella town centre and the old town. Good if you want a more relaxed vibe before or after your trip.

Cabopino, Small, quiet marina near Artola beach. Ideal if you want to avoid the crowds. The sand dunes and pine forests nearby make for a scenic departure. Only suitable for smaller groups, the marina can’t handle big boats.

Estepona, About 15 minutes west of Banus. The marina here is modern, with a nice promenade and the old town a short walk away. Good for groups staying in Estepona or the western Costa del Sol.

Sotogrande, A bit further west, near Gibraltar. This is a luxury residential area with a large marina. Great if you want to combine your boat trip with a visit to the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins and maybe whales.

Benalmádena, East of Marbella, near Málaga. The marina is huge, with plenty of bars and restaurants. A good option if you’re based in Torremolinos, Fuengirola, or Mijas.

Your skipper will meet you at the marina 15 minutes before departure. They’ll walk you to the boat, do the safety briefing, and you’re off. No queues, no paperwork.

What Types of Speedboats Are Available for Groups?

When we say speedboat, we’re usually talking about a RIB, a rigid inflatable boat with a fibreglass hull and inflatable tubes. They’re fast, stable, and perfect for groups. Here are the main options.

RIB speedboats (6-8 people), These are the most common. Typically 6 to 8 metres long with outboard engines from 150 to 250 hp. They’ll do 30 to 40 knots on a calm sea. Enough power for a thrill, but not so fast that it’s scary. Good for a family group or a small group of friends. Prices start from around EUR 400 for a 4-hour rental.

Larger RIBs (10-12 people), If your group is bigger, you can get a 9-10 metre RIB with a pair of 200 hp outboards. These can carry up to 12 passengers comfortably. They’re a bit slower, maybe 25-30 knots, but more stable in choppy water. Prices from around EUR 600 for 4 hours.

Licence-free day boats, Some owners offer smaller speedboats that you can drive yourself if you have a licence. But for groups, it’s better to have a skipper. We only list boats with skippers, so you don’t need to worry about that.

Motor yachts vs speedboats, If your group is 12+ people, you might want to look at a small motor yacht instead. They’re slower but have a cabin, a toilet, and more deck space. We cover those on our search page.

Pricing Guidance for a Group Speedboat Rental

Prices vary depending on the boat size, duration, and season. Here’s a rough guide so you know what to expect.

Low season (October to May), 4-hour rentals for a 6-person RIB start from around EUR 350. For a 10-person RIB, expect EUR 500-600. Half-day trips (4 hours) are the most popular. Full-day (8 hours) can cost EUR 800-1,200 for a larger boat.

High season (June to September), Prices go up by about 20-30%. A 6-person RIB might be EUR 450-500 for 4 hours. A 12-person RIB could be EUR 700-800. Book early, July and August slots sell out weeks in advance.

What’s included in the price?, Skipper, fuel, insurance, snorkel gear, cooler. You bring your own food and drinks. Some owners offer optional extras like a GoPro rental or a BBQ pack. Check the listing on BoatHire24 for exact details.

How to split the cost, If you have 8 people and the rental is EUR 600, that’s EUR 75 per person. Not bad for a day on the Med. Even with 6 people, it’s EUR 100 each. Compare that to a theme park ticket or a round of golf, and it’s good value.

We don’t list exact prices for every boat because owners update them seasonally. Use our search page to see current rates and availability.

Best Time of Year for a Speedboat Trip in Puerto Banus

The Costa del Sol has over 300 days of sunshine a year, so you can go boating almost any time. But the experience changes with the seasons.

Summer (June to September), Hot, clear, and busy. Sea temperatures hit 24-26 degrees C. Perfect for swimming and snorkelling. The sea is calm most days, especially in the morning. Afternoons can get a bit choppy if the Levante wind picks up. Book a morning slot (10am-2pm) for the best conditions.

Spring and autumn (April-May, October), Still warm, 20-24 degrees C. Fewer boats on the water, so you feel like you have the coastline to yourself. The water might be a bit cooler for swimming, but still doable with a wetsuit. Good for dolphin watching, they’re more active in spring.

Winter (November to March), Chilly for swimming (sea temp around 15-17 degrees C), but great for a fast ride. The air is crisp, the sun is lower, and the mountains behind Marbella look stunning with snow on La Concha. You’ll need a jacket, but the boat will keep you dry. Prices are lower, and availability is wide open.

If you’re booking for a group in summer, do it at least 2 weeks ahead. Winter and spring can be last-minute.

How to Book a Speedboat Rental for Your Group

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Here’s the process.

1. Go to our BoatHire24 homepage and use the search bar. Enter Puerto Banus as the departure port, select your date, and choose the number of people. The system will show you available speedboats that fit your group size.

2. Browse the listings. Each one includes photos, a description, the boat’s capacity, and the price. Look for the ones marked as “with skipper”, that’s all of them. Check the included items list for fuel, snorkel gear, etc.

3. Click “Book Now” and fill in your details. You’ll pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or card depending on the owner’s preference.

4. You’ll receive a confirmation email with the meeting point, the skipper’s contact number, and any last-minute instructions. On the day, arrive at the marina 15 minutes early. The skipper will be there to greet you.

5. Enjoy your trip. The skipper will take you where you want to go, you can suggest a route or let them choose based on conditions. Most groups want to see the coastline, stop for a swim, and maybe visit a beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club for a drink (you can moor up nearby).

Cancellation policies vary by owner. Most offer a full refund if you cancel 48 hours in advance. Check the terms before you book.

Who Is a Group Speedboat Rental Best For?

This isn’t for everyone. If you’re looking for a luxury yacht with a jacuzzi and a champagne bar, you want a superyacht charter, not a speedboat. But if you want a fun, active day out with friends or family, a speedboat is perfect.

Hen and stag parties, Speedboats are a hit with groups celebrating something. You get the thrill of the ride, the chance to swim, and the option to stop at a beach club. Just keep the drinking sensible, the skipper will cut you off if anyone gets rowdy.

Family groups, Kids love speedboats. The RIB tubes are safe, and the skipper can go slow if anyone is nervous. Snorkelling gear lets the kids explore the coves. Bring snacks and suncream.

Corporate groups, A team building day on a speedboat is a lot more memorable than a meeting room. You can combine it with a lunch at a beachfront restaurant. The skipper will handle the logistics.

Friends on holiday, If you’re a group of 6-10 friends staying in Marbella, this is a no-brainer. It’s a shared experience that beats lying on a sun lounger all day.

If your group is bigger than 12, you’ll need a catamaran or a motor yacht. Check our search page for larger options.

What to Bring on Your Speedboat Trip

Keep it simple. You don’t need much.

, Swimwear and a towel. You’ll definitely get wet, especially on a RIB.

, Suncream (factor 50). The reflection off the water doubles the UV exposure.

, A light jacket or windbreaker. Even in summer, the wind at 30 knots feels cool.

, Sunglasses with a strap. You don’t want them flying off.

, Food and drinks. Bring a cooler bag. Most boats have a small ice box, but bring your own if you want a lot. Alcohol is fine, but don’t overdo it, the skipper has the final say on safety.

, A waterproof phone case or a dry bag. Splashes happen.

, Cash for tips. EUR 20-50 per group is standard if the skipper does a good job.

Leave behind: high heels (you’ll ruin them), glass bottles (banned on most boats), and any valuables you don’t want to get wet.

Local Highlights You’ll See on Your Trip

Your skipper will tailor the route to your group, but here are some sights you can expect.

Puerto Banus marina, You’ll depart from here, so you’ll see the superyachts up close. The entrance is flanked by the luxury shopping arcades.

Cala del Faro, A small cove just north of Banus, near the lighthouse. Good for swimming and snorkelling. The water is clear and usually calm.

Estepona coastline, Heading west, you’ll pass the beaches of Estepona. The old town is visible from the water, with its whitewashed buildings and flower pots.

La Concha mountain, The iconic mountain behind Marbella. From the sea, it looks like a sleeping giant. Best seen in the morning when the light hits the limestone.

Strait of Gibraltar (longer trips), If you book a full-day trip and head west, you can reach the Strait. This is where you see dolphins, common dolphins, striped dolphins, and sometimes pilot whales. The skipper will know the hotspots.

Nerja caves (longer trips east), A full day east from Banus can take you past the cliffs of Maro and the Nerja caves. The caves are accessible from the sea only by boat. It’s a beautiful stretch of coastline.

Your skipper will also point out the best beach clubs for a stop. Some popular ones include Playa Padre (Marbella) and La Cabane (Estepona).

Common Questions About Group Speedboat Rentals

We get asked the same things a lot. Here are the answers.

Do I need a boating licence? No. The skipper is licensed and handles all navigation. You just enjoy the ride.

Can I drive the boat myself? Not on a standard rental. If you want to drive, you need a licence and you need to rent a licence-free boat (which we also list, but not for groups this size).

What if the weather is bad? The skipper will decide. If it’s unsafe, the trip is cancelled and you get a full refund. If it’s just a bit cloudy, you can still go.

Can we bring our own music? Yes. Most boats have a Bluetooth speaker or an aux cable. Ask the skipper when you board.

Is there a toilet on board? On a speedboat RIB, no. You stop at a beach or a beach club for toilet breaks. Larger yachts have a toilet.

What about seasickness? The coast here is relatively sheltered. If you’re prone to it, take a seasickness tablet an hour before. The skipper can also keep the boat in calmer waters.

Can we customise the route? Absolutely. Tell the skipper what you want to see. They know the coast and will suggest a plan.

For more detailed advice, check our blog where we cover topics like “Best Time to Rent a Boat in Marbella” and “How to Choose a Boat for a Group”.

Ready to Book Your Speedboat Rental Puerto Banus Group Trip?

You’ve got the info. Now it’s time to make it happen. A speedboat rental in Puerto Banus for your group is a straightforward way to spend a day on the water without the usual holiday stress. You get a skipper, you get fuel, you get the freedom to explore the Costa del Sol from the sea. Split the cost among friends, and it’s one of the most affordable group activities you can do in Marbella.

Head to BoatHire24 to start your search. Enter Puerto Banus, your date, and your group size. You’ll see a list of available speedboats with prices and photos. Pick one that fits your group, book with a deposit, and show up on the day. The skipper will do the rest.

Don’t leave it too long, especially in summer. The best boats go fast. If you have any questions, use the contact form on the site or email us. We’ll help you find the right boat for your group.

bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Private Catamaran for a Birthday

A catamaran is the ideal party platform because it doesn't heel over like a monohull. You get a stable, wide deck with plenty of space for lounging, dancing, or just sunbathing. Most catamarans on our platform are between 40 and 60 feet, with a flybridge, a trampoline net at the bow, and a shaded cockpit. You can bring your own food and drink, or order a catering package. The skipper will anchor in a calm bay like Cala del Faro or near the dunes of Cabopino, so you can swim, snorkel, or just float on a paddleboard. The whole point is that you don't have to lift a finger. The skipper handles the navigation, the safety briefing, and the mooring. You handle the birthday cake.

Which Ports Can You Depart From

Your private catamaran hire for a birthday in Marbella can start from several ports. The most popular is Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina with the superyachts and the designer shops. It is also the most convenient if you are staying in the Golden Mile or Nueva Andalucía. Marbella Marina, also called Puerto Deportivo, is a quieter option closer to the old town. You can also depart from Cabopino, a small marina near the Artola dunes, or from Estepona, which gives you access to the waters near the Strait of Gibraltar. Sotogrande is further west, ideal if you want a longer cruise towards Gibraltar. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near the marina with the dolphin statue. Each port has its own vibe, but the experience is the same: a private catamaran with a skipper, ready for your birthday party.

Boat Options for Your Birthday Charter

We list a range of catamarans suitable for birthdays. The most common are Lagoon, Fountaine Pajot, and Bali models, all between 40 and 50 feet. A 40-foot cat can comfortably host 10 to 12 guests. A 50-foot cat can take up to 18. If you want more space, there are larger cats up to 60 feet, but those are price on request. All boats come with a full safety kit, a sound system (bluetooth or aux), and a bimini top for shade. Some have a grill or a small kitchen. You can also add extras like a photographer, a DJ, or a water toys package with a jet ski tow. The skipper will give you a full briefing at the start, and you can plan the route together. Typical routes include heading east towards the Cabopino dunes or west towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro. You can also just anchor in the bay off Puerto Banús and watch the superyachts go by.

Pricing Guidance for a Birthday Catamaran

Prices for private catamaran hire in Marbella for a birthday vary by season, boat size, and duration. In the low season (October to May), a half-day (4 hours) on a 40-foot cat starts from around EUR 1,500. A full day (8 hours) is from EUR 2,500. In the high season (June to September), prices increase by 30 to 50 percent. A half-day in August can be EUR 2,000 to EUR 2,500. A full day can be EUR 3,500 to EUR 5,000. These prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. Extras like catering, drinks, or water toys are additional. You can also book a sunset cruise for a shorter duration, usually 2 to 3 hours, from around EUR 800. Always confirm the exact price with the boat owner before booking. We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance for summer weekends, as availability is limited.

The Best Season for a Birthday Charter

The Costa del Sol has over 300 days of sunshine a year, so you can technically celebrate your birthday on a catamaran in any month. The best weather is from May to October, when temperatures range from 25 to 35 degrees C and the sea is calm. July and August are the hottest and busiest, with sea temperatures around 24 degrees C. If your birthday falls in winter (November to February), you can still charter, but expect cooler temperatures (15 to 20 degrees C) and a higher chance of wind. The catamarans are still comfortable, and you can use the indoor saloon. The light in winter is beautiful for photos, and the marinas are less crowded. Just bring a jacket. Spring and autumn are the sweet spots: warm enough to swim, but not too hot, and prices are lower than in summer.

What to Bring and What to Expect

You should bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, and a swimsuit. The skipper will provide life jackets and a safety briefing. You can bring your own food and drink, but most boats have a cooler or a fridge. Some owners offer a catering service with tapas, paella, or a barbecue. You can also order a birthday cake from a local bakery and have it delivered to the boat. The skipper will anchor in a sheltered spot so you can swim or use the paddleboard. The typical itinerary includes a slow cruise along the coast, a swim stop, and then a return to port. You can also request a stop near the dolphin watching areas off Estepona or the Strait of Gibraltar. The skipper knows the best spots and will adjust the route based on the weather and your preferences. Expect a relaxed, informal atmosphere. This is not a formal yacht club event. It is your birthday, so you set the tone.

Who Is This For

Private catamaran hire for a birthday in Marbella works for groups of friends, family gatherings, or even a milestone birthday like a 30th, 40th, or 50th. It is also popular for hen and stag parties, as long as the group is respectful of the boat and the skipper. Children are welcome on most catamarans, but check with the owner if you have toddlers, as the deck can be slippery. The minimum age for chartering is usually 18, but younger guests can join as passengers. The maximum guest count is strictly enforced for safety, so do not try to sneak extra people on board. If you have a large group, you can charter two catamarans and raft them together. This is common for big birthday parties with 20 or more guests. The skippers coordinate the route and the anchor spot so you can party together.

How to Book Your Private Catamaran

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You go to the BoatHire24 homepage, select your port, date, and number of guests. You can filter by catamaran and see the available boats. Each listing has photos, a description, and the price. You send an inquiry, and the owner confirms availability. You pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) to secure the booking. The balance is due on the day, either in cash or by card. We recommend reading the terms and conditions carefully, especially the cancellation policy. Most owners offer a full refund if you cancel at least 14 days in advance. For last-minute cancellations, you may lose the deposit. If the weather is bad (winds over 30 knots or thunderstorms), the skipper can cancel and you get a full refund or a reschedule. Always communicate with the owner directly through our platform to avoid misunderstandings.

Local Colour and Things to See

From the catamaran, you will see the iconic La Concha mountain behind Marbella, the whitewashed houses of Estepona old town from the sea, and the rock of Gibraltar on a clear day. If you head east, you can see the cliffs of Cala del Faro and the Cabopino dunes. If you go west, you might spot dolphins near the Strait of Gibraltar. The water colour changes from turquoise near the shore to deep blue further out. The sunset from a catamaran is a cliché for a reason: it is genuinely impressive, with the sun dipping behind the mountains of Africa. You can also request a stop near the Nerja caves if you do a full-day charter from the eastern ports, but that is a longer trip (about 2 hours each way from Marbella). Most birthday charters stick to the area between Puerto Banús and Estepona, which is about 15 nautical miles of coastline with plenty of anchorages.

Why Choose BoatHire24

BoatHire24 is a marketplace that lists catamarans from local owners and charter companies. We do not own the boats, so we can offer a wide selection without bias. You can compare prices, read the descriptions, and see the photos. We handle the booking process, but the owner handles the actual charter. This means you get a personal service from someone who knows the boat and the area. We have been operating since 2015 and have a good reputation on the Costa del Sol. If you have any questions, you can contact us through the website. We also have a blog with guides on boat chartering, packing lists, and local tips. For a birthday, a private catamaran hire in Marbella is a memorable way to celebrate. You get the sea, the sun, and the freedom to do what you want. No DJ, no dress code, no last call. Just you and the Mediterranean.

Choosing the Right Duration for Your Birthday Charter

Most birthday charters on a private catamaran in Marbella run for either 4 hours (half-day) or 8 hours (full-day). A half-day is enough for a leisurely cruise, a swim stop, and a toast with champagne. It works well if you have dinner plans afterwards in Puerto Banús or Marbella old town. A full-day charter gives you time to cruise further, maybe to Estepona or even towards Gibraltar, with multiple swim stops and a proper lunch on board. Some groups book a sunset charter of 2 to 3 hours, which is cheaper but still gives you the best light for photos and a relaxed vibe. For a birthday, a half-day is the most common choice. You get the experience without it feeling too long. If you want to make a day of it, go for the full-day and bring a picnic or order catering.

Specific Catamaran Models You Might Find

On BoatHire24, you will see several specific models available for private catamaran hire in Marbella for a birthday. The Lagoon 450 is a popular 45-foot cat with four cabins, a large saloon, and a flybridge that seats 12. The Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40 is a bit smaller but has a modern layout and a spacious cockpit. The Bali 4.3 has an open-plan saloon that connects directly to the cockpit, which makes it feel bigger than it is. Some owners list older models like the Lagoon 380 or the Fountaine Pajot Lavezzi 40, which are cheaper but still comfortable. All of them have a sound system, a fridge, and a bimini. If you want something more luxurious, there are a few catamarans over 50 feet, like the Lagoon 52 or the Fountaine Pajot Saba 50, but those are price on request and usually require a longer booking.

Adding Extras for Your Birthday Party

You can customise your private catamaran hire with a range of extras. Common additions include a catering package with Spanish tapas, paella, or a barbecue. Prices for catering start from around EUR 30 per person for a basic menu and go up to EUR 80 for a premium option with seafood and wine. You can also order a birthday cake from a local bakery; expect to pay EUR 40 to EUR 60 for a custom cake. Water toys are popular: a paddleboard costs around EUR 50 to rent for the day, a jet ski tow is EUR 150 to EUR 200, and a full water toys package with snorkel gear, noodles, and a floating mat is EUR 100 to EUR 200. Some owners offer a photographer for EUR 200 to EUR 400 for a few hours, or a DJ with a small sound system for EUR 300 to EUR 500. You can also arrange for a flower arrangement or balloon decorations, but check with the owner first as some boats have strict rules about confetti or glitter.

What Happens if the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is known for good weather, but it can change. If the wind is over 25 to 30 knots or there is a storm warning, the skipper will cancel the charter for safety. In that case, you get a full refund or you can reschedule. If the weather is marginal, the skipper might suggest a different route or a shorter duration. For example, if the wind is coming from the east, they might stay close to the coast or anchor in a sheltered bay instead of heading out to open water. You should always have a backup date in mind, especially if your birthday falls in a windy month like March or November. The skipper has the final say on whether to go out. Do not argue with them. They know the local conditions better than you do.

How to Handle the Deposit and Payment

When you book through BoatHire24, you will pay a deposit to secure the date. This is usually 30 to 50 percent of the total price. The deposit is non-refundable if you cancel within 14 days of the charter, unless the owner agrees otherwise. The balance is paid on the day of the charter, either in cash or by bank transfer. Some owners accept credit cards, but not all. Always confirm the payment method with the owner before the day. If you pay by cash, bring the exact amount as the skipper may not have change. Some owners ask for a security deposit (EUR 200 to EUR 500) in case of damage, which is returned at the end if everything is fine. Read the terms carefully before you pay. BoatHire24 acts as a platform, so any disputes are between you and the owner, but we can help mediate if needed.

Tips for a Smooth Birthday Charter Experience

Arrive at the port 15 minutes before the departure time. The skipper will do a safety briefing and show you the facilities. Bring your own drinks if you want specific brands, as the boat's fridge might be small. Do not bring glass bottles, as broken glass on deck is dangerous. Use plastic or cans. If you plan to swim, bring a towel and a change of clothes. The catamaran has a fresh water shower on the back deck to rinse off salt. Do not expect a full bathroom with a shower inside; most cats have a small head (toilet) but no shower cabin. The skipper will anchor in a spot with good water quality, but avoid swallowing seawater. If you get seasick, take medication an hour before departure. The catamaran is stable, but if you are sensitive, the motion can still affect you. Keep your phone in a waterproof case. The sun reflection off the water is strong, so use a high SPF sunscreen and reapply every two hours.

What to Do After the Charter

Your private catamaran hire for a birthday in Marbella usually ends back at the departure port. From there, you can walk to a nearby restaurant for dinner. In Puerto Banús, options include the beach clubs like Ocean Club or the seafood restaurants on the marina. In Marbella Marina, you are close to the old town with its tapas bars and fine dining. If you departed from Cabopino, there is a beachfront chiringuito called Los Sardinales that does good grilled fish. Estepona has a lovely old town with narrow streets and plenty of places to eat. Sotogrande is more upscale, with the marina restaurants and the nearby golf clubs. Benalmádena has the Tivoli World amusement park if you want to keep the party going. The skipper can recommend a place if you ask. Most owners will let you leave your bags on the boat until the end, but do not leave valuables unattended.

Why a Catamaran Beats a Motor Yacht for a Birthday

For a birthday party, a catamaran has clear advantages over a motor yacht. The deck space is much larger, with a trampoline at the front, a flybridge on top, and a cockpit at the back. You can spread out and have different groups doing different things. The stability means you can walk around with a drink without spilling it. The shallow draft allows the skipper to anchor closer to the beach, so you can wade ashore. Motor yachts are faster and more luxurious, but they are also narrower and more prone to rolling. If you want to dance, a catamaran is better. If you want a quiet, elegant cruise, a motor yacht might be a better choice. For a birthday with 10 to 18 guests, a catamaran is the practical choice. It is also generally cheaper than a motor yacht of similar size, which leaves more budget for catering and extras.

Booking for a Group Larger Than 18 Guests

If you have more than 18 guests, you cannot fit everyone on one catamaran. The maximum capacity is set by the boat's licence and insurance. The solution is to charter two catamarans and raft them together. This is common for milestone birthdays with 20 to 30 guests. You can book two identical cats or different ones, depending on availability. The skippers will coordinate the route and anchor side by side so you can move between the boats. You will need to book both boats through BoatHire24 separately, but you can mention in the inquiry that you want them to be together. The cost will be roughly double, but you can split it among the guests. For very large groups, you might also consider a superyacht, but those are price on request and usually require a longer booking. Catamarans are the most practical option for a birthday party on the water in Marbella.

title: Rent Catamaran Marbella Port
metaDescription: Rent a catamaran in Marbella port with a skipper. Compare prices, ports & boats. Book your Costa del Sol charter today on BoatHire24.
h1: Rent a Catamaran in Marbella Port
intro: You want to rent a catamaran in Marbella port. That means you want a proper day out on the water without the hassle of driving a boat yourself. Every catamaran on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper, so you can sit back, drink something cold, and let someone else handle the navigation. Marbella port (Puerto Deportivo) is one of the main departure points on the Costa del Sol, right next to the golden-mile strip and a short walk from the old town. From here you can head towards Puerto Banús, Cabopino, or even the Marbella coast towards Estepona. The boats are modern, well-maintained, and typically range from 35 to 55 feet. Prices start from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day and go up depending on size, season, and extras. You can browse available catamarans on BoatHire24 and book directly with the owner.
bodyHtml:
What You Get When You Rent a Catamaran in Marbella Port

A catamaran charter in Marbella port includes the boat, a licensed skipper, fuel for a standard route, and basic safety equipment. Most charters also provide a cooler with ice, a Bluetooth speaker, and sometimes snorkelling gear. You can bring your own food and drinks or ask the owner about catering options. The skipper speaks English and Spanish, and will handle the mooring, anchoring, and any weather decisions. You do not need a boating licence. The boat is yours for the agreed time, usually 4, 6, or 8 hours. Some owners offer sunset cruises or half-day morning trips. The price is per boat, not per person, so splitting with friends makes it cheaper.

Marbella Port: The Best Starting Point for Your Catamaran Trip

Marbella port, officially called Puerto Deportivo de Marbella, sits right in the centre of town. It has 220 berths and a row of restaurants along the quay. You can park nearby (paid parking) and walk straight to the boat. The port is protected by a breakwater, so boarding is calm even when the sea is a bit choppy outside. From here you have quick access to the Marbella coastline east towards Cabopino and west towards Puerto Banús. The advantage of departing from Marbella port is that you avoid the crowds of Banús and get a more relaxed start. The port also has a fuel station and a small supermarket if you need last-minute supplies. For more details on departure options, see our search page.

Catamaran Sizes and Layouts Available for Rent

Most catamarans for rent in Marbella port are between 35 and 55 feet. A 40-foot catamaran typically has 4 cabins and 2 toilets, sleeps 8-10 people, and has a large trampoline net at the front. The cockpit has a table and bench seating for dining. The flybridge (upper deck) gives you 360-degree views and sun pads. A 50-foot catamaran adds more space, a bigger saloon, and sometimes a small galley. All boats have a bimini top for shade. You can also find smaller 30-foot cats for couples or small groups, and larger 60-foot ones for events. Each boat listing on BoatHire24 includes a deck plan and photos. If you are unsure which size fits your group, contact the owner through the platform.

Popular Routes from Marbella Port

When you rent a catamaran in Marbella port, the skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences. The most common route goes west along the coast past Puerto Banús, then to Cala del Faro or the Cabo Pino lighthouse. This takes about 1.5 hours each way, leaving time for swimming and lunch. Another option is to head east towards the Marbella beach clubs and then to the sand dunes of Cabopino. If you want a longer trip, you can go to Estepona (about 2 hours west) or even to the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins, but that requires a full-day charter. The skipper will always anchor in a sheltered bay for swimming. You can also request a stop at a beach club for lunch, but you need to book that separately.

Prices and What Affects the Cost

Prices to rent a catamaran in Marbella port start from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day (4 hours) on a 40-foot boat. A full day (8 hours) on the same boat is around EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,500. Larger catamarans (50 feet plus) cost EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,000 for a full day. Prices are higher in July and August, and lower in May, June, September, and October. Bank holidays and weekends also cost more. Extras like catering, water toys (paddleboard, jet ski), or a hostess add EUR 100 to EUR 300 per item. Fuel is usually included for a standard route, but if you go far (e.g. to Gibraltar), you may pay extra. The price includes VAT and the skipper. You pay a 30% deposit to confirm the booking, and the balance is due on the day, usually in cash or by card. For exact prices, check the listings on BoatHire24.

Best Time of Year to Rent a Catamaran in Marbella Port

The season runs from April to October, with the best weather from June to September. In July and August, average air temperature is 30°C, sea temperature is 24°C, and there is very little wind in the mornings. This is perfect for swimming and lounging. However, it is also the busiest time, so book at least two weeks in advance. May and June are cooler (25°C air, 20°C sea) but less crowded. September and October are warm and calm, with lower prices and fewer boats. The water is still swimmable until mid-October. From November to March, most catamarans are not available for charter, though some owners do winter maintenance or off-season trips on request. For a more detailed guide, read our blog.

Who Should Rent a Catamaran in Marbella Port

Catamarans are ideal for groups who want stability, space, and comfort. They do not heel like monohulls, so nobody gets seasick. They are good for families with children because the trampoline net is safe and the shallow draft allows anchoring close to shore. They are also popular for birthday parties, hen or stag groups, corporate events, and photo shoots. The wide deck and flybridge make them suitable for up to 12 passengers (the legal limit for a catamaran under 24m). If you want a more active trip, you can add water toys. If you want a romantic sunset cruise, a smaller catamaran with just your partner works well. Basically, if you want a floating terrace with a skipper, rent a catamaran.

How to Book a Catamaran in Marbella Port on BoatHire24

Go to the search page, select Marbella port as the departure location, choose catamaran as the boat type, and pick your date and duration. The system shows available boats with prices, photos, and owner profiles. You can send a message to the owner to ask questions or request extras. Once you agree, you pay a deposit via the platform (secure payment). The owner confirms the booking and sends you the meeting point details. On the day, you meet the skipper at the port, sign a simple rental agreement, and board. The skipper gives a safety briefing and then you depart. At the end, you pay the balance and tip the skipper if you wish. The whole process takes about 10 minutes online. For help, contact BoatHire24 support.

What to Bring on Your Catamaran Charter

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50), a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a swimsuit. The sun is strong even in May. Bring a light jacket or windbreaker for the evening. You can bring your own food and drinks in a cooler, but most boats have a fridge and ice. Do not bring glass bottles because broken glass on deck is dangerous. Bring a waterproof phone case or a dry bag. If you plan to snorkel, bring your own mask or ask the owner if they provide them. Some owners supply paddleboards or kayaks on request. You do not need to bring towels for the boat, but bring your own for swimming. The skipper will have a first aid kit and a VHF radio. Leave valuables onshore. The boat has a safe for small items.

Nearby Attractions and Things to Do After Your Charter

Marbella port is surrounded by restaurants, bars, and shops. After your catamaran trip, you can walk to the old town (Casco Antiguo) for tapas or to the beachfront promenade (Paseo Marítimo). The port itself has several seafood restaurants with terrace seating. If you want to extend your day, Puerto Banús is 10 minutes by taxi and has luxury boutiques and nightclubs. For a quieter evening, go to the fishing port of Cabopino or the dunes of Artola. The La Concha mountain is visible from the port and offers hiking trails. If you have time, drive to Estepona old town (25 minutes) or visit the dolphin colonies near Gibraltar (1.5 hours). For a full guide, check our blog.

Frequently Asked Questions About Renting a Catamaran in Marbella Port

Below are the most common questions we get from customers. If you have a specific query, contact the owner through the listing.

Why Choose Marbella Port Over Puerto Banús for Your Catamaran

Puerto Banús is flashier, but Marbella port is more practical. Banús gets packed with superyachts and party boats, meaning more noise and less space to manoeuvre. Marbella port has wider berths, cheaper parking (around EUR 2 per hour versus EUR 4 in Banús), and a supermarket right on the quay. You also avoid the bottleneck at the Banús harbour entrance, which can take 20 minutes to clear on a Saturday. The sea conditions are identical from both ports because they are only 3 km apart. The main difference is the vibe: Banús is for people who want to be seen, Marbella port is for people who want to enjoy the boat. If you are renting for a relaxed family day or a quiet group, Marbella port is the better choice.

Catamaran Charter for Large Groups: Capacity and Layout Tips

If you have 10 to 12 people, you need a catamaran of at least 45 feet. A Lagoon 450 or Bali 4.6 works well because they have four double cabins, two heads, and a large saloon that opens to the cockpit. The trampoline at the front can hold four people lying down, and the flybridge seats another six. For 12 passengers, the skipper is the 13th person, which is the legal limit under Spanish maritime regulations. Do not try to squeeze more people on board; the Guardia Civil does random checks and fines can reach EUR 3,000. If you have more than 12, you need to charter two catamarans or a larger monohull. On BoatHire24, each listing clearly states the maximum passenger count including the skipper, so filter by that number.

What to Expect from the Skipper on Your Catamaran Charter

The skipper is not a tour guide, but they know the coast well. They will point out landmarks like La Concha mountain, the Marbella Club Hotel, and the Cabopino dunes. They can recommend swimming spots based on the wind direction. If the wind is from the east (Levante), they will anchor in the lee of Cabo Pino. If it is from the west (Poniente), they will head towards Cala del Faro. The skipper will also handle the anchor, the fenders, and the lines. They will not serve drinks or cook, but they are happy to help you set up the BBQ if the boat has one. Most skippers work on a tip basis, with EUR 50 to EUR 100 being standard for a good day. You can request a skipper who speaks your language when you book.

Catamaran Charter with Water Toys: What Is Available

Many catamarans in Marbella port offer optional water toys. The most common is a paddleboard (SUP), which costs around EUR 50 extra for the day. Some boats have a towable banana or a donut for EUR 100 to EUR 150. A few owners keep a small inflatable kayak on board. Jet skis are rare on catamarans because of storage space, but you can arrange a separate jet ski rental that meets you at the anchorage. Snorkelling gear is usually included for free, but the quality varies. Bring your own mask if you have one. The best snorkelling spots near Marbella port are at the Cabopino reef and the rocky area near Cala del Faro. Visibility is better in the morning before the wind picks up. Ask the owner what toys are available before you book.

How Weather Affects Your Catamaran Trip from Marbella Port

The Costa del Sol has reliable weather, but the wind can be a problem. The Levante wind blows from the east and can reach 25 knots, creating a choppy sea along the coast. The Poniente wind from the west is lighter and smoother. Most skippers will cancel or reschedule if the wind exceeds 20 knots, especially on a catamaran because the wide hulls slam into waves. In July and August, the wind is usually calm until 2 pm, then a light sea breeze picks up. In May and June, the wind is more unpredictable. If the forecast is bad, the owner will offer you a different date or a full refund. Do not argue with the skipper's decision; they know the local conditions. For real-time weather, check the AEMET forecast for the Costa del Sol before your trip.

What to Do If You Have Never Been on a Catamaran Before

If you are a first-timer, a catamaran is the best choice because it does not tilt. You will feel stable even when anchored. The skipper will give a short safety briefing about the life jackets, the toilet (do not flush paper), and the location of the fire extinguisher. You can ask them to show you how to steer at the helm, but they will not let you dock or anchor. Most first-timers spend the day on the trampoline net or the flybridge sun pads. Bring seasickness tablets if you are worried, but on a catamaran the motion is minimal. The only time you might feel sick is if you anchor in a swell, which the skipper will avoid. The crew on the boat are there to help, so ask questions. For more tips, read our blog on catamaran etiquette.

Catamaran Charter for Special Occasions: Birthdays, Proposals, and Events

Catamarans are popular for celebrations in Marbella port. For a birthday, you can decorate the boat with balloons and banners, but check with the owner first because some do not allow confetti or glitter. For a proposal, the skipper can anchor at sunset near the Cabopino lighthouse or in the calm waters of Cala del Faro. You can arrange a photographer to meet you at the port or come on board (extra fee). For corporate events, catamarans work well for up to 12 people with a catered lunch and a presentation screen on the flybridge. Some owners offer a DJ setup or a sound system upgrade for an extra EUR 200. The key is to book at least three weeks in advance for any special occasion, especially in July and August. The owner will help you plan the itinerary.

How to Get to Marbella Port and Where to Park

Marbella port is at Avenida del Mar, right next to the old town. If you drive, use the underground parking at Puerto Deportivo (entrance on Calle de la Cruz). It costs around EUR 2 per hour and has 300 spaces. It fills up by 11 am on weekends, so arrive early. Alternatively, park at the surface lot near the roundabout at the port entrance (EUR 1.50 per hour). From Malaga airport, it is a 40-minute drive via the AP-7 toll road (EUR 5 toll). From Puerto Banús, it is a 10-minute taxi ride (EUR 12). If you are staying in Marbella centre, you can walk to the port in 10 minutes. The meeting point for your charter is usually at the main ramp near the petrol station. The skipper will send you the exact pontoon number by message. Do not rely on Google Maps inside the port because the layout is confusing.

intro:
If you want to charter a motor yacht in Puerto Banus, you are looking at the most direct way to experience the Costa del Sol from the water. Puerto Banus is the superyacht capital of southern Spain, a marina built for showing off, and a motor yacht is the right tool for the job. bodyHtml:
What a Motor Yacht Charter in Puerto Banus Includes

When you charter a motor yacht in Puerto Banus, you get the boat, a licensed skipper, and usually fuel for a standard day trip. The skipper is a local professional who knows the coast, the anchorages, and the best spots for swimming. You do not need a boating licence, and you do not need to worry about navigation or docking. The charter includes the boat for a set number of hours, typically 4, 6, or 8 hours. Some companies offer half-day or full-day rates. You can also book multi-day charters for overnight trips to places like Estepona or Gibraltar.

Most motor yachts come with a flybridge or a sun deck, a cabin with a bathroom, a kitchen or galley, and a sound system. You bring your own food and drinks, or you can add catering. Some charters include a crew member who serves drinks and snacks. The skipper can also arrange a water toys package: jet skis, paddleboards, or snorkel gear. You pay extra for these, but they are worth it if you want to make the most of a calm anchorage.

Puerto Banus: The Best Departure Port for a Motor Yacht Charter

Puerto Banus is the most famous marina on the Costa del Sol, and for good reason. It sits right in the middle of the Marbella coastline, surrounded by luxury boutiques, restaurants, and nightclubs. The marina has over 900 berths, and it is the home base for some of the largest motor yachts in the Mediterranean. Departing from Puerto Banus means you are five minutes from the open sea, with direct access to the best cruising grounds in the area.

From Puerto Banus, you can head east toward Marbella and Cabopino, or west toward Estepona and Gibraltar. The coastline is a mix of sandy beaches, rocky coves, and cliffside villas. The water is calm for most of the year, and the visibility is excellent for swimming and snorkeling. The marina itself is a destination: you can dock for lunch at one of the waterfront restaurants, or walk into the port town for shopping. If you are staying in Marbella, Puerto Banus is the most convenient departure point.

Other Departure Ports on the Costa del Sol

If you are based elsewhere on the coast, you can still charter a motor yacht. BoatHire24 lists boats in six ports along the Costa del Sol. Search all available motor yachts to find the nearest departure point to your accommodation.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a smaller, more relaxed port than Puerto Banus. It is located in the center of Marbella, close to the old town and the beach promenade. The marina has a mix of fishing boats and leisure yachts, and it is a good option if you want a quieter start to your day.

Cabopino is a small marina in the dunes between Marbella and Fuengirola. It is popular with families because the beach is wide and the water is shallow. The marina has a few restaurants and a chiringuito on the beach. Cabopino is a good choice for a half-day charter with kids.

Estepona is a traditional Andalusian town with a modern marina. The old town is worth a visit before or after your charter. The coast west of Estepona is less developed, with more natural coves and fewer crowds.

Sotogrande is an exclusive residential area with a large marina and a polo club. The boats here tend to be larger and more expensive. Sotogrande is close to Gibraltar, so it is a good base for a day trip to the Strait.

Benalmadena is a lively port with a large marina and a casino. It is close to Torremolinos and Fuengirola, and it is a good option if you are staying on the western Costa del Sol. The marina has plenty of bars and restaurants for after your charter.

Types of Motor Yachts Available for Charter

Motor yachts come in different sizes and styles. The most common types for charter in Puerto Banus are flybridge motor yachts, sport yachts, and express cruisers. Flybridge yachts have an upper deck with a helm station and seating, which gives you panoramic views and extra space. Sport yachts are faster and more streamlined, with a lower profile and a focus on performance. Express cruisers have a single-level layout with a large cockpit and a sun pad on the bow.

For a group of 6 to 12 people, a 40 to 60 foot motor yacht is the sweet spot. These boats have enough space for everyone to lounge on the deck, eat at the table, and use the cabin for changing. For larger groups, you can charter a 70 to 100 foot yacht with multiple cabins, a flybridge, and a crew of two or three. Superyachts over 100 feet are available on request, with prices starting from around EUR 10,000 per day.

If you want speed, look for a RIB or a speedboat. These are smaller, faster, and more agile. They are not as comfortable as a motor yacht for a full day, but they are perfect for a 2 or 3 hour trip to a nearby cove. Some RIBs can seat up to 10 people and reach speeds of 40 knots. You can also charter a fishing boat if you want to try deep-sea fishing. These boats are equipped with rods, reels, and a fish finder, and the skipper knows the best spots for tuna, dorado, and sea bass.

Pricing Guidance for Motor Yacht Charters

Prices for a motor yacht charter in Puerto Banus vary by boat size, age, and season. A 30 to 40 foot motor yacht for a half day (4 hours) costs from around EUR 800 to EUR 1,500. A full day (8 hours) on the same boat costs from around EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500. For a 50 to 60 foot yacht, expect to pay from EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,500 for a full day. Larger yachts over 70 feet start from EUR 5,000 per day and go up to EUR 15,000 or more for a superyacht.

Fuel is usually included in the price for a standard day trip within 20 nautical miles of the port. If you want to go further, for example to Gibraltar or Marbella, you may need to pay extra for fuel. Some charters include a crew of two (skipper and deckhand), while others charge extra for a second crew member. Always confirm what is included before you book. Prices are higher in July and August, when demand is highest. Shoulder season (May, June, September, October) offers better value and still good weather.

Best Seasons for a Motor Yacht Charter in Puerto Banus

The charter season on the Costa del Sol runs from April to October. The best months for a motor yacht charter are May, June, September, and October. The weather is warm but not too hot, with air temperatures between 22 and 30 degrees Celsius. The sea temperature is comfortable for swimming from June to October, reaching 24 degrees in August. July and August are the hottest months, with temperatures often above 35 degrees. The water is warm, but the ports and anchorages are crowded. If you want a quieter experience, book for May or September.

Winter charters are possible but less common. The weather can be windy and the sea rough. Some boats are available for day trips in November and December, but you should check the forecast carefully. The advantage of a winter charter is lower prices and empty anchorages. You can still get a sunny day with 18 degrees and calm seas, but it is a gamble.

Popular Destinations for a Motor Yacht Charter from Puerto Banus

From Puerto Banus, you have several options for a day cruise. The most popular destination is Cala del Faro, a small cove about 3 nautical miles west of the port. It has a sandy beach, clear water, and a cliffside restaurant. The cove is sheltered from the wind, so it is a good spot for swimming and anchoring. Another option is Cabo Pino, a nature reserve with dunes and a beach. The water is shallow and calm, ideal for families.

If you want a longer trip, head west to Estepona. The old town is worth a visit, and the marina has good restaurants. The coast between Puerto Banus and Estepona is dotted with small coves and beaches. You can stop for lunch at a chiringuito on the beach. For a full-day adventure, go to the Strait of Gibraltar. The crossing takes about 2 hours from Puerto Banus. You will see dolphins and sometimes whales. You can anchor near Tarifa or Gibraltar and have lunch on board.

East of Puerto Banus, you can cruise to Marbella and Cabopino. The coastline is lined with villas and hotels. You can stop at the Marbella Club beach or the Puente Romano beach. Further east, you can reach Benalmadena and Fuengirola. These are more built-up areas, but the beaches are good for swimming.

Who Should Charter a Motor Yacht in Puerto Banus

A motor yacht charter is for anyone who wants to spend a day on the water without the hassle of driving a boat. It is popular with couples, families, and groups of friends. The skipper handles everything, so you can relax and enjoy the scenery. Motor yachts are also a good choice for corporate events, birthday parties, and celebrations. You can book catering, music, and decorations. The boat becomes a private venue for your event.

If you are a first-time boater, a motor yacht is easier to enjoy than a sailing yacht. There is no heeling, no sails to manage, and no need to understand wind direction. The boat is stable and comfortable, even at speed. You can sit on the bow or the flybridge and watch the coast go by. The skipper will point out landmarks and tell you about the area.

How to Book a Motor Yacht Charter in Puerto Banus

Booking a motor yacht charter through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, select Puerto Banus as the departure port, choose your dates and group size, and browse the available boats. Each listing includes photos, a description, a price, and a calendar of availability. You can send an inquiry or book directly online. The platform handles the payment and the contract.

When you book, you will need to provide a deposit, usually 30 to 50 percent of the total. The balance is due on the day of the charter. You can cancel up to 48 hours before the charter for a full refund, but check the terms of each listing. The skipper will meet you at the marina at the agreed time. You will go through a safety briefing and then set off. The skipper will ask you where you want to go and how long you want to stay at each stop. You can change the plan during the day if the weather or your mood changes.

For more tips on planning your charter, read the BoatHire24 blog. You will find guides on what to bring, how to choose a boat, and the best anchorages on the Costa del Sol.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Motor Yacht Charter

BoatHire24 is a marketplace that lists boats from multiple owners and charter companies. You compare prices, sizes, and amenities in one place. The platform is free to use, and you pay the same price as booking directly with the owner. The benefit is that you see all the options in one search, rather than contacting each company separately. The platform also provides secure payment and customer support.

All boats on BoatHire24 are licensed and insured. The skippers are experienced and speak English and Spanish. The platform verifies the boats and the skippers, so you know you are getting a legitimate charter. If you have any questions, you can contact the BoatHire24 team before you book. They know the local market and can recommend a boat that fits your group and budget.

title: Hire Speedboat Marbella No Licence
metaDescription: Hire a speedboat in Marbella with no licence needed. Self-drive RIBs and day boats from Puerto Banús. Book online. Prices from around EUR 250.
h1: Hire Speedboat Marbella No Licence: Self-Drive Fun
intro:
You want to race across the Mediterranean without a boat licence. That is possible on the Costa del Sol. A handful of day boats and small RIBs are available for hire without any paperwork, as long as you follow the rules: stick to daylight hours, stay within 2 nautical miles of the coast, and keep the engine under 15 horsepower (or equivalent electric power). The result is a surprisingly affordable way to explore the coastline on your own terms.

On BoatHire24 you can filter for licence-free options in Marbella, Puerto Banús, and nearby ports. Most of these boats are simple to operate, stable at low speeds, and come with a quick safety briefing. You do not get a skipper, but you do get freedom. Here is what you need to know before you book.
bodyHtml:
What "No Licence" Actually Means in Spain

Spanish maritime law divides recreational boats into two categories: those requiring a skipper with a licence (Patrón de Navegación Básica or similar) and those that do not. The licence-free boats are limited to less than 15 horsepower (or 11 kW electric), a maximum length of 5 metres, and a top speed of around 10 knots. In practice, that means small RIBs with a 9.9 hp outboard, or electric day boats that are basically battery-powered pontoons. You can carry up to 5 passengers, and you must stay within 2 nautical miles of the shore. No night navigation, no crossing to Africa, no racing. But for a day out on the water, it is more than enough.

These rules are enforced by the Guardia Civil and local port authorities. If you are caught outside the limits or with an overpowered engine, you risk a fine of several hundred euros. Stick to the guidelines and you will be fine. The boat owner will explain the limits during the handover.

Where You Can Pick Up a Licence-Free Speedboat

Most licence-free boats are based in Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) and Puerto Banús. A few are also available in Cabopino, Estepona, and Benalmádena. The advantage of Marbella is the sheltered bay and the short run to the coastline. From Puerto Banús you can head east towards the Marbella beaches or west towards the Cala del Faro and the cliffs of Cabo Pino. From Estepona you have the old town beach and the long promenade. Each port has its own charm, but the boats are essentially the same: small, simple, and restricted.

If you want a bit more power, you can hire a RIB with a 25 hp or 40 hp engine, but that requires a Spanish or international boating licence. The licence-free option is strictly for the low-horsepower boats. Check the boat listing on BoatHire24 for the engine specs before you book.

Typical Boats Available: RIBs, Day Boats, and Electric Launches

The most common licence-free boat is a 4.5-metre RIB with a 9.9 hp outboard. It seats 4 to 5 people, has a small canopy for shade, and tops out at about 8 knots. You can also find electric day boats, which are quieter and have zero emissions. These are essentially battery-powered pontoons with a tiller steering, cruising at 4-5 knots. They are perfect for a lazy afternoon of swimming and sunbathing. Some operators also offer small aluminium fishing boats with the same engine restrictions.

All these boats are easy to drive. If you have ever used an outboard motor on a dinghy, you can handle these. The controls are a tiller with a twist-grip throttle and a kill-switch lanyard. The briefing takes 10 minutes. You do not need any prior experience, but you do need to be comfortable with basic manoeuvring in a marina.

Pricing Guidance: What You Will Pay

Prices for a licence-free speedboat hire in Marbella start from around EUR 250 for a half-day (4 hours) and EUR 350 for a full day (8 hours). Electric boats are slightly cheaper, from EUR 200 for half a day. Fuel is usually included in the price because the engines are so small. Some operators charge a refundable deposit of EUR 200-500, payable by credit card. You can also book by the hour, typically EUR 80-120 per hour for a RIB.

Peak season (July and August) prices are about 20% higher. Off-peak (October to May) you can find deals for EUR 150 half-day. Always check the cancellation policy. Most operators offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before departure. You can compare prices and availability on BoatHire24.

Do You Need a Licence for a Jet Ski or a Small Inflatable?

Jet skis are a different category. In Spain, you need a specific licence (Patrón de Navegación Básica or PNB) to drive a jet ski, regardless of engine power. No licence-free jet skis exist. Small inflatable boats with a 3.5 hp engine are technically licence-free, but they are not commonly rented because they are too slow for most people. Stick to the RIBs and day boats listed on the site.

Best Time of Year to Hire a Speedboat in Marbella

The Mediterranean coast of Spain is pleasant from April to October. Water temperatures reach 22-26 degrees C in summer. The wind is usually light in the morning, picking up in the afternoon. The best conditions for a small boat are between 9am and 2pm, before the sea breeze builds. If you go in July or August, book early morning to avoid the heat and the afternoon chop. Spring and autumn offer calm seas and fewer crowds. Winter is possible but the water is cold (14-16 degrees C) and the days are short.

Check the wind forecast on Windy or Windguru before you go. A small RIB is fine in up to 15 knots of wind. Anything stronger and it gets bumpy. The boat owner will typically cancel if the forecast is bad, but you can also reschedule.

How to Book a Licence-Free Speedboat on BoatHire24

Go to BoatHire24 search and filter by "No Licence Required" under the boat features. Select your preferred port, date, and duration. The system will show you available boats with real-time pricing. You can book online and pay by card. The confirmation email includes the exact meeting point, the owner's contact details, and a checklist of what to bring. Most operators require a valid ID or passport and a credit card for the deposit. You do not need a licence, but you do need to be at least 18 years old (or 21 for some operators).

If you have any questions about a specific boat, use the chat function on the listing page. The owner usually replies within an hour. You can also call the BoatHire24 support line for general advice.

Who Should Hire a Licence-Free Speedboat

This option is ideal for tourists who want a few hours of independence on the water without the expense of a skipper. Families with older children, couples, and small groups of friends all enjoy it. You can anchor in a quiet cove, swim, have a picnic, and explore the coastline at your own pace. It is not suitable for watersports like wakeboarding or tubing because the engine is too weak. It is also not for long-distance trips. You are limited to the area near the port.

If you want to go further, hire a boat with a skipper. That gives you access to larger engines, faster speeds, and the ability to visit remote beaches and coves. But for a simple, licence-free day out, these small boats are hard to beat.

Local Tips for Your Day on the Water

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, and plenty of water. There is no shade on a RIB. Pack a waterproof bag for your phone and wallet. Swim fins and a mask are useful for snorkelling. The best spots near Marbella are the Cala del Faro (a rocky cove with clear water), the beach at Cabopino (sand dunes and a nudist area), and the area off the Marbella Club hotel (calm and shallow). Avoid anchoring near the busy swimming zones in front of Puerto Banús. The Guardia Civil patrols and will move you on.

Fuel is included in the price, so you do not need to worry about refuelling. The small outboard engine will run for 6-8 hours on a single tank. If you run out, call the owner and they will come to assist. But that rarely happens if you keep the throttle at cruising speed (around 6 knots) instead of full throttle.

Frequently Asked Questions About Licence-Free Speedboat Hire

This section answers common questions. For more details, read our blog post on boating licences in Spain.

The Ports in Detail: Where to Launch and What to Expect

Puerto Banús is the glitzy option. You launch from the marina next to the superyachts and designer shops. The channel is busy with water taxis and tenders, so take it slow. Once outside, you have a straight run east to Marbella's beaches or west to the Cala del Faro. The harbour fee is usually included in the rental price, but check. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more relaxed. It sits at the western end of the promenade, with a fuel dock and a ramp. From here you can head to the Rio Verde estuary, which is a calm spot for anchoring. Cabopino is a small marina with a sandy beach and the Artola dunes. It is quieter than the others, and the run to the coves is short. Estepona has a long pier and a protected bay. You can motor along the old town beach and stop for lunch at a chiringuito. Benalmádena is further east, near the marina with the dolphin statue. It is a longer drive from Marbella, but the coastline is varied. Each port has its own character, but the boat experience is the same: small, simple, and restricted to the near-shore zone.

Realistic Range: How Far You Can Actually Go

With a 9.9 hp engine and a 2-nautical-mile limit, your range is about 5 nautical miles from the port, maybe 7 if you push it. That sounds limited, but along the Costa del Sol coast that covers a lot of ground. From Puerto Banús you can reach the Cala del Faro (2 NM west), the Marbella Club beach (1 NM east), and the Cabopino dunes (3 NM east). From Estepona you can get to the Playa del Cristo (1 NM west) and the Punta de la Doncella (1 NM east). The key is to plan your route before you leave. Do not try to go from Marbella to Sotogrande in a licence-free boat. That is 15 NM and you will run out of fuel and time. Stick to the local area. The best strategy is to pick a port that is close to the spots you want to visit. If you want the sand dunes, launch from Cabopino. If you want the Marbella beaches, launch from Puerto Banús. If you want the old town, launch from Estepona. The boat owner will give you a map with the permitted zones. Follow it.

What to Bring and What the Boat Provides

The boat comes with life jackets for everyone (mandatory), a kill-switch lanyard, a paddle, a buoyancy aid, and a basic tool kit. Some operators include a small cooler bag and a bottle of water. You should bring your own towels, sunscreen (factor 50, the sun is brutal), a hat, and polarised sunglasses. A waterproof phone pouch is essential. You will want to take photos and use the GPS on your phone. The boat does not have a radio or GPS, so your phone is your navigation aid. Download the Navionics app or use Google Maps in satellite mode. The signal is good close to shore. Bring snacks and drinks, but no glass on board. A small inflatable paddleboard or snorkel gear is fine, but check the weight limit. The boat can carry a maximum of 400 kg including passengers. Four adults and a paddleboard is near the limit. Pack light.

Safety Briefing and Handover Process

The owner meets you at the port 15 minutes before your booking time. They show you the boat, explain the controls, and go through the safety briefing. This includes the kill-switch procedure, the location of the life jackets, the fire extinguisher, and the emergency contact number. They also show you the permitted navigation area on a map. You sign a rental agreement and a liability waiver. The deposit is held on your credit card as a pre-authorisation. The whole process takes 20 minutes. Then you are free to go. The owner watches you leave the marina and will call you if you look like you are heading out of bounds. They are usually friendly and helpful. If you have any issues on the water, call the number they gave you. They will either talk you through it or come out to assist. The handover is straightforward. Do not be nervous. The boat is simple.

Weather and Sea Conditions: When to Stay Ashore

The Costa del Sol is known for calm seas, but the afternoon wind is a real factor. From May to September, the westerly wind (Poniente) picks up around 1pm and can reach 15-20 knots by 4pm. That is fine for a larger boat but uncomfortable in a small RIB. The sea state becomes choppy with 0.5-1 metre waves. Your small boat will bang and spray. The best plan is to go out at 9am, enjoy the calm morning, and return by 2pm. If you book a full day, take a long lunch break on the beach during the windy hours and go back out at 6pm when the wind drops. In spring and autumn, the wind is lighter and more variable. Winter can have days of flat calm, but also storms. Check the forecast the night before. If the wind is forecast above 20 knots, the boat owner will cancel. You can reschedule for free. Do not argue with them. They know the local conditions.

Licence-Free Boats vs. Skippered Charters: Which Is Right for You

If you want to drive yourself, explore at your own pace, and save money, the licence-free boat is the choice. It costs EUR 250-350 for a full day. If you want to go further, faster, and with more comfort, hire a boat with a skipper. A 30-foot motor yacht with a skipper costs from EUR 800 for a half day. That includes fuel, the skipper's fee, and insurance. You sit back and relax. The skipper knows the best coves, the anchor spots, and the local restaurants. You can also go to places like the Nerja caves (20 NM from Marbella) or the Strait of Gibraltar (40 NM) to see dolphins. The licence-free boat cannot do that. The skippered charter is better for groups of 6-8 people, for celebrations, or for a full-day excursion. The licence-free boat is better for a couple or a small family who want a simple day out. Both are available on BoatHire24. Filter by "No Licence Required" or "With Skipper" to compare.

The Deposit and Insurance Explained

Most operators require a refundable deposit of EUR 200-500. This is held as a pre-authorisation on your credit card. It is not charged unless you damage the boat. Common damages include hitting the propeller on a rock, tearing the fabric of the RIB tube, or losing the kill-switch lanyard. The deposit covers the first EUR 200-500 of damage. If the damage costs more, you pay the excess. Insurance is included in the rental price but it is basic third-party liability. It does not cover damage to the boat itself. That is why the deposit exists. To avoid losing your deposit, take care when anchoring. Do not run the engine in shallow water. Do not beach the boat. Keep the kill-switch lanyard attached to you at all times. If you lose it, you pay EUR 50 for a replacement. The deposit is released within 48 hours of returning the boat, provided there is no damage. Check the terms on the listing page before you book.

What Happens If You Break the Rules

The Guardia Civil and the port police patrol the coast. They stop boats to check licences, life jackets, and navigation limits. If you are caught outside the 2 NM zone or with an unlicensed driver, the fine is EUR 300-600. The boat can be impounded. The owner will also charge you for the impound fees and lost rental days. It is not worth the risk. The rules are clear and enforced. The owners also track the boats via GPS on some models. They will call you if you go too far. If you ignore them, they can remotely cut the engine on some newer boats. Stay within the limits. The permitted area is large enough for a good day out. Do not try to cross to Morocco or reach Gibraltar. You will not make it and you will get caught.

Last-Minute Bookings and Availability

Licence-free boats are popular in summer. Book at least a week in advance for July and August. In June and September, a few days ahead is enough. In spring and autumn, you can often book the day before. The BoatHire24 website shows real-time availability. If a boat is booked, the system suggests similar options at the same port or nearby. You can also set an alert for cancellations. Some operators offer a discount for last-minute bookings (within 48 hours) if the boat is still available. Check the "Deals" section on the search page. The best availability is for half-day morning slots. Full-day slots go first. If you are flexible on the date, you will find a boat. If you are set on a specific date, book early. The fleet of licence-free boats is small, maybe 10-20 units across all ports. They sell out quickly.
