title: Luxury Yacht Rental Marbella Week – Premium Weekly Charters
metaDescription: Book a luxury yacht rental Marbella week with a licensed skipper. Compare motor yachts, catamarans & superyachts from Puerto Banús. Reserve your premium weekly charter today.
h1: Luxury Yacht Rental Marbella Week, Premium Weekly Charters
intro:
You want a week on the water around Marbella, not a few hours. A luxury yacht rental Marbella week gives you the freedom to explore the Costa del Sol at your own pace, with a licensed skipper who knows the best coves, beach clubs, and fishing spots. No need to own a boat or have a licence. Just pick your dates, choose your yacht, and let someone else handle the navigation while you soak up the sun.

BoatHire24 connects you with private owners and charter companies across Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. Every weekly charter includes a professional skipper, fuel, and standard insurance. You pay for the boat and crew, nothing hidden. Whether you want a 15-metre motor yacht for eight guests or a 30-metre superyacht for twelve, we have options that work for a full week.
bodyHtml:
What a Luxury Yacht Rental Marbella Week Includes

A weekly charter is different from a day trip. You get the yacht for seven consecutive days, with the skipper living onboard or coming each morning, depending on the arrangement. Most charters include a stewardess or host for larger yachts, especially if you plan to entertain guests. The standard package covers the yacht, crew, fuel for a reasonable cruising range, and basic insurance. Food, drinks, marina fees, and extra fuel for long distances are usually extra. You can negotiate a full catering package or bring your own provisions. The skipper will plan a route based on your preferences, from the glitzy ports of Puerto Banús and Marbella to the quieter anchorages near Estepona or the Strait of Gibraltar.

Departure Ports for Your Weekly Charter

You can start your luxury yacht rental Marbella week from any of the main marinas on the Costa del Sol. BoatHire24 lists yachts based in Puerto Banús, the most famous luxury port in Europe, with its designer shops and superyacht berths. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a good alternative if you want to be close to the old town and the beach clubs. Cabopino is smaller and quieter, ideal if you want to head east towards Nerja or the Cala del Faro. Estepona offers a charming old town and easy access to the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can spot dolphins and pilot whales. Sotogrande is a private estate with a world-class marina, perfect for a more exclusive start. Benalmádena is a practical base with plenty of berths and a lively promenade. The skipper will advise on the best departure point based on your itinerary and the yacht’s draft.

Boat Types for a Weekly Charter

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for a week-long trip. They offer speed, space, and stability, with flybridges for sunbathing and large saloons for dining. A 15-metre motor yacht sleeps four to six guests in two or three cabins, while a 20-metre model can accommodate eight. Catamarans are another strong option, especially if you want more deck space and shallower draft for anchoring close to beaches. They are wider than monohulls, so you get more room for lounging. Sailing yachts appeal to those who want a more traditional experience, though you still get a skipper who handles the sails. RIBs and speedboats are not ideal for a full week because they lack accommodation and comfort, but you can combine a day on a RIB with a stay ashore. Fishing boats are available for angling trips, but again, not for overnight stays. Licence-free day boats are for short hops, not week-long charters. Superyachts over 24 metres are the top end, with multiple cabins, crew quarters, jet skis, and tenders. Prices for superyachts start from around EUR 50,000 per week and go up. For a standard motor yacht, expect to pay from around EUR 8,000 to EUR 25,000 per week depending on size, age, and season.

Pricing Guidance for a Weekly Charter

There is no fixed price for a luxury yacht rental Marbella week. The cost depends on the yacht’s size, age, brand, and the time of year. High season (June to September) is the most expensive, with prices 30-50% higher than low season (November to March). A 12-metre motor yacht from 2010 might cost around EUR 8,000 per week in low season, while a 20-metre yacht from 2023 could be EUR 20,000 in high season. Fuel is extra and can add EUR 1,000 to EUR 3,000 depending on how far you cruise. Marina fees are usually included in the charter price for the home port, but if you overnight in a different marina, you pay the berthing cost. Crew gratuity is not mandatory but standard at 10-15% of the charter fee. You can search our listings to compare prices and contact owners directly for a custom quote. Always ask for a full breakdown before booking.

Best Time for a Luxury Yacht Rental Marbella Week

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days a year. The best months for a weekly charter are May, June, September, and October. The weather is warm (22-28 degrees C), the sea is calm, and the marinas are less crowded than July and August. July and August are peak season, with temperatures hitting 32 degrees C and the beaches packed. You still get great conditions, but you need to book at least three months in advance. Winter charters (November to February) are possible but the sea can be rougher, and some yachts are out of the water for maintenance. The water temperature in winter drops to 15-17 degrees C, so swimming is less appealing. Spring and autumn offer the best balance of good weather and availability.

How to Book a Weekly Yacht Charter

Booking a luxury yacht rental Marbella week through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Browse the listings, filter by length, type, and price, and read the boat description and skipper profile. Contact the owner or charter company directly through the platform to check availability for your chosen week. You will need to pay a deposit (usually 50%) to secure the booking, with the balance due two weeks before departure. The platform handles the payment securely. Make sure you read the terms and conditions, especially regarding cancellation policies and weather clauses. Most charters require a security deposit (refundable) of EUR 1,000 to EUR 5,000, depending on the yacht’s value. The skipper will contact you a few days before to finalise the itinerary and discuss provisioning. You can also read our blog for tips on planning your week, from packing lists to recommended anchorages.

Who Should Book a Weekly Charter

A weekly charter is ideal for families, groups of friends, or couples celebrating a milestone. If you have six to ten people, splitting the cost makes it more affordable than you might think. Business groups also use weekly charters for corporate retreats or client entertainment, with the yacht acting as a floating meeting room and party venue. The skipper can arrange water toys like jet skis, paddleboards, and snorkelling gear. If you are a solo traveller, a weekly charter might be too expensive unless you join a shared charter (sometimes available through larger operators). The key advantage of a week is that you can cover more ground. You could cruise from Marbella to Gibraltar, stop at Estepona for lunch, anchor at Cala del Faro for a swim, and then head east to Nerja to see the caves. Or you could island-hop to the Chafarinas Islands or cross to North Africa, though that requires a visa and extra paperwork. The skipper will advise on the best route within a week’s range.

Local Highlights to Include in Your Itinerary

The Costa del Sol is packed with places worth visiting. Puerto Banús is the obvious start, with its luxury boutiques and restaurants. The La Concha mountain provides a dramatic backdrop for photos. The Río Verde estuary is a good spot for birdwatching. Cala del Faro, near Cabopino, is a secluded cove with clear water, perfect for anchoring and swimming. Estepona old town has white-washed streets and flower pots, a nice contrast to the glitz of Banús. The Strait of Gibraltar is a marine hotspot where you can see dolphins, pilot whales, and even orcas in summer. If you have time, a day trip to the Nerja caves is possible from the eastern side of the coast, though it is a two-hour cruise from Marbella. Your skipper will help you plan a route that balances cruising time with stops.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a boating licence for a weekly charter?

No. Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles all navigation and docking. You just relax and enjoy the trip.

Can I bring my own food and drink?

Yes. Most charters allow you to bring your own provisions. Some owners offer a catering package at an extra cost. Check with the owner before booking.

What is the maximum number of guests on a weekly charter?

The number depends on the yacht’s safety certificate. Most motor yachts up to 20 metres carry 8 to 12 guests. Superyachts can take up to 16. The skipper will confirm the limit.

Is fuel included in the weekly price?

Standard charters include fuel for a set number of cruising hours per day, usually 4-6. Extra fuel for longer distances is charged at cost. Ask for the fuel policy before booking.

Can I cancel my weekly charter?

Cancellation policies vary by owner. Most require 30 days’ notice for a full refund of the deposit. Check the terms on the listing page before paying.

What happens in bad weather?

The skipper has the final say on safety. If the weather is dangerous, the charter may be postponed or rerouted. You are not charged for days you cannot sail. Insurance covers cancellations due to severe weather.

Can I charter a superyacht for a week?

Yes. Superyachts over 24 metres are available for weekly charters from Puerto Banús and Sotogrande. Prices start from around EUR 50,000 per week. Contact the owner for a custom quote.

Sample Itinerary for a Marbella Week Charter

Here is a realistic seven-day route starting from Puerto Banús. Day one: board in the afternoon, settle in, and take a short evening cruise to Marbella Marina for dinner at a beach club. Day two: head east to Cabopino, anchor at Cala del Faro for swimming, and overnight at the Cabopino marina. Day three: cruise to Estepona, moor at the marina, and explore the old town with its flower-filled streets. Day four: cross to the Strait of Gibraltar area, where you will likely see common dolphins and pilot whales; anchor in a sheltered bay near Tarifa for the night. Day five: return west to Sotogrande for a day at the private marina and a round at the golf course if you are a member. Day six: cruise back towards Marbella, stopping at the Río Verde for a quiet lunch and birdwatching. Day seven: final morning in Puerto Banús, a last swim off the yacht, and disembark by midday. This itinerary covers about 120 nautical miles total, which is comfortable for a 15-20 knot motor yacht with 4-6 hours of cruising per day.

What to Pack for a Week on a Luxury Yacht

Space on a yacht is limited, even on a 20-metre model. Pack light soft bags, not hard suitcases. Bring swimwear, sun protection (SPF 50, a hat, and UV-rated clothing), and a light jacket for evenings on the water. Non-marking shoes are essential; most yachts ban black-soled shoes on deck. If you plan to eat at marinas, bring smart-casual clothes for restaurants in Puerto Banús or Sotogrande. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos on the bow. Seasickness medication is worth having even if you are not prone to it; the Strait can get choppy. The skipper will have basic first aid and safety equipment, but bring any personal medication for a full week. Leave drones at home unless you have written permission from the owner; many marinas restrict drone use.

How Crews Handle Weekly Charters

For a luxury yacht rental Marbella week, the crew typically consists of a skipper and a stewardess or host. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and docking. The stewardess manages the interior, serves meals, and keeps the yacht clean. On yachts under 15 metres, you might only get a skipper, so expect a more DIY experience. The crew live onboard for the week, usually in separate quarters. They work long hours but are entitled to rest periods. You should treat the crew with respect; they are there to make your trip safe and enjoyable, not to be servants. A common arrangement is for the crew to have a separate cabin and bathroom, so your privacy is maintained. If you want a chef, request one when booking; it adds around EUR 200-400 per day to the total cost.

Extra Costs You Might Not Expect

Beyond the charter fee and fuel, there are a few extras to budget for. Marina fees for overnight stops outside your home port range from EUR 50 to EUR 200 per night depending on the size of the yacht and the marina’s prestige. Puerto Banús is the most expensive, at around EUR 150-300 for a 15-metre yacht. Water and electricity at marinas are usually included in the berthing fee but confirm first. If you want to use the yacht’s water toys like jet skis or paddleboards, expect a surcharge of EUR 200-500 per week. Some owners charge a cleaning fee of EUR 100-300 if you leave the yacht in a mess. Provisioning for a week for six people can cost EUR 500-1,500 depending on how fancy you go. The crew gratuity at 10-15% of the charter fee is customary, so add that to your mental budget.

Legal and Insurance Details for Weekly Charters

Every yacht on BoatHire24 has valid insurance covering third-party liability and hull damage. The security deposit covers your excess in case of damage caused by guests. The deposit is typically EUR 1,000 to EUR 5,000 and is refunded within 14 days of the charter end, provided there is no damage. You should read the charter contract carefully; it will specify your responsibilities, such as not exceeding the maximum guest count and not taking the yacht outside the agreed cruising area. If you want to cross to North Africa, you need a visa for Morocco or Ceuta, and the owner must approve the crossing. The skipper will handle the paperwork for entering a different country, but it adds complexity. For charters within Spanish waters, no extra permits are needed.

title: Speedboat Hire Marbella Hourly Rate – Quick & Fun Rentals
metaDescription: Looking for speedboat hire Marbella hourly rate? Compare prices, boats & ports. Book a RIB or speedboat from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina & more. Instant quotes.
h1: Speedboat Hire Marbella Hourly Rate: Quick & Fun Rentals
intro: You want a fast boat, a short burst of adrenaline, and you don't want to spend a fortune. Speedboat hire in Marbella with an hourly rate is exactly that. Forget the day-long yacht charter, you can jump on a RIB or speedboat for an hour or two, blast along the coast, and be back in time for lunch. The hourly rate for a speedboat hire in Marbella starts from around EUR 200 per hour depending on the boat, the season, and the port you depart from. That includes a licensed skipper who knows the best spots for dolphin spotting or a quick run to Cala del Faro. No licence needed, no hidden costs, just you, the sea, and a very big engine.
bodyHtml:
What You Actually Get for the Hourly Rate

When you book a speedboat hire in Marbella on an hourly rate, you are paying for the boat, the fuel, and the skipper. The boat is typically a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) or a small motor yacht, between 5 and 9 metres long, with an engine ranging from 150 to 350 horsepower. You get life jackets, a Bluetooth speaker if you ask nicely, and a cooler with ice (bring your own drinks). The skipper handles all navigation and safety, you just sit back or take the helm if you want a go. Most operators allow up to 8 passengers on a speedboat, but check the specific boat's capacity. The hourly rate is usually quoted for a minimum of two hours, so expect to pay from around EUR 400 for a two-hour trip. Some operators offer a one-hour option, but that barely gets you out of the marina.

Ports of Departure: Where to Start Your Speedboat Adventure

You can pick up a speedboat from several ports along the Costa del Sol. The most popular is Puerto Banús, where the boats are parked right next to the superyachts. From there, you can head west to Cala del Faro or east toward Marbella's beaches. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is another good option, closer to the town centre. Cabopino is quieter and gives you quick access to the dunes. Estepona port is further west, near the old town, and Sotogrande is for the golf crowd. Benalmádena is a bit further east but still within the Marbella orbit. Each port has its own vibe and slightly different hourly rates, Puerto Banús tends to be pricier, while Estepona or Cabopino might save you EUR 20-30 per hour. Check availability at BoatHire24 for real-time pricing.

Boat Options: RIBs, Speedboats, and Small Motor Yachts

The term 'speedboat hire Marbella hourly rate' covers a few different types of vessel. The most common is a RIB, a rigid inflatable boat with a powerful outboard engine. These are light, fast, and can hit 40-50 knots. They are perfect for a short, thrilling ride. Then there are proper speedboats, fibreglass hulls with inboard or outboard engines, often more comfortable but slightly slower. Some operators offer small motor yachts (around 7-9 metres) that can still do 20-30 knots but with a bit more shade and a toilet. Fishing boats are also available at an hourly rate if you want to combine speed with a bit of angling. For the fastest experience, go for a RIB. For a bit more comfort, choose a small motor yacht. You can browse all options on the search page.

Pricing Guidance: What to Expect and What Affects the Rate

Hourly rates for speedboat hire in Marbella vary by season, boat size, and demand. In low season (November to March), you might find rates from around EUR 150 per hour. In high season (June to September), expect EUR 200-350 per hour. The most expensive boats are the large RIBs with 300+ horsepower engines. Fuel is usually included in the hourly rate, but some operators add a fuel surcharge for long distances or high speeds. Always confirm what is included before booking. Some operators also charge extra for a second skipper or for extending the trip beyond the agreed hours. A two-hour trip is the sweet spot, enough time to get to a nice cove, have a swim, and race back. For a three-hour trip, you could reach Cala del Faro from Puerto Banús, have a swim, and return. For a full day, you are better off with a half-day or full-day charter, which works out cheaper per hour. For detailed price comparisons, read our blog post on Marbella boat rental costs.

Seasons and Weather: When to Book Your Speedboat

The best time for speedboat hire in Marbella is from May to October, when the sea is calm and the sun is hot. In July and August, the water temperature hits 25 degrees C, and you can swim comfortably. The wind is usually light in the mornings, so a 10am or 11am start gives you the flattest sea. Afternoons can get choppy, especially in the western Alboran Sea near Estepona. In winter, the water is colder (around 15-17 degrees C) and the wind is stronger, but you can still go out on a calm day. The hourly rate drops significantly in low season, so if you are flexible, you can get a bargain. Check the weather forecast before booking, most operators cancel if the wind is above 20 knots or the swell is over 1.5 metres.

How to Book a Speedboat by the Hour

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24, select 'speedboat' or 'RIB' in the boat type filter, choose your port, and pick a date. The search results show available boats with their hourly rates and minimum hours. You can book online and pay a deposit (usually 30-50 percent) with the balance due on the day. Some operators accept cash on arrival. You will need to provide a list of passengers and sign a waiver. No licence is required because the skipper is included. If you want to drive the boat yourself, you need a valid boating licence (a Spanish licence or an ICC). Most speedboat hires are skipper-only, so you don't need to worry about that. You can also call or WhatsApp the operator directly through the listing.

Who Is This For? The Perfect Speedboat Experience

Speedboat hire by the hour is ideal for couples, small groups of friends, or families who want a quick thrill without committing to a full day. It is also popular for bachelor or bachelorette parties, a two-hour blast along the coast with music and a few beers. Business groups use it for team-building activities or client entertainment. If you are staying in a hotel near Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina, you can walk to the dock, jump on a boat, and be back in time for dinner. It is not for people who get seasick easily, speedboats bounce more than larger yachts. If you want a smoother ride, consider a catamaran or a sailing yacht instead. But if you want speed, wind in your hair, and the roar of an engine, this is your choice.

Local Highlights: What You Can See in an Hour or Two

From Puerto Banús, head west and you will pass the exclusive villas of the Golden Mile, then the cliffs of Cala del Faro. From Estepona, you can cruise past the old town's colourful houses and the marina. If you go east from Marbella, you get views of La Concha mountain and the Cabopino dunes. In the Strait of Gibraltar, dolphins are common, you might see common dolphins, bottlenose dolphins, or even pilot whales. Some speedboat trips from Sotogrande go toward Gibraltar itself, but that requires a longer charter. For a two-hour trip, stick to the coast near your departure port. The skipper will know the best spots for a swim or a photo stop.

Safety and Regulations

All speedboats on BoatHire24 are licensed and insured. The skipper holds a professional licence (Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo or higher). Life jackets are provided for all passengers, and children must wear them at all times. The boat is equipped with a VHF radio, flares, and a first aid kit. Speed limits apply within 500 metres of the shore (usually 3-5 knots), but once you are outside that zone, you can open the throttle. The skipper will brief you on safety before departure. Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper must remain sober, do not pressure them to drink. If you have any medical conditions, inform the operator in advance.

Comparing Hourly Rates with Other Charter Options

Speedboat hire by the hour is the most expensive way to rent a boat per hour, but it is also the cheapest total cost for a short trip. A two-hour speedboat trip for up to 8 people at EUR 200 per hour costs EUR 400 total, which is EUR 50 per person. A half-day (4 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht might cost EUR 800-1200, which is EUR 200-300 per hour but cheaper per hour than speedboat rates. If you want a longer day out, consider a half-day or full-day charter. For a quick blast, the hourly speedboat is unbeatable. You can compare all options on the search page.

Tips for Getting the Best Hourly Rate

Book in advance, especially in July and August. Last-minute bookings often cost more because of demand. Consider a weekday trip, Monday to Thursday rates can be 10-20 percent lower than weekends. Join a group to split the cost, the price is per boat, not per person, so the more people you bring (up to the capacity), the cheaper per head. Negotiate with the operator for a longer trip, sometimes a three-hour booking gets a small discount on the hourly rate. Check for special offers on BoatHire24, some operators run early-bird or last-minute deals. And always confirm the total price including any extras like fuel, tax, or cleaning fees. Read the cancellation policy, most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 48 hours in advance.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a licence to hire a speedboat in Marbella?

No, you do not need a licence because a licensed skipper is included in the hourly rate. You can relax or take the helm under the skipper's supervision, but you cannot drive alone without a licence.

What is the minimum rental period for a speedboat?

Most operators require a minimum of two hours. Some offer one-hour trips, but these are rare and usually cost more per hour. Two hours gives you enough time to enjoy the experience without feeling rushed.

Can I bring my own food and drinks on the speedboat?

Yes, you can bring your own food and drinks. Most boats have a cooler with ice. Alcohol is permitted, but the skipper must remain sober. Avoid glass bottles, use plastic or cans for safety.

What happens if the weather is bad on the day of my booking?

If the weather is unsafe (high winds, rough seas), the operator will cancel and offer a full refund or reschedule. You can also cancel up to 48 hours in advance for a full refund. Check the policy on BoatHire24.

How many people can fit on a speedboat?

Most speedboats and RIBs for hire in Marbella carry between 4 and 8 passengers, including the skipper. The exact capacity is listed on the boat's details page. Do not exceed the limit, it is a safety requirement.

Are there any hidden fees in the hourly rate?

The advertised hourly rate usually includes the boat, skipper, fuel, and basic equipment. Some operators charge extra for long distances, additional hours, or cleaning. Always confirm the total price before booking to avoid surprises.

Can I book a speedboat for a party or special occasion?

Yes, speedboat hire is popular for bachelor/bachelorette parties, birthdays, and anniversaries. Let the operator know in advance so they can arrange music, decorations, or a special route. Some boats have Bluetooth speakers.

Why the Hourly Rate Works Better Than You Think

You might look at the speedboat hire Marbella hourly rate and think it is expensive compared to renting a car. But split it among six people, and you are looking at around EUR 70 each for two hours of adrenaline. A jet ski rental for one hour costs about EUR 100-150 per person, so the speedboat is actually better value for a group. Plus you get a skipper who knows the coastline, the best swimming spots, and how to avoid the crowded areas. You also get the freedom to stop wherever you want, something you do not get on a scheduled boat tour. The hourly rate is a premium for flexibility, but the per-person cost is often lower than a similar experience on a larger charter boat.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Hourly Booking

Not all speedboats are the same. A 5-metre RIB with a 150hp engine is fine for two people and hits 35 knots. A 9-metre RIB with a 350hp engine carries eight people and does 50 knots. If you want to feel the spray and bounce, go for the smaller RIB. If you want a smoother ride with a toilet and a sunpad, choose a small motor yacht. The hourly rate for the smaller RIB might be from around EUR 150, while the larger RIB could be EUR 300 per hour. Check the boat's specifications on the search page to see the length, engine power, and amenities. If you are unsure, call the operator, they will recommend the right boat for your group size and desired experience.

What a Two-Hour Trip Actually Looks Like

From Puerto Banús, a typical two-hour speedboat trip goes west to Cala del Faro. You leave the marina, pass the Golden Mile villas, and after about 15 minutes at full throttle you reach the cliffs. The skipper cuts the engine, you jump into clear water, swim for 20 minutes, then race back. Total distance is about 10 nautical miles each way. From Marbella Marina, you can go east to Cabopino, which takes about 20 minutes at speed. From Estepona, head toward the Punta de la Doncella or the old town beaches. The skipper will point out landmarks like La Concha mountain or the Rio Verde estuary. You will be back at the dock with plenty of time for lunch or a siesta.

When the Hourly Rate Drops: Low Season Bargains

From November to March, the speedboat hire Marbella hourly rate can drop by 30-40 percent. You might find a RIB for EUR 100-120 per hour instead of EUR 200. The sea is cooler but still swimmable on sunny days. The air temperature ranges from 15 to 20 degrees C, so bring a jacket for the ride. The wind is more unpredictable, but many days are calm enough for a trip. The advantage is fewer boats on the water, so you have the coves to yourself. Some operators run winter specials, like a third hour free on a two-hour booking. Check the listings on BoatHire24 for low-season deals. If you are visiting Marbella in winter for the golf or the Christmas lights, a speedboat trip is a memorable addition.

title: Private Yacht Charter Marbella Group – Large Party Rentals
metaDescription: Book a private yacht charter Marbella group for up to 50 guests. Compare large party rentals with skipper, from Puerto Banús. Reserve your day on the water.
h1: Private Yacht Charter Marbella Group, Large Party Rentals
intro: If you are rounding up a dozen friends, a family reunion, or a corporate team for a day on the Costa del Sol, a private yacht charter Marbella group option is the most practical way to keep everyone together. Instead of splitting into several small boats and trying to coordinate anchor spots, you hire one vessel big enough for your whole party. Most large motor yachts and catamarans in Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina accommodate between 12 and 50 guests, and every booking includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation, mooring, and safety. You just bring the people, the music, and the drinks.
bodyHtml:
What a Group Yacht Charter Actually Includes

A private yacht charter Marbella group rental is not the same as turning up at a beach club. You get the entire boat for your group for a set number of hours, typically 4, 6, or 8. The skipper is included in the price, as is fuel for a standard itinerary along the coast. Most operators provide a cooler with ice, basic snorkelling gear, and a Bluetooth speaker. Some premium yachts throw in stand-up paddleboards, a barbecue, or a small inflatable water toy. What you do not get is food and drink unless you pay extra, or you bring your own. Many groups pre-order a catering package from the charter company, or they stop at a supermarket in Puerto Banús before boarding. The charter company will tell you exactly what is included when you send an enquiry, so ask about the cooler situation and whether you need to bring your own cups.

Which Ports Work for Large Groups

Most group charters depart from Puerto Banús because it has the largest concentration of superyachts and catamarans over 15 metres. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a close second, especially if you want a shorter transfer from the town centre. Cabopino, to the east, is quieter and better for groups who want to avoid the Banús crowds. Estepona and Sotogrande to the west are options if your group is based there, but the choice of large vessels is smaller. Benalmádena, further east, works for groups staying on the Costa del Sol coast between Fuengirola and Torremolinos. The skipper will choose a departure port based on where the boat is berthed, so check the listing on BoatHire24 to see which ports are available for your preferred yacht.

Boat Types for Groups of 10 to 50

For a private yacht charter Marbella group, your main choices are motor yachts, catamarans, and sailing yachts. Motor yachts from 15 to 30 metres give you speed, air-conditioned salons, and flybridges with sun pads. Catamarans offer more deck space per guest because the beam is wider, and they are more stable at anchor. A 15-metre catamaran can comfortably hold 20 people for a day charter, while a 25-metre motor yacht can take 30. Sailing yachts are slower and have less deck space, so they work better for groups under 12 who actually want to sail. RIBs and speedboats are too small for groups above 8. Fishing boats can take up to 12 but are not designed for lounging. Superyachts over 30 metres are available for groups of 40 to 50, but you pay a premium for the size and the crew. Licence-free day boats are limited to 6 people, so they are not suitable for this type of rental.

Pricing Guidance for Group Charters

You should expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day (4 hours) on a 12-metre motor yacht for up to 12 people. A full day (8 hours) on a 20-metre catamaran for up to 25 people starts at about EUR 3,500. For a 30-metre superyacht handling 40 guests, prices begin at EUR 8,000 for a full day and go up depending on the season and the extras. These are base prices that include the skipper, fuel, and standard equipment. Food, drinks, water toys, and port fees are usually extra. Always ask for a full breakdown before you pay a deposit. The best way to compare prices for a private yacht charter Marbella group is to browse the listings on BoatHire24 and send enquiries to three or four operators. They will come back with a custom quote based on your group size and preferred date.

Best Season for a Group Charter

The Costa del Sol has a long season. May, June, September, and October offer pleasant temperatures around 24 to 28 degrees C, fewer crowds, and lower prices. July and August are peak season, with temperatures hitting 32 degrees C and water temperatures around 24 degrees C. If you book in high season, you need to reserve at least two weeks in advance for a group charter, because the large vessels get snapped up by corporate events and wedding parties. April and November are hit and miss: you might get a sunny 22-degree day, but the water is cooler and the wind can pick up. The skipper will decide whether to go out based on the forecast, so have a backup plan if you book in the shoulder months.

What You Can Do on a Group Charter

A typical day starts at 10am or 11am from Puerto Banús. The skipper heads west towards the Marbella coastline or east towards Cabopino, depending on the wind and your preferences. You can anchor off Cala del Faro for swimming, or stop near the Río Verde estuary for a quieter spot. Many groups ask the skipper to cruise past the Puerto Banús marina entrance so they can see the superyachts from the water. If you head west towards Estepona, you can anchor off the old town beach and walk into town for lunch. Dolphin watching is popular near the Strait of Gibraltar, but that is a longer trip of at least 6 hours from Banús. For a shorter trip, the waters off Cabopino often have bottlenose dolphins. The skipper will know the best spots on the day.

Who Should Book a Group Charter

A private yacht charter Marbella group rental suits bachelor and bachelorette parties, milestone birthdays, family reunions, corporate away days, and wedding guest excursions. It also works for sports teams, university societies, and friend groups who want a shared experience without the hassle of organising individual tickets. The key constraint is that the boat has a maximum capacity, and the skipper will enforce it for insurance reasons. If you have a group of 22, you cannot squeeze onto a boat rated for 18. So check the capacity carefully on BoatHire24 before you send the invite. Also consider the mix of your group: if half of them get seasick, a catamaran is a better choice than a motor yacht because it rolls less at anchor.

How to Book a Group Charter

You find a suitable boat on BoatHire24, then click the enquiry button to send a message to the operator. You need to specify your group size, preferred date, and whether you want a half-day or full-day charter. The operator will reply with availability and a price. You pay a deposit, usually 30 to 50 percent, to secure the date. The balance is due on the day of the charter, often in cash or by card on board. Read the cancellation policy before you pay, because some operators are strict about refunds if the weather turns. Most will reschedule rather than refund, so check that. The operator will also ask for a guest list with names and passport numbers for the manifest, so have that ready.

Extra Services to Consider

Many charter companies offer add-ons for group charters. You can pre-order a catering menu with paella, tapas, or a barbecue. Some provide a bartender or a hostess for an extra fee. Water toys like a jet ski, a donut, or a banana boat can be towed behind the yacht, but you need to check if the operator has the licence and insurance for that. A photographer or a DJ can also be arranged for a premium. If you want a specific add-on, ask when you send the enquiry rather than on the day, because the operator needs time to organise it.

Local Tips for Your Group Charter

Start the day with a light breakfast, because the sea can be choppy in the morning. Bring sunscreen with a high SPF, even if it is cloudy, because the reflection off the water is strong. Take a dry bag for your phone and wallet. If your group is prone to seasickness, pick a catamaran and take medication an hour before departure. The skipper will have a first aid kit but not seasickness pills. For the best photos, the golden hour light around 6pm works well against the backdrop of La Concha mountain. And if you are departing from Puerto Banús, arrive 15 minutes early to park and find the pontoon, because the marina is busy and the gates can be confusing.

Alternatives to a Private Yacht Charter

If your group is larger than 50, or if the budget does not stretch to a private charter, consider a shared catamaran trip. Some operators run daily group excursions with a fixed itinerary and a set price per person. You will share the boat with strangers, but it costs a fraction of a private charter. Another option is to book two smaller boats and cruise together, anchoring at the same spot. That works if your group is split between people who want to party and those who want a quieter day. Check the BoatHire24 blog for more ideas on group boating on the Costa del Sol.

How to Split Costs Among a Large Group

The biggest headache with a private yacht charter Marbella group is collecting money without awkwardness. A common approach is to divide the total by the number of guests and ask everyone to transfer their share to one organiser a week before the charter. For a 12-metre motor yacht at EUR 1,200 for half a day, that works out at EUR 100 per person for 12 guests. A 20-metre catamaran at EUR 3,500 for 25 people is EUR 140 each. Add catering at around EUR 30 to EUR 50 per head and you are looking at EUR 130 to EUR 190 per person for a full day. Some groups use a splitwise app to track who has paid. The charter company will not deal with individual payments, so the organiser pays the deposit and balance from their account and collects from the group afterwards. That keeps things clean.

What to Do If Someone Cancels Last Minute

Last-minute cancellaries happen in every group. The operator will still hold you to the agreed number because the boat is chartered as a whole, not per person. If one guest drops out two days before, you either pay their share yourself or find a replacement. Some groups build a buffer into the per-person cost, say an extra EUR 10 to EUR 20, to cover the risk of a no-show. Another tactic is to over-invite by one or two people, knowing that someone will inevitably drop out. The skipper does not care who is on board as long as the total does not exceed the boat's capacity. If you end up with fewer guests than expected, you can still enjoy the extra space, but you still pay the same price.

How to Handle Seasickness in a Group

Seasickness can ruin a private yacht charter Marbella group if half the guests are green at anchor. The Costa del Sol is generally calm in summer, with swell rarely above 0.5 metres, but the sea can be lumpy in the morning or after a windy night. If your group includes people who are prone to motion sickness, book a catamaran rather than a motor yacht. Catamarans have a much lower roll motion because the hulls are separate. Advise everyone to take oral seasickness medication an hour before departure, and to avoid heavy food or alcohol before boarding. Ginger biscuits and acupressure bands help some people. The skipper will anchor in sheltered spots like Cala del Faro or the lee of Cabopino point if the sea is rough. If someone does get sick, they will feel better once they are in the water swimming.

What to Wear on a Group Charter

Comfort and practicality matter more than style on a private yacht charter Marbella group. Non-marking rubber-soled shoes are essential because white deck surfaces mark easily and the crew will not be happy. Bare feet are fine once you are on board, but you need shoes for walking to the boat. Swimwear under a cover-up or loose clothing works for most of the day. A light jumper or windbreaker is useful for the return leg in the evening, especially from June to September when the sea breeze picks up. Hats with chin straps stay on better in the wind. Avoid dark colours that absorb heat, and leave heels and black-soled shoes at home. The skipper will tell you if there is a dress code for a particular yacht, but most group charters are casual.

How to Choose Between Half-Day and Full-Day

A half-day private yacht charter Marbella group works well for a quick celebration, a pre-wedding gathering, or a corporate event that runs into the afternoon. Four hours gives you time to cruise to a swimming spot, anchor for an hour, and return. You can do that from Puerto Banús to Cabopino and back, or west to the Marbella coastline. A full day of 8 hours lets you go further, such as from Banús to Estepona old town for lunch, or east towards Cala del Faro with a longer swim stop. If your group wants to see dolphins near the Strait of Gibraltar, you need at least 6 hours. Full-day charters also allow for a more relaxed pace with a longer lunch and more time for water toys. The price difference is roughly 50 to 60 percent more for a full day compared to a half day, so the value per hour improves with the longer booking.

What to Do About Children on a Group Charter

If your private yacht charter Marbella group includes children, check the boat's policy before booking. Most operators allow children, but they count towards the maximum capacity. Some catamarans have safety netting around the deck, which is useful for toddlers. The skipper will provide life jackets for children, but you need to specify the ages and weights when you book so they have the right sizes. Children under 12 should not sit on the bow while the boat is moving, and they need supervision near the rails. If your group includes several families, a catamaran with a large trampoline net at the front is a hit with kids because they can sit and watch the water through the mesh. Avoid superyachts with high freeboards because small children cannot see over the side easily.

How to Arrange Catering for a Large Group

Catering for a private yacht charter Marbella group can be organised through the charter company or self-catered. Most operators offer a menu with options like paella cooked on board, cold buffets with Spanish meats and cheeses, or grilled fish and meat. Prices range from around EUR 25 per person for a simple buffet to EUR 60 per person for a full barbecue with drinks. If you bring your own food, pack it in reusable containers and avoid glass bottles because broken glass on deck is a hazard. Many groups stop at a supermarket in Puerto Banús or Marbella before boarding to buy drinks, snacks, and disposable cups. The boat will have a fridge and a cooler, but space is limited for 20-plus people. Coordinate with the organiser so you do not end up with six bags of crisps and no water.

What to Do If the Weather Turns Bad

The skipper has the final say on whether a private yacht charter Marbella group goes ahead. If the forecast shows strong winds above 25 knots or thunderstorms, the operator will cancel or reschedule. In summer, this is rare, but it happens in spring and autumn. If the weather is marginal, the skipper might offer a modified itinerary that stays closer to port or uses a sheltered bay. You do not get a refund if the charter proceeds but you decide not to go because it is cloudy. Most operators have a weather clause that allows rescheduling without penalty if the skipper cancels. If you cancel because you do not like the forecast, you lose your deposit. Check the operator's weather policy on BoatHire24 before booking, and consider travel insurance that covers weather-related cancellations for large groups.

h1: Fishing Charter Marbella Full Day Price, What to Expect
keyword: fishing charter Marbella full day price
intro:
You want to know the fishing charter Marbella full day price. The short answer: from around EUR 600 for a half day for up to 6 people, and from EUR 900 for a full day. But the price depends on the boat size, season, and how far you want to go for tuna or marlin. We run down the costs, what you get, and how to book without the nonsense.

BoatHire24 is a marketplace for boat rentals and yacht charters along the Costa del Sol. Every booking includes a licensed skipper, so you just show up with your tackle (or they provide it). We cover ports from Puerto Banús to Estepona, and boats from RIBs to luxury motor yachts. This page is about the full day price for a fishing charter in Marbella, and how to get the best deal.
bodyHtml:
What a Full Day Fishing Charter in Marbella Includes

A full day charter typically runs 8 hours, from around 9am to 5pm or 10am to 6pm. The price covers the boat, fuel, a skipper who knows the local waters, and basic fishing gear. Some charters include bait, ice, and soft drinks. You usually get a choice of bottom fishing for bream and grouper, or trolling for tuna and dorado. The skipper will decide based on the season and weather. You keep your catch, and some boats will clean and bag it for you. Lunch is not always included, but you can bring your own or ask the skipper to stop at a beach club.

Fishing Charter Marbella Full Day Price by Boat Type

The price varies a lot by boat. A standard fishing RIB or speedboat (around 6-8 metres) for a full day starts at EUR 900 for up to 6 people. A larger motor yacht (10-12 metres) with a cabin and toilet might cost EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500 for a full day. Catamarans are stable for families and run EUR 1,800 to EUR 3,000. Superyachts for serious game fishing are price on request, but expect EUR 5,000 or more. The best value is often a dedicated fishing boat from Cabopino or Estepona, where the skippers are specialists. Check the search page for current listings.

Ports and How They Affect the Price

Where you depart changes the price because of fuel costs and travel time. Puerto Banús is the most expensive port, with full day prices from EUR 1,200 for a basic boat. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is slightly cheaper, from EUR 1,000. Cabopino and Estepona are more affordable, from EUR 900 for a full day. Sotogrande is further south and good for tuna fishing, but the price is similar to Marbella. Benalmádena is a bit cheaper again, from EUR 850. The fishing grounds are similar from all ports, but the time to reach the best spots (like the Strait of Gibraltar for tuna) adds fuel cost. If you want dolphin watching and fishing, the Strait is a 1-2 hour cruise from Estepona or Sotogrande, so expect a premium.

Seasonal Price Differences

Summer (June to September) is peak season. Prices are 20-30% higher than spring or autumn. A full day that costs EUR 900 in May might be EUR 1,200 in August. Winter (November to February) is cheaper, from EUR 700 for a full day, but the weather is less reliable and some fish species are not around. The best months for big game fishing are July to September for bluefin tuna, and April to June for amberjack and dorado. If you want a bargain, book in May or October, when the weather is still good but prices drop. Always check the forecast before booking.

What Affects the Fishing Charter Marbella Full Day Price

Several factors push the price up or down. The number of people matters: most boats charge per group, not per person, but larger boats cost more. The boat age and amenities: a new 2024 model with GPS fish finder, live bait well, and air conditioning will cost more than an older boat. The skipper’s experience: a specialist fishing guide with 20 years of local knowledge charges a premium. The duration: a full day is usually 8 hours, but some operators offer 10 hours for an extra EUR 200-300. The target species: if you want to chase bluefin tuna, you need a faster boat and more fuel, so the price is higher. Always ask what is included: some charters charge extra for bait, lunch, or cleaning the fish.

How to Book a Fishing Charter in Marbella

You book through BoatHire24 directly. Search by date, port, and number of people. You can filter by boat type and price range. Once you find a boat, you send a booking request. The owner confirms availability and sends a quote. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the date. The balance is due on the day, in cash or card. We recommend booking at least a week in advance in summer. For last-minute bookings, call us or use the live chat. We have a cancellation policy: full refund if cancelled 48 hours before. No-shows are charged in full.

Who Is a Full Day Fishing Charter For

This is for anyone who wants to fish seriously, not just a quick spin. A full day gives you time to reach offshore grounds, try different techniques, and target bigger fish. It is suitable for groups of friends, families with older children (over 8), and corporate teams. If you are a beginner, the skipper will teach you the basics. If you are an experienced angler, you can bring your own gear and the skipper will take you to the best spots. The boat is private, so you have the whole day to yourself. No crowds, no set times. You can stop for a swim or a beach lunch if you want.

Local Fishing Spots and What You Catch

From Marbella, the common fishing grounds are the reefs off Cabopino, the drop-offs near Cala del Faro, and the deep water off Estepona. In summer, the tuna run along the Strait of Gibraltar, about 20 nautical miles from Estepona. You can also fish around the Río Verde estuary for bass and mullet. The catch varies: bream, grouper, red snapper, amberjack, dorado, bonito, and bluefin tuna. The skipper knows where to go based on the season and weather. If you want a specific species, ask when booking. Some boats specialise in catch and release for billfish like marlin, which are rare but possible in August.

Comparing Half Day vs Full Day Prices

A half day (4-5 hours) costs from EUR 600 for a small boat up to 6 people. A full day is roughly 50-80% more. For example, a half day at EUR 600 becomes a full day at EUR 900-1,000. The value is better on a full day because the fuel cost is the same for the first few hours, and you have time to go further. If you only want a taste, a half day is fine. But for serious fishing or a family day out, the full day is worth the extra. You also get more time to relax, swim, and enjoy the coast. Check the blog for tips on choosing between half and full day.

Extra Costs to Consider

The fishing charter Marbella full day price is usually quoted as the boat hire fee. But watch for extras. Some boats charge for fuel separately, especially if you go far. Bait is sometimes extra (EUR 20-50). Lunch or snacks are not included on most boats. Gratuity for the skipper is customary, around 10-15% of the charter fee. If you want to keep the fish, some boats charge for cleaning and bagging (EUR 10-20). If you need a transfer from your hotel to the port, that is extra. Ask for a full breakdown before you book. We list what is included on each boat page on BoatHire24.

Frequently Asked Questions About Fishing Charter Marbella Full Day Price

Here are answers to common questions. The price is per group, not per person, so splitting with friends makes it cheap. You can bring your own food and drink. The boat has a toilet on larger yachts. You do not need a fishing licence on a charter boat. The skipper has the licence. Children are welcome, but check the boat's age policy. In case of bad weather, the charter is rescheduled or refunded. The best time for fishing is early morning, so most full day charters start at 8 or 9am. You can also do a sunset fishing trip, which is usually a half day.

Real Price Examples from Popular Ports

To give you a concrete idea, here are some real price ranges we see on BoatHire24. A 7-metre fishing RIB from Cabopino, with a 200hp engine, costs around EUR 900 for a full day in June. From Estepona, a similar boat might be EUR 950, but you save 30 minutes of cruising time to the tuna grounds. From Puerto Banús, the same RIB jumps to EUR 1,200 because of the port fees and the clientele. A 10-metre motor yacht with a flybridge and cabin, departing Marbella Marina, costs EUR 1,800 in May and EUR 2,200 in August. A 12-metre catamaran from Sotogrande, ideal for groups of 10, runs EUR 2,500 for a full day with bait and ice included. These are real numbers from actual listings, not hypotheticals. Always check the search page for the latest prices, as they change with demand.

How Boat Size and Engine Power Impact the Cost

The size of the boat directly affects the fishing charter Marbella full day price. A 6-metre RIB with a 150hp outboard is the cheapest option, starting at EUR 800. It is fast (25-30 knots) but cramped for more than 4 people. A 9-metre boat with twin 250hp engines costs EUR 1,500-2,000, but it is stable in choppy water and can reach the Strait of Gibraltar in 1 hour instead of 2. The fuel consumption is the hidden cost: a twin-engine boat burns about 80-100 litres per hour at cruising speed, which at EUR 1.50 per litre adds EUR 120-150 to the operator's cost. That is why larger boats cost more. For bluefin tuna, you need a boat that can do at least 25 knots to chase the schools, so expect to pay a premium for speed. Smaller boats are fine for bottom fishing close to shore, where you save fuel and money.

Best Value Fishing Charters from Benalmádena

Benalmádena is often overlooked, but it offers the best value for a full day fishing charter. The port is less glamorous than Puerto Banús, but the fishing grounds are just as good. A full day from Benalmádena starts at EUR 850 for a 7-metre RIB, and you can often negotiate a discount for cash. The skippers there are mostly local fishermen who have been working the waters for decades. They know the reefs off Cabopino and the drop-offs near Fuengirola. The catch includes bream, grouper, and amberjack. In summer, you can also troll for bonito and small tuna. The downside is that the boats are older and less luxurious, but for serious fishing, that does not matter. If you want a cheap day out with a high chance of catching fish, Benalmádena is your best bet.

Luxury Fishing Charters: What You Get for EUR 3,000+

If you want to fish in style, a luxury charter from Puerto Banús or Sotogrande costs EUR 3,000-5,000 for a full day. You get a 15-metre plus motor yacht with air conditioning, a full galley, a toilet with shower, and a professional crew of two (skipper and deckhand). The boat is equipped with top-of-the-range fish finders, GPS, and live bait wells. The skipper is a specialist in big game fishing, often with experience in tournaments. Lunch is included, usually a BBQ or paella prepared on board. You also get premium bait and tackle, including heavy-duty rods for tuna. The experience is more about comfort than catching fish, but you still have a good chance of landing a bluefin or amberjack. This is ideal for corporate clients or groups who want to impress. The price per person drops to EUR 300-500 if you split it among 10 people.

How the Season Affects What You Catch and the Price

The fishing charter Marbella full day price fluctuates with the season, but so does the catch. In April and May, the water temperature is around 16-18 degrees C. You catch bream, grouper, and red snapper close to shore. The price is low, around EUR 800-900. In June, the water warms to 20 degrees C, and the amberjack and dorado arrive. Prices rise to EUR 1,000-1,200. July to September is peak season for bluefin tuna, with water temperatures of 22-25 degrees C. The price hits EUR 1,200-1,500 for a standard boat, and EUR 2,500+ for a tuna specialist. The catch is worth it: a 50kg bluefin is a trophy fish. In October, the tuna leave, but the bonito and mackerel are abundant. Prices drop back to EUR 900-1,000. November to February is the low season, with prices from EUR 700, but the catch is mostly small bream and mullet. The best value is May or October, when you pay moderate prices for good fish.

Hidden Gems: Fishing Spots Near Estepona and Sotogrande

Most tourists fish off Marbella or Puerto Banús, but the real action is further south. Estepona has a reef called "El Faro" about 3 nautical miles offshore, where you find large grouper and red snapper. The water depth drops from 20 to 60 metres, creating a feeding zone. A full day charter from Estepona costs around EUR 950, and you spend less time cruising because the fishing grounds are closer. Sotogrande is the gateway to the Strait of Gibraltar, where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean. This area is famous for bluefin tuna, but also for dolphin watching. The charter price from Sotogrande starts at EUR 1,000 for a full day, but you need a fast boat to reach the Strait in 45 minutes. The catch includes tuna, bonito, and occasional marlin. The scenery is stunning, with views of Gibraltar and Africa on a clear day. These ports are less crowded, so you get more personalised service from the skipper.

What to Bring and What the Skipper Provides

The skipper provides the boat, fuel, basic rods and reels, and some bait. But you should bring sunscreen (SPF 50, the sun is brutal), a hat, sunglasses, and a windbreaker (it gets cold offshore even in summer). Bring your own food and drinks unless the charter specifies lunch. Most boats have a cooler with ice, but check. If you have your own fishing gear, bring it, especially if you are after specific species. The skipper will advise on the right tackle. You should also bring cash for the balance payment and gratuity. Some boats accept card, but not all. A waterproof bag for your phone and wallet is a good idea. The skipper will provide life jackets and safety equipment, but you should know where they are stored. If you are prone to seasickness, take a pill 30 minutes before departure. The skipper will also provide a fish cleaning service for a small fee, usually EUR 10-20.

How to Get a Discount on the Fishing Charter Marbella Full Day Price

You can save money if you book smart. First, book in May or October, when prices are 20% lower than summer. Second, book a boat from Cabopino or Benalmádena instead of Puerto Banús. Third, go with a group of 6-8 people to split the cost. The per-person price can drop to EUR 150-200 for a full day. Fourth, ask for a discount if you book two days in a row. Some operators offer 10% off for multi-day bookings. Fifth, pay in cash on the day, which saves the operator the 3% card fee. Sixth, book directly through BoatHire24 rather than a third-party agent, as we have no booking fees. Finally, be flexible with the date. If you can go on a Tuesday instead of Saturday, you might get a better price. Always ask the skipper if there is any room for negotiation, especially in the low season.

Comparing Fishing Charters with Other Boat Rentals

A fishing charter is more expensive than a simple boat rental because it includes the skipper, gear, and local knowledge. A licence-free day boat (up to 15hp) costs around EUR 300-400 for a full day, but you cannot fish seriously and you are limited to shallow water. A RIB rental without a skipper costs EUR 500-700, but you need a boating licence and you have to navigate yourself. A fishing charter is better value if you want to catch fish, because the skipper knows the spots and the techniques. For a family day out, a catamaran charter with a skipper costs EUR 1,800-2,500, which includes swimming and lunch, but not fishing. If you want both, some catamarans offer fishing as an add-on for EUR 200-300 extra. For serious anglers, the fishing charter is the only option. Check the blog for a full comparison of boat types.

Last-Minute Deals and How to Find Them

If you are flexible, you can get a last-minute fishing charter at a discount. On BoatHire24, we list availability in real time. Boats that are not booked 48 hours in advance sometimes drop the price by 10-20% to fill the slot. You can also call the port office in Cabopino or Estepona and ask if any skippers have a free day. In the low season, you can often negotiate a price of EUR 700-800 for a full day by showing up at the marina in the morning. The risk is that the best boats are already booked, so you might end up with an older vessel. For peak season, last-minute deals are rare, but you can try. We recommend booking at least a week ahead for the best selection. If you are in Marbella, visit the Puerto Deportivo and talk to the skippers directly. Some of them speak English and will give you a cash discount.

You want sun, sea, and a skipper who keeps the prosecco flowing while you and the girls take over a private yacht. Private boat hire Marbella hen do is exactly that: a floating party with no crowds, no queues, and no hangover from bad decisions.

At BoatHire24, we connect you directly with licensed skippers and boat owners in Marbella, Puerto Banús, and the Costa del Sol. bodyHtml:
What a Private Boat Hire Marbella Hen Do Actually Includes

You are not renting a boat and hoping for the best. Every private boat hire Marbella hen do through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the coast, the anchor spots, and the best places to stop for a swim. The boat is yours for the agreed hours, typically 4, 6, or 8 hours, and you decide the itinerary. Most groups start from Puerto Banús, cruise past the mansions of the Golden Mile, drop anchor at Cala del Faro for a dip, and then drift back with the sun setting over La Concha mountain. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and the music if you bring a Bluetooth speaker. You handle the champagne.

Why a Boat Beats a Bar for a Hen Do

You have been to the hen do where you queue for 20 minutes to get a round of shots and then lose your friend in the crowd. On a private boat, the bar is on board, the toilet is clean, and the view is a moving postcard of the Mediterranean. The average temperature in Marbella from May to October is 28 degrees C, and the water temperature hits 24 degrees C in August. You can swim, sunbathe, and take photos that do not have a stranger's elbow in the frame. A private boat hire Marbella hen do gives you control over the playlist, the food, and the pace. If someone wants to nap on the sunpad, that is allowed. If someone wants to jump off the bow in a inflatable flamingo, that is also allowed.

Which Ports Work Best for a Hen Do Departure

Marbella has several departure ports, and each gives a different vibe. Puerto Banús is the obvious choice: the marina is packed with superyachts, designer shops, and bars where you can pre-game before boarding. It is also the most expensive port for mooring fees, so your boat hire will reflect that. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a quieter alternative, closer to the old town and the beach clubs. Cabopino, to the east, is smaller and more relaxed, with a sandy beach and a dune reserve. Estepona port, west of Marbella, is growing fast and offers lower prices and less crowds. Sotogrande is for the more exclusive group: think polo fields and private villas. Benalmádena, further east, has a lively marina with plenty of bars for after the trip. Your skipper will advise the best departure point based on your boat choice and itinerary, but Puerto Banús remains the top choice for a private boat hire Marbella hen do because of the sheer glamour factor.

Boat Options for Your Hen Group

You need a boat that fits your group size and your party ambitions. For a group of 8 to 12, a motor yacht from 12 to 18 metres works: plenty of deck space, a saloon for shade, and a decent sound system. Catamarans are popular for hen dos because they have a wide, stable deck and a trampoline net at the front where you can lie down. Sailing yachts are an option if you want a more traditional feel, but they have less deck space and more rigging to trip over. RIBs and speedboats are for the adrenaline crowd: fast, loud, and limited to around 6 people. Licence-free day boats are available from Cabopino and Estepona, but they are small and have no toilet, so not ideal for a full hen party. Superyachts are available on request for groups of 15 or more, with prices from around EUR 8,000 for a half day. You can browse all options on our search page and filter by capacity, price, and port.

Pricing Guidance for a Private Boat Hire Marbella Hen Do

Prices vary by boat type, season, and duration. For a half-day (4 hours) on a motor yacht for 10 people, expect from around EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,000. A full day (8 hours) on a catamaran for 12 people starts from around EUR 3,500 and can go up to EUR 6,000. Superyachts for 20-plus guests start from EUR 8,000 for a half day and go up to EUR 20,000 for a full day with a full crew. These prices include the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and basic insurance. Extras like food catering, premium drinks, water toys (jet skis, inflatables), and pick-up from your hotel add to the total. You should budget an extra 20 to 30 percent for food and drink if you want a catered experience. Our blog has a detailed breakdown of Marbella boat hire prices if you want to compare.

Best Season for a Hen Do on the Water

The Costa del Sol has a long summer, but the best months for a private boat hire Marbella hen do are June, July, August, and September. June and September are slightly cooler (average 26 degrees C) but less crowded, and prices are lower than peak July and August. July and August are hot (30 degrees C plus) and busy, but the sea is warm and the beach clubs are in full swing. May and October are possible if you want a quieter trip, but you risk cooler evenings and a chance of wind. The sea temperature in May is around 18 degrees C, which is swimmable but brisk. If you book in July or August, aim for a morning or late afternoon departure to avoid the midday heat. The skipper will know the best anchor spots to catch a breeze.

How to Book Your Private Boat Hire Marbella Hen Do

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You go to the search page, enter your group size, preferred date, and port, and you see available boats with instant pricing. You can message the owner directly to ask about catering, music policies, and any special requests. Once you confirm, you pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) and the balance is due a week before the trip. The owner will send you a meeting point and time. On the day, you meet the skipper at the port, he gives a safety briefing, and you are off. No hidden fees, no last-minute surprises. If you have questions before booking, check our blog for guides on what to bring, how to split costs, and which boat type suits your group.

Who This Is For and Who Should Think Twice

Private boat hire Marbella hen do is for groups that want a private, flexible, and photogenic experience. It works for brides who want a relaxed day with close friends, for groups that like to swim and sunbathe, and for anyone who wants to avoid the chaos of a packed bar. It is not for the budget-conscious: a boat hire costs more per person than a club night, but you get a private space, a dedicated crew, and the ability to bring your own food and drink. It is also not for anyone who gets seasick easily: the Mediterranean is usually calm in summer, but a catamaran is more stable than a motor yacht if you are worried. If your group includes heavy drinkers, be aware that the skipper has the right to cut the trip short if anyone becomes a danger to themselves or others. That is rare, but it happens. The key is to treat the skipper with respect and keep the party safe.

What to Bring and What Is Provided

The boat provides the skipper, safety equipment, a basic sound system (usually Bluetooth), and sometimes a cooler with ice. You bring the food, the drinks, the decorations, and the playlist. Most boats allow you to bring your own alcohol, but some have a corkage fee for glass bottles. Check with the owner before you load up the car. You also need sunscreen, towels, sunglasses, and a change of clothes if you plan to go out after. Some groups bring bridal sashes, inflatable unicorns, and banners, but check with the skipper if they allow decorations that could blow overboard. The wind in the Strait of Gibraltar can pick up in the afternoon, so secure everything. A waterproof phone case is a good idea for photos on the swim step.

Local Spots to Include in Your Itinerary

Your skipper will suggest a route, but you can request specific stops. Cala del Faro, near the lighthouse at the western end of Marbella, is a quiet cove with clear water and a small beach. The Bay of Estepona has calm waters and views of the Sierra Bermeja mountains. If you head east from Marbella, you can see the cliffs of Cabopino and the dunes. For a longer trip, some boats go to the Strait of Gibraltar to spot dolphins and whales, but that is a full day and requires a bigger boat. The Nerja caves are too far for a day trip from Marbella by boat, but you can see the coast from Cabo de Gata if you have a fast RIB. Stick to the Marbella to Estepona stretch for a relaxed hen do with plenty of anchor spots.

What Happens If the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is known for 300 days of sunshine a year, but the wind can pick up. If the skipper decides the conditions are unsafe, the trip will be rescheduled or cancelled. Most owners have a weather policy: if they cancel, you get a full refund. If you cancel because of a forecast you do not like, you may lose your deposit. Check the policy before you book. August is the safest month for calm seas, but even in June you can get a Levanter wind that kicks up waves. The skipper is the authority: if he says no, do not argue. Your safety is the priority.

How to Split Costs Without Awkward Conversations

Money talk is the fastest way to kill the buzz before you even step on the boat. For a private boat hire Marbella hen do, the total cost is usually paid by one person (often the maid of honour) and then split afterwards. Use a free app like Splitwise or Tricount to track who owes what. A typical breakdown for a EUR 3,000 half-day on a motor yacht for 10 people works out at EUR 300 per person. Add EUR 60 per person for catering and drinks, and you are at EUR 360 each. That is less than a night out in Puerto Banús where you queue for overpriced cocktails. If some people are on a tighter budget, consider a shorter trip (4 hours instead of 6) or a smaller boat. The bride usually goes free, so factor that into the split. Book through BoatHire24 and you can see the total upfront, no surprises.

What the Skipper Actually Does (and Does Not Do)

Your skipper is not a butler, a DJ, or a babysitter. He is a licensed professional who drives the boat, keeps you safe, and knows the best anchor spots. He will help you tie up the inflatable flamingo and might even take a group photo, but he will not serve drinks or clean up your mess. If you want a crew member to handle catering, you need to book a boat with a steward or a hostess, which costs extra. Most skippers speak Spanish and English, but check when you book if you need one language over the other. The skipper has the final say on the itinerary based on weather and safety. If he says the wind is too strong for Cala del Faro, trust him. He has done this for years and wants you to have a good time, not a trip to the hospital.

How to Handle the Bride's Expectations

Every hen do has that one friend who wants a luxury yacht experience on a RIB budget. Be realistic from the start. If the bride wants a superyacht with a jacuzzi and a crew of six, the price will be from around EUR 8,000 for a half day. If the group can only stretch to EUR 2,500, a 12-metre motor yacht from Estepona port still has deck space, a bimini for shade, and a Bluetooth speaker. The key is to manage expectations early. Send a group message with the budget and the options. Let everyone vote on the boat type and the duration. No one wants to be the person who complains after the deposit is paid. A private boat hire Marbella hen do is about the people, not the size of the yacht. The photos will look great regardless.

What to Do If Someone Gets Seasick

Seasickness is real, and it can ruin a day for everyone. The Mediterranean is usually calm in summer, but if you have a group member who gets queasy on a ferry, take precautions. Buy over-the-counter seasickness tablets (like Biodramina in Spain) and take them 30 minutes before departure. Avoid alcohol before boarding and stick to light food. Ginger biscuits and still water help. If someone does feel sick, the best cure is to sit in the middle of the boat (the most stable spot), look at the horizon, and avoid the cabin. The skipper will have a bucket and a bag, but aim to avoid using them. Catamarans are more stable than motor yachts because they do not roll as much. If you are worried, choose a catamaran for your private boat hire Marbella hen do. The trampoline net at the front is also a good place to lie down if the sea is flat.

How to Get the Best Photos Without a Professional

Your hen do photos will be on social media, so make them count. The best light is in the morning (9 am to 11 am) or late afternoon (5 pm to 7 pm), when the sun is low and the water turns turquoise. Avoid midday when the light is harsh and everyone has squinty eyes. Use portrait mode on a phone to blur the background, and take shots from the bow looking back at the boat. A waterproof phone case or a GoPro on a stick is useful for photos in the water. If you want drone shots, check with the skipper first: some ports have restrictions, and the owner may have a drone pilot available for an extra fee. The backdrop of La Concha mountain and the Marbella coastline is already photogenic. You do not need a filter.

What Happens After the Trip: Bars and Beach Clubs

Your private boat hire Marbella hen do does not have to end when you dock. Most trips finish at the same port you left from, so you can step off the boat and into a bar or beach club. Puerto Banús has Ocean Club, a beach club with a pool and a DJ, and several rooftop bars overlooking the marina. Marbella Marina has La Sala and the beach clubs of the Golden Mile. Estepona port has a quieter scene with seafood restaurants and a few cocktail bars. If you want to continue the party, book a table in advance for larger groups. Some boat owners offer a transfer service to a beach club for an extra fee. Ask when you book. The key is to plan the evening before you board, so no one is wandering around Puerto Banús in a soggy swimsuit looking for a table.

keyword: luxury motor yacht rental Marbella day
intro:
You want a luxury motor yacht rental Marbella day charter that doesn't come with hidden fees or a tedious booking process. On BoatHire24, every yacht includes a licensed skipper, so you can focus on the champagne and the views of La Concha mountain. We list motor yachts from 40 to 120 feet, available for day trips from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and other Costa del Sol ports.
