h1: Puerto Banus Boat Rental for Stag Do
keyword: Puerto Banus boat rental for stag do
intro:
If you are planning a stag do in Marbella, you probably want to do something that doesn't involve a sticky-floored club or a hangover by the pool. A boat rental in Puerto Banus is the obvious answer. You get a private yacht, a licensed skipper who does the driving, and a day on the Mediterranean that actually feels like a celebration. No queues, no wristbands, no last-minute cancellations. Just you, your mates, and the sea.

BoatHire24 is a marketplace for boat and yacht charters on the Costa del Sol. We list everything from small speedboats to superyachts, all with a skipper included. You book online, pick your departure port (Puerto Banus, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena), and turn up. The boat is ready, the fuel is paid for, and the skipper knows the best spots for swimming, dolphin watching, and getting the perfect photo for the group chat.

This page is specifically for stag dos. We will cover what you get, how much it costs, which boats work best for a group of lads, and how to book without the hassle. No fluff. Just the details you need to make a decision.
bodyHtml:
What a Stag Do Boat Rental Includes

When you rent a boat for a stag do through BoatHire24, the package is simple. You get the boat for a set number of hours, usually from 4 to 8 hours, and a skipper who handles navigation, anchoring, and safety. The skipper is licensed and speaks English and Spanish. They do not join the party, but they are there to make sure everything runs smoothly.

Most charters include fuel, insurance, and basic safety equipment. Some include a cooler with ice, a Bluetooth speaker, and snorkelling gear. You can bring your own food and drink, or order catering through the charter company. Many boats have a fridge, a sink, and a small toilet. Larger yachts have a full kitchen, air conditioning, and a cabin where someone can sleep off the afternoon.

The skipper will take you to spots like the Cala del Faro, a quiet cove near Marbella, or along the coast past the luxury villas of Puerto Banus. If you want to see dolphins, the Strait of Gibraltar is about a 40-minute cruise from Estepona. The skipper knows where the dolphins usually hang out, but it is not guaranteed. That is nature, not a theme park.

You do not need a licence for any boat on BoatHire24 because the skipper is always included. That means you can drink, swim, and relax without worrying about driving the boat back to port.

Departure Ports for Stag Do Boat Rentals

The most popular departure port for a stag do is Puerto Banus itself. It is the flashy marina with the superyachts, the designer shops, and the restaurants where you might spot a footballer. Departing from here means you start the day in the centre of the action. You can walk from most hotels in the area, and the marina has plenty of bars for a pre-boat drink.

Other options include Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), which is quieter but still close to the old town and the beach clubs. Cabopino is a smaller marina near the dunes of Artola, good if you want a more relaxed start. Estepona is further west, with a charming old town and easy access to the dolphin grounds. Sotogrande is the upmarket option, with a long marina and a country club vibe. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near the marina with the large ferris wheel and the sea life centre.

Each port has its own character, but the experience on the water is similar. The skipper will take you to the best spots for swimming, snorkelling, and sightseeing, regardless of where you start. For a stag do, Puerto Banus is the most convenient because it is central and has the most nightlife options for after the boat.

Boat Types for a Stag Do

The type of boat you choose depends on your group size and your budget. For a stag do, the most common choices are motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs.

Motor yachts are the classic option. They are fast, sleek, and have plenty of deck space for lounging and drinking. A 12-metre motor yacht can take up to 10 guests comfortably. Prices start from around EUR 1,200 for a 4-hour charter in high season. You get a sun pad at the bow, a saloon with air conditioning, and a small cabin for changing. The skipper will anchor in a cove where you can jump off the side of the boat.

Catamarans are wider and more stable, which means less seasickness and more space for moving around. A 14-metre catamaran can take up to 12 guests. They have a large trampoline net at the front, perfect for sunbathing or lying down after a few beers. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a 4-hour charter. Catamarans are slower than motor yachts, but the ride is smoother and the space is better for groups.

RIBs and speedboats are for smaller groups who want a faster, more adrenaline-fuelled experience. A 7-metre RIB with a 200 HP engine can take up to 8 guests. You zip along the coast, stop for a swim, and have a picnic on a deserted beach. Prices start from around EUR 600 for a 4-hour charter. These boats are less luxurious, but they are cheaper and more fun if you want to feel the speed.

Sailing yachts are also available, but they are less common for stag dos because they are slower and require more skill from the skipper to anchor in tight spots. If you want the classic sailing experience, a 14-metre sailing yacht can take up to 10 guests and costs from around EUR 1,000 for a 4-hour charter. The advantage is that sailing is quieter and more relaxing, which might be what you need after a heavy night.

Fishing boats are an option if you want to combine the stag do with some actual fishing. A 9-metre fishing boat with a skipper who knows the best spots can take up to 8 guests. You can catch sea bass, bream, and sometimes tuna. Prices start from around EUR 800 for a 4-hour charter. The boat has a livewell, rods, and bait included. Just be prepared for a few hours of patience before the fish bite.

Licence-free day boats are a newer option, but they are not suitable for stag dos because they do not include a skipper. You need a licence to drive them yourself, and the rental companies usually require a deposit and a briefing. For a stag do, you want to relax and drink, so stick with the skippered charters.

Superyachts are available for larger groups or bigger budgets. A 25-metre superyacht can take up to 20 guests and costs from around EUR 4,000 for a 4-hour charter. These come with a crew of two or three, including a steward who serves drinks and food. The interior is luxury, with leather sofas, a full bar, and a master cabin. If you want to impress the groom, this is the way to go.

Pricing Guidance for Stag Do Boat Rentals

Prices vary depending on the season, the boat size, and the duration of the charter. High season is June to September, when the weather is hottest and the demand is highest. Low season is October to May, excluding Easter and Christmas, when prices are lower.

For a 4-hour charter in high season, expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for a motor yacht, EUR 1,500 for a catamaran, and EUR 600 for a RIB. For an 8-hour charter, prices roughly double. Some companies offer half-day and full-day rates, with full-day being better value per hour.

Extras like catering, drinks, and water toys can add to the cost. A catering package with paella, tapas, and drinks costs from around EUR 35 per person. A jet ski or a paddleboard can be added for an extra fee, usually EUR 100 to EUR 200 per item. If you want a DJ or a sound system, some companies offer that for an additional charge, but most boats already have a Bluetooth speaker.

You should also budget for a tip for the skipper. 10% to 15% of the charter price is standard, but it is not mandatory. If the skipper does a good job, it is appreciated.

Booking early can save you money. Prices increase as the date gets closer, especially in high season. You can compare prices on our search page to see what is available for your dates.

Best Time of Year for a Stag Do Boat Rental

The best time for a boat rental in Puerto Banus is May to October. The sea temperature is warm enough for swimming, from around 18 degrees C in May to 26 degrees C in August. The air temperature is also pleasant, with highs of 25 to 35 degrees C. July and August are the hottest and busiest months, so book well in advance if you want a specific boat.

April and November can still work, but the weather is less predictable. You might get a sunny day with 20 degrees C, or you might get a cloudy day with a breeze. The sea is cooler, around 15 to 17 degrees C, so swimming is less comfortable. If you are flexible, you can find lower prices in these months.

December to March is off-season. The weather is cooler, with highs of 15 to 20 degrees C, and the sea is too cold for swimming for most people. Some boats are still available, but the atmosphere is quieter. It is not ideal for a stag do unless you are planning a winter trip with a focus on eating and drinking in the marina.

Sunset charters are popular for stag dos because the light is beautiful and the temperature drops to a comfortable level. From June to August, sunset is around 9:30 PM, so a 6:30 PM to 10:30 PM charter works well. You get the golden hour, the sunset, and the lights of the coast coming on as you return to port.

How to Book a Stag Do Boat Rental

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You go to the website, enter your dates, your group size, and your preferred port. The system shows you available boats with prices and photos. You can filter by boat type, capacity, and price range. Once you find a boat you like, you request a booking. The charter company confirms availability and sends you a payment link. You pay a deposit, usually 30% to 50%, and the balance is due on the day of the charter.

You can also contact us directly for help with larger groups or special requests. We work with multiple charter companies, so we can find the best option for your stag do. Just send us your requirements and we will send you a few options with prices.

For a stag do, you should book at least two weeks in advance, especially in high season. Last-minute bookings are possible but the choice is limited. If you want a specific boat like a superyacht or a catamaran with a DJ, book a month ahead.

Read the terms and conditions carefully. Some charters have a cancellation policy that allows a full refund if you cancel 14 days before the date. Others are non-refundable. Make sure you know what you are signing up for. You can find more details on BoatHire24.

Who Is This For

This page is for anyone planning a stag do in Marbella or the Costa del Sol. It is for the best man who wants to organise something different from the standard pub crawl or golf day. It is for the groom who loves the sea and wants a day on a boat with his mates. It is for the group that wants to combine drinking, swimming, and sightseeing without the hassle of driving or queuing.

If your group is 6 to 12 people, a private charter is a good option. If you have more than 12 people, you might need a larger boat or multiple boats. Some charter companies offer two boats that sail together, so you can have a flotilla effect. For groups over 20, a superyacht or a large catamaran is the best choice.

If you are on a tight budget, a RIB or a small motor yacht is the most affordable option. You can bring your own food and drink to save money. If you want luxury and have a bigger budget, a superyacht with a crew is the way to go.

For more tips on planning a stag do in Marbella, check out our blog for guides on the best bars, restaurants, and activities in the area.

bodyHtml:
Why Rent a Boat in Puerto Banús for NYE?

Puerto Banús is the epicentre of luxury on the Costa del Sol. On New Year's Eve, the marina transforms into a glittering party hub, with restaurants, bars, and clubs all competing for your attention. But the real magic happens on the water. From a boat, you get an unobstructed view of the fireworks launched from the pier, you can anchor in a quiet cove away from the crowds, and you have total control over the vibe. Plus, you avoid the traffic chaos that hits Marbella on NYE.

A Puerto Banus boat rental for New Year's Eve means you can start the evening with a sunset cruise along the coast, drop anchor near the Cala del Faro for a swim (if you're brave enough in December), then cruise back into the marina for the countdown. Most charters include a sound system, so you can blast your own playlist, and the skipper will handle all the logistics.

What's Included in Your NYE Charter

Every boat rental through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters. That's non-negotiable. But for NYE, you can add extras: champagne, catering, a DJ, or even a fireworks display of your own (subject to permits). The standard package usually includes fuel for a few hours of cruising, basic insurance, and life jackets. You'll need to bring your own food and drink unless you arrange a catering package. Some boats have a galley with a fridge, others just a cooler. Check the listing details.

Typical NYE charters run from around 5 PM to 1 AM, giving you time for a sunset sail, the fireworks at midnight, and a slow cruise back. If you want to go longer, many operators offer overnight options, though you'll pay extra for mooring fees and crew overtime. Prices for a Puerto Banus boat rental for New Year's Eve start from around EUR 1,200 for a mid-sized motor yacht, going up to EUR 10,000+ for a superyacht with full crew and catering.

Best Departure Ports for NYE Fireworks

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice, but you have other options along the coast. If you want a quieter evening, consider leaving from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) and cruising towards Banús for the fireworks. The distance is only 3 NM, so you can anchor off the coast and watch the show from a distance. Cabopino is another good option, especially if you want a more relaxed vibe before heading to Banús. Estepona and Sotogrande are further west, so you'd need to plan a longer cruise or stay local for their smaller fireworks displays.

Benalmádena, east of Marbella, has its own NYE fireworks over the marina, and you can rent a boat there too. But for the biggest party, Puerto Banús is the place. The marina is protected from the wind, so you'll have a stable anchorage. Just be aware that the area gets crowded, so book early. Most operators require a deposit of 50% to secure a NYE booking, and cancellations are rare.

Boat Types for Your NYE Party

Not all boats are created equal for a New Year's Eve party. Here's a breakdown of what works best:

Motor yachts: The classic choice. They have plenty of deck space, a flybridge for views, and a cabin for shelter if it gets cold. Sizes range from 30 ft (9 m) to 80 ft (24 m) and beyond. A 40 ft motor yacht can comfortably host 10-12 guests. Prices from EUR 1,200.

Catamarans: These are stable and spacious, with a large trampoline at the front and a flybridge. They're great for groups who want to move around without feeling seasick. A 40 ft catamaran can take up to 12 guests. Expect to pay from EUR 1,500.

Sailing yachts: If you want a more traditional experience, a sailing yacht offers a cosy feel. But the deck space is limited, and they can be chilly in December. Best for small groups (4-6 people). From EUR 800.

RIBs and speedboats: These are for the adventurous. You'll feel the wind in your hair, but you'll also get cold. They're best for a short blast before heading to a marina party. Max 8 guests. From EUR 600.

Licence-free day boats: No skipper needed, but you'll need to stay within 2 NM of the coast and avoid the busy areas. Not ideal for NYE unless you're experienced. From EUR 400.

Superyachts: For the ultimate luxury. Crew, catering, DJ, and a private fireworks display. Prices on request, but expect EUR 10,000+.

Pricing Guidance for NYE Charters

New Year's Eve is peak season, so prices are higher than a standard summer charter. Expect to pay a 50-100% premium over the usual rate. Here are rough estimates for a 4-hour evening charter (5 PM to 1 AM):

  • 30-40 ft motor yacht: EUR 1,200 - 2,500
  • 40-50 ft motor yacht: EUR 2,500 - 5,000
  • 50-60 ft motor yacht: EUR 5,000 - 10,000
  • Catamaran 40-50 ft: EUR 1,500 - 4,000
  • Sailing yacht 40-50 ft: EUR 800 - 2,000
  • RIB 8-10 m: EUR 600 - 1,200

These prices include the skipper, fuel for the hours booked, and basic insurance. Extra costs: catering (EUR 50-100 per person), champagne (EUR 30-100 per bottle), and a tip for the crew (10-15% of the charter fee). Some operators require a security deposit of EUR 500-2,000, refundable if no damage occurs.

Weather and What to Wear

December in Marbella averages 15-18 degrees C during the day, dropping to 10-12 degrees C at night. The sea temperature is around 16 degrees C, so swimming is possible but not recommended after dark. Bring warm layers: a jacket, jumper, and trousers. The wind on the water can make it feel colder, especially on open boats. A hat and gloves are a good idea. Most boats have a cabin with heating, but you'll spend most of the evening on deck.

If rain is forecast, check with the operator. Most boats have a bimini or hardtop for shelter, but a heavy downpour could ruin the party. The good news is that the Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, so the odds are in your favour.

How to Book a Puerto Banus Boat Rental for New Year's Eve

Step one: decide your budget and group size. Step two: browse our listings on BoatHire24 and filter by date, boat type, and capacity. Step three: contact the owner directly through our platform to check availability and negotiate extras. Step four: pay a deposit (usually via bank transfer or card) to secure the booking. Step five: confirm the itinerary with the skipper a few days before.

We recommend booking at least 2-3 months in advance for NYE, as popular boats sell out by October. If you're flexible, you might find last-minute cancellations, but that's a risk. For groups of 10 or more, consider a catamaran or a larger motor yacht. For couples, a smaller sailing yacht or RIB can be more intimate.

Who Is This For?

A Puerto Banus boat rental for New Year's Eve suits a few types of people: groups of friends who want a private party without club queues, families with older children who want a unique experience, couples looking for a romantic evening on the water, and corporate groups entertaining clients. It's not ideal for very young children (safety concerns on deck at night) or anyone prone to seasickness (though the marina is sheltered).

If you're visiting from abroad, combine the boat rental with dinner at a restaurant in Puerto Banús before or after the cruise. Many operators offer a pick-up and drop-off service from your hotel. And if you want to extend your stay, consider a day charter on January 1st to recover with a gentle sail along the coast.

Local Tips for NYE in Puerto Banús

The fireworks in Puerto Banús usually start at midnight and last 10-15 minutes. The best anchorages are just outside the marina entrance, near the lighthouse, or off the beach at Rio Verde. Avoid anchoring inside the marina itself, as the space is reserved for moored boats. The skipper will know the best spots.

After the fireworks, the party continues on land. If you want to dock and go to a club like Pangea or Ocean Club, you'll need to arrange a mooring in advance. Most clubs have a guest list system, so book tables early. Alternatively, stay on the boat and watch the chaos from a distance. It's a great way to end the year.

For more ideas on planning your trip, check out our blog for guides on Marbella's best NYE events, restaurant recommendations, and tips for renting a boat in winter.

Why Puerto Banús Beats the Land-Based Parties

You could queue for an hour to get into a club on the Golden Mile, pay EUR 50 for a mediocre cocktail, and spend the countdown staring at someone's phone screen. Or you could be on a boat, sipping cava, watching the fireworks reflect off the water. The difference is night and day. A Puerto Banus boat rental for New Year's Eve gives you a private vantage point that no restaurant or club can match. You see the entire marina lit up, the mountains behind it, and the sky exploding with colour. And when the music stops, you're not fighting for a taxi. You're already on your way back to port, with the skipper handling the navigation.

The sound carries differently over water too. The bass from the marina's speakers travels across the bay, so you get the party atmosphere without the crush. Some boats even have underwater lights that attract fish, adding a surreal glow to the evening. It's a sensory experience that land-based venues can't replicate.

The Best Anchorage Spots for Fireworks Viewing

The skipper will know the exact coordinates, but you should too. The prime spot is off Playa de Río Verde, about 200 metres from the Puerto Banús entrance. You're close enough to see the faces on the pier but far enough to have space. Water depth here is around 5-8 metres, so anchoring is straightforward. Another option is the area near the Club de Mar, just east of the marina. It's slightly quieter, with a direct line of sight to the main firework launch point on the western pier.

If you're leaving from Marbella Marina, the best anchorage is off the beach at Nagüeles, about 1.5 NM from Banús. You'll see the fireworks clearly, but they'll be smaller. For a more exclusive view, head towards Cabopino. The dunes there are protected, so you can anchor in the natural harbour and watch the distant glow. Just remember that the wind can pick up in the evening, so choose a spot with shelter from the levante or poniente winds.

What to Eat and Drink on Your NYE Charter

Most boats come with a basic galley: a fridge, a hob, and sometimes a microwave. But cooking a full meal on a moving boat in December is a hassle. Better to order a catering package. Local companies like Marbella Catering or Costa del Sol Events can deliver platters to the boat before departure. Expect to pay around EUR 35-50 per person for a selection of Spanish ham, cheeses, olives, prawns, and mini sandwiches. For drinks, bring your own. The skipper won't drink, but you can. A good rule is one bottle of cava or champagne per two people for the toast, plus beer, wine, and soft drinks for the evening.

Some operators offer a champagne bar with a dedicated steward. That adds EUR 200-400 to the bill but means you don't have to lift a finger. For a truly memorable touch, order a personalised cake from a Marbella bakery. Just make sure it's delivered to the boat before you set sail.

How to Handle Seasickness on NYE

You don't want to spend midnight leaning over the rail. The good news is that Puerto Banús is sheltered, and the sea is usually calm in December. But if you're prone to seasickness, take precautions. Avoid heavy meals before boarding, stick to the deck rather than the cabin, and keep your eyes on the horizon. Ginger tea or seasickness tablets (like Stugeron) work well. Most boats have a stabiliser system, especially larger motor yachts, which reduces roll by up to 80%.

If you're on a catamaran, you're even safer. Their wide beam means almost no motion at anchor. But if you're on a RIB or speedboat, the ride can be bumpy. Stick to the inner bay and avoid going beyond the Punta de la Mona headland. The skipper will adjust the route based on conditions, but it's worth asking when you book.

What Happens If It Rains on NYE

The Costa del Sol averages only 5-6 rainy days in December, but it can happen. Most boats have a bimini top or a hardtop that covers the main deck. Larger yachts have an enclosed saloon with heating, so you can stay dry and warm. If the forecast is bad, ask the operator if they have a backup plan. Some will offer a refund or reschedule, but read the terms carefully. Many NYE bookings are non-refundable because the operator turns away other customers.

Your best bet is to book a boat with a fully enclosed cabin. Motor yachts over 40 ft usually have a saloon that seats 8-10 people. Catamarans have a large interior with windows all around. Sailing yachts are more exposed, so avoid them if rain is likely. And if the weather is truly terrible, consider moving the party to a marina-side restaurant and using the boat as a base for the evening.

How to Get to Puerto Banús on NYE

Driving to Puerto Banús on NYE is a nightmare. The A-7 motorway gets gridlocked from 8 PM onwards, and parking in the marina costs EUR 30-50 for the night, if you can find a space. Better to take a taxi or private transfer. From Marbella town, the fare is around EUR 15-20. From Estepona, it's EUR 30-40. From Málaga airport, expect EUR 70-90. Book your taxi in advance through services like Marbella Transfers or Suntransfers, as Uber is limited in the area.

If you're staying in a hotel in Puerto Banús, walk to the marina. The distance from the Gran Meliá or the Marbella Club is less than 1 km. For groups, consider a minibus. And if you're coming from Sotogrande or Benalmádena, factor in an extra 30-45 minutes for traffic. The skipper will meet you at the designated dock, usually in the main marina near the statue of the bull.

What Happens After Midnight

The fireworks end around 12:15 AM. Then you have options. Stay on the boat and continue the party with your own music. Most charters run until 1 AM, but you can extend for an extra hour or two for around EUR 200-400 per hour, depending on the boat size. Or head to a club. Pangea and Ocean Club have dedicated boat docks where you can moor for the night. You'll need to book a table in advance, and the minimum spend is usually EUR 100-200 per person.

If you want to keep it low-key, cruise back to port and walk to a nearby bar like La Plage or the Marbella Club Hotel. They have outdoor terraces with views of the marina. Or just go to bed. The skipper will help you disembark and call a taxi. Most operators include a 30-minute grace period for docking and disembarking, so you're not rushed.

Why Book Through BoatHire24 for NYE

Booking directly with a boat owner can be risky. You might not get a written contract, the boat might not be as described, or the skipper might cancel at the last minute. On BoatHire24, every listing is verified. You see real photos, read genuine reviews, and pay through a secure platform. We handle the deposit and ensure the operator sticks to the agreed terms. If something goes wrong, we mediate. For a high-stakes night like NYE, that peace of mind is worth the booking fee.

Plus, our search filters let you narrow down by boat type, capacity, and price. You can compare multiple options in minutes. And if you're unsure, our customer service team can recommend boats based on your group size and budget. We've been doing this for years, so we know which operators are reliable and which boats are best for fireworks viewing.

intro:
Starlite Festival in Marbella is a summer staple, but getting there and back can be a nightmare. The traffic on the A-7, the queues for parking, the heat. You can skip all of that by renting a boat. Instead of sitting in a car, you cruise along the Costa del Sol, drop anchor for a swim, and then pull into Puerto Banús for the concert. Every charter on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper, so you just relax and enjoy the evening.

This page covers everything you need to know about a BoatHire24 rental for Starlite Festival: which ports to depart from, what boat types work best, how much it costs, and how to book without the hassle. We are not fans of fluff, so we get straight to the point.
bodyHtml:
Why Rent a Boat for Starlite Festival

Starlite Festival takes place in the Cantera de Nagüeles, a quarry turned open-air venue near Puerto Banús and Marbella's Golden Mile. The venue is about 3 km inland, but the nearest marina is Puerto Banús, which is a 10-minute taxi ride away. Renting a boat means you avoid the car altogether. You park at the marina (or get dropped off by water taxi), walk to the venue, and after the concert, you walk back to your boat. No waiting for taxis, no traffic jams, no parking fees.

Plus, you can make an evening of it. Most charters are half-day (4 hours) or sunset (3 hours). You leave the marina around 17:00, cruise along the coast, stop for a swim at Cala del Faro or near the Río Verde, have some drinks, and then head back to Puerto Banús for the concert. The boat is your private base for the night.

The festival runs from June to August, with temperatures averaging 30 degrees C in the day and 22 degrees C at night. The sea is warm, around 24 degrees C, so swimming is comfortable. The water is calm in the evenings, especially in the Bay of Marbella, so even if you are prone to seasickness, you should be fine.

Which Ports Can You Depart From

BoatHire24 lists boats from six ports along the Costa del Sol. For Starlite Festival, the most convenient departure port is Puerto Banús. It is a 10-minute walk to the venue (1.5 km). You can also depart from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), which is about 3 km away, a 10-minute taxi ride. If you are staying in Estepona or Sotogrande, you can depart from there, but factor in a 30-40 minute drive to the venue.

The other ports, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, Benalmádena, are further away. Cabopino is 20 km east, Estepona is 20 km west, Sotogrande is 40 km west, Benalmádena is 30 km east. If you are staying in those areas, it makes sense to rent a boat for the whole day and make the cruise part of the experience. You can leave at 14:00, cruise for 2-3 hours, stop for a swim, arrive in Puerto Banús by 18:00, and then go to the concert.

For those in Marbella, the Marina is a good alternative if Puerto Banús is fully booked. But Puerto Banús is the closest and most convenient.

What Boat Types Work Best for Starlite Festival

You have a few options, depending on your group size and budget.

Motor Yachts (20-40 feet)

These are the most common for a couple or a small group of up to 8 people. They are fast (20-30 knots), so you can cover more distance in less time. A 30-foot motor yacht from Puerto Banús costs from around EUR 600 for a half-day (4 hours). You get a sun deck, a small cabin, a bathroom, and a kitchenette. The skipper handles everything. Examples include the Azimut 36 or Sunseeker 34. These are ideal if you want a quick cruise and a swim stop before the concert.

Catamarans (30-50 feet)

Catamarans are more stable, have more deck space, and are better for larger groups (up to 12 people). They are slower (10-15 knots), but the ride is smoother. A 40-foot catamaran costs from around EUR 900 for a half-day. They have a large trampoline net at the front, perfect for lounging. The Lagoon 42 or Fountaine Pajot 40 are common. If you have a group of 8-12 friends, a catamaran is a good choice.

Sailing Yachts (30-50 feet)

Sailing yachts are quieter and more traditional, but they are slower (5-8 knots) and require wind. They are not ideal if you have a tight schedule before the concert. However, if you want a relaxed afternoon, they work. A 40-foot sailing yacht costs from around EUR 500 for a half-day. They have less deck space than a catamaran but more than a motor yacht of the same length. The Bavaria 46 or Jeanneau 45 are standard.

RIBs and Speedboats (20-30 feet)

These are for the adrenaline seekers. They are fast (30-40 knots), open, and have no cabin. You get wet. They are best for a short trip (2-3 hours) and for groups of 4-6 people. A 25-foot RIB costs from around EUR 400 for a half-day. They are not ideal for the concert because you have no shelter, but if you want a quick blast before the show, go for it. The Zodiac 25 or Ribcraft 24 are typical.

Fishing Boats (20-30 feet)

If you want to combine fishing with the concert, you can rent a fishing boat. They are slower (10-15 knots) and have basic amenities. A 25-foot fishing boat costs from around EUR 350 for a half-day. They are not the most comfortable for lounging, but they are functional. The Quicksilver 25 or Bayliner 24 are common.

Licence-Free Day Boats (6-10 feet)

These are small boats that do not require a licence to drive. They are limited to 4-6 people and a maximum speed of 6 knots. They are not practical for Starlite Festival because they are too slow to get to Puerto Banús from any distance. They are better for a calm day in the bay. Prices start from around EUR 200 for a half-day. The Quicksilver 6 or Brig 6 are examples.

Superyachts (60+ feet)

If you have a bigger budget, you can rent a superyacht. These come with crew, multiple cabins, and full amenities. Prices are on request, but expect EUR 5,000+ for a half-day. They are for groups of 12-20 people. The Sunseeker 80 or Azimut 68 are typical. You can have a party on board before the concert.

Pricing Guidance for Starlite Festival Charters

Prices vary depending on the boat, the season, and the duration. Starlite Festival runs from June to August, which is peak season. Expect prices to be 20-30% higher than in May or September. Here are ballpark figures for a half-day (4 hours) from Puerto Banús:

  • Motor yacht (30 ft): from around EUR 600
  • Catamaran (40 ft): from around EUR 900
  • Sailing yacht (40 ft): from around EUR 500
  • RIB (25 ft): from around EUR 400
  • Fishing boat (25 ft): from around EUR 350
  • Licence-free day boat: from around EUR 200
  • Superyacht (60 ft): price on request

These are the base rates. Fuel is usually not included, and you should budget EUR 100-200 for fuel for a half-day. The skipper's fee is included in the price on BoatHire24. Some boats include a welcome pack (water, soft drinks, ice), but check the listing. You can also add catering (food and drinks) for an extra cost, usually EUR 20-40 per person.

For a full-day charter (8 hours), expect to pay double the half-day rate. For a sunset charter (3 hours), expect 70-80% of the half-day rate. The best value is the half-day, as you get enough time to cruise, swim, and still make it to the concert.

Best Times and Seasons for a Starlite Boat Rental

Starlite Festival runs from mid-June to the end of August. The weather is hot and sunny, with sea temperatures around 24 degrees C. The sea is calm in the mornings and evenings, but there can be a light breeze in the afternoon (the levante wind). The water is clearest in July and August.

For the concert, the best time to rent a boat is a half-day from 16:00 to 20:00. You leave the marina at 16:00, cruise for an hour, stop for a swim at Cala del Faro or near the Río Verde for 45 minutes, then cruise back to Puerto Banús for 18:30. You dock at 19:00, walk to the venue, and the concert starts at 21:00. After the concert, you walk back to the boat and sleep on board (if your charter includes overnight stay) or take a taxi to your hotel.

If you want a sunset cruise, book a 3-hour charter from 18:00 to 21:00. You cruise during sunset (around 21:00 in July), then go to the concert. The sunset view from the sea is stunning, with La Concha mountain in the background.

August is the busiest month, so book at least 2-3 weeks in advance. June and July are slightly less busy, but still book 1-2 weeks ahead. The best days are Tuesday to Thursday, as weekends are more expensive and crowded.

How to Book a Boat for Starlite Festival on BoatHire24

The process is straightforward. You go to the search page, enter your dates, select Puerto Banús as the departure port (or another port if you prefer), and filter by boat type and price. You will see a list of available boats with photos, descriptions, prices, and skipper details. Each listing includes the boat's length, capacity, amenities, and cancellation policy.

Once you find a boat you like, you click on it, check the availability, and send a booking request. The owner will confirm within 24 hours. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking, and the balance is due on the day of the charter. You can pay by credit card or bank transfer. BoatHire24 does not charge any booking fees. The price you see is the price you pay, except for fuel and optional extras.

If you are unsure which boat to choose, you can contact the owner directly through the platform. They can advise on the best boat for your group size and budget. You can also read our blog for tips on what to bring and what to expect.

Who Is This Rental For

This rental is for anyone attending Starlite Festival who wants to avoid the traffic and make the evening special. It is ideal for couples, groups of friends, families, and corporate groups. If you are a couple, a motor yacht or sailing yacht is perfect. If you have a group of 8-12, a catamaran is best. If you want a party, a superyacht is the way to go.

It is also for people who are staying in Marbella, Estepona, or Sotogrande and want a unique pre-concert experience. If you are staying in a hotel on the beach, you can be picked up by water taxi and taken to the boat. Some charters offer a beach pick-up service, but check the listing.

It is not for people who are on a tight budget, as boat rentals are not cheap. But if you split the cost among a group, it can be affordable. For example, a catamaran for 12 people at EUR 900 works out to EUR 75 per person for a half-day, plus fuel and food. That is less than a round of drinks at the festival bar.

Local Colour and Things to See

The Costa del Sol has plenty to see from the water. From Puerto Banús, you can cruise east towards Marbella. You will see the iconic La Concha mountain, which looks like a giant seashell. The coastline is lined with villas and hotels, including the Marbella Club and Puente Romano. You can stop at Cala del Faro, a small cove with a lighthouse, for a swim. The water is clear and calm.

If you go west from Puerto Banús, you head towards Estepona. The coast is less developed, with cliffs and small beaches. You can see the Strait of Gibraltar in the distance, and if you are lucky, you might spot dolphins. The water is deeper and cooler here.

For a longer trip, you can go to the Nerja Caves, but that is a full-day charter (8 hours) and not practical for a Starlite evening. The same goes for a trip to Gibraltar, which is 60 km west. Stick to the Marbella-Puerto Banús area for a half-day.

The sunset from the sea is incredible. The sky turns orange and pink, and the lights of Puerto Banús start to twinkle. It is a perfect pre-concert vibe.

What to Bring and What to Expect

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a towel, a swimsuit, and a light jacket for the evening. The boat will have a cooler for drinks, but you can bring your own. The skipper will provide ice and water. If you want food, you can order a catering pack or bring your own. Some boats have a grill, but check the listing.

The skipper will give a safety briefing and handle all navigation. You do not need any boating experience. The skipper will also recommend the best spots for swimming and sightseeing. They are local and know the area well.

After the concert, you walk back to the boat. If your charter includes an overnight stay, you can sleep on board. Otherwise, you take a taxi to your hotel. Taxis are available at the marina, but they can be busy after the concert. Book a taxi in advance if possible.

faqs.q: How far is Puerto Banús from the Starlite Festival venue?
faqs.a: Puerto Banús is about 1.5 km from the Cantera de Nagüeles, a 10-15 minute walk. You can also take a taxi for around EUR 10. The marina is the closest port to the venue.

faqs.q: Can I rent a boat for just the evening of the concert?

faqs.q: Do I need a boating licence to rent a boat on BoatHire24?

faqs.q: Is it safe to swim in the sea near Marbella?
faqs.a: Yes, the water is generally calm and clean, especially in the Bay of Marbella. The skipper will choose a safe spot for swimming, such as Cala del Faro or near the Río Verde. Always follow the skipper's instructions.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book a boat for Starlite Festival?
faqs.a: Book at least 2-3 weeks in advance for August, and 1-2 weeks for June and July. The festival is popular, and boats in Puerto Banús sell out quickly. Early booking gives you more choice.

title: Puerto Banus Boat Rental for Starlite

h1: Puerto Banus Boat Rental for Starlite
keyword: Puerto Banus boat rental for Starlite
intro:
Starlite is Marbella's summer festival in Nagüeles, a hillside venue that gets hot, crowded, and expensive on the ground. A Puerto Banus boat rental for Starlite is the smart workaround: you spend the afternoon on the water, anchor for a swim, then dock at the port and take a short taxi to the concert. No traffic jams, no parking stress, and you get a proper day out before the music starts.

You choose the boat, the departure time, and whether you want lunch on board or a stop at a chiringuito. Then you head up to Starlite for the evening, already relaxed and on holiday time.
bodyHtml:
Why a Boat Rental Makes Sense for Starlite

Starlite runs from June to August, with temperatures hitting 30 degrees C in the afternoon. The venue sits at the foot of La Concha mountain, which traps heat. Queues for taxis and shuttles can take an hour after the headline act. A boat changes the equation: you leave Puerto Banus at 16:00, cruise past the Golden Mile, drop anchor off Cala del Faro for a swim, and arrive back at the marina by 20:00. Taxi to the venue is 10 minutes. After the concert, you walk back to the port and sleep on board or head to a hotel. No waiting, no sweating.

What's Included in Your Boat Rental

Every booking through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, fuel for the trip, and basic insurance. The boat is cleaned before you board. You can bring your own food and drink or arrange catering through the skipper. Most boats have a cooler, sound system, and deck shower. What is not included: mooring fees at Puerto Banus (around EUR 30-50 for a few hours), taxi to Starlite (EUR 15-20 each way), and concert tickets. You pay for the boat, the skipper, and the fuel. That is it.

Ports and Departure Points

The most convenient port for Starlite is Puerto Banus, because it is closest to the venue. A taxi from the port to Nagüeles takes 10 minutes and costs around EUR 15. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is also an option, adding 5 minutes to the taxi ride. Cabopino, Estepona, and Sotogrande are further south, which means a longer drive to the concert. If you are staying in Estepona or Sotogrande, you can still rent a boat from there and drive up, but the time saving is smaller. Benalmádena is 40 minutes north of Marbella, so it is less practical for Starlite unless you are already based there.

Boat Options for Starlite

Motor yachts from 10 m to 20 m are the most popular choice for Starlite. They have a cabin, a bathroom, and a flybridge, so you can escape the sun. Prices start from around EUR 600 for a half-day charter on a 10 m yacht. Catamarans offer more deck space and stability, ideal for groups of 8 to 12 people. A 12 m catamaran costs from around EUR 800 for a half day. Sailing yachts are slower but quieter, and you can sail under engine if the wind is light. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper and faster, starting from EUR 350 for a 2-hour trip, but they have less shade and no cabin. Licence-free day boats (under 6 m) are available from Cabopino and Marbella, but they are not ideal for Starlite because they have no toilet and limited shelter. Superyachts from 24 m upwards are available on request, with prices starting around EUR 3,000 for a half day.

Pricing Guidance

Prices depend on boat size, season, and duration. For a half-day charter (4 hours) during Starlite season, expect to pay from around EUR 600 for a 10 m motor yacht, EUR 800 for a 12 m catamaran, and EUR 350 for a RIB. Full-day charters (8 hours) start at around EUR 1,200 for a motor yacht. Superyachts are price on request, typically EUR 3,000-10,000 per day. Mooring fees at Puerto Banus are extra, around EUR 30-50 for a few hours. Fuel is included in the charter price, so you do not pay extra for the trip to the coast and back.

Best Time to Book for Starlite

Starlite runs from June to August, with the busiest weeks in July and August. Book your boat at least two weeks in advance for July and August, or one week for June. Departure times matter: aim for 16:00 to 17:00, so you have time for a swim and a drink before heading to the concert. If you want to watch the sunset from the boat before the show, depart at 18:00 and skip the swim. The sea is warmest in August, around 24 degrees C, but June and July are still pleasant at 20-22 degrees C.

How to Book Your Boat

Use the search page on BoatHire24 to filter by port, boat type, and date. Enter "Puerto Banus" as the departure port, select "Starlite" as the event (if available) or just pick a half-day charter. You can book online with a deposit, and the balance is paid to the skipper on the day. Cancellation policies vary by boat owner, but most offer a full refund if you cancel 7 days before. If you need help choosing, contact us and we will recommend a boat based on your group size and budget.

Who Is This For

This is for anyone attending Starlite who wants to turn a concert night into a full day out. Couples, groups of friends, families with older children, and corporate clients all use boat rentals for Starlite. If you are a group of 6 to 12 people, a catamaran or motor yacht works best. If you are a couple, a smaller motor yacht or RIB is fine. If you are celebrating a birthday or anniversary, the skipper can arrange champagne and a cake. The boat is yours for the afternoon, so you control the itinerary.

Local Tips for Your Starlite Boat Trip

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a towel. The sun is strong on the water, even at 16:00. Pack a light jacket for the evening, because the temperature drops after sunset. If you want to eat on the boat, order a catering platter from the skipper in advance, or bring your own food. Chiringuitos on the coast, like Trocadero or La Pesquera, are good for a quick lunch before you head out. After the concert, taxis are plentiful at the venue exit, but you can also arrange a private transfer through the skipper. Do not forget your Starlite tickets: the boat does not include entry.

Alternatives to Boat Rental for Starlite

If you prefer to stay on land, you can book a private driver or a VIP shuttle from your hotel. But a boat gives you the added benefit of a day on the sea, which is the real draw of Marbella in summer. If you are not attending Starlite but still want a boat trip, check out our BoatHire24 homepage for general charters. For more ideas on what to do in the area, read our blog on the best day trips from Puerto Banus.

Navigating Puerto Banus Marina on Concert Days

Puerto Banus gets chaotic during Starlite season, with extra traffic both on land and water. The marina office assigns specific berths for charter boats, so your skipper will have a spot booked. Arriving at the port 30 minutes before your departure time gives you room to park (if driving) and find your boat. The main taxi rank is at the entrance to the marina, near the casino. If you are staying in a hotel in Marbella, the taxi ride to the port is about 10 minutes and costs EUR 10-15. For groups, a private transfer from the port to Starlite costs around EUR 30-40 for a minivan, which is worth it if you are splitting the fare four ways.

What to Do on the Water Before Starlite

A typical pre-concert itinerary starts with a cruise east from Puerto Banus towards Marbella. You pass the Golden Mile, where you can see the villas from the water. The first stop is usually Cala del Faro, a small cove with clear water and a rocky beach. Drop anchor for 30 minutes, swim, and have a drink. From there, head back towards Cabopino, which has a sand beach and a chiringuito called La Pesquera that serves grilled fish. If you want to see dolphins, ask your skipper to take you south towards the Strait of Gibraltar, but that adds 45 minutes each way, so only do it on a full-day charter. For a half-day trip, stick to the coast between Puerto Banus and Marbella, which gives you enough time for a swim and a relaxed cruise before heading to the concert.

Group Sizes and Boat Recommendations

For a group of 2 to 4 people, a 10 m motor yacht or a RIB works well. The RIB is faster and cheaper, but you get wet and there is no cabin to change in. For 5 to 8 people, a 12-14 m motor yacht or a catamaran gives you enough space. Catamarans are better for groups because the deck is larger and the ride is more stable. For 9 to 12 people, you need a 15-18 m motor yacht or a 14-16 m catamaran. For larger groups, superyachts from 24 m upwards can take up to 20 guests. As an example, a 14 m Azimut motor yacht sleeps 6 and has a flybridge, a salon, and a bathroom, costing around EUR 900 for a half day. A 15 m Lagoon catamaran sleeps 8 and has a large trampoline net at the bow, perfect for sunbathing, costing around EUR 1,100 for a half day.

Weather and Sea Conditions in Summer

June through August on the Costa del Sol means calm seas and light winds. The prevailing wind is the Poniente, which blows from the west and keeps the sea flat. The Levante wind, from the east, is less common in summer but can bring a chop of 0.5-1 m. Your skipper will check the forecast and adjust the route. Sea temperatures in June are around 20 degrees C, warming to 24 degrees C by August. Air temperatures range from 28 degrees C in June to 32 degrees C in August, with humidity around 60%. The sun sets around 21:30 in June and 21:00 in August, so a 16:00 departure gives you golden light for photos and a sunset view before heading to the concert.

Booking a Boat for Multiple Starlite Nights

If you are attending more than one Starlite concert, you can book the same boat for multiple days. Some owners offer a discount for multi-day bookings, typically 10-15% off the total. For example, a 3-day charter of a 12 m motor yacht might cost EUR 2,400 instead of EUR 2,700. You can also mix boat types: a motor yacht one day and a catamaran the next. The search page lets you filter by available dates, so you can see which boats are free for consecutive days. If you are staying in Marbella for a week, consider a full-day charter on your first day to explore the coast, then a half-day charter on concert days.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a change of clothes for the concert. Leave high heels at home: boat decks are slippery, and you will need to step onto the dock. Flat shoes or sandals are better. If you bring a bag, keep it small, because storage on boats is limited. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos on the water. Do not bring glass bottles, as most boats prohibit glass for safety reasons. Plastic cups and cans are fine. If you want to bring a speaker, the boat already has one, but you can connect your phone via Bluetooth. Leave any illegal substances at home; the skipper will not allow them, and the marina has security.

Eating and Drinking on the Boat

You can bring your own food and drink, which is the most cost-effective option. A supermarket like Mercadona in Puerto Banus is a 5-minute walk from the marina. For catering, skippers can arrange platters of Spanish ham, cheese, olives, and bread for around EUR 15-20 per person. Drinks like beer, wine, and soft drinks can be added at EUR 5-10 per person. Some boats have a barbecue on the back deck, which the skipper can prepare for an extra fee. If you want a full meal, the skipper can dock at a chiringuito for lunch, but that eats into your cruise time. For Starlite, a light snack and drinks on the boat are enough, because you can eat dinner at the concert venue.

Parking and Access to Puerto Banus

If you drive to Puerto Banus, parking is expensive during summer. The main car park near the marina costs around EUR 3 per hour, with a daily maximum of EUR 25. There is free street parking in the residential areas behind the port, but it fills up by 10:00. For Starlite, consider parking at the venue itself, which has a large car park costing EUR 10-15. Then take a taxi to the port for your boat trip, and taxi back to the venue for the concert. This avoids the hassle of finding parking in Puerto Banus twice. Alternatively, use the train from Fuengirola to Marbella, then a taxi to the port, which costs around EUR 10 total.

Combining Boat Rental with Other Activities

You can extend your Starlite day by adding other activities. A morning fishing trip from Puerto Banus costs around EUR 400 for a half day on a fishing boat, targeting sea bass and bream. After lunch, you return to port, switch to a motor yacht, and head out for the pre-concert cruise. Some skippers offer a combined deal if you book both trips. Alternatively, take a paddleboard or kayak from the boat during your swim stop. Most boats carry a paddleboard on request. If you have children, a stop at Cabopino beach is better than Cala del Faro, because the water is shallower and there is a playground on the sand.

What Happens if the Weather Is Bad

Starlite season is generally sunny, but afternoon thunderstorms can occur in August. Your skipper will monitor the forecast and may delay departure by an hour or change the route to stay closer to port. If the weather is dangerous, the charter can be rescheduled or cancelled for a full refund. The marina in Puerto Banus is protected, so even if the sea is rough outside, you can stay in the harbour and have a drink on the boat. For peace of mind, book a boat with a cabin or salon, so you have shelter if it rains. Most motor yachts and catamarans have indoor seating.

Legal Requirements and Age Restrictions

You do not need a boat licence, because the skipper handles everything. The minimum age to charter a boat is 18, but children are welcome. For RIBs and speedboats, the skipper may require everyone to wear a life jacket, which is provided. Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper will stop serving if anyone becomes unsafe. The legal blood alcohol limit for boat passengers in Spain is 0.25 mg/L in breath, but the skipper is responsible for safety and can end the trip early if needed. For Starlite, it is best to drink moderately on the boat and save the heavy drinking for the concert.

Comparing Puerto Banus with Other Ports for Starlite

Puerto Banus is the best option, but here is how the others stack up. Marbella Marina is 5 minutes further by taxi and has cheaper mooring fees (EUR 20-30). Cabopino is 15 minutes south of Marbella, so the taxi to Starlite costs around EUR 25. Estepona is 30 minutes south, adding EUR 35 each way for a taxi. Sotogrande is 45 minutes south, which is too far for a half-day trip unless you combine it with a day on the water. Benalmádena is 40 minutes north, making it impractical for Starlite. If you are staying in Estepona or Sotogrande, it is better to rent a boat from there for a different day and drive to Starlite separately.

Budget Tips for a Starlite Boat Trip

To save money, book a RIB or a licence-free day boat from Cabopino, which costs from EUR 250 for a half day. You will not have a cabin or toilet, but you get the same swim and cruise experience. Share the cost with friends: a group of 6 on a EUR 600 motor yacht pays EUR 100 each. Bring your own food and drink instead of catering. Book on a weekday (Monday to Thursday) when prices are 10-20% lower than weekends. Avoid the peak week of August 15, when prices are highest. If you are flexible, ask the skipper if they have any last-minute cancellations, which can save 20-30%.

Making the Most of Your Evening at Starlite

After your boat trip, you arrive at Starlite refreshed and with a buzz from the sea. The venue opens at 19:00 for dinner and drinks, with concerts starting around 22:00. If you have a VIP ticket, you get access to a private area with better views and shorter bar queues. The food at Starlite is good but expensive, with main courses around EUR 30-50. Eat a light meal on the boat to save money. The concert ends around 01:00, and taxis are available at the exit. If you want to sleep on the boat, your skipper can arrange overnight mooring at Puerto Banus for an extra fee of around EUR 50-80. This is a good option if you have had a few drinks and do not want to drive.

bodyHtml:
Why Choose a Boat Rental for the F1 Weekend in Marbella

The F1 weekend in Marbella is not just about the race. It is a social event, with parties, dinners, and a general buzz that fills every corner of the coast. But that also means higher prices and limited availability at hotels and restaurants. A boat gives you your own floating venue. You can moor up near a beach club showing the race, or drop anchor in a quiet cove like Cala del Faro and watch on a tablet. Your skipper knows the best spots and will handle the mooring fees and the local regulations.

Another advantage is flexibility. You are not tied to a single location. If the wind picks up or you want a different view, you can move. Most charters include a full crew, so you do not need a boating licence. You just show up and enjoy. BoatHire24 has listings for motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts, and RIBs, all with experienced skippers.

What Is Included in a Marbella Boat Rental for F1 Weekend

When you book through BoatHire24, each charter includes a licensed skipper as standard. Fuel is usually extra, but some owners include it in the price. Ask before you book. Most boats come with a basic sound system, a cooler, and a sun deck. For the F1 weekend, you might want to request a TV or a projector screen. Some larger yachts have built-in entertainment systems that can stream the race live. If you want catering, many owners can arrange a platter of local ham, cheese, and wine, or a full barbecue. Prices vary, so check the details on the listing.

The duration is typically half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours). For the F1 weekend, a full-day charter makes sense if you want to watch the race and then party afterwards. You can depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. The port you choose affects the cruising area and the time to reach the best spots. BoatHire24's search page lets you filter by port and boat type.

Best Departure Ports for F1 Weekend Boat Charters

Puerto Banús is the most popular departure point for F1 weekend charters. It is where the action is, with luxury boutiques, high-end restaurants, and a marina full of superyachts. You can step off your charter straight into the nightlife. But it is also the busiest. If you want a quieter start, consider Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), which is a 10-minute drive east. It has easier parking and a more relaxed vibe. Cabopino is a small marina near Artola beach, good for groups who want to avoid the crowds. Estepona and Sotogrande are further west, closer to the Strait of Gibraltar, where you might see dolphins. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near the Nerja caves, and offers a different coastal scenery.

For the F1 weekend, we recommend Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina. Both have easy access to the main F1 parties and beach clubs. Your skipper can advise on the best anchorages based on the wind and the day's events.

Boat Options: From Speedboats to Superyachts

BoatHire24 offers a wide range of vessels for the F1 weekend. If you are a small group of 4 to 6 people, a RIB or speedboat is a practical choice. These boats are fast, so you can zip between beach clubs and anchor in shallow coves. They are also cheaper, with half-day rates from around EUR 400. For a group of 8 to 12, a motor yacht or catamaran gives you more space and comfort. Catamarans are stable and have large sun decks, ideal for lounging while the race is on. Prices for a half-day catamaran start at around EUR 1,200. For a larger party of 20 or more, consider a superyacht or a luxury motor yacht. These come with crew, a full bar, and sometimes a Jacuzzi. Prices are on request, but expect to pay upwards of EUR 5,000 for a full day.

Sailing yachts are also available, but they are slower and less suited to the F1 weekend if you want to move between multiple spots. Fishing boats are an option if your group prefers a more casual vibe with rod fishing. Licence-free day boats are available for those who want to drive themselves, but for the F1 weekend, a skipper is recommended so you can relax.

Pricing Guidance for F1 Weekend Boat Rentals

Prices for a Marbella boat rental for F1 weekend are higher than usual due to demand. Expect to pay a premium of 20 to 40 percent compared to a standard summer weekend. A half-day RIB charter might cost from around EUR 500 to EUR 800. A half-day motor yacht for 10 people could be from EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. Full-day charters for larger groups can go from EUR 4,000 to EUR 10,000 or more. Always confirm what is included: fuel, crew gratuity, food, and drinks. Some owners offer all-inclusive packages, others charge separately.

To get the best deal, book early. The F1 weekend is one of the busiest periods on the Costa del Sol. BoatHire24 recommends booking at least two months in advance. You can compare listings on our platform and message owners directly with questions. Read the cancellation policy carefully, as some owners have strict terms for high-demand dates.

Seasons and Weather for the F1 Weekend

The Spanish Grand Prix usually takes place in late May or early June. The weather in Marbella at that time is warm, with average highs of 26 to 28 degrees C. Sea temperatures are around 20 degrees C, comfortable for swimming. The wind is generally light, especially in the morning, but the afternoon can bring a breeze from the Strait of Gibraltar. Your skipper will monitor the forecast and choose a sheltered anchorage if needed. Rain is rare but possible, so bring a light jacket. The sun is strong, so sunscreen and a hat are essential.

The water conditions are usually calm in the bays, but the open sea can have a slight swell. If you are prone to seasickness, consider a catamaran or a larger motor yacht. Ribs and speedboats can be bumpy in choppy water. Most charters provide safety equipment and life jackets.

How to Book a Marbella Boat Rental for F1 Weekend

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and use the search filters to select your port, boat type, and date. You will see a list of available boats with photos, descriptions, and prices. Click on a listing to see the full details, including the owner's profile and the terms. You can send a booking request or a message to ask questions. The owner will confirm availability and send a payment link. Deposit is usually 50 percent, with the balance due on the day. You can also book a full-day charter with a flexible itinerary if you want to combine the race with a lunch stop at a beach club.

For the F1 weekend, we recommend booking a full-day charter from 10am to 6pm. That gives you time to anchor near a beach club for the race, then cruise to a quieter spot for swimming and sunset. If you want to party into the night, some owners offer evening charters with a DJ or a sound system. Check the listing for extras. BoatHire24 also has a blog with tips on the best beach clubs and anchorages for the F1 weekend.

Who Is This For: Groups, Couples, and Corporate Events

A Marbella boat rental for F1 weekend works for different types of groups. If you are a group of friends, a motor yacht or catamaran gives you a private party space away from the crowded beach clubs. For couples, a smaller sailing yacht or RIB offers a more intimate experience, with the option to watch the race from a quiet cove. Corporate groups can book a superyacht for client entertainment or team bonding. The crew can arrange catering, a bar, and even a live stream of the race on a large screen. Some owners offer branded decorations or welcome drinks.

Families with children are also welcome. Most boats have safety rails and life jackets for kids. The skipper can adjust the speed and itinerary to keep everyone comfortable. Just let the owner know your requirements when you book.

Local Highlights Near Marbella for the F1 Weekend

If you want to combine your boat charter with other activities, the Costa del Sol has plenty to offer. The old town of Estepona is a short drive west, with whitewashed buildings and flower-filled streets. The Nerja caves are east, about 45 minutes by car, and are worth a visit if you have an extra day. From the boat, you might see dolphins near the Strait of Gibraltar, especially on a charter from Sotogrande. The views of La Concha mountain from the sea are stunning, especially at sunset. Puerto Banús itself is a spectacle, with superyachts and designer shops. Your skipper can recommend the best spots for swimming, like Cala del Faro or the coves near Cabopino.

For the race itself, many beach clubs in Marbella and Puerto Banús set up large screens. You can anchor nearby and watch from your boat, or go ashore for the atmosphere. Some clubs offer mooring buoys for a fee. Ask your skipper to arrange this in advance.

Which Beach Clubs Show the F1 Race Near Marbella

Several beach clubs along the Costa del Sol set up big screens for the Grand Prix. In Puerto Banús, clubs like Ocean Club and Pangea host viewing parties with DJs and bottle service. You can anchor your boat nearby and either swim to the club or take a tender. Some clubs offer mooring buoys for around EUR 50 to EUR 100 for the day. In Marbella, Nikki Beach and Playa Padre are popular options. Both have a lively atmosphere and direct access to the sea. If you prefer a quieter spot, try a club in Cabopino or Estepona. Your skipper can call ahead to reserve a buoy. For the best experience, book a full-day charter and arrive early to secure a good position.

What to Pack for a Boat Charter During the F1 Weekend

Packing for a boat charter requires a bit of planning. Bring sunscreen with a high SPF, a hat, and sunglasses. The sun is strong even in late May. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful for the afternoon breeze. Swimwear and a towel are essential if you plan to swim. For the race, bring a tablet or phone with a data plan to stream the race if the boat does not have a TV. Some boats have Bluetooth speakers, but a portable speaker is a good backup. If you are prone to seasickness, bring medication or acupressure bands. The crew usually provides bottled water, but you can bring your own drinks. Check with the owner if you can bring a cooler. Most charters allow you to bring food, but some offer catering. Confirm in advance to avoid surprises.

How to Handle Mooring and Anchoring Near F1 Events

Mooring near a beach club during the F1 weekend requires planning. Many clubs have limited buoy space and charge a fee. Your skipper will handle the booking, but you should confirm the cost in advance. If you anchor in a cove, make sure the depth and seabed are suitable. Sandy bottoms are best for anchoring. Rocky or seagrass areas can damage the anchor and the environment. The skipper will use the boat's GPS and chartplotter to find a safe spot. If you want to go ashore, the skipper can drop you at the club's jetty or beach. For larger groups, a tender is useful for ferrying people to and from the boat. Some superyachts have their own tenders. For smaller boats, you may need to swim ashore. Bring a waterproof bag for your valuables.

Best Times to Depart and Return During the F1 Weekend

Timing is important for a smooth charter during the F1 weekend. The race usually starts in the late afternoon, around 3pm Spanish time. If you want to watch the race from the boat, depart around 10am. That gives you time to cruise to a good spot, anchor, and have lunch before the race. After the race, the party continues until late. If you have a full-day charter until 6pm or 8pm, you can enjoy the sunset cruise back to port. For evening charters, depart around 6pm and return by midnight. The sea is usually calm in the morning, so an early start is comfortable. Afternoon winds can pick up, but the skipper will adjust the itinerary. Avoid departing too late, as the ports get busy with returning boats. Your skipper will coordinate with the marina for a berth.

Cost Breakdown for a Typical F1 Weekend Boat Charter

To give you a clearer picture, here is a rough cost breakdown for a group of 10 people on a motor yacht. The charter fee for a full day might be EUR 3,000 to EUR 5,000. Fuel is extra and can cost EUR 200 to EUR 500 depending on distance and speed. Crew gratuity is typically 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee, so EUR 300 to EUR 750. Food and drinks from the owner or a caterer can be EUR 30 to EUR 60 per person, or EUR 300 to EUR 600 total. Mooring fees at a beach club might be EUR 50 to EUR 100. Total for the day could be around EUR 4,000 to EUR 7,000. For a RIB or speedboat for 6 people, the total might be EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. Always ask for a written quote that lists all extras. BoatHire24 listings show what is included and what is not.

How to Avoid Crowds and Still Enjoy the F1 Weekend

The F1 weekend is busy, but you can avoid the worst crowds with a few tricks. Choose a departure port away from Puerto Banús, such as Cabopino or Estepona. These ports have fewer boats and less traffic. Anchor in a less popular cove like Cala del Faro or near the dunes of Artola. Your skipper can find secluded spots that are still within a short cruise of a beach club. For the race itself, consider watching from a quieter club or even from the boat with a live stream. Many boats have good internet connectivity. If you want to party, go to the clubs after the main rush, around 8pm. Book your charter early to get the best boat and the best skipper. What You Get with a Puerto Banus Boat Rental for F1 Weekend

When you book through BoatHire24, you are not just getting a boat. You are getting a complete package that includes a licensed skipper, fuel, basic insurance, and usually a welcome pack of drinks and snacks. The skipper handles all the navigation, docking, and safety, so you can relax and enjoy the race weekend without worrying about anchoring or sea conditions. Most charters also offer optional extras like a barbecue, a DJ, or a dedicated hostess. You can add a gourmet lunch, a sushi platter, or a full open bar. Prices start from around EUR 1500 for a half-day on a motor yacht and go up to EUR 15,000 or more for a superyacht over the entire weekend. The exact cost depends on the boat size, the number of guests, and how far you want to go.

Where You Can Go during the F1 Weekend

Puerto Banus is the obvious departure point, but you are not stuck there. From the marina, you can head east towards Marbella and see the coast from a different angle. You can anchor off the beach at Cabopino, which is quieter and has a nice dune system. Westwards, you can cruise to Estepona and its old town, or further to Sotogrande and the exclusive marina there. If you are feeling adventurous, you can go all the way to the Strait of Gibraltar and watch for dolphins. The F1 race itself is usually on a Sunday afternoon, so you can plan your day around it. Many charter operators will set up a screen on deck so you can watch the race live while anchored near the port. After the race, you can head back to Puerto Banus for the parties or stay on the water and let the crowds thin out. Other departure ports available through BoatHire24 include Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena, so you have options if Puerto Banus is fully booked.

Boat Options for Your F1 Weekend

The type of boat you choose makes a big difference to your experience. For a group of 6 to 10 people, a motor yacht in the 40 to 60 foot range is ideal. You get a spacious deck, a saloon with air conditioning, and a flybridge for sunbathing. Catamarans are popular for larger groups because they offer more deck space and stability. A sailing yacht is a quieter option if you want to combine the race with a proper sailing experience. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper and faster, but they have less comfort and shade. Fishing boats are available if you want to combine the weekend with some angling. Licence-free day boats are a new option for 2025, letting you drive the boat yourself without a licence, though they are limited to smaller sizes. Superyachts are available for those who want the full luxury experience, with crew, jet skis, and a helicopter pad. You can browse all these options on the BoatHire24 search page and filter by size, price, and availability.

Pricing Guidance for F1 Weekend

Prices for a Puerto Banus boat rental during the F1 weekend are higher than normal because demand spikes. Expect to pay from around EUR 1500 to EUR 3000 for a half-day on a mid-range motor yacht. Full-day charters start at EUR 2500 and go up to EUR 5000 for a well-equipped boat. Catamarans for 12 people start around EUR 3000 for a half-day. Superyachts are price on request, but you should budget at least EUR 10,000 per day. The price usually includes the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and basic insurance. Extras like food, drinks, and port fees are extra. If you want a DJ, a photographer, or a fireworks display, that will cost more. Book early because the best boats go quickly. BoatHire24 recommends booking at least two months in advance for the F1 weekend.

Best Time of Year and Weather

The F1 weekend is usually in early June, which is a great time for boating on the Costa del Sol. The sea temperature is around 20 degrees C, and air temperatures hit the high 20s. The wind is generally light, though the afternoon sea breeze can pick up to 15 knots. The water is calm in the morning, making it ideal for a cruise before the race. After the race, the sea state can be slightly choppy, but nothing a well-maintained boat cannot handle. The sun is strong, so bring sunscreen and a hat. The evenings are warm, so you can stay out late. If the weather turns bad, your skipper will know the best sheltered spots, like the lee of La Concha mountain or the bay at Cala del Faro.

This is for anyone who wants to experience the F1 weekend without the hassle of crowded hotels and traffic jams. Families with children are welcome, but check with the operator about age restrictions and safety equipment. If you are a serious F1 fan, you can watch the race from the water and then head to the port for the post-race events. If you are not into racing, you can still enjoy the boat and avoid the chaos. Either way, a Puerto Banus boat rental for the F1 weekend is a smart way to maximise your time on the coast.

Local Tips for Your F1 Weekend Boat Rental

Puerto Banus is busy during the F1 weekend, so arrive early to find parking and board your boat. The marina has security, so bring your booking confirmation. The best anchor spots for watching the race are near the entrance to the port, where you can see the big screens set up on the promenade. If you want a quieter spot, head towards the beach at San Pedro de Alcántara or the dunes at Artola. The water is clear, so bring snorkelling gear. If you want to eat on the water, order a paella or a seafood platter from a catering service that delivers to the boat. Avoid the overpriced restaurants on the port if you can. The skipper will know the best places to anchor for a swim. For a sunset cruise after the race, head west towards Estepona, where the sun sets over the sea. More local tips are available on the BoatHire24 blog.

What to Bring on Your Boat Rental

Pack light but smart. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (factor 50), a hat, and sunglasses. A light jacket or jumper is useful for the evening. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure. The boat will have a first aid kit, but bring your own if you need specific items. You can bring your own drinks and food, but check with the operator first. Most boats have a fridge and a sound system, so bring a playlist. If you want to take photos, a waterproof camera is a good idea. Do not bring glass bottles on board; use plastic or cans. The skipper will provide life jackets and safety briefings. Leave valuables at home or in a secure locker. The boat will have a toilet and a shower, but space is limited, so keep it minimal.

Comparing Departure Ports for F1 Weekend Access

You can structure your weekend around the race schedule. Friday is practice day. Charter a half-day boat from 10:00 to 14:00 and cruise to Cala del Faro for a swim. Return to port by 15:00 to watch the afternoon practice on a bar screen. Saturday is qualifying. Take a full-day boat from 09:00 to 18:00.
