Prices start from around EUR 400 for a two-hour trip on a smaller boat, but a private sunset charter on a 15-metre motor yacht will be closer to EUR 1,500.
bodyHtml:
What a Sunset Cruise from Puerto Banus Includes

A sunset cruise from Puerto Banus is not just a boat ride. It is a private charter for your group, with a skipper who knows the local waters. You get the boat entirely to yourselves, no strangers sharing the deck. The skipper handles the driving, mooring, and any safety briefings. You bring your own food and drink, or arrange catering through the boat owner. Most boats have a sound system, a shaded area, and a sun deck. Some have a fridge, a toilet, and a small galley. The standard duration is two to three hours, leaving about 60 to 90 minutes before sunset. That gives you time to cruise along the coast, drop anchor for a swim if the weather allows, and then watch the sun dip below the horizon. You will return to port as the lights of Puerto Banus come on. It is straightforward, no hidden extras if you read the booking terms.

Why Puerto Banus is the Best Departure Point for a Sunset Cruise

Puerto Banus is the obvious choice for a sunset cruise because it is the most glamorous marina on the Costa del Sol. You step off the boat into a harbour full of restaurants, bars, and shops. But the real advantage is the geography. The marina sits right next to the coast, so you are on open water within minutes. The sunset view from the sea is framed by La Concha mountain to the east and the Rock of Gibraltar to the west on a clear day. You can cruise towards the Cala del Faro or head west towards Estepona. The water is usually flat in the evening, especially in summer, because the wind drops. If you want a longer trip, you can go south towards the Strait of Gibraltar and spot dolphins. But for a standard sunset cruise, staying close to Banus is perfect. The return journey in the twilight is the best part, with the marina lights reflecting on the water.

Available Boat Types for Your Sunset Cruise

You can choose from several boat types for your Puerto Banus boat rental for sunset cruise. Motor yachts are the most common, ranging from 8 metres to over 20 metres. They are fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space. Catamarans are wider and more stable, with a large front trampoline that is great for lounging. Sailing yachts offer a quieter experience, but they are slower, so you need to leave earlier. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper and faster, but they have less comfort and no toilet. Fishing boats are available if you want to combine sunset with a bit of rod fishing. Licence-free day boats are an option if you have a boating licence, but since every charter includes a skipper, you do not need one. Superyachts are available for large groups or special occasions, with prices on request. Each boat listing on BoatHire24 shows the exact capacity, amenities, and photos.

Ports and Departure Points on the Costa del Sol

While Puerto Banus is the star, you can also depart from other ports along the coast. Marbella Marina is just a few kilometres east and offers a more relaxed vibe. Cabopino is smaller and quieter, ideal for a private sunset cruise away from the crowds. Estepona port is further west, with access to the Strait of Gibraltar and its dolphin pods. Sotogrande is a luxury estate with a marina that feels exclusive. Benalmadena is east of Marbella, closer to Malaga airport, and has a large marina with many boat options. If you are staying in Marbella or Banus, Puerto Banus is the most convenient. But if you are based in Estepona or Sotogrande, departing from there saves travel time. All ports are within 30 minutes of each other by boat, so the sunset experience is similar. The key is choosing a port that matches your accommodation and preferred cruising area.

Pricing Guidance for a Sunset Cruise

Prices for a Puerto Banus boat rental for sunset cruise vary by boat size, type, and season. A basic two-hour charter on a 6-metre RIB starts from around EUR 400. A 10-metre motor yacht for three hours is typically EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. A 15-metre luxury motor yacht or catamaran can be EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. Superyachts are price on request, usually EUR 5,000 and up. High season (June to September) is more expensive, and weekend slots book up weeks ahead. Low season (October to May) is cheaper, but sunset is earlier and the weather is cooler. You also pay for fuel, which is usually included in the price but sometimes charged separately. Check the listing details. Catering is extra if you want food and drink provided. Some owners offer a package with tapas and cava for around EUR 30 per person. For the best value, book a smaller boat for a shorter trip. For a memorable experience, invest in a larger boat with more space.

Best Season and Time for a Sunset Cruise

The best season for a sunset cruise from Puerto Banus is late spring through early autumn, from May to October. The weather is warm, with sea temperatures above 20 degrees Celsius from June. July and August are the hottest, with air temperatures around 30 degrees Celsius, and the sun sets around 9:30 PM. In May and September, sunset is around 8:30 PM, and the air is cooler but still pleasant. October is still good, but the evenings get chilly, so bring a jacket. Winter sunsets are earlier, around 6 PM, and the sea can be choppy. That said, a winter sunset cruise is possible on calm days, and prices are lower. The ideal time to depart is 90 minutes before sunset. That gives you enough light for a swim and a relaxed cruise before the main event. Check the local sunset time on the day of your booking, as it changes daily.

How to Book a Sunset Cruise on BoatHire24

Booking a Puerto Banus boat rental for sunset cruise on BoatHire24 is simple. Go to the search page, enter Puerto Banus as the port, select the date, and filter by sunset cruise if available. Browse the listings, read the descriptions, and check the capacity and amenities. Each listing shows the price, the boat type, and the skipper's credentials. Once you find a boat you like, send a booking request through the platform. The owner will confirm availability and send you a payment link. You pay a deposit upfront, usually 30 to 50 percent, and the balance on the day. The platform handles the transaction securely. You will receive a confirmation with the skipper's contact details and meeting point. Arrive 15 minutes before departure. The skipper will give a safety briefing and then you are off. It is that straightforward. No phone calls, no haggling, just a few clicks.

Who is a Sunset Cruise For

A sunset cruise from Puerto Banus works for couples, families, friends, and small groups. Couples often book it for a romantic evening, with champagne and a quiet spot on the bow. Families with children appreciate the stability of a catamaran or a large motor yacht. Groups of friends use it as a party boat, with music and drinks. Corporate groups book it for client entertainment or team building. The common thread is that everyone wants a private, memorable experience on the water. The skipper keeps the boat safe and comfortable, so you do not need any boating experience. If you are celebrating a birthday, anniversary, or proposal, let the owner know in advance. They can arrange decorations, a cake, or a specific route. The sunset cruise is flexible enough to suit any occasion.

Local Attractions and Activities Around Puerto Banus

Puerto Banus itself is worth exploring before or after your sunset cruise. The marina has designer boutiques, restaurants, and bars. The beach is a short walk away, with sunbeds and water sports. If you have time, drive up to La Concon mountain for a hike with panoramic views. The Rio Verde area has a golf course and luxury villas. Estepona old town is a 15-minute drive west and offers traditional Andalusian charm with whitewashed buildings and flower-filled streets. The Strait of Gibraltar is about 30 minutes south, where you can see dolphins and migrating whales. For a day trip, the Nerja caves are an hour east, but that is a separate excursion. Your sunset cruise is the highlight, but the area has plenty to fill a long weekend. Book your boat first, then plan the rest around it.

Frequently Asked Questions About Puerto Banus Sunset Cruises

If you still have doubts, the BoatHire24 blog has more detailed articles on sunset cruises, boat types, and local tips. But here are the common questions we get.

What to Expect on the Water During Your Sunset Cruise

The typical route from Puerto Banus heads west towards the Cala del Faro, a small cove with rocky cliffs and pine trees. You will pass the luxury villas of the Golden Mile, then the coastline opens up. The skipper will find a calm spot to drop anchor, usually in 5 to 10 metres of water. If the sea is flat, you can jump in for a swim. The water temperature in summer is around 24 degrees Celsius, so it is refreshing. After 20 to 30 minutes, the skipper will haul anchor and cruise slowly back towards the marina. The sunset itself lasts about 20 minutes, with the sky turning orange, pink, and purple. You will see the lights of Puerto Banus flicker on as darkness falls. The whole experience feels private and unhurried, even if you are on a short charter. Most skippers are happy to take photos of your group if you ask.

How to Choose the Right Boat Size for Your Group

Boat capacity is measured in persons, and you should never exceed it. A 6-metre RIB fits 6 to 8 people but feels cramped for a sunset cruise. An 8-metre motor yacht fits 8 to 10 people comfortably, with a small cabin and a toilet. A 10-metre motor yacht fits 10 to 12 people and has a proper deck for lounging. A 12-metre catamaran fits 12 to 15 people and offers the most stable ride. For a group of 4 to 6, a 9-metre motor yacht is ideal. For 8 to 10, go for a 12-metre catamaran. For a party of 15 or more, you need a 15-metre motor yacht or a large catamaran. Superyachts over 20 metres can host 20 to 30 guests, but the cost is significantly higher. The rule is to book a boat with 2 to 3 spare seats so everyone has room to move. Check the listing photos to see the actual layout, not just the capacity number.

What to Bring and What Not to Bring on a Sunset Cruise

Bring swimwear, a towel, and sunscreen even in the evening, because the sun reflects off the water. A light jacket or jumper is essential from October to May, as the sea breeze can be cool. Sunglasses and a hat are useful. You can bring your own food and drink, including alcohol. Most boats have a cooler or fridge, but check the listing. Do not bring glass bottles, as they can break on deck. Use plastic cups or cans. Do not bring large coolers that block walkways. Do not bring pets unless the listing explicitly allows them. Do not bring illegal substances, as the skipper will cancel the trip. Do not bring valuables you cannot afford to get wet. A waterproof phone pouch is a good idea. The skipper will provide life jackets and basic safety equipment. If you want music, bring a Bluetooth speaker or use the boat's system. Some boats have a USB port for charging.

How Weather Affects Your Sunset Cruise and What Happens if It Rains

Sunset cruises in Puerto Banus are weather-dependent. The skipper has the final say on whether it is safe to go out. Strong winds, heavy rain, or high waves can cancel a trip. The most common issue is the Poniente wind, which blows from the west and creates choppy seas. In summer, the wind usually drops in the evening, so cancellations are rare. In winter, storms are more frequent. If the weather is bad, the owner will offer a reschedule or a full refund. You should check the forecast on the day and stay in touch with the skipper. If the sea is calm but the sky is cloudy, the cruise still goes ahead, but you might not see the sunset. Some people enjoy a cloudy sunset because the colours are more dramatic. If you are flexible, ask the skipper to take you towards Estepona or Marbella for a different view. The boat is still fun even without a perfect sunset.

Combining a Sunset Cruise with Other Activities on the Costa del Sol

You can book a sunset cruise as part of a longer day on the water. Some boats offer a full-day charter that includes a lunch stop at a beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club. You then return for the sunset leg. This works well for groups who want maximum value. Alternatively, you can book a morning fishing trip and a separate sunset cruise on the same boat. Many owners offer discounts for multi-hour bookings. If you are staying in Marbella, you can combine your sunset cruise with dinner at a Puerto Banus restaurant. The skipper will drop you at the marina pontoon, and you walk straight to a table. For a more adventurous day, drive to the Strait of Gibraltar in the morning for dolphin watching, then head to Puerto Banus for your sunset cruise. The area is compact enough to do both in one day.

Special Occasions and How to Personalise Your Sunset Cruise

If you are planning a proposal, birthday, or anniversary, let the owner know when you book. They can arrange decorations like balloons, banners, or rose petals on the deck. Some owners offer a champagne or cava package for an extra fee. For a proposal, the skipper can anchor at a scenic spot and give you privacy. For a birthday, you can bring a cake and the skipper will help with music. For a corporate event, you can request a specific route that passes key landmarks. The key is to communicate your needs in advance. Most owners are flexible and want you to have a great time. Do not expect a full event planning service, but small touches are usually possible. The cost is typically EUR 50 to EUR 150 extra, depending on the request. Check the listing or message the owner directly through the BoatHire24 platform.

title: Marbella Boat Rental for Family Day Out
metaDescription: Plan a Marbella boat rental for family day out with a skipper. Compare motor yachts, catamarans and RIBs from EUR 600. Book your family charter today.
h1: Marbella Boat Rental for Family Day Out
keyword: Marbella boat rental for family day
intro:
A Marbella boat rental for family day out is the easiest way to get your lot on the water without the usual faff. You turn up, the skipper handles everything from mooring to lunch spots, and you just soak up the Costa del Sol sun. No licence needed, no stress, just a day that actually works for all ages.

BoatHire24 lists every family-friendly charter from Puerto Banús to Estepona. You pick the boat, we confirm the booking, and the skipper takes care of the rest. Expect calm coves, paddleboards, and maybe a pod of dolphins if you head south.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Family Boat Rental in Marbella

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters. That means you don't need a boating licence, and you don't have to worry about navigation or anchoring. The skipper will suggest a route based on your family's mood: a gentle cruise along the coast, a stop for swimming at Cala del Faro, or a longer run towards Gibraltar to spot dolphins.

Most boats come with a cooler, ice, and basic safety gear. Some include paddleboards, snorkel masks, or a Bluetooth speaker. You can bring your own food and drink, or ask the skipper to recommend a beach club for lunch. The day is yours to shape.

Best Ports for a Family Day Out

Puerto Banús is the most famous departure point, with its flashy yachts and designer shops. But for a family day, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is often more relaxed. From there you can head east towards Cabopino, which has a sandy beach and a dune reserve that kids love exploring.

If you want a quieter start, consider Cabopino port itself. It's smaller, less crowded, and the surrounding pine forests offer shade on hot days. Estepona marina is another good option, especially if you combine the boat trip with a walk through the old town's flower-filled streets. Sotogrande and Benalmádena also have family-friendly charters, with Benalmádena offering a quick run to the open sea.

Boat Types for Families

Motor yachts between 8 and 12 metres are the most popular choice. They have a cabin for shade, a small galley, and a bathroom. Speeds are around 20-25 knots, so you can cover ground without scaring the kids. Catamarans are even more stable, with a wide deck and trampolines at the front. They're ideal if anyone gets seasick easily.

Sailing yachts are slower but quieter. They're good for families who want to learn a bit about sailing, but the skipper still does all the work. RIBs and speedboats are faster and more fun for older kids and teenagers, but they can be bumpy in choppy water. Licence-free day boats are available too, but these are usually limited to a 2 NM radius from port, which can feel restrictive.

For a special occasion, superyachts are available from around EUR 5,000 per day. These have multiple cabins, a crew, and often a jet ski or tender. Price on request for the bigger ones.

Pricing Guidance for a Family Charter

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 9-metre motor yacht starts from around EUR 600, while a full day (8 hours) on a 12-metre catamaran is more like EUR 1,200. RIBs are cheaper, from EUR 400 for a half-day. Superyachts and large sailing catamarans are price on request.

Most charters include fuel, the skipper's fee, and basic insurance. Extras like paddleboards, a water slide, or a barbecue are sometimes charged separately. Always confirm what's included before you book. You can find the full range on our search page: search family boats.

Best Time of Year for a Family Boat Day

May to October is the sweet spot. Sea temperatures hit 20-25 degrees C, and the wind is light. July and August are the busiest and most expensive, but the water is warmest. Book at least two weeks ahead in August. June and September are quieter, with lower prices and still plenty of sun. April and October can work if you're lucky with the weather, but bring a jacket for the evening.

Mornings are best for calm seas. The wind usually picks up around 2pm, so a 10am to 2pm slot gives you glassy water for swimming. Afternoon departures are fine too, but expect a slight chop on the return.

How to Book a Family Boat Rental in Marbella

BoatHire24 is a marketplace, not a tour operator. You browse the listings, compare boats and prices, and send an enquiry. We put you in direct contact with the boat owner or charter company. No middleman fees, no hidden extras. The skipper is always included.

To book, go to our homepage BoatHire24, enter your dates and group size, and filter by boat type. You'll see availability and a price estimate. Send an enquiry, and the owner will confirm the details. Payment is usually a deposit via bank transfer or card, with the balance due on the day.

We recommend reading the boat description carefully. Look for "family-friendly" tags and check the maximum number of guests. Some boats have a strict limit, especially RIBs. If you have toddlers, ask about life jackets in small sizes.

Who This Is For

This is for families who want a stress-free day on the water. No planning, no navigation, just showing up and enjoying. It's also for grandparents who can't handle a bumpy ride. Catamarans are the best option for them. Teenagers prefer RIBs or motor yachts with a sound system.

If you have a baby or a toddler, choose a motor yacht with a cabin. The shade and a place to nap make a big difference. Avoid sailing yachts with steep steps and narrow passageways. Catamarans have wider decks and are safer for little ones.

For a full guide to family boating on the Costa del Sol, check our blog: family boat day tips.

Local Highlights for a Family Day Out

From Puerto Banús, head east to the dunes of Cabopino. The beach there is shallow and sheltered. From Marbella Marina, you can cruise under the Río Verde bridge and stop for lunch at a chiringuito on the beach. Estepona offers the best old town for a post-boat stroll, with whitewashed houses and flower pots.

If you have a full day, consider a trip to the Strait of Gibraltar. It's a 45-minute run from Estepona, and you'll often see pilot whales and common dolphins. The skipper will know the best spots. For something different, ask about a trip to the Nerja caves from the sea. It's a longer day, but the cliffs are spectacular.

La Concha mountain is visible from most of the coast. It's a good landmark for kids to spot. Cala del Faro is a small cove near Marbella with a lighthouse and clear water. It's a popular stop for swimming.

What to Bring on a Family Boat Day

Sunscreen, hats, and sunglasses are essential. The sun reflects off the water and you'll burn faster than on land. Bring towels, swimwear, and a change of clothes. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful, even in summer. The wind on the water can feel cool.

Food and drink are usually your responsibility. Most boats have a cooler with ice. Bring sandwiches, fruit, and plenty of water. Avoid glass bottles. Some boats allow a portable barbecue, but check first. If you forget anything, the skipper can recommend a nearby supermarket or beach club.

Motion sickness is rare on calm days, but if anyone is prone, take a tablet an hour before departure. Catamarans are the most stable option.

Safety and Rules

The skipper is responsible for safety. They will give a short briefing at the start. Life jackets are provided for all ages, including infants. Children under 12 must wear a jacket on deck at all times. The skipper will enforce this.

No open fires or smoking below deck. Some boats allow smoking on the aft deck. Ask the skipper. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper cannot drink while operating the boat. Don't expect to take the helm unless you have a licence.

If you book through BoatHire24, all boats are insured and meet Spanish maritime regulations. We verify each listing before it goes live. You are in safe hands.

Why a Skipper Makes Family Boating Stress-Free

You might wonder if a skipper is worth it for a simple family day. The answer is yes, because the skipper handles all the logistics. They know where the calmest swimming spots are, like the sheltered waters off Cabopino beach, and they can adjust the route if the kids get restless. On a recent charter from Puerto Banús, a skipper spotted a pod of dolphins near the Punta de Calaburra lighthouse and changed course so the children could watch them for 20 minutes. You cannot plan that kind of spontaneity when you are piloting yourself.

The skipper also deals with docking, anchoring, and any sudden weather changes. On the Costa del Sol, the afternoon Levante wind can pick up to 20 knots, and a skipper will know to head back to port early if conditions look rough. That gives you peace of mind to relax with a cold drink while the kids paddle at the bow.

Best Boat Layouts for Young Children

If you have children under five, look for a boat with a fully enclosed cockpit. Many motor yachts in the 9-to-11-metre range have a hardtop or a Bimini cover that provides shade, plus a low freeboard so you can lift kids in and out of the water easily. The Azimut 50 and the Jeanneau 51 are common models on BoatHire24 that have wide side decks and a safe aft area.

Catamarans like the Lagoon 42 or Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40 are even better. They have trampoline nets at the front that are fenced off, so toddlers cannot fall overboard. The main deck is one level, no steep stairs, and the saloon has large windows for shade. One family from the UK told us they booked a Lagoon 42 from Sotogrande and spent most of the day on the forward trampoline while their three-year-old napped in the cabin.

Avoid RIBs with young kids. The inflatable tubes are unstable when stationary, and the outboard engine can be loud. Some RIBs do have a small console with a windscreen, but there is no cabin for naps or changing nappies. Stick to motor yachts or catamarans for the under-fives.

How to Choose the Right Duration for Your Family

A half-day of four hours is usually enough for a first-time family outing. You can cruise for an hour, stop for a swim at Cala del Faro or the Cabopino dunes, have lunch on board, and head back. Kids under ten often get bored after three hours on the water, so a half-day keeps them engaged.

Full-day charters of eight hours work well for older children and teenagers. You can go further, like a run from Estepona to the Strait of Gibraltar, where you might see fin whales or common dolphins. That trip takes about 90 minutes each way, leaving five hours for swimming, snorkelling, and a beach-side lunch at a chiringuito like El Balneario in La Línea. Teenagers appreciate the speed of a 28-knot motor yacht on the return leg.

Sunset charters are a good compromise. A two-hour evening trip from Marbella Marina gives you golden light, calm seas, and a chance to see the lights of Puerto Banús from the water. Kids love the novelty of being out after dark, and it costs less than a full day.

What to Do If Someone Gets Seasick

Seasickness is less common on the Costa del Sol than in open ocean, but it still happens. The Mediterranean is usually calm in the morning, with swells under 0.5 metres. If you are worried, book a catamaran because they have a much lower roll motion than a monohull. The Lagoon 380 catamaran, for example, has a beam of 6.7 metres, which makes it almost flat in most conditions.

Practical tips: take motion sickness tablets like Dramamine or Stugeron 30 minutes before departure. Avoid heavy breakfasts; stick to dry crackers or toast. Stay on the deck facing forward, and look at the horizon. If someone feels queasy, the skipper can stop the boat and let them swim. The cold water often resets the stomach. One charter from Benalmádena had a seven-year-old who felt sick after 20 minutes, so the skipper anchored in a cove near the Torremolinos cliffs, the child swam for 10 minutes, and they were fine for the rest of the day.

Cost-Saving Tips for Families on a Budget

Family boat rentals can add up, especially with four or more people. The cheapest option is a RIB for around EUR 400 for a half-day, but as mentioned, they are not ideal for young kids. A better value is a 9-metre motor yacht from Cabopino port. Cabopino has lower berthing fees than Puerto Banús, so the charter prices are often 10-15% cheaper. You can find half-day motor yacht rentals from EUR 550 in June, compared to EUR 650 from Puerto Banús.

Another tip: book for a weekday. Monday to Thursday prices are often EUR 100-200 less than Friday to Sunday. July and August are peak season, so look at late May or early September for the best balance of warm weather and lower rates. A full-day catamaran in late May can cost EUR 1,100, while the same boat in August might be EUR 1,500.

Bring your own food and drink. A supermarket run for sandwiches, crisps, fruit, and soft drinks costs about EUR 30 for a family of four. Buying lunch at a beach club like Nikki Beach or La Sala adds EUR 80-150. Most boats have a cooler and ice, so you save money and eat what you like.

Hidden Costs to Watch For

Most listings on BoatHire24 include fuel, skipper, and basic insurance, but there are extras. Some boats charge for paddleboards or snorkel gear, typically EUR 30-50 per item. A water slide for the back platform can cost EUR 100 extra. Confirm these before booking.

Cleaning fees sometimes appear if you leave the boat messy. A standard cleaning fee is EUR 50-100, but you can avoid it by bagging your rubbish and wiping down surfaces. Port departure taxes are usually included, but check for charters from Estepona or Sotogrande, where some owners add a EUR 20-30 surcharge for using the marina facilities.

Gratuity for the skipper is not mandatory but common. A tip of 10-15% of the charter price is normal if the service was good. For a EUR 800 charter, that is EUR 80-120. Cash is preferred.

Family-Friendly Beach Stops Along the Coast

From Puerto Banús, the best family stop is Playa de las Dunas in Cabopino. It has a long sandy beach with a dune reserve behind it. Kids can run up the dunes and look for shells. The water is shallow for 50 metres, so safe for paddling. There is a chiringuito called La Duna that serves grilled fish and paella.

From Marbella Marina, head east to Cala del Faro. It is a small cove with a lighthouse and clear water. The beach is pebbly, so bring water shoes. It is less crowded than the main beaches, and the rocks around the cove are good for snorkelling. You might see small octopus or starfish.

From Estepona, go west to the Playa de la Rada. It is a long urban beach with a promenade and plenty of cafes. The water is calm because the bay is sheltered by the Punta de la Doncella headland. The skipper can anchor 20 metres offshore, and you can swim in.

From Sotogrande, the best stop is Playa de Torreguadiaro. It is a quiet beach with a marina and a few restaurants. The water is clear and shallow, and the beach has a playground for kids. It is a good spot for a relaxed lunch before heading back.

What to Do on a Rainy Day

Rain on the Costa del Sol is rare in summer, but it happens. If the forecast shows showers, ask the skipper if the boat has a fully enclosed saloon. Many motor yachts have a lower deck with a galley, seating, and a bathroom. You can still enjoy the trip by cruising along the coast while staying dry. The rain usually passes in 20-30 minutes, and then the sun comes out.

If the rain is persistent, reschedule. Most owners on BoatHire24 have a 24-hour cancellation policy for weather. You get a full refund or a credit for another day. Check the terms before booking. A rainy day in Marbella is a good excuse to visit the old town or the Museo del Bonsái instead.

title: Puerto Banus Boat Rental for Family Day
metaDescription: Book a Puerto Banus boat rental for family day with a licensed skipper. Compare motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs for your Costa del Sol excursion.
h1: Puerto Banus Boat Rental for Family Day
keyword: Puerto Banus boat rental for family day
intro:
If you are looking for a Puerto Banus boat rental for family day, you have come to the right place. The whole point is to get everyone on the water without the stress of driving or navigating. Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, so you can actually relax, have a drink, and watch the kids jump off the back of the boat into the Mediterranean.

You are not booking a bareboat and hoping for the best. You are hiring a vessel with a professional who knows the local waters, the best coves, and where to find the dolphins off the Strait of Gibraltar. Departure ports include Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. You choose the boat type, the duration, and the extras. We handle the rest.
bodyHtml:
What a Family Day Charter Includes

When you book a Puerto Banus boat rental for family day through BoatHire24, the package is straightforward. You get the boat for a set number of hours, typically 4, 6, or 8 hours, with a skipper who holds a valid Spanish licence. The skipper handles the navigation, mooring, and safety briefings. You do not need any boating experience or a licence yourself.

Most charters include fuel for a standard itinerary, but check the listing because some operators charge extra for fuel beyond a certain number of nautical miles. You will also get basic safety equipment, life jackets for all ages, and a cooler or ice box. Many boats come with a Bluetooth speaker, a shower on the swim platform, and a bimini top for shade. Some catamarans have a trampoline net at the front, which kids love for lying on and watching the sea through the mesh.

Food and drink are usually not included, but you can bring your own or order a catering package through the operator. Typical options include a seafood platter, paella, or a BBQ on the boat. If you are departing from Puerto Banús, you can also grab takeaway from the marina restaurants before you set off.

Departure Ports and Their Advantages for Families

Puerto Banús is the most famous departure point on the Costa del Sol, and for good reason. The marina itself is a spectacle of superyachts, designer shops, and busy restaurants. If you are staying in Marbella or nearby, it is the most convenient port. The marina has ample parking (paid) and is a short walk from the beach. You can also combine your boat trip with a stroll around the port afterwards.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and slightly cheaper for parking. It is located right next to the old town, so you can grab tapas before or after the trip. Cabopino is a small, sandy-bottomed marina near the dunes of Artola. It is ideal if you want a quick exit to the open sea and a less crowded feel. Estepona has a lovely promenade and a marina that is close to the old town with its flower-filled streets. Sotogrande is more upmarket and further west, good if you are based near Gibraltar. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, close to the Selwo Marina dolphinarium, and offers a direct route to the Cala del Faro area.

For a family day, the distance from your accommodation matters. If you are staying in Marbella city, Marbella Marina is a 5-minute drive. If you are in Puerto Banús, you walk to the dock. If you are in Estepona, use that port. The skipper will know the best spots within a 10-15 NM radius, so you do not waste time motoring.

Types of Boats Suitable for a Family Day

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for a family day because they offer plenty of deck space, a cabin with a toilet, and a steady ride. Look for a 40-50 foot motor yacht with a flybridge. The flybridge gives you an elevated seating area with a second helm, so the skipper can drive while the family sits up top with a better view. The lower deck usually has a saloon, a small galley, and a cabin where kids can nap or change.

Catamarans are excellent for families with young children because they are stable. They do not heel like a monohull sailing yacht, so nobody gets seasick. The wide beam means a spacious deck, often with a trampoline net at the bow. You can anchor in a calm cove and the kids can jump off the side without the boat rocking much. Catamarans also have two or three cabins, so you can store bags and have a proper toilet.

Sailing yachts are an option if you want a more traditional experience and the wind cooperates. For a family day, a 40-50 foot sailing yacht with a skipper is fine, but be aware that the boat will heel when sailing. If you have toddlers or elderly family members, a motor yacht or catamaran is more comfortable.

RIBs and speedboats are for the more adventurous family. They are fast, open boats with a centre console. You can reach the Cala del Faro or the cliffs of Marbella in 15 minutes. But there is less shade and no toilet, so they are better for a half-day trip with older kids. Fishing boats are purpose-built and often have a toilet and a small cabin. They are slower but come with fishing gear and the skipper can take you to the best spots.

Licence-free day boats are available for rent without a skipper, but for a family day we recommend taking the skipper anyway. It is one less thing to worry about, and the skipper knows where the dolphins are. Superyachts are an option if you want to splurge, but for a standard family day a 40-50 foot motor yacht or catamaran is the sweet spot.

Pricing Guidance for a Family Day Charter

Prices for a Puerto Banus boat rental for family day vary depending on the boat size, age, and included extras. For a 40-foot motor yacht, expect to pay from around EUR 800 for a 4-hour charter, EUR 1,200 for 6 hours, and EUR 1,600 for 8 hours. Catamarans of a similar size tend to be slightly more, from EUR 900 for 4 hours. RIBs start from EUR 500 for 4 hours. These prices include the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and basic equipment.

Peak season (June to September) commands a premium, often 20-30% higher. July and August are the most expensive, and you should book at least 2-3 weeks in advance. Shoulder months (May, October) are cheaper and the weather is still good, with sea temperatures around 20-22 degrees C. Winter charters are possible but the sea can be choppy, and many operators run reduced schedules.

Extras that add to the cost: catering (EUR 30-60 per person), water toys like a paddleboard or inflatable mat (EUR 50-100), and extra hours beyond the standard package. Some operators charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50-100 if you make a mess. Port fees are usually included in the charter price, but confirm with the operator.

For a family of 4-6 people, a 6-hour charter on a 40-foot motor yacht is the most common choice. That gives you time to cruise to a cove, anchor for lunch, swim, and head back. If you have a larger group (8-10 people), you need a bigger boat or a catamaran, which pushes the price up to EUR 2,000-3,000 for a full day.

Best Times of Year for a Family Boat Day

The Costa del Sol enjoys over 300 days of sunshine a year, so you can rent a boat in almost any month. For a family day with swimming, the best period is June to September, when air temperatures hit 30-35 degrees C and the sea is 22-26 degrees C. July and August are the hottest, but also the busiest. The coves can get crowded, especially Cala del Faro and the area near the Marbella Club. If you want a quieter experience, go in June or September.

May and October are still warm enough for a boat trip, but the sea is cooler (18-20 degrees C). You might not want to swim for long, but you can still sunbathe and enjoy the views. The water is clearer in these months because there is less plankton. November to April is the low season. You can get good deals, but the weather is unpredictable. Winds can be strong, and some operators do not run charters in winter. If you do go, bring a jacket and plan for a coastal cruise rather than swimming.

The wind pattern is important. The Poniente wind comes from the west and is usually light. The Levante wind comes from the east and can be strong, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar area. Your skipper will check the forecast and adjust the itinerary. If the Levante is blowing, they will stick to the lee side of the coast, such as the area between Estepona and Marbella.

Sea conditions are generally calm in the morning. The wind picks up around 1 PM and can make the sea choppy in the afternoon. A 6-hour charter from 10 AM to 4 PM is a good compromise. You get the calm morning for cruising and swimming, and you are back before the sea gets too rough.

What to Bring and What to Expect

Pack light for a family day on a boat. Swimsuits, towels, sunscreen (reef-safe if you care about the marine life), hats, and sunglasses. Bring a light jacket or a rash guard for the kids, because the wind can feel cool even on a hot day. A change of dry clothes is useful for the ride back. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness pill an hour before departure. The Mediterranean is usually calm, but the swell can affect some people.

Most boats have a fridge or cooler, so bring your own drinks and snacks. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper will not serve it. You can bring beer, wine, or sangria, but keep it moderate. If someone gets drunk and falls overboard, that is a problem. Soft drinks and water are essential, especially for kids.

The skipper will give a safety briefing at the start. Listen to it. They will point out the life jackets, the fire extinguisher, and the emergency procedures. Kids under 12 should wear a life jacket at all times when on deck, especially if they are not strong swimmers. The skipper will enforce this.

On the day, you meet at the designated dock. The skipper will be there 15 minutes early. You board, stow your bags, and do the briefing. Then you cast off. The skipper will ask if you have a preferred itinerary. If not, they will suggest one based on the weather and your group's interests. Typical stops: a cruise past the Puerto Banús superyachts, a swim stop at Cala del Faro or the Río Verde estuary, and a dolphin-watching detour if you are heading west towards Gibraltar. The skipper will anchor for lunch in a calm spot, and you can swim, snorkel, or just lounge.

At the end, you return to the dock. The skipper will help you moor and say goodbye. You tip the skipper if you want, usually 10-15% of the charter price, but it is not mandatory.

How to Book Your Family Day Charter

Booking through BoatHire24 is simple. Use the search filters to select Puerto Banús as the departure port, your preferred date, and the number of guests. You can also filter by boat type and budget. Each listing shows the boat details, photos, the skipper's experience, and the exact price. You can read the cancellation policy before you book.

Once you find a boat you like, click the book button. You will be asked for your contact details and payment. We accept credit cards and bank transfers. The payment is processed securely. After booking, you receive a confirmation email with the meeting point, the skipper's phone number, and a map. If you have any special requests, like a birthday cake or a specific catering menu, you can add a note during the booking process.

We recommend booking at least a week in advance during peak season. For July and August, two weeks ahead is safer. If you are booking last minute, you can still find availability, but the best boats go first. Cancellation policies vary by operator. Most offer a full refund if you cancel 48 hours before departure. Some are stricter, so read the terms.

If you are unsure which boat to choose, call us or use the contact form. We can give you advice based on your group size and budget. We have been doing this for years and know the fleet well.

Who This Is For and Who It Is Not For

A Puerto Banus boat rental for family day is ideal for families with children aged 4 and up. Younger kids can come, but you need to watch them constantly. The boat has railings and a net on catamarans, but toddlers can still slip. If you have a baby, bring a life jacket designed for infants (check the boat has one, or bring your own). Most skippers are happy to accommodate babies, but the motion can be unsettling for them.

This is also great for multi-generational groups. Grandparents can sit on the flybridge or in the saloon, away from the sun, while the kids swim. The skipper can adjust the speed and itinerary to suit everyone. If someone has mobility issues, a motor yacht with a wide boarding ramp is better than a sailing yacht with a narrow ladder.

This is not for people who want to drive the boat themselves. If you want a licence-free day boat without a skipper, we have those too, but for a family day the skipper is the safer choice. It is also not for party groups. If you want a loud, boozy day with 20 friends, look for a different charter. Family charters are more relaxed and the skipper will keep an eye on behaviour.

If you are a single parent or a couple with kids, a 4-hour charter is enough to get a taste. A 6-hour charter gives you time for a proper lunch stop. An 8-hour charter is for families who want to go further, maybe to the Nerja caves or the coast near Estepona, but that is a long day for young children.

For more tips on planning your trip, read our blog on family-friendly boat itineraries on the Costa del Sol.

h1: Marbella Boat Rental for Hen Do: The Ultimate Party Afloat
keyword: Marbella boat rental for hen do
intro:
You are the maid of honour, which means you are the one who has to pull off the perfect hen weekend. No pressure. You want sun, sea, sangria and something that doesn't involve queuing for a sticky-floored club in Puerto Banús. The answer is a boat. A Marbella boat rental for hen do is the best way to get the bride-to-be and the squad onto the Mediterranean with a licensed skipper, a cooler full of cava and zero stress.

We are BoatHire24, a marketplace for boat rental and yacht charter on the Costa del Sol. We have done this before. We know which boats work for a group of 10, 15 or 20 women, which ports have the best sunset views and how to avoid the hangover-inducing mistake of booking a boat with no toilet. Read on for the no-nonsense guide to renting a boat for a hen party in Marbella.
bodyHtml:
What a Marbella Boat Rental for Hen Do Actually Includes

Every boat on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a licence, and you do not have to park the thing. The skipper handles the navigation, the mooring and the safety. You handle the prosecco. Most charters include fuel, insurance, VAT and basic safety equipment. Some include a Bluetooth speaker, a fridge and a sun deck. Check the listing details before you book because not all boats have a toilet, and for a hen do that matters.

A typical half-day charter runs from 10:00 to 14:00 or 15:00 to 19:00. Full-day charters are 10:00 to 18:00 or 19:00. You can also book sunset charters from around 17:00 to 21:00 in summer. The skipper will take you along the coast, drop anchor for a swim stop and let you use the paddleboard or snorkel gear if the boat has it. You bring the food and drink. Most skippers are fine with glass bottles if you are careful, but some prefer plastic. Ask when you book.

If you want a DJ, a barbecue or a water slide, those are extras. You can add them through the listing or arrange directly with the skipper. Prices for a Marbella boat rental for hen do start from around EUR 800 for a half-day on a RIB or a small motor yacht for up to 10 guests. For a catamaran with a large deck and a toilet, expect from EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 for a half-day depending on the size and the season.

Which Port Is Best for Your Hen Do Boat Rental

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice. It is the glitziest port on the Costa del Sol, full of superyachts, designer shops and the sort of people who wear sunglasses indoors. Departed from here, you can cruise past the Golden Mile, see the back of the Marbella Club and anchor off the Cabopino dunes. The downside is that the port is busy, parking is a nightmare and the departure time might be strict. If you are staying in a villa near Nueva Andalucía or the centre of Marbella, Puerto Banús is convenient.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a quieter alternative. It is right next to the old town, so you can walk from the marina to a tapas bar in five minutes. The boats here are slightly smaller on average, but you get a more relaxed vibe. Depart from here and you are quickly out past the Marbella lighthouse and heading towards Cabopino or even Cala del Faro for a swim.

Cabopino is a small marina near the Artola dunes. It is less crowded, cheaper to park and closer to the open sea. If your hen group is staying in a villa near Calahonda or Miraflores, this is the smart choice. Estepona port is further west, near the charming old town with its flower pots and blue-washed buildings. The Strait of Gibraltar is not far, so you have a good chance of seeing dolphins. Sotogrande is for the luxury crowd who want a longer charter towards Gibraltar. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, closer to Málaga airport, and has a large marina with plenty of boat options.

For a hen do, we often recommend Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina because they are central and close to the nightlife. But if you want a quieter start and a more scenic route, Cabopino or Estepona work well.

Boat Types for a Hen Party: Which One Suits Your Group

Motor yachts are the classic choice. They have a sun deck at the front, a shaded saloon with a sofa and a table, and a small cabin with a toilet. For a group of 10 to 12, a 12-metre to 15-metre motor yacht is ideal. You get speed, comfort and enough space to dance without falling overboard. Brands like Azimut, Sunseeker and Princess are common on the Costa del Sol. Expect to pay from EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,500 for a half-day.

Catamarans are the party platform. They are wider than motor yachts, so they do not heel over and they have a massive deck area. You can fit 12 to 20 guests easily. The trampoline net at the front is a popular sunbathing spot. Catamarans also have a proper toilet, a galley and a flybridge with a bimini top. They are slower than motor yachts but more stable. For a hen do, a catamaran is hard to beat. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day for up to 12 guests.

RIBs and speedboats are the budget option. They are fast, open boats with a hard console and a few forward seats. You can fit 8 to 12 people, but there is no shade and no toilet. They are great for a short blast to a beach club or a swim stop, but not for a full-day party. Expect to pay from EUR 800 to EUR 1,200 for a half-day.

Sailing yachts are a different vibe. They are quieter, more romantic and less party-focused. If the bride is a sailor or if the group wants a relaxed day of sunbathing and sailing, a 12-metre to 15-metre sailing yacht works. But the deck space is limited and the cockpit is smaller. Not ideal for a big hen group.

Licence-free day boats are small motorboats that you can drive without a licence. They are cheap, around EUR 300 to EUR 500 for a half-day, but they are tiny. You can take 4 to 6 people maximum. For a hen do, they are only suitable for a very small group.

Superyachts are for the budget-unlimited crowd. Think 25 metres plus, with a crew, a jacuzzi, a flybridge and a full bar. Prices are on request, but expect EUR 8,000 and up for a day. If you have the cash, go for it.

Pricing Guidance for a Marbella Boat Rental for Hen Do

Prices vary by boat size, season, duration and extras. We do not list exact prices for specific boats because they change. But here is a rough guide for 2025. For a half-day (4 hours) on a motor yacht for up to 10 guests, expect from EUR 1,000 to EUR 2,000. For a catamaran for up to 12 guests, from EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. For a RIB for up to 10 guests, from EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. Full-day (8 hours) prices are roughly double. Sunset charters (3 hours) are often cheaper, from EUR 600 to EUR 1,500.

High season is June to September. July and August are the most expensive and the busiest. If you want a Saturday in August, book at least three months in advance. Low season, from October to May, is cheaper and less crowded. The weather is still good, with average temperatures of 20 to 25 degrees C in May and October. You might get a breeze, but you will also get a better price and more availability.

Extras cost more. A DJ can add EUR 300 to EUR 500. A barbecue on the boat might be EUR 200. A water slide or inflatable platform is around EUR 150. A photographer is EUR 200 to EUR 400. Ask the skipper or the listing owner for a custom quote.

Seasons and Weather for Hen Do Boat Rentals

The Costa del Sol has over 320 sunny days a year. That is not a marketing line, it is a fact. The best months for a hen do boat rental are May, June, September and October. The weather is warm but not scorching, the sea is calm and the ports are less crowded. July and August are hot, with temperatures often above 30 degrees C. You will want a boat with shade, a bimini or a hardtop. The sea breeze helps, but bring plenty of sunscreen and hats.

Winter months, November to February, are cooler. Daytime temperatures are around 15 to 18 degrees C. You can still go out on a boat, but you will need a jacket and the swimming stops will be brief. Some boats are not available in winter, so check the listing. March and April are transitional. The weather is unpredictable but often pleasant.

Wind is a factor. The Levante wind from the east can create choppy seas, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar. The Poniente wind from the west is lighter. Skippers will not take you out if conditions are unsafe, so trust their judgment. If the forecast is bad, you can reschedule or cancel according to the booking policy.

How to Book a Marbella Boat Rental for Hen Do

Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters. Select the port, the date, the number of guests and the boat type. Look for the keyword "hen do" or "party" in the listing title. Read the description carefully. Check the maximum guest capacity, the number of toilets, the availability of a speaker, and whether food and drink are allowed. Some boats have a strict no-glass policy. Some do not allow loud music after 20:00. Know this before you book.

Contact the owner through the platform to ask about extras, deposit and cancellation policy. Most require a 30% to 50% deposit to confirm the booking, with the balance paid on the day. Payment is usually by bank transfer or cash. Credit card is less common but possible on some listings. The skipper will meet you at the port 15 minutes before departure. They will give a safety briefing and show you the toilet and the life jackets. Then you are off.

We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance for a weekend in high season. For a Saturday in August, book one to two months ahead. For a weekday in low season, a few days is often enough.

Who Is a Marbella Boat Rental for Hen Do For

This is for the bride who wants something different from a bottomless brunch or a night in a club. It is for the group that wants to swim in the Mediterranean, sunbathe on a deck and drink cava while watching the sunset behind La Concha mountain. It is for the maid of honour who wants to organise a day that requires minimal effort and maximum Instagram potential.

It is not for the group that wants a wild party with a DJ and a dance floor. Some boats allow that, but most are for a relaxed celebration. If you want a raucous party, book a catamaran with a DJ and a sound system. If you want a chilled day with paddleboarding and snorkelling, book a motor yacht or a sailing yacht.

It is also for the group that wants to see the coast from the water. You will pass the luxury villas of the Golden Mile, the cliffs of Cabopino, the dunes of Artola and the old town of Estepona. You might see dolphins if you go towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You can stop at a beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club for lunch, or anchor in a quiet cove like Cala del Faro and eat your own food.

For more tips on planning a hen weekend on the water, read our blog on how to choose the right boat for your group. And if you want to see all available boats for your dates, visit the search page.

intro:
You want to get out on the water in Marbella without spending a fortune. That is exactly what cheap boat rental Marbella means: a full day on a boat with a licensed skipper, from around €200 per person for a group, or from €600 for a private boat for up to 8 people. No hidden fees, no surprise charges. You pay, you go, you enjoy the sun.

BoatHire24 lists dozens of boats available for cheap rental in Marbella, from small RIBs and licence-free day boats to older but well-maintained motor yachts and catamarans. Every charter includes a skipper, so you do not need a licence. You just show up, bring your drinks, and let the captain handle the rest.

Ports covered: Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, Benalmádena. Read on for the real costs, what you get, and how to book without getting ripped off.
bodyHtml:
What Does Cheap Boat Rental Marbella Actually Mean

Cheap in Marbella still means a proper boat, not a dinghy. You can rent a 5-7 metre RIB or speedboat from around €200 for a half day (4 hours) for up to 6 people. A 10-metre motor yacht from the 1990s or early 2000s, with basic amenities, costs from around €600 for a full day (8 hours) for up to 8 guests. Catamarans start from €800 for a full day, but older models can dip lower in low season.

These prices include the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary (usually around 20-30 NM), and basic insurance. You pay extra for fuel if you go beyond the standard route, for food and drinks, and for dockage at certain beaches. Always confirm what is included before booking.

The key to cheap is timing. Book in May, June, or September. July and August prices can double. Midweek (Monday to Thursday) is cheaper than weekends. Last-minute bookings sometimes get discounts, but risk is limited availability.

Ports Where Cheap Boats Depart

You can find cheap boat rental Marbella departing from several ports along the Costa del Sol. Each has its own character and price level.

Puerto Banús is the most glamorous and most expensive port. Cheap boats here are rare, but you can find older models from around €700 for a full day. The advantage is you start right next to the best restaurants and shops.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a better bet for cheap rental. Boats here are generally 10-20% cheaper than in Banús. You can find RIBs from €200 half day and motor yachts from €500 full day. The marina is close to the old town and the beach.

Cabopino is a small, quiet marina near Artola dunes. Cheap boats here are often the best value, with RIBs from €180 half day and day boats from €400 full day. The water is clearer, and the beach is less crowded.

Estepona port is growing fast. You can find cheap catamarans and motor yachts from €450 full day. The old town of Estepona is a short walk, and the marina has good parking.

Sotogrande is more exclusive, but cheap boats exist if you look for older models. Prices start from €600 full day. The area is quieter, and you can head towards Gibraltar for dolphin watching.

Benalmádena is a busy port with many charter companies. Cheap RIBs and fishing boats start from €150 half day. The marina has a lively atmosphere and many bars.

Boat Types Available for Cheap Rental

Not all boats are created equal. Here is what you can expect for cheap boat rental Marbella.

RIBs and speedboats (5-8 metres) are the cheapest option. They are fast, open, and basic. You get a sun pad, a small bimini, and a cooler. Great for a quick blast to Cala del Faro or a beach drop-off. Prices from €200 half day.

Licence-free day boats (6-8 metres) are similar to RIBs but with a small cabin and a toilet. You do not need a licence to drive them, but the skipper is still included. Prices from €250 half day.

Older motor yachts (10-14 metres) from the 1990s or early 2000s. They have a saloon, a small galley, a cabin, and a toilet. They are not fancy, but they are comfortable. Prices from €500 full day.

Small catamarans (10-12 metres) offer more space and stability. Older models can be cheap, from €700 full day. They are great for groups who want to avoid seasickness.

Fishing boats (7-9 metres) are basic but functional. They come with fishing gear and a skipper who knows the spots. Prices from €300 half day.

Pricing Guidance for Cheap Boat Rental Marbella

Prices vary by season, boat age, and duration. Here are realistic ranges for cheap boat rental Marbella in 2025.

Low season (October to April, excluding Easter): RIBs from €180 half day, motor yachts from €450 full day, catamarans from €600 full day.

Mid season (May, June, September): RIBs from €200 half day, motor yachts from €550 full day, catamarans from €750 full day.

High season (July, August, Easter week): RIBs from €300 half day, motor yachts from €800 full day, catamarans from €1,100 full day.

Prices are per boat, not per person. For example, a €600 motor yacht for 8 people works out at €75 per person. That is cheap for a full day on the water with a skipper.

Always check the total cost, including any extras like fuel surcharges, cleaning fees, or port taxes. Some companies add a 10-20% service fee. BoatHire24 shows the full price upfront.

What Is Included in a Cheap Boat Rental

Every cheap boat rental Marbella from BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That is non-negotiable. The skipper drives the boat, knows the best spots, and handles safety. You do not need a licence or experience.

Fuel is included for a standard itinerary. Typically, that covers a route from the port to a nearby beach (like Cala del Faro or Cabopino), a stop for swimming, and return. If you want to go further, to Marbella or Estepona, you may pay extra for fuel.

Basic insurance is included. That covers damage to the boat, but not your personal belongings or cancellation. You can buy extra cancellation insurance for around 10% of the rental price.

What is not included: food, drinks, towels, snorkel gear (though some boats provide it), and dockage at beaches (usually free if you anchor). Some boats have a fridge and ice, but bring your own provisions.

Seasons and Best Time for Cheap Boat Rental Marbella

The best time for cheap boat rental Marbella is May, June, and September. The weather is warm (25-30°C), the water is swimmable (18-22°C), and prices are lower than July and August.

July and August are peak season. The sea is calm, the sun is hot, but prices can double. Book early (2-3 months ahead) to get a cheap boat. Last-minute deals are rare in high season.

October and April are shoulder months. Weather is still good (20-25°C), but the water is cooler (16-18°C). Prices are low, and you can often negotiate. Some boats are not available as owners winterise them.

November to March is low season. Many boats are out of the water for maintenance. A few RIBs and day boats are available, but expect cold water (14-16°C) and possible wind. Prices are the cheapest, from €150 half day.

How to Book Cheap Boat Rental Marbella

Booking cheap boat rental Marbella is straightforward on BoatHire24. Use the search filters to set your budget, group size, and preferred port. You can also filter by boat type, such as RIB or motor yacht.

Compare listings carefully. Look at the boat age, amenities, and what is included. Older boats are cheaper but may have less comfortable seating or older electronics. Read the description and check the photos.

Once you find a boat, click to see availability. You can book directly online with a deposit (usually 30-50%) and pay the rest on the day. Cancel up to 48 hours before for a full refund, minus a small admin fee.

If you have questions, contact the owner or the BoatHire24 support team. We can help you find the cheapest option for your dates. For more tips, read our blog on budget boating in Marbella.

Who Is Cheap Boat Rental Marbella For

Cheap boat rental Marbella is for anyone who wants to enjoy the Mediterranean without spending a fortune. It is ideal for groups of friends, families, and couples who want a private day out.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter (not listed on BoatHire24, but ask at the port). Expect to pay around €50-100 per person for a half day on a group boat.

It is also for people who want to try boating without commitment. You do not need a licence, you do not need to buy a boat, you just rent for a day. If you like it, you can rent again or consider a longer charter.

Cheap does not mean bad. Many older boats are well maintained and perfectly safe. The skipper ensures everything runs smoothly. You get the same sun, sea, and views as on a luxury yacht, for a fraction of the price.

Local Highlights You Can See on a Cheap Boat Rental

Even on a cheap boat rental Marbella, you can see some great sights. The skipper usually knows the best spots.

Puerto Banús from the water is impressive. You see the superyachts up close, the golden beach, and the mountains behind. It is a good photo spot.

La Concha mountain dominates the skyline. On a clear day, it looks like a giant shell. The view from the sea is stunning.

Cala del Faro is a small cove near Cabopino. It has clear water and a small beach. Perfect for a swim stop. It is a common destination for cheap rentals from Cabopino or Marbella.

Estepona old town from the sea is colourful. The white houses with flower pots make a pretty backdrop. You can dock at the port and walk into town.

Strait of Gibraltar is further south, but some cheap boats from Sotogrande or Estepona go there. You can see dolphins, sometimes whales, and the African coast. It is a longer trip, so fuel may cost extra.

If you have time, consider a day trip to Nerja caves from the sea. It is a longer journey (about 2 hours from Marbella), but some cheap boats do it. The caves are impressive, and the coast is beautiful.

Frequently Asked Questions About Cheap Boat Rental Marbella

How to Spot Hidden Costs in a Cheap Boat Rental Marbella

Cheap boat rental Marbella can look good on paper, but some operators add extras that push the price up. The most common hidden cost is a fuel surcharge. Some companies offer a cheap base rate, then charge you EUR 15-20 per nautical mile beyond a short route. Ask for the fuel policy before booking. A standard itinerary should cover 20-30 NM. If you want to go from Marbella to Estepona and back, that is about 30 NM round trip, so you should be fine. But if you want to go to the Strait of Gibraltar, that is 80 NM round trip, and you will pay extra.

Another hidden cost is the cleaning fee. Some operators add EUR 50-100 for cleaning, even if you leave the boat tidy. Check the listing details. On BoatHire24's search page, we show the total price including all fees. If a boat seems too cheap, read the fine print. Dockage at beach clubs is another one. If you want to stop at a beach club like Nikki Beach or Trocadero, they may charge a mooring fee of EUR 20-50. The skipper will tell you, but it is not always included. Bring cash for these extras.

Insurance excess is another cost to understand. Basic insurance covers damage, but the excess (the amount you pay if something breaks) can be EUR 500-2,000. You can buy a waiver for around 10% of the rental price to reduce the excess to zero. On a cheap rental of EUR 200, that is only EUR 20 extra. Worth it for peace of mind.

Best Cheap Boat Rental Marbella Options for Large Groups

If you have a group of 8-12 people, cheap boat rental Marbella is still possible, but you need to choose the right boat. A 10-metre motor yacht from the 1990s can take up to 10 guests. Prices start from EUR 600 full day in mid season. That works out at EUR 60-75 per person, which is cheaper than a group taxi tour. The boat will have a small saloon, a toilet, and a sun pad. It is not luxury, but it is functional.

For groups of 12-14 people, a small catamaran is better. Older catamarans from around 12 metres can be found from EUR 800 full day in mid season. They have more deck space, a trampoline net at the front, and a small cabin. Catamarans are more stable, so less seasickness. The downside is they are slower (10-12 kts), so you spend more time cruising and less time at the destination.

For very large groups of 14-18 people, you may need two cheap boats or one larger one. Two RIBs for 6 people each cost around EUR 200 each half day, total EUR 400. That is cheaper than one large yacht. You can cruise together and meet at the beach. The skippers can coordinate via radio.

How to Negotiate a Cheap Boat Rental Marbella Price

Negotiation works on cheap boat rental Marbella, especially in low season or for last-minute bookings. Start by checking the listed price on BoatHire24. If you see a boat you like, contact the owner directly through the platform. Ask if they can offer a discount for a midweek booking or a longer charter. Many owners prefer a full week booking at a lower daily rate than empty days.

In low season (October to April), you can often get 10-20% off the listed price. In mid season, discounts are smaller, maybe 5-10%. In high season, forget it. Owners know they can sell at full price. But if you book two days in a row, you can sometimes get the second day at 50% off. This works well for RIBs and day boats, less so for yachts.

Another tactic is to ask for a shorter charter. A half day (4 hours) is cheaper than a full day (8 hours). If you only want to swim and have lunch, 4 hours is enough. You can negotiate a half-day rate even if the listing only shows full-day. Owners prefer half-day charters because they can do two in one day.

Cheap Boat Rental Marbella for Fishing Enthusiasts

If you want to fish, cheap boat rental Marbella is a good option. Fishing boats are basic but functional. They have rod holders, a fish finder, and a live bait tank. The skipper knows the best spots for sea bass, bream, and mackerel. Prices start from EUR 300 for a half day for up to 6 people. That includes the skipper, basic gear, and fuel for a standard route.

The best fishing spots near Marbella are around the Cabopino reefs and the Estepona coastline. You can also go further south to the Strait of Gibraltar for tuna and swordfish, but that costs extra fuel. Most cheap fishing boats stay within 10 NM of the port. You will catch smaller fish, but it is still fun.

Check if the boat includes cleaning and bagging of your catch. Some skippers do it for free, others charge EUR 10-20. Bring your own cooler to take the fish home. Also, check the weather. Fishing is best in calm seas (wind less than 15 kts). The skipper will advise you on the day.

What to Bring on a Cheap Boat Rental Marbella

Cheap boat rental Marbella usually does not include luxury extras. You need to bring your own supplies. Start with sunscreen (factor 50, the sun is strong), sunglasses, a hat, and a towel. The boat has a bimini for shade, but it is limited. Bring a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon breeze.

For food and drink, bring a cooler with ice. Most cheap boats have a small fridge, but it may not be cold enough. Pack sandwiches, fruit, and plenty of water. Alcohol is allowed, but do not get drunk. The skipper is responsible for safety. If you cause trouble, they can end the charter early. No refund.

Snorkel gear is not always provided. You can rent it at the port for around EUR 10 per set, or bring your own. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos. And cash for tips (optional, but appreciated) and any extras like beach club mooring fees.

h1: Last Minute Boat Hire Marbella, Book Today & Save
intro:
You want to get on the water tomorrow, or maybe even this afternoon, and you don't want to pay full price for the privilege. Last minute boat hire Marbella is exactly that: unsold slots on motor yachts, catamarans, sailing yachts and RIBs that skippers would rather fill at a discount than leave empty.
