bodyHtml:
What a Wedding Boat Hire in Puerto Banús Includes

A private boat hire for a wedding in Puerto Banús typically includes the vessel, a licensed skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. Most operators will let you bring your own decorations, but you need to check if they allow confetti or flowers that might stain the deck. Some packages include a small table for the cake, a sound system for the vows, and a canopy for shade. Catering is usually extra, but many boats work with local caterers who can set up a buffet or a sit-down meal on the aft deck. You should also factor in a photographer, because the light over the Strait of Gibraltar at sunset is something else.

If you want a civil ceremony, you'll need to arrange a legal officiant separately. The boat can act as the venue, but the marriage must be registered on land. A symbolic ceremony is easier, and many couples go with that option, then have the legal bit done at the town hall in Marbella or Estepona a few days before.

Departure Ports for Your Wedding Charter

Puerto Banús is the most popular departure point for wedding charters because of its glitzy backdrop and easy access to the open sea. But you have other options. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and closer to the old town, which works if you want to walk from the hotel to the boat. Cabopino is a smaller, more relaxed marina near the Artola sand dunes, ideal for a bohemian-style wedding. Estepona offers a charming old town and a marina that's less crowded, while Sotogrande is upscale and private. Benalmádena is further east, near the marina with the Sealife centre, and it's a good choice if you're staying in Torremolinos or Fuengirola.

Each port has its own character, but the sea is the same Mediterranean. You can anchor at Cala del Faro for a ceremony with the cliffs behind you, or cruise along the coast to the Strait of Gibraltar where you'll likely spot dolphins. If you want a longer charter, you can head to the Nerja caves area, though that's a full-day trip from Puerto Banús.

Boat Options for Your Wedding Party

The boat you choose depends on the size of your guest list and the vibe you want. Motor yachts are the most common for weddings because they have a large aft deck for the ceremony and a spacious saloon for the reception. A 50-foot motor yacht like a Sunseeker or Azimut can comfortably host 20 to 30 guests for a seated dinner. Catamarans are wider and more stable, which is a plus if you have guests who get seasick. A 40-foot catamaran can take up to 40 guests, and the trampoline at the front is a great spot for photos.

Sailing yachts are less common for weddings because the mast and rigging can interfere with decorations, but they do offer a classic, romantic feel. RIBs and speedboats are too small for a ceremony, but you can use them for a small elopement with just the two of you and the skipper. Fishing boats are not ideal. Licence-free day boats are an option if you want to self-drive, but remember that every charter we arrange includes a skipper, so you don't have to worry about the boat handling.

Superyachts are available for hire, but they are price on request. Expect to pay upwards of EUR 10,000 for a half-day on a 80-foot plus vessel with a full crew, including a stewardess to serve drinks and a chef for the meal.

Pricing Guidance for a Wedding on a Boat in Puerto Banús

Prices vary depending on the boat size, duration, and season. For a half-day charter (4 hours) on a 40-foot motor yacht, you're looking at around EUR 2,500 to EUR 3,500. A full-day charter (8 hours) on a 50-foot catamaran will be around EUR 4,500 to EUR 6,500. Superyacht charters start from EUR 8,000 and go up to EUR 20,000 for a full day with all the extras.

Additional costs include catering (EUR 50 to EUR 100 per person for a buffet), drinks (EUR 20 to EUR 50 per person for an open bar), decorations (EUR 500 to EUR 2,000 depending on flowers and setup), and a photographer (EUR 500 to EUR 1,500 for the day). Some operators offer all-inclusive wedding packages that bundle the boat, catering, and decorations for a fixed price, usually from EUR 5,000 for 20 guests.

If you want to save money, consider a weekday charter. Monday to Thursday rates are often 20% to 30% lower than weekend rates. The low season (November to March) is also cheaper, though the weather is cooler and you might get rain.

Best Season for a Boat Wedding in Puerto Banús

The best months for a wedding on a boat in Puerto Banús are May, June, September, and October. The weather is warm (25 to 30 degrees C), the sea is calm, and the crowds are smaller than in July and August. July and August are hot (35 degrees C plus) and busy, but the evenings are still pleasant. If you want a sunset ceremony, aim for a start time around 7 PM, when the sun is low and the light is golden.

Winter months (November to February) are cooler (15 to 20 degrees C) and there is a higher chance of wind and rain. However, you can still have a ceremony on a boat if you book a vessel with a covered deck or a saloon. The advantage of winter is that you'll have the marina to yourselves and prices are lower.

How to Book a Private Boat for Your Wedding

Booking a private boat for your wedding in Puerto Banús is straightforward. You can BoatHire24 search our fleet of available vessels, filter by guest count and budget, and send an enquiry. We'll connect you with the boat owner or charter company, who will confirm availability and send a contract. A deposit of 30% to 50% is usually required to secure the date, with the balance due one week before the charter.

You should book at least three months in advance for a summer wedding, and two months for the rest of the year. Last-minute bookings are possible, but you'll have limited choice. If you're planning a large wedding with over 50 guests, you might need to book two boats or a superyacht, so start planning six months ahead.

Once you've booked, you can arrange a visit to the boat beforehand to plan the layout and decorations. Most operators are happy to accommodate a short inspection, especially if you're spending a significant amount.

Who a Wedding Boat Charter Is For

A private boat hire for a wedding in Puerto Banús is for couples who want something different from a traditional venue. It works for intimate elopements with just the two of you, the skipper, and a photographer. It works for small groups of up to 20 guests on a motor yacht, and for larger parties of up to 60 guests on a catamaran. It's also a good option if you're having a destination wedding and want to combine the ceremony with a sightseeing cruise of the coast.

It's not ideal if you have guests with severe mobility issues, because boats require stepping over gaps and navigating stairs. It's also not great if you want a formal sit-down dinner for 100 people, because the space is limited. But for a relaxed, elegant celebration with the sea as your witness, it's hard to beat.

For more ideas and tips, check out our blog on destination weddings in Marbella. And when you're ready to compare options, use our search feature to find the perfect boat for your big day.

Decorating Your Wedding Boat in Puerto Banús: What Works

You can transform a standard motor yacht into a wedding venue with the right decorations. Most operators allow you to bring your own setup, but check the rules on tape, hooks, and adhesives. Balloon arches work well on the aft deck, but avoid latex near the radar or navigation equipment. Florists in Marbella, like those on Avenida del Mar, can deliver arrangements directly to the marina. Expect to pay around EUR 300 for a simple bouquet and table centrepiece, or EUR 800 for a full arch of roses and greenery. If you want to scatter petals on the deck, use biodegradable ones to avoid fines from the port authority. Fairy lights are a popular choice for evening ceremonies, but you'll need a generator or a battery pack, because most boats only have 12V outlets. The skipper can help you string them along the canopy frame, but keep them away from the helm station.

Photography and Videography Tips for a Boat Wedding

The best photos from a Puerto Banús boat wedding are taken during the golden hour, roughly 7 PM to 8.30 PM in summer. Hire a photographer who knows how to shoot on a moving vessel, because the boat rocks slightly even in calm seas. A drone shot from above, showing the boat anchored at Cala del Faro with La Concha mountain behind, is worth the extra EUR 200. For the ceremony, position the couple on the starboard side so the sun lights their faces, not the photographer's lens. The saloon windows can cause glare, so close the curtains or shoot from the deck. Videographers need a stabiliser, because handheld footage on a boat looks shaky. Ask the skipper to keep the boat at anchor for the vows, and only cruise during the reception. A typical photography package for a half-day charter runs EUR 600 to EUR 1,200, depending on the number of edited images and albums.

Legal Steps for a Civil Wedding on a Boat in Spain

If you want a legally binding marriage on the boat, you need to jump through some hoops. Spanish law requires a civil ceremony to be performed by a judge, mayor, or designated official in a registered venue. A boat is not a registered venue, so you must have the ceremony on land, then celebrate on the water. The closest option is the Marbella Town Hall, which has a chapel for civil weddings. You can book a slot there, then charter the boat for the reception and a symbolic vow renewal. For foreign couples, you need to provide your birth certificates, passports, and a certificate of no impediment from your home country, all translated into Spanish by a sworn translator. Start the paperwork at least four months before your date. If that sounds like too much hassle, a symbolic ceremony on the boat is far simpler, and you can make it official at your home embassy later.

Weather Contingency Plans for Your Boat Wedding

The Costa del Sol is sunny most of the year, but you need a plan for wind or rain. July and August are the safest months, with less than 5% chance of rain. September can bring the occasional storm, and May has a 10% chance of a cloudy day. If the forecast shows strong winds (above 20 knots), the skipper may cancel the charter for safety. To avoid disappointment, book a boat with a covered aft deck or a large saloon. Catamarans are more stable in choppy seas, so they are a better choice for autumn weddings. Most operators offer a free reschedule if the weather is bad, but check the cancellation policy before you pay the deposit. You can also set a backup date three days after the original, so you have a window. If you are set on a specific date, consider a marina-based ceremony on the boat while it is docked, then cruise later when the weather improves.

Unique Boat Types for a Small Wedding or Elopement

If you are eloping with just the two of you, a RIB or speedboat is a fun, intimate option. A 30-foot RIB can fit you, the skipper, a photographer, and a small cake. You can zip to the Strait of Gibraltar, spot dolphins, and exchange vows with the African coast in the background. Prices for a half-day RIB charter start at around EUR 800. Licence-free day boats are another option, but remember you still get a skipper with every BoatHire24 booking, so you don't need a licence. For a classic feel, a 40-foot sailing yacht like a Bavaria or Jeanneau works well. The mast creates a natural arch for photos, and the gentle motion of the sail adds romance. Expect to pay around EUR 1,500 for a half-day sailing charter, including a skipper. These boats are less common for weddings, so you will have more availability, especially in May and October.

Catering and Drinks: What to Serve on a Boat

Catering on a boat requires food that stays fresh and doesn't slide off plates. Local Marbella caterers, such as those near the Río Verde market, can prepare a Spanish buffet with jamón ibérico, manchego cheese, prawns, and paella. For a formal dinner, a three-course meal with grilled fish or beef tenderloin works well. Expect to pay EUR 60 to EUR 90 per person for a buffet, and EUR 100 to EUR 150 for a plated dinner. Drinks are usually charged per bottle, not per person. A bottle of cava costs around EUR 15, Spanish wine EUR 20, and spirits EUR 40. Many operators allow you to bring your own alcohol, but they charge a corkage fee of EUR 5 to EUR 10 per bottle. The galley on most motor yachts has a fridge and a small stove, but the crew can't cook a full meal, so plan for cold dishes or pre-cooked food. If you want a barbecue on the aft deck, check if the boat has a grill and if the marina allows flames.

Music and Entertainment for Your Boat Wedding

Most charter boats have a Bluetooth sound system, but the speakers are designed for background music, not a party. If you want a DJ, you need a boat with a generator and enough power for professional speakers. Some superyachts have a built-in sound system with subwoofers. For a live musician, a guitarist or saxophonist can play on the aft deck without taking up too much space. Expect to pay around EUR 300 for a musician for two hours. If you want dancing, the saloon is usually the best spot, but move the furniture to the side. A catamaran's wide deck gives you more room for a dance floor, especially on the flybridge. Avoid fireworks, because they are banned in most marinas, and sparklers are risky near the fuel tanks. Instead, use LED candles or glow sticks for a safe, romantic glow.

Departure Ports Beyond Puerto Banús for Your Wedding

While Puerto Banús is the star, other ports offer unique advantages. Cabopino is a 15-minute drive from Marbella and has a small, quiet marina with a sandy beach. You can anchor near the Artola dunes for a ceremony with a natural, rustic backdrop. Estepona's marina is 20 minutes west and has a charming old town where guests can explore before boarding. Sotogrande is 30 minutes north and offers a private, exclusive feel, ideal for high-end weddings with fewer guests. Benalmádena is 40 minutes east and works if your guests are staying in Málaga or Torremolinos. Each port has its own vibe, but the sea is the same. If you want a longer charter, you can combine a wedding with a trip to the Nerja caves, but that adds 2 hours of cruising each way, so budget for a full day. The skipper can recommend the best anchorage based on wind and tide on the day.

Cost-Saving Tips for a Wedding Boat Charter

You can reduce the cost of a wedding boat charter by booking on a weekday, choosing a smaller boat, or skipping extras. A half-day charter on a 35-foot motor yacht for a Tuesday in May might cost EUR 1,800, compared to EUR 3,000 on a Saturday in August. Bring your own decorations and cake, and ask a friend to be the photographer. Skip the open bar and serve cava and wine only, which cuts drink costs by half. If you have fewer than 15 guests, consider a RIB or a small sailing yacht, which are cheaper than a motor yacht. Some operators offer a discount if you book two charters at once, for example, a wedding charter and a separate party cruise the next day. Always ask for a package deal, because many boat owners prefer a single booking over multiple small ones. And remember, the deposit is usually non-refundable, so only pay when you are sure of the date.

title: Catamaran Charter Marbella for Group – Social Sailing

h1: Catamaran Charter Marbella for Group, Social Sailing
intro:
You want a day on the water with your group, not a crowded beach bar with overpriced drinks. A catamaran charter Marbella for group social sailing gives you space, sun, and a proper party platform without the wobble of a monohull. These boats are wide, stable, and built for lounging. No seasickness, no cramped cockpit, just you, your friends, and the Costa del Sol coastline.

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, so you don't need a licence or any sailing experience. You just bring the snacks, the playlist, and the sunscreen. Departure ports range from Puerto Banús to Estepona, and the boats are motor catamarans or sailing catamarans depending on your vibe. Prices start from around EUR 800 for a half-day on a standard 40-foot cat, and go up to EUR 3,500 for a full-day on a luxury 60-footer with a flybridge and jacuzzi.
bodyHtml:
What a Catamaran Charter Marbella for Group Actually Includes

When you book a catamaran charter Marbella for group through BoatHire24, the package is straightforward. You get the boat for a set number of hours, a licensed skipper who handles navigation and mooring, and basic safety equipment. Fuel is usually included in the price, but check the listing because some operators charge extra for long distances. Most catamarans come with a Bluetooth sound system, a cooler or fridge, a bimini or hardtop for shade, and a bow trampoline for sunbathing. You do not get food and drink unless you pay for a catering upgrade, but you can bring your own. The skipper does not serve drinks or cook; that is your job.

The group capacity depends on the boat length. A 40-foot catamaran typically holds 10 to 12 passengers. A 50-footer can take up to 16. For larger groups, you might need two boats or a superyacht. The skipper stays on board and keeps things legal, so no overloading. If you want to swim, the skipper will anchor in a calm bay like Cala del Faro or off Cabopino. If you want to see dolphins, they will head toward the Strait of Gibraltar, but that requires a longer charter, usually 6 to 8 hours.

Departure Ports for Your Group Charter

Marbella has several marinas, and each gives you a different starting point for your catamaran charter Marbella for group. Puerto Banús is the obvious choice if you want glitz, gin palaces, and people-watching. The downside is that the marina is busy, and you might spend 20 minutes getting out of the harbour. Marbella Marina, also called Puerto Deportivo, is quieter and closer to the old town. From there, you can head east toward Cabopino or west toward Estepona. Cabopino itself has a small marina with a sandy beach and a nature reserve behind it. Estepona Marina is further west, near the old town with its flower-filled streets. Sotogrande is south, closer to Gibraltar, and Benalmádena is east, near Torremolinos. Each port has its own character, but the sailing conditions are similar: calm in the morning, a bit of chop in the afternoon when the wind picks up.

If you are staying in central Marbella, Puerto Banús is the most convenient. If you want a more relaxed vibe, start from Cabopino or Estepona. The skipper will advise on the best route based on the wind and your group's preferences. You can search all available catamarans from these ports on the BoatHire24 search page.

Boat Options: Motor Cat vs Sailing Cat

For a catamaran charter Marbella for group, you have two main types: motor catamarans and sailing catamarans. Motor cats are faster, quieter, and have more deck space because they lack the mast and rigging. They burn more fuel, but that is usually included in the price. Sailing cats are slower but more eco-friendly and give you that authentic sailing experience. They also have a lower centre of gravity, so they are even more stable than motor cats. For a party or social gathering, motor cats are better because you can spend more time at the swimming spots and less time tacking. For a relaxed cruise with lunch and a nap, sailing cats work fine.

Size matters. A 40-foot catamaran has two hulls, each with cabins below, but you will not use them unless you book an overnight charter. For a day charter, you care about the deck area. Look for boats with a large trampoline at the bow, a shaded cockpit aft, and a flybridge if you want a panoramic view. Some luxury catamarans have a jacuzzi on the flybridge, which sounds ridiculous but is actually popular for groups. The newer models from Lagoon, Fountaine Pajot, and Bali are common in Marbella. You can also find older Leopard cats, but they tend to have less shade.

Pricing Guidance for Group Charters

Prices for a catamaran charter Marbella for group vary by season, boat size, and duration. In low season, October to May, a half-day (4 hours) on a 40-foot cat starts at around EUR 800. A full day (8 hours) is EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,000. In high season, June to September, those prices jump by 30 to 50 percent. A 50-foot luxury cat with a flybridge and jacuzzi can cost EUR 3,500 for a full day in August. You also need to budget for extras: food catering from EUR 30 per person, drinks packages from EUR 20 per person, and fuel surcharges if you go beyond the standard cruising area. Some operators charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50 to EUR 100 if you leave a mess. Always confirm what is included before you book.

For groups of 10 to 16 people, the per-person cost works out cheaper than a night out in Puerto Banús. Split EUR 1,500 among 12 people, and you are paying EUR 125 each for a private boat with a skipper, unlimited swimming, and a view of La Concha mountain. That is good value for a memorable day.

Best Seasons for Social Sailing

The Mediterranean season runs from April to October. The best months for a catamaran charter Marbella for group are May, June, September, and early October. The weather is warm but not scorching, the water temperature is pleasant for swimming, and the marinas are less crowded. July and August are peak season: air temperatures hit 35 degrees C, the sea is like bathwater, and Puerto Banús is a zoo. If you book in August, expect to pay top prices and fight for a berth at lunch spots. The wind in summer is usually a light thermal breeze, 10 to 15 knots, which is perfect for sailing cats. In spring and autumn, you might get a stronger Levante wind from the east, which can make the sea choppy. Skippers are experienced and will adjust the route accordingly.

Winter charters are possible but less popular. From November to March, the temperature drops to 15-20 degrees C, and the water is cold. You can still sail, but you will not swim. The advantage is low prices and empty marinas. Some operators offer reduced rates for winter charters, but availability is limited.

How to Book Your Catamaran Charter Marbella for Group

Booking through BoatHire24 is simple. You browse the listings, filter by boat type, capacity, and port, then send an enquiry or book directly if the calendar is live. You pay a deposit, usually 50 percent, and the balance is due on the day. Cancellation policies vary, but most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days before. For last-minute bookings, you can sometimes negotiate a discount if the boat is empty, but that is risky in high season.

When you book, you need to provide the exact number of guests, any dietary requirements for catering, and a preferred departure time. Most charters start at 10:00 or 11:00. Half-day charters run until 14:00 or 15:00. Full-day charters go until 18:00 or 19:00. Sunset charters are also available, usually 16:00 to 20:00, and are popular for groups who want to see the sun go down behind La Concha. The skipper will meet you at the marina, give a safety briefing, and then you are off.

Who Is This Charter For?

A catamaran charter Marbella for group is ideal for birthday parties, bachelor or bachelorette groups, family reunions, corporate team-building, or just a group of friends who want to escape the hotel pool. It is not suitable for people who get seasick easily, but catamarans are the most stable option, so even sensitive stomachs usually cope. It is also not for groups who want to go fast or waterski, because catamarans are slow, displacement hulls. If you want speed, book a RIB or a speedboat instead. For a relaxed social day with swimming, sunbathing, and maybe a bit of sailing, a catamaran is the best choice.

If your group is larger than 16 people, you might need to charter two catamarans or look at a superyacht. Some operators offer catamaran flotillas, where two or three boats sail together, which can be fun for big events. You can also combine a catamaran charter with a visit to the Nerja caves, but that is a long day, about 10 hours, and requires an early start from Marbella.

Local Highlights and Itinerary Ideas

From Puerto Banús, a typical route for a catamaran charter Marbella for group goes east toward Cabopino or west toward Estepona. Heading east, you pass the sand dunes of Artola and the Cala del Faro, a quiet cove with clear water. The skipper will anchor there for swimming. Then you can cruise to Cabopino beach for lunch at a chiringuito, though you need to dinghy ashore. Heading west, you pass the Marbella coastline, the Río Verde estuary, and then the old town of Estepona. The water is deeper on this side, and you might see dolphins. If you have a full day, you can go all the way to the Strait of Gibraltar, but that is a 2-hour cruise each way. The dolphins are almost guaranteed there, but the sea can be rougher.

For a shorter trip, stay close to Puerto Banús and anchor off the beach near the Marina Banús. You get the view of the superyachts and the mountains. If you want to impress your group, book a catamaran with a flybridge and watch the sunset with a glass of cava. The light on La Concha mountain turns pink, and the whole scene is very Instagrammable. Just remember that the skipper is not your photographer, so bring your own camera.

For more ideas on itineraries and boat types, check the BoatHire24 blog for local guides and tips.

What to Bring and What to Expect

Bring swimwear, towels, sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the wind. The boat will have a cooler, but bring your own drinks and ice if the operator does not supply them. Food is your responsibility unless you order catering. Some operators have a fridge, but it is small. If you bring glass bottles, the skipper might ask you to use plastic cups because broken glass on deck is a hazard. Bluetooth speakers are allowed, but keep the volume reasonable so you do not annoy other boats. The skipper has the right to cut the charter short if the group is dangerously drunk or abusive. So keep it civil.

The skipper speaks English and Spanish, sometimes French or German. They will give a safety briefing and show you where the life jackets are. They will not join your party; they stay in the helm area and focus on navigation. If you want a crewed charter with a host or hostess, you can book that as an add-on, but it costs extra. For most groups, the skipper alone is enough.

Why Book Through BoatHire24

BoatHire24 aggregates catamarans from multiple operators in Marbella and the Costa del Sol. You can compare prices, boat specs, and availability in one place. The platform vets the operators for licences and insurance, so you are not booking a dodgy boat that breaks down. The search filters let you narrow down by port, capacity, and price range. You can read the boat descriptions and see photos. There are no fake reviews, just the facts. If you have questions, you can contact the operator directly through the platform. The booking process is secure, and you get a confirmation with the skipper's contact details.

For a catamaran charter Marbella for group, this is the most efficient way to find a boat that fits your group size and budget. You are not wasting time calling ten different companies. You search once, compare, and book.

keyword: luxury yacht charter Marbella day price
intro: You want to charter a luxury yacht in Marbella for a day without the sales pitch. You want a straight answer on what it costs, what you get, and where to find the best deal. A luxury yacht charter in Marbella for a day typically starts from around EUR 1,500 for a 12-metre motor yacht and can go up to EUR 10,000 or more for a 20-metre-plus superyacht. bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day Price

When you see a luxury yacht charter Marbella day price, it usually covers the boat hire for up to eight hours, a licensed skipper, fuel for a set cruising range (typically 30-50 nautical miles), and basic safety equipment. Some packages include soft drinks, water, ice, and a basic sound system. You might also get a welcome bottle of cava or wine. What is not included: food (unless you order a catering upgrade), extra fuel beyond the agreed limit, dockage fees at places like Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina, and gratuities for the crew. Always check the fine print on fuel caps, some operators charge extra if you burn more than 100 litres, which is common if you push the throttles. Search our listings to see what each boat includes.

Ports of Departure for Your Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Your luxury yacht charter Marbella day price will vary depending on which port you leave from. The most popular departure point is Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina lined with superyachts and designer boutiques. From there you can cruise east toward Marbella's Golden Mile or west toward the dunes of Cabopino. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a cheaper alternative with easier parking. Cabopino offers a quieter start with fewer crowds. Estepona port gives you quick access to the Strait of Gibraltar and dolphin watching. Sotogrande is further west, ideal for a longer day trip. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, closer to Málaga airport. Each port affects the price because of different berthing fees and fuel distances. A charter from Puerto Banús will generally cost 10-15 percent more than one from Estepona or Cabopino due to the premium location.

Boat Types and Their Typical Day Prices

The luxury yacht charter Marbella day price depends heavily on the type of boat. Motor yachts from 12 to 15 metres (40-50 feet) start around EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500 per day. Catamarans of similar length (13-15 metres) are slightly cheaper, from EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,000, because they are more fuel-efficient. Sailing yachts over 14 metres can be EUR 1,000 to EUR 1,800, but they are slower and less suited for a tight day schedule. RIBs and speedboats (8-10 metres) are cheaper at EUR 600 to EUR 1,200 but are not luxury, they are fast and fun, not comfortable lounging. Fishing boats with a skipper cost EUR 800 to EUR 1,500. Licence-free day boats (under 6 metres, no licence needed) are EUR 300 to EUR 600, but these are basic dinghies, not luxury. For true luxury, superyachts over 20 metres (65 feet) start at EUR 5,000 and go up to EUR 15,000 or more per day, depending on the season and extras like jet skis or a chef.

Pricing Guidance: What You Actually Pay

Let's break down a realistic luxury yacht charter Marbella day price. For a 14-metre Sunseeker motor yacht in June, expect to pay around EUR 2,500 for a full day (10:00 to 18:00). That includes the skipper, fuel for 40 nautical miles, a cooler with ice, and basic Bluetooth speakers. If you want a full catering package with paella, salads, and drinks, add EUR 40 per person. A 16-metre Azimut with a crew of two (skipper plus stewardess) costs about EUR 3,800. Superyacht charters are price on request, but expect EUR 8,000 to EUR 12,000 for a 24-metre boat with a crew of four. Discounts are rare in high season (July-August), but you might negotiate a 10 percent reduction for a last-minute booking or a weekday charter. Low season (October to May) can slash prices by 20-30 percent. Always ask about the fuel policy, some operators include unlimited fuel, others charge EUR 2 per litre after the first 100 litres.

Seasons and Their Impact on Price

The luxury yacht charter Marbella day price fluctuates wildly with the season. High season runs from mid-June to mid-September, when demand peaks. July and August are the most expensive, with prices 30-50 percent higher than May or October. Shoulder season (April-May and September-October) offers the best value: good weather (22-28 degrees C), fewer crowds, and lower rates. Winter (November-March) is cheaper but riskier due to wind and rain, many boats are laid up. If you want to save, book a weekday in May or September. A 15-metre motor yacht that costs EUR 2,500 in August might be EUR 1,800 in May. Also, the time of day matters: a half-day charter (four hours) is typically 60 percent of the full-day price, but you lose the afternoon sun and the chance to anchor for lunch.

How to Book Your Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day

Booking a luxury yacht charter Marbella day price is straightforward on BoatHire24. Use the search filters to set your date, group size, and budget. You will see a list of available boats with prices, photos, and skipper profiles. Read the inclusions carefully, some boats list extras like water toys or a DJ setup. Contact the operator directly through the platform to ask about availability and negotiate if you want to customise the menu or route. Most operators require a 30-50 percent deposit to secure the booking, with the balance due on the day. Cancellation policies vary: many offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days ahead, but last-minute cancellations (within 48 hours) often forfeit the deposit. For a stress-free experience, book at least two weeks in advance for high season. Our blog has tips on what to expect during your charter.

Who Is a Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day For

A luxury yacht charter Marbella day is not for everyone. It suits groups of 6 to 12 people who want a private, high-end experience. It is ideal for birthdays, anniversaries, bachelor or bachelorette parties, corporate events, or simply a day of indulgence with friends. Families with children are welcome, but check that the boat has child safety features like railings and a shaded area. Couples looking for romance might prefer a smaller sailing yacht or a catamaran with a private cabin. If you are a solo traveller, a shared charter (joining a group) is cheaper, but you lose the exclusivity. Avoid luxury charters if you are on a tight budget, the entry price is high, and you will feel pressured to add extras. For a more affordable day on the water, consider a licence-free day boat or a group RIB tour.

Local Highlights You Can Expect on Your Charter

Your luxury yacht charter Marbella day price includes more than just the boat, it gives you access to the best of the Costa del Sol. From Puerto Banús, you can cruise past the mansions of the Golden Mile, see the backdrop of La Concha mountain, and anchor at Cala del Faro for a swim. Head west toward Estepona to see the old town's whitewashed streets from the water. Further west, the Strait of Gibraltar offers dolphin and whale sightings (common from April to October). Eastward, you can reach Benalmádena and, with a longer day, the Nerja caves (though that requires a full day and extra fuel). The skipper knows the best spots for lunch, many will recommend a beach club like Nikki Beach or a cala for a private picnic. You can also arrange a stop at the Río Verde for a shallow swim.

Common Questions About Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day Price

Many people ask if the luxury yacht charter Marbella day price includes alcohol. Usually no, but you can bring your own or order a drinks package (EUR 20-50 per person). Another question: can you negotiate the price? Yes, especially for last-minute bookings or weekdays in shoulder season. Operators would rather have a booking at a lower rate than no booking. What about the skipper's tip? Standard is 10-15 percent of the charter fee, but it is discretionary. Do you need a visa? If you are a non-EU citizen, check Spain's visa rules, the charter itself does not require one, but entry to Spain does. Finally, what happens if the weather is bad? Most operators will reschedule or refund if the forecast shows unsafe conditions (winds over 25 knots or thunderstorms). Check the cancellation policy before you pay.

Comparing Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day Price to Other Options

You might wonder how the luxury yacht charter Marbella day price compares to other water activities. A private RIB tour for 8 people costs around EUR 800 for two hours, but you get no luxury, no comfort, and no catering. A shared catamaran cruise is EUR 60-100 per person, but you share with strangers and follow a fixed route. A luxury yacht charter gives you privacy, customisation, and a higher standard of service. For a group of 8, a EUR 2,500 charter works out to EUR 312 per person, competitive with a high-end restaurant dinner. If you want the full experience without the cost, consider a half-day charter (EUR 1,500 for 4 hours) or a sunset cruise (EUR 1,200 for 3 hours). These are cheaper but still offer the same boat and crew.

Tips to Get the Best Value for Your Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day Price

To maximise your luxury yacht charter Marbella day price, follow these tips. Book early for high season, prices rise as availability drops. Choose a weekday (Tuesday to Thursday) for lower rates and less traffic on the water. Bring your own food and drinks to avoid catering markups (check with the operator first). Negotiate the fuel cap, ask for unlimited fuel or a higher allowance if you plan to cruise far. Split the cost among your group, the more people, the lower the per-person cost. Avoid unnecessary extras like a DJ or water toys unless you really want them. And always confirm the departure port, a charter from Puerto Banús costs more but offers better photo opportunities and proximity to nightlife.

Comparing Day Prices Across Different Marbella Ports

The luxury yacht charter Marbella day price shifts noticeably depending on your departure port. Puerto Banús commands a premium because of its glamour and convenience, expect to pay roughly EUR 2,800 for a 14-metre motor yacht in July. Marbella Marina is typically EUR 200-300 cheaper for the same boat because berthing fees are lower. Cabopino offers even better value, around EUR 2,200 for a comparable vessel, but you sacrifice proximity to Marbella's nightlife. Estepona port gives you a EUR 2,000 option for a 14-metre boat, with the bonus of quicker access to dolphin-rich waters. Sotogrande starts at EUR 2,500 due to its exclusive residential setting. Benalmádena is the cheapest luxury departure, around EUR 1,800 for a 12-metre motor yacht, but you spend extra fuel cruising to the best anchorages near Marbella. Factor in the fuel cost difference, a round trip from Benalmádena to Puerto Banús burns about 60 litres, adding roughly EUR 120 at current diesel prices.

Fuel Costs and How They Affect Your Total Day Price

Fuel is a hidden variable in your luxury yacht charter Marbella day price. Most operators include a fuel allowance of 100-150 litres for a full day. A 14-metre motor yacht burns about 40-60 litres per hour at cruising speed (20-25 knots). If you push to 30 knots, consumption jumps to 80 litres per hour. For a typical day covering 40 nautical miles, you will use around 120 litres, which may exceed the allowance. Extra fuel costs EUR 1.80 to EUR 2.50 per litre, so a 20-litre overage adds EUR 40-50. Catamarans are more efficient, burning 20-30 litres per hour, so they rarely exceed the allowance. Sailing yachts use minimal fuel under sail, but you pay for engine hours when manoeuvring in port. Ask the operator for a fuel policy in writing before booking. Some premium charters include unlimited fuel, which is worth seeking out if you plan a long cruise to Nerja or the Strait of Gibraltar.

Hidden Extras That Can Inflate Your Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day Price

Beyond the base luxury yacht charter Marbella day price, several extras can add 20-40 percent to your total. Catering packages range from EUR 30 per person for a basic platter to EUR 80 per person for a full gourmet menu with paella, grilled seafood, and premium wines. Water toys like a jet ski (EUR 200-300 per hour), a seabob (EUR 150 per hour), or a paddleboard (EUR 50 per hour) are separate costs. A DJ or premium sound system adds EUR 300-500. Dockage fees at beach clubs like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club cost EUR 50-150 for a mooring buoy. Gratuities for the skipper and crew are not included, standard is 10-15 percent of the charter fee. If you want a photographer or videographer, budget EUR 400-800 for a few hours. Always ask for a full price breakdown before paying the deposit to avoid surprises.

Best Times of Year for a Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day at Lower Prices

If you want a luxury yacht charter Marbella day price that is 30-40 percent below peak rates, target May or September. In May, the sea temperature is around 18-20 degrees C, air temperature 22-25 degrees C, and the water is calm. You can swim, but a wetsuit helps. September offers warmer sea temperatures (22-24 degrees C) and still reliable sunshine. Prices for a 14-metre motor yacht drop to around EUR 1,800 from the EUR 2,500 peak. October is even cheaper, EUR 1,500, but the risk of wind and rain increases. Easter week and the week after Christmas see moderate demand, with prices around EUR 2,000. Avoid August if you can, that is when prices hit the ceiling and the marinas are overcrowded. Weekday bookings in any month reduce the price by 10-15 percent because operators struggle to fill Monday-Thursday slots.

How Group Size Affects Your Luxury Yacht Charter Marbella Day Price

The luxury yacht charter Marbella day price is fixed per boat, so the per-person cost drops as your group grows. A 14-metre motor yacht typically sleeps 8-10 guests for day trips, but the maximum capacity for cruising is usually 12. For a EUR 2,500 charter, 8 people pay EUR 312 each, while 12 people pay EUR 208 each. That is competitive with a night out in Puerto Banús. Larger groups (12-16 people) need a bigger boat, a 17-metre motor yacht costs EUR 3,500-4,500, so the per-person cost stays similar. For small groups of 2-4, a luxury charter feels expensive, EUR 625-1,250 per person. Consider a shared charter or a smaller RIB tour instead. Couples might prefer a 12-metre sailing yacht at EUR 1,200, which works out to EUR 600 each, more reasonable for a private experience.

title: Charter a Motor Yacht in Marbella for a Day – 2025
metaDescription: Charter a motor yacht in Marbella for a day in 2025. Compare prices, ports, and boats with a licensed skipper. Book your luxury day out on the Costa del Sol.
h1: Charter a Motor Yacht in Marbella for a Day, 2025 Guide
intro:
If you want to charter a motor yacht in Marbella for a day, the short answer is yes, you can, and it costs from around EUR 1,200 to EUR 5,000 depending on the size, season, and extras. You get a licensed skipper, fuel, and a crew that knows where to drop anchor for the clearest water. No hidden fees, no surprise charges. This page tells you exactly what to expect, which ports to use, and how to book without the usual holiday faff.

Marbella and the Costa del Sol have a ridiculous concentration of luxury. Puerto Banús alone has more superyachts than most Mediterranean capitals. But you don't need a superyacht budget. A 12-metre motor yacht for a day is the sweet spot: fast enough to reach the best coves, comfortable enough for six to eight people, and easy to charter with a skipper who handles all the paperwork. You just turn up with drinks and sunscreen.

We run BoatHire24, a marketplace that lists real boats from local owners and charter companies. Every listing includes a skipper, insurance, and a clear price. No bait-and-switch. No endless email chains. You pick the boat, pick the date, and pay online. This guide covers the boats, ports, costs, seasons, and what to do with your day. If you want to skip the reading, go straight to our search page and filter by motor yacht, date, and number of guests.
bodyHtml:
What You Get When You Charter a Motor Yacht in Marbella for a Day

A standard day charter runs from 10:00 to 18:00, though you can often extend to sunset for an extra fee. The boat comes with a professional skipper who holds a Spanish navigation licence. Some boats also include a steward or deckhand, especially the larger yachts over 15 metres. Fuel is included in the price for a typical day itinerary within 20 nautical miles of the port. If you want to go further, say to Gibraltar or the Nerja caves, the skipper will quote extra fuel costs.

You also get use of the onboard amenities: sun pads, a bimini or hardtop for shade, a sound system, a galley with fridge and ice maker, and a bathroom (usually one, sometimes two, on larger yachts). Snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and inflatable toys are often available on request, sometimes included, sometimes for an extra EUR 50, 100. Some boats have a barbecue setup on the aft deck. And all charter agreements include liability insurance and basic cancellation terms.

What you do not get: a captain who also serves as a bartender. The skipper drives the boat and keeps everyone safe. If you want a crew member dedicated to drinks and food, you pay for a steward or host separately. Also, the boat is yours for the day, but the skipper has the final say on where to go based on weather and sea conditions. That is not a sales trick. It is a legal requirement under Spanish maritime law.

Which Port to Use for Your Motor Yacht Charter

The Costa del Sol has six main departure ports for day charters. Your choice depends on where you are staying and what coastline you want to explore. Puerto Banús is the most famous, with the highest concentration of motor yachts from 10 to 30 metres. Leaving from Banús gives you quick access to the western coves: Cala del Faro, Cala de las Tortugas, and the beaches of San Pedro Alcántara. It is also the most expensive port for parking, so charter prices here are slightly higher than from Marbella Marina.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a few kilometres east of Banús, closer to the town centre. It has a good selection of motor yachts, often at lower rates. From here you can head west to the same coves or east towards Cabopino and Calahonda. The marina itself has cafes and a small beach. Cabopino is a smaller, quieter port near the Artola dunes. It is a good choice if you want a more relaxed start and direct access to the Cabopino beach and the nudist coves nearby.

Estepona port is further west, about 15 minutes from Puerto Banús by road. It is a modern marina with good facilities and slightly cheaper charter rates. The coastline west of Estepona is less developed, with wilder coves and fewer boats. Sotogrande is the southernmost option, close to Gibraltar. It is a luxury residential port with a polo crowd. Chartering from here lets you explore the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can see dolphins and sometimes whales. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near Torremolinos. It is a large marina with many charter operators, often at competitive prices. The coastline eastwards is more built-up, but you can reach the Mijas coast and the La Cala de Mijas area.

For a day charter, the typical cruising radius is about 15 to 25 nautical miles. From Puerto Banús, you can reach Estepona in 30 minutes, Gibraltar in 90 minutes, and the Nerja caves in about two hours at 25 knots. Most skippers will plan a route that includes two or three anchor stops, a lunch spot, and a scenic cruise along the coast.

Motor Yacht Options: Sizes, Speeds, and Layouts

Motor yachts on the Costa del Sol range from 8-metre day boats to 30-metre luxury vessels. For a day charter with a group of four to eight people, the most common sizes are 10 to 15 metres. A 10-metre motor yacht typically sleeps two in a cabin but has a large cockpit and sun deck. It cruises at 20, 25 knots and has a range of about 150 nautical miles. Examples include the Jeanneau Leader 8 or the Sunseeker Portofino. These boats are nimble, easy to board, and have a shallow draft for anchoring close to shore.

From 12 to 15 metres, you get more space, a proper galley, a larger bathroom, and often a second cabin. Boats like the Azimut 43 or the Princess 50 are popular. They cruise at 22, 28 knots and can handle a bit of chop. The layout usually has a bow sun pad, a large cockpit with a table and L-shaped seating, and a flybridge on some models. The flybridge is a big plus for sunny days: it gives you a second steering position and a sun deck with a better view.

For groups of ten or more, you need a yacht over 18 metres. These are the semi-displacement or planing hulls that can carry more weight without losing speed. A 20-metre motor yacht like the Ferretti 620 or the Sunseeker Manhattan 60 has three or four cabins, a full kitchen, and a crew cabin. The flybridge is huge, often with a wet bar and grill. These yachts cost more to charter, from EUR 3,500 to EUR 6,000 per day, but the per-person cost can be lower for a large group.

If you want speed, look for a RIB or a sports cruiser. A 9-metre RIB with twin 300hp outboards can hit 40 knots and is perfect for a thrill ride to the Strait of Gibraltar. But the ride is bumpy, and there is no shade. For a relaxing day with lunch and drinks, a proper motor yacht with a flybridge is the better choice.

Pricing Guidance: What You Pay and Why

Charter prices for a motor yacht in Marbella for a day vary by size, age, and season. In low season (November to March), a 10-metre motor yacht costs from around EUR 1,200 for a day. In high season (July and August), the same boat is EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,200. A 15-metre yacht in high season runs EUR 2,500 to EUR 3,500. For a 20-metre-plus superyacht, you are looking at EUR 4,500 to EUR 8,000 per day. These prices include the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and VAT. They do not include food, drinks, or port fees for overnight stays.

Extras to budget for: a paddleboard or kayak costs EUR 50, 100 per item. A host or steward costs EUR 150, 250 for the day. Catering from a local deli or restaurant runs EUR 30, 50 per person. Some boats have a minimum spend on food and drink if you use their catering partner. Always ask what is included in the base price and what is optional. We list all inclusions and exclusions on each boat page on BoatHire24.

You pay a deposit of 30% to 50% at booking, with the balance due two weeks before departure. Cancellation policies vary: most operators offer a 50% refund up to 30 days before, and no refund within 14 days unless the weather is bad. Bad weather cancellation is free and full refund, because the skipper makes the call.

Best Time of Year for a Motor Yacht Day Charter

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with 320 sunny days a year. The sea temperature is 16, 18°C in April and rises to 24, 26°C in August. The best months for a day charter are May, June, September, and October. The weather is warm but not scorching, the sea is calm, and the anchorages are less crowded. July and August are hot (32, 36°C) and busy. You will see more boats at every cove, but the atmosphere is lively and the water is perfect for swimming.

Winter charters (November to February) are possible but less popular. The air temperature is 15, 20°C, and the sea is 14, 16°C. You can still go out in a motor yacht with a heated cabin, but swimming is cold. Some operators run winter charters at half price. If you want a quiet day with a hot drink and a view of the coast, it is a good deal. Just check the weather forecast for wind, especially the Poniente and Levante winds that can make the sea uncomfortable.

Sample Itinerary for a Day on the Water

A typical day charter from Puerto Banús goes like this. You meet the skipper at 10:00 at the charter office in the port. He walks you to the boat, gives a safety briefing, and shows you the layout. By 10:15, you cast off and head west towards Estepona. The first stop is Cala del Faro, a rocky cove with clear water and a small lighthouse. The skipper anchors, and you have an hour to swim, snorkel, or paddleboard. The water is 3, 8 metres deep, calm, and usually clean.

At 12:30, you cruise further west to the Estepona coast, past the marina and the old town. The skipper finds a second spot near the beach of El Cristo or the Punta de la Doncella. You have lunch on board: either bring your own or order from a local catering service that delivers to the boat. Many boats have a fridge, ice maker, and a barbecue. After lunch, you cruise slowly back east, passing the coast of San Pedro and the Marbella skyline. You stop for a final swim near the Cabopino dunes at around 16:00. Then you return to port by 17:30, with time to clean up and have a drink on the terrace before the 18:00 return.

If you leave from Estepona or Sotogrande, the itinerary can include a trip to the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins. The common dolphin and striped dolphin are resident year-round. In summer, you also see pilot whales and sometimes fin whales. The skipper knows the best spots. The journey from Sotogrande to the strait is 20 minutes at 25 knots.

Who Should Charter a Motor Yacht for a Day

This is for anyone who wants a private, flexible day on the water without the hassle of owning a boat. It works for families with children (the skipper can adapt the pace), groups of friends celebrating a birthday or stag do, couples wanting a romantic day, or corporate clients entertaining clients. The boat is your floating base: you decide the music, the food, the stops, and the pace. There is no set schedule, no other guests, no waiting for a tour bus.

It is not for people who get seasick easily, though modern motor yachts with stabilisers are much more comfortable than smaller boats. It is also not for people who want to drive the boat themselves. Spanish law requires a licence for any motor boat over 5 metres, and the charter includes a skipper. You can ask the skipper to let you take the helm for a photo, but he stays in control.

If you are a solo traveller or a couple on a tight budget, a shared charter on a catamaran might be cheaper. But for a private day with your own group, a motor yacht is the standard choice. We have a blog post on the differences between motor yachts and catamarans if you want to compare.

How to Book Your Motor Yacht Day Charter

Booking through BoatHire24 takes five minutes. You go to our search page, select the date, number of guests, and boat type (motor yacht). You see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on a boat to see the full description, inclusions, and cancellation policy. You can send a message to the owner to ask questions. When you are ready, you book online and pay the deposit by card or bank transfer. The owner confirms within 24 hours. On the day, you meet at the port, sign a waiver, and go.

We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance for high season, four weeks for the most popular boats. Last-minute bookings are possible but the selection is smaller. If you need help choosing, contact us via the website. We know the boats and the skippers personally and can match you to the right one.

bodyHtml:
What You Get with Private Catamaran Hire Puerto Banus for Birthday

When you book a private catamaran through BoatHire24, you get the whole boat for your group. No sharing with strangers. The skipper is included in the price, so you don't need a licence or any experience. The boat comes with safety equipment, a sound system (usually Bluetooth), and a basic kitchen area (galley) with a fridge. Some catamarans have a grill on the back deck, useful if you want to cook fresh fish or just burn some sausages.

Typical catamarans available for birthday hire in Puerto Banus range from 35 to 50 feet. A 40-foot catamaran can comfortably hold 12 to 15 people. Larger ones, 50 feet and above, can take up to 20 or even 25. The price depends on the size, the season, and the duration. Expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day (4 hours) on a mid-sized catamaran in low season, up to EUR 3,500 for a full day (8 hours) on a larger boat in July or August. Fuel is usually extra, but the skipper will give you an estimate before you leave.

You can bring your own food and drink. Most skippers are fine with that, as long as you don't break the furniture. Some companies offer catering options, like a paella lunch or a barbecue, but that costs more. Check with the boat owner before you book.

Why Puerto Banus for a Birthday Catamaran Party

Puerto Banus is the epicentre of Marbella's luxury scene. The marina is full of designer shops, expensive cars, and people who look like they just stepped out of a magazine. But once you leave the dock, the noise fades and you get the real Costa del Sol coastline. The water is clear, the mountains are in the background, and the sun is almost always out.

For a birthday, Puerto Banus offers a few advantages. First, it is easy to get to. The marina is 10 minutes from Marbella town and 45 minutes from Malaga airport. Second, the departure is smooth. The harbour master is efficient, and the channel is deep enough for catamarans. Third, the anchorages near Puerto Banus are good. You can stop at Cala del Faro, a small cove with a beach club, or head towards Cabopino for a quieter spot.

If you want to make a weekend of it, you can start the party on the boat, then head back to the marina for dinner at one of the portside restaurants. The birthday person gets to be the captain for a day, even if they don't know a bow from a stern.

Available Catamarans for Birthday Hire in Puerto Banus

On BoatHire24, you can filter by boat type, so select catamarans and Puerto Banus as the departure port. The fleet includes Lagoon, Fountaine Pajot, and Bali models, among others. Most are between 38 and 50 feet, with 4 to 6 cabins. For a birthday party, you probably don't need all the cabins, but they are useful for changing clothes or storing bags.

Some catamarans have a trampoline net at the front, which is a popular spot for lounging. Others have a flybridge with a second steering station and more seating. The interior is usually open-plan, with a salon that connects to the cockpit. This layout works well for parties because guests can move between inside and outside without stepping over each other.

If you have a large group, consider a catamaran with a generator and air conditioning. Not essential, but nice when the temperature hits 35 degrees C in August. Also check if the boat has a water slide or a paddleboard. Some owners offer these as extras.

Pricing Guidance for Private Catamaran Hire Puerto Banus Birthday

Pricing for private catamaran hire in Puerto Banus varies. There is no fixed price because each boat is owned by a different person. However, you can expect the following ranges based on typical listings:

  • Half-day (4 hours) low season (October to May): from around EUR 1,200 for a 38-foot catamaran.
  • Half-day high season (June to September): from around EUR 1,800 for the same boat.
  • Full day (8 hours) low season: from around EUR 2,000 for a 40-foot catamaran.
  • Full day high season: from around EUR 3,000 for a 40-foot catamaran.
  • Larger catamarans (50 feet) full day high season: from around EUR 4,500 to EUR 6,000.
  • Charter a Motor Yacht in Marbella for a Day, 2025 Guide

These prices usually include the skipper, fuel for a typical route (up to 30 nautical miles), and basic insurance. Extras like food, drinks, and water toys cost extra. Some boats charge a cleaning fee if you make a mess. Confirm what is included before you pay.

Best Time of Year for a Birthday Catamaran Party in Puerto Banus

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate, which means hot summers and mild winters. For a birthday party on a catamaran, the best months are May through October. In May and June, the weather is warm (25-30 degrees C) and the sea is calm. July and August are peak season, with temperatures often above 35 degrees C and the water at 24-26 degrees C. September and October are still pleasant, with fewer crowds and lower prices.

If you book in winter (November to March), the weather is cooler (15-20 degrees C) and the sea can be choppy. Some catamarans are still available for hire, but you will need to wrap up warm. The advantage is that prices are lower and the marinas are quiet. Not ideal for a swim party, but fine for a cruise with a hot drink.

Wind is a factor. The Levante wind (from the east) can pick up in the afternoon, especially in summer. Catamarans handle wind well because they are stable, but the skipper may adjust the route to avoid the worst of it. Trust the skipper on this.

How to Book a Private Catamaran for a Birthday in Puerto Banus

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter Puerto Banus as the port, select catamaran as the boat type, and choose your date. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specifications, and prices. Each listing includes the owner's contact details or a booking button.

You can send an enquiry to the owner directly. Tell them it is a birthday party, how many guests you have, and what you want to do (swim, eat, drink, anchor somewhere specific). The owner will confirm availability and send you a quote. Payment is usually by bank transfer or credit card. Some owners require a deposit (50% is common) and the balance on the day.

Read the cancellation policy before you book. Most owners offer a full refund if you cancel more than 14 days before the date. Closer to the date, you may lose your deposit. Check the weather forecast a few days before. If the weather is bad, the skipper may cancel for safety reasons, and you should get a full refund.

Who Is Private Catamaran Hire in Puerto Banus For

Private catamaran hire for a birthday is suitable for groups of friends, family celebrations, or even a corporate birthday (if your boss is cool). It works for adults and children, as long as the kids are supervised. Catamarans are safer than motor yachts for children because they have higher railings and less heeling.

If you are planning a surprise birthday, the skipper can help. You can arrange for decorations, a cake, or even a musician. Just communicate with the owner in advance. Some owners offer a birthday package with balloons, banners, and a bottle of cava. It costs extra, but it saves you the hassle.

For large groups (over 20 people), consider a larger catamaran or a superyacht. Catamarans above 50 feet can usually take 25 guests. If you have more than that, you might need two boats or a different vessel. Check the maximum capacity on the boat listing.

What to Bring on a Birthday Catamaran Trip

Bring swimwear, towels, sunscreen (factor 50), sunglasses, and a hat. The sun is strong even in spring and autumn. Bring a light jacket or a windbreaker for the evening. The temperature drops when the boat is moving.

For food, bring easy-to-eat things: sandwiches, salads, fruit, chips. Avoid heavy sauces or things that stain. Drinks: bring water, soft drinks, beer, wine, and champagne. No glass bottles on some boats, so check. You can bring a cake, but make sure it is stored in the galley fridge. The skipper will have a cooler for drinks.

Music: most catamarans have a Bluetooth speaker or a sound system. Make a playlist beforehand. The skipper will not want to hear your argument about what song to play. Also bring a camera or a phone for photos. The backdrop of the coast and the mountains is worth capturing.

Alternative Options for a Birthday on the Water

If a catamaran is not your style, consider a motor yacht for a faster, more glamorous feel. Or a sailing yacht if you want a more traditional experience. For a small group, a RIB speedboat is fun but less spacious. For a big party, a superyacht is the ultimate luxury. Check our blog for more ideas on birthday boat parties in Marbella.

Other departure ports near Puerto Banus include Marbella Marina, Cabopino, and Estepona. Each has its own character. Marbella Marina is closer to the town centre. Cabopino is quieter and has a nice beach. Estepona has a charming old town and a long promenade. You can also depart from Sotogrande or Benalmadena, but those are further away.

For a longer trip, consider a day charter to the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins and whales. Or head east to the Nerja caves for a cultural stop. But for a birthday, staying close to Puerto Banus is usually enough. You want to maximise party time, not travel time.

How to Find the Best Catamaran for Your Birthday

Use the search filters on BoatHire24 to narrow down your options. Sort by price, capacity, or rating. Read the boat descriptions carefully. Look for recent photos and reviews from previous guests. If a boat has no reviews, ask the owner for references.

Contact multiple owners to compare prices and availability. Some owners are flexible on duration and route. Negotiate if you are booking for a large group or a long duration. Owners prefer full-day bookings because they are more profitable, so you might get a better rate for a half-day if you are flexible on timing.

Check the boat's insurance and safety certificate. All boats on BoatHire24 should have valid insurance and a commercial licence. If the owner cannot provide proof, do not book. The skipper is responsible for your safety, so make sure they are experienced and have a good track record.

Final Thoughts on Private Catamaran Hire Puerto Banus for Birthday

Private catamaran hire in Puerto Banus for a birthday is a practical way to celebrate. You get a private space, a skipper, and a day on the water. The cost is reasonable for a group, and the experience is memorable. Just plan ahead, communicate with the owner, and bring what you need. The rest is up to the Mediterranean.

If you have any questions, contact us through the BoatHire24 website. We do not own the boats, but we can help you find the right one. Happy birthday.

title: Private Yacht Charter Marbella for Your Wedding Day
metaDescription: Book a private yacht charter Marbella wedding day with BoatHire24. Licensed skipper, Puerto Banús departure, catering options. Check availability now.
h1: Private Yacht Charter Marbella Wedding Day
intro:
You want a wedding that doesn't feel like a conference in a hotel ballroom. A private yacht charter Marbella wedding gives you the Mediterranean as a backdrop, a crew to handle the details, and zero risk of rain ruining your photos. BoatHire24 connects you with skippered motor yachts, catamarans, and superyachts that can host your ceremony, reception, or both while cruising the Costa del Sol.

Forget the usual venues. On a yacht, your aisle is the deck, your altar is the sea, and your first dance happens under the stars off Puerto Banús. We have boats for small elopements of 6 guests and for blowouts with 50-plus. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you just show up and say yes.
bodyHtml:
What a Private Yacht Wedding Includes

When you book a private yacht charter Marbella wedding through BoatHire24, you get the vessel, the skipper, and the freedom to design your day. Most charters run 4 to 8 hours, starting from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or Cabopino. The skipper handles navigation and anchoring, leaving you to focus on the ceremony and your guests.

Catering is not included by default, but we can arrange onboard catering from local providers. Think paella, grilled seafood, or a champagne reception. Some yachts have full galleys; others have basic fridges and ice. You can also bring your own food and drink, subject to the boat's policy. DJs and musicians are welcome on most larger yachts, but check the sound system and power supply beforehand.

Decor is your responsibility, but the crew can help with setup. Flowers, bunting, and table centrepieces work well. Avoid heavy items or anything that might blow away. The boat will have a basic sound system for the officiant's microphone, but you might want a portable speaker for the playlist.

Best Ports for a Wedding Departure

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice. It is flashy, central, and close to Marbella's best hotels. Your guests can arrive by taxi from Marbella, Estepona, or Málaga airport. The marina has ample parking, and you can take pre-ceremony photos against the superyacht backdrop. BoatHire24 lists most of its fleet here.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and more intimate. It is a 10-minute walk from the old town, so you can do a civil ceremony at the town hall and then walk to the boat. Cabopino is smaller and sandy, with a dune-backed beach for a barefoot ceremony before boarding. Estepona offers a more relaxed vibe, with the old town's flower-filled streets as a prelude to the yacht. Sotogrande is exclusive and further west, ideal if you want privacy and a longer cruise toward Gibraltar. Benalmádena works for guests staying on the eastern Costa del Sol, near Torremolinos and Fuengirola.

Yacht Types for Your Wedding

Motor yachts are the most popular for weddings. They have stable decks, plenty of indoor space with air conditioning, and a flybridge for photos. A 15-metre motor yacht can seat 10 to 12 for dinner, while a 25-metre superyacht can handle 30 to 40. Speed is not the point, but you can cover ground to find a calm anchorage.

Catamarans offer the most deck space per euro. They are wider than motor yachts of the same length, with a large trampoline net at the bow for lounging. A 12-metre catamaran can host up to 30 guests for a cocktail reception. They are also more stable, which helps if anyone gets seasick. Sailing yachts are romantic but less practical for a large wedding. The deck slopes, and the interior is usually cramped. They work for a tiny elopement of 4 to 6 people.

RIBs and speedboats are not suitable for weddings. They are too small and lack facilities. Licence-free day boats are also a no-go because they have no skipper and limited range. Stick to motor yachts, catamarans, or superyachts for your private yacht charter Marbella wedding.

Pricing Guidance for a Wedding Charter

You will pay from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a 12-metre motor yacht for up to 10 guests. A full-day charter on a 20-metre catamaran for 20 guests starts around EUR 3,500. Superyachts over 30 metres cost from EUR 8,000 per day, with prices on request for the largest vessels. These prices include the skipper and fuel for a reasonable cruising range, typically 20 to 30 nautical miles from port.

Extras add up. Catering can cost EUR 50 to EUR 100 per person for a sit-down meal. Drinks are extra if you do not bring your own. Some yacht owners charge a cleaning fee of EUR 100 to EUR 200. Gratuity for the crew is customary, usually 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee. You also need to factor in decorations, an officiant, a photographer, and transport for guests.

Peak season is June to September. Prices can be 30 to 50 percent higher than in May or October. If your wedding date is flexible, aim for late April, early May, or late September. The weather is still good, and the sea is warm enough for a swim. Winter charters are possible but riskier due to wind and cooler temperatures, around 15 to 18 degrees C in January.

How to Book Your Wedding Yacht

Go to the search page on BoatHire24 and filter by guest count and port. You will see available yachts with photos, specs, and a contact form. Reach out to the owner or broker directly through the platform. They will ask about your date, duration, and any special requirements. You can then negotiate the price and terms.

Most owners require a 50 percent deposit to secure the date, with the balance due 2 to 4 weeks before the charter. Cancellation policies vary, but you usually get a partial refund if you cancel more than 30 days out. We recommend booking at least 3 months in advance for a wedding, especially in peak season. Last-minute bookings are possible but limit your choice of yachts.

You do not need a boating licence. The licensed skipper handles everything. You just need to provide a guest list, a timeline, and any specific requests like a particular anchorage or a stop for photos. The skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and sea conditions. Popular wedding routes include cruising past the Marbella coastline, anchoring off Cala del Faro for a beach ceremony, or heading toward the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin sightings.

Who Should Book a Private Yacht Wedding

This is for couples who want something different. If you hate the idea of a hotel function room with beige walls and a buffet, a yacht is your answer. It works for small weddings where every guest is someone you actually want there. It also works for larger weddings if you choose a superyacht or catamaran with enough deck space.

It is not for people who get seasick easily, though catamarans and large motor yachts are stable in calm conditions. It is also not for weddings that need a lot of indoor space for dancing or a sit-down dinner for 100. The galley on most yachts is small, so catering is limited to cold dishes or a barbecue on the deck. If you want a formal white-tablecloth dinner, stick to a restaurant.

Your guests should be reasonably mobile. Boarding a yacht involves stepping from the dock onto the boat, which can be tricky in heels or for anyone with mobility issues. The skipper can help, but it is not wheelchair accessible. Children are fine, but you need to watch them near the railings. The crew will brief everyone on safety at the start.

Weather and Sea Conditions for a Wedding

The Costa del Sol has over 300 days of sunshine a year, so rain is unlikely. The main risk is wind, especially the Poniente wind from the west, which can whip up waves in the afternoon. Morning charters are calmer. The skipper will monitor the forecast and can adjust the route or anchor in a sheltered bay if needed.

Sea temperature in summer is 22 to 26 degrees C, perfect for a swim if you want a post-ceremony dip. In spring and autumn, it is 18 to 22 degrees C, still pleasant but brisker. Winter sea temperatures drop to 15 to 17 degrees C, which is cold for swimming. The air temperature in July and August hits 30 to 35 degrees C, so air conditioning on the yacht is essential for an afternoon wedding.

Sunset in Marbella is around 21:30 in June and 20:30 in September. A sunset ceremony with the sun dipping behind La Concha mountain is a classic choice. The golden hour light makes for stunning photos. Plan your ceremony for 90 minutes before sunset, then cruise back to port as the lights come on along the coast.

Legal Aspects of a Yacht Wedding in Spain

A civil ceremony on a yacht is legal in Spain if the boat is docked in port and the officiant is a Spanish judge or registrar. You need to arrange this through the local town hall in Marbella, Estepona, or the port's municipality. The process involves paperwork, translations, and appointments, so start at least 6 months ahead. Most couples opt for a symbolic ceremony on the yacht and handle the legal marriage separately at a registry office.

If you choose a symbolic ceremony, you can use any officiant, including a friend or a professional celebrant. No legal restrictions apply. The skipper will anchor in a scenic spot, and you exchange vows without any bureaucracy. This is the simpler and more common option for a private yacht charter Marbella wedding.

You need to provide a guest list to the yacht owner for insurance purposes. The number of guests cannot exceed the boat's certified capacity, which is clearly stated on the listing. Overloading the boat invalidates insurance and is dangerous. Stick to the limit.

Photography and Videography on a Yacht

The best wedding photos come from the flybridge, the bow, and the stern. The flybridge gives a wide-angle view of the coastline. The bow gives you the sea as a backdrop. The stern works for group shots with the port in the distance. The golden hour light is soft and warm, so schedule your photo session for late afternoon.

Bring a polarising filter for the camera to cut glare on the water. Drone photography is allowed if you have permission from the skipper and the port authority. Some ports restrict drones, so check in advance. The yacht's movement is minimal at anchor, but a gimbal or stabiliser helps for video. The crew can help with positioning and lighting, but they are not professional photographers.

You can also hire a local photographer who specialises in yacht weddings. They know the best angles and the lighting conditions. They will also know the ports and the best spots for a quick stop on land. The cost is typically EUR 300 to EUR 800 for a few hours, depending on the package.

What to Wear on a Yacht Wedding

Brides should avoid long trains or heavy fabrics. They get dirty on deck and are hard to manage on stairs. A knee-length or midi dress works best. Grooms can wear a suit, but skip the heavy wool. Linen or cotton blends are cooler. Shoes should have a low heel or a flat sole. Stilettos get stuck in the teak deck grooves and are dangerous on a moving boat.

Guests should dress smart-casual. A sundress or a shirt and chinos are fine. No one expects black tie on a yacht. Bring a light jacket or pashmina for the evening, as the sea breeze can be cool after sunset. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential, even in the late afternoon.

The crew will provide life jackets for the boat, but you do not need to wear them unless you are on a small RIB or in rough conditions. For a motor yacht or catamaran in calm seas, life jackets are stowed away. The skipper will give a safety briefing at the start.

Why Use BoatHire24 for Your Wedding

We list only skippered boats from reputable owners. You avoid the risk of a no-show or a boat that does not match the photos. Every listing has clear specs, photos, and a direct contact option. You can compare multiple yachts and choose the one that fits your wedding vision and budget.

We also have a blog with guides on planning a yacht wedding, including tips on catering, decorations, and legalities. Read it before you book to avoid common mistakes. And if you need help, contact us through the site. We do not charge a booking fee, and we do not add a markup. The price you see is the price the owner sets.

A private yacht charter Marbella wedding is not for everyone. But if you want a day that is intimate, beautiful, and totally yours, it is hard to beat. The sea does the decorating. The sun does the lighting. And you just have to show up and say yes.
