title: Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Weekend – Book Now
metaDescription: Book a luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend with a skipper. Puerto Banús departures, 30+ guests, from around EUR 3,500. Check availability now.
h1: Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Weekend
intro:
You want a weekend on the Costa del Sol that doesn't involve queuing for a sun lounger or fighting for space at a beach club. A luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend is the answer. You get a private, spacious deck, a licensed skipper who knows the best coves, and the freedom to anchor where you please. Think Puerto Banús on Saturday, a swim stop at Cala del Faro on Sunday, and cold Cava all the while.

BoatHire24 connects you with the best catamarans in Marbella, from sleek Lagoon 450s to premium Bali 4.6s. Every charter includes a professional crew, so you do nothing but relax. Departure ports include Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, and Estepona. Prices start from around EUR 3,500 for a weekend (Friday to Sunday) for up to 12 guests, with larger catamarans for 20-30 people available on request. No hidden fees, no surprises.
bodyHtml:
What a Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Weekend Includes

A luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend typically runs from Friday afternoon to Sunday evening, though you can customise the timings. You get the entire boat to your group, a professional skipper (and sometimes a hostess or chef), fuel for the itinerary, use of water toys (stand-up paddleboards, snorkel gear, sometimes a jet ski), and bed linens and towels. Food and drink are usually extra, but you can bring your own or order a catering package through the charter company. Most catamarans have a fully equipped galley (kitchen) with a fridge, freezer, hob, and oven, plus a barbecue on the aft deck. You sleep in air-conditioned cabins with en-suite bathrooms. The boat is your floating hotel, restaurant, and water park rolled into one.

Why a Catamaran for a Weekend Charter

Catamarans have two hulls, which means they are more stable than monohull yachts. You feel less motion at anchor and underway, so even guests prone to seasickness can enjoy the experience. The deck space is generous: a large forward trampoline for sunbathing, a shaded cockpit with sofas and a dining table, and a flybridge (on many models) with additional seating and a sun pad. You can host a lunch party for 12 without anyone feeling cramped. The shallow draft (around 1.2 metres) lets you anchor close to beaches and in coves that deeper-draft yachts cannot reach. For a weekend, you want a boat that maximises living space and minimises hassle. A catamaran does exactly that.

Departure Ports for Your Weekend Charter

Your luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend can start from several ports along the Costa del Sol. The most popular is Puerto Banús, where you step aboard in the glitzy marina surrounded by supercars and designer boutiques. From there, you can head west towards Estepona or east towards Marbella's Golden Mile. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a quieter alternative, closer to the old town and the beachfront chiringuitos. Cabopino, near the Artola dunes, offers a more relaxed vibe and easy access to the Cabopino Marina. Estepona port is ideal if you want to explore the western coastline and the Strait of Gibraltar. Sotogrande, further west, is a luxury residential marina with excellent facilities. For a weekend, departing from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina is the most convenient, as you have the widest choice of restaurants, shops, and nightlife within walking distance of the boat.

Sample Weekend Itinerary: Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro

Day 1 (Friday afternoon): Board at Puerto Banús around 16:00. Settle into your cabins, meet the skipper, and do a safety briefing. Motor out of the marina and anchor off the Marbella coastline for a sunset swim and dinner on the aft deck. Day 2 (Saturday): After breakfast, sail west to Cala del Faro, a secluded cove near Estepona with crystal-clear water. Anchor for a long lunch, paddleboarding, and snorkelling. Late afternoon, head back towards Puerto Banús, stopping at the beach club Ocean Club for a drink on the water. Evening in Puerto Banús for dinner and nightlife. Day 3 (Sunday): Slow morning with a swim stop at Playa de la Fontanilla. Brunch on board, then return to port by 16:00. This itinerary is relaxed and leaves plenty of time for doing nothing, which is the whole point.

Catamaran Options for Your Weekend

BoatHire24 lists several catamaran models suitable for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend. The Lagoon 450 is a favourite: four double cabins, four bathrooms, a large saloon, and a flybridge. It sleeps 8-10 guests comfortably. The Bali 4.6 offers an open-plan layout with a huge aft deck and a forward cockpit, ideal for socialising. For larger groups (up to 20), the Lagoon 620 or a custom-built catamaran like the Sunreef 60 provides extra cabins and deck space. All boats come with a skipper, and many include a hostess who can serve drinks and prepare simple meals. You can also add a private chef for an additional fee. Prices vary by model, season, and duration, but expect to pay from around EUR 3,500 for a weekend on a standard 45-foot catamaran for up to 12 guests. Larger or more luxurious models cost more, typically EUR 5,000-8,000 for a weekend.

Pricing Guidance for a Weekend Charter

Pricing for a luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend depends on the boat size, age, and season. Low season (November to March) rates start from around EUR 3,500 for a 45-foot catamaran for three days. Mid-season (April, May, October) adds about 20-30%, so EUR 4,200-4,800. High season (June to September) and peak weeks (Easter, Christmas, New Year) can be EUR 5,500-7,000 or more. Fuel is usually included for a standard itinerary (up to 4-6 hours of engine time per day), but longer distances may incur a surcharge. Food and drink are extra: a basic catering package with breakfast, lunch, and snacks costs around EUR 30-50 per person per day. A private chef with a gourmet menu is EUR 80-150 per person per day. You can also bring your own provisions and cook on board. Always ask for a full breakdown before booking. Use our search to filter by price, guests, and dates.

Best Time of Year for a Catamaran Weekend

The Costa del Sol enjoys over 300 sunny days a year, so you can charter a catamaran in any month. For a weekend, the best weather is from May to October, when daytime temperatures range from 25°C to 35°C, sea temperatures are 18-26°C, and the wind is typically light to moderate (10-15 knots). July and August are the hottest and busiest, with marinas full and anchorages crowded. If you prefer a quieter experience, book in May, June, or September. The water is warm enough for swimming from June to October. Even in winter, you can enjoy a weekend charter if you dress warmly and focus on coastal cruising rather than swimming. The wind can be stronger in winter (15-25 knots), which makes for a more exciting sail if you choose a sailing catamaran.

What to Bring and What to Wear

Pack light. You need swimwear, a sun hat, sunglasses with a strap, reef-safe sunscreen (SPF 50+), a light jumper or windbreaker for evenings, and non-marking deck shoes or bare feet. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos on the water. If you plan to eat out at beach clubs or restaurants in Puerto Banús, bring smart-casual clothes. The boat provides towels for swimming and showering, but you may want your own beach towel for sunbathing. Avoid dark-soled shoes that can mark the deck. Most catamarans have a music system with Bluetooth, so bring your own playlist. And remember: seasickness tablets if you are prone, though catamarans are stable enough that most people do not need them.

Who Is This Weekend Charter For

A luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend suits groups of friends, families with older children, couples celebrating a milestone, or corporate teams. It is not ideal for very young children because of safety risks around the water and the lack of childproofing on boats. For a hen or stag party, a catamaran weekend is a classy alternative to a nightclub, with the option to dock at beach clubs and bars. For a family reunion, the multiple cabins give everyone privacy while the shared deck space brings you together. For a romantic weekend, a smaller catamaran with a skipper and a private chef creates an intimate setting. Whatever your group, the skipper handles navigation and safety, so you can focus on enjoying the coast.

How to Book Your Luxury Catamaran Charter Marbella Weekend

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Browse our listings, filter by boat type (catamaran), number of guests, and dates. Each listing shows the boat specifications, photos, price, and what is included. Once you find a catamaran you like, send an enquiry with your preferred weekend and any special requests (e.g., catering, water toys, specific itinerary). We will confirm availability and send a booking contract with payment terms. A deposit of 30-50% is usually required to secure the dates, with the balance due 2-4 weeks before departure. We recommend booking at least 2-3 months in advance for high-season weekends, as popular catamarans fill up quickly. Last-minute bookings (within 2 weeks) are sometimes available at a discount, but choice is limited. For more tips, read our blog on planning a yacht charter on the Costa del Sol.

Local Highlights to Include in Your Weekend

Beyond the boat itself, a luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend lets you explore the coast's best spots. Anchor off the Marbella Club Hotel and swim to the beach for lunch at the Beach Club. Cruise past the mansions of the Golden Mile and imagine who lives there. Head west from Puerto Banús to the Río Verde estuary, where you might see herons and kingfishers. Further west, the coastline opens up to the dunes of Cabopino and the pine forests of the Artola Natural Area. If you have time, take a day trip to the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can spot dolphins and pilot whales. The skipper can tailor the itinerary to your interests, whether that is snorkelling, paddleboarding, or simply drifting with a book. The weekend is yours to design.

Comparing Catamarans to Other Boat Types for a Weekend

If you are deciding between a catamaran and a motor yacht for your luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend, the key difference is space versus speed. A motor yacht of similar length (e.g., 45 feet) has a narrower beam, so the interior and deck areas feel tighter. A catamaran gives you roughly 30-40% more deck space, plus the trampoline at the bow. Motor yachts are faster (20-30 knots versus 8-12 knots for a catamaran under power), so you can cover more coastline in a weekend. But for a weekend where the goal is relaxing, anchoring, and swimming, the catamaran's stability and space win. Sailing yachts are cheaper to charter (from around EUR 2,500 for a weekend) but require more heel when sailing and have less deck space. RIBs and speedboats are fun for a day trip but lack the cabins and amenities for an overnight stay. For a weekend, a catamaran is the sweet spot between comfort and practicality.

Puerto Banús Departure: What You Need to Know

Starting your luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend from Puerto Banús means you are in the centre of the action. The marina has 24-hour security, fuel dock, water, electricity, and waste disposal. You can park your car in the underground car park (around EUR 25 per day) or arrive by taxi. The boarding point is usually at the end of the pontoon, so you walk past the superyachts and the designer shops. The marina has several supermarkets (El Corte Inglés, Carrefour Express) within 500 metres for provisioning. If you want to eat out on Friday night, book a table at a waterfront restaurant like La Pesquera or Babilonia. On Saturday night, you can walk from the boat to the clubs (Pangea, Olivia Valere) without needing a taxi. The only downside is noise: the marina can be lively until 2-3 am, so if you want an early night, ask for a berth on the quieter east side of the marina.

Marbella Marina Departure: A Quieter Alternative

Departing from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) gives you a more relaxed start to your luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend. The marina is smaller and less flashy than Puerto Banús, with a mix of fishing boats and leisure craft. Parking is easier and cheaper (around EUR 10 per day in the open lot). The marina is a 10-minute walk from Marbella's old town, where you can explore the Plaza de los Naranjos, the orange tree square, and the narrow streets with tapas bars. The beachfront promenade (Paseo Marítimo) runs east from the marina to the Golden Mile, so you can walk or cycle to the beach clubs. The marina has a fuel dock, but the facilities are more basic. For provisioning, the nearest supermarket is Mercadona on Avenida del Mar, about 15 minutes on foot. If you want a quieter weekend with easy access to Marbella's old town and beaches, this is the better departure point.

Estepona Departure: Western Coastline Access

Starting your luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend from Estepona port opens up the western Costa del Sol. The marina is modern with 500 berths, a fuel dock, and a small supermarket (Supercor) on site. The old town of Estepona is a 15-minute walk, with its flower-filled streets and the Orchidarium (a botanical garden worth visiting if you arrive early). From Estepona, you can cruise west to the Strait of Gibraltar, where the water is deeper and the marine life more abundant. You can anchor off the Playa del Cristo beach, a sheltered cove with a beach bar. Further west, the coast becomes more rugged, with cliffs and small coves like Cala de la Sardina. The wind is often stronger here (15-20 knots in the afternoon), so you get a more exhilarating sail if you choose a sailing catamaran. For a weekend, Estepona is ideal if you want to avoid the crowds of Puerto Banús and explore less developed coastline.

Fuel Costs and Surcharges for Weekend Charters

Fuel is usually included in the price of a luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend, but only for a standard itinerary. Most charters allow 4-6 hours of engine running per day, which is enough for a typical weekend route (e.g., Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro and back). If you want to go further, such as a day trip to the Strait of Gibraltar (about 40 nautical miles from Puerto Banús), you may need extra fuel. Catamarans burn around 20-30 litres per hour per engine at cruising speed (7-8 knots), so a 4-hour run costs about EUR 80-120 in fuel. Most charter companies add a fuel surcharge if you exceed the allowance, typically EUR 50-100 per extra hour. Always confirm the fuel policy before booking. Some companies offer unlimited fuel for a flat fee of EUR 200-300 extra. For a weekend, the standard allowance is usually sufficient.

Water Toys and Extras to Enhance Your Weekend

A luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend can be upgraded with additional water toys. Standard equipment usually includes stand-up paddleboards (2-3), snorkel masks and fins, and sometimes a kayak. You can rent a jet ski for the weekend (from around EUR 300-500), a seabob (EUR 200-300 per day), or a water trampoline (EUR 150-250). Some catamarans have a slide from the deck into the water, which is popular with children and groups. If you want to fish, you can add a fishing rod and tackle (EUR 50-100). For entertainment, many catamarans have a Bluetooth speaker system, a TV in the saloon, and board games. If you are celebrating a special occasion, you can order a cake, champagne, or flowers through the charter company (EUR 50-150). Discuss your wish list with the charter manager when booking, as availability varies by boat.

Insurance and Deposit for Weekend Charters

When you book a luxury catamaran charter Marbella weekend, you will need to pay a security deposit. This is typically EUR 1,000-3,000, held as a credit card pre-authorisation or cash deposit at check-in. The deposit covers damage to the boat, equipment, or third-party property. It is refunded after the charter if no damage occurs. Some charter companies offer a damage waiver (non-refundable fee of EUR 100-300) that reduces your liability to zero. Check if your travel insurance covers boat charter liability; many policies exclude it. The boat itself is insured by the owner, so you do not need separate insurance for the vessel. But you are responsible for any damage caused by your group, so treat the boat with care. The skipper will do a walk-around at check-in and check-out, noting any existing damage. Take photos of the boat before departure for your own records.

title: Catamaran Hire Benalmadena: Affordable Fun
metaDescription: Searching for catamaran hire Benalmadena? Compare prices, see what's included, and book a skipper-led catamaran charter from Benalmadena Marina. Fun on the Costa del Sol.
h1: Catamaran Hire Benalmadena: Affordable Fun on the Costa del Sol
intro:
You want a day on the water in Benalmadena without the hassle of driving a boat yourself. Catamaran hire in Benalmadena gives you exactly that: a spacious, stable boat with a licensed skipper who does all the work. You just turn up, relax, and enjoy the views of the Mediterranean, the Sierra de Mijas, and the coast from Fuengirola to Torremolinos.

Benalmadena Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is the launch point for most charters. It is a practical, well-equipped port with plenty of parking, bars, and restaurants within a few minutes' walk. The catamarans here range from 30 to 50 feet, with capacities from 6 to 20 guests. Every charter includes fuel, a skipper, and basic safety equipment. You can bring your own food and drink, or arrange catering through the operator.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Hire in Benalmadena

When you book a catamaran through BoatHire24, the base package is simple. You get the boat for a half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours). The skipper is included. Fuel is included. The boat has a sound system, a cooler, and a shaded seating area. Some operators provide paddleboards or snorkelling gear. You do not need a licence. The skipper handles all navigation, mooring, and safety briefings.

What is not included: food, drink, and tips for the crew. Most charters allow you to bring your own supplies. Some operators offer catering packages at extra cost, typically from around EUR 25 per person for a basic platter and drinks. You can also request a barbecue on board, though that depends on the boat and the operator.

If you want to swim, the skipper will drop anchor at a suitable spot. Common stops include the area off the coast of Benalmadena Pueblo, or near the Cala del Faro lighthouse. The water is usually calm, and the catamaran's shallow draft means you can get close to the shore.

Benalmadena Marina: Your Departure Point

Benalmadena Marina, also called Puerto Deportivo de Benalmadena, is one of the busiest marinas on the Costa del Sol. It has over 900 berths and a wide range of services. For catamaran hire, you will meet the skipper at the charter company's office, which is usually located on the marina promenade. The office will give you a berth number, and you walk to the boat.

Parking in the marina is paid and can be tight in summer. There is a large car park just outside the marina entrance. From there, it is a 5-minute walk to the charter offices. If you are staying in Benalmadena Pueblo or Arroyo de la Miel, you can take a taxi for around EUR 10. The marina is also connected by the local train line (Cercanías) from Malaga and Fuengirola.

The marina itself has plenty of places to grab breakfast or a coffee before you depart. There is a supermarket nearby for last-minute supplies. You can also buy ice and drinks at the marina chandlery.

What Catamarans Are Available for Hire in Benalmadena

The fleet in Benalmadena is mostly made up of production catamarans from brands like Lagoon, Fountaine Pajot, and Bali. These boats are designed for comfort and stability. You will find models such as the Lagoon 42, the Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40, and the Bali 4.1. All have at least 3 cabins and 2 heads (bathrooms). The interior is more spacious than a monohull of the same length, and the deck area is where you will spend most of your time.

For a smaller group, a 40-foot catamaran works well for up to 8 guests. For larger parties, a 50-foot catamaran can take up to 20 guests. The larger boats have a flybridge, which gives you a higher viewing platform and more sunbathing space. The cost scales with size. A half-day on a 40-foot catamaran starts from around EUR 800. A full day on a 50-foot catamaran can be EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,500, depending on the season.

All catamarans have a trampoline net at the bow, which is the best spot for sunbathing or sitting with your feet over the water. The stern has a large platform for swimming and boarding the tender.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Hire Benalmadena

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. The low season (November to February) is cheapest. A half-day on a 40-foot catamaran can be had for around EUR 550 to EUR 700. Full-day rates in low season are typically EUR 900 to EUR 1,200. In the mid-season (March to May and September to October), prices increase by about 20 percent. High season (June to August) sees the highest demand, and prices can be 30 to 50 percent above low-season rates. A full day in August on a 45-foot catamaran could be EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,200.

Some operators offer discounts for multi-day bookings or for groups of 10 or more. You can also find last-minute deals if you are flexible with dates. The best way to compare prices is to use the search tool on BoatHire24, which shows live availability and prices from multiple operators.

Remember that the price includes the skipper and fuel. You will not pay extra for the boat's basic equipment. Additional costs: food and drink, a tip for the skipper (10-15 percent is standard), and any extras like jet skis or water toys if you want them.

Best Time of Year for a Catamaran Charter in Benalmadena

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 days of sunshine a year. You can charter a catamaran in any month, but the experience changes with the season. Summer (June to September) is hot, with average temperatures of 28 to 32 degrees C. The sea is warm, around 22 to 26 degrees C. This is the peak season, so book well in advance. The water is calm, and you can swim comfortably.

Spring (March to May) and autumn (October to November) are milder, with temperatures of 20 to 25 degrees C. The sea is cooler, but still swimmable in May and October. These months are less crowded, and you can often get a better price. The wind is usually light, so the catamaran will be stable. Winter (December to February) is quiet. Temperatures are 15 to 20 degrees C, and the sea is cold for swimming. But you might see more dolphins, and the coastline is less busy. Some operators run winter charters at reduced rates.

If you want to combine a catamaran trip with a visit to the nearby attractions, the summer months allow you to anchor near the beach clubs of Puerto Banús or the coves of Cabopino. In spring and autumn, you can explore the coast without the crowds.

Where You Can Go from Benalmadena on a Catamaran

From Benalmadena Marina, you have several options for a day trip. The most common route is to head south-west towards Fuengirola and Mijas Costa. You can anchor off the beach at Fuengirola, or continue to the Cala del Faro, a small cove with a lighthouse. The water there is clear and good for snorkelling.

Another option is to go east towards Torremolinos and Malaga city. The coast here is more built up, but you can see the mountains of the Sierra de Mijas from the water. If you have a full-day charter, you can reach the waters off Malaga city, but you will not have time to go ashore. The skipper will usually recommend a route based on the wind and your preferences.

For a longer trip, you can request a charter to Puerto Banús, which is about 12 nautical miles west. The trip takes about 1.5 hours each way. You can anchor in the bay off Puerto Banús and watch the superyachts. Some catamarans can also go to Estepona, but that is a 3-hour trip each way, so you would need a full day or an overnight charter.

If you are interested in wildlife, the waters off the Costa del Sol are home to common dolphins, bottlenose dolphins, and occasionally pilot whales. The skipper will know the best spots. You can also see the Strait of Gibraltar from a distance on a clear day.

Who Catamaran Hire in Benalmadena Is For

Catamaran hire in Benalmadena suits groups who want a social, comfortable day on the water. It is popular for birthday parties, stag and hen groups, corporate events, and family outings. The stability of the catamaran means even people who get seasick on monohulls usually feel fine. The deck space allows everyone to sit together, eat, and talk.

It is also a good option for couples or small groups who want a private charter without the expense of a motor yacht. You do not need any sailing experience. The skipper handles everything. If you want to learn a bit about sailing, the skipper is usually happy to show you the basics, but you are not required to help.

For families with children, catamarans are safer than monohulls because the deck is flat and there are no steep stairs. The net at the bow is a safe place for kids to sit, though they should always wear a life jacket. Some operators provide child-sized life jackets on request.

How to Book a Catamaran in Benalmadena

Booking is straightforward through BoatHire24. You select the date, the number of guests, and the duration. The system shows available catamarans with prices. You can filter by size, capacity, and amenities. Once you choose a boat, you pay a deposit (usually 30 to 50 percent) to confirm the booking. The balance is due on the day of the charter, paid to the skipper in cash or by card.

You should book at least a week in advance in summer. In low season, you can often book a few days ahead. The cancellation policy varies by operator. Most allow free cancellation up to 48 hours before the charter. After that, you may lose the deposit.

On the day, you arrive at the charter office 15 minutes before the start time. The skipper will give a safety briefing and show you the boat. You can then board and depart. The skipper will ask where you want to go and how long you want to spend at anchor. You can change plans during the trip.

For more tips on what to expect, check the BoatHire24 blog for articles on packing, weather, and local hotspots.

Why Choose Benalmadena for Your Catamaran Charter

Benalmadena offers a practical alternative to the glitz of Puerto Banús. The marina is less crowded, parking is easier, and the prices are generally lower. The town itself has a lively promenade, a casino, and a large aquarium (Sea Life). You can combine a catamaran trip with a visit to the Benalmadena Pueblo, the old town on the hill, which has whitewashed houses and a 17th-century church.

The location is central on the Costa del Sol. From Benalmadena, you can reach Malaga airport in 15 minutes by car, and the A-7 motorway connects you to Marbella, Estepona, and Sotogrande. This makes it a convenient base for a day charter or a longer stay.

The catamaran itself is a stable platform for swimming, sunbathing, and socialising. You get the experience of a private yacht charter without the complexity. The skipper takes care of navigation, anchoring, and safety. You just relax and enjoy the day.

Frequently Asked Questions About Catamaran Hire in Benalmadena

Do I need a licence to hire a catamaran in Benalmadena?

No, you do not need a licence. Every catamaran charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who operates the boat. You are a passenger.

How many people can a catamaran in Benalmadena hold?

Most catamarans for hire in Benalmadena carry between 6 and 20 guests. The exact capacity depends on the boat size and the operator's license. A 40-foot catamaran typically takes 8 to 10 guests. A 50-foot catamaran can take up to 20.

Can I bring my own food and drink on a catamaran charter?

Yes, you can bring your own food and drink. Most operators provide a cooler with ice. You can also arrange catering through the operator at extra cost.

What is the cancellation policy for catamaran hire in Benalmadena?

Cancellation policies vary by operator. Most offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before the charter. After that, you may lose the deposit. Check the terms at the time of booking.

Is catamaran hire in Benalmadena suitable for children?

Yes, catamarans are safe for children. The deck is flat and stable. Life jackets are provided for all guests, including children. The skipper will advise on safety.

Can I swim from a catamaran in Benalmadena?

Yes, the skipper will anchor at a suitable spot for swimming. The stern platform makes it easy to get in and out of the water. Some operators provide snorkelling gear.

How far in advance should I book a catamaran in Benalmadena?

In summer (June to August), book at least 1 to 2 weeks in advance. In low season, a few days ahead is usually enough. Last-minute bookings are possible if availability exists.

h1: Motor Yacht Charter Benalmadena: Day Excursions
intro:
If you are looking for a motor yacht charter in Benalmadena, you want a boat that gets you out on the water fast, with space to relax and a crew that knows the coast. Benalmadena Marina is a solid departure point for day trips east to Cabopino or west past Marbella and Puerto Banus, and the motor yachts available here are built for comfort at cruising speeds of 20-30 knots. You get a licensed skipper included, so no licence required from you, just pick your route and let them handle the navigation.

On a day excursion from Benalmadena, you can cover ground quickly. A typical 8-hour charter might take you to Cala del Faro for a swim stop, then along the coast to see the Sierra Blanca mountains behind Marbella, or head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar if you want dolphin spotting. The boats range from 40 to 70 feet, with flybridges, sun pads, and indoor saloons with air conditioning for the hot summer months.
bodyHtml:
What You Get on a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmadena

Every motor yacht charter through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles the boat, safety briefings, and local knowledge. You do not need a boating licence. The boat comes with fuel for the day, a full tank of water, and basic safety equipment. Most yachts also include a Bluetooth sound system, a galley with fridge and ice maker, and a deck shower. Some larger yachts have a crew of two, a skipper and a hostess, who can serve drinks and food if you arrange catering in advance.

You can bring your own food and drink, or order a catering package from the marina. Typical add-ons include a paddleboard, snorkel gear, and a seabob for water sports. The skipper will anchor in sheltered coves for swimming, and you can decide the itinerary on the day based on weather and your preferences.

Benalmadena Marina: Your Starting Point

Benalmadena Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Benalmadena) is one of the larger marinas on the Costa del Sol, with over 900 berths. It is well positioned for day excursions east to Cabopino and Fuengirola, or west to Marbella and Puerto Banus. The marina has a fuel dock, chandlery, and several bars and restaurants on the waterfront. You can park in the underground car park next to the marina, or take a taxi from Malaga airport, which is about 15 minutes away.

Departing from Benalmadena gives you quick access to open water. Within 10 minutes you are past the breakwater and heading along the coast. The marina is also close to the A-7 motorway, so easy to reach from Malaga, Torremolinos, or Fuengirola.

Boat Options for a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmadena

The motor yachts available in Benalmadena typically range from 12 metres (40 feet) to 21 metres (70 feet). Smaller yachts like the Azimut 40 or Sunseeker Portofino 40 seat up to 8 guests and cruise at 25 knots. Mid-range options like the Princess 56 or Sea Ray 510 Sundancer seat up to 12 guests and have a flybridge with a second helm station. Larger yachts like the Sunseeker Predator 74 or Ferretti 70 seat up to 14 guests and have a crew cabin.

All yachts have a bow sun pad, a cockpit with table and seating, and a saloon with sliding windows. Air conditioning is standard on boats over 50 feet. Some yachts have a swim platform with a hot and cold shower, and a tender for getting to shallow beaches.

Pricing Guidance for a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmadena

Prices for a motor yacht charter in Benalmadena start from around EUR 1,200 for a half day (4 hours) on a 40-foot yacht, and from EUR 1,800 for a full day (8 hours). Mid-range yachts of 50-60 feet cost from EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,000 per day. Larger yachts over 60 feet cost from EUR 5,000 to EUR 8,000 per day. These prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic equipment. VAT at 21% is added to all prices. Catering, water toys, and port fees for overnight stays are extra.

Peak season (July and August) prices can be 20-30% higher than June or September. You can check current availability and exact prices on the search page.

Best Routes for Day Excursions from Benalmadena

A classic day route from Benalmadena heads west towards Marbella. You cruise past Fuengirola, then on to Cala del Faro, a small cove with a beach bar and crystal clear water. Stop for a swim and lunch, then continue to Puerto Banus to see the superyachts and maybe have a drink at the marina. The return trip takes about 30 minutes at cruising speed.

Another route goes east towards Cabopino, a quieter area with sand dunes and a nature reserve. Anchor near the Cabopino beach and swim, or take the tender to the beach for a walk. Further east is Calahonda, with several coves for swimming. If you have a full day, you can head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin watching. The area between Estepona and Tarifa is known for common dolphins, striped dolphins, and sometimes pilot whales.

You can also charter a motor yacht for a trip to the Nerja caves. The journey from Benalmadena is about 1.5 hours each way, so you need a full day. Anchor near Nerja and take a taxi to the caves, which are a 10-minute drive from the port.

When to Book a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmadena

The best months for a motor yacht charter in Benalmadena are May through October. Sea temperatures range from 18 degrees C in May to 26 degrees C in August. July and August are the hottest months, with air temperatures reaching 35 degrees C, so air conditioning on the yacht is welcome. June and September are quieter, with fewer boats on the water and lower prices. April and November can work if the weather is settled, but you risk wind and cooler water.

Book at least 2 weeks in advance for June and September, and 4-6 weeks for July and August. Last-minute bookings are possible but you will have less choice of yachts.

Who Is a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmadena For

A motor yacht charter in Benalmadena suits groups of friends, families with older children, and corporate groups. The boats are stable at anchor and comfortable for cruising, so they work for people who want to relax without sailing. The licensed skipper adds a layer of safety and local knowledge, and you can focus on enjoying the day.

If you want to drive the boat yourself, you need a valid boating licence. Benalmadena Marina also has licence-free day boats (under 15 metres) that you can rent without a licence, but these are slower and have less range. For longer distances or higher speeds, a motor yacht with a skipper is the better choice.

How to Book a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmadena

To book a motor yacht charter in Benalmadena, visit the search page, select Benalmadena as the departure port, choose your date and number of guests, and browse the available yachts. Each listing shows the boat details, photos, and a price range. You can send an enquiry directly through the site, and the BoatHire24 team will confirm availability and send a booking contract.

Payment is typically 50% deposit at booking and 50% on the day, or a single payment if you book within 14 days. We accept bank transfer, credit card, and PayPal. Cancellation policies vary by yacht owner, but most offer a full refund if cancelled 14 days before the charter.

Local Tips for Your Day Excursion

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses. The sun on the water is intense even in spring and autumn. Pack a light jacket or jumper for the evening, as the wind can pick up after sunset. If you want to swim, bring a towel and swimwear. Most yachts have a changing room and a small toilet.

For lunch, you can order a catering package from the marina or bring your own food. Many yachts have a barbecue on the flybridge, so you can grill fresh fish or meat. If you stop at a beach club like Cala del Faro, you can eat there and charge it to the yacht.

If you want to see dolphins, ask the skipper to head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The best time is early morning or late afternoon. The skipper will know the recent sightings and can adjust the route.

For more information on boat types and destinations, read our blog on the best day trips from Benalmadena.

Why Benalmadena Works Better Than Puerto Banus for a Motor Yacht Charter

Puerto Banus gets the attention, but Benalmadena has practical advantages. The marina is less crowded, so you spend less time manoeuvring out of the berth. Parking is cheaper: around EUR 20 for the day versus EUR 40 in Banus. The fuel dock at Benalmadena is open from 8am to 8pm, and the marina staff speak English. If you are staying in Torremolinos or Malaga, Benalmadena is 10-15 minutes closer than Banus, saving you half an hour of driving each way. The marina also has a direct bus from Malaga airport (line M-110) that drops you at the roundabout 200 metres from the main gate.

What to Expect from the Skipper on Your Benalmadena Charter

The skipper on a motor yacht charter in Benalmadena is usually a local with years of experience on this stretch of coast. They know the shallow spots near Cabopino, the best anchorages in Calahonda, and which beach clubs serve cold drinks. They will give a safety briefing before departure, showing you where the life jackets are and how to use the VHF radio in an emergency. They will also ask about your preferred music playlist and whether you want to eat early or late. You do not tip the skipper, but EUR 50-100 is appreciated if they go out of their way, like arranging a last-minute catering order or finding a quiet cove when the sea is busy.

Fuel Costs and Range on a Benalmadena Day Trip

Fuel is included in the charter price, but it helps to understand the range. A 40-foot motor yacht burns about 80 litres per hour at cruising speed (25 knots). A 50-foot yacht burns around 120 litres per hour. A full day of cruising, with stops for swimming and lunch, uses roughly 400-600 litres of diesel. At EUR 1.50 per litre, that is EUR 600-900 worth of fuel. The skipper will plan the route to keep the engine running efficiently, typically cruising at 20-22 knots instead of full throttle. If you want to go further, like to the Strait of Gibraltar, the skipper may ask for an additional fuel surcharge of EUR 200-300, though most include it in the base price.

Water Toys and Add-Ons for Your Benalmadena Charter

Most motor yachts in Benalmadena offer a paddleboard and basic snorkel gear for free or a small fee of EUR 50. A seabob, which lets you swim underwater at speed, costs around EUR 200 for the day. Some yachts have a small inflatable tender with a 15hp outboard, useful for exploring shallow coves or dropping you at a beach club. If you want a jet ski, you can rent one from the water sports centre at Benalmadena Marina and the skipper will tow it behind the yacht. Expect to pay EUR 150-250 for a jet ski for an hour. All add-ons should be requested at booking, not on the day, to ensure availability.

How Weather Affects a Benalmadena Motor Yacht Charter

The Costa del Sol is known for calm seas, but the wind can pick up in the afternoon, especially in July and August when the thermal wind (poniente) blows from the west. The skipper will monitor the forecast and may adjust the route to stay in sheltered water. If the wind exceeds 25 knots, most skippers will cancel for safety, and you get a full refund or a reschedule. In spring and autumn, the sea can be choppy in the Strait of Gibraltar, so the skipper will avoid that area if the forecast shows strong winds. The best conditions are in the morning, from 9am to 1pm, when the water is flat and the sun is not too hot. After 3pm, the wind often picks up, making the return journey bumpy but still manageable.

Comparing Benalmadena to Other Departure Ports for Motor Yacht Charters

Benalmadena is a middle ground between the busy marinas of Malaga and the exclusive ones of Marbella. From Malaga, you lose 30 minutes cruising east to reach the best coves. From Marbella, you have quicker access to Puerto Banus and the western beaches, but the marina fees are higher. Benalmadena gives you a balanced option: 20 minutes to Cabopino, 30 minutes to Marbella, and 45 minutes to the Strait of Gibraltar. The marina itself has a better selection of restaurants than Cabopino, and the parking is easier than in Estepona. For groups staying in the central Costa del Sol, Benalmadena is the most convenient port for a motor yacht charter.

What to Do If You Have a Large Group (12-14 Guests)

If you have 12 to 14 guests, you need a yacht of at least 60 feet. The Sunseeker Predator 74 and Ferretti 70 are common choices in Benalmadena. These yachts have a crew of two: a skipper and a hostess. The hostess can serve drinks, prepare light meals, and keep the yacht clean. For a group of 12, expect to pay from EUR 6,000 for a full day in July. You can also charter two smaller yachts, like two 40-foot Azimuts, which gives you more flexibility for different itineraries. The cost for two yachts is roughly EUR 3,000 each, totalling EUR 6,000, similar to a single large yacht. The advantage of two yachts is that you can split the group for swimming or separate activities.

How to Combine a Motor Yacht Charter with a Visit to Marbella Old Town

A popular itinerary from Benalmadena is to cruise west, stop for lunch at a beach club in Marbella, then take a taxi into Marbella old town for an hour. The skipper can drop you at the Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), which is a 5-minute walk from the old town. You can visit the Plaza de los Naranjos, the orange tree square, and the narrow streets with shops and tapas bars. The taxi from the marina to the old town costs about EUR 8. After an hour, the taxi brings you back to the marina, and you reboard the yacht for the return trip to Benalmadena. This works well for groups who want a mix of sea time and cultural sightseeing.

What to Do in Bad Weather: Indoor Alternatives on the Yacht

If the weather turns bad, most motor yachts have a saloon with air conditioning, a TV, and a sound system. You can spend a few hours inside with drinks and snacks while the skipper waits for the wind to drop. Some yachts have a galley with a microwave and hob, so you can cook a meal. The saloon windows on boats like the Princess 56 slide open, giving you a breeze without the rain. If the forecast is very poor, the skipper will recommend cancelling early, but if the rain is light, you can still enjoy the cruise with the bimini top up. The skipper will also know a few sheltered spots, like the inner harbour of Benalmadena Marina, where you can anchor and wait out the weather.

How to Save Money on a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmadena

To save money, book a half-day charter instead of a full day. Half-day charters (4 hours) cost around EUR 1,200 and give you enough time for a swim stop and a light lunch. You can also book in June or September, when prices are 20-30% lower than July and August. Another way to save is to choose a smaller yacht, like a 40-foot Azimut, which costs less than a 50-foot Princess. If you have a group of 8, a 40-foot yacht is comfortable for a day trip. You can also bring your own food and drink instead of ordering catering, saving EUR 30-50 per person. Finally, book a Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday, as weekends are often 10-15% more expensive due to higher demand.

What to Expect from the Booking Process and Payment Terms

When you book a motor yacht charter in Benalmadena through BoatHire24, you will receive a confirmation email within 24 hours. The email includes the yacht details, skipper contact, and a map of the meeting point at Benalmadena Marina. Payment is 50% deposit via bank transfer or credit card, and the remaining 50% is paid in cash or card on the day. Some owners accept a single payment if you book within 14 days. The cancellation policy is usually a full refund if cancelled 14 days before the charter, 50% refund if cancelled 7 days before, and no refund if cancelled within 48 hours. You can read the full terms on the search page before booking.

How to Get the Best Photos on Your Benalmadena Motor Yacht Charter

The light on the Costa del Sol is best for photos in the morning, from 9am to 11am, and late afternoon, from 5pm to 7pm. The skipper can position the yacht with the sun behind the bow so you get clear shots of the coastline. The best photo spots from Benalmadena are the white sand of Cabopino, the cliffs at Calahonda, and the skyline of Marbella from the sea. If you have a drone, check with the skipper first, as some marinas restrict drone flights. Most yachts have a flybridge that gives you a high vantage point for wide-angle shots. Bring a waterproof phone case or a GoPro for swimming photos.

bodyHtml:
What’s Included in Your Motor Yacht Hire

Every motor yacht charter through BoatHire24 comes with a few non-negotiables. First, a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the wind patterns around La Concha, and where to find the best swimming spots. Second, fuel for standard cruising (check the terms for long distances). Third, basic safety gear, life jackets, and insurance. Some yachts also include paddleboards, snorkelling kit, or a cooler for your drinks. Always confirm what’s on board before you book, but expect the basics to be covered.

Why Benalmadena Works for Motor Yacht Charters

Benalmadena’s marina, Puerto Deportivo, is one of the largest on the Costa del Sol. It has direct access to the Mediterranean, no bridges or locks, and plenty of berths for yachts up to 30 metres. You can head west to Cabopino’s sand dunes or east to the cliffs of Rincon de la Victoria. The water is calm most of the year, with average summer temperatures around 26 degrees C. For a quick escape, the marina itself has restaurants, shops, and a casino. But the real draw is the open water.

Types of Motor Yachts Available in Benalmadena

You’ll find a mix of motor yachts in Benalmadena, from 30-foot day cruisers to 60-foot flybridges. Day cruisers (30-40 feet) handle 6-8 guests and run at 20-25 knots, ideal for a half-day trip to Cala del Faro or a spin past the marina. Flybridge yachts (40-60 feet) offer more space, a sun deck, and a lower cabin, good for 8-12 guests and longer trips to Estepona or the Strait of Gibraltar. If you want outright speed, some RIBs and sports boats hit 40 knots, but they’re not typical for motor yacht hire Benalmadena. Stick to the flybridge for comfort.

Pricing Guide for Motor Yacht Hire Benalmadena

Prices vary by yacht size, season, and duration. For a half-day (4 hours) on a 35-foot motor yacht, expect from around EUR 1,500. A full day (8 hours) on a 45-foot flybridge runs from EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,000. High season (June to September) pushes prices up 20-30 per cent. Some operators offer sunset charters (3 hours) from EUR 900. Always check the total cost, including fuel, port fees, and any extras like food or water toys. Compare multiple yachts on our search page to find the best deal.

Popular Routes from Benalmadena

Most charters head west. A typical half-day route: Benalmadena to Cala del Faro (20 minutes), anchor for a swim, then cruise past Puerto Banus to see the superyachts, then back. Full-day trips go further: stop at Cabopino beach, then Marbella’sGolden Mile, lunch at a chiringuito in Estepona old town, and a slow cruise back. For a longer day, head east to Nerja caves (2.5 hours one way) or south to the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin watching. The skipper will suggest the best route based on weather and your group.

Best Time of Year for Motor Yacht Hire Benalmadena

The Costa del Sol runs on a long season. April to October is prime, with May and September offering the sweet spot of warm weather and fewer crowds. July and August are hot (30+ degrees C) and busy, but the sea is flat and the evenings are long. November to March is quieter; you can still charter, but expect cooler winds and shorter days. Winter rates are lower, sometimes 40 per cent less than summer. If you’re flexible, book outside July-August for better availability and price.

How to Book Motor Yacht Hire Benalmadena Fast

On BoatHire24, you can filter by yacht size, price, and availability. Pick your date, duration, and number of guests. Each listing shows the exact boat, photos, and skipper details. You book online, pay a deposit (usually 30-50 per cent), and the balance is due on the day. No hidden fees. If you need help, the team can suggest yachts based on your group. For a fast booking, use the search tool and check the “available now” filter.

Who Should Hire a Motor Yacht in Benalmadena

This works for small groups, couples, and families who want a private day out without the party vibe. If you’re celebrating a birthday, anniversary, or just escaping the hotel pool, a motor yacht gives you space and freedom. It’s also good for business clients or small corporate groups (up to 12 guests on most yachts). If you want a big party boat, look for catamarans or larger yachts. But for a relaxed cruise with a skipper who handles everything, motor yacht hire Benalmadena is straightforward.

Local Tips for Your Benalmadena Charter

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light jacket even in summer, the wind can chill you at 25 knots. Most yachts have a fridge, so bring your own drinks and snacks, or pre-order a catering package. The skipper will know the best spots for swimming, so ask. If you want to see dolphins, head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar, but that’s a longer trip. For a quick photo op, cruise past Puerto Banus and the superyachts. And don’t forget to tip the skipper, 10-15 per cent is standard for good service.

Comparing Benalmadena to Other Departure Ports

Benalmadena is more relaxed than Puerto Banus. Less glitz, lower prices, and easier parking. It’s also closer to Malaga airport, so you can charter directly after landing. Estepona and Sotogrande are further west, better for longer trips, but Benalmadena offers quick access to both the western and eastern Costa del Sol. For a half-day charter, Benalmadena is hard to beat. For a full day, you can still reach most key spots. Check BoatHire24 for yachts based in Benalmadena and compare with other ports.

Safety and Skipper Qualifications

All skippers on BoatHire24 hold a valid Spanish licence (Patron de Embarcaciones de Recreo or higher). They know the local hazards, from shallow spots near Cabopino to the busy shipping lanes off Gibraltar. The yacht is insured for charter use, and safety equipment (life jackets, flares, radio) is mandatory. If the weather turns bad, the skipper will adjust the route or cancel for safety. You’re never pressured to go out in unsafe conditions. For more on what to expect, read our blog on charter safety.

What to Expect When You Arrive at Puerto Deportivo Benalmádena

Your skipper will meet you at the designated berth, usually 15 minutes before departure. The marina is well signposted, with pay parking right next to the main promenade (around EUR 20 for a full day in summer). You'll walk past the fishing boats and the chiringuitos to find your yacht. Most skippers send a WhatsApp with the exact location the day before. Bring your booking confirmation and ID. The boat will be fuelled, cleaned, and ready to go. No queues, no paperwork beyond a quick safety briefing.

Motor Yacht Hire for Half-Day vs Full-Day: Which One Fits

A half-day (4 hours) is enough for a swim stop at Cala del Faro, a slow cruise past the marina, and a drink on deck. You'll cover about 15-20 nautical miles. A full day (8 hours) lets you reach Estepona or Puerto Banús, anchor for lunch, and still have time for a second swim. If you want to see dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar, you need at least 8 hours, preferably 10. For a sunset charter (3 hours), you stay close to the coast and watch the sun drop behind La Concha. Most groups choose half-day for a first trip, then upgrade if they want more.

Fuel Costs and Hidden Charges Explained

Fuel is usually included for standard cruising, but check the contract. Some operators cap it at 50-60 litres for a half-day, which covers about 25 nautical miles at cruising speed. If you go further or run the generator for air conditioning, you might pay extra. Port fees for stopping at Puerto Banús or Estepona are typically EUR 30-60, sometimes added to your bill. Water toys like paddleboards or jet skis cost extra, around EUR 50-100 per item. Ask for a full breakdown before you book, and compare total prices on our search page.

Best Motor Yachts for a Family Group in Benalmádena

For a family of 4-6, a 35-40 foot day cruiser with a small cabin works well. Kids can nap inside while adults sit on the aft deck. Look for yachts with a bimini top for shade and a swim platform for easy water access. Some have a toilet (head) and a small galley for snacks. The Azimut 40 and Jeanneau 45 are common in Benalmádena, both reliable and stable. Avoid RIBs or speedboats with young children, the ride is too bumpy. Stick to a flybridge for space and comfort.

Corporate Events and Business Charters on Motor Yachts

Benalmádena is a solid choice for corporate groups of up to 12 guests. You can charter a 50-foot flybridge with a lower saloon for presentations or informal meetings. The skipper handles navigation while you work or network. Most yachts have Bluetooth speakers, a fridge, and seating for everyone. Catering can be arranged, from tapas to a full paella lunch. The relaxed setting works better than a conference room. Book at least two weeks ahead for corporate charters, especially in May or September when demand is high.

Weather Conditions and Sea State in Benalmádena

The Mediterranean here is mostly calm from May to October. Typical sea state is force 2-3 (light breeze, small waves under 1 metre). The prevailing wind is from the west, so heading east to Nerja can be smoother than going west towards Gibraltar. In July and August, the sea is often flat calm by 10am, ideal for watersports. Winter months bring occasional Levante winds from the east, which can create choppy conditions. Your skipper monitors the forecast and will advise if a route change is needed. Always book with a flexible cancellation policy for winter charters.

What to Pack for a Motor Yacht Charter in Benalmádena

You need sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, and polarised sunglasses to cut glare off the water. A light windbreaker or fleece is useful even in summer, the breeze at 25 knots can feel cool. Swimwear and a towel are essential, most yachts have a freshwater shower to rinse off. Non-marking shoes only on deck, so no black soles. If you plan to eat on board, bring your own food or pre-order from a local deli. The skipper usually has a basic first aid kit, but bring any personal medication. Leave valuables in the marina locker if you're swimming.

Dining Options Onboard and Ashore During Your Charter

Most motor yachts have a fridge and a small galley, but no full kitchen. You can bring your own picnic or order a catering package from the charter company (from EUR 25 per person for tapas and drinks). For lunch ashore, popular stops include Chiringuito El Faro at Cala del Faro (fresh fish and paella) or a beach club in Puerto Banús. The skipper can recommend spots and will wait at anchor while you eat. If you want a barbecue on the beach, some operators provide a portable grill and cooler. Ask when booking.

How to Get the Best Deal on Motor Yacht Hire Benalmádena

Book early, at least two to three weeks ahead for summer dates. Last-minute deals exist but are rare for motor yachts. Mid-week charters (Tuesday to Thursday) are cheaper than weekends, sometimes by 20 per cent. Avoid the first two weeks of August if you can, prices peak and availability drops. Compare at least three yachts on BoatHire24 before committing. Some operators offer discounts for half-day bookings if you pay in full upfront. Ask about off-peak rates for September or October, the weather is still good.

Accessibility: Is a Motor Yacht Suitable for Guests with Limited Mobility

Most day cruisers and flybridges have steps to board from the pontoon, usually 2-3 steps. The main deck is accessible once onboard, but the lower cabin and flybridge require climbing ladders or steep stairs. For guests with wheelchairs or walkers, a 40-foot motor yacht with a wide aft deck and a single-level main saloon is the best option. Some operators in Benalmádena have yachts with a hydraulic swim platform that lowers to the water. Contact the team at BoatHire24 to filter for accessible yachts. The skipper can assist with boarding if needed.

Combining Your Motor Yacht Charter with Other Activities

You can pair your charter with a visit to the Selwo Marina or the Benalmádena cable car (both near the marina). Or book a sunset cruise followed by dinner at a marina restaurant like El Mero or El Barco. For a longer day, combine a morning charter with an afternoon at the beach at Cabopino. Some groups book a half-day yacht trip to Puerto Banús, then spend the evening at the port's bars and clubs. The skipper will drop you at the marina and you can arrange a taxi back to Benalmádena. Read our blog for more itinerary ideas.

Everything is bookable online, and you can compare boats side by side without the usual holiday-rental fluff.
bodyHtml:
Why Benalmadena for a Speedboat Rental

Benalmadena sits between Torremolinos and Fuengirola, about 15 minutes from Málaga airport. The marina, Puerto Marina, is a purpose-built complex with restaurants, shops, and a long promenade. It is also the departure point for most speedboat rentals in the area. From here you can head west to Cabopino or east to Cala del Faro and the cliffs of La Araña. The water is calm for most of the year, and the wind rarely kicks up enough to cancel a trip. Average sea temperatures in summer hit 24 degrees C, so swimming stops are a given.

Benalmadena itself has a bit of a reputation for package tourism, but once you are on the water that disappears. The coastline is varied: sandy beaches, rocky coves, and the odd fishing village. You can anchor off Torrebermeja for a swim, or cruise past the marina’s flashy superyachts on your way out.

What You Get with Every Speedboat Rental

Every boat listed on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That is not a upsell; it is standard. The skipper knows the local waters, the no-go zones, and the best spots for a dip. They also handle the fuel, insurance, and any port fees. You do not need to worry about a boating licence, insurance, or navigation. Your only job is to decide where you want to go and how long you want to be out.

Most speedboats come with a Bluetooth speaker, a bimini top for shade, and a cooler. Some have a small cabin with a toilet, which is useful if you are out for a full day. The boats are cleaned and fuelled before you arrive, so you step on and go.

Types of Speedboats Available in Benalmadena

You have a few choices speedboat rental in Benalmadena. The most common are rigid inflatable boats (RIBs). These are lightweight, fast, and stable. A typical 6-metre RIB seats 6 to 8 people and hits 35 to 40 knots. They are open boats, so you get the full sun and spray. Good for a short blast to a cove and back.

Next up are sports cruisers. These are fibreglass speedboats with a bowrider or cuddy cabin. They are a bit heavier, so they ride smoother in chop. Seating is usually for 6 to 10 people, and the top speed is around 30 knots. They have more shade and often a small toilet. Prices are higher, but you get more comfort.

Then there are high-performance day boats. These are the ones you see in Puerto Banús: sleek, powerful, and designed for showing off. They can hit 50 knots and carry 8 to 12 people. Expect to pay a premium, and you will need to book well in advance in July and August.

Departure Ports and Routes

Most speedboat rentals in Benalmadena depart from Puerto Marina. That is the main marina, with easy parking and direct access to the sea. You can also find boats departing from Cabopino, which is a smaller marina west of Benalmadena, or from Marbella Marina if you are willing to drive a bit.

A typical route from Benalmadena heads east towards Cala del Faro. That is a rocky cove with clear water, about 15 minutes at cruising speed. You can anchor, swim, and have lunch. From there you can continue to the cliffs of La Araña or turn back. Another route goes west to Cabopino. The dunes there are a protected area, and the beach is quiet on weekdays. You can also head straight out to sea for a dolphin-watching trip. The Strait of Gibraltar is about 45 minutes south, but you do not need to go that far. Dolphins are common all along the coast, especially in the summer.

Pricing Guidance for Speedboat Rental Benalmadena

Prices vary by boat size, duration, and season. Here is a rough guide, not exact figures for specific boats. For a half-day (4 hours) on a 6-metre RIB, expect to pay from around EUR 350. A full day (8 hours) on the same boat is from EUR 500. For a 9-metre sports cruiser, half-day starts at EUR 600, full day at EUR 900. High-performance day boats start at EUR 1,200 for a half-day and go up to EUR 2,500 for a full day. All prices include the skipper, fuel, and insurance. Fuel is typically included for a standard route; if you want to go far, like to Marbella or Nerja, there may be a fuel surcharge.

Booking online through our search page gives you a price comparison across multiple operators. You can filter by boat type, capacity, and price. No hidden fees. The price you see is the price you pay, unless you add extras like food or drinks.

Best Season for Speedboat Rental in Benalmadena

The season runs from April to October. May, June, and September are the sweet spots. The weather is warm (24 to 28 degrees C), the sea is calm, and the crowds are thinner. July and August are peak season. The marina is busy, the beaches are packed, and prices are 20 to 30 percent higher. If you book in August, do it at least two weeks in advance. The water is warmest in August and September, hitting 24 degrees C. In April and October, you might get cooler days and a bit of wind, but the sun is still strong. You can rent a speedboat year-round, but the best months for comfortable cruising are May through September.

How to Book a Speedboat in Benalmadena

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24, select Benalmadena as your port, choose speedboat as the boat type, and pick your date. You will see a list of available boats with prices, photos, and specifications. Click on a boat to see the full details: capacity, length, engine power, and what is included. Select your duration (half-day, full-day, or multi-day), and proceed to checkout. Payment is by credit card or PayPal. You will receive a confirmation email with the meeting point and skipper contact details. On the day, arrive at the marina 15 minutes early. The skipper will meet you at the boat. No need to print anything; a digital confirmation works.

Cancellation policies vary by operator. Most offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure. Some require 72 hours. Check the terms before you book.

Who Is Speedboat Rental Benalmadena For

Speedboat rental in Benalmadena suits groups of friends, families with older children, and couples who want a private day on the water. It is not ideal for large groups (over 12 people) or for those who want a party boat with a DJ. For that, look at catamarans. It is also not for people who want to sail; speedboats are motor vessels. If you want a sailing experience, go for a sailing yacht charter. Speedboats are best for short trips, swimming stops, and sightseeing along the coast. They are also popular for dolphin-watching because you can cover ground quickly and get to where the dolphins are.

If you are a solo traveller or a couple, you might find a RIB too big. Some operators offer smaller boats for 4 people. Check the capacity before booking.

What to Bring on a Speedboat Rental

Bring sunscreen, a towel, swimwear, and a hat. The sun is strong even in spring and autumn. A windbreaker or light jacket is useful for the ride back in the afternoon when the wind picks up. Most boats have a cooler, but you can bring your own drinks and snacks. No glass bottles on most boats. The skipper will have water on board. If you want a meal, some operators offer catering as an add-on. You can also stop at a beachside chiringuito for lunch. Popular spots include Chiringuito El Cabo in Cala del Faro and Chiringuito La Luna in Cabopino. Both are accessible by boat, and you can tie up at their mooring buoys.

Do not bring large suitcases or bulky bags. Space on a speedboat is limited. A small backpack or dry bag is fine.

Safety and Regulations

The skipper holds a valid Spanish licence and knows the local maritime regulations. Life jackets are provided for all passengers. The boat is equipped with a first aid kit, flares, and a VHF radio. You will be given a safety briefing before departure. The skipper has the final say on the route and weather conditions. If the sea is rough, they may suggest a different itinerary or cancel the trip. That is rare in summer, but it happens in April and October. If the trip is cancelled due to weather, you get a full refund or the option to reschedule.

Benalmadena port has a 5-knot speed limit inside the marina. Once you are past the breakwater, you can open up. The skipper will find a safe spot for high-speed runs, away from swimmers and other boats.

Local Attractions Accessible by Speedboat

From Benalmadena, you can reach several points of interest by speedboat. Cala del Faro is the closest, a 15-minute ride. It is a rocky cove with clear water and a small beach. The lighthouse on the cliff gives it its name. Further east, you have the cliffs of La Araña, a geological formation with caves. You can anchor and snorkel there. West of Benalmadena is Cabopino, a quiet beach with dunes and a marina. The beach has a nudist section if that is your thing. Further west, you can reach Puerto Banús in about 30 minutes. That is the glitzy marina with superyachts and designer shops. You can dock there for lunch, but you need to pay a mooring fee. South of Benalmadena, you can head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. That is a longer trip, about 45 minutes, but you have a good chance of seeing dolphins and whales. The skipper will know the best spots.

For a full-day trip, you can go as far as Marbella or even Estepona. Estepona old town is worth a visit for its flower-filled streets and tapas bars. The marina there is small but welcoming.

Comparing Benalmadena to Other Ports

Benalmadena is a good choice for a speedboat rental because it is close to the airport and has a wide selection of boats. Puerto Banús is more expensive and flashier. Marbella Marina is quieter but has fewer speedboats. Cabopino is smaller and more relaxed. If you want a quick trip without driving far, Benalmadena is the most convenient. If you want to be in the middle of the action, pick Puerto Banús. If you want a more local vibe, go for Cabopino. The prices in Benalmadena are generally lower than in Puerto Banús, but the boats are similar. You are paying for the location, not the quality.

For more information on different ports and boat types, check out our blog. We have guides on the best coves, dolphin-watching tips, and seasonal advice.

Renting a Speedboat for a Full Day vs Half Day

A half-day trip (4 hours) from Benalmadena is enough to reach Cala del Faro, swim for an hour, and cruise back. You will not feel rushed. A full day (8 hours) lets you go further: west to Puerto Banús for a lunch stop, or east past the cliffs of La Araña towards the Nerja caves area. The extra time also means you can fit in a dolphin-watching detour. If you are a group of 6 or more, the cost per person drops significantly on a full-day booking. For example, a half-day on a 6-metre RIB for 6 people works out at around EUR 58 per person. A full day is about EUR 83 per person. That is a good deal for a private boat with a skipper.

Skipper Tips for the Best Spots Near Benalmadena

Your skipper will have local knowledge that is not on Google Maps. Many will suggest anchoring off Torrebermeja, a stretch of coastline between Benalmadena and Fuengirola. The water there is deep and clear, and the seabed is sandy. It is a good spot for snorkelling. Another favourite is the area just east of the Benalmadena marina breakwater, where the water is calm even on windy days. If you want to see the superyachts up close, the skipper can take a slow pass through Puerto Banús. Do not expect to dock there unless you have booked a lunch stop. The skipper will also know which chiringuitos have mooring buoys. Chiringuito El Cabo at Cala del Faro has a few buoys, but they go fast in summer. Book ahead if you can.

Fuel Costs and Surcharges Explained

Most speedboat rentals in Benalmadena include fuel for a standard route. That usually means a trip to Cala del Faro and back, or a similar distance. If you want to go further, for example to Marbella or Nerja, there may be a fuel surcharge. This is typically EUR 50 to EUR 100 extra, depending on distance and boat size. The skipper will tell you before you depart. Some operators offer unlimited fuel for a flat fee, but that is rare on speedboats. On a typical half-day trip, expect to burn about 30 to 50 litres of petrol. At current prices (around EUR 1.60 per litre), that is EUR 48 to EUR 80 in fuel. The operator covers that in the base price. If you book through our search page, the listing will state whether fuel is included or extra.

Speedboat Rental Benalmadena for Families with Young Children

Speedboats can be a good option for families, but there are limits. Most RIBs and sports cruisers are not ideal for toddlers because the seats are not designed for child safety seats. The ride can be bumpy in choppy water. If you have children under 5, consider a catamaran instead, which is more stable and has more deck space. For children aged 6 and up, a speedboat is fine. The skipper will provide life jackets in child sizes. Make sure to request them when booking. The boats have a bimini top for shade, but the sun is strong. Bring a UV suit for the kids and reapply sunscreen every hour. The best time for families is morning, between 9am and 1pm, when the sea is calmest and the sun is less intense.
