bodyHtml:
What a Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena Includes

Every private yacht charter Benalmadena on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper as standard. That means you do not need a boating licence, you do not need to worry about navigation, and you definitely do not need to park the thing. The skipper handles everything: steering, anchoring, safety briefings, and local knowledge of the best coves and beach clubs. You just decide where you want to go and how long you want to stay. Most charters also include fuel, insurance, and basic onboard amenities like a sound system, a fridge, and sometimes a paddleboard or snorkel gear. Check the listing details for each boat, because extras like food, drinks, or water toys are sometimes charged separately.

Charters are typically offered for half-day (4 hours), full-day (8 hours), or sunset slots (2-3 hours). Some boats also offer multi-day trips to Marbella, Estepona, or even Gibraltar, but that depends on the skipper's availability and the boat's range.

Departure Ports for Your Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena

Your private yacht charter Benalmadena departs from Puerto Marina Benalmadena, which is the main marina in town. It has over 900 berths, a handful of chandlers, and a few decent bars and restaurants right on the water. The marina is about 15 minutes from Malaga Airport by taxi, and about 10 minutes from the centre of Benalmadena Costa. If you are staying in Torremolinos or Fuengirola, you are looking at a 20-30 minute drive. The marina has plenty of public parking, though it can fill up in July and August, so book a spot in advance or get dropped off.

Alternatively, some private yacht charter Benalmadena options can depart from nearby ports like Cabopino (15 minutes east), Marbella Marina (30 minutes west), or even Puerto Banus (35 minutes west). The skipper will usually meet you at the boat, so you just need to get to the marina. If you want a pick-up from your hotel or villa, ask the boat owner when you enquire. Many are happy to arrange a taxi or transfer for a small fee.

Types of Boats Available for Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena

The range of boats for private yacht charter Benalmadena is broader than you might expect. Here is a breakdown of the main categories you will find on BoatHire24.

Motor Yachts

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for a private yacht charter Benalmadena. They range from 30 to 70 feet, with flybridges, sun pads, and spacious saloons. A 40-foot motor yacht will typically take 8 to 12 guests comfortably. Prices start from around EUR 800 for a half-day and go up to EUR 2,500 for a full day on a larger vessel. Brands like Azimut, Princess, and Sunseeker are common in the local fleet. You get speed, comfort, and the ability to cover more distance. A typical itinerary from Benalmadena might take you to the cliffs of Cala del Faro, then to a swimming spot off the coast of Mijas, then back via the marina for a late lunch.

Catamarans

Catamarans are the stable, spacious option for a private yacht charter Benalmadena. They have two hulls, which means almost no rolling at anchor, and a huge deck area. A 40-foot catamaran can easily seat 12 guests for lunch, with a trampoline net at the front for sunbathing. Prices for a catamaran start from around EUR 900 for a half-day and EUR 1,500 for a full day. They are slower than motor yachts, but the comfort and stability make them ideal for families with children or anyone prone to seasickness. Most catamarans in Benalmadena are Lagoon or Fountaine Pajot models, well maintained and equipped with a sound system, a fridge, and a BBQ.

Sailing Yachts

Sailing yachts are for people who want the experience of being under sail, not just a floating party platform. For a private yacht charter Benalmadena, you can find 40 to 50-foot sailing yachts from Bavaria, Dufour, or Jeanneau. Prices start from around EUR 600 for a half-day and EUR 1,000 for a full day. The skipper will handle the sails, but you can help if you want to learn the ropes. Sailing yachts are quieter, more intimate, and use less fuel, so they are a good option if you want a relaxed, eco-conscious day on the water. The typical route from Benalmadena is to sail towards the lighthouse at Punta Calaburras, then cruise back with the wind.

RIBs and Speedboats

RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) and speedboats are the adrenaline option for a private yacht charter Benalmadena. They are fast, nimble, and can get you to the best swimming spots quickly. A 7-metre RIB with a 200hp outboard will take up to 8 guests and costs from around EUR 400 for a half-day. These boats are ideal for a short, punchy trip: zoom out to a cove, jump in the water, have some snacks, then blast back. They are not designed for lounging in the sun, but for speed and agility. If you want to see dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar from Benalmadena, a RIB is the most practical choice, though it is a 45-minute run at full throttle.

Fishing Boats

Fishing boats for private yacht charter Benalmadena are purpose-built for angling. They come with rod holders, a fish finder, a live bait well, and a skipper who knows the local fishing grounds. You can book a half-day or full-day trip targeting species like sea bass, bream, mackerel, and sometimes tuna or swordfish further out. Prices start from around EUR 500 for a half-day, including tackle and bait. Catch and release is common, but you can keep your catch if you want to cook it later. The skipper will clean and fillet the fish for you.

Licence-Free Day Boats

If you want to drive the boat yourself but do not have a licence, a licence-free day boat is the answer. These are small, slow boats (usually under 5 metres and 15hp) that you can rent for a few hours without any paperwork. They are not technically a private yacht charter Benalmadena, but they are available on BoatHire24 for those who want independence. They are limited to inshore waters and calm weather, and the rental company gives you a quick briefing before you go. Prices are from around EUR 150 for 2 hours. They are a good choice for a couple or a small family who want a simple, cheap day on the water.

Pricing Guidance for Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena

Pricing for a private yacht charter Benalmadena varies by boat size, type, season, and duration. Here are rough benchmarks to help you budget. For a half-day (4 hours) on a 40-foot motor yacht, expect to pay between EUR 800 and EUR 1,200. A full day (8 hours) on the same boat will be EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500. Catamarans are similar, slightly cheaper for the same length. Sailing yachts are cheaper, typically EUR 600 to EUR 1,000 for a half-day. RIBs and speedboats start from EUR 400 for a half-day. Fishing boats are around EUR 500 to EUR 800 for a half-day. Licence-free day boats are the cheapest, from EUR 150 for 2 hours.

Prices are higher in July and August, when demand peaks and the weather is hottest. You can save money by booking in May, June, September, or October, when the sea is still warm (22-26 degrees C) and the marinas are less crowded. All prices on BoatHire24 are quoted in EUR and include the skipper, fuel, and insurance unless stated otherwise. Extras like food, drinks, water toys, or a hostess are usually optional and charged separately. Always confirm the total price before booking.

Best Time of Year for a Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days a year, so you can book a private yacht charter Benalmadena almost any month. The main season runs from April to October. In April and May, the sea temperature is around 17-19 degrees C, which is fine for swimming if you are brave, but most people prefer to wait until June. June, July, August, and September are the peak months, with sea temperatures of 22-26 degrees C and air temperatures of 28-35 degrees C. August is the hottest and busiest, so book early. October is still pleasant, with sea temperatures around 20-22 degrees C, but the chance of wind increases. November to March is the low season, with cooler air (15-20 degrees C) and rougher seas, but you can still get a private yacht charter Benalmadena if you want a coastal cruise rather than swimming. Prices are lower in winter, and the marinas are quiet.

How to Book Your Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena on BoatHire24

Booking a private yacht charter Benalmadena on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter Benalmadena as the departure port, and filter by boat type, number of guests, and budget. You will see a list of available boats with photos, descriptions, and prices. Click on a listing to see full details, including the boat's specifications, the skipper's bio, and what is included. Use the enquiry form to send a message to the boat owner. They will respond within a few hours with availability and a confirmed price. Once you agree, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking, and the balance is due on the day of the charter. Payment is handled securely through the platform. Cancellation policies vary, but most owners offer a full refund if you cancel at least 7 days before the charter.

If you are unsure which boat to choose, contact us via the website and we can recommend options based on your group size, preferences, and budget. We do not charge a booking fee, and the price you see is the price you pay.

Who Is a Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena For

A private yacht charter Benalmadena works for almost any group. Couples use it for a romantic sunset cruise with a bottle of cava. Families use it for a day trip to a quiet beach where the kids can swim and snorkel in safety. Groups of friends use it for a party at sea, with music, drinks, and a stop at a beach club. Business groups use it for corporate events, team building, or client entertainment. The common thread is that you want the boat to yourself, with no strangers, and you want a skipper who handles the work.

If you are visiting the Costa del Sol for a week or two, a private yacht charter Benalmadena is a memorable experience that gives you a different perspective on the coast. You see the mountains, the marinas, and the coastline from the water, which is always better than from a crowded beach. And because it is private, you can set your own pace. Want to stop for a swim every 20 minutes? No problem. Want to anchor off a deserted cove and read a book for three hours? Go for it. The skipper adapts to you, not the other way around.

Local Attractions Near Benalmadena for Your Charter

When you book a private yacht charter Benalmadena, you have several good options for destinations. The most popular is to cruise east towards the cliffs of Cala del Faro, a small cove with a lighthouse and clear water. It is about 15 minutes from the marina. Further east, you can reach the beaches of Fuengirola or the marina at Cabopino, which has a sandbar and a nudist beach if you are that way inclined. Westwards, you can head to the coast of Mijas, where the mountains come down to the sea, and anchor off a small beach with no development. If you want a longer trip, you can go to Marbella Marina (30 minutes) or Puerto Banus (35 minutes), where you can tie up and have lunch at a waterfront restaurant. Some private yacht charter Benalmadena trips go as far as Estepona (1 hour) or even the Strait of Gibraltar (2 hours), where you can see dolphins and, on a clear day, the coast of Africa. The skipper will advise on what is realistic given the time you have booked.

What to Expect on the Day of Your Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena

On the day of your private yacht charter Benalmadena, you arrive at the marina 15 minutes before the start time. The skipper meets you at the boat, shows you around, and gives a safety briefing. You stow your bags, put on sunscreen, and decide on the itinerary. The skipper will suggest options based on the weather, sea conditions, and your preferences. Then you cast off and head out. The boat will have a fridge with ice, so you can bring your own food and drinks, or order catering in advance. Some boats have a BBQ. You can swim, snorkel, paddleboard, or just lie on the deck. The skipper will anchor in a sheltered spot for swimming. At the end of the charter, the skipper brings you back to the marina. You tip the skipper if you want (10-15% of the charter fee is standard for good service), and you leave.

If you want to learn more about the different boat types and itineraries, check our blog for guides and tips on chartering in the Costa del Sol.

h1: Boat Rental Fuengirola: Top Choices with Skipper
intro:
Fuengirola sits on the Costa del Sol between Marbella and Málaga, but its own marina doesn’t have the same range of charter boats you’ll find a few miles west. That’s fine, because the best boat rental Fuengirola options actually depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina or Cabopino, all within a 15- to 25-minute drive. You get a licensed skipper, a clean boat, and a day on the water that takes in Fuengirola’s coastline, the Sierras, and maybe a stop at Cala del Faro.

BoatHire24 lists private charters from around EUR 400 for a half-day RIB up to EUR 2,500 for a full-day catamaran. Every booking includes a skipper, fuel, insurance, and VAT. You just turn up, bring your drinks, and tell the skipper where you want to go, Fuengirola beach, the castle, or further east to the Nerja caves if you’ve got the time.
bodyHtml:
Why Consider a Boat Rental Fuengirola

Fuengirola’s own port is small and mostly used by local fishing boats and a few small motorboats. For a proper charter, a 40-foot motor yacht, a catamaran with a sun pad, or a RIB that can hit 30 knots, you need to look at the bases that have the fleet. Puerto Banús, 12 km west, has the biggest choice: over 200 boats available through BoatHire24, from 6-metre speedboats to 30-metre superyachts. Marbella Marina is closer, about 8 km, and has a good mix of sailing yachts and catamarans. Cabopino, 5 km east of Marbella, offers licence-free day boats for those who want to drive themselves.

Booking from these ports means you get a boat that’s properly maintained, a skipper who knows the coast, and the flexibility to cruise along Fuengirola’s 8 km of beach or head further out. The water temperature in summer hits 24 degrees C, and the prevailing winds from the west keep the sea calm most days. You can anchor off Fuengirola’s castle, have lunch at a chiringuito on the beach, or take a longer run to the Strait of Gibraltar to watch dolphins, about 50 NM from Puerto Banús.

What’s Included in a Boat Rental Fuengirola

Every charter listed on BoatHire24 includes a professional skipper, fuel for the day, insurance, and VAT. You don’t need a licence, and you don’t pay extra for the captain, it’s built into the price. The boat comes with basic safety equipment, life jackets, and a first-aid kit. Most boats have a Bluetooth speaker, a cooler, and a shaded area. Some catamarans and larger yachts include a paddleboard, snorkelling gear, or a SUP board, check the listing details.

What’s not included: food and drinks. You can bring your own, or order a catering package from the charter company (typically EUR 25-50 per person for a paella lunch and drinks). Mooring fees at restaurants or beaches are usually paid by you if you stop at a private club. Tipping the skipper is optional but common, around 10-15% if you’re happy with the service. Fuel is included, but if you want to do a long run, say, from Marbella to Nerja and back, about 60 NM, some charters may ask for a fuel supplement for larger engines.

Boat Options for Fuengirola Charters

Motor yachts from 8 to 15 metres are the most popular choice for groups of 6-12 people. They have a cabin, a toilet, a small galley, and a sun deck. A half-day (4 hours) on a 10-metre Azimut or Jeanneau costs from around EUR 600-900. Catamarans, 12-14 metres, offer more deck space and stability, good for families with kids or anyone prone to seasickness. Prices start at EUR 1,200 for a half-day and go up to EUR 2,500 for a full day with a crew of two.

RIB speedboats, 6-8 metres, are the cheapest option: from EUR 400 for 3 hours. They seat 6-8 people and hit 30-40 knots, so you can cover the coast quickly. Fishing boats, 7-9 metres, come with basic tackle and a skipper who knows the spots, from EUR 500 for a half-day. Licence-free day boats, available from Cabopino, are 5-6 metres with a 15-40 hp outboard. No licence needed, but you’re limited to calm conditions and you can’t go far from port. Price: from EUR 250 for a full day.

Departure Ports for Fuengirola Boat Trips

Most charters for Fuengirola leave from Puerto Banús (12 km west, 15 minutes by car). This is the largest charter base on the Costa del Sol, with over 20 companies operating from its pontoons. You’ll find parking in the underground car park (around EUR 25 for the day) or free street parking a 10-minute walk away. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is 8 km west, with free parking nearby and a more relaxed vibe. Cabopino, 5 km east of Marbella, is smaller but has a handful of boats, including licence-free day boats.

Estepona and Sotogrande are further west (30-40 minutes by car) but offer bigger boats and quieter waters. Benalmádena, 20 km east, has a large marina with a few charter companies, useful if you’re staying on that side of Málaga. All these ports are within a reasonable drive from Fuengirola, and the A-7 motorway connects them directly. If you don’t have a car, taxis cost EUR 20-30 from Fuengirola to Puerto Banús.

Pricing Guidance for Boat Rental Fuengirola

Prices vary by boat size, season, and duration. Here’s a rough guide based on BoatHire24 listings:

  • RIB speedboat (6-8 m, 6-8 pax): EUR 400-700 for 3-4 hours.
  • Motor yacht (9-12 m, 8-10 pax): EUR 800-1,500 for 4 hours; EUR 1,200-2,500 for 8 hours.
  • Catamaran (12-14 m, 10-14 pax): EUR 1,200-2,000 for 4 hours; EUR 2,000-3,500 for 8 hours.
  • Sailing yacht (10-13 m, 6-10 pax): EUR 600-1,000 for 4 hours; EUR 1,000-1,800 for 8 hours.
  • Licence-free day boat (5-6 m, 4-6 pax): EUR 250-400 for a full day.
  • Superyacht (20-30 m, 12-20 pax): price on request, typically EUR 5,000+ for a day.
  • Private Yacht Charter Benalmadena: Exclusive, Skippered, Personal

High season (July, August, September) sees prices 20-30% higher. Low season (November to February) can be 10-20% cheaper. Booking a month in advance gives you the best choice, especially for catamarans and larger yachts.

Best Time for a Boat Trip from Fuengirola

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with 320 sunny days a year. The best months for boating are April to October. June to September offers water temperatures above 20 degrees C and air temperatures around 28-32 degrees C. July and August are the busiest, but the sea is flat calm most days. May and October are quieter, with cooler air (22-26 degrees C) and still pleasant water. Winter charters (November to March) are possible on calm days, but expect rougher seas and fewer operators running trips. Some RIBs and motor yachts still operate, but catamarans and sailing yachts often stay in port.

Wind patterns: the Poniente (west wind) brings calm seas and clear skies. The Levante (east wind) can kick up waves of 1-2 metres, especially in the afternoon. Your skipper will know the forecast and can adjust the route. Morning departures (10:00-11:00) are generally calmer than afternoon ones. Sunset charters (17:00-20:00) are popular in summer, with golden light over La Concha mountain and the coast.

How to Book a Boat Rental Fuengirola

Visit BoatHire24 and use the search filters to set your port, date, number of guests, and budget. You can compare boats side by side, see real photos, and read the terms. Once you pick a boat, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) online by card or PayPal. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or by card. Cancellation policies vary: most offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure, with a partial refund after that. Some operators require 7 days’ notice for full refunds on larger yachts.

If you’re unsure which boat suits your group, use the search page to filter by type, price, and capacity. You can also call or WhatsApp the BoatHire24 team for advice, the number is on the website. We recommend booking at least a week in advance during high season. For last-minute bookings (1-2 days ahead), check the listings marked “instant book”, those are available immediately.

Who Is a Boat Rental Fuengirola For

Groups of friends celebrating a birthday or stag/hen do often go for a RIB or motor yacht with a sound system. Families with young children prefer catamarans for the space and stability. Couples looking for a romantic day out choose a sailing yacht or a small motor yacht with a private cabin. Fishing enthusiasts can book a specialised fishing boat with tackle and a skipper who knows the local marks. Corporate groups or team-building events use larger catamarans or superyachts for the day, with catering included.

If you’re staying in Fuengirola itself, the charter is a short taxi ride from the port. If you’re in Mijas, Benalmádena, or Torremolinos, the drive is 15-30 minutes. The skipper speaks English and Spanish on all boats, and some speak German or French. You don’t need any sailing experience, the skipper handles everything. Just bring sunscreen, a towel, and your camera.

Local Highlights You Can See from the Boat

From the water, you get a different perspective on Fuengirola. The castle of Sohail, a 10th-century Moorish fortress, sits right on the beach and looks impressive from the sea. The 8 km beachfront is lined with chiringuitos and hotels. To the west, you see the Sierra Blanca mountains and La Concha peak. To the east, the coast stretches towards Málaga. If you head south-west from Puerto Banús, you can reach the Strait of Gibraltar in about 1.5 hours at 25 knots, a popular trip for dolphin and whale watching. The Nerja caves are 45 NM east, a 2-hour cruise at cruising speed, best done as a full-day charter with a stop for lunch.

Closer to port, Cala del Faro is a small cove near Cabopino with clear water and a beach bar. It’s a common stop for swimming and snorkelling. The Río Verde estuary, near Marbella, is a nature reserve where you might see herons and egrets. Your skipper can tailor the route to your interests, just ask.

Frequently Asked Questions About Boat Rental Fuengirola

For more tips on planning your trip, read the BoatHire24 blog on Costa del Sol boating guides, best anchorages, and seasonal advice.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Fuengirola Trip

Your choice depends on group size and what you want to do. For a group of 6-8 friends who want to party, a RIB speedboat from Puerto Banús is a solid option. You get a fast ride, a loud speaker, and a cooler for drinks. For families with kids, a catamaran from Marbella Marina is better, it has a trampoline net at the front, a shaded cockpit, and a toilet. Prices for a 12-metre Lagoon catamaran start around EUR 1,400 for a half-day. For a couple wanting a quiet day, a 10-metre sailing yacht from Cabopino costs from EUR 700 for 4 hours, with a cabin and a small galley. If you want to fish, book a specialised fishing boat from Benalmádena, which has a live bait tank and a fighting chair, from EUR 550 for a half-day.

What to Expect on a Full-Day Charter from Fuengirola

A full-day charter (8 hours) typically departs at 10:00 and returns at 18:00. You cruise east or west along the coast, stop for swimming and lunch, and maybe visit a beach club. From Puerto Banús, a common route is west to Estepona, about 12 NM, where you can anchor off the old town and have lunch at a chiringuito. Another route is east to Cabopino and then to Cala del Faro, about 8 NM. On a catamaran, you can also head south to the Strait of Gibraltar, about 25 NM, for dolphin watching. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring, and safety. You just relax, swim, eat, and drink. Fuel is included, but if you do the Gibraltar run, some charters add a EUR 100-150 supplement for the extra distance.

How to Save Money on a Boat Rental Fuengirola

Book in low season (May, June, or September) and you can save 20-30% compared to July and August. Choose a half-day instead of a full day, which cuts the price by 40-50%. Opt for a RIB or a sailing yacht, which are cheaper than motor yachts and catamarans. Share the cost with a larger group, the per-person price drops from EUR 150 to EUR 50-80. Book directly through BoatHire24 to avoid agency fees, the price you see is the price you pay. Some operators offer last-minute discounts on the day before, check the listings marked “special offer”. Avoid extras like catering or paddleboards unless you really want them, you can bring your own food and snorkelling gear.

What to Bring and Wear on Your Boat Trip

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, and sunglasses, the sun is strong even in May. Pack a towel, swimwear, and a light jacket for the wind. Wear non-marking shoes, no black soles, as they stain the deck. Bring a waterproof phone case or a dry bag. If you’re prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure, the pharmacist in Fuengirola sells Biodramina for around EUR 5. Bring cash for tips, mooring fees, and beach club drinks. Most boats have a cooler with ice, so bring your own drinks and snacks. If you book catering, the skipper will have it ready on board. Leave valuables at the hotel, there’s no safe on most boats.

How the Weather Affects Your Boat Trip from Fuengirola

The Costa del Sol has 320 sunny days a year, but the sea can change quickly. In summer, the Poniente wind from the west keeps the sea flat calm, with waves under 0.5 metres. The Levante wind from the east can bring waves of 1-2 metres and reduced visibility, especially in the afternoon. Your skipper checks the forecast the night before and on the morning of the trip. If the sea is too rough, they may suggest a later start or a different route. In winter, the sea is rougher, with waves of 1.5-2.5 metres common. Most catamarans and sailing yachts stay in port, but RIBs and motor yachts still operate on calm days. Check the forecast on Windy or the AEMET website before booking.

Where to Park and How to Get to the Marinas from Fuengirola

If you drive to Puerto Banús, use the underground car park at Puerto Banús Shopping Centre, which costs around EUR 25 for the day. Free street parking is available on Avenida del Puerto Deportivo, a 10-minute walk from the pontoons. For Marbella Marina, park on Calle José Meliá, free and close to the port. For Cabopino, there’s a free car park at the marina entrance, but it fills up by 11:00 in summer. Taxis from Fuengirola to Puerto Banús cost EUR 20-25 and take 15 minutes. To Marbella Marina, EUR 15-20 and 10 minutes. To Cabopino, EUR 12-15 and 8 minutes. Uber and Cabify are also available, prices are similar. If you’re staying in a hotel in Fuengirola, ask the concierge to arrange a transfer, some charter companies offer pickup for an extra fee.

What to Do If You Need to Cancel or Reschedule

Check the cancellation policy on your booking confirmation. Most charters offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure, with a full refund of the deposit. Between 24 and 48 hours, you get a 50% refund. Less than 24 hours, no refund. Some operators allow rescheduling for free if you give 48 hours’ notice, subject to availability. If the weather is bad and the skipper cancels, you get a full refund or the option to reschedule. If you need to cancel because of illness or flight delay, contact BoatHire24 support, they may offer a partial refund or a credit. Always read the terms before booking, especially for larger yachts where cancellation periods may be longer, up to 7 days.

bodyHtml:
Why Choose Catamaran Hire in Fuengirola

Fuengirola sits right in the middle of the Costa del Sol, between Marbella and Málaga. The coastline here is a mix of sandy beaches, rocky coves, and the occasional cliff. A catamaran gives you a stable platform to explore it all. Unlike a monohull, a catamaran doesn't heel over, so you can walk around, eat, drink, and sunbathe without feeling seasick. The shallow draft lets you anchor close to beaches like Cala del Faro or the coves near Cabopino. You also get more deck space per person than on a motor yacht of the same length. For a group of 6 to 12 people, it is the most comfortable option.

What Is Included in a Catamaran Hire Fuengirola

Every catamaran charter through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a licence or any sailing experience. The skipper will navigate, anchor, and give you a safety briefing. Most charters also include fuel, insurance, and basic safety equipment. Some include a cooler with ice, snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and a Bluetooth speaker. Food and drinks are usually not included unless you book a catering package. You can bring your own or order a hamper from the charter company. Always check the listing details for what is included. Search for catamaran hire Fuengirola to see specific inclusions for each boat.

Departure Ports Near Fuengirola

Fuengirola does not have a marina big enough for catamarans, so you will depart from one of the nearby ports. The best options are:

  • Puerto Banús (12 km west): The glitzy superyacht harbour. You can leave Fuengirola by taxi in about 15 minutes. Catamarans here range from 35 to 60 feet. The port is busy, so book ahead.
  • Marbella Marina (10 km west): Also called Puerto Deportivo de Marbella. Slightly quieter than Banús, with good parking. Good for a relaxed departure.
  • Cabopino (8 km west): A small, charming marina near the Artola dunes. Ideal if you want a quick exit to the open sea. Catamarans here are typically 30 to 45 feet.
  • Estepona (30 km west): A bit further but worth it for the views of the Sierra Bermeja mountains. Estepona old town is a bonus if you want a pre or post charter meal.
  • Sotogrande (50 km west): The most upmarket option, near the Strait of Gibraltar. You can see dolphins and sometimes whales. Catamarans here are larger, often 50 feet plus.

All these ports are accessible from Fuengirola by taxi or rental car. The charter company can also arrange a transfer for an extra fee.

Types of Catamarans Available

You will find two main categories on BoatHire24: cruising catamarans and luxury catamarans. Cruising catamarans, like the Lagoon 38 or Fountaine Pajot 40, are practical and comfortable. They have 4 to 6 cabins, a saloon, and a large cockpit. Perfect for a family group or a few couples. Luxury catamarans, like the Lagoon 62 or Sunreef 60, have more space, better finishes, and often a flybridge. They come with a crew of two (skipper plus hostess) and can include a chef. Prices for luxury catamarans start around EUR 1,500 for a half day. You can also find smaller catamarans, around 30 feet, for smaller groups of 4 to 6 people. These are cheaper, from around EUR 350 for a half day.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Hire Fuengirola

Prices vary by boat size, age, season, and duration. Here is a rough guide:

  • Half day (4 hours): From EUR 400 to EUR 1,200 for a standard catamaran. Luxury models from EUR 1,500.
  • Full day (8 hours): From EUR 700 to EUR 2,500 for standard. Luxury from EUR 2,800.
  • Sunset charter (3 hours): From EUR 350 to EUR 800. Popular for couples or small groups.
  • Multi-day charter: From EUR 1,500 per day for a week-long rental. This includes accommodation on board.

These are starting prices. Fuel surcharges may apply if you travel far. Peak season (July, August) prices are 20-30% higher. Always check the final price before booking. You can compare catamaran hire Fuengirola prices on BoatHire24.

Best Time of Year for Catamaran Hire

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days a year. The best months for catamaran hire are May to October. Sea temperatures are 18-24 degrees C. July and August are the hottest, with air temperatures up to 35 degrees C. The sea is calmest in the mornings, with the afternoon wind (the Poniente) picking up around 2pm. If you want a flat sea, book a morning charter. If you like a bit of breeze, go for the afternoon. Winter charters (November to March) are possible but less popular. The sea is cooler (14-16 degrees C) and the days shorter. You will find lower prices and fewer crowds. Read our blog on Costa del Sol weather for more details.

What to Expect on the Day

You arrive at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The skipper greets you, shows you the boat, and gives a safety briefing. You then cast off and head out. Most charters include a stop for swimming and snorkelling at a cove or bay. Popular spots near Fuengirola include Cala del Faro, Cabopino beach, and the area off Marbella's Golden Mile. The skipper will choose based on wind and sea conditions. You can also ask to go further, to Estepona or even to the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin watching. That will cost extra fuel. Lunch is usually on board, either a picnic you brought or a catering option you booked. The skipper will anchor in a sheltered bay. After lunch, you cruise back to port. Total time is typically 4 or 8 hours.

Who Is Catamaran Hire For

Catamaran hire works for almost any group. Families with children appreciate the stability and space. Groups of friends can party on the deck. Couples can book a private sunset cruise. Corporate groups use it for team building or client entertainment. The only limitation is that catamarans are not fast. You cruise at 6 to 10 knots, so you cover maybe 15 to 25 nautical miles in a half day. If you want speed, a RIB or speedboat is better. But if you want comfort, space, and a relaxed day on the water, a catamaran is the best choice.

How to Book Catamaran Hire Fuengirola

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, select your preferred date, group size, and port. You will see available catamarans with photos, specifications, and prices. Click on a boat to see full details, including what is included, cancellation policy, and skipper information. You can then send a booking request or pay online. The charter company confirms within 24 hours. Payment is secure via credit card or bank transfer. You will receive a confirmation email with the meeting point and skipper contact. If you have questions, you can message the charter company directly through the platform. BoatHire24 also offers a best-price guarantee: if you find the same boat cheaper elsewhere, we will match it.

Local Tips for Your Catamaran Charter

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a towel. The sun reflects off the water, so you burn faster. Pack a light jacket for the afternoon breeze. If you are prone to seasickness, take a pill an hour before departure, even though catamarans are stable. The skipper will have water and soft drinks on board, but you can bring your own alcohol. Glass bottles are not allowed on some boats, so use plastic or cans. For food, order a catering hamper from the charter company at least 48 hours in advance. They can do a mix of Spanish ham, cheese, olives, baguettes, fruit, and drinks. Or just bring your own picnic. If you want to see dolphins, ask the skipper to head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The best time is early morning. You can also combine the charter with a visit to Marbella's old town or Puerto Banús after the trip.

Why Book with BoatHire24

BoatHire24 is a marketplace that lists only verified charter companies on the Costa del Sol. Each boat is checked for safety, insurance, and skipper qualifications. You get transparent pricing, no hidden fees, and a secure booking system. The platform covers all the ports near Fuengirola, so you can compare options in one place. Customer support is available by phone and email during office hours. We also have a blog with guides on the best anchorages, weather, and local attractions. BoatHire24 is the easiest way to find and book catamaran hire Fuengirola.

Comparing Catamaran Sizes for Your Group

Choosing the right size catamaran matters more than you think. A 38-foot catamaran sleeps 6 to 8 people but feels cramped with 12 on board for a day charter. For a group of 10 to 12, aim for 45 feet or more. The deck space increases significantly with each extra 5 feet. A 50-foot catamaran gives you a flybridge, a large trampoline at the bow, and a spacious saloon. The skipper usually has their own cabin, so that does not reduce your space. For a half-day charter with 6 people, a 38-footer is fine. For a full day with 10 people, you want at least a 42-footer. Check the passenger capacity in the listing. Some boats are licensed for 12 passengers, others for 8. Overcrowding is not allowed and the skipper will enforce it.

Specific Catamaran Models You Will Find

On BoatHire24, the most common catamaran models near Fuengirola are Lagoon, Fountaine Pajot, and Bali. The Lagoon 380 is a popular choice for small groups. It has 4 cabins, a simple layout, and a reliable engine. The Fountaine Pajot 40 is slightly newer, with better hull design and more natural light in the saloon. For larger groups, the Lagoon 52 or 620 are available from Puerto Banús. These have 6 cabins, a flybridge, and a professional crew. The Bali 4.0 is a modern design with an open saloon that connects directly to the cockpit. It feels bigger than its length. Some luxury charters offer a Sunreef 60 or 70, which are true floating villas. Prices for those start around EUR 3,000 for a half day. You can filter by model on the search page.

What to Do During a Catamaran Charter

A typical catamaran charter is not just about sailing. You swim in crystal-clear water at Cala del Faro, a rocky cove near Marbella. The water is 4 to 6 metres deep, perfect for snorkelling. You might see bream, seabass, and the occasional octopus. Some charters include paddleboards or a kayak. You can explore the coastline at your own pace. The skipper will anchor near Cabopino beach, where the sand dunes meet the sea. You can also visit the area off the Golden Mile, where the water is calm and the views of La Concha mountain are stunning. If you want to see dolphins, the skipper can take you towards the Strait of Gibraltar. That is a 2-hour cruise each way from Fuengirola, so it works best on a full-day charter. The dolphins are common in the summer, often in pods of 20 to 50. The skipper knows the best spots.

Costs Beyond the Base Price

The base price for catamaran hire Fuengirola covers the boat, skipper, fuel, and basic equipment. But there are extras you should budget for. A catering hamper costs EUR 25 to EUR 50 per person. That includes a selection of Spanish meats, cheeses, bread, fruit, and drinks. A full barbecue lunch with grilled fish or meat costs EUR 40 to EUR 70 per person. Some charter companies offer a hostess for EUR 150 to EUR 250 extra. The hostess serves food and drinks, cleans up, and helps with guests. If you want a photographer or videographer, that is EUR 200 to EUR 400 for the day. Transfers from Fuengirola to the departure port cost EUR 20 to EUR 40 per person in a minibus. Some companies include transfer in the price, so check the listing. Fuel surcharges apply if you travel more than 20 nautical miles from the port. That is rare for a half-day charter but common for full-day trips to the Strait of Gibraltar.

How Weather Affects Your Charter

The Costa del Sol is known for calm seas, but weather can change. The best conditions are from May to June and September to October. The sea is warm, the air is pleasant, and the wind is light. July and August are hot, with afternoon winds of 15 to 20 knots. That creates a choppy sea, especially near Cabopino and the open coast. The morning is always calmer. If you book a half-day charter in summer, choose the 10am to 2pm slot. The afternoon wind can make swimming uncomfortable. In winter, the sea is calm but the air temperature is 12 to 16 degrees C. You can still charter a catamaran, but you will not swim. The views of the snow-capped Sierra Nevada mountains from the sea are spectacular. The skipper will check the weather forecast 24 hours before departure. If conditions are unsafe, you can reschedule or cancel for a full refund. BoatHire24 includes this in the cancellation policy for all listings.

Special Occasions and Event Charters

Catamaran hire Fuengirola is popular for birthdays, anniversaries, and bachelor or bachelorette parties. Many charter companies offer packages with decorations, a cake, and sparkling wine. A birthday package costs around EUR 100 extra. For a proposal, you can arrange for the skipper to anchor at a scenic spot, like the sunset view off Cabopino. Some companies provide a photographer hidden on board to capture the moment. Corporate events are also common. You can charter a catamaran for a product launch, client meeting, or team-building activity. The stable deck works well for presentations or casual networking. The cost for a corporate charter is usually the same as a private charter, but you can add catering and AV equipment. For weddings, you can rent a catamaran for the ceremony or the reception. The legal marriage must be done on land, but the party can be on the water. Some catamarans can accommodate up to 30 guests for a standing reception. Check the passenger limit before booking.

Combining Catamaran Hire with Local Attractions

Your catamaran charter can be part of a bigger day out. Start with a morning charter from Puerto Banús, then have lunch at a beach club like Ocean Club Marbella or Nikki Beach. The skipper can drop you at the beach club's jetty and pick you up later. Or you can anchor near the club and swim ashore. That costs extra fuel but is worth it. After the charter, visit Marbella's old town for tapas and a walk through the orange-tree-lined streets. If you depart from Estepona, you can combine the charter with a visit to the old town, known for its flower-filled streets and colourful houses. The port of Sotogrande is close to the Valderrama golf course, so you can play a round of golf in the morning and charter in the afternoon. For a full-day adventure, charter a catamaran from Benalmádena and visit the Nerja caves. The caves are 4 km inland, so you dock at the Nerja marina and take a taxi. The caves are EUR 10 entry and take about 1.5 hours to explore.

Booking for Large Groups and Events

If you have a group of 15 to 25 people, you need a larger catamaran or two smaller ones. On BoatHire24, you can book multiple catamarans from the same company. They will coordinate the departure and return times so you all meet at the same anchorages. This works well for corporate events, wedding parties, or large family reunions. The cost for two catamarans is roughly double the price of one, but you can negotiate a discount for multiple bookings. Some companies offer a 10% discount for booking two or more boats. The skipper will keep in radio contact with the other boat. You can also book a luxury catamaran with a flybridge that can host up to 30 guests for a standing party. These are available from Puerto Banús. The price starts from EUR 2,500 for a half day. Always confirm the maximum capacity with the charter company before booking. The official limit is strict and enforced by the port authorities.

title: Motor Yacht Charter Fuengirola: Day Trips

h1: Motor Yacht Charter Fuengirola: Day Trips with Skipper
intro:
You want a motor yacht charter Fuengirola. The good news is that Fuengirola sits between Marbella and Benalmádena, so you can actually depart from several nearby ports. Every boat on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, so you don't need a licence or any experience. You just show up, the skipper handles navigation and mooring, and you get to focus on the day.

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for day trips along the Costa del Sol because they are fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space. You can cover a lot of coastline in a few hours, stop for a swim in a cala, and still be back in time for dinner. The typical trip runs from 10am to 6pm, but you can often arrange half-day or sunset options.
bodyHtml:
What You Get on a Motor Yacht Charter Fuengirola

A motor yacht charter Fuengirola includes the boat, the skipper, and fuel for a standard day. Most boats have a sun pad area at the bow, a shaded cockpit with seating, a small kitchen or galley, and a bathroom. You bring your own food and drink, or you can ask the skipper to stop at a beach club for lunch. Some yachts have a Bluetooth sound system, a ladder for swimming, and a dinghy for exploring shallow coves.

The skipper speaks English and Spanish and knows the local coastline. They will suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences. You do not need to tip, but it is common to offer 10-15% if you had a good day. The price you see on BoatHire24 is the total for the boat, not per person. If you have a group of 6-10, the per-person cost becomes very reasonable.

Departure Ports for Your Motor Yacht Charter Fuengirola

Fuengirola has its own marina, but most motor yacht charters depart from Puerto Banús (15 minutes by taxi) or Marbella Marina (20 minutes). Both offer a wider selection of boats and more experienced skippers. You can also charter from Benalmádena, Estepona, or Sotogrande, but that adds travel time. If you are staying in Fuengirola, the easiest option is to take a 10-minute taxi to Cabopino Marina, which is small but has a few motor yachts available.

Your skipper will meet you at the port and walk you to the boat. They will do a safety briefing, show you the life jackets, and explain the itinerary. You set off as soon as everyone is ready. Returning is usually around 5pm or 6pm, but you can negotiate a later return if you want to watch the sunset from the water.

Types of Motor Yachts Available

The fleet on BoatHire24 ranges from 30-foot day boats to 60-foot luxury yachts. A 30-40 foot motor yacht suits a group of 4-6 people. It has a cabin below deck with a double bed and a small bathroom, but you are mostly using the outdoor spaces. A 40-50 foot yacht gives you more deck space, a larger sun pad, and a proper dining table. A 50-60 foot yacht feels like a small ship, with multiple cabins, a flybridge, and a full kitchen.

All boats are less than 10 years old and are maintained to Spanish maritime standards. You can see photos of each boat on the listing page, including the interior and exterior. Some yachts have a jet ski or a paddleboard that you can use during the trip. Ask the skipper about this when you book.

Pricing Guidance for Motor Yacht Charter Fuengirola

Prices for a motor yacht charter Fuengirola start from around EUR 800 for a half day on a 30-foot boat. A full day on a 40-foot yacht is typically EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,800. Larger yachts over 50 feet cost EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,500 per day. These prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. They do not include food, drink, or port fees if you stop at a beach club.

Peak season (June to September) is more expensive, and you should book at least two weeks in advance. Off-peak (October to May) is cheaper and less crowded. You can often negotiate a discount for a midweek booking. The search page on BoatHire24 shows real-time availability and prices for each boat.

Best Season for a Motor Yacht Charter Fuengirola

The best months are May, June, September, and October. The air temperature is 24-28 degrees C, the water is 20-24 degrees C, and the sea is calm. July and August are hot (32-36 degrees C) and crowded, but the water is warm (26 degrees C). Winter charters are possible, but the sea can be choppy and the temperature drops to 15-18 degrees C. Most skippers only operate from April to October.

If you are visiting in spring or autumn, a half-day trip (4 hours) is often enough. In summer, a full day (8 hours) lets you escape the heat and enjoy the sea breeze. Sunset charters are popular in all seasons, especially from Puerto Banús, where you can watch the sun go down behind La Concha mountain.

How to Book Your Motor Yacht Charter Fuengirola

Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters to select motor yachts, your preferred port, and the date. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on a boat to see the full description and a calendar showing which days are free. You can book online with a deposit (usually 30%) and pay the rest on the day.

After booking, you will receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and meeting instructions. You can message the skipper via the platform if you have special requests. Cancellation is usually free up to 48 hours before the trip. Check the specific terms on the listing page.

Who Is This For?

A motor yacht charter Fuengirola works for families with children, groups of friends, couples, and corporate events. Children must be at least 4 years old for safety reasons. The skipper can provide life jackets for all sizes. If you are celebrating a birthday or anniversary, you can arrange for a cake or champagne (extra cost).

If you want a more active trip, consider a catamaran charter for a stable platform with more space. If you want speed, a RIB or speedboat is cheaper and faster, but less comfortable. For a luxury experience, look at superyacht charters with a crew and catering.

Local Highlights on Your Day Trip

From Fuengirola, you can cruise east to the cliffs of Cala del Faro, where you can anchor for a swim in clear water. Further east, you reach the Cabopino sand dunes and the Torre del Mar lighthouse. Westward, you pass the Marbella coastline with its villas and beach clubs, then the Strait of Gibraltar, where you often see dolphins. Some skippers offer a trip to the Nerja caves, but that is a longer day (8-9 hours).

If you want to stay closer, the Rio Verde estuary is a quiet spot for lunch. You can also stop at a beach club like Ocean Club or Nikki Beach for a drink and a meal. Your skipper will advise on the best options based on the wind and swell.

What to Bring

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a light jacket or windbreaker. The sun is strong even in spring. Wear non-slip shoes or go barefoot on the deck. Bring your own food and drink unless you plan to eat at a beach club. The boat has a fridge and a cooler. Alcohol is allowed, but drink responsibly because you are on the water.

Do not bring glass bottles onto the boat. Use plastic or cans. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness pill an hour before departure. The Mediterranean is usually calm, but the wind can pick up in the afternoon.

For more tips, read the BoatHire24 blog on preparing for a day charter on the Costa del Sol.

Why Choose a Motor Yacht Over Other Boat Types

A motor yacht charter Fuengirola gives you speed, comfort, and flexibility. Unlike a sailing yacht, you do not depend on the wind. You can cover more coastline in less time. A 40-foot motor yacht cruises at 18-22 knots, so you can reach Marbella in 20 minutes or Estepona in 40 minutes. A catamaran is more stable but slower, around 8-12 knots. A RIB is faster but has no shade, no toilet, and no cabin. If you want a proper day out with a bathroom, a table, and a place to nap, a motor yacht is the better choice.

Motor yachts also handle choppy water better than smaller boats. On a windy afternoon, when the sea state reaches Force 3 or 4, a 40-foot yacht feels solid. A RIB or a small speedboat will bounce and spray. If anyone in your group gets nervous on the water, a motor yacht is the safe option.

Specific Motor Yacht Models You Might Find

The BoatHire24 fleet includes brands like Jeanneau, Beneteau, Azimut, and Sunseeker. A Jeanneau Leader 8 is a 28-foot day boat with a small cabin, good for 4-6 people. A Beneteau Gran Turismo 40 has a full galley, a large sun pad, and a cabin with a double bed and a separate shower. An Azimut 50 is a luxury yacht with a flybridge, a saloon with air conditioning, and three cabins. A Sunseeker Portofino 53 is a classic model with a spacious cockpit and a swim platform.

Each boat listing on the site shows the year of build, engine hours, and a layout diagram. If you want a specific model, use the search filters. If you are flexible, you can see what is available on your dates and choose based on the photos. Some owners allow you to visit the boat at the marina before booking, especially for larger yachts.

Half Day vs Full Day: Which Works for You

A half-day motor yacht charter Fuengirola (4 hours) costs less and is easier to fit into a busy holiday. You leave at 10am or 2pm, cruise to a nearby cove, anchor for a swim, and return. You can cover the area between Cabopino and Marbella. A full day (8 hours) lets you go further, like to Estepona for lunch or to the cliffs of Cala del Faro for a longer swim. You can also stop at two or three different spots.

If you have children, a half day is usually enough. They get bored after a few hours. If you are a group of adults who want to drink, eat, and relax, a full day is better. Some skippers offer a sunset extension for an extra fee. You leave at 4pm and return at 9pm, watching the sun set over the Strait of Gibraltar.

How to Choose the Right Departure Port

Fuengirola Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Fuengirola) has a few motor yachts available, but the selection is smaller than in Puerto Banús. If you want a wider choice, book from Puerto Banús and take a 15-minute taxi from Fuengirola. The taxi costs around EUR 20-25 each way. Marbella Marina is another option, with a good mix of boats and a shorter taxi ride from Fuengirola (12 minutes).

Cabopino Marina is the closest to Fuengirola (8 minutes by taxi). It is a small marina with a handful of motor yachts, mainly 30-40 feet. The advantage is that you avoid the traffic around Puerto Banús. The departure is quick, and you are on the open sea within 10 minutes. Check the BoatHire24 search page for boats available at each port.

What the Skipper Does (and Does Not Do)

The skipper on your motor yacht charter Fuengirola is a licensed professional with a Spanish Patron de Embarcaciones de Recreo (PER) or a Commercial Yachtmaster certificate. They handle navigation, anchoring, and safety. They will point out landmarks like the La Concha mountain or the Marbella Club Hotel. They will also recommend where to swim based on the current and the wind.

The skipper does not cook or serve food. They are not a hostess. If you want catering, you need to book a yacht with a crew option, or bring your own food. The skipper will help you set up the table and the cooler, but they are there to drive the boat, not to wait on you. If you want a more service-oriented trip, look at superyacht charters with a stewardess.

Anchor Spots Near Fuengirola

One of the best anchor spots is Cala del Faro, a rocky cove with clear water and a small lighthouse. The depth is 5-8 meters, and the bottom is sandy, so the anchor holds well. You can swim to the rocks and jump off. Another spot is the area off the Cabopino sand dunes, where the water is shallow and calm. You can anchor and walk to the beach for a picnic.

West of Fuengirola, the coast between Marbella and Estepona has several coves, like Playa de la Vibora and Playa del Cristo. These are less crowded than the beaches in town. Your skipper will know which spots are busy and which are quiet. On a busy August day, you might need to anchor further out and swim to the shore.

Fuel and Extra Costs

The price for a motor yacht charter Fuengirola includes fuel for a standard day of cruising, usually 4-6 hours of engine time. If you want to go further, like to the Nerja caves or to Gibraltar, the skipper will charge extra for fuel. The rate is around EUR 1.50-2.00 per liter, and a 40-foot yacht burns about 60-80 liters per hour at cruising speed. A round trip to Nerja (60 NM) would add roughly EUR 200-300 in fuel.

Other extras include port fees if you stop at a beach club with a dock (EUR 30-50 per stop), food and drink, and a tip for the skipper. Some yachts charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50-100 if you leave the boat messy. Check the listing terms before you book.

Weather and Sea Conditions

The Mediterranean off Fuengirola is usually calm in the morning, with a light breeze from the east. By midday, the wind picks up from the west (the Poniente wind), creating a small chop of 0.5-1 meter. This is fine for a motor yacht of 35 feet or more. If the Levante wind blows from the east, the sea becomes rougher, with waves of 1-2 meters. Your skipper will decide if it is safe to go out.

In summer, the sea temperature is 22-26 degrees C, comfortable for swimming. In spring and autumn, it drops to 16-20 degrees C, so you might want a wetsuit. The air temperature in July and August can reach 36 degrees C, so the sea breeze on a motor yacht is a relief. Always check the forecast on the day of your charter.

Booking for a Special Occasion

A motor yacht charter Fuengirola works well for a birthday, anniversary, or proposal. You can arrange for a bottle of cava or champagne on board, a cake, or a bouquet of flowers. The skipper can help you coordinate this, but you need to order it in advance. The cost is around EUR 30-50 for a bottle of cava, EUR 20-30 for a cake.

For a proposal, tell the skipper so they can choose a scenic spot. The sunset view from the water off Puerto Banús is a popular choice. Some skippers will play music and leave you alone on the bow for the moment. You cannot reserve a specific spot, but the skipper will do their best to find a quiet area.

What Happens in Bad Weather

If the weather is bad, the skipper will cancel the trip. You get a full refund or the option to reschedule. Do not try to push the skipper to go out if they say it is unsafe. The wind and waves can change quickly. If the forecast shows a chance of rain but the sea is calm, the trip usually goes ahead. The skipper will provide a rain jacket if needed.

In winter (November to March), most motor yachts are out of the water for maintenance. A few skippers operate year-round, but the sea is colder and the days are shorter. If you want a winter charter, contact the skipper directly through the BoatHire24 platform to check availability.

bodyHtml:
What You Actually Get with Motor Yacht Hire Fuengirola

When you book through BoatHire24, the headline is simple: a motor yacht, a skipper who knows the coast, and a day that runs on your schedule. The boats range from 10-metre cruisers that seat six to 24-metre flybridge yachts with cabins, sundecks, and enough space for a small wedding party. Every charter includes the skipper’s fee, basic insurance, and fuel for up to 8 hours of cruising (typically 9am to 6pm, though you can negotiate half-days). What is not included: food and drink (you can bring your own or order catering through us), dockage fees if you decide to overnight, and crew gratuity (standard is 10-15%). The skipper handles navigation, safety, and anchoring, you handle the rosé and the Spotify playlist.

Puerto Banús: The Real Starting Point for Your Fuengirola Day

Puerto Banús is 15 km east of Fuengirola, a 20-minute drive or a 30-euro taxi. It is where the serious motor yachts live: Sunseeker Predators, Azimut Flybridges, Princess V-class. You can charter a 40-foot Sunseeker from around €1,200 for a day, or a 70-foot Azimut with a flybridge and jacuzzi from €3,500. The marina itself is a tourist attraction, think supercars, designer shops, and people who look like they just stepped off a yacht. But the real draw is the water. From Banús you can head west to Fuengirola (30 minutes at 20 knots), east to Marbella’s golden beaches, or south to the open sea where the dolphins play. If you are staying in Fuengirola, your best bet is to meet the yacht at Banús. The skipper can arrange a water taxi from Fuengirola beach to the yacht if you prefer, but it adds 30 minutes and around €50.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo): Closer to Fuengirola, Still Solid

Marbella’s Puerto Deportivo is 10 km from Fuengirola, about a 15-minute drive. The fleet here is smaller than Banús but well-maintained: 30- to 50-foot motor yachts from brands like Jeanneau, Beneteau, and Sea Ray. Prices start around €900 for a 32-foot weekender, rising to €2,200 for a 50-foot flybridge with a bow thruster and generator. The advantage is proximity, you can be onboard by 10am after a late breakfast in Fuengirola. The disadvantage is that the marina lacks the buzz of Banús. But if you care more about the sea than the scene, this is your move. From Marbella, you can cruise to Fuengirola in 20 minutes, anchor off the beach for lunch, then head to Cabopino for a swim in the dunes.

Cabopino Marina: The Quiet Alternative

Cabopino is 5 km west of Fuengirola, a tiny marina with maybe 20 charter boats. It is quiet, low-key, and perfect if you want to avoid the crowds. The motor yachts here are mostly 25- to 35-foot day cruisers, ideal for a couple or a small family. Prices from €600 for a half-day. The real selling point is the Artola Dunes, a protected natural area with a beach that feels almost empty even in August. You can anchor, swim, and pretend you are on a desert island. The downside is limited boat choice, if you want a flybridge or a cabin, you will need to go to Banús or Marbella.

What Kind of Motor Yacht Should You Hire?

Motor yachts fall into three broad categories on the Costa del Sol. First, the open day cruiser: 25-35 feet, outboard or inboard engines, basic cabin, bimini top. These are cheap (€500-€900) and fun for a day of buzzing around the coast, but they lack shade, space, and a proper toilet. Second, the flybridge yacht: 35-55 feet, a raised helm station with a sunpad and seating, a saloon below, and a galley. These are the sweet spot for groups of 6-10, with prices from €1,200 to €2,500. You get a proper kitchen, a toilet with a shower, and enough deck space to spread out. Third, the luxury motor yacht: 60 feet and up, with cabins, crew quarters, and all the toys (jet skis, paddleboards, tenders). Prices start at €3,500 and go up to €15,000 for a 100-footer with a jacuzzi and a professional chef. For a day trip from Fuengirola, a 40- to 50-foot flybridge is the sweet spot: enough space for comfort, but not so big that you feel like you are in a hotel.

Pricing Guidance for Motor Yacht Hire Fuengirola

Prices vary by boat size, age, and season. Here is a rough guide based on what we see on the platform. Low season (November to March): €700-€1,500 for a 35-50 foot motor yacht. Mid season (April to June, September to October): €1,000-€2,500. High season (July and August): €1,500-€4,000. Fuel is included in the daily rate for up to 8 hours of cruising (typically 60-80 nautical miles, depending on the boat’s consumption). If you want to go further, say, to Gibraltar or the Nerja caves, expect a fuel surcharge of €200-€500. You can also add extras: a water sports package (jet ski, wakeboard, inflatables) for €300-€600, a chef for €250-€400, or a photographer for €200. Most charters require a 50% deposit to confirm, with the balance due 7 days before departure. Cancellation policies vary, but most owners offer a 50% refund up to 14 days out, and no refund within 7 days.

Best Seasons for Motor Yacht Hire on the Costa del Sol

The Mediterranean season runs from April to October. July and August are peak: air temps hit 30-35°C, water temps 24-26°C, and the sea is calm 90% of the time. The downside is crowds, Puerto Banús is a zoo, and anchorages fill up by 11am. If you want solitude, go in May or September. The weather is still warm (25-28°C), the water is swimmable (20-22°C), and you can anchor in Cabopino or Cala del Faro without fighting for space. October is a wildcard: some years it stays warm into November, other years the wind picks up and the sea gets choppy. November to March is low season: cheaper prices, but expect 15-20°C air, 16-18°C water, and a higher chance of wind (Levante or Poniente). You can still cruise, but swimming is a brave person’s game.

Where to Go from Fuengirola on a Motor Yacht

You have three classic routes from Fuengirola. The east route: head to Marbella (20 minutes), then past the Golden Mile to Puerto Banús (another 20 minutes), then on to the cliffs of Cala del Faro. Anchor there for lunch, the water is deep and clear, and you can see La Concha mountain behind you. The west route: from Fuengirola to Cabopino (15 minutes), then Estepona (45 minutes at 20 knots). Estepona’s old town is worth a walk, but the real attraction is the beach clubs, you can tie up at a buoy and have lunch delivered by paddleboard. The south route: straight out to sea, past the Strait of Gibraltar. If the weather is good, you can reach the dolphin pods off Tarifa in about 90 minutes. The skipper will know the hot spots. For a longer trip, you can go to Gibraltar (2 hours from Fuengirola) or the Nerja caves (1.5 hours east). Both require a full-day charter and a fuel surcharge.

How to Book Motor Yacht Hire Fuengirola on BoatHire24

Go to our search page and filter by “motor yacht” and “Fuengirola” as the departure port. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Each listing shows the boat’s length, engine type, number of cabins, and included amenities. Click “Request to Book” and fill in your date, number of guests, and any special requests. The owner or a local agent will confirm availability within 24 hours. You can also call or WhatsApp us, the number is on the site. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance in high season, though last-minute cancellations sometimes free up boats. Payment is via bank transfer or credit card. Once confirmed, you will receive a charter agreement and a skipper’s contact. On the day, you meet the skipper at the marina, sign a safety briefing, and you are off. Simple.

Who Should Hire a Motor Yacht in Fuengirola?

This is for anyone who wants a private day on the water without the hassle of owning a boat. It works for couples, families, groups of friends, and corporate events. The skipper does all the work, you just relax. If you are a first-timer, a 35-foot flybridge is a safe bet: stable, shaded, and easy to move around. If you are a seasoned sailor, you might prefer a 50-foot performance cruiser with more speed and a bit of heel. The Costa del Sol is forgiving for beginners: the sea is usually calm, the coast is visible, and the anchorages are sheltered. Just be aware that the water is colder than the Caribbean (18-26°C depending on season) and the sun is fierce, bring a hat and factor 50.

For more tips on planning your day, read our blog posts on Costa del Sol yacht itineraries. And if you are still on the fence, remember: the worst day on a yacht is better than the best day in the office.

Why Fuengirola Works as a Base for a Motor Yacht Day

Fuengirola is not a major charter port, Puerto Banús and Marbella have the fleets. But it is a good place to start your day because the coastline either side is interesting and the town itself has a decent beach for anchoring. The Fuengirola beachfront is 8 km of sand, with chiringuitos every few hundred metres. You can anchor off the Paseo Marítimo and have lunch delivered by dinghy from a beach club like Los Marinos or La Cubana. The water depth is shallow (5-10 metres) so the anchor holds well. The downside is that Fuengirola does not have a marina for berthing a large motor yacht, you will use the mooring buoys or anchor. If you want to dock for lunch, you need to go to Cabopino or Marbella. But for a pure day on the water, Fuengirola is fine.

What to Expect from the Skipper on Your Charter

The skipper is a licensed professional, usually with a PPER (Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo) or higher qualification. They speak English and Spanish, sometimes German. They will brief you on safety, show you the heads (toilet) and the galley, and ask where you want to go. They will not hover, they stay at the helm or on the flybridge, out of your way. But they are not a tour guide, they will not give a running commentary on the coastline. If you want a guide, book a private tour with a local company. The skipper’s job is navigation, safety, and anchoring. They will also help with mooring lines and fenders if you stop at a marina. Do not expect them to serve drinks or cook, that is the charter host or chef, which costs extra. Most skippers are happy to let you take the helm for a photo, but only in open water with no traffic.

Estepona: The Western Option for Your Day Trip

Estepona is 20 km west of Fuengirola, about 45 minutes at 20 knots. The marina is small but has a few charter boats, mostly 30- to 40-foot motor yachts. The old town is worth a visit, whitewashed streets, flower pots, and a plaza with orange trees. You can tie up at the marina for a few hours (€20-€30) and walk into town. The beach clubs on the Estepona coast are quieter than Marbella’s, try El Palangreros or La Escollera for grilled fish. The water off Estepona is often clearer than Fuengirola because the Guadalmansa River carries less sediment. If you want a longer day, continue west to the Strait of Gibraltar. The dolphin pods are active year-round, and in summer you might see pilot whales. The skipper will know the marine traffic, the Strait is busy with cargo ships. Do not try this route without a local skipper.

Sotogrande: The Luxury Option for a Full Day

Sotogrande is 40 km west of Fuengirola, about 1 hour at 20 knots. It is an exclusive residential marina with a polo club, golf courses, and a private beach. The charter fleet here is small but high-end: 50- to 80-foot motor yachts from Princess and Sunseeker. Prices start at €2,500 for a day. The advantage is exclusivity, you will not see the crowds of Banús. The water is deep and clean, and the beach at Sotogrande is one of the few on the Costa del Sol where you can anchor without a dozen other boats around. The marina has a restaurant, El Chiringuito de Sotogrande, that serves excellent seafood. If you are celebrating something, this is the place. The downside is the distance from Fuengirola, you will spend 2 hours round-trip in transit. Make it a full-day charter and stop at Estepona on the way back.

Benalmádena: The Closest Port to Fuengirola

Benalmádena marina is 8 km east of Fuengirola, a 10-minute drive or a 15-euro taxi. It is a working marina with a few charter boats, mostly 25- to 35-foot motor yachts and RIBs. Prices from €500 for a half-day. The marina itself is not glamorous, but it has a decent beach and a few restaurants. The real draw is the proximity to Fuengirola, you can be on the water in 15 minutes from your hotel. The downside is the same as Cabopino: limited boat choice. If you want a flybridge or a luxury yacht, go to Banús. But for a quick half-day with a small group, Benalmádena works. The route east to the cliffs of Torremolinos is scenic, and you can anchor off the beach for a swim. The water is shallow and warm, good for kids.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (factor 50, the sun reflects off the water), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. Leave behind high heels (they damage the deck), glass bottles (most charters ban them for safety, use plastic or cans), and large coolers (the boat has a fridge and ice). The skipper will have a first aid kit and life jackets, but bring any personal medication. If you are prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure, the Costa del Sol is usually calm, but the Strait can be choppy. Most boats have a Bluetooth speaker, but bring your own if you want a specific playlist. Do not bring illegal substances, the Guardia Civil patrol the coast and will board for random checks. The fine is heavy and the charter will be terminated immediately.

How to Save Money on Motor Yacht Hire Fuengirola

Book a half-day instead of a full day. Half-days are 4 hours, usually 9am to 1pm or 2pm to 6pm. Prices are about 60% of a full day. Go in mid season (May or September) when prices drop by 30-40%. Share the cost with a group, a 40-foot flybridge fits 8-10 people, so the per-person cost can be as low as €150 each. Avoid July and August if you can, the prices are highest and the anchorages are crowded. Book directly through BoatHire24 rather than a third-party aggregator, we do not add a booking fee and we have the best prices. Check for last-minute deals, sometimes owners discount unsold dates 48 hours before. And always ask if fuel is included, some charters charge extra for fuel, which can add €200-€500 to the bill.
