bodyHtml:
Why Fuengirola Works for a Private Yacht Charter

Fuengirola sits in the middle of the Costa del Sol, so you can reach three major departure ports in under half an hour. Puerto Banús is 15 minutes west, Marbella Marina is 20 minutes, and Cabopino is 25 minutes east. This means you get access to a fleet of over 200 boats, from 8-metre open speedboats to 40-metre superyachts, without the premium prices you'd pay in Banús itself.

The coastline between Fuengirola and Marbella is mostly low-rise, with sandy beaches and the Sierra de Mijas mountains behind you. La Concha mountain provides a dramatic backdrop for photos. You can anchor off Cala del Faro for a swim, or head west towards Estepona for a longer cruise. The water is calm from May to October, with average sea temperatures of 22-26 degrees C.

What's Included in a Private Yacht Charter Fuengirola

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation, mooring and safety. You don't need a boating licence or any experience. The skipper will also act as a host, they can recommend anchor spots, serve drinks and help with music. Fuel is included in the price for most charters up to 8 hours, but check the listing details. Insurance, VAT and port fees are always included.

What's not included: food and drinks (though you can bring your own or order catering), dock tips for the skipper (optional, 10-15% is standard), and transfers from Fuengirola to the departure port. You'll need a taxi or rental car. Parking at Puerto Banús costs around EUR 25 per day in the underground car park.

Which Boat Type Suits Your Trip

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for private yacht charters in Fuengirola. They offer speed (20-30 knots), plenty of deck space and a cabin below for changing or shelter. A 40-foot motor yacht from around EUR 600 for half a day can take 8-10 guests. For a more luxurious experience, a 60-foot yacht with a flybridge and jacuzzi costs from EUR 1,200.

Catamarans are better for families or groups who want stability. They don't heel over, so no one gets seasick. A 40-foot catamaran costs from EUR 700 for a half day and can take 10-12 guests. The wide deck is perfect for sunbathing and dining.

Sailing yachts appeal to those who want the classic experience. They're slower (6-10 knots under sail) but quieter and more eco-friendly. A 38-foot sailing yacht from around EUR 450 for a half day is the cheapest option for a private charter.

RIBs and speedboats are for adrenaline seekers. 8-10 metre RIBs with 250-350 HP outboards can hit 40-50 knots. They cost from EUR 350 for 2 hours and are great for dolphin watching or a fast transfer to a beach club.

Licence-free day boats are the only boats you can drive yourself without a licence, but they're limited to 5 HP and 6 knots. They cost from EUR 150 for a half day and are available in Fuengirola port itself, not through BoatHire24. We don't list them because they're not skippered.

Departure Ports for Your Charter

Most private yacht charters from Fuengirola depart from Puerto Banús, which is a 15-minute drive west. This is where the biggest fleet of luxury motor yachts and catamarans is based. You'll meet the skipper at the dock near the casino. From there, you can head east towards Fuengirola or west towards Marbella and Estepona.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is 20 minutes east of Fuengirola. It's a quieter, more relaxed port with fewer superyachts but plenty of mid-range boats. It's a good choice if you want to avoid the crowds of Banús.

Cabopino is 25 minutes east, near Cala del Faro. This is a small, sandy-bottomed marina with a handful of fishing boats and sailing yachts. It's ideal if you want to explore the Cabopino dunes or anchor off the nudist beach.

Benalmádena and Estepona are also within 30-40 minutes, but we'd only recommend them if you specifically want to start from those ports. BoatHire24 covers all of them, just use the search page to filter by port.

Popular Itineraries from Fuengirola

Most charters last 4 hours (half day) or 8 hours (full day). Here are three common routes:

1. Fuengirola Coastline Cruise, Head east from Puerto Banús, pass the Fuengirola castle and the marina, then anchor off Los Boliches beach for a swim. Continue to Cala del Faro for lunch at a chiringuito. Total distance: 10-12 nautical miles each way. Suitable for any boat type.

2. Marbella to Estepona Sunset, Leave Puerto Banús, cruise past Marbella's golden beaches and the Sierra Blanca mountains, then anchor off Estepona old town. Watch the sunset over the Strait of Gibraltar. Return in the dark with the city lights. Total distance: 15-18 NM each way. Best on a motor yacht with GPS and radar.

3. Dolphin Watching & Gibraltar, Head south-west towards the Strait of Gibraltar. Wild dolphins (common and striped) are almost guaranteed from May to September. You can't land in Gibraltar without a passport, but you can cruise close enough to see the Rock. Total distance: 25-30 NM from Banús. Requires a fast boat (RIB or motor yacht) and a full day.

Pricing Guidance for Private Yacht Charter Fuengirola

Prices vary by boat size, type, season and duration. Here are realistic ranges for a private charter with skipper:

  • RIB / speedboat (4-8 guests, 2-4 hours): from EUR 350
  • Sailing yacht (6-10 guests, half day): from EUR 450
  • Motor yacht 40ft (8-10 guests, half day): from EUR 600
  • Catamaran 40ft (10-12 guests, half day): from EUR 700
  • Motor yacht 60ft (12-15 guests, half day): from EUR 1,200
  • Superyacht 80ft+ (15-20 guests, full day): price on request, typically EUR 5,000-15,000

These are base rates. High season (July-August) adds 20-30%. Fuel surcharges apply for long distances or high speeds. Always confirm the total before booking.

Best Time of Year for a Yacht Charter in Fuengirola

The Costa del Sol has a microclimate. Even in winter, daytime temperatures average 16-18 degrees C and the sun shines 5-6 hours a day. But for swimming and sunbathing, aim for May to October. July and August are the busiest, expect 32-35 degrees C and crowded anchorages. September and October are quieter, with sea temperatures still at 22-24 degrees C.

If you're booking a private yacht charter Fuengirola in winter, choose a motor yacht with a heated cabin or a sailing yacht with a bimini. The wind can pick up in November-February, so check the forecast. Skippers will cancel if conditions are unsafe, and you'll get a full refund.

How to Book Your Private Yacht Charter Fuengirola

Go to our search page, enter your date, number of guests and preferred port. Filter by boat type and budget. Each listing shows photos, specifications, availability and the total price (including skipper, fuel and taxes). Click 'Book Now' and pay a 30% deposit online. The balance is due to the skipper on the day, in cash or by card (check with the skipper).

You'll receive a confirmation email with the meeting point, skipper's contact number and a map. Arrive 15 minutes early. The skipper will do a safety briefing, then you're off. No hidden costs, no stress.

For more tips on choosing the right boat, read our blog on Costa del Sol yacht charter FAQs.

Who Is This For

A private yacht charter Fuengirola works for couples, families, groups of friends, corporate events and celebrations. It's not a party boat, you can drink, but the skipper must stay sober. If you want a loud party with a DJ and dancers, you'll need a superyacht with event permission, which costs extra.

It's also suitable for non-swimmers, you can stay on deck and enjoy the views. Life jackets are provided for everyone. Children are welcome, but there's no specific child safety equipment beyond life jackets. Toddlers should wear a life jacket at all times on deck.

If you have mobility issues, check with the skipper before booking. Most motor yachts have a step up from the dock to the deck, and a ladder down to the cabin. Catamarans are easier because they have a lower freeboard.

What to Bring and What to Leave Behind

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50), a hat, sunglasses, a towel, swimwear and a light jacket for the evening. If you're prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure. You can bring your own food and drink, most boats have a fridge and a cooler. Glass bottles are discouraged on some boats, so use plastic or cans.

Leave behind: large suitcases, heavy bags, pets (unless the skipper agrees in advance), and illegal substances. The skipper has the right to refuse boarding if anyone appears intoxicated or aggressive.

Why Book Through BoatHire24 Instead of Directly

BoatHire24 is a marketplace, not a charter company. We list boats from multiple local operators, so you can compare prices, specs and reviews in one place. You get the same boats as booking direct, but often at lower prices because operators compete on our platform.

We also handle the deposit securely via Stripe, and we provide 24/7 customer support. If the boat breaks down or the skipper doesn't show up, we'll find a replacement or refund you. Book direct with a random company and you have no backup.

Plus, you can read real reviews from previous guests on each listing. No fake testimonials, just honest feedback from people who actually took the charter.

Start your search now: BoatHire24, private yacht charter Fuengirola made simple.

How to Choose the Right Port for Your Fuengirola Charter

You're based in Fuengirola, but your boat leaves from one of the nearby marinas. Puerto Banús is the obvious choice if you want the biggest selection of luxury motor yachts and catamarans, but it's also the most expensive for parking and the busiest in summer. Marbella Marina is a solid alternative, it's quieter, cheaper to park (around EUR 15 per day), and still has a good range of 30-50 foot motor yachts. Cabopino is the wildcard, it's smaller and more rustic, but it puts you closer to the Cabopino dunes and the nudist beach at Cala del Faro. If you're staying in the eastern part of Fuengirola, near the castle, Cabopino is actually quicker to reach than Banús. Use the search page to compare availability at each port on your chosen date.

What Happens if the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is known for 300 days of sunshine, but the wind can pick up quickly, especially in the afternoon. The Poniente wind blows from the west and is usually gentle, but the Levante wind from the east can hit 30-40 knots and make the sea choppy. Your skipper will monitor the forecast and has the final say on whether to sail. If the conditions are dangerous, they'll cancel and you'll get a full refund through BoatHire24. If the weather is marginal, you might still go out but stay close to the coast, anchoring in sheltered bays like Cala del Faro or Cabopino. In July and August, the sea is almost always flat calm, so cancellations are rare. In winter, allow for a 10-20% chance of cancellation on any given day.

How to Save Money on Your Private Yacht Charter Fuengirola

Book on a weekday, Monday to Thursday, and you'll pay 15-25% less than weekend rates. Choose a half-day charter (4 hours) instead of a full day, it's enough time for a swim, lunch and a scenic cruise. Pick a sailing yacht instead of a motor yacht, they're cheaper to run and the skipper will use the sails when the wind allows, saving fuel costs. Book at least two weeks in advance, last-minute charters in high season can cost double. Avoid August if you can, July and September are almost as warm but 20-30% cheaper. Consider departing from Cabopino or Marbella Marina instead of Puerto Banús, the boats there tend to be slightly older and therefore cheaper. And always check the listing for fuel inclusion, some operators charge extra for fuel over a certain distance or speed.

What to Expect from the Skipper

Your skipper is a licensed professional with at least a PPER (Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo) or higher qualification. They speak English and Spanish, and often German or French too. They'll meet you at the designated dock 15 minutes before departure, help you board, and give a safety briefing covering life jacket locations, emergency procedures and toilet use. During the charter, they'll navigate, anchor and handle all lines. They won't join you for meals or drinks unless invited, but they'll happily take photos, recommend anchor spots and adjust the music. You can tip them at the end, 10-15% of the charter price is normal. If you have any issues with the skipper, contact BoatHire24 immediately and we'll mediate.

Can You Combine a Yacht Charter with Other Fuengirola Activities

Yes, and many guests do. A common combo is a morning yacht charter followed by lunch at a beach club in Puerto Banús or Marbella. The skipper can drop you at the dock of a beach club like Ocean Club or Nikki Beach, and you can spend the afternoon there. Another option is to charter a RIB for a fast transfer to the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin watching, then return to Fuengirola for tapas in the old town. If you're interested in history, you can anchor off the Fuengirola castle (Sohail Castle) and take a short walk up to see the ruins. For a full day, you could cruise to Estepona, have lunch at a chiringuito on the beach, then visit the old town's flower-filled streets before returning. The skipper will help you plan the itinerary, just let them know what you want to do.

What About Large Groups and Events

If you have more than 12 guests, you'll need a superyacht or a large catamaran. Superyachts of 80 feet and above can take 15-20 guests for a full day, but they're priced on request and usually start around EUR 5,000 in low season. Catamarans up to 55 feet can handle 15-18 guests for around EUR 1,500-2,000 for a half day. For corporate events, you can book a boat with a sound system, a BBQ on deck and a dedicated host. Some operators offer catering packages with paella, tapas and drinks. Wedding proposals are popular, the skipper can arrange champagne, flowers and a secluded anchorage. Just mention it when you book and they'll coordinate the details. All private charters are exclusive to your group, you won't share the boat with strangers.

How Far Can You Go in a Half-Day or Full-Day Charter

In a half-day charter (4 hours), you can cover about 10-15 nautical miles from the departure port. From Puerto Banús, that takes you east to Fuengirola or west to Marbella. You'll have time for one long swim stop or two short ones. In a full-day charter (8 hours), you can reach Estepona (15 NM west) or Cabopino (10 NM east) and still have time for a long lunch and multiple swim stops. If you want to go to Gibraltar (25-30 NM from Banús), you need a full day and a fast boat, a RIB or a motor yacht capable of 25+ knots. Going to Nerja or the Nerja caves is not realistic from Fuengirola in a single day, it's 40 NM east and would take 4 hours each way on a motor yacht. Stick to the western Costa del Sol for day trips.

The Legal Stuff: Insurance, Deposits and Cancellations

Every boat on BoatHire24 has third-party liability insurance and passenger insurance. You're covered for accidents, but not for personal belongings, so leave valuables on shore. The 30% deposit you pay online is held securely by Stripe and released to the operator after the charter is completed. If you cancel more than 14 days before the charter, you get a full refund. Within 14 days, the deposit is non-refundable unless the operator agrees to reschedule. If the operator cancels due to weather or mechanical issues, you get a full refund or a free reschedule. Read the cancellation policy on each listing before booking. For any disputes, contact BoatHire24 support and we'll act as a mediator between you and the operator.

h1: Catamaran Hire Estepona: Affordable Fun on the Costa del Sol
intro:
Estepona is one of the Costa del Sol's most underrated spots for a catamaran charter. You get the calm, clear water of the western Mediterranean, a marina that doesn't try to be Puerto Banús, and a backdrop of the Sierra Bermeja mountains. If you are looking for catamaran hire Estepona, you are probably after a stable, spacious boat that can handle a group without making anyone seasick. Good news: catamarans do exactly that, and Estepona has a decent selection at prices that undercut Marbella by a noticeable margin.

Every catamaran on our platform comes with a licensed skipper. You do not need a licence, and you do not need to know how to dock a 40-foot boat. You just turn up, bring your drinks, and let someone else do the work. The typical charter is a half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours), and you can usually add water toys, a barbecue, or a stop at a beach club. Below is the practical side of booking a catamaran in Estepona, from what you get for your money to which ports actually have catamarans available.
bodyHtml:
Browse the full fleet at BoatHire24.

What You Get with Catamaran Hire Estepona

A catamaran is basically a floating terrace. Two hulls mean it does not heel over like a monohull sailing yacht, so you can walk around without holding on, and your wine glass stays where you put it. Most of the catamarans available for hire in Estepona are between 38 and 50 feet, with capacity for 8 to 12 passengers plus the skipper. You get a flybridge (upper deck with seating and a bimini shade), a saloon with a fridge and sometimes a small galley, and a bow net or trampoline at the front where you can lie down and watch the water pass underneath.

All charters include fuel, insurance, and the skipper. What is not included: food and drinks (though you can bring your own or order a catering package), dockage fees if you decide to stop at a marina for lunch, and any extra water toys like a jet ski or banana ride. Some operators offer a paddleboard or snorkel gear for free, so check the listing details before you book. The skipper handles the navigation and safety, and they usually know the best coves along the Estepona coastline, like the ones near the Guadalmansa river mouth or the rocky points east of the marina.

Departure Ports for Estepona Catamaran Charters

Most catamaran hire Estepona departures happen from two main locations: Puerto Deportivo de Estepona (the main marina) and occasionally from the small dock at the Estepona port proper. The marina is about 10 minutes from the town centre on foot, and it has plenty of parking (paid, about EUR 2 per hour in summer). If you are staying in a hotel along the beachfront, you can probably walk there in 20 minutes.

For larger catamarans (over 50 feet), some operators might ask you to meet in Puerto Banús or Sotogrande, because those marinas have deeper docks and more space. But for the typical 40-foot Lagoon or Fountaine Pajot, Estepona marina is fine. The channel is well marked, and once you are outside the breakwater, you are in open water within 5 minutes. From there, you can head east towards Marbella and Puerto Banús (about 8 NM) or west towards the Guadiaro river and Sotogrande (about 12 NM).

Boat Options: Motor Catamarans vs Sailing Catamarans

When you search for catamaran hire Estepona, you will find two distinct types: motor catamarans and sailing catamarans. The sailing ones still have engines (all charter boats do), but they also have a mast and sails. If you want the experience of raising the main and cutting the engine for an hour of silent cruising, go for a sailing cat. If you just want to get to a swimming spot quickly and park up, a power catamaran is more practical.

Most of the fleet in Estepona is sailing catamarans, because they are more common in Mediterranean charter bases. Motor cats are rarer but available, usually in the 40-50 foot range with top speeds around 20 knots. The sailing cats motor at 6-8 knots under power and can add a couple of knots with sails up. Neither is fast, but that is the point: you are there to relax, not to race. For a full-day trip, a sailing catamaran uses about 30-40 litres of diesel, which is included in the price, so you do not need to worry about fuel surcharges.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Hire in Estepona

Prices for catamaran hire Estepona vary by season, boat size, and whether you want a half-day or full-day charter. In low season (October to April), a half-day on a 40-foot sailing catamaran starts around EUR 900 for up to 8 passengers. Full-day rates go from EUR 1,500. In high season (May to September), the same boat jumps to about EUR 1,400 for a half-day and EUR 2,200 for a full day. Motor catamarans cost roughly 20-30% more because of the higher fuel consumption and engine maintenance.

For a larger group (10-12 people), you need a 45-50 foot catamaran. Prices for those start from EUR 1,800 in low season and go up to EUR 3,000 for a full day in August. Some operators offer a sunset charter (3 hours, usually 6 PM to 9 PM) for around EUR 800-1,200, which is a good option if you just want a short cruise with drinks and photos. Check the listing on our site for exact prices, as they change with availability. You can also search catamarans in Estepona to see current rates.

Best Time of Year for Catamaran Hire Estepona

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate, which means hot summers and mild winters. The best months for a catamaran charter are May, June, September, and October. In May and June, the water temperature is around 18-22 degrees C, air temperature 24-28 degrees C, and the wind is usually a gentle thermal breeze from the west. July and August are hotter (air 30-35 degrees C, water 24-26 degrees C) and more crowded, but the sea is calm in the morning before the Levante wind picks up around 2 PM.

Winter charters (November to March) are possible but less popular. Air temperatures hover around 15-20 degrees C, and the sea can be choppy if the Poniente wind blows. Some operators run half-day trips on sunny days, but you will want a jacket and maybe a windproof layer. The upside is that winter prices are about 40% lower than summer, and you might have the entire coast to yourself. If you are flexible with dates, a November catamaran hire in Estepona is a bargain.

What to Do on a Catamaran Charter in Estepona

Most catamaran itineraries from Estepona head east towards the coast of Marbella or west towards the Guadiaro estuary. A typical half-day trip goes to the area around the Cala del Faro, a small cove with a lighthouse about 3 NM east of Estepona marina. You anchor there for an hour or two, swim, use the paddleboard, and eat lunch. The water is clear and shallow near the rocks, so you can see the seabed at 5 metres depth.

For a full-day charter, you can go further east to Puerto Banús (about 8 NM) and anchor near the beach of San Pedro Alcántara or the dunes of Artola. Alternatively, head west to the mouth of the Guadiaro river, where the water is warmer and the dolphin sightings are common. The skipper will know the best spots based on the wind direction and tide. You can also request a stop at a beach club like the one in Puerto Banús or the Chiringuito de la Playa in Estepona, but you need to pay for mooring or dockage separately (around EUR 20-50 per stop).

Who Is Catamaran Hire Estepona For?

Catamarans are ideal for groups that want to stay together. Families with children, because the stable platform means kids can run around without falling overboard (though life jackets are mandatory for anyone under 12). Corporate groups, because you can hold a meeting on the flybridge and then drop anchor for a swim. Birthday parties, hen or stag groups, and wedding parties all use catamarans as a floating party venue. Just be aware that the skipper has the final say on safety, and if your group gets too rowdy, they will cut the trip short (it happens).

If you are a solo traveller or a couple, a catamaran might feel too big and expensive. You are better off looking at a RIB or speedboat, which costs less and is more intimate. But if you have 6-8 friends and want a day on the water without anyone getting seasick, catamaran hire Estepona is the most comfortable option. You can book directly on our site, where we list the available boats with photos, specs, and skipper profiles. We do not charge booking fees, and the price you see is the price you pay (unless you add extras like catering or water toys).

How to Book Catamaran Hire Estepona

Booking is straightforward. Go to the catamaran hire Estepona page, choose your date and group size, and browse the available boats. Each listing shows the capacity, length, amenities, and price. Click on one to see the full details, including the cancellation policy (most are flexible with 48-hour notice). You can send an enquiry or book directly online. The operator will confirm within 24 hours, and you pay a deposit (usually 30%) upfront, with the balance due on the day of the charter.

If you have questions about a specific boat or need a custom itinerary, use the contact form on the listing page. The operators speak English and Spanish, and some have German or French-speaking skippers. We recommend booking at least a week in advance in summer, because the good catamarans go quickly. For last-minute bookings, check the availability calendar on each listing. Sometimes there are cancellations, and you can snag a half-day slot for a reduced rate.

Local Tips for Your Catamaran Trip in Estepona

Estepona old town is worth a visit before or after your charter. It has narrow cobbled streets with flowerpots on the walls, a few good tapas bars, and a market on Sunday mornings. The marina itself has a few restaurants and a supermarket where you can buy drinks and snacks for the boat. Most operators allow you to bring your own food and drink, but some prohibit glass bottles (use plastic cups instead).

If you are prone to sunburn, bring factor 50 and a hat. The reflection off the water is intense even on a cloudy day. Also, bring a towel and a change of clothes, because you will get wet when you swim. The skipper will have a first aid kit and life jackets, but if you have specific medical needs (like an EpiPen), bring it yourself. And please, do not feed the seagulls. They will remember your boat and follow you for the rest of the day.

Why Estepona Is a Better Base Than Puerto Banús for Catamaran Hire

Puerto Banús gets the Instagram attention, but Estepona has a few advantages if you are hiring a catamaran. First, the marina fees in Estepona are lower, which means the charter prices reflect that. Second, the departure channel is shorter. You are outside the breakwater in 5 minutes, whereas in Banús you sometimes wait 15 minutes for the bridge to open and then negotiate the busy harbour traffic. Third, Estepona has less swell near the coast because the seabed drops off more gradually, so the anchorages feel calmer. If you are worried about seasickness, starting from Estepona instead of Banús makes a real difference, especially for the first hour of the trip.

The coastline east of Estepona towards Marbella has more sandy beaches and fewer rocky cliffs than the stretch west of Banús. That means you can anchor closer to shore and wade in if the water is shallow enough. The area around the Guadalmansa river mouth (about 4 NM east of Estepona) has a sandy bottom and good holding for the anchor, so the catamaran stays put while you swim. The river itself sometimes creates a small current that keeps the water clear, and you can see the sand ripples at 3-4 metres depth. It is a popular spot for local charter boats, so arrive early (before 11 AM) to get the best position.

Catamaran Hire Estepona for Fishing: What You Need to Know

Catamarans are not ideal for serious fishing, but they work for casual trolling or bottom fishing if you bring your own gear. The wide beam and shallow draft of a catamaran mean it drifts more in a crosswind than a monohull, so you will need a sea anchor or a drift sock to stay over a spot. Most skippers will allow fishing from the back platform or the bow, but they will not supply rods or bait. You need to bring your own tackle and a valid fishing licence (available online from the Junta de Andalucía for about EUR 25 per year for non-residents).

The waters off Estepona hold bream, sea bass, and the occasional amberjack near the rocky outcrops east of the marina. If you head west towards the Guadiaro river mouth, you might hook a small tope or a ray in the sandy areas. Do not expect trophy fish. The Costa del Sol is overfished, and the commercial trawlers work the same grounds. For a proper fishing trip, you are better off with a dedicated fishing boat that has rod holders, a fish finder, and a skipper who knows the wrecks. But if you just want to dangle a line while the catamaran is anchored for lunch, it is a pleasant way to pass the time.

Sunset Catamaran Charters in Estepona: Timing and Costs

Sunset charters on a catamaran in Estepona run from about 6 PM to 9 PM in summer (May to September) and 4 PM to 7 PM in winter. The sun sets behind the mountains west of Estepona, so you get a good view if you anchor near the shore or head a mile offshore for an unobstructed horizon. The wind usually drops in the evening, so the sea flattens out, and the catamaran barely rocks. It is the most comfortable time to be on the water, and the light is good for photos.

Prices for a sunset catamaran hire in Estepona start around EUR 800 for a 40-foot sailing catamaran with up to 8 passengers in low season, and go up to EUR 1,400 in August. Some operators include a bottle of cava and soft drinks, but you should check the listing to confirm. Food is usually extra or BYO. The shorter duration means you do not need a full catering package, just some tapas and a bottle of wine. The skipper will anchor at a spot with a view of the sunset, and you can swim if the water is warm enough (usually until late October). Book these in advance because they are popular with couples and small groups, and the good boats go first.

What Happens If the Weather Turns Bad on Your Catamaran Charter

The Costa del Sol has reliable weather, but the Levante wind can blow from the east at 20-30 knots, especially in July and August afternoons. If the forecast shows winds over 25 knots or a yellow weather warning, the skipper will cancel or reschedule the charter at no cost to you. If you are already on the water and the wind picks up, the skipper will head back to port early. You will not get a refund for the unused time, but most operators offer a partial credit if you rebook within 30 days.

For catamarans, the main risk is not the wind itself but the chop that builds up in the Strait of Gibraltar. The sea state can go from flat to 1.5 metre waves in an hour when the Levante blows against the current. Catamarans handle chop well because the two hulls cut through the waves, but the motion becomes a fast, jerky bounce rather than a slow roll. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure, even if the forecast looks calm. The skipper will have a supply of ginger biscuits and plastic bags, but prevention is better than cure.

How to Choose the Right Catamaran for Your Group Size in Estepona

Catamaran hire Estepona listings usually show a maximum capacity of 10 or 12 passengers, but that number includes the skipper. So a boat listed for 10 people means you can have 9 guests plus the skipper. The legal limit is based on the boat's safety certificate, and the skipper will enforce it. If your group has 8 adults and 4 children, you need a boat with a capacity of at least 13 (12 guests plus skipper). The children count as passengers even if they are small, so do not try to squeeze in extra people. The skipper will check the headcount before departure and can refuse to leave if you exceed the limit.

For a group of 6 or fewer, a 38-40 foot catamaran is fine. You will have plenty of space on the flybridge and in the saloon. For 8-10 people, go for a 44-48 foot boat. The extra length gives you a larger cockpit and a bigger bow trampoline, which is where most people sit anyway. For 12 people, you need a 50+ foot catamaran, which is rare in Estepona but available. Those larger boats often have a generator and air conditioning, which is useful if you plan to stay in the saloon during the hot afternoon. Check the amenities list on each listing to see if the boat has a generator, because without it, the fridge and lights run on the engine battery, and the skipper will not let you drain it.

Combining Catamaran Hire Estepona with a Trip to Gibraltar or Marbella

A full-day catamaran charter from Estepona can cover a lot of coastline. If you head east, you can reach Puerto Banús in about 1.5 hours at cruising speed, anchor near the Banús beach for a swim, and then motor back to Estepona in the afternoon. That gives you a tour of the Marbella coastline without staying overnight. If you head west, you can go to the Guadiaro river mouth and then continue to Sotogrande marina (about 2 hours from Estepona). Sotogrande has a beach club and a few restaurants, but the marina is private and you need permission to dock (the skipper will arrange it in advance).

Some full-day charters go all the way to the Strait of Gibraltar, about 15 NM west of Estepona. That takes 2.5-3 hours each way, so you need a full day (8 hours) to make it worthwhile. The area near the Strait has a good chance of dolphin sightings, especially common dolphins and striped dolphins, and sometimes pilot whales in the summer. The skipper will know the spots where the fishing boats attract the dolphins. You cannot swim with them (it is illegal in Spain), but you can watch them bow-ride for 10-15 minutes before they move on. If you want to see the Rock of Gibraltar from the water, this is the charter to book, but be prepared for a longer trip and a bumpier ride if the wind picks up.

title: Motor Yacht Charter Estepona: Day Excursions

h1: Motor Yacht Charter Estepona: Day Excursions with Skipper
intro:
You want a motor yacht charter in Estepona for a day on the Costa del Sol. The answer is straightforward: you can hire a private motor yacht with a professional skipper from around EUR 1,200 for a full day, departing from Puerto de Estepona. BoatHire24 lists verified boats, all including fuel, insurance, and a crew member who knows the local waters. You get a proper day out, not a rushed tourist trip.

Estepona sits between Marbella and Gibraltar, so your day can include dolphin spotting in the Strait, a swim stop at Cala del Faro, or lunch in the old town. The port is less crowded than Puerto Banús, which means quicker departure and more time on the water. You control the itinerary, the music, and the pace.
bodyHtml:
What a Motor Yacht Charter in Estepona Includes

Every motor yacht charter on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper as standard. That means you do not need a boating licence or any experience. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety. You just turn up with your group and enjoy. Most charters also include fuel for a standard day (usually 8 hours), insurance, and onboard amenities like a sound system, a fridge, and a shaded deck. Some yachts have a bow sun pad, a wet bar, or a small cabin for changing. Check the listing for specifics, but the base package is always skipper, fuel, and insurance.

Food and drinks are not included unless you book a catered option. You can bring your own or ask the skipper to stop at a chandlery on the way out. The crew can recommend a local supermarket or a deli in Estepona old town. Many yachts have a cooler and a barbecue grill, so you can eat onboard without leaving the water.

Departure Port: Puerto de Estepona

The main departure point for a motor yacht charter in Estepona is Puerto de Estepona, a working marina with around 400 berths. It is quieter than Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina, which means less traffic and easier parking. The marina has a few restaurants and a small shop for last-minute supplies. You meet the skipper at the berth, usually 15 minutes before departure. The port is a 10-minute walk from the old town, so you can combine a morning stroll with an afternoon charter.

For larger yachts (over 15 metres), some charters depart from Sotogrande or La Duquesa, both a short drive east. BoatHire24 listings show the exact departure port, so check before booking. If you are staying in Estepona, the local port is your best bet for a quick start.

Boat Options for Motor Yacht Charter Estepona

Motor yachts in Estepona range from 8-metre day boats to 20-metre flybridge cruisers. A typical 10-metre motor yacht sleeps 6-8 passengers for a day trip and costs from around EUR 1,200. A 15-metre flybridge with a saloon and a sun deck runs from EUR 2,500. Superyachts over 20 metres are available on request, with prices starting at EUR 5,000. Every boat is privately owned and maintained, so condition varies. BoatHire24 verifies each listing with photos and a description, but you can ask the owner for a video walkthrough before booking.

If you want speed, look for a RIB or a centre-console boat. Those hit 30-40 knots and can cover more ground in a day. For comfort, a flybridge motor yacht with a stabiliser is better for longer trips to Gibraltar or Marbella. Catamarans are also available if you prefer stability and deck space, but the primary search here is motor yachts.

Pricing Guidance for a Day Excursion

Prices for a motor yacht charter in Estepona depend on boat size, season, and duration. Here are rough ranges:

  • 8-10 metres: EUR 1,200-1,800 for 8 hours.
  • 10-15 metres: EUR 1,800-3,500 for 8 hours.
  • 15-20 metres: EUR 3,500-6,000 for 8 hours.
  • 20+ metres: EUR 6,000-15,000, price on request.

Half-day charters (4 hours) are available from around EUR 800. Evening cruises for sunset are usually the same price as a half-day. Fuel is included in the base price for a standard day, but if you plan to go to Gibraltar and back (about 30 NM each way), the skipper may charge a fuel supplement. Always confirm the fuel policy in the booking message. You can compare prices on the search page.

Best Seasons for Motor Yacht Charter Estepona

April to October is the prime season for a motor yacht charter in Estepona. July and August are the busiest and most expensive, with prices up to 30% higher than May or September. Water temperature hits 24-26 degrees C in August, so swimming is comfortable. June and September offer a good balance of warm weather and lower crowds. Winter charters (November to March) are possible but less popular because the sea can be choppy and the air temperature drops to 15-18 degrees C. Some boats are laid up for maintenance in winter, so availability is limited.

Wind is a factor in Estepona because the Levante (easterly) can blow hard in the Strait. Skippers monitor forecasts and will advise on safe routes. If the wind is above 20 knots, they may suggest a sheltered itinerary along the coast rather than crossing to Gibraltar. You can still do a day trip, but the ride will be bumpier.

Popular Day Excursion Routes from Estepona

From Puerto de Estepona, you have several routes for a day trip. The most common is north-east towards Marbella and Puerto Banús. That takes about 30 minutes at 20 knots, passing beaches like Playa del Cristo and the cliffs of Cala del Faro. You can stop for a swim at Cala del Faro, a rocky cove with clear water, then continue to Puerto Banús for a lunch stop at a beach club. The return trip adds another 30 minutes, so the whole loop is about 5-6 hours with a lunch break.

Another route is south-west to the Strait of Gibraltar, about 20 NM from Estepona. Here you can spot pilot whales, common dolphins, and occasionally orcas in summer. The skipper knows the best spots and will slow down for photos. The trip takes 40 minutes each way, leaving plenty of time for swimming and a picnic. You can also anchor off the coast of Gibraltar and see the Rock from the water, but you need a passport if you go ashore.

For a longer day, head east to Marbella Marina or Cabopino. Cabopino has a sandy beach and a dune reserve, good for a quiet swim. The distance from Estepona to Cabopino is about 15 NM, so 45 minutes at cruising speed. A full-day charter can cover Estepona to Marbella and back, with a stop for lunch at a chiringuito in Cabopino. You can read more about itineraries on the blog.

Who Is a Motor Yacht Charter in Estepona For

This is for groups of 4-12 people who want a private day out on the water. It suits families with children because the skipper handles safety and you can set a relaxed pace. It also works for corporate groups or stag and hen parties, provided you respect the skipper's rules on noise and alcohol. Couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise can book a smaller boat with a champagne package. The main point is that you have the boat to yourselves, no strangers.

If you are a solo traveller or a couple on a budget, a shared charter might be cheaper, but BoatHire24 does not offer shared bookings. You can join a group through a local tour operator, but you lose the privacy. For a proper motor yacht charter, you book the whole boat.

How to Book a Motor Yacht Charter in Estepona

You book directly through BoatHire24. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage, enter Estepona as the port, select motor yacht, and pick your date. The system shows available boats with prices and photos. You can send a booking request with your preferred date and group size. The owner responds within 24 hours to confirm availability and answer questions. Payment is handled through the platform, and a deposit (usually 50%) secures the booking. The balance is due 7 days before departure.

Cancellation policy varies by owner, but most offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days before. For last-minute bookings (within 7 days), you pay the full amount upfront. Always read the terms before paying. If you have special requests like a specific route or catering, mention them in the booking message. The skipper can adjust the itinerary within reason.

Local Tips for Your Day in Estepona

Estepona old town is worth a visit before or after your charter. It has cobblestone streets, flower pots, and a few tapas bars. The port is a 10-minute walk from the old town, so you can park your car there or take a taxi. For supplies, Mercadona in Estepona has a good selection of drinks and snacks. Avoid glass bottles on the boat; use plastic or cans. The skipper will have a bin for rubbish.

If you want to swim, bring a towel and sunscreen. The sun is strong from May to September, even on cloudy days. The water temperature in August is 24-26 degrees C, so a wetsuit is not needed. In June and October, the water is cooler, around 20-22 degrees C. You can also bring snorkel gear; some boats have masks and fins onboard. Check with the owner before booking if you need specific equipment.

For a longer excursion, consider the Nerja caves, but that is about 80 km east of Estepona, so you would need a full-day charter with a fast boat. Most skippers recommend staying within 20 NM of the port to maximise time on the water. The Strait of Gibraltar is the best option for wildlife and a sense of adventure.

Why Book Through BoatHire24

BoatHire24 lists only boats that include a licensed skipper, so you avoid the hassle of finding a captain separately. All boats are privately owned and vetted for safety equipment and insurance. You book directly with the owner, which cuts out middleman fees. The platform handles payments and provides a secure booking system. You can read the owner's profile and previous guest reviews before committing. If something goes wrong, the support team helps resolve disputes.

You are not limited to Estepona. The same platform covers Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. If you want to compare options across ports, use the search page to filter by boat type, capacity, and price. For more advice on choosing a boat, check the blog.

Comparing Estepona with Other Costa del Sol Ports

Estepona sits about 20 km west of Puerto Banús and 30 km west of Marbella Marina. The main difference is crowd size. Puerto Banús is a glitzy hub with 50-metre superyachts and beach clubs charging EUR 50 for a sun lounger. Estepona port is a working marina with fewer tourists and lower parking costs (around EUR 15 for the day versus EUR 30 in Banús). The water quality is the same, and the sea conditions are similar because the coastline is mostly open. If you want a quieter start with less bow-to-stern traffic, Estepona wins. If you want to step off the boat into a flashy restaurant, Banús is better. Sotogrande, 15 km east, is even quieter and has a golf resort vibe, but fewer charter boats are based there.

For a motor yacht charter in Estepona, you get the same access to the Strait of Gibraltar and the Marbella coastline as you would from Banús, but you save 20 minutes of cruising time if your goal is the Strait. The trade-off is that the marina facilities are basic: one fuel dock, a small chandlery, and a couple of cafes. No superyacht berths either, so if your group is 20+ people, you may need to depart from Sotogrande or Banús. Check the boat length on the listing before booking.

Fuel Costs and What a Standard Day Covers

Fuel is included in the base price for a standard 8-hour day, but that assumes a cruising speed of 18-22 knots and a total distance of 50-70 NM. If you push the throttle to 30 knots for a full day, you burn more fuel, and the skipper may charge a supplement. For example, a 10-metre motor yacht with twin 250 HP engines burns about 80 litres per hour at 20 knots. At current diesel prices in Spain (around EUR 1.40 per litre), that is EUR 112 per hour. Over 8 hours, that is EUR 896 in fuel alone. The base price covers this, but only if you stay within the standard itinerary. If you insist on a full-speed run to Gibraltar and back (60 NM round trip at 30 knots), you add about 40 litres extra, which is EUR 56. Most skippers absorb that, but always ask in the booking message.

The fuel policy is usually stated in the listing. If it says "fuel included for up to 8 hours of operation", you are fine. If it says "fuel included for up to 50 NM", then any extra distance costs you. You can negotiate a flat fuel supplement before confirming the booking. The BoatHire24 platform lets you message the owner directly, so use that to clarify.

Booking for Large Groups: 10-12 Passengers

For a group of 10-12 people on a motor yacht charter in Estepona, you need a boat of at least 12 metres. Most 10-metre yachts are licensed for 8-10 passengers, so you will exceed the limit if you have 12. A 14-metre flybridge can take 12 comfortably, with seating on the aft deck, the saloon, and the flybridge. Prices for a 14-metre yacht start around EUR 2,800 for 8 hours. Check the passenger capacity on the listing; it is a legal limit based on the boat's safety certificate. Do not try to sneak extra guests onboard. The skipper will refuse to depart. If you have 14 people, you need two boats or a superyacht. Two 8-metre boats side by side work well for stag groups or family reunions, and the cost per person drops to about EUR 150 each.

For corporate events, some owners offer catering packages with paella, tapas, and drinks. That adds EUR 30-50 per person. You can also bring your own food, but the skipper will need to know in advance for fridge space. Avoid red wine on white upholstery; stick to white wine or beer.

Weather and Sea Conditions in Estepona

The Levante wind is the main risk for a motor yacht charter in Estepona. It blows from the east, funneling through the Strait of Gibraltar and creating short, steep waves. In summer, the Levante is strongest in July and August, often reaching 20-25 knots in the afternoon. Skippers usually depart early (9 am) to avoid the build-up. By 2 pm, the sea can be choppy, especially west of Estepona towards the Strait. The Poniente wind from the west is lighter and creates calmer seas. Check the wind forecast on Windy or the skipper's local knowledge. If the Levante is forecast at 25 knots, the skipper may suggest staying in the lee of the coast near Marbella, where the waves are smaller. Do not expect a refund if the weather is poor; the skipper decides on safety grounds, and the trip goes ahead with a modified route.

Water temperature in Estepona peaks at 26 degrees C in August and drops to 16 degrees C in February. For swimming, June to October is best. In May, the water is 18-20 degrees C, which is okay for a quick dip but not for lounging. Bring a rash vest if you are sensitive to cold. The visibility for snorkelling is 5-10 metres along the coast, better near the rocky areas like Cala del Faro.

What to Do in Estepona Before or After the Charter

Estepona old town is a 10-minute walk from the port. The streets are lined with flower pots and whitewashed buildings. You can grab a coffee at Plaza de las Flores or a beer at a terrace bar. The market on Wednesday mornings sells local produce and crafts. If you have time, walk up to the Castillo de Estepona, a 16th-century watchtower with views of the coast. It is free and takes 15 minutes. For lunch after the charter, try El Murallon for grilled fish or La Escollera for paella. Both are near the port and serve fresh seafood. Book a table for 2 pm to avoid the rush.

If you are driving, park in the underground car park at the port (EUR 15 per day) or on the street near the old town (free after 8 pm). The port also has a taxi rank. A taxi from Estepona to Marbella costs about EUR 25 and takes 20 minutes. For a full day out, combine the charter with a walk through the old town and a late lunch. That makes a solid 10-hour itinerary without rushing.

Every charter booked through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the best anchorages, and the nearest chiringuito that does decent grilled fish. Motor yachts from around 8 to 20 metres. These are the fastest option, typically cruising at 20-25 knots. Good for covering distance if you want to reach Marbella or Gibraltar in under an hour. Prices from around EUR 600 for a half day.

RIBs and speedboats from 6 to 10 metres. Open boats, no cabin, but fast and fun for a quick blast along the coast. Prices from around EUR 350 for a half day.

Fishing boats specifically equipped for angling, with rod holders, fish finders, and a skipper who knows the local marks. Prices from around EUR 400 for a half day.

All boats are privately chartered, meaning you and your group have exclusive use. No sharing with strangers.

A typical private yacht charter Estepona might head east towards the Marbella coastline. You can anchor off the beach at San Pedro de Alcántara, near the Guadalmina River mouth, where the water is shallow and clear. Further east you reach Puerto Banús, which is worth a slow cruise past to see the superyachts from the water, but you do not need to dock there.

Heading west, you can go towards the Punta de la Doncella and then on to the Strait of Gibraltar. The waters off Tarifa and Algeciras are rich in marine life. On a good day you see common dolphins, striped dolphins, and occasionally fin whales. The strait is a migratory corridor, so the best months for wildlife are April to October.

For a quieter option, head to the coves around the Cala del Faro or the Playa del Cristo. These are sheltered spots with good swimming conditions. Your skipper will know which anchorages are sheltered from the wind on any given day.

Deposits are usually 30-50% at booking, with the balance due a week before departure or on the day. Cancellation policies vary, but most offer a full refund if you cancel more than 14 days out.

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 days of sunshine a year. For a private yacht charter Estepona, the best months are May to October. Sea temperatures range from 18 degrees C in May to 26 degrees C in August. Air temperatures hit 30-35 degrees C in July and August, so bring a hat and plenty of water.

April and November can be pleasant but the water is cooler (16-18 degrees C) and there is a higher chance of wind or rain. December to March is possible if you are hardy, but many boats are laid up for maintenance and the sea can be rough. If you want to swim comfortably, aim for June to September.

On the day, you meet the skipper at the assigned berth, board, and go through a safety briefing. Then you cast off and enjoy your private yacht charter Estepona.

If you need help choosing, contact BoatHire24 support and we can recommend a boat based on your group size and budget. We do not charge booking fees.

Who Is a Private Yacht Charter Estepona For

A private yacht charter Estepona works for couples, families, groups of friends, and corporate events. The maximum group size depends on the boat, but most yachts take 8 to 12 passengers comfortably. Some larger catamarans can take up to 20.

If you are celebrating a birthday, anniversary, or wedding, you can arrange catering and decorations through the boat owner. For a corporate day out, you can use the yacht as a floating meeting room or team-building venue. The skipper will tailor the route to your preferences.

Children are welcome on most boats, but check the listing for age restrictions. Life jackets are provided for all sizes. Pets are not usually allowed, but some owners make exceptions, so ask.

Frequently Asked Questions About Private Yacht Charter Estepona

Estepona Marina: Your Departure Point for a Private Yacht Charter Estepona

Estepona Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Estepona) is a modern facility with around 400 berths. It is less flashy than Puerto Banús but more practical. You will find a fuel dock, water and electricity hookups, and a few bars and restaurants on the marina front. The marina is a short walk from Estepona old town, so you can grab breakfast or supplies before boarding. For a private yacht charter Estepona, the marina offers easy access to both the eastern and western routes. The harbour entrance is straightforward, and there is no tide to worry about in the Mediterranean. Parking is available nearby if you drive, but most visitors arrive by taxi from Marbella or Málaga airport.

Why Estepona Beats Puerto Banús for a Private Yacht Charter Estepona

Puerto Banús gets the crowds and the Instagram crowd. Estepona gets better value and less hassle. A private yacht charter Estepona typically costs 10-20% less than the equivalent charter from Banús because the marina fees are lower and the demand is not as manic. You also avoid the queue to leave the harbour on a Saturday morning. The coastline west of Estepona is less built up, with more natural coves and fewer beach clubs blasting music. If you want a relaxed day on the water without the noise and expense of the Banús scene, Estepona is the smarter choice. You can still cruise past Banús if you want to see the superyachts, but you do not have to dock there.

What to Expect from the Skipper on a Private Yacht Charter Estepona

The skipper is not a tour guide but they know the area well. On a private yacht charter Estepona, the skipper will ask about your preferences before casting off: do you want to swim, eat, explore, or just cruise? They will suggest a route based on the wind, sea state, and your interests. Most skippers speak English and Spanish. They are licensed by the Spanish authorities and have the required safety certifications. They will give a safety briefing at the start and show you where the life jackets, fire extinguishers, and radio are. You do not need to tip, but if the skipper does a good job, a 10-15% tip is appreciated. Cash is easiest.

Food and Drink Options on a Private Yacht Charter Estepona

You can bring your own food and drink on most charters. The boat will have a cooler with ice, and some yachts have a small galley with a fridge and a hob. For a private yacht charter Estepona, you can also arrange catering through the boat owner. Options range from a simple platter of Spanish ham, cheese, and olives to a full sit-down meal with paella and grilled fish. Drinks can be provided too, including beer, wine, cava, and soft drinks. If you want to stop at a chiringuito for lunch, the skipper can recommend one and dock if the conditions allow. The chiringuito at Playa del Cristo is popular for its grilled sardines and cold beer. Expect to pay around EUR 30-50 per person for a decent lunch onshore.

Wildlife Encounters on a Private Yacht Charter Estepona

The waters off Estepona are part of the Alboran Sea, a rich feeding ground for marine life. On a private yacht charter Estepona, you have a good chance of seeing common dolphins and bottlenose dolphins year-round. From April to October, you might also see pilot whales, fin whales, and orcas. The Strait of Gibraltar is one of the best places in Europe for whale watching. Your skipper can adjust the route to spend more time in the strait if wildlife is a priority. Remember that the animals are wild and sightings are not guaranteed. Do not expect a dolphin show. If you want a guaranteed encounter, book a dedicated wildlife-watching trip from Tarifa instead.

What to Bring for a Private Yacht Charter Estepona

Pack light. You need swimwear, a towel, sun cream (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses, and a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure. The boat will have a first aid kit but bring your own if you need specific items. A waterproof phone pouch is useful for photos. Do not bring glass bottles on board as broken glass is a hazard. Most skippers ask you to leave shoes at the dock and go barefoot or wear non-marking deck shoes. If you are chartering for a full day, bring a change of clothes for the evening. The skipper will have water on board, but bring your own if you prefer a specific brand.

Private Yacht Charter Estepona for Corporate Events

A corporate day on the water works well for team building, client entertainment, or a board meeting away from the office. For a private yacht charter Estepona, you can book a motor yacht or catamaran with a large deck area and a shaded saloon. Many boats have Bluetooth speakers, a TV screen, and Wi-Fi. You can arrange a catered lunch with local wines and beers. The skipper will keep the cruise smooth and stop at a calm anchorage for swimming or water sports. Prices for a corporate charter start from around EUR 1,500 for a half day on a 12-metre motor yacht. You can also book a sunset cruise for a more relaxed networking event. Contact the owner through BoatHire24 to discuss specific requirements.

Multi-Day Private Yacht Charter Estepona

If a day is not enough, you can book a multi-day private yacht charter Estepona. Larger yachts with cabins allow you to sleep on board and explore further afield. You could sail to Gibraltar, spend a night in Sotogrande, or head to the coast of North Africa. A typical two-day itinerary: depart Estepona, cruise to the Strait of Gibraltar, anchor for lunch and swimming, then dock at Algeciras or Gibraltar for the night. The next day, you head back along the coast, stopping at Marbella or Puerto Banús. Prices for a multi-day charter start from around EUR 2,000 per day for a 12-metre motor yacht with two cabins. Fuel, food, and marina fees are extra. Book well in advance as multi-day charters are popular in summer.

How to Get to Estepona for Your Private Yacht Charter Estepona

Estepona is easy to reach. Málaga airport is 80 km away, about a 50-minute drive by taxi or rental car. Gibraltar airport is 20 km away, about 25 minutes by taxi. If you are staying in Marbella or Puerto Banús, the drive to Estepona is 20-30 minutes along the AP-7 motorway. Taxis from Marbella cost around EUR 30-40. From Málaga airport, expect to pay EUR 80-100. You can also take a bus from Málaga to Estepona bus station, which is a 10-minute walk from the marina. If you are driving, the marina has paid parking nearby. For a private yacht charter Estepona, aim to arrive at the marina 15 minutes before your scheduled departure time to meet the skipper and complete the safety briefing.

title: Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day: Speed Cruise
metaDescription: Book a motor yacht charter Marbella day cruise with skipper. Speed from Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro. Prices from around EUR 1,500. Reserve online.
h1: Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day: Speed Cruise with Skipper
intro:
You want a day on the water in Marbella that feels fast, private, and a bit flash. A motor yacht charter Marbella day trip gives you exactly that: a sleek, powerful boat, a licensed skipper who knows the coast, and a route that can take you from the bling of Puerto Banús to the quiet coves east of Marbella in under an hour. No queues, no crowded ferries, just you, your group, and the Mediterranean doing what it does best.

BoatHire24 lists dozens of motor yachts available for day charters out of Marbella, Puerto Banús, and nearby ports. Every booking includes a professional skipper, so you don’t need a licence or any experience. You just turn up, step aboard, and decide where you want to go. The boat does the rest.
bodyHtml:
What a Motor Yacht Charter Marbella Day Includes

A typical day charter on a motor yacht in Marbella runs from around 10:00 to 18:00, though you can often arrange shorter or longer hours. The boat comes fuelled, cleaned, and ready. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety. You get the use of the yacht’s amenities: sun pads, a shaded cockpit, a sound system, a small galley, and a marine toilet. Most yachts also have a swim platform and a freshwater shower for after you dip in the sea.

What is not included is food and drink, unless you pay extra for a catering package. You can bring your own supplies or ask the charter company to arrange a hamper or a restaurant stop. Fuel is usually included in the day rate for a fixed itinerary, but if you decide to go much further than planned, there may be a surcharge. Check the terms before you confirm.

For a full list of available yachts and to compare what each includes, use the search page on BoatHire24.

Typical Itineraries for a Day Cruise from Marbella

Most motor yacht charters from Marbella head west towards the Gibraltar Strait or east towards the Costa Tropical. The classic Marbella day trip goes from Puerto Banús out to Cala del Faro, a rocky cove with clear water about 8 NM east. That leg takes 30-40 minutes at cruising speed on a 40-foot motor yacht. You drop anchor, swim, have lunch, then maybe cruise back past the Marbella coastline before returning to port.

Another popular route is west to Estepona, then on to the dolphin grounds off the Strait of Gibraltar. The pilot whales and common dolphins are around most of the year, and the run from Puerto Banús to the strait is about 20 NM, so you need a fast boat to do it in a day without rushing. A 50-knot motor yacht can get you there in 25 minutes. That leaves plenty of time for a swim stop near Estepona old town or a lunch at a chiringuito on the beach.

If you want to go further, some motor yachts can reach the Nerja caves in about 1.5 hours from Marbella, but that makes for a long day. Most day charters stick to the 10-30 NM radius around the departure port.

Departure Ports and What Each Offers

Your motor yacht charter Marbella day can start from several ports. Puerto Banús is the most popular: it has the biggest concentration of charter yachts, easy parking, and plenty of bars and restaurants for a post-cruise drink. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter, closer to the town centre, and often has slightly lower berthing fees, which can mean a lower charter price.

Cabopino, east of Marbella near the Artola dunes, is a smaller port with a relaxed vibe. It is a good option if you are staying in the Calahonda area. Estepona marina is west of Marbella, near the old town and the new port development. Sotogrande is further west, closer to Gibraltar, and tends to have larger yachts and a more exclusive atmosphere. Benalmádena, east of Marbella, is a busy port with a wide range of boats and good road access from Málaga.

Each port has its own character, but the quality of the charter experience depends more on the boat and the skipper than on the departure point. You can browse all available yachts by port on the BoatHire24 homepage.

Boat Options for a Motor Yacht Day Charter

The term “motor yacht” covers a lot of ground. For a day charter in Marbella, you will typically find boats from 30 to 60 feet. A 35-40 foot motor yacht like a Fairline Targa or a Sunseeker Portofino is a good size for up to 8 guests. It has enough space to move around, a decent galley, and a comfortable interior cabin if you need to escape the sun.

If you have a larger group, look at 50-60 foot yachts like a Princess V58 or a Azimut 55. These can take up to 12 guests and have more deck space, a larger flybridge, and better sound systems. For a smaller, faster experience, consider a RIB or a speedboat. These are not technically motor yachts, but they offer a similar day-cruise experience at a lower price point, often from around EUR 600 for a half day.

Superyachts over 80 feet are also available for day charters, but expect to pay from EUR 5,000 upwards, and you will need to book well in advance. The BoatHire24 blog has a guide to choosing the right boat size for your group.

Pricing Guidance for a Day Charter

Prices for a motor yacht charter Marbella day vary widely depending on the boat size, age, and the season. In low season (November to February), a 35-foot motor yacht might cost from around EUR 1,200 for a full day. In high season (June to September), the same boat can be EUR 1,800 to 2,500. Larger yachts, over 50 feet, start from around EUR 2,500 in low season and go up to EUR 4,000 or more in August.

RIB and speedboat day charters are cheaper: from EUR 600 for a half day, EUR 900 for a full day. These boats are faster but have less comfort and shade. Fishing boat charters are a different category, usually priced per angler rather than per boat, starting from around EUR 100 per person for a half day.

Always ask what is included in the quoted price. Some operators include fuel, water, and ice; others add them as extras. The final price you see on BoatHire24 includes the boat, the skipper, and standard amenities. Any optional extras like food, drinks, or water toys are listed separately.

Best Time of Year for a Motor Yacht Day Cruise

The Costa del Sol has a mild climate year-round, but the best months for a motor yacht charter Marbella day are May, June, September, and October. The sea temperature is warm enough for swimming (20-25 degrees C), the air temperature is pleasant (25-30 degrees C), and the marinas are less crowded than in July and August. July and August are peak season: the weather is hot (often 35 degrees C), the sea is warm, but the ports and anchorages can be busy. You will need to book at least a week in advance.

Winter charters are possible, especially on sunny days, but the water is cooler (15-18 degrees C) and the days are shorter. Some operators run reduced schedules from November to February. If you want to see dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar, the best months are April to October, though they are present year-round.

How to Book a Motor Yacht Charter in Marbella

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, select your port (Puerto Banús, Marbella, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena), choose the date, and filter by boat type to motor yacht. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specifications, and prices. Click on a listing to see the full details, including the itinerary options, what is included, and the cancellation policy.

Once you pick a boat, you can send a booking request directly through the site. The charter company will confirm availability and send you a payment link. Most require a 50% deposit to secure the date, with the balance due on the day of the charter. You can also contact the company directly if you have specific questions about the boat or the route.

If you are unsure which boat suits your group, use the chat function on the site or call the number listed. The team at BoatHire24 can recommend a boat based on your group size, budget, and preferred activities.

Who Is This Charter For?

A motor yacht charter Marbella day is for anyone who wants a private, fast, and comfortable day on the sea. It works well for couples looking for a romantic escape, families with older children who can swim, or groups of friends celebrating a birthday or a stag/hen do. It is also popular with business clients who want to impress guests or hold a small meeting on the water.

If you have young children or people with limited mobility, check the boat’s layout. Some motor yachts have steep steps and narrow gangways. RIBs are not suitable for anyone with back problems or who is pregnant, as the ride can be bumpy. For a smoother, more stable experience, consider a catamaran instead. Catamarans have more deck space and less motion, but they are slower and typically more expensive per hour.

Whatever your group, the skipper is there to ensure a safe and enjoyable day. You do not need to know anything about boats. Just tell the skipper where you want to go, and they will handle the rest.

Local Highlights You Can Visit on a Day Charter

From Marbella, you can visit a range of coastal spots. Cala del Faro is a small, sheltered cove east of Marbella, near the Cabopino dunes. It is good for swimming and snorkelling, with clear water and rocky seabed. Further east, the beach at Artola is quieter than the central Marbella beaches.

West of Marbella, the coast around Estepona has several small bays, including Playa del Cristo and the area near the Estepona lighthouse. The old town of Estepona is visible from the sea, with its whitewashed buildings and colourful flower pots. If you head further west towards Sotogrande, you pass the luxury villas and golf resorts that line the shore.

The Strait of Gibraltar is a special area for wildlife. The nutrient-rich waters attract dolphins, pilot whales, and sometimes orcas. A motor yacht can get you there fast, and the skipper will know the best spots to look for marine life. Remember that the strait can have strong currents and wind, so check the weather forecast before you go.

What to Bring on a Day Charter

Pack light. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe if possible), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket or windbreaker. The wind on a fast motor yacht can feel cool even on a hot day. A camera or phone for photos is useful, but keep it in a waterproof case. You can bring your own food and drinks, but check with the charter company first. Some do not allow glass bottles on board for safety reasons.

If you plan to swim, bring a mask and snorkel. Most boats do not provide them. If you want to listen to your own music, check if the boat has Bluetooth or an AUX input. Many modern motor yachts have a good sound system, but older ones may not.

The skipper will have life jackets for everyone, a first aid kit, and a VHF radio. You do not need to bring any safety equipment. Just your personal items and a good attitude.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Far Can You Cruise in a Day from Marbella

The range of a motor yacht charter Marbella day depends on the boat's speed and fuel capacity. A typical 40-foot motor yacht cruising at 20 knots can cover about 40 nautical miles each way in a day, giving you a comfortable 80 NM round trip with time for stops. That gets you from Puerto Banús to the Nerja caves (25 NM east) or to the dolphin grounds off Tarifa (30 NM west). A faster 50-knot yacht can push to 60 NM each way, reaching the cliffs of La Herradura or the Bay of Algeciras. The skipper will plan the route to avoid running the tanks dry, so you usually get a 6-7 hour cruising window with a 1-2 hour anchor stop. If you want to go further, book a longer charter or an overnight trip.

Fuel Costs and Surcharges Explained

Fuel is one of the biggest variables on a motor yacht charter Marbella day. Many operators include fuel for a standard itinerary of 30-40 NM total. If you ask to go further, expect a surcharge of around EUR 50-100 per additional 10 NM, depending on the boat's consumption. A 40-foot motor yacht burns roughly 80-120 litres per hour at cruising speed, which at current diesel prices (around EUR 1.40 per litre) adds up to EUR 112-168 per hour. Some charter companies quote a flat rate with fuel included, while others charge fuel at cost after the trip. Always ask before booking. If you book through BoatHire24, the listing will state whether fuel is included or extra. For a budget-conscious day, stick to the included itinerary and enjoy the swim stops close to port.

What to Expect from the Skipper

Every motor yacht charter Marbella day includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters. They handle the navigation, mooring, and safety briefings. They also know the best anchorages, like the quiet side of Cala del Faro or the sandbar at Cabopino. Most skippers speak English and Spanish, and many speak German or French. They are not waiters, but they will help with the anchor, the swim ladder, and the sound system. If you want a full catering service, you need to book a host or stewardess separately, which adds around EUR 150-250 for the day. The skipper's job is to keep you safe and on schedule, so listen to their advice on weather and sea conditions. They have the final say on where you can go, especially if the wind picks up in the afternoon.

Water Toys and Extras You Can Add

Many motor yachts available for charter in Marbella offer optional water toys. A paddleboard costs around EUR 50-80 for the day, a seabob (underwater scooter) is EUR 100-150, and a small inflatable kayak is EUR 40-60. Some larger yachts have a jet ski towed behind, but that requires a separate licence and insurance, usually adding EUR 200-300. If you want a full water sports setup, look for a yacht that advertises "toys included" in the listing. Otherwise, you can bring your own inflatables, as long as they are not motorised. The skipper will help you inflate and launch them. Water toys are best for groups with kids or active adults who want more than just swimming. For a relaxed day, the swim platform and a snorkel mask are enough.

Booking Last Minute vs in Advance

In high season (June to September), you should book a motor yacht charter Marbella day at least 1-2 weeks in advance, especially for popular boats like Sunseeker or Azimut models. Last-minute bookings (within 48 hours) are possible but limited to whatever is left, often older boats or smaller sizes. In low season (November to February), you can often book 1-2 days ahead, and some operators offer discounts of 20-30% for same-week bookings. The best deals appear in May and October, when the weather is good but demand is lower. If you are flexible on boat size, you can save EUR 200-400 by booking a 35-foot model instead of a 45-foot one. Use the search filters on BoatHire24 to see availability and compare prices across different dates.
