bodyHtml:
What Does a Private Boat Charter Marbella Day Include?

A private boat charter Marbella day means you hire the entire vessel for your group. No strangers. You get a licensed skipper who handles navigation, safety, and mooring. You get fuel, insurance, and standard safety equipment. Most charters include a basic cooler with ice, and some offer snorkelling gear, paddleboards, or a sound system. Food and drinks are usually extra, or you can bring your own. The skipper will suggest a route based on weather and your preferences. Typical stops include Cala del Faro, Cabopino beach, or a swim stop near the Marbella coast. If you want to see dolphins, the Strait of Gibraltar is a popular full-day option, but that's more of a long day from Marbella.

Departure Ports for Your Private Boat Charter Marbella Day

Your private boat charter Marbella day can start from several ports. Puerto Banús is the most famous, with its superyacht marina and designer shops. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is closer to the old town and more laid back. Cabopino is a small, sandy cove with a quiet marina, ideal for a relaxed start. Estepona offers a charming old town and a modern marina. Sotogrande is upscale, with a polo club vibe. Benalmádena is further east, near Torremolinos, good if you're staying on that side. Each port has its own character, but all offer easy access to the coast. For a private boat charter Marbella day, we recommend Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina for the best balance of convenience and scenery.

Boat Options for a Private Day Charter

You have choices. Motor yachts are the most common for a private boat charter Marbella day. They range from 8m to 20m, with speeds up to 30 knots. Catamarans offer more deck space and stability, good for groups of 10 to 20. Sailing yachts are slower but quieter, with a classic feel. RIBs and speedboats are faster and cheaper, but less comfortable for a full day. Fishing boats are equipped for angling, with rod holders and fish finders. Licence-free day boats (under 15 hp) are available for self-drive, but you said private with skipper, so ignore those. Superyachts over 24m are available for a private boat charter Marbella day, but expect to pay from around EUR 5,000. You can see all options on our search page.

Pricing Guidance for a Private Boat Charter Marbella Day

Prices for a private boat charter Marbella day depend on boat size, age, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 9m motor yacht starts from around EUR 800 in low season. A full day (8 hours) on the same boat might be EUR 1,200. Mid-season (May, June, September) adds about 20%. High season (July, August) can double the price. Catamarans for a full day start from EUR 1,500. Superyachts are price on request, but budget EUR 5,000 to EUR 15,000 for a day. Extras like fuel surcharges, port fees, food, drinks, and water toys add up. Always ask for a full quote before booking. We list all-inclusive prices where possible, but some operators charge extra for fuel beyond a certain distance. For a private boat charter Marbella day, expect to pay between EUR 800 and EUR 3,000 for a standard yacht, depending on your requirements.

Best Seasons for a Private Boat Charter Marbella Day

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate. Summer (June to September) is hot, 30-35 degrees C, with calm seas and lots of sun. That's peak season for a private boat charter Marbella day. Spring (April, May) and autumn (October) are milder, 20-25 degrees C, with fewer crowds and lower prices. Winter (November to March) is cooler, 15-20 degrees C, and windier. You can still charter, but you'll want a cabin or a windproof jacket. The water temperature is around 16-18 degrees C in winter, 22-26 degrees C in summer. For swimming, aim for June to October. For a quieter experience, May or September are ideal. For a private boat charter Marbella day, we recommend May, June, or September for the best balance of weather and price.

How to Book a Private Boat Charter Marbella Day

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters. Select your port, date, group size, and boat type. You'll see available yachts with photos, specs, and prices. Contact the owner or charter company directly through the platform. We don't take a booking fee. You pay the operator. We recommend booking at least a week in advance in high season. For a private boat charter Marbella day, you can often book last minute in low season. Confirm the itinerary, skipper, and any extras before paying. Read the cancellation policy. Some operators offer free cancellation up to 48 hours. Others are strict. Our blog has more tips on what to ask before booking.

Who Is a Private Boat Charter Marbella Day For?

A private boat charter Marbella day works for couples, families, groups of friends, and corporate events. It's not a party boat unless you bring the party. Most skippers are professional and will adapt to your vibe. If you want a loud party, charter a catamaran with a sound system. If you want a romantic sunset cruise, book a small motor yacht. Families with kids will appreciate the stability of a catamaran or a large motor yacht. Corporate groups can use the charter for client entertainment or team building. Fishing enthusiasts can charter a specialised fishing boat. The key is that you have the whole boat to yourselves. That's the point of a private boat charter Marbella day.

Local Highlights on a Private Boat Charter Marbella Day

From the water, you see Marbella differently. The La Concha mountain looms behind the coast. Puerto Banús looks like a mini Monaco. You can cruise past the mansions of the Golden Mile. Stop for a swim at Cala del Faro, a rocky cove near Cabopino. If you head west, you'll see the coast of Estepona, with its whitewashed old town. Further west, the Strait of Gibraltar offers dolphin and whale sightings. To the east, the cliffs of Nerja and the famous caves are a longer trip, maybe two days. For a private boat charter Marbella day, we recommend staying within 10-15 nautical miles of your departure port. That gives you time for swimming, lunch, and a relaxed pace.

Safety and Skipper Details

All skippers on BoatHire24 hold a valid Spanish licence (PER or higher) and have insurance. They know the local waters, currents, and weather patterns. They'll give a safety briefing at the start. Life jackets are onboard. The boat has a VHF radio and basic first aid. For a private boat charter Marbella day, you don't need any experience. The skipper handles everything. You just enjoy. If you have specific needs, like a wheelchair-accessible boat or a child-friendly skipper, mention it when booking. Most operators can accommodate.

What to Bring on Your Private Boat Charter Marbella Day

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, swimwear, a towel, and a light jacket for the breeze. If you're prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure. The sea is usually calm in summer, but it can get choppy in the afternoon. Bring your own food and drinks unless you've arranged catering. Some boats have a fridge and a grill. Check with the operator. Music is usually allowed, but keep it reasonable. The skipper might have a Bluetooth speaker. For a private boat charter Marbella day, pack light and leave valuables onshore.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why Choose a Private Charter Over a Shared Trip

Shared boat trips in Marbella cost less per person, but you get a fixed route, set times, and strangers. A private boat charter Marbella day gives you control. You decide the departure time. You choose the route. You stop where you want for as long as you want. If you want to spend two hours swimming at Cabopino instead of one, you can. If you want to skip the crowded beaches and anchor at a quiet cove like Cala del Faro, the skipper adjusts. The only downside is cost, but for groups of six or more, the per-person price often beats a shared trip when you factor in the flexibility. You also avoid the awkwardness of other passengers being late or loud.

Puerto Banús: The Glamorous Start

Puerto Banús is the most popular departure port for a private boat charter Marbella day. The marina is packed with superyachts, designer boutiques, and restaurants. You board your boat near the famous Casino Marbella and the port's central square. The advantage is immediate access to the best coastline. Head west and you're at the Golden Mile within ten minutes. Head east and you reach Cabopino in 20 minutes. The marina has plenty of parking, but it costs around EUR 30 for a day. Book a spot in advance during July and August. The port can be chaotic in peak season, but that's part of the appeal. For a quieter start, choose Marbella Marina instead.

Marbella Marina: Laid-Back and Central

Marbella Marina, also called Puerto Deportivo, sits right next to the old town. It's less flashy than Puerto Banús but more convenient for exploring Marbella's historic centre. You can walk from the marina to the Plaza de los Naranjos in five minutes. The marina has a more local feel, with smaller yachts and fishing boats. For a private boat charter Marbella day from here, you get quick access to the coast east towards Cabopino and west towards Puerto Banús. The water is calm near the marina, making it a good choice for families with young children. Parking is cheaper than Puerto Banús, around EUR 15 for the day. The marina also has several good seafood restaurants for a post-charter meal.

Cabopino: Quiet and Sandy

Cabopino is a small marina in a natural cove between Marbella and Cala del Moral. It's quieter than the main ports, with a sandy beach right next to the marina. If you want a private boat charter Marbella day that starts with a relaxed vibe, Cabopino works well. The marina has limited facilities, but the beach is excellent. You can swim before you even board. The route from Cabopino goes east towards the dunes of Artola or west towards Cala del Faro. The marina is small, so book your charter early in high season. There's free parking nearby, which saves you money. Cabopino is ideal for groups who want to avoid the crowds of Puerto Banús.

Estepona: Charming Old Town and Modern Marina

Estepona is about 20 minutes west of Marbella. Its marina is modern and well-equipped, with restaurants and shops. The old town is a short walk away, with whitewashed buildings and flower-filled streets. A private boat charter Marbella day from Estepona gives you access to the coast towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You can head west to see dolphins or east towards Marbella. The water is often calmer on this side. Estepona is less touristy than Marbella, so prices for charters can be slightly lower. Expect to pay around 10% less for the same boat compared to Puerto Banús. The marina has ample parking at EUR 10 per day.

Sotogrande: Upscale and Exclusive

Sotogrande is a luxury development with a marina, golf courses, and polo fields. It's about 30 minutes west of Marbella. The marina is home to large yachts and superyachts. A private boat charter Marbella day from Sotogrande feels exclusive. The route goes towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you can spot dolphins and whales. The marina has high-end restaurants and shops. Charters from Sotogrande tend to be more expensive, reflecting the clientele. A full day on a 12m motor yacht starts from around EUR 1,500. Parking is free in some areas, but the marina is less accessible without a car. Sotogrande is best for groups who want a premium experience away from the crowds.

Benalmádena: Eastern Access

Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near Torremolinos and Fuengirola. Its marina is one of the largest on the Costa del Sol, with a wide range of boats. A private boat charter Marbella day from Benalmádena gives you access to the coast east towards Nerja and the caves. The marina has a lively atmosphere with bars and restaurants. Charters from Benalmádena are often cheaper than from Puerto Banús, especially for smaller boats. A half-day on a 8m RIB starts from around EUR 500. Parking costs around EUR 15. Benalmádena is a good option if you're staying on the eastern side of the coast. The drive to Marbella is about 30 minutes.

Motor Yacht Charter: Speed and Comfort

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for a private boat charter Marbella day. They offer speed, comfort, and space. A typical 10m motor yacht has a cabin, a small kitchen, a bathroom, and a sun deck. Speeds range from 20 to 30 knots, so you can cover distance quickly. For example, from Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro is about 5 nautical miles, taking 15 minutes at cruising speed. Motor yachts are stable in calm seas, but can be bumpy in choppy conditions. For a group of six to eight, a 10m to 12m motor yacht is ideal. Prices for a full day range from EUR 1,000 to EUR 2,000 in high season. Check if fuel is included, as some operators charge extra for long distances.

Catamaran Charter: Space and Stability

Catamarans have two hulls, giving you more deck space and better stability. They are ideal for groups of 10 to 20 people. A 12m catamaran has a large trampoline at the front, a shaded cockpit, and a spacious saloon. Speeds are lower, around 8 to 12 knots, but the ride is smoother. For a private boat charter Marbella day, a catamaran is perfect for families with children or groups who want to socialise. The wide deck makes it easy to move around. You can anchor near Cabopino beach and use the paddleboards. Prices for a full-day catamaran start from EUR 1,500 for a 12m model. Larger catamarans over 15m cost from EUR 2,500. Catamarans are popular, so book at least two weeks in advance in summer.

Sailing Yacht Charter: Classic and Quiet

Sailing yachts offer a different experience. They are quieter, relying on wind power. A 12m sailing yacht has a classic feel, with teak decks and a traditional layout. Speeds are slower, around 5 to 8 knots, so you cover less distance. For a private boat charter Marbella day, a sailing yacht is best for couples or small groups who want a relaxed pace. You can sail along the coast, stop for a swim, and enjoy the silence. The skipper handles the sails, so you don't need experience. Prices are similar to motor yachts, from EUR 900 for a full day. Sailing yachts are less common on the platform, but we have several listed. Check the wind forecast before booking, as light winds can mean motoring.

RIB and Speedboat Charter: Fast and Affordable

RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) and speedboats are faster and cheaper than yachts. A 7m RIB with a 200hp engine can reach 40 knots. They are open boats, so you get wind in your hair. For a private boat charter Marbella day, a RIB is good for adrenaline seekers or small groups of four to six. You can cover more distance, reaching the Strait of Gibraltar in under an hour from Marbella. The downside is less comfort: no cabin, no toilet, and limited shade. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone. Prices start from around EUR 500 for a half-day. RIBs are popular for dolphin-watching trips because of their speed. Book a RIB if you want a fast, fun day on the water.

Fishing Boat Charter: For Anglers

Fishing boats are equipped for sport fishing. They have rod holders, a fish finder, and a bait station. A private boat charter Marbella day for fishing means you target species like sea bass, bream, or bonito. The skipper knows the best spots, often near rocky reefs or the Strait of Gibraltar. The boat is usually a motor yacht or a specialised fishing vessel. You can keep your catch, but check regulations. Most charters include basic tackle. Prices are similar to motor yachts, from EUR 800 for a half-day. Fishing charters are less common, so search specifically on our platform. Bring a hat and sunscreen, as you'll be in the sun all day.

Half-Day vs Full-Day Charter: What to Choose

A half-day private boat charter Marbella day is typically 4 hours, usually 10am to 2pm or 2pm to 6pm. A full day is 8 hours, often 10am to 6pm. Half-day is enough for a swim stop, a cruise along the coast, and lunch. Full day gives you time to visit multiple spots, like Cabopino and Cala del Faro, plus a longer lunch stop. For dolphin watching, you need at least 6 hours to reach the Strait of Gibraltar. For a sunset cruise, a half-day from 4pm to 8pm works well. Prices for half-day are about 60% of full-day rates. If you're unsure, start with a half-day. You can always extend if the boat is available.

What to Expect in High Season (July and August)

July and August are the busiest months for a private boat charter Marbella day. Temperatures hit 35 degrees C. The sea is warm, 24-26 degrees C. The coast is crowded, especially near Puerto Banús and Cabopino. You'll see many boats at anchor. Book at least two weeks in advance. Prices are at their highest, often double the low-season rate. The wind picks up in the afternoon, creating a choppy sea. Plan your route to return by 4pm if you want calm conditions. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. The sun is intense. Some operators offer a morning departure to avoid the afternoon heat. Expect to pay a premium for popular boats like catamarans.

What to Expect in Low Season (November to March)

Low season means fewer crowds and lower prices. A private boat charter Marbella day in winter costs around 30-40% less than summer. The weather is cooler, 15-20 degrees C, and windier. The sea can be rough, especially on the western side. Swimming is possible but cold, with water temperatures around 16 degrees C. You'll need a wetsuit. The advantage is that you have the coast to yourself. The marinas are quiet, and you can often book last minute. The skipper might suggest a shorter route to avoid wind. Bring a warm jacket and a hat. Winter charters are best for sightseeing rather than swimming. Some operators reduce their fleet in winter, so options are limited.

How to Get the Best Price

To get the best price for a private boat charter Marbella day, book early or late. Early means before May, late means after September. Midweek is cheaper than weekends. Monday to Thursday can be 20% less. Negotiate directly with the owner through our platform. Some operators offer discounts for cash payments. Ask about fuel surcharges, port fees, and cleaning fees. These can add EUR 100 to EUR 300. Compare multiple boats on our search page. We list prices from different operators. Don't book the first boat you see. Check the cancellation policy. Flexible cancellation might cost more but gives you peace of mind. For a group of 10, a catamaran might be better value per person than a motor yacht.

What to Ask Before Booking

Before you confirm a private boat charter Marbella day, ask these questions. Is the skipper included? Yes, always. Is fuel included? Some charters include a set amount, others charge extra. Are port fees included? These are usually extra, around EUR 50 to EUR 100. What is the maximum capacity? Don't exceed it. Is there a deposit? Some operators ask for a deposit of 30% to secure the booking. Is there a toilet on board? Smaller boats might not have one. Is food and drink provided? Most charters don't include it. Can we bring our own music? Usually yes. What is the cancellation policy? Get it in writing. Our blog has a full checklist.

Nearby Attractions for a Day Charter

From the water, you can see Marbella's landmarks. The La Concha mountain is visible from anywhere on the coast. Puerto Banús looks like a mini Monaco. The Golden Mile has luxury hotels and mansions. Cala del Faro is a rocky cove near Cabopino, good for snorkelling. Cabopino beach is sandy and less crowded. Estepona's old town is whitewashed and photogenic. The Strait of Gibraltar offers dolphin and whale watching. Nerja's caves are a longer trip, best for a two-day charter. For a private boat charter Marbella day, focus on the area within 10 nautical miles of your port. That gives you time to relax and enjoy without rushing.

Environmental Considerations

The Costa del Sol's marine environment is fragile. Avoid anchoring in seagrass meadows, which are protected. Use mooring buoys where available. Don't throw rubbish overboard. Bring a bag for your waste. Some operators offer eco-friendly charters with solar panels and biodegradable products. Ask about their practices. For a private boat charter Marbella day, choose an operator that respects the environment. The water is clear, and you want to keep it that way. If you see dolphins, maintain a distance of at least 100 metres. The skipper knows the rules. Follow their guidance.

Final Tips for a Great Day

Arrive 15 minutes early to meet the skipper and do the safety briefing. Wear non-slip shoes. Leave valuables onshore. Bring cash for tips, the skipper works hard. Tip 10-15% of the charter fee if you're happy. Take seasickness medication if you're prone, even on calm days. The afternoon can get choppy. Use a waterproof phone case. Take photos, but don't spend the whole day on your phone. Enjoy the experience. A private boat charter Marbella day is about being on the water, with your group, away from the crowds. It's worth the cost. Book through BoatHire24 and compare options. We make it easy.

h1: Sunset Boat Rental Marbella: Evening Cruise with Skipper
intro:
You want to watch the sun drop behind La Concha mountain with a cold drink in your hand, but you don't own a boat. That's fine. A sunset boat rental Marbella puts you on the water for the golden hour without the hassle of ownership or a licence. Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, so you just show up, sip your drink, and let someone else steer.

The best light happens between 19:00 and 21:30 (depending on the month), and the sea breeze turns the Mediterranean into a mirror. You can leave from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. Most sunset trips last 2-3 hours, but you can stretch it to 4 if you want to watch the stars come out.
bodyHtml:
What you get with a sunset boat rental Marbella

Every booking on our platform includes a professional skipper. You do not need a boating licence, and you do not need to know how to anchor. The skipper handles navigation, safety, and mooring. You handle the rosé, the snacks, and the photos.

Typical inclusions for a sunset cruise: fuel, insurance, onboard Bluetooth speaker, a basic cooler with ice (you bring your own drinks and food), and sometimes a paddleboard or snorkel gear if you want a dip before the sun goes down. Some boats offer a complimentary bottle of cava or a fruit platter, but check the listing details. You can also hire a private chef or catering service for an extra cost, though that usually requires advance notice.

The boat types available for sunset charters range from motor yachts (25-60 feet) to catamarans (30-50 feet), sailing yachts, and even RIBs for a faster, more adrenaline-fuelled sunset ride. For a relaxed evening, a catamaran gives you more deck space and stability. For a bit of speed, a motor yacht gets you to the best sunset spots quicker.

Best departure ports for your sunset cruise

You have six main ports to choose from on the Costa del Sol. Each has its own vibe and proximity to sunset viewpoints.

Puerto Banús is the most glamorous departure point. You cruise past the superyachts, then head west towards the coast of Benahavís or south towards the open sea. The sunset from the water here is framed by the Sierra Blanca mountains. Boats from Puerto Banús tend to be larger and more luxurious, with prices starting around EUR 600 for a 2-hour trip. Browse sunset boats from Puerto Banús.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more laid-back. You leave from the town centre, pass the fishing boats, and motor towards Cabopino or the Marbella coastline. The sunset view here includes the old town skyline and the mountains behind. Prices from around EUR 450 for a 2-hour charter.

Cabopino is a small, quiet marina near the Artola dunes. It is ideal if you want a less crowded departure and a quicker route to the open sea. The sunset from Cabopino often has fewer boats in the frame. Prices from around EUR 400.

Estepona gives you a view of the Strait of Gibraltar and the African coast on clear days. You can combine a sunset cruise with dolphin spotting (common in the summer months). Estepona old town is worth a pre-cruise stroll. Prices from around EUR 350.

Sotogrande is the most exclusive option, with a longer cruise to reach the best sunset spots near Gibraltar. This is a good choice if you want a full evening out, not just a short trip. Prices from around EUR 700.

Benalmádena offers a more budget-friendly departure, with smaller boats and shorter cruises. The sunset from the marina area is pleasant, but you get better views if you head towards Torremolinos or Fuengirola. Prices from around EUR 300.

Boat options for your sunset rental

Not all boats are equal sunset cruising. Here is what you should consider.

Motor yachts (25-60 feet) are the most popular choice. They have a flybridge for panoramic views, a shaded saloon, and a bow sunpad. You can move around easily, and the skipper usually anchors for a swim if the light is still good. A 40-foot motor yacht from Marbella Marina costs around EUR 550-700 for 3 hours.

Catamarans (30-50 feet) offer more deck space and stability. They are better for groups of 8-12 people. The wide beam means less rocking, so if you are prone to seasickness, a catamaran is the smarter pick. Prices from around EUR 600 for 3 hours on a 40-foot Lagoon or Fountaine Pajot.

Sailing yachts (30-50 feet) give you a quieter, more traditional experience. The skipper will often turn off the engine for the last 30 minutes if the wind cooperates. Sailing at sunset is a different kind of magic, but the boat is slower, so you cover less distance. Prices from around EUR 400 for 3 hours.

RIBs and speedboats (20-30 feet) are for the thrill-seeker. You can get to the sunset spot fast, but there is less space and no toilet on most RIBs. Best for couples or small groups of 4-6. Prices from around EUR 300 for 2 hours.

Licence-free day boats (up to 6 metres) are a newer option. You can drive these yourself without a licence, but for a sunset cruise you still need a skipper if you want the boat to be included in our platform (all our charters include a skipper for safety and convenience). These boats are basic but cheap. Prices from around EUR 250 for 2 hours.

Superyachts (60+ feet) are for the full VIP experience. You get a crew of 2-3, a gourmet dinner option, and a jacuzzi on some models. Prices are on request, but expect EUR 2,000+ for a 3-hour sunset charter. View superyacht sunset charters.

Pricing guidance for sunset boat rental Marbella

Prices vary by boat size, port, season, and duration. Here are realistic ranges for 2025.

2-hour sunset cruise: EUR 250-500 for a small motorboat or RIB, EUR 400-700 for a medium motor yacht or catamaran, EUR 800-1,500 for a large motor yacht (50+ feet).

3-hour sunset cruise: EUR 350-600 for small boats, EUR 550-900 for medium boats, EUR 1,000-2,000 for large boats.

4-hour sunset cruise (includes stargazing): EUR 450-800 for small, EUR 700-1,200 for medium, EUR 1,200-3,000 for large.

Fuel is included in all prices on BoatHire24, unless stated otherwise on the listing. Gratuities for the skipper are not included; 10-15% is standard if you are happy with the service.

You can also add extras like a private chef (EUR 150-300 per person), photographer (EUR 200-400 per hour), or a DJ setup (EUR 300-500). These must be arranged at least 48 hours in advance.

Best season for a sunset cruise in Marbella

The sunset boat rental Marbella season runs from April to October, with the best conditions in June, July, August, and September.

In April and May, the sun sets around 20:30-21:00, and the air temperature is 18-24 degrees C. You will want a light jacket. The water is still cool (16-18 degrees C), so swimming is possible but brisk.

June to August is peak season. The sun sets at 21:30-21:45, and the air is 28-35 degrees C. The water is 22-26 degrees C. This is the most popular time, so book at least a week in advance. Prices are 20-30% higher than in May or September.

September and October are the best months in my opinion. The sun sets around 20:00-20:30, the crowds thin out, and the sea is still warm from summer (20-24 degrees C). Prices drop back to shoulder-season rates.

November to March is possible but less reliable. The sun sets early (18:00-19:00), and the wind can pick up. Some boats are still available, but you risk choppy seas or rain. If you want a winter sunset cruise, check the forecast and book a larger, more stable boat.

How to book a sunset boat rental Marbella

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. You go to our search page, select your preferred port, date, and time (evening recommended), and filter by boat type. Each listing shows the boat specifications, included amenities, skipper profile, and availability calendar.

Once you find a boat you like, you send a booking request. The owner or charter company confirms within 24 hours (usually faster). You pay a deposit (typically 30-50%) to secure the date, and the balance is due on the day of the charter, either in cash or by card. We recommend paying the balance in cash to avoid card fees, but check with the owner first.

You can also book a custom sunset itinerary. If you want to combine a sunset cruise with a visit to Cala del Faro (a hidden cove near Marbella) or a dolphin-watching detour near the Strait of Gibraltar, mention it in the booking notes. Most skippers are flexible if the timing works.

Cancellation policy: free cancellation up to 48 hours before the charter. Within 48 hours, you lose the deposit unless the owner agrees to reschedule. Bad weather cancellations are free, and the deposit is refunded or transferred to another date.

For last-minute bookings (same day or next day), call the owner directly via the phone number on the listing. Not all owners accept last-minute bookings, but some do if the boat is available.

Who is this sunset boat rental for

A sunset boat rental Marbella works for couples, small groups of friends, families with older children (most boats allow children, but check the listing for age limits), and corporate events. It is not ideal for large parties of 20+ unless you book a superyacht or a large catamaran (50+ feet).

If you are celebrating a birthday, anniversary, or proposal, most skippers are happy to help with decorations or a special moment. Just let them know in advance. Some boats have a policy against confetti or glitter (it is a pain to clean), but rose petals and balloons are usually fine.

If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness pill an hour before departure. The sea is usually calm in the evening, but the swell can pick up if the wind is from the east (levante). A catamaran or a large motor yacht will minimise the movement.

If you want to combine the sunset cruise with a meal, you can either bring your own food (tapas, sushi, pizza) or arrange a catered dinner. Some boats have a small galley with a fridge and a sink, but most do not have an oven or a stove. Cold food works best.

What to bring on a sunset boat rental Marbella

You will need: sunscreen (even at sunset, the UV reflection off the water is strong), a light jacket or sweater (the wind picks up after sunset), sunglasses, a hat, a camera or phone, and a swimsuit if you plan to swim before the sun goes down. The skipper will have a cooler with ice, but you should bring your own drinks and food. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper has the right to cut the trip short if anyone becomes dangerously intoxicated.

Do not bring: glass bottles (some boats ban glass for safety reasons, use plastic or cans), large coolers (the boat has limited space), or pets without prior approval (some skippers allow well-behaved dogs, but you must ask first).

If you are booking a RIB or a speedboat, bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables. These boats get wet, especially if the skipper opens the throttle.

Frequently asked questions about sunset boat rental Marbella

Here are the answers to the most common questions we get from customers.

Best sunset spots you will visit on a Marbella cruise

Your skipper knows the prime locations. From Puerto Banús, the usual route heads west towards the coast of Benahavís, where the sun sinks behind the Sierra Blanca. The reflection off the water here is almost theatrical. From Marbella Marina, you often cruise past the Cabopino dunes or anchor near the Cala del Faro lighthouse, a quiet cove with a small beach and a rocky outcrop. If you depart from Estepona, the skipper may take you towards the Punta Doncella lighthouse, where the African coastline becomes visible on clear days. The Strait of Gibraltar is a common destination for longer sunset charters, especially if you want to spot dolphins feeding in the evening light. For a more secluded experience, ask about anchoring near the Río Verde estuary, where the mangroves and sandbars create a different kind of sunset atmosphere.

How weather affects your sunset boat rental Marbella

The Costa del Sol is known for 300-plus sunny days a year, but the evening wind can be a factor. The levante wind (from the east) picks up in the afternoon and can make the sea choppy, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar. Your skipper will check the forecast before departure and may suggest a different route or a sheltered cove. The poniente wind (from the west) is gentler and usually brings calm seas. In July and August, the thermal wind dies down around 19:00, leaving a glassy surface for the sunset. If you book in spring or autumn, ask the skipper about the wind forecast the day before. Most charter companies will offer a free reschedule if conditions look bad. Do not risk it: a rough sunset cruise is not romantic, and the skipper may cancel for safety reasons.

What sunset times mean for your charter duration

Sunset times shift significantly across the season. In June, the sun sets around 21:45, so a 2-hour charter starting at 20:00 gives you the golden hour, the actual sunset, and the first 30 minutes of twilight. In September, sunset is around 20:30, so a 2-hour charter starting at 19:00 works better. For a 3-hour charter, you get the pre-sunset light, the main event, and then a stargazing period after the sun dips below the horizon. The sky often turns deep purple and orange for 20-30 minutes after sunset, especially in summer. If you want to see the stars come out, book a 3-hour charter. Your skipper will likely turn off the engine and let you float in the dark, which is a completely different experience from a standard sunset cruise.

How to choose the right boat size for your group

Boat size matters more than you think. A 25-foot motor yacht works for 4-6 people, but the deck space is limited and you cannot move around easily. For 8-10 people, you need at least a 40-foot motor yacht or a 40-foot catamaran. Catamarans have a wider beam, so the deck feels larger and you can spread out. For 12-16 people, a 50-foot motor yacht or a 50-foot catamaran is the minimum. Superyachts (60+ feet) can handle 20-30 guests comfortably, with multiple decks and a crew to serve drinks. If you are a couple, a 30-foot sailing yacht or a 25-foot RIB is plenty. Do not overcrowd the boat: the skipper will enforce the maximum capacity, and it is not fun being squashed on a small boat for 2 hours. Check the listing for the official passenger limit, not just the number of seats.

What drinks and food work best on a sunset charter

Most boats provide a cooler with ice, but you bring your own drinks and food. For drinks, rosé, cava, and white wine are the classics. Beer and gin and tonics work too. Avoid red wine unless you are okay with stains on the deck. For food, cold tapas (jamón, cheese, olives, bread) is the easiest. Sushi, cold pasta salads, and fruit platters also travel well. Some boats have a small fridge but no freezer, so keep that in mind. If you want a hot meal, you need a boat with a full galley or a private chef. The chef will bring a portable stove and prepare the food on board. Expect to pay EUR 150-300 per person for a chef, depending on the menu. For a simpler option, order a picnic basket from a local deli and bring it on board. The skipper will usually have plates, cups, and cutlery, but check the listing to be sure.

How to get the best value on your sunset boat rental Marbella

Booking a sunset charter can be expensive, but there are ways to save. First, book on a weekday (Monday to Thursday) rather than Friday to Sunday. Prices are often 15-25% lower, and the marinas are quieter. Second, book in May, September, or October instead of July or August. The weather is still excellent, and the prices drop by 20-30%. Third, choose a smaller boat or a RIB if you are a couple or a small group. A 2-hour RIB charter from Benalmádena can cost as little as EUR 300, compared to EUR 700 for a 40-foot motor yacht from Puerto Banús. Fourth, share the cost with friends. A 3-hour catamaran charter for 10 people at EUR 800 works out to EUR 80 per person, which is cheaper than a dinner at a nice restaurant. Fifth, ask the owner about last-minute discounts. If the boat is not booked, some owners will offer a 10-20% discount to fill the slot. You can find these deals by checking the listings a day or two before your desired date.

What to do if you get seasick on a sunset cruise

Seasickness is rare on the Costa del Sol in the evening, but it happens. The best prevention is to take a motion sickness pill (like Dramamine or Kwells) one hour before departure. Eat a light meal beforehand, nothing greasy or heavy. Avoid alcohol until after the sunset, as alcohol dehydrates you and makes nausea worse. Stay on the deck, not inside the cabin, and keep your eyes on the horizon. If you start feeling queasy, tell the skipper. They can move the boat to a calmer spot or head back to port early. Some boats have a small toilet (a marine head) that you can use, but it is not a pleasant experience if you are sick. Better to stay on deck and breathe fresh air. If you know you are prone to seasickness, book a catamaran instead of a motor yacht. Catamarans have a much gentler motion because of their twin hulls. A 40-foot catamaran will barely rock in a light swell, while a 30-foot motor yacht will feel every wave.

intro:
You want to watch the sun sink into the Mediterranean from the deck of a private boat, a glass of something cold in your hand, and no one else telling you where to go. That is exactly what a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus gives you. No queuing for a crowded beach bar, no fighting for a photo spot on the promenade. Just you, your people, and the sky turning orange over La Concha mountain.

Every charter on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the best spots to drop anchor for the golden hour. bodyHtml:
What You Get With a Sunset Boat Rental Puerto Banus

A sunset boat rental Puerto Banus is not just a boat ride. It is a private charter with a professional skipper who handles the navigation, mooring, and safety. You get the whole boat to yourselves, no strangers, no set itinerary. The skipper can take you along the coast towards the Marbella skyline, out towards the Cabopino dunes, or just stay in the bay and let the sun do the show. Most charters include a cooler with ice, and you can bring your own drinks and food. Some boats have a Bluetooth speaker, a sun deck, and a shaded cabin if the evening breeze gets cool. The standard duration for a sunset cruise is two hours, but many people book three or four hours to combine the sunset with a dinner stop or a swim.

Departure Ports and Best Sunset Spots

The main departure port for a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus is, obviously, Puerto Banús itself. But you can also leave from Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, or Benalmádena. Each port gives you a different angle on the sunset. From Puerto Banús, the sun sets behind the western arm of the marina, with the yachts silhouetted against the glow. From Marbella Marina, you get the long curve of the beach and the peak of La Concha. From Cabopino, the dunes and the natural park add a wilder feel. The skipper will know the local wind and current patterns, so they can position the boat for the best view. Favourite anchor spots include the calm waters off Cala del Faro, the stretch between Puerto Banús and the Río Verde estuary, and the open sea beyond the Strait of Gibraltar where you sometimes see dolphins at sunset.

Types of Boats Available for Sunset Charters

You have a few choices when you book a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus. Motor yachts are the most popular: fast, stable, and with plenty of deck space for lounging. A 40-foot motor yacht can carry up to 12 guests and costs from around EUR 500 for two hours. Catamarans are wider and more stable, with nets at the front where you can lie down and watch the sky. A 36-foot catamaran starts from around EUR 650 for a sunset trip. Sailing yachts are quieter and more romantic, but they depend on the wind, so the skipper may motor if the breeze drops. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper and more nimble, good for a small group of four or five, starting from around EUR 350. Fishing boats are available too, if you want to combine a sunset cruise with a bit of trolling. Superyachts are price on request, but they come with crew, champagne, and a full bar.

Pricing Guidance for Sunset Boat Rental Puerto Banus

Prices for a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus vary by boat size, duration, and season. In the low season (October to April), a two-hour sunset cruise on a 30-foot motor yacht starts from around EUR 350. In the high season (May to September), the same boat costs from around EUR 450. For a 50-foot motor yacht with a flybridge and a sound system, expect from around EUR 800 for two hours. Catamarans of the same size are usually EUR 100 to EUR 200 more. Superyachts and luxury charters are price on request, and you should contact the owner directly through BoatHire24 for a quote. Some owners offer a sunset plus dinner package that includes a stop at a beach club or a restaurant in Puerto Banús, which adds EUR 100 to EUR 200 per person. Always check what is included: fuel, skipper, and VAT are usually included, but food and drinks are extra unless stated.

Best Season for a Sunset Boat Rental Puerto Banus

The best time for a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus is from late April to early October, when the days are long and the weather is warm. Sunset in July is around 9:30 PM, so a 7:30 PM departure gives you an hour of golden light and then the full sunset. In September, sunset is around 8:30 PM, so a 6:30 PM start works well. In the winter months, sunset is around 6:00 PM, and the air temperature can drop to 15 degrees C, so you will want a boat with a cabin or a windproof jacket. The sea is calmer in the summer, but the marinas are busier, so you need to book at least a week in advance. In the spring and autumn, you can often book a few days ahead and get a better price.

How to Book a Sunset Boat Rental Puerto Banus

Booking a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter Puerto Banús as the port, select your date and time, and filter by boat type. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and the owner's contact details. You can message the owner directly through the platform to ask about availability and negotiate the price. Most owners require a deposit of 30% to 50% to confirm the booking, with the balance paid on the day. You can also read the owner's profile and reviews from previous guests. If you are not sure which boat to choose, you can call the BoatHire24 support team for advice. They know the local fleet and can recommend a boat that matches your group size and budget.

Who Is a Sunset Boat Rental Puerto Banus For?

A sunset boat rental Puerto Banus is for couples who want a romantic evening away from the crowds. It is also for groups of friends celebrating a birthday, a hen or stag party, or just a night out. Families with children are welcome on most boats, as long as the children are supervised. The skipper will provide life jackets for all ages. If you are planning a proposal, tell the owner in advance, and they can arrange champagne, flowers, and a photographer on the dock. Some boats have a sound system for music, so you can set the mood. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared sunset cruise on a catamaran, which costs around EUR 80 per person and includes drinks. Check the BoatHire24 blog for tips on planning the perfect sunset cruise.

What to Bring and Wear

For a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus, bring a light jacket or a sweater, even in summer, because the wind on the water can feel cool after the sun goes down. Wear non-slip shoes or go barefoot, but avoid high heels. Bring sunglasses and sunscreen for the earlier part of the cruise. If you plan to swim, bring a towel and a change of clothes. The boat will have a cooler with ice, so bring your own drinks and snacks. Some owners provide a welcome drink, but do not rely on it. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness pill an hour before departure, although the sea is usually calm in the bay. Do not bring glass bottles, as they can break on deck; use plastic or cans instead.

Local Attractions and Landmarks Visible From the Boat

From a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus, you can see the La Concha mountain peak, which is often pink at sunset. The skyline of Marbella's Golden Mile is visible to the east, with the white buildings of the Marbella Club and Puente Romano. To the west, you see the dunes of Cabopino and the Sierra Bermeja mountains. If the skipper takes you further out, you might see the Rock of Gibraltar in the distance, especially on a clear day. The coastline between Puerto Banús and Estepona is dotted with small coves and cliffs, including Cala del Faro, where you can anchor for a swim. The Río Verde estuary is a good spot for birdwatching, with herons and egrets feeding at dusk. If you book a longer charter, you can go as far as the Nerja caves, but that is a full-day trip, not a sunset cruise.

Frequently Asked Questions About Sunset Boat Rental Puerto Banus

Do I need a boat licence for a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus?

No. Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who operates the boat. You just relax and enjoy the sunset.

How many people can join a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus?

Most boats can carry between 6 and 12 passengers. Larger superyachts can take up to 20. Check the boat's capacity on the listing page.

Can I bring my own food and drinks?

Yes, you can bring your own food and drinks. Most boats provide a cooler with ice. Avoid glass bottles for safety.

What happens if it rains or the sea is rough?

How far in advance should I book a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus?

In the high season, book at least a week ahead. In the low season, you can often book a few days in advance.

Can I include a dinner stop at a beach club?

Yes, many owners offer a sunset plus dinner package. You can anchor near a beach club like Ocean Club or La Sala, and the skipper will arrange a table.

Is a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus suitable for children?

Yes, children are welcome on most boats. Life jackets are provided for all ages. The skipper will ensure a safe and family-friendly cruise.

Why a Sunset Cruise Beats a Restaurant Dinner

You could sit in a crowded terrace on the Golden Mile and watch the sun go down over the sea, but a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus gives you a better view and no noise from the next table. The boat moves with the light, so you are always facing the horizon. The skipper can kill the engine and let you drift in silence, which is something no restaurant can do. If you want to eat, you can order takeaway from a place like La Pesquera in Puerto Banús and eat on the deck while the sky turns orange. A two-hour sunset cruise costs about the same as a dinner for two at a mid-range restaurant in Marbella, but you get a private boat, a skipper, and a memory that lasts longer than a plate of paella.

How to Choose the Right Boat for a Romantic Sunset

If you are booking a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus for a romantic occasion, a sailing yacht is the quietest option. The sails catch the evening breeze and the only sound is the water against the hull. A 35-foot sailing yacht like a Bavaria or a Dufour costs from around EUR 450 for two hours and feels more intimate than a motor yacht. Motor yachts with a flybridge give you a higher vantage point, but the engine noise can be distracting. Catamarans are the most stable, so if your partner gets seasick, a 38-foot Lagoon catamaran is a safe choice. For a proposal, ask the owner to have the boat decorated with fairy lights and a bottle of cava on ice. Some owners will also arrange a photographer to meet you at the dock when you return.

Sunset Timing and How to Get the Best Light

The golden hour on the Costa del Sol lasts about 45 minutes before the sun hits the horizon. For a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus in July, the sun sets at 9:38 PM, so a 7:30 PM departure gives you the best light for photos. In August, sunset is at 9:15 PM, so aim for 7:00 PM. In September, it drops to 8:30 PM, so a 6:30 PM start works. The skipper will position the boat so the sun is behind the La Concha mountain or the Sierra Bermeja range, depending on the wind direction. The best photos are taken from the bow of the boat, with the sun behind you and the golden light on your face. If you want a silhouette shot, stand on the flybridge with the sun at your back and the Costa del Sol coastline in the foreground.

What to Expect From the Skipper on a Sunset Charter

The skipper on a sunset boat rental Puerto Banus is a licensed professional who knows the local waters. They will greet you at the dock, help you board, and give a safety briefing. They will not intrude on your party unless you ask them to. They can recommend a route based on the wind and the sunset direction. Most skippers speak English and Spanish, and some speak German or French. They will handle the mooring, the anchor, and any navigation. If you want to swim, they will find a calm spot away from other boats. They will also clean the boat after the trip, so you do not have to worry about tidying up. Tip the skipper 10% to 15% of the charter price if you are happy with the service.

Sunset Boat Rental From Other Ports on the Costa del Sol

While Puerto Banús is the most famous departure point, a sunset boat rental from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and cheaper. A 30-foot motor yacht from Marbella Marina starts from around EUR 300 for two hours, compared to EUR 350 from Puerto Banús. From Cabopino, you get the view of the dunes and the natural park, and the marina is less crowded. From Estepona, the sunset sets behind the old town and the Sierra Bermeja mountains, which gives a different colour palette. From Sotogrande, you are closer to the Strait of Gibraltar, and you might see the lights of Africa across the water. From Benalmádena, you get the view of the Málaga coastline and the marina with its pagoda-style buildings. Each port has its own character, and the skipper will adapt the route to suit the location.

Adding a Swim Stop to Your Sunset Cruise

If you book a three-hour sunset boat rental Puerto Banus, you have time for a swim stop before the sun goes down. The best spots are the calm waters off Cala del Faro, between Puerto Banús and Estepona, or the beach at Cabopino. The water temperature in July and August is around 24 degrees C, so it is warm enough for a quick dip. The skipper will anchor the boat and put out a ladder. Bring a towel and a change of clothes because you will get wet. Some boats have a freshwater shower on the swim platform to rinse off the salt. If you are booking a sunset cruise for a group, a swim stop adds a fun element and breaks up the time on the water. Just remember that the sun sets quickly, so the swim stop should be early in the charter, not at the end.

How to Avoid Crowds on a Sunset Boat Rental

Puerto Banús is busy in the high season, and the sunset cruises can feel crowded if you are in a shared charter. To avoid the crowds, book a private sunset boat rental and ask the skipper to take you away from the main bay. The area between the Río Verde and Cala del Faro is quieter, with fewer boats and more space. Another option is to depart from Cabopino or Estepona instead of Puerto Banús. These ports have fewer charter boats, and the sunset views are just as good. If you are flexible, book a sunset cruise on a weekday, Tuesday to Thursday, when the marinas are less busy. Sunday sunset cruises are popular with local families, so expect more traffic on the water.

title: Sunset Catamaran Charter Marbella: Best Views
metaDescription: Book a sunset catamaran charter Marbella. See the sun drop into the Med from Puerto Banus or Marbella. Champagne, skipper included. Reserve your evening now.
h1: Sunset Catamaran Charter Marbella: Best Views
intro:
You want the best seat for the sunset on the Costa del Sol. That seat is on a catamaran, drifting off Puerto Banus with a cold drink in your hand and the Sierra Blanca turning pink behind you. A sunset catamaran charter Marbella is not just a boat trip. It is the way to watch the day end, away from the crowds on the beach, with the sea stretching out to the horizon and the sky doing its thing.

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, so you do not need a licence or any experience. You just turn up, step aboard, and let someone else handle the navigation while you soak up the last hour of daylight. This page covers what you get, which ports work best, what it costs, and how to book the whole thing without any fuss.
bodyHtml:
What You Get on a Sunset Catamaran Charter Marbella

A catamaran is the right boat for sunset because it has a wide, stable deck and plenty of space to move around. You are not cramped on a narrow hull. You can sit at the bow with your feet over the water, lounge on the trampoline nets, or stand at the stern with a glass of cava. The skipper handles the sails and the engine. You handle the relaxation.

Most sunset charters last between two and three hours. You depart about an hour before sunset, cruise along the coast, anchor for a swim if the light is still good, and then watch the sun go down from the water. The boat usually has a sound system, a cooler with ice, and sometimes a BBQ or a selection of tapas. You can bring your own food and drink if you prefer. The skipper will have local knowledge about the best spot for the sunset view, which changes slightly with the season.

Champagne or cava is standard on these trips. Some operators include a bottle, others offer it as an add-on. Check the listing details when you book. The skipper will also point out landmarks along the coast: the Marbella skyline, the lighthouse at Cabopino, the mountains behind Estepona. If you are lucky, you might see dolphins feeding near the shore as the light fades.

Which Port to Depart From

The departure port affects the view and the duration of the trip. Here are the main options for a sunset catamaran charter Marbella.

Puerto Banus. This is the most popular starting point. You leave the marina with its superyachts and designer shops behind you, head west towards the coast of Estepona, and watch the sun sink behind the Rock of Gibraltar on clear days. The marina itself is lively before and after the trip, so you can grab dinner or a drink on the front. The journey from Puerto Banus to the sunset spot takes about 15 to 20 minutes.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo). From here you head east towards Cabopino or west towards Puerto Banus. The advantage is the view of La Concha mountain, which catches the last light and turns a deep orange. The marina is quieter than Puerto Banus, with a more relaxed vibe. Parking is easier too.

Cabopino. This small port near the dunes of Artola is good if you want a more natural setting. The sunset view is over the sea with no development on the skyline. The catamarans here tend to be smaller and more intimate. The marina has a few restaurants but nothing flashy.

Estepona. Departing from Estepona gives you a sunset framed by the old town and the Sierra Bermeja mountains. The port is modern and well-equipped. The trip usually goes west towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where the water gets deeper and the dolphin sightings are more frequent.

Sotogrande and Benalmadena. These are further afield. Sotogrande offers a more exclusive, quiet departure. Benalmadena is closer to Malaga and gives a different angle on the sunset, looking west across the bay. Both are viable but less common for a sunset catamaran charter Marbella specifically.

Types of Catamarans Available

Not all catamarans are the same. Here is what you can expect to find on BoatHire24 for a sunset charter.

Luxury catamarans. These are 40 to 50 feet long, with a spacious flybridge, a large saloon, and a galley. They have a professional crew of two (skipper and hostess). The hostess serves drinks and can prepare a light meal. These boats are the best for a group of 8 to 12 people who want a premium experience. Prices start from around EUR 1,200 for a two-hour charter.

Standard cruising catamarans. These are 35 to 40 feet, with a simple layout. The skipper is included, but there is no hostess. You manage your own drinks and food. These are good for a smaller group of 4 to 6 people. Prices start from around EUR 600 for a two-hour charter.

Sailing catamarans with full canvas. These are older models, often used for day trips. They have a bimini top for shade and a basic sound system. They are functional and cheaper. Prices start from around EUR 400 for a two-hour charter.

All catamarans have a toilet on board. Most have a shower at the stern for rinsing off after a swim. Check the listing for specific amenities like a BBQ, paddleboard, or snorkelling gear.

Pricing Guidance for a Sunset Catamaran Charter Marbella

Prices vary depending on the boat size, the season, the duration, and what is included. Here is a rough guide to what you will pay.

Low season (November to March). A two-hour sunset charter for up to 6 people costs from around EUR 400 to EUR 800. For a larger luxury catamaran for 12 people, expect from around EUR 1,000 to EUR 1,500.

Mid season (April to June, September to October). Prices increase by about 20 to 30 percent. A standard catamaran for 6 people costs from around EUR 600 to EUR 1,000. A luxury catamaran for 12 people costs from around EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,000.

High season (July and August). This is the peak. A standard catamaran for 6 people costs from around EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. A luxury catamaran for 12 people costs from around EUR 2,000 to EUR 3,000. Availability is tight, so book at least two weeks in advance.

These prices are for the boat hire and the skipper. Extras like champagne, catering, or a longer duration add to the cost. Some operators charge a fuel surcharge in high season. Always confirm the total price before booking.

Best Seasons and Sunset Times

The sunset time changes dramatically through the year. This affects when you depart and how comfortable the conditions are.

Summer (June to August). Sunset is between 21:30 and 21:45. The air temperature is 28 to 32 degrees Celsius. The sea is warm, 22 to 26 degrees. You can swim before sunset without a wetsuit. The evenings are long and light until after 22:00. This is the most popular time, so book early.

Spring and autumn (April to May, September to October). Sunset is between 20:00 and 21:30. The air temperature is 20 to 28 degrees. The sea is cooler, 18 to 22 degrees. A light jacket or sweater is useful after the sun goes down. These months offer the best balance of good weather and lower prices.

Winter (November to March). Sunset is between 18:00 and 19:30. The air temperature is 15 to 20 degrees. The sea is cold, 14 to 17 degrees. Swimming is possible but not comfortable for long. The sunset colours are often more dramatic in winter because of the lower angle of the sun and the clearer air. Prices are lowest in this season.

Check the exact sunset time for your date on a weather site. The skipper will confirm the departure time a day before the charter.

How to Book a Sunset Catamaran Charter Marbella

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You do not need to call around or send multiple emails. The platform lists available catamarans with real-time availability and prices.

Go to the search page, select Marbella or Puerto Banus as the location, choose your date, and filter by boat type (catamaran) and duration (2 to 3 hours). The results show the boats, their capacity, the included amenities, and the price. Click on a listing to see full details, including photos, the skipper profile, and the cancellation policy.

Once you pick a boat, you book and pay online. The platform handles the payment securely. You receive a confirmation email with the meeting point, the skipper's contact number, and a map. On the day, you arrive at the port 15 minutes before departure. The skipper meets you at the boat and you are off.

If you are unsure which catamaran to choose, read the BoatHire24 blog for tips on choosing the right boat and what to bring. The blog also has guides to the best sunset spots on the Costa del Sol.

Who This Is For

A sunset catamaran charter Marbella works for couples, small groups of friends, and families with older children. It is not ideal for toddlers or babies because of the safety risks on a moving boat. Most operators allow children from age 5 or 6, but check the listing.

If you are celebrating a birthday, anniversary, or engagement, the skipper can arrange decorations, a cake, or a special bottle of champagne. Just mention it when you book. Some operators also offer a sunset ceremony for weddings or vow renewals, but that requires a longer charter and more planning.

Corporate groups use sunset charters for client entertainment or team events. The catamaran provides a relaxed setting for networking without the formality of a restaurant. You can book a luxury catamaran for up to 12 guests and include catering. The cost is tax-deductible for business expenses in Spain.

If you are a solo traveller, a sunset catamaran charter might be too expensive unless you join a shared group. Some operators offer shared sunset trips where you book a single spot on a catamaran with other guests. These are cheaper, from around EUR 80 per person, and a good way to meet people. Check the platform for shared charters.

What to Bring and What to Wear

The dress code is casual. In summer, wear shorts and a t-shirt or a light dress. In spring and autumn, bring a sweater or a light jacket for after the sun goes down. In winter, wear trousers and a warm jacket. The wind on the water makes it feel cooler than on land.

Bring sunglasses, a hat, and sunscreen even for a sunset trip. The sun is lower but still strong, especially in summer. The reflection off the water increases UV exposure. Bring a camera or phone for photos. The light at sunset is excellent for pictures. Bring a swimsuit and a towel if you plan to swim. The boat has a freshwater shower to rinse off.

Do not bring glass bottles on board. Most operators prohibit glass for safety reasons. Use plastic cups or cans. The boat will have a cooler with ice, but bring your own drinks if you prefer a specific brand or type. Some operators provide a welcome drink, but check the listing.

What Happens in Bad Weather

Weather on the Costa del Sol is generally good, but strong winds or thunderstorms can cancel a sunset charter. The skipper makes the decision based on safety. If the weather is poor, the operator will offer a reschedule or a full refund. The cancellation policy varies by operator, but most are flexible for weather-related cancellations.

Light rain is not usually a problem. The catamaran has a covered area in the saloon or under the bimini. The sunset can still be visible even with some cloud cover. The colours are often more intense after a rain shower.

If you are booking in winter, check the forecast a few days ahead. The wind is stronger in winter, especially in the afternoon. The skipper may recommend a morning or midday charter instead of sunset for safety and comfort.

Why a Catamaran and Not a Yacht

You might wonder why a catamaran is better than a motor yacht for sunset. The answer is space and stability. A catamaran has two hulls, which means a wider deck and less rolling motion. You can walk around without feeling seasick. The trampoline nets at the bow are perfect for lying down and watching the sky. A motor yacht of the same length has a narrower beam and more engine noise.

Catamarans also have a shallower draft, so they can anchor closer to shore. This gives you a better view of the coast and the mountains. The sail adds a sense of peace. The only sound is the water against the hulls and the wind in the rigging. A motor yacht relies on engines, which create vibration and noise.

If you want a party atmosphere with loud music and a fast ride, a motor yacht might be better. But for sunset, the catamaran wins every time.

Local Tips for the Best Sunset Experience

The best sunset spot changes with the season. In summer, the sun sets further north, so the view is better from the west side of Marbella, near Puerto Banus. In winter, the sun sets further south, so the view is better from the east side, near Cabopino or Marbella Marina. The skipper will know the best spot for the date.

If you want to combine the sunset charter with dinner, book a later departure that ends at 21:00 or 21:30, then head to a restaurant on the port. Many restaurants in Puerto Banus have tables with a view of the marina. In Marbella Marina, try the seafood places on the front.

For a truly memorable experience, book a full-moon sunset charter. The moon rises as the sun sets, and the light on the water is magical. These dates are rare, so check the lunar calendar and book early.

If you are interested in the marine life, ask the skipper to take you near the Cabopino reef or the Estepona coast. Dolphins are common in these areas, especially in the evening when they feed. The skipper can also point out the bioluminescence in the water on dark nights, which is visible from late spring to early autumn.

title: Snorkeling Boat Trip Marbella: Book Adventure
