What a Photoshoot Yacht Charter Marbella Actually Includes

You get a private yacht or catamaran with a licensed skipper for a set number of hours, usually three to eight. The boat is yours, so you control the itinerary, the stops, and the vibe. Most charters include fuel, taxes, and basic refreshments like water and soft drinks. You can add catering, a photographer, or even a drone operator if you want aerial shots of the coastline.

The skipper knows the waters between Marbella and Estepona, including quiet coves like Cala del Faro where the water is glassy and the crowds are thin. They will anchor where the light is best, usually late afternoon for golden hour, and they can adjust the position as the sun moves. No rushing, no fixed schedule. You decide when to move and when to stay put for that perfect frame.

Boat types vary. A motor yacht gives you sleek lines and a sunpad for lying on. A catamaran offers more deck space and stability, which helps if you are shooting video or using a gimbal. A sailing yacht adds a classic aesthetic, all wood and canvas, for a more timeless look. RIBs are faster but less spacious, better for action shots or a quick run to the Strait of Gibraltar to shoot with dolphins in the frame. Superyachts are available on request if you need serious scale and luxury.

Every boat includes safety equipment, insurance, and a skipper who speaks English and Spanish. You do not need a boating licence. Just turn up with your crew and your camera gear.

Ports and Departure Points for Your Shoot

Puerto Banús is the obvious starting point. It is the most famous marina on the Costa del Sol, packed with superyachts, designer shops, and the kind of backdrop that screams money. You can shoot on the dock before you even leave, using the boats and the palm trees as set dressing. Departures from here put you minutes from the open sea and the Marbella shoreline.

Marbella Marina, also known as Puerto Deportivo, is a quieter alternative. It sits right in the centre of Marbella, close to the old town and the orange-tree-lined squares. If you want a more relaxed vibe, shoot here and then head towards the dunes of Artola or the cliffs at Cabopino. Cabopino itself is a small port with a sandy beach and a nature reserve behind it, good for a rustic feel without the bling.

Estepona port is further west, near the old town with its flower pots and whitewashed walls. The water here is calmer, and the views stretch across to Gibraltar on a clear day. Sotogrande is the polo set territory, manicured and exclusive, with a long estuary that makes for interesting reflections. Benalmádena, east of Marbella, gives you quick access to the coastline towards Torremolinos and the mountains behind.

Each port has its own character, and your photographer will have a preference based on the look you want. Talk to us about which one suits your mood. We can arrange pickup from any of them.

Boat Options for Your Photoshoot Yacht Charter Marbella

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for photoshoots because they look expensive and modern. Think Azimut, Sunseeker, or Princess models from around 40 to 80 feet. They have large sunpads, a flybridge with a panoramic view, and a salon that doubles as a dressing room. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day charter, depending on the size and season.

Catamarans offer more deck space per euro, so if you have a large crew or need room for lighting equipment, this is the smarter pick. A Lagoon 42 or similar gives you a wide bow, a shaded cockpit, and a trampoline net that looks great from above. Half-day rates begin around EUR 2,000, but you get more usable area than a monohull of the same length.

Sailing yachts bring a different energy. The lines of a classic sloop or a ketch, the mast against the sky, the sails catching the wind. They are slower, so you cover less distance, but the aesthetic is hard to beat for editorial or fashion work. Expect to pay from EUR 1,200 for a half-day on a 40-foot sailboat.

RIBs and speedboats are for the action crowd. If you want spray, speed, and a sporty look, a RIB with outboards can deliver. They are also the cheapest option, from around EUR 600 for a couple of hours. Use them for swimwear shots or to chase the sunset along the coast.

Licence-free day boats are a niche option. These are small motorboats that do not require a licence to drive, but since every charter includes a skipper anyway, the main advantage is the lower cost and the simplicity. They are fine for casual shoots but lack the wow factor of a proper yacht.

Superyachts are the top tier. If you need a 30-metre-plus vessel with a helipad, a jacuzzi, and a crew of eight, price on request. These are for major productions, luxury brand campaigns, or private clients who want to flex. We can source them through our network with a few days notice.

Pricing Guidance for Your Photoshoot Charter

Prices depend on the boat, the duration, the season, and the port. As a rough guide, a half-day motor yacht charter from Puerto Banús in June starts around EUR 1,500. A full day on a catamaran in August can go up to EUR 4,000 or more. Off-peak months like May or October drop by about 20 to 30 percent.

Extra costs to consider: catering (EUR 50 to EUR 150 per person for a decent spread), photographer hire (EUR 300 to EUR 800 for a few hours, depending on their portfolio), drone permits (some areas restrict drone use, but your skipper can advise), and fuel surcharges for long distances. The base price usually covers the boat, the skipper, and basic drinks. Everything else is optional.

We do not add hidden fees. The price you see on the booking quote is the price you pay, minus any optional extras you choose. Payment is by bank transfer or card, with a deposit upfront and the balance due a week before departure.

Best Seasons for a Photoshoot Yacht Charter Marbella

May through October is the prime window. Air temperatures range from 22 to 32 degrees C, water temperatures from 18 to 26 degrees C. The sun sets late, around 9 pm in June and July, giving you a long golden hour that starts around 7 pm and lasts until dusk. That is the sweet spot for photography.

April and November are shoulder months. The weather is still good, with highs around 20 degrees C, but the crowds are thinner and prices lower. You might get some cloud cover, which can actually help with even lighting. December through March is winter. The marina is quieter, the light is lower, and the water is cooler. Some boats run year-round, but the vibe is different. If you want a moody, off-season look, it works. If you want bikinis and blue skies, wait until May.

Wind matters. The Levante wind blows from the east and can kick up chop, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar area. The Poniente from the west is gentler. Your skipper will know the forecast and can adjust the route to find calm water. Catamarans handle chop better than monohulls, so if you are shooting in spring or autumn, consider a cat.

How to Book Your Photoshoot Yacht Charter Marbella

Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters to pick your port, boat type, and date. You can browse available yachts with photos and specs, then send an enquiry for the one you like. We will confirm availability within a few hours and send you a quote.

Tell us in the notes that this is for a photoshoot. That way we can suggest boats with the best deck layouts, sun exposure, and storage for your gear. We can also recommend photographers if you do not have one. We have worked with several local pros who know the coastline and the light.

Once you book, we send you the skipper contact details and the meeting point instructions. On the day, you arrive at the port, meet the skipper, load your equipment, and go. The boat is prepped and fuelled. You just bring your camera, your talent, and your vision.

For last-minute bookings, call us. We can sometimes arrange same-day departures if a boat is available, especially on weekdays. Weekends in July and August book out weeks in advance, so plan ahead.

Who This Photoshoot Yacht Charter Is For

Influencers and content creators who need a fresh backdrop for Instagram or TikTok. The Marbella coast is saturated with poolside shots, but a yacht charter sets you apart. Brands launching a new product, from swimwear to watches to cosmetics, can use the boat as a mobile set. Couples doing engagement or anniversary shoots get the romance of the sea without the crowds of a public beach.

Fashion editors and magazine teams looking for a location that combines luxury with nature. The contrast between the blue water and the white hulls, the green hills behind, and the sky is a palette that works for editorial spreads. Even corporate teams use yacht charters for team photos or executive portraits that say success without saying it out loud.

If you are a photographer yourself, you can rent the boat as your studio. Bring your own lighting, models, and assistants. The skipper stays out of the way but is there if you need to move. You get full creative control.

Local Colour and Shooting Locations

Puerto Banús is the obvious hero shot. The marina itself, with the luxury cars parked on the quay and the yachts lined up, is a visual shorthand for wealth. But the real magic is offshore. Head out past the breakwater and look back at the coast. The mountains rise behind the town, and the water turns a deep blue. Shoot from the bow looking towards the shore for a classic Marbella image.

Cala del Faro, a small cove between Marbella and Cabopino, has a lighthouse and rocky cliffs. The water is clear and shallow, good for waist-deep shots or reflections. Estepona old town, from the sea, shows a different side of the coast. The white buildings and the church tower stand out against the green hills.

Sail further west and you reach the Strait of Gibraltar. This is where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean, and where pods of common dolphins and pilot whales often feed. If you time it right, you can get shots with dolphins in the frame. It is not guaranteed, but the skipper knows the hotspots and can increase your odds.

For a completely different look, go east towards the Nerja caves. The cliffs here are dramatic, with caves carved into the limestone and clear water below. It is a longer trip, about two hours from Marbella, so you need a full-day charter. But the payoff is a set of images that look nothing like the usual Costa del Sol fare.

We have written more about the local spots on our blog. Check it for route ideas and photography tips from people who have done it before.

Finding the Right Boat for Your Photoshoot

Use the search tool on BoatHire24 to filter by port, boat type, and availability. You can see real photos of each boat, not stock images, so you know exactly what you are getting. Compare deck plans, cabin layouts, and amenities. If you need a boat with a flybridge for overhead shots, filter for motor yachts. If you want a flat deck for a group shot, choose a catamaran.

Read the boat descriptions carefully. Some boats have a large sunpad on the bow, others have a shaded cockpit. Some have a tender for getting closer to the shore. The more you know, the better your shoot will be.

If you are unsure, contact us. We have been on most of the boats in our fleet and can give you honest advice. We do not upsell. We tell you which boat fits your brief.

Practical Tips for a Smooth Photoshoot on a Yacht

Arrive early. The port can be busy, and parking near Puerto Banús is a hassle. Give yourself 30 minutes to find the boat, meet the skipper, and load your gear. Bring a dry bag for your camera equipment. Salt spray and electronics do not mix. A UV filter on the lens helps reduce glare from the water.

Wear sunscreen, even if it is overcast. The reflection off the water doubles the UV exposure. Your models will thank you. Bring water and snacks. Most boats have a fridge and a cooler, but stock up before you board. If you are shooting for several hours, order catering in advance. Cold seafood and a chilled bottle of Albariño look good in the frame and keep everyone happy.

Communicate with the skipper about the shots you want. They can position the boat to block the wind or to catch the sun at a specific angle. They know where the jellyfish are in August and where the sea is calmest. Use their local knowledge.

Finally, have a backup plan for weather. The Costa del Sol has 320 sunny days a year, but a cloudy day can still happen. If the forecast is iffy, consider a catamaran with a large shaded area so you can shoot under cover. Or reschedule. We can move your booking to another day with no penalty if you give us 48 hours notice.

h1: Hen Do Boat Rental Marbella: Party Packages
intro:
You are planning a hen do in Marbella and you want something that doesn't involve a sweaty nightclub or a crowded beach. A private boat rental is the answer. You get your own floating party venue with a licensed skipper, a sound system, and a fridge full of cava. No queues, no dress codes, no drama. Just you, your crew, and the Mediterranean.

BoatHire24 connects you with owners of motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs in Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and other Costa del Sol ports. Every charter includes a professional skipper, so you can focus on the prosecco and the playlist. We have seen every type of hen party, from low-key sunset cruises to all-day raves with a DJ. You tell us what you want, and we find the boat that fits.

This page covers everything you need to know about hen do boat rental Marbella: which ports to use, what boats work best, how much it costs, and how to book without stress. Read on.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Hen Do Boat Rental Marbella

Every hen party charter through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation, safety, and docking. You do not need a boating licence or any experience. The skipper stays sober and professional, which is a relief when the bride-to-be is already three glasses deep.

Most boats come with a Bluetooth sound system, a cooler or fridge, and basic safety equipment. Some owners offer optional extras such as a paddleboard, a snorkel set, or a floating mat for swimming stops. You can also add catering: tapas platters, paella, sushi, or a full barbecue. Drinks are usually BYO, but some packages include a welcome bottle of cava or a cocktail kit.

Typical inclusions: skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary (usually 3-4 hours), insurance, and VAT. Exclusions: food, drinks, dockage fees if you stop at a beach club, and tips for the crew. Always confirm what is included before you pay.

Which Port Is Best for a Hen Party Boat

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice. It is the glitzy marina with the superyachts, the designer shops, and the constant buzz. You depart from the heart of Marbella's nightlife, so you can go straight from the boat to a club or a restaurant. The downside: it gets busy, and parking is a nightmare. If you are staying in a hotel in the area, take a taxi.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and more relaxed. It is closer to the old town and the beachfront promenade. Boats here tend to be slightly cheaper because the location is less flashy. Good for a hen party that wants a chilled afternoon with a swim stop at Cala del Faro.

Cabopino is a small, sandy marina near the dunes of Artola. It is popular with catamarans and sailing yachts. If your group prefers a natural setting over a glitzy one, Cabopino works well. Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena are also options, especially if you are staying on the western side of the Costa del Sol or near Gibraltar.

Best Boat Types for a Hen Do

Catamarans are the top choice for hen parties. They have a wide, stable deck, plenty of seating, and a shallow draft that lets you anchor close to the beach. A 40-foot catamaran can take 12-16 guests comfortably. You get a trampoline net at the front for sunbathing and a shaded area at the back for the cooler. The motion is gentle, so seasickness is less likely.

Motor yachts are faster and more glamorous. A 50-foot Sunseeker or Princess gives you that celebrity vibe. You can cruise to the Marbella coastline in style, drop anchor off the Río Verde, and jump into the sea. Motor yachts are better for smaller groups (up to 10-12) because the deck space is narrower than a catamaran.

RIBs and speedboats are for the adventurous hen. They are fast, open, and wet. You can zip to the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins, or explore the coves near Estepona. But they are not ideal for lounging or drinking heavily. Use them for a short, high-energy trip.

Sailing yachts are the quiet option. They are slower, more romantic, and less party-oriented. If the bride wants a peaceful sail with a glass of wine rather than a rave, a sailing yacht works. But for a classic hen party, stick to a cat or a motor yacht.

Licence-free day boats are small, slow, and easy to handle. They are legal to drive without a licence in Spain (under 6 metres and under 15 hp). You can rent one yourself, but we recommend hiring a skipper anyway so you can relax. These boats are best for a small group of 4-6 people.

How Much Does a Hen Do Boat Rental Marbella Cost

Prices vary by boat size, duration, season, and extras. As a rough guide: a 4-hour charter on a 40-foot catamaran for up to 12 people costs from around EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,000 in high season. A 50-foot motor yacht for 10 people might run EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,000 for half a day. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper, from EUR 500 to EUR 1,000 for 3-4 hours.

Full-day charters (6-8 hours) cost roughly double the half-day rate. Sunset cruises (2-3 hours) are cheaper, from EUR 600 to EUR 1,200 for a catamaran. Superyachts are price on request, but expect EUR 10,000 and up for a day.

Peak season is July to September, when demand is highest and prices are 20-30% more than in May or October. Easter and the Feria de Marbella (June) also push prices up. If you are flexible, book in May or late September for better rates and still-good weather (25-28 degrees C).

Extra costs to budget for: food and drinks (EUR 20-40 per person for catering), crew tip (10-15% of the charter fee), and dockage fees if you stop at a beach club like Ocean Club or Nikki Beach (EUR 50-150 per stop).

What to Expect on the Day

You meet the boat at the marina 15 minutes before departure. The skipper gives a quick safety briefing and explains the itinerary. You board, put your bags down, and the party starts. Most charters include a swim stop at a calm cove like Cala del Faro or near the Río Verde. You can jump off the boat, use a paddleboard, or float on a mat.

The skipper will anchor for 30-60 minutes. After swimming, you cruise along the coast, past the luxury villas and the La Concha mountain in the background. Music plays, drinks flow, and you take photos with the Marbella skyline behind you.

Return to port is usually 30 minutes before the end time, so you have time to freshen up and head out for dinner or clubbing. Some groups book a second boat for the evening, or reserve a table at a beach club. Your skipper can recommend a restaurant or a club if you ask.

Weather is key. If the wind is strong or the sea is rough, the skipper may cancel or change the itinerary. This is rare in summer, but it happens. We always recommend a backup plan, such as a beach club or a private dining room.

How to Book a Hen Do Boat Rental Marbella

You can browse available boats on our search page and filter by date, group size, and budget. Each listing shows the boat specs, photos, and the owner's contact details. You can message the owner directly to ask about availability and customise the package.

Payment is usually a deposit (30-50%) at booking, with the balance due a week before departure. We recommend reading the cancellation policy carefully. Most owners offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days or more in advance, but stricter policies apply in peak season.

If you need help choosing, send us an email or use the chat widget. We have organised dozens of hen parties and know which boats work best for dancing, swimming, and drinking. We can also suggest a DJ, a photographer, or a catering company if you want to upgrade.

For more tips on planning a boat party, check out our blog.

Who Is a Hen Do Boat Rental For

This is for any group of women celebrating a bride-to-be, whether it is a small group of 6 or a big crew of 20. It works for all ages, from 20-something party girls to 50-something second-wedding celebrations. The boat adapts to your vibe: loud music and dancing, or quiet sunbathing and conversation.

It is also for groups who want a private, exclusive experience. You do not share the boat with strangers. You control the playlist, the food, and the itinerary. No bouncers, no queue for the bar, no one spilling your drink. Just your crew and the sea.

If the bride loves the water, hates crowds, or just wants a memorable day, a boat rental is a solid choice. It is also a great option for a joint hen-and-stag party, if you rent two boats and meet at a beach club.

Local Colour and Activities

Marbella and the Costa del Sol offer more than just a boat ride. You can combine your charter with a visit to the Nerja caves (about 45 minutes east), a dolphin-watching trip near the Strait of Gibraltar, or a walk through Estepona old town with its flower-covered streets. Many hen parties do a boat trip in the afternoon, then head to Puerto Banús for dinner and a nightclub.

If you want a full day out, book a charter that stops at a beach club for lunch. Ocean Club in Marbella, Nikki Beach in Estepona, and Playa Padre in Cabopino all have mooring buoys for boats. You can dock, eat, swim, and dance without leaving the water.

For a more relaxed vibe, anchor near the Río Verde and swim to the shore. The water is clear, the sand is soft, and there are no crowds. It is a favourite spot for locals.

If you are interested in the history of the area, ask your skipper about the Moorish watchtowers along the coast or the Roman ruins in Benalmádena. Some skippers are happy to give a mini tour.

Frequently Asked Questions

How to Choose the Right Duration for Your Hen Party

Half-day charters (4 hours) are the most popular for hen dos. You get enough time for a swim stop, some cruising, and a few glasses of cava without it dragging on. A 4-hour slot works well if you plan to go out in the evening. Full-day charters (6-8 hours) suit groups that want a proper beach club lunch, two swim stops, and a relaxed pace. Sunset cruises (2-3 hours) are cheaper and photogenic, but you skip the swimming and the lunch. If your group is heavy on the drinking, stick to half-day. Eight hours on a boat with unlimited booze can end with someone asleep in the bathroom.

What to Bring on a Hen Do Boat Trip

Suncream (factor 50, reapply), sunglasses, a hat, and a towel are non-negotiable. The Spanish sun is brutal even at 10am. Bring a waterproof phone case or a dry bag for your valuables. Seasickness tablets are a good idea if anyone is unsure, even on a catamaran. Take them 30 minutes before departure. For the bride, a veil, a sash, or a inflatable swan float makes for good photos. Bring your own speaker if the boat's sound system is weak, but check with the skipper first. Leave glass bottles at home, most skippers ban glass on deck. Cans and plastic cups are fine.

Best Months for a Hen Do Boat Rental Marbella

June and September are the sweet spots. The weather is 27-30 degrees C, the sea is warm enough for swimming, and the marinas are less crowded than July and August. Prices are 15-20% lower than peak season. May and October are also possible, but the water is cooler (18-20 degrees C in May) and evenings can be chilly. July and August are hot (32-35 degrees C) and busy, but the party atmosphere is at its peak. Avoid November to March unless you want a winter hen do with possible rain and rough seas. April is hit and miss, some years are warm, some are windy.

How to Split Costs Among the Group

Most hen parties divide the total charter fee equally among all guests. For a 12-person catamaran at EUR 1,800, that is EUR 150 per person. Add catering at EUR 30 per person and drinks at EUR 20 per person, and the total is EUR 200 per head. Some groups ask the bride to pay nothing, others split her share among the group. Decide before booking. Use a payment app like Bizum or Revolut to collect money from everyone. The person booking the boat should collect deposits from the group before paying the owner. If someone drops out, you need a backup plan or a cancellation policy that covers you.

Can You Have a Hen Do Boat Party Without a Skipper

Technically, yes, if you rent a licence-free day boat (under 6 metres, under 15 hp). These are small, slow, and limited to 4-6 people. You can drive them yourself without a licence in Spain. But for a hen party of 8 or more, you need a proper boat with a skipper. The skipper is not just a legal requirement, they handle the anchor, the music, and the safety. They also know the best coves and can recommend a good beach club. Without a skipper, you are stuck navigating, parking, and watching the fuel gauge. That is not a hen do, that is a chore.

What to Do If the Weather Turns Bad on the Day

The skipper decides, not you. If the wind is over 20 knots or the sea state is rough, they may cancel or change the itinerary. In summer, this is rare but it happens, especially in the afternoon when the Levante wind picks up. Most owners offer a full refund or a reschedule if they cancel. If you cancel because of a weather forecast, the policy depends on the owner. Some are flexible, others are not. Book a morning charter if you want the calmest sea. Afternoons can get choppy, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar. Always have a backup plan, a beach club, a restaurant, or a private room at a hotel.

How to Combine a Boat Trip with a Beach Club Visit

Many hen parties book a charter that stops at a beach club for lunch. Ocean Club in Marbella and Nikki Beach in Estepona have mooring buoys for boats. You dock, walk up to the restaurant, and eat without leaving the water. The cost is around EUR 50-150 per stop, depending on the club and the season. Some clubs require a minimum spend per person. Book the mooring in advance, especially in July and August. Alternatively, anchor near the club and swim ashore. This works at Playa Padre in Cabopino and La Sala in Puerto Banús. Your skipper can arrange the mooring if you tell them in advance.

Are There Any Rules About Drinking on a Boat in Spain

There is no law against drinking alcohol on a private charter in Spanish waters. The skipper must stay sober, that is a legal requirement. Guests can drink as much as they want, within reason. If someone becomes dangerously drunk or aggressive, the skipper has the right to end the charter early and return to port. You will not get a refund for that. Open containers of alcohol are not allowed on the dock or in the marina. Finish your drink before you step off the boat. Glass bottles are banned on most boats for safety reasons. Use cans or plastic cups.

What to Wear on a Hen Do Boat Trip

Swimwear, a cover-up, and non-slip shoes. High heels are a bad idea on a boat, the deck gets slippery and you will fall. Flat sandals or barefoot is fine. A light jacket or a hoodie is useful for the return trip when the wind picks up. For photos, bright colours and coordinated outfits work well. Some hen parties do matching t-shirts or customised caps. Do not bring expensive jewellery or designer bags, they can get wet or damaged. A small cross-body bag is practical. Leave the big tote bags onshore.

How to Handle Seasickness in Your Group

Catamarans are the most stable, they roll less than monohulls. If anyone is prone to seasickness, book a catamaran. Take seasickness tablets 30 minutes before departure, not when you feel sick. Ginger sweets, mint tea, and dry crackers help. Avoid heavy food and alcohol before the trip. Stay on deck in the fresh air, not inside the cabin. Focus on the horizon, not your phone. If someone does vomit, the skipper will have a bucket and a plastic bag. It happens, it is not a big deal. The crew are used to it.

faqs.a: Yes, most boats have a Bluetooth sound system. You can connect your phone and play your playlist. Some owners provide a portable speaker if the boat's system is older. Check the listing for details.

faqs.q: How far in advance should we book a hen do boat rental?
faqs.a: Book at least 2-4 weeks in advance, especially in peak season (July-September). For popular boats like catamarans, book 2-3 months ahead if possible. Last-minute bookings are possible but limited.

title: Starlite Boat Rental Marbella: Concert Transfer
metaDescription: Book a Starlite boat rental Marbella for concert transfers. Luxury motor yacht or catamaran from Puerto Banús. Licensed skipper, drinks, and sunset views included.
h1: Starlite Boat Rental Marbella: Concert Transfer by Sea
intro:
Starlite Marbella is the Costa del Sol's most glamorous open-air concert series, held every summer in the Cantera de Nagüeles quarry. Getting there by road means traffic jams, parking stress, and a sweaty queue. A Starlite boat rental Marbella solves that. You arrive by sea, walk off the dock at Puerto Banús, and take a short taxi or pre-arranged transfer to the venue. The boat becomes your private lounge for the evening, with a licensed skipper, drinks, and a front-row seat for the sunset over La Concha mountain.

BoatHire24 connects you with skippered motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs that depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or Cabopino. Every charter includes fuel, insurance, and a professional crew. You just bring your tickets and your party.
bodyHtml:
Why Take a Boat to Starlite Marbella

Starlite is not near the coast. The venue sits inland, about 10 minutes by car from Puerto Banús. But the journey by sea turns the evening into an event. You meet your boat at the marina, cruise along the Marbella coastline with a drink in hand, watch the sun drop behind the Sierra Blanca mountains, then dock and take a short taxi to the quarry. After the concert, you reverse the process. No traffic jams, no parking fees, no designated driver.

The boat is yours for the entire evening, typically from around 19:00 to 01:00. You can anchor off Cala del Faro for a swim before the show, or simply enjoy the sea breeze and the skyline of Marbella. It is a flexible, private experience that beats any pre-booked table at a beach club.

What Is Included in a Starlite Boat Rental

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and VAT. You do not need a boating licence. The skipper handles navigation, docking, and safety. You handle the fun.

Typical inclusions for a Starlite evening charter:

  • 4-6 hours of cruising, usually 19:00-01:00 or 20:00-02:00
  • Skipper and crew (if applicable)
  • Fuel and port fees
  • Onboard sound system (Bluetooth)
  • Cooler with ice, soft drinks, and water
  • Snorkelling gear if you stop for a swim
  • Optional catering: tapas, paella, sushi, or a full dinner

You can bring your own drinks and food, or order a catering package through the boat owner. Many boats have a barbecue on the aft deck.

Which Ports Can You Depart From

Starlite boat rentals depart from the main marinas on the Costa del Sol. The closest and most convenient is Puerto Banús, about 10 minutes by taxi from the venue. Other options:

  • Puerto Banús, The most popular departure point. Glamorous, full of superyachts, and a short drive to Starlite. Taxi cost around EUR 15-20 each way.
  • Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Also close, about 15 minutes by taxi. Slightly less flashy than Banús, but easy parking if you drive to the marina.
  • Cabopino, A quieter marina east of Marbella, around 20 minutes by taxi. Good if you want a more relaxed start to the evening.
  • Estepona, About 25 minutes by taxi. A charming old town to explore before the charter.
  • Sotogrande, Further west, around 30 minutes. Ideal if you are staying in the Sotogrande area.
  • Benalmádena, East of Marbella, around 30 minutes. A practical option if you are based near Málaga or Torremolinos.

Your skipper will recommend the best departure time based on sunset, tide, and the concert schedule.

Boat Types for Starlite Transfers

The right boat depends on your group size and style. Here are the main options available on BoatHire24:

Motor Yachts

From 30 to 60+ feet. Speedy, stable, and luxurious. Most have a flybridge for panoramic views, a saloon with air conditioning, and a bow sunpad. Perfect for groups of 6-12 who want to arrive in style. Prices from around EUR 1,200 for a 4-hour charter.

Catamarans

Wide, stable decks, great for parties. Catamarans offer more deck space than monohulls of the same length. Ideal for groups of 10-20. Prices from around EUR 1,500 for a 4-hour charter.

Sailing Yachts

Slower but more atmospheric. If you want a quiet, romantic evening, a sailing yacht under engine or sail is a good choice. Typically 35-50 feet. Prices from around EUR 800 for a 4-hour charter.

RIBs and Speedboats

Fast, open, and exhilarating. RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) seat 6-12 and can reach 40+ knots. They are not ideal for formal events, but perfect for a young group who want to feel the wind. Prices from around EUR 600 for a 3-hour charter.

Licence-Free Day Boats

Smaller motorboats (up to 15 hp) that you can drive without a licence. Not recommended for Starlite because they are slow and lack amenities. Better for a daytime trip.

Superyachts

For high-net-worth groups, superyachts over 80 feet are available. Full crew, jet skis, helipad on some. Price on request, but expect EUR 10,000+ for an evening.

Browse all options on the search page and filter by boat type, capacity, and price.

Pricing Guidance for Starlite Boat Rentals

Prices vary by boat size, duration, season, and extras. Here is a rough guide for a 4-hour evening charter (19:00-23:00 or 20:00-00:00):

  • Motor yacht 30-40 ft: from around EUR 1,200
  • Motor yacht 40-50 ft: from around EUR 1,800
  • Catamaran 35-45 ft: from around EUR 1,500
  • Sailing yacht 35-45 ft: from around EUR 900
  • RIB 8-10 m: from around EUR 600
  • Superyacht: price on request

These are base rates. Extras like catering, open bar, or a photographer add EUR 200-500. Peak season (July-August) and weekends command a 20-30% premium. Booking early (at least 2 weeks ahead) helps secure the best boats.

All prices are in EUR and include skipper, fuel, insurance, and VAT. No hidden fees.

Best Season and Timing for Starlite

Starlite runs from late June to early September, with concerts most nights. The best time for a boat transfer is July and August, when the evenings are warm (25-30 degrees C at 8 PM) and the sunset is around 21:30-21:45. You get a golden hour cruise before the show.

Book your charter for 19:00 or 20:00 departure. This gives you 1.5-2 hours of cruising before you need to head to the venue. After the concert (usually ends around 01:00), you return to the boat for a nightcap and a slow cruise back. The sea is calm, the stars are out, and the coast is lit up.

If you book for a June or September concert, the sun sets earlier (around 21:00 in June, 20:30 in September), so adjust your departure accordingly.

How to Book a Starlite Boat Rental

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward:

  1. Go to the search page and enter your date, group size, and preferred port.
  2. Browse the available boats. Each listing shows photos, specs, capacity, and price.
  3. Send a booking request or use the instant booking option if available. You will pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the date.
  4. The boat owner or skipper confirms the charter and sends you the meeting point and departure time.
  5. On the day, you arrive at the marina, meet the skipper, and board. The remaining balance is paid on the day (cash or card, depending on the boat).

If you need help choosing, contact our team via the website. We can recommend boats that suit your group and budget.

For more tips on planning your evening, check our blog for guides on Marbella nightlife, marina dining, and the best sunset spots.

Who Is a Starlite Boat Rental For

This experience works for:

  • Couples celebrating an anniversary or birthday
  • Groups of friends who want a VIP night out
  • Corporate clients entertaining guests
  • Families with older children (teens and up)
  • Anyone who hates traffic and loves the sea

It is not ideal for very young children (safety concerns on open decks) or for people prone to seasickness (though the sea is usually calm in the evening).

If you are attending a Starlite concert, a boat transfer turns a simple night out into a memorable event. You arrive relaxed, you leave refreshed, and you get a story to tell.

How the Evening Unfolds: A Typical Starlite Boat Itinerary

You meet your skipper at the marina around 18:45. He greets you, helps with bags, and gives a quick safety briefing. Within five minutes you are casting off. The engine hums, the coast slides past, and someone pours a glass of cava. You cruise west past the golden sands of Marbella, the luxury hotels of the Golden Mile, and the pine-clad hills of the Sierra Blanca. Around 20:00, the skipper drops anchor in a quiet cove like Cala del Faro or off Cabopino beach. You swim in warm, calm water as the sun turns orange. At 20:45, you dry off, dress, and head back to the marina. A pre-booked taxi meets you at 21:00 and delivers you to the Starlite gate in ten minutes. After the concert ends around 01:00, the same taxi brings you back to the boat. You board, the skipper hands you a nightcap, and you cruise slowly back under the stars. You dock by 01:30, tired but happy.

Why Departing from Puerto Banús Is the Smartest Choice

Puerto Banús is the closest marina to Starlite, about 5.5 km inland via the A-7 motorway. A taxi takes 8-12 minutes and costs EUR 15-20 each way. The marina itself is a destination: designer boutiques, champagne bars, and superyachts. You can arrive early, have a drink at a beachfront terrace, then walk to your boat. After the concert, the taxi drops you back at the port, and you can extend the evening at a club like Pangea or Olivia Valere. No other departure port offers this combination of proximity, glamour, and nightlife. If you are staying in Marbella or Nueva Andalucía, Puerto Banús is the logical choice. If you are based further east or west, pick the marina closest to your accommodation to minimise taxi costs.

What to Wear and Bring for a Starlite Boat Evening

The evening splits into three phases: the boat cruise, the concert, and the return cruise. Pack accordingly. For the boat, bring a swimsuit, a towel, sunscreen (the sun is still strong at 7 PM), and a light jacket or jumper for the return after midnight when the sea breeze drops the temperature to around 22 degrees C. For the concert, smart-casual works: linen trousers and a shirt for men, a summer dress or jumpsuit for women. Starlite is not black-tie, but it is not a beach bar either. Avoid high heels on the boat (they damage the deck and are dangerous on wet surfaces). Bring a small bag for your phone, wallet, and keys. The boat has a cooler with water and soft drinks, but you can bring your own wine or champagne. Glass bottles are fine, but the skipper will ask you to use plastic cups on deck for safety.

How to Combine a Starlite Boat Charter with a Day at Sea

Starlite concerts start around 22:00, so you have the entire day free. Many guests book a full-day charter from 10:00 to 19:00, then a quick return to the marina, a taxi to the venue, and the concert. This gives you a full day of swimming, snorkelling, and sunbathing, followed by a world-class show. A typical day charter costs from around EUR 2,500 for a 40-foot motor yacht (10 hours). You cruise east to the cliffs of Cabopino or west to the dunes of Artola, stop for lunch at a chiringuito like Los Sardinales, and anchor for a siesta. Then you return to the marina, shower at the port facilities (most marinas have clean showers for charter guests), change, and head to Starlite. This combo works best for groups of 6-10 who want maximum value from their boat hire.

Which Artists Have Played Starlite and Why That Matters for Your Charter

Starlite has hosted Tom Jones, Sting, Lionel Richie, Norah Jones, and Jamie Cullum, among others. The venue holds around 3,000 people, so it is intimate by concert standards. The artist affects your boat planning in two ways. First, big-name acts sell out months in advance, so you need to book your boat early too (March or April for a July concert). Second, the concert end time varies: a solo acoustic artist might finish by 23:30, while a full band with encores can run until 01:30. Confirm the expected end time with the venue when you buy tickets, then tell your skipper so he can adjust the charter duration. Most skippers offer a flexible return window of plus or minus 30 minutes without extra charge. If the concert runs late, you pay a small overtime fee (around EUR 100-150 per extra hour).

Taxi Logistics from the Marina to Starlite and Back

You need a reliable taxi service, not a random street cab. Pre-book a taxi in Marbella through a local company like Tele Taxi Marbella (+34 952 82 82 82) or Radio Taxi Puerto Banús (+34 952 81 21 21). Book two separate trips: one for the outward journey (pickup at the marina at 20:45, drop-off at Starlite at 21:00) and one for the return (pickup at Starlite at 01:00, drop-off at the marina at 01:15). The return trip can be chaotic as hundreds of people leave at once. Your pre-booked taxi will be waiting at a designated spot. Confirm the exact meeting point with the driver in advance (e.g., "the taxi rank outside the main entrance, near the Starlite sign"). The cost is EUR 15-20 each way. If you are a group of 6-8, you might need a minibus or two taxis. Factor this into your budget.

The Best Boats for a Starlite Evening Based on Group Size

For two people, a 30-foot motor yacht like a Jeanneau Leader or a small sailing yacht (35 feet) works well. You get privacy, a sunpad, and a small saloon. For four people, a 40-foot motor yacht like a Sunseeker Portofino or a Beneteau Gran Turismo offers more space and a flybridge. For six to eight people, a 50-foot motor yacht or a 42-foot catamaran gives everyone room to spread out. For ten to twelve people, a 55-foot motor yacht or a 50-foot catamaran is ideal. For larger groups of 14-20, you need a catamaran over 45 feet or a superyacht. The key constraint is seating for the evening cruise: you want enough deck space for everyone to sit comfortably with a drink. Catamarans win here because the deck is wide and flat. Motor yachts have more enclosed space but less open deck area per person.

How Weather Affects Your Starlite Boat Charter

Summer evenings on the Costa del Sol are usually calm, but the sea can get choppy if the Levante wind blows from the east. The Levante is common in July and August and can create waves of 1-2 metres in the Alboran Sea. Your skipper monitors the forecast and will advise if conditions are safe. If the sea is too rough, you have two options: cancel and get a full refund (if you booked with a free cancellation policy) or switch to a larger, more stable boat like a catamaran. Catamarans handle chop much better than monohulls. In practice, 95% of Starlite evening charters go ahead without issues. If the wind picks up, the skipper will adjust the route to stay in sheltered waters close to the coast. The worst-case scenario is a cancelled charter, but that is rare. Check the forecast on the day and stay flexible.

How to Save Money on a Starlite Boat Rental

Book early (March or April) to lock in lower rates. Avoid the peak Starlite dates (July 15 to August 15) if possible, as prices are 20-30% higher. Choose a weekday concert (Monday to Thursday) instead of Friday or Saturday. Depart from a smaller marina like Cabopino or Estepona instead of Puerto Banús, as some boat owners offer discounts for less popular ports. Skip the catering package and bring your own food and drinks. A cooler with sandwiches, fruit, and a bottle of wine costs a fraction of the EUR 300-500 catering fee. Limit the charter duration to 4 hours (19:00-23:00) instead of 6 hours. You get the sunset cruise, a swim stop, and time to dress before the concert. The return cruise after the show is short (15-20 minutes), so you do not need extra hours. If you are on a tight budget, consider a RIB or speedboat for EUR 600-800 for a group of 6-8, splitting the cost per person to around EUR 75-100 each.

faqs.q: How far is Starlite from Puerto Banús marina?
faqs.a: Starlite is about 5 km inland, a 10-minute taxi ride from Puerto Banús. Taxis cost around EUR 15-20 each way. Your skipper can help arrange a taxi or a private transfer.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own drinks and food on the boat?
faqs.a: Yes, most boats allow you to bring your own drinks and food. Some boats have a minimum catering spend or a corkage fee. Check the boat listing or ask the owner. Many boats offer catering packages if you prefer.

faqs.q: Do I need a boating licence?
faqs.a: No. Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles all navigation and safety. You just enjoy the ride.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.a: The skipper will assess conditions on the day. If the sea is unsafe, the charter can be rescheduled or cancelled with a full refund. Starlite concerts are rarely cancelled due to weather.

faqs.q: Can I book a boat for just the transfer, without the cruise?
faqs.a: You can, but it is not common. Most charters include a pre- and post-concert cruise. If you just want a direct transfer, mention it in the booking request and the skipper may offer a reduced rate.

faqs.q: How many people can fit on a boat for Starlite?
faqs.a: Boats range from 6 to 20+ guests. Motor yachts and catamarans typically seat 8-12 comfortably. RIBs seat 6-12. Superyachts can accommodate larger groups. Check the boat capacity on the listing.

faqs.q: Is parking available at the marina?
faqs.a: Yes, all major marinas have paid parking. Puerto Banús has a large underground car park (around EUR 3 per hour). Marbella Marina also has parking. We recommend arriving 15-20 minutes before departure to find a spot.

title: Austin Rental Boats
metaDescription: Searching for austin rental boats? BoatHire24 has motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs with skippers in Marbella and Costa del Sol. Book direct today.
h1: Austin Rental Boats, Book a Skippered Charter on the Costa del Sol
intro:
If you typed “austin rental boats” into Google expecting a lake in Texas, you are in for a surprise, or a pleasant detour. We are BoatHire24, based in Marbella, Spain, and we rent boats with skippers on the Costa del Sol. There is no lake, no barbecue joint, and no Willie Nelson soundtrack. What you get is a motor yacht, catamaran, or RIB with a licensed skipper, leaving from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or any port between Estepona and Sotogrande.

You are probably looking for a day on the water, a sunset cruise, or a fishing trip. The answer is yes, we do all of that. Every charter includes a skipper, so you sit back and watch the coastline slide by. Prices start from around EUR 300 for a half-day on a small speedboat, up to EUR 5,000+ for a superyacht. No hidden fees, no captain’s hat required.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in Every Austin Rental Boat Charter

Every boat on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a boating licence, and you do not have to worry about navigation, docking, or fuel. The skipper handles all of that. What you get is the boat, fuel, insurance, and the skipper’s time. Some charters include drinks, snacks, or a BBQ pack, check the listing details. The standard rental period is half-day (4 hours) or full day (8 hours), but you can negotiate longer trips or multi-day charters. The skipper knows the local waters, so you get tips on where to swim, where the dolphins hang out, and which beach bars allow docking.

Departure Ports for Your Austin Rental Boat

You can depart from any of these ports, all within 45 minutes of Marbella. Puerto Banús is the glitzy one, think superyachts, designer shops, and paparazzi. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more relaxed, with a few bars and a fish restaurant. Cabopino is small and quiet, ideal for a quick getaway. Estepona has a long promenade and a charming old town. Sotogrande is exclusive, with a polo club vibe. Benalmádena is further east, near Málaga, and offers a lively marina. Pick the port closest to your hotel, or choose one you want to explore. The skipper will meet you at the dock.

Boat Types Available for Austin Rental Boats

We have five main categories. Motor yachts, from 30 to 60 feet, with cabins, a saloon, and a sun deck. Good for groups of 6 to 12. Catamarans, stable, spacious, and great for families. They have a shallow draft, so you can anchor close to beaches. Sailing yachts, if you want the quiet thrill of wind power, from 35 to 50 feet. RIBs and speedboats, fast, open, and fun. Ideal for 4 to 6 people who want to zoom to Cala del Faro or spot dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar. Fishing boats, equipped with rods, bait, and a skipper who knows the best spots for sea bass, bream, or even tuna. Licence-free day boats, small motorboats under 15 feet that you can drive yourself without a licence, but they are rare and only available from certain ports. Superyachts, over 60 feet, with crew, jet skis, and a price tag to match. Price on request.

Pricing Guidance for Austin Rental Boats

Here is a rough guide. A half-day on a RIB or small motor yacht costs from around EUR 300 to EUR 600. A full day on a 40-foot motor yacht for 8 people costs from around EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,000. A catamaran for 12 people for a full day costs from around EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500. Superyachts start at EUR 5,000 per day and go up. All prices include the skipper and fuel. Some boats charge extra for food, drinks, or port fees, read the listing carefully. You can book directly on BoatHire24 and pay securely online. No booking fee.

Best Seasons for Austin Rental Boats on the Costa del Sol

The season runs from April to October. July and August are peak months, hot (30-35 degrees C), crowded, and expensive. Book two weeks ahead if you want a specific boat. May, June, and September are the sweet spots, warm (25-30 degrees C), fewer tourists, and lower prices. October is still pleasant but the sea cools down. Winter charters are possible but rare, the water is cold (16-18 degrees C) and the weather can be windy. The best time for dolphin spotting is May to September, when the Strait of Gibraltar is calmer. For fishing, spring and autumn are best.

How to Book an Austin Rental Boat with BoatHire24

Go to our search page, enter your preferred date, port, and number of guests. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on one to see the full description, what is included, and the cancellation policy. Then select your time slot, add any extras (like a BBQ or a water sports package), and pay online. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper’s contact details. On the day, meet the skipper at the port 15 minutes before departure. That is it. No paperwork, no hidden costs.

Who Is an Austin Rental Boat For

It is for anyone who wants a day on the water without the hassle of owning a boat. Families with kids, catamarans are stable and have shade. Groups of friends, motor yachts with a sound system and a sun deck. Couples, a sunset cruise on a small sailing yacht. Business clients, a superyacht for a corporate event. Fishermen, a fishing boat with a skipper who knows the local waters. Tourists who want to see the Costa del Sol from the sea, you get views of La Concha mountain, the Marbella skyline, and the cliffs at Cala del Faro. If you are visiting from Austin, Texas, you might not find a paddle steamer on the Colorado River, but you will find a proper Mediterranean charter.

Local Highlights You Can See on Your Austin Rental Boat Trip

From the water, you see a different side of the coast. Puerto Banús from the sea is a forest of masts and white hulls. La Concha mountain looms behind Marbella, often with a cloud cap. Río Verde is a small river mouth near San Pedro, good for a quiet anchorage. Cala del Faro is a rocky cove with a lighthouse, popular for swimming and snorkelling. Estepona old town from the bay looks like a white cube village. The Strait of Gibraltar, if you go far enough west, you might see the African coast and pods of common dolphins or pilot whales. Nerja caves are 50 km east, but a full-day charter can get you there if you start early. The skipper knows the best spots for photos, so ask.

Frequently Asked Questions About Austin Rental Boats

If you have never chartered a boat in Spain, you probably have questions. Here are the most common ones we get. The answers are short and practical.

What to Bring on Your Austin Rental Boat Charter

Pack light. Towel, sunscreen (factor 50, the Spanish sun is brutal), sunglasses, a hat, and a swimsuit. A light jacket or windbreaker for the return trip, the breeze picks up in the afternoon. Non-marking shoes, boat decks are white and scratch easily. Drinks are usually provided, but you can bring your own if the listing allows. No glass bottles, use plastic or cans. Snacks are fine, but avoid anything that melts or crumbles. A waterproof phone case is a good idea for photos. Do not bring large suitcases, there is limited storage on board. The skipper will tell you if the boat has a fridge, ice box, or BBQ. Most do.

How Austin Rental Boats Compare to Other Mediterranean Destinations

The Costa del Sol is not the Balearics or the French Riviera. It is cheaper, less crowded, and more relaxed. A half-day charter from Puerto Banús costs around EUR 300 to EUR 600, while the same boat in Ibiza would be EUR 800 to EUR 1,500. The water is calmer here, the Strait of Gibraltar is protected from the big Atlantic swells. The coastline is varied, from sandy beaches like Cabopino to rocky coves like Cala del Faro. You also get the backdrop of La Concha mountain, which you do not see in the flat islands. If you are used to lake boating in Austin, the Mediterranean is saltier, clearer, and deeper. No alligators, but you might see a loggerhead turtle.

Special Occasions and Events on Austin Rental Boats

Birthday parties, anniversaries, proposals, and corporate events are common. The skipper can help arrange a cake, champagne, or a DJ. Some catamarans have a built-in sound system and a dance floor. For a proposal, the best spots are sunset at Cala del Faro or a quiet anchorage near Río Verde. The skipper will coordinate the timing and keep the crew out of the shot. Corporate charters often include a catered lunch, a presentation area, and water toys like a jet ski or a paddleboard. Prices for events start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a 40-foot motor yacht. For a superyacht with full crew, expect EUR 5,000 to EUR 15,000 per day. Book at least two weeks ahead for events.

Safety and Insurance for Austin Rental Boats

Every boat on BoatHire24 has a valid insurance policy that covers third-party liability and damage to the vessel. The skipper holds a professional licence from the Spanish government. Life jackets are on board for all passengers, and the skipper will give a safety briefing before departure. The boat has a VHF radio, flares, and a first aid kit. In case of bad weather, the skipper decides whether to sail or cancel. You get a full refund if the trip is cancelled due to weather. Do not worry about seasickness, the Costa del Sol is generally calm, but if you are prone to it, take a pill an hour before departure. The skipper will avoid rough areas if you ask.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Austin Rental Trip

Match the boat to your group size and activity. For 2 to 4 people who want speed, a RIB or speedboat is best. You can cover 30 nautical miles in an hour, enough to reach Estepona from Marbella. For 6 to 10 people who want comfort, a motor yacht with a saloon and a sun deck. For families with kids, a catamaran is stable and has a shallow draft, so you can anchor close to the beach. For a romantic sunset, a sailing yacht is quiet and intimate. For fishing, a dedicated fishing boat with rod holders and a live bait well. For a party, a motor yacht with a loud sound system. The search page on BoatHire24 lets you filter by boat type, capacity, and price. Read the description for any restrictions, like no loud music after 8 pm or no smoking inside.

Typical Itineraries for Austin Rental Boats from Puerto Banús

A half-day from Puerto Banús often goes west to Cala del Faro. You leave at 10 am, cruise for 30 minutes, anchor for swimming and snorkelling for 1.5 hours, then head to a beach bar like Chiringuito El Faro for a drink. Back by 2 pm. A full day goes further west to Estepona. You stop at Cala del Faro for the morning, then cruise to Estepona for lunch at a beachfront restaurant, then anchor off the old town for a swim. Back by 6 pm. If you go east from Puerto Banús, you reach Marbella Marina in 15 minutes, then Cabopino in 30 minutes. Cabopino has a quiet beach and a dune reserve. For a longer trip, you can go to the Strait of Gibraltar, about 25 nautical miles west, to see dolphins. That takes 1.5 hours each way, so a full day is needed.

Hidden Costs and Tips for Austin Rental Boats

Most listings include the skipper, fuel, and insurance. But some charge extra for port fees (EUR 20 to EUR 50 per trip), food and drinks (EUR 15 to EUR 30 per person for a BBQ), or water toys (EUR 50 to EUR 100 for a jet ski). Read the listing details carefully. Tipping the skipper is not mandatory but appreciated. A standard tip is 10% of the charter price, given in cash at the end. bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Motor Boat Hire in Crete

A motor boat charter in Crete includes the boat, a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance and basic safety equipment. You don't need a boating licence or any previous experience. The skipper handles navigation, mooring and any paperwork. You just decide the itinerary. Most operators offer half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours) hire. Some also do sunset cruises or multi-day charters. The boat is cleaned and fuelled before you arrive. You bring your own food and drink unless you arrange catering separately. Some larger yachts have a fridge and ice maker. Smaller RIBs have a cooler box. Ask the operator when you book.

Crete's Ports and Departure Points

Motor boat hire in Crete departs from several ports. Heraklion is the main commercial port and has the widest range of boats. Chania has a smaller harbour with a few operators, good for trips to Balos and Gramvousa. Agios Nikolaos is quieter and closer to the eastern coves. Rethymno has a marina with a handful of charter companies. If you're staying in a resort away from these towns, you might need to drive to the departure point. Most operators offer free parking near the marina. Check the location on the booking page before you confirm.

Types of Motor Boats Available in Crete

You can hire several types of motor boat in Crete. RIBs and speedboats are the cheapest option. They are fast and nimble, good for a small group of up to 6 people. They have a basic toilet and a small cabin, but no real living space. Motor yachts are larger and more comfortable, with a saloon, galley, cabins and a proper bathroom. They suit families or groups of up to 12. Superyachts are available for hire but are rare and expensive. Most operators in Crete focus on the 8 to 15 metre range. Fishing boats are also available if you want to combine a day out with some angling. Each boat has a maximum capacity, so check before you book.

Motor Boat Hire Crete Prices and What They Include

Prices for motor boat hire in Crete start at around EUR 400 for a half-day on a small RIB. A full-day on a mid-size motor yacht (10 to 12 metres) is typically EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. Larger yachts with more cabins and a flybridge can cost EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500 per day. Superyacht charters are price on request. The price includes the boat, skipper, fuel, insurance and VAT. It does not include food, drink, marina fees (usually EUR 20 to EUR 50 per day) or tips. Some operators charge extra for water toys like a paddleboard or snorkel gear. Ask when you book. Payment is usually 50% deposit at booking and 50% on the day. Most operators take credit card or bank transfer.

The season affects prices. July and August are peak season, so expect a 20-30% premium. May, June and September are shoulder season, cheaper and less crowded. October is low season, but the weather is still good for motor boating. Book early in peak season to get the boat you want. The BoatHire24 homepage shows current availability for Crete.

Best Itineraries for a Motor Boat Day in Crete

From Heraklion, a popular route is east to the island of Dia. It is a nature reserve with no permanent buildings, just a few beaches and a chapel. The water is clear and calm. From Chania, the trip to Balos lagoon is a classic. The lagoon is shallow and turquoise, but it gets busy in summer. Gramvousa island with its Venetian castle is nearby. From Agios Nikolaos, head south to the coves around Ierapetra or east to the island of Chrissi. Chrissi has a cedar forest and white sand beaches. From Rethymno, the coast west towards Plakias has several sea caves and secluded beaches. Your skipper will know the best spots for swimming and anchoring. You can also visit the island of Spinalonga from Elounda, but it is better known for history than swimming.

What to Expect from the Weather and Sea Conditions

Crete has a Mediterranean climate. Summer temperatures are 28 to 35 degrees C. The sea is warm from June to October, around 22 to 26 degrees C. The meltemi wind can pick up in July and August, especially in the north. It is a north-westerly wind that can make the sea choppy in the afternoon. Most motor boats handle it fine, but you might get a bumpy ride on a RIB. Morning departures are calmer. The south coast is more sheltered, so if you are prone to seasickness, consider a south coast itinerary. Your skipper will check the forecast and adjust the route if needed. In spring and autumn, the weather is more variable. Always bring a light jacket and sunscreen.

Who Should Hire a Motor Boat in Crete

Motor boat hire in Crete works for families, couples and groups of friends. Families with children appreciate the stability of a motor yacht and the ability to stop at beaches the kids can swim from. Couples might prefer a smaller RIB for a more active day. Groups of friends can split the cost of a larger yacht. The skipper handles everything, so you can relax. If you want a party boat, some operators allow music and alcohol, but check their policy. Business groups sometimes charter a motor yacht for a client day or team building. The boat is a private space, so you can work or socialise without interruptions.

How to Book Motor Boat Hire Crete with BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter your dates and group size, and filter by motor boats. You will see available boats with photos, specifications and prices. Each listing shows the departure port, capacity and included items. Click on a boat to see more details and book. You pay a deposit online, and the balance is due on the day. The operator will confirm the booking by email. If you have questions, use the contact form on the site. We recommend booking at least a week in advance in peak season. For last-minute bookings, check the availability on the search page. The operator might have a cancellation that frees up a boat.

If you are not sure which boat suits you, read the blog for tips on choosing a motor boat in Crete. We have articles on the best itineraries, what to pack and how to get the most out of your day.

What to Bring on a Motor Boat Charter in Crete

Pack sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, swimwear, a towel, a light jacket and a camera. Bring food and drink unless you arranged catering. Most boats have a fridge or cooler. Some operators provide snorkel gear, but check. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication an hour before departure. Bring cash for marina fees and tips. Leave valuables at home or in a waterproof bag. The skipper will store your bags in a dry place. Wear non-slip shoes on the boat. Sandals with a strap are fine. Flip-flops are not ideal on a moving deck.

Frequently Asked Questions about Motor Boat Hire Crete

Why Crete Works Better for Motor Boat Hire Than the Cyclades

Crete is bigger and more diverse than islands like Mykonos or Santorini. The coastline is about 1,046 km, so you have more options for a day trip without feeling crowded. The Cyclades are more exposed to the meltemi wind, which can cancel a small motor boat charter. Crete's north coast gets some wind, but the south coast is often flat calm. If you want to guarantee a smooth day on the water, pick a south coast departure like Ierapetra or Plakias. The water visibility is also better in Crete because there is less sand and silt. You can see the seabed at 15 metres depth in many spots. The Cyclades have more sand, so the water can look milky after a windy day. For motor boat hire, Crete is the safer bet for a reliable day out.

Licence-Free Motor Boats in Crete: What You Need to Know

Some operators in Crete offer licence-free motor boats up to 30 hp. These are small RIBs or day boats that you can drive yourself without a licence. They are cheap, from around EUR 200 for a half-day, and you get a quick briefing on how to handle the boat. You are restricted to a small area near the port, usually within 1 to 2 NM. You cannot go to distant beaches or islands. The boats are basic, with no toilet or cabin. They work for a short trip to a nearby cove for swimming. If you want to explore further, book a boat with a skipper. The skipper knows the local hazards, like rocks and shallow patches, and can take you to the best spots. Licence-free boats are a good option if you are on a tight budget or just want a few hours on the water.

Motor Boat Hire Crete for Fishing Enthusiasts

You can combine motor boat hire with fishing in Crete. Some operators have dedicated fishing boats with rod holders, a fish finder and a live bait tank. The skipper knows the local fishing grounds. Common catches in Crete include sea bream, grouper, red mullet and tuna. The best fishing is from March to June and September to November. Summer is okay but the fish are deeper. You can also troll for tuna and mahi-mahi in the deeper water off the south coast. The price for a fishing charter is similar to a standard motor boat hire, around EUR 500 to EUR 1,000 for a full day. The boat will clean and pack your catch. You can take it to a taverna in the evening and they will cook it for you. Check the operator's policy on catch and release if you prefer not to keep the fish.

The Best Time of Day for a Motor Boat Charter in Crete

Most people book a full-day charter from 9 am to 5 pm. That gives you time to reach a good spot, swim, eat lunch and return. If you want to avoid the heat and the crowds, consider an early departure at 7 am. The sea is calm, the light is good for photos, and you have the beaches to yourself until around 10 am. Sunset cruises are popular from June to September. You leave at 4 pm, watch the sun go down over the sea, and return at 8 pm. The temperature drops, so bring a jacket. Sunset cruises are cheaper than full-day charters, usually EUR 300 to EUR 600 for a small group. They work well for couples or small groups who want a relaxed evening on the water. Some operators include a glass of wine or a light meal.

Motor Boat Hire Crete for Large Groups and Events

If you have a group of 10 to 20 people, you need a motor yacht or a catamaran. Catamarans are more stable and have more deck space, but they are slower. Motor yachts are faster and more luxurious. Prices for a group charter start at around EUR 1,500 for a full day on a 14-metre motor yacht. That works out to EUR 150 per person for a group of 10, which is cheaper than a day on a commercial boat trip. The boat is private, so you can play your own music, bring your own food and drink, and choose your own itinerary. Some operators allow events like birthday parties, bachelor or bachelorette parties, and corporate days. They usually require a deposit and a signed agreement about behaviour and damage. The skipper has the final say on safety, so keep it sensible.

How to Save Money on Motor Boat Hire in Crete

Book in the shoulder season, May, June or September. Prices are 20-30% lower than July and August. Book a half-day instead of a full day. You still get a good experience but pay less. Share the cost with a group. A EUR 1,000 charter split among 6 people is EUR 167 each. That is less than a day on a commercial boat trip, which costs around EUR 80 to EUR 120 per person and you share the boat with strangers. Look for last-minute deals. Some operators discount boats that are not booked a day or two in advance. Check the search page on BoatHire24 for availability. Avoid extras like catering and water toys if you are on a budget. Bring your own food and drink. Use the boat's basic snorkel gear or bring your own. Marina fees are usually included in the price, but confirm when you book.

What Happens if the Weather Is Bad on Your Charter Day

Motor boat charters in Crete are weather-dependent. If the forecast is bad, the operator will cancel or reschedule. You get a full refund or a new date. Do not try to force the charter in bad weather. The skipper knows the limits of the boat and the sea. If the weather turns during the day, the skipper will head back to port early. You might lose an hour or two, but safety comes first. Some operators have a "weather guarantee" that lets you cancel up to 24 hours before departure without penalty. Check the terms when you book. In July and August, weather cancellations are rare, maybe 1 in 20 charters. In spring and autumn, it is more common, maybe 1 in 5. If you are visiting in a variable season, book a flexible charter.

Motor Boat Hire Crete for Solo Travellers

Solo travellers can hire a motor boat in Crete, but it is expensive because you pay for the whole boat. A RIB or small day boat costs EUR 300 to EUR 500 for a half-day. That is a lot for one person. A better option is to join a shared charter. Some operators offer group trips where you pay per person, around EUR 80 to EUR 150. You share the boat with other travellers, usually 6 to 12 people. The itinerary is fixed, but you get the experience without the full cost. Shared charters are common from Heraklion and Chania. They are not private, so you cannot choose the route or stop whenever you want. But for a solo traveller on a budget, it is a good way to see the coast from the water. Check the search page for shared charters in Crete.

Local Customs and Etiquette on a Motor Boat in Crete

Greek hospitality applies on the water. The skipper will offer you a drink and maybe a snack. Accept it, it is part of the experience. Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated. A tip of 10-15% of the charter price is normal if the service was good. Hand it to the skipper . Do not bring glass bottles on the boat. They can break and cause injuries. Use plastic or metal containers. Smoking is usually allowed on deck but not in the cabin. Ask the skipper. Do not play loud music near other boats or beaches. Keep it at a reasonable volume. Respect the marine environment. Do not throw rubbish overboard. Do not touch marine life like turtles or fish. The skipper will enforce these rules. Follow them and you will have a good day.
