bodyHtml:
What Boat Hire In Crete Means On BoatHire24

Crete is the largest Greek island, with over 1,000 km of coastline. Hiring a boat here is not about driving yourself unless you have a licence. Every charter on our platform includes a skipper. That means you sit back, drink something cold, and let someone else handle the navigation. You get a private boat, not a shared tour. The skipper takes you to coves, beaches and tavernas that are only reachable by sea. You decide the itinerary, within reason. If you want to spend the whole day anchored off Balos lagoon, that is your call.

Which Ports Can You Depart From

Crete has several marinas and harbours where boats are based. The main ones are Heraklion (the capital), Chania (west coast), Agios Nikolaos (east), Rethymno (north coast) and Elounda (east, near Spinalonga). Each port gives you access to different parts of the coast. From Chania you can reach Balos, Falassarna and the Samaria Gorge from the sea. From Agios Nikolaos you are close to the island of Chrissi and the Vai palm forest. Heraklion is central, good for day trips to Dia island or down to Matala. You can also start from smaller spots like Plakias or Paleochora, but the boat selection is smaller. Check the search page to filter by port and boat type.

Types Of Boats Available For Hire In Crete

Motor yachts are the most common option for boat hire in Crete. They range from 8 m RIBs with a 200 hp outboard up to 20 m flybridge yachts with cabins, a saloon and a sun deck. A 10 m motor yacht costs from around EUR 600 per day in low season. Catamarans are popular for groups, offering more deck space and stability. A 12 m catamaran sleeps 8 and costs from EUR 900 per day. Sailing yachts are available if you want the wind experience, but they are slower. A 12 m sailing yacht costs from EUR 500 per day. RIBs and speedboats are good for shorter trips or watersports. Fishing boats with gear are also listed. If you want something larger, superyachts up to 30 m are available on request. Every boat has safety equipment, insurance and a licensed skipper included.

What Is Included In The Price

The charter price includes the boat, the skipper, fuel for up to 8 hours of cruising, and basic safety gear. Some listings include snorkelling equipment, a cooler with ice, or a small welcome pack. You do not pay extra for the skipper. What is not included: food and drinks (you bring your own or order at a taverna), port fees if you stay overnight, and any extras like jet skis or paddleboards. Some boats have a refundable deposit for damage, usually around EUR 300 to EUR 500, paid on the day and returned after the trip. Tips for the skipper are not mandatory but are common, around 10% to 15% of the charter cost. Always read the listing details before booking.

Pricing Guidance For Boat Hire In Crete

Prices vary by season, boat size and duration. Low season (April to May, October) is cheaper. A half-day (4 hours) on a 8 m RIB costs from around EUR 350. A full day (8 hours) on a 10 m motor yacht costs from EUR 600 to EUR 800. A 14 m catamaran for a full day costs from EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,800. High season (July to August) prices are 30% to 50% higher. For superyachts or week-long charters, you pay per day and accommodation is extra. Prices are in euros. You can compare multiple boats on the search page. Book early for July and August, as boats get reserved months in advance.

Best Time Of Year For Boat Hire In Crete

Crete has a Mediterranean climate with hot summers and mild winters. The best months for boating are May through October. May and June have pleasant temperatures around 25 degrees C, fewer crowds, and the sea is calm. July and August are hotter, up to 35 degrees C, with strong meltemi winds in the north, especially in August. September and October are still warm, with sea temperatures around 24 degrees C, and the crowds thin out. April and November are possible but cooler, around 18 degrees C, and some boats are not available. Winter charters are rare; most boats are out of the water for maintenance. If you want calm seas and lower prices, go in May or September. If you want guaranteed sun and don't mind the wind, July works.

Popular Destinations And Itineraries

From Chania, a typical day trip goes to Balos lagoon and Gramvousa island. The water is turquoise and shallow. Another option is Falassarna beach, with long sandy shores. From Heraklion, you can sail to Dia island, a nature reserve with hiking and clear water. From Agios Nikolaos, head to the island of Chrissi (Golden Island) with white sand and cedar trees. The trip takes about 45 minutes each way. From Elounda, you can visit Spinalonga island, the former leper colony, and swim in the coves around the peninsula. For a longer charter, some skippers will take you to Santorini, but that is a full day crossing each way, so better as a multi-day trip. You can also explore the south coast, which is less developed, with caves and remote beaches like Preveli beach and the palm forest. The skipper knows the best spots and can adjust the plan based on weather.

Who Should Hire A Boat In Crete

Boat hire in Crete works for families, groups of friends, couples and solo travellers who want privacy. If you are a group of 6 to 12 people, a catamaran or motor yacht is ideal. Families with children appreciate the space and the ability to stop whenever the kids want to swim. Couples can charter a smaller RIB or sailing yacht for a romantic day. It is not a good option if you want to drive the boat yourself without a licence. Some boats are available for bareboat charter if you have an ICC or equivalent, but those are not listed on BoatHire24. If you are on a tight budget, shared boat tours are cheaper, but you share the space with strangers. Private hire costs more but gives you control. If you are celebrating a birthday, anniversary or corporate event, a private charter is a strong choice.

How To Book Boat Hire In Crete

Booking is done online through the BoatHire24 website. You select your port, date, boat type and duration. You see available boats with photos, specs and prices. You send an enquiry or book directly if the listing allows instant booking. The platform does not charge booking fees. You pay a deposit (usually 30% to 50%) to confirm, and the balance is paid to the skipper on the day. Cancellation policies vary by boat; most offer full refund if cancelled 14 days before. We recommend you read the terms before paying. After booking, you receive contact details for the skipper. You agree on the meeting time and location at the marina. On the day, you meet the skipper, sign a liability waiver, and board. The skipper does a safety briefing. Then you go. For more tips, check the blog for articles on what to bring and how to prepare.

Frequently Asked Questions About Boat Hire In Crete

If you still have questions, the FAQ section below covers common queries. For anything specific, contact us via the website or email. BoatHire24 is a marketplace, not a charter company, so we connect you with local operators. We do not own the boats. We do not set prices. We do not take responsibility for cancellations by the skipper, but we help resolve issues. Always check the skipper's reviews and the boat's condition on the day. Crete is a large island with many options. Use the search filters to narrow down what you need. If you are unsure about the best port or boat type, read the blog or ask us. We have been doing this for a few years and we know which skippers are reliable.

Why Crete Is Different From Other Greek Islands For Boat Hire

Crete is not Mykonos or Santorini. It is bigger, rougher, and less polished. The coastline changes from long sandy beaches in the west to steep cliffs and hidden coves in the east. You get more variety in a single day. From Heraklion, you can be at Dia island in 30 minutes, a rocky nature reserve with no facilities, just clear water and silence. From Chania, you can reach Balos in 90 minutes, a lagoon that looks like the Caribbean but with fewer tourists if you go early. The south coast is wilder, with beaches like Preveli and Agia Roumeli that are only accessible by boat or on foot. The skipper knows the local conditions, which matter here because the wind can change fast. If you hire a boat in Crete, you are not just doing a beach hop. You are exploring an island that has its own weather systems and a history that shows up in the ruins and caves along the shore.

What To Expect From The Skipper On Your Charter

The skipper is a local, usually Greek, with years of experience in Cretan waters. They speak English well enough to explain the itinerary and point out landmarks. They do not join you for meals unless you invite them. They stay on the boat, keeping an eye on the anchor and the weather. Some skippers will grill fresh fish on board if you ask and bring the catch. Others will recommend tavernas on the coast that only serve locals. The skipper is not a tour guide. They do not narrate history unless you ask. They are there to navigate, anchor safely, and make sure you do not get seasick. If you want a more interactive experience, mention it when you book. Some skippers are happy to teach basic sailing or show you how to use the snorkelling gear. The key is communication. Tell them what you want before you leave the marina.

How To Choose Between A Motor Yacht And A Catamaran In Crete

The choice depends on your group size, budget, and tolerance for motion. Motor yachts are faster. A 10 m motor yacht cruises at 20 to 25 knots, which means you can cover more coastline in a day. From Agios Nikolaos, you can reach Chrissi island in 45 minutes, spend three hours there, and still have time for a swim stop on the way back. Motor yachts have a smaller deck space relative to length, but they have a saloon with air conditioning, which matters in July when the sun is brutal. Catamarans are slower, around 10 to 15 knots, but they offer more deck area. A 12 m catamaran has a front trampoline where you can lie down and a shaded cockpit. They are more stable, so if anyone in your group gets seasick, a catamaran is the better choice. For a group of 8 to 12, a catamaran works well because everyone has space. For a couple or a family of four, a motor yacht is more practical and cheaper.

What To Bring And What To Leave Behind On A Boat Hire In Crete

Bring sunscreen with high SPF, a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a change of clothes. The sun in Crete is strong even in May. Bring a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon, especially in July and August when the meltemi wind picks up. Leave behind high heels, heavy luggage, and anything that cannot get wet. The boat has limited storage. Do not bring glass bottles. Most skippers provide a cooler with ice, but you fill it with your own drinks and food. Bring water, at least 1.5 litres per person for a full day. Some boats have a small fridge, but it is not always cold enough. If you plan to eat at a taverna on the coast, bring cash. Many remote beach tavernas do not accept cards. Do not bring drones unless you have permission from the skipper and know the local regulations. Some areas near airports or military sites are restricted.

How The Meltemi Wind Affects Boat Hire In Crete

The meltemi is a strong, dry north wind that blows in the Aegean from June to September. It is most intense in August. In Crete, the meltemi affects the north coast more than the south. From Chania to Agios Nikolaos, the wind can reach 30 to 40 knots in the afternoon, making the sea choppy. Skippers monitor weather forecasts and may suggest a different route or a later start. In July 2023, we had a week where all north coast charters left at 8 AM and returned by 2 PM to avoid the worst of it. The south coast is sheltered, so if you want calm seas in August, choose a port like Plakias or Paleochora. The meltemi is not dangerous if you have an experienced skipper. They know how to handle it. But it can make the ride uncomfortable for passengers. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication before you board. The meltemi also means the sea is clearer, which is good for snorkelling.

How To Combine A Boat Charter With A Visit To The South Coast

The south coast of Crete is less developed and harder to reach by road. A boat charter is the best way to see it. From Heraklion, you can sail south to Matala, a village with caves that hippies lived in during the 1960s. The bay is sheltered and good for swimming. From Agios Nikolaos, you can go south to the island of Chrissi, which has a cedar forest and white sand. The water is shallow and turquoise. From Chania, the south coast is further, around 2 hours each way, but you can reach Preveli beach with its palm forest and freshwater lagoon. Some skippers offer multi-day charters that include an overnight stop in Loutro, a small village with no roads, only a few tavernas and rooms. The south coast has fewer marinas, so you anchor and come ashore by dinghy. It is worth the effort. The water is cleaner and the crowds are thinner. Book a full day or a two-day charter to make the most of it.

What To Do If You Have Never Been On A Boat Before

If you are new to boating, do not worry. The skipper handles everything. You just show up at the marina, step on board, and sit down. The skipper gives a safety briefing, shows you where the life jackets are, and explains how to use the toilet. On a motor yacht, the ride is smooth unless the sea is rough. On a catamaran, you barely feel the motion. If you get seasick, sit on the deck and look at the horizon. Do not stay inside the cabin. Drink water, eat something light, and avoid alcohol until you are anchored. Most people are fine after 20 minutes. The first stop is usually a calm bay where you can swim and adjust. By the second stop, you will wonder why you waited so long to try it. Boat hire in Crete is accessible to anyone who can step onto a boat. No fitness level required. Just bring a positive attitude and a willingness to follow the skipper's instructions.

How To Save Money On Boat Hire In Crete

Book in May or September. Prices are lower and the weather is still good. Avoid August if you can. That is when demand peaks and prices jump. Choose a half-day instead of a full day. A half-day is 4 hours, enough to visit one or two spots and have lunch. From Heraklion, a half-day to Dia island and back costs from around EUR 400 on a 8 m RIB. A full day costs from EUR 600. If you are a group of 6 or more, a catamaran works out cheaper per person than a smaller boat. Share the cost among friends. Do not book extras like jet skis or paddleboards unless you really want them. They add EUR 100 to EUR 200 per day. Bring your own food and drinks. Buying them at the marina is expensive. Some skippers offer discounts for repeat customers or for booking multiple days. Ask when you enquire. The worst they can say is no.

bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Boat Hire Crete Greece

Every boat hire on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, fuel for a standard day trip, and basic insurance. You get the boat for a full day, usually 8-10 hours, from around 9am to 6pm. Some operators offer half-day options, from 4-5 hours, at a lower rate. The skipper knows the local waters, the best swimming spots, and the tavernas that only serve locals. They also handle mooring, anchoring, and any unexpected weather changes, so you don't have to worry about a thing.

Most boats come with a cooler, snorkelling gear, and a Bluetooth speaker. Some larger yachts include a paddleboard, a small inflatable tender, or even a water slide. You are welcome to bring your own food and drinks, or you can arrange a catering package through the operator. The skipper will have a list of recommended tavernas if you want to stop for lunch onshore. Just remember that the skipper's tips are not included, and it's customary to tip around 10-15% of the charter fee if you are happy with the service.

All charters are private, meaning you and your group are the only passengers. No shared tours, no strangers. You decide the itinerary, the pace, and the music. The skipper will advise on what's feasible given the wind and sea conditions, but the final call is yours.

Boat Types Available for Crete

The fleet in Crete is diverse. Motor yachts from 30 to 60 feet are the most popular, with flybridge or sun deck layouts. A 40-foot motor yacht typically sleeps 4-6 in cabins but is used for day charters with up to 12 guests. Prices start from around EUR 800 per day for a 30-footer and go up to EUR 3,000 for a 55-foot luxury yacht. Catamarans are also big in Crete, especially for groups who want stability and space. A 40-foot catamaran has a wide beam, a large trampoline net at the bow, and a shaded cockpit. Day rates start from EUR 1,200 for a Lagoon 38 and rise to EUR 2,500 for a 50-foot Bali or Leopard. Sailing yachts are available too, but they are slower and less common for day hire. A 38-foot monohull sailboat costs around EUR 600 per day, but you will be sailing, not motoring, so the itinerary is wind-dependent. RIBs and speedboats are the cheapest option, from EUR 400 per day for a 6-metre RIB with a 150hp outboard. They are fast, fun, and can access shallow coves that larger yachts cannot. Fishing boats are also listed, with basic equipment included, from EUR 500 per day. Superyachts over 80 feet are available on request, with prices starting at EUR 8,000 per day.

Popular Departure Ports in Crete

Most boat hires depart from Heraklion, Chania, Agios Nikolaos, or Rethymno. Heraklion is the largest port, with the most options for motor yachts and catamarans. From here you can reach Dia Island, a marine reserve with crystal clear water and no development. Chania port is smaller but more picturesque, with the Venetian lighthouse and the old town. Boats from Chania often head to the Gramvousa peninsula and Balos lagoon, famous for its turquoise water and white sand. Agios Nikolaos is on the east coast, close to the Spinalonga island fortress and the Elounda bay. Rethymno is on the north coast, with easy access to the caves of Matala and the southern beaches. Some operators also offer pickups from smaller harbours like Kissamos, Ierapetra, or Sitia. You can check the exact departure port on the boat listing page before booking.

How to Book a Boat Hire Crete Greece on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter your preferred port and date, and filter by boat type, group size, and budget. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and the total price. Click on a boat to see the full description, the itinerary suggestions, and the cancellation policy. To confirm, you pay a deposit online, usually 30-50% of the total. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or by card. We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance during peak season, July and August, because the best boats go fast. For last-minute bookings, you can contact us directly and we will check availability with our partner operators. All bookings come with a 48-hour free cancellation policy, so you can change your mind without penalty.

Best Time for Boat Hire in Crete

The season runs from April to October. June, July, August and September are the best months, with air temperatures around 28-32 degrees C and water temperatures above 24 degrees C. The Meltemi wind, a strong northerly, can blow in July and August, especially on the north coast. It makes the sea choppy but also keeps the heat bearable. If you are prone to seasickness, choose a catamaran or a large motor yacht for stability. May and October are quieter and cheaper, with fewer tourists and lower prices. The water is cooler, around 18-22 degrees C, but still pleasant for swimming. The south coast of Crete is more protected from the Meltemi, so it's a good choice for sailing yachts in summer. Winter charters are not common because many operators close from November to March. If you want a boat in the off-season, contact us and we will check availability.

Who Is Boat Hire Crete Greece For

Boat hire in Crete suits everyone from couples to large groups. Families with children love the catamarans because of the space and the safety net. Groups of friends prefer motor yachts for the party vibe and the sun deck. Solo travellers can join a shared tour if they want, but most boats are private. Corporate events and team-building trips are also possible, with catering and AV equipment available on larger yachts. If you are a non-swimmer, don't worry, the skipper will provide life jackets and the boat has a ladder for easy access. The only requirement is that you can climb the boarding ladder from the water, which is usually a few steps. If you have mobility issues, let us know and we will find a boat with a swim platform at water level.

You don't need any sailing experience, a licence, or even the ability to swim. The skipper handles everything. You just need to bring sunscreen, a towel, and a sense of adventure. Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper will not serve it if you are going to swim. You can bring your own beer and wine, but no glass bottles on the boat, use plastic cups.

What to Expect on the Day

On the morning of your charter, you meet the skipper at the designated port. They will give a safety briefing, show you the toilet and the cabin, and ask about your preferred itinerary. Most skippers have a default route but are happy to customise. A typical day starts with a 30-minute cruise to the first swimming spot, then a couple of hours of swimming, snorkelling, and sunbathing. Around 1pm, you stop for lunch, either on the boat or at a beach taverna. The skipper will recommend a place and can call ahead to reserve a table. After lunch, you cruise to a second spot, maybe a sea cave or a hidden beach, then head back to port around 5pm. The skipper will clean the boat, so you don't have to do anything. You can tip them directly .

Why Book Through BoatHire24

We are a marketplace, not a boat operator. That means you can compare multiple boats and prices in one place, without having to contact each company separately. We verify all operators and skippers, so you know they are licensed and insured. Our BoatHire24 platform handles the booking and payment securely. If anything goes wrong, we act as the middleman to resolve disputes. We also have a blog with guides on the best beaches, anchorages, and tavernas in Crete, written by locals. Check it out before you book to get ideas for your itinerary.

Price Guidance for Boat Hire Crete Greece

Prices vary by boat type, size, season, and duration. For a half-day (4-5 hours) on a 6-metre RIB, expect to pay from around EUR 400. A full day on a 40-foot motor yacht costs from EUR 800 to EUR 1,200 in low season, and from EUR 1,400 to EUR 2,000 in August. Catamarans are more expensive, from EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,500 per day. Superyachts are price on request, but you can expect EUR 8,000 and up. Fuel is included in the price, but if you want to go on a long trip, like from Chania to Balos, the operator may charge a fuel supplement. Always confirm what is included before you book. The price you see on the listing is the total for the boat, not per person. You can split it among your group. For a group of 10, a EUR 1,500 motor yacht costs EUR 150 per person, which is cheaper than a day trip on a tourist boat.

Local Tips for Your Crete Boat Trip

Crete has some of the best snorkelling in the Mediterranean. The waters around Dia Island and the south coast are clear and full of fish. Bring an underwater camera. The sea caves near Matala are worth a visit, but the skipper will know which ones are safe to enter. If you want to see turtles, head to the bay of Elounda. For a quiet anchor, try the beach of Plakias on the south coast. The water is calm and the taverna on the beach serves fresh fish. Avoid the north coast ports in the afternoon if the Meltemi is blowing, it can get rough. The skipper will adjust the itinerary accordingly. If you are prone to seasickness, take a tablet an hour before departure. You can buy them at any pharmacy in Greece.

Crete is a big island, and you cannot see it all in one day. Focus on one region. If you are staying in Chania, explore the west. If you are in Heraklion, go east to Agios Nikolaos. The boat trip is about relaxing, not racing. Let the skipper set the pace. You can always book another day if you want to see more.

Exploring Crete’s South Coast by Boat

The south coast of Crete is a different world from the busier north. The Libyan Sea is warmer and usually calmer, especially in July and August when the Meltemi wind hits the north. Departing from Ierapetra or Matala, you can reach beaches that are inaccessible by road. Try the beach of Preveli, where a palm forest meets the sea, or the cove of Agiofarago with its sandstone cliffs. The village of Loutro is only reachable by boat or on foot, so it feels like a secret. A full-day charter from Ierapetra to Chrissi Island, a protected nature reserve with white sand and cedar trees, costs around EUR 900 for a 30-foot motor yacht. The water is so clear you can see the sea grass 15 metres down. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, because some areas are protected and regular sunscreen damages the marine life.

Half-Day vs Full-Day Charters: Which One Works

A half-day charter, usually 4-5 hours, is enough for a quick swim and a taverna lunch. It costs from around EUR 400 for a RIB and EUR 600 for a small motor yacht. You depart at 9am or 2pm, so you either get the morning calm or the afternoon heat. A full day, 8-10 hours, lets you cover more ground, visit two or three swimming spots, and stop for a longer lunch onshore. The price difference is roughly 40-60% more for a full day. If you are a family with young children, a half-day might be better because kids get tired and bored after six hours. If you are a group of adults who want to party and swim, go for the full day. The skipper will have a cooler with ice, so your drinks stay cold all day.

What to Pack for a Boat Day in Crete

You need a swimsuit, a towel, sunscreen (factor 50, water-resistant), and a hat. The sun is strong from 11am to 4pm, and the reflection off the water burns you faster. A light long-sleeve shirt or a rash guard helps. Bring a dry bag for your phone and wallet, because splashes happen. Most boats have a small toilet and a cabin where you can change. If you plan to eat onshore, bring cash because some tavernas on remote beaches do not accept cards. The boat has a Bluetooth speaker, but bring your own playlist. Do not bring glass bottles; the skipper will provide plastic cups. A pair of water shoes is useful if you want to walk on pebble beaches. And a windbreaker for the afternoon, because the wind picks up and the boat ride back can be cool.

Boat Hire for Special Occasions in Crete

Birthday parties, anniversaries, and proposals are common on Crete boat charters. Many operators offer decoration packages, including banners, balloons, and a bottle of sparkling wine. For a proposal, the skipper can arrange a secluded cove, a sunset timing, and a photographer on a separate boat if you want. The cost for extras is around EUR 50-150, depending on what you ask. Some larger catamarans have a DJ setup and a sound system for parties. If you want a catered meal on board, the operator can arrange a Greek meze platter with grilled octopus, tzatziki, and fresh bread for around EUR 25 per person. Just tell us when you book, and we will pass the request to the skipper. No glass, no confetti that goes into the sea, because that harms marine life and the skipper will refuse.

Most charters also include snorkelling gear, towels and a cooler box for your drinks. You can add catering, from a simple picnic to a full barbecue, depending on the package you choose.

Departure Ports for Boat Hire Crete

Crete has several main ports where you can start your charter. In the north-west, Chania (Souda Bay and the old Venetian harbour) is the most popular departure point, with easy access to the Rodopou peninsula and the island of Gramvousa. Further east, Rethymno offers a shorter run to the caves and beaches of the northern coast. Heraklion, the capital, has a busy marina and gives you quick access to the Dia island nature reserve. On the south coast, Agios Nikolaos and Elounda are the main ports, with calm waters and the famous Spinalonga island just offshore. For a quieter start, try Sitia in the far east, where the coastline is less developed and the water is crystal clear.

Boat Types Available for Crete Charters

You can choose from several boat types when you search for boat hire Crete. Motor yachts are the most common, fast, comfortable and ideal for covering longer distances. A 40-50 ft motor yacht will take you from Chania to Balos lagoon in about an hour. Catamarans offer more deck space and stability, perfect for groups who want to spread out and sunbathe. Sailing yachts are quieter and more traditional, though the skipper will handle the sails, you just enjoy the ride. RIBs and speedboats are smaller and faster, great for a day of island hopping or watersports. Fishing boats are available for half-day trips if you want to try your luck with rod and line. Prices for a full-day charter on a motor yacht start from around EUR 800 for a 30 ft boat in low season, rising to EUR 2,500 or more for a 50 ft catamaran in August.

Best Time of Year for Boat Hire Crete

The charter season in Crete runs from April to October, with the peak months being July and August. In April and May the sea temperature is around 18-20 degrees C, and the weather is warm but not hot, good for sailing and sightseeing but less ideal for swimming. June and September are the sweet spots: water temperatures of 22-25 degrees C, fewer crowds and lower prices than July and August. October can still be pleasant, especially in the south, but the Meltemi wind can pick up in the afternoon. If you are booking in July or August, reserve at least 2-3 weeks ahead, especially for catamarans and larger motor yachts. In shoulder months you can often book a week in advance and still find availability.

What to See on a Crete Boat Charter

The coastline of Crete is full of highlights that are best seen from the water. From Chania, a classic route is to Balos lagoon and the Gramvousa island fortress, turquoise water and white sand, but crowded in high season. A better option is the Rodopou peninsula, where you can anchor in secluded coves like Kolokytha or the beach at Stravos. From Heraklion, a trip to Dia island gives you snorkelling in clear water and views back to the city. From Agios Nikolaos or Elounda, the must-see is Spinalonga, the former leper colony with a fascinating history, accessible only by boat. On the south coast, the beaches of Plakias and Preveli beach (with its palm trees) are worth the longer trip. If you have a full day, you can go as far as the Samaria Gorge mouth at Agia Roumeli, though that is a long run from any northern port.

How to Book Boat Hire Crete on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter your preferred date, group size and departure port (or choose 'any port' to see all options). The results show available boats with photos, specs, price and what is included. Click on a listing to see full details, then select your package, half-day, full-day or sunset cruise. You pay a deposit online (usually 30-50%) and the balance to the skipper on the day. Cancellation policies vary by operator, but most offer free cancellation up to 72 hours before departure. After booking, you get a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and meeting point instructions. If you have questions before you book, use the contact form on each listing and the operator will usually reply within a few hours.

Who Is Boat Hire Crete For?

Boat hire Crete is for anyone who wants a day on the water without the responsibility of driving the boat. Families with children appreciate the safety of a professional skipper. Groups of friends use charters for birthday parties, bachelor/bachelorette trips or just a day of swimming and sun. Couples book sunset cruises for a romantic evening with dinner and wine. Business groups use charters for team-building or client entertainment. The only people who should not book are those who want to drive the boat themselves, for that you need a licence-free day boat, which we also list in some locations, but the majority of our Crete inventory is skippered.

Prices and What Affects the Cost

Prices for boat hire Crete vary by boat size, type, season and duration. A half-day (4-hour) charter on a 30 ft motor yacht in May costs from around EUR 500. A full-day (8-hour) on a 45 ft catamaran in August can be EUR 2,000-3,000. The biggest cost factor is season, July and August are roughly double the low-season rates. Fuel is usually included, but check, some operators charge extra for longer trips. Catering adds EUR 30-60 per person for a barbecue or buffet. Port fees and cleaning are normally included. For the most accurate pricing, use our search filters and look at specific listings. For superyachts and larger vessels (50 ft+), prices are on request and you should contact the operator directly.

Why Use BoatHire24 for Your Crete Charter

We are a marketplace, not a charter company. That means you see boats from multiple operators in one place, and you can compare prices, reviews and inclusions side by side. Every boat on our site is verified by us, and we only list operators who include a licensed skipper in the price. You get the same price as booking direct, no mark-up. And because we handle the deposit payment online, you do not have to exchange bank details with a stranger. If something goes wrong on the day, our support team can mediate between you and the operator. For more tips on planning your trip, check out our blog on the best Crete charter routes and what to pack.

Ready to find your boat? Start your search on BoatHire24 and pick the best option for your group. Whether you want a fast RIB to explore the coves of the south coast or a luxury catamaran for a sunset cruise from Chania, we have the boat for you.

Detailed Port Guide: Chania and Souda Bay

Chania's old Venetian harbour is picturesque but has limited space for larger yachts, so most charters depart from Souda Bay, 7 km east. Souda Bay is a deep natural harbour with modern marina facilities, fuel docks and parking. From here, you can reach Balos lagoon in 45-60 minutes on a fast motor yacht, or the Rodopou peninsula in 30 minutes. The advantage of Souda is that you avoid the narrow harbour entrance at Chania, which can be tricky in afternoon winds. If you are chartering a catamaran or sailing yacht, Souda Bay is the better starting point. For smaller RIBs and speedboats, the old harbour is fine, just check with the operator about meeting point details before you book.

Detailed Port Guide: Agios Nikolaos and Elounda

Agios Nikolaos sits on the Mirabello Bay, one of the largest natural bays in the Mediterranean. The water is calm, protected by the Sfakidia peninsula, making it ideal for less experienced skippers or families. Elounda, 10 km north, is even more sheltered and has a smaller marina used mainly by luxury resorts. From either port, you can reach Spinalonga island in 20 minutes, Kolokytha beach in 30 minutes, and the uninhabited island of Psira in 45 minutes. Water temperatures in Mirabello Bay are often 1-2 degrees C warmer than the north coast, good for early-season swimming. Both ports have good tavernas for lunch stops, but most charters include a meal on board or at a beachside restaurant you choose.

Detailed Port Guide: Heraklion and the Dia Island Reserve

Heraklion marina is the busiest in Crete, with good facilities but less charm than Chania or Agios Nikolaos. The main attraction is Dia island, a protected nature reserve 13 km north. Dia has no permanent residents, just wild goats, seabirds and a small seasonal taverna. You can anchor in the bays of Agios Georgios or Kapari, both with clear water and sandy seabeds. The snorkelling here is excellent, with rocky reefs and occasional sea turtles. From Heraklion, you can also head east to the beaches of Hersonissos or west to the Minoan palace of Malia, viewable from the water. For a full-day charter, combine Dia with a lunch stop at one of the coastal villages like Gournes or Kokkini Hani.

Detailed Port Guide: Sitia and the Far East

Sitia is the least crowded departure port on the north coast, with a small marina and a relaxed atmosphere. The coastline east of Sitia is rugged and sparsely populated, with hidden beaches like Vai (the famous palm beach) and Erimoupoli. From Sitia, you can reach the island of Koufonisi in 60-90 minutes, a protected archaeological site with Roman ruins and pristine beaches. The water here is exceptionally clear, with visibility often exceeding 20 metres. The Meltemi wind is less strong in the east, so afternoon conditions are usually calmer than around Chania. Prices from Sitia are generally 10-15% lower than from Chania or Heraklion, because demand is lower. If you want a quieter, more exclusive charter experience, Sitia is worth the drive from the airport.

What to Eat and Drink on Your Charter

Most charters offer optional catering packages, but you can also bring your own food and drink. Typical Greek catering includes a lunch of grilled meat or fish, Greek salad, tzatziki, bread and fruit, costing EUR 30-50 per person. Drinks are often extra, a bottle of local wine is EUR 15-20, soft drinks EUR 3-4 each. If you are on a budget, stop at a supermarket before departure and buy your own supplies. Many operators provide a cooler box and ice. For a special occasion, order a barbecue on the beach, the skipper will grill fresh fish or souvlaki while you swim. Avoid heavy meals if you are prone to seasickness, stick to light food like fruit and crackers.

Weather and Wind Conditions Month by Month

April: air temperature 18-22 C, sea 17-18 C, light winds from the north-west, occasional rain. May: air 22-26 C, sea 19-20 C, moderate Meltemi winds in afternoons, mostly sunny. June: air 26-30 C, sea 22-23 C, steady north-westerly winds 10-15 knots, excellent sailing conditions. July: air 28-33 C, sea 24-25 C, strong Meltemi 15-20 knots, choppy on north coast in afternoons. August: same as July but slightly warmer sea, winds can gust to 25 knots. September: air 26-30 C, sea 24-25 C, winds easing to 10-15 knots, best month for calm conditions. October: air 22-26 C, sea 21-22 C, variable winds, more chance of calm days than July. For motor yachts and catamarans, wind matters less, but for sailing yachts and RIBs, check the forecast before you go.

How to Get to Your Departure Port

Crete has two international airports, Heraklion (HER) and Chania (CHQ). Heraklion is the larger airport with more flights from the UK, Germany and Scandinavia. From Heraklion, it is a 15-minute taxi to the marina (EUR 15-20). Chania airport is 20 minutes from Souda Bay (EUR 20-25 by taxi) or 30 minutes from the old harbour (EUR 25-30). If you are departing from Agios Nikolaos or Elounda, fly to Heraklion and drive east for 60-90 minutes. Car rental is EUR 30-50 per day, and parking at the marinas costs EUR 5-10 per day. For Sitia, the drive from Heraklion is 2.5 hours, so consider flying to Chania and driving across the island, which takes 3.5 hours. For a stress-free start, book a charter that includes hotel pickup, some operators offer this for an extra fee.

What to Bring on a Crete Boat Charter

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat and sunglasses. The sun in Crete is intense, even in April and October you can burn in 30 minutes. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful for the afternoon breeze, especially on a RIB or sailing yacht. Non-slip shoes are recommended for walking on deck and on rocky beaches. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication 30 minutes before departure, the Meltemi can make the north coast choppy. A waterproof phone case or dry bag is handy for keeping valuables dry. Most operators provide snorkelling gear, but if you have your own mask and fins, bring them for a better fit. Cash is useful for tips, the skipper expects around 10-15% of the charter price for good service.

Licence-Free Day Boats in Crete

If you want to drive the boat yourself, some operators in Crete offer licence-free day boats. These are small motorboats up to 30 hp, typically 4-6 metres long, that do not require a boating licence. You get a 15-minute briefing on safety and navigation, then you are free to explore. Licence-free boats are available from Chania, Agios Nikolaos and Elounda, but not from Heraklion or Sitia. Prices start from around EUR 150 for a half-day and EUR 250 for a full day. The downside is that you are limited to calm, sheltered waters, you cannot go to Balos or Dia island in these boats because of the distance and wind. They are best for a relaxed day swimming in nearby coves. On BoatHire24, you can filter by "licence-free" to see these options.

Evening and Sunset Cruises

Sunset cruises are popular in Crete, especially from Chania and Agios Nikolaos. They typically run from 5 PM to 8 PM in summer, or 4 PM to 7 PM in shoulder months. You get a slow cruise along the coast, a glass of wine or beer, and often a light meal or meze. Prices are EUR 50-100 per person on a shared cruise, or EUR 400-800 for a private charter for up to 10 guests. The best sunset views are from the west coast, where the sun sets over the sea. From Chania, you can anchor off the Rodopou peninsula and watch the sun dip below the horizon. From Agios Nikolaos, the sunset over the Mirabello Bay is equally impressive, with the mountains of Sfakia in the background. Evening cruises are a good option if you have a short stay and want to experience the sea without committing to a full day.

Combining Boat Hire with Other Activities

You can combine a boat charter with a visit to the Samaria Gorge by departing from Agia Roumeli on the south coast, but this requires a long drive from the north. A more practical combo is a boat trip to Spinalonga followed by lunch in Elounda or Plaka. Some operators offer a "boat and hike" package where you anchor near the gorge mouth and walk a short section. Another option is a fishing charter that includes a barbecue of your catch. For wine lovers, some charters stop at a coastal vineyard for a tasting. If you are staying in a resort, ask the concierge about local operators who offer packages that include transfer, lunch and entry fees. On BoatHire24, you can message the operator directly to customise your itinerary.

Booking Tips for Last-Minute or Peak Season

If you are booking in July or August, start looking at least 3-4 weeks ahead. Popular boats like catamarans and large motor yachts sell out quickly. For last-minute bookings (within 7 days), check our search page and use the "available now" filter. Some operators offer discounts of 10-20% for last-minute cancellations. In shoulder months (May, June, September), you can often book a few days ahead and still find good options. For groups of 12 or more, book well in advance because only larger catamarans and motor yachts can accommodate you. If your preferred port is fully booked, try a different port, Chania and Heraklion often have more availability than Agios Nikolaos. Use our search page to compare options across all ports at once.

h1: Private Yacht Hire on the Costa del Sol
intro:
Private yacht hire means you get the whole boat to yourself, no strangers, no queuing for a sunbed, just your group and a professional skipper who knows the best coves along the Costa del Sol. Whether you want to cruise past the mansions of Puerto Banús, anchor for lunch off Cabopino, or chase dolphins near the Strait of Gibraltar, a private charter gives you the freedom to set your own pace. At BoatHire24, every booking includes a licensed skipper, so you don't need a licence or experience. You just turn up, relax, and let someone else handle the navigation.

The typical private yacht hire runs from 4 hours to a full day, though longer trips to the Balearics or North Africa are possible if you want a proper escape. Boats range from 40-foot motor yachts that sleep six to 80-foot superyachts with flybridges and jacuzzis. Prices start from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day on a mid-range motor yacht and go up to EUR 15,000 or more for a full-day on a superyacht. You pay for the boat, the skipper, and fuel. Food and drinks are usually extra, unless you choose a catered package.

This page covers everything you need to know about private yacht hire on the Costa del Sol: what you get, which ports to depart from, the different types of boats available, how much it costs, the best time of year, and how to book without getting ripped off. If you have a specific date or group size in mind, the search page lets you filter by boat type, price range, and departure port.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Private Yacht Hire

When you book a private yacht through BoatHire24, the base price covers the vessel, a licensed skipper, and standard insurance. The skipper handles all navigation, docking, and safety briefings, so you are free to swim, eat, drink, or just lie on the deck. Most boats come with a Bluetooth speaker, a cooler, and basic snorkelling gear. Some larger yachts include stand-up paddleboards, a small inflatable dinghy, or even a barbecue on the back deck.

Fuel is typically included for a defined cruising area, say up to 5 nautical miles from the departure port. If you want to go further, for example from Marbella to Gibraltar or across to Ceuta, the skipper will quote an extra fuel surcharge. Food and drinks are not included unless you book a catered charter. You can either bring your own supplies, order a catering package from the boat operator (from around EUR 35 per person for a cold buffet), or arrange a stop at a chiringuito on the beach for lunch.

Gratuities for the skipper are not mandatory but are common, around 10-15% of the charter fee if you are happy with the service. Some operators include a hostess or steward for an extra EUR 150-250 per day, which can be worth it if you want someone to serve drinks and prepare food while you relax.

Departure Ports for Private Yacht Hire

Your choice of departure port affects the scenery, the cruising options, and the price. The main ports along the Costa del Sol are listed below, with notes on what each offers.

Puerto Banús is the most famous and most expensive. You step off the boat straight into the heart of the luxury shopping and nightlife district. Cruising from here gives you views of the Golden Mile mansions, the Sierra Blanca mountains, and the island of Gibraltar on a clear day. The port is busy, so expect a little noise from other boats and the beach clubs. Private yacht hire from Puerto Banús starts around EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a 40-foot motor yacht.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is a quieter alternative, just a 10-minute walk from the old town. You get the same coastal views as Puerto Banús but with lower prices and less chaos. Half-day charters from here start from around EUR 1,200. The marina has plenty of parking and a few decent restaurants if you want a pre-charter breakfast.

Cabopino is a small, sandy-bottomed marina near the Artola dunes. It is ideal if you want a relaxed vibe and quick access to the Cala del Faro cove and the Cabopino nudist beach. Prices are slightly lower, with half-day motor yacht charters from around EUR 1,000. The port itself is less glamorous, but the water quality is excellent.

Estepona offers a more authentic Andalusian experience. The old town is a 5-minute walk from the marina, and the cruising area includes the Selwo Marina dolphin park and the Punta de la Doncella lighthouse. Half-day charters from Estepona start from around EUR 1,100. The marina is less crowded, so you can often get a last-minute booking.

Sotogrande is the most exclusive residential port on the Costa del Sol, with a Polo Club and a golf course nearby. The cruising area includes the Guadiaro River estuary and the Playa de Torreguadiro. Charters from here tend to be longer, usually full-day at a minimum, starting from around EUR 2,000 for a 50-foot motor yacht.

Benalmádena is a large marina with a lively promenade and the Sea Life aquarium. It is a good option if you are staying in Torremolinos or Fuengirola. Half-day charters start from around EUR 1,000. The port is close to the Fuengirola castle and the Mijas mountains, so you can combine a boat trip with a visit to the hilltop villages.

Types of Boats Available for Private Hire

The boat you choose affects the experience, the cost, and the number of guests you can bring. Here is a breakdown of the main types available for private charter.

Motor yachts are the most popular choice for private yacht hire. They are fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space for sunbathing. Typical sizes range from 35 to 80 feet. A 40-foot motor yacht sleeps 6-8 guests comfortably for a day trip and has a small cabin with a toilet and shower. Top speed is around 25 knots, so you can cover 20-30 nautical miles in a half-day. Prices start from EUR 1,200 for a half-day and go up to EUR 5,000 for a full-day on a 60-footer.

Catamarans are wider than monohulls and have a very stable ride, making them ideal if anyone in your group gets seasick. They have a large flybridge, a trampoline net at the bow, and often a small kitchen. A 40-foot catamaran can take 12-14 guests for a day trip. Half-day charters start from around EUR 1,500, full-day from EUR 2,500. The trade-off is slower speed, around 15 knots, and slightly higher fuel consumption.

Sailing yachts are for purists who want the silence of wind power. They are slower (8-12 knots) and require the skipper to handle sails, so you cannot just sit back and motor around. A 40-foot sailing yacht sleeps 6-8 guests and costs from EUR 900 for a half-day, EUR 1,600 for a full-day. You get a more authentic maritime experience, and the lack of engine noise makes swimming stops feel more serene.

RIBs and speedboats are the cheapest option for small groups. These are rigid inflatable boats with powerful outboard engines, capable of 40-50 knots. They are great for a short blast to a cove or a dolphin-spotting trip, but they have limited shade and no toilet. A 30-foot RIB takes up to 8 guests and costs from EUR 500 for a 2-hour trip, EUR 800 for a half-day.

Fishing boats are equipped with rod holders, a fish finder, and a live bait well. The skipper knows the best fishing spots for sea bass, bream, and tuna. Half-day fishing charters start from EUR 700 for up to 6 guests. You keep whatever you catch, and some operators will clean and fillet it for you.

Licence-free day boats are small motorboats (up to 6 metres) that you can drive without a licence, but they are not typically part of private yacht hire. If you want to be your own skipper, check the search page for these options. For private yacht hire, you always get a skipper.

Superyachts are for those who want the full luxury experience. These are 80-150 feet long, with multiple decks, a jacuzzi, a crew of 4-6, and a full galley. Prices start from around EUR 10,000 for a full-day and go up to EUR 50,000 or more for a week-long charter. Superyachts are available from Puerto Banús and Sotogrande, and they can accommodate 12-20 guests for a day trip.

Private Yacht Hire Pricing Guidance

Prices vary by boat size, age, brand, and the reputation of the operator. Below are rough price bands for a half-day (4 hours) and full-day (8 hours) charter, excluding food and drinks, based on departures from Marbella or Puerto Banús.

  • 30-40 foot motor yacht: EUR 1,200-2,500 half-day, EUR 2,000-4,500 full-day.
  • 40-50 foot motor yacht: EUR 1,500-3,500 half-day, EUR 2,500-6,000 full-day.
  • 50-60 foot motor yacht: EUR 2,500-5,000 half-day, EUR 4,000-9,000 full-day.
  • 40-50 foot catamaran: EUR 1,500-3,000 half-day, EUR 2,500-5,500 full-day.
  • 40-50 foot sailing yacht: EUR 900-1,800 half-day, EUR 1,600-3,000 full-day.
  • 30-40 foot RIB: EUR 500-1,000 half-day, EUR 800-1,800 full-day.
  • Superyacht 80+ feet: price on request, typically EUR 10,000-25,000 per day.

These are guide prices. Actual quotes depend on the season, availability, and the specific boat. The best way to get an accurate price is to use the search page to compare offers from multiple operators.

What to Expect in Different Seasons

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and hot summers. The private yacht hire season runs from April to October, with peak demand in July and August.

April and May are shoulder season. Air temperatures are 18-24 degrees C, water temperature around 16-18 degrees C. You can still swim, but it is brisk. The sea is calmer, and there are fewer boats on the water. Prices are 20-30% lower than peak season. Bookings are easier to get at short notice.

June is the sweet spot. The water warms to 20-22 degrees C, the weather is hot but not unbearable, and the tourist crowds have not fully arrived. Prices start to rise in the second half of the month.

July and August are peak season. Air temperatures hit 30-35 degrees C, water temperature 24-26 degrees C. The sea is busy, especially around Puerto Banús and Marbella. Prices are at their highest, and you need to book at least 2-3 weeks in advance. The trade-off is perfect swimming conditions and long, sunny evenings.

September and October are still warm, with air temperatures 25-30 degrees C in September, dropping to 20-24 degrees C in October. Water stays warm through September, then cools to 20 degrees C by late October. Prices drop back to shoulder-season levels. October is a good month for dolphin spotting as the water is still clear.

November to March is low season. Most charter boats are in dry dock or undergoing maintenance. A few operators still run trips in good weather, but the water is too cold for swimming (14-16 degrees C) and the days are shorter. If you want a winter escape, consider a motor yacht with a heated cabin, but expect limited availability.

How to Book a Private Yacht Hire

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You search for available boats in your chosen port, compare prices and photos, and then send a booking request. The operator confirms availability and sends you a payment link. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the date, with the balance due 7-14 days before the charter.

You will need to provide the number of guests, the date and time, your preferred duration, and any special requests (catering, specific route, water toys). The operator will then tailor the itinerary to your group. Most operators accept bank transfer, credit card, or PayPal. Some also accept cryptocurrency.

Cancellation policies vary. Most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 14 days before the charter, 50% refund if you cancel 7 days before, and no refund within 7 days. If the operator cancels due to bad weather or mechanical issues, you get a full refund or the option to reschedule.

On the day, you arrive at the port 15 minutes before departure. The skipper greets you, does a safety briefing, and then you cast off. You can bring your own food and drinks, but glass bottles are usually banned on boats. Some operators provide a cooler with ice. You are responsible for your own sun protection and any seasickness medication.

For a full list of available boats and to check real-time availability, head to the search page.

Who Private Yacht Hire Is For

Private yacht hire suits a range of groups. Couples looking for a romantic day out often choose a small motor yacht or a sailing yacht for two, with a stop for lunch at a quiet cove. Families with children prefer catamarans because they are stable and have plenty of space for kids to play. Groups of friends celebrating a birthday or a stag/hen party usually go for a motor yacht with a flybridge, a good sound system, and a full bar.

Corporate groups use private yacht hire for client entertainment, team-building, or product launches. A 60-foot motor yacht can host up to 12 guests for a business lunch, with Wi-Fi and a presentation screen on some boats. The skipper can anchor near a beach club for a swim, then return to port in time for an evening dinner.

If you are a solo traveller, private yacht hire is expensive because you pay for the whole boat. You might be better off joining a shared charter or a group tour. But if you value privacy and want a bespoke itinerary, it is worth the premium.

One group that should avoid private yacht hire is anyone with severe seasickness. Even with a catamaran, the Mediterranean can get choppy, especially in the afternoon when the Levante wind picks up. If you are prone to motion sickness, choose a morning charter when the sea is calmer, and take medication an hour before departure.

Popular Destinations for Private Yacht Charters

Most private yacht charters stay within 10-15 nautical miles of the departure port, but you can go further if you pay extra fuel. Here are some common routes.

Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro is a classic 3-hour round trip. You leave the marina, cruise past the Marbella Club Hotel and the Sierra Blanca mountains, and anchor at the Cala del Faro cove for a swim. The water is clear and calm, and there is a small beach bar on the sand if you want to wade ashore.

Estepona to the Strait of Gibraltar is a longer trip, about 20 nautical miles each way. You pass the Punta de la Doncella lighthouse and the Selwo Marina, then head south to the strait where you often see pods of common dolphins, and sometimes pilot whales or orcas. The current is strong here, so the skipper will keep the engine running.

Marbella to Nerja is a full-day trip of about 30 nautical miles. You go past the cliffs of the Maro-Cerro Gordo nature reserve and anchor near the Nerja caves for a swim. The caves themselves are not accessible by boat, but the view from the water is impressive. This trip requires good weather and a calm sea, so it is usually only offered in June to September.

Sotogrande to Gibraltar is a 15-nautical-mile run that takes about 45 minutes by motor yacht. You can anchor off the beaches of Catalan Bay or cruise past the Rock of Gibraltar. The skipper will point out the Barbary macaques on the upper rock. This route is popular with families because the water is usually calm and the scenery is dramatic.

Benalmádena to Fuengirola is a short 5-nautical-mile hop that works well for a half-day charter. You stop at the Fuengirola castle for a photo, then anchor near the El Chaparral cove for lunch. The water is shallow and warm, good for snorkelling.

For more detailed route ideas, check the blog for guides on day trips and anchorage spots.

What to Bring on a Private Yacht Hire

Pack light. You need swimwear, a towel, sun cream (reef-safe if possible), a hat, and sunglasses. A light jumper or windbreaker is useful for the afternoon breeze. Non-slip shoes are recommended if you plan to walk around while the boat is moving. Most boats have a small fridge, so you can bring your own drinks and snacks. If you want to play music, bring a Bluetooth speaker, though many boats already have one.

Do not bring glass bottles, as broken glass on deck is a hazard. Cans, plastic bottles, and reusable cups are fine. Some operators prohibit red wine because it stains. Check with the operator before you bring any alcohol. If you are prone to sunburn, bring a high-SPF sunscreen and reapply every two hours. The reflection off the water intensifies the sun's rays.

If you plan to swim, bring a mask and snorkel. Most boats provide basic gear, but it is often low quality. A waterproof phone pouch is useful for taking photos without risking your phone. Cash is handy if you want to tip the skipper or buy drinks from a beach bar that does not take cards.

Safety and Legal Requirements

All boats on BoatHire24 are licensed and insured for commercial use. The skipper holds a valid Spanish Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo or a higher qualification. The boat carries life jackets for all passengers, a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher, and an emergency radio. The skipper is required to do a safety briefing before departure, covering the location of life jackets, the emergency procedures, and the use of the VHF radio.

Spanish law limits the number of passengers on a private charter to 12 for most boats, unless the boat has a special passenger certificate for up to 20. This is enforced by the Guardia Civil and the Port Authority. If you have a larger group, you may need to charter two boats or choose a superyacht with a higher capacity.

Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper cannot drink any alcohol while in charge of the boat. If you or your guests become intoxicated and behave dangerously, the skipper has the right to terminate the charter and return to port early. You will not get a refund in that case.

Weather cancellations are rare but happen. The skipper makes the final call based on wind speed and wave height. If the wind exceeds 25 knots or the waves are over 2 metres, the charter will be postponed or cancelled for safety. You get a full refund or a reschedule in that situation.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group

Start with the group size. If you have 6-8 people, a 40-foot motor yacht or a 40-foot catamaran works well. For 10-12 people, you need a 50-60 foot motor yacht or a 50-foot catamaran. If you have more than 12, you need a superyacht or multiple boats.

Next, consider the activity. If you want to swim and snorkel, a catamaran is better because it has a wide swim platform and a shallow draft. If you want to cover distance and see multiple spots, a motor yacht is faster. If you want to fish, choose a dedicated fishing boat with a fighting chair and rod holders. If you want to party, look for a motor yacht with a flybridge, a good sound system, and a large sun pad.

Think about the budget. If you are on a tight budget, a sailing yacht or a RIB is cheaper. If you want luxury, a motor yacht with a flybridge and a jacuzzi is the way to go. If you want to impress clients, a superyacht is the obvious choice.

Finally, check the operator's reputation. Look for boats that are well-maintained, with recent photos and clear descriptions. Read the terms and conditions carefully, especially regarding fuel, catering, and cancellation. If something seems too cheap, it probably is. A 40-foot motor yacht for EUR 500 half-day is likely an old boat with a tired engine and a grumpy skipper.

If you are still unsure, contact BoatHire24 support for a recommendation. We can match you with a suitable boat based on your requirements.

Why Book Private Yacht Hire Through BoatHire24

BoatHire24 is a marketplace, not a broker. We list boats from multiple operators, so you can compare prices, photos, and availability in one place. You book directly with the operator, but we handle the payment processing and provide a secure platform. If a problem arises, we mediate between you and the operator.

We cover all the major ports on the Costa del Sol, from Sotogrande to Benalmádena. Our search filters let you narrow down by boat type, price, capacity, and amenities. Every boat on our platform is verified for licensing and insurance. We do not list boats without a licensed skipper.

We also publish a blog with guides on the best anchorages, weather conditions, and local events. It is a useful resource for planning your itinerary. If you have any questions before booking, you can email us or use the live chat on the site.

bodyHtml:
What Is Included with Every Marmaris Boat Hire

Every boat rental through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a boating licence or any experience. The skipper knows the local waters, the best anchorages, and how to handle the boat. Fuel is usually included for standard day trips, but check the listing details. You can add extra services like watersports equipment, a private chef, or a photographer. Always read the inclusions on the listing page before booking.

Marmaris Departure Ports and Nearby Marinas

The main departure point is Marmaris Marina, right in the town centre. It is a large marina with plenty of restaurants and shops. Netsel Marina is also in Marmaris, a bit quieter. For a more exclusive start, consider Göcek, about 20 minutes by car from Marmaris. Göcek has smaller marinas and is closer to the famous bays like Cleopatra's Bay and the Twelve Islands. Fethiye is about an hour and a half drive east, but it opens up the Ölüdeniz area and Butterfly Valley. Each port has its own character. Marmaris is lively and touristy. Göcek is more upmarket and peaceful. Fethiye is a mix of history and natural beauty.

Types of Boats Available for Marmaris Boat Hire

You can hire motor yachts from 30ft to 100ft in Marmaris. A standard 40ft motor yacht sleeps 6-8 people and costs from around EUR 800 per day. Gulets are traditional Turkish wooden yachts, perfect for day charters or week-long cruises. A 50ft gulet can take up to 12 guests for a day trip from EUR 1,200. RIBs and speedboats are best for short trips to nearby bays. A 6m RIB with a 150hp engine costs from EUR 300 for a half day. Sailing yachts are available for those who want a quieter experience. A 40ft sailing yacht with skipper costs from EUR 600 per day. Fishing boats are also available, with equipment included, from around EUR 400 for a half day.

Popular Marmaris Boat Hire Itineraries

A classic day trip from Marmaris goes to Paradise Island, also known as Sedir Island, with its famous Cleopatra Beach. The trip takes about 30 minutes by speedboat. Another popular route is the Twelve Islands tour from Göcek, which includes stops for swimming, lunch, and sunbathing. For a longer charter, you can sail to Dalyan to see the Lycian rock tombs and the Iztuzu Beach, a turtle nesting site. That is a full day trip, about 2 hours each way by motor yacht. If you want a week-long gulet charter, common routes include Marmaris to Fethiye, with stops at Göcek, Ekincik, and Kaunos. Prices for a week on a gulet start from around EUR 5,000 for a 50ft boat, all inclusive.

Marmaris Boat Hire Pricing Guidance for 2025

Prices for Marmaris boat hire vary by season, boat size, and duration. In the low season (April, May, October), a half-day RIB trip costs from EUR 250. In high season (June to September), the same RIB costs from EUR 350. A full-day motor yacht charter for up to 10 guests ranges from EUR 800 in low season to EUR 1,500 in high season. Gulets are more expensive. A day on a 60ft gulet for 15 guests starts at EUR 1,500 in low season and goes up to EUR 2,500 in August. Superyachts over 80ft are price on request, but expect EUR 5,000 per day and above. Always check the listing for exact pricing and any extras like fuel surcharges or port fees.

Best Time for Marmaris Boat Hire

The best time for a boat trip in Marmaris is from May to October. May and June have pleasant temperatures around 25-30°C and fewer crowds. July and August are peak season, with temperatures up to 40°C and busy marinas. The sea is warmest in August, around 28°C. September and October are still warm, with temperatures around 25-30°C, and the water is still swimmable. Winter months (November to March) are too cold and windy for most boat trips. If you want to avoid the crowds, book for late May or early September. You will get good weather and lower prices.

How to Book a Boat in Marmaris

Booking through BoatHire24 is simple. Go to our search page, enter your dates, group size, and preferred boat type. You will see a list of available boats with prices, photos, and skipper details. Read the inclusions carefully. Some charters include food and drinks, others do not. Once you find a boat you like, click to book. You pay a deposit online, and the balance is paid to the skipper on the day. You can also contact the operator directly through our platform with any questions. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for high season, but last-minute bookings are sometimes available.

Who Is Marmaris Boat Hire For

Marmaris boat hire is for anyone who wants to see the Turkish coast from the water. Families with children will enjoy the calm bays and shallow waters. Groups of friends can rent a gulet for a party trip. Couples might prefer a private motor yacht for a romantic sunset cruise. Business groups can hire a superyacht for corporate events. The skipper handles everything, so you do not need any experience. If you want to drive the boat yourself, you need a valid boating licence. But most people prefer to relax and let the skipper do the work. Marmaris is a family-friendly destination, but the nightlife is also vibrant, so you can combine a day on the water with evening entertainment.

Marmaris Boat Hire vs Other Destinations

Marmaris is one of the most popular boat hire destinations in Turkey, but it is not the only one. Bodrum offers a similar experience but with more luxury options. Fethiye is quieter and more focused on natural beauty. Göcek is smaller and more exclusive. Marmaris has the advantage of a large marina, easy access to shops and restaurants, and a wide range of boat types. The bays around Marmaris are stunning, but they can get crowded in August. If you want more seclusion, consider hiring a boat from Göcek instead. For more information on other destinations, check our blog for guides on Bodrum, Fethiye, and the Greek Islands.

Local Tips for Your Marmaris Boat Trip

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a swimsuit. The sun is strong, even in May. Most boats have a shaded area, but you will want to swim. Pack a light jacket for the evening if you are doing a sunset cruise. The wind can pick up, and it gets cooler. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication before you board. The water is generally calm in the bays, but the open sea can be choppy. Ask your skipper for recommendations on where to eat lunch. Many bays have beachfront restaurants that only serve boaters. For example, in Göcek, the Sargerme Bay has a great fish restaurant. Tip the skipper and crew if they do a good job. 10% of the charter fee is standard.

Why Book Marmaris Boat Hire with BoatHire24

We are BoatHire24, a marketplace that connects you directly with local boat operators in Marmaris and the Costa del Sol. We do not own the boats. We list them so you can compare prices, photos, and reviews. Every charter includes a licensed skipper. We handle the booking and payment securely. If you have any issues, our support team is available by email. We do not charge any booking fees. The price you see is the price you pay. We have been operating since 2020 and have thousands of satisfied customers. For Marmaris boat hire in 2025, we offer the best selection of boats at competitive prices.

Marmaris Boat Hire for a Day: Typical Timetable

A standard day charter from Marmaris Marina usually starts at 10:00. You board, meet the skipper, and get a safety briefing. By 10:30 you are motoring out of the harbour. The first stop is often a nearby bay for swimming, like Turunç Bay or Amos Bay, about 20 minutes away. Around 12:30 the skipper anchors for lunch, either on board or at a waterfront restaurant. After lunch you have free time for more swimming, sunbathing, or using the boat’s paddleboard. The return to port is around 17:00. If you book a sunset cruise, you leave at 16:00 and return around 20:00, watching the sun go down over the bay. Half-day trips are also available, typically 4 hours, from 10:00 to 14:00 or 14:00 to 18:00.

Marmaris Boat Hire for a Week: Gulet Charter Example

A 7-day gulet charter from Marmaris is a popular option for groups. You sail along the coast, stopping at different bays each night. A typical itinerary might start in Marmaris, then head to Bozburun for the first night. Day two you sail to Selimiye, a quiet fishing village. Day three you reach Hisarönü, with its famous fish market. Day four you cross to Rhodes, Greece, if you have passports (visa rules apply). Day five you explore the Datça Peninsula. Day six you return to Marmaris via the Gulf of Hisarönü. Day seven you disembark after breakfast. Prices for a 50ft gulet for 8 guests start from around EUR 5,000 for the week, including crew, fuel, and meals. You pay extra for drinks, port fees, and any excursions.

Marmaris Boat Hire for Fishing Enthusiasts

If you want to fish, Marmaris has good options. You can hire a dedicated fishing boat, typically a 7m to 9m motor boat with outriggers and a fish finder. The skipper knows the best spots, like the reefs off the Datça Peninsula or the deeper waters near Rhodes. A half-day trip costs from EUR 400 for up to 4 anglers. Full-day trips from EUR 600. The boat provides rods, reels, bait, and tackle. Common catches include sea bream, grouper, and occasionally tuna. The skipper will clean and fillet your catch, and you can take it to a restaurant to be cooked. Fishing is best from April to June and September to October, when the water is cooler and the fish are active. July and August are quieter but still productive early morning.

Marmaris Boat Hire for Large Groups and Events

For groups over 12 people, a gulet is the best choice. A 60ft gulet can take up to 20 guests for a day charter. Prices start from EUR 1,500 in low season and go up to EUR 3,000 in August. Some gulets have a DJ booth, sound system, and a bar, making them suitable for birthday parties, bachelor or bachelorette parties, or corporate events. You can also hire a catamaran, which offers more deck space and stability. A 50ft catamaran for 15 guests costs from EUR 1,200 per day. For a really large event, superyachts over 80ft are available, with capacity for 50 guests or more. These are price on request but typically EUR 8,000 per day and above. Always confirm the maximum guest capacity and any noise restrictions with the skipper.

Marmaris Boat Hire in Low Season: Pros and Cons

Booking a boat in Marmaris in April, May, or October has clear advantages. Prices are 30-40% lower than in July and August. The marinas are less crowded, and you have more choice of boats. The weather is still pleasant, with temperatures around 22-28°C in May and 20-25°C in October. The sea is swimmable from mid-May onwards. The downside is that some restaurants and beach clubs in the bays are closed until June. The water is cooler, around 18-20°C in April. Wind can be stronger in April and October, making the sea choppy. If you want calm conditions and warm water, June or September are better. But if you are on a budget and want peace, low season is a smart choice.

Marmaris Boat Hire for Sunset Cruises

A sunset cruise from Marmaris is a romantic option. You leave the marina around 17:00 and head to a quiet bay like Icmeler Bay or the bay of Turunç. The skipper anchors, and you watch the sun set over the mountains while sipping a drink. Most sunset cruises last 3 to 4 hours and include a light meal or snacks. A motor yacht for 6 guests costs from EUR 400 for a sunset trip. A gulet for 10 guests starts at EUR 600. The best time for sunset is June to September, when the sun sets around 20:30. In April and October, it sets around 19:00. Bring a jacket, as it gets cooler after sunset. Some boats offer a DJ or live music for an extra fee.

Marmaris Boat Hire for Watersports

Many boats available for hire in Marmaris come with watersports equipment. You can add a jet ski, wakeboard, or water skis to your charter for an extra cost. A jet ski rental for 30 minutes costs around EUR 100. A wakeboard session for an hour is around EUR 150. Some boats have a paddleboard and snorkelling gear included. The best bays for watersports are those with calm, clear water, like Cleopatra Bay or the bays around Göcek. If you want to do serious watersports, look for a RIB or speedboat with a powerful engine, as they can tow you faster. Always use the provided life jackets and follow the skipper’s instructions. The water is warm enough from June to October for comfortable swimming and watersports.

Marmaris Boat Hire for Families with Children

Families with children are well catered for in Marmaris. Most boats have safety rails and a shaded cockpit. The skipper will choose calm bays for swimming, like the shallow waters of Turunç Bay or the lagoon at Dalyan. You can bring your own food and drinks, or the boat can provide a kid-friendly lunch. Some charters include a children’s menu and soft drinks. A motor yacht or catamaran is better for families than a gulet, as they have more stable decks. For a family of 4, a half-day trip on a 30ft motor yacht costs from EUR 500. Full-day from EUR 800. Always tell the skipper you have children when booking, so they can prepare. Life jackets for children are provided, but check the sizes fit. The best time for families is June or September, when it is not too hot and the sea is warm.
