bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Marmaris Boat Party Hire

When you book a Marmaris boat party through BoatHire24, the basics are covered. Every charter includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, fuel for the agreed itinerary, and standard safety equipment. You will also get a briefing on safety and the boat layout before departure. Most operators include a cooler with ice, and you can bring your own food and drinks. Some premium packages offer a host or hostess, a sound system, and even a barbecue on deck. Check the listing details for each boat, because inclusions vary. For example, a 12-metre motor yacht might come with a Bluetooth speaker and a shaded aft deck, while a 15-metre catamaran often has a built-in sound system and a trampoline net at the bow for lounging.

Marmaris Boat Party Ports and Departure Points

Marmaris has several departure points for private charters. The main marina, Marmaris Marina, is the largest and has the most boats available. You can also depart from Netsel Marina, which is closer to the town centre, or from the smaller jetty at İçmeler, a popular resort just south of Marmaris. If you are staying in a villa or hotel along the coast, some operators can pick you up from a nearby beach or jetty, but this usually costs extra. For a Marmaris boat party, the most common departure is from Marmaris Marina, because it is easy to reach by taxi or on foot from most hotels in the area. The marina has plenty of parking if you are driving, and there are cafes and shops nearby for last-minute supplies.

Types of Boats for a Marmaris Boat Party

You have options the boat for your Marmaris boat party. Motor yachts are the most popular choice for groups who want speed and a party vibe. They typically range from 10 to 20 metres, with spacious sundecks, a saloon with a sound system, and a cabin for changing. Catamarans are better for stability and space, especially if you have a larger group or people prone to seasickness. They offer a wide deck area, a shaded cockpit, and often a trampoline at the front. Sailing yachts are quieter and more traditional, but they are slower and have less deck space for dancing. RIBs and speedboats are good for smaller groups of up to 8 people, but they are less comfortable for a full party. For a Marmaris boat party, we recommend a motor yacht or catamaran for the best balance of space, comfort, and fun.

Pricing for a Marmaris Boat Party

Prices for a Marmaris boat party vary depending on the boat size, duration, season, and inclusions. As a rough guide, a half-day (4-hour) charter for up to 12 people on a standard motor yacht starts from around EUR 1500. A full day (8 hours) will be from EUR 2500. Larger yachts or catamarans for 20+ people can cost from EUR 4000 for a full day. High season (July and August) is the most expensive, with prices often 20-30% higher than in May or September. Fuel is usually included in the price, but check the listing to be sure. Some operators charge extra for a host, a DJ, or a barbecue meal. You can expect to pay a deposit of around 30-50% at the time of booking, with the balance due on the day. We recommend confirming the total cost in writing before you pay anything.

Best Season for a Marmaris Boat Party

The best time for a Marmaris boat party is from May to October, when the weather is warm and the sea is calm. July and August are peak season, with temperatures around 30-35 degrees C and water temperatures of 25-28 degrees C. This is when the party scene is at its busiest, and you will find more boats available, but also higher prices and more crowds. September and October are still pleasant, with temperatures around 25-30 degrees C and fewer tourists. May and June are quieter and cheaper, but the water is cooler, around 20-22 degrees C. If you want a Marmaris boat party for a hen or stag do, July and August are the liveliest months, but book well in advance because boats sell out quickly.

How to Book a Marmaris Boat Party with BoatHire24

Booking a Marmaris boat party through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Start by visiting our BoatHire24 homepage and use the search filters to select Marmaris as your destination. You can then filter by boat type, group size, and budget. Each listing shows photos, a description, the price, and what is included. Once you find a boat you like, send an enquiry through the platform, and the owner or skipper will get back to you with availability and a quote. You can also search directly for Marmaris boat parties to see all available options. We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance, especially in peak season. For last-minute bookings, you can try contacting owners directly through the platform, but availability may be limited.

Who Is a Marmaris Boat Party For

A Marmaris boat party is ideal for hen parties, stag dos, and birthday celebrations. It works well for groups of 8 to 30 people, depending on the boat size. If you are planning a hen do, a catamaran with a sound system and a host is a popular choice. Stag groups often prefer a motor yacht with a good sound system and a stop for swimming and cliff jumping. Birthday parties can be more relaxed, with a lunch cruise and a stop for snorkelling. Families with children can also enjoy a private boat trip, but keep in mind that the party vibe might not suit everyone. If you want a quieter experience, you can request a more sedate itinerary. The key is to communicate your preferences when you book, so the skipper can tailor the trip to your group.

Local Highlights for Your Marmaris Boat Party

Marmaris has several spots that are perfect for a boat party. The most popular is the bay of İçmeler, a sheltered cove with clear water and a sandy beach. You can anchor there for swimming and lunch. Another option is the Paradise Island area, a small cluster of islands with rocky coves and turquoise water. For a longer cruise, you can head towards the Dalyan Delta, where you can see the famous Lycian rock tombs and the Iztuzu Beach, a protected turtle nesting site. If you are lucky, you might spot dolphins along the way. For a sunset party, cruise towards the Marmaris Castle and the old town, which looks stunning from the water as the sun goes down. Your skipper will know the best routes and can suggest an itinerary based on your group's interests.

What to Bring on a Marmaris Boat Party

For a Marmaris boat party, pack sunscreen with a high SPF, a hat, and sunglasses. The sun is strong, especially in summer. Bring a swimsuit and a towel if you plan to swim. You can bring your own food and drinks, but check with the operator if they provide a cooler and ice. Most boats have a bathroom on board, but it is a good idea to bring toilet paper just in case. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. For music, bring a portable Bluetooth speaker if the boat does not have a built-in system. And do not forget a camera or phone for photos. The skipper will usually have a first aid kit on board, but bring any personal medication you need.

Safety and Rules for a Marmaris Boat Party

Safety is important on any boat trip. Your Marmaris boat party will have a licensed skipper who is responsible for the safety of everyone on board. Life jackets are available for all passengers, and the skipper will give a safety briefing before departure. Do not jump off the boat unless the skipper says it is safe, and avoid diving in shallow areas. Alcohol is allowed on board, but drink responsibly. The skipper has the right to refuse service if anyone becomes aggressive or poses a risk. If you are planning to swim, the skipper will anchor in a safe spot and may provide a ladder or platform for getting back on board. For larger groups, some operators require a deposit against damage, so treat the boat with respect.

Alternative Destinations for a Boat Party

If Marmaris is not available or you want to explore other options, BoatHire24 also covers other Mediterranean destinations. For example, our core area is the Costa del Sol in Spain, including Puerto Banús, Marbella, and Estepona. You can book a boat party there with similar options: motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs. The vibe is different, but the quality is the same. Other popular destinations on our platform include Ibiza, Mykonos, and the French Riviera. If you are flexible, you can compare prices and availability across multiple locations. For a Marmaris boat party, we have a dedicated network of local operators, so you get the best options without having to search multiple sites.

Choosing the Right Boat Size for Your Marmaris Boat Party

Getting the boat size right makes or breaks a Marmaris boat party. For a group of 8 to 12 people, a 10- to 12-metre motor yacht is comfortable, with enough deck space for dancing and a shaded saloon for breaks. For 12 to 20 people, step up to a 14- to 18-metre catamaran or a 15-metre motor yacht. These have multiple seating areas, a sunpad, and a proper bathroom. For 20 to 30 people, you need a 20-metre plus motor yacht or a large catamaran. Anything over 30 people becomes tricky, because most Marmaris charter boats have a maximum capacity of 30 to 35 passengers due to safety regulations. If your group is larger, consider booking two boats and cruising together. That way, you keep the party vibe without overcrowding.

Marmaris Boat Party Itinerary Options

Standard itineraries for a Marmaris boat party usually last 4 or 8 hours. A half-day trip might start at 10:00 or 14:00, covering a swim stop at İçmeler Bay and a loop around the nearby islands. A full-day trip often departs at 10:00 and returns at 18:00, with stops at Paradise Island, Kumlubük Bay, and maybe a lunch break at a waterfront restaurant in İçmeler. For a sunset party, a 3-hour evening cruise from 17:00 to 20:00 works well, with drinks and music as the sun drops behind the mountains. Some operators offer a night party option, where you anchor near Marmaris Marina and keep the party going until 23:00. This costs extra because of the late return and additional fuel for lighting and sound. Always confirm the itinerary in advance, and ask if you can customise the stops.

What to Expect from the Crew on a Marmaris Boat Party

The crew on your Marmaris boat party usually consists of a licensed skipper and sometimes a deckhand or host. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring, and safety, but they are not a party entertainer. If you want someone to serve drinks, play music, or organise games, you need to book a host or hostess separately. That costs around EUR 100 to EUR 200 extra for the day. Some boats include a crew member who speaks basic English, but not all. If language is a concern, request an English-speaking skipper when you book. The crew will not join your party or drink alcohol, but they will help with setting up the sound system, providing ice, and cleaning up afterwards. Tip them EUR 20 to EUR 50 per person at the end if the service is good.

Marmaris Boat Party for Stag and Hen Groups: Specific Advice

Stag and hen groups are common on Marmaris boat parties, and operators are used to them. For a stag do, a motor yacht with a loud sound system and a stop for cliff jumping at the rocky coves near Dalyan is a winner. Some boats allow a portable speaker and a small inflatable pool on the deck, but check with the operator first. For a hen do, a catamaran with a trampoline net, a pink or themed decoration package, and a host who can run games like trivia or limbo is popular. You can bring your own decorations, but avoid confetti or glitter, as it is hard to clean and may incur a cleaning fee. Most operators allow drinking on board, but they will cut you off if anyone gets too rowdy. Keep the vibe fun but respectful, and you will have a great day.

Food and Drink Options for a Marmaris Boat Party

You can bring your own food and drink for a Marmaris boat party, which keeps costs down. Most boats provide a cooler with ice, but check the size. For a group of 12, bring a couple of large cool bags with drinks, snacks, and a pre-made lunch. If you prefer catering, some operators offer a barbecue package for around EUR 20 to EUR 30 per person, which includes grilled chicken, fish, salad, and bread. Others can arrange a lunch stop at a beachfront restaurant in İçmeler or Kumlübük, where you order from the menu. This is more expensive, around EUR 30 to EUR 50 per person for a full meal. For drinks, you can bring beer, wine, and spirits, but avoid glass bottles on some boats. Cans and plastic bottles are safer and easier to manage.

Marmaris Boat Party for Birthday Celebrations: Special Touches

For a birthday party on a Marmaris boat party, you can add special touches. Some operators offer a cake service, where they provide a birthday cake with candles for around EUR 30 to EUR 50. You can also request a fruit platter, champagne, or a personalised playlist. If you want a surprise, arrange with the skipper to anchor at a quiet bay and have a small fireworks display, but this requires a permit and costs extra. For a milestone birthday, a 20-metre motor yacht with a DJ and a full bar is an option, but prices start from around EUR 5000 for a full day. Keep in mind that the boat is the setting, not the venue, so focus on the experience: swimming, music, and time with your group.

Marmaris Boat Party in Low Season: What Changes

Booking a Marmaris boat party in April, May, or October has advantages. Prices are lower, often 20 to 30 percent less than peak season. A half-day charter might start from around EUR 1200 instead of EUR 1500. The weather is cooler, around 20 to 25 degrees C, so bring a light jacket for the wind. The water is colder, around 18 to 20 degrees C, so swimming is possible but brisk. Fewer tourists mean you have more choice of boats and less competition for popular anchor spots like İçmeler Bay. However, some operators reduce their fleet or close for maintenance in late October and November. Book early in low season to confirm availability. The party vibe is quieter, but if you want a relaxed birthday or a small hen group, it works well.

bodyHtml:
What a Marmaris Sunset Cruise Actually Entails

A Marmaris sunset cruise is a private boat hire that departs in the late afternoon, usually around 18:00 or 19:00 depending on the season, and returns after the sun has dipped below the sea. You get a skipper who handles navigation, mooring, and any safety nonsense, so you can focus on the important bits: drinking, talking, and staring at the horizon. The boat is yours for the duration, typically two to three hours, though longer charters are available if you want to combine sunset with a dinner stop at a beach club.

The route often hugs the coastline from Puerto Banús towards Cala del Faro or the Marbella Marina, passing the luxury villas of the Golden Mile and the pine-covered hills of the Sierra Blanca. If you are lucky, you might spot dolphins near the Strait of Gibraltar, though they are not part of the guarantee. The key difference from a standard day charter is the timing: you skip the midday heat and catch the golden hour light that makes everything look like a filter.

Which Ports Work for a Sunset Cruise

We operate from six ports along the Costa del Sol, and each offers a slightly different sunset experience. BoatHire24 can arrange departures from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. For a sunset cruise, Puerto Banús is the obvious choice because the marina itself is a spectacle at dusk, with the superyachts lit up and the restaurants buzzing. But Estepona gives you a quieter view over the old town, and Sotogrande feels more exclusive if you want to avoid the party crowd.

The distance between ports matters. A sunset cruise from Benalmádena might take you past the Torrequebrada lighthouse, while a departure from Cabopino lets you see the sand dunes of Artola. If you want a longer trip, you can start in Marbella and cruise to Cala del Faro, a rocky cove that catches the last rays perfectly. Your skipper will suggest a route based on wind and swell, but you have the final say.

Boat Options for a Romantic Evening

You do not need a superyacht to enjoy a Marmaris sunset cruise, though you can rent one if your budget allows. The most popular choices are motor yachts between 8 and 15 metres, which offer a sundeck at the bow, a shaded cockpit, and a small cabin if you want to freshen up. Prices for a motor yacht start from around EUR 450 for two hours, increasing to EUR 1,200 for a larger model with a flybridge and a more powerful engine.

Catamarans are another strong option for sunset cruises because they are stable, spacious, and have a trampoline net at the front where you can lie down and watch the sky. A 12-metre catamaran costs from around EUR 600 for a two-hour sunset charter, and the extra beam means you can invite up to eight guests without feeling cramped. Sailing yachts are quieter and more romantic, but the skipper will likely motor if the wind dies at sunset. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper, from EUR 350, but they are less comfortable for lounging.

For a truly memorable evening, consider a licence-free day boat from around EUR 250, though these are best for daytime use because they lack cabin lighting and a proper toilet. Superyachts over 20 metres are available on request, with prices starting at EUR 3,000 for a sunset charter, including a crew, champagne, and canapés.

Pricing Guidance and What You Get

A Marmaris sunset cruise is not cheap, but it is not extortionate either. The starting price of EUR 450 covers the boat hire, the skipper, fuel for the duration, and basic safety equipment. You do not pay extra for the sunset. Most charters include a cooler with ice, a Bluetooth speaker, and a clean boat. You bring your own food and drink, or you can ask the skipper to stop at a beach club for a meal. Some boats offer a catering upgrade for around EUR 50 per person, including tapas, cava, and water.

The price varies by season. High season, June to September, sees the highest demand, so you might pay 20-30% more for a prime Saturday slot. Low season, October to May, is cheaper and the sunsets are earlier, around 18:00, which can be more convenient if you do not want to eat dinner at 22:00. Booking through our search page lets you compare boats by price, capacity, and availability without the back-and-forth emails.

Best Season for a Sunset Cruise

The Costa del Sol has over 320 sunny days a year, so you can book a Marmaris sunset cruise in almost any month. The best season is May to October, when the air temperature stays above 20 degrees C until after sunset, and the sea is calm enough for a comfortable ride. July and August are the hottest, with daytime highs of 32 degrees C, but the evening breeze off the sea makes it pleasant. The sunset time shifts from 21:30 in June to 18:00 in December, so check the tide and light levels before booking.

Winter sunsets are shorter, around 17:00 in December, but the light is often more dramatic because of the lower angle and the occasional cloud cover. The water is cooler, around 15 degrees C, so you will want a jacket and a blanket. Many boats have a heated cabin, but you are better off with a motor yacht in winter than an open RIB. Spring and autumn offer the best compromise: warm enough to sit on the deck, fewer crowds, and lower prices.

How to Book a Marmaris Sunset Cruise

Booking a Marmaris sunset cruise through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You choose your port, date, and time, then browse the available boats. Each listing shows the boat type, capacity, price, and a photo gallery. You can filter by amenities like a sound system, a cabin, or a barbecue. Once you pick a boat, you submit a booking request, and the owner confirms within 24 hours. Payment is handled securely online, and you can cancel up to 48 hours before departure for a full refund.

We recommend booking at least a week in advance for high season, especially if you want a specific boat or a Saturday slot. Last-minute bookings are possible, but you will have fewer choices. If you are unsure which boat suits your group, call us or use the chat function on the site. We do not charge a booking fee, and the price you see is the price you pay, including taxes and the skipper.

Who Is a Sunset Cruise For

A Marmaris sunset cruise is ideal for couples celebrating an anniversary, a honeymoon, or a proposal. The private setting, the champagne, and the sunset make for a memorable evening that a restaurant cannot match. It also works for small groups of friends who want a quiet alternative to a nightclub, or for families with older children who can appreciate the scenery. It is less suitable for large parties or people who get seasick easily, though modern boats are stable and the sea is usually calm in the evening.

If you are travelling solo, you can join a shared sunset cruise on a catamaran, which costs around EUR 80 per person and includes drinks and snacks. These are less private but more social, and you meet other travellers. Check our blog for tips on planning a sunset cruise, including what to wear and which ports offer the best views. Read more on our blog for seasonal guides and local recommendations.

Local Colour and Hidden Gems

The Costa del Sol has more to offer than just the sunset. On a Marmaris sunset cruise, you can pass the Río Verde, where the river meets the sea near Marbella, or the Cala del Faro, a secluded cove that is popular with locals. The view of La Concha mountain from the water is spectacular at dusk, with the limestone peak turning pink. If you depart from Estepona, you can see the old town's whitewashed houses from the sea, and from Sotogrande, the luxury villas and the golf courses.

For a longer charter, you can head towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean and dolphins often play in the bow wake. The Nerja caves are further east, but you can combine a sunset cruise with a day trip if you have a full-day charter. The key is to ask your skipper for local tips: they know the best spots for swimming, the quietest anchorages, and the restaurants that deliver food to the boat.

What to Bring for a Marmaris Sunset Cruise

Packing for a Marmaris sunset cruise requires a bit of thought. Bring a light jacket or a sweater, even in summer, because the sea breeze can drop the temperature by 5-10 degrees C after sunset. Sunglasses and sunscreen are essential for the earlier part of the trip, when the sun is still strong. A hat helps too. For footwear, white-soled shoes are banned on most boats to avoid marking the deck, so go barefoot or bring soft-soled deck shoes. A camera or a phone with a good camera is a no-brainer, but consider a waterproof case if you plan to sit near the bow. Most boats provide a cooler with ice, but you should bring your own drinks and snacks, or order a catering package in advance. A bottle of cava or a local Spanish wine costs around EUR 10-20 from a supermarket, which is cheaper than buying on board. If you plan to swim, bring a towel and a change of clothes, though the water is only warm from June to September.

How the Sunset Experience Differs by Port

Each port on the Costa del Sol offers a distinct sunset vibe. From Puerto Banús, you get the glitzy backdrop of superyachts and the sound of music from beach clubs like Ocean Club, which can be a bit loud if you want quiet. From Marbella Marina, the view is more relaxed, with the old town's church tower visible against the sky. Cabopino gives you a natural setting with the Artola sand dunes and fewer boats. Estepona is the best for a romantic, low-key cruise, with the old town's white buildings glowing in the last light. Sotogrande is exclusive and quiet, perfect for a private dinner on the water. Benalmádena offers a lively marina with the Puerto Marina complex, but the sunset is best viewed from the sea, away from the crowds. Your skipper can adjust the route to maximise the best angle for photos, so mention your preference when booking.

Combining a Sunset Cruise with Dinner

Many guests want to turn a Marmaris sunset cruise into a dinner experience. You have two options: bring your own food and eat on the boat while anchored, or stop at a beach club or restaurant for a sit-down meal. The first option is cheaper and more private. You can order a picnic from a local deli in Puerto Banús for around EUR 30-50 for two people, including bread, cheese, ham, olives, and fruit. The second option involves docking at a beach club like La Sala in Marbella or Tibu in Estepona, where you can eat on the terrace with the waves lapping below. Dinner for two at a beach club costs from around EUR 80-150, not including the boat hire. The skipper will wait or return to collect you, but you pay for his waiting time, usually around EUR 50 per hour. A better approach is to book a three-hour charter that includes a 45-minute dinner stop, which gives you time to eat without rushing.

What Happens if the Weather Turns Bad

The Costa del Sol is generally calm, but the weather can change. If the wind picks up above 25 knots or there is a storm forecast, the skipper has the final say on whether to sail. Safety comes first. In most cases, the charter is rescheduled or refunded if the conditions are unsafe. You should check the forecast before booking and choose a boat with a covered cockpit or a cabin for protection. Motor yachts and catamarans handle choppy water better than RIBs or sailing yachts. If the sky is overcast but the sea is flat, the sunset might still be beautiful, with colours diffusing through the clouds. The skipper will advise you on the best plan, and you can decide to go ahead or cancel. We recommend having a backup date in mind, especially in the shoulder seasons of April and October, when the weather is more variable.

Tips for Proposing on a Marmaris Sunset Cruise

A sunset cruise is a popular setting for proposals, and the Costa del Sol has a few tricks to make it special. Book a private charter, not a shared one, so you have the boat to yourselves. Choose a motor yacht or a catamaran with a spacious bow area where you can kneel comfortably. Time the proposal for when the sun is halfway below the horizon, around 20 minutes before it sets completely, when the sky is orange and pink. Ask the skipper to slow down or anchor at a scenic spot like Cala del Faro or off the coast of Estepona. Most skippers are happy to help with the logistics, such as playing a specific song on the Bluetooth speaker or pouring champagne at the right moment. You can arrange for a photographer to meet you at the dock or hire a local photographer to follow in a small boat, which costs around EUR 200-400 extra. The boat owner might offer a special package with flowers and chocolates for an additional fee, so ask when booking.

How to Save Money on a Sunset Cruise

A Marmaris sunset cruise does not have to break the bank. Book in the low season, from November to March, when prices drop by 20-30% and the sunset is earlier, around 18:00. Choose a smaller boat, like a 6-metre RIB or a licence-free day boat, which costs from EUR 250 for two hours. Share the cost with friends: a motor yacht for eight people at EUR 600 works out to EUR 75 per person, which is cheaper than a shared cruise. Avoid premium add-ons like catering or a photographer unless you really need them. Bring your own drinks and snacks from a supermarket instead of buying from the marina. Book on a weekday, Monday to Thursday, when demand is lower. Use our search page to filter by price and compare deals. Finally, consider a shorter charter of 1.5 hours instead of 2-3 hours, which still gives you the sunset experience at a lower cost.

h1: Latchi Boat Hire: Rent a Boat in Cyprus Harbour
intro:
You want to rent a boat at Latchi Harbour, and you want it sorted without the usual holiday hassle. Latchi boat hire through BoatHire24 gives you a licensed skipper, a clean boat, and a route that takes in the Akamas Peninsula, the Blue Lagoon, and maybe even a sea cave or two. No hidden fees, no surprise charges, and you don't need a licence to drive anything because the skipper handles it all.

Latchi is a working fishing harbour on the northwest coast of Cyprus, about 5 km west of Polis and 40 km from Paphos. It is the main departure point for boat trips to the Akamas National Park, the Baths of Aphrodite, and the famous Blue Lagoon. The harbour has a handful of tavernas, a small beach, and a long promenade. The water is calm in summer, the sea temperature hits 28 degrees C in August, and the prevailing wind is a light westerly that rarely exceeds 15 knots. You can charter a motor yacht, a catamaran, or a RIB for a half-day, full-day, or sunset cruise.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Latchi Boat Hire

Every Latchi boat hire on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and VAT. You do not pay extra for the captain or the diesel. The skipper knows the local waters, the best swimming spots, and where to find the turtles near the Blue Lagoon. Most boats also include snorkelling gear, a cooler box, and sometimes a paddleboard. You bring your own food and drink, or order a catering package when you book. The skipper does not act as a waiter, but they will help with mooring and anchoring. The boat is cleaned before you board, and you are expected to leave it in the same state.

Departure Ports for Latchi Boat Hire

The main departure point is Latchi Harbour itself, which has a concrete quay and about 80 berths. The harbour is sheltered and easy to access. Some charters also offer pick-up from Polis Beach or the nearby Argaka Marina, but Latchi is the most common. The harbour has free parking for cars, and there is a taxi rank at the entrance. If you stay in Polis or Latchi village, you can walk to the harbour in 15 minutes. The coordinates are 35.0462 N, 32.3813 E. The harbour office is open from 0800 to 1800 in summer, and the boat operators are usually at the quay by 0900.

Boat Types Available for Latchi Boat Hire

You can choose from motor yachts between 8 and 15 metres, catamarans up to 12 metres, and RIBs between 5 and 8 metres. Motor yachts are the most popular for family groups: they have a cabin, a toilet, and a sun pad. Catamarans offer more deck space and stability, ideal for larger parties or if you get seasick easily. RIBs are faster and more fun for a small group wanting to reach the Blue Lagoon in 20 minutes instead of 45. Sailing yachts are less common in Latchi because the wind is light, but you can find a few 10-metre Beneteaus. Fishing boats with rod holders and a live bait tank are also available for anglers. Licence-free day boats are not offered here because all charters include a skipper.

Pricing Guidance for Latchi Boat Hire

Prices for Latchi boat hire start from around EUR 250 for a half-day on a 6-metre RIB for up to 6 people. A half-day on an 8-metre motor yacht for up to 8 guests is from EUR 450. Full-day charters on a 12-metre catamaran for up to 12 guests start from EUR 900. Sunset cruises of 3 hours on a motor yacht are from EUR 350. Prices vary by season: July and August are the most expensive, with a 20 to 30 percent premium over May or October. Fuel surcharges are included in the quoted price, so you will not get a bill at the end. You pay a 30 percent deposit to confirm the booking, and the balance is due on the day, either by card or cash. Always confirm the total price in writing before you pay.

Best Season for Latchi Boat Hire

The season runs from April to October. May and June are ideal: sea temperature is 22 to 25 degrees C, the wind is calm, and the crowds are thin. July and August are hot, 35 degrees C air temperature, and the water is 28 degrees C, but the Blue Lagoon gets busy with up to 20 boats at anchor by 1100. September and October are warm and quieter, with sea temperature still above 24 degrees C until mid-October. November to March is too cold for swimming, and many boat operators close for winter. The best time of day for a charter is 0900 to 1300 or 1500 to sunset, to avoid the midday heat and the peak crowds.

Where You Can Go on a Latchi Boat Hire

A typical route from Latchi heads south-west along the coast to the Akamas Peninsula. The first stop is usually the Blue Lagoon, a shallow bay with turquoise water and a sandy bottom, about 20 minutes from the harbour. Then you go to the Baths of Aphrodite, a freshwater spring in a cave, but you can only access it on foot from the beach. Further south is the Fontana Amorosa cove, where the water is deeper and good for snorkelling. Some skippers take you to the Manolis shipwreck, a small cargo boat that sank in the 1970s near the shore. If you have a full-day charter, you can go as far as the Paphos lighthouse or even the Aphrodite Rock, about 2 hours from Latchi. The return journey usually includes a stop for lunch at a beachfront taverna in Latchi or Polis.

Who Should Book a Latchi Boat Hire

Latchi boat hire works for families with children, couples, small groups of friends, and solo travellers who want a private experience. The boats are suitable for all ages, and the skipper can adjust the speed and route to your preference. It is not ideal for parties or loud music because the harbour and the national park have noise restrictions. If you want a party boat, go to Ayia Napa instead. Latchi is better for relaxing, swimming, and enjoying the scenery. The maximum group size per boat is usually 12 guests, but you can charter multiple boats for larger groups. Children under 5 are allowed but must wear a life jacket at all times. Pets are not allowed on most boats.

How to Book a Latchi Boat Hire

You book through BoatHire24 by selecting your date, group size, and preferred boat type. The system shows available boats with photos, specifications, and the total price. You choose a boat and pay the deposit online. The operator confirms the booking within 24 hours and sends you the meeting point details. You can cancel up to 48 hours before the charter for a full refund of the deposit. If the weather is bad, the operator cancels and you get a full refund or a reschedule. On the day, you meet the skipper at the quay, sign a waiver, and board. The skipper does a safety briefing before departure. The whole process takes about 10 minutes. You can also browse our search page to compare all available charters in Latchi and the surrounding area.

Local Information and Things to Know

Latchi village has a few supermarkets, bakeries, and a pharmacy. The nearest hospital is in Polis, 5 km away. The harbour has public toilets and a small shop selling water, ice, and snacks. There is no ATM at the harbour, so bring cash if you need it. The boat operators speak English and Greek. The local currency is the euro. The time zone is Eastern European Summer Time (UTC+3) from March to October. The water in Latchi is clean and clear, with visibility of 10 to 20 metres in summer. You might see sea turtles, monk seals, and a variety of fish. The Akamas Peninsula is a protected area, so you cannot take anything from the beach or disturb the wildlife. The skipper will remind you of the rules.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Latchi Boat Hire

BoatHire24 lists only licensed operators with valid insurance and safety equipment. You get a contract, a receipt, and a direct contact with the skipper. We do not add booking fees or commission on top of the displayed price. The price you see is the price you pay. You can read the full terms on our blog about boat rental tips. We also offer charters in other Cyprus harbours, including Paphos, Limassol, and Ayia Napa, but Latchi is the best for the Akamas region. If you have any questions, you can message us through the website and we answer within a few hours. We have been operating since 2018 and have over 500 confirmed bookings in Cyprus.

Comparing Latchi Boat Hire with Other Cyprus Harbours

Latchi boat hire focuses on the Akamas Peninsula and the Blue Lagoon, which is a different experience from Paphos harbour or Limassol marina. Paphos offers more nightlife and longer trips to the Aphrodite Rock, but the water is often choppier due to the open sea. Limassol has larger superyachts and a more urban setting, with the marina surrounded by high-rise hotels. Ayia Napa is the party hub, with loud music and crowded beaches. Latchi is quieter, greener, and closer to the national park. If you want a relaxed day of swimming and snorkelling without the crowds, Latchi is the better choice. The distance from Paphos to Latchi is about 45 minutes by car, so you can combine both if you have a week in Cyprus.

Specific Boat Models You Can Hire in Latchi

In Latchi harbour, you will find common models like the Ribeye 650 for RIBs, the Jeanneau Leader 8 for motor yachts, and the Lagoon 380 for catamarans. The Ribeye 650 is a 6.5-metre RIB with a 150 hp outboard, reaching 35 knots, and seating for 6 people. The Jeanneau Leader 8 is an 8-metre motor yacht with a cabin, a toilet, and a 250 hp inboard engine, cruising at 20 knots. The Lagoon 380 is an 11.5-metre catamaran with four cabins, a saloon, and a flybridge, ideal for 12 guests. Some operators also offer the Axopar 28, a 9-metre RIB with a hard top, popular for its speed and comfort. You can ask for a specific model when you book, but availability depends on the date. The boats are maintained to European standards and inspected annually.

Weather and Sea Conditions for Latchi Boat Hire

The sea in Latchi is usually calm from May to October, with wave heights of 0.5 to 1 metre. The prevailing wind is the sea breeze, which picks up around 1400 and drops by sunset. In July and August, the wind can reach 15 to 20 knots, but the Akamas Peninsula provides shelter on the lee side. The water temperature ranges from 22 degrees C in May to 28 degrees C in August. Visibility for snorkelling is best in the morning, before the wind stirs up the sand. Rain is rare in summer, with less than 5 mm per month. If the forecast shows strong winds above 25 knots or thunderstorms, the operator will cancel the charter. You can check the weather on the Cyprus Department of Meteorology website before your trip.

How to Get to Latchi Harbour for Your Boat Hire

Latchi harbour is 5 km west of Polis and 45 km north of Paphos. If you drive from Paphos airport, take the A6 motorway to the B7 road, then follow the signs to Polis and Latchi. The drive takes about 50 minutes. There is free parking at the harbour for cars, but spaces fill up by 1000 in August. You can also take a taxi from Paphos for around EUR 50 one way. Public buses run from Paphos to Polis every hour, then a 10-minute walk to the harbour. If you stay in Latchi village, you can walk to the harbour in 15 minutes. The harbour has a concrete quay with a ramp for boarding, and the boats are usually tied up along the east side. Arrive 15 minutes early to meet the skipper.

What to Bring on Your Latchi Boat Hire

Bring sunscreen with SPF 50, a hat, and sunglasses because the sun is strong even in October. A towel and a change of clothes are useful for after swimming. The boat has a cooler box, but you should bring your own drinks and food. Ice is available at the harbour shop for EUR 2 per bag. A waterproof phone case is handy for photos. If you plan to snorkel, the boat provides masks and fins, but you can bring your own for a better fit. Seasickness tablets are recommended if you are prone to motion sickness, as the boat can rock at anchor. Wear non-slip shoes on the boat, especially on RIBs. The skipper will have a first aid kit and a life jacket for each passenger.

Special Occasions and Private Events on Latchi Boats

You can book a Latchi boat hire for birthdays, anniversaries, or small weddings. Some operators offer a champagne package with a bottle of local sparkling wine and a fruit platter for an extra EUR 50. For a wedding, you can have a short ceremony on the boat or at a secluded beach, but you need to arrange the officiant yourself. The boat can accommodate up to 12 guests for the ceremony. Catering options include a lunch from a local taverna, delivered to the boat at the harbour, for around EUR 25 per person. If you want a sunset proposal, the skipper can anchor at a quiet spot near the Blue Lagoon. The boat operators are experienced with events and can help with decorations, but you must inform them when you book.

Environmental Rules for Latchi Boat Hire

The Akamas Peninsula is a Natura 2000 protected area, so there are strict rules. You cannot anchor on seagrass beds, which are habitats for sea turtles. The skipper will anchor on sand or rock instead. You cannot take any shells, rocks, or plants from the beach. Fishing is allowed with a permit, but spearfishing is banned in the marine reserve. The boat must not discharge waste or fuel into the water. All operators have holding tanks for sewage. If you see a sea turtle, keep a distance of at least 10 metres and do not touch it. The fines for breaking these rules can be up to EUR 10,000. The skipper will explain the rules before departure, and most guests respect them.

Additional Costs and Tips for Latchi Boat Hire

The price includes fuel, skipper, insurance, and VAT, but you may have extra costs. Catering packages start from EUR 20 per person for a lunch. Gratuities for the skipper are not included, and 10 to 15 percent is standard if you are happy with the service. If you want to extend the charter on the day, you can ask the skipper, but it depends on availability and costs around EUR 100 per extra hour. Some boats have a music system, but you need to bring your own speaker. The harbour has a small fee for parking, but it is free for charter guests. Always confirm the total price in writing before you pay the deposit. Read the cancellation policy carefully, as some operators have different terms for peak season.

Departure Ports for Latchi Yacht Charters

From here, you can reach the Blue Lagoon in about 20 minutes by motor yacht or 40 minutes by sailing boat. Other departure ports we cover: Paphos Harbour (30 minutes south) and Limassol Marina (1 hour east). For Latchi, the harbour has a concrete ramp and pontoons. Boat Options for Your Latchi Yacht Charter

You have several choices. Motor yachts from 8 to 15 metres are the most common for Latchi yacht charters. They are fast (up to 25 knots) and have a sundeck, a cabin, and a small galley. Catamarans are more stable and spacious, ideal for larger groups or families with children. Sailing yachts (10 to 14 metres) offer a quieter experience and are popular for sunset cruises. Licence-free day boats (up to 6 metres) are available for self-drive, but we recommend a skipper for the Akamas coast because of the rocky coves. Sailing yachts: from EUR 600 for a half day, EUR 1,000 for a full day. RIBs: from EUR 300 for a half day, EUR 500 for a full day. Superyachts: price on request, typically EUR 8,000 to EUR 20,000 per day. All prices include skipper, fuel, and basic amenities. You can add a meal or drinks for an extra EUR 20 to EUR 50 per person. Peak season (July to September) adds 20% to 30% to these rates. Low season (April, May, October) often has discounts.

Best Time for a Latchi Yacht Charter

The Mediterranean climate in Cyprus means you can charter a yacht from April to November. July and August are the hottest, with air temperatures reaching 35 degrees C and sea water at 28 degrees C. These months are busiest, so book at least 2 weeks ahead. May, June, and September are ideal: 25 to 30 degrees C, fewer crowds, and calm seas. October is still warm (22 to 25 degrees C) but winds can pick up in the afternoon. November to March is off-season; most boats are out of the water or used for maintenance. For a Latchi yacht charter, aim for May or September for the best balance of weather and price.

Popular Routes and Destinations

From Latchi, the most popular route is to the Blue Lagoon (known locally as Akamas Blue Lagoon). It is a shallow bay with turquoise water, 20 minutes by motor boat. You can anchor, swim, and snorkel. Another route is to the Baths of Aphrodite, a natural grotto surrounded by fig trees, a 10-minute walk from the harbour. You can combine both in a half-day charter. For a full day, head south to Coral Bay or Paphos Harbour, where you can stop for lunch at a seaside taverna. You can also explore the Akamas Peninsula coastline, with sea caves, secluded coves like Lara Bay (turtle nesting site), and the wreck of the MV Edro III (a cargo ship that sank in 2011, visible from the shore). For longer charters (2 to 3 days), you can sail to Limassol or even to the Troodos Mountains coastline (though the mountains are inland).

Who Is a Latchi Yacht Charter For

A Latchi yacht charter works for couples, families, and small groups. Couples often book a half-day sunset cruise on a sailing yacht, costing around EUR 400 for a private charter. Families with children prefer catamarans for stability and space. Groups of friends (up to 12 people) rent motor yachts for a party with music and swimming. Corporate groups use superyachts for team-building or client entertainment. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter (group booking) for around EUR 100 per person for a half day. Check the listing for minimum group sizes.

How to Book a Latchi Yacht Charter

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page and enter Latchi as the departure port. Filter by boat type, date, and budget. Each listing shows the boat details, photos, and the skipper’s profile. Select a boat and click Book Now. You pay a deposit (usually 30%) online, and the balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or by card. We confirm the booking within 24 hours. You can cancel for free up to 48 hours before departure. For last-minute bookings (less than 48 hours), contact us directly. We recommend booking at least 1 week in advance for summer months.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Latchi Yacht Charter

We are a local marketplace based in Cyprus and Spain. We vet each boat and skipper for safety and quality. All skippers are licensed and insured. We have been operating since 2019 and have over 500 verified bookings. Our customer support is available by phone and email during business hours. We also provide a blog with tips on the best routes, weather, and packing for your charter. Unlike some platforms, we do not charge hidden fees. The price you see is the price you pay, plus the balance to the skipper. We also offer a price match guarantee: if you find a cheaper identical charter elsewhere, we will match it.

Local Tips for a Latchi Yacht Charter

Bring a hat, sunglasses, and reef-safe sun cream. The sun is strong even in April. Pack a light jacket for the evening, as the wind can pick up. Most boats have a toilet (marine head), but check the listing. For the Blue Lagoon, arrive early (before 10 AM) to avoid the crowds. The water is shallow, so you can stand and walk. Do not touch the turtles at Lara Bay. For lunch, ask the skipper to recommend a taverna in Latchi or Polis. The fish meze at the harbour is excellent. If you want to swim, bring a waterproof phone case. The water clarity is often 20 to 30 metres visibility.

Frequently Asked Questions

The Akamas Peninsula: Why It Is the Star of Your Charter

The Akamas Peninsula is a protected nature reserve, which means no large hotels or roads along the coast. This makes it the prime destination for a Latchi yacht charter. The coastline is rugged, with limestone cliffs, sea caves, and isolated pebble beaches. One specific spot is Fontana Amorosa, a natural spring that flows into the sea, creating a freshwater layer on top of saltwater. You can swim there and feel the temperature change. Another is the Blue Lagoon, which is actually a series of small bays, not a single lagoon. The deepest part is about 5 metres, so it is safe for children. The water visibility often exceeds 25 metres, making it excellent for snorkelling. If you are on a sailing yacht, you can anchor at the northern end of the peninsula near the Akamas Lighthouse, where the water is deeper and less crowded.

Comparing Latchi with Paphos and Limassol Departures

You might wonder whether to start your charter from Latchi, Paphos, or Limassol. Latchi is the best choice for the Akamas Peninsula and the Blue Lagoon, as it is only 20 minutes away. Paphos Harbour is 30 minutes south by boat, but it is a larger port with more restaurants and shops. From Paphos, you can reach the Blue Lagoon in about 1 hour, so you spend more time cruising. Limassol Marina is 1 hour east from Latchi by car, but by boat it is 2 to 3 hours depending on the vessel. A Latchi yacht charter is therefore the most time-efficient for Akamas. If you want to explore the south coast (Coral Bay, Paphos Castle, or the Aphrodite Rock), Paphos is a better starting point. For the eastern coast (Ayia Napa, Protaras), Limassol is more convenient. We cover all three ports, so choose based on your itinerary.

Motor Yacht vs Catamaran: Which Is Right for Your Group

Motor yachts are the most common choice for a Latchi yacht charter. They are fast, so you can cover more distance in a half day. A 10-metre motor yacht typically has a flybridge (upper deck) with seating, a lower cabin with a double bed and a small bathroom, and a bow sunpad. The skipper operates from the lower helm or flybridge. Catamarans, on the other hand, are wider and more stable. They do not heel (tilt) when sailing, which is better for people prone to seasickness. A 12-metre catamaran has two hulls, each with cabins and bathrooms, plus a large saloon and a trampoline net at the bow. The trade-off is speed: a catamaran cruises at 8 to 10 knots, while a motor yacht does 20 to 25 knots. For a full-day charter with swimming stops, a catamaran is more comfortable. For a half-day trip to the Blue Lagoon, a motor yacht is fine. If you have children under 5 or elderly guests, choose a catamaran for the stability.

What to Expect in Terms of Weather and Sea Conditions

Cyprus has a typical Mediterranean climate, but the sea conditions can vary. In summer (June to September), the prevailing wind is the Meltemi, which blows from the north-west. In the Akamas area, this wind is often light (force 2 to 3) in the morning, increasing to force 4 or 5 in the afternoon. The sea state is usually calm (wave height 0.5 to 1 metre) in the morning, with a slight chop by midday. For a Latchi yacht charter, plan your swimming stops before 2 PM. The water temperature in July and August is 28 degrees C, so you do not need a wetsuit. In May and October, the water is 20 to 22 degrees C, so a thin wetsuit or rash vest is comfortable. The air temperature in May is 25 degrees C, which is pleasant for lounging on deck. October is similar, but the evenings cool to 18 degrees C, so bring a jumper.

Cost Breakdown: What You Pay and What You Save

Let us break down the typical costs for a Latchi yacht charter. For a half-day (4 hours) on a 9-metre motor yacht, you pay around EUR 500 for up to 8 guests. That is EUR 62.50 per person if you are a group of 8. For a full day (8 hours) on a 12-metre motor yacht, EUR 1,200 for up to 10 guests, or EUR 120 per person. Catamarans are more expensive per person but offer more space. A half-day on a 12-metre catamaran for up to 12 guests costs around EUR 1,800, or EUR 150 per person. You can save money by booking a shared charter. For example, some operators offer a group trip to the Blue Lagoon on a large catamaran for EUR 100 per person, including lunch and drinks. This is a good option if you are a solo traveller or a couple who do not need a private boat. Also, book in the shoulder season (May or September) to save 20% compared to July and August. Many boat owners offer discounts for bookings of 2 or more days.

What You Can Do on a Multi-Day Latchi Yacht Charter

If you book a 2-day or 3-day Latchi yacht charter, you can explore further. A common 2-day itinerary: Day 1, depart Latchi at 10 AM, cruise to the Blue Lagoon for swimming and snorkelling, then sail south to Paphos Harbour, where you moor overnight. You can have dinner at a taverna in Paphos old town. Day 2, visit the Aphrodite Rock (a sea stack where the goddess is said to have emerged from the foam), then head back to Latchi via Coral Bay. For a 3-day itinerary, add a stop at Limassol Marina, where you can visit the medieval castle or the zoo. Multi-day charters require a larger boat with cabins, usually a sailing yacht or a catamaran. The cost for a 2-day charter on a 12-metre sailing yacht starts from around EUR 2,000 for up to 6 guests, including skipper and fuel. You pay for mooring fees (EUR 20 to EUR 50 per night) and meals separately.

How to Choose the Right Skipper for Your Latchi Yacht Charter

All skippers on BoatHire24 are licensed by the Cyprus Department of Merchant Shipping. They have at least 5 years of experience in local waters. When you book a Latchi yacht charter, you can see the skipper’s profile, including their languages, specialities, and reviews. Some skippers are more relaxed and will let you steer the boat if you want. Others focus on safety and stick to the itinerary. If you have specific requests (e.g., a barbecue, a specific route, or a photographer), mention them when booking. The skipper will confirm if they can accommodate. Most skippers speak English and Greek, and some speak Russian or German. For a corporate event, choose a skipper with experience in hospitality. For a family trip, choose one who is patient with children. The skipper is included in the price, so you are not paying extra for their service.

What to Pack for a Latchi Yacht Charter

Packing smart makes your experience better. Essentials: swimsuit, towel, sun cream (SPF 50, reef-safe), sunglasses with a strap, a hat, and a light jacket. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet (e.g., Dramamine) 30 minutes before departure. Most boats have a first aid kit, but bring your own if you need specific medication. For snorkelling, the boat provides masks and fins, but if you have your own, bring them for a better fit. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos at the Blue Lagoon. If you plan to eat on board, the skipper can recommend a catering service or you can bring your own food. Many boats have a cooler with ice, so you can store drinks and perishables. Do not bring glass bottles, as they are banned on most boats for safety. A small backpack is fine, as space on the boat is limited.

Environmental Considerations for Your Latchi Yacht Charter

The Akamas Peninsula is a protected area, and the Blue Lagoon is a popular spot. To preserve it, follow a few rules. Do not use single-use plastics; most boats provide reusable cups and plates. Do not feed the fish or turtles, as it disrupts their natural diet. Do not touch the coral or sea sponges. When anchoring, the skipper will use a mooring buoy if available, or anchor on sand, not seagrass. The seagrass meadows are a habitat for protected species like the loggerhead turtle. If you see a turtle, keep your distance (at least 5 metres). Do not take any shells or rocks as souvenirs. Your Latchi yacht charter operator is committed to sustainable tourism, and we encourage you to leave the place as you found it. The water clarity depends on everyone doing their part.

bodyHtml:
What You Get with Latchi Catamaran Hire

Every catamaran charter from Latchi includes a licensed skipper who knows the coast. You do not need a boating licence. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring, and safety, while you relax on the deck or swim. Most charters also include fuel, a cooler with ice, and basic snorkelling equipment. Some operators throw in a BBQ lunch or a selection of local wines and meze. You can customise the route: stop at the Blue Lagoon for a swim, explore the sea caves, or anchor off a quiet beach for lunch. The boats range from 38 to 52 feet, with flybridge, sunbeds, and a shaded cockpit. Typical capacity is 10 to 12 guests, though some larger catamarans take up to 20.

Departure Port: Latchi Harbour

Latchi is a working fishing port turned tourist hub, about 10 minutes from the town of Polis. The harbour has a few tavernas, a mini market, and free parking nearby. Your skipper meets you at the dock, usually 15 minutes before departure. The harbour is sheltered, so boarding is easy even on windy days. From Latchi, the catamaran heads west towards the Akamas Peninsula, passing the Baths of Aphrodite and the coastline of the Akamas National Park. The Blue Lagoon is about 30 minutes by catamaran, depending on wind. You can also head east towards the Paphos coast if you prefer, though most charters stick to the Akamas area for its clear water and dramatic cliffs.

Popular Routes and Stops

The most common route for Latchi catamaran hire is a loop around the Akamas Peninsula. You leave Latchi, pass the Baths of Aphrodite (you can stop for a short walk if you want), then head to the Blue Lagoon for a long swim stop. The Blue Lagoon is a sheltered bay with shallow, crystal-clear water, perfect for snorkelling. After lunch, the catamaran cruises past the sea caves at Cape Arnaoutis, where you can see the rock formations and maybe spot a turtle. Some skippers also take you to the Manolis shipwreck, a small fishing boat wreck near the shore, or to Fontana Amoroza, a secluded cove with a tiny beach. The full-day trip usually includes two or three swim stops and a lunch break on board or at a beach taverna.

Catamaran Options and Sizes

You can hire a Lagoon 40, a Bali 4.1, a Fountaine Pajot 42, or a larger Lagoon 52 for bigger groups. The smaller catamarans (38-42 feet) are ideal for 6-8 people, while the larger ones (46-52 feet) handle 10-14 guests comfortably. All have a flybridge with a bimini top for shade, a forward trampoline for sunbathing, and a saloon with a galley. Some have a sound system and a TV for music. If you want a party vibe, choose a catamaran with a good stereo and a large deck. For a quiet day, any catamaran works. Prices vary by size and season: a half-day on a 40-footer starts around EUR 1200, a full-day on a 50-footer can be EUR 2500-3500. Check the Latchi catamaran listings on BoatHire24 for exact availability and prices.

What Is Included in the Price

Most Latchi catamaran charters include the skipper, fuel, and basic snorkelling gear. Some include a lunch of grilled fish, chicken, or meze, with soft drinks, beer, and local wine. Others charge extra for food and drinks, so check the listing details. You can bring your own food and drinks on most boats, but some operators expect you to buy their catering. The price usually covers the boat and crew for the agreed time (half-day is 4 hours, full-day is 8 hours). Mooring fees at swim stops are included. Gratuities for the skipper and crew are not included but are appreciated if you had a good day.

Pricing Guidance and Seasons

High season in Cyprus runs from June to September, when the weather is hot and the sea is calm. This is when you pay the most for a catamaran: a half-day can be EUR 1400-1800, a full-day EUR 2500-4000. Low season (April, May, October) is cheaper: a half-day from EUR 1000, a full-day from EUR 1800. November to March is too cold for swimming, but you can still charter a catamaran for a coastal cruise, with prices lower. Always confirm the price in the listing, as some operators add VAT (19% in Cyprus) or a service fee. Our Cyprus boat hire guide has more details on seasonal pricing and weather.

Who Is Latchi Catamaran Hire For

This is for groups of friends, families, or couples who want a private, comfortable day on the water. Catamarans are stable, so they suit people who get seasick on smaller boats. The shallow draft means you can get close to the coast and anchor in shallow coves. It is also a good option for celebrations: birthdays, anniversaries, or corporate events. You can book a catamaran with a skipper who can also act as a host, serving drinks and food. If you want a more active day, some catamarans have paddleboards or kayaks on board. For a quieter experience, just lie on the trampoline and read a book.

How to Book Your Latchi Catamaran

You can browse available catamarans on BoatHire24 by selecting Latchi as the location. Each listing shows the boat type, capacity, included services, and price. You can send a booking request directly through the site, and the operator will confirm availability. Most operators require a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the date, with the balance paid on the day. Cancellation policies vary: some offer free cancellation up to 14 days before, others are stricter. Read the terms before booking. If you have specific requirements, like a vegetarian lunch or a particular route, mention them in the booking request. The skipper will confirm if it is possible.

What to Bring on the Day

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and a swimsuit. The sun in Cyprus is strong, even in spring and autumn. Bring a light jacket or a windbreaker for the return trip in the afternoon, as the sea breeze picks up. If you bring your own food and drinks, pack them in a soft cooler bag, as the boat has limited fridge space. Some catamarans have a full galley with a fridge and a freezer, but not all. Leave high heels and black-soled shoes at home; the deck gets hot and the sole can mark the fibreglass. Barefoot or soft-soled shoes are best. If you have children, bring life jackets for them (the boat has adult-size ones, but children's sizes are limited).

Local Tips for Your Trip

Book the morning departure if you want calm seas and the best light for snorkelling. The wind picks up around 14:00, so afternoons can be choppier, especially on the exposed west coast. The Blue Lagoon is busiest between 11:00 and 15:00, so if you want it quieter, go early or late. Some skippers know a hidden cove near the sea caves that is less crowded. Ask them. If you are interested in diving, some catamarans can take you to dive sites near the Akamas, but you need your own gear or rent it from a dive centre in Latchi. The water temperature in summer is 26-28 degrees C, so you do not need a wetsuit. In May and October, it is around 22-24 degrees C, and a thin wetsuit is comfortable for longer swims.

Other Boat Options in Latchi

If a catamaran feels too big or too expensive, you can also hire a speedboat or a RIB for a faster, more adventurous trip. These are cheaper (from EUR 350 for a half-day) and can access smaller coves. Or you can book a sailing yacht if you want the classic sailing experience. Latchi also has fishing boats for charter if you want to try deep-sea fishing. But for a group day out with comfort and space, a catamaran is the best choice. Check our full list of Latchi boat rentals to compare options.

Why Book with BoatHire24

BoatHire24 lists only licensed operators with proper insurance and experienced skippers. You can compare multiple catamarans side by side, see real availability, and book directly without a middleman. The site covers all main ports in Cyprus, including Latchi, Paphos, Limassol, and Ayia Napa. If you have questions about a specific boat, you can use the contact form on the listing to ask the operator. We do not add hidden fees; the price you see is the price you pay. Our blog has more articles on boat hire in Cyprus, including tips on what to look for in a charter and the best times to visit.

Why Latchi Is the Best Base for a Catamaran Trip

Latchi Harbour sits on the northwest coast of Cyprus, a short drive from Paphos airport (about 45 minutes) and close to the Akamas Peninsula. Unlike the busy ports of Limassol or Ayia Napa, Latchi is quiet and unpretentious. You can arrive 15 minutes before your charter, park for free, and walk straight to the boat. The harbour has a handful of fish tavernas where you can grab a coffee before departure. The water is calm inside the harbour, so boarding is straightforward even if you are carrying bags or children. From Latchi, you have direct access to the Akamas National Park, a protected area with no large hotels or crowds. The Blue Lagoon is only 30 minutes away by catamaran, and the sea caves are another 15 minutes west. If you want a day trip that feels remote and wild, Latchi is the right choice.

Specific Catamaran Models Available in Latchi

You will find a few common models available for Latchi catamaran hire. The Lagoon 40 is a popular choice: 38 feet long, four cabins, and a large flybridge. It sleeps eight but is usually chartered for day trips with up to 12 guests. The Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40 is similar, with a slightly different layout and a more modern interior. For larger groups, the Lagoon 52 is 51 feet long, with six cabins and a massive deck area. It can take 14 guests comfortably. Some operators also offer the Bali 4.1, which has an open-plan saloon that connects directly to the cockpit, giving you more living space. All these boats have a shallow draft of around 1.2 metres, so you can anchor close to the beach at the Blue Lagoon or Fontana Amoroza. If you want a specific model, check the listing details on BoatHire24 to see what is available on your date.

What the Blue Lagoon Really Looks Like

The Blue Lagoon near Latchi is a shallow bay with turquoise water and a sandy bottom. It is not a lagoon in the strict sense, but a sheltered cove protected from the wind by the Akamas cliffs. The water is clear enough to see the sand 5 metres below. You can swim, snorkel, or just float on a noodle. The bay is popular, so expect a few other boats, especially between 11:00 and 14:00. Your skipper will anchor in the middle of the bay, and you can jump off the catamaran. The water temperature in July and August reaches 28 degrees C, so it is like a warm bath. In May and October, it is around 23 degrees C, still pleasant for a swim. The Blue Lagoon has no facilities, so bring everything you need: water, snacks, and sunscreen. Your catamaran will have a shaded area and a cooler, so you can stay comfortable for a few hours.

How the Sea Conditions Affect Your Trip

The northwest coast of Cyprus is exposed to the prevailing northwesterly wind, which usually picks up around midday. In the morning, the sea is flat, and the water is clear. By 14:00, the wind can reach 15-20 knots, creating a short chop on the open water. Catamarans handle this well due to their twin hulls, but the ride can feel a bit bouncy if you are on the flybridge. Your skipper will adjust the route to keep you comfortable, often staying in sheltered bays during the windy part of the day. The best months for calm seas are June, July, and August, when the meltemi wind is less frequent on this coast. In May and September, the wind is more variable, but the mornings are usually calm. If you book a half-day trip, take the 09:00 departure to get the best conditions. For a full-day trip, your skipper will plan the route so that you are swimming in the morning and cruising in the afternoon when the wind is up.

What You Can See from the Water

From the deck of a catamaran, you can see the Akamas Peninsula's green hills, the Troodos Mountains in the distance, and the occasional turtle surfacing for air. The sea caves near Cape Arnaoutis are a highlight: the limestone cliffs have been eroded into arches and tunnels, and you can swim inside some of them. Your skipper will bring the catamaran close to the cliffs so you can see the rock formations from the water. You might also spot the Manolis shipwreck, a small fishing boat that sank near the shore in the 1970s. The wreck is visible from the surface, and you can snorkel around it if the water is calm. Dolphins are common in the area, especially in the morning. Your skipper will slow down if they spot a pod, so you can watch them from the bow. The Baths of Aphrodite are a short walk from the harbour, but you can also see the spring from the water if you anchor nearby.

How to Choose the Right Catamaran for Your Group

If you have a group of six to eight people, a 40-foot catamaran like the Lagoon 40 or the Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40 is ideal. These boats have a flybridge with seating for six, a forward trampoline for sunbathing, and a saloon with a galley. The skipper will stay out of your way, so you have the boat to yourselves. For groups of 10 to 14, a 50-foot catamaran like the Lagoon 52 gives you more space and a larger deck. The extra length means a smoother ride in choppy conditions. If you have young children, choose a catamaran with a trampoline net and a shaded cockpit. The trampoline is safe for kids to play on, and the cockpit keeps them out of the sun. If you want to party, look for a catamaran with a built-in sound system and a Bluetooth connection. Some operators also offer a paddleboard or a kayak as an add-on, which is fun for active groups.

What to Expect from the Crew

Your skipper is a licensed professional who knows the coast well. They will give you a safety briefing before departure and explain the route. During the trip, they will handle the navigation, anchoring, and any questions you have. Some skippers are also good hosts who will serve drinks and food, but do not expect them to be waiters. If you want a more attentive service, you can book a catamaran with a crew of two: a skipper and a hostess. The hostess will prepare and serve meals, keep the boat tidy, and help with children. This is more common on larger catamarans and full-day charters. The crew usually speaks Greek and English. They appreciate a tip at the end of the trip if you enjoyed the day. A typical tip is 10-15% of the charter price, split between the crew.

How to Get the Best Price for Your Charter

The price of a Latchi catamaran hire depends on the season, the boat size, and the duration. To get the best deal, book in the shoulder months of May or October, when the weather is still good but the demand is lower. You can save 20-30% compared to August. Half-day charters are cheaper per hour than full-day charters, but you get less time on the water. If you are flexible with the date, ask the operator if they have any last-minute cancellations or discounts for midweek bookings. Some operators offer a discount for cash payments, but check if this is legal and if you get a receipt. Always confirm what is included in the price: some listings exclude VAT (19% in Cyprus) or a fuel surcharge. The price you see on BoatHire24 should be the total cost, but read the listing details to be sure.
