title: Latchi Speedboat Rental: Hire Without Licence Cyprus
metaDescription: Book a Latchi speedboat rental without a licence in Cyprus. Explore the Akamas coast at your own pace. Instant quotes, free cancellation, skipper optional.
h1: Latchi Speedboat Rental: Hire a Boat Without a Licence in Cyprus
intro: If you want to race across the Mediterranean without a boat licence, Latchi is your spot. This small fishing harbour on Cyprus's northwest coast is the gateway to the Akamas Peninsula, the Blue Lagoon, and the Baths of Aphrodite. You can hire a speedboat for the day, no paperwork, no exam, just your credit card and a quick safety briefing. Prices start from around EUR 200 for a half day, and you get a boat that seats up to six people, a 40hp or 60hp outboard, and a map of the best coves. BoatHire24 compares the local operators so you can pick the right boat without the hassle.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Licence-Free Speedboat in Latchi

These boats are designed for the casual driver. They are rigid inflatables (RIBs) or small motorboats with a console steering wheel, a bimini top for shade, and a fuel tank that lasts a full day if you don't hammer the throttle. You do not need any previous experience. The operator gives you a 10-minute briefing on the controls, the no-go zones, and the speed limits near the shore. Then you are free to explore. The boat comes with life jackets, a basic tool kit, and a VHF radio if you get into trouble. You can also add a skipper for around EUR 50 extra, but most people go alone.

Why Latchi Works Better Than Paphos or Ayia Napa

Paphos harbour has more boats, but the sea can get choppy and the anchorages are crowded. Ayia Napa is party central, not a place for a quiet swim. Latchi sits on the edge of the Akamas National Park, a protected area with steep cliffs, sea caves, and almost no development. You can anchor at the Blue Lagoon and have the water to yourself on a weekday. The port is small, so you walk from the car to the boat in two minutes. No queues, no shuttle buses. BoatHire24 lists boats from three operators here, all with the same licence-free policy.

Which Speedboat to Choose: Size, Power, and Price

The standard licence-free boat is a 4.5-metre to 5.5-metre RIB with a 40hp to 60hp engine. That is enough for six adults and a cooler. Half-day hire (four hours) is around EUR 200 to EUR 250. Full day (eight hours) is EUR 300 to EUR 400. Fuel is extra and costs roughly EUR 30 to EUR 50 for a day of cruising. Some operators offer bigger boats with 90hp engines for EUR 450 a day, but those require a licence. Stick to the 60hp limit if you want to drive yourself. Check the search page on BoatHire24 for current prices and availability.

Where You Can Go: Akamas, Blue Lagoon, and Beyond

From Latchi, head west along the coast. The first stop is the Blue Lagoon, a shallow bay with turquoise water about 15 minutes away. Further west is the Baths of Aphrodite, a freshwater spring in a cave. You can tie up at the small jetty and walk up the path. If you want a longer trip, go around the corner to Fontana Amorosa, a rocky cove with a small beach. Do not attempt to go past the Akamas lighthouse unless you have a local guide; the currents get strong. The maximum safe range from Latchi is about 10 nautical miles, which covers the entire Akamas coastline. For more ideas, read the BoatHire24 blog on Cyprus boating routes.

What to Bring and What to Avoid

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, and a towel. The sun is intense from May to October, and the reflection off the water burns fast. Bring snacks and drinks in a soft cooler; most boats have a small dry storage compartment. Avoid glass bottles (they break and attract fines). Do not bring a drone unless you check the local restrictions; the Akamas area is a national park and drone use is limited. Also avoid wearing flip-flops on the boat; they slip on wet fibreglass. Barefoot or rubber-soled shoes are better. The operator will provide a map and a list of prohibited anchorages (usually near sea turtle nesting sites).

Best Time of Year for a Latchi Speedboat Rental

The season runs from April to November. May, June, and September are the sweet spots: air temperature around 28 degrees C, water temperature 22 to 25 degrees C, and fewer tourists. July and August are hot (35 degrees C plus) and the Blue Lagoon gets busy by 11am. Go early, anchor before 10am, and you will have the best spot. October is still warm, but the sea can get a bit of a swell from the north. November is a gamble; some operators close after the first week. Winter is too cold and windy for a small speedboat. Book through BoatHire24 to see the calendar and pick a good weather window.

How Booking Works: No Licence, No Stress

You book online with a deposit of around 30%. The rest is paid on arrival at the port. You must show a valid passport or ID. No driving licence needed. The operator checks you are over 18 and not obviously drunk. They give you a quick safety briefing, then you sign a waiver. That is it. You get the boat keys and a fuel card. When you return, they check the fuel level and charge you for what you used. The whole process takes 15 minutes. If you want a skipper, add that when you book. The skipper will drive and show you the best spots, but you lose the freedom to go where you want. BoatHire24 handles the booking and the operator confirmation.

Who This Is For: Families, Couples, Small Groups

Licence-free speedboats are ideal for families with kids aged 5 and up (life jackets in all sizes). Couples who want a private day on the water without a crowd. Small groups of friends who want to explore coves and have a picnic. It is not suitable for watersports like wakeboarding or towing a tube; the engines are too small for that. If you want to fish, ask the operator if they allow rods; some do, some do not. For a more luxurious experience, look at the motor yachts with a skipper, but those require a full charter price. For the best value, the speedboat is the way to go. Compare options on the BoatHire24 search page.

Safety and Rules: What You Need to Know

You must stay within the designated area: from Latchi harbour to the Akamas lighthouse, no further. You cannot go past the Cape Arnaoutis point because the currents are dangerous. Speed limit is 5 knots within 100 metres of the shore and in the harbour. No alcohol while driving. The operator will give you a VHF radio and a mobile phone number for the base. If you break down, call them and they send a rescue boat. It is free within the operating area. Do not anchor on seagrass beds; the fines are heavy (up to EUR 10,000). Stick to sand or rock bottoms. The Blue Lagoon has a sandy bottom, so that is safe. Always check the weather forecast before you go; if the wind is above 25 knots, the operator may cancel your booking.

Local Tips from the BoatHire24 Team

Bring a waterproof phone case. The spray from the boat can soak your pockets. Pack a dry bag for valuables. The best spot for a swim is the second cove past the Blue Lagoon, called Manolis Bay. It is quieter and has a small cave. For lunch, tie up at the Latchi waterfront and eat at one of the fish tavernas. The best one is To Ktimato, which has a dock for small boats. If you want a longer trip, consider a full-day hire and go to the Baths of Aphrodite, then to the Blue Lagoon, then back via the sea caves. That is about 6 hours of cruising and swimming. For more local secrets, check the BoatHire24 blog.

What to Do If You Have Never Driven a Boat

Do not worry. The boats are simple: push the throttle forward to go, turn the wheel to steer, pull the kill cord if you need to stop fast. The operator will let you practice in the harbour for five minutes before you head out. Keep the speed low until you are clear of the breakwater. Once you are in open water, you can open it up to 20 knots or so. The boats are stable and forgiving. If you feel nervous, take a skipper for the first hour. Most people get the hang of it in 10 minutes. The main thing is to watch the depth sounder; stay in water deeper than 2 metres to avoid hitting rocks. The Blue Lagoon is 3 to 5 metres deep, so it is safe.

Why Book Through BoatHire24 Instead of Direct

Direct booking with a local operator can be cheaper by EUR 10 to EUR 20, but you lose the flexibility. BoatHire24 offers free cancellation up to 48 hours before, a best-price guarantee, and a customer service line in English and Spanish. If the operator cancels on you, we find you an alternative boat or refund you in full. We also show you all the available boats in one place, so you can compare power, size, and price without visiting five websites. The BoatHire24 homepage has a search tool that filters by licence-free boats, location, and date. It takes 30 seconds to find your boat.

How the Latchi Speedboat Differs from a RIB Hire in Paphos

In Paphos you are limited to the harbour area and the coast towards Coral Bay. The water is often busy with tourist boats and jet skis. Latchi gives you direct access to the Akamas Peninsula, which is quieter and has more varied coastline. The boats in Latchi are typically newer because the operators here cater to the licence-free market specifically. In Paphos you might get an older hull with a smaller engine. For the same EUR 300 full-day price, you get a better boat and a better cruising ground in Latchi. BoatHire24 lists both locations, so you can compare directly on the search page.

Fuel Costs and How to Avoid Overpaying

Most Latchi operators charge fuel separately based on what you use. The boat has a fuel gauge, and they top it up before you leave. When you return, they fill it again and charge you the difference. A typical day of cruising at moderate speed uses 20 to 30 litres of unleaded petrol. At around EUR 1.50 per litre, that is EUR 30 to EUR 45. If you run the engine at full throttle all day, you might use 40 litres. Some operators offer a fuel-inclusive package for an extra EUR 50, which is usually not worth it unless you plan to race around. Ask at the desk before you book. BoatHire24 lists the fuel policy for each boat on the listing page.

What Happens if the Weather Turns Bad

The Mediterranean can change quickly. A flat calm morning can turn into a 30-knot wind by lunchtime. The operator monitors the forecast and will call you back if conditions become dangerous. You are expected to return to port immediately if the wind picks up above 20 knots. If you are caught out, the VHF radio is your lifeline. The rescue boat can reach any point in the Akamas area within 30 minutes. If the forecast is bad in the morning, the operator may cancel your booking. BoatHire24 offers a full refund in that case. Check the weather on the day from the BoatHire24 blog for links to reliable forecast sites.

How to Anchor Safely in the Blue Lagoon

The Blue Lagoon has a sandy bottom, which is good for anchoring. Drop the anchor when you are in about 4 metres of water. Let out enough chain so the boat does not swing into other boats. Do not tie up to other boats; that causes damage and arguments. If you are not confident, anchor near the shore in waist-deep water and use the boat's ladder to get in and out. The current is minimal, so you will not drift far. Do not anchor on the rocky areas near the cliffs; the anchor will get stuck. The operator will show you a simple knot for the anchor line. Practice it once and you will be fine.

Where to Eat on the Water in Latchi

You can bring your own food and eat on the boat, but the real treat is the fish tavernas on the Latchi waterfront. Most have small docks where you can tie up for free if you eat there. The best is To Ktimato, which serves grilled octopus and fresh sea bass. A meal for two with wine costs around EUR 50. Another option is the restaurant at the Baths of Aphrodite, which has a jetty and serves meze plates. If you want a beach picnic, buy supplies at the Latchi supermarket before you leave. The boat has a small cooler under the seat. Avoid eating on the boat in the Blue Lagoon; the seagulls will mob you.

What to Do with Kids on a Licence-Free Speedboat

Kids love the speed and the swimming stops. The boats have life jackets in sizes for children from about 15 kg upwards. Keep the speed under 15 knots when kids are on board. Stop at the shallow part of the Blue Lagoon where the water is only 1.5 metres deep. Let them jump off the side of the boat with a life jacket on. The operator can provide a small inflatable ring if you ask. Do not let them sit on the bow while the boat is moving; that is dangerous and illegal. The best age is 6 and up. Younger children may get bored after an hour. Bring a waterproof toy or a bucket for them to play with.

How to Get the Best Price on a Latchi Speedboat Rental

Book midweek for the lowest price. Monday to Thursday is typically 20% cheaper than Friday to Sunday. Book at least a week in advance to secure the best boat. Last-minute bookings may only have older boats left. Half-day rentals are cheaper per hour than full-day, but you lose the ability to explore the far coves. If you are on a tight budget, share with another couple. The boat holds up to six people, so splitting the EUR 300 full-day cost four ways is EUR 75 each. That is cheaper than a taxi tour. BoatHire24 shows the best prices for each date on the homepage. Compare three or four options before you book.

What Not to Do on a Licence-Free Speedboat

Do not try to jump the boat's wake. Do not go close to the cliffs; the rocks are sharp and the water is shallow near the base. Do not drink alcohol and drive; the police patrol the Akamas area and will breathalyse you. Do not leave the engine running while people are swimming near the prop. Do not tie up to a mooring buoy that is not marked as public; they are private and expensive to replace. Do not ignore the no-go zones marked on the map. The fines for entering the turtle nesting area are EUR 500. Do not take the boat out of the designated area; the insurance is void beyond the Akamas lighthouse. Follow these rules and you will have a trouble-free day.

title: Latchi Fishing Charter: Deep Sea Boat Hire Cyprus
metaDescription: Book a Latchi fishing charter on BoatHire24. Deep sea boat hire Cyprus with skipper, rods, bait included. Compare boats for 6-12 guests from EUR 450.
h1: Latchi Fishing Charter: Deep Sea Boat Hire Cyprus
intro:
You want a Latchi fishing charter. You want to get out on the deep blue off Cyprus, haul in something big, and not deal with the hassle of owning a boat or finding a crew. BoatHire24 lets you book a private fishing trip from Latchi harbour with a licensed skipper, all the gear, and a boat that suits your group. No hidden extras, no messing about.

Latchi sits on the northwest coast of Cyprus, a quiet fishing village turned launch point for serious anglers. The waters here drop off fast into deep channels where tuna, dorado, and amberjack run. You can book a half-day or full-day charter, motor yacht or RIB, with everything included except your lunch and your suncream. Prices start from around EUR 450 for a half-day for up to 6 people.
bodyHtml:
What a Latchi Fishing Charter Includes

Every Latchi fishing charter on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local grounds. He handles the navigation, the bait, and the rods. You just turn up, cast, and reel. The standard package includes trolling and bottom fishing gear, live or artificial bait, ice boxes for your catch, and safety equipment. Most boats have a cabin with a toilet and a small galley for drinks. You can bring your own food and booze, or ask the skipper to arrange a lunch stop at a beach taverna. Fuel is included in the price, so no surprises . Catch and release is encouraged for protected species, but you can keep what you catch within local size limits.

Why Latchi for Deep Sea Fishing

Latchi is not just another marina. It is the gateway to the Akamas Peninsula, a protected area where the coast is rugged and the water is clear. The seabed drops to 200 metres within a couple of miles offshore, which means pelagic fish come close. You can target bluefin tuna, skipjack, mahi-mahi, and barracuda. In summer, the surface temperature hits 26 degrees C, so the fish are active and feeding. Latchi also has the advantage of being less crowded than Paphos or Limassol. You get more time fishing and less time queuing at the fuel dock.

Boat Options for Your Latchi Fishing Charter

You have a few choices. The most common is a 7-9 metre motor yacht, usually a Fairline or Sunseeker, with twin outboards. These boats cruise at 18-22 knots and have a range of 50-80 nautical miles. They are stable enough for trolling and have a fighting chair on the aft deck. For a faster, more adrenaline-fuelled trip, you can book a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with a single 250hp engine. These hit 35-40 knots and get you to the fishing grounds in 15 minutes. They are less stable in a swell but more manoeuvrable. If you have a larger group, up to 12 people, you can charter a catamaran or a sailing yacht with fishing gear. These are slower but offer more deck space and comfort. All boats are licensed for commercial charter and have up-to-date safety certificates.

Latchi Fishing Charter Pricing Guidance

Prices vary by boat size, duration, and season. A half-day charter (4 hours) for up to 6 people on a standard motor yacht starts from around EUR 450. A full day (8 hours) runs from EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. RIBs are slightly cheaper, from EUR 350 for half a day. Catamarans and larger yachts for 10-12 guests cost from EUR 1,500 for a full day. These prices include the skipper, fuel, rods, reels, bait, and ice. They do not include food, drinks, or gratuities. You can book a sunset fishing trip for EUR 600, which combines a couple of hours of fishing with a cruise along the coast. For exact pricing on a specific boat, you need to send an enquiry via BoatHire24.

Best Season for Latchi Fishing Charters

The fishing season runs from April to November. The peak is June to September, when the water is warmest and the fish are most active. In April and May, you get good catches of amberjack and barracuda. June to August is prime time for tuna and dorado. September and October see the arrival of larger tuna and the start of the swordfish season. November is quieter but still fishable, especially for bottom fishing. Avoid December to March, when the weather is rough and many boats are laid up. You can still find a few operators running half-day trips, but the catch rate drops significantly.

How to Book a Latchi Fishing Charter on BoatHire24

Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter Latchi as your destination. Choose your date and group size. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Each listing shows the boat type, length, engine power, and included equipment. You can filter by price, duration, or boat type. Once you find a boat you like, click the booking button. You will need to provide your contact details and a deposit of 30% to confirm. The balance is paid on the day of the charter, directly to the skipper. You can also search all fishing charters in Cyprus to compare options. If you have questions, use the enquiry form on each listing page.

Who Is a Latchi Fishing Charter For

These charters suit anyone who wants a private fishing experience without the commitment of boat ownership. They are ideal for small groups of friends, families with older children (8+), or corporate outings. The skipper tailors the trip to your skill level, so beginners are welcome. You do not need a fishing licence; the boat’s commercial licence covers you. If you are a serious angler, you can request specific techniques such as jigging, trolling, or live baiting. The boats have fish finders and GPS, so you spend more time fishing and less time searching. Non-fishing guests can come along for the ride and enjoy the scenery, the sun, and the occasional dolphin sighting.

What to Bring on Your Latchi Fishing Charter

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, sunglasses, and a light jacket for the wind. Wear non-slip shoes. The boat will have a cooler for your drinks and food. You can bring your own tackle if you prefer, but the boat supplies all the gear. Bring a camera or phone in a waterproof case. If you want to keep your catch, bring a cool box with ice for the journey home. The skipper can clean and fillet the fish for you. Do not bring glass bottles, as they are a hazard on deck. Seasickness tablets are a good idea if you are prone. Take them an hour before departure.

Local Attractions Near Latchi

Latchi itself has a small harbour with a few tavernas and a fish market. You can walk along the promenade to the Blue Lagoon, a popular swimming spot. The nearby town of Polis has a traditional Cypriot square with cafes and shops. The Akamas Peninsula is a 15-minute drive away, with hiking trails and the Baths of Aphrodite. If you are staying in Paphos, Latchi is a 40-minute drive north. You can combine your fishing charter with a visit to the archaeological sites at Kato Paphos or the Paphos Castle. For a longer trip, the Troodos Mountains are an hour’s drive inland.

Safety and Cancellation Policy

All boats on BoatHire24 are licensed by the Cyprus Department of Merchant Shipping. They carry life jackets, flares, a first aid kit, and a VHF radio. The skipper holds a professional captain’s licence and a first aid certificate. Weather cancellations are free. If the skipper decides the sea conditions are unsafe, you get a full refund or a rescheduled date. If you cancel more than 48 hours before departure, you get a full refund minus the booking fee. Cancellations within 48 hours forfeit the deposit. We recommend travel insurance that covers trip cancellation. For more tips, read our boat hire blog.

Deep Sea Species You Can Target from Latchi

The waters off Latchi hold a mix of pelagic and reef fish. In summer, you can chase bluefin tuna weighing 20-50 kg, with occasional specimens over 100 kg. Skipjack tuna are more common and run 3-8 kg. Mahi-mahi (dorado) appear from June, often near floating debris. Barracuda are year-round, usually 2-5 kg. Amberjack and greater amberjack are caught on bottom rigs near the 50-metre contour. Dentex, red snapper, and grouper live on the deeper wrecks and rocky reefs. Swordfish are a night-time target from August to October, using specialised gear. The skipper will brief you on the best techniques for the day's conditions. You can also try light tackle for smaller species like mackerel, scad, and bogue, which make good bait or a light meal.

Typical Itinerary for a Latchi Fishing Charter

A half-day charter usually starts at 0800 or 1400. You meet at Latchi Harbour, board the boat, and receive a safety briefing. The skipper motors out of the harbour, past the small beach at Polis, and heads west towards the Akamas Peninsula. The first stop is often a shallow reef at 20 metres depth for bottom fishing. After 30-45 minutes, you move to deeper water for trolling. The skipper sets up the outriggers and puts out lures or live bait. You troll at 6-8 knots along the edge of the drop-off. If you hook a tuna, the fight can last 15-30 minutes. The skipper will coach you on rod angle and reeling technique. After a few hours, you head back, with the option to stop for a swim at the Blue Lagoon if time allows. A full-day charter includes a longer run to the deeper grounds 10-15 nautical miles offshore, with a lunch break at a quiet cove.

RIB Fishing Charters: Speed and Agility

For a fast, focused trip, a RIB is a good choice. These boats are 6-8 metres long with a single 250-300hp outboard. They plane at 30 knots and can reach 40 knots in calm conditions. The ride is bumpier than a monohull, but you get to the fishing grounds in 10-15 minutes instead of 30. RIBs are ideal for trolling for tuna and mahi-mahi because you can quickly change position. They have less deck space, so you are limited to 4-6 anglers. The skipper sits at the centre console, and you stand or sit on bench seats. RIB charters cost from EUR 350 for half a day and EUR 600 for a full day. They are popular with younger groups and experienced anglers who want maximum fishing time. You need to be comfortable with a wet ride if the sea is choppy.

Catamaran Fishing Charters for Groups

If you have 8-12 people, a catamaran is the most comfortable option. These boats are 10-15 metres long with a wide beam, so they are stable at anchor and while trolling. They have a large shaded deck, a cabin with air conditioning, and a galley. The skipper can set up multiple fishing rods on the aft deck. Catamarans are slower than monohulls, cruising at 10-12 knots, so the run to the grounds takes longer. But you can fish while moving, trolling at 5-7 knots. Catamarans are also good for families with children, as there is more room to move around. A full-day charter for 10 guests costs from EUR 1,500. You can also book a half-day sunset trip that combines fishing with a cruise along the coast. The skipper will clean and bag your catch at the end of the trip.

Night Fishing Charters from Latchi

Night fishing is a different experience. The water is calmer, the air is cooler, and the fish feed differently. Night trips target swordfish, which are caught on drifting rigs with squid or mackerel bait. You also catch red snapper, grouper, and other bottom fish that are more active after dark. The boat uses powerful floodlights to attract baitfish, which in turn attract predators. Night charters usually run from 1900 to 2300 or 2000 to 0100. They cost from EUR 600 for a half-night trip. You need to bring warm clothing, as the temperature drops 5-10 degrees C after sunset. The skipper provides glow sticks and special lights for your rod tips. Night fishing is less popular, so you often have the sea to yourself. It is a good option if you want to avoid the midday sun.

Fishing Techniques Used on Latchi Charters

The skipper adapts the technique to the target species and conditions. Trolling is the most common method for pelagic fish. The boat drags lures or natural bait behind it at a steady speed. You use heavy rods with 30-50 lb test line and a fighting . Bottom fishing involves anchoring or drifting over a reef or wreck. You use a weighted rig with a single hook and a piece of squid or fish. Jigging is a vertical technique where you drop a metal lure to the bottom and jerk it up and down. This works for amberjack and dentex. Live baiting uses small fish caught on site, hooked through the nose, and drifted in the current. This is effective for tuna and mahi-mahi. The skipper will teach you the basics, so no experience is needed.

What to Do with Your Catch

You can keep your catch within the legal limits. The skipper will gut and fillet the fish on the boat or at the harbour. You can take it to a local taverna in Latchi or Polis, where they will cook it for you for a small fee. The fish market in Latchi sells fresh catch, but yours will be fresher. If you are staying in a villa or apartment with a kitchen, you can cook it yourself. Popular recipes include grilled tuna steaks with lemon and oregano, fried red snapper, and mahi-mahi ceviche. For larger fish like swordfish, ask the skipper to cut steaks. If you are flying home, you can pack frozen fillets in a cool box as checked luggage, but check with your airline first. Catch and release is encouraged for marlin, sailfish, and other billfish, which are rare but occasionally caught.

Combining a Fishing Charter with a Coastal Cruise

Many charters offer a hybrid trip. You spend 2-3 hours fishing, then cruise along the Akamas coastline. You can anchor at the Blue Lagoon for a swim, snorkel over the reefs, or explore the sea caves near the Baths of Aphrodite. The skipper can drop you at a beach taverna for lunch, then pick you up later. This is a good option if you have non-fishing guests in your group. The cost is the same as a standard charter, but you need to specify the itinerary when booking. The boats have snorkelling gear, towels, and a ladder for easy access to the water. You can also ask for a stop at the wreck of the MS Zenobia, a ferry that sank off Larnaca, but that is a 2-hour cruise from Latchi, so it requires a full-day charter.

Accessing Latchi from Other Cyprus Resorts

Latchi is on the northwest coast, 40 minutes by car from Paphos. If you are staying in Limassol, the drive is 1 hour 30 minutes. From Nicosia, it is 2 hours. There is a car park at the harbour, free for charter guests. You can also take a taxi from Paphos for around EUR 50 each way. If you are in Ayia Napa or Protaras, Latchi is a 2-hour 30-minute drive, so a full-day charter is more practical. Some guests combine a fishing charter with a stay in Polis, which has several hotels and villas. The harbour has a small kiosk where you buy bait and ice, and a cafe for coffee before departure. You can also rent a car in Paphos or Limassol to explore the area.

Booking Tips for Your Latchi Fishing Charter

Book at least a week in advance during peak season (June to September). Popular boats sell out, especially on weekends. When you enquire, tell the skipper your target species and experience level. If you want to keep the catch, confirm that the boat has a fish box and that the skipper will clean it. Check the cancellation policy before paying the deposit. Some skippers require 48 hours' notice for a full refund, others 72 hours. Ask about the maximum group size and whether non-fishing guests are charged the same rate. Most boats charge per person, not per rod. If you have a group of 6, you pay the same price whether you all fish or not. You can also ask about discounts for repeat bookings or multi-day charters. For more advice, read our boat hire blog for Cyprus fishing tips.

title: Latchi Private Boat Hire: Exclusive Cyprus Rentals
metaDescription: Book Latchi private boat hire with a licensed skipper. Explore Cyprus coves, Blue Lagoon, and Akamas from EUR 350. Instant online booking, no hidden fees.
h1: Latchi Private Boat Hire: Exclusive Cyprus Rentals
intro:
If you want to explore the Cyprus coast without the crowds, Latchi private boat hire is your best bet. You get a whole boat to yourself, a licensed skipper who knows the hidden spots, and zero queuing for public ferries. Think of it as having your own floating base for the day, one that can take you to the Blue Lagoon, the sea caves of Akamas, or a quiet cove only reachable by water.

Latchi harbour, just north of Paphos, is the launch point for most of these trips. It is a working fishing port turned tourist hub, so you get fresh seafood tavernas on the waterfront and a choice of motor yachts, sailing yachts, catamarans, and RIBs. Every charter includes a skipper, fuel, and insurance. You just pick the boat, pick the route, and turn up.

Prices start from around EUR 350 for a half-day on a small motorboat and go up to EUR 1,200 for a full-day catamaran for eight people. No hidden fees, no surprise charges. You book online, pay a deposit, and the rest on the day. Simple.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Latchi Private Boat Hire

When you book a private boat in Latchi, the package is straightforward. You get the vessel for an agreed time, usually half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours). A licensed skipper is included, so you do not need a boating licence or any experience. Fuel is covered, as is insurance. Most boats come with a cooler box, ice, and basic safety equipment. Some larger yachts have a sound system, a small kitchen, and a toilet. You can bring your own food and drink, or ask the charter company to arrange catering. Snorkelling gear is often provided free of charge. The skipper will handle the navigation, mooring, and any questions you have about the area. You just sit back and enjoy.

Why Choose Latchi for a Private Boat Rental

Latchi is a better base than Paphos or Limassol for a few reasons. First, it is closer to the Akamas Peninsula, which is the most scenic stretch of coast in western Cyprus. The Blue Lagoon, the sea caves, and the Baths of Aphrodite are all a short cruise away. Second, the harbour is smaller and less busy, so you spend less time manoeuvring out of the marina and more time on the water. Third, the waterfront has a relaxed vibe, with fish restaurants and a few bars, but no high-rise hotels or nightclubs. If you want a quiet day on the sea with good food afterwards, Latchi works.

Boat Types Available for Private Hire in Latchi

You have a few options depending on your group size and what you want to do. Motor yachts from 8 to 15 metres are the most common, good for cruising at 20-25 knots and covering distance to the Blue Lagoon or as far as Coral Bay. Catamarans are more stable and have more deck space, ideal for families with kids or anyone prone to seasickness. Sailing yachts are slower but quieter, and you can help with the sails if you want. RIBs and speedboats are faster, up to 40 knots, and better for a thrill ride or a short trip to a nearby cove. A few companies also offer licence-free day boats, which are simple motorboats under 30hp that you can drive without a licence, but these are less common for private hire because the skipper is included anyway.

Popular Routes from Latchi Harbour

The most popular route is north to the Blue Lagoon, a sheltered bay with turquoise water about 20 minutes from Latchi. You anchor there for a swim, maybe see a few turtles. From there, you can go further into the Akamas Peninsula to the sea caves, which are arches and tunnels in the limestone cliffs. Another option is to head south past the Baths of Aphrodite and along the coast towards Paphos, stopping at quiet beaches like Lara Bay, which is a turtle nesting site. If you have a full day, you can go all the way to the shipwreck of the MV Edro III near Polis, or cross to the western side of the Akamas for a completely isolated swim stop. The skipper will suggest a route based on wind and sea conditions.

Pricing Guidance for Latchi Private Boat Hire

Prices vary by boat size, duration, and season. For a half-day (4 hours) on a 7-metre motorboat for up to 6 people, expect to pay from around EUR 350. For a full-day on a 10-metre motor yacht for 8-10 people, the price is typically EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. Catamarans are more expensive, from EUR 1,000 for a half-day and EUR 1,500 for a full-day. Sailing yachts are similar to motor yachts, around EUR 400-600 for a half-day. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper but smaller, from EUR 250 for a 2-hour trip. All prices include skipper, fuel, and insurance. You pay a 30-50% deposit online and the rest in cash or card on the day. No hidden extras.

Best Time of Year for a Private Boat Trip from Latchi

The season runs from April to October, with the best months being June, July, August, and September. In July and August, air temperatures hit 35 degrees C and sea temperatures are around 27 degrees C, perfect for swimming. The water is calmest in the morning before the meltemi wind picks up. May and October are cooler, around 25 degrees C air temperature, but still fine for a boat trip. The sea can be a bit choppier in October. Winter charters are rare because the weather is unpredictable and most boats are out of the water for maintenance. If you want to avoid the peak crowds, June and September are the sweet spots.

How to Book Latchi Private Boat Hire Online

Booking is done through BoatHire24 where you can compare boats from multiple local operators. You choose your date, group size, and preferred boat type, then see available options with prices and photos. Select a boat, pay the deposit online, and receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and meeting point at Latchi harbour. On the day, you meet the skipper at the agreed time, sign a waiver, and pay the balance. The whole process takes about 10 minutes. You can also use the search function to filter by price, capacity, or boat type. For more tips on choosing a boat, check the blog.

Who Is Private Boat Hire in Latchi For

Private boat hire suits couples, families, small groups of friends, and even solo travellers who want a bespoke experience. It is not for budget backpackers because the cost per person is higher than a group tour. But if you want privacy, flexibility, and the ability to stop wherever you like, it is worth the extra. Families with young children like the catamarans because they are stable and have shaded areas. Groups of friends often go for the motor yachts with a sound system and a cooler full of drinks. Couples sometimes book a sailing yacht for a romantic sunset cruise. If you are celebrating a birthday, anniversary, or a special occasion, you can ask the charter company to arrange decorations, a cake, or a photographer.

What to Bring on Your Private Boat Trip

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses. The Cyprus sun is strong even in spring and autumn. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful because the sea breeze can feel cool when the boat is moving. If you plan to snorkel, the boat usually provides masks and fins, but you can bring your own. Food and drink are not included, so bring a picnic or order from a local deli. Most boats have a cooler with ice, but check in advance. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness pill an hour before departure. The skipper will have a first aid kit, but bring any personal medication.

Safety and Skipper Qualifications

All skippers on BoatHire24 hold a valid Cyprus Boatmaster licence or equivalent. They know the local waters, the weather patterns, and the emergency procedures. The boats are inspected annually and carry life jackets, a VHF radio, flares, and a fire extinguisher. The skipper will give a safety briefing at the start of the trip. If the weather turns bad, the skipper has the authority to change the route or cancel the trip for safety. In that case, you get a full refund or a rescheduled date. You are not expected to know anything about boats; the skipper handles everything.

Nearby Attractions and Things to Do After Your Boat Trip

After your boat trip, Latchi has a few good options. The harbourfront has tavernas serving grilled fish, calamari, and meze. Try the octopus or the sea bass. A short walk away is the Baths of Aphrodite, a natural grotto with a freshwater spring, though it is more of a photo stop than a swimming spot. The Akamas Peninsula has hiking trails if you want to stretch your legs. Polis, the nearest town, has a small square with cafes and a few shops. If you have a car, you can drive to the Paphos archaeological park or the Tombs of the Kings, both about 40 minutes south.

Frequently Asked Questions About Latchi Private Boat Hire

How Latchi Compares to Paphos and Limassol for Private Boat Hire

Paphos harbour is bigger and busier, with more charter companies, but it adds 20-30 minutes cruising time to reach the Akamas Peninsula. Limassol is even further, a 90-minute motor to the Blue Lagoon, so you lose a chunk of your charter time just getting there and back. Latchi sits right at the edge of the Akamas, so you are on site within 10 minutes of leaving the harbour. The water around Latchi is also clearer because there is less commercial traffic. If you are staying in Paphos or Limassol, it is worth the 30-40 minute drive north to Latchi for a better day out. The parking at Latchi harbour is free and usually has space, unlike Paphos where you pay EUR 5-10 per day.

What the Blue Lagoon Actually Looks Like in Peak Season

The Blue Lagoon is a large bay with shallow, turquoise water, but in July and August it gets crowded. You will see 20-30 boats anchored there by midday, including party boats with loud music. The skipper can take you to a quieter spot nearby, such as the smaller cove at Fontana Amorosa or the stretch of coast between the lagoon and the sea caves. These spots have the same water colour but fewer people. If you want the classic photo of the Blue Lagoon without the crowds, go early, departing Latchi at 8:30 or 9:00. You will have the place mostly to yourself until 10:30 when the first group tours arrive. The water temperature in summer is 26-28 degrees C, so you can stay in for hours.

How the Meltemi Wind Affects Your Boat Trip

The meltemi is a northwesterly wind that blows across Cyprus from June to September, strongest in the afternoons. In Latchi, it usually picks up around 13:00 and can reach 20-25 knots, which makes the sea choppy on the exposed west coast of the Akamas. The skipper will plan the route to avoid the worst of it, keeping the boat in sheltered bays or heading south towards Paphos where the wind is lighter. Morning charters are generally smoother. If you book a half-day in the afternoon, expect a bumpier ride, especially on a small RIB or speedboat. Catamarans handle the chop better because of their twin hulls. The meltemi is predictable, so your skipper will not be caught off guard.

What Happens if You Want to Swim but the Sea Is Rough

If the wind kicks up and the anchor drags, the skipper will find a lee shore, a spot where the land blocks the wind. The Akamas has many small coves that offer shelter, such as the bay near the Baths of Aphrodite or the inlet at Lara Bay. These spots have calmer water even on a windy afternoon. The skipper will also check the forecast before departure and may suggest a different route if the wind is expected to be strong. You will still get a swim stop, just maybe not at the Blue Lagoon. If the conditions are truly unsafe, the skipper will cancel the trip, and you get a full refund. This happens maybe 5-10 days per season.

How to Choose Between a Motor Yacht and a Catamaran in Latchi

A motor yacht is faster, so you can cover more distance in a half-day trip. For example, you can go from Latchi to the Blue Lagoon, then to the sea caves, and still have time for a swim stop. A catamaran is slower, around 8-12 knots, but it has more deck space, a trampoline net at the front, and usually a shaded cockpit. If your group has 6 or more people, a catamaran gives everyone room to spread out. If you want to sunbathe, the trampoline is a good spot. If you want to get to a specific destination quickly, go with a motor yacht. Catamarans are also more stable at anchor, so if you plan to spend a lot of time swimming or eating on board, they are a better choice.

What the Skipper Does During Your Charter

The skipper drives the boat, navigates, and handles the mooring. They also act as a guide, pointing out landmarks like the sea caves, the Baths of Aphrodite, and the turtle nesting beaches. They will not cook or serve food, but they can help set up the cooler and clean up at the end. If you want to stop for a swim, the skipper finds a good spot, drops the anchor, and waits. If you want to try water sports like waterskiing or paddleboarding, some boats have equipment available for an extra fee. The skipper speaks English and Greek, and they know the local restaurants in Latchi if you want a recommendation for dinner after the trip.

How to Combine Latchi Boat Hire with a Stay in Polis or Latchi

Latchi village has a handful of apartments and villas within walking distance of the harbour. Polis, 3 km inland, has more accommodation options, including hotels like the Polis 1900 and the Aphrodite Beach Hotel. If you stay in Latchi, you can walk to the boat in 5 minutes. If you stay in Polis, it is a 5-minute drive or a 20-minute walk. The area also has a few agrotourism farms where you can stay in traditional stone houses. Booking a private boat hire from Latchi works well as a one-day activity during a longer holiday in the Paphos region. You can spend the morning on the water and the afternoon exploring the Akamas on foot or by quad bike.

What to Do if the Boat Trip Is Cancelled Due to Weather

If the skipper cancels, you get a full refund or a rescheduled date. If you cancel more than 48 hours before departure, you usually get a 50-70% refund depending on the operator. Within 48 hours, refunds are rare unless the weather is bad. To avoid disappointment, check the forecast a few days ahead and book a flexible date if possible. June and September have fewer cancellations than July and August because the meltemi is less intense. If you are on a tight schedule, consider booking a catamaran, which can operate in slightly rougher conditions than a small motorboat. The blog has more tips on dealing with weather cancellations.

How Latchi Private Boat Hire Handles Large Groups and Events

For groups of 12 or more, you need a catamaran or a large motor yacht. Some catamarans in Latchi carry up to 20 passengers, but check the licence limits because exceeding the capacity is illegal. For events like a birthday or a corporate outing, you can arrange catering, a DJ, or a photographer through the charter company. The cost goes up, from around EUR 2,000 for a full-day catamaran with catering for 15 people. The skipper will still be there to manage the boat, but you can bring your own playlist and decorations. The harbour in Latchi has a few shops where you can buy balloons or banners in advance.

title: Mandelieu Cannes Boat Hire: Rent a Boat in France
metaDescription: Looking for Mandelieu Cannes boat hire? Rent a boat with a skipper on the French Riviera. Compare motor yachts, catamarans and RIBs from EUR 350. Book online.
h1: Mandelieu Cannes Boat Hire: Rent a Boat on the French Riviera
intro:
You want to hire a boat in Mandelieu or Cannes, but you don't want the hassle of a licence, insurance or fuel calculations. We get it. BoatHire24 connects you with skippered boats in the French Riviera, from Mandelieu-La Napoule to Cannes and the Lérins Islands. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you just turn up, relax and enjoy the Côte d'Azur sun.

Mandelieu is the quieter, less flashy neighbour of Cannes, but its marina is a gateway to the same turquoise waters. You can cruise to the Île Sainte-Marguerite, anchor off the Croisette, or head west to the Esterel massif for dramatic red-rock coves. Prices start from around EUR 350 for a half-day on a RIB, up to EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a 40-foot motor yacht. All boats are inspected for safety, and the skipper knows the local anchor spots.

This page covers everything you need to know about boat hire in Mandelieu and Cannes: what you get, which ports to depart from, boat options, pricing, seasons, how to book and who this is for. No fluff, just the details that matter for your day on the water.
bodyHtml:
What’s Included in Your Mandelieu Cannes Boat Hire

When you book through BoatHire24, the price includes the boat, the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and basic safety equipment. The skipper handles navigation, mooring and any local knowledge, like which restaurant has the best bouillabaisse for a lunch stop. You do not need a boating licence or any prior experience. You just need to bring sunscreen, swimwear and a good attitude.

Most charters also include a cooler with ice, a Bluetooth speaker and snorkelling masks. Some larger yachts have a stand-up paddleboard or a seabob. Check the individual listing for specifics. What is not included is food and drink, unless you book a catered option. You can bring your own picnic or order from the skipper’s recommended suppliers. Gratuity for the skipper is discretionary, usually 10-15 percent if you are happy.

All boats are insured and maintained to French maritime standards. The skipper is a licensed professional, often with years of local experience. You are in safe hands, even if the Mistral wind picks up.

Departure Ports: Mandelieu, Cannes and Beyond

The primary departure port for this service is Mandelieu-La Napoule, a modern marina at the mouth of the Siagne river. It is less crowded than Cannes Vieux Port, so boarding is quick and parking is easier. From here, you are 15 minutes from the Lérins Islands and 20 minutes from the Cannes Croisette.

If you prefer to start from Cannes, we also have boats departing from Cannes Vieux Port (the old port) and Port Pierre Canto. These are closer to the Palais des Festivals and the luxury hotels, but parking is expensive and traffic can be heavy. We recommend Mandelieu for a stress-free start, unless you are staying in central Cannes.

Other nearby departure ports include Théoule-sur-Mer (west of Mandelieu) and Golfe-Juan (east of Cannes). These are available on request for certain boats. The skipper will meet you at the dock, help you aboard and give a brief safety talk before casting off.

Boat Options: Motor Yachts, Catamarans, RIBs and More

Your choice of boat depends on your group size, budget and preferred vibe. For a couple or a small group of up to six, a RIB or speedboat is the most affordable and fun option. You get the wind in your hair and can zip into shallow coves that bigger yachts cannot reach. Prices start from around EUR 350 for a half day.

For a family or group of up to 12, a motor yacht is the standard choice. These range from 30 to 50 feet, with a flybridge, a saloon, a galley and a sun pad at the bow. You can lounge, swim and eat in comfort. Half-day prices run from EUR 800 to EUR 1,500. A full day is roughly double.

Catamarans are more stable and spacious, ideal if anyone in your group gets seasick. They have a wide deck, a trampoline net at the front and plenty of shade. A 40-foot catamaran sleeps up to 12 for a day charter, with prices from EUR 1,200 for a half day. Sailing yachts are available too, but they are slower and require more wind. If you want a proper sailing experience, book a monohull from around EUR 600 for a half day.

For a luxury celebration, consider a superyacht or a prestige motor yacht over 60 feet. These come with a crew of two or three, a full galley and amenities like a jacuzzi. Prices are on request, but expect upwards of EUR 3,000 for a half day.

Pricing Guidance: What You Actually Pay

Boat hire prices on the French Riviera vary by season, boat size and duration. Here is a realistic range for Mandelieu and Cannes in 2025:

  • RIB or speedboat (up to 6 pax): half day from EUR 350, full day from EUR 600
  • Motor yacht 30-40 ft (up to 10 pax): half day EUR 800-1,200, full day EUR 1,500-2,200
  • Motor yacht 40-50 ft (up to 12 pax): half day EUR 1,200-1,800, full day EUR 2,200-3,500
  • Catamaran 40-50 ft (up to 12 pax): half day EUR 1,200-1,800, full day EUR 2,200-3,500
  • Sailing yacht 35-45 ft (up to 8 pax): half day EUR 600-1,000, full day EUR 1,000-1,800
  • Superyacht or prestige (up to 20 pax): price on request, typically from EUR 3,000 half day

These prices include the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary (usually up to 4-5 hours cruising), insurance and VAT. Extras like watersports equipment, catering or extra hours are charged separately. Always confirm the total before booking. The final price is usually quoted in euros.

Best Time to Hire a Boat in Mandelieu Cannes

The boating season runs from April to October, with the peak in July and August. June and September offer the best balance of warm weather, calm seas and fewer crowds. Water temperatures in summer reach 24-26 degrees C, perfect for swimming. In April and October, you might need a light jacket on the water, but the light is beautiful and the anchorages are quiet.

July and August are hot (30-35 degrees C) and busy. You will share the water with dozens of other boats, especially around the Lérins Islands. Book well in advance, at least two weeks ahead. For a more relaxed experience, aim for a weekday charter or a morning departure.

Wind is a factor. The Mistral can blow from the north-west, making the sea choppy, especially in the Golfe de la Napoule. Your skipper will check the forecast and may suggest a sheltered route or a different departure time. Rarely, a charter is cancelled due to unsafe conditions. In that case, you get a full refund or a reschedule.

How to Book Your Boat Hire in Mandelieu Cannes

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24 and use the search filters to select Mandelieu or Cannes as the departure port. Choose your date, group size and preferred boat type. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs and the skipper’s profile. Read the description carefully, especially the maximum passenger number and any restrictions (no pets, no parties, etc.).

Once you find a boat you like, click “Book Now”. You will pay a deposit of 30-50 percent to secure the date. The balance is due on the day of the charter, usually in cash or by card on board. You receive a confirmation email with the meeting point and the skipper’s contact details. You can also message the skipper directly through the platform for any special requests.

If you need help choosing, use the search page to compare multiple boats side by side. Or read our blog for tips on itineraries, packing and local restaurants.

Who Is Mandelieu Cannes Boat Hire For?

This service is for anyone who wants to experience the French Riviera from the water without the stress of owning or operating a boat. It is perfect for couples celebrating an anniversary, families with children (all boats have life jackets for kids), groups of friends on holiday, or corporate clients hosting a client event. It is also great for photographers, wedding proposals or just a day of sunbathing and swimming.

If you are a seasoned sailor who wants to charter a bareboat (without skipper), this is not the right service. We only offer skippered charters. For licence-free boat hire (small boats under 6 hp), check the local rental offices in Mandelieu port, but those are limited to calm inland waters.

If you have a large group (over 12), we can arrange multiple boats or a superyacht. Contact us through the website for a custom quote.

Popular Itineraries from Mandelieu and Cannes

Most charters follow one of three routes, depending on your preferences and the weather.

Route 1: Lérins Islands, Depart Mandelieu, cruise past Cannes to the Île Sainte-Marguerite. Anchor in the bay near the Fort Royal (where the Man in the Iron Mask was held). Swim, snorkel, have lunch. Then cross to the smaller Île Saint-Honorat, home to a monastery and a vineyard. Return via the Cannes Croisette for a view of the hotels. Duration: 4-6 hours.

Route 2: Esterel Coast, Head west from Mandelieu towards Théoule and the Corniche d’Or. The red porphyry cliffs plunge into the sea, creating hidden coves like Calanque du Maupas and Calanque du Petit Caneiret. Anchor for a swim, then continue to the village of Le Trayas. This route is quieter and more scenic. Duration: 4-5 hours.

Route 3: Golfe-Juan and Juan-les-Pins, East from Cannes, past the Cap d’Antibes to the sandy beaches of Juan-les-Pins. Your skipper will suggest the best route based on the wind and your interests. You can also request a custom itinerary, like a sunset cruise or a transfer to a specific beach restaurant.

What to Bring and What to Expect

Pack light: swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses with a strap, and a light jacket or windbreaker. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The skipper will have a first-aid kit, but bring any personal medication.

The skipper will provide drinking water.

On the day, arrive 15 minutes early at the meeting point. The skipper will greet you, show you the boat and give a safety briefing. You will sign a liability waiver. Then you are off. bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

When you book a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter through BoatHire24, you get a fully crewed boat with a licensed skipper as standard. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety. Fuel is usually included in the price for half-day and full-day charters, but check the listing details because some operators charge extra for long distances. You also get a welcome pack with water, soft drinks, and sometimes a bottle of local rosé. Snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and a Bluetooth speaker are common extras. What you do not get is a meal unless you upgrade to a catering option. You can bring your own food or ask the charter company to arrange a catered lunch from a local traiteur. Most boats have a fridge, a galley, and a shaded cockpit. The skipper will recommend a restaurant onshore if you want to stop for lunch at a port like Golfe Juan or Théoule-sur-Mer.

Departure Ports for Your Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

Your Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter can start from several ports along the French Riviera. The most popular is Cannes Vieux Port, right in the heart of the city, close to the Palais des Festivals and the luxury boutiques. You can also depart from Port Pierre Canto, which is a bit quieter and closer to the Croisette. If you are staying in Mandelieu itself, the La Napoule port is a good option, with easy parking and direct access to the Esterel coast. Other departure points include Golfe Juan, near Juan-les-Pins, and Port Vauban in Antibes if you want a longer trip. Each port has its own vibe. Cannes is glamorous and busy. Mandelieu is more relaxed, with a marina full of local fishing boats and smaller yachts. We can help you pick the best departure point based on where you are staying and what you want to see.

Boat Options for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

We offer a range of boat types for your Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter. Motor yachts are the most common, from 8 metres to 20 metres, with speeds of 20 to 30 knots. They are ideal for covering distance quickly, like zipping from Cannes to Saint-Tropez in under two hours. Catamarans are more stable and spacious, perfect for groups who want to lounge on the nets and swim. Sailing yachts are available if you prefer a quieter, wind-powered experience. RIBs and speedboats are a cheaper option for a fast, open-air ride. Licence-free day boats are also available for small groups who want to drive themselves, but the skipper is still included for safety. Superyachts over 30 metres are available on request, with prices starting around EUR 10,000 per day. Each boat listing on our site includes photos, specs, and a clear price. You can filter by length, capacity, and price range.

Pricing Guidance for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

Prices for a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter vary by boat size, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht starts from around EUR 800 in low season. A full day (8 hours) on the same boat is roughly EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,800. Catamarans are more expensive, from EUR 2,000 for a half-day and EUR 3,500 for a full day. Sailing yachts are often cheaper, starting at EUR 600 for a half-day. Superyachts are price on request, but expect to pay EUR 10,000 to EUR 30,000 per day depending on size and crew. High season (July and August) adds 20 to 30 percent to these prices. We recommend booking at least two weeks in advance for summer, especially for larger boats. You can compare prices on our search page and filter by your budget.

Best Time for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

The best time for a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter is from May to September. Water temperatures range from 18 degrees C in May to 26 degrees C in August. July and August are the hottest and busiest months, with sea conditions generally calm in the morning and a light breeze in the afternoon. September is quieter, with warm water and fewer crowds. April and October are possible but cooler, with average air temperatures of 15 to 20 degrees C, and the Mistral wind can make the sea choppy. Winter charters are rare because many boats are in dry dock. If you want to see the Cannes Film Festival in May, book your charter months in advance because prices surge and availability drops. For a more relaxed trip, June or September offer the best balance of good weather and reasonable prices.

Routes and Destinations for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

A typical Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter route heads to the Îles de Lérins, a pair of islands just 15 minutes from Cannes. Sainte-Marguerite is the larger island, with a pine forest, a small village, and the famous Fort Royal where the Man in the Iron Mask was held. Saint-Honorat is a monastery island with a winery and a quiet beach. Another popular route is along the Esterel coast, from Mandelieu to Théoule-sur-Mer, with red rock cliffs and hidden coves like Calanque du Trayas. You can also head east to Golfe Juan and the Bay of Antibes, or west to Saint-Tropez for a longer day trip. Dolphin watching is common near the Esterel, especially in the morning. Your skipper will tailor the route to your preferences, whether you want to swim, eat, or just cruise.

How to Book a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

Booking a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to our BoatHire24 homepage, enter Cannes or Mandelieu as your location, and choose your date and group size. You will see a list of available boats with photos, descriptions, and prices. Click on any boat to see the full details, including the skipper profile, cancellation policy, and what is included. You can book directly online with a deposit of 30 to 50 percent. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day of departure, usually in cash or by card. We recommend reading the terms carefully, especially for weather cancellations. If the Mistral blows too hard, the charter may be cancelled for safety, and you get a full refund or a reschedule. Our customer support team can help you choose the right boat if you are unsure.

Who Is a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter For

A Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter suits couples, families, and groups of friends. Couples often book a small motor yacht for a romantic sunset cruise with champagne. Families with children prefer catamarans for the stability and space to play. Groups of up to 12 people can book a catamaran or a large motor yacht for birthday parties, bachelor or bachelorette trips, or corporate events. Business clients sometimes charter a boat for a client meeting or a team-building day. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter on some boats, but availability is limited. The common thread is that you want a private, hassle-free day on the water with a professional crew. You do not need any boating experience, and you can customise the itinerary to your interests.

Local Tips for Your Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

If you are planning a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter, here are a few local tips. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light jacket because the wind can pick up even on sunny days. Pack swimwear and a towel if you plan to swim. Most boats have a shower on the swim platform to rinse off saltwater. For lunch, ask the skipper to reserve a table at a restaurant on the Île Sainte-Marguerite or at a beach club in Golfe Juan. Bring cash for tips and extras like fuel surcharges or port fees. If you are prone to seasickness, take a pill an hour before departure. The sea is usually calm in the morning and gets choppier in the afternoon. Finally, respect the environment: do not throw anything overboard, and use the onboard bins for rubbish. The Mediterranean is fragile, and we want to keep it clean for everyone.

Typical Itinerary for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

A full-day Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter often starts at 10am from Cannes Vieux Port. You motor out past the Palais des Festivals, turn west towards the Esterel massif, and stop for a swim at a quiet cove like Calanque du Trayas or Calanque de la Mauboussière. Lunch is at anchor near Théoule-sur-Mer, where you can eat on board or take a tender to a beachside restaurant. After lunch, you head to the Îles de Lérins for a walk on Sainte-Marguerite or a wine tasting on Saint-Honorat. The return leg takes you past the Cannes skyline, with the Croisette and the hills of La Californie behind it. You dock by 6pm, with time for a drink at a waterfront bar. Half-day charters usually skip the islands and focus on a single destination like the Esterel coast or the bay of Cannes.

What to Expect from the Skipper on a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

Your skipper on a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter is a local professional with a valid licence and years of experience on the French Riviera. They speak English and French, and they know the best anchor spots, the wind patterns, and the restaurant recommendations. The skipper will give you a safety briefing at the start, show you the life jackets and the emergency equipment, and explain the itinerary. They do not serve drinks or cook, but they are happy to help with the music and the mooring. You can chat with them or leave them alone, it is your day. If you want a more hands-on experience, some skippers let you steer the boat under their supervision. The crew is there to make sure you have a safe, enjoyable trip, not to hover over you.

Weather and Sea Conditions for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

The weather on the French Riviera is generally reliable from May to September, but the Mistral wind can disrupt a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter. The Mistral comes from the north-west, often in spring and autumn, and can blow at 30 to 50 knots. It creates short, steep waves in the bay of Cannes, especially near the islands. If the forecast shows Mistral over 25 knots, the skipper may cancel or suggest a protected route along the coast. The sea is calmest in the morning, from 8am to 11am, and the afternoon breeze picks up to 10 to 15 knots, which is fine for sailing. In July and August, thunderstorms can appear in the late afternoon, but they usually pass quickly. Check the forecast on Windy or Meteo France before your charter, and trust the skipper's judgment.

Cost Comparisons for Different Group Sizes on a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

A Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter for two people on a 10-metre motor yacht costs around EUR 800 for a half-day in low season. For four people, the same boat is still EUR 800 because the price is per boat, not per person. For eight people, you need a larger boat, like a 14-metre motor yacht or a 12-metre catamaran, which costs EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500 for a half-day. For 12 people, a 16-metre catamaran or a 18-metre motor yacht costs EUR 3,000 to EUR 5,000 for a full day. Superyachts for 12 to 20 guests start at EUR 10,000 per day. If you are a small group, you can save by booking a shared charter, but these are rare in Cannes. The per-person cost drops significantly with a larger group, making a full-day charter for eight people around EUR 200 to EUR 300 each, which is competitive with a beach club lunch.

Special Events and Festivals for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

If you book a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter during the Cannes Film Festival in May, you can see celebrities on the Croisette and at the Palais des Festivals from the water. The harbour is full of superyachts, and the atmosphere is electric. Prices triple or quadruple, and availability is tight, so book six months ahead. Another event is the Cannes Yachting Festival in September, where new boats are on display. The MIPIM property fair in March also brings a business crowd. For a more relaxed vibe, the Fête de la Saint-Pierre in June celebrates fishermen with a procession and a blessing of the boats. The fireworks display on Bastille Day, 14 July, is spectacular from a boat in the bay of Cannes. You can anchor near the Île Sainte-Marguerite for the best view. Book early for any event date.

Nearby Attractions for a Mandelieu Cannes Yacht Charter

Beyond the sea, a Mandelieu Cannes yacht charter lets you access attractions along the coast. You can dock at Golfe Juan and walk to the Picasso Museum in Antibes, which has a terrace overlooking the harbour. In Cannes, you can visit the Musée de la Castre in the old town, with a tower offering panoramic views. On the Esterel coast, the Corniche d'Or road runs along the cliffs, and you can stop at the village of Théoule-sur-Mer for a hike. The Île Sainte-Marguerite has a nature reserve with walking trails and the Fort Royal prison. The Île Saint-Honorat has a working monastery where monks produce wine and lavender products. If you have a full day, you can combine a swim stop with a cultural visit. Your skipper can suggest a route that fits your interests.

What Is Included in a Mandelieu Cannes Catamaran Hire

When you book a catamaran hire in Mandelieu or Cannes through BoatHire24, the standard package includes the vessel, a licensed skipper, fuel for a typical day trip (around 30-50 NM), and insurance.
