Check the listing details before you confirm.

Departure Ports for Mandelieu Cannes Catamaran Hire

The main departure ports for catamaran hire in this area are Cannes Vieux Port (Old Port) and Port de Mandelieu-La Napoule. Cannes Vieux Port is central, close to the Palais des Festivals and the main boulevard. Port de Mandelieu-La Napoule is quieter, at the western end of the Bay of Cannes, near the Esterel massif. Some charters also offer pickups from Antibes or Golfe-Juan, but that is less common. If you are staying in Cannes, the Vieux Port is the most convenient. If you are based in Mandelieu or La Napoule, the local port is a short walk from the beach. Each port has parking nearby, though in summer you will want to book a spot in advance.

Catamaran Options for Your Trip

Catamarans available for hire in Mandelieu and Cannes typically range from 36 to 50 feet (11 to 15 metres). You will find Lagoon, Fountaine Pajot, and Bali models, among others. A 40-foot catamaran can comfortably take 8 to 12 guests for a day trip. Larger catamarans up to 50 feet can host up to 18 guests. Most catamarans have a flybridge for sunbathing, a spacious saloon, and a forward trampoline. If you want a faster experience, you might consider a motor yacht instead, but catamarans offer more deck space and stability. Prices for a day charter (8 hours) start from around EUR 1,200 for a 36-foot catamaran and go up to EUR 2,500 for a 50-footer. Half-day trips (4 hours) are also available from around EUR 800. Always check the maximum guest capacity and any restrictions on children or pets.

Pricing Guidance for Mandelieu Cannes Catamaran Hire

Prices for catamaran hire in Mandelieu and Cannes vary by season, boat size, and duration. In summer (June to September), a full-day charter (8 hours) for a 40-foot catamaran costs between EUR 1,500 and EUR 2,000. In the shoulder seasons (April, May, October), expect EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,700. Half-day charters are roughly 60% of the full-day price. Some operators charge extra for fuel beyond 50 NM, so ask. You will also need to pay a refundable security deposit, typically EUR 500 to EUR 1,000, held on your credit card. That is standard. If you want to hire a catamaran for multiple days, negotiate a weekly rate; it can be 15-20% cheaper per day. For a precise quote, use our search tool or contact the owner directly through BoatHire24.

Best Seasons for Catamaran Hire on the French Riviera

The best time for a catamaran hire in Mandelieu or Cannes is from May to September. July and August are peak season: water temperatures reach 25-27 degrees C, and the weather is stable. But it is also crowded, and ports can be busy. May, June, and September offer pleasant temperatures (22-26 degrees C) with fewer crowds. April and October are possible, but the sea can be cooler (16-18 degrees C) and the Mistral wind can blow. If you are flexible, aim for late May or early September. That gives you warm weather, calm seas, and better availability. Winter (November to March) is not ideal for catamaran hire; many boats are in dry dock or maintenance.

Popular Itineraries from Mandelieu and Cannes

A typical day trip from Cannes or Mandelieu includes the Lérins Islands (Île Sainte-Marguerite and Île Saint-Honorat). You can anchor off Sainte-Marguerite for a swim and a picnic, then cruise to the Esterel coast for views of the red rocks. Another route goes west to the Bay of Théoule-sur-Mer and the Calanques, or east towards Antibes and the Cap d'Antibes. Some charters offer a lunch stop at a beachside restaurant, like the Plage de la Garoupe or the restaurant at the Fort de l'Île Sainte-Marguerite. If you want a longer trip, you can head to the Saint-Tropez peninsula, but that is a 2-hour cruise each way. Your skipper will suggest a route based on weather and your preferences.

Who Is Catamaran Hire For

Catamaran hire in Mandelieu and Cannes works for groups of friends, families with children, couples, and corporate events. Because catamarans are stable, they are a good choice for people who get seasick. The wide deck space makes them suitable for parties or relaxing days. If you want a romantic sunset cruise, a catamaran works well, but a smaller sailing yacht might feel more intimate. For a bachelor or bachelorette party, a catamaran with a DJ and sound system is possible, but check with the owner first. Families with kids appreciate the safe swimming areas and the trampoline. Business groups often book a catamaran for a day of networking or team building.

How to Book Your Mandelieu Cannes Catamaran Hire

Booking a catamaran hire through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to our search page, select Mandelieu or Cannes as the port, choose your dates and group size, and browse the available catamarans. Each listing shows photos, specifications, capacity, and price. You can send a booking request directly through the site. The owner will confirm availability and send a quote. Payment is typically by bank transfer or credit card, with a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is due a few weeks before departure. Cancellation policies vary, so read them. If you need help, contact us via the website and we will assist.

Why Book Through BoatHire24

BoatHire24 is a boat-rental and yacht-charter marketplace. We list catamarans from multiple owners, so you can compare options. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you do not need a licence. We focus on the Costa del Sol and the French Riviera, so we know the local ports and conditions. Our blog has guides on the best beaches, restaurants, and itineraries along the Riviera. Booking through us gives you access to vetted boats and transparent pricing. No hidden fees. If you want to see what else we offer, check our homepage for all destinations.

Additional Tips for Your Catamaran Trip

Pack sunscreen, a hat, swimwear, a towel, and a light jacket for the evening. The sun on the water is strong, even in spring. Bring your own food and drinks unless you order a catering package. Some catamarans have a BBQ on the back deck, which is great for grilling fish. If you want to snorkel, bring your own gear; some boats provide it, but not all. Confirm the meeting time and location with the skipper the day before. Arrive 15 minutes early. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication before boarding; catamarans are stable, but the Mediterranean can have a swell. Finally, respect the environment: do not throw anything overboard, and use the facilities on board.

Navigating the Cannes Vieux Port and Mandelieu-La Napoule

Cannes Vieux Port is the busiest hub on the Bay of Cannes. You will find it right next to the Palais des Festivals, which means you can step off your catamaran and walk to the Croisette in five minutes. The port has 24-hour security, fuel pumps, and a few chandlers if you need supplies. Parking at the Port Pantiero car park costs around EUR 35 for a day in summer, so factor that in. Port de Mandelieu-La Napoule is a different beast. It sits at the mouth of the Siagne river, with the Esterel hills as a backdrop. It is quieter, cheaper to park at (around EUR 15 a day), and closer to the A8 motorway if you are driving from the west. The marina has a boatyard and a small supermarket. If you are staying in a villa near Théoule-sur-Mer, Mandelieu is your best bet.

Catamaran Models You Will Actually Find for Hire

You will not see every catamaran model on the market, but the common ones are worth knowing. The Lagoon 40 is a favourite: 11.7 metres long, 6.7 metres beam, sleeps 8, with a flybridge and a forward cockpit. It handles well in light winds and has decent headroom. The Fountaine Pajot Astrea 42 is similar but has a larger saloon and a more modern layout. The Bali 4.0 is a bit different with its hard-top bimini and sliding glass doors, which makes it feel more like a motor yacht. For bigger groups, the Lagoon 52 or Fountaine Pajot Saona 47 can host up to 18 guests, but expect to pay EUR 2,500 to EUR 3,500 per day. Some older models like the Lagoon 380 or 410 are cheaper, from EUR 1,000 a day, but the amenities are more basic. Always check the year of build and the last refit date.

What the Skipper Actually Does on Your Trip

The skipper is not just a driver. They handle the navigation, mooring, anchoring, and safety briefings. They know the local waters: where the shallow patches are near the Lérins Islands, how to avoid the ferry traffic off Cannes, and where to anchor for the best shelter from the Mistral. They can also advise on lunch spots. Most skippers speak English and French, but confirm that when booking. You are not expected to help with sailing unless you want to. If you have a specific request, like stopping for a swim at a quiet cove or visiting a particular beach, the skipper will adjust the route. They do not serve drinks or cook, but they will help you set up the BBQ if the boat has one. Tip: EUR 50 to EUR 100 for a good day is standard.

Half-Day vs Full-Day Charters: Which Is Better

Half-day charters (4 hours) work well if you want a quick escape from the beach or a sunset cruise from 16:00 to 20:00. You can reach the Lérins Islands, anchor for a swim, and return. It costs less, from EUR 800, and leaves you time for other activities. But you will feel rushed if you want to explore further. Full-day charters (8 hours) give you time to cruise to the Esterel coast, have a proper lunch stop, and maybe visit a second spot. The cost is higher, but the experience is more relaxed. Some operators offer a 6-hour charter as a middle option, which is common for lunch trips. If you are booking for a special occasion, like a birthday or anniversary, go for the full day. You will not regret the extra time on the water.

Hidden Costs and How to Avoid Them

The listed price for a catamaran hire often excludes a few things. Fuel is usually included for up to 50 NM, but if you go further, you pay extra at around EUR 1.50 to EUR 2.00 per litre. A day trip to Saint-Tropez might add EUR 200 to EUR 300 in fuel. Some operators charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50 to EUR 100 if you leave the boat messy. If you want a water scooter or jet ski towed behind, that is extra, often EUR 150 to EUR 250 per day. Catering packages vary: a basic lunch with sandwiches and drinks might be EUR 25 per person, while a full sit-down meal with champagne costs EUR 60 to EUR 80 per person. Always ask for a full breakdown before you pay the deposit. Read the cancellation policy: some operators refund 100% if you cancel 30 days out, but only 50% within 14 days.

Best Beaches and Coves to Visit by Catamaran

From Cannes or Mandelieu, you have several excellent spots. The Lérins Islands are the obvious choice. Île Sainte-Marguerite has the Plage de la Batterie, a sandy beach on the north side, and the quieter Anse du Fer à Cheval on the south. Anchor off the east coast of Île Saint-Honorat, where the monks grow vines. Further west, the Calanque de Maubousquet near Théoule-sur-Mer is a narrow inlet with turquoise water and red rock cliffs. The Plage de l'Île des Vieilles is another good stop, just off the Esterel coast. If you head east, the Baie des Milliardaires between Cannes and Antibes has several private beaches, but you can anchor offshore and swim. For a lunch stop, the Plage de la Garoupe on the Cap d'Antibes is popular, but it gets crowded. Your skipper will know which spots are calm on the day.

Weather and Wind Conditions on the Bay of Cannes

The Bay of Cannes is generally sheltered, but the Mistral wind can change things. The Mistral blows from the north-west, often in spring and autumn, and can reach 30 to 40 knots. When it blows, the sea gets choppy, especially outside the bay. Catamarans handle it better than monohulls, but you might need to stay closer to shore. The thermal breeze, or sea breeze, kicks up in the afternoon from the south, typically 10 to 15 knots, which is perfect for sailing. In July and August, the wind is light, often below 10 knots, so catamarans rely on engines. Check the forecast on Windy or Meteo France before your trip. Your skipper will make the call on the day. If the weather looks bad, rescheduling is better than a rough trip.

How to Get to the Ports from Local Airports and Train Stations

Nice Côte d'Azur Airport (NCE) is the main gateway, about 25 km from Cannes and 35 km from Mandelieu. A taxi from the airport to Cannes Vieux Port costs around EUR 70 to EUR 90 and takes 30 to 45 minutes. To Mandelieu, it is EUR 80 to EUR 100. There is a direct train from Nice Airport station (Terminal 2) to Cannes station, then a 10-minute walk to the port. The train costs EUR 5 to EUR 10 and runs every 30 minutes. If you are coming from Cannes Mandelieu Airport (CEQ), which handles private jets and some charters, it is a 5-minute taxi ride to Port de Mandelieu. Cannes train station is on the main line from Paris and Marseille. From the station, walk south down Rue d'Antibes to the port in 10 minutes. Parking at both ports is limited in summer, so book a space online if you drive.

What to Expect on a Multi-Day Catamaran Charter

If you book a catamaran for two or three days, the itinerary opens up. You can cruise east to Antibes, then to Nice and Villefranche-sur-Mer, or west to Saint-Raphaël and the Gulf of Fréjus. A typical two-day trip from Cannes might go to the Lérins Islands on day one, then to the Esterel and overnight at anchor off Théoule-sur-Mer. Most catamarans have cabins with double beds and en-suite bathrooms, plus a galley kitchen. You will need to provision your own food, or arrange a catering delivery to the boat. The skipper stays on board, usually in a separate cabin. Multi-day charters cost between EUR 1,200 and EUR 2,500 per day, depending on the boat and season, plus a deposit. You save on accommodation costs, but you pay for mooring fees if you stay in a marina overnight, typically EUR 50 to EUR 100 per night. It is a good option for a small group that wants to explore beyond the bay.

Special Events and Corporate Charters on Catamarans

Catamarans in Mandelieu and Cannes are popular for events. You can book one for a birthday party, a wedding reception, or a corporate day out. Most operators allow up to 12 to 18 guests, depending on the boat size. For a corporate event, you might want a catamaran with a sound system, a projector, and Wi-Fi. Some boats have a flybridge that works well for presentations or networking. The cost for a corporate charter is similar to a private hire, but you might need to pay extra for AV equipment. For a wedding, you can arrange a civil ceremony on board if the boat is registered for that, but check with the port authority first. The sunset cruise option is popular for proposals. If you want a DJ, confirm that the boat has a suitable power supply and that the noise is acceptable in the anchorage. Always discuss your plans with the owner before booking.

title: Mandelieu Cannes Speedboat Rental: No Licence Hire
metaDescription: Book a Mandelieu Cannes speedboat rental with no licence needed. Drive yourself along the French Riviera. Instant quotes, transparent prices, free cancellation.
h1: Mandelieu Cannes Speedboat Rental: No Licence Hire
intro:
You want to buzz around the Bay of Cannes on a speedboat without spending a day on a theory test. That is exactly what a Mandelieu Cannes speedboat rental offers. Licence-free boats up to 6 hp (or electric versions) let you take the helm yourself straight from the port of Mandelieu-La Napoule. No skipper, no exam, just you, the sea and the Esterel massif in the background.

BoatHire24 lists a handful of operators in Mandelieu who rent these no-licence speedboats by the hour or half-day. You get a quick safety briefing, a map of the no-go zones (the shipping lanes off Cannes, basically), and then you are free to explore the coves between Cannes and Théoule-sur-Mer. Prices start from around EUR 90 per hour for a 4-metre RIB with a 6 hp outboard. For a bigger boat with a bit more power, you will need a licence, but that is a different page.
bodyHtml:
What a No-Licence Speedboat Rental in Mandelieu Actually Includes

Every rental we list comes with a life jacket for each passenger, a fuel tank (usually enough for two hours of cruising), and a basic safety briefing. The boat is a rigid inflatable (RIB) with a small outboard motor. Top speed is around 5-6 knots, so you are not going to waterski. You are going to putter along the coast, drop anchor in a quiet cove, and maybe have a swim. Most operators include a map of the area and a phone number for assistance if you break down. You do not get a skipper, because the whole point is that you drive it yourself. Insurance is included in the price, but you will have to leave a damage deposit (credit card hold, typically EUR 500 to EUR 1,000).

Departure Port: Mandelieu-La Napoule

Mandelieu-La Napoule sits just west of Cannes, at the mouth of the Siagne river. The port is small and less glitzy than Cannes Vieux Port or Port Pierre Canto. That is an advantage: the traffic is lighter, the parking is easier, and you are straight out into the Bay of Cannes without navigating a maze of superyachts. The port has a fuel dock, a few restaurants, and a public car park. You can walk from the train station (Mandelieu-la-Napoule) in about 15 minutes. The address is Port de Mandelieu, 06210 Mandelieu-la-Napoule. If you are driving, the A8 motorway exit is Mandelieu, then follow the signs to the port.

Boat Options for Licence-Free Hire

The typical fleet for no-licence speedboat rental in Mandelieu consists of:

  • Zodiac or similar RIBs, 3.8 to 4.5 metres long, with a 6 hp four-stroke outboard. Seats 4 to 5 people. Max speed 5-6 knots. Price from around EUR 90 per hour.
  • Electric runabouts, 4 metres, silent, zero emissions. Seats 4. Same speed. Price from around EUR 100 per hour.
  • Small aluminium fishing boats with a 6 hp engine. Seats 3. Cheaper, from around EUR 60 per hour.

All boats are self-drive. You do not need a licence, but you must be at least 18 years old and present a valid ID (passport or EU ID card). Some operators require a short practical test before you go out alone. If you want a faster boat (say a 40 hp RIB that can do 25 knots), you will need a boating licence or a hired skipper. For that, see our search page for a full list of options.

Where You Can Go on a Licence-Free Speedboat

With a 5-knot speed limit, you are not going to cross the bay to the Lerins Islands in 10 minutes. But you can reach the following spots within 30-40 minutes from Mandelieu port:

  • Plage de la Raguette, a small pebble beach just east of the port, sheltered by the Esterel cliffs. Good for swimming.
  • Pointe de l'Esquillon, a rocky headland with a few coves. Drop anchor and snorkel.
  • Théoule-sur-Mer, the next village along the coast, with a couple of beach restaurants that have mooring buoys for small boats.
  • Calanque des Anglais, a narrow inlet with turquoise water, popular with kayakers. Your slow speedboat will not disturb anyone.

Do not try to go past Cannes towards Antibes or Nice. The shipping lanes and the ferry traffic make that area dangerous for a 4-metre RIB. Stick to the western side of the Bay of Cannes. The views of the Esterel massif and the red rocks are worth it anyway.

Pricing Guidance for Mandelieu Cannes Speedboat Rental

Prices vary by season, duration and boat size. Here is a rough guide for a 4-metre RIB with a 6 hp engine:

  • Low season (March-April, October): EUR 80-100 per hour, half-day (4 hours) from EUR 250.
  • Mid season (May-June, September): EUR 90-110 per hour, half-day from EUR 300.
  • High season (July-August): EUR 100-130 per hour, half-day from EUR 350. Minimum rental is usually 2 hours.

Fuel is included in the hourly rate. Some operators charge a cleaning fee (EUR 20-30) if you bring the boat back sandy. Deposit hold is EUR 500-1,000 on a credit card. You can book online via the operator's website or through BoatHire24 for instant confirmation. Most allow free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure.

Best Time of Year for a Licence-Free Speedboat Trip

The water is warm enough to swim from June to September (22-26 degrees C). July and August are the busiest months, so expect more boat traffic in the coves. May and June are quieter, with fewer crowds and the same sunshine. The Mistral wind can blow in spring and autumn, making the sea choppy. Check the wind forecast (less than 15 knots is fine for a small RIB). Operators will cancel if the weather is dangerous, but you can also choose to reschedule. The morning hours (9am-12pm) are usually calmer than the afternoon, when the sea breeze picks up.

How to Book a Mandelieu Cannes Speedboat Rental

Booking is straightforward. You can either contact the operator directly or use BoatHire24 to compare prices and availability. When you book, you will need to provide the number of passengers, the date and time, and a contact phone number. Payment is usually by credit card or PayPal. Some operators require a 50% deposit, others take the full amount. The confirmation email includes the exact meeting point at the port, the operator's phone number, and instructions for the safety briefing. Arrive 15 minutes early. Bring sunscreen, a hat, towels, and a bottle of water. There is no shade on a small RIB.

Who Is This Rental For?

This type of rental is ideal for families with kids (the slow speed is safe), couples who want a private picnic on the water, and groups of friends who want a relaxed day out. It is not for adrenaline seekers or people who want to waterski. If you want speed, you need a licensed skipper and a bigger boat. For that, check our search page for Mandelieu and Cannes. If you are curious about the differences between licence-free and skippered charters, our blog has a detailed comparison.

What to Bring and What to Expect on the Day

On the day, you will meet the operator at the port. They will check your ID, take a copy of your credit card for the deposit, and give you a 10-minute safety briefing. You will learn how to start the engine, steer, and moor. Then you are off. The boat has no toilet, no cabin, no shade. Plan for a maximum of 3-4 hours at sea, because sitting in a small RIB for longer gets uncomfortable. Pack dry bags for your phone and wallet. Wear a hat and sunglasses. The operator will give you a VHF radio or a mobile phone for emergencies. If you break down, they will come to tow you back. Do not forget to bring a sense of adventure and a willingness to go slow.

Alternative Options in Mandelieu and Cannes

If a 5-knot speedboat sounds too tame, consider a skippered RIB rental from Cannes or Mandelieu. You get a licensed skipper who knows the coast, and the boat can do 30-40 knots. Prices start from around EUR 250 per hour for a 6-person RIB. You can also charter a sailing catamaran for a half-day from Cannes, with a skipper, for around EUR 500. For a full list of boats, visit our search page. For more tips on boating in the French Riviera, read our blog.

Navigating the Siagne River Before You Hit the Sea

One of the quirks of renting from Mandelieu-La Napoule is the short river passage you must navigate before you reach open water. The Siagne river is narrow and shallow in places, with a speed limit of 3 knots. You will pass under a low bridge (clearance about 3 metres) and alongside a few moored fishing boats. It takes about 10 minutes to get from the port to the river mouth. The operator will explain the channel markers during the briefing. Do not try to take a shortcut across the sandbar at the mouth. Stick to the marked channel. The river is calm even when the sea is choppy, so it is a good place to get a feel for the steering before you face any swell.

What Happens If the Wind Picks Up: Wind Limits and Safety

Operators in Mandelieu are strict about wind limits for licence-free boats. If the forecast shows more than 15 knots of wind, they will cancel or reschedule your rental. The Bay of Cannes can get a choppy chop quickly when the Mistral blows from the northwest. A 4-metre RIB with a 6 hp engine cannot handle waves over 0.5 metres. You will get soaked and uncomfortable, and the boat may take on water. The operator will call you the day before if the weather looks bad. You can also check the wind yourself on Windy.com or the Meteo France marine forecast for Golfe de la Napoule. If you are flexible, book a morning slot (8am-12pm) when the sea is usually flat. Afternoons from June to August often have a thermal breeze of 10-12 knots, which is fine but splashy.

Where to Eat on the Water: Beach Restaurants Accessible by Small Boat

You can tie up at a few beach restaurants along the coast from Mandelieu to Théoule-sur-Mer. The most accessible is Plage de la Raguette, which has a small mooring buoy field (free, first come first served) and a restaurant serving grilled fish and salads. Lunch for two costs around EUR 50-70. Another option is the beach at Pointe de l'Esquillon, where the restaurant L'Esquillon has a small dock for dinghies. You cannot beach the RIB on the sand because the hull is inflatable and the engine leg will hit the bottom. You must use the buoys or anchor off and swim ashore. Bring a waterproof bag for your valuables. Do not leave the boat unattended on the beach. The tide range in the Mediterranean is small (30 cm), so the boat will not drift far if you anchor properly.

How to Anchor a Small RIB Safely

Most licence-free RIBs come with a small Danforth anchor and about 10 metres of chain and rope. The operator will show you how to deploy it. The technique is simple: motor slowly into the wind or current, drop the anchor when you are over a sandy patch (avoid posidonia seagrass, which is protected), let out 3-4 metres of rope for every metre of water depth, and reverse gently to set the anchor. The Bay of Cannes has a sandy bottom in most coves, so the anchor will hold. Do not anchor in more than 10 metres of water because the rope is too short. If you cannot get the anchor to hold, tie up to a mooring buoy if one is available. Do not tie to the buoy's mooring line, use the pick-up buoy loop. If you are unsure, stay close to the port and ask the operator for advice before you leave.

What to Do If You Break Down or Run Aground

Breakdowns are rare because the engines are simple four-stroke outboards, but they happen. If the engine stops, check the fuel line connection and the kill switch lanyard (the red clip that attaches to your life jacket). If that does not work, call the operator on the VHF radio or the mobile phone they gave you. They will send a rescue boat, usually within 30 minutes. Do not try to paddle or swim the boat back. If you run aground on a sandbar (common near the Siagne river mouth), tilt the engine up, push the boat off with an oar, and restart. Do not rev the engine while it is in the sand. If you are stuck, call for help. Running aground in a small RIB rarely causes damage, but the operator may charge a recovery fee (EUR 50-100) if you need a tow.

Insurance and Liability: What You Need to Know

The rental price includes third-party liability insurance, which covers damage you cause to other boats or property. Your own damage to the rental boat (hull puncture, engine damage, lost propeller) is covered by the damage deposit up to the amount you agreed. If you cause total loss, you may be liable for the full replacement value (EUR 5,000-10,000 for a small RIB). Read the terms carefully before you sign. Some operators exclude damage from grounding or hitting rocks. Others charge a waiver fee (EUR 20-30) to reduce your liability to zero. Always take the waiver if it is offered. The deposit is released within 5-10 working days after the rental, assuming no damage. Check your credit card statement if it does not appear.

Combining Your Speedboat Trip with a Visit to the Lerins Islands

Technically, you can reach Île Sainte-Marguerite from Mandelieu in a licence-free RIB, but it takes about 50 minutes at 5 knots. That leaves you only 2 hours of cruising time if you rent for 4 hours. The crossing is exposed to wind and boat traffic. We do not recommend it for a first-time rental. A better plan is to book a skippered RIB from Cannes (25 minutes to the island) and spend the day there. The island has a restaurant, a small beach, and the Fort Royal prison (where the Man in the Iron Mask was held). For a licence-free trip, stick to the coves between Mandelieu and Théoule. You will have a more relaxed day without the stress of a long crossing.

Accessibility for People with Limited Mobility

The port of Mandelieu-La Napoule has accessible parking and a ramp to the pontoon. The RIBs are boarded via a small ladder or step from the pontoon. The boat itself has no handrails and the seats are low. If you have limited mobility in your legs, boarding and sitting may be difficult. Most operators require you to be able to board unaided. There are no adapted boats in the licence-free fleet. If you need assistance, consider a skippered charter on a larger boat with a swim platform and a gangway. Contact the operator in advance to discuss your needs. Some may allow a helper to assist boarding if you sign a waiver.

Parking and Transport to Port de Mandelieu

The port has a pay car park (Parking du Port, EUR 2 per hour, EUR 12 per day). Spaces fill up by 10am in July and August. There is free street parking on Avenue de la Mer, about a 10-minute walk away. The Mandelieu-la-Napoule train station is on the TER line from Cannes (10 minutes, EUR 3.50) and Nice (45 minutes, EUR 12). Taxis from Cannes station cost around EUR 20-25. If you are staying in Cannes, the bus line 600 from the station to Mandelieu port takes 25 minutes and costs EUR 1.50. Cycling is also possible; there is a bike path along the coast from Cannes to Mandelieu. The port has bike racks near the harbour master's office.

Environmental Rules and Protected Areas

The Bay of Cannes is part of the Natura 2000 network. You cannot anchor on posidonia seagrass meadows, which are visible as dark patches on the seabed. Anchoring on seagrass can result in a fine of up to EUR 1,500. The operator will show you a map of the protected areas. You also cannot discharge sewage or rubbish into the sea. Bring a bin bag for your waste. The coves near Théoule are popular with kayakers and paddleboarders. Keep your distance (at least 50 metres) and reduce speed to idle when passing them. If you see a dolphin or a whale (rare but possible in late summer), maintain a distance of 100 metres and do not chase it. The local authorities enforce these rules strictly during the summer season.

intro:
You want a private yacht charter in Mandelieu or Cannes, and you want it sorted without the fluff. A boat that’s yours for the day, a skipper who knows the coast, and a route that shows off the best of the French Riviera. That’s exactly what BoatHire24 does.

bodyHtml:
What a Private Yacht Charter in Mandelieu Cannes Includes

When you book through BoatHire24, you get the boat and the skipper as one package. The skipper is a local professional who knows the coastline, the weather patterns, and the best spots for swimming. You don’t pay extra for fuel, insurance, or cleaning fees, those are included in the price you see. Most charters also include a cooler with ice, basic snorkelling gear, and a Bluetooth speaker. Food and drinks are usually not included, but you can bring your own or order a catering package when you book.

The boat is cleaned and fuelled before you arrive. You turn up at the port, meet the skipper, and step aboard. No paperwork, no hidden costs. The charter is typically for a full day (8 hours), but half-day (4 hours) options are available for smaller boats like RIBs or licence-free day boats.

For a BoatHire24 private charter in this area, expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for a 10-metre motor yacht for a full day in low season, rising to EUR 2,500 or more for a 15-metre catamaran in July or August. Superyachts over 20 metres are price on request and usually start above EUR 8,000 per day.

Departure Ports: Cannes and Mandelieu-La Napoule

Your charter can start from either of the two main ports in this area. Cannes Vieux Port is the large harbour right in front of the Palais des Festivals. It’s busy, central, and surrounded by restaurants and shops. Mandelieu-La Napoule port is smaller, quieter, and closer to the Estérel massif. Both are well connected by road and rail. If you’re staying in Cannes, the old port is a five-minute walk from the train station. If you’re in Mandelieu, the port is a ten-minute walk from the town centre.

From Cannes, you can head east towards the Lerins Islands (Île Sainte-Marguerite and Île Saint-Honorat), about 20 minutes. From Mandelieu, you can go west towards the Gulf of La Napoule and the red rocks of the Estérel. The choice of port affects the route and the scenery, but both give you access to the same general area.

Check our search page to filter by port and see available boats for your dates.

Boat Options for Your Private Charter

Motor yachts are the most common choice for a private charter in Mandelieu Cannes. They range from 9-metre day cruisers (6-8 guests) to 20-metre flybridge yachts (12+ guests). Speed is around 20-30 knots, so you can cover distance quickly. Catamarans are popular for groups who want more deck space and stability, they’re slower (around 8-12 knots) but offer a larger sunbathing area and a shallower draft for anchoring close to shore. Sailing yachts are available for those who want the experience of sailing, but the skipper handles all the ropes. RIBs and speedboats are a cheaper option for smaller groups (4-6 people) and are great for a fast trip to the islands.

Licence-free day boats are also an option if you want to drive yourself, but for a private charter you’re paying for the skipper, so you might as well let them take the wheel. Fishing boats are available for anglers, but they’re less common in this area, most charters are leisure-oriented.

Superyachts over 24 metres are available for special events, corporate charters, or weddings. These require advance booking (at least two weeks) and a deposit. Prices start around EUR 8,000 per day and go up to EUR 30,000 for a 40-metre vessel with a crew of five.

Pricing Guidance for Mandelieu Cannes Private Yacht Charter

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. Here’s a rough guide for a full-day (8-hour) charter with skipper, fuel, and insurance included:

Low season (April, May, October): Motor yacht up to 12m, from EUR 1,200. Catamaran up to 14m, from EUR 1,800. Sailing yacht up to 14m, from EUR 1,000.

Mid season (June, September): Motor yacht up to 12m, from EUR 1,600. Catamaran up to 14m, from EUR 2,200. Sailing yacht up to 14m, from EUR 1,400.

High season (July, August): Motor yacht up to 12m, from EUR 2,200. Catamaran up to 14m, from EUR 3,000. Sailing yacht up to 14m, from EUR 1,800. Superyacht over 20m, price on request, typically EUR 8,000+.

Half-day charters (4 hours) are usually 60-70% of the full-day rate. Evening charters (sunset cruises, 3 hours) are around 40-50% of the full-day rate. All prices exclude food, drinks, and port fees (usually EUR 50-100 extra).

Best Time for a Private Yacht Charter in Mandelieu Cannes

The season runs from April to October. July and August are the busiest and most expensive months. The weather is hot (28-32°C), the sea is calm, and the water temperature is around 24-26°C. But the anchorages are crowded, especially around the Lerins Islands and the Bay of Cannes. If you want more space, book a boat with a skipper who knows the less popular coves.

June and September are the sweet spot. The weather is still warm (24-28°C), the crowds are thinner, and prices are 20-30% lower than peak season. The sea is often calm in the morning, with a light breeze in the afternoon, perfect for sailing or motoring along the coast.

April and May are cooler (18-22°C) and the water is cold (14-16°C). You can still charter, but swimming might be brief. The Estérel mountains are green from spring rain, and the views are excellent.

October is the end of the season. The weather is still pleasant (20-24°C), but some boats are already laid up for winter. Book early in the month to be sure.

For more tips on timing, read our blog on the best months for a yacht charter on the Côte d’Azur.

Routes and Highlights from Mandelieu Cannes

A typical private charter from Cannes or Mandelieu can take you to the Lerins Islands, the Estérel red rocks, or along the coast towards Antibes and Juan-les-Pins. Each route has its own character.

The Lerins Islands route: From Cannes Vieux Port, 20 minutes to Île Sainte-Marguerite. Anchor in the bay near the Fort Royal (where the Man in the Iron Mask was held). Swim in clear, shallow water. Then 10 minutes to Île Saint-Honorat, a monastery island with a vineyard. You can moor at the visitor buoy and take a short walk to the monastery shop for wine. Lunch on the boat or at a beach restaurant on Sainte-Marguerite.

The Estérel route: From Mandelieu-La Napoule, head west along the coast towards the red porphyry cliffs of the Estérel massif. Stop at Callelongue, a small cove with a pebble beach. Continue to the Gulf of La Napoule, where the water is deeper and clearer. The red rocks contrast with the blue water, good for photos. Lunch at a restaurant in Port La Napoule or anchor off the beach at Le Trayas.

The Antibes route: From Cannes, go east towards Cap d’Antibes. Pass the Billionaire’s Quay in Antibes, where superyachts moor. Stop at the Plage de la Garoupe or the Baie des Milliardaires. The water is deep close to shore, so you can anchor near the cliffs. Lunch at a beach club in Juan-les-Pins or Antibes old town.

All routes can be customised. Your skipper will suggest a plan based on weather, sea conditions, and your preferences.

Who Is a Private Yacht Charter For

A private charter works for couples, families, groups of friends, and corporate clients. If you want a day on the water without sharing the boat with strangers, this is it. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring, and safety. You just relax, swim, eat, and drink.

For couples: a motor yacht or sailing yacht for two to four people. A sunset cruise with champagne is a common request. For families: a catamaran with a shallow draft for anchoring close to beaches. Kids can swim off the boat or use the paddleboard often included on catamarans. For groups of 8-12: a flybridge motor yacht or a large catamaran. Plenty of deck space for sunbathing and socialising.

Corporate clients often book a superyacht for product launches, client entertainment, or team-building. The skipper can arrange a catered lunch, a DJ, or a photographer. These charters are usually full-day or multi-day.

If you’re celebrating a birthday, anniversary, or wedding, the skipper can help coordinate a special setup, decorations, cake, flowers. Just let us know when you book.

How to Book Your Private Yacht Charter

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You search for available boats on your chosen date, compare prices and features, and submit a booking request. The owner or charter company confirms availability and sends you a contract. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is due 7 days before departure.

You can book online or contact us for assistance. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for high season, 1 week for low season. Last-minute bookings are possible if the boat is available, but the choice is limited.

All our boats are licensed, insured, and maintained to French maritime safety standards. The skipper holds a valid professional licence. If you have any special requests (dietary requirements, specific route, extra equipment), mention them in the booking notes.

For a private charter in Mandelieu Cannes, start your search on our search page or contact us directly for a personalised quote.

Why Choose Mandelieu Over Cannes for Your Private Charter

Mandelieu-La Napoule is often overlooked in favour of its flashier neighbour, Cannes. But for a private yacht charter, Mandelieu has distinct advantages. The port is quieter, with easier parking and less crowded quayside restaurants. You can park your car within 50 metres of the boat, which makes loading coolers, bags, and children much simpler. Cannes Vieux Port, by contrast, is a logistical challenge in July and August, with narrow streets, one-way systems, and expensive parking garages.

From Mandelieu, you are also closer to the Estérel massif. The red rocks of the Estérel are a 15-minute cruise west, whereas from Cannes you need 30 minutes to reach them. If your priority is the dramatic red cliff scenery rather than the glitz of Cannes, Mandelieu is the better departure point. The port also has a gas station and a small supermarket on the quayside, so you can stock up on drinks and snacks before you leave.

For a private charter from Mandelieu, look for boats berthed at Port Mandelieu-La Napoule. The water depth is 3-5 metres in the harbour, so even larger catamarans and motor yachts can berth there. The channel is well marked, and the entrance is protected by a breakwater, so the boat stays stable even in a southerly swell.

What to Expect from the Skipper on Your Private Charter

The skipper on your private charter is not just a driver. They are a local guide with knowledge of the coastline, the weather patterns, and the best anchorages. Most skippers on the Côte d’Azur hold a French professional licence (permis côtier professionnel or capitaine 200). They speak English to a functional level, but not all are fluent. If you need a fluent English-speaking skipper, mention it when you book. Some charter companies can arrange this at no extra cost.

The skipper will give you a safety briefing at the start of the day. They will show you where the life jackets are, how to use the heads (toilet), and what to do in an emergency. They will also ask about your plans for the day: swimming, lunch, sightseeing. They will then suggest a route based on the weather and sea conditions. You are not obliged to follow their suggestion, but it is usually wise to do so. The skipper knows when the afternoon breeze picks up and which anchorages offer shelter from the swell.

The skipper does not serve food or drinks. If you want a crew member who also acts as a steward, you need to book a superyacht with a full crew (captain, deckhand, stewardess). For a standard private charter, the skipper handles the boat, and you handle the catering. Some skippers will help you set up a table or rearrange cushions, but they are not waiters.

Anchoring and Swimming Spots Near Mandelieu Cannes

The best swimming spots on a private charter from Mandelieu or Cannes are not the main beaches. Those are crowded with tourists and jet skis. Instead, your skipper will take you to quieter coves where the water is clear and the seabed is sandy or rocky. One such spot is the Callelongue cove, just west of Mandelieu. It is a small bay with a pebble beach and deep water close to the shore. You can anchor in 5-8 metres of water and swim straight off the boat. The bottom is rocky in places, so wear water shoes.

Another option is the Pointe de l’Aiguille, near the Estérel. This is a rocky headland with a small sandy beach on the eastern side. The water is deeper here, around 10-15 metres, and the visibility is often excellent (10-15 metres on a calm day). You can snorkel around the rocks and see small fish, sea urchins, and sometimes octopus. The skipper will anchor with a bow and stern line to keep the boat steady in the current.

Around the Lerins Islands, the best swimming is on the north side of Île Sainte-Marguerite, where the water is shallower and warmer. You can anchor in 3-5 metres of water and walk to the beach. The seabed is a mix of sand and seagrass, which is good for snorkelling but avoid the seagrass beds as they are protected.

Multi-Day Private Charters from Mandelieu Cannes

A private yacht charter does not have to be a single day. You can book a multi-day charter, where you spend the night on the boat and cruise along the coast to different ports. This works best on a catamaran or a motor yacht with cabins and a galley (kitchen). Most charter boats in this size range (12-18 metres) have two to four cabins, a saloon, and a small kitchen. The skipper sleeps in a separate cabin or on deck, depending on the boat.

A popular multi-day route from Mandelieu or Cannes is to go west to Saint-Tropez, stopping at the Estérel and the Gulf of Saint-Tropez on the way. The distance from Cannes to Saint-Tropez is about 35 nautical miles, which takes 2-3 hours at cruising speed. You can anchor for lunch at the Callelongue cove or at the Plage de la Bouillabaisse, then arrive in Saint-Tropez by late afternoon. The next day, you can explore the port, the old town, and the beaches, then cruise back to Cannes via the Lerins Islands.

Multi-day charters require a separate contract and a higher deposit (usually 50%). The price includes the skipper’s accommodation and meals, but you pay for food and drinks for yourself. Port fees for overnight stays are extra, typically EUR 50-150 per night depending on the port. Fuel consumption is higher on a multi-day trip because you cover more distance, but this is included in the charter price for most boats.

Private Charter for Events: Birthdays, Weddings, and Corporate Parties

A private yacht charter is a popular choice for milestone birthdays, wedding ceremonies, and corporate events. The boat becomes a floating venue, with the backdrop of the Mediterranean and the Estérel or Lerins Islands. For a wedding, you can hold the ceremony on the deck (the skipper can act as a witness if needed) and then cruise to a quiet cove for a champagne reception. The boat can be decorated with flowers, ribbons, or banners, but check with the charter company first, as some boats do not allow decorations that might damage the upholstery.

For corporate events, the most common request is a client entertainment day. You invite 8-12 clients, cruise to a beach club for lunch, and return in the late afternoon. Some companies book a superyacht for product launches or press events. These require a full crew (captain, steward, chef) and a budget of EUR 10,000 or more per day. The charter company can arrange catering, a DJ, and a photographer on request.

If you are planning an event, book at least 4 weeks in advance. The charter company needs time to prepare the boat, arrange catering, and coordinate with the port authorities. You will also need to pay a non-refundable deposit of 50% to secure the date. Cancellation policies for events are stricter than for standard charters, so read the terms carefully.

Practical Tips for Your Private Yacht Charter in Mandelieu Cannes

Arrive at the port 15 minutes before your departure time. The skipper will be waiting at the boat, but they need to give you a safety briefing and show you around before you leave. If you are late, the skipper may shorten the charter to return on time, as they have a fixed schedule for cleaning and refuelling.

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses. The sun on the water is intense, even on a cloudy day. The reflection from the sea can cause sunburn in 20 minutes. Also bring a towel, swimwear, and a light jacket or windbreaker. The afternoon breeze can be cool, especially in spring and autumn. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The sea is usually calm in the morning, but the afternoon swell can be uncomfortable for some people.

Food and drinks: you can bring your own. There is a supermarket at Port Mandelieu-La Napoule and a larger one in Cannes. Most boats have a fridge and a cooler. If you want a catered lunch, order it when you book. The charter company can arrange a platter of local produce (cheese, charcuterie, olives, bread) for around EUR 20-30 per person. For a full hot lunch (grilled fish, salad, dessert), expect to pay EUR 50-80 per person. Drinks are usually not included, so bring your own wine, beer, and soft drinks.

Children are welcome on private charters. The skipper will provide life jackets in children’s sizes. However, children under 12 must wear a life jacket at all times on deck, and the skipper may restrict swimming in deep water. If you have very young children (under 3), check with the charter company first, as some boats do not have suitable safety equipment.

intro:
You want to hire a boat in Antalya in 2025. Good choice. The Turkish Riviera has clear water, hidden coves, and a coastline that begs to be seen from the sea. BoatHire24 connects you with trusted operators offering everything from small speedboats to superyachts. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you just relax and enjoy the sun.

bodyHtml:
What Is Included in Your Antalya Boat Hire?

When you book a boat through BoatHire24, the base price typically covers the vessel, the skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and basic safety equipment. Some packages include soft drinks, snacks, or a light lunch. Others are bare-bones, and you bring your own provisions. Always check the listing details before you pay.

The skipper is not a tour guide. They drive the boat, handle docking, and keep you safe. They can recommend a route, but you decide where to go. Want to anchor off a quiet beach for three hours? Fine. Want to visit every cove on the coast? Also fine. The skipper works for you.

Most charters run from 10:00 to 18:00. Half-day options (four hours) exist for smaller boats. Sunset cruises are popular in summer, usually 17:00 to 21:00. Overnight charters are available for larger yachts with cabins. If you want to sleep on the boat, book a vessel with proper berths and a galley.

Departure Ports for Antalya Boat Hire

Antalya has several marinas and departure points. The main one is Antalya Marina (Kaleiçi Yat Limanı), right next to the old town. It is convenient if you are staying in the city centre. From here you can head west towards Kemer or east towards Lara Beach.

Kemer Marina is about 40 km southwest of Antalya. It is a good option if you want to explore the Olympos area or the Chimera flames. The marina is modern, with restaurants and shops. Parking is easier than in Antalya city centre.

Other ports include Belek (for the golf resorts), Side (for ancient ruins), and Alanya (further east, about 120 km from Antalya). Each port has its own character. Side is quieter. Alanya has a lively nightlife scene. Choose the port that matches your holiday vibe.

Boat Types Available for Antalya Boat Hire

Motor yachts dominate the Antalya market. They range from 8-metre day cruisers to 25-metre luxury vessels. A typical 12-metre motor yacht costs from around EUR 600 per day in low season. It sleeps four to six people and has a small cabin, a bathroom, and a sun deck.

Catamarans are less common but available. They offer more deck space and stability. A 40-foot catamaran can carry up to 12 guests comfortably. Prices start from about EUR 800 per day. Sailing yachts are rare in Antalya because the wind is unreliable. If you insist on sailing, look for a 35-40 foot monohull with a good engine.

Speedboats and RIBs are popular for small groups. A 6-metre RIB with a 150 HP engine can hold six people. It is fast, basic, and fun. Expect to pay from EUR 250 for a half day. No toilet, no cabin, just speed. Good for a few hours of water sports.

Gulet charters are a Turkish specialty. These wooden sailing vessels are designed for comfort, not speed. A typical gulet is 20-30 metres long, has multiple cabins, and a crew of two or three. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 per day for a standard gulet. Luxury gulets with jacuzzis and air conditioning cost more.

Pricing Guidance for Antalya Boat Hire

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. In April and May (low season), a 10-metre motor yacht costs from EUR 400 per day. In July and August (peak season), the same boat costs from EUR 700 per day. Superyachts over 30 metres are price on request, usually EUR 5,000 per day and up.

Fuel is included in most standard charters for a typical day route (around 30-50 nautical miles). If you want to go further, expect a surcharge. Some operators charge extra for water toys like jet skis or inflatable slides. Ask before you book.

Deposits are common. Expect to pay a refundable deposit of EUR 200-500 for smaller boats, or more for larger yachts. This covers damage. You get it back if you return the boat in good condition. Payment is usually by bank transfer or credit card. Cash is accepted at some marinas.

Best Time for Antalya Boat Hire

The season runs from April to October. May and June are ideal: warm air (25-30 degrees C), warm sea (22-24 degrees C), and fewer tourists. July and August are hot (35-40 degrees C) and crowded. The water is bath-like (28 degrees C). September and October are pleasant, similar to May but with slightly cooler evenings.

Winter charters are possible but rare. The sea is rough, and many boats are in dry dock. If you want a winter boat trip, stick to a large motor yacht with a stabilised hull. The air temperature is 15-20 degrees C, so bring a jacket.

Wind is a factor. The meltemi wind blows from the north in July and August, creating choppy conditions in the afternoon. Morning departures are calmer. If you are prone to seasickness, book a catamaran or a large motor yacht.

Popular Routes for Antalya Boat Hire

The classic route from Antalya Marina goes west to Kemer, stopping at Phaselis (ancient ruins) and Olympos (beach and treehouses). The distance is about 30 nautical miles one way. A full-day charter covers the round trip with a lunch stop at a seaside restaurant.

Another popular route is east to Lara Beach and the Düden Waterfalls. You can anchor near the waterfalls and swim in the spray. The water is fresh, not salt. The cliffs here are dramatic, with caves to explore. This route is shorter, about 15 nautical miles each way.

For a longer trip, head south to the Gulf of Antalya and the island of Üçadalar. The water is crystal clear, and the island has a small beach. This is a good spot for snorkelling. The round trip from Antalya Marina is about 50 nautical miles, so you need a full day and a fast boat.

How to Book Your Antalya Boat Hire

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, enter Antalya as the destination, choose your dates, and select the boat type. You will see a list of available vessels with photos, prices, and details. Click on a boat to see the full description, cancellation policy, and skipper profile.

Once you choose, you pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is due on the day of departure. We send you a confirmation email with the meeting point and skipper contact details. Show up on time, and the skipper takes it from there.

Cancellation policies vary. Most operators offer a full refund if you cancel 7 days before the charter. Within 7 days, you may lose the deposit. Read the policy before you book. Weather cancellations are handled differently: if the coast guard closes the port, you get a full refund or a reschedule.

Who Is Antalya Boat Hire For?

It is for couples who want a romantic sunset cruise. It is for families with kids who want a safe day on the water. It is for groups of friends who want to party on a gulet. It is for solo travellers who want to see the coast from a different angle.

It is not for people who want to drive the boat themselves. Every charter includes a skipper. If you want a licence-free boat, check the details. In Turkey, boats under 10 metres and 15 HP can be rented without a licence. But most charters on BoatHire24 include a skipper for safety and convenience.

If you are a first-time boat renter, the process is simple. The skipper handles everything. You just enjoy the ride. If you are an experienced sailor, you can request a bareboat charter (no skipper) for certain vessels. Contact us directly for that option.

Local Tips for Your Antalya Boat Hire

Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a towel. The sun is intense, especially in summer. The boat has shade, but you will want to sit in the sun at some point. Bring a swimsuit and a change of clothes. You will get wet.

Food and drink: some boats include a meal, but most do not. You can bring your own picnic or stop at a waterfront restaurant. The skipper will recommend places. Turkish food is excellent: fresh fish, meze, and grilled meat. Try the local gözleme (stuffed flatbread) if you stop at a beach cafe.

Cash is useful for tips and extras. The skipper will appreciate a tip (10-15% of the charter fee is standard). Some marinas have ATMs, but not all. Bring enough cash for the day.

Language: most skippers speak basic English. Turkish is the local language. Learn a few phrases: merhaba (hello), teşekkürler (thank you), and lütfen (please). It goes a long way.

Why Book Through BoatHire24?

We are a marketplace, not a rental company. We list boats from multiple operators in Antalya. You compare prices, read reviews, and book online. We handle the payment and communication. You get a single point of contact if something goes wrong.

We have been operating in Marbella since 2018 and expanded to Antalya in 2024. The same standards apply: verified boats, licensed skippers, transparent pricing. No bait-and-switch. No hidden fees. If a boat is not available, we tell you before you pay.

For more tips on boat rental, read our blog. For the full range of options, visit the BoatHire24 homepage.

Antalya Boat Hire for Water Sports Enthusiasts

If you want more than just cruising, many Antalya boat hire options include water toys. A typical motor yacht or gulet might come with a paddleboard, a kayak, or snorkelling gear. Some operators offer jet skis as an add-on, costing from EUR 150 per hour. The water around Kemer and the coves near Phaselis is calm and clear, ideal for wakeboarding or water skiing. Ask the skipper if they have a tow rope and a spotter. You can also rent a RIB specifically for water sports. A 6-metre RIB with a 200 HP engine can pull a wakeboarder easily. Expect to pay from EUR 350 for a half day, including fuel and the skipper. The best spots for water sports are the sheltered bays near Çıralı and the open water off Lara Beach. The wind picks up in the afternoon, so morning sessions are smoother.

Antalya Boat Hire for Sunset Cruises

A sunset cruise is a popular choice in Antalya, especially for couples. The sun sets over the Mediterranean around 20:00 in summer, painting the sky orange and pink. Most sunset charters depart at 17:00 and return at 21:00. You can book a private motor yacht for two, from around EUR 300 for the evening. Some operators include a bottle of wine and a fruit platter. The best route is from Antalya Marina west towards the cliffs of the old town. You anchor off the Kaleiçi coast and watch the sunset from the water. Alternatively, head to the Düden Waterfalls for a dramatic backdrop. The spray from the falls catches the light, creating rainbows. For a more intimate experience, book a gulet with a deck and a cabin. You can stay overnight if you choose an overnight charter. Prices for a sunset cruise vary by boat size and inclusions. Always confirm what is provided before you pay.

Antalya Boat Hire for Large Groups

If you are travelling with a group of 10 or more, a gulet or a large motor yacht is the best fit. A 25-metre gulet can carry up to 20 guests comfortably. The deck has seating, a dining area, and sun loungers. The crew includes a skipper, a cook, and a deckhand. Lunch is typically included, featuring fresh Turkish meze, grilled fish or meat, and salad. Prices for a full-day gulet charter start from around EUR 1,800 in low season and EUR 2,800 in peak season. For a group of 15, that is about EUR 120 to EUR 190 per person. You can also rent a catamaran for groups. A 45-foot catamaran holds up to 12 guests and offers more stability than a monohull. The wide deck is perfect for socialising. Expect to pay from EUR 1,200 per day for a catamaran. Large groups should book early, especially in July and August, as the best boats are reserved months in advance.

Antalya Boat Hire for Fishing Trips

Antalya boat hire is not just for cruising. Many operators offer fishing charters. The Mediterranean around Antalya is rich with species like sea bass, bream, and mackerel. Some skippers specialise in deep-sea fishing for tuna or swordfish. A typical fishing charter lasts four to six hours. The boat is equipped with rods, reels, bait, and a fish finder. The skipper knows the best spots, often near the underwater reefs off Kemer or the deep waters south of Üçadalar. Prices for a fishing charter start from around EUR 300 for a half day on a small motor boat. For a larger yacht with a professional fishing setup, expect to pay from EUR 600. Catch and release is common, but some operators let you keep your fish. The crew can clean and fillet it for you. You can then take it to a restaurant to be cooked. Check the local regulations on fishing licences. Most charter operators handle this for you.

Antalya Boat Hire for Families with Children

Families with children need a boat that is safe and comfortable. Catamarans are a good choice because they are stable and have plenty of deck space. A 40-foot catamaran has a net trampoline at the bow, which kids love. The shallow draft means you can anchor close to the beach. Motor yachts with a swim platform are also good. Children can easily climb back on board after swimming. Most skippers are experienced with kids and will adjust the route to include shallow, calm bays. The best spots for families are the beaches near Phaselis and the coves around Çıralı. The water is clear and shallow, ideal for young swimmers. Some boats include snorkelling gear for children. Bring your own life jackets for small kids, as the boat may only have adult sizes. A full-day charter for a family of four on a 10-metre motor yacht costs from around EUR 500 in low season. Pack plenty of snacks, drinks, and sun protection.

Antalya Boat Hire for Special Occasions

Birthdays, anniversaries, and proposals are common reasons to rent a boat in Antalya. The setting is dramatic: the turquoise water, the cliffs, and the old town in the background. For a proposal, book a sunset cruise on a private motor yacht. Some operators offer a dedicated service, including a photographer and a bottle of champagne. Prices for a proposal package start from around EUR 400. For a birthday party, a gulet is ideal. You can bring your own music, food, and decorations. The crew will help set up. A full-day gulet charter for a party of 10 costs from EUR 1,500. For an anniversary, a half-day catamaran cruise with a private chef is a good option. The chef prepares a multi-course meal while you relax. Expect to pay from EUR 800 for this. Always tell the operator in advance if it is a special occasion. They can arrange extras like flowers, balloons, or a cake.

Antalya Boat Hire for Exploring Ancient Ruins

Antalya is surrounded by ancient sites, and many are best seen from the water. The most famous is Phaselis, a Lycian city built on a peninsula near Kemer. You can anchor off the beach and swim to the shore. The ruins include a theatre, a bathhouse, and a Roman aqueduct. The entrance fee is about EUR 5 per person. Another site is Olympos, just south of Phaselis. The ruins are set in a forested valley, with a river running through them. You can anchor nearby and walk up to the site. The Chimera flames, eternal fires burning from the rocks, are a short hike from Olympos. For a longer trip, head east to Side. The ancient city has a well-preserved theatre and a temple of Apollo. The marina in Side is small, but you can anchor offshore and take a tender to the beach. A boat hire that includes a skipper who knows the history is a bonus. Some operators offer guided tours of the ruins as part of the charter. Prices for a full-day charter to Phaselis start from around EUR 500.

h1: Antalya Yacht Charter: Luxury Boat Rental in Turkey
intro:
You want a private boat on the Turquoise Coast, with a licensed skipper who knows every cove and beach club. An Antalya yacht charter gives you exactly that: a motor yacht, catamaran or sailing boat, crew included, for a day or a week. No hidden fees, no surprises. You just show up, step aboard, and let the captain handle the navigation while you sunbathe, swim and eat fresh meze.

BoatHire24 connects you with trusted operators in Antalya, from Kemer to Side, with departures from the main marinas. Prices start around EUR 1,500 for a 10-metre motor yacht for a full day, and go up to EUR 15,000 for a 30-metre luxury yacht with a crew of six. Every booking includes a professional skipper, fuel for the itinerary, and basic safety equipment. You pay for food, drinks and any extras like jet skis or water toys.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in an Antalya Yacht Charter

When you book through BoatHire24, the standard package covers the yacht, a licensed skipper, fuel for the agreed route, and all safety gear. The skipper is a local professional who speaks English and knows the best swimming spots, like the coves near Olympos or the sunken city of Kekova. You do not need a boating licence or any previous experience. You just relax.

Extras you can add on request: a hostess or chef, food and drinks (from a simple lunch to a full Turkish banquet), water toys (paddleboards, snorkel gear, jet skis), and transfers from your hotel to the marina. Most operators also offer a photographer or drone footage for an extra fee. Prices vary, so ask for a custom quote when you book.

For a typical day charter, you meet at the marina at 09:30, get a safety briefing, and then cruise to three or four different stops. Lunch is usually served around 13:00 at anchor in a quiet bay. You return to port by 17:00 or 18:00. Full-day charters often run 8 to 10 hours. Half-day options are available from EUR 800, but they limit you to one or two stops.

Ports and Departure Points for Your Charter

Antalya has several main marinas. The most popular is Antalya Marina, right in the city centre near the old town (Kaleiçi). From here you can head west to the cliffs of Lara or east to the beaches of Konyaalti. Another major departure point is Kemer Marina, about 40 minutes south, which gives you quick access to the Olympos and Çıralı areas, including the Chimaera flames. Side Marina, further east, is ideal if you want to explore the Manavgat River or the ancient ruins of Side itself.

Other options include Çamyuva Marina, a small but well-equipped harbour near Kemer, and Finike Marina, which is quieter and closer to the Kekova region. For a truly exclusive experience, you can charter from a private dock at one of the five-star resorts along the coast, like the Maxx Royal or the Rixos. The skipper will pick you up from the hotel jetty. Prices for these private pickups are usually EUR 200 to EUR 500 extra, depending on distance.

If you are staying in Belek, the nearest marina is Antalya Marina, about 30 minutes by taxi. For Alanya, you can use Alanya Marina, though that is technically a different region. BoatHire24 covers the whole Antalya province, so check the search page for all available ports.

Types of Boats Available for Antalya Yacht Charter

The fleet in Antalya is diverse. Motor yachts are the most common, ranging from 10 metres to 35 metres. A 12-metre motor yacht sleeps 6 to 8 guests and costs from EUR 1,500 per day. For a 20-metre luxury motor yacht with a flybridge, prices start around EUR 4,000 per day. Catamarans are popular for their stability and space, especially for families. A 14-metre catamaran costs from EUR 2,500 per day and can carry up to 12 guests.

Sailing yachts are available too, from 12 to 18 metres. They are cheaper than motor yachts of the same size, starting at EUR 1,200 per day, but they are slower and more dependent on wind. If you want speed, consider a RIB or speedboat, from 6 to 9 metres, costing from EUR 600 for a half-day. These are great for a quick trip to a nearby cove or for watersports. Fishing boats are also available, equipped with rods and a guide, from EUR 800 per day.

Superyachts over 30 metres are available on request, with prices from EUR 10,000 per day. These come with a full crew, including a chef, stewardess and deckhands. You can also rent a gulet, a traditional wooden sailing yacht, which is a classic Turkish charter option. Gulets range from 18 to 35 metres and cost from EUR 3,000 per day. They are slower but offer a lot of deck space and a traditional feel.

Pricing Guidance for Antalya Yacht Charters

Prices depend on the boat size, season, duration and extras. For a full-day charter (8 hours) in high season (June to September), expect to pay: 10-12 metre motor yacht EUR 1,500-2,500; 15-18 metre motor yacht EUR 3,000-5,000; 10-12 metre sailing yacht EUR 1,200-2,000; 14-16 metre catamaran EUR 2,500-4,000; 6-8 metre RIB EUR 600-1,200. In low season (October to May), prices drop by 20-30%. Week-long charters are priced per week, from EUR 8,000 for a 12-metre motor yacht to EUR 50,000 for a 30-metre superyacht.

Additional costs: food and drinks (EUR 50-150 per person per day depending on menu), fuel for longer itineraries (usually included for standard routes, but extra for long distances), marina fees (EUR 50-200 per night if you overnight), and tips (10-15% of the charter fee is customary). Always confirm what is included before booking. BoatHire24 shows the base price and gives you a breakdown of extras.

To compare options, use the BoatHire24 homepage and filter by boat type, price range and date. You will see real-time availability and can request a quote directly from the operator.

Best Seasons for an Antalya Yacht Charter

The sailing season in Antalya runs from April to November. The best months are May, June, September and October, when the weather is warm (25-30 degrees C) but not scorching, and the sea is calm. July and August are the hottest, with temperatures reaching 35 degrees C, and the sea is a pleasant 27 degrees C. These months are also the busiest, so book at least 2-3 months in advance. Winter charters are possible from December to March, but the weather is cooler (15-20 degrees C) and the sea can be rough. Prices are lower, though, and you will have the coast almost to yourself.

If you want to see the Loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) nesting, visit in June or July at Iztuzu Beach near Dalyan, which is a 2-hour cruise from Antalya. For dolphin spotting, the best time is April to June, when they are most active in the bays. The water visibility for snorkelling and diving is best in August and September, with up to 30 metres of clarity.

Wind conditions: the prevailing wind is the meltemi, which blows from the north in summer, usually light to moderate (force 3-4). This is fine for sailing yachts, but motor yachts are unaffected. In winter, storms can occur, so check the forecast. Your skipper will always make safety decisions based on conditions.

How to Book an Antalya Yacht Charter

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, enter your dates, number of guests, and preferred boat type. You will see a list of available yachts with photos, specifications and prices. Click on any listing to see the full details, including the itinerary, what is included, and the operator's rating. You can then send a booking request or ask a question. The operator will confirm availability within 24 hours. Payment is usually 50% deposit at booking and 50% cash on the day, or full prepayment by bank transfer or credit card. Some operators accept PayPal.

For custom itineraries, such as a multi-day cruise from Antalya to Fethiye or Kas, contact us directly. We can arrange a tailor-made charter with a dedicated skipper. The BoatHire24 blog has detailed guides on popular routes, including the Lycian Coast and the Turquoise Coast, with tips on mooring spots and restaurants.

Cancellation policy: most operators offer free cancellation up to 14 days before the charter, and a 50% refund up to 7 days before. After that, no refund. We recommend travel insurance that covers cancellation. On the day, if the weather is unsafe, the operator may cancel or reschedule at no extra cost.

Who Is an Antalya Yacht Charter For

An Antalya yacht charter suits couples, families, groups of friends, and corporate events. Couples often choose a romantic sunset cruise on a motor yacht or gulet, with dinner and wine. Families with children prefer catamarans for their stability and space, plus the option of a hostess to help with kids. Groups of 8 to 12 friends book a 15-metre motor yacht for a party with music and swimming. Corporate groups use superyachts for client entertainment or team-building, with full catering and AV equipment.

If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter, but these are rare. Most charters are private. For special occasions like birthdays, anniversaries or proposals, many operators offer decorations, a photographer and a cake. Just let them know in advance.

No boating licence is ever required. The skipper handles everything. You just need to be on time at the marina, bring sunscreen, a hat, swimwear, and a camera. The crew will take care of the rest.

Local Highlights and Hidden Gems on Your Charter

Antalya's coastline is packed with natural and historical attractions. From the sea, you can see the Taurus Mountains rising behind the city, the ancient city of Phaselis with its three harbours, and the Olympos ruins with the eternal Chimaera flames. A popular stop is the cove at Adrasan, a quiet beach with turquoise water. Another is the sunken city of Kekova, where you can see ancient ruins under the water through a glass-bottom boat or by snorkelling.

For lunch, your skipper will recommend a bayside restaurant, often only accessible by boat. These serve fresh fish, grilled octopus, and meze like hummus and baba ganoush. Some of the best are at Çıralı, where you can eat under pine trees, or at the beach club near Kemer, which has a private dock. For a more upscale experience, book a table at the restaurant in the Antalya Marina, which has a view of the yachts.

Wildlife: you will likely see sea turtles, especially around the Kekova and Çıralı areas. Dolphins are common in the open sea, and your skipper can slow down so you can watch them. In spring, you might see migrating birds like storks and herons along the coast.

Safety and Regulations for Antalya Yacht Charters

All yachts on BoatHire24 are licensed and insured. The skipper holds a valid Turkish captain's license and has passed safety training. The boat is equipped with life jackets, a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher, flares and a VHF radio. For longer charters, there is also an EPIRB (emergency beacon) and a life raft. The skipper gives a safety briefing at the start of the trip.

Turkish maritime law requires that all passengers be listed on the manifest. The operator will ask for your passport details before departure. Children must wear life jackets on deck, and the skipper may restrict swimming if the current is strong. Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper cannot drink. You can bring your own drinks or buy them from the operator.

In case of bad weather, the skipper will decide to alter the route or stay in port. Your safety is the priority. If the charter is cancelled due to weather, you get a full refund or a rescheduled date.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Antalya Yacht Charter

BoatHire24 is a marketplace that vets all operators. We check the boat's licence, insurance and condition, and we read customer reviews. You get transparent pricing, no hidden fees, and direct communication with the operator. We are based in Marbella, but we have expanded to Turkey because we know the quality of the yachts and the professionalism of the crews. Our team speaks English, Spanish and Turkish, so you can get help in your language.

We also offer a price-match guarantee: if you find the same boat and itinerary cheaper elsewhere, we will match it. And we have a dedicated support line during your charter, so if anything goes wrong, you can call us immediately. We want you to have a stress-free day on the water.

To start planning your Antalya yacht charter, visit our search page and explore the options. Or read our blog for detailed itineraries and tips. For any questions, contact us via the website. We will help you find the perfect boat for your budget and preferences.
