title: Antalya Catamaran Hire: Private Boat Trips Guide
metaDescription: Antalya catamaran hire for private boat trips with a skipper. Compare prices, ports, and boat options on the Costa del Sol marketplace.
h1: Antalya Catamaran Hire: Private Boat Trips Guide
intro:
If you are searching for Antalya catamaran hire, you are probably picturing a lazy afternoon on the Turkish Riviera, not a boat in Marbella. But here is the thing: we are BoatHire24, and we operate on the Costa del Sol, Spain. So if you actually want a catamaran in Antalya, you will need a different site. However, if you want a catamaran hire experience that rivals Antalya, turquoise water, private skipper, no crowds, then stick around. We have catamarans in Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, and Estepona, and they are ready for your private boat trip.

This guide covers everything: what you get with a catamaran charter, which ports to depart from, typical prices, and how to book. No waffle, just the facts. And yes, you can hire a catamaran for a day, a sunset cruise, or a week-long voyage along the Costa del Sol.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Hire

When you book a catamaran through BoatHire24, you get a private boat with a licensed skipper. That means you do not need a licence, and you do not have to steer. The skipper handles the navigation, anchoring, and safety. You just relax, swim, eat, and drink. Most catamarans come with a sound system, a sun deck, a shaded cockpit, and a galley. Some have a grill, a paddleboard, or snorkelling gear. Fuel, port fees, and VAT are usually included in the price, but check the listing details. Crew gratuity is not included, so budget around 10-15% of the charter fee if you want to tip.

Departure Ports for Catamaran Trips

You can start your catamaran trip from several ports along the Costa del Sol. BoatHire24 lists catamarans in Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. Puerto Banús is the most glamorous, with superyachts and designer shops. Marbella Marina is more laid-back, close to the old town. Cabopino is quieter, near the sand dunes of Artola. Estepona offers a charming old town and a long promenade. Sotogrande is exclusive, with luxury villas and a golf resort. Benalmádena has a lively marina with restaurants and bars. Choose your port based on your vibe and where you are staying.

Boat Options: Catamarans vs Other Types

Catamarans are stable, spacious, and great for groups. They have two hulls, so they do not heel like a monohull sailing yacht. That makes them ideal for people who get seasick. You can walk around without holding on. Most catamarans on our platform are 35 to 50 feet long, with capacity for 8 to 12 guests. They have a shallow draft, so you can get close to beaches and coves. If you want something faster, a motor yacht or a RIB might suit you better. For a more traditional sailing experience, a sailing yacht is the way to go. But for pure comfort and space, a catamaran is hard to beat.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Charters

Prices for catamaran hire depend on the size, age, amenities, and season. A half-day charter (4 hours) starts from around EUR 800 to EUR 1,200. A full day (8 hours) ranges from EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. For a sunset cruise (2-3 hours), expect to pay EUR 500 to EUR 800. High season (July and August) is the most expensive. Shoulder seasons (May, June, September, October) are cheaper. Winter charters are possible but less common, with lower demand and prices. Always ask for a quote for your specific dates and group size. We do not list exact prices on the site because they change with availability and demand.

Best Time of Year for Catamaran Hire

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with over 300 sunny days per year. The best time for a catamaran trip is May through October. In May and June, the water is warm, the air is around 25-30 degrees C, and the beaches are not too crowded. July and August are peak season: hot (30-35 degrees C), busy, and higher prices. September and October are still warm, with water temperatures around 22-25 degrees C, and fewer tourists. Winter charters are possible on calm days, but the water is cooler and the weather is less predictable. If you are flexible, aim for late May or early September for the best balance of weather and price.

How to Book a Catamaran on BoatHire24

Booking is straightforward. Go to our search page, filter by boat type (catamaran), port, and date. You will see a list of available boats with photos, specs, and prices. Click on one to see the full details. Then send an enquiry with your preferred date, group size, and any special requests. We will confirm availability and send you a quote. Once you accept, we handle the booking and payment. You get a confirmation with the skipper's contact details. On the day, you meet the skipper at the port, and off you go. Simple.

Who Is a Catamaran Charter For

Catamaran charters work for families, couples, groups of friends, and corporate events. They are especially good for families with young children because the boat is stable and has plenty of space. Couples can enjoy a romantic sunset cruise with champagne. Groups of friends can party, swim, and sunbathe. Corporate groups use catamarans for team-building days or client entertainment. The skipper takes care of everything, so you can focus on having a good time. If you have a specific occasion, like a birthday or anniversary, let us know and we can arrange extras like catering, decorations, or a photographer.

Local Spots to Visit on a Catamaran

From Puerto Banús, you can cruise to the Marbella coastline, anchor near the dunes of Cabopino, or head to the cliffs of Cala del Faro. From Estepona, you can explore the coast towards Gibraltar, where you might spot dolphins in the Strait of Gibraltar. From Sotogrande, you can sail to the mouth of the Río Guadiaro. From Benalmádena, you can head to the beaches of Torremolinos or the port of Málaga. Most skippers know the best coves and beaches for swimming and snorkelling. They will also suggest a good spot for lunch, either on board or at a beach club.

Frequently Asked Questions

We get a lot of questions about catamaran hire. Below are the most common ones, with straight answers. If you have more, check our blog or contact us directly.

Catamaran vs Motor Yacht: Which Is Right for You

If you are torn between a catamaran and a motor yacht, think about your priorities. Catamarans offer more deck space for the same length, so a 40-foot catamaran feels bigger than a 40-foot motor yacht. They are also more fuel-efficient, which keeps running costs lower. The shallow draft means you can anchor closer to shore at places like Cala del Faro or the sandbanks of Cabopino. Motor yachts are faster, so you can cover more distance in a day, say from Puerto Banús to Estepona and back. They also have a more traditional yacht aesthetic. If your group includes people prone to seasickness, the catamaran wins every time. For a speedier, more glamorous vibe, go with a motor yacht.

What to Expect from the Skipper on Your Catamaran

Every catamaran hire through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. These skippers are local, experienced, and speak English and Spanish. They know the coastline, the wind patterns, and the best spots for swimming. You do not need to plan the route, but you can discuss it with them. If you want to spend the morning near the dunes of Artola and the afternoon at a beach club in Puerto Banús, they will make it happen. They also handle mooring, anchoring, and any safety issues. Some skippers offer a light commentary about the landmarks, like the La Concha mountain or the old town of Estepona. They are not tour guides, but they will point out interesting things. If you want a more interactive experience, ask questions.

Catamaran Hire for Large Groups: Capacity and Comfort

Catamarans are the best option for groups of 8 to 12 people. The layout usually includes a large saloon, a forward sun deck, and a shaded cockpit. Some catamarans have a flybridge, which gives you a higher vantage point. For groups larger than 12, you may need a bigger catamaran or two boats. On our platform, the largest catamarans are around 50 feet and can take up to 12 guests. If you have a party of 15 or more, consider a motor yacht or a superyacht. For a group of 6 to 8, a 38-foot catamaran is ideal. It has enough space for everyone to spread out without feeling cramped. The skipper usually stays in the helm area, so the rest of the boat is yours.

Sunset Catamaran Cruises: Timing and Atmosphere

A sunset cruise on a catamaran is a popular choice for couples and small groups. The best time is 2 to 3 hours before sunset, usually from 17:00 to 20:00 in summer. You sail out to a calm spot, anchor, and watch the sun dip behind the mountains. The light turns golden, then orange, then pink. The water reflects the colours. Most sunset cruises include a glass of cava or champagne. Some catamarans have a grill, so you can have a barbecue on board. The price for a sunset charter is lower than a full day, from around EUR 500 to EUR 800. You need to book in advance, especially in July and August, because these slots fill up quickly. The skipper will choose a spot with an unobstructed view of the horizon.

Catamaran Hire for Fishing: What You Need to Know

If you want to combine catamaran hire with fishing, you can, but catamarans are not purpose-built fishing boats. They are stable, which helps when you are casting lines, but they are slower than a dedicated fishing boat. The shallow draft allows you to get close to rocky areas where fish gather, like the cliffs near Cala del Faro or the coast of Benalmádena. You can bring your own fishing gear, or some catamarans provide basic tackle. The skipper will know the best spots for sea bass, bream, or mackerel. For serious sportfishing, a RIB or a motor yacht is better. But for a relaxed day of fishing with swimming and lunch, a catamaran works fine. Check with the skipper beforehand if you want to keep the catch.

Catamaran Hire with Catering: Food and Drink Options

Most catamaran charters offer a catering option. You can bring your own food and drink, or you can order a catering package. Typical options include a Mediterranean lunch with paella, grilled fish, salads, and fruit. Some catamarans have a barbecue on the aft deck. Drinks can be soft, beer, wine, or cava. A full catering package for a day charter costs around EUR 30 to EUR 50 per person, depending on the menu. If you have dietary restrictions, let us know when you book. You can also arrange for a birthday cake, a cheese platter, or a champagne breakfast. The skipper can recommend a good catering company. Alternatively, you can stop at a beach club for lunch, like the ones in Cabopino or Estepona.

Catamaran Hire in Low Season: Winter and Early Spring

Catamaran hire is possible in winter and early spring, but the experience is different. From November to March, the weather is cooler, around 15-20 degrees C. The water is colder, so swimming is less appealing. The sea can be choppy, especially in the Strait of Gibraltar area. However, the upside is lower prices and fewer boats on the water. You can often get a catamaran for half the high-season rate. The days are shorter, so a half-day charter makes more sense. The light is softer, and you might see dolphins more frequently. If you are in Marbella for the winter, a catamaran trip can still be enjoyable, especially if you stay in the sheltered coves. Check the weather forecast and book a catamaran with a heated cabin if possible.

How to Choose the Right Catamaran for Your Group

When you browse catamarans on our search page, look at the length, age, and amenities. A newer catamaran will have better sound systems, more comfortable seating, and cleaner bathrooms. Older catamarans are cheaper but may show wear. Check the number of cabins if you plan to stay overnight. For a day charter, you only need a saloon and a bathroom. For a week-long charter, you need cabins and a galley. Look at the photos carefully. Some catamarans have a trampoline net at the bow, which is great for sunbathing. Others have a fixed sun deck. The flybridge is a plus if you want a panoramic view. Read the description for details about the sound system, the grill, and the water toys. If you have questions, send an enquiry.

Catamaran Hire for Special Occasions: Birthdays, Anniversaries, Proposals

Catamarans are a popular choice for celebrations. For a birthday, you can bring decorations, a cake, and music. The skipper can help with a playlist. For an anniversary, a sunset cruise with champagne and strawberries is a classic. For a proposal, the skipper can anchor in a secluded cove at sunset. Some catamarans have a photographer available. You can arrange for a private chef to prepare a meal on board. The cost for extras varies, but expect to pay around EUR 100 to EUR 300 for decorations, catering upgrades, or a photographer. Let us know the occasion when you book, and we will help you set it up. The team at BoatHire24 has experience with these requests, so do not hesitate to ask.

Catamaran Hire and Environmental Considerations

The Costa del Sol is a protected marine area in parts. When you hire a catamaran, the skipper follows environmental guidelines. You cannot anchor in seagrass meadows, and you must not disturb wildlife. Dolphins are common in the Strait of Gibraltar, and the skipper will keep a respectful distance. You should not feed them or throw rubbish overboard. Most catamarans have a waste tank, and the skipper will dispose of waste properly at the port. If you want to be more eco-friendly, choose a catamaran with a hybrid engine or solar panels. These are rare but available. You can also bring reusable water bottles and avoid single-use plastics. The skipper will appreciate it, and the marine life will thank you.

Catamaran Hire for Non-Swimmers: Safety and Comfort

If someone in your group cannot swim, a catamaran is still a good choice. The boat is stable, and the deck has railings. Life jackets are available for all guests, including children. The skipper will give a safety briefing at the start. You can stay on board while others swim, or you can use the paddleboard or snorkel gear near the boat. The water in the coves is usually calm and shallow, so even non-swimmers can wade in with a life jacket. The skipper will anchor in a spot where the depth is manageable. If you are nervous, tell the skipper. They will keep the boat close to the shore. A catamaran is one of the safest boats for non-swimmers because it does not tip or rock much.

Catamaran Hire and Weather: What Happens in Bad Conditions

The Mediterranean can be unpredictable. If the weather is bad, the skipper has the final say on whether to sail. Safety comes first. If the wind is strong or the sea is rough, the skipper may cancel or change the route. In that case, you can reschedule or get a refund. We do not charge cancellation fees if the skipper cancels due to weather. If you cancel because of bad weather, we will try to find a suitable alternative date. The best months for reliable weather are June to September. In spring and autumn, check the forecast a few days before. If you are flexible, you can book a catamaran on short notice when the weather is good. Our blog has more tips on weather patterns.

title: Antalya Speedboat Rental: Hire Without Licence
metaDescription: Antalya speedboat rental without a licence? Yes. Rent a RIB or day boat from Kemer to Side. Book online with BoatHire24. Prices from EUR 150.
h1: Antalya Speedboat Rental: Hire Without Licence
intro:
You want to rent a speedboat in Antalya without a licence. Good news: you can. Several boats on our platform require no paperwork at all, just a quick safety briefing and a credit card. We cover the whole coast from Kemer to Side, with departure points in Antalya Marina, Kemer, Belek, and Alanya.

Every rental includes a licensed skipper if you want one, but the real draw here is the licence-free day boats. These are small, powerful RIBs and open speedboats that you can drive yourself. Top speed around 30-40 knots, range of 30-40 nautical miles, and enough space for 4-6 people. Prices start from around EUR 150 for a half day.
bodyHtml:
What You Get With a Licence-Free Speedboat Rental in Antalya

The boats available for licence-free rental are mostly RIBs (rigid inflatable boats) or small open motorboats. They come with a 40-100 hp outboard engine, a fuel tank, life jackets, and a basic navigation kit. You get a 15-minute briefing on how to operate the boat, where the no-go zones are, and what to do in an emergency. Then you are free to go.

You do not need an ICC, a VHF licence, or any previous experience. The boat is limited to a certain horsepower and speed by local regulations, but you will still hit 25-35 knots easily. That is fast enough for water sports, exploring coves, or just feeling the wind in your hair. Bring sunscreen.

Departure Ports for Antalya Speedboat Hire

You can pick up your boat from several marinas along the coast. The main ones are:

  • Antalya Marina (Kaleiçi): Right in the city centre, near the old town. Easy to reach by taxi or on foot if you are staying in Lara or Konyaalti.
  • Kemer Marina: About 40 km west of Antalya. Popular for trips to Phaselis, Olympos, and the three-island route.
  • Belek Marina: Near the golf resorts and the Kadriye area. Good for a quick blast along the coast to Side or Manavgat.
  • Alanya Marina: Further east. Ideal if you are based in Alanya or Mahmutlar. You can head towards Dim Çayı or the ancient city of Syedra.

Each marina has a fuel station, a small shop, and parking. You need to return the boat with the same fuel level you started with, or pay for what you used. Most operators accept credit cards for the deposit.

Boats Available: RIBs, Speedboats, and Day Boats

The fleet for licence-free rentals is limited to boats under a certain size and power. Here is what you can expect:

  • RIB 4.5m-5.5m: 40-90 hp, seats 4-5 people. Top speed around 30 knots. Good for a couple or a small family.
  • Open speedboat 5m-6m: 60-115 hp, seats 5-6 people. More space, a bit more stable. Still licence-free.
  • Day boat 6m-7m: Some models have a small cabin or a sun pad. These may require a skipper if over a certain power, but many are still licence-free. Check the listing.

All boats are serviced regularly and have valid safety equipment. You will be asked to sign a damage waiver or leave a refundable deposit (typically EUR 300-500) which you get back if you do not crash into anything.

Pricing Guidance for Antalya Speedboat Rental

Prices vary by season, boat size, and rental duration. Here are rough figures to help you budget:

  • Half day (4 hours): from around EUR 150 for a small RIB, up to EUR 300 for a larger speedboat.
  • Full day (8 hours): from EUR 250 to EUR 500.
  • Fuel: Not usually included. Expect to pay EUR 50-100 extra depending on how far you go.
  • Deposit: EUR 300-500, refundable.

These are ballpark figures. Actual prices depend on the specific boat and the time of year. July and August are peak season, so expect a 20-30% premium. Book early.

For exact prices, check the listings on BoatHire24.

Best Time of Year for Speedboat Hire in Antalya

The season runs from April to October. The water is warm enough to swim from May to September. July and August are hot (35-40°C), so morning or late afternoon trips are best. June and September are more comfortable, with sea temperatures around 25°C.

If you come in April or October, expect cooler air (20-25°C) and possibly some wind. The sea is still calm enough for a speedboat, but you might want a jacket. Winter rentals are possible but less common, and many operators close from November to March.

For the best balance of weather and price, aim for May, June, or September.

What to See on Your Speedboat Trip

Antalya's coastline is full of hidden coves, ancient ruins, and clear blue water. Here are some routes:

  • From Antalya Marina: Head west to Konyaalti Beach, then continue to the Beydağları coast. Stop at Çıralı or Olympos for a swim. About 20 NM one way.
  • From Kemer: The classic three-island trip: Phaselis, Olympos, and the sunken city. You can also go to the ancient port of Andriake. 15-25 NM round trip.
  • From Belek: Head east to Side. Visit the Temple of Apollo from the water. Then go up the Manavgat River if the water level allows. 20-30 NM.
  • From Alanya: Go west to the Dim River mouth, or east to the Gazipaşa coast. The water is clear and quiet. 15-20 NM.

All these routes have plenty of spots to anchor, swim, and have a picnic. Bring snorkel gear.

Who Is This For?

Licence-free speedboat rental is perfect for:

  • Tourists who want a few hours of freedom on the water without organising a skipper.
  • Families with older children (most boats have a minimum age of 18 to drive, but younger passengers are fine).
  • Groups of friends looking for a fun day out. Six people max on most boats.
  • Couples who want a private trip to a secluded bay.

It is not ideal if you want to go far offshore, carry a lot of luggage, or need a toilet on board. For longer trips or more comfort, consider a motor yacht with a skipper. Check our search page to filter by boat type.

How to Book Your Antalya Speedboat Rental

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward:

  1. Go to BoatHire24 and enter 'Antalya' as your destination.
  2. Filter by 'Licence-Free' under the boat type options.
  3. Pick your dates and rental duration.
  4. Choose a boat that suits your group size and budget.
  5. Pay a deposit online (usually 30-50% of the total). The rest is due on arrival.
  6. Bring your ID or passport on the day. No licence needed.

Cancellation policies vary by operator. Most offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before. Read the terms before you book.

For more tips on renting a boat without a licence, read our blog.

Important Rules and Safety Tips

Even without a licence, you are expected to follow basic rules:

  • Stay within the coastal zone. Do not go more than 3-5 NM from shore.
  • No alcohol while driving. Zero tolerance.
  • Wear life jackets at all times, especially when underway.
  • Respect swimming areas and other boats. Speed limit near beaches is usually 5 knots.
  • Return the boat on time. Late returns may incur extra charges.

If you have any doubts, ask the operator for a detailed briefing. They will show you the chart and mark the no-go areas.

Why Antalya Is One of the Best Places for a Licence-Free Speedboat

The Turkish Riviera, and Antalya specifically, has a legal carve-out that allows tourists to rent small powerboats without any paperwork. That is not the case in many Mediterranean countries. In Spain, for example, you generally need a licence for anything over 15 hp. In Greece, the rules are stricter for non-EU visitors. Turkey keeps it simple: if the boat is under a certain length and power, you can drive it with just a passport and a 15-minute briefing. This makes Antalya a prime destination for spontaneous water fun. You do not need to plan weeks ahead or take a course. You just turn up, pick a boat, and go.

Specific Marina Details: What to Expect at Each Departure Point

Each marina in Antalya has its own character and practical quirks. Antalya Marina (Kaleiçi) is the most convenient if you are staying in the city. It is right next to the old town, so you can grab a simit and coffee before you head out. Parking is limited and expensive (around EUR 10 per day). Kemer Marina is more tourist-oriented, with lots of restaurants and boat tours. The fuel dock is easy to access. Belek Marina is quieter, mostly used by golf tourists. The water is shallower near the shore, so watch your depth. Alanya Marina is the largest of the four, with a dedicated speedboat rental zone near the entrance. All marinas have basic facilities: toilets, a small market, and a cash machine. None have a dedicated speedboat launch ramp for public use, so the boats are kept in the water on moorings or lifted in daily.

Fuel Costs and How to Manage Them

Fuel is the hidden variable in your speedboat rental budget. A typical RIB with a 60 hp engine burns about 15-20 litres per hour at cruising speed. At current Turkish fuel prices (around EUR 1.30 per litre for petrol), that is EUR 20-26 per hour. A full day of active driving could cost you EUR 100-150 in fuel alone. Some operators offer a "fuel included" option at a higher daily rate, which can be worth it if you plan to cover a lot of distance. Others give you the boat with a full tank and ask you to refill before returning. Always ask about the fuel policy before you book. If you are on a tight budget, plan a route that minimises high-speed running. Puttering along at 10-15 knots burns half the fuel of full throttle.

Hidden Costs: Deposits, Insurance, and Extras

Beyond the rental fee and fuel, there are a few other costs to factor in. The refundable deposit is usually EUR 300-500, held as a credit card pre-authorisation. If you damage the boat, the operator will deduct from this. Some operators offer a damage waiver for an extra EUR 30-50 per day, which caps your liability at the deposit amount. That is usually worth taking. Other extras include: a cooler box with ice (EUR 10-15), snorkel gear (EUR 10 per set), a skipper if you want one (EUR 100-150 per day), and a GPS tracker or VHF radio rental (EUR 20-30). If you plan to anchor near a beach club or restaurant, some charge a mooring fee (EUR 10-20). Always ask for a full list of optional extras when you book.

Seasonal Variations: What Changes Month by Month

April: The water is cold (16-18°C). Fewer tourists, lower prices. You can still go out but bring a wetsuit if you want to swim. May: Water warms to 20-22°C. Perfect for a quick dip. Prices are still 20% below peak. June: Ideal. Sea temperature hits 24°C. Air is warm but not scorching. July and August: Peak season. Prices are 30% higher. The sea is 27-29°C. Crowded marinas and busy coves. Book at least two weeks ahead. September: Still warm (26°C water). Crowds thin out after the 15th. Good value. October: Water drops to 22°C. Cooler air. Some operators close mid-month. November to March: Most rental companies shut down. A few may rent on request, but the weather is unpredictable. The sea can be rough.

Best Routes for Beginners and Nervous Drivers

If you have never driven a boat before, stick to sheltered waters. From Antalya Marina, the safest route is to head west along the coast towards Konyaalti Beach. The water is calm inside the bay, and there are no major hazards. You can anchor near the beach and swim. Total distance is about 3 NM each way. From Kemer Marina, the easiest trip is to go south to the small bay of Çamyuva. It is about 2 NM, well-marked, and has a sandy beach. From Belek, head east towards the Kadriye river mouth. The water is flat, and you can explore the delta. From Alanya, go west to the Dim River. The entrance is shallow, so stay in the deeper channel. These routes give you confidence without challenging navigation.

What to Do If the Weather Turns Bad

The Mediterranean can change quickly. A flat calm morning can turn into a choppy afternoon with 20-knot winds. If you see dark clouds building or the wind picks up, head back to the marina immediately. Do not try to outrun a storm in a small speedboat. Most operators will give you a weather briefing and may cancel rentals if conditions are dangerous. If you get caught out, reduce speed, put on life jackets, and head for the nearest shore. All marinas have VHF channels (usually 16 or 12) for emergencies. Keep a charged phone in a waterproof pouch. If you have to abandon the boat, stay with it. It is easier to spot than a person in the water.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group

For two people, a 4.5m RIB with 40 hp is plenty. It is nimble, cheap to run, and easy to handle. For a family of four with kids, go for a 5.5m open speedboat with 90 hp. The extra beam gives stability, and the higher power lets you plane with a full load. For five to six adults, you need a 6m day boat with at least 115 hp. Check the weight capacity. Most licence-free boats have a maximum of 6 passengers including the driver. If you exceed that, the boat will be sluggish and unsafe. Also consider the seating arrangement. RIBs have bench seats that are fine for short trips but uncomfortable for a full day. Open speedboats often have a small sun pad or bow seating, which is more pleasant for lounging.

Combining Speedboat Hire with Other Activities

You can use your speedboat as a base for other adventures. Bring a fishing rod and try your luck near rocky headlands. Common catches in Antalya include sea bream, mackerel, and small tuna. No licence is needed for recreational fishing from a rented boat. You can also rent a stand-up paddleboard or a kayak from some operators and tow it behind the boat. Anchor in a quiet bay and spend an hour paddling. If you are near Kemer, you can stop at the Olympos Beach and hike up to the Chimera flames (eternal fires) in the evening. Just be back at the marina before sunset. Most operators require the boat to be returned by 7 pm in summer and 5 pm in winter.

What to Pack for a Day on a Speedboat in Antalya

The sun in Antalya is strong, especially from May to September. Pack: sunscreen (SPF 50, waterproof), a hat with a strap, polarised sunglasses, a rash guard or long-sleeve shirt, a towel, swimwear, and a change of clothes. Bring plenty of water (at least 2 litres per person) and snacks. Most boats have a small dry storage compartment under the seats. Do not bring anything that cannot get wet. Leave your passport in the marina office or hotel safe. Bring a waterproof phone case or a cheap backup phone. A small first aid kit is useful for cuts and scrapes. If you plan to anchor near a beach, bring cash for the beach club or restaurant. Cards are not always accepted at remote spots.

Legal Stuff: Age Limits, Alcohol, and Liability

The minimum age to drive a licence-free speedboat in Antalya is 18. You must show a valid passport or national ID. No driving licence is required. Alcohol is strictly forbidden while operating the boat. If you are caught, the boat will be impounded, and you may face a fine or legal action. Passengers can drink, but the driver must stay sober. Liability for damage is yours up to the deposit amount. If you cause a collision or run aground, you pay for repairs. Most operators have insurance for third-party damage, but not for the rental boat itself. Read the rental agreement carefully. Some contracts have hidden clauses about towing fees or environmental fines if you spill fuel. Ask for a translated copy if you do not read Turkish.

Comparing Antalya to Other Licence-Free Destinations

Antalya is not the only place where you can rent a boat without a licence. Croatia has similar rules for small boats under 15 hp, but the boats are slower and less powerful. Greece allows licence-free rental only in certain areas (like the Ionian) and for boats under 30 hp. Turkey gives you more power and speed for the same price. In the USA, you can rent a boat without a licence in most states, but you need a boating safety certificate in some. Antalya also has the advantage of consistently calm seas from May to October, whereas the Aegean and Adriatic can be windy. The cost is also lower in Turkey. A half-day rental in Antalya is roughly half the price of the same in Croatia or Greece. For a budget-conscious traveller who wants maximum freedom, Antalya is hard to beat.

Booking Tips: How to Get the Best Deal

Book directly through BoatHire24 to compare multiple operators in one place. Look for listings that include free cancellation up to 48 hours. Avoid operators that ask for a full payment upfront without a refund policy. Check the boat's age and maintenance history. Newer boats (2020 or later) are more reliable and have better safety equipment. Read the reviews, but take them with a grain of salt. Some operators post fake positive reviews. Look for detailed reviews that mention specific issues like engine problems or poor communication. If you are booking last minute, call the operator directly to confirm availability. Online calendars are not always updated in real time. Finally, consider a half-day rental for your first time. You can always extend if you enjoy it, but you do not want to be stuck on a boat for eight hours if you get seasick or bored.

h1: Antalya Fishing Charter: Deep Sea Boat Rentals
intro: You want to catch something big off the Turkish Riviera. An Antalya fishing charter is the way to do it. We connect you with local skippers who know the waters around Kemer, Side, and the open Mediterranean. Forget crowded tour boats. You get a private vessel, licensed captain, and all the gear. Prices start from around EUR 400 for a half-day trip on a well-equipped motor boat. Full-day deep sea expeditions for tuna or swordfish run from EUR 800. Every booking includes a safety briefing, rods, reels, bait, and ice. You just show up with sunscreen and a sense of adventure.
bodyHtml:
What You Get on an Antalya Fishing Charter

Every Antalya fishing charter through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local hotspots. No need to bring your own gear. The boat is equipped with rods, reels, bait, lures, and a fishfinder. You get a cooler for your catch, life jackets, and a basic first aid kit. Most charters include soft drinks and water. Some full-day trips throw in a simple lunch. The skipper cleans and fillets your fish at the end. You keep what you catch, within legal limits. No hidden fees. The price you see is the price you pay, unless you want to tip the crew.

Ports and Launch Points for Your Trip

Antalya fishing charters depart from several ports along the coast. The main ones are Antalya Marina near the city centre, Kemer Marina about 40 km south, and Side Harbour further east. Each has its own character. Antalya Marina is convenient if you are staying in the city. Kemer gives you quicker access to deeper water. Side is quieter and closer to ancient ruins you can see from the boat. Your skipper will advise the best departure point based on the species you are after and the weather. We list each port on the search page so you can filter by location.

Boat Options for Antalya Fishing Charters

You have choices. The most common Antalya fishing charter boats are motor yachts between 8 and 15 metres, purpose-built fishing boats with outriggers, and a few catamarans for stability. Speedboats and RIBs are less common for fishing but can work for light tackle inshore trips. Expect a cruising speed of 8 to 15 knots, depending on the vessel. Larger yachts have a cabin, toilet, and a small galley. Smaller boats are open deck. All are maintained to Turkish Maritime Authority standards. If you want a specific boat type, use the filters on the BoatHire24 homepage. You can compare photos, specs, and skipper profiles before booking.

Pricing Guidance for Antalya Fishing Charters

Prices vary by boat size, trip duration, and season. A half-day Antalya fishing charter (4 hours) costs from around EUR 400 for a group of up to 6 people. Full-day trips (8 hours) start at EUR 800. For larger groups or bigger boats, expect EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,000. Superyachts with full luxury amenities are price on request. Peak season is June to September, when demand is highest. You might pay 20-30% more then. Shoulder months (April, May, October) offer better rates and still good fishing. Winter charters are cheaper but weather can be rough. Always confirm the total cost, including fuel, port fees, and any extras like food or drinks, before you book.

Best Seasons for Fishing in Antalya

Antalya's fishing calendar is generous. Spring (March to May) brings bonito, amberjack, and sea bass. Summer (June to August) is prime for mahi-mahi, bluefish, and shark. Autumn (September to November) sees tuna, swordfish, and red snapper moving closer to shore. Winter (December to February) is quieter but you can still catch grouper and bream in deeper waters. Water temperature ranges from 16 degrees C in winter to 28 degrees C in summer. Your skipper will know the best spots based on the season. The Strait of Gibraltar is not relevant here, but the Mediterranean off Antalya has its own rich ecosystem. You might see dolphins, sea turtles, and even the occasional whale.

What to Bring on Your Antalya Fishing Charter

Pack light. Sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket or windbreaker. The sun is strong even in spring. Wear non-slip shoes. Bring a camera or phone in a waterproof pouch. If you get seasick, take medication an hour before departure. The boat provides life jackets, but you can bring your own if you prefer. A small bag for personal items is fine. Leave valuables at your hotel. Most skippers allow you to bring your own food and drinks, but check first. Alcohol is usually okay in moderation, but don't overdo it. The crew is there to help, not to deal with drunk passengers.

How to Book an Antalya Fishing Charter

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the search page, select Antalya as your destination, and choose the fishing charter category. You will see a list of available boats with prices, photos, and skipper details. Pick your preferred vessel and date, then complete the online form. You pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking. The balance is due on the day, either in cash or by card, depending on the skipper. We send you a confirmation email with the skipper's contact information and meeting point. Cancellations are free up to 48 hours before departure. After that, the deposit is non-refundable. We recommend booking at least a week in advance during peak season.

Who Is an Antalya Fishing Charter For

This is for anyone who wants a private fishing experience on the Mediterranean. Families with children are welcome. Skippers are patient and happy to teach beginners. Groups of friends can split the cost and make a day of it. Solo anglers can join a shared charter if available, but private is more common. You do not need a fishing license for charter boats in Turkey. The skipper holds the necessary permits. If you are a serious angler targeting trophy fish, let us know. We can match you with a skipper who specialises in deep sea trolling or jigging. For a more relaxed trip, choose a half-day inshore charter. Either way, you get a proper Antalya fishing charter that delivers.

Local Attractions Near Antalya Marinas

After your Antalya fishing charter, explore the area. Antalya Marina is close to Kaleici, the old town with Roman walls and narrow streets. Kemer has a lively promenade with restaurants and bars. Side offers the ancient theatre and Temple of Apollo. You can also visit the Duden Waterfalls or take a cable car up Mount Tahtali for views of the coast. The region is known for its pine forests and turquoise coves. Many charter operators can combine fishing with a swim stop at a secluded bay. Ask your skipper. If you want to extend your trip, consider a multi-day charter that includes overnight stays in different ports. Talk to us about custom itineraries.

Safety and Regulations on Antalya Fishing Charters

Safety is taken seriously. All Antalya fishing charter boats are inspected annually by the Turkish Maritime Authority. They carry life rafts, flares, fire extinguishers, and VHF radios. The skipper has a commercial license and first aid training. You will get a safety briefing before departure. Wear your life jacket when the skipper says so. Listen to the crew. Do not stand on the bow while the boat is moving. Fishing regulations are enforced. You can keep a reasonable number of fish per person, but size and bag limits apply for certain species. The skipper will tell you what is allowed. Illegal fishing, such as using dynamite or prohibited nets, is not tolerated. Stick to the rules and you will have a great day.

For more tips and destination guides, check our blog. We cover everything from packing lists to species identification. If you have questions about a specific Antalya fishing charter, contact us. We are here to help you find the right boat at the right price.

Target Species by Depth and Technique

An Antalya fishing charter can target different species depending on where you drop the line. Inshore, in 10 to 30 metres of water, you are likely to hook sea bass, bream, and grouper using bottom rigs with squid or sardines. Move out to 50 to 100 metres and you find amberjack, bonito, and barracuda, best caught by trolling with Rapala-style lures or feather jigs. Beyond 100 metres, the deep water holds tuna, swordfish, and mahi-mahi, requiring heavy tackle and live bait. Your skipper will adjust the plan based on the day's conditions. For example, if a warm current pushes closer to shore, the mahi-mahi might be within 5 nautical miles of the coast. Ask about electric reels if you want to save your arms on deep drops.

Half-Day vs Full-Day Antalya Fishing Charters

The choice between half-day and full-day trips depends on what you want to catch and how much time you have. A half-day Antalya fishing charter, typically 4 hours from 8am to 12pm or 1pm to 5pm, covers inshore grounds within 3 to 5 nautical miles of the port. You can expect to land bream, sea bass, and smaller bonito. A full-day charter, 8 hours from 8am to 4pm, lets you steam 10 to 15 nautical miles offshore, reaching the deeper reefs and drop-offs where larger predators feed. The extra time also allows for a swim stop or a beach lunch at a cove like Phaselis Bay near Kemer. If you are after trophy tuna or swordfish, book a full day. For a casual family outing, half a day is plenty.

Specific Ports: Antalya Marina, Kemer Marina, Side Harbour

Each port gives you different access to fishing grounds. Antalya Marina, at 36.88 N, 30.71 E, is the busiest. From here, you are 15 minutes from the 30-metre contour line south of the city. The marina has parking, cafes, and a fish market where you can compare your catch. Kemer Marina, 40 km south, is quieter and closer to the deep water off the Bey Mountains. You can reach 50 metres within 20 minutes. Side Harbour, 70 km east, is smaller but gives you proximity to the Manavgat River mouth, where sea bass and mullet gather. The ancient ruins of Side are visible from the boat. Each port has its own charter fleet. Filter by port on the search page to compare options.

Boat Types for Antalya Fishing Charters

Not all boats fish the same. Purpose-built fishing boats, 9 to 12 metres long, have outriggers for trolling, a large cockpit with rod holders, and a bait tank. They cruise at 12 to 15 knots and can handle moderate chop. Motor yachts, 10 to 15 metres, offer more comfort with a cabin, toilet, and galley, but their fishing setup is less specialised. They are fine for bottom fishing and light trolling. Catamarans, 12 to 14 metres, provide a stable platform for families and groups, but their speed is lower at 8 to 10 knots. RIBs and speedboats are rare for fishing but can work for light tackle inshore trips. Check the boat's equipment list on the BoatHire24 listing before booking. A good skipper will have at least 6 rods, a fishfinder, and a GPS plotter.

Pricing Breakdown by Group Size and Season

Prices scale with group size. A half-day charter for up to 6 people costs from EUR 400 in low season (November to March) and EUR 500 in high season (June to September). For 8 to 10 people, expect EUR 600 to EUR 800 for half a day. Full-day rates for 6 people start at EUR 800 low season and EUR 1,000 high season. For 10 people, EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,600. Fuel surcharges are rare but ask. Port fees at Antalya Marina are around EUR 20 to EUR 30 per trip, usually included in the price. If you want a luxury motor yacht with a flybridge and air conditioning, the price jumps to EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000 for a full day. Always confirm what is included. Some skippers charge extra for premium bait like live mackerel.

What the Skipper Does for You

The skipper is not just a driver. He knows the local waters, the tides, and the fish behaviour. He will set up the rods, choose the right bait, and show you how to cast and reel. If you are a beginner, he will be patient. If you are experienced, he will let you take over. He monitors the fishfinder and moves the boat to follow the schools. He also handles the safety checks, the radio, and the paperwork. At the end of the trip, he cleans and fillets your catch, bagging it for you to take away. Some skippers speak English, some speak Turkish with basic English. Check the skipper profile on the listing. If language is a concern, mention it when booking.

How to Handle Your Catch

After your Antalya fishing charter, you have options for your catch. The skipper fillets the fish and packs it in a plastic bag with ice. You can take it back to your hotel or holiday rental and cook it yourself. Many hotels will cook your catch for a small fee if you ask in advance. Some local restaurants in Antalya and Kemer will also prepare it for you, charging a per-kilo cooking fee. If you are flying home, check the airline's policy on transporting fish. Most allow frozen fillets in checked luggage if packed properly. You can also donate your catch to the skipper or the crew. They will appreciate it. Do not waste fish. Respect the bag limits and size regulations.

Combining Fishing with Sightseeing

Many Antalya fishing charters can be combined with a sightseeing element. Ask your skipper if you can include a stop at the Duden Waterfalls, where the river falls directly into the sea. The boat can anchor near the spray for a photo. You might also cruise past the ancient city of Olympos or the Chimera flames at Yanartas. Some skippers offer a lunch stop at a beach club near Tekirova or a swim at a secluded cove. This works best on a full-day charter. The fishing is still the main event, but you get a break between drifts. Check the itinerary before booking. Not all skippers are flexible. Those who are will charge a small extra fee for the extended route.

Weather and Sea Conditions

The Mediterranean off Antalya is generally calm from May to October. Wind speeds average 5 to 10 knots, and wave heights are under 1 metre. July and August can have a light meltemi wind in the afternoons, but it rarely stops fishing. November to March sees stronger winds, up to 20 knots, and waves of 1.5 to 2 metres. Your skipper will cancel if conditions are unsafe. You get a full refund or a reschedule. The water is clearest in summer, with visibility up to 20 metres. Winter brings more plankton, reducing visibility but not the fishing. Check the forecast on Windy or Windfinder before your trip. If you are prone to seasickness, avoid windy days and book a larger boat for stability.

Booking Tips for Antalya Fishing Charters

Book early in peak season. June to September sees high demand, especially for weekend slots. Weekdays are easier to secure. If you want a specific boat or skipper, book at least two weeks ahead. Use the search page to compare availability. Read the skipper's profile and recent reviews. Look for mentions of equipment quality, fish caught, and crew attitude. Contact the skipper directly through the platform if you have questions. Confirm the meeting time and location in writing. Arrive 15 minutes early. Bring cash for the balance if the skipper does not take cards. Tipping is customary, 10-15% of the charter price if you are happy. The crew works hard. A tip in euros or Turkish lira is fine.

Fishing Without a License on Antalya Charters

One of the best things about an Antalya fishing charter is that you do not need a personal fishing license. The charter boat holds a commercial fishing permit that covers all passengers. This is standard in Turkey. You can fish with rods and handlines only. Spear fishing from the boat is not allowed. The skipper will enforce the rules. You can keep a reasonable amount of fish, usually up to 5 kg per person, but check local limits for specific species. For example, sea bass must be at least 25 cm. Bluefin tuna has strict quotas, and the skipper will release any undersized fish. Respect the regulations. They exist to keep the fishery sustainable. If you see illegal activity, report it to the Turkish Coast Guard.

What to Do If You Get Seasick

Seasickness can ruin a trip. If you are prone to it, take medication like Dramamine or a scopolamine patch at least one hour before departure. Eat a light breakfast, nothing greasy. Stay on the deck, keep your eyes on the horizon, and avoid reading your phone. Ginger candies or peppermint tea can help settle your stomach. Most boats have a cabin where you can lie down if needed. The skipper will keep the boat steady while you recover. If you vomit, do not worry. It happens. The crew is used to it. Bring a plastic bag just in case. The best prevention is a calm day and a large boat. If you are nervous, book a catamaran for extra stability. Do not let seasickness stop you. The fishing is worth it.

bodyHtml:
What a Private Yacht Charter in Antalya Includes

When you book an Antalya private yacht charter through BoatHire24, you get the vessel, a licensed skipper, and fuel for a standard day's cruising. Most charters run from 10:00 to 18:00, though half-day and sunset options are available. The crew typically includes a captain and a deckhand or steward, depending on the boat size. Lunch is often included on full-day charters, prepared onboard or ordered from a local restaurant. Soft drinks, water, and ice are standard; alcohol is usually bring-your-own or available at an extra cost. Snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and inflatable toys are common additions. You pay nothing extra for the skipper's expertise, and the boat is cleaned and prepped before you step aboard.

Departure Ports for Antalya Charters

Most charters depart from Antalya Marina, right next to the historic Kaleiçi district. It's a modern facility with parking, cafes, and easy access from the city centre. Other options include Kemer Marina, about 40 km southwest, which is closer to the Olympos and Çıralı areas. For a more exclusive start, you can arrange a pickup from private docks at luxury resorts like the Maxx Royal or the Rixos Sungate. Each port gives you a different slice of the coastline. From Antalya Marina, you reach the Lara cliffs and the Düden Waterfalls in about 30 minutes. From Kemer, you are minutes from the three islands (Üç Adalar) and the sunken city of Phaselis.

Boat Options for Your Antalya Private Yacht Charter

The fleet in Antalya covers the usual suspects. Motor yachts from 10 m to 25 m are the most popular for private charters, offering space, speed, and comfort. Expect flybridge lounges, sun pads, and cabins with air conditioning. Gulets, the traditional wooden sailing vessels, are a Turkish speciality and perfect for larger groups or overnight trips. They are slower but more spacious, with a shallow draft that lets you anchor close to shore. Catamarans are available for stability and deck space, ideal for families. Speedboats and RIBs work for shorter trips or watersports-focused days. Superyachts over 30 m are bookable on request, with prices from around EUR 5,000 per day. The key is to match the boat to your group size and the kind of day you want. A motor yacht for a couple's anniversary, a gulet for a group of 12, a speedboat for a quick swim stop.

Pricing Guidance for Antalya Private Yacht Charter

Prices for an Antalya private yacht charter vary by boat size, season, and duration. A standard day charter on a 12 m motor yacht for up to 8 guests starts from around EUR 450 in low season (April, May, October). In high season (June to September), the same boat is from EUR 650 to EUR 900. A 20 m luxury motor yacht for 12 guests runs from EUR 1,200 to EUR 2,500 per day. Gulets are often priced per person for day trips, but private hires start from EUR 800 for a 15 m boat. Overnight charters include accommodation and full board, from EUR 1,500 for a basic gulet to EUR 5,000 plus for a superyacht. Fuel surcharges apply if you cruise beyond the standard range, and port fees at some marinas are extra. Always confirm what's included before booking. BoatHire24 shows you the total upfront, no surprises.

Best Time for a Private Yacht Charter in Antalya

The season runs from April to November, with the peak in July and August when temperatures hit 35 degrees C and the sea is 27 degrees C. May and June are the sweet spot: warm, sunny, and fewer crowds. September is similar, with the added bonus of the grape harvest and local festivals. October is still pleasant for cruising, though evenings cool down. Winter charters are possible but less common, with shorter days and cooler winds. If you want calm seas and guaranteed sunshine, aim for June through September. For lower prices and quieter anchorages, May and October are your best bet. The Meltemi wind can pick up in July and August, but Antalya's coast is relatively sheltered compared to the Aegean.

What to See on an Antalya Private Yacht Charter

The coastline between Antalya and Kemer is packed with things to see. The Düden Waterfalls cascade directly into the sea, a popular photo stop. The ancient city of Phaselis, with its three harbours and Roman ruins, is a protected site you can anchor near and swim to. The Üç Adalar (Three Islands) off Kemer offer clear water and caves to explore. Further south, the Chimera flames near Çıralı are a natural wonder, though better visited by land. For dolphin watching, head towards the Gulf of Antalya, where pods are common in the morning. Lunch stops at beach clubs like the one at Olympos or the private coves near Tekirova are typical. Your skipper knows the best spots for swimming, snorkelling, and avoiding the crowds.

Who Is an Antalya Private Yacht Charter For

This is for anyone who wants a day on the water without the hassle of a tour bus. Couples celebrating an anniversary or honeymoon often book a private motor yacht with a champagne welcome and a quiet anchorage. Families with children appreciate the space and safety of a catamaran or a gulet, with onboard toys to keep everyone entertained. Groups of friends use the charter for a party or a relaxed barbecue. Corporate clients book for client entertainment or team-building, with catering and AV equipment available. Solo travellers can join a shared charter on a gulet, but the private option gives you full control. The common thread is that you value your time and want a tailored experience, not a crowded ferry.

How to Book Your Antalya Private Yacht Charter

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. You browse the available boats in Antalya, check the calendar for your date, and send a booking request. We confirm availability within 24 hours and send you a payment link for the deposit, usually 30 to 50 percent. The balance is due a week before departure. You can also search by port or boat type to narrow down options. For last-minute bookings, call us and we will check live availability. Cancellations made 14 days or more before the charter get a full refund, less a small admin fee. We recommend booking at least two weeks ahead in high season, though some boats are available on short notice. Read our blog for tips on choosing the right boat and planning your itinerary.

What's Not Included in a Private Charter

Standard charters exclude dockage fees at some marinas, which run from EUR 50 to EUR 150 per night. Fuel is included for a set cruising range, typically 30 to 50 nautical miles, but longer trips incur a surcharge. Food and drinks are extra unless specifically stated as full board. Crew gratuity is at your discretion, but 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee is customary. Watersports equipment like jet skis or parasailing is not included, but your skipper can arrange rentals at the stop. Transfers to the marina are your responsibility, though some charters offer pickup from local hotels for a fee. Always read the terms before booking to avoid surprises.

Safety and Licensing on Antalya Charters

All boats on BoatHire24 are licensed by the Turkish Ministry of Transport, with valid safety equipment, life jackets, fire extinguishers, and first aid kits. The skipper holds a professional captain's licence and is experienced in local waters. You do not need a boating licence to charter a private yacht with a skipper. The boat is insured for third-party liability and passenger injury. For children, life jackets are available in all sizes. The crew conducts a safety briefing at the start of the charter. In case of bad weather, the skipper has the authority to cancel or alter the itinerary for safety, and you will be offered a reschedule or refund. We recommend travel insurance that covers cancellation and medical evacuation.

Antalya Marina vs Kemer Marina: Which Departure Point Suits You

Antalya Marina puts you inside the city, five minutes from Kaleiçi's cobbled streets and Roman-era walls. You can grab a coffee at the marina cafes before boarding, and the Lara beachfront is a short cruise east. Kemer Marina is quieter, with a more resort feel and direct access to the Beydağları mountains. It is closer to the popular swimming spots like Çıralı and the Olympos beach, cutting your cruising time by about 20 minutes. If you are staying at a hotel in Kemer or Tekirova, departing from Kemer saves you the drive to Antalya. Both marinas have ample parking, though Kemer's is cheaper at around EUR 5 per day versus EUR 10 in Antalya. Your choice depends on where you are staying and whether you want a city buzz or a coastal calm at the start of your charter.

Overnight and Multi-Day Charters: What to Expect

An overnight Antalya private yacht charter gives you a different experience. You anchor in a quiet bay near Phaselis or Olympos, have dinner on deck under the stars, and wake up to a swim before breakfast. Gulets are the standard choice for overnight trips, with cabins for 6 to 12 guests, a full galley, and a crew cabin. Prices for a 3-day, 2-night gulet charter for 8 guests start from around EUR 2,500 in low season, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Motor yachts are also available for overnight charters, but their fuel consumption is higher and cabins are smaller. You can extend to a week-long itinerary that covers Antalya, Kemer, Çıralı, and even down to Kaş if the weather allows. The crew handles all meals and navigation, you just relax. Book at least a month ahead for multi-day charters in high season, as availability is limited.

Food and Drink Options on Board

Most full-day Antalya private yacht charters include a lunch, either prepared by the crew or delivered from a local restaurant. Typical Turkish lunch spreads include grilled fish or chicken, salads, mezes like hummus and baba ghanoush, rice, and fresh fruit. Vegetarian and halal options are available if you request them when booking. For a premium, you can order a barbecue on the aft deck or a seafood feast. Drinks are usually bring-your-own for alcohol, though some charters offer a stocked bar at extra cost. Soft drinks, water, and tea are included. If you have specific dietary needs, confirm them in advance. The crew can also arrange a champagne welcome or a birthday cake for a celebration. For sunset charters, a cheese and wine platter is a popular add-on, costing around EUR 25 per person.

Typical Itinerary for a Day Charter from Antalya

A standard day on an Antalya private yacht charter starts at 10:00 from Antalya Marina. You cruise east past the Lara cliffs, stopping at the Düden Waterfalls for photos. By 11:30, you anchor at a quiet cove near Kemer for swimming and snorkelling. Lunch is served around 13:00 on deck or in the saloon. After lunch, you move to the Üç Adalar for more swimming, paddleboarding, or exploring the caves. Around 15:30, you cruise back towards Antalya, passing the ancient city of Phaselis for a quick swim stop if time allows. You return to the marina by 18:00, with the option to extend for a sunset cruise at an extra cost. This itinerary is flexible; your skipper adjusts based on weather, sea conditions, and your preferences. If you want to skip the Düden stop and spend more time at Phaselis, just say so.

Best Boat Type for Different Group Sizes

For a couple or a small family of 4, a 10-12 m motor yacht is ideal. It offers a sun deck, a small cabin for changing, and enough speed to cover distance quickly. For 6 to 8 people, a 15-18 m motor yacht or a catamaran gives you more deck space and separate seating areas. Catamarans are especially good for families with young children because they are stable and have large trampolines. For 10 to 12 guests, a 20-25 m gulet is the best choice. It has a spacious aft deck for dining, cabins for overnight stays, and a shallow draft for anchoring close to beaches. For a party group of 12 to 16, a 22-25 m motor yacht with a flybridge and a large saloon works well. Speedboats and RIBs are best for 4 to 6 people who want a fast, action-packed day with watersports.

Hidden Costs to Watch For

While the base price covers the boat, skipper, and fuel for a standard range, there are extras you should budget for. Dockage fees at some marinas, especially for overnight stays, can add EUR 50 to EUR 200 per night. If you cruise beyond the standard 30-40 nautical mile range, fuel surcharges apply at around EUR 150 per additional 10 nautical miles. Food and drinks are extra unless you choose a full-board package. Crew gratuity is not mandatory but is expected; EUR 50 to EUR 100 per crew member for a day charter is standard. Watersports rentals like jet skis cost from EUR 150 per hour, and parasailing from EUR 80 per person. Transfers from your hotel to the marina are usually not included, but can be arranged for EUR 30 to EUR 60 each way. Always ask for a full breakdown before confirming your booking.

Booking for Special Occasions: Birthdays, Proposals, and Weddings

An Antalya private yacht charter is a popular choice for celebrations. For a birthday, you can request a decorated boat, a cake, and a playlist on the sound system. Proposals are often arranged with a private anchorage, a photographer hidden on board, and a bottle of champagne. Weddings are possible on larger yachts or at anchor in a scenic bay, with a civil ceremony arranged through a local wedding planner. These extras come at an additional cost: decoration packages start from around EUR 200, a photographer from EUR 300, and a wedding setup from EUR 1,000. The crew can also coordinate with beach clubs for a reception on shore. If you are planning a surprise, let the booking team know in advance so they can brief the crew without spoiling it.

Weather and Sea Conditions: What to Expect Month by Month

In April and May, the sea temperature is 17-20 degrees C, and air temperatures are 20-25 degrees C. The water is cool but swimmable, and the air is pleasant. June to September sees sea temperatures of 24-28 degrees C and air temperatures of 28-35 degrees C. The Meltemi wind can blow in July and August, but Antalya's coast is sheltered, so waves rarely exceed 1 m. October has sea temperatures of 22-24 degrees C and air temperatures of 22-28 degrees C, with calm seas. November is cooler at 16-20 degrees C air temperature, and the sea drops to 18-20 degrees C, making swimming less comfortable. Rain is rare from May to September, with occasional showers in April, October, and November. Your skipper monitors weather forecasts and will adjust the itinerary if needed. If a storm is forecast, you can reschedule without penalty.

What to Bring on Your Charter

Pack light for an Antalya private yacht charter. Swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (SPF 50, reef-safe if possible), sunglasses, and a hat are essential. A light jacket or sweater is useful for evening cruises, even in summer, as the wind picks up. Non-slip deck shoes or flip-flops are fine, but avoid black-soled shoes that can mark the deck. A waterproof phone case or a dry bag keeps your electronics safe. If you are prone to motion sickness, bring medication or acupressure bands; the sea is usually calm, but the Gulf of Antalya can have a gentle swell. For overnight charters, pack a small overnight bag with a change of clothes and toiletries. The boat has towels and bedding, but you might want your own beach towel. Leave valuables at the hotel; the crew provides lockers on larger yachts.

At BoatHire24, we connect you with licensed, insured operators who know the coast from the Alanya Marina to the ancient Seljuk shipyard. Every booking includes a professional skipper, so you can focus on the sun, the sea, and that cold drink in your hand. This page tells you everything you need to know about renting a boat in Alanya in 2025: what you get, what it costs, which ports to use, and how to avoid the tourist traps.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with Alanya Boat Hire

When you book a boat through BoatHire24, you are not just renting a vessel. You are getting a full package: a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, a boat that has been inspected, and a clear price with no surprises. The skipper handles the navigation, docking, and safety. You handle the sunbathing, swimming, and eating. Most rentals include fuel, snorkelling gear, and a cooler for drinks. Some include a paddleboard or a seabob. Check the listing details before you book. The boats range from 6-metre RIBs for a fast blast to 15-metre motor yachts for a day of luxury. Catamarans are popular for groups because they have more deck space and a shallower draft, which is handy for anchoring close to the beaches near Cleopatra Beach and the Dim Cave.

Alanya’s Main Departure Ports

Alanya has one main marina: Alanya Marina, located west of the city centre near the Alanya Aquapark. It is modern, with parking, cafes, and a fuel dock. Most of our boat rentals depart from here. Some smaller operators work from the fishing harbour near the Red Tower, but those boats are usually older and less comfortable. We stick to the marina. If you are staying in the resorts to the east, like Incekum or Konaklı, you might also find a few boats that pick up from the beach via a dinghy. That is less common and usually costs extra. For the best experience, start from Alanya Marina. You can walk from the city centre or take a taxi for about EUR 5. The marina has a public slipway and a small beach if you want to get in the water before you even board.

Types of Boats Available for Alanya Boat Hire

You have options. The most popular is the motor yacht, typically 8 to 12 metres, with a cabin, a toilet, a small galley, and a sun pad on the bow. These are great for families or couples who want comfort. Next is the catamaran, usually 10 to 14 metres, with a wide deck and a trampoline net at the front. Catamarans are stable, so if you get seasick, this is your best bet. Then there are RIBs and speedboats, 6 to 8 metres, open hull, no cabin, just a steering console and seats. These are for the adrenaline crowd: you can do 35 knots, stop for a swim, then blast to the next cove. Fishing boats are also available, typically 7 to 9 metres, with rod holders and a live bait well. They come with a skipper who knows the fishing spots around the Alanya Canyon, where you can catch sea bream and amberjack. Finally, there are licence-free day boats, which are small motorboats you can drive yourself without a licence. These are limited to 4 metres and 15 horsepower, and you must stay close to the shore. They are cheap, around EUR 80 for half a day, but you get what you pay for.

Pricing Guidance for Alanya Boat Hire

Prices vary by boat size, season, and duration. A half-day (4 hours) on a motor yacht starts from around EUR 350. A full day (8 hours) is from EUR 500. Catamarans are more: from EUR 700 for a half day, from EUR 1,000 for a full day. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper: from EUR 200 for a half day, from EUR 350 for a full day. Fishing boats are usually half-day only, from EUR 250. Superyachts, 20 metres and over, are price on request: expect EUR 3,000 to EUR 10,000 per day. All prices include the skipper and fuel. Food and drinks are extra unless the listing says otherwise. Some operators offer a lunch option: grilled fish, salad, meze, fruit, for about EUR 30 per person. You can also bring your own food and drink. The skipper will usually have a cooler with ice. Just ask.

Best Time for Alanya Boat Hire

The season runs from April to October. July and August are peak: 35 degrees C, crowded beaches, and full marinas. If you want a quieter experience, go in May, June, or September. The water is warm (24-28 degrees C), the sun is strong, and the tourist numbers are lower. October is still pleasant, around 25 degrees C, but the sea can be choppier. Winter rentals are rare because the weather is unpredictable and many boats are hauled out for maintenance. If you want to go in March or November, check with us first. We might find a boat, but do not expect the same availability or conditions.

What to See on an Alanya Boat Trip

From the water, Alanya is stunning. You have the Seljuk-era Alanya Castle perched on the peninsula, the Red Tower at the harbour, and the shipyard (Tersane) carved into the cliff. Most boat trips head west towards the Dim River, where you can anchor in the Dimçay River mouth, a calm spot with a restaurant on the bank. Or east towards the ancient city of Syedra, where the coastline is rugged and there are fewer boats. Some trips go to the Dim Cave, accessible only by sea, where you can swim inside a cavern. For a longer trip, you can go to the Manavgat Waterfall, about 2 hours by boat, but you need a full day for that. Snorkelling is good around the rocky points near the castle. You might see sea turtles if you are lucky. Dolphins are less common here than in the Strait of Gibraltar, but they do appear occasionally near the Alanya Canyon.

Who Is Alanya Boat Hire For?

It is for anyone who wants to see the coast without the crowds. Families with kids: the shallow waters near the beaches are safe for swimming, and the skipper will keep an eye on the children. Couples: a private yacht for two is romantic, especially at sunset. Groups of friends: a catamaran with a sound system and a grill is a party platform. Anglers: the fishing boats are equipped and the skipper knows the spots. Business groups: a corporate day out on a motor yacht with catering and a bar. The only people who should not book a boat in Alanya are those who get seasick easily (go for a catamaran, it is steadier) or those who want a bareboat charter without a skipper. All our boats come with a skipper. That is the law in Turkey for commercial charters, and it is safer anyway.

How to Book Your Alanya Boat Hire

Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and search for Alanya. Or use the search page to filter by date, boat type, and number of guests. Once you find a boat you like, click through to the listing. You will see a calendar with available dates. Select your date and time, then fill in your details. You pay a deposit of 30% to confirm the booking. The balance is paid in cash to the skipper on the day. You can cancel up to 48 hours before for a full refund. If the weather is bad, the skipper may cancel and you get a full refund. We handle the communication between you and the operator. If you have questions, use the contact form on the listing page. We usually reply within 2 hours during business hours.

Alanya vs Other Destinations on the Costa del Sol

Alanya is not in Spain, but it is a popular destination for boat hire in Turkey. If you are comparing it to Marbella or Puerto Banús, the main difference is price. Alanya is cheaper: a day on a motor yacht here costs about half of what it costs in Puerto Banús. The scenery is different too: Alanya has a castle and a river, while Marbella has the La Concha mountain and the luxury port. Both are good. It depends on your budget and what you want to see. If you are planning a trip to the Costa del Sol, check out our blog for comparisons and tips. For Alanya specifically, you are in the right place.

Frequently Asked Questions About Alanya Boat Hire

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group Size

Group size is the main factor. For two people, a 7-metre motor yacht or a 6-metre RIB works fine. You get a cabin for privacy and a small deck for sunbathing. For four to six people, go for an 8 to 10-metre motor yacht or a 10-metre catamaran. The catamaran gives you more space to move around without bumping into each other. For eight to twelve people, you need a 12-metre catamaran or a 14-metre motor yacht. These have two cabins, two toilets, and a large aft deck for dining. For groups over twelve, you are looking at a superyacht or a large gulet, which are price on request. Do not try to squeeze more people onto a boat than the capacity allows. The skipper will refuse to sail if the boat is overloaded, and you will lose your deposit.

What to Pack for a Day on the Boat in Alanya

Bring sunscreen with SPF 50, a hat, and sunglasses. The sun in Alanya is intense, especially between 11am and 3pm. A rash guard or a light long-sleeve shirt helps prevent burns while swimming. Bring a towel, a change of clothes, and a waterproof bag for your phone and wallet. If you plan to swim, bring fins or a mask if you have your own, though most boats provide snorkelling gear. Do not bring glass bottles. They break and leave shards on the deck. Use plastic or metal containers. Bring a light jacket or a windbreaker for the afternoon, because the wind can pick up and the boat creates its own breeze. If you are prone to seasickness, take a dramamine an hour before departure. The skipper will have a first aid kit but not seasickness pills.

Alanya Marina Facilities and Parking

Alanya Marina has 400 berths and can accommodate vessels up to 50 metres. It has a fuel dock, a chandlery, a repair yard, and a crane for hauling boats. For you, the important facilities are the car park, the toilets, and the cafes. Parking costs around EUR 3 per hour or EUR 15 for the day. There is a public car park outside the marina gate that is cheaper, about EUR 5 for the day, but it fills up by 10am in summer. The marina has a small supermarket where you can buy drinks and snacks before boarding. If you forget something, there is a Migros supermarket a 5-minute walk away. The marina office is open 8am to 8pm. If you arrive after 8pm, you might have trouble finding the boat. Plan to arrive at least 30 minutes before your departure time to check in and meet the skipper.

Extended Trips: Overnight and Multi-Day Charters

If a day trip is not enough, you can book an overnight or multi-day charter. Most motor yachts and catamarans have cabins with beds, a toilet, and a shower. An overnight trip from Alanya can go to Gazipaşa, about 30 nautical miles east, where there is a small marina and a nice beach. Or you can go west to Side, about 20 nautical miles, and anchor near the ancient ruins. Multi-day charters often include a route along the coast with stops at different coves and villages. The price for an overnight charter starts from around EUR 800 for a motor yacht and includes the skipper, fuel, and overnight mooring. Food is extra. You can eat at restaurants on shore or ask the skipper to cook on board. Overnight charters are popular in June and September when the nights are warm and the marinas are less crowded.

Fishing Charters in Alanya: What to Expect

Fishing boats in Alanya are typically 7 to 9 metres with a outboard or inboard engine. They have rod holders, a live bait well, and a fish finder. The skipper knows the best spots around the Alanya Canyon, where the seabed drops to 200 metres. You can catch sea bream, amberjack, grouper, and sometimes tuna. The season for tuna is May to July. For sea bream, it is year-round. A half-day fishing charter costs from EUR 250 and includes bait, tackle, and the skipper. You do not need a fishing licence because the boat has a commercial licence. The skipper will clean and fillet your catch. You can take it to a restaurant to be cooked, or bring it back to your accommodation. Fishing charters usually depart at 6am or 7am to catch the early bite. Bring a hat, sunscreen, and a cooler for your catch. Do not expect luxury. These boats are functional, not fancy.

Sunset Cruises in Alanya

A sunset cruise is a shorter trip, usually 2 to 3 hours, departing around 5pm in summer and 3pm in winter. You cruise along the coast, watch the sun set behind the Alanya Castle, and return after dark. The price is lower than a full-day charter: from EUR 150 for a RIB, from EUR 250 for a motor yacht. Most sunset cruises include a glass of champagne or a soft drink. Some offer a small snack like nuts or fruit. The best time for a sunset cruise is from May to September when the sun sets over the sea. In April and October, the sun sets behind the mountains, which is still pretty but less dramatic. If you are celebrating a birthday or an anniversary, let the operator know. They can arrange decorations, a cake, or a special dinner on board.

What Happens If the Weather Is Bad

Alanya has a Mediterranean climate, so bad weather is rare in summer. But it can happen. If the wind is above 25 knots or there is a storm warning, the skipper will cancel the trip. You get a full refund or the option to reschedule. If the weather is marginal, the skipper might suggest a shorter trip or a different route that stays closer to shore. You can decide to go ahead or cancel. Our cancellation policy covers weather cancellations. Do not try to pressure the skipper into going out in unsafe conditions. It is not worth the risk. In spring and autumn, check the forecast the day before. If a front is coming, consider booking a flexible date. The skipper has the final say on safety.

How to Get to Alanya Marina from Popular Resorts

If you are staying in Alanya city centre, you can walk to the marina in 15 minutes from the Atatürk statue. From the resorts to the east, like Incekum (15 km), Konaklı (12 km), or Avsallar (22 km), take a taxi. The fare is around EUR 10 to EUR 20 depending on distance. From the west, like Mahmutlar (5 km), it is a short taxi ride or a dolmuş (minibus) that stops near the marina. If you are staying in Side (35 km), a taxi costs about EUR 30. Some boat operators offer a transfer service for an extra fee, usually EUR 5 per person each way. Ask when you book. Do not rely on public buses if you have a tight schedule. They are frequent but can be late.
