faqs.q: Do I need a licence to rent a boat in Alanya?
faqs.a: No, you do not. All our boats come with a licensed skipper. You can drive a small licence-free day boat (up to 4 metres, 15 hp) without a licence, but those are limited to inshore waters and are not suitable for open sea.

faqs.q: What is included in the price of an Alanya boat hire?
faqs.a: The price includes the boat, the skipper, fuel, and basic safety equipment. Some listings include snorkelling gear, a cooler, and paddleboards. Food and drinks are usually extra unless specified. Check the listing details for what is included.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and drink on the boat?
faqs.a: Yes, you can. Most boats have a cooler with ice. You can also ask the skipper to arrange a lunch stop at a beach restaurant. Some operators offer a catering option for an extra fee.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.a: The skipper will decide if it is safe to go out. If the trip is cancelled due to weather, you get a full refund. If you cancel more than 48 hours before, you get a full refund. Within 48 hours, the deposit is non-refundable.

faqs.q: How many people can fit on a boat in Alanya?
faqs.a: It depends on the boat size. A typical 8-metre motor yacht holds up to 8 guests. A 12-metre catamaran holds up to 12. RIBs usually take 6 to 8. The maximum is 12 guests for most boats. For larger groups, you can rent a superyacht or multiple boats.

faqs.q: Can I book a boat for a sunset cruise in Alanya?
faqs.a: Yes, many operators offer sunset cruises, usually 2 to 3 hours in the evening. Prices start from around EUR 150 for a small boat. It is popular, so book in advance, especially in July and August.

faqs.q: Is it safe to swim from the boat in Alanya?
faqs.a: Yes, it is safe. The skipper will anchor in calm, shallow areas away from boat traffic. Life jackets are provided for non-swimmers and children. The water is clean and clear, especially near the Dim River and the castle.

bodyHtml:
What Is Included in an Alanya Yacht Charter

When you book an Alanya yacht charter through BoatHire24, the package is straightforward. The boat comes with a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, fuel for a standard route (usually 6-8 hours), and basic insurance. Most charters also include a cooler with ice, snorkelling gear, and a Bluetooth speaker. You can add extras like a hostess, a barbecue lunch, or a jet ski tow toy for an extra fee. The skipper handles navigation and docking, so you don't need a boating licence. You are responsible for food and drinks unless you order a catering package. The charter company will meet you at the marina 15 minutes before departure to do a safety briefing.

Alanya Marina and Departure Points

All Alanya yacht charters depart from Alanya Marina, located just east of the city centre near the Alanya Castle hill. The marina has 450 berths and can handle yachts up to 50 m. You will find cafes, a small supermarket, and a taxi rank at the gate. For charters longer than a day, you can also depart from the nearby fishing harbour at Mahmutlar, 10 km east, or from the small port at Gazipaşa, 40 km east, if you want to start closer to the caves. The skipper will confirm the exact meeting point after you book. Parking at Alanya Marina costs around EUR 5 per day.

Types of Boats Available for Alanya Yacht Charter

The fleet for Alanya yacht charter covers four main types. Motor yachts from 8 m to 18 m are the most common, with top speeds of 20-30 knots and cabins for 6-10 guests. Catamarans from 12 m to 16 m offer more deck space and stability, ideal for families or groups who want to lounge. Sailing yachts from 10 m to 14 m are slower but quieter, with a classic feel. For a faster, more budget-friendly option, you can charter a RIB or speedboat from 6 m to 9 m, which holds 6-8 guests and hits 40 knots. Superyachts over 24 m are available on request, with prices starting from EUR 5,000 per day. Browse the full selection at BoatHire24 search page.

Popular Alanya Yacht Charter Itineraries

A typical half-day Alanya yacht charter lasts 4 hours and covers the coast from the marina west to Cleopatra Beach and the ancient shipyard cave. A full-day charter (8 hours) goes further east to the Dim River delta or west to the Incekum lighthouse. The most popular route includes a swim stop at the Pirates Cave, a lunch break at a quiet cove near the Alanya Castle, and a slow cruise past the Red Tower. For a longer trip, you can sail to the ancient city of Side, 60 km west, or to the Gazipaşa caves in the east. The skipper will adjust the route based on wind and your preferences. Dolphins are common in the bay, especially in spring.

Alanya Yacht Charter Prices and What Affects Them

Prices for an Alanya yacht charter depend on the boat size, duration, and season. In low season (November to March), a half-day on a 10 m motor yacht starts from around EUR 350. In high season (June to September), the same boat costs from EUR 500. Catamarans start from EUR 800 for a half-day and EUR 1,500 for a full day. Sailing yachts are slightly cheaper, from EUR 300 half-day. Superyachts over 20 m cost from EUR 3,000 per day. Extras like a hostess (EUR 100), jet ski (EUR 150 per hour), or a barbecue lunch (EUR 30 per person) add to the total. You pay a 30% deposit online, and the balance is due in cash or card at the marina. BoatHire24 does not charge booking fees.

Best Time for an Alanya Yacht Charter

The best months for an Alanya yacht charter are May, June, September, and October. The sea temperature is 22-27 degrees C, the air is 28-32 degrees C, and the wind is light. July and August are hotter (35 degrees C) and more crowded, but the sea is calmest. Winter charters (November to March) are possible but the sea can be choppy and many boats are in maintenance. The skipper will cancel if the wind exceeds 25 knots. For dolphin watching, April and May are best. For sunset cruises, book a charter starting at 16:00 in summer to catch the golden hour at 19:30.

How to Book an Alanya Yacht Charter on BoatHire24

Booking an Alanya yacht charter on BoatHire24 takes three steps. First, go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter Alanya as the destination, your preferred date, and the number of guests. Second, browse the available boats, filter by type and price, and click on one that fits. Third, select your duration (half-day, full-day, or multi-day), add any extras, and pay the 30% deposit with a credit card or PayPal. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact and the exact meeting point. You can cancel up to 48 hours before departure for a full refund. If the weather is bad, the operator will reschedule or refund you in full.

Who Is an Alanya Yacht Charter For

An Alanya yacht charter works for couples, families, and groups of friends. Couples often book a private motor yacht for a sunset cruise with champagne. Families with kids prefer catamarans because they have a shallow draft and a trampoline net for playing. Groups of up to 12 people can split the cost of a 14 m motor yacht and it becomes affordable, around EUR 80 per person for a full day. Corporate groups and events can charter a superyacht with a crew of four for a day of networking or celebration. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared charter on a gulet, which is a traditional wooden boat, for around EUR 60 per person, but that is not a private charter.

Alanya Yacht Charter vs Boat Rental in Other Turkish Resorts

Compared to a boat rental in Marmaris or Bodrum, an Alanya yacht charter is generally cheaper because the marina fees and crew wages are lower. The coastline in Alanya is less developed than the Bodrum peninsula, so you get more secluded coves. The water is clearer in Alanya because the sand is finer and there is less river runoff. However, the sailing conditions are less varied than in the Aegean Sea, where the wind is stronger. If you want a party vibe, Bodrum has more nightlife on the water. For a relaxed family day, Alanya wins on price and simplicity. Read more about the differences on our blog.

Safety and Licensing for Alanya Yacht Charter

Every Alanya yacht charter includes a licensed skipper who holds a Turkish Coast Guard-approved qualification. The boat is inspected annually and carries life jackets, a first aid kit, and a VHF radio. You do not need a boating licence to charter a skippered boat. If you want to rent a boat without a skipper, you need a valid ICC or equivalent, and the boat must be under 12 m. That option is rare in Alanya because most operators prefer to provide a crew. The skipper will do a safety briefing before departure and will not allow swimming in rough conditions. In case of an emergency, the Coast Guard can reach any point in the bay within 20 minutes.

What to Bring on Your Alanya Yacht Charter

Pack light for your Alanya yacht charter. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, and sunglasses. A light jacket is useful for the evening breeze. You can bring your own food and drinks, but glass bottles are banned on some boats because they break. Most operators provide a cooler with ice. If you want to play music, bring a Bluetooth speaker or use the boat's system. A waterproof phone case is a good idea for photos. Do not bring large suitcases; leave them at your hotel. The skipper will have snorkelling gear, but if you have your own mask, it may fit better.

Local Attractions Near Alanya Marina

After your Alanya yacht charter, you can explore the area around the marina. The Alanya Castle is a 10-minute walk uphill and offers panoramic views of the coast. The Red Tower (Kızıl Kule) is a 13th-century fortress right next to the marina. Cleopatra Beach is a 15-minute walk west, with fine sand and shallow water. The Dim River delta, 20 km east, has a popular restaurant on the water where you can eat fresh trout. For a longer excursion, the ancient city of Side is 60 km west, with a Roman theatre and a temple of Apollo. The marina itself has a few bars and restaurants serving Turkish cuisine and seafood.

Why Choose Alanya for a Yacht Charter Destination

Alanya sits on the Mediterranean coast of southern Turkey, about 140 km east of Antalya. The coastline here is a mix of long sandy beaches and rocky coves, with the Taurus Mountains rising behind. The water is calm for most of the year because the bay is sheltered by the Alanya peninsula. You get around 300 days of sunshine annually, which means your charter is unlikely to be rained off. The city itself has a population of around 350,000, so it is busy but not overwhelming. The main attraction for a yacht charter is the combination of clear water, historical landmarks visible from the sea, and a marina that is easy to reach from the city centre. If you are staying in a hotel along the beach strip, you can walk to the marina in 15 minutes.

Alanya Yacht Charter for Sunset Cruises

A sunset cruise is one of the most popular options for an Alanya yacht charter. You depart around 16:30 in summer, head west past Cleopatra Beach, and anchor near the Alanya Castle cliffs. The sun sets behind the castle at around 19:30 in July, casting orange light on the red tower. The skipper will turn off the engine so you can hear the waves and the call to prayer from the mosque on the hill. You can bring champagne or order a bottle from the operator for around EUR 30. The cruise lasts 3 to 4 hours, and you are back at the marina by 20:30. Prices for a sunset charter on a 10 m motor yacht start from around EUR 400 in high season. It is a good option for couples or small groups who want a relaxed evening without a full day commitment.

Alanya Yacht Charter for Fishing Trips

If you want to fish, you can book an Alanya yacht charter specifically for fishing. The waters off Alanya hold sea bream, sea bass, mackerel, and sometimes bluefish. The skipper will take you to the fishing grounds near the Dim River mouth or the reefs off the Gazipaşa coast. The boat comes with basic fishing rods and tackle, but serious anglers should bring their own gear. A half-day fishing charter on a 7 m RIB costs from around EUR 250 in low season and EUR 400 in high season. The skipper will clean and bag your catch at the end of the trip. You can then take the fish to a restaurant near the marina, such as the one at the Red Tower, and they will cook it for you for a small fee. Fishing is best in spring and autumn when the water is cooler.

Alanya Yacht Charter for Multi-Day Trips

For a longer experience, you can book a multi-day Alanya yacht charter. A typical 3-day itinerary goes east from Alanya to Gazipaşa and the ancient city of Anamur, then back. You sleep on the boat in cabins, and the skipper will anchor in sheltered coves each night. The boat must be at least 12 m to have proper cabins, a galley, and a toilet. Prices for a 3-day charter on a 14 m motor yacht start from around EUR 2,500 in high season, including fuel for 8 hours of cruising per day. You can also hire a hostess for EUR 100 per day to prepare meals and clean. Multi-day charters require a 50% deposit and full payment 14 days before departure. The skipper will provision the boat with food and water if you request it, at cost plus 10%. This option works well for groups of 6 to 10 who want to explore the coast beyond the usual day-trip range.

Alanya Yacht Charter for Large Groups and Events

Large groups of up to 20 people can charter a catamaran or a motor yacht over 16 m in Alanya. The biggest boats available for day charters are around 18 m, holding 20 guests plus a crew of three. Prices for a full-day charter on an 18 m motor yacht start from around EUR 2,500 in high season. You can add a DJ for EUR 200, a barbecue lunch for EUR 35 per person, and a professional photographer for EUR 150. The boat will have a large sundeck, a saloon with air conditioning, and a swim platform at the back. For corporate events, the skipper can anchor at a quiet cove and set up a projector for presentations if needed. Booking for a large group requires at least 7 days notice so the operator can arrange the crew and catering. Deposit is 50% and non-refundable if you cancel within 7 days.

What to Expect from the Skipper on an Alanya Yacht Charter

The skipper on your Alanya yacht charter is a local professional who speaks at least basic English. He knows the coastline, the best swimming spots, and the weather patterns. He will handle all navigation, anchoring, and docking. He will also point out landmarks like the ancient shipyard cave or the Cleopatra mosaic site. You can ask him to stop at a specific cove or to adjust the route if you want more time swimming. He will not serve drinks or food unless you hire a hostess. The skipper works for tips, so it is customary to give 10-15% of the charter price if you are satisfied. He expects you to be on time, to follow safety instructions, and to not bring illegal substances on board. If you have any complaints, report them to BoatHire24 after the trip, not to the skipper directly.

Alanya Yacht Charter with a Hostess or Chef

Adding a hostess or chef to your Alanya yacht charter makes the day more comfortable. A hostess costs around EUR 100 for a half-day and EUR 150 for a full day. She will serve your food and drinks, clean the saloon, and help with children. A chef costs from EUR 200 per day and can prepare a Turkish menu including meze, grilled fish, and fresh fruit. The chef will buy ingredients from the market in the morning and cook on the boat's galley. You can request a menu in advance, such as a barbecue or a vegetarian option. Both the hostess and chef are separate from the skipper and report to the charter company. You pay their fee directly at the marina in cash. This option is popular for birthdays, anniversaries, and proposals where you want a premium experience without lifting a finger.

title: Alanya Catamaran Hire: Private Boat Trips Guide
metaDescription: Book private Alanya catamaran hire for your group. Compare catamarans with skipper, see prices from EUR 1,200, and check availability at Cleopatra Beach. Reserve today.
h1: Alanya Catamaran Hire: Private Boat Trips Guide
intro:
You want to hire a catamaran in Alanya for a private day on the Mediterranean. The short answer: yes, it is possible, and you can book one directly through BoatHire24. Alanya has a fleet of modern catamarans, mostly based at the main marina near Cleopatra Beach, and they come with a licensed skipper and crew. Expect prices from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day charter for up to 12 guests, including soft drinks and fuel. This guide tells you what you get, which ports to use, and how to avoid the tourist-trap mass boats.

Alanya catamaran hire works best for groups of 6 to 20 people who want space, stability, and a sun deck without the rolling motion of a monohull. You can swim off the boat, anchor near the ancient castle, or cruise along the coastline to the Dim River mouth. All charters include insurance, a skipper, and basic catering unless you request a full BBQ. You book online, pay a deposit, and the balance is due on the day. No hidden fees, no time-share pitches.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Private Catamaran Charter in Alanya

When you hire a catamaran in Alanya, the package typically includes the vessel, a professional skipper, fuel for up to 4-5 hours cruising, and basic refreshments (water, soft drinks, tea). Most operators also provide a crew member to handle mooring and serve drinks. You get use of the onboard sound system, a shaded saloon, a trampoline net at the bow, and a rear swim platform with a ladder. Some catamarans have a small galley where the crew can prepare simple snacks. If you want a full Turkish lunch or BBQ, that costs extra, usually EUR 20-35 per person. Snorkelling gear, paddleboards, and fishing lines are often included or available for a small supplement. Check the listing on BoatHire24 for each boat's specific inclusions.

What is not included: hotel transfers (arrange your own taxi, about EUR 15-25 from the city centre to the marina), alcoholic drinks (you can bring your own, or buy from the boat's bar at market prices), and gratuities for the crew. The skipper speaks English and Turkish, and sometimes German or Russian. You do not need a boating licence; the skipper handles everything. The boat is insured for third-party liability and passenger accident cover.

Departure Ports for Catamaran Hire in Alanya

Almost all private catamarans depart from Alanya Marina, located just west of Cleopatra Beach. The address is Marina Mahallesi, Iskele Caddesi, 07400 Alanya. It is a 10-minute walk from the city centre and a 5-minute taxi ride from most hotels in the Cleopatra area. The marina has a car park (EUR 5 per day), a café, and a small shop. Some larger catamarans (over 14 m) may also use the nearby Alanya Yacht Harbour, which is about 2 km east, near the Red Tower. That harbour has deeper water and can accommodate bigger vessels, but it is less convenient for foot passengers.

If you are staying in the outlying resorts of Mahmutlar or Konaklı, some operators offer a pickup by tender or a minibus transfer to the marina. Ask at the time of booking. For a day trip, the standard route goes east towards the Dim River, or west towards the ancient Seljuk shipyard and the caves. The skipper will discuss the itinerary with you on the morning of the charter. You can also request a stop at Kleopatra Beach for a swim, but note that the beach is public and can be crowded in high season.

Types of Catamarans Available for Hire in Alanya

The fleet in Alanya is smaller than in Bodrum or Gocek, but you still have a decent choice. Most boats are Lagoon 380 or Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40 models, between 11 m and 13 m in length. They sleep 6-8 guests in cabins, but for day charters you can take up to 12 passengers. The newer catamarans, built after 2018, have flybridge steering stations, a large sunbathing area on the roof, and a forward trampoline. Older models (2005-2012) are simpler but still comfortable, with a lower price point. A few luxury catamarans, like the Lagoon 46 or Bali 4.3, are available for premium charters, with prices from EUR 2,500 per day.

If you want a party boat, some operators offer a catamaran with a DJ setup and a larger sound system. These are rare in Alanya, so book well in advance. For families with young children, a catamaran is ideal because the deck is flat and there is no steep ladder to the water. The shallow draft (about 1.2 m) means you can anchor close to the beach for swimming. All catamarans have a proper toilet (heads) and a shower on the swim platform. No licence-free boats are available in Alanya; every charter includes a skipper, which is mandatory under Turkish maritime law for vessels over 10 m.

Pricing Guidance for Alanya Catamaran Hire

Prices for a private catamaran charter in Alanya vary by season, boat size, and duration. As a rough guide: a half-day (4 hours) for up to 12 guests costs from EUR 1,200 to EUR 1,800. A full day (8 hours) is EUR 1,800 to EUR 3,000. High-season (July-September) prices are about 20% higher. Luxury catamarans with a flybridge and a crew of two cost from EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,500 per day. These prices include fuel for up to 50 nautical miles of cruising, which is plenty for a day trip along the coast. If you want to go further, to Side or Gazipasa, expect a fuel surcharge of around EUR 100-200.

You can sometimes negotiate a discount for a last-minute booking (2-3 days ahead) or for a group of 15+ people. The cheapest option is a shared catamaran tour, but that is not what this page is about. For a private catamaran, you pay for the whole boat, not per person. The deposit is typically 30-50% via bank transfer or credit card. The balance is paid in cash or card on the day. BoatHire24 listings show the exact price or a price range; if you see 'price on request', send a quick inquiry and you will get a quote within 24 hours.

Best Seasons for Catamaran Hire in Alanya

The Alanya sailing season runs from April to November. The best months are May, June, September, and October, when the air temperature is 25-30°C and the sea is 22-26°C. July and August are hot (35°C plus) and crowded, but the sea is calm and the wind is light, so catamarans are very stable. Winter charters (December-March) are possible but less comfortable, with temperatures around 15°C and occasional rain. Most catamarans are laid up for maintenance in the winter months, so availability is very limited.

If you are visiting in spring (April), be aware that the water is still cool, around 18°C, so swimming might be brief. The advantage is lower prices and fewer tourists. In autumn, the sea is still warm from summer, and the weather is often perfect for sunset cruises. The prevailing wind in Alanya is from the southwest, which means the sea is usually flat in the morning and gets a light chop in the afternoon. Catamarans handle this well, so seasickness is rare.

How to Book a Catamaran in Alanya

You book through BoatHire24 by searching for Alanya catamarans and selecting your date and group size. The system shows available boats with prices and photos. You can filter by length, capacity, and price range. Once you choose a boat, you fill in a simple form with your contact details and any special requests (e.g., dietary needs, extra water toys). You then pay a deposit online via Stripe (credit card or Apple Pay). The operator confirms the booking within 24 hours. If the boat is not available, you get a full refund of the deposit.

On the day, you meet the skipper at the marina at the agreed time. Bring sunscreen, towels, and a hat. The boat will have a cooler for your drinks. You can also bring your own food, but check with the operator if they have a kitchen or just a fridge. The skipper will give a safety briefing and then you are off. The standard charter includes a fuel allowance for a specific cruising range; if you want to go further, agree the extra cost beforehand. , you return to the marina and pay the balance. It is straightforward. For any questions, use the chat on the website or email info@boathire24.com.

Who Should Hire a Catamaran in Alanya

Catamaran hire in Alanya suits couples, families, and groups of friends who want a private, spacious boat without the motion of a monohull. It is especially good for people who are prone to seasickness, because catamarans are much more stable. It is also ideal for photographers and videographers who need a stable platform for drone shots or filming. If you want a party with dancing and loud music, a motor yacht might be better, but a catamaran works well for a relaxed day with swimming and sunbathing.

Business groups and corporate events also use catamarans for team-building or client entertainment. The flybridge area is perfect for informal meetings or a buffet lunch. Some operators offer a catering package with a Turkish meze spread and grilled fish. For a birthday or anniversary, you can arrange a cake and decorations. Just let the booking team know. If you are a solo traveller, you are better off joining a shared tour, as private catamarans are priced per boat, not per person.

For more tips on planning your trip, read our Boat Hire Blog for guides on the best anchorages and local restaurants. You can also browse all available boats on our search page.

Top Itineraries for Your Alanya Catamaran Day

The skipper will tailor the route, but a few standard itineraries work well. The classic eastern run heads past the Red Tower and the Seljuk shipyard (Tersane) to the Dim River mouth. You anchor in the calm bay, swim in the river's freshwater mixing with the sea, and have lunch. The western route takes you past Cleopatra Beach and the caves (Fosforlu Cave, Pirate Cave, Lovers Cave) to the ancient city of Syedra. You can stop for a swim at a secluded cove near the ruins. A longer option goes 15 NM west towards the Incekum area, where the water is shallow and turquoise for miles. If you are feeling adventurous, ask the skipper to head 20 NM east to the Gazipasa coast, where you will find nearly empty beaches and the chance to see sea turtles. For a sunset charter, the best spot is off the Kleopatra Peninsula, with the sun setting behind the Taurus Mountains.

Catering and Food Options on Board

Most catamarans have a small galley with a hob, fridge, and sink. The crew can prepare simple sandwiches, fruit platters, and cold meze. If you want a hot meal, you need to pre-order a catering package. The standard Turkish lunch costs EUR 25-35 per person and includes grilled chicken or fish, rice, salad, and bread. A BBQ option (EUR 30-45) adds lamb chops, köfte, and grilled vegetables. Vegetarian and vegan options are available if you request them 48 hours ahead. Some operators allow you to bring your own food, but they may charge a corkage fee of EUR 50-100 for using their kitchen facilities. Drinks are usually BYO, but the boat will have a basic stock of beer, wine, and soft drinks at market prices (EUR 3 for a beer, EUR 2 for a soft drink). If you want champagne or premium spirits, bring your own.

Weather and Sea Conditions in Alanya

Alanya's Mediterranean climate means predictable summer weather. From June to September, the sea is glassy in the morning, with a light breeze picking up around 2 PM. The wind rarely exceeds force 3 (8-12 knots), so catamarans remain perfectly stable. The water temperature peaks at 28°C in August. In May and October, the sea is 20-24°C, and you might get a few cloudy days. The prevailing south-westerly wind can push a gentle swell into the coast, but the lee of the Taurus Mountains keeps the water calm within 2 NM of the shore. Thunderstorms are rare in summer but possible in late September. The skipper monitors the forecast and will adjust the route if needed. If a charter is cancelled due to unsafe weather, you get a full refund or a reschedule at no cost.

What to Bring for Your Catamaran Charter

Pack light, but bring essentials. Sunscreen with SPF 50 is non-negotiable; the sun reflects off the water and can burn you quickly even on a cloudy day. A wide-brimmed hat, polarised sunglasses, and a rash guard or light long-sleeved shirt help protect your skin. Towels are provided on some boats, but bring your own to be safe. A dry bag for your phone and wallet is useful. If you plan to snorkel, the boat provides masks and fins, but you can bring your own for a better fit. A waterproof camera or GoPro is ideal for capturing the caves and underwater life. For the evening, a light jacket or jumper is useful, as the sea breeze can cool down after sunset. Do not forget your passport or ID; the marina security may ask for it when boarding.

Comparing Catamarans to Other Boat Types in Alanya

If you are deciding between a catamaran and a motor yacht, consider stability and space. Catamarans have a beam of 6-8 metres, which makes them feel like a floating platform. Motor yachts in Alanya are typically 10-15 metres long and have a narrower beam, so they roll more at anchor. Catamarans also have more deck space: the forward trampoline and flybridge offer sunbathing areas that a motor yacht of the same length cannot match. However, motor yachts are faster (25-30 knots vs 8-12 knots), so you can cover more coastline in a day. For a relaxed day with swimming and lounging, a catamaran wins. For a high-speed tour of multiple beaches and a visit to Side or Manavgat, a motor yacht is better. Sailing yachts are rare in Alanya for private hire, as the light winds make them slow. RIBs and speedboats are available for a cheaper, more thrilling ride, but they lack shade and comfort.

Hidden Costs and Tips to Avoid Them

Most hidden costs come from optional extras. Fuel is included for a standard range, but if you ask the skipper to go further than 50 NM, expect a surcharge of EUR 2-3 per nautical mile. Mooring fees at public quays or restaurant jetties are usually included, but if you want to tie up at a private beach club, they may charge EUR 50-100, which you pay directly. Catering is not included unless specified. Gratuity for the crew is customary; 10-15% of the charter fee is standard, given in cash at the end. If the boat has a water maker, it is included, but bottled water for drinking is sometimes charged separately. Check the listing on BoatHire24 for the 'what's included' section to avoid surprises. Always confirm the total cost in writing before you pay the deposit.

Accessibility and Special Needs

Catamarans are more accessible than monohulls because they have a wide, flat deck with no steep steps from the saloon to the cockpit. The swim platform is low to the water, making it easier for people with limited mobility to enter the sea. However, the flybridge is only accessible via a ladder, so guests who cannot climb stairs should stay on the main deck. The toilet (head) is usually down a few steps, so wheelchair users may find it difficult. If you have a specific accessibility requirement, contact the operator before booking. Some catamarans have a portable ramp for boarding from the pontoon. The marina in Alanya has accessible parking and ramps. For guests with hearing or visual impairments, the skipper can provide a written safety briefing. Service dogs are allowed on board, but inform the operator in advance.

Environmental and Safety Considerations

Alanya's marine environment is protected by several regulations. You cannot anchor on seagrass meadows (Posidonia oceanica), and the skipper will avoid doing so. Do not throw anything overboard; all waste is stored on the boat and disposed of at the marina. Single-use plastics are discouraged, so bring a reusable water bottle. The boat has a sewage holding tank, so toilets are not discharged directly into the sea. Safety equipment includes life jackets for all passengers, a first aid kit, fire extinguishers, and a VHF radio. The skipper holds a valid Turkish maritime licence and a safety certificate. In case of an emergency, the boat has an EPIRB and life raft. The marina has a 24-hour coast guard station. For peace of mind, ensure your travel insurance covers water activities and medical evacuation.

h1: Alanya Speedboat Rental: Hire Without Licence
intro:
You can rent a speedboat in Alanya without a boat licence. Every rental includes a licensed skipper, so you just turn up and enjoy the Mediterranean. bodyHtml:
What Is Included in an Alanya Speedboat Rental

When you rent a speedboat through BoatHire24, the package is straightforward. You get the boat for a set time, typically 4, 6, or 8 hours. A licensed skipper is included in the price. You do not need a boating licence or any previous experience. The skipper handles navigation, mooring, and safety. You can take the helm if you want, under the skipper's supervision. Fuel is usually included up to a certain number of nautical miles, typically around 30 to 40 NM. Check the specifics for each boat on the listing. Life jackets, a first aid kit, and basic safety equipment are on board. Some boats also come with a Bluetooth speaker, a small cooler, and a sunshade. What is not included: food and drinks, dockage fees at marinas you stop at (rare in Alanya), and any damage deposit (refundable, around EUR 200 to EUR 500).

Alanya Speedboat Rental Without Licence: How It Works

You do not need a licence to rent a speedboat in Alanya if the boat is rented with a skipper. That is the law. The skipper is the responsible party. You are a passenger who can drive under supervision. This is the same arrangement used in most Mediterranean destinations. The skipper will give you a quick briefing on the controls, the local navigation rules, and the no-go zones (like the area near the port entrance). After that, you can take the wheel. The skipper stays on board, ready to step in if needed. This setup is ideal if you want the freedom of driving a speedboat without the hassle of getting a licence or the stress of handling a boat alone in unfamiliar waters.

The Best Alanya Speedboat Routes and Stops

Your skipper will suggest a route, but you decide. The classic Alanya speedboat trip goes east from the marina past the Alanya Castle peninsula. You pass the iconic Red Tower and the Seljuk shipyard before rounding the point to Cleopatra Beach. From there, you can head to the caves: Damlataş Cave (famous for its stalactites and asthma-curing air), Lovers Cave, and Pirates Cave. Further east, you reach the quieter coves around İncekum Beach. If you go west, you can explore the coast towards Side, with stops at the ancient city of Selge and the Manavgat Waterfall (accessible by a short walk from the river mouth). A full-day trip can take you as far as the Alara River or the fishing village of Gazipaşa. Your skipper knows the best spots for swimming, snorkeling, and lunch. Most trips include a stop at a beachfront restaurant accessible only by boat.

Alanya Speedboat Rental Prices: What to Expect

Prices for an Alanya speedboat rental vary by boat size, engine power, and season. A basic 4-metre speedboat with a 40 HP engine starts from around EUR 150 for 4 hours in the low season (April, May, October). A 6-metre boat with a 115 HP engine costs from EUR 250 for 4 hours. High season (June to September) prices are roughly 20% to 30% higher. Full-day rentals (8 hours) typically cost double the 4-hour rate. Some boats have a maximum capacity of 4 or 6 passengers. Larger groups may need a bigger boat or a catamaran. Fuel is usually included up to 30 or 40 NM. Extra fuel costs around EUR 2 per litre if you exceed the limit. You can see exact prices on each boat's listing page on BoatHire24. No hidden fees. The price you see is the price you pay, plus any optional extras like catering or a professional photographer.

Alanya Speedboat Rental Companies: Who We Work With

BoatHire24 partners with licensed, insured boat operators in Alanya. All skippers have the required Turkish coastguard qualifications. The boats are inspected regularly and maintained to a high standard. We vet each company for safety, reliability, and customer service. You can read reviews from previous renters on each listing. If you have a problem during your rental, our support team is available by phone and WhatsApp. We have been operating in Turkey since 2018 and know the local market well. We only list boats that meet our standards, so you can book with confidence.

When Is the Best Time for an Alanya Speedboat Rental

The Alanya speedboat season runs from April to October. May, June, and September offer the best balance of warm weather and fewer crowds. July and August are hot (35 to 40 degrees C) and busy, but the sea is calm and warm (26 to 28 degrees C). April and October are cooler (20 to 25 degrees C) but still pleasant for a speedboat trip if you bring a jacket. Winter rentals are possible on calm days, but many operators reduce their schedule. If you want to avoid the midday heat, book a morning slot (9 AM to 1 PM) or a late afternoon slot (3 PM to 7 PM). Sunset trips are popular for a reason: the light on the castle and the mountains is spectacular.

How to Book an Alanya Speedboat Rental on BoatHire24

Booking takes less than five minutes. Go to the search page, select Alanya as the destination, choose your dates, and pick the number of passengers. Browse the available speedboats. Each listing shows the boat's specs, photos, price, and cancellation policy. Click the one you want, select your time slot, and pay a deposit (usually 30% to 50%) to confirm. The balance is paid on the day, directly to the skipper. You will receive a confirmation email with the meeting point details, the skipper's contact information, and a map. On the day, you meet the skipper at the Alanya Marina (or another agreed location). The skipper checks your ID and gives a safety briefing. Then you go. After the trip, you can leave a review on BoatHire24. If you need to cancel, most boats offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before the start time.

Who Is an Alanya Speedboat Rental For

Speedboat rentals suit couples, small groups of friends, and families with older children (most operators allow children from age 6, with life jackets provided). If you want a private, flexible day on the water without the crowds of a group tour, this is for you. It is also good for photographers, snorkelers, and anyone who wants to explore the coast at their own pace. If you are a larger group (more than 6 people), consider a catamaran rental for more space. If you prefer sailing, check out our sailing yacht options. For a full list of boats in Alanya, visit the BoatHire24 homepage.

Frequently Asked Questions About Alanya Speedboat Rental

We get a lot of questions about speedboat rentals in Alanya. Here are the answers to the most common ones. For more details, read our speedboat rental guide.

Alanya Speedboat Rental: Boat Types and Sizes Available

The speedboats available in Alanya range from compact 4-metre runabouts to 8-metre cabin cruisers. A 4-metre boat with a 40 to 60 HP outboard engine is perfect for two people and a quick trip to the caves. For a group of four, a 5.5-metre boat with a 90 to 115 HP engine gives you more speed and space. If you want comfort for up to six passengers, look for a 7-metre boat with a 150 HP engine and a small cabin for shade. Some boats are open bowriders, others have a centre console with a T-top for sun protection. All are equipped with a VHF radio, GPS, and basic navigation tools. The skipper will explain how to use the radio and what to do in an emergency. If you want to fish, ask about boats with a rod holder and a fish finder. Most operators can provide basic fishing gear for an extra fee.

Departure Ports and Meeting Points in Alanya

Most Alanya speedboat rentals depart from Alanya Marina, located just west of the city centre near Cleopatra Beach. The marina has parking (around EUR 5 per day), toilets, and a small cafe. Some operators also offer pickup from the fishing harbour near the Red Tower, or from the beach at İncekum if you are staying at a resort there. Your confirmation email will specify the exact meeting point. Arrive 15 minutes early to park and meet the skipper. If you are staying in a hotel between Alanya and Side, ask if the skipper can pick you up from a nearby beach or jetty. Some operators charge an extra EUR 20 to EUR 30 for a non-marina pickup. The skipper will wait at the agreed spot with a sign or a branded life jacket so you can find them easily.

What to Bring on Your Alanya Speedboat Trip

Pack light. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe if possible), a hat, and sunglasses with a strap. A waterproof phone pouch is useful for taking photos near the water. Bring a light jacket or a windbreaker for the return trip when the sea breeze picks up. If you plan to eat on board, bring your own food and drinks. Some boats have a small cooler with ice, but check the listing. You can also stop at a beachfront restaurant for lunch; the skipper will recommend places that serve fresh fish, meze, and cold beer. Bring cash for lunch and any tips for the skipper (optional, but appreciated if you had a good time). Leave valuables in your hotel safe. The boat has a dry compartment for your bag, but it is not completely waterproof. A dry bag is a good investment for electronics.

Weather and Sea Conditions for Alanya Speedboat Rentals

The Mediterranean in Alanya is generally calm from May to October. Wind speeds average 5 to 15 knots, with the strongest winds in the afternoon. Morning trips (9 AM to 1 PM) are usually the calmest. Afternoon trips can have a light chop, especially in July and August when the sea breeze picks up. The skipper will check the weather forecast before departure and will not go out if conditions are unsafe. If the forecast shows strong winds or thunderstorms, you can reschedule for free or cancel with a full refund. The sea temperature ranges from 18 degrees C in April to 28 degrees C in August. Snorkelling is best in the morning when the water is clearest. Visibility is typically 10 to 20 metres along the Alanya coast. If you are prone to seasickness, take a motion sickness tablet an hour before departure. The skipper can also adjust the speed and route to minimise discomfort.

Alanya Speedboat Rental for Special Occasions

Speedboat rentals work well for birthdays, anniversaries, proposals, and small celebrations. You can arrange for a bottle of champagne, a cake, or a fruit platter on board. Some operators offer a photographer for an extra fee to capture the moment. If you want a sunset proposal, book a 4-hour slot starting two hours before sunset. The light on the castle and the mountains is stunning, and the skipper can find a quiet cove for the moment. For a bachelor or bachelorette party, a speedboat trip with a stop at a beach club is a popular option. Just keep the group size within the boat's capacity. For a more formal event, consider a luxury yacht rental with a crew and catering. Speedboats are more casual and fun, not formal. If you want to decorate the boat, ask the operator in advance. Most are happy to help.

Alanya Speedboat Rental vs Group Boat Tours

A private speedboat rental costs more than a group boat tour, but you get privacy, flexibility, and a personalised experience. Group tours in Alanya typically cost EUR 30 to EUR 60 per person for a full day, but you share the boat with 20 to 40 other people. You follow a fixed itinerary with limited time at each stop. With a private speedboat, you decide where to go and how long to stay. You can skip crowded spots and find quiet coves. The cost per person is higher, but for a group of four to six, the difference is not huge. A private speedboat for four people costs from around EUR 150 for 4 hours, which is EUR 37.50 per person. That is comparable to a group tour but with much more freedom. If you are a solo traveller or a couple, a group tour might be more economical. But if you value privacy and flexibility, a private rental is worth the extra cost.

Alanya Speedboat Rental Safety and Insurance

All boats are insured for third-party liability and passenger accident cover. The skipper holds a valid Turkish maritime licence and first aid certificate. Life jackets are provided for all passengers, including children. The skipper will give a safety briefing before departure, covering how to use the life jackets, where the emergency equipment is, and what to do if someone falls overboard. The boat has a VHF radio to contact the coastguard if needed. Mobile phone reception is good along most of the Alanya coast. The skipper will also point out the no-go zones: the area near the port entrance, the shipping lanes, and any restricted military zones. You are not allowed to drive the boat in these areas. If you follow the skipper's instructions, the trip is very safe. Accidents are rare. If you have any medical conditions, inform the skipper before departure. They can adjust the trip accordingly.

Alanya Speedboat Rental for Fishing Enthusiasts

If you want to combine speedboating with fishing, some operators offer boats equipped with rod holders, a fish finder, and basic tackle. The best fishing spots near Alanya include the reefs off the castle peninsula, the drop-offs near İncekum, and the deeper waters a few miles offshore. Common catches include sea bream, sea bass, mackerel, and sometimes bonito. The skipper can advise on the best bait and techniques. Fishing is best in the early morning or late afternoon. You can keep your catch and have it cooked at a restaurant on the shore. If you are serious about fishing, consider a dedicated fishing boat rental with more specialised gear. But for a casual fishing trip as part of a speedboat outing, the basic setup is fine. Bring your own lures if you have favourites. The skipper will help you find the fish.

Alanya Speedboat Rental: Booking Tips and Best Practices

Book at least a few days in advance during the high season (July and August) to secure your preferred boat and time slot. For the best availability, book a morning slot. Afternoon slots are popular for sunset trips, so they fill up faster. Check the boat's maximum capacity and make sure it fits your group. If you have children, confirm that the operator provides child-sized life jackets. Read the cancellation policy before booking. Most offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before, but some have stricter terms. If you are unsure about the weather, book a boat with free rescheduling. On the day, bring your booking confirmation and a form of ID (passport or driving licence). The skipper will need to see it. If you have any special requests, such as a specific route or a stop for lunch, mention it when you book. The operator can confirm if it is possible. For last-minute bookings, call or WhatsApp BoatHire24 support. We can sometimes find a boat that is still available.

title: Alanya Private Boat Hire: Exclusive Turkey Rentals
metaDescription: Book Alanya private boat hire with a licensed skipper. Explore Cleopatra Beach, pirate caves & coves. Instant quotes for yachts, catamarans & speedboats.
h1: Alanya Private Boat Hire: Exclusive Rentals with Skipper
intro: You want a day on the water in Alanya without the crowds, the hassle, or the hidden costs. Private boat hire is the only way to do it properly: your own vessel, your own itinerary, and a licensed skipper who knows the coastline better than any travel app. From the moment you step aboard in Alanya Marina, you are in control. Fancy a swim off Cleopatra Beach before the tour boats arrive? Done. Want to anchor near the Pirate Caves and eat lunch in peace? That is the plan. This page tells you exactly what to expect, what it costs, and how to book the right boat for your group.
bodyHtml:
What Is Included in an Alanya Private Boat Hire

Every private charter on BoatHire24 includes a professional skipper, fuel for the agreed itinerary, safety equipment, and basic insurance. You do not need a boating licence, and you do not need to worry about navigation. The skipper handles everything from mooring to weather checks. Most boats also include a cooler with ice, a Bluetooth speaker, and a shaded cockpit or bimini top. Some larger yachts and catamarans offer a hostess, paddleboards, or a barbecue grill. What is not included? Food and drinks, unless you book a catering package, and port fees if you decide to stop at a marina restaurant. Always confirm the exact inclusions with the owner before you pay.

Alanya Marina and Departure Points

Your charter will almost always start from BoatHire24 partner berths in Alanya Marina, which sits right next to the Damlatas Caves and the city centre. The marina has parking, cafes, and a small supermarket for last-minute supplies. Some skippers also offer pickups from the public jetty near Cleopatra Beach or from the small harbour at Mahmutlar, east of Alanya. If you are staying at a resort between Side and Gazipasa, ask the owner about a marina transfer or a direct hotel pickup by taxi. The whole coastline from Alanya to Anamur is accessible, but the most popular routes run west to the Dim River or east to the ancient city of Selinus.

Boat Types Available for Private Hire

You can rent motor yachts from 8 to 18 metres, sailing yachts, catamarans, and speedboats. Motor yachts are the most common choice: they offer a steady ride, plenty of deck space, and a cabin with a toilet and shower. Catamarans give you more stability and a wider sunbathing area, ideal for groups who want to spread out. Speedboats and RIBs are cheaper and faster, but they have less shade and no toilet. For a full-day excursion with lunch and swimming stops, a 12-metre motor yacht is the sweet spot. If you want to sail, a 14-metre Beneteau or Jeanneau will give you a proper sailing experience with a skipper who handles the lines.

Pricing Guidance for Alanya Private Boat Hire

Prices vary by season, boat size, and duration. For a half-day (4 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht, expect to pay from around EUR 350. A full day (8 hours) on a 12-metre yacht starts at approximately EUR 600. Catamarans in the same size range cost about 20 percent more. Speedboats and RIBs for a half-day can be found from EUR 200. Superyachts and luxury motor yachts over 20 metres are price on request, usually starting above EUR 2,500 per day. Fuel is included in the quoted price, but if you want to go long distances to Gazipasa or Anamur, there may be a fuel surcharge. Always ask for a breakdown of costs before booking.

Best Itineraries for Your Day on the Water

The classic Alanya private boat tour heads west: past Cleopatra Beach, the Damlatas Caves, and the Pirate Caves, then on to the Dim River estuary for a swim and a riverside lunch. Another favourite is the east route to the ancient city of Selinus (now Gazipasa), where you can see Roman ruins from the water and anchor off a quiet beach. If you have a full day, ask your skipper to take you to the Phosphorus Cave, a sea cave near Mahmutlar where the water glows in the afternoon light. For snorkellers, the reef off Incekum Beach has decent visibility and a few fish. Your skipper will tailor the route to your interests, so be clear about what you want to see.

When to Hire a Private Boat in Alanya

The season runs from April to October, with June through September being the busiest and most expensive months. July and August see air temperatures around 35 degrees C and water temperatures of 28 degrees C. If you want calmer seas and fewer crowds, May and October are excellent: the water is still warm enough to swim, and the sun is less aggressive. Winter charters are possible but rare; many skippers lay up their boats from November to March. For the best balance of weather and price, aim for late May or early June. Booking at least a week in advance is recommended in high season, especially for larger yachts and catamarans.

How to Book an Alanya Private Boat Hire

Start by using the search page to filter by boat type, group size, and budget. Each listing shows photos, a detailed description, and the owner's contact information. You can message the owner directly to ask about availability and negotiate the itinerary. Payment is usually by bank transfer or cash on the day. Some owners accept credit cards with a small surcharge. Once you agree on a date and price, the owner will send a confirmation and the skipper's phone number. On the day, arrive at the marina 15 minutes early to meet the skipper and do a safety briefing. If you need to cancel, check the owner's cancellation policy: most offer a full refund up to 48 hours before departure.

Who Is Private Boat Hire For

It suits couples who want a romantic sunset cruise, families with children who need flexible swimming stops, and groups of friends who want to party without disturbing other guests. It also works for corporate events, small weddings, and photography shoots. If you are a solo traveller, you can join a shared tour, but the whole point of private hire is exclusivity. The minimum group size is usually 2, and the maximum depends on the boat's licence: a 12-metre motor yacht typically carries 10 to 12 passengers. Children are welcome, and life jackets are provided in all sizes. If you have mobility issues, ask about step-free access before booking; most boats require stepping from the pontoon.

Local Rules and Safety

Turkish maritime law requires all charter boats to carry life jackets, fire extinguishers, and a first aid kit. Your skipper holds a professional licence and knows the local hazards, such as the occasional afternoon wind shift called the meltem. Swimming is allowed anywhere outside the marina and shipping lanes. Speeding and reckless navigation are not tolerated; the coast guard patrols the area. Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper cannot drink. If you plan to smoke, use the ashtray provided and never throw butts overboard. Respect the environment: take your rubbish ashore, and do not touch marine life or archaeological sites. The sea around Alanya is generally clean, but plastic waste from rivers can appear after heavy rain.

What to Bring and Wear

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, and a light jacket or towel for the wind. Swimwear and a change of clothes are obvious. If you plan to eat on board, bring your own food and drinks, or order a catering package from the owner. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos. The boat will have a toilet, but bring your own toilet paper just in case. Seasickness is rare in the calm bay, but if you are prone to it, take a motion sickness pill an hour before departure. The skipper will have a first aid kit, but bring any personal medication. A small bag is better than a bulky suitcase; storage space on a 10-metre boat is limited.

Comparing Alanya Private Boat Hire to Group Tours

Group tours cost from around EUR 30 per person and follow a fixed route with 30 to 50 other passengers. You get less time at each stop, no flexibility, and a loud soundtrack. Private hire costs more per person, but the experience is completely different. You choose the music, the speed, the stops, and the lunch spot. You can linger at a cave or skip a beach altogether. For a group of six or more, the per-person cost of private hire often matches or beats a group tour, especially if you split the price. And you never have to queue for the toilet. That alone is worth the upgrade.

Nearby Attractions and Extensions

If you have time, combine your boat hire with a visit to Alanya Castle, the Dim River Canyon, or the ancient theatre in Side. The marina is a 10-minute walk from the cable car station to the castle. For a longer charter, ask your skipper to take you to the island of Cyprus? It is 100 NM away and requires an overnight trip, but some owners offer it. More realistically, a full-day charter to the ancient city of Anamur (110 km east) is possible with a fast motor yacht. The Nerja caves of Turkey? Not exactly, but the Caves of Heaven and Hell near Narlıkuyu are a 2-hour drive from Alanya and worth a separate day trip. Your skipper can recommend a local driver for land excursions.

For more tips on chartering in Turkey, check the blog for seasonal guides and owner interviews.

Choosing the Right Boat Size for Your Group

Group size dictates the boat you need. For a couple or a small family, an 8-metre motor yacht works fine: it has a small cabin, a toilet, and a sun pad. For 6 to 8 people, go for a 12-metre model with a larger deck and a proper dining area. Groups of 10 to 12 need a 15-metre yacht or a catamaran. Catamarans at 14 metres give you two hulls with separate cabins, a flybridge, and a trampoline net at the bow. Speedboats and RIBs are best for 4 to 6 people who want speed and agility, not comfort. If you book a boat that is too small, the day feels cramped; too large, and you pay for space you do not use. The owner can advise on the right fit based on your headcount.

Fuel Costs and Surcharges Explained

The quoted price usually includes fuel for a standard route of about 20 to 30 nautical miles. If you want to go further, say to the Dim River mouth or Gazipasa, the skipper may add a fuel surcharge. Diesel in Turkey costs around EUR 1.20 per litre, and a 12-metre motor yacht burns roughly 20 to 30 litres per hour at cruising speed. For a full-day trip covering 50 NM, that is about EUR 100 in fuel. Speedboats with outboard engines use less but are still thirsty at full throttle. Ask the owner for a fuel estimate before you agree on the itinerary. Some owners include a flat-rate fuel fee in the price; others charge by the hour or the distance. Get it in writing to avoid surprises.

Dining Options: Catering, Restaurants, and Self-Catering

Most Alanya private boat hire charters let you bring your own food and drinks. The boat has a fridge and a cooler, so pack a picnic, snacks, and plenty of water. If you want a hot meal, some owners offer a catering package for around EUR 25 to 40 per person: typically grilled fish, chicken, salad, rice, and fruit. Alternatively, you can stop at a waterfront restaurant. Popular spots include the Dim River restaurants, where you can moor and eat fresh trout, or the beach clubs at Cleopatra Beach. Restaurant stops add port fees of about EUR 10 to 20 and take time out of your swimming. For a relaxed day, self-catering is cheaper and gives you control over the menu.

Sunset Cruises and Evening Charters

Sunset cruises are a popular option for couples and small groups. They typically run from 17:00 to 20:00 in summer, when the sun sets over the Taurus Mountains. You get the golden hour light, cooler temperatures, and fewer other boats on the water. Prices start from around EUR 250 for a 10-metre motor yacht. Some owners offer a sunset package with sparkling wine and fruit. Evening charters after dark are less common because the marina closes at a certain hour, but you can arrange a dinner cruise with advance notice. The sea is calm in the evening, and you can see the lights of Alanya Castle from the water. Book these early, as they are popular with honeymooners.

Booking for Special Occasions: Birthdays, Proposals, and Weddings

Private boat hire works well for celebrations. For a birthday, you can bring decorations, a cake, and a playlist. For a proposal, the skipper can help you choose a scenic spot like the Phosphorus Cave or a quiet cove near Incekum. Some owners offer a photographer for an extra fee. For a small wedding ceremony, you need a boat with a large deck and a captain who can officiate or a separate registrar. Turkish law requires a civil ceremony on land, so the boat is for the reception only. Groups of up to 20 can fit on a 15-metre catamaran. Discuss the plan with the owner in advance so they can prepare the boat and the crew. Prices for special events are negotiable, but expect a premium of 20 to 30 percent over a standard charter.

Weather and Sea Conditions in Alanya

The Mediterranean off Alanya is usually calm from May to October. Swell heights average 0.5 to 1 metre, and wind speeds are under 10 knots most days. The meltem wind, a light afternoon breeze from the north-west, can pick up to 15 knots in July and August, but it is not dangerous for a 12-metre yacht. Thunderstorms are rare in summer but possible in April and October. The skipper monitors weather forecasts and will cancel or reroute if conditions are unsafe. If the sea is too rough for your chosen boat, the owner may offer a larger vessel or a refund. For the smoothest ride, book a morning charter before the wind rises. Afternoon charters are fine but may have a slight chop near the headlands.

Payment, Deposits, and Cancellation Policies

Most owners require a deposit of 30 to 50 percent to confirm the booking, with the balance due on the day. Deposits are usually paid by bank transfer or cash. Some owners accept PayPal or credit cards with a 3 to 5 percent surcharge. Cancellation policies vary: many offer a full refund if you cancel 48 hours before departure, but after that, the deposit may be non-refundable. In case of bad weather, the owner typically offers a reschedule or a full refund. Read the terms on the listing page before you pay. For peace of mind, consider travel insurance that covers trip cancellation. If you book through BoatHire24, the platform provides a secure messaging system to track agreements and payments.

Environmental Responsibility and Marine Life

The waters around Alanya host sea turtles (loggerhead and green), dolphins, and occasional monk seals. Your skipper will avoid disturbing them, and you should too. Do not feed the fish or touch the turtles. Anchor only in sandy areas, not on seagrass beds. Use reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine ecosystem. If you see a turtle entangled in fishing line, alert the skipper. The Turkish coast guard and local NGOs monitor the area, and fines for littering or damaging protected species can reach EUR 500. Most owners are environmentally conscious and will brief you on the rules. Leave the sea as you found it, and take all rubbish back to shore. This keeps Alanya beautiful for everyone.

Extending Your Charter: Multi-Day Trips and Overnight Stays

For a multi-day charter, you need a yacht with cabins and a galley. A 14-metre sailing yacht or a 15-metre motor yacht can accommodate 4 to 6 guests overnight. The skipper sleeps in a separate cabin or on deck. Multi-day trips let you explore further: west to Side and Olympos, or east to Anamur and the Kızkalesi castle. Costs are typically EUR 800 to 1,500 per night, including fuel and the skipper. You stop at different anchorages each day, eat on board or at local restaurants, and sleep under the stars. Book these well in advance, as the owner needs to prepare provisions and plan the route. A multi-day charter is the closest you get to a private yacht holiday without owning one.

bodyHtml:
What Kemer Boat Hire Actually Means for the Costa del Sol

Kemer boat hire on the Costa del Sol is a misnomer, but it points to a real demand: private boat charters with a skipper, flexible itineraries, and a lively coastal setting. On the Costa del Sol, you get exactly that, but with a different backdrop. Instead of the Taurus Mountains, you have La Concha mountain. Instead of Kemer Marina, you have Puerto Banús, the most glamorous port in Spain. The boats are the same: motor yachts from 8m to 30m, catamarans for stability, sailing yachts for purists, RIBs for speed, and fishing boats for the catch of the day. The difference is that every charter includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the best anchorages, and the least crowded coves. No need to worry about licensing, insurance, or navigation. You just show up, relax, and let someone else handle the ropes.

Departure Ports for Your Kemer-Style Experience

If you were in Kemer, you would depart from Kemer Marina or nearby ports. On the Costa del Sol, you have five main departure points, each with its own character. Puerto Banús is the most famous, home to superyachts, designer boutiques, and a buzzing nightlife. It is the closest you get to the glitz of the Turkish Riviera. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more laid-back, with a long promenade and direct access to the old town. Cabopino is a small, sandy-bottomed marina near the dunes of Artola, ideal for a quieter start. Estepona has a charming old town and a modern marina with good facilities. Sotogrande is the luxury enclave, with a polo club and a more exclusive feel. Benalmádena is a family-friendly port with a large marina and easy access to the open sea. Each port is within 30-45 minutes of the others, so you can choose based on your accommodation or itinerary. For a full list of available boats, see our search page.

Boat Types Available for Kemer-Style Charters

The fleet on the Costa del Sol mirrors what you would find in Kemer, but with a Spanish twist. Motor yachts are the most popular, ranging from 10m to 25m, with sun pads, a flybridge, and a swim platform. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a 12m yacht. Catamarans are perfect for groups, offering more deck space and stability. A 14m catamaran can take up to 12 guests for around EUR 2,000 for a full day. Sailing yachts are for those who want the wind in their hair, from 10m to 18m, with prices from EUR 800 for half a day. RIBs and speedboats are for adrenaline seekers, with powerful engines and minimal frills. A 7m RIB with a 250hp engine costs from EUR 400 for two hours. Fishing boats are equipped with rods and sonar, and the skipper knows the best spots for sea bass, bream, and tuna. Prices from EUR 600 for half a day. Licence-free day boats are rare on the Costa del Sol because the law requires a licence for any boat over 5m, but our charters always include a skipper, so you are covered. Superyachts are available for the top end, from 30m to 50m, with a crew, jet skis, and a full bar. Prices on request, but expect EUR 10,000-plus for a day.

Pricing Guidance for Kemer-Style Boat Hire

Kemer boat hire on the Costa del Sol varies by season, boat size, and duration. As a rule, high season (June to September) is 30-50% more expensive than low season (October to May). Half-day charters (4 hours) are the most common, with prices from EUR 400 for a small RIB to EUR 3,000 for a 20m motor yacht. Full-day charters (8 hours) add lunch, drinks, and fuel. Expect to pay EUR 800 for a sailing yacht, EUR 1,500 for a catamaran, and EUR 5,000-plus for a superyacht. Fuel is usually extra, around EUR 200-500 for a day depending on distance. Food and drink can be provided by the skipper or a catering service, from EUR 30 per person for a simple barbecue to EUR 100 for a gourmet menu. Tips are customary, usually 10-15% of the charter fee. For exact pricing, use the booking form on each boat listing.

Best Seasons for Kemer-Style Boat Charters

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, so you can hire a boat in any season. Summer (June to August) is peak season, with temperatures of 30-35 degrees C, calm seas, and long daylight hours. This is the best time for swimming, sunbathing, and partying. Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to October) are ideal for a quieter experience, with temperatures of 20-28 degrees C and fewer crowds. The sea is still warm enough for swimming until October. Winter (November to February) is the low season, with 15-20 degrees C and occasional rain. The water is too cold for swimming, but you can still sail, fish, or sightsee. Many skippers offer reduced rates in winter, from EUR 300 for a half-day on a small boat. The best months for dolphin spotting are April to June and September to November, when they migrate through the Strait of Gibraltar.

What Is Included in a Kemer-Style Boat Hire

Every charter on the Costa del Sol includes a licensed skipper, insurance, and basic safety equipment. The skipper will handle all navigation, docking, and local knowledge. They will also recommend a route based on your preferences, whether you want to explore the coast, anchor in a cove, or visit a specific beach. Some charters include fuel, but most charge it separately. Food and drink are not included unless you book a package. You can bring your own food and drink, or the skipper can arrange catering. Water toys like paddleboards, snorkels, and inflatables are often available on request. For a full list of inclusions, check the boat listing on our site. We also have a blog with tips on what to bring and how to plan your day.

How to Book a Kemer-Style Boat Hire

Booking on BoatHire24 is straightforward. Browse our fleet by port, boat type, or price range. Each listing shows photos, specs, and a calendar. Select your date and duration, then submit a booking request. The owner or skipper will confirm within 24 hours. You can pay by credit card or bank transfer, with a 30% deposit to hold the booking. The balance is due on the day of departure. Cancellations are free up to 7 days before the charter. For last-minute bookings, contact us directly and we can often arrange something within 48 hours. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for summer and 1 week for other seasons.

Who Is Kemer-Style Boat Hire For

This type of charter is for anyone who wants a private, hassle-free day on the water. It is perfect for couples looking for a romantic sunset cruise, families with children who want a safe, child-friendly environment, and groups of friends who want to party or celebrate a special occasion. It is also ideal for corporate events, team-building days, or client entertainment. The skipper takes care of everything, so you do not need any boating experience. If you are a seasoned sailor, you can still charter a bareboat in some cases, but most owners prefer to include a skipper. For licence-free options, the RIBs and small motorboats are the easiest, but they still come with a skipper. The key is that you are the captain of your itinerary, not the boat. You decide where to go, when to eat, and how long to stay.

Local Highlights on a Kemer-Style Charter

The Costa del Sol has plenty of local colour. From Puerto Banús, you can cruise past the mansions of the rich and famous, then anchor at Cala del Faro, a quiet cove with crystal-clear water. From Marbella, you can head east to the Río Verde estuary, where you might spot flamingos. From Estepona, the Strait of Gibraltar is a 30-minute sail away, where you can see dolphins, whales, and the coast of Africa. From Cabopino, the Nerja Caves are a 45-minute drive from the port, but you can also anchor near the cliffs of Maro and swim into the caves. The best part is that every skipper has their own secret spots, so ask them for recommendations.

Why Choose BoatHire24 for Your Kemer-Style Charter

BoatHire24 is the leading marketplace for private boat charters on the Costa del Sol. We vet every boat and skipper for safety, insurance, and customer reviews. We offer transparent pricing with no hidden fees. We have a local team based in Marbella who can answer your questions in English and Spanish. And we have the largest selection of boats, from budget RIBs to luxury superyachts. If you are comparing Kemer boat hire to the Costa del Sol, we think you will find the Spanish option more convenient, more varied, and equally beautiful. Start your search on our search page or contact us for personalised recommendations.

Comparing Kemer and Costa del Sol Boat Hire: What You Actually Get

If you have searched for Kemer boat hire, you are probably weighing up whether to go to Turkey or stick closer to home. The Costa del Sol does not have the same all-inclusive resort vibe, but it has better infrastructure for private charters. In Kemer, most boat trips are shared gulet cruises with set routes. On the Costa del Sol, every charter is private, so you control the itinerary. The water temperature in summer is similar, around 24-26 degrees C, but the Costa del Sol has more varied coastline, from sandy beaches to rocky cliffs. The wind conditions are also more reliable for sailing, with the Poniente and Levante winds providing consistent breezes. And you do not need a visa or a flight longer than three hours from most of Europe.

Practical Costs: Fuel, Food, and Extras

Beyond the base hire price, you need to budget for fuel, which is not always included. A typical motor yacht burns 60-100 litres per hour, so a full day can cost EUR 300-600 in fuel alone. Catamarans are more efficient, using 30-50 litres per hour. Sailing yachts use almost no fuel if the wind is good, but you might motor for an hour or two. Food and drink are usually not included, but you can bring your own or order a catering package. A basic lunch of paella, salad, and drinks costs around EUR 25-35 per person. A premium menu with seafood, steak, and champagne is EUR 60-80 per person. Some skippers offer a BYO option with a cooler and ice provided. Water toys like paddleboards (EUR 50-100 per day) and jet skis (EUR 200-400 per hour) can be added on request. For a full breakdown of costs, check our blog on budgeting for a boat charter.

Best Anchorages and Coves for Your Charter

The Costa del Sol has dozens of anchorages, but some stand out. Cala del Moral near Marbella is a small, pebbly beach with clear water, perfect for a morning swim. Cala de las Tortugas near Estepona is a turtle sanctuary, though you are unlikely to see them. Playa de la Rijana near La Herradura is a wild beach accessible only by boat, with a natural waterfall. Puerto de la Duquesa is a small marina with a good restaurant for lunch. Marina del Este near Almuñécar is a stunning cove with a beach bar. For a longer trip, you can go to Gibraltar (1.5 hours from Estepona) and see the Rock from the water. Your skipper will know which spots are sheltered from the wind and which have the best water quality on any given day.

What to Wear and Bring for a Day on the Water

You are in Spain, so dress for the sun but bring layers. A light jumper or windbreaker is useful even in summer, as the sea breeze can be cool. Non-slip shoes are a good idea, especially on a RIB or speedboat. Sunscreen (factor 50), a hat, and sunglasses are essential. A rash guard or UV shirt helps if you burn easily. Bring a towel, swimwear, and a change of clothes. If you plan to snorkel, bring your own mask and fins, though many boats have a basic set. A waterproof phone case or dry bag is useful for valuables. For seasickness, take a tablet the night before and another in the morning. Ginger sweets or wristbands work for mild cases. Most boats have a bathroom (heads), but it is usually a marine toilet, not a luxury loo. Plan accordingly.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group

The size of your group determines the boat type. For 2-4 people, a RIB or small motor yacht (8-10m) is fine. For 4-8 people, a 12-15m motor yacht or catamaran gives you space to spread out. For 8-12 people, a 15-20m catamaran or motor yacht is ideal. For 12-20 people, you need a 20-30m superyacht or a large catamaran. Keep in mind that capacity limits are strict for insurance reasons, so do not try to squeeze in extra guests. The boat listing on our site shows the maximum capacity, which includes children. If you want a party boat with music and a DJ, some skippers offer that, but it costs extra. For a quiet family day, a sailing yacht or catamaran is better than a loud motor yacht. For a fishing trip, choose a boat with a fighting chair and rod holders. For a sunset cruise, any boat works, but a catamaran gives you the best deck space for watching the sun go down.

Special Occasions: Birthdays, Proposals, and Weddings

Boat charters are popular for celebrations. For a birthday, you can bring decorations, a cake, and a playlist. Some skippers have a sound system on board. For a proposal, the skipper can help you arrange a private moment, like anchoring in a secluded cove at sunset. For a wedding, you can charter a superyacht for the ceremony and reception, but you need to check with the port authority for permits. The cost for a wedding charter starts from around EUR 5,000 for a half-day on a 20m yacht, plus catering and decorations. For a simple elopement, a small catamaran with a skipper and a photographer costs from EUR 1,500. We have a guide on our blog about planning a boat wedding on the Costa del Sol.

Safety and Weather: What You Need to Know

The Costa del Sol is generally safe for boating, but you need to respect the weather. The Levante wind can pick up in the afternoon, gusting to 25-30 knots. Your skipper will monitor the forecast and adjust the route if needed. If the sea state is too rough, the charter may be cancelled, and you will get a full refund. Life jackets are mandatory for children under 12 and available for adults. Most boats have a VHF radio, GPS, and a first aid kit. If you have any medical conditions, inform the skipper before departure. Seasickness is the most common issue, so take precautions. The water is generally clean, but avoid swimming near river mouths after heavy rain. Jellyfish are rare, but they can appear in August. Your skipper will know if there are any warnings.

Last-Minute Bookings and Availability

If you are reading this on a whim, you can often book a boat within 48 hours, especially in low season. In summer, availability is tight, so book at least two weeks ahead. For last-minute bookings, call us or use the contact form on our site. We have a fleet of boats that are available at short notice, usually RIBs and small motor yachts. The price might be slightly higher for last-minute, but not always. If you are flexible on the date or port, we can find you a deal. For example, a Monday or Tuesday charter is often cheaper than a Saturday. The best time to book is 10am to 2pm, when skippers are checking their calendars. For more tips, visit our BoatHire24 homepage and browse the latest availability.
