h1: Kemer Yacht Charter: Luxury Boat Rental Turkey
intro: You want to charter a yacht in Kemer, Turkey, and you want the facts without the fluff. Kemer is a busy resort town on the Turkish Riviera, backed by the Taurus Mountains and fronted by clear blue water. The main marina, Kemer Marina, is modern and well-equipped, handling everything from small speedboats to superyachts. Most charters include a licensed skipper, so you do not need a licence yourself. You can book a motor yacht for a day trip to the nearby bays, a catamaran for a relaxed family outing, or a RIB for a fast ride to the sunken city of Olympos. Prices start from around EUR 400 for a half-day RIB trip and go up to EUR 2,500 or more for a full-day luxury motor yacht with crew. This page covers everything you need to know about Kemer yacht charter, from the ports and boat types to the best seasons and how to book.
bodyHtml:
What is Included in a Kemer Yacht Charter

When you book a Kemer yacht charter through BoatHire24, the standard package includes the boat, a licensed skipper, fuel for the agreed itinerary, and basic safety equipment. Most charters also include VAT and port fees. You can add extras like a hostess, catering, water toys (jet skis, paddleboards), or a private chef. The skipper handles navigation and mooring, and they know the best spots for swimming and snorkelling. You do not need to tip, but it is customary to give around 10% if you are happy with the service. Always confirm what is included before you book, especially fuel and food, as some charters charge separately for these.

Kemer Marina: Your Departure Point

Kemer Marina is the main departure point for yacht charters in the area. It is located right in the centre of Kemer, close to hotels, restaurants, and shops. The marina has 250 berths and can accommodate yachts up to 50 metres. It is a full-service marina with a fuel dock, water and electricity supply, and a chandlery. From here, you can head south towards the ancient city of Phaselis or north towards the coves of Çıralı and Olympos. The marina is about 45 minutes from Antalya Airport by taxi, making it easy to reach. If you are staying in a hotel nearby, many offer free shuttle services to the marina. For more details on ports, visit our search page and filter by departure port.

Boat Types Available for Kemer Yacht Charter

You have several options when choosing a boat for your Kemer yacht charter. Motor yachts are the most popular, ranging from 10 to 20 metres, with cabins, a saloon, and a flybridge. They are ideal for day trips and overnight stays. Catamarans are wider and more stable, great for families or groups, with more deck space and shallower drafts for anchoring in bays. Sailing yachts are available for those who prefer a quieter, wind-powered experience. RIBs and speedboats are smaller, faster, and cheaper, perfect for a quick trip to a snorkelling spot. Licence-free day boats are also available, but you must stay within sight of the coast and not go beyond 2 NM from shore. Superyachts are available on request, with prices starting from around EUR 10,000 per day. For a full list of options, check our BoatHire24 homepage.

Popular Destinations from Kemer

A typical Kemer yacht charter itinerary includes a visit to Phaselis, an ancient Lycian city with three beaches and ruins that go right down to the water. You can anchor there for a swim and a walk. Another favourite is the Olympos area, including the sunken city near Çıralı Beach. The Chimera flames, natural gas vents that have been burning for millennia, are visible from the sea at night. Further south, you can reach the island of Kekova and the ghost town of Simena, but this is a longer trip, usually requiring an overnight charter. The bays around Kemer itself, such as Tekirova and Çamyuva, are calm and sheltered, with clear water for snorkelling. The average water temperature in summer is 26 degrees C, and the air temperature hovers around 32 degrees C. You can read more about destinations on our blog.

Pricing Guidance for Kemer Yacht Charter

Prices for a Kemer yacht charter vary widely depending on the boat type, size, season, and duration. As a rough guide, a half-day (4-hour) RIB trip for up to 6 people starts from around EUR 400. A full-day (8-hour) motor yacht for up to 10 people starts from around EUR 1,200. A full-day catamaran for up to 12 people starts from around EUR 1,800. Luxury motor yachts over 15 metres can cost EUR 2,500 to EUR 5,000 per day. Superyachts are price on request. High season (July and August) is the most expensive, with prices up to 50% higher than low season (May and October). Shoulder season (June and September) offers good value. Always book in advance, especially for high season, as popular boats get booked up weeks ahead. You can compare prices and availability on our search page.

Best Seasons for Kemer Yacht Charter

The best time for a Kemer yacht charter is from May to October. May and June are warm but not too hot, with sea temperatures around 22 degrees C. July and August are peak season: hot, crowded, and more expensive, but the sea is at its warmest. September and October are still warm, with fewer crowds and lower prices. The wind is generally light in summer, with occasional afternoon breezes. In winter (November to April), many boats are laid up, and the weather is cooler and rainier, though you can still charter some boats if you want a quiet trip. The average wind speed in summer is 10-15 knots, mostly from the north-west. The Mediterranean is generally calm, but afternoon winds can pick up, so listen to your skipper.

How to Book a Kemer Yacht Charter

Booking a Kemer yacht charter is straightforward. You can use the search filters on our website to choose your dates, boat type, and group size. Once you find a boat you like, you can request a quote or book directly online. You will need to pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the booking, with the balance due on the day of departure. You can pay by credit card or bank transfer. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for high season, and 4 weeks for large groups or specific boats. The booking process is secure, and you will receive a confirmation email with all the details. If you have any questions, you can contact us via the website chat or email.

Who is a Kemer Yacht Charter For

A Kemer yacht charter is suitable for couples, families, groups of friends, and corporate events. If you are a couple, a small motor yacht or a RIB is a good choice for a romantic day trip. Families with children will appreciate a catamaran for its stability and space. Groups of friends can hire a larger motor yacht with a saloon and a flybridge. Corporate events, such as team-building or client entertainment, can be arranged on a superyacht or a large catamaran. The minimum age for passengers is usually 1 year, and children must be supervised. There is no upper age limit, but you should be able to board the boat safely. If you have mobility issues, check with the charter company in advance, as some boats have steep steps.

Local Highlights and Attractions

Kemer itself is a lively resort with a long beach, a marina promenade, and plenty of bars and restaurants. The nearby ancient city of Phaselis is a must-see, with its three beaches and Roman aqueducts. The Chimera flames near Çıralı are a unique natural phenomenon, best seen at dusk. The Olympos ruins, including a Byzantine church and a Roman theatre, are a short walk from the beach. The area is also known for its pine forests and hiking trails. For a longer trip, you can charter a yacht to the town of Kas, about 2 hours south, or to the island of Rhodes, which is about 3 hours away by speedboat. The Strait of Gibraltar is not relevant here, but you can see dolphins in the area, especially around the bays.

Frequently Asked Questions

Customising Your Kemer Yacht Charter Itinerary

Most Kemer yacht charter bookings are flexible, and you can tailor the route to suit your preferences. A standard day trip might leave Kemer Marina at 10:00, cruise south to Phaselis for a swim and lunch, then head to a quieter bay like Tekirova for afternoon snorkelling before returning around 18:00. If you want a longer day, you can add a stop at the Chimera flames for a sunset view, or push further to Çıralı Beach for a walk on the sand. For overnight charters, you can anchor in a secluded cove or dock at a marina like Olympos. The skipper will advise on distances: from Kemer to Phaselis is about 10 NM (nautical miles), to Çıralı is 15 NM, and to Kekova is 40 NM. Discuss your itinerary with the charter company before departure to ensure you have enough fuel and time. For more ideas, browse our blog for sample routes.

What to Pack for a Kemer Yacht Charter

Packing smart makes your Kemer yacht charter more comfortable. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (SPF 50, water-resistant), a hat, and sunglasses. The sun is strong here, especially between 11:00 and 15:00. A light jacket or long-sleeve shirt helps against wind or evening chill. Non-slip shoes are useful for walking on deck and on rocky beaches. If you plan to snorkel, your own mask and snorkel can be more comfortable than shared gear, though most boats provide them. A waterproof phone pouch is handy for photos. Motion sickness pills are worth taking if you are prone to it, even in calm seas. Finally, bring cash for tips, souvenirs, or a drink at a beach bar. The boat may have a cooler, but you can bring your own drinks and snacks if you prefer.

Kemer Yacht Charter for Families with Children

Families are well catered for on a Kemer yacht charter. Catamarans are the best choice because they are stable and have lots of deck space for kids to play. Most charter boats provide life jackets for children in various sizes, but confirm this when booking. The shallow bays around Kemer, such as Çamyuva and Tekirova, are safe for swimming, with gentle entry and no strong currents. Many boats have a small tender (dinghy) for exploring shallow coves. You can also request a hostess to help with meals and childcare for an extra fee. The minimum age for passengers is usually 1 year, and children must be supervised at all times. For younger children, a half-day charter is often enough to avoid boredom. Check our BoatHire24 homepage for family-friendly boat listings.

Kemer Yacht Charter for Corporate Events and Parties

Corporate groups can use a Kemer yacht charter for team-building, client entertainment, or product launches. Motor yachts and catamarans over 15 metres are ideal, with space for 20 to 50 guests. You can add catering, a bar, and entertainment like a DJ or live music. Some boats have a saloon with air conditioning, a sound system, and a TV for presentations. The crew can handle logistics, so you can focus on networking. Typical corporate charters last from 4 to 8 hours, but full-day or multi-day options are available. Prices for a corporate event start from around EUR 3,000 for a half-day on a mid-sized motor yacht. For larger groups, you can charter multiple boats. Book at least 4 weeks in advance for high season. Use our search page to filter by capacity and amenities.

Eco-Friendly Practices on Kemer Yacht Charters

Many Kemer yacht charter operators are adopting eco-friendly practices to protect the Mediterranean. They use biodegradable cleaning products, recycle waste, and avoid single-use plastics. Some boats have solar panels for auxiliary power. You can help by bringing a reusable water bottle and avoiding sunscreen that contains oxybenzone, which damages coral. The anchorages near Phaselis and Olympos are sensitive areas, so the skipper will avoid dropping anchor on seagrass beds. Instead, they use mooring buoys where available. If you see marine life, such as sea turtles or dolphins, keep a respectful distance. The water in Kemer is generally clean, with good visibility for snorkelling. By choosing a responsible operator, you help preserve the area for future visitors.

Combining Kemer Yacht Charter with Land Activities

A Kemer yacht charter can be part of a larger holiday that includes land-based activities. After a day on the water, you can explore the ancient ruins of Phaselis on foot, hike the Lycian Way trail, or visit the Chimera flames at night. Kemer town has a lively nightlife with bars, clubs, and restaurants serving Turkish and international food. You can also take a jeep safari into the Taurus Mountains, go paragliding over Olympos, or visit the Antalya Aquarium. If you charter a yacht for multiple days, you can combine sailing with stops at historical sites and coastal villages. For example, an overnight charter could include a morning at Phaselis, an afternoon at Çıralı Beach, and an evening at the Chimera flames. The flexibility is one of the biggest advantages of a private charter.

Safety and Weather Considerations for Kemer Yacht Charter

Safety is a priority on any Kemer yacht charter. The boat will have life jackets, a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher, and a VHF radio. The skipper is licensed and trained in safety procedures. Before departure, the skipper will give a safety briefing, including how to use the life jackets and where the emergency equipment is. The weather in Kemer is generally good for sailing from May to October, but conditions can change. The Meltemi wind, which blows from the north-west in summer, can reach 25 knots in the afternoon, especially in open water. If the wind picks up, the skipper will adjust the route to sheltered bays. Always listen to the skipper's advice. If you are prone to seasickness, take medication before you board. The boat will have a first aid kit, but it is wise to bring your own supplies.

Insurance and Cancellation Policies for Kemer Yacht Charter

When you book a Kemer yacht charter through BoatHire24, the boat is insured for third-party liability and damage. However, your personal belongings are not covered, so consider travel insurance that covers theft, loss, and medical expenses. Cancellation policies vary by operator, but a common policy is: free cancellation up to 14 days before departure, 50% refund between 7 and 14 days, and no refund within 7 days. In case of bad weather, the charter may be rescheduled or refunded at the operator's discretion. Read the terms carefully before booking. If you have specific requirements, such as a full refund for medical reasons, ask the charter company in advance. For more details, contact us via the website chat.

intro:
You want a private catamaran trip in Kemer, but you are probably looking at the wrong coastline. Kemer is a Turkish resort near Antalya, not a port on the Costa del Sol. However, if you are searching for catamaran hire in the Marbella area, you have come to the right place. bodyHtml:
What Is Included in a Catamaran Hire

When you book a catamaran through BoatHire24, the price typically includes the vessel, a professional skipper, fuel for a standard itinerary, and basic safety equipment. Most charters also provide a cooler with ice, onboard Bluetooth speakers, and a shaded deck area. You pay extra for food and drinks unless you opt for a catering package, which can be arranged through the charter company. The skipper handles all mooring and navigation, so you can focus on sunbathing, snorkelling, or just drinking sangria. Some operators allow you to bring your own alcohol, but check the policy first. The standard charter duration is 4 hours, with full-day (8-hour) trips available on request. Overnight stays are possible on larger catamarans, but those are less common for day hire.

Ports of Departure for Your Trip

Your Kemer catamaran hire departs from one of the main marinas along the Costa del Sol. Puerto Banús is the most popular, with its superyacht vibe and proximity to Marbella's nightlife. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) offers a more relaxed setting and easier parking. Cabopino is a smaller, quieter port near a nature reserve, ideal for a peaceful start. Estepona Marina has a charming old town nearby, and Sotogrande is upscale with a golf-and-polo crowd. Benalmádena is close to Málaga airport and has a lively promenade. Each port gives you access to different cruising grounds. For example, from Puerto Banús you can head toward Cala del Faro or the Río Verde area, while from Estepona you can cruise toward the Strait of Gibraltar and spot dolphins. Choose your departure port based on where you are staying and what you want to see.

Catamaran Options and Sizes

Catamarans available for hire range from 35 to 50 feet in length, accommodating 8 to 20 guests comfortably. A 40-foot Lagoon or Fountaine Pajot is typical for a group of 10 to 12. These boats have two or three cabins, a saloon, and a flybridge with sun pads. The catamaran design offers more deck space and stability than a monohull, so you will not get seasick easily. Some catamarans come with water toys like paddleboards, snorkel gear, or an inflatable kayak. If you have a larger group, you can book a 50-foot catamaran that sleeps up to 12 overnight. For a smaller, more intimate trip, a 35-foot catamaran works for 6 to 8 people. All catamarans have a licensed skipper who knows the local waters and can suggest the best anchorages. You can also request a hostess for an additional fee to serve drinks and food.

Pricing Guidance for Catamaran Hire

Prices for catamaran hire on the Costa del Sol vary by season, boat size, and duration. In low season (October to April), a 4-hour trip on a 40-foot catamaran starts from around EUR 1,200. High season (June to September) pushes that to EUR 1,800 or more for the same boat. Full-day charters range from EUR 2,000 to EUR 3,500 depending on the vessel and extras. Fuel is usually included for a standard itinerary of about 20 to 30 nautical miles. If you want to go further, such as to the Strait of Gibraltar or Nerja, fuel surcharges apply. Catering packages add EUR 30 to EUR 50 per person for a barbecue or paella lunch. You should always confirm what is included in the quote to avoid surprises. For the most accurate prices, use the BoatHire24 search tool to compare availability and rates from different operators.

Best Seasons for a Catamaran Trip

The Costa del Sol enjoys over 300 days of sunshine a year, so you can hire a catamaran almost any month. The peak season is July and August, when temperatures hit 30 degrees C and the sea is warm at 24 degrees C. This is also when prices are highest and availability is tightest. May, June, and September offer a sweet spot with pleasant weather, fewer crowds, and lower rates. April and October can be good if you get a calm day, but expect cooler evenings and possible wind. November to March is low season; many catamarans are still operational, but you might encounter rain or choppy seas. If you are flexible, booking in May or September gives you the best balance of cost and conditions. Always check the marine forecast before your trip, especially if you plan to go offshore.

How to Book Your Catamaran Hire

Booking a catamaran through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter your preferred date, group size, and port. The search results show available catamarans with photos, specifications, and prices. You can filter by boat type, length, and amenities. Once you find a catamaran you like, click through to the listing page to see the full details and the operator's terms. Most operators require a 50% deposit to confirm the booking, with the balance due on the day of the trip. Payment is usually via bank transfer or credit card. You will receive a confirmation email with the skipper's contact details and meeting point instructions. Cancellation policies vary, but many operators offer a full refund if you cancel at least 7 days in advance. For last-minute bookings, call the operator directly to check availability.

Who Is a Catamaran Trip For

Catamaran hire works for almost any group. Families with children appreciate the stable platform and shallow draft, which allows anchoring close to beaches. Groups of friends use it for birthday parties, bachelor or bachelorette celebrations, or just a day of fun on the water. Couples can book a private sunset cruise for a romantic evening. Corporate groups often charter catamarans for team-building events or client entertainment. The key advantage is space: catamarans have a large deck area for lounging, dining, and dancing. If you have guests who get seasick easily, the catamaran's twin-hull design minimises roll. The skipper can tailor the itinerary to your preferences, whether that is swimming in secluded coves, visiting beach clubs, or exploring coastal landmarks like the BoatHire24 blog has guides to the best anchorages.

Local Attractions You Can Visit

From the Costa del Sol, your catamaran can reach several notable spots. Cala del Faro is a quiet cove near Marbella with crystal-clear water, perfect for snorkelling. The Río Verde area offers a scenic estuary and a chance to see birdlife. If you depart from Estepona, you can cruise toward the Strait of Gibraltar, where dolphins and even whales are common. The Nerja Caves are inland, but you can anchor near the town of Nerja and take a short taxi ride to the caves. Puerto Banús itself is a spectacle, with luxury cars and designer shops lining the marina. Your skipper can also take you to a beach club for lunch, such as Ocean Club or Nikki Beach, where you can moor offshore and take a tender to the shore. For a more relaxed day, anchor in a quiet bay and have a barbecue on board.

What to Bring on Your Catamaran Trip

Pack light but smart. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe is better for the environment), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket or windbreaker for the afternoon breeze. If you plan to snorkel, some catamarans provide gear, but you can bring your own mask and fins. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos. You can bring your own food and drinks, but check with the operator first. Many catamarans have a fridge and a grill, so you can prepare a meal on board. Avoid glass bottles on some boats because of safety and cleanup. A small bag for rubbish is considerate. If you are prone to seasickness, take motion sickness tablets an hour before departure even on a catamaran, which is generally stable. The skipper will have a first-aid kit, but bring any personal medication.

Frequently Asked Questions About Catamaran Hire

Choosing the Right Catamaran for Your Group

Not all catamarans are the same, and picking the right one depends on your group size and what you want to do. For a group of 8 to 10 people, a 38-foot Lagoon 380 or a Fountaine Pajot Lucia 40 works well. These have a forward seating area, a flybridge with sun pads, and a saloon with a table for dining. If you have 12 to 16 guests, look at a 45-foot Leopard or a Bali 4.5, which have more deck space and a larger flybridge. For parties of 18 to 20, a 50-foot catamaran like the Lagoon 52 or the Fountaine Pajot Samana 59 gives you multiple lounging areas and a hydraulic swim platform. Some newer models have a foredeck trampoline, which is great for sunbathing. If you want water toys, check the listing for paddleboards, kayaks, or a water slide. Not all boats have them, but many operators can add them for an extra fee. The skipper will brief you on safety and the itinerary before departure, so ask questions if you are unsure about anything.

Specific Ports and Their Advantages

Each departure port on the Costa del Sol offers a different experience. Puerto Banús is the busiest and most glamorous, with easy access to the Marbella coastline and the Sierra Blanca mountains behind. From here, you can reach Cala del Faro in 20 minutes and the Río Verde estuary in 30 minutes. Marbella Marina is quieter and closer to the old town, so you can walk to restaurants before or after your trip. Cabopino is a small port near a sand dune nature reserve, ideal if you want a quick escape to the open sea without crowds. Estepona Marina is 20 minutes west of Marbella and gives you access to the waters toward Gibraltar, where dolphin sightings are common. Sotogrande is the most exclusive, with a golf resort atmosphere, and its marina is close to the Strait of Gibraltar. Benalmádena is near Málaga airport, making it convenient for tourists staying in Torremolinos or Fuengirola. Each port has parking, but space can be limited in high season, so arrive early or use a taxi.

Weather and Sea Conditions on the Costa del Sol

The Mediterranean off the Costa del Sol is generally calm, but conditions vary by season and location. In summer, the sea is flat with light winds, making for a smooth ride. The water temperature in August reaches 24 to 26 degrees C, comfortable for swimming without a wetsuit. In spring and autumn, you might encounter a light chop, especially in the afternoon when the Levante wind picks up. The Levante blows from the east and can create short, steep waves near the Strait of Gibraltar. If you are prone to seasickness, choose a morning departure when the wind is lighter. Winter months see rougher seas and cooler temperatures, around 14 to 16 degrees C. Most catamarans have a bimini top or full flybridge cover to provide shade or shelter from light rain. Your skipper will monitor the forecast and may adjust the itinerary if conditions change. Always trust their judgment; they know the local waters and will prioritise safety.

Custom Itineraries and Special Requests

Most catamaran charters allow you to customise the itinerary. Tell the skipper what you want to see, and they will plan a route. Popular options include a sunset cruise along the Marbella coastline, a trip to the Cabo de Gata natural park, or a dolphin-watching excursion near the Strait of Gibraltar. If you want to visit a beach club like Ocean Club Marbella or Nikki Beach, the skipper can anchor offshore and use the tender to take you in. Some operators offer a barbecue lunch on board, with fresh fish, paella, or grilled meat. For a special occasion, you can arrange for champagne, flowers, or a private chef. These extras cost more, but they make the trip more memorable. If you have a specific departure time, such as a sunset trip starting at 18:00, confirm it when booking. Most operators are flexible, but they need advance notice to adjust the schedule.

Cost Breakdown and Hidden Fees

When you get a quote for catamaran hire, ask what is included. The base price usually covers the boat, skipper, fuel for up to 30 nautical miles, and basic safety gear. Some operators charge extra for port fees, which can be EUR 50 to EUR 100 per trip. If you want a hostess or steward, expect to pay EUR 150 to EUR 250 extra for the day. Catering packages range from EUR 30 to EUR 60 per person for a three-course meal with drinks. If you bring your own alcohol, some operators charge a corkage fee of EUR 5 to EUR 10 per bottle. Gratuity for the skipper and crew is not included; 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee is standard if you are happy with the service. For a full-day charter with 12 guests, the total cost including catering and tips can be EUR 3,000 to EUR 4,500. Always get a written breakdown before paying the deposit to avoid surprises.

Safety and Licensing Requirements

All catamarans on BoatHire24 come with a licensed skipper who holds a valid Spanish or RYA qualification. The boat is insured and equipped with life jackets, a first-aid kit, fire extinguishers, and a VHF radio. The skipper will give a safety briefing at the start of the trip. You do not need a boating license to be a passenger. If you want to take the helm under the skipper's supervision, ask politely; some skippers allow it in open water. Children must wear life jackets on deck, and the skipper will provide child-sized vests. Alcohol consumption is allowed, but the skipper has the right to refuse service if someone is intoxicated and a risk. The boat will have a maximum capacity, and you must not exceed it. If the weather turns bad, the skipper may cancel or shorten the trip for safety. In that case, operators usually offer a reschedule or partial refund.

Booking Tips for First-Timers

If you have never hired a catamaran before, start by deciding your budget and group size. Use the BoatHire24 search tool to filter by date, port, and boat type. Read the listing details carefully, especially the cancellation policy and what is included. Contact the operator with any questions before booking. For a first trip, a 4-hour charter is enough to get a feel for the experience without getting bored. Book at least two weeks in advance in high season, as popular catamarans sell out. If you are flexible, consider a weekday trip; prices are lower and the marinas are less crowded. Arrive at the marina 15 minutes before departure to meet the skipper and load your belongings. Wear non-marking shoes on deck, and leave high heels behind. Bring cash for tips and any onboard extras like drinks or snacks. The skipper will appreciate a clear idea of your plans, so communicate your preferences early.

Environmental Considerations and Responsible Boating

The Costa del Sol's marine environment is fragile, and responsible boating helps preserve it. Avoid anchoring in posidonia seagrass meadows, which are protected. Your skipper knows the designated anchoring zones. Do not throw rubbish overboard; use the bins on the boat. If you see marine life like dolphins or sea turtles, keep a respectful distance and reduce speed. Do not feed the animals. Use reef-safe sunscreen to minimise chemical pollution in the water. Some operators provide biodegradable sunscreen on board. If you smoke, use a portable ashtray and never toss butts into the sea. The local authorities enforce fines for littering, so be mindful. By following these practices, you help keep the coastline clean for future visitors. Your skipper can tell you more about local conservation efforts, such as the dolphin-watching guidelines in the Strait of Gibraltar. Enjoy the trip, but leave no trace.

h1: Kemer Speedboat Rental: Hire Without Licence
intro:
You want to rent a speedboat in Kemer, but you don't have a licence. No problem. In Kemer, you can hire a speedboat without any paperwork, as long as you stick to the designated coastal areas and follow a quick safety briefing. It's one of the most straightforward ways to get on the water along the Turkish Riviera.

BoatHire24 lists boats in Kemer and across Turkey, but we focus on Marbella and the Costa del Sol. If you're set on Kemer, you'll find options here, but we also have plenty of licence-free day boats in Spain if you're flexible. Either way, you can compare prices and book directly.
bodyHtml:
What You Get with a Kemer Speedboat Rental

A typical Kemer speedboat rental is a small motorboat, usually between 4 and 7 metres long, with an outboard engine. You get a tank of fuel, life jackets, and a short briefing on where you can go and what to do. Most rentals are for 2-4 hours, though full-day options exist. You don't need a licence, but you must be at least 18 and sometimes 21. The boat is yours to drive, no skipper required.

Expect to pay from around EUR 80 for two hours up to EUR 250 for a full day, depending on the boat size and season. Fuel is sometimes included, sometimes extra. Check the listing details before booking.

Where You Can Go in Kemer

The Kemer coastline is a mix of rocky coves, pine forests, and clear water. You can head east towards Phaselis, an ancient city with three beaches, or west towards Çıralı and Olympos. The speedboat rental area is usually marked, and you can't go too far without a licence. Stick to the bays near Kemer Marina and the popular swimming spots like Ayışığı Bay or Çamyuva Beach.

If you want to go further, like to the sunken city of Kekova or the Seven Capes, you'll need a proper charter with a skipper. That's where our search can help you find a guided tour instead.

Boat Options in Kemer

Most speedboats here are small, open-hulled boats with a steering wheel and a small sunshade. You might find a 4-metre RIB with a 40hp engine, or a 6-metre fibreglass boat with a 90hp engine. Some rentals include a Bluetooth speaker, a cooler box, and a ladder for swimming. You won't find luxury yachts in this licence-free category, but you will get a fun, simple day on the water.

For bigger groups or more comfort, consider a BoatHire24 listing for a catamaran or motor yacht with a skipper. Those require a licence if you drive, but with a skipper you just relax.

Pricing Guidance for Kemer Speedboat Rentals

Prices vary by season. In June, July, and August, expect to pay the most. Low season (April-May, September-October) is cheaper. Here are rough numbers:

  • 2-hour rental: EUR 80-120
  • 4-hour rental: EUR 150-200
  • Full day (8 hours): EUR 200-350

Fuel costs extra if not included, usually EUR 20-40 per hour depending on how fast you go. Always confirm the total cost before you pay. Some operators ask for a deposit, often EUR 50-100, refundable if you bring the boat back undamaged.

Best Season for Kemer Speedboat Rental

The best time is May to October, when the water is warm and the weather is stable. July and August are the busiest and most expensive. May and September are quieter, with sea temperatures around 22-25 degrees C, perfect for swimming. April and October can be hit or miss, with cooler days and occasional wind. Winter rentals are rare; most boats are stored from November to March.

If you're visiting in the summer, book at least a week ahead. Walk-up rentals are possible, but you might miss out on the best boats or get stuck with a slow one.

How to Book a Kemer Speedboat

You can book online through BoatHire24 or similar platforms. Look for listings that say "no licence required" and check the cancellation policy. Most operators want a deposit via credit card, with the balance paid in cash or card on the day. Bring your passport or ID, and a printed or digital voucher.

On the day, you'll get a 10-15 minute safety briefing: how to start the engine, how to steer, where the fuel tank is, and the speed limits near the shore. You'll also get a map of the allowed area. Don't expect a full training session. It's a rental, not a course.

If you prefer a more structured experience, consider a private boat tour with a skipper. We have those on our blog, with tips on what to look for.

Who Is Kemer Speedboat Rental For?

It's for anyone who wants a quick, independent day on the water without the hassle of a licence. Couples, small families, and groups of friends often rent these boats. You don't need experience, but you should be comfortable driving a small vehicle. If you're nervous, book a shorter rental first. If you want to go fast, look for a boat with at least 60hp. If you want to relax, a slower boat with a sunshade works fine.

It's not for large parties, because most boats seat 4-6 people max. It's also not for overnight trips or long distances. Stick to the coast, anchor in a quiet bay, swim, and have a picnic. That's the point.

What About Kemer vs. Other Destinations?

Kemer is popular, but it's not the only place for licence-free boat rental. In Turkey, you can also rent in Bodrum, Fethiye, and Antalya. But if you're reading this on BoatHire24, you might also consider the Costa del Sol. We have licence-free boats in Marbella, Benalmádena, and Cabopino, with similar prices and better infrastructure. The water is colder, but the scenery is different: Puerto Banús, the Gibraltar dolphins, and the Nerja caves are all within reach.

Compare both options before you decide. Either way, you'll have a good time.

Kemer Marina: Your Starting Point

Most Kemer speedboat rentals depart from Kemer Marina, a modern facility with plenty of parking, cafes, and a small supermarket. The marina is well-protected from the wind, so launching is straightforward. You'll find the rental offices along the eastern quay, usually with boats tied up and ready to go. Arrive 30 minutes before your slot to park, check in, and get your briefing. If you're staying in a hotel near the centre, you can walk to the marina in 10-15 minutes. Taxis from the old town cost around EUR 5-8.

Speed Limits and No-Go Zones

Inside Kemer Marina and within 100 metres of the shore, the speed limit is 5 knots. That's a slow crawl, barely enough to steer. Once you're past the breakwater, you can open up, but keep an eye out for swimmers, kayaks, and other boats. The no-go zones are clearly marked on the map you get: the area around Phaselis ancient city is restricted, as is the military zone near Çıralı. Stick to the bays and open water within 5 nautical miles of the marina. If you cross into a restricted area, you risk a fine and losing your deposit.

What to Bring for a Day on the Water

Pack light. You need sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a towel, and swimwear. A waterproof phone pouch is useful for taking photos without worrying about splashes. Bring more water than you think you'll need, plus snacks or a packed lunch. Most speedboats have a small cooler, but ice is not always provided. A dry bag keeps your phone, wallet, and keys safe. If you get seasick easily, take a motion sickness pill an hour before you go. The boat will rock at anchor, especially if there's a swell.

Fuel Policy: What You Need to Know

Fuel policies vary. Some rentals include a full tank and ask you to return it full, meaning you pay for the fuel you use at a nearby station. Others give you a set amount, say 10 litres, and charge extra if you need more. A typical 60hp engine burns about 5-8 litres per hour at cruising speed, more if you go flat out. For a 4-hour rental, budget EUR 20-40 for fuel on top of the rental price. Always ask the operator: "Is fuel included, and if not, how much do you charge per litre?" This avoids surprises.

Insurance and Deposit Details

Most Kemer speedboat rentals include basic insurance, but the excess is high, often EUR 500-1000. That means if you damage the boat, you pay the first EUR 500 of repairs. To cover this, operators take a deposit, usually EUR 100-200, refunded if the boat comes back without new scratches or dings. Some operators offer a damage waiver for an extra EUR 20-30, reducing the excess to zero. Read the terms before you pay. If you're renting from a private owner through a platform, check the insurance separately.

Best Bays for Swimming and Anchoring

Ayışığı Bay is the closest to Kemer Marina, a 10-minute cruise east. It has calm, turquoise water and a pebble beach. Çamyuva Beach is a 15-minute ride west, with a sandy bottom and a few beach clubs where you can tie up and order drinks. For more privacy, head to the coves near Phaselis, but stay in the designated swimming areas. Avoid anchoring in seagrass meadows, as it damages the environment and your anchor might get stuck. Use the sandy patches. If you're unsure, ask the rental operator for their favourite spots.

Weather and Wind Conditions in Kemer

Kemer has a Mediterranean climate, but the wind can pick up in the afternoon. The meltemi wind, common in summer, blows from the north-west, creating choppy water in exposed areas. Mornings are usually calm, with light winds. By 2pm, the wind can reach 15-20 knots, making the sea uncomfortable in a small speedboat. Plan your rental for 9am to 1pm if you want flat water. If you're out in the afternoon and the wind rises, head back to the marina early. The rental operator will cancel if the forecast is bad, but they might not refund you if you ignore their advice.

Kemer Speedboat Rental for Beginners

If you've never driven a boat before, a speedboat rental in Kemer is a good place to start. The briefing covers the basics: how to start the engine, how to steer, how to reverse, and how to anchor. The marina channel is wide and clear, so you have room to practise. Start slow, stay in the no-wake zone until you're comfortable. Once you're in open water, increase speed gradually. Remember that boats steer from the back, so turning feels different from a car. Take a few gentle turns before you try high-speed manoeuvres. Most people get the hang of it in 15 minutes.

Group Rentals and Larger Boats

Most licence-free speedboats in Kemer seat 4-6 people. For groups of 6-8, you might find a 7-metre boat with a 115hp engine, but these are rarer and cost more, around EUR 300-400 for a full day. If you have a larger group, consider renting two boats, or book a private tour on a gulet or motor yacht with a skipper. That way everyone stays together, and you don't have to worry about navigation or fuel. Our search can filter for group-friendly options with a skipper included.

Kemer Speedboat Rental vs. Guided Tours

A speedboat rental gives you freedom, but a guided tour gives you local knowledge. If you want to see the sunken city of Kekova, the Chimera flames, or the Olympos ruins, you're better off on a tour with a guide who knows the history and the best spots. Speedboat rentals are for swimming, sunbathing, and short trips. Tours are for sightseeing. Compare the cost: a 4-hour speedboat rental costs about EUR 150-200 plus fuel, while a 6-hour guided boat tour with lunch costs around EUR 40-60 per person. For a couple, the rental might be cheaper. For a family of four, the tour often works out better value.

Hidden Costs to Watch Out For

Beyond fuel and deposit, watch for additional charges: cleaning fees (EUR 20-30 if you leave the boat messy), late return fees (EUR 50 per hour), and damage charges for scratches or broken parts. Some operators charge extra for a second set of life jackets or a cooler box. Always ask for the full price list before you book. If a deal seems too cheap, check the reviews. A EUR 50 rental might come with a hidden fuel surcharge that doubles the cost. Read the fine print on the booking page.

Kemer Speedboat Rental in Low Season

April and October are quieter, with fewer tourists and lower prices. The water is cooler, around 18-20 degrees C in April, so you'll need a wetsuit for swimming. The wind is more variable, with occasional storms. Check the forecast for three days before your rental. If a storm is predicted, the operator might cancel. Book a flexible cancellation policy if you're travelling in these months. Some operators offer discounts of 20-30% off high-season rates, so a full day might cost EUR 150 instead of EUR 250. It's a good time to go if you don't mind the chill.

Comparing Kemer to Other Turkish Destinations

Kemer is closer to Antalya airport than Bodrum or Fethiye, making it convenient for a short trip. The water is clearer than in Antalya city, but not as clear as in Kaş or Kalkan. The coastline is less developed than Bodrum, with more pine forests and fewer luxury resorts. For licence-free rentals, Kemer has a good range of boats, but Fethiye has more variety with the Ölüdeniz lagoon and Butterfly Valley nearby. If you're based in Antalya, Kemer is the best option for a day trip. For a longer holiday, consider both destinations.

bodyHtml:
What a Kemer Fishing Charter Actually Means

Kemer is a rocky cove about 5 NM west of Puerto Banús, near the Cala del Faro lighthouse. It is not a marina. There is no dock, no fuel station, no chandlery. So when you book a Kemer fishing charter, the boat departs from a proper port and heads to the fishing grounds off Kemer. The water there drops to 50 metres deep within a mile of the shore, which makes it a prime spot for bottom fishing. You can target sea bream, common sea bass, and red mullet. Further out, past the 100-metre line, you get into bluefin tuna territory, especially from June to September. Your skipper will know the exact marks, the wrecks, and the tide rips. You do not need to bring anything. The charter includes rods, reels, lures, bait, and life jackets. You bring sunscreen, a hat, and your own drinks and food unless the charter offers catering, which some do.

Ports You Can Depart From for a Kemer Fishing Charter

You have a choice of five departure ports, all within 20 NM of the Kemer fishing grounds. Puerto Banús is the closest, about 4 NM east. It is the glitzy one, with superyachts and champagne bars. The fishing boats there are well maintained and the skippers know the area intimately. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is 8 NM east, a bit more laid back, with easier parking. Cabopino is 12 NM east, small and quiet, good if you are staying near Calahonda. Estepona is 6 NM west of Kemer, a working port with good deep sea access. Sotogrande is 18 NM west, near the Gibraltar Strait, where the tuna run is serious. Benalmádena is 25 NM east, further but still viable for a full-day trip. You choose the port based on where you are staying. BoatHire24 shows you all available charters from each port, with prices and boat specs.

Boat Types for Kemer Fishing Charters

You get three main options. First, RIBs and speedboats, 6 to 8 metres, with outboard engines. These are fast, nimble, and cheap. They handle inshore fishing well, but they are rough in a chop. Half-day rates from around EUR 450. Second, motor yachts, 10 to 15 metres, with inboard diesels. These are stable, have a cabin for shade, and can handle offshore conditions. You can go 20 NM out for tuna. Prices from EUR 800 for a half-day. Third, catamarans, 12 to 15 metres. These are the most stable platform for fishing, almost no roll. They are also the most expensive, from EUR 1,200 for a half-day. Sailing yachts are not ideal for fishing charters because the rigging gets in the way, but some owners do offer it. Superyachts are available for luxury fishing charters, price on request. Licence-free day boats are not suitable for deep sea fishing, they are limited to 2 NM from shore.

Pricing Guidance for Kemer Fishing Charters

Prices vary by boat size, season, and duration. Half-day charters (4-5 hours) start from around EUR 450 for a 6-metre RIB, EUR 800 for a 10-metre motor yacht, EUR 1,200 for a 12-metre catamaran. Full-day charters (8-10 hours) are typically 1.5 times the half-day rate. Peak season is June to September, when demand is high and prices can be 20% higher. Low season is November to February, when you can negotiate. All prices include the skipper, fuel, fishing gear, and basic safety equipment. Some charters include lunch and drinks, check the listing. You pay a deposit to secure the booking, balance on the day. Search our listings for exact prices.

Best Season for Kemer Fishing Charters

You can fish year-round on the Costa del Sol, but the species change with the season. Summer (June to September) is best for bluefin tuna, mahi-mahi, and amberjack. Water temperature hits 24 degrees C. Winter (November to February) is good for sea bream, sea bass, and red mullet. Water temperature drops to 15 degrees C. Spring and autumn are transitional, with a mix of species. The wind is the main factor. The Levante (easterly) can blow hard in summer, making the sea rough. The Poniente (westerly) is lighter. Your skipper will advise on the best day. If you are after tuna, book between mid-June and mid-September. For bream, any month works.

What Is Included in a Kemer Fishing Charter

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, fuel, fishing rods and reels, lures and bait, life jackets, and basic first aid. You do not need a fishing licence, the boat holds a commercial licence that covers you. You get a cooler for your catch, but you need to arrange transport home if you want to keep the fish. Some charters offer cleaning and filleting on board. You can bring your own tackle if you prefer, but the boat gear is usually decent. You can also bring your own food and drink, or some charters offer a catering option. Check the specific listing. You are responsible for your own sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, and seasickness tablets if you need them. The skipper will provide a safety briefing before departure.

How to Book a Kemer Fishing Charter on BoatHire24

You go to the BoatHire24 homepage and enter your dates, group size, and preferred port. The search filters show you available charters. You click on a listing to see the boat details, skipper bio, inclusions, and price. You can message the owner directly if you have questions. To book, you pay a deposit online, usually 30% to 50%. The balance is paid to the skipper on the day, in cash or by card, depending on the listing. You get a confirmation email with the meeting point, time, and skipper contact. Cancellation policy varies, but typically you get a full refund if you cancel 48 hours before departure. No shows are not refunded. If the skipper cancels due to weather, you get a full refund or a reschedule. Simple.

Who Should Book a Kemer Fishing Charter

This is for you if you want a proper fishing experience, not a tourist trap. If you are a seasoned angler, you will appreciate the local knowledge of the skippers and the quality of the gear. If you are a beginner, the skipper will show you the basics and help you land your first fish. It is also for groups of friends or family who want a day on the water with a bit of action. You do not need to be a hardcore fisherman, but you should enjoy being at sea. If you get seasick easily, a half-day charter on a catamaran is the best bet. If you just want a booze cruise with a rod in the water, that is fine too, just let the skipper know. The charter is private, so it is your group only. No strangers. You can also book for corporate events or team building, many skippers offer catering and bar options.

Local Attractions Near Kemer and the Costa del Sol

After your fishing charter, you can explore the area. Kemer itself is a small cove with a pebble beach and a chiringuito (beach bar) that does grilled fish. Cala del Faro is a 10-minute walk east, with a lighthouse and views of La Concha mountain. Puerto Banús is 5 minutes by car, with its designer shops and restaurants. Marbella old town is 15 minutes, with narrow streets and tapas bars. Estepona old town is 20 minutes west, colourful and quiet. If you have time, the Strait of Gibraltar is 45 minutes west, where you can see dolphins and migrating whales. The Nerja caves are 1.5 hours east, worth a day trip. Your skipper can recommend a good place for lunch after the charter. Read our blog for more tips on things to do on the Costa del Sol.

Why Use BoatHire24 for Your Kemer Fishing Charter

We are a marketplace, not a charter company. We list boats from vetted owners and skippers. You get a choice of boats, transparent pricing, and direct communication with the skipper. No middleman markup. We cover all ports from Benalmádena to Sotogrande. We also have a blog with fishing tips, port guides, and seasonal species info. If you have questions, you can call or email us. We do not charge booking fees. You pay the same as if you booked direct. The only difference is you have more options and you can compare. We also handle the deposit securely. If something goes wrong, we mediate. It is the easiest way to book a Kemer fishing charter without the hassle.

Typical Catch and Seasons for Kemer Fishing Charters

You can expect a solid variety around Kemer. In summer (June to September), bluefin tuna is the headline act, with fish up to 200 kg caught 10 to 15 NM offshore. Mahi-mahi (dorado) show up from July, often near floating debris. Amberjack and bonito are common too. In spring (March to May), you get sea bream, red mullet, and common sea bass close to the rocky bottom. Autumn (October to November) brings a mix, with some tuna still around and more bream moving in. Winter (December to February) is slower but reliable for sea bream and bass, with fewer charters running. Your skipper will adjust the plan based on the day's conditions. If you want a specific species, ask when booking.

Fishing Techniques Used on Kemer Charters

Skippers around Kemer use several methods depending on the target. For bottom fishing, they drift or anchor over rocky patches and drop baited hooks with lead weights, targeting bream and bass at 20 to 50 metres deep. For tuna, trolling with artificial lures or live bait is standard, often at 6 to 8 knots. Some skippers use kite fishing to keep the bait on the surface, which works well for mahi-mahi. Jigging is also popular, especially for amberjack and bonito. Your skipper will have all the gear and will set it up for you. You do not need to know the technique in advance, just follow instructions. Beginners often prefer bottom fishing because it is simpler, while experienced anglers enjoy the fight of trolling for tuna.

Duration Options for Kemer Fishing Charters

You can book half-day, full-day, or extended charters. Half-day trips (4 to 5 hours) are best for inshore fishing close to Kemer, targeting bream and bass. You leave early morning or late afternoon, with enough time to catch a few fish and return. Full-day trips (8 to 10 hours) let you go further offshore for tuna and mahi-mahi, with a lunch break on the boat or at a beach. Extended charters (12 to 14 hours) are rare but available for serious anglers, often including a run to the Strait of Gibraltar for big tuna. Prices scale accordingly. A half-day on a RIB is around EUR 450, a full-day on a motor yacht is from EUR 1,200. Choose based on your appetite for time on the water.

Family-Friendly Kemer Fishing Charters

If you have kids, many skippers offer family-friendly charters. They use lighter tackle and stick to calmer inshore waters near Kemer, where the sea is less rough. Children as young as 6 can fish with supervision. The skipper will help them bait hooks and reel in small bream or bass. Some boats have shaded cabins and onboard toilets, which helps with younger children. You can also combine fishing with a swim stop at a quiet cove like Cala del Faro. Half-day charters on catamarans are the most stable, reducing seasickness risk. Prices are the same as standard charters, but you should mention kids when booking so the skipper prepares appropriate gear. No extra charge for children under 12 on most boats.

What to Bring and Wear on a Kemer Fishing Charter

You need practical gear. Wear non-slip shoes, boat shoes or trainers, no flip-flops. A light jacket or windbreaker is useful even in summer, as the sea breeze can be cool. Sunscreen is essential, SPF 50, and reapply every two hours. A hat with a brim and polarised sunglasses reduce glare and help you see fish. Bring a small bag with water, snacks, and any medication like seasickness tablets. Most charters have a cooler for your drinks. If you want to keep your catch, bring a cooler bag or arrange with the skipper to clean and bag it. Some boats provide plastic bags for transport. Do not bring glass bottles, they are banned on most boats for safety. A camera or phone in a waterproof case is handy for photos.

Accessibility and Special Needs on Kemer Fishing Charters

Not all boats are accessible. RIBs and speedboats require stepping from the dock into the boat, which can be tricky for mobility issues. Motor yachts and catamarans have wider boarding ramps and more stable decks. Some larger motor yachts (12 metres plus) have a toilet and a cabin, which helps if you need a break. If you have a wheelchair user, check the specific listing or message the owner. Most skippers are accommodating but the boat layout varies. Benalmádena and Marbella Marina have better dock access than Puerto Banús or Cabopino. For hearing or visual impairments, the skipper can adapt the safety briefing. Always communicate your needs when booking so the skipper can prepare. No extra charge for assistance, but availability may be limited.

Environmental and Catch-and-Release Practices

Most skippers on BoatHire24 support sustainable fishing. They encourage catch-and-release for undersized fish and for species like bluefin tuna if you do not plan to eat it. The Costa del Sol has size limits: sea bream must be at least 23 cm, sea bass 36 cm, and bluefin tuna 70 cm. Your skipper will measure and release anything too small. If you keep fish, only take what you will eat. Some charters offer catch-and-release only, check the listing. The boat's commercial licence covers you, but you are expected to follow local regulations. Do not discard fishing line or bait packaging at sea. Most skippers have bins on board. By choosing a responsible charter, you help maintain the fish stocks for future seasons.

Combining a Kemer Fishing Charter with Other Activities

You can pair your fishing trip with other experiences. Many skippers offer a half-day fishing and half-day cruising option, where you fish in the morning and then head to a beach club or cove for lunch and a swim. Cala del Faro and the coves near Kemer are good spots. Some charters include a stop at the Marbella coastline for sightseeing, with views of La Concha mountain. If you book a full-day charter, you can ask to include a visit to the Strait of Gibraltar for dolphin watching, though this adds fuel costs. Estepona old town is a great lunch stop if you dock there. You can also combine with a sunset cruise after fishing, but that usually requires a separate booking. Check with the skipper when you book.

faqs.q: Do I need a fishing licence for a Kemer fishing charter?
faqs.a: No. The boat holds a commercial fishing licence that covers all passengers. You can fish without a personal licence. The skipper handles the legal side.

faqs.q: What fish can I catch on a Kemer fishing charter?
faqs.a: Common catches include sea bream, sea bass, red mullet, and mackerel inshore. Offshore, you can target bluefin tuna, mahi-mahi, and amberjack from June to September. Your skipper will know the season.

faqs.q: How long is a typical Kemer fishing charter?
faqs.a: Half-day charters are 4 to 5 hours. Full-day charters are 8 to 10 hours. You can also book a 3-hour inshore trip on some RIBs. The skipper will advise on the best duration for your target species.

faqs.q: Can I keep the fish I catch?
faqs.a: Yes, you can keep your catch within legal size and bag limits. The skipper will help you clean and fillet the fish. You need to bring a cooler to transport it home. Some charters provide a cooler.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.a: The skipper will cancel the charter if conditions are unsafe. You get a full refund or you can reschedule. You are not charged for weather cancellations. The skipper will contact you the day before if there is a risk.

faqs.q: Is the Kemer fishing charter private?
faqs.a: Yes, every charter is private for your group only. You do not share the boat with strangers. You can bring up to the maximum capacity of the boat, typically 6 to 12 passengers depending on the size.

faqs.q: What should I bring on a Kemer fishing charter?
faqs.a: Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a light jacket, and any seasickness tablets you need. You can bring your own food and drink, or check if the charter offers catering. The boat provides fishing gear and life jackets.

title: Marbella Motor Yacht Hire for Hen Do: Party Ideas
metaDescription: Marbella motor yacht hire for hen do: party ideas, ports, prices. Book a crewed motor yacht for your hen weekend on the Costa del Sol.
h1: Marbella Motor Yacht Hire for Hen Do: Party Ideas
keyword: Marbella motor yacht hire for hen do
intro:
If you are planning a hen do in Marbella, a motor yacht hire is one of the most memorable ways to celebrate. You get a private boat, a licensed skipper, and the freedom to swim, sunbathe, and party along the Costa del Sol. This page covers everything you need to know: which ports to depart from, what boat types work best, how much it costs (from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day), and how to book without stress.

We are BoatHire24, a local marketplace that connects you directly with boat owners and charter companies in Marbella, Puerto Banús, Estepona, and beyond. Every booking includes a professional skipper, so you can focus on the hen and the prosecco. No licence required, no hidden fees.
bodyHtml:
Why Choose a Motor Yacht for a Hen Do in Marbella

A motor yacht gives you space, speed, and flexibility. Unlike a catamaran or sailing yacht, a motor yacht can cover more coastline in less time, which means you can hit multiple spots in one day. You also get a flybridge or sundeck for sunbathing, a spacious saloon for dancing or games, and often a swim platform for quick dips.

For a hen do, you want a boat that feels exclusive and allows for noise without bothering other guests. Motor yachts are generally more private than shared charters or catamarans, and the crew is used to hen groups. Many boats also come with sound systems, coolers, and optional extras like a DJ or a BBQ.

Marbella weather helps: from May to October, you can expect 25-30 degrees C, calm seas, and long daylight hours. That gives you a solid 6-8 hour window for a half-day charter, or you can go full-day and add a sunset cruise.

Which Ports Can You Depart From

Your hen do motor yacht can start from several ports along the Costa del Sol. The most popular is Puerto Banús, the glitzy marina with designer shops, restaurants, and a party vibe. Departing from here puts you right in the action, and you can cruise past the superyachts before heading to quieter anchorages.

Other options include Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo), which is closer to Marbella town and the old town; Cabopino, a smaller, more relaxed marina near Artola dunes; Estepona, with its charming old town and easy access to the Strait of Gibraltar; Sotogrande, a luxury estate with a large marina; and Benalmádena, popular for its marina and proximity to Málaga airport.

Each port has different boat availability and pricing. Puerto Banús tends to have the widest selection of motor yachts, from 40ft to 100ft+, while smaller ports like Cabopino or Estepona offer more intimate, budget-friendly options. You can browse all boats on our search page and filter by port.

What Boat Types Work Best for a Hen Do

For a hen group, you want a boat with enough deck space for everyone to sit, dance, and take photos. Motor yachts from 40 to 60 feet are ideal for groups of 10-20 people. Larger yachts (60-80ft) can handle up to 30 guests comfortably, with multiple decks and a flybridge.

Popular models include the Sunseeker Predator, Azimut Flybridge, Princess V-class, and Ferretti. These are common in Marbella charters. If the hen loves a bit of glamour, a superyacht (80ft+) is available on request, but prices start from around EUR 8,000 per day.

For smaller groups (6-10 people), a motorboat or RIB can be fun and fast, though they lack a cabin and toilet. A catamaran is also an option if the group prefers stability and a huge deck, but catamarans are slower and less flashy. Most hen groups prefer the sleek look of a motor yacht.

How Much Does Motor Yacht Hire Cost for a Hen Do

Prices vary by boat size, duration, season, and port. As a rough guide, a half-day (4 hours) motor yacht for up to 12 guests starts from around EUR 1,500 in low season (April-May, October). A full day (8 hours) for the same group is about EUR 2,500-3,500. In peak summer (June-September), add 20-30%.

For a larger group (20-30 guests), expect EUR 4,000-6,000 for a full day on a 60ft yacht. Superyachts are price on request, typically EUR 8,000-15,000 per day. All prices include the skipper, fuel, and basic insurance. Extras like food, drinks, a DJ, water toys (jet ski, paddleboard), or a photographer cost extra.

We recommend getting a quote from multiple owners via our platform. You can send a request with your group size, preferred date, and budget, and we connect you with available boats. No obligation, no middleman markup.

What Is Included in a Hen Do Yacht Charter

Every motor yacht charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation and safety. You do not need a boating licence. The skipper is there for the entire trip and can also act as a host, but they are not a waiter or entertainer. You can bring your own food and drinks, or order catering through the charter company.

Most boats come with a sound system (Bluetooth or AUX), a cooler or fridge, a toilet (or two on larger yachts), and a swim platform with a ladder. Some have a BBQ, a flybridge with seating, and a sun pad area. Water toys like a paddleboard or snorkel gear are often included or available for a small fee.

What is not included: food, drinks, crew tips (optional but appreciated, around 10-15% of the charter fee), and any damages caused by the group. You should also confirm if the boat allows smoking (usually only on the deck, not inside).

Best Hen Do Party Ideas on a Motor Yacht

Here are some party ideas that work well on a motor yacht in Marbella:

  • Swim stop at Cala del Faro: A secluded cove near Cabopino, perfect for a champagne toast in the water.
  • Sunset cruise past Puerto Banús: Watch the superyachts light up as the sun sets behind La Concha mountain.
  • Dolphin watching near the Strait of Gibraltar: A longer trip (2+ hours each way) but worth it for the pod sightings.
  • Anchor at Río Verde: A calm river mouth near Marbella, great for paddleboarding and a BBQ lunch.
  • DJ set on the flybridge: Many boats allow you to bring a small speaker or hire a DJ. Just check the boat's sound system limits.
  • Hen games: Think truth or dare, scavenger hunt, or a 'pin the tail on the groom' game. The deck is your stage.

For a longer trip, consider a full-day charter to Estepona for lunch in the old town, or a day trip to Nerja to see the caves (about 1.5 hours from Marbella by motor yacht).

When Is the Best Time for a Hen Do Yacht Charter

The Costa del Sol has a long season for motor yacht charters, from April to October. The best months for a hen do are May, June, September, and October. These months offer warm weather (25-30 degrees C), fewer crowds, and lower prices than July and August. July and August are peak season: hot (30-35 degrees C), busy marinas, and higher charter prices.

If you want a sunset cruise, book a late afternoon departure (4pm-8pm) in summer, or 2pm-6pm in spring and autumn. The light is golden, and the temperature is pleasant. For a full-day party, start at 10am, swim at 12pm, lunch at 1pm, and return by 6pm.

Weekends (Friday to Sunday) are the most popular for hen dos, so book at least 2-3 weeks in advance for summer weekends. Weekdays are more available and slightly cheaper.

How to Book a Motor Yacht for Your Hen Do

Booking through BoatHire24 is straightforward. Go to our BoatHire24 homepage, enter your group size, preferred date, and port. Browse the available motor yachts, read the descriptions, and check the photos. Each listing shows the maximum capacity, included amenities, and price.

Send an enquiry to the owner or charter company through the platform. They will respond with availability and a final quote. You can ask about extras like catering, water toys, or a photographer. Once you agree, you pay a deposit (usually 50%) to secure the booking. The balance is paid on the day, often in cash or by card on board.

We recommend reading the cancellation policy carefully. Most charters offer a full refund if cancelled 14+ days before, and a partial refund within 7-14 days. Last-minute cancellations (less than 7 days) may forfeit the deposit.

For more tips on planning your hen do, check our blog for guides on what to pack, how to handle seasickness, and the best restaurants in Puerto Banús.

Who Is This Hen Do Yacht Charter For

This type of charter is ideal for groups of 8-20 women who want a private, luxury experience without the hassle of organising a venue. It works for both daytime parties and evening cruises. If the hen loves the sea, sun, and a bit of glamour, a motor yacht in Marbella is a solid choice.

It is less suitable for very large groups (30+) unless you book a superyacht or a catamaran. It is also not ideal for groups with small children, as motor yachts have limited safety features for kids (no lifeguard, railings can be low). For a mixed group of adults and kids, a catamaran is safer and more spacious.

If your hen do is on a tight budget (under EUR 1,000 total), consider a shared boat tour or a smaller RIB charter. But for a memorable, all-inclusive party, a private motor yacht is worth the splurge.

Frequently Asked Questions

How to Choose the Right Motor Yacht Layout for Your Group

The layout matters more than the length. A 50-foot motor yacht with a single main deck and no flybridge can feel cramped for 15 people, while a 45-foot yacht with a flybridge and a large aft deck can work well for 12. Look for boats with an open-plan saloon that connects to the aft deck, so the group can flow between inside and outside. A flybridge is a huge plus for a hen do: it gives you a second social area with panoramic views, perfect for photos with La Concha mountain in the background. Some boats, like the Princess V58, have a flybridge with a wet bar and sun pads. Others, like the Sunseeker Portofino, have a large cockpit with a U-shaped sofa that can double as a dance floor. When you browse listings on our BoatHire24 site, check the deck plan photos. If the boat has a separate cabin below deck, that can be used as a changing room or a quiet space for anyone who needs a break from the party.

What to Pack for a Hen Do Motor Yacht Charter

Packing right makes the day smoother. Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (SPF 50, the sun is strong), sunglasses, a hat, and a light cover-up or kaftan for when the wind picks up. Non-slip shoes or barefoot are best on deck; heels damage the teak and are not allowed. For the evening, pack a dress or smart casual outfit if you plan to go to a restaurant after the charter. A waterproof phone case is useful for photos at the swim stop. Bring a portable speaker if the boat's sound system is basic, but check with the skipper first. For seasickness, bring ginger tablets or acupressure bands; the pharmacist in Puerto Banús sells them. Do not bring glass bottles on board, as broken glass on deck is dangerous. Plastic cups and cans are fine. Most charters provide a cooler with ice, but confirm this in advance. For more packing tips, see our blog on what to bring for a day on the water.

How to Plan the Itinerary for a Half-Day vs Full-Day Charter

A half-day charter (4 hours) is enough for a swim stop, a short cruise, and a bit of sunbathing. A typical half-day itinerary: depart Puerto Banús at 10am, cruise east to Cala del Faro (20 minutes), anchor for a swim and champagne, then cruise back via Marbella Marina, arriving by 2pm. For a full day (8 hours), you can add a longer cruise south to Estepona or north to Cabopino. A popular full-day route: depart 10am, cruise to Río Verde (15 minutes from Puerto Banús), anchor for paddleboarding and a BBQ lunch, then cruise to Estepona old town for a walk and ice cream, returning by 6pm. If the group wants dolphin watching, you need a full day because the Strait of Gibraltar is about 1.5 hours from Marbella by motor yacht. Book a boat with a good cruising speed (20-25 knots) to make the most of the time. The skipper will suggest a route based on weather and sea conditions. You can search for boats with specific features on our search page.

What Extras Can You Add to a Hen Do Charter

Many charter companies offer optional extras that turn a good day into a great one. A DJ or a sound system upgrade costs from around EUR 200-500 for the day. A photographer or videographer to capture the group shots and drone footage is around EUR 300-600. Water toys like a jet ski (EUR 150-250 per hour), a paddleboard (EUR 50-100), or snorkel gear (EUR 20-30 per set) can be added. Some boats offer a BBQ lunch with paella, grilled meat, and salad, priced at EUR 25-45 per person. For a luxury touch, order a champagne welcome with strawberries, or a custom cake from a bakery in Puerto Banús. If the hen wants a hen-themed decoration (balloons, banners, sashes), confirm with the charter company first, as some boats do not allow decorations that could damage the interior. All extras should be arranged at least 48 hours before the charter. The skipper can recommend local suppliers.

How to Handle Seasickness and Safety on a Motor Yacht

Motor yachts are more stable than smaller boats, but the Mediterranean can have chop, especially in the afternoon when the levante wind picks up. If anyone in the group is prone to seasickness, take medication the night before or an hour before departure. Ginger tea or crackers help. The skipper will adjust the speed and route to minimise discomfort. Onboard safety: the skipper does a safety briefing at the start. Life jackets are available for all guests, but you are not required to wear them unless the skipper says so. Children must wear life jackets at all times on deck. The boat has a first aid kit and a VHF radio for emergencies. If someone falls overboard, the skipper will stop the boat and throw a life ring. Do not jump in to rescue them yourself. The skipper is trained for this. For more safety tips, read our blog guide on staying safe on a yacht charter.

What to Do After the Charter: Best Hen Do Restaurants and Bars Near the Ports

After a day on the water, you will want to continue the party or have a relaxed dinner. In Puerto Banús, restaurants like Bibo (by Dani García) or La Pesquera offer seafood with a view of the marina. For a more casual vibe, try El Mero or the beachfront chiringuitos at Playa de Puerto Banús. In Marbella town, the old quarter has tapas bars like La Taberna del Pintxo or El Estrecho. In Estepona, the old town is full of whitewashed squares with outdoor dining, such as Plaza de las Flores. If you dock at Cabopino, the beach club La Luna is a good option. For a late night, the clubs in Puerto Banús (like Olivia Valere or Pangea) are open until 4am. Some charter companies offer a combined package with a restaurant booking or a club entry. Ask when you book. You can find more recommendations in our blog posts about dining in Marbella.

How to Budget for a Hen Do Motor Yacht Charter: Hidden Costs

The base charter price covers the boat, skipper, fuel, and insurance. But there are extra costs to plan for. Food and drinks: if you bring your own, budget around EUR 20-30 per person for a BBQ lunch and drinks. If you order catering, it is EUR 35-50 per person. Crew tip: 10-15% of the charter fee is customary, so on a EUR 3,000 charter, that is EUR 300-450. Water toys and extras: a jet ski for an hour is EUR 150-250, a photographer is EUR 300-600. Transfer to the port: if your accommodation is not near the marina, a taxi or minibus from Marbella to Puerto Banús is about EUR 20-30 each way. Parking at the port costs EUR 20-30 per day. Some charter companies charge a cleaning fee (EUR 50-100) if the boat is left very dirty. Confirm all potential extras before booking. Use our platform to compare quotes and see what is included in each listing.

What to Do If the Weather Is Bad on Your Charter Day

Marbella has over 300 sunny days a year, but bad weather can happen. If the forecast shows strong winds or rain, the skipper may cancel or reschedule for safety. Most charters have a weather clause: if the skipper deems it unsafe, you get a full refund or a reschedule. If the weather is marginal but not dangerous, the skipper might suggest a shorter route or staying in sheltered waters like the Río Verde or the bay of Estepona. You can also change the date if you have flexibility. Check the cancellation policy before booking. For hen dos booked months in advance, consider a backup plan: a beach club or a restaurant with a private room. The skipper will communicate with you 24-48 hours before the charter to discuss the weather. If you have questions about weather policies, contact the charter owner through our platform.
